Multivariable logistic regression showed that OBPM was independently associated with lower odds of delirium (OR = 0.409, 95% CI: 0.184-0.909, p = 0.028). Mechanical ventilation (OR = 3.500, P = 0.010), sepsis-related organ failure assessment (SOFA) score (OR = 1.139, p = 0.010), and ratio of arterial oxygen partial pressure to fraction of inspired oxygen (PaO2/FiO2) (OR = 0.995, p = 0.014) were also independently associated with delirium. No significant differences were observed between groups in hospital length of stay or mortality. Independent risk factors for mortality included sepsis, Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) II score, lactate level, and prothrombin time. Cerebral regulation-targeted optimal blood pressure management was associated with a reduced incidence of delirium and shorter ICU stay in elderly critically ill patients, without increasing mortality. Larger multicenter randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings and guide clinical implementation.

42875939.title: Clinical characteristics and risk factors for intensive care unit admission and mortality in rapid response team-activated ward patients: a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital in South Korea.
42875939.abstract: Factors driving intensive care unit (ICU) transfer decisions and mortality after rapid response team (RRT) activation remain unclear. We identified independent predictors of ICU admission, 28-day mortality, and in-hospital mortality in RRT-activated ward patients. This retrospective cohort study included adults with first RRT activation from September 2023 to August 2025 at a Korean tertiary hospital (n=549). Multivariable logistic regression with backward elimination was used. Of 549 patients, 191 (34.8%) were transferred to the ICU. ICU admission was independently predicted by procalcitonin >0.5 ng/ml (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.833; P=0.021) and lower hemoglobin (aOR, 0.808 per g/dl; P=0.040), whereas solid tumor was associated with lower transfer likelihood (aOR, 0.142; P<0.001). Mortality did not differ significantly between ICU and ward groups at 28 days (27.7% vs. 27.7%, P=0.937) or during hospitalization (46.1% vs. 40.2%, P=0.162). Declining peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂)/fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO₂) ratio, rising lactate, and hyperkalemia predicted both mortality outcomes. Lower platelet count uniquely predicted 28-day mortality, whereas solid tumor, chronic kidney disease, and deep learning-based continuous cardiac arrest risk score (DeepCARS) additionally predicted in-hospital mortality. ICU admission itself was not independently associated with mortality. ICU transfer after RRT activation appears to reflect acute reversibility, clinical trajectory, and possible at/after-activation goals-of-care processes rather than severity alone. Mortality was more closely associated with oxygenation failure, hypoperfusion, and electrolyte instability than with disposition.

42875287.title: EACTS/STS/AATS Guidelines on Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Adult Cardiac Surgery: An Expert Analysis for Cardiothoracic Anesthesia and Critical Care.
42875287.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

42867743.title: The use of capillary refill time In adult critically ill patients: a narrative review on potentials, pitfalls, and perspectives.
42867743.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
42867743.abstract: The evolution of Capillary refill time (CRT) use in clinical medicine is interesting, transforming a simple bedside observation into a reliable tool for assessing tissue perfusion in critically ill patients. When Henry Beecher and colleagues first systematized CRT measurement in 1947, they recognized its potential as a rapid method to evaluate circulatory status in trauma casualties, establishing a foundational framework that would influence intensive care practice for decades to come. However, clinicians soon discovered that relying on visual inspection alone introduced troubling variability between observers and even within the same observer's assessments, with expertise and training significantly influencing measurement accuracy. This recognition of CRT's limitations sparked a concerted effort to transform the measurement from a purely subjective exercise into a standardized, objective clinical tool. Researchers systematically refined protocols by establishing consistent pressure application techniques, standardized measurement sites, and defined normal thresholds (approximately 3 s for healthy adults). These methodological advances set the stage for rigorous clinical validation. Subsequent research revealed that CRT correlated powerfully with microvascular blood flow and independently predicted mortality and organ dysfunction in septic patients. Meta-analyses encompassing over 60,000 patients confirmed that abnormal CRT carried substantially elevated mortality risk, particularly when measured using standardized techniques. More recently, the ANDROMEDA-SHOCK trials demonstrated that CRT could serve not merely as a prognostic marker but as an actionable resuscitation target. CRT is nowadays considered an adjunct bedside marker to guide fluid and vasopressor resuscitation in adults with sepsis and septic shock, supporting individualized hemodynamic strategies while reducing over-resuscitation risks.

42866097.title: Cardiogenic Shock Systems of Care Best Practices, Part 3: Regionalization of Care, Organizational Components, and Critical Care Transport Medicine.
42866097.abstract: This paper explores the regionalization of care, organizational components, and critical care transport medicine for cardiogenic shock patients. It discusses the establishment of cardiogenic shock centers, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the necessary infrastructure to ensure optimal patient outcomes. Emphasizing the importance of a regionalized treatment algorithm and transfer strategy, the paper builds on the foundational understanding of managing cardiogenic shock, aiming to provide a comprehensive framework for advanced management and regional transfer strategies essential for high-risk patients.

42864191.title: Continuous glucose monitoring for diabetes mellitus in the perioperative and intensive care setting: a prospective observational validation study(✰).
42864191.abstract: In-hospital diabetes mellitus management currently relies on intermittent glucose monitoring with point-of-care (POC) testing, rather than continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Most studies on CGM have focused on its benefits and accuracy in the outpatient setting, in contrast to the hospital setting, where the accuracy may be different. In this prospective observational study (NCT06297850), we assessed the accuracy of CGM (Dexcom G7, Dexcom Inc.) compared with POC monitors in people with diabetes mellitus requiring glucose-lowering medication undergoing surgery or admission to the ICU. The primary outcome was agreement between CGM and POC measurements, defined as median absolute relative difference (MARD). Clarke error grid (CEG) and Bland-Altman analyses were used to quantify the accuracy. Secondary analyses assessed agreement during periods of hypoperfusion, defined as a mean arterial pressure of <65 mm Hg, infusions with vasopressors, or reduced peripheral perfusion index. In 58 participants (mean [standard deviation] age 71 [11]yr; 34% female), the median MARD was 10.9% (5.1-19.4%); 1186 of 1212 paired POC and CGM measurements (98%) were within clinically acceptable ranges (CEG zones A and B). MARD was 4.5% higher (95% confidence interval 2.3-6.7%) during periods of hypoperfusion. Given that hypoglycaemia (<4 mM) did not occur, no paired readings were obtained. Bland-Altman analysis showed similar CGM and POC measurements, with a mean difference of -1 mM (95% limits of agreement -5.6 to 3.4 mM). For the vast majority of interstitial glucose measurements, CGM was accurate in people with diabetes mellitus. Although overall performance was good, caution may be warranted when interpreting CGM data during periods of impaired peripheral perfusion. NCT06297850.

42862751.title: Clinical Validation of the Nursing Diagnosis "Risk for Shock" in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction Admitted to the ICU.
42862751.abstract: ObjectiveTo clinically validate the nursing diagnosis "Risk for shock" in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) admitted to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).MethodA retrospective case-control study conducted at a high-complexity university hospital in Brazil. The sample consisted of 116 medical records of adult patients with AMI, equally distributed between the case group (with cardiogenic shock; n = 58) and the control group (without cardiogenic shock; n = 58). Diagnostic accuracy measures (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios) were calculated, and multivariate binary logistic regression using the Stepwise Forward method was applied to identify independent predictors and control for confounders.ResultsIn the accuracy analysis, the indicator "Unstable blood pressure" showed the best clinical balance, with a sensitivity of 85.0% (95% CI: 76.2-93.8) and a specificity of 83.6% (95% CI: 74.4-92.8). "Hyperthermia" and "Inadequate fluid volume" showed the highest individual specificities (90.1% and 80.3%, respectively). After adjusting the logistic regression model (Nagelkerke R2 = 0.614; Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.782), only four factors remained significant as independent predictors of the outcome: unstable blood pressure (aOR = 7.80; 95% CI: 3.10-19.60; p < 0.001), hypoxia (aOR = 3.70; 95% CI: 1.50-9.20; p = 0.006), hypoxemia (aOR = 2.90; 95% CI: 1.40-6.10; p = 0.004), and inadequate fluid volume (aOR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.00-4.50; p = 0.048). Thermal and hemorrhagic indicators lost significance after adjustment.ConclusionThe study clinically validated the diagnosis and confirmed a robust predictive model composed of four indicators. Prioritizing the monitoring of these risk factors enables critical care nurses to anticipate hemodynamic collapse, support targeted care protocols, and optimize multiprofessional decision-making at the bedside.

42853471.title: Immunonutritional status and survival after cardiac arrest: prognostic value of the prognostic nutritional index, the cholesterol-modified prognostic nutritional index, and the controlling nutritional status score in post-cardiopulmonary resuscitation intensive care patients.
42853471.abstract: Patients achieving return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after cardiac arrest experience marked systemic inflammation, metabolic stress, and nutritional impairment, all of which contribute to high mortality. Practical prognostic indices reflecting immunonutritional status may facilitate early risk stratification in this population. To evaluate the prognostic value of immunonutritional indices for predicting mortality in patients with ROSC after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. This single-center, retrospective cohort study included adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit after ROSC following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest between January 2015 and January 2025. Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI), cholesterol-modified Prognostic Nutritional Index (CPNI), and Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) scores were calculated from laboratory parameters obtained within the first 24 h of ICU admission. Patients were classified as survivors or non-survivors based on ICU outcome. Associations with mortality were evaluated using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses, and discriminatory performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Among 444 post-ROSC patients, non-survivors had lower PNI (43.66 ± 15.47 vs. 55.06 ± 17.21) and higher CPNI (81.10 ± 13.70 vs. 66.90 ± 18.25) and CONUT scores (4.27 ± 3.04 vs. 2.43 ± 2.43; all p < 0.001). In separate stepwise multivariable models, PNI (aOR 0.64 per 10-point increase), CPNI (aOR 1.25 per 10-point increase), and CONUT (aOR 1.24 per 1-point increase) remained independently associated with mortality. AUCs were 0.689, 0.631, and 0.681, respectively; PNI showed the highest sensitivity (86.3%) at a cut-off of ≤ 59.90. PNI, CPNI, and CONUT were significantly associated with ICU mortality after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. These indices may reflect systemic inflammation, immune dysfunction, metabolic stress, and nutritional reserve rather than nutritional status alone. Their availability from routine laboratory parameters may support early risk stratification. Further prospective studies are needed to confirm their prognostic value and clinical applicability.

42840398.title: Association Between Hour-by-Hour ICU Admission Timing and 24-h Mortality: A Single-Center Retrospective Observational Study.
42840398.abstract: Prior studies of ICU admission timing often use broad categories (day vs. night), potentially masking hour-level effects. We examined hour-by-hour ICU admission timing and mortality, with attention to nighttime periods and routine handovers. We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study in a closed ICU with 24/7 on-site intensivist coverage, using prospectively registered data from the Japanese Intensive Care Patient Database. Adults (≥ 18 years) admitted to the E-ICU between April 2017 and July 2025 were included. Admission hour (0-23) was modeled as a continuous exposure using restricted cubic splines (reference 14:00). The primary outcome was 24-h mortality and the secondary outcome was ICU mortality. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for demographics, APACHE II, invasive mechanical ventilation at admission, comorbidities, diagnostic categories, admission source, and post-cardiac arrest status. Bootstrap resampling was used to estimate 95% confidence intervals. Additional analyses examined handover, nighttime, and 24-h periodic patterns. Among 5724 patients, 24-h and ICU mortality were 3.4% and 10.6%, respectively. Compared with 14:00, adjusted odds of 24-h mortality were higher in the early morning. The early-evening estimate was imprecise, with the 95% CI including unity. In contrast, ICU mortality showed no clear temporal pattern. Handover comparisons showed no clear mortality association; nighttime admission was not associated with higher mortality, and cosinor analysis was nonsignificant. Hour-by-hour analysis showed higher adjusted odds of 24-h mortality in the early morning, whereas evidence of an increase in the early evening was inconclusive. Direct comparisons of handover periods showed no clear association with mortality.

42834393.title: Extrapolation of MAP trends predicts hypotension and vasopressor up-titration in the ICU.

42833118.title: Long-term survival following in-hospital cardiac arrest in patients admitted to the intensive care unit: A matched cohort study.
42833118.abstract: Survival after in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) has improved; however, long-term outcomes among patients who experience IHCA during intensive care unit (ICU) admission and survive to hospital discharge remain poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term survival of patients who experienced IHCA during ICU admission. This population-based cohort study included adult patients admitted to the ICUs between 2015 and 2019. Patients who experienced IHCA during ICU admission and survived to discharge were compared with ICU patients who did not experience IHCA. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed at a 1:3 ratio based on age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and ICU interventions. Long-term mortality was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression with additional adjustment for socioeconomic and hospital-related factors. Time-interval analysis assessed temporal changes in mortality risk after discharge. After PSM, 80,908 patients were included. During a follow-up of up to 9 years, survival was significantly lower in the IHCA group than in matched controls (log-rank p < 0.001). One-year survival rates were 0.47 (95% CI: 0.46-0.47) and 0.70 (95% CI: 0.70-0.71) in the IHCA and non-IHCA groups, respectively. IHCA during ICU admission was independently associated with higher long-term mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.72; 95% CI: 1.68-1.75). Excess risk was greatest within the first 6 months after discharge (aHR, 2.35; 95% CI: 2.29-2.41) and gradually attenuated thereafter, remaining significant for up to 2 years. IHCA during ICU admission was associated with higher long-term mortality than matched ICU controls. The early post-discharge period represents a period of particularly high mortality risk and may warrant closer clinical attention. These findings highlight the need to recognize ICU survivors of IHCA as a high-risk population. Further studies are needed to determine whether structured post-discharge follow-up can improve long-term outcomes.

42825956.title: [Core data set telemedicine in intensive care medicine. Requirement catalogue via Delphi study].
42825956.abstract: Telemedicine in intensive care medicine has not yet been uniformly defined or standardized in its implementation in Germany. While the evidence predominantly comes from nonrandomized US studies, German randomized controlled studies (RCT) show potential for improving guideline-compliant treatment. The aim is to develop a consensus-based core data set that standardizes teleconsultations, strengthens data-based care processes and enables future artificial intelligence (AI)-supported analyses. The Delphi study, conducted according to the CREDES standard, comprised three rounds with a panel of experts from the German Society of Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine. Documentation templates were extracted, parameters catalogued and iteratively evaluated. Consensus threshold-controlled inclusion or exclusion. Anonymized data analysis was performed descriptively using Excel, supplemented by approval rates and consensus levels. In the first round, 8 of the 12 participants (66.6%) submitted their documentation templates. The initial catalogue created on this basis contained 95 parameters (e.g., patient name, body temperature, mean arterial pressure), which the steering committee classified into 16 categories, such as consultation-related data, imaging and diagnostics, or laboratory values. In the second round, feedback was received from all participants (12/12, 100%) of the expert panel. After applying the exclusion criteria, 7 parameters were removed from the catalogue and 37 new parameters were added. These 125 parameters were then reassigned by the steering group to the categories formed in the first round. In the third round evaluation of the remaining 125 parameters was received from 10 of the 12 participants (83.3%) of the expert panel. Of these, 31 parameters (24.8%) were excluded, 73 (58.4%) were classified as optional and 21 parameters (16.8%) were classified as mandatory. The consensus level rose from 75% to 90%. All categories achieved stable consensus values, thus fulfilling the termination criterion of content saturation. This consensus-based core data set could contribute to consistent and reproducible documentation of telemedicine consultations. Also, a mandatory integration of the required parameters into existing clinical documentation systems as well as the early adaptation of technical interfaces, are further key prerequisites for sustainable implementation. Beyond implementation, the catalogue can support harmonization among Tele-ICU networks, facilitate the benchmarking of consultation processes and provide a structured foundation for future multicenter analyses. In particular, the distinction between mandatory and optional parameters enables a pragmatic balance between clinical relevance, documentation burden and local technical readiness. Consistent use of the core data set supports guideline-based processes, improves comparability across sites and can contribute to the development of future quality indicators and AI-supported analyses.

42957303.title: Effects of perfusion-guided permissive hypotension and early vasopressin initiation in adults with septic shock: protocol for a multicentre 2×2 factorial randomised controlled trial in Japanese intensive care units.

42952867.title: Comparative analysis of the hemodynamic and metabolic effects of alternative fluid resuscitation strategies in critically ill patients with combined chest trauma and hemorrhagic shock: impact on oxygen delivery-consumption balance and coagulation homeostasis.
42952867.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effects of different fluid resuscitation strategies on clinical efficacy, oxygen metabolism, coagulation function, and inflammatory response in critically ill patients with chest trauma complicated by hemorrhagic shock, so as to provide evidence for optimizing emergency treatment strategies. A total of 107 patients with severe chest trauma and hemorrhagic shock who were admitted to our hospital between June 2023 and April 2025 were retrospectively enrolled. According to the type of treatment received, patients were divided into two groups. The control group (n = 55) received conventional fluid resuscitation, while the observation group (n = 52) received restrictive fluid resuscitation. The two groups were compared in terms of fluid resuscitation parameters, oxygen metabolism indicators [mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2), oxygen consumption (VO2), oxygen delivery (DO2)], coagulation indicators [activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), prothrombin time (PT), hematocrit (HCT)], inflammatory indicators [interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-10 (IL-10), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)], as well as mortality and complication rates during resuscitation. Compared with the control group, the observation group had significantly lower fluid input volume (P < 0.05); there were no significant differences in early resuscitation time or colloid use between the two groups (P > 0.05). After resuscitation, SvO2, VO2, DO2, and HCT levels were all significantly increased compared with before resuscitation, while APTT, PT, IL-6, IL-10, and TNF-α levels were significantly decreased in both groups. The magnitude of changes in the observation group was significantly greater than in the control group (P < 0.05). During the resuscitation period, the survival rate of the observation group was significantly higher than that of the control group, while the incidence of ARDS, DIC, and MODS was significantly lower (P < 0.05). Compared with conventional fluid resuscitation, restrictive fluid resuscitation shows more significant clinical advantages. Its application in patients with severe chest trauma complicated by hemorrhagic shock can reduce unnecessary fluid overload, more effectively improve oxygen metabolism, correct coagulation dysfunction, suppress inflammatory responses, thereby increasing survival rates and reducing the risk of complications.

42946258.title: Depressive and Anxiety symptoms associated with ICU admission in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a prospective cohort study.
42946258.journal: Journal of the Academy of Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry
42946258.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly in Latin America. Depression and anxiety are frequent during pregnancy and may influence HDP severity, yet their impact on clinical outcomes remains unclear. To determine whether depressive and anxiety symptoms are associated with obstetric intensive care unit (ICU) admission and hospital length of stay among women with HDP. A prospective cohort study was conducted at a Colombian tertiary-care referral hospital (July 2024-January 2025). Women aged ≥16 years in their third trimester hospitalized for HDP completed the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7). Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression and Cox regression models assessed associations with ICU admission and length of stay RESULTS: Among 234 participants (median age 25 years), 61.1% required ICU care; only 14 of the 143 ICU patients (9.8%) were assessed before ICU transfer. An EPDS score ≥10 or a positive response to item 10 was independently associated with ICU admission (OR 4.83 , 95% CI 1.56 -14.94, p=0.006) and longer hospitalization (HR 0.69 , 95% CI 0.48 -1.00, p=0.048). In an exploratory finding, a GAD-7 score ≥10 showed an inverse association with ICU admission (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.09-0.88, p=0.029). Hemoglobin <11 g/dL and a post hoc mean arterial pressure threshold ≥102.5 mmHg were also significantly associated with ICU admission. Depressive symptoms were associated with obstetric ICU admission and prolonged hospitalization in patients admitted for HDP, whereas anxiety appeared protective, which seems counterintuitive and requires future research to confirm its association; however, because most assessments took place after ICU transfer, causality could not be established. Integrating mental health screening into HDP management may improve maternal outcomes.

42945909.title: Observational study for perioperative intensive care unit (OPICU): Planned and unplanned ICU admissions, follow-up, discharge, and outcomes.
42945909.abstract: Due to limited resources, identifying high-risk surgical patients who derive clinical benefit from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission is essential. Our primary aim was to characterize resource allocation and evaluate the true clinical benefit of ICU admissions using modified Wang criteria. Secondary aim is to identify independent risk factors for ICU admission; validate clinical scoring systems; and compare inter-group outcomes, including Clavien-Dindo complication rates, lengths of stay, and mortality. This multicenter, prospective, observational study was conducted across 75 ICUs. Adult inpatient surgery cases were categorized into four groups: planned admission (PAG), unplanned admission (UPAG), planned but not admitted (PBNAG), and emergent admission (EAG). Data included preoperative/intraoperative/postoperative(ICU) variables, modified Wang criteria, and mortality rates (ICU, hospital, 30/90-day). Of 55,963 preoperatively evaluated patients, 2764 (4.9%) were planned for ICU admission; 804/2764 patients could not be admitted because of limited ICU beds, remaining of 1960 patients with a planned ICU admission, 411/1960 did not require postoperative ICU care forming the PBNAG (14.8% of 2764). Overall, 1980 patients (3.09% of all cases) were admitted to the ICU (78.2% PAG, 12.5% EAG, 9.1% UPAG). POSSUM scores effectively differentiated PBNAG (lower) and EAG (higher) from PAG. ICU benefit indicators (e.g., vasopressor need, prolonged ventilation >12 h, arrest events) were significantly higher in UPAG and EAG versus PAG (p < 0.001). Emergency surgery (OR 12.4), intraoperative complications (OR 3.1), and ASA >2 (OR 2.7) independently increased UPAG risk, whereas minimally invasive surgery and regional anesthesia reduced ICU admissions. Overall ICU and 90-day mortality rates were 5.9% and 7.5%, respectively, peaking in the EAG group (18.1% and 18.9%). Integrating modified Wang criteria, POSSUM scores, intraoperative complications, emergency status, and ASA class >2 is effective in predicting the necessity of ICU admission.

42941500.title: Clinical Reasoning, Pathophysiology, and Artificial Intelligence in Critical Care: A Conceptual Framework for Integrating Decision-Making.
42941500.abstract: Medical practice is an interpretive, decision-making activity conducted under uncertainty, and care quality depends on clinicians' ability to organize knowledge into hypotheses, understand mechanisms, estimate probabilities, and revise decisions as the clinical course evolves. In critical care, where physiology is unstable and trajectories are nonlinear, these demands are magnified. We propose a conceptual framework integrating three complementary dimensions: clinical reasoning, which provides the cognitive architecture of decision-making; pathophysiology, which supplies the causal structure to interpret biological phenomena; and artificial intelligence, which, when well designed and critically used, can organize data, generate hypotheses, and reduce cognitive load. Tracing the evolution of clinical reasoning from the anatomoclinical model to hypothetico-deductive, probabilistic, cognitive, and sociotechnical models, we examine how diagnostic and therapeutic errors arise from interacting cognitive biases, system factors, and case characteristics, and how better problem representation, differential diagnosis, and team culture may mitigate them. We also frame Bayesian reasoning and decision thresholds as the probabilistic grammar of bedside decisions, analyze the risks of artificial intelligence, including automation bias, opacity, and limited metacognition, and propose principles for its safe use. Rather than replacing physicians, artificial intelligence should strengthen clinical reasoning and reinforce calibrated, accountable bedside judgment. These principles are intended as a framework for future research and require empirical validation before clinical translation.

42941396.title: Diverging Trends in Treated In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in Intensive Care Units and General Wards Using Location-Specific Patient-Days.
42941396.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hospital-level incidence estimates may obscure differences between intensive care units (ICUs) and general wards. We compared temporal trends in treated adult in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) using location-specific patient-days. Methods: This retrospective study covered January 2016 to June 2026 at a South Korean teaching hospital. Monthly treated IHCA counts were modeled using negative binomial regression with patient-days as an offset, a setting × time interaction, and adjustment for the COVID-19 period and seasonality. Calendar-month score-based HAC analyses assessed robustness to serial correlation. January-March 2022 was excluded because arrest location was unavailable. Results: The incidence cohort comprised 1712 events: 1373 in ICUs and 339 in general wards. The combined rate was 1.06 per 1000 patient-days. The setting × time interaction was significant (monthly IRR 0.9843, model-based 95% CI 0.9768-0.9918), corresponding to a 17.3% annual decrease in the ICU-to-ward rate ratio. Calendar-month score-based HAC confidence intervals also excluded 1. ICU incidence declined (monthly IRR 0.9875, 95% CI 0.9825-0.9925), whereas the general-ward model showed no statistically significant temporal trend (IRR 1.0033, 95% CI 0.9975-1.0090; p = 0.263). Conclusions: Location-specific patient-day denominators identified different temporal trajectories in treated IHCA. These findings describe observed treated events and do not establish changes in underlying arrest risk or resuscitation performance.

42928831.title: High-Dose Tigecycline for Multidrug-Resistant Serratia Infections in Critically Ill Adults: A Systematic Review of Direct and Indirect Clinical Evidence.
42928831.abstract: Evidence for high-dose tigecycline in severe multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections comes mainly from non-Serratia cohorts. Its value in critically ill adults with resistant Serratia infection is uncertain. PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, and Consensus were searched up to July 17, 2026. Two evidence sets addressed high-dose tigecycline effectiveness, pharmacokinetics, and safety, and clinical and microbiological evidence for resistant Serratia. Study-level risk ratios were presented without pooling. Searches identified 2,294 records, and 36 studies reported in 37 publications were included. No study reported a verified high-dose regimen in confirmed resistant Serratia infection with a separately extractable organism-specific outcome. Six observational studies used the same high-dose and standard-dose definitions. Fixed 28-day or 30-day mortality risk ratios ranged from 0.34 to 1.30, and all 95% confidence intervals crossed 1.0. Clinical response favored high dose in two studies, with risk ratios of 1.73 (95% confidence interval: 1.22-2.46) and 1.48 (95% confidence interval: 1.08-2.02). Microbiological response favored high dose in two studies, with risk ratios of 1.75 (95% confidence interval: 1.09-2.81) and 1.92 (95% confidence interval: 1.12-3.28). No pooled estimate was calculated. High dose produced a greater fibrinogen decline in one cohort (-3.05 ± 1.67 versus -1.75 ± 1.90 g/L; p=0.038) and more hepatic or platelet abnormalities in another. Direct evidence for high-dose tigecycline in resistant Serratia infection is absent. Indirect studies show possible response benefits without a consistent survival advantage. Treatment decisions should consider infection site, susceptibility, active alternatives, and coagulation risk. By synthesizing both pathogen-specific studies and relevant indirect clinical evidence, this review aimed to provide a more comprehensive assessment of the potential role of high-dose tigecycline in critically ill adults with resistant S. marcescens infections.

42923126.title: Ultrasound-guided circulatory management strategy for improving microcirculatory dysfunction and promoting organ function recovery in critically ill shock patients.
42923126.abstract: To evaluate whether ultrasound-guided circulatory management improves microcirculatory perfusion, accelerates organ function recovery, and enhances clinical outcomes in critically ill shock patients compared with standard care. Our retrospective cohort study was performed in the adult ICUs of Xuanwu Hospital and consecutive screening of ICU admissions of January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025. In total, 200 eligible shock patients were categorized in accordance with the leading initial circulatory management approach following shock detection: conventional guideline consistent care (control, n=100) and organized point-of-care ultrasound guided care (observation, n=100) on the basis of protocolized evaluation at pre-arranged decision points to phenotype hemodynamics and progressively oversee the administration of fluids and vasoactive introduction/adjustment with reassessment. The primary outcome was organ support-free days until day 28 (death = 0). While time to shock resolution, shock-free days to day 7, ICU/hospital length of stay, ICU mortality, ICU readmission, discharge disposition, and 90-day EQ-5D were some of the secondary outcomes. Mechanistic endpoints included 0-6 h metrics of resuscitation, 24-h hemodynamic/ultrasound phenotype, SOFA trajectory, day 5 and baseline/24-h biomarkers. Compared with usual care, the ultrasound-guided strategy reduced early fluid exposure and net fluid balance within 6 h (P=0.004 and P=0.001, respectively) and lowered norepinephrine dose and norepinephrine ≥0.30 μg/kg/min use at 6 h (P<0.001 and P=0.010). At 24 h, patients receiving ultrasound-guided management had higher MAP, improved cardiac performance, and less vasopressor dependence (all P≤0.015), with a lower prevalence of moderate-severe LV dysfunction (P=0.001). Clinically, the intervention shortened time to shock resolution (P<0.001) and increased organ support-free days to day 28 (P<0.001). SOFA scores improved more rapidly (P<0.01 at 24 h; P<0.001 at 48 h, 72 h, and 5 days), accompanied by better renal perfusion and lower injury biomarkers (all P<0.001). Optimized early resuscitation (less fluid and lower vasopressor exposure), better 24-h hemodynamic and renal microcirculatory phenotypes, faster SOFA recovery, more organ support-free days, and faster shock resolution, with at least a partial association with reduced renal injury, were observed in patients receiving ultrasound-guided circulatory management. These findings indicate potential benefits but do not establish causality due to the retrospective, single-center study design.

42919451.title: Brachial-to-Radial Pressure Gradient in Critically Ill Patients Treated With Vasoactive Agents: A Prospective Observational Study.
authors: Polish Perioperative and Critical Care Research Group (PERI-CRIT)
42919451.abstract: To determine the incidence of a significant noninvasive brachial-to-radial arterial pressure gradient (NIBR-APG) and its clinical associations in critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents. Prospective, multicenter, observational study. Thirteen ICUs in Poland. Adult ICU patients with radial arterial catheters receiving vasoactive agents hospitalized between April 2025 and July 2025. None. Invasive radial mean arterial pressure (MAP) and noninvasive brachial MAP were measured twice and averaged. A NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg was predefined as clinically significant. Baseline characteristics, hemodynamic variables, and outcomes were recorded. Among 303 patients, 49.5% were surgical admissions and 33.3% had septic shock. The median NIBR-APG was 4.5 mm Hg (interquartile range, 0.0-10.0 mm Hg). Fifty-six patients (18.4%) exhibited a NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg. Compared with patients without a significant gradient, these patients received higher norepinephrine-equivalent doses (0.23 vs. 0.10 µg/kg/min), had higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (11 vs. 10), prolonged capillary refill time (3.0 vs. 2.5 s), and higher lactate concentrations (2.7 vs. 1.3 mmol/L). In multivariable analysis, only vasoactive drug dose was independently associated with NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg (odds ratio, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.12-2.52). ICU mortality was higher in patients with significant gradients (48.0% vs. 30.1%). Nearly one in five critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents demonstrated a clinically significant NIBR-APG. The presence of this gradient was independently associated with higher vasoactive drug requirements and was accompanied by greater illness severity and higher ICU mortality.

42907747.title: Prognostic value of early point-of-care blood gas analysis in critically ill non-trauma patients.
42907747.abstract: Critically ill non-trauma patients treated in the emergency department have a high risk of in-hospital mortality. While point-of-care diagnostics such as blood gas analysis are established tools for urgent management, data on their prognostic value in this specific patient cohort remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether initial blood gas parameters are independently associated with in-hospital mortality in critically ill non-trauma patients. This retrospective cohort study included adult critically ill non-trauma patients treated in the emergency department of a German university hospital. Initial blood gas parameters and clinical data were analyzed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression to assess their association with in-hospital mortality. Of 879 screened patients, 542 met the inclusion criteria. In-hospital mortality was 20% (n = 110). In addition to older age and out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, anemia (hemoglobin < 12 g/dL; OR of 2.07, 95% CI 1.20-3.58; p = 0.009), acidosis (pH < 7.35; OR 2.26, 95% CI 1.09-4.95; p = 0.033) and hypobicarbonatemia (< 22 mmol/L; OR 2.79, 95% CI 1.42-5.69; p = 0.004) were independently associated with in-hospital mortality. The association for hyperlactatemia was borderline (> 2.2 mmol/L; OR 1.85, 95% CI 0.93-3.77; p = 0.08). Multivariate analysis did not reveal significant associations between other electrolyte imbalances and in-hospital mortality in this cohort. In this retrospective cohort, the presence of anemia, acidosis or hypobicarbonatemia on admission to the resuscitation room were independently associated with an elevated risk of in-hospital mortality in critically ill non-trauma patients. These readily available point-of-care parameters may support early risk stratification. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

42901551.title: Impact of an early extended rehabilitation programme combining individually tailored nutrition and physical activity on patient outcomes after invasive mechanical ventilation and vasopressor therapy in the ICU: design and conduct of a multicentre, randomised, controlled, open-label, assessor-blinded trial (NUTRIREA-4).
42901551.abstract: Survivors of severe critical illness often experience long-lasting physical, quality of life and psychological impairments. Intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired weakness develops early and is associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, delayed functional recovery, impaired quality of life and greater healthcare utilisation. Nutritional support and early mobilisation are considered key components of ICU care. However, trials have evaluated either nutritional or physical rehabilitation strategies and have not consistently demonstrated long-term benefits. A strong physiological rationale exists for combining nutritional therapy and structured physical rehabilitation. Moreover, most interventions were limited to the ICU stay. The NUTRIREA-4 trial will assess whether an individualised, integrated rehabilitation strategy of nutritional support, physiotherapy and adapted physical activity initiated early in the ICU and continued throughout and after the hospital stay improves long-term physical performance and recovery. NUTRIREA-4 is the first large-scale multicentre randomised controlled trial evaluating such a comprehensive approach in survivors of severe critical illness. NUTRIREA-4 is a randomised controlled, multicentre, open-label trial comparing two parallel groups of patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation and vasopressor therapy for shock and randomised to either an individualised rehabilitation programme or usual care. The rehabilitation programme combines goal-directed nutritional support, physiotherapy and adapted physical activity delivered from ICU admission to 12 weeks after the return home. We will include 830 patients in 52 French ICUs. The primary endpoint is the 6-minute walk distance measured by blinded assessors 6 months after randomisation. Secondary outcomes include muscle strength, physical activity, nutritional intake, ICU-acquired infections, quality of life, mortality and psychological recovery. The NUTRIREA-4 trial has been approved by the appropriate ethics committee. Patients are included after informed consent according to French law. The results will be published in international peer-reviewed journals and presented at conferences. NCT06581939.

42897407.title: Race, Gender, and Survival: a Scoping Review of Disparities in ICU Post-Resuscitation Care and Neurological Outcomes Following Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
42897407.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
42897407.abstract: Racial and ethnic disparities in healthcare are well documented, yet limited attention has been given to the intersection of race/ethnicity and gender in high-acuity critical care. Black women experience compounded inequities affecting access to and quality of intensive care unit (ICU) treatment following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Because outcomes after OHCA are influenced by each link in the chain of survival, disparities in early intervention and subsequent clinical decision-making may contribute to differences in survival and neurological recovery. This study synthesizes evidence on disparities in ICU treatment and outcomes among Black women in the United States while examining how inequities across the chain of survival may influence post-resuscitation care, neurocritical care, and outcomes following OHCA. We conducted a scoping review, guided by the Arksey and O'Malley framework, to analyze peer-reviewed studies identified through electronic databases (e.g., PubMed, CINAHL, and ScienceDirect). Fifteen studies met inclusion criteria and were analyzed using thematic synthesis. Findings indicate persistent disparities, including lower bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) rates, delayed emergency response, reduced access to ICU interventions, and higher rates of early do-not-resuscitate (DNR) orders and withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies (WLST). These inequities may contribute to poorer outcomes and likely reflect a combination of systemic, institutional, and social factors, although relatively few studies directly examined Black women from an intersectional perspective. Addressing these disparities requires improved data disaggregation, culturally responsive care, and interdisciplinary interventions to promote equitable post-resuscitation care and outcomes.

42893350.title: Efficacy and Safety of Etomidate Versus Ketamine for Endotracheal Intubation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42893350.abstract: Rapid sequence intubation (RSI) is a commonly used technique for critically ill patients requiring emergency intubation, and the choice of induction agent is crucial for minimizing peri-intubation morbidity and maintaining hemodynamic stability. The most commonly used induction agents are etomidate and ketamine, although controversy remains about their effectiveness and safety. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis compared the efficacy and safety of etomidate versus ketamine for endotracheal intubation in critically ill patients. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2000 and May 2026 were systematically searched in PubMed, The Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect. The included studies compared etomidate with ketamine for emergency endotracheal intubation in critically ill adults. We analyzed data with RevMan 5.4 and Mantel-Haenszel random-effects models and calculated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Seven RCTs involving 5234 patients were included in the final analysis. No significant difference was observed between etomidate and ketamine regarding 28-day mortality (RR 1.01; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93-1.10; p=0.84), cardiac arrest (RR 0.91; 95% CI 0.62-1.34; p = 0.64), failed intubation (RR 1.09; 95% CI 0.68-1.76; p=0.71), or vasopressor requirement (RR 1.27; 95% CI 0.94-1.72; p=0.13). Sensitivity analyses suggested possible hemodynamic differences between the two agents, which should be interpreted cautiously, and etomidate was relatively cardiovascularly stable in some analyses. Overall, etomidate and ketamine showed similar efficacy and safety for endotracheal intubation in critically ill patients. No statistically significant differences were observed between the two agents in mortality, cardiac arrest, failed intubation, or vasopressor use. Thus, clinicians should choose the induction agent on a case-by-case basis, based on patient, hemodynamic, and clinician-specific factors. Randomized trials in selected critically ill patient populations should be conducted on a larger scale.

42964225.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Corticosteroids vs. No Corticosteroids in Septic Shock Intensive Care Unit Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42964225.abstract: Septic shock carries a high intensive care unit (ICU) mortality. The role of adjunctive corticosteroid therapy is controversial, with conflicting signals from trial-level meta-analyses, individual patient data syntheses, and large randomized trials. This review aimed to assess the comparative efficacy and safety of systemic corticosteroids versus no corticosteroids in adult ICU patients with septic shock. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched from inception, supplemented by trial registry and gray literature searches, for randomized trials of systemic corticosteroids versus placebo or standard care in adults with septic shock. Pooling used a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. The Risk of Bias 2 and Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) frameworks were used for the methodological appraisal. Heterogeneity was quantified using I2, τ2, and 95% prediction intervals. Publication bias was assessed using contour-enhanced funnel plots, Egger's regression test, and the Duval-Tweedie trim-and-fill method. Eleven randomized controlled trials (RCTs) (n = 6,332; 1,929 deaths) were included. Corticosteroids reduced 28-day all-cause mortality by 8.7% relative to control (pooled risk ratio (RR) 0.91, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86-0.97; P = 0.008; I2 = 0%; prediction interval 0.84-0.99), corresponding to 27 fewer deaths per 1,000 (10-44 fewer). Time to shock reversal was shortened by 1.25 days (95% CI -2.09 to -0.41), with the standardized mean difference (SMD) sensitivity analysis confirming a robust effect (SMD -0.41, 95% CI -0.51 to -0.32). Shock reversal incidence (RR 1.08, 0.99-1.19) and ICU length of stay (LOS) (mean difference (MD) -2.07 days, -6.50 to 2.36) favored corticosteroids without reaching significance. Hyperglycemia occurred more frequently in the corticosteroid arm of every contributing trial. Egger's test (P = 0.972) and trim-and-fill imputation provided no evidence of small-study effects. GRADE certainty was moderate for mortality and shock reversal incidence, high for time to shock reversal, and low for ICU LOS and hyperglycemia. Corticosteroid therapy in adults with septic shock was associated with a reduction in 28-day mortality and with accelerated shock reversal, with no evidence of publication bias. The direction of effect was consistent across pre-specified subgroups but was offset by a consistent excess of hyperglycemia, reinforcing the need for vigilant glucose surveillance during corticosteroid administration.

42958234.title: A Delphi study to identify competencies of registered nurses in Kenyan intensive care units.
42958234.abstract: Nurses form the largest professional group in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) workforce. Their competency in care delivery contributes to improved patient outcomes, reduced morbidity and mortality, and overall reduced cost of care. Many countries have established frameworks to support a set of core competencies that all qualified ICU nurses are expected to possess. Kenya has yet to embark on a unifying competency framework, leading to ICU nurses' poor transfer of knowledge, skills, and attitudes because of differences in the scope and depth of competencies learned. Unification of competencies may best be achieved through stakeholders' agreement on the required set of competencies. The aim of this study was to establish consensus on the initial set of competencies required by registered nurses working in Kenyan ICUs. The study adopted a mixed-method design with a multistage approach. This involved two stages: an integrative review, and two rounds of e-Delphi. The integrative review of competencies and competency frameworks for ICU nurses informed the development of an initial set of 91 competencies. These competencies were subsequently subjected to expert evaluation by a heterogeneous panel of experts in a two-round e-Delphi process. However, All the competencies in the two rounds achieved consensus by attaining a priori mean of ≥ 4. This manuscript reports findings from the integrative review and the first round of the e-Delphi process. Findings from subsequent Delphi rounds are reported separately. Notably, despite ICU competencies being universal, some competencies are culturally specific and may require contextual tweaking for their acceptability. These include competencies touching on palliative and end-of-life care, involvement of patients and their families in pain management, and competencies that require autonomous practice of nurses, like performance of invasive procedures. This study identified and synthesised competencies for registered nurses in Kenyan ICUs through an integrative review and further evaluated their relevance through the first round of a Delphi process. The findings provide an initial, evidence-informed set of competencies that can inform curriculum development, clinical practice, and policy discussions. Further Delphi round will build on these findings to establish final consensus on the competency framework. Not applicable.

42874048.title: Case Report: Veno-Arteriovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Management of Pheochromocytoma-Induced Cardiac Arrest in a Post-Partum Patient.
42874048.abstract: A 34-year-old woman, 2 days post-partum, was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for management of hypertensive crisis and respiratory failure. An 18-cm left adrenal mass was found on computed tomography (CT), suspicious for a pheochromocytoma. After cardiac arrest, the patient was placed on veno-arteriovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-AV ECMO) given recurrent destabilizing arrhythmias. After successful ECMO decannulation, the patient underwent an uncomplicated resection of her adrenal mass. Although VA-ECMO has been used to support patients with pheochromocytoma, this appears to be the first published case describing the use of a V-AV configuration in the management of a complex cardiac arrest.

42866661.title: Phaeochromocytoma Crisis Presenting As Inverted Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy in a Young Woman: A Successful Outcome.
42866661.abstract: Phaeochromocytoma crisis is a rare, life-threatening endocrine emergency characterised by profound haemodynamic instability and multiorgan dysfunction. We report the case of a previously healthy 31-year-old woman who presented with sudden-onset cardiopulmonary decompensation, marked blood-pressure variability, pulmonary oedema, and cardiogenic shock, with biochemical evidence of myocardial injury. Echocardiography demonstrated apical hypercontractility with akinesia of the basal and midventricular segments and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%, consistent with reverse takotsubo cardiomyopathy. Cross-sectional imaging revealed a large 9 cm left adrenal mass, which, together with markedly elevated plasma and urinary metanephrines, confirmed the diagnosis of phaeochromocytoma crisis. The patient required mechanical ventilation, vasoactive support, and intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation. Following successful resuscitation and stabilisation with α- and β-adrenergic blockade, she underwent elective laparoscopic left adrenalectomy. Histopathological examination confirmed a high-risk phaeochromocytoma, while genetic testing was negative. Postoperatively, metanephrine concentrations normalised and bi-ventricular cardiac function recovered completely. This case highlights the importance of considering phaeochromocytoma crisis in patients presenting with otherwise unexplained haemodynamic instability and stress cardiomyopathy. Early recognition, multidisciplinary critical care, appropriate adrenergic blockade, and timely definitive surgery are essential and can be lifesaving.

42859976.title: [Successful treatment of hypokalemic cardiac arrest with massive potassium replacement in a patient with Bricker urinary diversion].
42859976.abstract: Severe hypokalemia is a rare but potentially reversible cause of malignant arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Early recognition of significant fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base disturbances in patients with intestinal urinary diversion may be life-saving. We present the clinical course of a 55-year-old woman who developed severe hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and extreme hypokalemia following prolonged vomiting and high-output fluid loss through a Bricker ureteroileocutaneostomy. The patient was admitted to the intensive care unit in a peri-arrest condition, where cardiac arrest occurred shortly thereafter. The monitored rhythm was ventricular fibrillation alternating with "torsade de pointes" ventricular fibrillation. During advanced life support, targeted high-dose intravenous potassium replacement, magnesium sulfate administration, and bicarbonate substitution were performed. A total of 120 mL of 7.4% potassium chloride was administered during resuscitation, resulting in return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 18 minutes. During the first 24 hours, a total of 460 mmol potassium chloride replacement was required. Following the return of spontaneous circulation, intermittent hemodialysis was performed to correct severe metabolic acidosis. During subsequent intensive care treatment, sepsis and bilateral pneumonia developed; however, with targeted antimicrobial therapy, organ support, and continuous electrolyte correction, the patient's condition gradually improved. Successful extubation was performed on day 7, and the patient was transferred back to the nephrology ward with favourable neurological outcome. This case highlights that rapidly developing severe hypokalaemia and metabolic acidosis in patients with Bricker urinary diversion may lead to malignant arrhythmias and cardiac arrest; however, prompt recognition of reversible metabolic abnormalities and aggressive targeted potassium replacement can be life-saving. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(41): 1664-1668.

42855134.title: Oral or Enteral Levothyroxine for Myxedema Coma When Intravenous Therapy Is Unavailable: A Systematic Review and Descriptive Evidence Synthesis.
42855134.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
42855134.abstract: Intravenous levothyroxine is generally preferred for myxedema coma but may be unavailable in many healthcare settings. We summarized published treatment regimens and outcomes with oral or enteral levothyroxine when intravenous therapy was unavailable. Intravenous-only and mixed-route reports were included for clinical context. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 2026. Studies reporting myxedema coma treated with oral, enteral, nasogastric, or intravenous levothyroxine and extractable clinical outcomes were included. Pooled proportions were calculated only as descriptive summaries of oral/enteral reports and were not interpreted as treatment-effect estimates. Intravenous-only and mixed-route studies were summarized narratively. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Nine studies comprising 70 patients were included: six oral/enteral, two intravenous-only, and one mixed-route study. Oral/enteral loading doses ranged from 300 to 1000 μg. Descriptively pooled proportions were 0.20 for mortality, 0.76 for intensive care unit admission, 0.54 for mechanical ventilation, and 0.62 for vasopressor requirement. These estimates are descriptive summaries of selected published reports and should not be interpreted as population-level event rates, treatment-effect estimates, route-specific risks, or expected outcome probabilities in routine clinical practice. Published reports document oral or enteral levothyroxine as a rescue approach when intravenous treatment is unavailable. However, evidence is insufficient to establish comparative efficacy, safety, equivalence, or an optimal dosing regimen. Intravenous levothyroxine should remain preferred when available, particularly in patients with shock, ileus, or unreliable gastrointestinal absorption.

42921464.title: Clinical outcomes during the 2025-2026 and 2024-2025 influenza seasons in a US EHR network: an ecological comparison during A(H3N2) subclade K predominance.
42921464.abstract: The influenza A(H3N2) subclade K virus has predominated in the 2025-2026 season. This study compared the clinical severity of influenza between 2025-2026 and 2024-2025 seasons. In this retrospective cohort study, a multicenter electronic health record database (TriNetX) was used. The clinical outcomes after influenza infection confirmed by nucleic acid detection were ecologically compared between the 2025-2026 and 2024-2025 seasons with propensity score matching. There were 8965 and 8937 children and 7488 and 6947 adults with confirmed influenza A(H3N2) infection in the 2025-2026 and 2024-2025 seasons, respectively. After each propensity score matching, the odds ratios for children and adults were not assessed (due to the small number of events) and 0.87 (95% confidence interval 0.71-1.05), P = 0.148 for death; 1.32 (1.10-1.59), P = 0.003 and 0.91 (0.82-1.02), P = 0.092 for critical care admission; 1.06 (0.97-1.16), P = 0.191 and 1.01 (0.94-1.08), P = 0.803 for hospitalization; 0.88 (0.73-1.07), P = 0.197 and 0.93 (0.83-1.04), P = 0.194 for mechanical ventilation; and 1.10 (0.91-1.32), P = 0.320 and 0.93 (0.83-1.03), P = 0.177 for vasopressor use, respectively. In this electronic health record-based season-level comparison, no consistent adjusted differences were observed; however, the study could not directly assess subclade K-specific severity or rule out clinically relevant differences. Rapid and timely monitoring of clinical characteristics and severity in the case of an emerging influenza strain or subclade is important to guide preventive and therapeutic strategies against influenza.

42905942.title: Comparing the Post-Omicron Impact of COVID-19 and Non-COVID-19 Respiratory Viral Infections in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients.
42905942.abstract: Effective treatment and prevention for respiratory viral infections (RVI) in solid organ transplant recipients (SOTR) are lacking; clinical differences in COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 (ncRVI) post-omicron are unknown. We compared severity and outcomes across SOT groups. A single-center retrospective study of health system RVI in adult SOTR during 2022-2023 was conducted. Overall, 520 RVI episodes in 504 patients were included: 488 had 1 episode and 16 had 2 episodes. Lung, kidney, and heart transplant recipients comprised of 40.9%, 34.3%, and 20.8% of the cohort. There were 352 episodes of COVID-19 RVI and 148 ncRVI. All-cause and RVI-related hospitalization were comparable between COVID-19 and ncRVI (47.7% vs. 43.9%, p = 0.50; 32.1% vs. 31.1%, p = 0.91 respectively). Oxygen supplementation occurred in 11.9% of COVID-19 RVI and 11.5% of ncRVI with a maximum requirement (median, IQR) of 4.0 (2.0-18.8) and 2.0 (2.0-3.0) liters respectively (p = 0.005). Intensive care unit (ICU) admission occurred in 7.1% and 6.1%; non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in 2.3% and 4.1%; mechanical ventilation (I&V) in 4.0% and 2.0%; and inotropic/vasopressor support in 1.7% and 1.4%, for COVID-19 versus nCRVI, respectively. Patients with COVID-19 had ongoing symptoms in 16.8%, 10.2%, and 2.6% at 30 days, 3 month, and 12 month follow up respectively, compared with 16.9%, 4.7%, and 2.0% in ncRVI. Twelve-month mortality, rejection and graft dysfunction were similar between groups. COVID-19 and ncRVI pose significant and comparable risk to SOTR in this post-omicron era, in hospitalization, oxygen requirement, and persistent symptoms. Treatment and prevention should be prioritized in this population.

42965211.title: Emergency department extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: Current concepts, systems-based implementation, and future directions.
42965211.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) has emerged as a time-critical resuscitative strategy for carefully selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest and other reversible causes of circulatory or respiratory failure. As the role of emergency department ECMO (ED ECMO) continues to expand, emergency physicians have become integral members of multidisciplinary extracorporeal resuscitation teams. This review aims to summarize the current evidence on ED ECMO while highlighting practical considerations for program implementation, workflow optimization, and future directions. This invited narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the indications, patient selection, cannulation strategies, pericannulation management, and postcannulation physiological challenges of ED ECMO, with particular emphasis on extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation. In addition to published literature, practical aspects of ED ECMO implementation, including multidisciplinary team organization, operational governance, workflow optimization, quality metrics, and institutional experience, are discussed. Emerging concepts such as artificial intelligence-assisted decision support, digital twin-enabled system modeling, and regional implementation strategies are also reviewed. Current evidence indicates that successful ED ECMO depends not only on technical proficiency but also on timely patient selection, standardized protocols, efficient multidisciplinary coordination, and optimized operational systems. Contemporary implementation frameworks emphasize integrated governance, continuous quality improvement, and structured performance metrics to enhance clinical effectiveness. Emerging digital technologies, including artificial intelligence and systems modeling, may further improve patient selection, operational efficiency, and program scalability. ED ECMO should be regarded as a comprehensive, systems-based resuscitation strategy rather than a standalone rescue procedure. Future progress is likely to depend on the integration of evidence-based patient selection, standardized workflows, multidisciplinary collaboration, intelligent operational systems, and continuous quality improvement. The development of regional ED ECMO networks supported by robust emergency medical service infrastructure may improve timely access to extracorporeal resuscitation and optimize patient outcomes.

42962711.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions.
authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)(⁎)
American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)(⁎)
Asia-Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL)
Latin American Association for the Study of the Liver (ALEH)
Society on Liver Disease in Africa (SOLDA)
42962711.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.

42960283.title: Pre-emptive Circulatory Support Before Emergency Tracheal Intubation: A Systematic Review.
42960283.abstract: Emergency tracheal intubation is associated with peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse, and pre-emptive circulatory support is frequently used to mitigate this risk despite uncertain evidence. We conducted a systematic review of randomised and comparative non-randomised studies evaluating pre-emptive circulatory support initiated before or at induction in adults undergoing emergency or urgent tracheal intubation. Eligible interventions included prophylactic vasopressors, intravenous fluid boluses, hypertonic saline, blood products, deliberate circulation-first strategies, and multi-component care bundles. The primary outcome was peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse within 30 minutes of induction, defined according to individual study criteria. MEDLINE via PubMed, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 30 August 2026, with additional searches of ClinicalTrials.gov and citation lists. Risk of bias (RoB) was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool for randomised trials and the Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool for non-randomised studies. Fourteen independent cohorts comprising two randomised trials and 12 comparative non-randomised studies, with more than 7,400 participants overall, were included. Two randomised trials evaluated a pre-emptive 500 mL crystalloid bolus and found no reduction in peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse. Observational evidence for prophylactic vasopressors was inconsistent, with substantial changes between crude and adjusted estimates and substantial concerns regarding confounding. Studies evaluating circulation-first strategies or pre-intubation blood products generally reported associations favouring earlier circulatory resuscitation, but these findings were strongly influenced by confounding and treatment selection. Multi-component care bundles were also associated with fewer peri-intubation complications, but the independent contribution of their circulatory components could not be determined. Overall, the available evidence indicates that pre-emptive crystalloid administration does not reduce peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse, while evidence for prophylactic vasopressors, circulation-first strategies, and multi-component interventions remains insufficient to support routine use. Further randomised trials are needed, particularly among physiologically high-risk adults.

42911388.title: Patterns, and outcomes of airbag -related penetrating injuries: a retrospective analysis from a level 1 trauma center.
42911388.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
42911388.abstract: The deployment of defective airbag inflators can generate high-velocity metallic fragments that cause face, neck or chest penetrating injuries with potentially lethal consequences. This study aimed to describe the injury patterns, management, and outcomes of suspected airbag-related penetrating injuries (ARPI) among patients in a Middle Eastern country. A retrospective observational study of patients presenting with penetrating injuries suspected of being related to defective airbag deployment. Data were obtained from the Qatar National Trauma Registry (QNTR), electronic medical records, emergency medical services (EMS), emergency department (ED), and Mortuary. Data were collected and analyzed descriptively. A total of 16 patients had suspected ARPIs between April 2019 and February 2026. The mean age was 33.1 ± 8.3 years, and 93.8% were male. Metallic foreign bodies (FBs) from airbag inflator fragmentation were documented in 11/16 (68.8%) patients by imaging, and surgical removal while in 4/16 patients there were only entry-exit wounds after deployment of airbags following car crash. In one case, airbag deployed while mechanic was repairing a car steering wheel. Penetrating neck (43.8%), thoracic (31.3%), and maxillofacial injuries (31.3%), predominantly mandibular fractures, were most common. Surgical intervention was required in 11 (68.8%) patients and 7/16 required intensive care unit admissions. Five patients died (31.3%), including one at the scene (transported directly by the EMS, no CPR, and moved to the hospital mortuary), two died at the ED after unsuccessful CPR and two died during the hospital course (one presented with cardiac arrest and died on the sixth day and the other one required prolonged ECMO for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and died after 4 months). Airbag inflator rupture can produce serious injury patterns resembling patterns of ballistic trauma, characterized by penetrating neck wounds, maxillofacial fractures and thoracic injuries. These injuries are potentially associated with high mortality, surgical intervention, and critical care utilization. The full extent of these injuries is undetermined as some victims may have simply died at the scene without the benefit of trauma center evaluation or post-mortem examination.

42885414.title: [Persistent inflammation, immunosuppression, and catabolism syndrome].
42885414.abstract: Reduced early mortality in sepsis and severe injuries led to the formation of a cohort of patients with chronic critical conditions (diseases). One of the mechanisms of chronization of acute critical conditions is the development of persistent inflammation, immunosuppression and catabolism syndrome (PICS). Diagnosis of PICS is currently based on clinical and laboratory markers, whereas morphological changes insufficiently studied. Lack of pathogenesis and morphogenesis understanding makes it difficult to stratify patients with prolonged critical conditions and develop new treatment approaches, and also leads to the absence of PICS in clinical and anatomical diagnoses. The article systematized current understanding of PICS mechanisms of development and morphological manifestations. Examples of clinical cases are presented.

42876688.title: Prognostic discrimination of SOFA-2 vs. SOFA-1 and incremental information from cardiovascular scoring and vasoactive support intensity in patients with sepsis receiving early vasoactive therapy.
42876688.abstract: Patients with sepsis who require vasoactive support during the first 24 h of intensive care represent a heterogeneous population. It is uncertain whether the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-2 score improves mortality discrimination compared with the SOFA-1 score and whether observed circulatory support intensity provides complementary prognostic information. This multicohort observational study used Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) for a 24-h conditional landmark analysis. Patients alive and still in the ICU beyond 24 h were followed from ICU admission +24 h through ICU day 28 for reconstructed all-cause mortality. We compared SOFA-1 and SOFA-2, evaluated SOFA-2 total and cardiovascular scores, analyzed first-24-h five-agent norepinephrine-equivalent peak burden (norepinephrine, epinephrine, dopamine, phenylephrine, and vasopressin), and internally evaluated an exploratory drug-composition model. Fixed strata were assessed directionally in eICU Collaborative Research Database and an independent-center high-risk stress test cohort with cohort-specific endpoints. The MIMIC-IV 24-h landmark cohort included 11,892 patients and 2,687 post-landmark deaths. SOFA-2 showed no observed discrimination advantage over SOFA-1 (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, 0.731 vs. 0.732; difference, -0.0005; 95% confidence interval, -0.0086 to 0.0076; P = 0.908). The SOFA-2 cardiovascular score had lower discrimination than the SOFA-1 cardiovascular score (0.663 vs. 0.676; P = 0.006). Mortality was 51.94% for the exploratory SOFA-2 ≥12 group and 17.09% below 12, and increased from 11.30% to 47.45% across four study-defined peak burden categories. The SOFA-2-plus-drug-composition model had an apparent AUROC of 0.768 and a bootstrap-corrected AUROC of 0.767, but it was not externally validated. Fixed strata preserved the direction of risk ranking in both external cohorts, whereas absolute risk and calibration differed. SOFA-2 did not show an observed overall mortality discrimination advantage over SOFA-1 in this population. SOFA-2 total and cardiovascular scores, together with observed vasoactive support intensity, provided complementary prognostic description at 24 h. The ≥12 rule is exploratory, and drug-related associations do not establish causal treatment effects or clinical decision utility.

42873554.title: Escalating Vasopressor Intensity and the Goals-of-Care Documentation Gap in Septic Shock: Relevance to the Proposed Refractory Shock Threshold.
42873554.abstract: BackgroundThe 2026 joint SCCM/ESICM Delphi consensus identified vasopressor intensity as a defining feature of refractory septic shock, yet its relationship to real-world goals-of-care documentation remains unclear.ObjectivesWe assessed the association between escalating vasopressor intensity and documented surrogate goals-of-care markers among septic shock decedents.MethodsRetrospective cohort study of adult septic shock decedents in MIMIC-IV (2008-2022) requiring vasopressors ≥6 h and surviving ≥24 h after initiation. Vasopressor intensity was quantified by peak norepinephrine equivalent (NEE) dose during ICU stay and stratified as: 0.01-0.50 (stratum 1), >0.50-0.99 (stratum 2), and ≥1.00 µg/kg/min (stratum 3). The primary outcome was death without documented surrogate goals-of-care markers, defined as having neither a documented do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order nor documented palliative care involvement.ResultsThe final cohort included 2458 patients: stratum 1 (n = 1033), stratum 2 (n = 909), and stratum 3 (n = 516). Death without documented goals-of-care markers increased across strata (23.8%, 28.3%, 31.2%; p-for-trend=0.001). After multivariable adjustment, stratum 3 patients remained more likely than stratum 1 to die without documented goals-of-care markers (aOR 1.32; 95% CI 1.02-1.69; p = 0.03). Palliative care documentation declined progressively with increasing vasopressor intensity (59.2%, 52.0%, 46.9%; p-for-trend<0.001), accompanied by lower rates of integrated DNR/palliative care documentation (47.0%, 40.0%, 36.4%; p-for-trend<0.001). Patients exceeding the Delphi-proposed refractory shock threshold (NEE >0.50 µg/kg/min) were more likely to die without documented goals-of-care markers than those below the threshold (29.3% vs 23.8%; p = 0.002).ConclusionHigher vasopressor intensity was paradoxically associated with a greater likelihood of death without documented goals-of-care markers and with lower palliative care documentation. These findings suggest a disconnect between escalating physiologic severity and documentation of surrogate goals-of-care markers in refractory septic shock and warrant further evaluation.

42855756.title: [A preliminary study on the protective effect of dapagliflozin on multi-organ function in the early stage of sepsis].
42855756.abstract: Objective: This preliminarily study aims to evaluate the short-term efficacy and safety of dapagliflozin on multi-organ functions in patients with sepsis. Methods: This single-center, prospective, randomized controlled clinical trial enrolled 136 patients with sepsis to the Intensive Care Unit of Northern Jiangsu People's Hospital between April and December 2025. The patients were randomly assigned to the intervention group and the control group. Both groups received standardized treatment for sepsis, and the intervention group was also administered with dapagliflozin at a dose of 10 mg for 5 days. Changes in the sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores after the intervention served as the primary outcome. The secondary outcomes included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), renal function indicators, and clinical prognosis. Results: There were no statistically significant differences in the baseline data and changes in SOFA scores before and after treatment between the two groups (50 patients per group, P>0.05). On the 5th day of treatment, the median LVEF was significantly higher in the intervention group [60.0% (55.0%, 62.5%)] than in the control group [55.0% (49.0%, 58.0%), P<0.001]. The 28-day all-cause mortality rate in the intervention group [26% (13/50)] was lower than in the control group [36% (18/50)], but the variance did not reach statistical significance (P=0.387). The incidences of adverse events were comparable between both groups. The intervention group showed higher distribution of urine ketone body grades (Z=-2.1, P=0.040), but ketoacidosis was not observed. Conclusions: The short-term treatment of sepsis patients with dapagliflozin did not significantly reduce the SOFA scores, but improved LVEF and showed a trend of reducing all-cause mortality at 28 days. The short-term treatment was safe.
