Sustained return of spontaneous circulation was achieved in 6200 (35.2%) patients, of whom 222 (3.6%) received temperature control therapy and 320 (5.2%) underwent coronary angiography. Overall, 1610 (9.1%) patients survived to 30 days or discharge, with 1241 (7.1%) having a favorable neurological outcome. At 12 months, 1075 (6.1%) patients remained alive, and 986 (5.6%) had a favorable neurological outcome. This multicenter registry highlights a substantial burden of IHCA in China, with markedly low survival rates. Despite prompt initial resuscitation, critical gaps persist in postresuscitation care. Systemic and cultural factors, including the infrequent use of do not attempt cardiopulmonary resuscitation orders, may further contribute to survival disparities. These findings suggest several system-level opportunities to improve IHCA outcomes, including structured response systems, optimized critical care resource allocation, and greater integration of advanced care planning.

42831735.title: Derivation and Validation of Operational Definitions From Claims Data for Identifying Cardiogenic Shock.
42831735.abstract: To derive and validate a claims-based operational definition for cardiogenic shock (CS) using administrative data against clinically adjudicated reference standards. Diagnostic accuracy study. Two independent clinical cohorts, a single-center cardiac ICU (CICU) registry and a multicenter CS registry (REtrospective and prospective observational Study to investigate Clinical oUtcomes and Efficacy of left ventricular assist device for Korean patients with cardiogenic shock [RESCUE]), and a nationwide administrative database from the Korean National Health Insurance Service. A total of 10,156 patients from the CICU registry and 1,247 patients from the RESCUE registry. For population-level application, 207,419 patients were identified from the national claims database. None. A claims-based algorithm defined CS using the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision code R57.0 or cardiac disease codes combined with treatment-based criteria reflecting hemodynamic support, including mechanical circulatory support or vasoactive therapy. In the CICU cohort, the algorithm demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.89 and specificity of 0.90, with an overall accuracy of 0.90. In the RESCUE cohort, sensitivity was 0.95. When applied to the nationwide database, 207,419 patients with CS were identified. The cumulative mortality rates were 37.9% at 12 months, 49.9% at 5 years, and 61.7% at 10 years. A claims-based definition combining diagnostic codes with treatment-based criteria demonstrated high diagnostic performance for identifying CS. This approach enables reliable large-scale epidemiologic studies and long-term outcome assessments using administrative data and may facilitate system-level evaluation of critical care delivery in patients with CS.

42829321.title: Resuscitative Transesophageal Echocardiography Simulation-Based Education for Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Cannulation Guidance.
42829321.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42829321.abstract: A simulation-based learning (SBL) resuscitative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) course was developed to teach a focused extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) cannulation guidance protocol for critical care practitioners. The four-hour SBL course was conducted for critical care practitioners with no prior formal TEE training. University hospital, simulation center. Critical care practitioners, voluntary. The course implemented ordered sessions: didactics, TEE simulation, and hands-on ECPR cannulation simulation scenarios. Pre and post course knowledge assessment and surveys were completed. Median knowledge assessment score improved from 53% to 93% (P < .001). Survey responses yielded significant median score improvement in comfort levels of SBL TEE for ECPR guidance using a 5-point Likert scale (p-value <0.001). An SBL resuscitative TEE course focused on ECPR cannulation guidance can provide a framework for teaching these skills to critical care practitioners.

42826738.title: Neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest: evidence review and institutional protocol proposal.
42826738.abstract: Cardiac arrest (CA) is associated with high mortality and neurological morbidity, mainly due to hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Accurate neurological prognostication in CA survivors is essential to guide therapeutic decisions and provide appropriate care. To review the current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA and to propose an institutional protocol adapted to the resources of Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre (HCPA). The current narrative review was conducted in two stages: a literature review and the development of an institutional protocol. Articles were selected according to their clinical relevance and their contribution to current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA. The PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and SciELO databases were searched. The protocol was developed considering the clinical tools available at HCPA, including neurological examination, electroencephalography (EEG), and neuroimaging. Brain injury after CA occurs in three stages: intra-arrest ischemia, immediate reperfusion, and delayed postreperfusion injury. Prognostic modalities include neurological examination, EEG, somatosensory-evoked potentials (SSEPs), serum biomarkers, and neuroimaging. Reliable predictors of poor outcome include absent brainstem reflexes at 72 hours, persistent EEG suppression, bilateral absence of cortical N20 potentials, and diffuse abnormalities on magnetic resonance imaging. The proposed protocol organizes assessments from admission to the Intensive Care Unit through day 5 after the return of spontaneous circulation. A standardized post-CA neurological prognostication protocol at HCPA may improve care quality, enhance communication with families, and support ethically-sound decision-making.

42825117.title: Quantification of blood-based neurovascular unit biomarkers: an analytical platform comparison study.
42825117.abstract: Hypoxic ischemic brain injury (HIBI) remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in patients following cardiac arrest. Many international guidelines for HIBI prognostication advocate for a multimodal approach with inclusion of blood-based biomarkers. However, advancements in analytical technology have increased uncertainty in selecting the optimal quantification tool and impeded application of these results across platforms in accordance with amalgamated prognostication thresholds. We conducted a post hoc analysis of a prospective observational cohort study in 32 critically ill patients undergoing withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies. Serum and plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament-light (Nf-L), tau, and ubiquitin carboxyl hydrolase L-1 (UCH-L1) were quantified on the Simoa HD-X and ARGO HT analytical platforms respectively. Plasma GFAP and UCH-L1 samples were additionally quantified using the point-of-care i-STAT Alinity. GFAP, Nf-L, Tau, and UCH-L1 were highly correlated between the ARGO HT and Simoa HD-X analytical platforms (all Pearson's r ≥ 0.97, P ≤ 4.5e-13). In contrast, absolute agreement between the i-STAT Alinity and Simoa HD-X platforms was poor-to-moderate for GFAP (Intraclass correlation coefficient; ICC: 0.25 [-0.14, 0.59], P = 0.11) and poor-to-good for UCH-L1 (ICC: 0.60 [0.20, 0.82], P = 0.0026). The ARGO HT demonstrated strong inter-analyzer correlation with the i-STAT Alinity for GFAP (r = 0.98, P = 6.2e-18) and moderate correlation for UCH-L1 (r = 0.66, P = 0.00022). Collectively, this cross-platform validation highlights the importance of device-specific analytical methods and prognostication thresholds for each analytical platform considered for use in clinical practice.

42824611.title: Cerebral Oxygenation Changes During Sequential Postural Transitions From Supine to Walking in Healthy Adults: An Exploratory Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Study.
42824611.abstract: Objective Early mobilization (EM) in the intensive care unit (ICU) reduces complications from prolonged bed rest and improves functional outcomes. However, there are still no objective criteria for cerebral hemodynamics during postural changes, especially walking. Methods This exploratory observational study used near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) to measure prefrontal cerebral oxygenation changes in 14 healthy adults during sequential postural transitions from supine rest to sitting, standing, and walking. The following parameters were assessed: oxygenated hemoglobin (O₂Hb), deoxygenated hemoglobin (HHb), total hemoglobin (tHb), regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO₂), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and heart rate (HR). Results ΔO₂Hb decreased, and ΔHHb increased relative to the supine baseline, with significant differences in the magnitude of change across sitting, standing, and walking (ΔO₂Hb, p = 0.012; ΔHHb, p < 0.001). rSO₂ differed significantly across the four postural conditions, with lower values observed in upright postures than in the supine position (p < 0.001). The magnitude of ΔtHb did not differ significantly among sitting, standing, and walking (p = 0.257). MAP (p = 0.015) and HR (p < 0.001) differed significantly across the four postural conditions. Conclusions Sequential postural transitions from supine rest to sitting, standing, and walking were associated with changes in NIRS-derived cerebral oxygenation in healthy adults, characterized by decreases in O₂Hb and increases in HHb during progression to upright postures. These findings characterize cerebral oxygenation changes across a stepwise mobilization sequence and may provide preliminary reference data for evaluating cerebral oxygenation during mobilization.

42820032.title: Association between destination hospital level and outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients under a dispatch-guided transport system: a population-based study in Nagoya, Japan.
42820032.abstract: The relationship between destination hospital level and outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients remains controversial. To examine the association between transport to critical care medical centers and outcomes, we analyzed all city-wide data from Nagoya City, where the initial hospital request is made without consideration of initial cardiac rhythm. This retrospective cohort study included 12,663 OHCA patients in Nagoya City between April 2019 and March 2025. Patients were classified by destination hospital: critical care medical center (n = 11,149) or other hospital (n = 1514). Favorable one-month neurological outcomes and one-month survival were evaluated. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) evaluated associations between destination hospital level and outcomes. Refractory shockable rhythm was explored. In the critical care medical center and other hospital groups, favorable one-month neurological outcome rates were 1.9% versus 1.7% (P = 0.683), and survival rates were 4.1% versus 4.5% (P = 0.494). IPTW showed no association between destination hospital level and favorable neurological outcomes overall or by rhythm. Transport to critical care medical centers was associated with lower one-month survival in patients with non-shockable rhythm (odds ratio, 0.66; 95% confidence interval, 0.46-0.95). Exploratory analysis showed higher one-month survival among patients with refractory shockable rhythm transported to critical care medical centers (19.7% vs. 3.3%), although the estimate was imprecise. Under a dispatch-guided transport system, transport to critical care medical centers was not associated with favorable neurological outcomes in either rhythm group. These findings do not establish a preferred transport strategy, although selected patients may have better outcomes at these centers.

42956386.title: Resting-State Functional MRI and Clinical Outcomes After Acute Disorders of Consciousness: A Systematic Review.
42956386.abstract: Accurate assessment and prognostication of patients with acute disorders of consciousness (DoC) after severe brain injury remain a substantial clinical challenge. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) measures spontaneous, temporally correlated brain activity in the absence of external stimulation and provides objective insight into the integrity of large-scale neural networks that support brain function. Emerging evidence suggests that assessing neural integrity using rs-fMRI may improve outcome prediction in patients with acute DoC. This review summarizes the current evidence of rs-fMRI as an assessment tool during the acute phase of severe brain injury. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature search using MEDLINE and Embase databases from January 2006 to March 2026. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed empirical investigations of adult patients with acute DoC (<28 days postinjury) that examined associations between rs-fMRI measures and clinical outcomes. The systematic review protocol was registered in the PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251085923). Of 396 studies screened, 30 met eligibility criteria. Across these studies, a total of 800 patients (mean age = 48, 69% male) were scanned at a weighted average of 9.31 days after intensive care unit admission. Ten studies included patients exclusively with traumatic brain injury, 8 with cardiac arrest, 2 with encephalopathy, and 10 included mixed etiologies. The most frequently assessed resting-state networks were the default mode (n = 20) and executive control networks (n = 11), followed by visual (n = 6), salience (n = 6), sensorimotor (n = 6), and auditory (n = 5) networks. Across studies, significant associations between rs-fMRI measures and outcome were consistently reported, despite heterogeneity in methodology. The most commonly reported patient outcomes were functional or neurologic status, assessed at hospital discharge or between 3 and 12 months postinjury. Current evidence consistently demonstrates that rs-fMRI acquired during the acute phase of brain injury is associated with neurologic and functional outcomes in patients with DoC. In addition, rs-fMRI may help identify patients more likely to recover consciousness and achieve favorable functional outcomes by characterizing the integrity of large-scale brain networks. However, substantial heterogeneity and small sample sizes limit comparability across studies. Standardized acquisition and analysis frameworks, along with larger prospective studies, are needed to validate the clinical utility of rs-fMRI and support translation into an assessment tool after brain injury.

42953261.title: Reverse Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Complicated by Neurogenic Pulmonary Edema in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Case Report.
42953261.abstract: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TTC) is a recognized and potentially severe cardiac complication in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Reverse TTC (rTTC), a rare variant characterized by basal hypokinesis with apical sparing, is infrequently reported in this setting. The coexistence of rTTC with neurogenic pulmonary edema has not been previously described and represents a complex neurocardiac interaction that can significantly worsen outcomes. We report the case of a previously healthy 30-year-old man who presented with high-grade aSAH secondary to rupture of an anterior communicating artery aneurysm. His course was complicated by neurogenic pulmonary edema, refractory hypoxemia, hemodynamic instability, and rTTC. Management required early airway protection, bronchoscopy, vasopressor support, and complex stent-assisted endovascular coiling. Echocardiography demonstrated reduced left ventricular ejection fraction with basal hypokinesis and apical sparing, consistent with rTTC. Careful hemodynamic management was essential to balance cerebral perfusion against myocardial dysfunction. With multidisciplinary critical care and structured rehabilitation, the patient achieved favorable neurological and functional recovery. This case highlights that rTTC in aSAH is not a benign condition and may be associated with increased morbidity when combined with neurogenic pulmonary edema due to massive catecholamine surge. Early recognition using bedside echocardiography, prompt aneurysm securing, and balanced hemodynamic support are critical for improving outcomes.

42952895.title: The effect of goal-directed fluid therapy on endothelial glycocalyx and short-term postoperative recovery quality in older patients undergoing laparoscopic hernia or gallbladder surgery: a randomized controlled double-blind clinical study.
42952895.abstract: This study aimed to observe the effects of intraoperative goal-directed fluid therapy on postoperative recovery in older patients undergoing laparoscopic hernia or gallbladder surgery. A total of 60 older patients were randomly assigned to the control group (C group) and the goal- directed fluid therapy group (G group). The primary outcome was the plasma concentration of syndecan-1. The secondary outcomes were the plasma concentrations of tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-1 (IL-1), intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1); mean arterial pressure; heart rate; regional cerebral oxygen saturation; intraoperative dopamine dosage; QoR-15 scale score; hematocrit; and postoperative adverse events. Compared with the C group, the G group showed decreased plasma concentrations of ICAM-1 at the end of surgery and 24 h after surgery (P = 0.010 and 0.005, respectively), decreased plasma concentrations of syndecan-1 at the end of surgery (P = 0.049), more significantly decreased plasma concentrations of VCAM-1 at the end of surgery and 24 h after surgery (P < 0.001 and P = 0.017, respectively), and decreased plasma concentrations of IL-1β at the end of surgery and 24 h after surgery (P = 0.009 and 0.008, respectively). The C group showed increased plasma concentration of TNF-α at the end of surgery and 24 h after surgery compared with those before surgery (P = 0.003 and 0.023, respectively). Compared with the C group, the QoR-15 scores were higher at 24, 48, and 72 h after surgery (P = 0.001, 0.001, and 0.005, respectively) in the treatment group. Intraoperative goal-directed fluid therapy in non-critically ill older patients may alleviate endothelial glycocalyx degradation with a lower incidence of adverse events. http://www.chictr.org.cn/, Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2500097999.

42952486.title: Interprofessional collaboration in emergency department nursing care for patients with diabetic ketoacidosis: a narrative review.
42952486.abstract: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is an acute metabolic emergency requiring timely risk recognition, fluid resuscitation, insulin therapy, electrolyte correction, dynamic monitoring, and coordinated care transitions. These interdependent tasks pose substantial challenges to emergency nursing. This narrative review aimed to synthesise current evidence on interprofessional collaboration in emergency DKA nursing and propose a conceptual framework to support coordinated care. A structured narrative review was conducted using literature retrieved from PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and the Web of Science Core Collection from database inception to July 10, 2026. DKA-specific clinical and implementation evidence was integrated with broader literature on interprofessional collaboration, communication, and healthcare implementation. The evidence was synthesised using Donabedian's structure-process-outcome framework. Current collaborative approaches include nurse-led standardised pathways, risk-stratified subcutaneous insulin and non-intensive care unit management, collaborative medication management, laboratory and point-of-care monitoring, structured communication, digital decision support, and multidisciplinary discharge planning. Available evidence suggests that standardised collaborative pathways may improve the timeliness and consistency of care, shorten emergency department length of stay, and reduce intensive care resource use. However, evidence evaluating complete interprofessional nursing teams and nursing-sensitive outcomes remains limited. Based on the synthesis, a conceptual closed-loop collaboration framework comprising six interconnected stages was proposed: recognition and activation, shared risk stratification, coordinated monitoring and execution, escalation, care transition, and recurrence prevention. Effective interprofessional DKA nursing requires shared clinical information, explicit responsibility, timely feedback, and predefined escalation procedures, with emergency nurses serving as continuous information integrators and process coordinators. The proposed framework provides an evidence-informed approach to organising collaborative emergency care. However, it has not been prospectively validated, and further implementation research is required to evaluate its feasibility, safety, and effects on nursing-sensitive and patient outcomes.

42948399.title: Postoperative cardiac arrest after cardiac surgery: Can we improve our rescue rate?
42948399.abstract: Despite improvements in rescue strategies, postoperative cardiac arrest in adults undergoing cardiac surgery has not been examined in the contemporary era. This study assesses the incidence, outcomes, and predictors of survival in patients who had an in-hospital cardiac arrest after cardiac surgery. Adult patients with cardiac arrest after open surgery from January 2012 to May 2019 at a single institution were studied. Patients were excluded if they underwent heart transplantation or left ventricular assist device implantation, experienced preoperative or intraoperative cardiac arrest, received preoperative or intraoperative temporary mechanical circulatory support, or were deemed as do not resuscitate or care was withdrawn before the arrest. Of 9946 patients, 162 (1.6%) experienced a postoperative arrest with failure to rescue in 59 patients (36.4%). The etiology of cardiac arrest was cardiovascular in 101 patients (62.3%), respiratory in 27 patients (16.7%), metabolic in 15 patients (9.3%), other in 12 patients (7.4%), and unknown in 7 patients (4.3%). Thirteen patients (8.0%) were placed on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation postarrest with only 4 (30.8%) surviving to discharge. Patients were more likely to die in-hospital if they had postoperative, prearrest organ dysfunction (adjusted odds ratio, 7.08, 95% CI, 2.92-17.16). Although the incidence of cardiac arrest was low, more than one-third of patients failed to be rescued. Prearrest major organ dysfunction portended a significantly worse prognosis. Early recognition of a nonthriving patient and rapid escalation of specialized care may be critical in successful rescue from cardiac arrest and aborting catastrophic outcomes.

42947281.title: Association of Initial Peripheral Venous pO(2) With 48-Hour Clinical Deterioration in Emergency Department Patients Undergoing Venous Blood Gas Testing.
42947281.journal: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
42947281.abstract: Peripheral venous pO2 is routinely reported with venous blood gas (VBG) results despite uncertainty regarding its prognostic significance. We evaluated whether initial peripheral venous pO2 was associated with 48-h clinical deterioration and provided prognostic information beyond age and lactate. We conducted an ambispective observational cohort study of adults undergoing VBG testing at a single urban academic emergency department, with prospective enrollment and index-data collection and retrospective ascertainment of 48-h outcomes. The primary outcome was a composite of ICU admission, death, vasopressor use, or positive-pressure ventilation within 48 h. The primary analysis modeled venous pO2 continuously and used multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and lactate. Incremental performance was evaluated exploratorily by comparing an age-and-lactate model with a model additionally containing venous pO2. Among 973 patients, 103 (10.6%) experienced the composite outcome. Median venous pO2 was 33 mmHg (IQR 25-44). Venous pO2 was not associated with clinical deterioration after adjustment for age and lactate (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.054 per 10-mmHg increase; 95% CI 0.957-1.161; p = 0.289). The AUROC was 0.649 for the age-and-lactate model and 0.654 after adding venous pO2 (ΔAUROC 0.005; DeLong p = 0.390). In this single-center cohort of adult ED patients undergoing VBG testing, no association was observed between peripheral venous pO2 and 48-h clinical deterioration. Adding venous pO2 did not improve apparent prognostic performance beyond age and lactate. We cannot exclude smaller associations or potential utility in selected disease-specific populations. Confirmation in larger multicenter cohorts using consecutive enrollment and external validation is needed.

42946504.title: Feasibility of Prehospital Central Venous Cannulation During Cardiac Arrest in an Ambulance.
42946504.abstract: Central venous cannulation is routinely performed in hospital settings but is rarely considered in the prehospital environment, where confined workspaces and concurrent resuscitative demands may limit procedural feasibility. We conducted a simulation-based feasibility study to evaluate whether central venous cannulation could be performed during ongoing cardiac arrest resuscitation within a standard ambulance. A multidisciplinary team consisting of emergency medical services clinicians and a physician participated in repeated simulations using a resuscitation manikin. A refractory shockable cardiac arrest scenario requiring ongoing advanced cardiac life support was simulated, while airway management, medication administration, cardiac monitoring, and chest compressions continued uninterrupted. Central venous cannulation was successfully completed in all simulations using standard sterile technique. The technical aspects of cannulation were largely unchanged from hospital-based practice, and left femoral venous access was identified as the most practical site. The primary challenges were limited workspace and unfavorable ergonomics related to the fixed stretcher height, which required the operator performing cannulation to work in an awkward position. Despite these constraints, all major advanced cardiac life support interventions were maintained throughout the procedure. These findings suggest that central venous cannulation during ongoing cardiac arrest resuscitation is technically feasible within a standard ambulance environment and support further investigation into advanced vascular access procedures in prehospital critical care.

42946325.title: DPP3 as a Biomarker in Patients with Cardiovascular Critical Illness.
42946325.abstract: Dipeptidyl peptidase 3 (DPP3) exerts vasodilatory and myocardial depressant effects in preclinical models and is a potential therapeutic target in cardiogenic shock (CS). Patients admitted to the CICU at Brigham and Women's Hospital were enrolled in a biorepository with samples collected at CICU admission. Using samples from 2017-2023, DPP3 was measured using an immunoluminometric assay (4TEEN4). Shock, defined by hypotension and end-organ hypoperfusion, was adjudicated as CS (classic or vasodilatory) or distributive (DS). Controls were CICU patients without shock. Models were adjusted for age, sex, eGFR, and SOFA score. Of 1082 CICU patients, 381 (35.2%) had CS, 70 (6.5%) had DS, and 618 (57.2%) were non-shock controls. DPP3 values were higher in CS (median, 42.7 [Q1-Q3, 25.6-84.3] ng/mL) than in non-shock controls (31.8 [20.2-57.2] ng/mL; p<0.001) but, nevertheless, were elevated (>30 ng/mL) in 53.6% of non-shock controls. CICU patients with DPP3 >30 ng/mL had higher in-hospital mortality (19.9% vs. 8.4%; OR 2.7 [95% CI 1.8-4.0]; p<0.001), with a consistent pattern across CS, DS, and non-shock patients (p-interaction=0.72) and across CS etiologic subgroups (p-interaction=0.18). In adjusted analyses including both shock and non-shock patients, DPP3 showed a graded association with mortality across quartiles (adj-OR Q4 vs. Q1: 3.0 [1.6-6.1]; p<0.001), and at a 30 ng/mL threshold (adj-OR: 2.1 [1.4-3.4]; p=0.001). Among critically ill CICU patients, DPP3 was elevated in shock and non-shock states and was associated with in-hospital mortality. These findings support a potential role for DPP3 as a biomarker for risk stratification and a possible target for therapy.

42946209.title: Shock Teams May Improve Outcomes of Patients with Cardiogenic Shock (STOP-CS): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
42946209.abstract: A multidisciplinary team-based approach became one of the main paradigms in health care. Current evidence regarding the efficacy of Shock Teams and related advanced shock care models in cardiogenic shock (CS) comes from observational studies, with limited synthetic data available. We aimed to assess the association between advanced shock care models and short- and mid-term outcomes of CS patients. This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO registration: CRD42024581904) were conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 Statement. We included observational studies of at least 25 adult CS patients managed with or without a Shock Team or related advanced shock care models. We searched Embase, Medline Ultimate, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from 01.01.2016 to 13.08.2024. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Meta-analyses were performed with a random-effects model. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Nine studies with a total of 658,708 patients met the inclusion criteria. For medium-term mortality, follow-up ranged from 60 to 365 days. Treatment of patients within the included models was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.81, 95%CI: [0.74, 0.90], p<0.0001, I2=58%), lower intensive care unit mortality (OR: 0.58, 95%CI: [0.43, 0.78], p=0.0004, I2=45%), and lower medium-term mortality (HR: 0.59, 95%CI: [0.48, 0.72], p<0.00001, I2=0%). These associations remained significant in sensitivity analyses, although clinical and methodological heterogeneity persisted. Advanced shock care models may be associated with improved short- and mid-term outcomes in CS patients including lower in-hospital and medium-term mortality. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these results.

42934677.title: Mortality risk model for acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: development, external validation, and exploratory application in a VA-ECMO cohort.
42934677.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
42934677.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) carries a high risk of in-hospital death. Randomized evidence does not support routine VA-ECMO use in unselected AMI-CS populations. Objective and interpretable risk stratification is clinically important when advanced mechanical circulatory support is considered. This was a retrospective, multi-database model development and validation study with exploratory application in a local VA-ECMO-treated AMI-CS cohort. An in-hospital mortality prediction model was developed in AMI-CS patients who did not receive ECMO treatment using the MIMIC-IV database. Candidate measurements were summarized using the worst values accumulated during the first 24 h after ICU admission. Variable shrinkage was performed using LASSO logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation, and the model was established using multivariable logistic regression. Internal validation included the original fixed-structure bootstrap and an additional full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity analysis. The latter repeated preprocessing, LASSO selection, post-LASSO handling, and model refitting within each resample. External validation was performed in the eICU cohort. The model was then applied exploratorily to the local VA-ECMO-treated AMI-CS cohort to describe model transportability and the relationship between observed and predicted outcomes. The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 355 patients, of whom 127 died in hospital (35.77%). LASSO selected 8 clinical predictors. The apparent AUC was 0.829 (95% CI 0.785-0.874). After the final model was refitted in 200 fixed-structure bootstrap resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.814. In 500 full-pipeline bootstrap resamples, all repetitions were valid, the mean optimism was 0.0436, and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.786 (empirical 2.5th to 97.5th percentile range: 0.745-0.832). The AUCs from the MIMIC-IV complete-case and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses were 0.820 and 0.840, respectively. In the eICU complete-case cohort, the AUC was 0.806 (95% CI 0.691-0.921), O/E was 0.733, the calibration intercept was - 0.986, and the calibration slope was 0.671. After multiple imputation in all 224 eligible eICU patients, the AUC was 0.771, O/E was 0.754, the calibration intercept was - 0.756, and the calibration slope was 0.528. The local cohort included 40 VA-ECMO-treated patients. Overall observed mortality was 42.5% (95% CI 27.0-59.1), mean predicted mortality was 59.2% (95% CI 50.6-67.2), and O/E was 0.717 (95% CI 0.418-1.149). This study developed and externally validated a mortality risk model for patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock. The model may provide a research reference for early risk stratification and individualized assessment. Uncertainty in variable selection and cross-population calibration drift limit its direct clinical application. Prospective multicenter studies are required for further validation and to evaluate its role in VA-ECMO patient selection.

42930894.title: Timing of Microaxial Flow Pump Support and In-Hospital Mortality in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock: The TIMING-CS Study.
42930894.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
42930894.abstract: (1) Background: The association between microaxial flow pump (mAFP) timing and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains uncertain. (2) Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of patients with AMI-CS admitted between January 2017 and July 2025. Prespecified 24 h landmark analyses included patients alive 24 h after intensive care unit (ICU) admission. The primary analysis compared patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) receiving mAFP within 6 h with STEMI patients managed without temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS). Later STEMI implantation (>6-≤24 h) and both non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) timing cohorts were exploratory. The primary endpoint was subsequent in-hospital mortality from the landmark onward. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and propensity score-weighted models. (3) Results: In the primary STEMI cohort, 106 patients received mAFP within 6 h and 59 received no-tMCS. Subsequeunt in-hospital mortality was 17.0% versus 23.7%, respectively (p = 0.293). Early mAFP implantation was associated with lower mortality in the fully adjusted model (OR, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.06-0.99]; p = 0.048). Propensity score-based estimates were directionally consistent, with significance in the doubly robust weighted model (OR, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.06-0.85]; p = 0.028) but not in all weighted models. Later-timing and NSTEMI estimates did not reach statistical significance and were imprecise. (4) Conclusions: Among patients with STEMI who survived the first 24 h after ICU admission, mAFP implantation within 6 h was associated with lower subsequent in-hospital mortality. Exploratory later-timing and NSTEMI estimates were inconclusive. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

42930871.title: Planned Impella 5.5 Support via Brachiocephalic Artery or Ascending Aorta for Low Ejection Fraction, High-Risk Cardiac Surgery.
42930871.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
42930871.abstract: Background: Surgically implanted microaxial flow pumps are increasingly being utilized to treat cardiogenic shock; however, data on their use in the realm of cardiac surgery are scarce. We report our single-institution experience in low-ejection-fraction, high-risk patients with a planned weaning strategy from cardiopulmonary bypass directly to Impella 5.5 inserted via the brachiocephalic artery or ascending aorta following corrective cardiac surgery. Methods: A prospectively maintained institutional database was queried from 2022 through to 2025. Primary endpoints included feasibility of implantation, weaning rate, and bedside removal; secondary endpoints included freedom from all-cause mortality at discharge and 1 year, in-hospital thromboembolic complications, postoperative pharmacologic hemodynamic support using vasoactive inotropic score (VIS), de novo renal failure, and revision for bleeding. Descriptive statistics were applied. Results: Sixteen patients (median age 66.5 years [IQR; interquartile range, 52.5-70.0], STS score 12.1% [IQR, 5.3-14.2%] and EF 20.0% [IQR, 15.0-31.5%]) underwent coronary revascularization (n = 6), valve procedures (n = 4) or a combination thereof (n = 6) and were weaned from cardiopulmonary bypass to Impella 5.5 implanted via the ascending aorta (25%) or brachiocephalic artery (75%). Primary endpoints were met in 100% (feasibility of implantation), 94% (weaning rate), and 100% (bedside removal). In terms of secondary endpoints, freedom from mortality at discharge and one year was 94.8%; there were two non-disabling strokes (12.6%) while still on Impella 5.5 support; the median VIS at the time of ICU arrival was 12.8 (IQR 10.8-22.1); renal failure occurred in two patients and four patients required revision for bleeding. Conclusions: Impella 5.5-supported cardiac surgery appears safe and may open a new avenue for high-risk patients.

42927337.title: Evaluating cardiopulmonary resuscitation in "The Pitt": accuracy, clinical realism, and adherence to international resuscitation guidelines.
42927337.abstract: Medical television dramas shape public perceptions of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). The Pitt has been praised for its clinical realism but has not been systematically evaluated. We assessed adherence of televised CPR to current European Resuscitation Council (ERC) and American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines. All cardiac arrest (CA) scenarios requiring chest compressions or defibrillation in seasons 1 & 2 (30 episodes) of The Pitt were prospectively analysed using a standardized assessment via an electronic case report form based on Utstein-style variables by at least 2 emergency and/or intensive care physicians experienced in CA management. Seventeen CA were identified. Most occurred in hospital (65%, n = 11/17) and had medical causes (59%, n = 10/17). ROSC was achieved in 56% (n = 9/16), and survival to discharge in 46% (n = 6/13). Key elements of the initial assessment, including consciousness and pulse checks, were fully guideline compliant, and correct hand placement was observed in 94% (n = 15/16). In contrast, guideline-compliant compression rate were achieved in only 19% (n = 3/16) of assessable cases, respectively, and pre-airway 30:2 compression-to-ventilation ratios were absent. Immediate post-shock rhythm reassessments were observed in 78% (n = 7/9) of appropriate cases. Nevertheless, no inappropriate shocks were delivered during asystole, and rhythm-based pharmacotherapy was appropriate, although medication timing and sequence could not be reliably assessed. The Pitt provides a highly realistic portrayal of cardiac arrest, although manual CPR technique and some algorithmic details remain imperfect.

42907224.title: [Construction of a prediction model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events after emergency percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction].
42907224.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
42907224.abstract: Objective: To construct a machine-learning-based prediction model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: A total of 5829 patients with STEMI who underwent emergency PCI at the Emergency Critical Care Center of Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Capital Medical University, from January 1, 2015, to July 1, 2025, were enrolled. Patients were divided into the MACE group (524 cases) and the non-MACE group (5 305 cases) according to the occurrence of in-hospital MACE and were further divided into the training set (4 080 cases) and test set (1 749 cases) at a ratio of 7∶3. MACE included cardiogenic shock, severe heart failure, severe arrhythmia, acute stent thrombosis or recurrent acute myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and cardiogenic death. Demographic data, lifestyle-related factors, past medical history, admission vital signs, laboratory test results within 24 hours after admission, echocardiographic parameters, Killip classification, and coronary interventional data were collected. Univariate analysis and Lasso regression were performed to select variables for model construction. Five machine-learning algorithms, including support vector machine (SVM), logistic regression, random forest, naive Bayes, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), were used to construct prediction models for in-hospital MACE. The optimal model was selected based on the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Calibration curve and decision curve analysis were used to assess the probability calibration and clinical net benefit of the model. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the contribution of each feature. Results: The patients were aged (58.1±12.3) years, and 4 875 (83.63%) were male. Fourteen variables were selected for model construction, including B-type natriuretic peptide, myoglobin, left ventricular ejection fraction, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, high-sensitivity troponin I, triglycerides, triglyceride-glucose index, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, glycated hemoglobin, creatine kinase-MB, smoking history, heart rate, Killip classification, and age. The XGBoost model yielded the best predictive performance, with an AUC-ROC of 0.992 and an AUPRC of 0.947, and exhibited favorable probability calibration and clinical net benefit. SHAP analysis demonstrated that the top five variables with the greatest contribution to model prediction were B-type natriuretic peptide, creatine kinase-MB, myoglobin, left ventricular ejection fraction, and triglyceride-glucose index. Conclusions: Machine-learning prediction models for in-hospital MACE after emergency PCI in patients with STEMI were successfully constructed and internally validated. The XGBoost model demonstrated good discriminative ability, probability calibration, and clinical net benefit and may serve as a reference for early in-hospital risk stratification and clinical decision-making in STEMI patients undergoing emergency PCI.

42907145.title: Association of Iron Deficiency Anemia with Outcomes in Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Analysis.
42907145.abstract: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently have iron deficiency anemia (IDA), but the mechanism by which this condition affects clinical outcomes is not well understood. The purpose of this study was to assess whether IDA is associated with mortality in patients with AF. Data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) for 2021-2022 examined IDA and inpatient outcomes in a nationally representative cohort of hospitalized adults diagnosed with AF. Patients were categorized by IDA status. The factors assessed were mortality, hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, thromboembolic and cardiovascular complications, and overall hospital expenses. Hospital, clinical, and demographic factors were included in multivariable logistic and linear regression models. Of the 8.35 million AF hospitalizations, 7.1% had associated IDA. IDA was linked to multiple comorbidities along with increased risk of hypotension (OR: 1.15, 95% CI 1.12-1.17, P<0.001), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.25, 95% CI 1.23-1.27, P<0.001), and heart failure (Adjusted Odds Ratio [AOR]: 1.29, 95% CI 1.27-1.31, P<0.001). Ironically, IDA was linked independently to decreased risks of cardiac arrest (AOR: 0.70, 95% CI 0.66-0.73, P<0.001), transient ischemic attack (AOR: 0.58, 95% CI 0.53-0.63, P<0.001), stroke (OR: 0.49,95% CI 0.47-0.51, P<0.001), and in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.66, 95% CI 0.64-0.68, P<0.001). IDA was also associated with increased hospital expenses and increased LOS (P<0.001). IDA was linked to higher morbidity and healthcare use in those with AF admitted to the hospital, but there was a decrease in mortality and thromboembolic events. These results suggest the possibility of tailored iron therapy and imply a complex interaction between IDA and AF-related outcomes.

42904388.title: Prehospital point-of-care ultrasound as a decision-support tool: A structured narrative review.
42904388.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) may support focused bedside decisions, but prehospital implementation remains limited by operational constraints, heterogeneous protocols, variable training, and limited outcome-focused evidence. This narrative review examines prehospital POCUS as a clinical decision-support tool across cardiac, thoracic, trauma, pediatric, and obstetric applications. A structured narrative review was conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central from April 2017 to February 2026. Search terms combined the prehospital setting, ultrasound, and clinical applications. Of 464 records identified, 38 full-text articles were included, including nine systematic reviews on cardiac evaluation (n = 2), thoracic evaluation (n = 3), and trauma assessment (n = 4). Screening and full-text assessment were performed by a single reviewer. No formal risk-of-bias assessment, certainty grading, quantitative synthesis, or meta-analysis was performed. In cardiac arrest, prehospital POCUS may identify cardiac activity and selected reversible causes, guide interventions, confirm return of spontaneous circulation, and support prognostic assessment, provided that image acquisition does not interrupt resuscitation or delay defibrillation. In nontraumatic shock and cardiac dysfunction, focused cardiac, lung, and vascular ultrasound may help characterize shock mechanisms, guide fluid therapy, and identify actionable findings such as pulmonary congestion, pericardial effusion, right ventricular strain, or major aortic pathology. In acute dyspnea, lung ultrasound may improve diagnostic confidence, particularly for cardiogenic pulmonary edema. In trauma, E-FAST has high specificity and may support triage, destination choice, trauma pathway activation, and preparation for definitive care; however, limited sensitivity prevents its use as a rule-out test. Pediatric and obstetric applications are feasible but remain emerging. Prehospital POCUS is an adjunctive decision-support tool rather than a standalone diagnostic test. Its value lies in answering actionable questions that may influence treatment, triage, transport destination, hospital prealert, or pathway activation. Implementation requires protocols, training, quality assurance, and governance, and must not delay time-critical care or transport.

42904250.title: Sudden Cardiac Arrest in a Previously Healthy Young Male: Perimyocarditis Presenting as Myocardial Infarction With Non-obstructive Coronary Arteries.
42904250.abstract: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a heterogeneous clinical entity that may mimic acute coronary syndromes despite the absence of significant epicardial coronary artery disease. Inflammatory myocardial conditions, such as myocarditis and perimyocarditis, represent important non-ischemic causes of MINOCA and may present with life-threatening complications, including malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac arrest. We report a case of a 37-year-old previously healthy male who presented with chest discomfort, syncope, and sudden cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation. Post-cardiac arrest electrocardiography revealed extensive anterior ST-segment elevation, with markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers and transient severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Coronary angiography demonstrated non-obstructive epicardial coronary arteries, leading to the diagnosis of MINOCA. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed late gadolinium enhancement in a pattern consistent with perimyocarditis. The patient required advanced life support and intensive care management for cardiogenic shock, followed by progressive clinical improvement with complete recovery of left ventricular function. This case highlights perimyocarditis as a rare but critical cause of MINOCA presenting with sudden cardiac arrest and malignant ventricular arrhythmias in a young patient. It underscores the importance of a systematic diagnostic approach and emphasizes cardiac magnetic resonance as a key tool for etiological diagnosis, guiding appropriate management and enabling full functional recovery.

42902397.title: Crystalloid vs colloid for Hemodynamics during Anesthesia INduction in TAVR patients (CHAIN-T): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
42902397.abstract: To assess whether preload with colloids could reduce hypotension during induction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared to crystalloids. This study is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled trial conducted at Xijing Hospital. A total of 116 patients scheduled for elective TAVR under general anesthesia will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the colloid group or the crystalloid group, receiving either 5 ml/kg of colloid or crystalloid solution before anesthesia induction infused over 15 min. The primary outcome is the area under curve (AUC) of the change in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from baseline during the induction period (until 15 min after induction). Secondary outcomes include the incidence of intraoperative hemodynamic instability, the use of intraoperative vasoactive drugs, the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on the first postoperative day, postoperative hospital length of stay, the rate of intensive care unit (ICU) admission postoperatively, all-cause mortality during hospitalization and by 30 days after surgery, and the incidence of renal replacement therapy by 30 days after surgery. The results of this study will provide evidence on optimizing fluid preload to prevent hypotension during induction, reduce postoperative complications, and enhance recovery for patients undergoing TAVR. The findings are expected to promote anesthesia protocols in this patient population. The study protocol and statistical analysis plan were approved by the institutional Ethics Committee of Xijing Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University (XJLL-KY-20252560). The study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07329660) on December 29, 2025.

42897648.title: Delayed life-threatening aortic rupture after rib fractures: a case report.
42897648.abstract: Aortic injury secondary to rib fractures is an extremely rare but life-threatening complication of blunt thoracic trauma. Most of the documented cases result in prehospital mortality or death shortly after arrival because of massive hemothorax. Although the surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) has become increasingly integrated into thoracic trauma care, there remains a lack of awareness regarding the potential for posteriorly displaced rib fractures to cause delayed aortic injury. A 71-year-old female patient sustained multiple left posterior rib fractures and solid-organ injuries following a traffic accident. Initial management involved exploratory laparotomy and splenectomy for hemoperitoneum. Several hours later in the intensive care unit, a sudden massive hemothorax developed, and cardiac arrest occurred due to active bleeding from a descending aortic laceration caused by displaced posterior rib fragments. Emergency thoracotomy revealed a 6-mm descending aortic laceration with diffuse intramural hematoma, which was repaired with proximal aorta clamped. After opening adventitial layer, the intima layer was repaired primarily using 5-0 Prolene sutures. Bovine pericardium was used as a reinforcement patch to restore the integrity of the adventitial layer rather than as a pledget for the primary repair. Following hemodynamic stabilization, SSRF was performed to fix the displaced sixth and seventh ribs and prevent further complications with plates and screws (MatrixRIB™ system). The patient was discharged on postoperative day 19 in good condition without any complication. This case illustrates a rare instance of survival following aortic injury induced by rib fractures and emphasizes the need for high clinical suspicion in similar presentations. Early vascular control combined with prompt rib fixation may reduce morbidity rates by restoring chest wall stability, improving respiratory mechanics, and preventing secondary complications.

42895373.title: [Idiopathic systemic capillary leak syndrome - a rare but serious differential diagnosis in the hypovolemic patient].
42895373.abstract: Idiopathic systemic capillary leak syndrome (SCLS) is a rare, life-threatening cause of hypovolemic shock characterized by hemoconcentration, hypoalbuminemia, and acute hypovolemia due to plasma extravasation. It should be suspected in patients presenting with unexplained hypotension and markedly elevated hemoglobin levels, often following nonspecific prodromal symptoms such as malaise. Management is supportive and includes aggressive crystalloid resuscitation, vasopressor therapy, corticosteroids, and intravenous immunoglobulins. Owing to the risk of rapid hemodynamic deterioration and multi--organ failure, intensive care monitoring is essential. We report a previously healthy middle-aged man with recent upper respiratory tract infection and syncope who developed fulminant SCLS with refractory shock and died despite intensive care treatment.

42891396.title: Cardiac arrest as the first sign of thyrotoxicosis: a case report of angiographically proven coronary vasospasm.
42891396.abstract: Cardiovascular manifestations of thyrotoxicosis are common, typically presenting as tachyarrhythmias or high-output physiology. Coronary artery spasm (CAS) is an uncommon but increasingly recognized complication, usually causing transient ischaemia rather than malignant ventricular arrhythmias. Cardiac arrest due to thyrotoxicosis-induced CAS is exceedingly rare. Early recognition is vital because management differs from that of typical acute coronary syndromes (ACS). A 63-year-old man suffered an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with an initial shockable rhythm, achieving return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after a single defibrillation. Initial evaluation revealed inferior ST-segment elevation, leading to urgent coronary angiography, which demonstrated severe right coronary artery spasm that resolved after intracoronary nitrate administration. Laboratory studies confirmed significant hyperthyroidism, and recurrent ST-segment changes in the intensive care unit further supported thyrotoxicosis-induced CAS as the underlying mechanism. The patient made a full neurological and cardiac recovery following temperature management, intensification of antithyroid therapy, and vasodilator treatment. This case underscored an unusual presentation of cardiac arrest triggered by thyrotoxicosis-related CAS in the absence of underlying coronary artery disease. Elevated thyroid hormone levels can impair endothelial function and heighten vascular smooth muscle reactivity, creating a predisposition to diffuse, therapy-resistant vasospasm. Recognizing this reversible yet potentially fatal condition is crucial, as prompt initiation of antithyroid therapy and vasodilators can rapidly alleviate ischaemia and reduce the risk of recurrence. The favourable outcome in this patient illustrates how early identification of the underlying cause can guide swift and effective management.

42891254.title: Post In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Simulation to Improve Medical Decision Making and Communication in Internal Medicine Residents.
42891254.journal: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources
42891254.abstract: Cardiac arrest is a common cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized patients, and is a critical event that hospital-based physicians must be prepared to manage. While cardiac arrest care follows established algorithms, management of patients after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) is more dynamic and nuanced. Resident physicians therefore need structured training to provide high-quality post-ROSC care. We developed a 90-minute simulation session on postarrest care for internal medicine interns. The session included 2 simulation cases: one involving a patient with ventricular tachycardia arrest in the intensive care unit, and another featuring a patient with pulseless electrical activity arrest in an acute care setting. Interns alternated between roles as participants and observers to both practice and analyze communication and clinical skills. Between simulation cases, a brief teaching talk was delivered to review a framework for post-ROSC care. The curriculum was evaluated using pre- and postsession questionnaires to evaluate changes in knowledge and confidence. Thirty-four learners participated in our curriculum over 2 academic years. We observed a statistically significant increase in the percentage of learners who correctly answered knowledge-based questions about target blood pressure (50% to 100%) and oxygen saturation (22% to 74%) in the post-ROSC period. We also saw significant increases in learners' self-reported confidence in communication (28% to 74%) and ability to generate a differential diagnosis for a cardiac arrest (25% to 74%). Our simulation session increased intern knowledge and confidence in managing patients in the post-ROSC setting.

42891070.title: Correlation of blood biomarkers with microstructural brain injury in survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
42891070.abstract: In-hospital mortality among resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients remains high. Identifying patients who will benefit from intensive care while avoiding prolonged, potentially unnecessary treatments is essential. Blood-based biomarkers provide a novel method for evaluating brain injury. The ability of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and total-tau (t-tau) to measure white and grey matter injury is unestablished in comatose OHCA survivors treated with targeted temperature management (TTM) or xenon combined with TTM. We examined correlations between the biomarkers and white and grey matter injury assessed with diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). This was a randomized, single-blind, phase 2 clinical drug trial involving two multipurpose intensive care units in Finland. It was conducted between August 2009 and March 2015. One hundred and ten comatose OHCA patients aged 24 to 76 years were randomly assigned to either inhaled xenon treatment combined with 24-h TTM (33°C) (n = 55, xenon group) or TTM alone (n = 55, control group). MRI data were available from 96 patients, with a median imaging time of 53 h (interquartile range, 47-64 h) after OHCA. Biomarker data were obtained from 105 patients. In the control group of 48 patients, after adjusting for age, sex and site, a disruption of white matter microintegrity as measured by decreased fractional anisotropy (FA) of DTI, the primary endpoint of the trial, showed a significant negative correlation with NfL at 24, 48 and 72 h (ρ = -0.28 to -0.37; P < 0.05), NSE at 48 and 72 h (ρ = -0.30 to -0.35; P < 0.05) and t-tau only at 72 h (ρ = -0.30; P < 0.05). In the xenon group (n = 48), these correlations were absent at all timepoints. The NfL-FA partial correlations showed progressive divergence between the xenon and control groups, with a statistically significant between-group difference observed at 72 h (ρ = -0.37 versus ρ = 0.14; P = 0.016). Cortical or basal ganglia grey matter mean diffusivity did not have a consistent correlation with biomarker levels at different time points. No statistically significant differences were found between the xenon and control groups in the adjusted geometric mean levels of GFAP, NfL, NSE or t-tau at various time points following OHCA. In conclusion, NfL correlated with FA in controls but not in the xenon group. This between-group difference reached significance at 72 h, suggesting that xenon may modify the relationship between axonal injury and white matter microstructure after OHCA.

42891020.title: Neuroprotective effect of early remote ischaemic post-conditioning after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (RIPOST-CA): study protocol for a randomised, single-blinded, monocentric, controlled trial.
42891020.abstract: Hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury is the leading cause of death and long-term disability after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and is driven by the ischaemia-reperfusion syndrome, for which no specific treatment exists. Remote ischaemic post-conditioning (brief, repeated cycles of limb ischaemia and reperfusion delivered with a pneumatic cuff), is protective across ischemia-reperfusion conditions. We aim to assess whether early conditioning reduces hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. This single-centre, single-blinded, randomised (1:1) controlled trial with blinded assessment of the outcome, enrols 48 comatose adults resuscitated from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Participants receive standard post-resuscitation care with three sham cuff sessions, or standard care plus three sessions of conditioning (thigh cuff, four cycles of 5-min inflation at 200 mmHg alternating with 5-min deflation), the first within 4 h of return of spontaneous circulation and repeated at the 12th and 24th hour. Randomisation is stratified by initial rhythm (shockable versus non-shockable). The primary endpoint is the change in serum neurofilament light chain between the 6th and 72nd hour after return of spontaneous circulation. Secondary endpoints include daily Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (days 1-3), serum neuron-specific enolase and protein S100-B kinetics, in-intensive care unit mortality by cause, and a favourable neurological outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-3) at intensive care unit discharge and at 90 days. RIPOST-CA is the first randomised trial to evaluate early remote ischemic post-conditioning on brain-injury biomarkers after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Its results could inform larger clinical trials of this simple, non-invasive intervention.Trial registration number: NCT06473207.

42890502.title: Clinical relevance of ventriculo-arterial coupling and how to assess it at the bedside.
42890502.abstract: This review describes ventriculo-arterial coupling (VAC), its clinical relevance and how to access it at the bedside. VAC refers to the interaction between the contractility of the ejecting ventricles and the load exerted by the arteries. It integrates cardiac performance with the properties of the vascular system to assess cardiovascular efficiency and workload ending in a stroke volume and energy required to create that work. This relationship is quantitatively expressed as the ratio between arterial elastance (Ea) and end-systolic ventricular elastance (Ees). VAC offers valuable insights into hemodynamic status that go beyond traditional parameters like blood pressure, stroke volume or ejection fraction and independently predicts outcome from critical illness. Optimal VAC reflects maximal efficiency of stroke work and preserved cardiovascular reserve, while uncoupling indicates impaired reserve and is associated with worse prognosis. Uncoupling can occur in both acute and chronic settings, can affect either the right ventricle and pulmonary circulation or left ventricle and systemic circulation or both, and is observed across most forms of shock. While VAC has traditionally been analyzed through invasive pressure-volume methods, it can now be approximated at the bedside using echocardiography and simplified elastance calculations. These approaches allow for dynamic assessments of therapeutic interventions, including fluids, vasopressors, inotropes, and mechanical circulatory support. By incorporating VAC into clinical practice, healthcare professionals can enhance hemodynamic phenotyping and support individualized, physiology-guided management of critically ill patients.

42889162.title: Temporal overlap of intraoperative hypotension and hypocapnia and postoperative outcomes after major open intracranial surgery: a time-weighted dual-hit cohort study.
42889162.abstract: Intraoperative hypotension reduces cerebral perfusion pressure, whereas hypocapnia may reflect either ventilation-related cerebral vasoconstriction or reduced pulmonary perfusion during a low-flow state. We evaluated whether the time-weighted overlap of hypotension and hypocapnia was associated with adverse postoperative outcomes after major open intracranial surgery. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using INSPIRE version 1.4.2. Adults undergoing major open intracranial surgery were included if mean arterial pressure (MAP) and end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) had at least 80% synchronous coverage. Dual-hit cerebral hypoperfusion burden (DHCB) was defined as the proportion of synchronously valid monitoring time with simultaneous MAP <65 mmHg and EtCO2 < 30 mmHg. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital death, postoperative intensive care unit stay of at least 2 days, or prolonged postoperative hospitalization. Patient-clustered multivariable logistic regression simultaneously modeled hypotension-only, hypocapnia-only, and concurrent exposure burdens. The final cohort included 2,286 operations in 2,092 patients. Concurrent hypotension and hypocapnia occurred in 708 operations (31.0%), and the composite outcome occurred after 676 operations (29.6%). Each 5-percentage-point increase in DHCB was associated with higher odds of the composite outcome (adjusted odds ratio, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.10-1.28; P < 0.001), whereas hypotension-only and hypocapnia-only burdens were not independently associated with the outcome. Adding DHCB improved model fit but only minimally increased apparent discrimination (C-statistic, 0.764 to 0.767). Results remained consistent across progressively adjusted and sensitivity analyses. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed an overall association (P < 0.001) but no significant evidence of nonlinearity (P for nonlinearity = 0.143). The standardized risk increased from 27.3% at DHCB = 0% to 45.6% at DHCB = 30%, although estimates at higher burdens were less precise. Greater temporal overlap between intraoperative hypotension and hypocapnia was associated with adverse short-term postoperative outcomes beyond the corresponding non-overlapping exposure burdens. DHCB should be interpreted as a hypothesis-generating marker of concurrent physiological exposure rather than evidence of two independent causal insults, and requires external validation with neurologically specific outcomes before clinical application.

42886566.title: In-Simulation Versus Post-Simulation Debriefing in Medical Training: A Scoping Review and Theoretical Framework for Military Application.
42886566.abstract: Simulation-based medical training is important for readiness. Feedback and debriefing are important components of simulation that support learning. Debriefs for military training are traditionally conducted at the conclusion of training, but recent evidence in the civilian medical training literature suggests that in-simulation debriefing may provide benefits for skill acquisition. The purpose of this scoping review is to map the body of literature examining post-simulation and in-simulation debriefing, highlight trends in the literature, and identify research gaps. A scoping review of the literature was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute Scoping Review Methodology, searching PubMed, the Web of Science Core Collection, and gray literature. Studies were included if they evaluated simulation-based emergency medicine or critical care medical training with an in-simulation debriefing intervention compared to post-simulation debriefing, measured at least one learning or performance outcome, and included a randomization element. Studies were excluded if they lacked a comparison group, involved non-acute care, utilized solely device-generated feedback, or did not explicitly articulate in-simulation debriefing protocols. A total of 21 articles met inclusion criteria; none involved military populations. The majority of studies (90.5%) employed rapid cycle deliberate practice as the in-simulation debriefing method, and the most studied domain was cardiac arrest and resuscitation (57.1%). No studies reported performance or retention measures favoring post-simulation debriefing, and 77.8% of studies measuring time to intervention found significant improvements when in-simulation debriefing was utilized. Effect sizes were only reported in 14.3% of included studies. The majority of reviewed studies reported outcomes favoring in-simulation debriefing; no studies favored post-simulation debriefing for performance measures. Effective implementation of in-simulation debriefing in a military training context would require deliberate instructor development and standardized methods for aligning debriefing methods with the experience level of the target audience. Future research should examine the effects of in-simulation debriefing on tactical medical skill performance and the time to intervention in a military training context.

42882125.title: Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Acute Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock: Lessons from Contemporary Randomized Trials.
42882125.abstract: Background: Acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains associated with high mortality despite advances in revascularization, critical care, and temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Recent randomized trials have challenged the concept of routine device-based therapy and highlighted the importance of matching MCS strategy to shock phenotype, timing, and patient risk profile. Methods: We reviewed contemporary randomized clinical trials and prespecified or post hoc analyses evaluating temporary MCS strategies in adult patients with AMI-CS. PubMed was searched for English-language studies published from January 2021 through June 2026, focusing on intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), microaxial flow pumps, and venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO/ECLS). Outcomes of interest included mortality, hemodynamic recovery, end-organ outcomes, and device-related complications. Results: Recent randomized evidence demonstrates that no temporary MCS device provides universal benefit across the heterogeneous AMI-CS population. Routine IABP use has not been associated with improved survival and is now reserved for selected patients requiring modest circulatory support, bridge-to-decision strategies, or specific mechanical complications. The DanGer Shock trial provided the strongest contemporary randomized evidence supporting temporary MCS, demonstrating reduced 180-day mortality with routine Impella CP support in carefully selected patients with STEMI-related cardiogenic shock. However, this benefit was accompanied by increased major bleeding, limb ischemia, acute kidney injury, and renal replacement therapy. Prespecified secondary and exploratory post hoc analyses have generated hypotheses that treatment response may vary according to age, baseline hemodynamics, timing of support, and shock phenotype; however, these findings require prospective validation and should not be interpreted as established treatment-selection criteria. In contrast, ECLS-SHOCK, ECMO-CS, EURO SHOCK, and randomized meta-analytic data did not demonstrate a survival benefit for routine early VA-ECMO in broad AMI-CS populations and consistently identified higher rates of bleeding and vascular complications. Strategies for routine early left ventricular unloading during VA-ECMO have improved physiologic parameters but have not demonstrated a mortality benefit. Conclusions: Contemporary randomized trials have shifted the role of temporary MCS in AMI-CS from routine device deployment toward individualized, phenotype-guided therapy. Impella CP, as evaluated in the DanGer Shock trial, currently provides the strongest randomized survival signal but should be applied selectively in patients with predominantly left ventricular failure treated within experienced shock systems. VA-ECMO remains an important rescue option in carefully selected patients with refractory circulatory collapse, severe hypoxemia, cardiac arrest, or biventricular failure, although routine early use is not supported. Future research should focus on earlier shock phenotyping, physiology-guided device selection, complication reduction, and strategies that integrate mechanical support with recovery-focused care.

42965206.title: Inferior vena cava peak velocity versus collapsibility index to predict volume status in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding: A pilot study.
42965206.abstract: Patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) with hemorrhagic shock secondary to acute gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding represent a substantial proportion of the critically ill population. Accurate evaluation of intravascular volume status in these patients is crucial for guiding fluid resuscitation. However, the limitations of invasive methods and inferior vena cava (IVC) diameter/collapsibility measurements in assessing intravascular volume have been widely discussed in the literature. Despite their validation, noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring techniques remain underutilized in the ED. Therefore, the present study aimed to investigate the predictive value of IVC blood flow velocity measured by Doppler ultrasonography in intravascular volume assessment and to compare it with the IVC collapsibility index. Electrical velocity measurement was used as a surrogate marker of volume deficit. Eighteen patients presenting with a preliminary diagnosis of acute GI bleeding were included in the study. The study population consisted solely of patients with suspected hypovolemia; therefore, no normovolemic control group was included in the study. Demographic, vital, and laboratory data were recorded, along with IVC diameter, collapsibility, IVC peak velocity measured by continuous-wave Doppler, and noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring parameters at admission, at the 30th and 60th min, and immediately after completion of fluid replacement. All data were subjected to statistical analysis. A significant correlation was observed between initial IVC peak velocity and stroke volume variation at admission (P = 0.009). The measurement demonstrated a specificity of 100% and a sensitivity of 84%, although the confidence interval was wide due to the small number of patients without volume deficit. No statistically significant differences were detected at the other time points. This can be explained by the ongoing bleeding and the lack of a valid gold standard. Measurement of IVC peak velocity was found to be a significant predictor of hypovolemia, although it showed limited utility for volume monitoring. Furthermore, it demonstrated superior performance compared to IVC diameter and collapsibility measurements. However, the study does not evaluate its ability to distinguish hypovolemia from true normovolemia.

42963148.title: Management of Patients After Cardiac Arrest.
42963148.abstract: Cardiac arrest remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, although contemporary care now enables potential survival with good neurologic outcome. The core acute management goals for survivors of cardiac arrest are to provide organ support, sustain adequate hemodynamics, and evaluate the underlying cause of the cardiac arrest. In this article, the authors review the current state of knowledge and clinical intensive care unit practice recommendations for patients after cardiac arrest, particularly focusing on important areas of uncertainty, such as targeted temperature management, neuroprognostication, coronary evaluation, and hemodynamic targets.

42958792.title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Knowledge Among Respiratory Therapy and Anesthesia Technology Students in Jordan: A Cross-Sectional Study.
42958792.abstract: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) knowledge among future critical-care professionals is essential for improving survival after cardiac arrest. Evidence on CPR preparedness among respiratory therapy (RT) and anesthesia technology (AT) students in Jordan is limited. This study assessed CPR knowledge, willingness to perform CPR, and perceived motivators and barriers to CPR training. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among RT and AT students (n = 360) in Jordan. Eligible participants were second-year students and above. The questionnaire collected demographics, prior CPR training, a 10-item CPR knowledge test (score 0-10), and self-reported motivators and barriers. Descriptive statistics, χ2 tests, and t-tests were used. Of the 360 participants, 46.9% had received CPR training; the mean age was 20.4 years, and 69.7% were female. The overall mean knowledge score was 5.22 (SD 2.00). Knowledge did not differ by prior training (5.27 vs. 5.18; p = 0.696). Students with basic life support training scored higher than those with advanced training (5.27 vs. 3.50; p = 0.001). Recognition of the emergency number (90.6%) and chest-compression technique (66.9%) were the most correctly answered items, whereas compression depth (34.7%) and initial response steps (13.9%) showed the poorest knowledge. Almost all students (98.1%) were willing to attend CPR training. Key motivators were helping others (36.4%) and family cardiac disease (25.6%); barriers included lack of interest (34.2%), limited time (25.0%), and cost (19.4%). RT and AT students demonstrated moderate CPR knowledge but notable deficits in essential technical skills. High willingness to train supports integrating mandatory and recurrent CPR instruction into allied health curricula.

42838703.title: Chronic posthypoxic myoclonus: Lance-Adams syndrome.
42838703.abstract: Lance-Adams syndrome (LAS) is a rare condition described as chronic intentional myoclonus following prolonged hypoxia. With limited cases of the condition, no standardised diagnostic criteria, and features overlapping acute myoclonus status epilepticus (MSE), diagnosis and management are challenging.Our case is a man in his 20s, who was admitted to the intensive care unit following two in-hospital cardiac arrests. He consequently developed persistent generalised myoclonic seizures despite multiple antiepileptics and sedation.
