Neurosurgical patients are particularly vulnerable because of frequent exposure to invasive devices such as external ventricular drains (EVDs), central venous catheters, urinary catheters, and mechanical ventilation, combined with impaired neurological status and prolonged ICU stays. Although quality improvement (QI) strategies have been widely implemented across critical care settings, evidence specific to neurosurgical and neurocritical care populations remains fragmented. To systematically evaluate the effectiveness of QI interventions in reducing HAI incidence among neurosurgical and neurological ICU patients and to assess their impact on secondary outcomes including ICU length of stay, device utilization, and bundle compliance. A comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from January 2010 to May 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies for the primary evidence synthesis included randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, and observational cohort studies evaluating structured QI interventions for HAI prevention in neurosurgical or neurological ICU populations, or mixed ICU settings with extractable neurocritical care data. Systematic reviews identified during screening were retained for contextual interpretation and reference screening but were excluded from the primary evidence synthesis to avoid duplication of overlapping primary data. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, Cochrane RoB 2, and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale according to study design. Seventeen primary studies from 14 countries met eligibility criteria and were included in the primary narrative synthesis. Three systematic reviews were retained for contextual interpretation. Structured QI interventions consistently reduced device-associated infection rates across studies. The strongest evidence was observed for EVD-specific care bundles, with EVD-related infection rates decreasing from 14.35 to 3.21 per 1,000 catheter-days following bundle implementation, and one study reporting 20 consecutive infection-free months after interprofessional bundle adoption. Device-associated infection prevention bundles also demonstrated clinically meaningful reductions, including VAP rates decreasing from 68.2 to 47.4 per 1,000 ventilator-days and CAUTI rates from 24.9 to 13.4 per 1,000 catheter-days following structured educational interventions. CLABSI rates declined substantially following standardized central venous catheter bundle implementation, reaching zero in one study with sustained monitoring. Risk of bias was predominantly low to moderate across included primary studies. Structured QI interventions, particularly EVD-specific care bundles, device-associated infection prevention protocols, and staff education programs with compliance monitoring, consistently reduce HAI incidence in neurosurgical and neurological ICU settings. Although the evidence base is predominantly non-randomized, findings are directionally consistent across diverse healthcare systems and institutional contexts. Universal adoption of evidence-based infection prevention frameworks in neurocritical care is strongly supported.

42919194.title: Antibiotic de-escalation in severe intra-abdominal infections: a single-center retrospective cohort study on safety and prognostic factors.
42919194.abstract: Antibiotic de-escalation is a key antimicrobial stewardship strategy aimed at reducing the ecological and adverse effects of broad-spectrum therapy without compromising efficacy. However, its real-world safety and impact on clinical outcomes in patients with severe intra-abdominal infections (IAIs) remain underexplored. A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted from June 2022 to June 2025. Adults with severe IAIs who received initial broad-spectrum antibiotics and achieved source control within 48 h were included. Patients were stratified into de-escalation and non-de-escalation groups on the basis of the antibiotic management strategy. Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcome was clinical cure at 30 days. Secondary outcomes included 28-day mortality, lengths of ICU and hospital stay, antibiotic duration, and the incidence of secondary infections and Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). Among 405 eligible patients, 212 were matched (106 per group). The de-escalation group had a significantly higher clinical cure rate (79.8% vs. 63.5%; OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.29-3.89; P = 0.004) and lower 28-day mortality (9.6% vs. 21.2%; OR 0.40, 95% CI 0.18-0.88; P = 0.02). De-escalation was also associated with shorter ICU and hospital stays, reduced antibiotic duration, and fewer secondary infections. Multivariable analysis confirmed de-escalation (aOR 2.71, 95% CI 1.48-4.97) and adequate source control (aOR 3.52, 95% CI 1.81-6.85) as independent predictors of clinical cure. Antibiotic de-escalation following adequate source control is associated with improved clinical outcomes and reduced mortality in severe IAIs without increasing the risk of complications. These findings support its integration into antimicrobial stewardship programs for this high-risk population. Not applicable.

42913935.title: A nomogram for predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with coagulase-negative staphylococcus bloodstream infections.
42913935.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
42913935.abstract: Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) have emerged as significant pathogens in bloodstream infections (BSIs). Currently, no validated models exist for specifically predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with CoNS-BSIs. A retrospective study was conducted on adult patients with CoNS-BSIs using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-III) database. Participants were randomly allocated into a training set (n = 366) and a validation set (n = 157). Demographic characteristics, severity scores, comorbidities and laboratory examinations from the first 24 h of ICU admission were analyzed. The optimal predictive variables for establishing a nomogram were screened through univariate, multivariate logistic regression and stepwise regression analyses. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA) and clinical impact curve (CIC). Among 523 patients enrolled, the overall in-hospital mortality was 22.9%. Four independent predictors were incorporated into the nomogram: age (OR = 1.04), anion gap (AG: OR = 1.11), total bilirubin (TBil: OR = 1.26) and respiratory failure (OR = 1.97). The area under the curve (AUC) values in the training set and validation set were 0.758 and 0.823, respectively. The P-values of the calibration curve in two sets were 0.258 and 0.432. The DCA curves were above the two extreme curves. The CIC analysis revealed a high concordance between predicted high-risk cases and observed clinical events when the risk threshold exceeded 60%. Age, AG, TBil and respiratory failure were independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality among patients with CoNS-BSIs. The nomogram based on these four parameters demonstrated good performance and clinical utility for risk assessment.

42913228.title: Clinical factors associated with noninvasive ventilation-associated pneumonia in acute respiratory failure: a prospective cohort study.
42913228.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
42913228.abstract: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is preferred to invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) as treatment for acute respiratory failure due to its lower complication rate, but NIV may still be associated with serious complications such as nosocomial pneumonia. However, risk factors associated with NIV-associated pneumonia remain insufficiently characterized. To investigate factors associated with NIV-associated pneumonia in patients treated with NIV for acute respiratory failure in a respiratory intensive care unit. In this prospective cohort study, we followed adult patients who were admitted to a respiratory intensive care unit in a tertiary hospital for acute respiratory failure. None of the patients had pneumonia on admission. All patients were treated with NIV and monitored daily for the development of nosocomial pneumonia, which was defined using standardized criteria. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors independently associated with NIV-associated pneumonia. Among 191 eligible patients admitted between March 2023 and May 2024, 84 developed NIV-associated pneumonia. Age was not independently associated with pneumonia development. In multivariable analysis, poor oral hygiene, poor secretion control, and longer NIV duration were independently associated with NIV-associated pneumonia. Patients who developed pneumonia also had longer ICU stay and higher rates of antibiotic modification. In patients receiving NIV for acute respiratory failure, poor oral hygiene, poor secretion control, and prolonged NIV exposure were independently associated with NIV-associated pneumonia, whereas chronological age, sepsis, and frailty were not. These findings suggest that clinical factors related to bedside care and NIV exposure may be more relevant to pneumonia development than age alone.

42912114.title: Analysis of factors associated with death in critically ill patients with COVID-19.
42912114.abstract: to assess the factors associated with death in critically ill COVID-19 patients. retrospective cohort of critically ill patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit and infected with SARS-CoV-2, followed for 30 days, ≥ 18 years old, with a positive nasopharyngeal RT-PCR test for SARS-CoV-2. Descriptive analysis regarding the outcome, chi-square test, and backward stepwise multiple logistic regression model were used to describe predictor variables of sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. 715 patients were analyzed, of whom 70.8% (n=507) died and 29.1% (n=209) survived. In the multivariate analysis, death outcome dependent variables, such as age range of 61-80 years, > 80 years, invasive mechanical ventilation, dialysis, corticosteroids, vancomycin, platelets after 24 hours, and other antibiotics, were identified as risk factors, and the ROC curve (AUC=0.904) predicted the proposed model. the multivariate model showed good discriminatory capacity, identifying independent factors associated with death in critically ill COVID-19 patients.

42912112.title: Assessment of cleaning and disinfection of Intensive Care Unit beds: quality management with Lean.
42912112.abstract: to analyze, using Lean Healthcare tools, the terminal hygiene process in Intensive Care Unit beds and to propose improvements for its standardization. a cross-sectional study was conducted at a university hospital in Rio de Janeiro between September 2023 and February 2024, observing ten terminal hygiene processes performed by five professionals. VSM, CRT Diagram, GUT Matrix, Prioritization Matrix, and 5W2H tools were used. Analysis considered scope, technical adherence, execution time, surface completeness, and the presence of fluorescent residues. failure to use protective equipment and disinfectant was identified in 100% of procedures, along with a lack of technical standards and movement patterns. Only 70% of processes were completed, and 33% of surfaces were free of residue. despite institutional guidelines, hygiene was not standardized. Lean tools allowed for the identification of root causes and the development of improvement strategies focused on the real existing problems.

42912019.title: Statistical analysis plan for a stepped-wedge cluster randomized clinical trial for the evaluation of the clinical impact of different telemedicine practices in intensive care units - TELESCOPE 2 trial.
42912019.abstract: The optimal model for delivering Tele-ICU is still to be determined. In the TELE-critical Care verSus usual Care on ICU Performance (TELESCOPE) trial, implementing medical-led daily multidisciplinary rounds did not show evidence of improved clinical outcomes. The TELESCOPE 2 trial was therefore designed to evaluate whether expanding this model to include a structured multidisciplinary care bundle, along with a formalized quality and safety management framework, would translate process improvements into measurable patient-centered outcome benefits. To evaluate whether a structured Tele-ICU intervention, comprising intensivist-led daily multidisciplinary rounds, a multidisciplinary care bundle (nursing, physical therapy, pharmacy), and a quality and safety management package, can reduce intensive care unit length of stay in Brazilian public intensive care units. TELESCOPE 2 is a multicenter, open-label, stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial including 25 intensive care units in Brazil from January 2024 to January 2026. Intensive care units are randomized to five sequences, receiving the intervention at staggered times. All adult patients admitted to participating units are eligible, except those admitted for non-medical reasons or those previously included in the study. The multifaceted telemedicine intervention comprises: i) daily multidisciplinary rounds led by board-certified intensivists; ii) coordinated care by a multidisciplinary team; and iii) a management strategy focused on quality improvement and patient safety. The primary outcome is intensive care unit length of stay. Secondary outcomes include clinical endpoints (mortality, ventilator-free days at 28 days, and ventilator-associated events), process-of-care indicators (mobilization, head-of-bed elevation, and sedation management), and unit-level organizational outcomes. We describe the statistical analysis plan for the TELESCOPE 2 trial, finalized prior to database lock. This pre-specified approach mitigates analysis bias and ensures the transparency and robustness of the reported results.

42909495.title: Health economic evaluation of polytrauma treatment in the current aG-DRG system - Results of a Level I Trauma Center.
42909495.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
42909495.abstract: Resource-intensive polytrauma care is associated with high treatment and readiness costs and poses a financial challenge for hospitals. The aim of this retrospective single-center study of the years 2020 to 2022 was to analyze polytrauma reimbursements and costs. Based on billing and clinical data of 201 polytrauma cases from a German University Hospital and Level I Trauma Center, revenues and costs of the eleven MDC 21 A polytrauma DRGs were analyzed. Ratios of the revenue in relation to LOS, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs as well as personnel costs were calculated. Contribution margins were determined as an upper-bound estimate. DRG reimbursement was highest for the most severely injured patients (50,852 €, DRG W36Z). It was lowest for patients who died within five days (2,214 €, DRG W60Z) or without surgeries (4,056 €, DRG W61B). The contribution margin was also highest for the most severely injured patients (52,775 €, DRG W36Z). Revenues in relation to ICU LOS (3,455 €/day, DRG W36Z) and ventilation time (238 €/hour, DRG W01B) were lowest for the most severe polytraumas. Regarding OR time and implant costs, reimbursement was lowest for injuries of the spine, pelvis and extremities with 62 €/min (DRG W02B) and 5 €/€ (DRG W02A). Treatment of polytrauma patients with long ICU stay, extended mechanical ventilation and multiple injuries of the extremities, pelvis and spine is not adequately reflected by the current per-case reimbursement in relation to the resources used (ICU days, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs).

42908088.title: Learning Curve of Robotic Atrial Septal Defect Repair: A Multidimensional CUSUM Analysis of 284 Consecutive Cases.
42908088.journal: The international journal of medical robotics + computer assisted surgery : MRCAS
42908088.abstract: To characterise the learning curve of robotic atrial septal defect (ASD) repair using a multidimensional cumulative sum (CUSUM) framework. In this retrospective study, 284 consecutive adult patients undergoing robotic ASD repair were analysed. CUSUM analysis was applied to operative time, cardiopulmonary bypass time, cross-clamp time, intensive care unit (ICU) stay, and hospital stay. Learning phases were identified according to inflection points of the CUSUM curves. Four distinct learning phases were observed. Technical proficiency was achieved at Case 158, marked by significant reductions in operative (186.8 ± 43.3 vs. 133.7 ± 27.7 min), bypass, and cross-clamp times (p < 0.001). ICU stay and transfusion requirements progressively declined, while mortality remained low across all phases. Notably, postoperative care optimisation lagged behind technical mastery. Multidimensional CUSUM analysis provides an objective, performance-based assessment of robotic ASD learning. Competency acquisition required substantial case volume, underscoring the need for structured training and longitudinal performance monitoring in robotic cardiac surgery.

42907946.title: Blood eosinophil count and intensive care unit admission in patients hospitalized for acute exacerbation of COPD: a retrospective cohort study.
42907946.abstract: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are major clinical events associated with hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and increased mortality. Blood eosinophil count has emerged as a potential inflammatory biomarker in COPD; however, its role in predicting ICU requirement among hospitalized patients remains unclear. This retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≥ 40 years hospitalized with acute COPD exacerbation at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital between 2020 and 2024. COPD diagnosis was based on Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) criteria. Blood eosinophil counts measured within the first 60 min of presentation to the emergency department were categorized as < 150 cells/µL, 150-299 cells/µL, and ≥ 300 cells/µL. ICU admission was defined as the primary outcome. Competing risk analysis using the Fine-Gray model was performed, with death as a competing event. A total of 385 patients were included. Eosinophil groups were not significantly associated with ICU requirement. Clinical variables significantly associated with ICU admission included GOLD group, GOLD grade, modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea score, long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT), nebulizer and non-invasive mechanical ventilation (NIMV) use, and need for NIMV at admission. In Fine-Gray models, GOLD group E was independently associated with increased ICU admission risk compared with GOLD A (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] = 3.35, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.57-7.15; p = 0.002), whereas eosinophil levels were not. In hospitalized patients with acute COPD exacerbations, blood eosinophil count - regardless of the threshold applied - was not independently associated with ICU admission after adjustment for disease severity and competing risks. GOLD group E emerged as the strongest independent predictor of ICU requirement in the same model. These findings suggest that clinical severity assessment, rather than eosinophil-based stratification, should guide risk assessment for ICU admission in this population. Not applicable.

42903095.title: Early hemoglobin trajectories and short-term mortality in ICU patients with traumatic brain injury: development in MIMIC-IV and external assessment in eICU-CRD.
42903095.abstract: Hemoglobin (Hb) changes dynamically after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but the prognostic relevance of distinct longitudinal patterns and their added value beyond early Hb remain uncertain. We characterized early Hb trajectories in ICU patients with TBI and examined associations with mortality after a 120-h landmark. MIMIC-IV was used for model development and multicenter eICU-CRD for external assessment. Daily median Hb values across five 24-h windows were modeled using a latent class linear mixed model. The three-class MIMIC-IV model was frozen before transport to eICU. Cox models evaluated mortality from 120 h through ICU day 28, with sensitivity analyses addressing selection, landmark attrition, simpler Hb summaries, classification uncertainty, PRBC exposure, missingness, and nonproportional hazards. In MIMIC-IV, 2,466 patients entered trajectory analysis and 2,409 entered post-landmark analysis. Three trajectories were identified: relatively high and stable, rapidly declining, and persistently low Hb. In fully adjusted models, rapidly declining (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.18-2.57) and persistently low Hb (HR 1.57, 95% CI 1.19-2.08) were associated with higher mortality. In eICU, 2,097 patients were classified and 1,557 entered outcome analysis; persistently low Hb remained associated with mortality (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.03-2.43), whereas the rapidly declining association was less precise (HR 1.24, 95% CI 0.80-1.92). Adding trajectory class to the MIMIC-IV clinical model increased the C-index from 0.786 to 0.792. After adjustment for first-day Hb, the rapidly declining trajectory remained associated with mortality (HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.20-2.62), whereas the persistently low association attenuated (HR 1.27, 95% CI 0.83-1.93). Independent three-class refitting in eICU did not recover the same latent-class structure (ARI 0.169). Early Hb trajectories after TBI showed distinct prognostic associations. Persistently low Hb had the most consistent transported association but was attenuated after first-day Hb adjustment; rapid decline retained an association in MIMIC-IV but had limited external support. Incremental discrimination was modest. These patterns should be interpreted as treatment-embedded clinical courses rather than fixed biological phenotypes or evidence for trajectory-specific transfusion thresholds.

42902574.title: Diagnostic Performance of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema Score for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome-Post Hoc Analysis of the "Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis" Study.
42902574.abstract: To determine the diagnostic accuracy of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema (RALE) score for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and its interobserver reliability. Post hoc analysis of a prospective observational cohort study. ICUs at Vanderbilt University Medical Center participating in the Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis study. Adult patients receiving invasive ventilation for at least two consecutive days, with chest radiographs available on the first 2 ICU days. None. Chest radiographs from the first 2 ICU days were scored independently by at least two experienced raters; scores were averaged per radiograph, and the highest averaged score from ICU day 1 or 2 was selected for analysis. The primary outcome was ARDS according to the Berlin definition during the first 2 ICU days. Of 236 patients, 92 (39%) had ARDS. The median RALE score was higher in patients with ARDS than in those without (29.5 [22.2-34.5] vs. 12.2 [7.5-17.8]; p < 0.01). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.93 (95% CI, 0.90-0.96). At the optimal cutoff of 20, sensitivity was 85%, specificity 83%, positive predictive value 76%, and negative predictive value 90%. Interobserver reliability was high, with pairwise intraclass correlation coefficients ranging from 0.81 to 0.87. In patients invasively ventilated for at least 2 days, the RALE score demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy for ARDS at a cutoff of 20, together with high interobserver reliability, supporting its potential role as a standardized radiographic tool in the diagnosis of ARDS.

42902313.title: Geographic differences in outcomes after emergency surgery in nonagenarians and centenarians admitted to intensive care in Australia: a population-based study.
42902313.abstract: Nonagenarian and centenarian patients increasingly undergo emergency surgery with subsequent intensive care unit (ICU) admission, but it remains unclear whether geographic disparities in outcomes arise during the index hospitalization or emerge after discharge in universal health systems. We conducted a national, population-based retrospective cohort study using linked data from the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society (ANZICS) Adult Patient Database and the Australian National Death Index. We included all nonagenarian and centenarian patients admitted to Australian ICUs after emergency surgery between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2024. Geographic residence on ICU admission was classified with the Modified Monash Model as metropolitan (MMM1) or regional/remote (MMM2-7). Outcomes were ICU mortality, in-hospital mortality, and all-cause post-discharge mortality at 5 years among patients discharged alive. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to examine associations between geographic residence and post-discharge mortality, with adjustment for age, sex, Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) III score, Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, major chronic comorbidities, and hospital type. Among 4,887 patients admitted to ICUs after emergency surgery, ICU and hospital mortality did not differ meaningfully by geographic residence. In contrast, among patients discharged alive, regional or remote residence was independently associated with higher post-discharge mortality at 5 years (adjusted HR, 1.133, 95% CI 1.027-1.250, p = 0.013) compared with metropolitan residence. Survival curves diverged after hospital discharge and remained separated throughout follow-up. In a secondary cohort of 7,896 patients undergoing elective surgery, geographic residence was not associated with ICU, in-hospital, or post-discharge mortality. Among nonagenarian and centenarian patients admitted to ICUs after emergency surgery, geographic residence was not associated with mortality during the index hospitalization but was independently associated with higher long-term mortality after discharge. While no differences were observed during the acute care episode, patients residing in regional or remote areas experienced lower post-discharge survival compared with those living in metropolitan areas. These findings highlight potential geographic variation in long-term outcomes and support further investigation into factors influencing post-discharge care and survival among the oldest surgical patients.

42897566.title: Decision volume and temporal workload structure as dissociable correlates of fatigue and mood in intensive care physicians: a real-time observational study.
42897566.abstract: Intensive care physicians make hundreds of decisions per shift under sustained cognitive and emotional demands. Decision fatigue, the tendency towards less effortful choices as cumulative decision load increases, may affect clinician wellbeing and decision processes. However, the associations of decision volume and temporal workload structure with within-shift fatigue and mood in intensive care unit (ICU) physicians remain unclear. This study explored whether decision volume and temporal clustering show distinct associations with fatigue, sleepiness, mood, and post-shift decision responses. Five physicians (two residents, three consultants) at a surgical ICU of a German university hospital were shadowed during 38 twelve-hour shifts (456 hours) between October and December 2025. Clinical decisions were classified by severity using a study-specific, non-validated Decision Severity Score. Because recruitment was feasibility-based and involved only five physicians, all analyses were considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Psychometric assessments of decision fatigue, sleepiness, and mood (Decision Fatigue Scale, Karolinska Sleepiness Scale, Profile of Mood States - Short Form) were administered at morning, midday, and shift end. Following each shift, physicians completed a standardised scenario task requiring three binary treatment decisions. Temporal workload structure was quantified using the burstiness metric; shifts were classified into four types by median split of decision density and burstiness (quiet-smooth, quiet-clustered, busy-smooth, busy-clustered). Linear and binomial mixed-effects models with physician as random intercept were used throughout. Across 17,953 recorded decisions (median 474 per shift; range 366-589), a higher mean decision rate was associated with greater end-of-shift decision fatigue: an increase of 0.5 decisions per 5-minute interval corresponded to a 2.1-point higher decision-fatigue score (95 % CI 0.6 to 3.6). Higher burstiness was associated with less mood disturbance, with a 0.10 increase in burstiness corresponding to a 6.3-point lower mood score (95% CI -10.2 to -2.3). Averaged across all shifts, changes between morning and evening were small and not statistically significant for any of the three scores. Within-shift trajectories differed by shift type, however, with mood disturbance increasing over the shift in quiet-smooth shifts only, a difference already apparent at midday. Quiet-smooth shifts, the least objectively demanding, showed the least favourable psychometric values. Response certainty in the post-shift scenario task was lower after shifts with more task interruptions, with each ten additional interruptions corresponding to a 0.29-point lower certainty score (p = 0.012), whilst a descriptive trend towards more conservative scenario responses was observed in busy-clustered shifts (odds ratio 2.25, p = 0.555). Decision volume and temporal workload structure showed different associations with psychometric outcomes: higher decision rates were associated with greater end-of-shift decision fatigue, whereas greater temporal clustering was associated with lower mood disturbance, already apparent from midday onwards. That more quiet, uniformly paced shifts showed the least favourable psychometric values suggests that reducing decision volume alone may not improve physician wellbeing; this observation requires replication. Mitigation strategies may therefore need to extend beyond reducing decision volume to protecting concentrated, meaningful clinical activity and minimising hindrance stressors such as interruptions. Future multicentre studies should determine whether these associations are reproducible and whether temporal workload structure is related to objective decision quality or patient-safety outcomes. German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS00037564. Registered 27th August 2025.

42897507.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of Candida auris in a tertiary intensive care unit: a four-year retrospective case series.
42897507.abstract: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant yeast associated with healthcare-associated transmission and severe outcomes in intensive care settings. Clinical ICU-based cohort data from Türkiye remain limited. We conducted a single-center retrospective case series in a tertiary adult intensive care unit in Türkiye, including patients with C. auris isolated from blood and/or urine cultures between January 1, 2021, and January 1, 2025. Species identification was performed by matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS). Antifungal susceptibility testing (AST) for selected isolates was conducted using the Sensititre™ YeastOne™ colorimetric microdilution system. Continuous variables were presented as mean ± standard deviation or median (minimum-maximum) according to distribution, whereas categorical variables were presented as frequencies and percentages. Comparative statistical analyses were not performed because of the descriptive case-series design and limited sample size. Among 5,778 ICU patients evaluated during the study period, C. auris was identified in 36 patients. No cases were detected in 2021-2022; all cases occurred between September 18, 2023, and December 23, 2024, representing 2.37% of 1,517 ICU admissions during that interval. Isolation was most frequent in urine cultures (77.8%), followed by blood cultures (33.3%), with simultaneous urine and blood positivity in 11.1% of patients. The mean length of hospitalization before the first C. auris-positive culture was 44.9 days. All patients had urinary and central venous catheters and had received broad-spectrum antibiotics before C. auris detection. In the preceding month, MDR bacterial bloodstream infections were identified in 16 patients. AST data were available for four blood culture isolates from three patients; fluconazole MIC values were > 256 µg/mL in all tested isolates, whereas micafungin showed the lowest arithmetic mean MIC value (0.188 µg/mL). C. auris emerged in our ICU after 2023 and was mainly detected in patients with prolonged hospitalization, invasive devices, broad-spectrum antimicrobial exposure, and frequent MDR bacterial co-occurrence. These single-center data from Türkiye highlight the importance of reliable species-level identification, infection control awareness, and antimicrobial stewardship. Larger multicenter prospective studies using standardized surveillance and reference-method-based AST protocols are needed to better define transmission dynamics, resistance patterns, and clinical outcomes.

42888589.title: Systemic immune-inflammation index and in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients with acute asthma exacerbation: A retrospective cohort study.
42888589.abstract: The prognostic value of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in critically ill patients with acute asthma exacerbations remains unclear. This study examined the association between SII and in-hospital mortality. We performed a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV (v3.1) database, including adult critically ill patients with asthma exacerbations. SII was calculated from laboratory values obtained during the peri-intensive care unit admission period. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Associations were assessed using restricted cubic spline and Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for confounders. A total of 575 patients were included, with an overall in-hospital mortality of 6.6%. Mortality rates differed significantly across SII tertiles and were highest in tertile 3 (11.5%), compared with tertile 2 (3.6%) and tertile 1 (4.7%) (P = .003). In Cox proportional hazards models, compared with tertile 2, patients in tertile 3 had a significantly increased risk of in-hospital mortality (unadjusted hazard ratio [HR] 2.88, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.21-6.83, P = .016; adjusted HR 2.82, 95% CI 1.12-7.10, P = .027), whereas no significant difference was observed for tertile 1. Restricted cubic spline analysis based on natural logarithm-transformed (ln-SII) demonstrated a significant nonlinear association with in-hospital mortality (P for nonlinearity < .001), with risk increasing markedly at higher ln-SII levels. Elevated SII was associated with increased in-hospital mortality and may serve as a simple prognostic marker in critically ill asthma exacerbations.

42888540.title: Impact of a zero-visitation policy on healthcare-associated infections in a non-COVID intensive care unit: A retrospective cohort study.
42888540.abstract: The impact of visitor restrictions in intensive care units (ICUs) during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic on healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remains unclear. This study aimed to compare HAI rates between the pre-pandemic restricted-visitation period and the pandemic zero-visitation period in a non-COVID tertiary ICU. This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients admitted to the Anesthesiology and Reanimation ICU of the Duzce University Health Practice and Research Center between March 14, 2019, and March 13, 2021. Patients admitted during the pre-pandemic restricted-visitation period were assigned to Group 19 -20, whereas those admitted during the pandemic zero-visitation period were assigned to Group 20-21. Patients with an ICU stay of < 48 hours, infection at admission, or infection developing within the first 48 hours were excluded. The primary outcome was HAI incidence. Secondary outcomes included the standardized infection ratio, cumulative attributable difference, inflammatory markers, and microbiological findings. A total of 933 patients were screened, and 206 patients met the inclusion criteria (Group 20-21, n = 115; Group 19-20, n = 91). In the patient-based analysis, the HAI rate was significantly lower in Group 20-21 than in Group 19-20 (6.1% vs 22.0%, P < .001). Similar findings were observed in the episode-based analysis (10.4% vs 33.0%, P < .001). The time to infection onset was significantly longer in Group 20-21 (P = .003). Procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, and lactate levels were significantly lower during the zero-visitation period. The standardized infection ratio for ventilator-associated pneumonia was significantly lower in Group 20-21 (P = .02). A marked reduction in the number of Acinetobacter spp. isolates was also observed during the pandemic. A zero-visitation policy in a non-COVID tertiary ICU was associated with lower HAI rates. The consistency of the surveillance indicators, inflammatory markers, and microbiological findings supports the observed association. However, these findings should not be attributed solely to visitor restrictions and should be interpreted in the context of multiple infection control measures implemented during the pandemic.

42888246.title: ICU-acquired pneumonia beyond pathogen detection.
42888246.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired pneumonia is often treated as a binary diagnosis, although clinical deterioration, imaging and microbial detection describe different aspects of disease. This Perspective proposes an explicit, graded and revisable assessment of whether a detected organism plausibly causes the current lung injury. The framework encompasses pneumonia arising during ventilation, pneumonia that precedes intubation and pneumonia in non-ventilated ICU patients. It places molecular results within clinical, anatomical, microbiological and host context and uses formal reassessment at 48-72 hours to guide treatment continuation, narrowing or discontinuation.

42886955.title: [Predictors of mortality and post-discharge quality of life in critically ill cancer patients].
42886955.abstract: The number of patients with cancer requiring intensive care is increasing. Critical illness and post-intensive care unit (ICU) syndrome may impair post-discharge recovery and quality of life. This study aimed to analyze ICU mortality, identify associated prognostic factors, and evaluate health-related quality of life after discharge in critically ill cancer patients. A prospective, observational, single-center cohort study was conducted including adults with oncologic disease admitted to a mixed ICU of a public hospital between 2021 and 2022. Clinical characteristics, illness severity, organ support, complications, and therapeutic adequacy were recorded. Quality of life was assessed at hospital discharge and at three months using the EQ-5D-3L instrument. Bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed. A total of 204 patients with cancer were included. ICU mortality was 41.7%, and in-hospital mortality reached 53.4%. Independent predictors of ICU mortality were hospital length of stay before ICU admission, invasive mechanical ventilation, septic shock, higher SAPS II scores, and COVID-19 at admission. All EQ-5D-3L dimensions were impaired at discharge; at three months, only mobility and self-care improved. A substantial proportion of survivors did not resume oncologic therapy. Mortality was primarily driven by critical illness severity and the impact of COVID-19. Partial recovery of quality of life and difficulties in resuming cancer-directed treatment highlight the need to reinforce post-ICU follow-up and targeted rehabilitation in this vulnerable population.

42886953.title: [Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on percutaneous tracheostomy practice: an eight-year analysis in an intensive care unit].
42886953.abstract: Percutaneous tracheostomy (PcT) is a common procedure in intensive care units, particularly among patients requiring prolonged mechanical ventilation. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially modified airway management practices, although evidence characterizing these changes in Latin American settings remains limited. This observational, retrospective study included adult patients who underwent PcT in the intensive care unit of a tertiary hospital between 2014 and 2021. Clinical characteristics and temporal trends were analyzed comparing the pre-pandemic period (2014-2019) and the pandemic period (2020-2021). A total of 398 PcT were performed during the study period. The annual procedural volume increased by 106% during the pandemic period compared with the pre-pandemic period (81.5 vs. 39.2 procedures/year). During the pandemic period, COVID-19 emerged as the leading cause of invasive mechanical ventilation among patients undergoing PcT, accounting for 75.5% of cases in 2021 (p<0.001). The duration of mechanical ventilation prior to tracheostomy was longer during the pandemic period, with significant differences observed between 2019 and 2020 (p=0.028). The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with an increased volume of PcT and a relevant etiological shift among critically ill patients undergoing this procedure. These findings highlight the need to adapt airway management and respiratory rehabilitation protocols during public health emergencies.

42885891.title: Intensive Care Unit Patients' Perspectives and Experiences in Using Virtual Reality Technology: A Qualitative Meta-Synthesis.
42885891.abstract: As Intensive Care Unit (ICU) survival improves, attention has shifted towards patients' psychological well-being and recovery. Although Virtual Reality (VR) is increasingly used in critical care, patients' experiences of VR interventions have not been comprehensively synthesised. To synthesise qualitative and mixed-methods evidence regarding ICU patients' perceptions, experiences and implementation-related considerations associated with VR interventions. A qualitative systematic review and thematic synthesis following Thomas and Harden's three-stage approach was conducted. Eight databases were searched from inception to September 2025. Studies employing qualitative methods or components of mixed methods exploring ICU patients' firsthand VR experiences were included. Methodological quality was appraised using the JBI checklist. Eight studies involving 247 participants were included. Four analytical themes were synthesised: (A) VR as a restorative escape, (B) VR as a route from passive endurance to active participation, (C) Patient readiness and personal preference shape VR engagement, and (D) VR as a co-produced intervention requiring contextual and relational adaptation. ICU patients perceived VR as a valuable tool that provided restorative escape and enabled active recovery, yet multiple barriers shaped its feasibility. Implementation should consider comfortable devices, customisable content and staff training. These findings inform patient-centred VR design in the ICU. VR offers a non-pharmacological approach that may support patient well-being and recovery during an ICU stay. It can provide meaningful focus and relief from distress, while encouraging engagement with rehabilitation. Nurses play a key role in facilitating sessions and assessing patient readiness. Implementation may be enhanced by comfortable, bed-compatible devices, customisable content and staff training. While not all patients may be suitable candidates, VR appears generally acceptable and could be integrated into individualised care plans. The review protocol had been registered in PROSPERO (International prospective register of systematic reviews). The registration number is CRD420251074650.

42885870.title: The Role of Family Needs in Emotional Distress Among Next of Kin of Critically Ill Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
42885870.abstract: Next of kin of critically ill patients frequently experience distress. Although family needs have been associated with psychological outcomes, their potential role as a pathway linking clinical and relational factors to emotional distress remains poorly understood. To examine whether family needs mediate the relationships between ventilatory support, relationship to the patient and emotional distress among the next of kin of critically ill patients. A cross-sectional study was conducted in an adult Intensive Care Unit in Portugal between September 2024 and February 2025. Emotional distress was assessed using the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scales-21 and family needs using the Family Needs Inventory in the Intensive Care Unit. Mediation analysis was performed using maximum likelihood estimation with bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals (5000 resamples). The study followed the A Guideline for Reporting Mediation Analyses (AGReMA) Statement. Data from 130 critically ill patient-next of kin dyads were analysed. Next of kin of patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation and those with closer relational proximity (spouses and sons/daughters) reported significantly higher emotional distress (p < 0.001). Family needs statistically mediated the relationship between ventilatory support and emotional distress (β = 2.386, p = 0.006), and between the relationship to the patient and emotional distress (β = 2.384, p = 0.012). Family needs were a significant predictor of emotional distress (β = 0.232, p < 0.001). The model explained 36.5% of the variance in emotional distress. Emotional distress among next of kin of critically ill patients was associated with clinical and relational factors. Family needs were identified as a significant mediating factor in these relationships, suggesting that they may represent an explanatory pathway linking critical illness experiences to psychological distress. Systematic assessment of family needs may help identify relatives at greater risk of emotional distress. Structured communication, emotional support and family involvement may help improve family-centred care in intensive care settings.

42884252.title: A Wearable Morphic Sensor for Unobtrusive Heart Rate and Respiratory Rate Monitoring in ICU Patients: A Pilot Validation Study.
42884252.abstract: This pilot study evaluated the real-world accuracy of a novel wearable morphic sensor system for unobtrusive, continuous heart rate (HR) and respiratory rate (RR) monitoring in critically ill patients within an intensive care unit (ICU). A hybrid piezoresistive/piezoelectric disk-shaped sensor was placed on patients' backs to capture cardiorespiratory activity via forcecardiographic principles. Data were acquired from 15 ICU patients using a custom wireless recorder. The piezoelectric channel was processed using discrete wavelet transform and an adaptive peak detection algorithm. Derived HR and RR were compared against reference measurements from clinical patient monitors and a ventilator. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -0.39 ± 1.99 beats per minute for HR and 0.06 ± 0.90 breaths per minute for RR. Linear regression revealed strong correlation with clinical monitors (HR R-squared = 0.982; RR R-squared = 0.966). The device's RR performance matched the agreement between two independent clinical reference devices. The proposed system met the pre-specified bias and standard deviation criteria for HR and RR monitoring in bed-bound ICU patients. Its skin-adhesive-free design enables unobtrusive, continuous vital sign surveillance without direct skin contact. These findings support ICU monitoring. Step-down ward and ambulatory applications remain to be validated in future studies.

42881501.title: Outcomes of Healthcare-Associated Infections in Respiratory Intensive Care Unit.
42881501.journal: Journal of Nepal Health Research Council
42881501.abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are the major cause of morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, microbiological profile, resistance patterns, risk factors, and outcomes of HAIs in a respiratory ICU (RICU) of a tertiary care hospital in Nepal. A prospective observational study was conducted in RICU. HAIs were diagnosed according to the CDC criteria. Descriptive statistics were reported as mean (SD) and frequencies. Unpaired t-tests, chi-square tests were used for comparisons, and multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the risk factors. Among 121 ICU admissions, 42 patients developed 50 episodes of HAI, yielding a prevalence of 34.7%. Ventilator-associated pneumonia was the most common HAIs. The most frequently isolated organisms were Acinetobacter baumannii in 42.0% and Klebsiella pneumonia in 18.0%. Both were resistance to Ceftriaxone. Resistance to Piperacillin-tazobactam were 85.8% and 77.8% and to carbapenems were 92% and 90% respectively. Tigecycline resistance was seen in 20% of Acinetobacter isolates and none of the Klebsiella isolates. Sensitivity to Polymyxin B was 100%. Mechanical ventilation, urinary catheters and history of prior hospitalization were the strongest predictors of HAI. Patients who developed HAI had a longer ICU stay (9.5 vs. 5.2 days, p=0.001) and higher mortality (28.6% vs. 13.9%, p=0.04). HAIs, particularly VAP caused by MDR organisms, were common in our ICU and there was a high resistance to beta lactams and carbapenem antibiotics. Low resistance to tigecycline and polymyxin B warrants careful stewardship.

42881451.title: Interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of deep vein thrombosis in elderly ICU patients: multicenter development and external validation.
42881451.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
42881451.abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a frequent complication in elderly intensive care unit (ICU) patients, while reliable prediction tools for this population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of DVT in critically ill elderly patients. In this multicenter retrospective study, ICU patients aged ≥ 75 years from two tertiary medical centers in China were enrolled. Patients with pre-existing DVT were excluded. A development cohort (Suzhou, n = 1,717) and an external validation cohort (Xi'an, n = 533) were established. Clinical variables collected within 24 h after ICU admission were used to predict incident DVT during ICU stay. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was applied for feature selection, and four machine learning models were developed and compared. Model discrimination, calibration, and interpretability were evaluated using area under the curve (AUC), calibration analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). DVT occurred in 15.2% and 21.0% of patients in the development and external validation cohorts, respectively. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost achieved the best performance, with AUCs of 0.843 in internal validation and 0.811 in external validation. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed risks. Key predictors included D-dimer, C-reactive protein, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, procalcitonin, mechanical ventilation, and mechanical thromboprophylaxis. SHAP analysis quantified the contribution of individual predictors. We developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for early DVT prediction in elderly ICU patients. The model may support risk stratification and clinical decision-making in critical care settings.

42966650.title: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Versus Standard-Dose Alteplase to Treat High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism.
42966650.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
42966650.abstract: The optimal dosing of alteplase in patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism is widely debated. To evaluate outcomes in patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism who received alteplase at a low dose or a standard dose. This was a retrospective cohort analysis of 65 patients who received alteplase for high-risk pulmonary embolism at a large academic medical center between June 1, 2011, and August 31, 2022. Patients were placed in 2 cohorts according to initial dose: low-dose alteplase (50 mg) and standard-dose alteplase (100 mg). The primary outcome was sustained hemodynamic stability within 24 hours of the start of alteplase infusion. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, hospital and intensive care unit length of stay, and major bleeding. The primary outcome of sustained hemodynamic stability within 24 hours did not differ significantly between the 2 cohorts (achieved in 32% of patients in the low-dose group and 38% in the standard-dose group; P = .65). In-hospital mortality did not differ significantly between groups (48% in the low-dose group vs 45% in the standard-dose group; P = .81). Patients in the low-dose group had fewer days of mechanical ventilation than patients in the standard-dose group (1.5 vs 6 days; P = .03) and a smaller percentage had major bleeding (12% vs 25%; P = .34). In patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism, sustained hemodynamic stability within 24 hours did not differ significantly between low-dose and standard-dose alteplase treatment strategies. Low-dose alteplase may be an appropriate alternative dosing strategy for patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism.

42966639.title: Management of Intensive Care Unit Admission of Patients With Blood Cancer.
42966639.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
42966639.abstract: Patients with blood cancer are at high risk of complications requiring intensive care. Admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) involves ethical and organizational complexities. To investigate the perspectives of hematologists and intensivists making ICU admission decisions in France. A nationwide survey of French hematologists and intensivists was conducted using clinical vignettes to assess ICU admission criteria. The influence of institutional practices, individual experiences, and cancer status on ICU transfer decisions was explored. All 174 participating physicians agreed on ICU admission for patients with immediately life-threatening conditions. Although the general principle of early ICU admission was supported by 75% of hematologists and 54% of intensivists, responses to specific clinical scenarios showed that intensivists recommended broader ICU access and earlier involvement, particularly for patients with noncritical but high-risk conditions. Hematologists more often deferred ICU discussions until clinical deterioration had occurred. Structural barriers such as lack of shared protocols, variations in training, and absence of ICU staff members in hematology decision-making contributed to inconsistent practices. Ethical guidelines were underrecognized and unevenly applied. Neither physician group routinely included nurses in discussions despite nurses' critical role in ICU care. In France, ICU admission practices for patients with blood cancer vary between hematologists and intensivists. Harmonizing practices through common training, early multidisciplinary discussions, risk assessment models, and improved knowledge of ethical standards is urgently needed. These findings may reflect global challenges in aligning ICU triage with evolving cancer care.

42965250.title: An Evaluation of ICU Follow-Up Clinic Attendance and Subsequent Healthcare Resource Utilization in Wales, United Kingdom: A Retrospective, Population-Level Data-Linkage Study.
42965250.abstract: Postintensive care syndrome encapsulates the long-term physical, psychologic, and cognitive impairments often seen among ICU survivors. Post-ICU follow-up clinics may support recovery and reduce avoidable healthcare utilization, but population-level evidence remains limited. To identify patient characteristics associated with follow-up clinic attendance and evaluate differences in healthcare resource utilization (HRU) across three groups: invited and attended, invited but did not attend, and not invited. A retrospective cohort study using anonymised, linked administrative data from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage Databank in Wales, United Kingdom. Adults (≥ 18 yr) with ICU admissions between 2016 and 2023 who survived to discharge were included. Follow-up clinic data were obtained from three regional health boards (healthcare organizations responsible for delivering National Health Services in Wales) with follow-up clinic availability. HRU outcomes included ICU readmissions, emergency department attendances, hospital admissions (elective and emergency), hospital bed days, outpatient appointments, and general practitioner (GP) events. Multivariable models assessed associations between clinic attendance and HRU. Of 6491 eligible patients, 761 attended a follow-up clinic, 1473 were invited but did not attend, and 4257 were not invited. Among invited patients, attendance was associated with increasing age, comorbidity, deprivation, and ICU length of stay. Compared with attendees, nonattendees and those not invited had higher adjusted odds of ICU readmission (odds ratio [OR] = 2.81 and 2.22, respectively), elective admissions, and hospital bed days. No significant differences were observed for emergency admissions or GP events. Attendees were more likely to have 4 or more (non-follow-up clinic) outpatient appointments. Clinic attendance was associated with differences in several HRU domains. Variability in access and engagement suggests potential inequalities in post‑ICU recovery pathways. Standardizing referral practices and expanding clinic availability may improve outcomes for ICU survivors.

42964145.title: A qualitative study on decent work perception among male nurses in the ICU.
42964145.abstract: To explore the lived experiences of decent work perception among male ICU nurses in China, so as to provide evidence for nursing administrators to improve management strategies and retain male nursing workforce. An interpretative phenomenological research design guided by the Psychology of Working Theory was adopted. Using purposive sampling, 14 male nurses working in ICUs were recruited from multiple tertiary hospitals across four provinces in China. Semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted between June and July 2026, and the data were analyzed using Van Manen's six-step phenomenological analysis method. Findings revealed a dynamic process underlying male ICU nurses' experiences of decent work. Participants constructed a sense of decent work through institutional safeguards, social recognition, and professional value. However, this experience was continuously challenged and eroded by high-pressure working conditions, gender stereotypes, and insufficient respect. Despite these challenges, male ICU nurses pursued more decent work through expectations for career development, supportive working conditions, and greater social recognition. Hospitals and nursing managers should pay attention to the unique challenges faced by male ICU nurses, including professional identity conflicts and insufficient social recognition arising from high-intensity work environments and culturally rooted masculine role expectations within the Chinese context. Targeted efforts should be made to strengthen professional recognition and provide diverse career development pathways to promote the sustainable development of the male nursing workforce.

42961212.title: Acute kidney injury in critically ill older adults: clinical severity and nursing workload.
42961212.abstract: To determine the incidence and association of acute kidney injury, clinical severity, and nursing workload with prognostic outcomes in older patients admitted to an Intensive Care Unit. A retrospective cohort study conducted between January and December 2023 in an Intensive Care Unit. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire applied to medical records. Two-sided p-values <0.05 were considered statistically significant. Among the 81 older patients analyzed, 32% developed acute kidney injury. Of these, 22.2% had moderate to severe impairment of renal function. The use of norepinephrine (p=0.019) and the need for mechanical ventilation (p<0.001) were significantly associated with the occurrence of acute kidney injury. In addition, nursing workload was significantly higher in the group with renal impairment (p=0.006). A relevant incidence of acute kidney injury of moderate to high severity was observed among older patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit. Patients with acute kidney injury had a higher nursing workload, as evidenced by higher Nursing Activities Score values. In addition, acute kidney injury was associated with unfavorable prognostic outcomes, including prolonged length of stay and a greater need for advanced support.

42958903.title: The Experiences and Needs of Nursing Staff During Patients' ICU-To-Ward Transition: A Meta-Synthesis of Qualitative Studies.
42958903.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) transitional care ensures continuous care for patients transferring from the ICU to general wards. Relevant qualitative studies show that nurses play a vital role here, so exploring their real experiences and needs is essential for nursing development. To summarise the current qualitative evidence on the experiences and needs of nursing staff during ICU transitional care. A meta-synthesis of qualitative studies retrieved through a search conducted in China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang, VIP Database, Cochrane Library, PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL and Embase from inception to June 2025. All studies that presented qualitative findings on the experiences, feelings and needs of nursing staff, based on participants' reports, were included. Data extracted included publication year, location, sample size, study design, data collection method, phenomenon of interest and all qualitative themes identified. Thirteen studies were selected for inclusion, resulting in four synthesised findings: the practical challenges faced by nursing staff during the ICU transition period, their perceptions and attitudes towards transitional care, their supportive needs for transitional care and recommendations for improving transitional care. The provision of transitional care services by nursing staff is influenced by factors such as existing medical resources, psychological support, workflows and organisational structures. These can guide nursing administrators and healthcare institutions in addressing the occupational needs of nursing personnel, optimising transitional care interventions and promoting the high-quality development of transitional care practices. Despite cultural differences, the experiences and needs of nursing staff during the transition period in the ICU reflect commonalities across cultures. The review gives specific advice for ICU transition care, including establishing effective communication models, psychological support and professional training, establishing ICU liaison nurses and formulating standardised ICU transition procedures.

42958154.title: Association between lactic dehydrogenase-to-albumin ratio and all-cause mortality in critical obstructive sleep apnea patients: a retrospective cohort study from the MIMIC-IV database.
42958154.abstract: Our study endeavors to elucidate the link of the lactic dehydrogenase-to-albumin ratio (LDAR) to all-cause mortality (ACM) among the critically ill obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) population. A retrospective observational cohort study was performed leveraging the MIMIC-IV 3.1 data. This study encompassed adult OSA patients first entering the intensive care unit (ICU). Patients were stratified into quartiles by LDAR. The primary outcomes were ACM at 30, 90, 180 days, and one year after ICU entry. ACM across LDAR quartiles was compared via the Kaplan-Meier (KM) survival analysis. The relation of LDAR to ACM was examined utilizing multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models. The consistency and robustness of our findings were rated through subgroup, interaction, and sensitivity analyses. One thousand one hundred eighteen critically ill OSA patients were encompassed. 749 (66.99%) were male, with a median age of 66. The 30-day, 90-day, 180-day, and one-year ACM rates were 14.58%, 19.59%, 22.00%, and 26.74%. KM curves demonstrated significantly higher mortality rates across increasing LDAR quartiles (log-rank P < 0.001). After possible confounders were adjusted, LDAR was independently related to elevated 90-day ACM risk (HR, 1.318; 95%CI, 1.142-1.520) as a continuous variable. In contrast to the lowest LDAR quartile, the highest quartile displayed a 139.8% greater likelihood of 90-day ACM (HR, 2.398; 95%CI, 1.512-3.803; Ptrend < 0.001). Similar relations were noted for 30-day, 180-day, and one-year ACM. RCS analysis revealed a positive linear relation of LDAR to death at all time points (Pnonlinear > 0.05). Subgroup and interaction analyses revealed insignificant effect modification, confirming the robustness of the association across various clinical strata. Among the critically ill OSA population, elevated LDAR is independently and linearly related to elevated ACM risk in short-term and long-term mortality. The foregoing findings suggest LDAR as a valuable prognostic biomarker for risk classification and clinical management among this high-risk population.

42880785.title: Photobiomodulation therapy combined with a static magnetic field in critically ill patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation: protocol for a multicentre randomised triple-blind placebo-controlled trial.
42880785.abstract: Ventilator-induced diaphragmatic dysfunction is a common complication in critically ill patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation and is associated with prolonged ventilatory support, delayed weaning and increased length of stay in the intensive care unit (ICU). Strategies that preserve respiratory muscle function may therefore improve recovery in this population. Photobiomodulation therapy combined with a static magnetic field (PBMT-sMF) has been proposed as a non-invasive intervention capable of modulating biological processes involved in muscle function. However, high-quality evidence in mechanically ventilated ICU patients remains limited. This is a multicentre, randomised, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. Critically ill patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation will be randomly allocated to receive PBMT-sMF or placebo. The intervention will be applied once daily to predefined anatomical sites over the respiratory muscles during ICU stay. The primary outcome is ICU length of stay, defined as days from ICU admission to ICU discharge. Secondary outcomes include diaphragm thickness by ultrasonography, time to successful weaning from mechanical ventilation, hospital length of stay and selected physiological and laboratory parameters. Data will be analysed using appropriate statistical methods. Ethics approval has been obtained by the Research Ethics Committee of the coordinating institution Associação Dr. Bartholomeu Tacchini (approval number: 7.525.651). Informed consent will be obtained from legally authorised representatives and from participants if capacity is regained. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific conferences. NCT06454006.

42880435.title: Electrolyte disturbance phenotypes and adverse outcomes in the intensive care unit: The role of magnesium and potassium abnormalities.
42880435.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
42880435.abstract: Magnesium and potassium disturbances are common in critically ill patients, but the prognostic value of their co-occurrence is poorly defined. To evaluate the association of combined magnesium-potassium phenotypes at intensive care unit (ICU) admission with 30-day in-hospital mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), and invasive mechanical ventilation. This retrospective cohort included 9462 adults admitted to the ICU of a tertiary hospital in Jordan (2012-2022) with admission magnesium and potassium, classified into nine phenotypes. Mortality was analyzed by Cox regression, censoring patients discharged alive at discharge, and AKI and ventilation by logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, and modified APACHE II score. Thirty-day mortality was 30.6%, ranging from 25.0% with normal magnesium and potassium to 63.6% with combined hypermagnesemia-hyperkalemia. The combined phenotype had the highest adjusted hazard of death (HR 3.01, 95% CI 2.60-3.49), with positive additive interaction (relative excess risk due to interaction 0.76, 95% CI 0.29-1.23). Isolated hyperkalemia (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.46-1.82) and isolated hypermagnesemia (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.42-1.86) were also associated with mortality. The combined phenotype was associated with AKI (aOR 2.66, 95% CI 2.09-3.38) and ventilation (aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.17-1.94). Modeled continuously, potassium showed a U-shaped and magnesium a J-shaped association with mortality. Co-occurring hypermagnesemia and hyperkalemia at ICU admission identify a high-risk phenotype. Because both are measured routinely, this combination may serve as a simple marker for early risk stratification.

42879999.title: Reducing hospital-provided plastic water bottle use in an intensive care unit: Environmental, economical, and behavioural outcomes of a sustainability initiative.
42879999.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
42879999.abstract: The Australian healthcare system generates substantial quantities of plastic waste annually, with hospital-provided water bottles (HPWBs) representing a potentially modifiable source of nonclinical, single-use plastic consumption. Evidence regarding pragmatic, low-cost strategies to reduce HPWB use in Australian healthcare settings remains limited. This study evaluated the environmental, financial, and behavioural impact of a multifaceted intervention designed to reduce HPWB utilisation. A quality improvement study was conducted in a regional Australian intensive care unit. The intervention comprised optimisation of ordering practices, relocation of HPWB supplies to patient-designated areas, and education of staff and visitors regarding the environmental, financial, and health implications of single-use plastics. Economic and environmental impacts were assessed through procurement audits over two 3-month periods before and after intervention. Repeated spot audits evaluated behavioural changes. Staff attitudes and hydration experiences were assessed using questionnaires completed by 66 multiprofessional respondents before intervention and 53 respondents after intervention. The primary outcome of interest was change in cost associated with HPWB procurement. Following implementation, HPWB procurement decreased from 972 to 72 bottles over a 3-month period, representing a 92.7% reduction in procurement costs ($903.96 vs $66.00 AUD), a 30-kg decrement in plastic waste generation, and a decreased carbon footprint associated with materials alone of 134.7 kg CO2e. Secondary outcomes were assessed through spot audits and questionnaires. Spot audits demonstrated reduced storage of HPWBs outside patient-designated areas (14 bottles vs one bottle) and reduced use within staff areas (four vs two bottles). Questionnaire results did not demonstrate a significant difference in self-reported hydration following intervention (mean difference: -0.1, p = 0.327; Cohen's d = -0.11). A modest behavioural effect with a trend towards reduced HPWB use was observed (mean difference: 0.4, p = 0.091; Cohen's d = 0.32). Perceptions regarding the primary contributors to HPWB use changed significantly following intervention (χ2 = 16.61, p = 0.011), with respondents increasingly identifying patients rather than visitors as the predominant users. This low-cost intervention was associated with substantial reductions in costs associated with HPWB procurement, plastic waste generation, and carbon footprint without adversely affecting staff-reported hydration. These findings suggest that simple behavioural and system-based interventions may represent a scalable approach to reducing single-use plastics and supporting sustainable healthcare delivery.

42879346.title: Dexmedetomidine Use and Short-Term All-Cause Mortality in Intensive Care Unit Patients with Ischemic Stroke and Atrial Fibrillation: A Propensity-Matched Analysis from MIMIC-IV.
42879346.abstract: Preclinical studies have demonstrated that dexmedetomidine (DEX), a sedative widely used in intensive care units (ICU), exerts neuroprotective effects. However, its potential protective role and underlying mechanisms in ischemic stroke patients with atrial fibrillation (IS-AF) remain unclear. The study's objective was to assess the connection between the early administration of DEX and short-term mortality from all causes in patients with IS-AF. From the MIMIC-IV database, patients with IS-AF were identified, including those who were administered DEX and those who were not. The primary endpoint was 7-day all-cause mortality, and the secondary endpoint was 90-day all-cause mortality. Propensity score matching (PSM) was utilized to ensure baseline covariates were balanced. Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier survival curves and were utilized to evaluate the association between DEX use and mortality, with subgroup analyses conducted to ensure the findings' robustness. In total, 1,355 patients with IS-AF participated, with 253 (18.7%) receiving DEX. After PSM, 208 pairs were matched. In the fully adjusted model, DEX administration was significantly associated with lower all-cause mortality compared with the control group at both 7 days (before PSM, HR = 0.36, 95% CI: 0.19-0.68, p = 0.002; after PSM, HR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.12-0.54, p < 0.001) and 90 days (before PSM, HR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.66-1.07, p = 0.162; after PSM, HR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.53-0.97, p = 0.031). The subgroup analyses revealed that DEX's protective effect was stronger in patients aged 70 and above, females, those with hypertension, and those without heart failure or chronic kidney disease. Kaplan-Meier survival curves consistently illustrated that DEX users had greater survival probabilities both before and after matching. In patients with IS-AF, DEX administration is connected to decreased all-cause mortality mortality, underlining the possible importance of DEX in ICU settings.

42876967.title: Antibiotic prescribing appropriateness among critically ill patients at a single tertiary care center in the United Arab Emirates: a retrospective cohort study.
42876967.abstract: Despite expanding antimicrobial stewardship initiatives, evidence evaluating the appropriateness of antibiotic prescribing and its clinical implications in intensive care settings in the United Arab Emirates remains limited. This study aimed to assess the appropriateness of antibiotic prescribing among intensive care unit patients, identify factors associated with appropriate antibiotic therapy, and examine its association with clinical outcomes. A retrospective cohort study was conducted in the intensive care unit of a tertiary care hospital in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. Adult patients aged 18 years or older who were admitted between January 2023 and December 2024, had a length of stay exceeding 24 h but less than 30 days, received at least one systemic antibiotic, and had complete medical records were included. Data were extracted from electronic medical records and a regional health information exchange platform. Antibiotic appropriateness was evaluated against institutional or Infectious Diseases Society of America guidelines. Overall, 36% of patients received inappropriate antibiotic therapy. The most common reason for inappropriateness was the absence of a clear indication, particularly for postoperative prophylaxis (44.4%). At the individual agent level, cefepime (48.2%), metronidazole (36.2%), and cefazolin (33.9%) exhibited the highest rates of inappropriate use. Multivariable logistic regression identified positive microbiological culture results (AOR = 3.34, p < 0.001) and sepsis (AOR = 2.12, p = 0.002) as factors independently associated with higher odds of appropriate antibiotic use. Conversely, the presence of a central venous catheter (AOR = 0.30, p = 0.003) was associated with lower odds of appropriate antibiotic use. Appropriate antibiotic therapy was associated with higher odds of organ dysfunction (AOR = 1.69, p = 0.032), nosocomial infection (AOR = 2.28, p = 0.005), and persistent infection despite therapy (AOR = 2.13, p = 0.005). Approximately one-third of patients received inappropriate antibiotic therapy, representing a substantial antimicrobial stewardship concern despite the observed strengths in culture-guided therapy and infection-focused management.

42875940.title: The effects of intravenous glutamine supplementation in critically ill patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
42875940.abstract: Studies evaluating intravenous (IV) glutamine supplementation in critically ill patients have shown inconsistent results. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of IV glutamine on mortality, infectious complications, length of stay, and duration of mechanical ventilation. A systematic search of Ovid Medline, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and KoreaMed was conducted from inception through October 2023 and updated in April 2025. Randomized controlled trials comparing IV glutamine supplementation with standard care in critically ill adults were included. Pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects models. A total of 10 randomized trials involving 1,593 critically ill patients were included in the analysis. IV glutamine supplementation was not associated with reduced overall mortality (risk ratio [RR], 0.93; 95% CI, 0.77-1.13) or overall infection rates (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.63-1.18). No mortality benefit was observed in either non-surgical or surgical/trauma subgroups. Glutamine supplementation was associated with reduced pneumonia incidence (RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.49-0.87) and shorter mechanical ventilation duration (mean difference, -0.97 days; 95% CI, -1.62 to -0.32); however, these findings were based on a limited number of small studies. Intensive care unit and hospital length of stay were longer in the glutamine group. IV glutamine supplementation was not associated with improved survival or overall infection rates in critically ill adults. Current evidence does not support routine IV glutamine supplementation in unselected critically ill patients.

42875287.title: EACTS/STS/AATS Guidelines on Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Adult Cardiac Surgery: An Expert Analysis for Cardiothoracic Anesthesia and Critical Care.
42875287.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

42874160.title: Concordance between upper and lower respiratory tract viral testing in mechanically ventilated ICU patients: A retrospective cohort study.
