This position statement calls upon anaesthesiologists in Singapore to exercise leadership and stewardship to reduce emissions without compromising care.

42934469.title: Point-of-care ultrasound for confirming endotracheal tube placement in prehospital and critical care transport: a scoping review.
42934469.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has demonstrated high pooled diagnostic accuracy for endotracheal tube (ETT) placement confirmation in adult Emergency Departments and Intensive Care Units,, but its translation to pre-hospital and Critical Care Transport (CCT) environments is unclear. We mapped the published evidence on POCUS-based ETT placement confirmation in transport, organized around six axes: clinical indication, transport modality, operator training, impact on management, technical barriers, and patient-oriented outcomes. Scoping review per the Joanna Briggs Institute 2020 framework, reported per PRISMA-ScR. Nine sources searched January 1st, 2015-May 12th, 2026: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Europe PMC, Consensus.app, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov, and forward-citation tracking. Dual independent screening and charting were performed in Covidence with built-in conflict adjudication. From 2447 unique records, 51 met final inclusion. One primary study evaluated diagnostic performance in adult patients in an out-of-hospital setting. The remaining 50 records comprised contextual primary studies and secondary evidence, including cadaver and simulation studies, training evaluations, feasibility implementations, and reviews. Distribution by modality was skewed toward ground emergency medical services (EMS); rotor-wing helicopter EMS (HEMS) evidence was predominantly training-based; fixed-wing evidence was essentially absent. Operator profiles in transport-relevant studies were predominantly paramedic, flight medic, or flight nurse, mismatched against the physician-dominant pooled in-hospital meta-analytic estimates. No included study measured patient-oriented outcomes. Evidence supporting POCUS-based ETT confirmation in pre-hospital and critical care transport remains limited. Most studies addressed training, simulation, feasibility, or implementation rather than diagnostic performance in transported patients, and none demonstrated an effect on patient-oriented outcomes. Transport-specific prospective studies are needed before hospital-derived diagnostic-accuracy estimates can be generalized to transport practice.

42933867.title: Management of dysglycemia in critically ill adults: current evidence, clinical practice and future directions.
42933867.abstract: Hyperglycemia is among the most common metabolic disturbances in critically ill patients, affecting up to 50% of adults admitted to intensive care units (ICUs), regardless of pre-existing diabetes. Both diabetes and stress-induced hyperglycemia are associated with increased risk of organ dysfunction, healthcare-associated infections, prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer ICU and hospital length of stay, and mortality. Clinical guidelines recommend initiating intravenous insulin therapy when blood glucose remains ≥180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) and targeting 140–180 mg/dL (7.8–10.0 mmol/L) for most critically ill adults. Recent advances in continuous glucose monitoring, computerized insulin dosing algorithms, automated insulin delivery systems and artificial intelligence-enabled clinical decision support are transforming glucose management in the ICU and have the potential to improve safety and efficiency. This review summarizes current understanding of the pathophysiology of stress hyperglycemia, the clinical consequences of dysglycemia, contemporary glucose targets, insulin therapy and glucose monitoring strategies. We also highlight emerging technologies, special patient populations and future directions expected to shape precision glycemic management for critically ill adults.

42933837.title: Effect of interferon gamma as a treatment for post-aggressive immunosuppression in critically ill (INFINITY trial): study protocol for a randomised Bayesian double-blind controlled trial.
42933837.abstract: Critically ill patients frequently develop a delayed immune dysfunction after the initial insult, commonly referred to as post-aggressive immunosuppression (PAIS). Persistently reduced monocytic human leucocyte antigen-DR (mHLA-DR) expression is a widely used biomarker of PAIS and has been associated with intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired infections, prolonged organ support and excess late morbidity and mortality. To date, no immunostimulatory strategy has proven efficacy in improving patient-centred outcomes in this population. Interferon gamma-1b (IFN-γ1b) can restore monocyte function and antigen presentation in experimental and clinical settings and has shown biological plausibility and acceptable tolerability in critically ill patients. The INFINITY trial aims to determine whether short-course IFN-γ1b, initiated in patients with biomarker-defined PAIS, increases ventilator-free days compared with placebo. INFINITY is a national, multicentre, phase II, Bayesian, superiority, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel-group trial with a 1:1 allocation ratio conducted in 6 ICUs in France. Adult ICU patients (≥18 years) with high initial severity (Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) at ICU admission ≥6), receiving invasive mechanical ventilation at inclusion, and presenting with mHLA-DR <8000 AB/C measured between days 5 and 10 are eligible. Key non-inclusion criteria include pre-existing immunodeficiency, expected prolonged ventilation due to chronic conditions and contraindication to IFN-γ1b. Randomisation is centralised via a secure electronic system and stratified by centre. Participants receive either IFN-γ1b (Imukin) 2×106 IU (0.1 mg) subcutaneously every 24 hours for 3 consecutive days or matched placebo (0.9% sodium chloride), in addition to standard care. The primary endpoint is ventilator-free days alive at day 28. Secondary endpoints include mHLA-DR kinetics (day 0–7), lymphocyte count, ICU-acquired infections, antibiotic-free days, ICU-free days, SOFA kinetics and all-cause mortality at day 28 and day 90, alongside safety outcomes. A total of 170 participants (85 per group) are planned. Analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle using Bayesian models with pre-specified interim analyses and stopping guidelines. The study will be conducted in accordance with European regulations and was independently reviewed and approved by the French Ethics Committee Comité de Protection des Personnes Ile de France (EUCT number: 2023–5 06 725-11-00). The results will be reported in international peer-reviewed journals and presented at international and national conferences. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06694740; registered on 19 November 2024 (submitted 12 November 2024). Available at: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06694740.

42932856.title: Recent advances in critical care nutrition: from dose escalation to phase-guided and response-guided care.
42932856.abstract: To critically appraise recent advances that are shifting critical care nutrition from uniform nutrient targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided care, with particular emphasis on major studies published in 2025-2026. Recent large trials do not support routine early full-dose energy or high-dose protein delivery in unselected critically ill patients, and some higher dose strategies have generated safety signals. Indirect calorimetry improves measurement of energy expenditure, but measured expenditure is not synonymous with the dose that should be delivered. Emerging data suggest that dynamic responses, including early phosphate trajectories, may help identify metabolic readiness for feeding, although no validated bedside marker exists. Pharmacological intravenous vitamin C has shown no benefit and recurring harm signals in shocked patients, whereas micronutrient care should distinguish physiological requirements and deficiency correction from megadosing. After ICU discharge, intake frequently falls during the transition from enteral to oral nutrition, and intake-guided protocols have achieved high nutritional adequacy in proof-of-concept studies. Critical care nutrition is moving from universal targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided treatment. Acute-phase caution should not become prolonged underfeeding; repeated metabolic assessment, body composition, reliable intake monitoring and continuity through recovery are central priorities.

42930768.title: Critical Care Ultrasound-Guided Targeted Volume Management as Precision Medicine: Predicting Clinical and Financial Impacts.
42930768.abstract: Precision medicine in the intensive care unit (ICU) is increasingly defined by individualized, bedside physiologic assessment rather than protocolized treatment algorithms. Critical care ultrasound for targeted volume management (CCUS-TVM) operationalizes this shift by helping clinicians answer two questions before administering intravenous (IV) fluids: is it safe, and will it be effective? Static measures, such as inferior vena cava (IVC) assessment and the Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (VExUS), identify venous congestion and predict fluid intolerance, while dynamic measures, such as change in left ventricular outflow tract velocity time integral or carotid flow time after passive leg raise, predict volume responsiveness. Together, these tools allow clinicians to tailor resuscitation to an individual patient's underlying hemodynamics, complementing the four-interface model of shock physiology. Recent meta-analyses and the 2024 Society and Critical Care Medicine and 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines show that CCUS-TVM-particularly dynamic assessment-contributes to fewer episodes of renal replacement therapy and mechanical ventilation, shorter ICU stays, and decreased mortality. Beyond clinical benefit, this communication presents an original, exploratory estimate of the potential per-patient cost savings associated with dynamic CCUS-TVM in sepsis- approximately $2600-4400-driven by reductions in renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation, and ICU length of stay. Taken together, CCUS-TVM offers a clinically validated and economically favorable framework for advancing precision medicine in resuscitation.

42930613.title: Physiology-Guided Management of Acute Right Ventricular Failure and Pulmonary Hypertension in Critically Ill Patients: Hemodynamic Phenotypes, Ventilator Interactions, and Rescue Strategies.
42930613.abstract: Patients with acute right heart failure or pulmonary hypertension require cautious resuscitation because the right ventricle is highly preload-sensitive and has a narrow therapeutic window; both hypovolemia and volume overload may worsen hemodynamics. Echocardiographic guidance can help optimize fluid administration. The management of right heart failure also includes increasing contractility and reducing systemic afterload with inodilators such as dobutamine and milrinone. In cases of high pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) contributing to right heart failure, the use of selective pulmonary dilators can decrease the right ventricular afterload, while largely avoiding the systemic hypotension associated with intravenous vasodilators. Hypoxemia, hypercapnia, and acidosis may increase PVR, while sedation, intubation, and positive-pressure ventilation (PPV) may reduce preload, precipitating hemodynamic collapse. When possible, noninvasive respiratory support may be cautiously used to optimize oxygenation and ventilation and avoid intubation. With either form of PPV, airway pressures should be minimized to reduce the risk of hemodynamic compromise. Additionally, preload should be carefully optimized; hypotension-inducing sedatives, such as propofol, should be minimized; vasopressors should be readily available. In ARDS complicated by acute cor pulmonale, a right ventricular-protective ventilation strategy should be considered alongside conventional lung-protective ventilation. This approach emphasizes limiting excessive plateau and driving pressures, avoiding severe hypercapnia and hypoxemia, and carefully titrating positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) to prevent excessive increases in PVR and right ventricular afterload. In patients with right-to-left intracardiac shunting, elevated right-sided pressures may worsen shunt flow and cause refractory hypoxemia that responds poorly to increasing FiO2 and ventilation pressures. Management should therefore focus on reducing PVR, optimizing right ventricular function, and limiting factors that increase right-sided pressures.

42929360.title: Safety and efficacy of volatile sedatives in critically ill patients receiving mechanical ventilation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
42929360.abstract: Volatile sedatives are increasingly utilised for sedation in critically ill patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. Despite numerous randomised controlled trials and observational studies comparing volatile sedation to intravenous sedation, questions regarding its safety and efficacy persist. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science databases for studies published up to July 2025. The analysis included randomised controlled trials and observational studies that compared the use of volatile sedation with intravenous sedation in patients admitted to the intensive care unit for mechanical ventilation. Eligible studies involved adults aged ⩾18 years, requiring mechanical ventilation, and utilising either volatile or intravenous sedatives. They also needed to report at least one outcome of interest: incidence of delirium, mortality, intensive care unit length of stay, or duration of mechanical ventilation. From 3182 identified publications, fifteen studies were included in the systematic review. Volatile sedation was not associated with a significant difference in the incidence of delirium compared to intravenous sedation (risk ratio 0.72; 95% confidence interval 0.38-1.34), mortality (risk ratio 0.97; 95% confidence interval 0.80-1.17), intensive care unit length of stay (mean difference 0.28 days; 95% confidence interval -1.74 to 2.30), or duration of mechanical ventilation (mean difference -37.20 h; 95% confidence interval -78.60 to 4.20). Volatile sedation was not associated with significant differences in mechanical ventilation duration, delirium incidence, intensive care unit length of stay, or mortality compared to intravenous sedation. Further large-scale, high-quality randomised trials are needed to clarify its clinical benefit in critical care settings.

42929076.title: Ward Failure After Severe Rib Fracture: What Unplanned ICU Transfer Teaches Us About Early Risk Stratification.
42929076.abstract: BackgroundSevere rib fractures are a major cause of morbidity and mortality after blunt thoracic trauma. The decision to directly admit these patients to the intensive care unit (ICU) vs initial ward placement remains debated. An unplanned ICU transfer may reflect delayed recognition of deterioration and worsen outcomes.MethodsAdult patients (≥18 years) with isolated severe thoracic injury (thorax AIS ≥3, AIS ≤1 in all other body regions) due to blunt trauma that resulted in one or more rib fractures were identified in the ACS Trauma Quality Improvement Program database from 2013-2021. Patients were stratified by admission pathway: direct ICU admission or unplanned ICU transfer from the ward. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable Poisson regression with robust standard errors was employed to adjust for potential confounding.ResultsAmong 52,332 patients who sustained isolated severe thoracic injury with rib fractures and were admitted to the ICU, 1830 (3.5%) experienced an unplanned ICU transfer. Adjusted analyses confirmed increased risks of mortality (RR 3.35, 95% CI 2.89-3.88), pneumonia (RR 2.68, 95% CI 2.08-3.45), ARDS (RR 4.52, 95% CI 3.42-5.97), and mechanical ventilation (RR 3.21, 95% CI 2.98-3.47) with unplanned admission.ConclusionsUnplanned ICU admission is independently associated with markedly worse outcomes in isolated severe thoracic injury with rib fractures. These findings suggest that improved early risk stratification may help identify patients at increased risk of subsequent unplanned ICU transfer.

42927703.title: Longitudinal assessment of pulmonary morphological patterns using structured serial chest radiography in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
42927703.abstract: Portable chest radiography is routinely available in mechanically ventilated ICU patients, yet serial findings are rarely standardized. We evaluated whether a structured morphological classification of serial chest radiographs could describe early radiographic evolution during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) and explored associations with clinical outcomes. Single-centre retrospective cohort of 57 adults receiving IMV ≥48 h in the ICU of Hospital General IESS Babahoyo, Ecuador (2018-2019). Radiographs from Days 1-5 of IMV were classified into 13 predefined predominant morphological categories; radiological change was defined as any modification of the predominant pattern relative to baseline. IMV duration, ICU length of stay, and mortality were analysed using an exploratory logistic regression model. Radiographs were available for 57 patients on Days 1-2, 46 on Day 3, 39 on Day 4, and 34 on Day 5. Normal predominant patterns decreased from 52.6% at baseline to 14.7% on Day 5, while alveolar patterns increased from 10.5% to 35.3%. Thirty-two patients (56.1%) had documented radiological pattern change, first identified at a median of Day 2. Patients with documented change had longer IMV duration (5.5 vs. 3 days; p < 0.001) and ICU stay (8 vs. 3 days; p < 0.001). In the exploratory adjusted model, IMV duration was associated with documented change (adjusted OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.0-1.6; p = 0.018). Structured serial chest radiography converted routine ICU images into comparable longitudinal morphological variables. Documented radiological change was common and frequently early; its association with longer IMV duration should be interpreted as concurrent and exploratory. Prospective multicentre studies are needed.

42926935.title: Outcomes of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis admitted to the ICU for acute respiratory failure.
42926935.abstract: Data on patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for acute respiratory failure are scarce, and early prognostic markers are lacking. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with ALS admitted for acute respiratory failure to two ICUs of a tertiary referral center between 2016 and 2022. The primary outcome was 3-month mortality. Factors associated with 3-month mortality were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Survival and functional outcomes were evaluated up to 12 months. Among 139 patients [median age 66 (IQR 57-73) years, 61.2% being men], 109 (78.4%) patients presented with hypercapnia and 82 (59.0%) with hypoxemia (defined as PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio < 300) at ICU admission, with frequent overlap between both conditions. Non-invasive ventilation was used in 79.9% of patients, while 13.7% were intubated, and 2.2% underwent tracheostomy. Three-month mortality was 48.2%, increasing to 61.2% and 74.1% at 6 and 12 months respectively. In multivariable analysis, hypoxemia at ICU admission was independently associated with increased 3-month mortality (HR = 2.27, 95% CI: 1.28-4.01; P = 0.005), along with older age (HR=1.03 per year, 95% CI: 1.00-1.06; P = 0.035). Among patients alive at 3 months, a majority (79.2%) were living at home. ICU admission for acute respiratory failure in ALS is associated with substantial short-term mortality, consistent with the poor prognosis inherent to the natural history of the disease. Hypoxemia at admission identifies a subgroup at particularly high risk of death and may help inform early prognostic assessment and shared decision-making. However, patients who survive the acute ICU phase frequently achieve favorable short-term outcomes, with most living at home at 3 months.

42926782.title: Dexmedetomidine Suspected Fever and Clinical Escalation: A Pilot Study Evaluating the Impact in the Intensive Care Unit.
42926782.journal: The Journal of pharmacy technology : jPT : official publication of the Association of Pharmacy Technicians
42926782.abstract: Dexmedetomidine, an alpha-2 agonist commonly used as a sedative agent in mechanically ventilated patients, has been associated with drug-induced fever. Concern for fever may prompt diagnostic evaluation and empiric antimicrobial therapy, potentially leading to unnecessary health care utilization. This pilot study aimed to evaluate if dexmedetomidine use in mechanically ventilated medical intensive care unit (ICU) patients was associated with increased escalation of care compared with alternate sedative agents. This single-center, retrospective, matched cohort study included patients 18 years or older who were admitted to the medical ICU and required a sedative agent to facilitate mechanical ventilation. Patients receiving dexmedetomidine were matched 1:1 with patients receiving alternate sedative agents. The primary outcome was the composite outcome of initiation of diagnostic evaluation and/or antimicrobial escalation (IDEA). A total of 150 patients were included (75 per group). Most patients were male (68%), and 45% had a primary diagnosis of respiratory failure. The primary outcome, IDEA, occurred in 53 patients (71%) receiving dexmedetomidine and 51 patients (68%) receiving alternate sedatives (P = .723). Fever occurred in 24 patients (32%) receiving dexmedetomidine compared with 17 patients (23%) receiving alternate sedatives. Median ICU length of stay was longer in the dexmedetomidine group (5 [interquartile range, IQR 1-8] vs 4 [IQR 1-5] days; [P = .002]). In-hospital mortality occurred in 14 patients (19%) receiving dexmedetomidine and 24 patients (32%) receiving alternate sedative (P = .060). There was no statistically significant difference between escalation of care in the use of dexmedetomidine versus other sedatives in ICU patients.

42925836.title: Effect of circadian-oriented goal-directed sedation on sleep quality and clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
42925836.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
42925836.abstract: Sleep disruption and circadian rhythm disturbances are common in mechanically ventilated intensive care unit (ICU) patients and are associated with delirium, prolonged ventilation, and poor clinical outcomes. Conventional sedation strategies may further impair sleep architecture and circadian regulation. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the effects of circadian-oriented, goal-directed sedation on sleep quality and clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. This study enrolled 65 mechanically ventilated patients admitted to ICU at Suzhou Ninth People's Hospital between March 2024 and December 2024. Using convenience sampling, 33 patients admitted between March and July 2024 were allocated to the control group and received routine sedation and nursing care, while 32 patients admitted between August and December 2024 were formed the intervention group and received sedation management individualized according to circadian sleep-wake patterns. Sleep quality was assessed on days 1, 3, 5, and 7 after intervention using the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) and a portable sleep monitor. Delirium was evaluated by Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU). Sedative dosage, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of ICU and hospital stay, , clinical improvement rate, complications, and hospitalization costs were compared between groups. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two groups. Sleep quality improved over time in both groups; however, Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire scores were significantly higher in the intervention group at all assessment points (p < 0.05). Patients receiving circadian-oriented sedation experienced shorter durations of mechanical ventilation, reduced ICU and total hospital stays, higher rates of clinical improvement, and lower hospitalization costs compared with the control group (p < 0.05). The incidence of complications, including delirium, was also significantly lower in the intervention group. Sedation management aligned with circadian sleep-wake patterns significantly improves sleep quality, reduces sedative requirements, lowers delirium incidence, and shortens mechanical ventilation duration, demonstrating a favorable safety profile in mechanically ventilated patients.

42923688.title: Prior use of dihydropyridines is associated with reduced mortality among patients with sepsis in the intensive care unit: a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV database.
42923688.abstract: Evidence regarding the survival benefits of dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers in patients with sepsis is limited. This study aimed to investigate whether prior use of dihydropyridines is associated with improved survival in patients with sepsis in the intensive care unit (ICU). We extracted relevant information on patients diagnosed with sepsis from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database (version 2.0). Patients were divided into a dihydropyridine group and a no-dihydropyridine group based on drug prescription records. The primary outcomes were 30-day, 60-day, and 90-day mortality. After propensity score matching, univariate and multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the association between dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker use and survival in patients with sepsis. A total of 20,796 patients were included in the analysis. After propensity score matching, 1,232 patients who had used dihydropyridines and 1,232 who had not were included. Multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models showed that prior use of dihydropyridines was significantly associated with reduced 30-day (hazard ratio [HR], 0.800; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.662-0.968; P = 0.021), 60-day (HR, 0.776; 95% CI, 0.653-0.922; P = 0.004), and 90-day (HR, 0.760; 95% CI, 0.645-0.895; P = 0.001) mortality. In this retrospective cohort study, prior use of dihydropyridines was associated with improved survival among patients with sepsis in the ICU.

42923592.title: Association of creatine kinase and arterial lactate upon admission with early ARDS exacerbation: a single-center retrospective ICU cohort study.
42923592.abstract: To evaluate whether admission levels of creatine kinase (CK) and arterial lactate (LAC), two routinely available ICU biomarkers, are associated with early in-hospital exacerbation of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and to assess their short-term discriminatory performance using a retrospective cohort. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 120 ARDS patients admitted to the ICU. Patients were divided into an exacerbation group and a non-exacerbation group according to whether ARDS worsened within 48 h after admission, with 60 patients in each group. CK, LAC, inflammatory markers, metabolic indices, and routine blood indices were measured at ICU admission and 24 h. Between-group comparisons, within-group dynamic comparisons, logistic regression, Spearman correlation analysis, and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed. CK and LAC levels were higher in the exacerbation group than in the non-exacerbation group at both 0 h and 24 h. In multivariable logistic regression, higher CK and LAC at ICU admission were independently associated with early ARDS exacerbation. The combined CK-LAC model yielded an AUC of 0.832. CK and LAC were also positively correlated with ICU length of stay and duration of mechanical ventilation. Routine inflammatory, metabolic, and blood routine indices showed limited between-group discriminative value. Higher admission CK and LAC levels were independently associated with early ARDS exacerbation. The combined assessment yielded a numerically higher AUC than either marker alone. However, the cut-off values were internally derived and require external validation before clinical application.

42923583.title: Factors Related to Length of Stay of Critical Patients in Intensive Care Unit: A Single-center Cross-sectional Study.
42923583.abstract: Intensive care units (ICUs) provide specialized care for critically ill patients, but prolonged length of stay (LOS) can strain limited ICU capacity, increase healthcare costs, and negatively affect patient outcomes. Predicting LOS at the time of ICU admission remains challenging because of the complex interplay of patients' clinical conditions and therapeutic needs. This study aimed to identify clinical and admission-related factors associated with ICU LOS and determine predictors of prolonged stay among ICU patients. This study employed a cross-sectional design, with data collected from patient medical records in 2024. The Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), Blood pressure (BP), and LOS were used as the dependent outcome variables. Data processing was conducted with the Pearson correlation coefficient, t-test, and Hierarchical multiple regression. A total of 146 ICU patients participated as respondents, with an average age of 63.36 ± 14.56 years, CCI (4.27 ± 2.33), GCS 12 ± 4, and the average LOS was 5.25 ± 4.99 days. The results showed that variables presenting a relationship with LOS were age (r = 0.17, p = 0.05), CCI (r = -0.46, p = 0.01), GCS (r = -0.54, p = 0.01), and use of a mechanical ventilator (MV) (t = 5.44, p = 0.01). Five variables identified as LOS predictors included age (B = 0.03), CCI (B = -0.37), GCS (B = -0.12), systolic blood pressure (SBP) (B = 0.01), and not using MV (B = -0.91), which were expected to cover 74% of the variance in LOS (adjusted R2 = 0.725, F = 48.67). Endeavors to minimize LOS can serve as a crucial strategy in reducing nosocomial infections, the financial burden of treatment, morbidity and mortality, and enhancing the quality of life of patients in the ICU. In addition, age, CCI, GCS, SBP, and MV were significant predictors of ICU patients' LOS, with CCI being the strongest predictor.

42923303.title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio and short-term mortality in critically ill patients with respiratory diseases: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
42923303.abstract: To systematically evaluate the association between the HbA1c-adjusted stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) and short-term mortality in patients with severe respiratory diseases and characterize its linear and nonlinear dose-response relationships. PubMed, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang, VIP, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database were searched for observational studies evaluating SHR and short-term mortality, including in-hospital, intensive care unit (ICU), 28-day, or 30-day mortality. Odds ratios (ORs) and hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled separately using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses, linear dose-response analyses, restricted cubic spline analyses, and exploratory analyses of low and high SHR were performed. Eleven studies were included. Four studies contributed to the OR-based primary meta-analysis. Short-term mortality tended to be higher in the highest SHR category than in the study-specific reference category, but the association was not statistically significant (OR = 2.72, 95% CI: 0.74-9.93, P = 0.091; I 2 = 86.4%). Three studies contributed to the HR-based primary meta-analysis, which showed a significant association between higher SHR and increased short-term mortality risk (HR = 1.87, 95% CI: 1.71-2.05, P = 0.001; I 2 = 0%). In HR studies, each 0.1-unit increase in SHR was associated with an approximately 5% increase in short-term mortality risk (HR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.08, P = 0.023). OR studies showed a similar direction of association but did not reach statistical significance. Restricted cubic spline analyses found no clear evidence of nonlinearity. Exploratory analyses suggested higher risks at both low and high SHR levels, but the estimates were imprecise. Current evidence suggests that higher SHR is associated with increased short-term mortality risk in patients with severe respiratory diseases. HR-based evidence was more consistent and supported a positive linear dose-response relationship. OR-based findings pointed in the same direction but showed substantial heterogeneity and did not reach statistical significance. The available evidence is insufficient to confirm a clear nonlinear pattern. Given the limited number of studies and wide confidence intervals, the apparent increase in risk at both low and high SHR levels should be interpreted as exploratory and does not yet support a stable U-shaped or J-shaped dose-response pattern. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261418259, PROSPERO CRD420261418259.

42921842.title: Molecular Characterization and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns of Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative Bacilli Isolated from Intensive Care Unit Patients in a Tertiary Care Hospital.
42921842.abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacilli (GNB) present a critical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), severely limiting therapeutic options. This study evaluated the prevalence and molecular resistance mechanisms of GNB in ICU patients. Hospital-acquired urinary tract infections are among the most common healthcare-associated infections in ICUs. The emergence of MDR Gram-negative bacilli has reduced available treatment options and increased morbidity. This study aimed to evaluate antimicrobial resistance patterns and characterize major resistance genes among Gram-negative bacilli isolated from ICU patients. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from 2019 to 2022 across two tertiary centers in North India. We analyzed 427 non-duplicate MDR GNB isolates from ICU urinary samples. Identification followed standard biochemical protocols. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed through Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion as per Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. Phenotypic detection of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL), AmpC, and carbapenemase production was performed, alongside molecular characterization of resistance genes (blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M, blaNDM, blaIMP, blaVIM, blaOXA). In the present study, most isolates originated from the medical ICU (66.0%). Most MDR GNB isolates were from males (52%), and the majority of patients belonged to the age group > 60 years. The predominant isolates were Escherichia coli (60%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (19%), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (12%). Alarmingly high resistance rates to Cephalosporins (>90%), Fluoroquinolones (>80%), and Carbapenems (70% overall) were observed. Overall, 40.9% of isolates were ESBL producers, 24.82% AmpC producers, and 13.81% Carbapenemase producers. Molecular analysis revealed a high prevalence of blaCTX M (100%), blaVIM (66%), and blaNDM (48%). The high prevalence of diverse resistance mechanisms underscores the impact of indiscriminate antimicrobial use. Implementation of stringent antimicrobial stewardship and robust infection control practices is essential to mitigate the spread of MDR pathogens in critical care settings.

42921153.title: Post-intensive care syndrome (PICS), an AAST Critical Care Committee Consensus Guideline: expectations, mental health impairments, financial hardship, and caregiver burden in PICS.

42919600.title: Inhaled sedation versus intravenous sedation in critically ill patients (IS-CRITIC): protocol for a multicentre, randomised, controlled clinical trial in Spain.
42919600.abstract: Intravenous sedatives are widely used in the intensive care unit (ICU) and are part of routine clinical practice. However, these agents and their active metabolites may be associated with adverse events. Volatile anaesthetics have recently emerged as an attractive alternative for ICU sedation, and isoflurane has been approved by regulatory agencies in several European countries for use in critically ill patients. Although isoflurane has been shown to be non-inferior to propofol-based sedation during short-term sedation periods, it remains unclear whether inhaled sedation with isoflurane offers advantages over intravenous sedation in patients requiring prolonged mechanical ventilation and, consequently, prolonged sedation. This is a phase IV, low-intervention, open-label, multicentre randomised clinical trial conducted on an intention-to-treat basis. A total of 620 patients will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio to receive either inhaled sedation with isoflurane administered using the Sedaconda ACD-S device or intravenous sedation with propofol. Adult patients expected to require more than 48 hours of mechanical ventilation will be included. The primary outcome is ventilator-free days through day 28 post-randomisation. The key secondary outcome is ICU-free days through day 28 post-randomisation. Patient recruitment began in December 2025 and is expected to conclude in December 2027. Final analysis is planned for 2028. The study protocol was approved by the ethics committee of Hospital Universitario La Paz, Madrid, Spain (#6844) and the European Medicines Agency on 13 March 2025. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations. NCT07000526. This clinical trial is registered in the European Union (EU) Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS), under the EU Clinical Trials Regulation (Regulation 536/2014). CTIS ID: (2024–5 18 521-14-00).

42914683.title: Hypoxemia and pulmonary infiltrates during T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody therapy: A pulmonary and critical care framework.
42914683.abstract: T-cell-engaging bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) have rapidly expanded treatment options for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, B-cell lymphomas, and small-cell lung cancer. Their off-the-shelf availability, step-up dosing, repeated administration, and migration into outpatient and community settings distinguish them from autologous chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy. These same features increasingly bring patients to pulmonary and critical care teams. Patients receiving BsAbs may present with fever, hypoxemia, pulmonary infiltrates, pneumonia, cytokine release syndrome (CRS), secondary antibody deficiency, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP), cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection, respiratory viral disease, pulmonary edema, pulmonary embolism, malignant pulmonary involvement, or suspected drug-induced lung injury. Existing guidelines provide essential CRS grading, rechallenge, and infection-prevention recommendations but do not fully address the bedside pulmonary differential diagnosis, indications for bronchoscopy, ventilatory escalation, or intensive care unit (ICU) triage. This focused narrative review synthesizes pivotal trials, current prescribing information, consensus statements, real-world studies, and pulmonary literature. We emphasize two overlapping risk windows: early step-up dosing, in which CRS and infection must be evaluated and treated in parallel, and later or prolonged therapy, in which infection, target-specific immune deficits, and noninfectious mimics become dominant considerations. A timed approach using oxygen trajectory, computed tomography pattern, host immune deficits, microbiologic data, and selective bronchoscopy may reduce diagnostic anchoring and improve multidisciplinary care.

42913474.title: Virtual Reality for Delirium Prevention in Intensive Care Unit Nurses and Mechanically Ventilated Patients: Descriptive Qualitative Study.
42913474.abstract: Patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) who are on mechanical ventilation are at high risk of developing delirium. Virtual reality (VR) technology, as an emerging intervention method, shows promising application prospects in delirium prevention, but its specific experience in clinical practice still requires in-depth exploration. This study aims to explore the real experiences of ICU nurses and mechanically ventilated patients in participating in VR delirium prevention, with the aim of providing practical evidence for the optimization and application of this technology in clinical practice. A descriptive qualitative research design was adopted. From March to June 2025, using purposive sampling, participants were selected from the internal medicine, surgery, central, and respiratory ICU departments of a tertiary hospital in Zhengzhou. A total of 73 patients on mechanical ventilation were screened. Among them, 49 were excluded due to not meeting the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) or Barthel Index (BI) score criteria, 5 had delirium at the time of enrollment, 1 was excluded due to visual impairment, and 2 voluntarily withdrew during the study. Finally, 16 patients on mechanical ventilation and 16 nurses were included for semistructured interviews. Data analysis was conducted using the inductive content analysis method. Through the analysis of the interview data, a total of 3 main themes and 14 subthemes were extracted. In terms of perceived benefits, patients experienced an immersive environment and a sense of empowerment driven by tasks, while nurses felt the convenience of resource integration, the intimacy of the nurse-patient relationship, and a sense of professional significance. In terms of perceived challenges, patients faced difficulties with the interaction interface and physical and mental obstacles, while nurses encountered difficulties in communication assessment and responsibility definition. In terms of perceived needs, patients expected personalized content design and continuity of nursing services, while nurses suggested differentiated content adjustment, comprehensive functional integration, and standardized safety management. The participants expressed a positive attitude towards the prevention of delirium based on VR and reported various perceived benefits, challenges, and needs. Future research should prioritize content personalization, functional integration, and safety management. Meanwhile, it is necessary to recognize the limitations of this technology in specific target populations. For those who do not meet the inclusion criteria, adaptive alternative intervention measures should be developed to promote the precise and sustainable application of VR-based delirium prevention.

42912115.title: Nursing Activities Score in critically ill patients on invasive mechanical ventilation.
42912115.abstract: to assess the association between invasive mechanical ventilation duration, classified as prolonged and non-prolonged, and nursing workload in critically ill patients. a prospective cohort study with adult patients on mechanical ventilation for up to 21 days or more. Nursing workload was measured using the Nursing Activities Score (NAS). Clinical data were collected using a structured questionnaire. A significance level of 5% was adopted. considering 61 patients, there was no significant difference in nursing workload between prolonged and non-prolonged mechanical ventilation according to NAS [111.2 (105.118) vs. 111.8 (107.119); p=0.880], nor was there an association between mechanical ventilation time and this score (AUC=0.512). Prolonged mechanical ventilation was associated with vasoactive drugs (96%; p=0.007) and greater severity of acute kidney injury (KDIGO=3.78%; p=0.009). mechanical ventilation duration was not associated with changes in nursing workload, which remained high regardless of the ventilatory support duration.

42912025.title: Advanced practice nurse in intensive care in the Brazilian context: a scoping review.
42912025.abstract: to map the scope of practice of advanced practice nurses in intensive care and its applicability in the Brazilian context. a scoping review conducted between September 2024 and February 2025, based on the JBI and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The search was carried out in PubMed, Virtual Health Library, CINAHL, SCOPUS, BDENF, Web of Science, COCHRANE, and LILACS, in addition to thesis and dissertation repositories. Two independent reviewers selected the studies, and a third resolved disagreements. Data extraction followed a standardized instrument, with descriptive synthesis. a final sample of 20 publications was selected. The advanced practice nurse in intensive care performs invasive procedures, such as central venous catheter insertion, orotracheal intubation, lumbar puncture, and chest tube insertion. Furthermore, the use of advanced technologies and the high level of clinical autonomy of this professional provide effective diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making for the management of critically ill patients. the scope of practice of advanced practice nurses in intensive care, although still incipient, presents perspectives for scientific, autonomous, and highly qualified advancement in the nursing field in Brazil, directly contributing to a responsive and effective healthcare approach. However, the scarcity of regulatory legislation and the lack of standardized and specific training for advanced practice nurses still constitute limitations to their implementation in Brazil.

42908777.title: Case Report: Herbal nutritional intervention in a critically ill ALS patient with multidrug-resistant infection.
42908777.abstract: We report a retrospective single case of a female patient with a 9-year history of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) who presented with respiratory failure due to a multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) infection, predominantly Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP), and who showed significant clinical improvement during a comprehensive treatment regimen that included an adjunctive herbal nutritional intervention. The objective of this retrospective single-case report was to describe the clinical course of this patient following a nutritional intervention with two herbal beverages: Sang Shen Pu Gong Ying (SSPGY) and Wu Zhi Mao Tao Hong Zao (WZMTHZ). The patient was admitted in critical condition and managed in three phases: initial antibiotics with occasional herbal beverages, daily herbal beverages, and a combination of herbal beverages with intermittent antibiotics. Retrospective analysis of clinical data revealed significant improvements post-intervention. Body weight increased from 26 kg to 35.5 kg at discharge and 39 kg at the 6-week follow-up. Vital signs normalized, with no detectable KP in the final hospital phase. Inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein and white blood cell count, decreased markedly. Neurological status, as indicated by neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels, improved, and the patient showed respiratory autonomy and positional changes. Nutritional markers, total protein and creatinine, also improved. This case documents clinical improvements, including extended ventilator-free breathing periods, in an ALS patient with MDRO infection following a combined therapeutic approach. Although concurrent medical interventions were administered in real-world clinical practice, these findings suggest the potential value of this adjunctive intervention, warranting further systematic investigation. Clinical Trial Registration: identifier ITMCTR2024000322.

42906879.title: Clinical nutrition for critically ill patients: A practical appraisal of guideline gaps and perspectives for future research.
42906879.abstract: Malnutrition and accelerated muscle wasting are frequent during critical illness and make nutritional support a central component of ICU care. Nutritional support is therefore central to ICU care, but its optimal timing, route, dose, and composition remain debated. Recent randomized trials have challenged the traditional objective of early full feeding and shifted practice toward progressive, phase-adapted, and tolerance-based nutrition. This narrative review compares current international guidelines for nutritional support in critically ill adults. Guidelines broadly agree that nutrition should be initiated early after clinical stabilization, acute-phase overfeeding should be avoided, energy and protein delivery should be increased progressively, and refeeding syndrome should be anticipated. However, important differences remain regarding acute-phase energy targets, protein dosing, enteral versus parenteral nutrition, supplemental parenteral nutrition, indirect calorimetry, and enriched enteral formulas. These discrepancies reflect differences in methodology, healthcare context, and interpretation of evidence largely derived from mechanically ventilated patients during the first ICU week. Several clinically important situations remain insufficiently addressed, including prolonged critical illness, obesity, sarcopenia, post-extubation nutrition, post-ICU rehabilitation, and nutrition after major surgery. Future research should move toward individualized strategies based on illness phase, metabolic trajectory, nutritional phenotype, tolerance, and recovery-oriented outcomes.

42906295.title: Modified NUTRIC score and clinical outcomes in critically ill medical patients: A prospective cohort study in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
42906295.abstract: Malnutrition and nutritional risk are prevalent among critically ill patients. However, research from medical intensive care units (ICUs) in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Western Balkans is scarce. This study sought to compare clinical characteristics, laboratory results, and hospital outcomes in critically ill medical patients, differentiating between those with low and high modified Nutrition Risk in the Critically Ill (mNUTRIC) scores. This prospective, single-center observational cohort study enrolled 102 adult patients admitted to a tertiary medical ICU from July 2025 to January 2026. The mNUTRIC score was evaluated within 48 hours of ICU admission, categorizing patients into low-score (0-4) and high-score (5-9) groups. A high mNUTRIC score was observed in 67 patients (65.7%). Compared to the low-score group, these patients exhibited greater illness severity, more comorbidities, less favorable laboratory findings, longer ICU stays (median: 11 vs. 7 days; p = 0.019), and extended durations of mechanical ventilation (median: 6 vs. 4 days; p = 0.037). No significant differences were found between the groups for overall hospital mortality (56.7% vs. 42.9%; p = 0.183) or ICU mortality (22.4% vs. 28.6%; p = 0.491). Among ICU survivors, post-ICU mortality was higher in the high-score group (44.2% vs. 20.0%; p = 0.038), though this observation was drawn from a specific subgroup. In this exploratory cohort, a high mNUTRIC score identified patients with increased clinical severity, longer ICU admissions, and prolonged mechanical ventilation. However, it did not independently predict mortality. The study could not ascertain the impact of mNUTRIC-guided nutritional interventions due to the lack of assessment of nutritional intake and interventions.

42906253.title: Occult hypoxemia in the ICU: Clinical risk factors, mortality and implications for nursing practice.
42906253.abstract: Pulse oximetry (SpO₂) is the primary tool used by Intensive Care Unit (ICU) nurses to monitor oxygenation. Occult hypoxemia - a reassuring SpO₂ despite low arterial saturation (SaO₂) - is a critical patient-safety concern. To measure SpO₂-SaO₂ discordance in ICU patients, identify situations in which SpO₂ cannot be trusted, and assess its impact on ICU mortality. Retrospective single-centre cohort study (September 2019 - January 2026), reported according to STROBE. SpO₂ was charted hourly; each arterial blood gas was paired with the most recent preceding entry. Analysis was restricted to pairs within 10 min, using Bland-Altman analysis for repeated measures. Predictors of occult hypoxemia (SpO₂ ≥ 92% with SaO₂ < 88%) and its association with ICU mortality were examined using generalized estimating equations, with adjustment restricted to early-stay covariates. The primary set comprised 39,554 paired measurements from 7082 ICU stays in 6348 patients. Mean bias was negligible (+0.1%) but limits of agreement were wide (-7.6% to +7.8%); 18.6% of pairs differed by ≥4%. Among 1219 pairs with SaO₂ < 88%, SpO₂ remained ≥92% in 702 (57.6%). Acidosis was most robustly associated with occult hypoxemia (adjusted OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.97-2.86 for pH < 7.35); invasive mechanical ventilation carried lower risk (OR 0.50, 0.42-0.60). Early occult hypoxemia (within 24 h) was independently associated with ICU mortality (adjusted OR 1.55, 1.17-2.05; 24-h landmark OR 1.45, 1.07-1.97). Point estimates were similar when exposure was ascertained only from pairs obtained within 10 or 5 min (1.44 and 1.49), with confidence intervals including unity because restriction reduced the number of exposed deaths by about 70%. Among sampled measurements with true arterial hypoxemia, SpO₂ frequently remained ≥92%, particularly in acidotic and patients not receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. Early occult hypoxemia was independently associated with ICU mortality. Because inclusion required a blood gas revealing the discordance, the treating team could act on it; the association reflects a severity signal rather than a causal effect of the discordance itself. In acidotic ICU patients and those on non-invasive oxygen support, SpO₂ frequently disagrees with concurrent SaO₂ and should not be relied on alone. Arterial blood gas confirmation may be considered when SpO₂ appears inconsistent with the clinical picture.

42904452.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Trends in COVID-19 Patients with Hospital Infection in Intensive Care: A Retrospective Study in Central Italy, 2020-2022.
42904452.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was exacerbated by COVID-19 pandemic. This study describes prevalence and trends of AMR in patients with diagnosed severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection admitted during 2020-2022 to the intensive care unit (ICU) in Molise region, central Italy. A retrospective study was conducted, including patients aged ≥ 18 years with at least one positive bacterial or fungal culture during ICU stay. Data were related to patient demographics, ICU outcomes, healthcare-associated infections, and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles. During the 2020-2022 period, 103 ICU admissions met the inclusion criteria, yielding 268 isolations, of which 157 underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Apart from high proportion of Candida albicans, Gram-negative bacteria predominated, with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Acinetobacter baumannii among the most frequent. Resistance to beta-lactams and carbapenems was consistently high, while it ranged from 53.8% to 66.7% to fluoroquinolones and remained above 50% to aminoglycosides. Tetracycline resistance showed significant year-to-year variation, increasing in 2022 compared with both 2020 and 2021. AMR rates in COVID-19 patients in ICU were persistently high throughout the pandemic, with critical resistance levels in Gram-negatives, underlining the need to reinforce infection prevention and control measures and antimicrobial stewardship programs and align prescribing practices with World Health Organization AWaRe recommendations, even during public health emergencies.

42904386.title: Individually Prescribed In-Bed Exergaming Using Nintendo Ring Fit Adventure in Posttransplant Inpatients With Marked Functional Impairment After Intensive Care: Prospective Single-Arm Feasibility Study.
42904386.abstract: Early rehabilitation is important after transplantation and critical illness, but profound weakness, fatigue, and motivational, psychological, and safety barriers may limit participation. Exergaming may facilitate rehabilitation, but the feasibility of full-body in-bed exergaming in this population remains unclear. We evaluated the feasibility and observed safety of individually prescribed in-bed exergaming using Nintendo Ring Fit Adventure (NFA; Nintendo Co, Ltd) in posttransplant inpatients after intensive care unit (ICU) care. This prospective, single-center, single-arm interventional feasibility study (October 2024-October 2025) enrolled 26 posttransplant adults with prior ICU care and Functional Ambulation Category (FAC) scores ≤3. Participants were referred after ward transfer by transplant-team advanced practice nurses, and the principal investigator confirmed eligibility based on prespecified inclusion and exclusion criteria. Ten individually prescribed, supervised in-bed NFA sessions, each scheduled for 30 minutes, including setup and operation, were planned alongside usual physical therapy. Data were obtained from medical records, standardized session logs, and prespecified clinical and questionnaire assessments. Outcomes included retention; session delivery, completion, and interruptions; exercise-item completion and interruptions; session-terminating adverse events; net exercise time; satisfaction; and exploratory strength, mobility, and health-related quality-of-life changes. Participants (mean age 53.0, SD 12.4 y; 14 men) included 23 liver and 3 bilateral lung transplant recipients. Mean ICU stay and mechanical ventilation duration were 24.3 (SD 11.0) days and 21.3 (SD 11.6) days, respectively; median baseline FAC and Medical Research Council Sum Score were 0.5 (IQR 0.0-1.0) and 38.0 (IQR 30.5-42.0), respectively. None had an FAC score above 2. Twenty completed the final assessment (20/26, 76.9%, 95% CI 57.9%-89%). Of 227 delivered sessions, 223 (98.2%, 95% CI 95.8%-100%) were completed. Of 2161 prescribed exercise items, 2072 (95.9%, 95% CI 93.4%-97.9%) were completed. No session-terminating adverse events were observed (0/227, 0%, 95% CI 0%-1.6%). Median within-participant net exercise time increased by 159.0 (IQR 35.5-296.3) seconds from sessions 1 to 10 (95% CI 81.0-284.0; Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P<.001). Friedman tests followed by Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (2-sided α=.05) showed baseline-to-final median within-participant changes of 8.0 Medical Research Council Sum Score points (IQR 2.3-10.3; 95% CI 4.0-10.0, P=.004), 2.0 Intensive Care Unit Mobility Scale points (IQR 1.0-4.3; 95% CI 1.0-3.5, P<.001), and 15.0 EQ-VAS points (IQR 0.0-30.0; 95% CI 5.0-25.0, P=.009). Questionnaire responses were favorable. Under therapist supervision, the individually prescribed in-bed NFA program showed favorable operational feasibility, with no session-terminating adverse events. By combining the accessibility of a commercial off-the-shelf exergame with individualized exercise prescription, the program extended bedside exergaming to posttransplant inpatients with substantial functional impairment after ICU care who had not achieved independent ambulation.

42902407.title: Severe perioperative immune-related adverse events requiring intensive care in patients with gastric cancer: a case series.
42902407.abstract: The treatment strategy for advanced gastric cancer is significantly changing with the development of immune checkpoint inhibitors. While the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors has been demonstrated, immune-related adverse events can present a wide spectrum of symptoms, ranging from mild and non-specific to severe symptoms. In some cases, intensive care unit management is required. Despite the widespread application of immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, perioperative immune-related adverse events remain under-reported and insufficiently discussed. Case 1 is a 46-year-old Japanese female underwent laparoscopic proximal gastrectomy after S-1, oxaliplatin plus nivolumab therapy for unresectable locally advanced esophagogastric junction cancer and developed diabetic ketoacidosis and fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus 37 days after surgery. Case 2 is a 78-year-old Japanese male underwent staging laparoscopy after S-1, oxaliplatin plus nivolumab therapy for unresectable advanced gastric cancer and developed fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus and bullous pemphigoid 13 days after surgery. Case 3 is a 64-year-old Japanese male underwent distal gastrectomy with D2 lymph node dissection and para-aortic lymph node sampling after S-1, oxaliplatin plus nivolumab therapy for unresectable advanced gastric cancer and developed clinically suspected immune-related encephalitis 2 days after surgery. All three patients required intensive care management with temporary ventilatory support. Appropriate treatment was performed, and all patients are alive and undergoing postoperative treatment. As immune checkpoint inhibitors are increasingly incorporated into multidisciplinary treatment for gastric cancer, surgeons may encounter severe perioperative immune-related adverse events requiring intensive care management. Awareness of these presentations and prompt multidisciplinary management may help facilitate early recognition and appropriate treatment.

42902175.title: Alcohol-positive polytrauma patients: injury patterns, ICU resource use and mortality at a German Level I trauma center.
42902175.abstract: In most countries, alcohol consumption is so culturally ingrained that even small amounts are permitted while driving. Even at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.5 g/L, ethanol impairs mental and cognitive performance. Studies from the US and Europe estimate that elevated blood alcohol levels may be detected in 10%-40% of all emergency department patients. Against this background, we investigated the impact of alcohol consumption on injury severity, injury patterns, as well as primary and secondary outcomes in polytrauma patients. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included patients admitted to a Level I trauma center via the trauma room and documented in the TraumaRegister DGU® between 2015 and 2023. Serum ethanol was determined routinely in all adolescent and adult trauma room patients. Patients without serum ethanol measurement or younger than 13 years were excluded. Patients with detectable serum ethanol (> 1 mg/dL, detection limit of the laboratory; ALC) were compared with patients without (noALC) using the χ² and Mann-Whitney U tests. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) and pre-injury ASA classification. A dose-response analysis was performed using serum ethanol categories. A total of 1,524 patients were analyzed: 431 (28.3%) were alcohol-positive (ALC) and 1,093 (71.7%) were not (noALC). ALC patients were younger, more often male and had a lower prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (p < 0.001), whereas the ISS did not differ (p = 0.396). They were more frequently victims of violent crime and were overrepresented among pedestrians and falls from < 3 m, whereas motorcyclists were more often sober. Alcohol-positive patients were more often treated in the ICU (90.0% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.048), but this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40; 95% CI 0.96-2.03). Length of ICU stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ, and alcohol was not independently associated with mortality (aOR 0.91; 95% CI 0.56-1.47). Severe TBI was more frequent in alcohol-positive patients (38.5% vs. 29.5%), increased with serum ethanol concentration, and was the strongest predictor of ICU treatment and mortality. Nearly one in three severely injured patients had detectable serum ethanol. After adjustment for confounders, alcohol was not independently associated with mortality or intensive care resource use, and no dose-response relationship was found for these outcomes. The more frequent ICU treatment of alcohol-positive patients appears to be explained by their distinct injury pattern, particularly the concentration-dependent increase in severe TBI.

42901551.title: Impact of an early extended rehabilitation programme combining individually tailored nutrition and physical activity on patient outcomes after invasive mechanical ventilation and vasopressor therapy in the ICU: design and conduct of a multicentre, randomised, controlled, open-label, assessor-blinded trial (NUTRIREA-4).
42901551.abstract: Survivors of severe critical illness often experience long-lasting physical, quality of life and psychological impairments. Intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired weakness develops early and is associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, delayed functional recovery, impaired quality of life and greater healthcare utilisation. Nutritional support and early mobilisation are considered key components of ICU care. However, trials have evaluated either nutritional or physical rehabilitation strategies and have not consistently demonstrated long-term benefits. A strong physiological rationale exists for combining nutritional therapy and structured physical rehabilitation. Moreover, most interventions were limited to the ICU stay. The NUTRIREA-4 trial will assess whether an individualised, integrated rehabilitation strategy of nutritional support, physiotherapy and adapted physical activity initiated early in the ICU and continued throughout and after the hospital stay improves long-term physical performance and recovery. NUTRIREA-4 is the first large-scale multicentre randomised controlled trial evaluating such a comprehensive approach in survivors of severe critical illness. NUTRIREA-4 is a randomised controlled, multicentre, open-label trial comparing two parallel groups of patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation and vasopressor therapy for shock and randomised to either an individualised rehabilitation programme or usual care. The rehabilitation programme combines goal-directed nutritional support, physiotherapy and adapted physical activity delivered from ICU admission to 12 weeks after the return home. We will include 830 patients in 52 French ICUs. The primary endpoint is the 6-minute walk distance measured by blinded assessors 6 months after randomisation. Secondary outcomes include muscle strength, physical activity, nutritional intake, ICU-acquired infections, quality of life, mortality and psychological recovery. The NUTRIREA-4 trial has been approved by the appropriate ethics committee. Patients are included after informed consent according to French law. The results will be published in international peer-reviewed journals and presented at conferences. NCT06581939.

42898838.title: Burden and risk factors of acquisition of multi-drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria among intensive care patients at a tertiary care setting.
42898838.abstract: Multi-drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (MDR-GNB) are a major healthcare challenge, particularly among patients admitted to intensive care units (ICUs). The objective of the current study was to assess the risk of acquisition of MDR-GNB in ICU patients and the associated risk factors and outcomes. A prospective cohort study among adult ICU patients was conducted in two tertiary care hospitals in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between 2021 and 2022. Specimens were examined at admission, during stay, and before discharge for all patients. Acquisition of MDR-GNB was confirmed by a positive culture/polymerase chain reaction before discharge among patients who were negative at admission. A total of 307 patients were included. The mean age was 56.7 ± 18.2 years and 62.2% were males. Out of 307, 82 (26.7%) patients acquired MDR-GNB during their ICU stay. The most common MDR-GNB pathogens were Klebsiella spp. (47.1%), Acinetobacter spp. (14.7%), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (12.7%), Enterobacter spp. (10.8%), and Escherichia coli (5.9%). Approximately 40.2% of MDR-GNB presented as infection and 59.8% as colonization. In multi-variate analysis, the following variables were independent predictors of MDR-GNB acquisition; pneumonia at admission, central line use, urinary catheter use, renal comorbidity, and prolonged hospitalization. Patients who acquired MDR-GNB had significantly higher mortality (34.1% vs 5.3%, P<0.001) and ICU length of stay (median of 26 vs 10 days, P<0.001). The findings underscore the high risk and burden of MDR-GNB acquisition in the ICU setting. There is an urgent need for enhanced infection control strategies and antimicrobial stewardship activities to reduce MDR-GNB acquisition and its negative impact.

42897792.title: Association Between Oral Health Status at Admission and Length of Hospital Stay in the Intensive Care Unit: A Retrospective Cohort Study (2024-2025).
42897792.abstract: Poor oral health is linked to prolonged hospitalization, but critical care data from Latin America remain virtually absent. This study characterized baseline oral health at intensive care unit (ICU) admission in a Chilean center and evaluated its association with ICU length of stay (LOS). A retrospective cohort study was conducted including first-admission adults (n = 105). Bedside clinical examinations at admission assessed the WHO Decayed, Missing, and Filled Teeth (DMFT) index, gingival inflammation, and salivary hypofunction. Adjusted associations with ICU LOS were evaluated using multivariable ordinary least squares (OLS) regression. At admission, gingival inflammation and salivary hypofunction were each present in 90.5% of patients. The mean DMFT was 8.87 ± 9.40. In multivariable analysis, the DMFT index was not associated with ICU LOS (β = -0.050, 95% CI [-0.187, 0.087], p = 0.477). Mechanical ventilation status emerged as the sole independent predictor of prolonged stay (β = 3.30 days, 95% CI [0.75, 5.85], p = 0.013). Results were robust across five sensitivity analyses. Despite a remarkably high baseline burden of oral disease at ICU admission, chronic caries experience was not independently associated with ICU LOS, which was driven primarily by ventilatory support.

42895987.title: Postregistration Training and Competency Assessment of Intensive Care Unit Physiotherapists: A Scoping Review.
42895987.journal: The Journal of continuing education in the health professions
42895987.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) physiotherapy practice requires additional skills and knowledge that is not mandated within entry-level physiotherapy education. Therefore, the training of ICU physiotherapists occurs in the workplace. The need to standardize the training requirements has led researchers to develop minimum practice standards. The extent to which these minimum practice standards are used in ICU training programs remains unclear. The aim of this review was to identify ICU physiotherapy training programs that use minimum practice standards for trainees. A scoping review following the Johanna Briggs Institute methodology was conducted. Six bibliographic databases and university and professional association websites were searched for ICU physiotherapy minimum practice standards and education programs. Two authors screened all relevant articles for inclusion, and data on setting, minimum standards, training-program duration, and qualifications/titles recognized were extracted. Twenty-two studies met the inclusion criteria from the 2081 screened studies. These comprised 12 standalone minimum practice standards, 9 standalone education programs, and one combined standard and education program from both published and gray literature sources. Only one study reported an education program that used a minimum performance standard. Qualification on completion varied between education program types. Minimum practice standards are rarely used in ICU physiotherapy training. To support high-quality care, an ICU physiotherapy training program that integrates minimum performance standards should be developed. Accreditation of such a program may assist in supporting recognition between centers.

42894097.title: Sedation strategy and the search for a better patient experience in ICU.

42893350.title: Efficacy and Safety of Etomidate Versus Ketamine for Endotracheal Intubation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42893350.abstract: Rapid sequence intubation (RSI) is a commonly used technique for critically ill patients requiring emergency intubation, and the choice of induction agent is crucial for minimizing peri-intubation morbidity and maintaining hemodynamic stability. The most commonly used induction agents are etomidate and ketamine, although controversy remains about their effectiveness and safety. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis compared the efficacy and safety of etomidate versus ketamine for endotracheal intubation in critically ill patients. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2000 and May 2026 were systematically searched in PubMed, The Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect. The included studies compared etomidate with ketamine for emergency endotracheal intubation in critically ill adults. We analyzed data with RevMan 5.4 and Mantel-Haenszel random-effects models and calculated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Seven RCTs involving 5234 patients were included in the final analysis. No significant difference was observed between etomidate and ketamine regarding 28-day mortality (RR 1.01; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93-1.10; p=0.84), cardiac arrest (RR 0.91; 95% CI 0.62-1.34; p = 0.64), failed intubation (RR 1.09; 95% CI 0.68-1.76; p=0.71), or vasopressor requirement (RR 1.27; 95% CI 0.94-1.72; p=0.13). Sensitivity analyses suggested possible hemodynamic differences between the two agents, which should be interpreted cautiously, and etomidate was relatively cardiovascularly stable in some analyses. Overall, etomidate and ketamine showed similar efficacy and safety for endotracheal intubation in critically ill patients. No statistically significant differences were observed between the two agents in mortality, cardiac arrest, failed intubation, or vasopressor use. Thus, clinicians should choose the induction agent on a case-by-case basis, based on patient, hemodynamic, and clinician-specific factors. Randomized trials in selected critically ill patient populations should be conducted on a larger scale.

42893059.title: Incidence and mortality of invasive fungal infections among patients admitted in intensive care units in India: findings from a multicentric registry-based study (2023-25).
42893059.journal: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia
42893059.abstract: Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) are challenging to treat in critical care, particularly among patients treated in Intensive care units (ICUs). The existing evidence on IFIs from India remains fragmented. This study characterises IFI incidence, risk factors, resistance pattern, treatment and outcome among patients admitted to ICUs. This multicentre observational study leveraged registry data on IFIs among patients admitted to 63 ICUs in eight Advanced Mycology Diagnostic and Research centres in India between January 2023 and November 2025. Patients with proven and probable IFI according to European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer/Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (EORTC/MSGERC) 2020 and the modified Aspergillus intensive care unit (AspICU) 2020 criteria were included. IFI incidence to hospital admission, all-cause in-hospital mortality, pathogen distribution and antifungal susceptibility were recorded. Mortality-associated factors were estimated using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards analysis. Among 178,417 ICU admissions, 2500 IFI patients were identified with an incidence of 14/1000 admissions (95% CI 13.5-14.6) and all-cause mortality of 53.6% (95% CI 51.7-55.6%). Invasive candidiasis was the most frequently reported (57.1%), followed by invasive aspergillosis (37%), mucormycosis (3.4%), trichosporonosis (1.8%), pneumocystis pneumonia (1.1%), and cryptococcosis (1.2%). Median age of the patients was 45 years (IQR: 26-60), with 61.9% males and 38.1% females. Among candidiasis, Candida tropicalis predominated (35.6%), while Candida auris exhibited high fluconazole resistance (61.7%) and elevated amphotericin B minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) (40.7%). Aspergillus fumigatus (50.8%) and Aspergillus flavus (38.7%) predominated among culture-positive aspergillosis, with generally low MICs. Exploratory multivariable analyses showed that sepsis, chronic liver disease, immunosuppression, corticosteroid exposure, and total parenteral nutrition were associated with higher mortality in invasive candidiasis, whereas mechanical ventilation, corticosteroid exposure, and immunosuppression were associated with higher mortality in invasive aspergillosis. The study findings highlight a high IFI burden and mortality among patients admitted in ICUs of India, with mortality exceeding 50%, underscoring the need for continuous surveillance, rapid diagnostics, infection control and antifungal stewardship. This study was funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Delhi (Grant ID: 157401).

42892527.title: Octreotide Plus Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) versus PPI alone in Non-Variceal Upper gastrointestinal (GI) Bleeding in intensive care unit (ICU): A Multi-Center Randomized Trial.
42892527.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
42892527.abstract: To compare clinical outcomes between PPI therapy alone and PPI combined with octreotide in patients with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. This prospective, randomized, double-blind, multi-center study included 56 patients allocated to either PPI alone or PPI plus octreotide. Baseline demographics and comorbidities were comparable between groups. Laboratory parameters were assessed over three days. Clinical outcomes included rebleeding, transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation, surgical intervention, ICU stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Prothrombin time was significantly higher in the PPI plus octreotide group (median 19 s vs 11.1 s; p=0.001), and urine output was significantly lower (p=0.011). Despite these differences, there were no significant differences in rebleeding rates, blood product transfusion, ICU stay, mechanical ventilation, or need for surgery. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in the PPI plus octreotide group (39.3% vs 7%; p=0.011). Hospital length of stay was significantly shorter in the PPI plus octreotide group, likely reflecting higher early mortality rather than improved clinical recovery. The addition of octreotide to PPI therapy did not improve bleeding-related outcomes. Prolonged prothrombin time did not correlate with increased bleeding or transfusion needs. These findings suggest no clinical benefit of adjunctive octreotide in this study and underscore the importance of appropriate patient selection.

42892215.title: Indications for flexible bronchoscopy in elderly patients (≥ 75 years) with hypoxemic respiratory failure not eligible for intensive care: Expert opinion based on a Delphi study.
42892215.abstract: The indications for flexible bronchoscopy (FB) remain poorly defined in elderly patients (≥ 75 years) with hypoxemic respiratory failure (HRF) (O₂ ≥ 5 L/min) who are not eligible for intensive care. The lack of specific data highlights the need to develop evidence-based recommendations in this setting.
