We report a large single-center cohort of patients undergoing TAxA minimally invasive mitral valve surgery and evaluate early safety, procedural efficacy, recovery and mid-term outcomes. Consecutive patients who underwent TAxA mitral valve surgery at the University Hospital of Marche, Ancona, Italy, between January 2017 and April 2026 were included. Mitral repair or replacement procedures were considered with or without concomitant tricuspid valve repair, atrial fibrillation ablation or left atrial appendage occlusion. Early outcomes were analyzed in the overall cohort. Mid-term survival and reoperation were assessed in patients undergoing repair for degenerative mitral regurgitation. The study included 763 patients. Mitral valve repair was performed in 640 patients and replacement in 123. The repair rate was 89% in patients with mitral regurgitation and 92% in patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation. Concomitant tricuspid repair, atrial fibrillation ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion were performed in 17%, 5% and 10% of patients, respectively. Mean cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were 103 and 63 minutes. Thirty-day mortality was 0.4%, stroke or transient ischemic attack occurred in 0.7%, and conversion to sternotomy was required in 0.7%; no conversion was due to poor exposure. Median ventilation time was 2 [interquartile range (IQR), 0-6] hours, 54% of patients were extubated in theatre and 80% were extubated within 6 hours. Median intensive care unit and hospital stays were 24 (IQR, 22-48) hours and 7 (IQR, 6-9) days. In the degenerative repair cohort, Kaplan-Meier survival was 97.0% at 5 years, and cumulative incidence of reoperation was 4.3% at 5 years. In this large contemporary experience, TAxA minimally invasive mitral valve surgery was associated with low early mortality and morbidity, reasonable operative times, frequent ultra fast-track extubation, and satisfactory mid-term results.

42870652.title: Long-Term Impact of Timing on Spinal Implantation for Lumbar Fractures in Polytrauma Patients: A Systematic Review.
42870652.journal: Journal of long-term effects of medical implants
42870652.abstract: The timing of osteosynthesis in polytrauma patients with lumbar spine fractures may influence key clinical outcomes, including hospital length of stay (HLOS), ICU length of stay (ICULOS), and mechanical ventilation duration (VENT DAYS). This systematic review aimed to evaluate how surgical timing affects these outcomes. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and CENTRAL was completed in February 2025. Inclusion criteria involved studies on adult polytrauma patients (> 18 years) with lumbar spine fractures from blunt trauma, requiring surgical fixation, comparing early ( 72 h) surgery. Studies had to report Injury Severity Scores (ISS), outcomes of interest (HLOS, ICULOS, and VENT DAYS), include statistical comparisons between groups, and meet a minimum of "moderate" risk of bias based on the ROBINS-I tool. Out of 588 studies initially identified, three fulfilled the inclusion criteria, involving 1,111 patients-759 underwent early fixation and 352 late. The weighted average age was 39.1 years in the early group and 41.2 years in the late group. The weighted average ISS was 27.3 (early) and 29.2 (late). The weighted average VENT DAYS was 4.9 in the early group and 7.8 in the late group. The weighted average ICULOS was 10.9 d (early) and 13.7 d (late). The weighted average HLOS was 37.9 d (early) and 36.8 d (late). The impact of osteosynthesis on VENT DAYS and ICULOS remains uncertain, while HLOS shows no clinically relevant difference. ISS significantly influences outcomes.

42870570.title: Burden of healthcare-associated infections in tertiary care hospitals in six countries of the Gulf Cooperation Council: A point prevalence survey.
42870570.abstract: A cross-sectional study using point prevalence survey (PPS) methodology was conducted on May 20, 2024, at 18 tertiary care hospitals located in the 6 Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to assess the prevalence of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and associated pathogens. The measured outcome was the presence of active HAIs in different hospital units. During the PPS day, 651 HAI events were detected among 580 patients after reviewing the information of 6826 patients. The prevalence of patients with HAIs was 8.5% (95% CI 7.8%-9.2%). The prevalence was higher in older patients (11.8%, 95% CI 10.2%-13.4%), in intensive care units (24.6%, 95% CI 21.5%-27.8%), and in specialty care areas (12.7%, 95% CI 9.8%-15.7%). The most frequent type of HAIs was pneumonia (27.8%), followed by bloodstream infection (25.0%), urinary tract infection (10.9%), and skin infection (9.7%). Device-associated HAIs represented 15.4% of all HAIs, with ventilator-associated pneumonia, central line-associated bloodstream infection, and catheter-associated urinary tract infection being the main types. Approximately 61.9% of HAIs were microbiologically confirmed. Out of them, 65.3% were caused by Gram-negative bacteria and 31.8% were caused by multidrug-resistant pathogens. The findings confirm that the high HAI burden in GCC hospitals is higher in high-resource countries but lower in lower/middle-resource countries.

42869871.title: High-dose sulbactam for extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infection in patients with critical illness.
42869871.journal: Journal of infection and public health
42869871.abstract: The therapeutic effect and tolerability of sulbactam, at a daily dose of at least 9 g, were assessed in critically ill individuals who acquired extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (XDR-AB) infection. This single-center retrospective cohort evaluated a primary composite endpoint of death from any cause or invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) within 28 days. Secondary endpoints comprising the 14-day composite outcome, IMV-free and ICU-free days through day 28. The study cohort comprised 114 patients diagnosed with XDR-AB infection, of whom 72 (63.2%) received high-dose SBT-containing therapy. The high-dose SBT group showed a lower incidence of the composite outcomes, a higher IMV-free rate, and more IMV-free days through 28 days, with consistent results after adjustment using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) or the overlap weighting (OW) approach. The observed association of high-dose SBT did not differ significantly by concomitant antibiotic regimen. Within-regimen analysis showed that patients receiving polymyxin B plus high-dose SBT had more IMV-free days through day 28 (mean difference 4.0 days, P = 0.025). No increased signal of nephrotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, or other SBT-related adverse events was observed during the 7-day monitoring period. With both high-dose and low-dose SBT combined with comparable antimicrobial regimens, the high-dose group was associated with potentially better outcomes, with no increased signal of adverse events. The observed association was independent of concomitant antibiotic choice, with more IMV-free days in the polymyxin B subgroup. These findings suggest high-dose SBT could serve as a therapeutic option in patients with critical illness who have XDR-AB infection.

42869495.title: Effect of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on perioperative psychological symptoms in patients undergoing elective thoracoscopic lung resection: A randomized controlled trial.
42869495.abstract: Perioperative anxiety is highly prevalent in patients undergoing thoracoscopic lung resection, adversely affecting postoperative recovery. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has emerged as a promising noninvasive neuromodulatory intervention with demonstrated efficacy in various psychiatric and stress-related conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of taVNS in reducing perioperative anxiety in this population. This single-center, parallel-group, randomized, double-blind, superiority trial was conducted at the Department of Anesthesiology and Thoracic Surgery, the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University between October 10, 2024, and April 30, 2025. A total of 176 eligible patients aged ≥18 years with ASA physical status I-III and scheduled for elective thoracoscopic lung resection were enrolled. Patients with neuropsychiatric disorders, auricular lesions, severe cardio-cerebrovascular diseases, implanted electronic devices, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score <15, long-term psychotropic medication use or postural tachycardia syndrome were excluded. All participants were randomly allocated to receive four sessions of either active taVNS or sham taVNS. Stimulation was delivered via the auricular branch of the vagus nerve at the cymba conchae of the left ear at four predefined perioperative time points: the afternoon before surgery, the morning of surgery, immediately after tracheal extubation, and the afternoon of the first postoperative day. The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative anxiety, assessed from the initiation of the first taVNS session through 3 days postoperatively. All participants, healthcare providers, outcome assessors and data analysts were blinded to group assignment during the whole study. A total of 176 patients were randomly assigned, with 88 participants in the active taVNS group and 88 in the sham taVNS group. After excluding 2 patients (1 patient from each group) who were transferred to the ICU postoperatively, a total of 174 patients (median age, 58 years; 105 women [60.4%]) completed the study and were analysed for the primary outcome, including 87 patients in each group. The incidence of perioperative anxiety was significantly lower in the active taVNS group than in the sham taVNS group (50.6% vs. 73.6%; relative risk [RR], 0.59; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.41-0.85; χ2 = 9.76; P = 0.002). Compared with sham stimulation, active taVNS was associated with reductions in anxiety and depression scores, postoperative pain intensity, and physiological stress indices and improvement in sleep quality and overall postoperative recovery. No severe adverse events were observed in either group. The main mild adverse reactions included nausea, vomiting, local tingling, dizziness and headache, and the incidence of adverse events was similar between the two groups. Four perioperative sessions of taVNS applied to the left cymba conchae significantly reduced the incidence of perioperative anxiety in patients undergoing thoracoscopic lung resection and were additionally associated with improvements in depressive symptoms, stress burden, sleep quality, and pain outcomes. Chinese Clinical Trial Register Identifier: ChiCTR2400090542 (http://www.chictr.org.cn).

42866661.title: Phaeochromocytoma Crisis Presenting As Inverted Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy in a Young Woman: A Successful Outcome.
42866661.abstract: Phaeochromocytoma crisis is a rare, life-threatening endocrine emergency characterised by profound haemodynamic instability and multiorgan dysfunction. We report the case of a previously healthy 31-year-old woman who presented with sudden-onset cardiopulmonary decompensation, marked blood-pressure variability, pulmonary oedema, and cardiogenic shock, with biochemical evidence of myocardial injury. Echocardiography demonstrated apical hypercontractility with akinesia of the basal and midventricular segments and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%, consistent with reverse takotsubo cardiomyopathy. Cross-sectional imaging revealed a large 9 cm left adrenal mass, which, together with markedly elevated plasma and urinary metanephrines, confirmed the diagnosis of phaeochromocytoma crisis. The patient required mechanical ventilation, vasoactive support, and intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation. Following successful resuscitation and stabilisation with α- and β-adrenergic blockade, she underwent elective laparoscopic left adrenalectomy. Histopathological examination confirmed a high-risk phaeochromocytoma, while genetic testing was negative. Postoperatively, metanephrine concentrations normalised and bi-ventricular cardiac function recovered completely. This case highlights the importance of considering phaeochromocytoma crisis in patients presenting with otherwise unexplained haemodynamic instability and stress cardiomyopathy. Early recognition, multidisciplinary critical care, appropriate adrenergic blockade, and timely definitive surgery are essential and can be lifesaving.

42866292.title: Video-assisted thoracoscopic diaphragmatic plication in a ventilator-dependent patient with an elevated and dysfunctional hemidiaphragm.
42866292.abstract: Unilateral hemidiaphragm dysfunction can reduce ventilatory reserve, but its contribution to weaning failure is difficult to isolate in a critically ill patient. A 61-year-old woman with asthma and a chronically elevated left hemidiaphragm developed severe pneumonia and acute hypercapnic respiratory failure, with an arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) of 164.9 millimeters of mercury (mmHg), followed by recurrent extubation failure and tracheostomy. Pulmonary embolism was excluded. Bronchoscopy, microbiological treatment, nutritional support, and treatment for suspected autoimmune disease improved several reversible problems, yet hypercapnia recurred during ventilator reduction. Prior imaging showed that the elevation predated the acute illness. Formal fluoroscopic sniff testing, diaphragm ultrasound, phrenic nerve studies, and complete ventilator-setting records were unavailable; the condition is therefore described cautiously as an elevated and dysfunctional hemidiaphragm, most consistent clinically with acquired paralysis rather than a true hernia. After multidisciplinary reassessment, three-port left video-assisted thoracoscopic diaphragmatic plication was performed under low-pressure capnothorax. The diaphragm was flattened with six rows of continuous nonabsorbable braided polyester suture, using repeated mattress-type bites reinforced with polytetrafluoroethylene pledgets. Operative time was 180 minutes. PaCO2 was 36.0 mmHg on postoperative day 1. Spontaneous-breathing trials began on postoperative day 2, and sustained side-arm oxygen through the tracheostomy began on postoperative day 7. Hypercapnic acidosis recurred on postoperative days 11-12 during ongoing pulmonary infection. She was transferred for rehabilitation off the ventilator on postoperative day 15 and remained off ventilatory support at last contact, with the tracheostomy still in place. This case does not establish that plication alone produced ventilator liberation. It shows how a familiar operation may be used after cautious selection to remove one potentially reversible mechanical burden in multifactorial weaning failure.

42864674.title: Robotic-assisted versus conventional coronary artery bypass grafting: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and trial sequential analysis of 39,918 patients.
42864674.abstract: Robotic-assisted coronary artery bypass grafting (RA-CABG) is an evolving minimally invasive alternative to conventional CABG (C-CABG), but comparative evidence remains fragmented. We conducted a comprehensive systematic review, meta-analysis, and trial sequential analysis to compare outcomes between RA-CABG and C-CABG. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science through January 2026. Studies comparing RA-CABG to C-CABG reporting at least one outcome of interest were eligible. Random-effects meta-analyses using DerSimonian-Laird estimators were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I. Trial sequential analysis evaluated the conclusiveness of cumulative evidence. Nine studies comprising 39,918 patients (13,638 RA-CABG; 26,280 C-CABG) were included. All included studies were observational in design, and long-term outcome data were sparse. RA-CABG was associated with significantly lower mortality (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.43-0.69; P < 0.001; I²=0%), atrial fibrillation (OR 0.53; P < 0.001), respiratory failure (OR 0.31; P < 0.001), blood transfusion (OR 0.28; P < 0.001), hospital length of stay (MD - 1.95 days; P < 0.001), and ICU stay (MD - 22.7 h; P < 0.001). Stroke showed a non-significant trend favoring RA-CABG (OR 0.76; P = 0.071). Trial sequential analysis confirmed conclusive evidence for mortality, atrial fibrillation, respiratory failure, and blood transfusion. Results were robust across sensitivity analyses. In this meta-analysis of observational studies, RA-CABG was associated with significantly improved short-term outcomes compared to C-CABG across multiple endpoints, with conclusive statistical evidence for four of seven binary outcomes. However, all included studies were observational, and these associations should be interpreted with caution given potential residual confounding and case-selection bias. Multicenter randomized trials with long-term follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

42864631.title: Early change in ventilatory ratio during prone positioning and 28-day mortality in patients with ARDS: a retrospective cohort study with exploratory eICU assessment.
42864631.abstract: Prone positioning (PP) improves outcomes in moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), but early bedside markers that reliably characterize physiological response remain uncertain. The ventilatory ratio (VR), calculated from minute ventilation, PaCO2, and predicted body weight, may capture ventilatory efficiency during PP. MIMIC-IV v3.1 was used as the primary retrospective cohort and eICU-CRD v2.0 as an exploratory cohort. Adult patients with moderate-to-severe ARDS receiving an initial PP session lasting at least 12 h were included. The primary exposure was exploratory VR response, defined as ∆VR% ≤ -20% using the nearest available post-PP VR within the predefined observation window. The minimum post-PP VR within 12 h was analyzed as a sensitivity definition. The primary MIMIC-IV cohort included 177 patients, with 73 deaths within 28 days. Only 6 patients were classified as VR responders under the primary nearest post-PP VR definition. Crude 28-day mortality was 33.3% among responders and 41.5% among non-responders; the unweighted Cox model did not show a statistically significant association (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.20-3.08; P = 0.737). Adjusted and IPTW-weighted models were considered exploratory and not reliably estimable because the responder group contained only 6 patients and 2 deaths. Sensitivity analyses using the minimum post-PP VR definition produced a stronger but definition-sensitive signal, whereas analyses using absolute VR change or baseline/post-PP VR did not confirm a stable association. In eICU-CRD, 29 patients had complete core VR data and only 3 were responders. Early VR change during PP was not significantly associated with 28-day mortality under the primary nearest post-PP VR definition. This study supports the feasibility of extracting dynamic VR metrics from routinely collected ICU data, but does not establish VR response as a validated prognostic marker or clinical threshold.

42862677.title: Understanding Anti-Diuretic Hormone Dynamics in Off pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (OPCABG) Patients: A Case Series.
42862677.abstract: The conundrum of Polyuria witnessed post-cardiac surgery has been attributed to altered antidiuretic hormone (ADH) release secondary to both osmotic and non-osmotic stimulus. This transient DI-like state is more often seen in on-bypass cardiac surgeries but a few off-bypass occurrences have also been reported. A lot of conflicting evidence has accumulated trying to explain this altered water balance but a broader conceptual framework is lacking, which we have attempted to provide, with an objective of designing a future prospective study. This prospective observational case-series included 12 cases, who underwent off pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG) at a single tertiary care hospital. All were operated and managed by the same anesthetist-cardiac surgeon team following a structured protocol, hence negating various confounders. Serum and urine osmolality samples were collected post-Intubation (Baseline) and within 1 hour of ICU-transfer and all relevant data associated with these cases was recorded for analysis. The data was systematically analyzed in terms of descriptives, paired T-test and correlation statistics. The pre-post serum osmolality was found to increase (P value 0.389, Cohen's d -0.26) whereas urine osmolality decreased significantly (P value 0.013, Cohen's d 0.85). This mean fall in urine osmolality was much higher compared to the rise seen in serum osmolality, both being negatively correlated (r -0.59, P value 0.04). This case series investigating the changes in osmolality alongside pre-perfusion reduced urine output and post-perfusion a state of polyuria, is our primer for a future assay-based objective study. We have created a framework of concepts that provide clarity to the dynamics of ADH-release in OPCABG patients. Furthermore, we are presenting a different hypothesis to explain increase in ADH-release that is evidence-based and open to critical comments.

42862674.title: Comparative Efficacy of Pecto-Intercostal Facial Plane Block vs Transversus Thoracic Facial Plane Block Combined with Rectus Sheath Block for Post-Sternotomy Analgesia: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
42862674.abstract: Ultrasound-guided facial plane blocks are central to enhanced recovery after cardiac surgery (ERACS) protocols, yet evidence comparing pecto-intercostal facial plane block (PIFB) and transversus thoracic facial plane block (TTPB) with rectus sheath block (RSB) remains limited. This prospective, randomized, controlled trial enrolled 100 adult patients (ASA II-III) undergoing elective median sternotomy at a tertiary care hospital in South India. Patients received standardized general anesthesia and were randomized to bilateral PIFB or TTPB (20 mL 0.25% bupivacaine + 4 mg dexamethasone per side) with RSB after cardiopulmonary bypass. The primary outcome was 24-hour postoperative fentanyl consumption. Secondary outcomes included visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores at 0, 3-, 6-, 12-, and 24-hours post-extubation, rescue analgesia, extubation timing, ICU/hospital stay, and complications. A total of 96 patients completed analysis (PIFB: n = 47; TTPB: n = 49). Mean 24-hour fentanyl consumption was 267.23 ± 92.54 µg (PIFB) vs 297.18 ± 88.09 µg (TTPB), mean difference - 29.95 µg (95% confidence interval: -66.60 to 6.70; P = 0.108). VAS scores showed no significant between-group differences (P > 0.05). Rescue analgesia rates were similar, with 84% and 90% not requiring additional opioids. Four PIFB patients (8%) stayed intubated >24 hours due to cardiac issues, vs none in the TTPB group (P = 0.121). This trial found no significant difference in opioid consumption or pain scores between PIFB + RSB and TTPB + RSB for post-sternotomy analgesia. Both techniques were safe within ERACS protocols. Larger noninferiority trials are needed before establishing equivalence or recommending one technique over another.

42862662.title: Impact of Erector Spinae Block on Postoperative Analgesia and Hospital Recovery in Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis, Meta-Regression, and Sequential Trial Analysis.
42862662.abstract: The erector spinae plane block (ESPB) is a promising regional technique for cardiac surgery. We evaluated the efficacy of ESPB regarding analgesia and in-hospital outcomes in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing ESPB versus control in adults undergoing CABG (CRD42025645045). Primary outcomes were opioid consumption (24 h/48 h) and pain intensity. Secondary outcomes included extubation time and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay. Data were pooled using random-effects models. Meta-regression and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were used to assess sources of heterogeneity and robustness, respectively, while the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations framework provided the certainty of the evidence for each outcome. Twelve studies (704 patients) were analyzed. ESPB significantly reduced the morphine milligram equivalent consumption at 24 h (mean difference (MD) -19.05 mg; 95% confidence interval (CI) [-22.50 to -15.61]; P < 0.001; high certainty) and 48 h (MD -19.42 mg; 95% CI [-28.75 to -10.09]; P < 0.001; moderate certainty). Pain scores, by the Numerical Rating Scale, were lower within 12 h (MD -0.93; P < 0.001; moderate certainty) and at 24 h (MD -0.58; P = 0.016; low certainty). ESPB shortened extubation time (MD -2.50 h; high certainty) and ICU stay (MD -12.55 h; moderate certainty). TSA confirmed robust evidence for opioid reduction, early pain relief, and extubation benefits. ESPB provides effective early analgesia, reduces perioperative opioid requirements, and accelerates recovery in CABG, representing a fundamental complement to conventional isolated intravenous analgesia. Future research should investigate continuous techniques.

42862032.title: Association between leukocytosis and adverse clinical outcomes in thrombocytopenic patients with acute pesticide poisoning: a cross-sectional study from a referral poisoning center in Iran.
42862032.journal: International journal of environmental health research
42862032.abstract: This study evaluated the association between leukocytosis and adverse clinical outcomes in patients with pesticide poisoning who also had thrombocytopenia. This cross-sectional study used medical records of patients who presented between 2016 and 2021, including 241 adult patients with confirmed pesticide poisoning. We extracted demographic data, clinical signs, laboratory parameters, and outcomes. We categorized hospitalization duration as >72 hours, 24-72 hours, and <24 hours. Leukocytosis was present in 43.2% of patients (n = 104). The overall mortality rate was 25.3% (n = 61), with 49.8% requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission (n = 120) and 44.4% requiring intubation (n = 107). Patients with elevated WBC had higher odds of prolonged hospitalization than those with normal counts: OR = 3.36, p = 0.004 for 24-72 h; and OR = 4.63, p < 0.001 for hospitalizations longer than 72 h. Leukocytosis was also strongly associated with intubation (OR = 3.50, p < 0.001) and ICU admission (OR = 3.58, p < 0.001). After adjustment, only ICU admission and leukocytosis remained significantly associated (OR = 2.20, p = 0.024). Leukocytosis may be a valuable parameter in predicting ICU admission and hospitalization duration in thrombocytopenic patients with acute pesticide poisoning. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed.

42861054.title: Prognostic value of pulmonary artery pulsatility index for perioperative adverse cardiovascular events in patients undergoing surgery for mitral regurgitation.
42861054.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
42861054.abstract: The pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi) demonstrates prognostic value across cardiopulmonary conditions, yet its utility in mitral regurgitation (MR) perioperative risk stratification remains undefined. This study aimed to evaluate whether the PAPi could independently predict perioperative adverse cardiovascular events in patients with MR, and to explore whether its addition to the European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II provided incremental value. This ambidirectional cohort study enrolled 302 consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe MR undergoing mitral valve surgery. PAPi was calculated as pulmonary artery pulse pressure (pulmonary artery systolic pressure minus diastolic pressure) divided by right atrial pressure, all estimated by echocardiography. Patients were grouped by PAPi tertiles and followed for 3 months. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Exploratory endpoints included mechanical ventilation duration and inotropic support. Incremental value was assessed by integrating PAPi into EuroSCORE II. Patients were stratified into low PAPi (<3.4, n=99), intermediate PAPi (3.4-4.8, n=101), and high PAPi (>4.8, n=102) groups. MACE incidence was 37.4% (37/99), 10.9% (11/101), and 3.9% (4/102), respectively (χ2=43.70, P<0.001). Lower PAPi was associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, inotropic support, and intensive care unit (ICU) stay (all P<0.001). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis showed that PAPi predicted MACE with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.82 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.76-0.88]. At cutoff 3.45, sensitivity was 81%, specificity 75%, positive predictive value (PPV) 40.0%, and negative predictive value (NPV) 94.9%. Bootstrap validation confirmed stability (AUC 0.82, 95% CI: 0.761-0.878). Multivariate analysis identified PAPi [odds ratio (OR) =0.26, 95% CI: 0.15-0.45, P<0.001], EuroSCORE II (OR=1.15, 95% CI: 1.03-1.28, P=0.012), and tricuspid annular plane systolicexcursion/pulmonary artery systolic pressure [TAPSE/PASP; OR =0.79 per 1-standard deviation (SD) decrease, 95% CI: 0.65-0.95, P=0.013] as independent predictors. Each 1-unit PAPi decrease was associated with a 3.8-fold increase in MACE risk. Adding PAPi to clinical risk score and echocardiographic right ventricular function models improved predictive performance [C-statistic 0.70 to 0.85; net reclassification improvement (NRI) =0.807; integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) =0.144; all P<0.001]. Bootstrap optimism correction yielded an AUC of 0.85 (95% CI: 0.80-0.90). Subgroup analyses showed consistent predictive value (all interaction P>0.05). The echocardiography-derived PAPi predicts perioperative MACE in patients with MR. Incorporation of this index into traditional risk scoring systems provides incremental value for preoperative risk assessment and facilitates the identification of high-risk patients.

42860369.title: Managing the Hospital Capacity Challenges of Medetomidine Withdrawal: A Retrospective Report of Dexmedetomidine Use in Intermediate Care Units.
42860369.abstract: Medetomidine, a veterinary alpha-2-adrenergic agonist, has emerged as a dominant adulterant in the Philadelphia illicit opioid supply, producing a severe withdrawal syndrome requiring significant inpatient support. We developed an intravenous dexmedetomidine protocol for intermediate care units (IMCU) and describe the safety and feasibility of delivering this care outside the intensive care unit (ICU). A retrospective descriptive analysis of patients who received dexmedetomidine under an IMCU orderset for alpha-2 withdrawal was conducted at two urban medical centers in Philadelphia, PA, from April 2024 to February 2026. Encounters were classified as protocol-concordant or protocol-discordant by dosing and level of support; the concordant cohort was primary. Variables included demographics and addiction consult status. Outcomes included length of stay (hospital and IMCU), ICU admission, rapid response team activation, intubation, and discharge disposition. Of 487 encounters, 449 (92.2%) were protocol-concordant and 38 (7.8%) protocol-discordant. All subsequent results describe the protocol-concordant cohort (n=449) unless otherwise noted. The cohort was predominantly male (58.1%) with a mean age of 41.8 years. Median hospital stay was 6.0 days and median IMCU stay was 2.2 days. ICU admission was not required in 50.1% of encounters. Rapid response team activation occurred in 38 encounters (8.5%), the majority for escalating withdrawal management. Patient-directed discharge occurred in 41.4% of encounters. An IMCU dexmedetomidine protocol deployed across seven monitored units at 2 hospitals offers a replicable framework for managing medetomidine withdrawal while potentially mitigating critical care capacity challenges. Identified opportunities include modification of titration and dosing strategies and further investment in addiction consult infrastructure.

42859976.title: [Successful treatment of hypokalemic cardiac arrest with massive potassium replacement in a patient with Bricker urinary diversion].
42859976.abstract: Severe hypokalemia is a rare but potentially reversible cause of malignant arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Early recognition of significant fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base disturbances in patients with intestinal urinary diversion may be life-saving. We present the clinical course of a 55-year-old woman who developed severe hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and extreme hypokalemia following prolonged vomiting and high-output fluid loss through a Bricker ureteroileocutaneostomy. The patient was admitted to the intensive care unit in a peri-arrest condition, where cardiac arrest occurred shortly thereafter. The monitored rhythm was ventricular fibrillation alternating with "torsade de pointes" ventricular fibrillation. During advanced life support, targeted high-dose intravenous potassium replacement, magnesium sulfate administration, and bicarbonate substitution were performed. A total of 120 mL of 7.4% potassium chloride was administered during resuscitation, resulting in return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 18 minutes. During the first 24 hours, a total of 460 mmol potassium chloride replacement was required. Following the return of spontaneous circulation, intermittent hemodialysis was performed to correct severe metabolic acidosis. During subsequent intensive care treatment, sepsis and bilateral pneumonia developed; however, with targeted antimicrobial therapy, organ support, and continuous electrolyte correction, the patient's condition gradually improved. Successful extubation was performed on day 7, and the patient was transferred back to the nephrology ward with favourable neurological outcome. This case highlights that rapidly developing severe hypokalaemia and metabolic acidosis in patients with Bricker urinary diversion may lead to malignant arrhythmias and cardiac arrest; however, prompt recognition of reversible metabolic abnormalities and aggressive targeted potassium replacement can be life-saving. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(41): 1664-1668.

42859838.title: Mass Effect Score Associations in Comatose Trauma Patients With Intracranial Hemorrhage Requiring Mechanical Ventilation: A Retrospective Study.
42859838.abstract: Objective There is a paucity of studies evaluating computed tomography (CT) scores in patients with Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores of 3-8. This study assessed the associations between risk factors (including admission GCS score, head Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) score, brain mass effect score (MES), and age) and unfavorable outcomes (including in-hospital mortality, adverse outcomes, failure to follow commands at hospital discharge, and failure to follow commands at three months) in mechanically ventilated patients with intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) and GCS scores of 3-8. In relation to these outcomes, we also compared the MES with the Marshall (MAR) classification and Rotterdam (ROT) score. Methods The adult blunt trauma cohort had ICH, GCS 3-8, need for mechanical ventilation, and level I trauma center admission (2018-2024). The GCS, age, AIS, ventilator status, intensive care unit (ICU) stay, hospital stay, and hospital mortality were obtained from the trauma registry. Adverse outcomes included hospital death, ICU stay ≥18 days, or hospital stay >20 days. MES indicated the presence (1) or absence (0) for each of the following: basal cistern compression, midline shift, and lateral ventricle compression (0-3). Brain CT images were reviewed to compute MES, MAR, and ROT. Electronic medical records (EMRs) were reviewed to determine following command status at hospital discharge and at three months after injury. Results Among the 148 blunt trauma patients, univariate associations with mortality were MES (p < 0.01), GCS (p = 0.46), age ≥70 (p < 0.01), and AIS (p < 0.01); multivariate associations were MES (p < 0.01), age ≥70 (p < 0.01), and AIS (p > 0.10). For adverse outcomes, univariate associations were MES (p < 0.01), GCS (p = 0.46), age ≥70 (p = 0.04), and AIS (p < 0.01); multivariate associations were MES (p < 0.01), age ≥70 (p > 0.05), and AIS (p > 0.05). For failure to follow commands at discharge, univariate associations were MES (p < 0.01), GCS (p = 0.75), age (p = 0.01), and AIS (p < 0.01); multivariate associations were MES (p < 0.01), age (p = 0.01), and AIS (p > 0.10). For failure to follow commands at three months, univariate associations were MES (p < 0.01), GCS (p = 0.30), age (p < 0.01), and AIS (p < 0.01); multivariate associations were MES (p < 0.01), age (p < 0.01), and AIS (p > 0.10). MES correlated strongly with MAR (p < 0.01; r = 0.83) and ROT (p < 0.01; r = 0.82). In multivariate stepwise continuous score regression (MCR), mortality and adverse outcome were associated with MES (both p < 0.01), but not MAR or ROT (both p > 0.05). For failure to follow commands at discharge and three months, MCR showed an association with ROT (both p < 0.01), but not MES or MAR (both p > 0.05). In multivariate stepwise dichotomous score regression (MDR), mortality and adverse outcomes were associated with MES ≥2 (both p < 0.01), but not MAR ≥4 or ROT ≥4 (both p > 0.05). Failure to follow commands at discharge was associated with ROT ≥4 (p < 0.01), but not MES ≥2 or MAR ≥4 (p > 0.05). Failure to follow commands at three months was associated with MES ≥2 (p < 0.01), but not MAR ≥4 or ROT ≥4 (p > 0.05). Conclusions MES was a better predictor of adverse outcomes than AIS and GCS in comatose patients with ICH. MES was competitive with other established brain CT scores for predicting adverse outcomes. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

42859827.title: Disseminated Pulmonary Coccidioidomycosis Presenting as a Wedge-Shaped Necrotic Mass Mimicking Malignancy.
42859827.abstract: Coccidioidomycosis is an endemic fungal infection of the southwestern United States that may rarely produce mass-like pulmonary abnormalities mimicking malignancy. We describe a 70-year-old Hispanic woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c >14%) who presented after three days of generalized weakness, nonproductive cough, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and progressive difficulty ambulating. CT demonstrated a 7.3 × 5.4 cm wedge-shaped necrotic right middle lobe mass with multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules. CT-guided biopsy of the mass demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with fungal elements, while subsequent serologic testing and bronchoalveolar lavage PCR supported pulmonary coccidioidomycosis. Her hospitalization was complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, prone positioning, and neuromuscular blockade; non-liposomal amphotericin B-associated acute tubular necrosis requiring hemodialysis; ventilator-associated Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia; and persistent encephalopathy with multifocal MRI abnormalities highly suggestive of central nervous system dissemination despite nondiagnostic cerebrospinal fluid studies. This case highlights how pulmonary coccidioidomycosis can mimic malignancy. It illustrates the multifactorial deterioration that may occur in susceptible hosts, emphasizing early tissue diagnosis, careful interpretation of suspected dissemination, and individualized antifungal and critical care management.

42859749.title: Diaphragmatic Rapid Shallow Breathing Index Versus Diaphragmatic Thickness Fraction for Predicting Weaning Success in Mechanically Ventilated Patients.
42859749.abstract: Introduction Timely liberation from mechanical ventilation is a central goal of critical care. This study aimed to compare two point-of-care ultrasound indices, the diaphragmatic rapid shallow breathing index (D-RSBI) and the diaphragmatic thickness fraction (DTF), in predicting successful weaning among mechanically ventilated adults. Methods In this prospective, single-center diagnostic-accuracy study, 44 adults who were mechanically ventilated for more than 48 hours but fewer than seven days and who met the readiness criteria for a spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) underwent diaphragm and lung ultrasound before the trial. Weaning outcomes were categorized using the Weaning according to a New Definition (WIND) framework; successful weaning (simple or difficult categories, n = 36) was the reference standard, whereas prolonged weaning (n = 8) was considered the adverse outcome. Diagnostic performance was assessed at operating thresholds and by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and the two indices were compared using the DeLong test (SPSS Statistics v23 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY); MedCalc (Ostend, Belgium)). Results At a threshold of 1.2 breaths/min/mm, the D-RSBI showed strong diagnostic performance for successful weaning, with a sensitivity of 94.44% and specificity of 100% (area under the curve (AUC): 0.99, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.97-1.00). The DTF discriminated poorly (sensitivity: 61.11%, specificity: 62.50%; AUC: 0.65, 95% CI: 0.42-0.88). The D-RSBI AUC was significantly higher than that of the DTF (DeLong p = 0.004). Notably, all eight patients with prolonged/failed weaning were also the eight most severely ill patients according to the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score (APACHE II score, 13-21 vs. ≤ 10 in every patient who succeeded), and the direction of association for both indices was opposite to that reported in previous literature. Conclusions In this cohort, a D-RSBI ≥ 1.2 was strongly associated with successful weaning and outperformed the DTF. However, weaning outcome was completely determined by illness severity in this cohort, and the direction of the associations for both indices was inverted relative to prior studies. Therefore, these findings must be interpreted with caution and require validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

42859704.title: Application of Non-Invasive Cardiac Output Monitoring in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery for Patients With Acute Type A Aortic Dissection.
42859704.abstract: To assess the clinical value of non-invasive cardiac output monitoring (NICOM) within an enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocol for patients undergoing acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair. This study included 242 patients who underwent total arch replacement for ATAAD between January 2024 and June 2025. Patients were stratified into two groups based on postoperative NICOM use (NICOM group, n = 141; control group, n = 101). This study compared hemodynamic parameters, 6-minute walk test (6MWT) results, postoperative recovery, and complications. Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. While 30-day mortality and ventilator time were comparable, the NICOM group demonstrated significantly superior outcomes inintensive care unit (ICU) stays [3.0 (2.0-5.0) vs. 5.0 (3.0-8.0) days; p < 0.001] and hospitalization time [16.0 (11.0-21.0) vs. 19.0 (14.0-23.0) days; p = 0.001]. The NICOM group also showed lower unadjusted rates of reintubation (1.4% vs. 7.9%; p = 0.029), ICU readmission (2.1% vs. 8.9%; p = 0.036), shock (0.7% vs. 5.9%; p = 0.045), and acute heart failure (2.1% vs. 9.9%; p = 0.018), as well as a longer 6MWT distance at discharge [488.0 (433.0-532.0) vs. 457.0 (410.0-521.0) meters; p = 0.02]. However, after applying Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, only ICU stay and hospitalization time remained statistically significant; the differences in re‑intubation, ICU readmission, shock, acute heart failure, and 6MWT did not meet the corrected significance threshold. Integrating NICOM into the postoperative care of patients with ATAAD provides reliable, continuous hemodynamic data that facilitate precise, individualized management. This approach stabilizes circulation, reduces key complications, accelerates recovery, and improves perioperative outcomes, underscoring the vital role of this method in implementing ERAS protocols in cardiac surgery.

42859575.title: Severe Colchicine Toxicity After Ingestion of a Dose Below Traditionally Reported Lethal Levels: A Case Report.
42859575.abstract: Colchicine is a widely utilised drug for the management of conditions such as gout, pericarditis and familial Mediterranean fever. It has a narrow therapeutic index, with a significant risk of toxicity in overdose leading to life-threatening consequences. We present a case of severe colchicine toxicity following ingestion of 20 mg (0.26 mg/kg), resulting in multi-organ failure requiring intensive care management. Rapid deterioration with hyperthermia, electrolyte derangement, rhabdomyolysis, coagulopathy and significant bone marrow suppression necessitated IV antibiotics, platelet transfusion and granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (GCSF) and subsequent admission to critical care for vasopressors and ventilatory support. The patient eventually improved with resolution of haematological and renal parameters, was reviewed by the mental health team and discharged with full functional recovery. This case underscores the importance of early recognition, aggressive supportive care, and multidisciplinary management of patients presenting with colchicine overdose, in order to achieve a favourable outcome. The unpredictable relationship between colchicine dose and clinical outcome highlights the need for close monitoring even following relatively low-dose ingestion. Increased clinician awareness of colchicine toxicity and its delayed manifestations is essential for timely intervention in such critical cases.

42859454.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Early Warning Systems for Early Detection of Clinical Deterioration in Hospitalized Patients: Current Clinical Applications and Future Directions.
42859454.abstract: Early recognition of clinical deterioration in hospitalized patients is essential for preventing adverse events such as cardiac arrest, sepsis, respiratory failure and unplanned intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Traditional Early Warning Systems (EWS), including the Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS) and National Early Warning Score (NEWS), are widely used to support bedside assessment through standardized evaluation of physiological parameters. However, conventional EWS are limited by intermittent monitoring, manual data entry and variable clinical interpretation. Recent advances in electronic health records, continuous physiological monitoring and artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled the development of AI-enhanced Early Warning Systems capable of real-time risk assessment and prediction of clinical deterioration before overt clinical manifestations occur. Machine learning algorithms can analyze large volumes of clinical data, identify subtle physiological trends and support earlier clinical intervention. Emerging evidence suggests that AI-enhanced EWS may improve rapid response activation, reduce ICU transfers, decrease in-hospital mortality and optimize workflow efficiency. This narrative review examines the evolution of EWS from traditional scoring systems to AI-driven predictive models, focusing on their current clinical applications in hospitalized adult patients. Particular emphasis is placed on practical implementation in routine clinical care, the role of nurses and multidisciplinary teams, interpretability of AI algorithms, ethical considerations and barriers to adoption. In addition, the review discusses the integration of AI-enhanced systems into clinical decision support pathways and highlights the importance of maintaining clinical judgment alongside technological innovation. AI-enhanced EWS should be viewed as decision-support tools that complement rather than replace healthcare professionals. Successful clinical implementation requires robust validation, interdisciplinary collaboration, organizational readiness and continuous staff education. When appropriately integrated into clinical workflows, AI-supported predictive systems may significantly contribute to earlier intervention and improved patient safety in acute hospital settings.

42859300.title: The impact of ventilation mode on systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction in a porcine model of abdominal sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome.
42859300.abstract: Sepsis commonly causes acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and immune hyperactivation may be a causal link. Ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) is common in ARDS, and VILI may potentiate organ dysfunction in severe sepsis. We used a porcine model of abdominal sepsis-associated ARDS to test whether ventilation strategy could impact systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction. Female Yorkshire pigs (6-8 months) underwent ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury of the small bowel and fecal clot implantation or sham laparotomy. The abdominal sepsis animals were ventilated with a volume-controlled (VC) mode using the ARDS-Net low tidal volume (LVt) method to set and adjust the mode, and applied at two time points. Late LVt, was applied once PaO2/FiO2 was ≤300, and Early LVt was applied immediately following injury. The third lung protective group used the airway pressure release ventilation (APRV) mode set and adjusted with the time-controlled adaptive ventilation (TCAV) method, also applied immediately after injury. Animals were supported for 48 h using standardized resuscitation protocols and euthanized. Physiologic variables, clinical lab data, lung histology, and plasma proteome were assessed. Sham animals showed no evidence of sepsis or ARDS, whereas all experimental animals developed septic shock, requiring fluid resuscitation and vasopressors. Both LVt groups developed ARDS as measured by PaO2/FiO2 ratio by the study end (Late LVt: 129.9±16.0; Early LVt: 205.2±24.2), while the Early APRV group did not (429.4±59.4). The Sham and experimental groups all had similar proteomes at baseline. The proteomes diverged over time and ended in three distinct groups: Sham, Late LVt/Early LVt, and Early APRV. The most significantly differentially expressed proteins distinguishing the groups were involved in the immune and inflammatory response, with APRV having the lowest inflammatory signature. In a porcine model of abdominal septic shock we found that animals ventilated with a higher mean airway pressure strategy (APRV) had decreased plasma proteomic signatures of inflammation compared to those ventilated with a conventional low tidal volume strategy. Our findings are hypothesis generating and not directly translatable to the clinical setting. Future studies should focus on further elucidating a link between VILI and its effect on systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction.

42859118.title: Biomarker profiles in COVID-19 and non-covid ARDS: Similar patterns with high-flow nasal cannula and mechanical ventilation, distinct by ARDS etiology.
42859118.abstract: Previous studies in non-COVID acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) demonstrated that hypoxemic patients treated with high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) and those receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (MV) have comparable biomarker profiles. We aimed to determine whether these findings apply to COVID-19 ARDS and to compare biomarker profiles between COVID-19 and non-COVID ARDS. Prospective cohort study. Medical-surgical intensive care units of two tertiary hospitals. Adults with COVID-19 ARDS managed with MV or HFNC and a previously published non-COVID ARDS cohort. None. Baseline demographics, clinical, respiratory hemodynamic, and laboratory variables were collected. Plasma concentrations of epithelial lung injury markers (receptor for advanced glycation end products [RAGE], surfactant protein D [SP-D]), endothelial injury marker (angiopoietin-2 [Ang-2]), and inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and IL-8) were measured. A total of 135 patients with COVID-19 were included (22 MV, 113 HFNC); 53 [46.9%] HFNC patients subsequently required intubation. In matched analyses, biomarker concentrations did not differ significantly between MV and HFNC groups. Within the HFNC cohort, higher RAGE concentrations were associated with HFNC failure [cutoff ≥ 3338.5 pg/mL; adjusted OR∼15 (95%CI 1.9-65.0)]. Patients with HFNC failure exhibited biomarker profiles similar to those of invasively ventilated patients. Comparison according to ARDS etiology showed higher RAGE and IL-6 concentrations in COVID-19 ARDS, whereas SP-D and Ang-2 concentrations were higher in non-COVID ARDS. Patients with COVID-19 acute hypoxemic respiratory failure managed with HFNC or MV exhibited broadly similar epithelial, endothelial and inflammatory biomarker profiles. These findings support further investigation into the inclusion of non-intubated patients fulfilling ARDS criteria apart from PEEP requirements within the ARDS spectrum. Differences in biomarker profiles between COVID-19 and non-COVID ARDS suggest biological heterogeneity according to ARDS etiology. Elevated RAGE concentrations were associated with HFNC failure and may reflect the prognostic relevance of epithelial injury in COVID-19 ARDS.

42855379.title: Injury patterns in a war zone: A comparative analysis of civilians and military personnel.
42855379.abstract: Modern armed conflicts increasingly affect both civilians and defense forces, resulting in heterogeneous injury patterns driven by diverse mechanisms. Direct comparative data between these populations treated within the same healthcare system remain limited. To compare injury mechanisms, anatomical injury patterns, injury severity, and early clinical outcomes between civilians and defense forces casualties treated at a single tertiary trauma center during an active conflict. A retrospective analysis was conducted of all consecutive war-related trauma admissions between October 7, 2023, and January 7, 2024. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, anatomical sites, Injury Severity Score (ISS), emergency interventions, and early outcomes were collected. Percentage-based comparative plots were used to visualize injury mechanism and anatomical site distributions. The cohort included 192 patients (128 defense forces, 64 civilians). Civilians were older and included more females. Overall injury severity and rates of airway management, ventilatory support, and ICU admission were comparable between groups. Defense forces more frequently required direct transfer from the emergency department to the operating room (28% vs. 14%, p = 0.047). Shrapnel-related injuries were significantly more common among defense forces, whereas acoustic trauma was observed exclusively among civilians (36%, p < 0.001). Injury-mechanism profiles differed between groups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the proportions of patients injured at the individual anatomical site. Despite similar overall injury severity, civilians and defense forces exhibit distinct injury profiles. Civilians are disproportionately affected by acoustic trauma, highlighting population-specific vulnerabilities with implications for triage, diagnostic evaluation, and trauma system preparedness, especially during mass casualty incidents, when rapid recognition of group-specific injury patterns is essential for appropriate resource prioritization and allocation.

42855134.title: Oral or Enteral Levothyroxine for Myxedema Coma When Intravenous Therapy Is Unavailable: A Systematic Review and Descriptive Evidence Synthesis.
42855134.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
42855134.abstract: Intravenous levothyroxine is generally preferred for myxedema coma but may be unavailable in many healthcare settings. We summarized published treatment regimens and outcomes with oral or enteral levothyroxine when intravenous therapy was unavailable. Intravenous-only and mixed-route reports were included for clinical context. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 2026. Studies reporting myxedema coma treated with oral, enteral, nasogastric, or intravenous levothyroxine and extractable clinical outcomes were included. Pooled proportions were calculated only as descriptive summaries of oral/enteral reports and were not interpreted as treatment-effect estimates. Intravenous-only and mixed-route studies were summarized narratively. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Nine studies comprising 70 patients were included: six oral/enteral, two intravenous-only, and one mixed-route study. Oral/enteral loading doses ranged from 300 to 1000 μg. Descriptively pooled proportions were 0.20 for mortality, 0.76 for intensive care unit admission, 0.54 for mechanical ventilation, and 0.62 for vasopressor requirement. These estimates are descriptive summaries of selected published reports and should not be interpreted as population-level event rates, treatment-effect estimates, route-specific risks, or expected outcome probabilities in routine clinical practice. Published reports document oral or enteral levothyroxine as a rescue approach when intravenous treatment is unavailable. However, evidence is insufficient to establish comparative efficacy, safety, equivalence, or an optimal dosing regimen. Intravenous levothyroxine should remain preferred when available, particularly in patients with shock, ileus, or unreliable gastrointestinal absorption.

42854888.title: Effect of Integrated Respiratory and Functional Training on Weaning from Mechanical Ventilation, Respiratory and Peripheral Muscle Strength, Functional Ability, and Pain After Emergency Abdominal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
42854888.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
42854888.abstract: To compare the effects of integrated respiratory and functional (multidimensional functional) training versus high-intensity inspiratory muscle training (IMT) plus conventional chest physiotherapy (CPT) on ventilator weaning after emergency abdominal surgery. Prospective, multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial. Two intensive care units. Ninety mechanically ventilated patients with difficult weaning following emergency abdominal surgery (N=90). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to the study group and control groups. The study group received multidimensional functional training, high-intensity IMT and conventional chest physiotherapy. The control group received high-intensity IMT and conventional chest physiotherapy. Primary outcomes were weaning success and maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP). Secondary outcomes included rapid shallow breathing index (RSBI), peripheral muscle strength, Functional Independence Measure (FIM), pain, weaning duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay. Weaning success was significantly higher in the study group (95.6% vs 82.2%; P = .044). Both groups significantly improved MIP, with no between-group difference after treatment (mean difference [MD]=0.30 cmH₂O; 95% confidence interval [CI], -4.11 to 4.72; P=0.89). Compared with control group, the study group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in all peripheral muscle strength measures and FIM domains (all P<0.001), greater reductions in RSBI (MD=-3.92 breaths/min/L; 95% CI, -6.85 to -1.00; P=0.01) and pain (MD=3.22; 95% CI, 3 to 3.44; P<0.001), and shorter weaning duration (MD=-5.82 days; 95% CI, -7.98 to -3.67; P<0.001) and ICU length of stay (MD=-7.74 days; 95% CI, -11.37 to -4.11; P<0.001). Both training approaches improved MIP, whereas multidimensional functional training resulted in higher weaning success and greater improvements in peripheral muscle strength, functional independence, pain, weaning duration, and ICU length of stay than high-intensity IMT+CPT in patients following emergency abdominal surgery.

42854592.title: Herpesvirus reactivation in critical illness: Pathogenesis, clinical consequences, and diagnostic challenges.
42854592.abstract: Human herpesviruses (HHV) remain latent after primary infection and may reactivate during critical illness. HHV reactivation has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes, yet its pathogenic significance and optimal management remain unclear. This review summarizes the dysregulated immune mechanisms and risk factors for HHV reactivation in critical illness, treatment options, outcomes, current diagnostic challenges, and emerging precision medicine approaches. Critical illness induces profound immune dysregulation characterized by an initial hyperinflammatory response followed by immunosuppression, T-cell exhaustion, impaired natural killer cell function, and disrupted antiviral surveillance. These changes facilitate reactivation of latent HHV, including herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1), cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6). HSV and CMV reactivation in mechanically ventilated and septic patients have been associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer intensive care unit (ICU) stay, secondary infections, and increased mortality. However, the distinction between clinically significant disease from asymptomatic reactivation remains challenging. Current evidence does not support routine antiviral prophylaxis in immunocompetent ICU patients. Emerging approaches including metagenomic next-generation sequencing, host transcriptomics, immune phenotyping, and multi-omics integration may improve risk stratification and identify patient subgroups that are most likely to benefit from targeted intervention. HHV reactivation may serve as a biomarker and potential mediator of adverse outcomes. Improved understanding of host-virus interactions, coupled with precision medicine that integrates virological and immunological data, is required to differentiate clinically relevant reactivation from epiphenomena and to guide individualized therapeutic strategies.

42854438.title: The impact of cannabis on clinical outcomes in burn patients: A systematic review.
42854438.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42854438.abstract: Burn injuries remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with survivors often requiring prolonged hospitalization, complex wound care, and intensive rehabilitation. Concurrently, cannabis use has risen substantially in North America and Europe, with recent data showing cannabis use in approximately 16-18% of burn admissions by 2025. Cannabinoids influence pain, immunity, and cardiopulmonary physiology, making their role in burn recovery clinically relevant but poorly defined. A systematic review was conducted evaluating cannabis exposure and outcomes in burn patients. MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to August 2025. Eligible studies included hospitalized burn patients of any age, with cannabis exposure identified via toxicology, history, or coding, and reported outcomes stratified by cannabis exposure. Outcomes of interest included mortality, infection, graft success, thromboembolism, ventilation, ICU and hospital length of stay, opioid use, discharge disposition, and readmission. Of 1009 studies, eight met inclusion criteria, with sample sizes ranging from 64 to over 300,000 patients. Cannabis exposure was identified via toxicology, history, or coding. Across studies, cannabis was not consistently associated with inpatient mortality. Some single-center analyses reported increased opioid and anxiolytic requirements, higher wound infection rates, longer ICU stays, and more reoperations. National database studies found lower adjusted mortality among cannabis-using patients but higher rates of ventilator-associated pneumonia, venous thromboembolism, and prolonged ICU stays. Heterogeneity was pronounced, with polysubstance use, burn severity, and demographic differences influencing outcomes. Overall, cannabis exposure does not appear to worsen survival in burn patients but may predispose to infectious, respiratory, and thromboembolic complications. The evidence base is limited by retrospective design, inconsistent exposure definitions, and confounding from polysubstance use. Cannabis positivity at admission should prompt heightened monitoring for complications and tailored pain management. Future prospective, multicenter studies with detailed exposure characterization and long-term follow-up are needed to clarify cannabis' role in burn recovery and to inform evidence-based analgesic strategies.

42851528.title: Spiked Helmet Sign Associated With Acute Gastric Distension and Hemodynamic Instability: A Case Report.
42851528.abstract: The spiked helmet sign is an uncommon pseudo-ST-segment elevation pattern reported in critical illness and recognized by an upward baseline shift beginning before the QRS complex and a dome-and-spike contour. Its distinction from acute coronary occlusion is clinically important but can be difficult when myocardial injury, left ventricular hypertrophy, electrolyte abnormalities, or post-resuscitation changes coexist. We report a 34-year-old male with end-stage kidney disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and thrombotic microangiopathy who developed aspiration-related respiratory failure, peri-intubation asystolic cardiac arrest, septic shock, and marked gastric distension. During peak instability, an electrocardiogram showed sinus tachycardia at 135 beats/min, left ventricular hypertrophy with secondary repolarization abnormalities, and a spike-helmet morphology that was most prominent in lead II and less distinct in V3. Urgent nasogastric decompression evacuated gas and gastric contents. A repeat tracing obtained 20 minutes later showed a lower heart rate and partial attenuation of the dynamic morphology. A late tracing, obtained after resolution of gastric distension and hemodynamic stabilization, showed sinus rhythm at 83 beats/min and disappearance of the pre-QRS dome-and-spike configuration in lead II and V3, while baseline hypertrophy-related repolarization abnormalities persisted. The serial relationship supports a reversible extracardiac contribution, but incomplete serial biomarkers, echocardiographic assessment, intra-abdominal pressure measurements, and electrode-position documentation prevent definitive exclusion of concurrent myocardial injury or artifact. This case emphasizes integrating electrocardiographic morphology with bedside physiology, abdominal examination, imaging, and response to reversible interventions while continuing to evaluate for true myocardial ischemia.

42849542.title: Long-term psychological, cognitive and quality of life outcomes in Covid-19 severe acute respiratory failure patients managed with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
42849542.abstract: ICU admission with severe acute respiratory failure (SARF) can result in extended recovery and rehabilitation. We sought to evaluate the long-term psychological, cognitive and quality of life outcomes of Covid-19 SARF patients to inform our understanding of the longer-term health burden to survivors. Retrospective single centre cohort study. All surviving SARF Covid-19 patients admitted to a regional ECMO centre in London between March 2020 - February 2022 attending ICU follow-up clinic. None. CORE ICU validated outcome measures alongside clinical interview. Of the surviving (n = 116) patients, 97 (83.6%) attended at least one ICU follow-up clinic. For those attending multiple reviews, despite an improvement in quality of life, depression, anxiety and PTSD were no different between 0 - 2 years and 2 - 4 years after discharge. Comprehensive long-term reviews held between 18 months and 4 years [ IQR 17.5 m - 44.8 m ] following discharge, n = 87) found prevalence of depression (44%), anxiety (25%) and PTSD (33%). Half were still receiving care from specialist healthcare teams. Cognitive impairment was seen in 63% and functional impairment in 31%. Over a quarter (26%) remained not working. Depression and PTSD scores were lower in those who had returned to work. Thematic analysis of long-term reviews revealed six key themes: a plateaued recovery, the traumatising experience, forgetfulness, family strain, appreciation and gratitude, and awareness of the fragility of life. Despite improvements to quality of life, impairments in psychological, cognitive and aspects of health-related quality of life can persist as long as four years after discharge in SARF ECMO survivors. Qualitative findings illustrated the enduring impact of critical illness alongside themes of gratitude an altered life perspective.

42849242.title: Patient centered outcomes after surgical stabilization of rib fractures: A prospective cohort study.
42849242.abstract: Rib fractures are associated with pain, impaired physical function, and reduced quality of life. Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is established for flail chest and ventilator-dependent patients, but its impact on longer-term patient-reported outcomes in broader injury patterns remains unclear. We evaluated whether SSRF is associated with improved physical functioning and pain outcomes compared to nonoperative management. We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of trauma ICU patients with rib fractures admitted between June 2023 and August 2024 at a single Level I trauma center. Patients met institutional criteria for SSRF, including flail chest, ≥ 3 contiguous rib fractures, or ventilator failure. Outcomes were assessed using the SF-36 and SF-MPQ-2 at discharge, 2 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for RibScore, flail chest, ISS, age, obesity, hospital length of stay, and associated injuries. Primary outcomes were SF-36 physical functioning and SF-MPQ-2 present pain intensity (PPI). Of 121 patients, 39 (32%) underwent SSRF. The SSRF group had greater chest injury severity, including higher RibScores and more pneumothorax and hemothorax, while overall injury severity and demographics were similar. There were no differences in ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, ventilator days, or mortality. After adjustment, SSRF was associated with improved physical functioning at discharge (β 13.29, 95% CI 6.53-20.05; p < 0.001) and at 6 months (β 23.40, 95% CI 7.52-39.28; p = 0.005). SSRF was associated with lower pain at discharge, but not at 6 months. SSRF was associated with improved short-term and six-month physical functioning without differences in inpatient outcomes or sustained differences in pain. These findings suggest SSRF may primarily accelerate functional recovery rather than provide durable pain reduction. II Study type: Prospective Cohort.

42847684.title: Lung microbiome community state types are associated with ventilator-associated pneumonia risk: a secondary analysis of the MicroNAV cohort.
42847684.abstract: In the publicly available MicroNAV cohort, baseline diversity analyses did not distinguish patients who developed ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) from non-VAP patients, leaving it unresolved whether community-state structure contains risk information. In an independent secondary analysis, we reprocessed raw 16S rRNA gene sequencing data from bronchoalveolar lavage samples using DADA2 exact amplicon sequence variant inference and decontam quality control, and analyzed 75 at-risk mechanically ventilated patients with paired longitudinal sampling (40 VAP and 35 non-VAP). No baseline genus distinguished future VAP from non-VAP by DESeq2 or MaAsLin3 after adjustment for sex and Glasgow Coma Scale (all adjusted P > 0.05). Dirichlet multinomial mixture modeling identified three community state types (CSTs) with distinct ecological profiles. In cause-specific Cox regression, CST1, a high-burden, oral-associated state, was associated with higher VAP hazard than CST2, a low-burden, diverse state (hazard ratio, 2.85; 95% CI, 1.15-7.02, P = 0.023; Gray's test, P = 0.042). Adding CST to a burden-only model improved fit (likelihood-ratio test, P = 0.041), whereas pathogen species cultured at VAP onset did not differ by baseline CST (simulated Fisher's exact test, P = 0.98). During ventilation, 12 oral-associated genera declined while total bacterial burden remained stable (linear mixed model, P = 0.66), but the association between commensal loss and subsequent VAP was not consistent across abundance scales. Baseline IL-1β and TNF-α concentrations were explained primarily by bacterial burden rather than community composition. These findings suggest that baseline lower-airway ecological states capture VAP susceptibility information not resolved by single-taxon, diversity, or burden-only analyses. In mechanically ventilated ICU patients without pulmonary infection at baseline, the early lower-airway ecosystem may contain information about subsequent ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) susceptibility. In this independent reanalysis of the public MicroNAV cohort, baseline lower-airway communities classified by Dirichlet multinomial mixture modeling resolved into ecological states with different subsequent VAP risk, while individual genera, bacterial burden alone, and the eventual cultured pathogen did not explain the signal. Mechanical ventilation produced shared community restructuring: oral-associated genera declined and other taxa expanded, yet total bacterial burden remained stable, indicating ecological replacement rather than bacterial clearance. This restructuring was not consistently VAP-specific, and apparent community state type-dependent differences in declining-genus loss partly reflected different starting proportions. Together, these findings extend the original cohort by separating starting state heterogeneity from ventilation-associated restructuring. They suggest that initially noninfected ventilated airways represent distinct host-microbial terrains that may differ in vulnerability to pneumonia.

42846643.title: Case Report: Electrical impedance tomography-guided ultra-protective lung ventilation during veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support for fat embolism syndrome complicated by severe acute respiratory distress syndrome.
42846643.abstract: Fat embolism syndrome (FES) is a rare complication of severe multiple trauma. Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) is a noninvasive, real-time, bedside tool for monitoring regional pulmonary ventilation. Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) may improve outcomes in critically ill patients in whom conventional mechanical ventilation fails. Ultra-protective lung ventilation strategy (ULPVS) uses very low tidal volumes to markedly reduce lung stress and mitigate ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI). In June 2025, a 57-year-old woman was admitted to the Department of Orthopedics with a femoral shaft fracture following a motor vehicle accident. Severe respiratory distress developed postoperatively, and she was urgently transferred to the ICU. Based on laboratory findings, chest CT findings, and Oil Red O staining of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), FES complicated by severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) was considered. In addition to conventional treatment, VV-ECMO was initiated to provide gas-exchange support. An ULPVS was implemented during the early phase of ventilation to reduce the risk of VILI, and EIT was used to guide ventilatory management and titration of the optimal Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) Following these interventions, static lung compliance increased from 46 mL/cmH2O to 67.1 mL/cmH2O. VV-ECMO support lasted 62 h, and the total duration of mechanical ventilation was 113 h. After stabilization, the patient was transferred back to the Department of Orthopedics and was ultimately discharged in good condition. Bedside EIT enables dynamic assessment of pulmonary status and may assist in optimizing ventilator settings, providing a useful reference for the management of FES complicated by severe ARDS.

42846282.title: Atypical Lyme Neuroborreliosis Presenting With Ventriculitis and Cerebritis: A Case Report.
42846282.abstract: Lyme neuroborreliosis is a neurological manifestation of infection by Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato and most commonly presents with lymphocytic meningitis, cranial neuropathy, or painful radiculitis. Central nervous system parenchymal involvement is uncommon, and ventriculitis is rarely reported. We describe a man in his late 70s who presented with acute confusion, dysarthria, and left-sided weakness following several days of severe lower-limb pain and progressive mobility impairment. His neurological status rapidly deteriorated, with secondary seizures requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and intensive care support. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated a marked systemic inflammatory response, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, and cholestatic liver dysfunction. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed pleocytosis with initial neutrophilic predominance, markedly elevated protein, and preserved glucose. Routine bacterial cultures and molecular testing for common central nervous system pathogens were negative. Anti-Borrelia IgG and IgM antibodies were detected in CSF, although a paired CSF-serum antibody index was unavailable. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated inflammatory material within the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles, bilateral leptomeningeal involvement, and focal parenchymal lesions with restricted diffusion suggestive of cerebritis. In the appropriate clinical context, these findings supported a diagnosis of probable Lyme neuroborreliosis with an unusual ventriculitis-like presentation. Despite prolonged antimicrobial therapy and partial improvement in CSF and radiological inflammatory findings, neurological recovery remained limited, and the patient subsequently died following ventilator-associated pneumonia complicated by septic shock. This case illustrates an uncommon and severe central nervous system presentation potentially associated with Lyme neuroborreliosis and highlights both the diagnostic value and limitations of CSF serology when demonstration of intrathecal antibody synthesis is unavailable.

42845921.title: Case Report: Fulminant meningococcus-meningitis under treatment with ravulizumab despite complete vaccination-a rare but severe complication.
42845921.abstract: Complement C5 inhibitors such as ravulizumab are increasingly used for acetylcholine receptor-positive generalized myasthenia gravis (MG) but confer a relevant risk of invasive meningococcal infection. We report a rare case of fulminant meningococcal meningitis despite complete vaccination, highlighting the limits of current preventive strategies. Case report. A 41-year-old woman with acetylcholine receptor-positive MG was treated with ravulizumab after two-dose series meningococcal vaccination (MenACWY and MenB). One month after therapy initiation, she presented with nausea, vomiting and rapidly developed impaired consciousness. CSF showed neutrophilic pleocytosis, hypoglycorrhachia, and high lactate, consistent with bacterial meningitis. Rapid testing and culture confirmed Neisseria meningitidis serotype Y. Despite immediate broad-spectrum antibiotics, neurological deterioration required intubation and intensive care. The patient recovered after 18 days of intravenous antibiotics and was switched from ravulizumab to rozanolixizumab. This case illustrates that vaccination does not abolish the risk of fulminant meningococcal infection under complement inhibition.
