Mean AAMRs were higher in males (26.19) than in females (19.04) and in non-Hispanic (NH) White adults (24.06) than in other groups. The West and nonmetropolitan areas had the highest rates. The 2018-2021 surge was steepest among Hispanic (APC 25.62) and NH Black adults (APC 24.06). Population mortality rates for deaths recording both AF and RF increased substantially over 25 years, beginning before the COVID-19 pandemic, persisting after excluding deaths listing COVID-19, and occurring with and without HF recorded. These data cannot separate changes in disease occurrence from changes in diagnosis or coding.

42953629.title: Severe and Prolonged Paroxetine Intoxication With Delayed Absorption and Extreme Serum Concentrations: A Case Report.
42953629.abstract: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are commonly prescribed antidepressants, known for their relatively safe pharmacological profile and mild symptoms in cases of overdose compared with other antidepressants. In this case report, we describe a near-fatal case of a 70-year-old woman who ingested multiple drugs with suicidal intent, including an unknown quantity of celecoxib 200 mg, clorazepate acid 5 mg, omeprazole 20 mg, and immediate-release paroxetine 30 mg tablets. The patient developed severe serotonin syndrome complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and required admission to the intensive care unit (ICU). Because of progressive respiratory deterioration, she required intubation and invasive mechanical ventilation. Serotonin syndrome persisted for an unusually long period, with serum paroxetine concentrations of 4805 µg/L at admission that continued to rise to a maximum of 7824 µg/L on day four, both well above the lethal threshold. Intensive therapeutic interventions aimed at lowering paroxetine concentrations and resolving serotonin syndrome included activated charcoal, whole-bowel irrigation lavage, and rifampicin. Paroxetine concentrations gradually declined and reached the therapeutic range after 16 days. Following further ICU treatment, including prone ventilation and corticosteroids, the ARDS resolved, and the patient was extubated 21 days after ingestion. This case highlights that paroxetine overdose may present more severely than commonly reported in the literature, with delayed and prolonged toxicity, including serotonin syndrome and ARDS. Paroxetine overdose may be life-threatening and underscores the need for close monitoring of serum paroxetine concentrations and timely consideration of activated charcoal and whole-bowel irrigation.

42952806.title: Multicenter cohort of necrotizing enterocolitis in Latin America: evaluation of risk factors and clinical outcomes in Chilean Hospitals.
42952806.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity. While risk factors are well documented in high-income countries, data from Latin American cohorts remain limited. We aimed to identify local predictors and clinical outcomes associated with NEC in two Chilean NICUs. A prospective multicenter cohort study (2017-2018) included newborns ≤32 weeks and/or ≤1,500 g. NEC (Bell stage ≥ IIA) was verified by a multidisciplinary team. Clinical and laboratory variables were analyzed using bivariate and multivariable penalized models to identify predictors of NEC and mortality. Among 177 newborns (mean GA 29.1 ± 3.0 weeks; BW 1,252 ± 448 g), NEC incidence was 7.9% (n = 14). In bivariate analysis, invasive mechanical ventilation (RR = 4.58; p = 0.02) and indomethacin (RR = 3.13; p = 0.04) were associated with NEC. In multivariable models, formula feeding was the most consistent predictor (OR = 2.69 vs. exclusive breast milk), though not statistically significant. Half of NEC cases (50%) were Bell stage IIIB. Surgery was required in 38.5% of cases (all stage IIIB; p = 0.009). Case fatality among NEC patients was 40%, associated with Bell stage IIIB (p = 0.048) and systemic shock (p = 0.048). Formula feeding was a consistent, though non-significant, predictor of NEC in multivariable analysis; the limited number of NEC cases (n = 14) precludes definitive causal inference. Exclusive breastfeeding remained the most protective feeding strategy, consistent with prior literature. Disease outcomes were driven by progression to Bell stage IIIB, and early monitoring of inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers may help identify infants at risk of progression to surgical NEC.

42951749.title: Perioperative Lactate, Survival, and Complications Following Lung Transplantation.
42951749.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42951749.abstract: To examine perioperative lactate and its association with survival and postoperative complications following lung transplantation (LTx). Single-center retrospective cohort study. Academic tertiary-care transplant center. Adult patients undergoing LTx between February 2018 and January 2023. None. Serum lactate was measured at 6-hour intervals from the start of surgery, and the maximum value within the first 0 to 6 hours was recorded. Patients were categorized into the high-lactate group (upper quartile, ≥4.2 mmol/L) and low-lactate group (lower 3 quartiles). Primary outcomes were 1-year and overall survival. Secondary outcomes included renal failure, venous thromboembolism (VTE), primary graft dysfunction grade 3 (PGD3), mechanical ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and post-transplant length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Among 225 recipients (median age, 62.3 years; 34.2% female), high lactate was not associated with 1-year or overall survival. However, recipients with high lactate had higher rates of PGD3 at 72 hours (42.1% v 13.1%, p < 0.001), longer mechanical ventilation duration (3 days v 2 days, p = 0.003), longer ICU stay (11.6 days v 7 days, p = 0.013), and higher in-hospital mortality rate (7% v 0.6%, p = 0.019). No significant differences were observed in renal failure, VTE, or post-transplant length of stay. Elevated perioperative serum lactate was associated with PGD3 at 72 hours, prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer ICU stay, and in-hospital mortality but not 1-year or overall survival following LTx. These findings suggest that perioperative lactate may aid in identifying high-risk patients early in their postoperative course despite its lack of association with long-term survival.

42948114.title: Left atrial pressure continuous monitoring improves early postoperative outcomes after double-lung transplantation for pulmonary hypertension.
42948114.abstract: Double-lung transplantation (DLTx) has become the treatment of choice for patients with end-stage pulmonary hypertension (PH). However, DLTx remains a demanding procedure, associated with a greater incidence of severe primary graft dysfunction (PGD) compared with other indications. PH-induced cardiac remodeling includes diastolic left heart dysfunction, which may increase the risk of PGD. We hypothesized that continuous monitoring of left atrial pressure (LAP) could improve early outcomes. We retrospectively reviewed the chart of patients who underwent DLTx for PH between 2015 and 2022. The use of postoperative LAP monitoring was left to the discretion of the attending transplant surgeon. A total of 135 patients underwent DLTx for PH. Among them, 72 were managed either with prophylactic postoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or with ECMO weaning guided by transesophageal echocardiography and Swan-Ganz catheter, whereas 63 underwent systematic ECMO weaning after the placement of a LAP catheter maintained for 3 to 5 days. Both groups were comparable regarding age, PH diagnoses, and disease severity. The LAP group showed significantly less postoperative ECMO use (25% vs 83%, P < .001), shorter duration of mechanical ventilation (5 days [2-13] vs 17.5 days [7-35], P < .001), shorter stay in the intensive care unit (10 days [6-25] vs 28 days [14-49], P < .001), and lower rates of bleeding, groin infection, and overall complications (P ≤ .05). Intraoperative red blood cell transfusion was identified as an independent predictor of LAP monitoring strategy failure. Ninety-day postoperative mortality was not significantly different between groups (1.5% vs 8.3%, P = .12). Continuous postoperative monitoring of LAP after DLTx for PH was associated with improved early outcomes. This strategy may help reduce the incidence of severe postoperative complications in this high-risk population.

42947783.title: Clinical and radiographic improvement in suspected pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis-associated hypoxemic respiratory failure following iruplinalkib-based treatment in ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma after sequential treatment with ensartinib and lorlatinib: a two-patient case report.
42947783.abstract: Pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis (PLC) is an uncommon but life-threatening manifestation of advanced lung cancer and may rapidly lead to hypoxemic respiratory failure. Evidence guiding subsequent anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-directed therapy after prior exposure to multiple ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitors remains limited, particularly in patients with acute respiratory compromise. In this report, we describe two never-smoking women with stage IVB ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma who developed type I respiratory failure. This was accompanied by clinical and radiographic findings suggestive of PLC after sequential treatment with ensartinib and lorlatinib. Case 1 achieved a partial response to first-line treatment with ensartinib for approximately 19 months. At progression, plasma next-generation sequencing identified an EML4-ALK variant 1 fusion with an acquired ALK p.L1196M resistance mutation. During subsequent lorlatinib therapy, the patient developed rapidly progressive dyspnea, diffuse bilateral peribronchovascular and reticular opacities suggestive of PLC according to radiographic findings, and type I respiratory failure. Rapid improvement in oxygenation was observed following initiation of third-line iruplinalkib monotherapy. Case 2 had ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma with an intravascular tumor thrombus on diagnostic biopsy. After ensartinib discontinuation due to grade 3 constipation and subsequent lorlatinib therapy, the patient developed type I respiratory failure, pleural effusion, and progressive bilateral pulmonary abnormalities suggestive of PLC according to radiographic findings. Iruplinalkib was administered in combination with salvage pemetrexed. Following initiation of the respective treatment regimens, both patients showed rapid improvement in oxygenation and radiographic observations of pulmonary abnormalities. Case 1 received iruplinalkib monotherapy, whereas case 2 received iruplinalkib and pemetrexed; therefore, treatment-specific attribution was not possible in case 2. No adverse events attributable to iruplinalkib were observed. In these two patients, initiation of iruplinalkib-based treatment was followed by rapid improvement in clinical and radiographic findings, supporting further evaluation of this treatment strategy in similar critically ill patients.

42947720.title: Trends in Tracheostomy Utilization, Tracheostomy Dependence, and Outcomes Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic.
42947720.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic led to an unprecedented demand for invasive mechanical ventilation and may have affected tracheostomy utilization, dependence, and airway-related outcomes. However, population-level trends before and after the pandemic remain poorly characterized. We evaluated temporal trends in tracheostomy utilization, dependence, and airway-related complications among intubated and mechanically ventilated patients before versus after the COVID-19 pandemic. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using de-identified data from the TriNetX U.S. Collaborative Network. Adults (≥ 18 years) who underwent endotracheal intubation and respiratory ventilation from 2016 to 2023 were included. Patients were stratified into pre-pandemic (2016-2019) and pandemic (2020-2023) cohorts. Propensity score matching was performed on 13 demographic and clinical covariates. Primary outcomes were tracheostomy and tracheostomy dependence, and secondary outcomes included airway-related complications. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Among 155,499 intubated and mechanically ventilated patients, the incidence proportions of tracheostomy, tracheostomy dependence, and dysphagia increased from 2016 to 2023 by approximately 2.1, 3.3, and 2.3 times, respectively. After matching (n = 64,732 per cohort), there was no difference in tracheostomy surgical rates between pre- and pandemic cohorts (RR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.91-1.02). However, pandemic patients had higher risks of tracheostomy dependence (RR: 1.14, 95% CI: 1.08-1.21) and dysphagia (RR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.04-1.10). Tracheostomy dependence and select airway complications increased in the pandemic period, suggesting lasting downstream effects of critical care practices after the pandemic. Proactive resource planning and long-term strategies for airway care in tracheotomized patients are needed. 3.

42947684.title: Body mass index, diabetes, inflammation and survival in COVID-19: a retrospective study evaluating the obesity paradox in an urban hospital center.
42947684.journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare
42947684.abstract: Severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is associated with increased morbidity and mortality, particularly among patients with comorbidities such as diabetes and obesity. The combined influence of glycemic control, hyperglycemia, and body mass index (BMI) on disease severity remains incompletely understood, particularly in underserved urban populations. This retrospective study evaluated 478 adults hospitalized with confirmed COVID-19 between March and May 2020 at an urban academic medical center to examine the impact of diabetes, glycemic control, and body mass index (BMI) on clinical outcomes. Data collected included demographics, comorbidities, BMI, diabetes type, baseline hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), inflammatory markers, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, mechanical ventilation, hyperglycemia, and glucocorticoid use. Among patients with available HbA1c measurements, those with diabetes who developed cytokine storm had significantly higher mean HbA1c than those without cytokine storm. Obesity and overweight were highly prevalent, with 45% of patients classified as obese (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) and 29% classified as overweight (BMI 25-29 kg/m²). Diabetes was associated with increased ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and steroid-induced hyperglycemia. Mortality was higher among older patients, Black patients, and those with diabetes, hypertension, hyperglycemia, greater glucocorticoid use, or ICU admission. Notably, patients with overweight or obesity demonstrated improved survival compared with those of normal weight, consistent with an obesity paradox in this urban cohort. Multivariable analysis identified steroid-induced hyperglycemia, obstructive sleep apnea, and higher methylprednisolone use as independent predictors of ICU admission, whereas higher BMI was associated with a lower risk of adverse outcomes. Diabetes and hyperglycemia were associated with greater COVID-19 severity, increased ICU utilization, and higher mortality, while higher BMI offered potential survival benefits. These findings highlight the complex interplay between metabolic dysfunction, obesity, and COVID-19 outcomes, suggesting the presence of an obesity paradox in hospitalized patients, and emphasize the importance of early recognition and management of diabetes and hyperglycemia to improve clinical outcomes.

42947228.title: The impact of prior asymptomatic COVID-19 infection on outcomes following coronary bypass surgery.
42947228.abstract: The optimal timing and expected postoperative course of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) after asymptomatic coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remain uncertain. Evidence guiding cardiac surgical practice has largely been extrapolated from mixed surgical cohorts or broader cardiac surgery series rather than from isolated CABG populations. This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults who underwent isolated CABG during 2021-2022. Patients with documented asymptomatic preoperative SARS-CoV-2 infection were compared with patients without documented prior COVID-19. Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative variables were extracted from institutional records. Outcomes included early clinical recovery, respiratory support, transfusion exposure, laboratory trajectories, and mortality. A timing subgroup analysis (< 4 weeks vs >= 4 weeks from infection to surgery) was prespecified as exploratory. Seventy-six patients met eligibility criteria: 37 with prior asymptomatic COVID-19 and 39 without documented prior COVID-19. The cohort was predominantly male (81.6%), low risk by EuroSCORE II, and largely elective. Baseline demographics, major comorbidities, ventricular function, operative priority, number of grafted vessels, cardiopulmonary bypass time, cross-clamp time, extubation time, intensive care unit stay, hospital stay, oxygen requirement, and transfusion exposure were similar between groups. Postoperative complications were more frequent in the prior-COVID group (16.2% vs 0.0%; risk difference 16.2%, 95% CI 3.8-31.1%; P = 0.011), whereas mortality remained rare and not significantly different (2.7% vs 0.0%; P = 0.487). Longitudinal laboratory analyses showed expected perioperative inflammatory and hematologic changes within both groups, without consistent between-group separation. In the exploratory timing subgroup, no statistically significant differences were detected between earlier and later surgery, but this analysis was markedly underpowered. In this single-center exploratory cohort of predominantly elective, low-risk CABG patients, prior asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection was not associated with a generalized worsening of early postoperative recovery, although postoperative complications were more frequent in the exposed group. These data are insufficient to inform CABG timing recommendations after asymptomatic infection and should not be extrapolated to unstable or higher-risk patients. Larger multicenter studies with better exposure characterization, vaccination data, and longer follow-up are required.

42946589.title: Machine Learning-Based Mortality Prediction for Mechanically Ventilated Liver Failure Patients: A Retrospective Study.
42946589.abstract: To develop a mortality prediction model for patients with liver failure who require mechanical ventilation (MV) in ICU. This retrospective study utilized data from the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV (v3.0) databases. Variables included demographics, liver function markers, ventilator parameters, severity scores, comorbidities, use of vasoactive drugs and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) as well as length of ICU and hospital stay. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Five machine learning algorithms were applied: logistic regression, decision tree, Bagging, neural network, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). The dataset was randomly split into a training set (70%) and a test set (30%). Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and calibration plots. Predictive factors were ranked for the best-performing model by importance. A total of 2336 patients were identified from the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV databases. On the test set, the AUC values for each model were as follows: logistic regression (0.836), decision tree (0.768), neural network (0.774), Bagging (0.854), and XGBoost (0.875). Calibration curves showed good agreement for all models except the neural network. Among the 5 algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the highest predictive performance. The top 5 predictors identified were length of hospital stay, SAPS II score, use of vasoactive drugs, total bilirubin and length of ICU stay. Machine learning-based models can effectively predict in-hospital mortality in liver failure patients receiving mechanical ventilation. Among the 5 algorithms tested, the XGBoost model achieved the best overall performance.

42946130.title: Which spontaneous breathing trial should be used to reproduce post-extubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related ARDS? A multicenter randomized crossover study.
42946130.abstract: Spontaneous breathing trials (SBT) guide extubation decisions in intensive care unit (ICU), predicting the respiratory effort required by the patient after extubation. Different SBTs exist and should be adapted to critical illness. Viral pneumonias such as COVID-19 combine lung injury, sepsis-induced systemic inflammation, and encephalopathy, making classification challenging. The objective was to assess which SBT could be used to reproduce postextubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) patients. In this multicenter randomized crossover study, COVID-19-related ARDS patients mechanically ventilated at least 24 hours and ready for extubation underwent 3 different 15-minute SBT at random order: pressure support ventilation of 7-cmH2O with positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 0-cmH2O (PSV7PEEP0), PSV 0-cmH2O with PEEP 0-cmH2O (PSV0PEEP0) and T-piece trial. At baseline, end of each SBT, and 20 minutes after extubation, surrogates of respiratory effort were measured: esophageal pressure-time-product (PTPes), PTPes per minute (PTPes.min), swing esophageal pressure (SwingPes), and SwingPes per minute (SwingPes.min). Sixty measurements of respiratory effort from 12 patients were analyzed. Median PTPes.min increased from 193.8 [170.8-227.2] cmH2O.s/min at baseline to 236.6 [192.1-313.6] after extubation, with no significant differences between SBTs and postextubation. SwingPes and SwingPes.min were lower during PSV7-PEEP0 than after extubation, with median paired differences of 4.7 (95% CI 0.6-9.8) and 115.3 (95% CI 4.8-297.8), but these differences did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. No SBT modality differed significantly from post-extubation respiratory effort, suggesting that none could be excluded in COVID-19-related ARDS patients.

42945812.title: Injury patterns and early operative demand in a combined military and civilian casualty cohort: A single-centre study from the first 11 weeks of the 2023 Israel-Hamas war.
42945812.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
42945812.abstract: Modern asymmetric warfare and large-scale terror attacks produce distinctive wounding patterns that differ from conventional state-on-state conflict and impose specific early demands on receiving trauma systems. The 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel and the ensuing war generated a compressed surge of combined civilian and military casualties. We characterized injury patterns and linked them to early in-hospital resource use at a single tertiary trauma centre across the opening weeks of the conflict. We performed a retrospective descriptive cohort study of 192 consecutive trauma casualties admitted between 7 October and 24 December 2023. Demographics, mechanism of injury, injured anatomical regions, Injury Severity Score (ISS) and acute interventions were abstracted from the institutional trauma dataset. Mechanism and anatomical categories were not mutually exclusive. Variables were summarised as medians (IQR) or counts (percentages); missing data were not imputed and percentages were computed over non-missing observations. Casualties were young (median age 24 years, IQR 21-35) and predominantly male (84.4%). Penetrating (43.2%) and shrapnel (31.2%) mechanisms predominated, followed by acoustic trauma (12.0%). Extremities were most often injured (lower limb 41.7%, upper limb 35.4%); 68.8% had at least one extremity injury and 37.0% had two or more injured regions. Median ISS was 9 (IQR 4-16); 26.5% of those with a recorded ISS had ISS ≥16. Blast and crush carried the highest median ISS (25 and 16). Early resource use was substantial: 23.4% required emergency surgery via direct emergency-room-to-operating-room transfer, 10.9% mechanical ventilation and 5.2% packed red-cell transfusion. This extremity-predominant, penetrating-and-shrapnel profile, with a small but disproportionately severe blast and crush subgroup and frequent acoustic trauma, translated into early demand for emergency surgery, ventilation and transfusion. These patterns support resourcing limb-salvage and damage-control surgery, blood-bank and intensive-care readiness, and audiologic follow-up in military and mass-casualty trauma planning.

42945027.title: Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: feasibility, practical benefits, and surgical pitfalls from a single-center experience.
42945027.abstract: To describe surgical outcomes, technical considerations, and feasibility of redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery using initial cases as a reference cohort. A single-center, retrospective review of minimally invasive mitral valve surgery performed between January 2014 and January 2024 was conducted. Perioperative data, mid-term survival, and cardiac-related events were assessed in both initial and redo groups. A total of 647 patients were included: 30 in the redo group and 617 in the initial group. The redo group had higher European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II scores (p < 0.001). In the redo group, 26 (86.7%) had undergone previous cardiac surgery via sternotomy, and 18 (60.0%) had previous mitral valve surgery. The operative time was longer in the redo group (p = 0.041), while the cross-clamping time was longer in the initial group (p = 0.019), and cardiopulmonary bypass time was comparable between groups (p = 0.95). Intubation time (p = 0.049), intensive care unit stay (p = 0.020), and in-hospital stay (p = 0.003) were longer in the redo group. However, there were no significant differences in postoperative chest tube output for 24 h (p = 0.32) or blood transfusion requirements (p = 0.087). The overall survival rates at 5 years were 70.7% (95% CI: 41.0%-87.0%) vs. 92.0% (95% CI: 88.0%-94.0%) for the redo and initial groups, respectively. Freedom from cardiac-related events did not significantly differ between groups. Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery was feasible despite higher surgical risk and longer operative times. Early and mid-term cardiac-related outcomes appeared acceptable, although overall survival was lower in redo cases.

42944623.title: Low-Use vs. High-Use Physical Restraint in Older Adults With Sepsis Receiving Mechanical Ventilation: A Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial.
42944623.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
42944623.abstract: Physical restraints are commonly used in patients receiving mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU), yet evidence regarding their effectiveness in older patients with sepsis is limited. This study evaluated whether a low-use physical restraint strategy improves outcomes in older patients with sepsis requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. This multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial was conducted in five ICUs in China from August 2023 to March 2026. Patients aged ≥ 65 years with invasive mechanical ventilation were randomly assigned (1:1) to a low-use restraint strategy (restraints applied only for severe agitation) or a high-use restraint strategy (routine restraint use until recovery of consciousness and liberation from mechanical ventilation). The primary outcome was days alive without delirium or coma within 7 days after randomization. Secondary outcomes included delirium incidence, ventilator-free days, coma-free days, sedative exposure, 28-day mortality, and safety events. Analyses were performed using intention-to-treat, per-protocol, and inverse probability weighting approaches. Among 485 randomized patients (median age, 74 years; 60.4% male), 244 received low-use and 241 high-use restraint. Delirium- and coma-free days did not differ between groups (adjusted mean difference, 0.17 days; 95% CI, -0.20 to 0.54; p = 0.37). Low-use restraint was associated with more ventilator-free days (0.69 days; 95% CI, 0.48-0.91; p < 0.001) and coma-free days (0.46 days; 95% CI, 0.19-0.74; p = 0.001). No significant between-group differences were observed in delirium incidence, sedative exposure, 28-day mortality, or safety outcomes. Among older mechanically ventilated patients with sepsis, a low-use physical restraint strategy did not improve days alive without delirium or coma but was associated with more ventilator-free and coma-free days. These findings suggest that reducing restraint use may facilitate short-term recovery, although the safety of restraint minimization requires further evaluation. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: ChiCTR1900025850.

42943553.title: Predictive Performance of Inflammatory Markers for Severe Disease Progression in Measles: A Retrospective Cohort Analysis.
42943553.abstract: The recent European measles resurgence has driven record-high hospitalization, yet objective tools for early risk stratification remain scarce. This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of routine admission inflammatory biomarkers for predicting severe disease and prolonged hospitalization. We retrospectively analyzed 509 patients with laboratory-confirmed measles hospitalized during a Romanian outbreak (November 2023-August 2025). Severe disease was defined via a clinical composite endpoint (intensive-care admission, mechanical ventilation, supplemental oxygen, acute respiratory failure, or sepsis). Biomarker discriminative performance was assessed using receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, Youden-optimal cut-offs, and DeLong tests. Multivariable logistic and Cox proportional-hazards regression evaluated independent predictors of severity and time to discharge. The cohort exhibited a pediatric predominance (median age: 3.0 years; 20% infants) with an 82% unvaccinated rate; 33% developed severe disease. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) demonstrated superior diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.863, 95% CI 0.820-0.898; cut-off ≥ 7 pg/mL, sensitivity 73%, specificity 93%), significantly outperforming ferritin (AUC 0.800) and conventional markers (all p < 0.001). Multivariable modeling established IL-6 and ferritin as the sole independent predictors of severity. All intensive-care admissions occurred exclusively for unvaccinated patients (5.0% vs. 0%). Severe disease, pneumonia, male sex, unvaccinated status and elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) independently predicted prolonged hospitalization. Admission IL-6 and ferritin serve as robust, independent prognostic biomarkers that accurately identify high-risk measles patients, providing objective criteria with which to optimize clinical triage and inpatient management during outbreaks.

42943441.title: A Comprehensive Review of the Underlying Mechanisms of Resistance and Therapeutic Options for DTR-PA in Bloodstream Infection and Pneumonia: A Clinical Vignette-Based Approach.
42943441.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a ubiquitous opportunistic pathogen and a leading cause of severe healthcare-associated infections, particularly ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) and bloodstream infections (BSIs) in critically ill patients. Its remarkable capacity for both intrinsic and acquired resistance leads to complex phenotypic profiles, culminating in difficult-to-treat resistant P. aeruginosa (DTR-PA). Managing DTR-PA presents a daunting clinical challenge characterised by a narrow therapeutic armamentarium, treatment delays, and high attributable mortality. To bridge the gap between complex molecular microbiology and bedside decision-making, this narrative review employs a pragmatic, clinical vignette-based approach. Through six representative fictional scenarios of pneumonia and BSI, we systematically dissect the underlying mechanisms of resistance and their direct therapeutic implications. The vignettes explore combinations of intrinsic adaptations-such as Pseudomonas-derived cephalosporinase (PDC/AmpC) hyperexpression, OprD porin loss, and efflux pump upregulation-as well as the acquisition of serine- (e.g., GES) and metallo-β-lactamases (e.g., VIM, NDM, IMP). Grounded in the updated 2026 Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) guidelines, we evaluate the optimal deployment of newer β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations. We highlight the specific preference for ceftolozane-tazobactam in pneumonia, the roles of ceftazidime-avibactam and imipenem-relebactam, and the critical use of cefiderocol for metallo-β-lactamase producers and highly resistant phenotypes. Furthermore, the review addresses pressing clinical controversies: the superiority of targeted monotherapy over historical, toxic combination regimens; the risks of unconditionally applying "shorter-is-better" duration paradigms to DTR-PA; and the alarming frequency of treatment-emergent cross-resistance among novel agents. We also clarify common clinical misconceptions, such as the limited utility of meropenem-vaborbactam and aztreonam-avibactam against specific pseudomonal mechanisms. Ultimately, effective DTR-PA management precludes class-based empirical assumptions. By providing a phenotype-driven bedside aide-mémoire, this review reinforces that rapid recognition, direct agent-specific antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD)-optimised dosing, and prompt source control remain the absolute cornerstones of survival for patients afflicted by these formidable infections.

42942512.title: High-Flow Nasal Cannula in Adult Acute Care: Physiological Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Persistent Misconceptions.
42942512.abstract: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy is widely used in emergency, intensive care, perioperative, and procedural settings, but it is often conceptually assimilated to non-invasive positive-pressure ventilation (NIPPV). This interpretation is physiologically misleading. HFNC is an open high-flow oxygen system whose main effects derive from dead-space washout, improved stability of inspired oxygen fraction (FiO2), heated humidification, patient comfort, and only modest flow-dependent positive airway pressure. Its open interface also facilitates eating, drinking, speaking, and secretion clearance. Clinical evidence supports HFNC mainly in selected patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, where it may reduce intubation compared with conventional oxygen therapy. However, evidence is more heterogeneous in hypercapnic respiratory failure, cardiogenic pulmonary edema, immunocompromised patients, obesity, and settings requiring substantial pressure support or ventilatory unloading. NIPPV remains preferred in acidotic hypercapnic COPD exacerbations, while CPAP or NIPPV is indicated in selected pressure-responsive conditions such as cardiogenic pulmonary edema. Persistent excessive effort or clinical deterioration requires timely assessment for invasive ventilation. HFNC should therefore be regarded as optimized high-flow oxygen therapy rather than as "non-invasive ventilation through nasal prongs." Recognizing this distinction may improve patient selection, guide escalation, and avoid overinterpretation of its clinical effects.

42942421.title: Efficacy of Ultrasound-Guided Pectointercostal Fascial Block Versus Control and Alternative Regional Techniques in Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Dose-Response Analysis.
42942421.abstract: Background and Objectives: Ultrasound-guided pectointercostal fascial block (USG-PIFB) is increasingly used for post-sternotomy analgesia, but its efficacy remains uncertain. Prior meta-analyses pooled ultrasound-guided blocks with surgeon-performed infiltration, introducing heterogeneity. We aimed to determine the analgesic efficacy of USG-PIFB in adult cardiac surgery by restricting inclusion to ultrasound-guided techniques. Materials and Methods: Six databases were searched through December 2025, with an update search of open sources and trial registries in September 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing USG-PIFB with control (Comparison 1) or with an alternative regional technique (Comparison 2) in adults undergoing sternotomy. The primary outcome was 24-h opioid consumption in intravenous morphine milligram equivalents. Random-effects meta-analysis (REML, Knapp-Hartung), subgroup, sensitivity and meta-regression analyses, an exploratory trial sequential analysis and GRADE assessment were performed. Results: Twenty-nine trials (2664 participants) were included: 24 in Comparison 1 and eight in Comparison 2. In 13 trials (902 participants), USG-PIFB reduced 24-h opioid consumption (mean difference -6.60 mg; 95% CI, -10.92 to -2.27; I2 = 97.7%), but the 95% prediction interval (-22.24 to 9.04 mg) included no effect and small-study effects could not be excluded. Pain scores were lower by 0.8 to 1.4 points at rest (extubation, 12 and 24 h) and during movement (12 h). Extubation was earlier and intensive care stay shorter, with extreme heterogeneity. No dose-response relationship was detected, and the difference from deep parasternal techniques was near zero. No local anesthetic systemic toxicity or block-attributable pneumothorax was reported; one block-site hematoma occurred in a USG-PIFB recipient. Certainty of evidence was low for rescue analgesic use and block-related complications and very low for all other outcomes. Conclusions: USG-PIFB may modestly reduce 24-h opioid consumption, but the magnitude and reproducibility of this effect across clinical settings remain uncertain. It is best regarded as one component of multimodal analgesia, and adequately powered multicentre trials are needed.

42942248.title: Comparison of Airway-Based and Transpulmonary Mechanical Power Across Ventilation Conditions in Moderate-to-Severe ARDS.
42942248.abstract: Background: Mechanical ventilation is essential for managing acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) but may contribute to ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI). Mechanical power (MP), an integrative measure combining tidal volume, respiratory rate, and airway pressures, has emerged as a predictor of VILI. However, conventional MP calculations based on airway driving pressure (ΔP) reflect the mechanical load applied to the entire respiratory system, including both lung parenchyma and chest wall. Estimation of transpulmonary pressure using esophageal pressure allows calculation of transpulmonary mechanical power (TPMP), which may more accurately represent lung stress. Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational study of 20 mechanically ventilated ICU patients with available esophageal pressure measurements at Wolfson Medical Center between 2012 and 2015. MP and TPMP were calculated across ventilation modes, including continuous mandatory ventilation assist/control (CMV/AC), synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation (SIMV), and continuous positive airway pressure/pressure support ventilation (CPAP/PSV). Paired comparisons were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test; repeated-measures Friedman tests were used to assess within-patient differences in MP, TPMP, and the MP-TPMP difference across the four ventilation conditions. Results: At baseline, MP and TPMP values were similar, with only a small absolute difference despite statistical significance (median 20 vs. 20 J/min; p = 0.0107). Differences were more pronounced and mode-dependent during CMV/AC, CPAP/PSV, and SIMV. During CMV/AC, TPMP exceeded MP (median 23 vs. 22 J/min; p = 0.0016). In contrast, TPMP was lower than MP during CPAP/PSV (median 14 vs. 20 J/min; p < 0.0001) and SIMV (median 17 vs. 23 J/min; p = 0.0073). In a repeated-measures analysis, the within-patient MP-TPMP difference varied significantly across ventilation conditions (χ2 = 33.06, df = 3, p < 0.0001), while MP alone did not differ significantly across conditions (χ2 = 6.90, df = 3, p = 0.075); these findings represent associations with ventilation condition and clinical state rather than a causal effect of ventilation mode. Conclusions: This exploratory study demonstrates that airway-based MP and esophageal pressure-derived TPMP provide different estimates of mechanical load and that the magnitude and direction of these differences vary across ventilation conditions. These findings support the physiological relevance of considering transpulmonary pressure when characterizing respiratory mechanical load. However, this study does not establish that TPMP-guided ventilation improves clinical outcomes or reduces VILI. The potential clinical value of TPMP should therefore be evaluated in larger prospective studies.

42941672.title: Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis.
42941672.abstract: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04-2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group (p < 0.001) with concomitantly longer hospital (p = 0.001) and ICU (p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03-0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions: In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

42941613.title: Bedside Lung Ultrasound for Early Postoperative Risk Stratification for Prolonged Mechanical Ventilation After Liver Transplantation.
42941613.abstract: Objectives: Pulmonary complications remain a major determinant of postoperative morbidity following liver transplantation and frequently lead to prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV). This study aimed to evaluate the value of lung ultrasound (LUS) for early postoperative risk stratification of PMV and to develop a multivariable model integrating LUS with conventional clinical variables. Methods: In this prospective cohort study, 116 adults undergoing primary liver transplantation were enrolled. A standardized 12-zone LUS examination was performed within 1-3 h of ICU admission. PMV was defined as the need for mechanical ventilation for ≥24 h. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was constructed by sequentially incorporating perioperative variables and postoperative PaO2/FiO2, followed by LUS. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis. Results: PMV occurred in 39.7% (n = 46) of the patients. Those requiring PMV had significantly higher early postoperative LUS scores than patients extubated within 24 h (median: 18.0 vs. 12.0, p < 0.001). LUS scores were inversely correlated with oxygenation (SpO2/FiO2 ratio, ⍴ = -0.615, p < 0.001). LUS remained independently associated with PMV (OR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.27-1.83). LUS alone demonstrated good discrimination (AUC: 0.830). After postoperative PaO2/FiO2 was included in the clinical model, incorporation of LUS significantly improved model discrimination (AUC: 0.935, 95% CI: 0.894-0.976) compared with the model without LUS (AUC: 0.862, DeLong p = 0.011). Decision curve analysis showed greater net benefit of the LUS-integrated model across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. Conclusions: Early postoperative LUS is independently associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation after liver transplantation. Integration of LUS into a multivariable framework provides incremental prognostic information beyond conventional postoperative respiratory assessment and may improve early postoperative risk stratification. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

42941358.title: A Simplified Physiology-Laboratory Score (PLS4) for Early Risk Stratification in Acute Cholangitis.
42941358.abstract: Objectives: Acute cholangitis is a common biliary infection in the emergency department (ED) that can progress rapidly to septic shock and multiorgan dysfunction. The Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG2018) is the current reference standard for severity assessment but may be cumbersome during the initial ED encounter. We aimed to develop a simplified physiology-laboratory score (PLS4) computable from four routine bedside variables and to compare its early risk-stratification performance with TG2018. Materials and Methods: This single-center retrospective observational cohort study included 482 adult patients with acute cholangitis (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision code K83.0) presenting to a tertiary university hospital ED between January 2016 and December 2021. Primary outcomes were ICU admission, vasopressor use, and prolonged hospital stay (length of stay ≥ 14 days); intubation was analyzed as an exploratory outcome. PLS4 assigned 1 point each for albumin < 3.5 g/dL, systolic blood pressure ≤ 100 mmHg, heart rate ≥ 100/min, and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio ≥ 1.2 (range 0-4). Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic curves, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and bootstrap optimism-corrected internal validation. Results: ICU admission occurred in 81 patients (16.8%), vasopressor use in 53 (11.0%), and prolonged stay in 111 (23.0%). The areas under the curve (AUCs) for ICU admission were 0.850 for TG2018 and 0.800 for PLS4 (p = 0.116), and the optimism-corrected AUC of PLS4 was 0.779. For vasopressor use, which is part of the TG2018 grade III definition, the AUCs were 0.936 and 0.843. When PLS4 was added to TG2018, the AUC for ICU admission increased to 0.886. At PLS4 ≥ 3, specificity reached 0.978 for ICU admission and 0.970 for vasopressor use, with event rates rising stepwise from 5.96% to 100% and 2.55% to 90.0%, respectively. Conclusions: In this single-center derivation study, PLS4 showed high specificity and added prognostic information to TG2018. It should be validated in other centers before clinical use.

42940536.title: Complications and Hospital Resource Utilization Associated with ECMO in COVID-19 ARDS with Acute Kidney Injury: Insights from United States National Inpatient Sample, 2020-2022.
42940536.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication of COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), yet the impact of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) on outcomes in this high-risk population remains unclear. We performed a retrospective, survey-weighted study using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database from 2020-2022 to compare outcomes among adults hospitalized with COVID-19-associated ARDS and AKI managed with invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) alone versus IMV and ECMO. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, while secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT), complications, hospital length of stay (LOS), and healthcare utilization. Among 198,395 hospitalizations with COVID-19 ARDS complicated by AKI, 4730 received IMV and ECMO. ECMO use was not associated with statistically significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.81-1.12). However, ECMO was associated with greater odds of RRT, intracranial hemorrhage, disseminated intravascular coagulation, cardiogenic shock, vasopressor use, tracheostomy, acute liver failure, deep vein thrombosis, ischemic stroke and ICU-acquired weakness. ECMO was also associated with longer LOS and higher hospitalization charges. Among hospitalizations with COVID-19-associated ARDS and AKI, ECMO was not associated with statistically significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality but was associated with markedly higher complication burden, longer hospitalization, and substantially greater healthcare resource utilization.

42938180.title: Combined Approach with Ultrasound and Pressure-Volume Loops to Manage Mechanical Ventilation in Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure.
42938180.abstract: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF), particularly acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), is characterized by marked heterogeneity in lung morphology and mechanics, requiring individualized mechanical ventilation strategies that balance adequate gas exchange with the prevention of ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI). Lung ultrasound (LUS) has become a cornerstone of critical care imaging, allowing differential diagnosis, quantitative assessment of lung aeration, phenotyping of ARDS morphology, and monitoring of disease evolution and complications. However, imaging alone does not provide direct guidance for optimizing ventilator settings. Some modern ventilators enable the rapid bedside acquisition of tidal pressure-volume (PV) loops, allowing tidal hysteresis to be measured and thereby providing complementary physiological information by identifying cyclic opening and closing of lung units and signs of overdistension. Emerging evidence supports the use of tidal hysteresis thresholds to identify insufficient positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) associated with tidal recruitment/derecruitment and to guide individualized PEEP titration during decremental PEEP trials. This review discusses the rationale and practical implementation of an integrated approach combining critical care ultrasound and PV loops throughout the management of mechanically ventilated patients with AHRF. We describe how ultrasound can support diagnosis, phenotyping, monitoring of lung aeration, and detection of ventilation-related complications, while PV loops provide a practical physiological framework for optimizing ventilator settings. This approach may provide a comprehensive, non-invasive, and repeatable bedside assessment of lung morphology, aeration, and respiratory mechanics, potentially facilitating personalized mechanical ventilation strategies aimed at reducing the risk of VILI and optimizing patient management.

42937764.title: Retrospective evaluation of predictors and clinical impact of postoperative delirium in liver transplant recipients.
42937764.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the epidemiology, predictors, and clinical outcomes of postoperative delirium (POD) in liver transplant (LT) recipients. Clinical data from 427 LT recipients from the Third Xiangya Hospital were retrospectively reviewed. The epidemiology (incidence, onset, and duration), predictors, and associated clinical outcomes of POD were analyzed using standardized delirium assessment tools and multivariate regression. POD occurred in 19.0% of recipients, with a median onset at 26.0 hours posttransplant. Multivariate analysis identified 4 independent pre and postoperative predictors, including a higher model for end-stage liver disease score and hepatic encephalopathy within 24 hours before LT, infection within 2 months prior to LT, and abnormal sodium within 1 hour after LT (all P < .05). In a sensitivity analysis treating early death or persistent coma as a composite outcome with POD (n = 436), the same 4 independent predictors were identified, with consistent effect estimates. Regarding clinical outcomes, POD was significantly associated with prolonged intensive care unit stays, extended mechanical ventilation requirements, and increased use of renal replacement therapy (all P < .01). Although recipients with POD showed higher 1- and 6-month all-cause mortality in unadjusted analyses, POD was not an independent predictor of mortality after adjustment for confounding factors. POD occurs frequently and early after LT, with identifiable pre and postoperative risk factors. While POD markedly increases perioperative morbidity and resource utilization, it does not independently predict short-term all-cause mortality in this cohort.

42937307.title: Clinical significance of different Histoplasma genotypes in human histoplasmosis: insights from a multicenter study from Québec comparing North American (NAm2) with Latin American (LAmA) isolates.
42937307.abstract: Histoplasmosis is recognized as endemic in Québec; however, no molecular epidemiological studies have been conducted to date. The clinical significance of identifying Histoplasma capsulatum genotypes remains unclear. We performed a retrospective multicenter study of 67 culture-confirmed histoplasmosis cases from four major academic hospitals in Québec between 1988 and 2014. Multi-locus sequence typing (MLST) was performed on isolates, and clinical data were analyzed for genotype-specific associations with demographics, clinical presentations, and outcomes. Most isolates belonged to either the North American clade 2 (48.1%) or Latin American clade A (39.2%), highlighting both endemic and imported disease patterns in Québec. A novel NAm2 sequence type (ST81) was identified, which was unique to Québec and accounted for 61% of the NAm2 isolates, but was not associated with significantly different clinical outcomes compared with other NAm2 strains. In multivariate analysis, disseminated disease was independently associated with immunosuppression (OR 14.18, P = 0.001), male sex (OR 6.01, P = 0.035), and LAmA genotype (OR 5.02, P = 0.031). Severe outcomes (intensive care unit admission, intubation, death, or amphotericin B use) were associated with immunosuppression (OR 4.48, P = 0.023), with a non-significant trend with LAmA infections (OR 3.06, P = 0.069). This first molecular characterization of histoplasmosis infections in Québec suggests a dual epidemiology, with locally acquired NAm2 and LAmA infections more often associated with travel or origin from endemic regions outside Québec. Host factors were associated with disease severity, while the potential contribution of fungal genotype requires further study. These findings highlight the value of molecular characterization for understanding the epidemiology of histoplasmosis in endemic settings. Histoplasmosis is an important dimorphic fungal infection in North America. Although Québec is a recognized endemic region, its molecular epidemiology has not been previously characterized, and the clinical relevance of different Histoplasma genotypes remains uncertain. In this multicenter study, we performed multi-locus sequence typing with detailed clinical data from 67 culture-confirmed cases diagnosed between 1988 and 2014. This represents the first molecular characterization of clinical Histoplasma isolates from Québec and the largest Canadian cohort examining the association between molecular genotypes, clinical presentation, and outcomes. We identified both North American NAm2 (Histoplasma ohiense) and imported Latin American LAmA (Histoplasma suramericanum) lineages, suggestive of a combination of locally acquired and travel-associated infections. We also identified a novel NAm2 sequence type (ST81) that appears unique to Québec, suggesting possible regional circulation. The LAmA genotype was associated with disseminated histoplasmosis, whereas immunosuppression was the principal predictor of severe outcomes. Overall, host factors were associated with disease severity, while the potential contribution of fungal genotype warrants further study. These findings highlight the value of molecular characterization for understanding the epidemiology of histoplasmosis in endemic settings.

42937280.title: Significant hypercapnia as an initial manifestation of COVID-19 without typical symptoms in chronic cervical spinal cord injury: A case series.
42937280.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
42937280.abstract: Few reports have described how Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) presents in patients with long-standing high cervical spinal cord injury (SCI). This case series suggests that clinically significant hypercapnia may be an early manifestation of COVID-19 in this population, even without classic respiratory symptoms or marked oxygen desaturation, potentially delaying recognition of ventilatory failure. We describe two men with chronic C4 ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS) A. Case 1: A 76-year-old vaccinated man developed drowsiness, confusion, and headache without cough or fever. Room-air oxygen saturation was 90-95%, and inflammatory markers did not clearly indicate infection. Arterial blood gas (ABG) showed new-onset, clinically significant hypercapnia (pH 7.306, PaCO₂ 62.4 mmHg, PaO₂ 77.3 mmHg). He required endotracheal intubation and intensive care unit (ICU) care; COVID-19 was subsequently confirmed and remdesivir was administered. Tracheostomy was later performed after unsuccessful ventilator weaning. Case 2: A 70-year-old unvaccinated man reported chest discomfort without cough or fever, then developed confusion. Room-air oxygen saturation remained 94-95%. ABG showed respiratory acidosis with new-onset, clinically significant hypercapnia (pH 7.304, PaCO₂ 59.4 mmHg, PaO₂ 76.7 mmHg). He also required intubation, mechanical ventilation, ICU care, and tracheostomy after COVID-19 was confirmed; he was treated with remdesivir and corticosteroids. These cases suggest that hypercapnia may be an early and potentially critical manifestation of COVID-19 in chronic high cervical SCI, without typical respiratory symptoms or marked hypoxemia. Clinicians should assess CO₂ retention in this vulnerable population to avoid delayed diagnosis and deterioration.

42936737.title: Age as a significant prognostic factor in patients meeting the global ARDS definition but not the Berlin definition.
42936737.abstract: ARDS (Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome) poses significant challenges in critical care, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. The new global definition of ARDS includes some patients who are not previously considered to have ARDS. This study aims to look at the prognostic characteristics of these patients and develop a prediction model. This multicenter retrospective study included 5,214 patients from the Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital between December 2022 and February 2023. Patients were categorized into four groups based on the 2023 Global Definition and 2012 Berlin Definition: Global-definition-only ARDS + COVID-19, Global-definition-only ARDS-COVID-19, Berlin ARDS + COVID-19, and Berlin ARDS-COVID-19. Patient characteristics were analyzed using LASSO regression and Cox proportional hazards models to identify factors associated with 28-day mortality. A prognostic model was developed using key variables. Among ARDS patients, the Berlin ARDS + COVID-19 group had the highest mortality, while the observed 28-day mortality in the Global-definition-only ARDS + COVID-19 group was of a similar magnitude to that in the Berlin ARDS without COVID-19 group. LASSO selected seven candidate predictors: heart rate, lactate dehydrogenase, platelet count, total bilirubin, D-dimer, age, and antiviral therapy. In the multivariable Cox model, lactate dehydrogenase, age, and antiviral therapy were independently associated with 28-day mortality. Compared with patients aged <75 years, the HRs for 28-day mortality were 2.09 (95% CI 1.07-4.10) for those aged 75 to <85 years and 3.78 (95% CI 2.08-6.86) for those aged ≥85 years. Antiviral therapy was associated with a lower hazard of 28-day mortality (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.40-0.84).The model's AUC for predicting 28-day mortality was 0.732 in the training set and 0.726 in the validation set. The 2023 Global ARDS definition holds significant value in identifying COVID-19 patients receiving high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO), the Global definition may facilitate earlier identification of ARDS patients. Age is a critical risk factor, highlighting the need for heightened clinical attention in elderly patients. Antiviral therapy was associated with a lower hazard of 28-day mortality. Seven candidate predictors were selected by LASSO and evaluated in a Cox prognostic model for 28-day mortality.

42936306.title: Mild Hypothermia Versus Normothermia During Barbiturate Coma Therapy After Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
42936306.abstract: Severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of death and long-term disability worldwide. Therapeutic hypothermia may lower intracranial pressure (ICP) and reduce metabolic demand. This study aims to compare mild therapeutic hypothermia with controlled normothermia in adult TBI patients undergoing Barbiturate Coma Therapy (BCT), and to explore artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted prognostic models. This single-center, pilot, parallel-group randomized trial evaluates the feasibility and safety of adding mild hypothermia to BCT and explores early signals of benefit or harm. The primary outcome, six-month Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE), is reported descriptively with exact 95% confidence intervals. Secondary outcomes include Cerebral Performance Category, mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation and vasopressor use, intensive care unit (ICU)/hospital length of stay, complications, and physiological/laboratory trends. An exploratory AI-assisted substudy (using prospectively collected clinical, radiological, physiological, and laboratory data) applies LASSO regression to admission predictors of six-month unfavorable outcome and mortality.

42936115.title: Case Report: Sepsis With Multisystemic Amyloid Light-Chain Amyloidosis.
42936115.abstract: Systemic light-chain (AL) amyloidosis is a complex disorder characterized by extracellular fibril deposition, leading to severe multisystem dysfunction. When sepsis superimposes on preexisting organ impairment, early clinical recognition becomes particularly challenging yet critical. We present a case of a 60-year-old female who presented with generalized edema, dyspnea, and cardiac/renal involvement, subsequently diagnosed with AL amyloidosis based on laboratory, imaging, bone marrow biopsy, and Congo red staining findings. Following chemotherapy with bortezomib and cyclophosphamide, the patient experienced transient cardiac arrest, received an implantable cardioverter defibrillator, and subsequently developed massive ascites. Upon developing Pseudomonas guariconensis bacteremia, she progressed to septic shock requiring intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor support, and targeted antimicrobial therapy. Through aggressive supportive care and source control, hemodynamic stabilization was achieved, allowing successful extubation and transfer to the general ward. Superimposed sepsis on severe, multi-organ amyloidosis significantly complicates diagnosis and management. High clinical vigilance, early infection recognition, and prompt targeted therapy are essential to prevent fatal outcomes in patients with preexisting chronic organ dysfunctions.

42935808.title: Pulmonary edema during cesarean delivery secondary to Takotsubo syndrome revealing pheochromocytoma: a case report.
42935808.abstract: Acute pulmonary edema during delivery is a serious condition with a wide range of etiologies, including Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), a form of transient left ventricular dysfunction most often presenting as apical ballooning. We report the case of a 35-year-old woman who developed severe hypertension (205/130 mmHg), polypnea, and a drop in oxygen saturation to 80% during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia. She received noninvasive ventilation while the cesarean section continued and was transferred to the intensive care unit. Point-of-care ultrasound showed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with apical ballooning and diffuse B-lines on lung ultrasound. Computed tomography identified a right adrenal mass. A diagnosis of pulmonary edema complicating TTS was made, and the patient received furosemide and oxygen therapy. Further investigations, including urinary catecholamine metabolites, confirmed the diagnosis of pheochromocytoma. One week later, LVEF had recovered to 57% with mild residual apical hypokinesia and complete clinical recovery. The patient was then transferred to the surgical unit for management of the pheochromocytoma. This case demonstrates that TTS can cause pulmonary edema in the peripartum period, and that timely diagnosis is essential for a favorable outcome. Point-of-care ultrasound can be instrumental in guiding the assessment of such critical situations, and noninvasive ventilation may be of particular value in selected pregnant patients. This case also underscores the importance of an etiological workup and prompt treatment of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, especially when pheochromocytoma is suspected, since anesthesia and surgery can precipitate decompensation.

42935540.title: Independent correlates of vancomycin steady-state trough concentration among patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery: observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump support.
42935540.abstract: Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) combined with valve surgery represent a high-risk surgical population with substantial perioperative hemodynamic disturbances and highly variable organ function, leading to high variability in vancomycin pharmacokinetics. Conventional vancomycin dosing solely on renal function frequently fails to achieve target trough concentrations in this complex subgroup. This study aimed to identify independent correlates c of vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations (Css-min), and to report observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, to inform individualized therapeutic drug monitoring. A single-center retrospective observational study enrolled adult patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery from January 2018 to October 2024. Clinical data and vancomycin TDM records were extracted from electronic medical records. Vancomycin Css-min was detected by enzyme-multiplied immunoassay technique. Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) accounting for within-patient repeated TDM measurements were used to identify clinical correlates of Css-min. IABP support was pre-specified and force-entered into the multivariable model based on clinical observations and pathophysiological reasoning, independent of univariate screening results. We performed a sensitivity analysis for patients with at least one TDM within postoperative day 7, prespecified interaction tests for effect modification, and binary logistic-GEE for the supratherapeutic endpoint (Css-min > 20 mg/L). A two-tailed P < 0.05 was set as statistical significance. A total of 283 eligible patients with 473 valid Css-min measurements were included. Multivariate GEE demonstrated that categorical vancomycin dosing regimen, age, ventilator dependence ≥96 h, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), IABP support, serum creatinine (Scr), and serum urea nitrogen (SUN) were positively associated with higher geometric-mean Css-min. Associations remained largely consistent in the sensitivity-analysis subgroup of patients with at least one early-phase TDM within postoperative day 7. A significant CRRT-by-postoperative-time interaction was detected, indicating that the influence of CRRT on vancomycin exposure varied across different postoperative phases. Of note, the association signal linking IABP to supratherapeutic trough concentrations (Css-min>20 mg/L) was modest and requires cautious interpretation. Multiple clinical factors jointly affect vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations in patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery, including dosing regimen, age, renal biomarkers, and critical-care supportive interventions such as IABP, CRRT and prolonged mechanical ventilation. IABP support represents an intriguing observational signal; this finding remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective external validation before it can guide formal dose-adjustment strategies. Individualized vancomycin management for this population should comprehensively integrate hemodynamic support measures and laboratory indices rather than depend merely on renal-function markers. This study focuses on clinically accessible trough concentration monitoring rather than constructing complex pharmacokinetic models, which is more in line with real-world clinical practice.

42934935.title: Prognostic significance of nucleated red blood cells in trauma patients.
42934935.abstract: Nucleated red blood cells are early erythroid precursors typically confined to the bone marrow. Their appearance in peripheral blood reflects stress erythropoiesis and has been linked to hypoxia and systemic inflammation. While nucleated red blood cells have prognostic value in sepsis and critical illness, their significance in trauma remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of nucleated red blood cells during the first 10 days in the intensive care unit following severe trauma, and their association with 30-day mortality. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study including 1636 adult trauma patients admitted to the Reims Level-1 Trauma Center between January 2019 and March 2025, recorded in the TraumaBase© registry. Nucleated red blood cell counts were measured daily for the first 10 intensive care unit days. K-means clustering identified four nucleated red blood cell phenotypes based on temporal patterns. Outcomes included 10- and 30-day mortality, incidence of acute respiratory distress syndrome, septic shock, mechanical ventilation, and length of stay. Survival analyses used Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, Injury Severity Score, Simplified Acute Physiology Score II, and the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, and propensity-weighted regression assessed dichotomised nucleated red blood cell status. Nucleated red blood cells were detected in 221 patients (13.5%). Phenotype classification revealed: transient early nucleated red blood cells (phenotype 1), single peak (phenotype 2), multiple intermittent peaks (phenotype 3), and persistent elevation (phenotype 4). Phenotype 2 was associated with reduced 10-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.06, 95% confidence intervals 0.01-0.46), while phenotype 4 exhibited markedly increased mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 9.6, 95% confidence intervals 2.23-41.4, P < 0.001). Nucleated red blood cell+ patients had higher risks of acute respiratory distress syndrome, septic shock, mechanical ventilation, and 30-day mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves confirmed significant differences in survival across phenotypes (log-rank P < 0.001). Nucleated red blood cell presence, particularly persistent elevation, identifies trauma patients at higher risk of adverse outcomes. Routine, daily nucleated red blood cell monitoring may serve as a simple, low-cost prognostic tool in intensive care unit trauma care. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings and integrate nucleated red blood cell dynamics into risk stratification.

42933694.title: Comparison of meropenem-based triple therapy vs minocycline-based triple therapy for carbapenem resistant Acinetobacter baumannii ventilator associated pneumonia - a prospective observational study.
42933694.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) resulted from Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) poses serious treatment challenges. Our objective was to assess two triple medication combinations for VAP caused by CRAB. This prospective observational research was performed in the critical care unit of an academic medical center from January 2024 to March 2025. Two hundred adult patients with culture-proven CRAB-VAP were enrolled and treated with either minocycline-polymyxin-sulbactam or meropenem-polymyxin-sulbactam. Various outcomes assessed were clinical recovery, 7 and 28-day mortality, microbiological eradication, duration of ICU and hospital stay. The clinical recovery rates were comparable in both groups (54% minocycline vs. 47% meropenem, p = 0.322). The microbiological eradication rate was similar (39%) at day 28 in both groups. Patients treated with the minocycline regimen had significantly shorter ICU stay (16 vs. 18 days, p = 0.003) and hospital stays (24 vs. 28 days, p < 0.001) than the meropenem group. There was no significant difference between 7-day mortality (21% vs. 32%, p = 0.078) or 28-day mortality (46% vs. 53%, p = 0.322). Minocycline-based triple therapy was comparable to meropenem-based therapy in treating CRAB-VAP, with potential advantages in reducing duration of ICU and hospital stay. Minocycline may be a suitable alternative for CRAB-VAP in resource-limited settings.

42933334.title: Doxycycline versus azithromycin in combination with beta-lactams for hospitalized community-acquired pneumonia: A propensity score-matched cohort study.
42933334.abstract: Azithromycin plus a beta-lactam is a commonly used empiric regimen for hospitalized community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Concerns about azithromycin resistance and patient-specific safety considerations have increased interest in doxycycline as an alternative; however, comparative effectiveness data for these two regimens remain scarce. Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (240 healthcare organizations; data accessed June 14, 2026), we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with CAP between January 2016 and December 2023. Doxycycline plus beta-lactam recipients were compared with azithromycin plus beta-lactam recipients following 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching (11,906 patients per group). Thirty-day and 90-day all-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (HR: 1.03, 95% CI: 0.95-1.12; and HR: 1.06, 95% CI: 0.98-1.14, respectively), whereas 180-day mortality was modestly but significantly higher in the doxycycline cohort (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02-1.16; p = 0.014). Doxycycline-based therapy was associated with a consistently lower risk of antibiotic escalation at all time points assessed (RR: 0.59-0.65; p < 0.001). The 30-day risk of incident sepsis was significantly higher with doxycycline (RR: 1.29, 95% CI: 1.03-1.61; p = 0.024). ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor use, and Clostridioides difficile infection did not differ significantly between the two groups. No statistically significant difference in 30-day mortality was detected between doxycycline plus beta-lactams and azithromycin plus beta-lactams. This finding does not establish equivalence or noninferiority. Secondary findings, including 30-day sepsis and 180-day mortality, were exploratory and require confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

42930891.title: Feasibility of the Pleural Sliding Test for Detection and Management of Lung Adhesions During Robotic Cardiac Surgery.
42930891.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
42930891.abstract: Pleural adhesions can complicate access in robotic cardiac surgery, risking lung injury or conversion to sternotomy. The sliding test using thoracic ultrasound can predict thoracic adhesions and guide the surgeon during robotic set-up. We evaluated the utility of the sliding test in robotic cardiac surgery. The pleural sliding test was performed in 300 consecutive robotic cardiac surgery patients between August 2022 and September 2025. The test was performed by the surgeon using a linear probe at six intercostal sites after intubation. Intraoperative findings were used to validate the test. Tailored port placement and minithoracotomy strategies were used when adhesions were suspected. The mean age was 60.3 ± 13.7 years and 91 (30.3%) of the patients were female. Adhesions were encountered in 20 (6.7%) patients. Prior cardiothoracic surgery was associated with thoracic adhesions (p < 0.001). The pleural sliding test had a sensitivity of 95.0%, specificity of 97.9%, positive predictive value of 76.0%, negative predictive value of 99.6%. No pulmonary injuries occurred and no conversions to sternotomy were necessary in the cohort. Patients with adhesions had higher 24 h chest tube output (p = 0.006) but had similar mechanical ventilation times and intensive care unit stay durations. Pleural adhesions are not rare in patients undergoing robotic cardiac surgery, and their optimal management enhances the safety and efficiency of robotic cardiac procedures. The pleural sliding test offers high accuracy for preoperative detection, enabling tailored access strategies that enhance safety and maintain benefits of the robotic approach.

42930806.title: Beyond Mallampati: From Universal Bedside Tests to Precision Airway Risk Stratification.
42930806.abstract: Airway management remains one of the few domains of anaesthetic practice still governed by universal, dichotomous screening thresholds applied to profoundly heterogeneous populations. Conventional bedside tests-the modified Mallampati test, thyromental distance and the upper lip bite test-retain modest and inconsistent diagnostic accuracy, leaving the majority of difficult intubations unanticipated while generating false alarms that drive resource-intensive contingency plans. This narrative review reframes preoperative airway evaluation as a problem of individualised risk stratification rather than population screening. We first summarise the performance limits of classical bedside predictors and the reasons for their ceiling effect, including low target prevalence, inter-observer variability, spectrum bias and heterogeneous outcome definitions. We then examine the data streams reshaping the field: point-of-care upper airway ultrasound, whose parameters provide operator-accessible and objective anatomical information; cross-sectional and craniofacial imaging; and machine-learning models based on clinical variables, facial images and voice analysis. For each we discuss accuracy, reproducibility, validation status and barriers to adoption. We then propose a phenotype-oriented framework in which assessment intensity is matched to pre-test probability, with dedicated pathways for obesity and obstructive sleep apnoea, obstetric, head-and-neck oncological and post-radiotherapy, critically ill and emergency, and paediatric populations. We map this framework onto the 2025 European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care and Difficult Airway Society recommendations and outline the validation, calibration and equity requirements-including algorithmic bias across skin tone, sex and ethnicity-that must be met before precision airway assessment can enter routine practice.

42930678.title: Epidemiological Characteristics, Species Distribution, and Antifungal Resistance Profiles of Candidemia Cases.
