42930678.abstract: Local species distribution and antifungal susceptibility are important for empirical candidemia management. We retrospectively evaluated patients with Candida-positive blood cultures from August 2019 to May 2024. Episodes were defined using a 30-day window; species distribution and susceptibility were analysed at the episode-species level and outcomes at the patient level. Among 566 patients, 605 episodes and 637 episode-species isolates were identified. Non-albicans Candida accounted for 59.7%; C. albicans (40.3%) and C. parapsilosis (34.2%) predominated. Of 217 C. parapsilosis isolates tested, 66 (30.4%) were fluconazole-susceptible, 58 (26.7%) were susceptible dose-dependent, and 93 (42.9%) were resistant. Recurrent candidemia occurred in 37 patients and documented microbiological persistence in 128 (22.6%); persistence was more frequent when the index culture included C. parapsilosis (27.6% vs. 20.1%; OR 1.52, 95% CI 1.01-2.28). Among 32 patients with a shared species in the initial and first recurrent episodes, newly detected resistance occurred in three, all involving fluconazole-resistant C. parapsilosis. Thirty-day all-cause mortality was 57.4%; older age, ICU care, mechanical ventilation, and solid malignancy were independently associated with higher mortality. These findings suggest that empirical reliance on fluconazole may be inappropriate in settings with similar resistance patterns and support species-level identification, repeat blood cultures, and episode-specific susceptibility testing.

42928916.title: The Value of the White Blood Cell-to-Hemoglobin Ratio in Acute Lower Respiratory Tract Infections of Pseudomonas Aeruginosa.
42928916.abstract: The white blood cell to hemoglobin ratio (WBC/Hb) shows potential in predicting the severity and poor prognosis of infectious diseases. However, the specific utility of WBC/Hb in acute lower respiratory tract infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (ALRTIs-PA) has not been fully elucidated. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic value of WBC/Hb for disease severity (ICU admission) and its prognostic value for 90-day mortality in patients with ALRTIs-PA. A retrospective study was conducted among patients with ALRTIs-PA admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University from January 2020 to January 2024. Baseline demographics, clinical characteristics, and laboratory parameters were extracted from electronic medical records. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors for ICU admission. A Cox proportional hazards model was used to determine predictors of 90-day all-cause mortality, and significant variables were subsequently into a prognostic prediction model. A total of 549 patients were enrolled, of whom 301 (54.8%) ICU admission, and 72 (13.1%) died within 90 days. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified WBC/Hb, total protein (TP), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), and neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR) as independent risk factors for ICU admission. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve showed the best predictive value of WBC/Hb. Multivariable Cox regression analysis identified WBC/Hb, along with NLR, TP, tracheotomy, tracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, acute renal failure, and the number of antibiotics used, as independent risk factors for 90-day mortality in patients with ALRTIs-PA. Notably, WBC/Hb was the strongest predictor (HR =8.130, 95% CI: 3.852-17.157, P < 0.001) of mortality among all examined variables. Our findings suggest that WBC/Hb represents a valuable predictor for ICU admission and 90-day mortality in patients with ALRTIs-PA.

42928725.title: Euglycemic SGLT2 Inhibitor-Associated Ketoacidosis in a Nondiabetic Patient: A Case Report.
42928725.abstract: We present the case of a 62-year-old nondiabetic woman receiving dapagliflozin for dilated cardiomyopathy presenting to the emergency department with severe hypoxemic respiratory failure because of suspected cardiogenic pulmonary edema. Despite treatment, she remained symptomatic and required intubation and intensive care admission. After intubation, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis was unmasked. After exclusion of other common causes, SGLT2 inhibitor-associated ketoacidosis due to dapagliflozin was suspected. Marked ketonuria confirmed the diagnosis despite the absence of hyperglycemia. Dapagliflozin was discontinued, and intravenous insulin, glucose infusion, and early enteral nutrition were initiated. Metabolic acidosis resolved completely within 24 h. The patient was successfully extubated and discharged from the intensive care unit 48 h later. SGLT2 inhibitor-associated ketoacidosis should be considered in patients receiving sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors who develop otherwise unexplained high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, irrespective of diabetic status or blood glucose concentration. Fasting and acute illness are relevant precipitating factors; prompt drug withdrawal, carbohydrate administration, insulin therapy, and nutritional support can lead to rapid resolution.

42926949.title: Scapulothoracic Disarticulation of the Right Upper Limb After a Car-to-Obstacle Collision: A Case Report.
42926949.abstract: This report details the case of a 26-year-old man, victim of a car-to-barrier collision followed by a rollover. The patient, found conscious, was intubated by the pre-hospital team and admitted in severe hypovolemic shock, with extensive injury to the shoulder and right upper limb. After hemodynamic stabilization, the team performed bilateral chest drainage, a massive transfusion protocol, and a forequarter amputation of the right upper limb with ligation of the subclavian vessels, in a joint procedure by the orthopedic and vascular surgery teams. Postoperatively, he remained in the intensive care unit (ICU), developing ventilator-associated pneumonia, treated with meropenem and vancomycin. After 10 days, the patient was transferred to a ward. He was discharged from the hospital after 15 days of hospitalization and continued with outpatient follow-up, where he presented with phantom limb pain initially treated with gabapentin and controlled with physiotherapy. In the end, he was definitively discharged with good healing, pain improvement, and favorable clinical evolution.

42926014.title: Early Invasive Aspergillosis after Liver Transplantation: A Matched Case-Control Analysis of Clinical Features and Risk Factors in a Chinese Cohort.
42926014.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
42926014.abstract: Early invasive aspergillosis (IA) is a severe complication of liver transplantation, but data from Chinese recipients remain limited. We evaluated its clinical characteristics, outcomes, and independent predictors. We retrospectively studied adult liver transplant recipients at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University from August 2018 to March 2023. Patients meeting 2020 EORTC/MSGERC criteria for proven or probable IA within 1 month post-transplant were matched 1:2 to non-IA controls by age, sex, and etiology. Postoperative ICU and intubation durations were excluded from multivariable regression to eliminate temporal bias. Among 1,051 recipients, 78 developed early IA (7.4% incidence; 3 proven, 75 probable), matched to 156 controls. Aspergillus fumigatus predominated (64.1%), with a median onset of 5 days. IA was associated with reduced 12-month survival (65.4% vs 80.1%, P = 0.014). Higher acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) grade, preoperative corticosteroid exposure, and postoperative 12-hour lactate >5 mmol/L were independent risk factors. ACLF severity, pretransplant corticosteroids, and early postoperative hyperlactatemia independently correlate with early IA. These hypothesis-generating findings help identify high-risk recipients requiring targeted surveillance.

42925630.title: Hemorheological optimization via isovolemic hemodilution in COVID-19 ARDS under chronic environmental hypoxia: A pilot proof-of-concept study.
42925630.abstract: Chronic environmental hypoxia induces compensatory secondary erythrocytosis and elevated whole-blood viscosity, which may aggravate microvascular thromboinflammation in severe COVID-19 acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). We evaluated the feasibility, safety, and exploratory outcomes of isovolemic hemodilution (IVHD) in high-altitude COVID-19 ARDS. Retrospective cohort study of 30 consecutive adult lifelong high-altitude residents (elevation 3,640 m) admitted to the ICU with severe COVID-19 ARDS on invasive mechanical ventilation. Seven patients underwent clinician-selected IVHD (controlled phlebotomy of 0.5-2.0 L with isovolemic crystalloid replacement over 6-12 hours), while 23 received conventional ICU management. Baseline illness severity scores (APACHE II, PaO₂) were comparable. Admission hematocrit was 59% (55-66) in the IVHD group versus 52% (36-68) in conventional controls (p=0.065). IVHD achieved rapid hemorheological decompression at 72 hours, reducing hematocrit to 38% (32-46, p=0.015) and hemoglobin to 11 g/dL (10-15, p=0.015). ICU survival was 71.4% (5/7) in the IVHD cohort versus 8.7% (2/23) in conventional controls (Fisher's exact p=0.003; crude odds ratio 26.25, 95% CI 2.9-234.3). No procedural adverse events occurred. Rapid hemorheological optimization via IVHD was feasible, safe, and associated with an exploratory survival signal in high-altitude COVID-19 ARDS, providing a physiological rationale for prospective randomized trials.

42924299.title: Omicron respiratory threat in renal transplant recipients.
42924299.abstract: Omicron was identified as one of the worrisome strains of corona virus. Renal transplant recipients (RTRs) are classified as high-risk groups due to immunosuppressed conditions. Thus, this study was conducted with the aim of comparing these patients infected with the Omicron variant with the general population infected with this variant compare. 62 RTRs infected with the Omicron strain and 60 patients with non-RTRs who were hospitalized from 2021 to 2022 at the peak of Omicron in Tehran, Shiraz and Babol, Iran were included in the study. The two groups were compared regarding clinical findings, laboratory results, pulmonary manifestations on high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), and adverse effects. In both groups the most common respiratory symptoms were similar. The ground glass opacity was the most frequent finding on CT scan and was seen in 86 cases (70.5%). There was a reduced absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) and platelet count (85.4% and 41.9%, respectively) in RTRs and the rise of creatinine levels was more in RTRs than those in non-RTRs (79% versus 31.6%). the disease severity (16.1% versus 5%, P = 0.008) and adverse outcomes, such as mechanical ventilation (MV) (12.9% versus 0%, P = 0.004), and the mortality rate was significantly higher in RTRs than the general population. There was no significant difference in clinical symptoms between two groups except diarrhea. MV, ICU admission and mortality were significantly higher in RTRs under prolonged immunosuppression.

42923850.title: The effect of competency-based educational application on the knowledge and skill of working with a ventilator in nursing students: A randomized controlled trial.
42923850.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
42923850.abstract: Mechanical ventilation is crucial for reducing mortality, hospital stay duration, and treatment costs in intensive care units. However, nursing students often receive insufficient training in ventilator management. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a competency-based educational application on nursing students' knowledge and practical skills in ventilator operation. This randomized controlled trial was conducted in 2023 on 72 fourth-semester undergraduate nursing students in Yazd, Iran. Participants were selected through purposive sampling and randomly assigned into intervention (n = 36, app-based training) and control (n = 36, lecture-based training) groups. The intervention group used a competency-based Android application over 30 days, progressing through structured modules and a final exam. The primary outcomes were knowledge and practical skills related to ventilator use, assessed using a validated 20-item multiple-choice questionnaire and an OSCE checklist. Secondary outcomes included ventilator setup time and students' satisfaction with the app. Data analysis was performed using SPSS v22, employing independent and paired t-tests, and Chi-square tests at a significance level of P < 0.05. Post-test knowledge scores (App: 13.91 ± 2.62; Lecture: 12.77 ± 2.71; P = 0.001), OSCE scores (App: 16.13 ± 1.85; Lecture: 14.54 ± 1.94; P = 0.001), and ventilator setup time (App: 189.43 ± 26.90 s; Lecture: 208.57 ± 30.04 s; P = 0.001) all significantly favored the app group. The mean satisfaction score with the application was 7.10 ± 1.20 out of 9. The competency-based educational application significantly enhanced nursing students' knowledge and skills in ventilator use compared to traditional methods. This approach offers a practical and effective training strategy for improving ventilator competency in nursing education.

42923439.title: Acute Confusion as the Presenting Feature of Hypoglycemia and Lactic Acidosis in an Adult With Known Fructose-1,6-Bisphosphatase Deficiency.
42923439.abstract: We report the case of a 29-year-old woman with genetically confirmed fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency, an inherited disorder of gluconeogenesis. She had been followed since childhood by a specialized metabolic unit and was brought to the emergency department by a mobile intensive care service because of acute confusion. Her symptoms had begun the previous evening with epigastric pain, repeated vomiting, anorexia, and intense asthenia. Consequently, she had eaten almost nothing for approximately 20 hours before the onset of confusion. The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score recorded during the pre-hospital assessment was 8, with a capillary blood glucose concentration of 0.4 g/L (2.2 mmol/L), which was partially corrected during transfer. On arrival, her GCS score was 10. She had no focal sensorimotor deficit, and her pupils were equal and reactive. Her respiratory rate was 26 breaths per minute, peripheral oxygen saturation was 98% on room air, blood pressure was 140/80 mmHg, and heart rate was 120 beats per minute. The abdomen was soft and non-tender. Arterial blood gas analysis showed severe metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation (pH 7.185; bicarbonate, 6.3 mmol/L) and a lactate concentration of 6.49 mmol/L. The full blood count showed moderate leukocytosis with neutrophil and monocyte predominance without anemia. Computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, performed after treatment had been initiated to exclude an intercurrent precipitating condition, was normal. She was treated with intravenous 30% dextrose, followed by a continuous intravenous dextrose infusion, and was admitted to the intensive care unit. Her consciousness returned to a GCS score of 15, and the acid-base disturbance corrected in parallel. Mechanical ventilation was not required. She was discharged from the intensive care unit after 48 hours, with complete neurological recovery. This episode did not represent a new diagnosis but rather an acute decompensation of an already known metabolic disease, precipitated by vomiting and a fast of approximately 20 hours. In a patient with a known disorder of gluconeogenesis, acute confusion following vomiting or reduced oral intake should prompt consideration of a hypoglycemic and lactic acidosis crisis until proven otherwise. Bedside glucose measurement and arterial blood gas analysis can establish the diagnosis within minutes, and intravenous dextrose is the treatment for both abnormalities.

42923309.title: Parathyroid Storm Secondary to a Parathyroid Adenoma Presenting With Recurrent Generalised Tonic-Clonic Seizures and Refractory Hypercalcaemia: A Case Report.
42923309.abstract: Parathyroid storm is a rare, life-threatening manifestation of primary hyperparathyroidism characterised by severe hypercalcaemia and acute multisystem deterioration. We report a 70-year-old woman with known primary hyperparathyroidism who presented with progressive weakness, confusion and reduced mobility and was found to have a corrected serum calcium concentration of 4.14 mmol/L. Despite aggressive intravenous hydration, she developed recurrent generalised tonic-clonic seizures, hypoventilation and reduced consciousness, requiring intubation and intensive care admission. Electroencephalography demonstrated severe diffuse cerebral dysfunction consistent with metabolic encephalopathy, while cerebrospinal fluid studies were unremarkable. Four-dimensional computed tomography of the neck identified a 1.8 cm right-sided parathyroid lesion. Hypercalcaemia remained difficult to control despite multimodal medical therapy, including pamidronate, calcitonin, cinacalcet and denosumab, with recurrent rebound hypercalcaemia. Urgent parathyroidectomy resulted in sustained normalisation of serum calcium and cessation of seizure activity, and histopathology confirmed a benign parathyroid adenoma. This case highlights the severe neurological complications of parathyroid storm and the importance of early multidisciplinary consideration of definitive surgery when hypercalcaemia remains refractory to intensive medical therapy.

42922945.title: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis with psychiatric manifestations and choreiform movements: a case report and literature review.
42922945.abstract: To summarize the clinical manifestations, ancillary examination findings, treatment course, and prognosis of a patient with neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis presenting with prominent psychiatric disturbances and choreiform movements, and to review the literature on the clinical spectrum of this disease. A 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and biopsy-proven podocytopathy with a "full-house" immunofluorescence pattern showing diffuse positivity for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q, diagnosed in February 2026; however, a definitive diagnosis of lupus podocytopathy remained uncertain, as the patient lacked systemic lupus erythematosus manifestations. She was admitted on April 3, 2026, with a 5-day history of psychiatric disturbances and involuntary choreiform movements in all four limbs, preceded by significant psychological stress (bereavement). Neurological examination revealed slowed responses and impaired calculation. Cranial MRI showed only bilateral periventricular small ischemic foci (Fazekas grade 1) with normal SWI. Initial EEG demonstrated sharp waves and spike-and-wave complexes in the left parietal, occipital, and temporal regions. CSF analysis revealed leukocytosis (21/μl, 90% mononuclear cells), protein of 0.4 g/L, elevated IgG index of 0.76, and elevated 24-hour intrathecal IgG synthesis rate of 5.63 mg/dl. CSF mNGS detected 453 EBV sequences (RPM) with a relative abundance of 97.48%. Serum EBV VCA-IgG and EBNA-IgG were elevated with negative IgM. Autoantibody testing followed a stepwise approach: initial screening for conventional autoimmune encephalitis, paraneoplastic, and demyelinating antibodies was negative; subsequent tissue-based assay (TBA) of CSF revealed strong positive immunoreactivity, prompting expanded antibody panel testing, which ultimately detected anti-neurexin-3α antibodies in serum (titer 1:30) and CSF (titer 1:100), confirmed by both cell-based assay (CBA) and TBA. The patient's condition progressively deteriorated, requiring endotracheal intubation on April 21 and tracheostomy on April 30. She received methylprednisolone pulse therapy at 500 mg/day for 5 days followed by a stepwise taper, intravenous immunoglobulin at 0.4 g/kg for 5 days, and five sessions of plasma exchange from April 30 to May 8 due to poor initial response. Choreiform movements gradually resolved after plasma exchange. She was weaned from mechanical ventilation on May 19 and decannulated on May 27. During the ICU course, she developed pulmonary infection with carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, which was controlled after antibiotic adjustment. Repeat EEG normalized on June 1. She was discharged from rehabilitation on June 9 on oral methylprednisolone 32 mg/day. On June 26, 2026, follow-up serum TBA showed weakly positive immunoreactivity, with the serum antibody titer remaining at 1:30. She subsequently received four infusions of efgartigimod at 400 mg each for consolidation immunotherapy and was transitioned to ofatumumab for long-term maintenance. At follow-up on August 6, 2026, the patient had no residual psychiatric symptoms or choreiform movements, with muscle strength recovered to 4+ in all limbs, full independence in daily activities, ambulation without assistance, and only mild gait instability. Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis is a rare but treatable condition. Choreiform movements expand its clinical spectrum. The coexistence of podocytopathy raises a hypothesis of shared antigenicity between renal and neuronal neurexin family members, though this remains purely speculative. CSF EBV reactivation may represent a bystander phenomenon or epiphenomenon of severe immune dysregulation rather than a confirmed trigger. Tissue-based assay provides crucial diagnostic direction when conventional screening is negative. Early recognition, comprehensive immunotherapy, and meticulous ICU management are important determinants of favorable outcomes. Given the inherent limitations of a single case report, these findings warrant confirmation through larger cohort studies.

42921992.title: Streptococcus constellatus-Associated Lemierre Syndrome Presenting With Cavitating Septic Pulmonary Emboli Managed by Video-Assisted Thoracoscopy.
42921992.journal: The American journal of case reports
42921992.abstract: BACKGROUND Lemierre syndrome is a rare septic thromboembolic disorder. Although historically associated with Fusobacterium necrophorum, non-fusobacterial cases caused by Streptococcus constellatus can present with dominant thoracic sepsis and delayed recognition. CASE REPORT A 25-year-old previously healthy man from northern Ecuador presented with 7 days of dyspnea, productive cough, fever, and hemoptysis, with profound hypoxemia and respiratory distress. Chest computed tomography showed bilateral cavitating septic pulmonary emboli and necrotizing pulmonary infection, and cervical vascular imaging confirmed left internal jugular vein thrombosis. One blood culture set grew Streptococcus constellatus susceptible to penicillin and ceftriaxone; sputum and pleural fluid cultures were sterile. He required intensive care, endotracheal intubation, empiric piperacillin-tazobactam plus vancomycin, escalation to meropenem plus vancomycin during clinical deterioration while resistant or polymicrobial infection was considered, therapeutic anticoagulation, and 2 video-assisted thoracoscopic procedures for empyema and a subsequent pulmonary abscess. After 4 weeks of intravenous antibiotics, he improved and was discharged on a direct oral anticoagulant for 1 additional month, remaining asymptomatic at short-term follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Lemierre syndrome should be considered in young adults with severe sepsis and multifocal cavitating lung lesions, even without pharyngeal symptoms. Empiric therapy should initially cover oral aerobes and anaerobes; once penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus constellatus is confirmed and no co-pathogen is recovered, de-escalation to targeted beta-lactam therapy, such as penicillin G or ceftriaxone, should be considered together with drainage of empyema or abscess when present.

42921827.title: Association Between Sputum Consistency and Extubation in Mechanically Ventilated Patients with Severe Pneumonia Receiving Nebulized Antibiotic Therapy.
42921827.abstract: Thick airway secretions may impair airway clearance and contribute to extubation failure in mechanically ventilated patients with severe pneumonia. Bedside sputum consistency assessment is commonly used in intensive care unit (ICU) practice, but its relationship with extubation outcomes remains insufficiently studied. Thus, we conducted a single-center prospective observational study of 80 mechanically ventilated adults with severe pneumonia who received nebulized sulfadiazine-polymyxin B as part of ICU care. Bedside sputum consistency was assessed using a semi-quantitative clinical scale before and after therapy. Change in bedside sputum consistency score was defined as the pre-treatment score minus the post-treatment score. The primary outcome was extubation success, defined as removal of the endotracheal tube without reintubation within 72 h. Nebulizer type, clinical characteristics, ventilator parameters, microbiological findings, and outcomes were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between changes in consistency and extubation success. Eighty patients were included: 27 received jet nebulization, 23 mesh nebulization, and 30 ultrasonic nebulization. Extubation success occurred in 50 patients. Patients with successful extubation had a greater improvement in the bedside sputum consistency score than patients without successful extubation (1.28 ± 0.78 vs 0.63 ± 1.00; p = 0.004). In a baseline-adjusted analysis, successful extubation was associated with a 0.63-point lower post-treatment score (adjusted mean difference, -0.63; 95% CI, -1.06 to -0.21; p = 0.003). In the parsimonious multivariable analysis, greater improvement in the bedside sputum consistency score remained associated with successful extubation (OR, 2.90; 95% CI, 1.51-5.56; p = 0.001), whereas baseline score was not independently associated with the outcome. Nebulizer type was not significantly associated with extubation success. In conclusion, the mechanically ventilated patients with severe pneumonia receiving nebulized sulfadiazine-polymyxin B, greater improvement in bedside sputum consistency was associated with successful extubation. Bedside secretion assessment may provide useful supportive information during extubation readiness evaluation. Further controlled studies using standardized and objective rheological measurements are warranted.

42921809.title: Music-Based Intervention in Postoperative Lung Transplant Care: A Feasibility Study.
42921809.abstract: Music-based interventions may support recovery in medical and surgical settings; however, their implementation during the immediate postoperative period following lung transplantation remains understudied. This single-center randomized feasibility study examined whether a structured music-based intervention delivered by board-certified music therapists could be implemented at clinically meaningful postoperative recovery milestones and explored preliminary trends in pain, anxiety, medication use, sleep, and length of stay. Twenty-nine adult lung transplant recipients (experimental n = 17, control n = 12) were enrolled between September 2021 and September 2023. Participants in the intervention group received music-based intervention sessions during spontaneous awakening trials, 24-48 hr following extubation, and within 72 hr of transfer from the intensive care unit to a step-down unit. Intervention components included patient-preferred live music, music-assisted relaxation, and optional receptive or active music engagement tailored to patient status. Intervention delivery was feasible across all three postoperative milestones, although challenges related to recruitment, retention, sleep measurement, and intervention standardization were identified. Exploratory analyses suggested lower observed pain scores and lower median acetaminophen use in the intervention group compared to standard care; however, no outcomes reached statistical significance. Anxiety outcomes did not differ between groups, and sleep measurement using consumer-grade wearable devices was not feasible. These findings support the feasibility of music-based interventions during postoperative lung transplant recovery and provide guidance for the design of future adequately powered trials using refined outcome measures, milestone-based intervention delivery, and improved implementation strategies.

42921488.title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Severity and Population-Specific Outcomes of Human Metapneumovirus Infection.
42921488.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a prevalent respiratory pathogen, but comprehensive estimates of severe clinical outcomes across populations are lacking. We synthesized the proportion of severe outcomes among people with laboratory-confirmed HMPV infection. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, medRxiv, bioRxiv, and Google Scholar from inception to 20 January 2026, without language restrictions. Observational studies reporting severe outcomes (hospitalization, intensive care unit [ICU] admission, respiratory support, mechanical ventilation, mortality) in laboratory-confirmed HMPV infection were eligible; studies enrolling only people who are immunocompromised without comparators were excluded. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed quality using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Pooled proportions were estimated using random-effects generalized linear mixed models with logit transformation. Subgroup analyses examined healthcare setting and age. Ninety-four studies (∼26 000 people who are HMPV positive) were included. Pooled proportions were 48% (95% CI, 20%-78%; 8 studies, n = 1445) for hospitalization; 12% (95% CI, 8%-16%; 26 studies, n = 14 522; Egger P = .03) for ICU admission; 40% (95% CI, 26%-56%; 18 studies, n = 4328) for respiratory support; 8% (95% CI, 5%-13%; 16 studies, n = 5543) for mechanical ventilation; and 3% (95% CI, 2%-5%; 29 studies, n = 13 657; I2 = 78.5%) for in-hospital mortality. Mortality was highest among adults (6%). Human metapneumovirus causes substantial hospitalization, ICU admission, and mortality, supporting strengthened surveillance, integration into respiratory virus prevention strategies, and accelerated vaccine development.

42921464.title: Clinical outcomes during the 2025-2026 and 2024-2025 influenza seasons in a US EHR network: an ecological comparison during A(H3N2) subclade K predominance.
42921464.abstract: The influenza A(H3N2) subclade K virus has predominated in the 2025-2026 season. This study compared the clinical severity of influenza between 2025-2026 and 2024-2025 seasons. In this retrospective cohort study, a multicenter electronic health record database (TriNetX) was used. The clinical outcomes after influenza infection confirmed by nucleic acid detection were ecologically compared between the 2025-2026 and 2024-2025 seasons with propensity score matching. There were 8965 and 8937 children and 7488 and 6947 adults with confirmed influenza A(H3N2) infection in the 2025-2026 and 2024-2025 seasons, respectively. After each propensity score matching, the odds ratios for children and adults were not assessed (due to the small number of events) and 0.87 (95% confidence interval 0.71-1.05), P = 0.148 for death; 1.32 (1.10-1.59), P = 0.003 and 0.91 (0.82-1.02), P = 0.092 for critical care admission; 1.06 (0.97-1.16), P = 0.191 and 1.01 (0.94-1.08), P = 0.803 for hospitalization; 0.88 (0.73-1.07), P = 0.197 and 0.93 (0.83-1.04), P = 0.194 for mechanical ventilation; and 1.10 (0.91-1.32), P = 0.320 and 0.93 (0.83-1.03), P = 0.177 for vasopressor use, respectively. In this electronic health record-based season-level comparison, no consistent adjusted differences were observed; however, the study could not directly assess subclade K-specific severity or rule out clinically relevant differences. Rapid and timely monitoring of clinical characteristics and severity in the case of an emerging influenza strain or subclade is important to guide preventive and therapeutic strategies against influenza.

42921273.title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Education and Training: A Review of Current Practices and Future Directions at a Single Center in Phoenix, Arizona.
42921273.abstract: The purpose of the study is to describe extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) training and education practices at our institution and participants' self-reported comfort with ECMO tasks before and after training sessions. ECMO is a life-sustaining intervention for critically ill patients with cardiac and/or respiratory failure. ECMO circuit management is complex and requires specialized training. This study describes pediatric and neonatal ECMO education practices at Phoenix Children's Hospital (PCH). We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected program-evaluation data. The education program ran from 2021 to 2025; anonymous pre- and post-training survey data were available only for 2024-2025. Registered nurses and ECMO primers completed surveys around 2024 water labs, and fellows completed surveys around boot camps in 2024 and 2025. Survey response rates were 90% (27/30) for spring 2024 water labs and 83% (25/30) for fall 2024 water labs. Among registered nurses and ECMO primers, self-reported comfort was numerically higher after training for managing ECMO emergencies (52% to 74%), ambulating patients (56% to 74%), independently maintaining circuit components (60% to 84%), and escalating pump issues (84% to 96%); all 95% confidence intervals for differences included zero. Fellow item-level response counts varied. Between 2021 and 2025, 273 patients were cannulated onto ECMO at PCH. In this single-center descriptive evaluation, self-reported comfort was numerically higher after sessions, with imprecise estimates; findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Neither competence nor patient outcomes were measured.

42920635.title: Low arterial oxygen-content burden during the first 24 h and hospital mortality in mechanically ventilated adults: analyses of MIMIC-IV and eICU.
42920635.abstract: Arterial oxygen content (CaO2) combines hemoglobin-bound and dissolved oxygen. A time-weighted CaO2 deficit could capture changing anemia and desaturation that a hemoglobin-only summary misses. We examined its association with hospital mortality and its added value beyond hemoglobin. In this retrospective cohort study, we included mechanically ventilated adults from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU). The MIMIC-IV 25th percentile of the first matched CaO2 value (12.48 mL O2/dL) was prespecified as an empirical cutoff and was applied unchanged to eICU. The first-24-h burden integrated the time-weighted deficit below this cutoff. Models were adjusted for demographics and diagnosis-derived case mix. We compared CaO2 burden with hemoglobin burden calculated at the same blood-gas time points and performed landmark, measurement-coverage, severity, and post hoc peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2)-stratified analyses. Burden was available for 14,050 MIMIC-IV and 20,780 eICU stays. CaO2 was strongly correlated with hemoglobin (r = 0.965 and 0.949, respectively), which explained R 2 = 0.932 and 0.901 of first-measurement CaO2 variation, respectively; median dissolved-oxygen contributions were 2.9% and 2.5%, respectively. Per 1-SD higher burden, adjusted odds ratios for hospital mortality were 1.33 (95% confidence interval 1.28-1.39) in MIMIC-IV and 1.29 (1.24-1.35) in eICU. Additional Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation adjustment attenuated the eICU estimate to 1.14 (1.10-1.19), while 24-h landmark estimates were 1.26 (1.21-1.32) and 1.19 (1.14-1.25), respectively. Cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) gains over matched hemoglobin burden were 0.006 and 0.010, respectively, and calibration was similar. In post hoc analyses, hemoglobin explained less CaO2 variation when first SpO2 was <90% (R 2 = 0.787 and 0.682, respectively) than when it was ≥95% (R 2 = 0.973 and 0.978, respectively); corresponding AUROC gains were 0.045 and 0.044 versus 0.002 in both databases. In cohorts dominated by preserved oxygen saturation, low CaO2 was predominantly an anemia-related signal, and its association with mortality was substantially attenuated by illness-severity adjustment. The burden is best viewed as a compact observational summary of the depth and duration of low arterial oxygen content, not as an independent measure of tissue oxygenation, a superior prediction model, or a treatment target.

42919446.title: Metabolic Syndrome Is Associated With Worsened Clinical Outcomes in Individuals With Necrotizing Pancreatitis.
42919446.abstract: Evaluate the relationship between metabolic syndrome (MetS) and clinical outcomes in individuals with necrotizing pancreatitis (NP) and infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN). MetS affects a significant proportion of the global population and is associated with low-grade systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation. This has implications for several disease processes, but the impact of MetS on patients with NP is not well characterized. A retrospective cohort study of patients admitted with NP at a single tertiary center was performed. MetS was defined as meeting any 3 of the following criteria: BMI ≥30 kg/m2, triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, fasting glucose ≥110 mg/dL, blood pressure ≥130/85 mm Hg, and low HDL (<40 mg/dL men, <50 mg/dL women). The need for intensive care, hospital length of stay, development of organ failure, and mortality were compared in patients with NP with or without MetS. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of IPN. A total of 276 (154 MetS, 55.8%) patients were identified. Individuals with MetS more frequently required ICU-level care (38.3% vs. 17.2%; P<0.001) and longer length of stay (9.0 vs. 5.0 d; P=0.029). There was a higher risk of sepsis in those with MetS (27.5% vs. 15.6%; P=0.019), as well as respiratory failure (31.2% vs. 18%; P=0.013), renal failure (35.7% vs. 21.3%; P=0.009), and in-hospital mortality (17.5% vs. 8.2%; P=0.024). The incidence of IPN was higher in patients with MetS (39.6% vs. 23.0%; P=0.003). The presence of MetS in individuals with NP was associated with worsened outcomes, including increased incidence of IPN, sepsis, organ failure, ICU admission, and mortality during index hospitalization.

42914956.title: Learning curve and clinical outcomes of robotic-assisted heart bypass surgery: Real-world evidence from India.
42914956.abstract: BackgroundRobotic-assisted coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) using bilateral internal mammary arteries (BIMA) provides a minimally invasive option for advanced coronary artery disease (CAD), but evidence on its learning curve and outcomes in the Indian population remains limited.ObjectivesTo evaluate the learning curve associated with robotic CABG using BIMA and to compare perioperative and clinical outcomes between the early and late phases of surgical experience in a real-world setting.DesignRetrospective, single-center, observational chart review conducted at a high-volume quaternary cardiac care center in India.MethodsThis retrospective chart review was performed for 341 patients who underwent robotic-assisted BIMA CABG between 2020 and 2025. The learning curve was assessed using risk-adjusted cumulative summation (CUSUM), while complication trends were examined through sequential probability CUSUM failure analysis.ResultsThe cohort comprised 295 (86.51%) males with a mean age of 59.56 ± 9.93 years and a body mass index (BMI) of 25.98 ± 3.74 kg/m2. Mean console time was 101.66 ± 29.99 minutes, ICU stay 2.85 ± 0.98 days, and hospital stay 6.01 ± 2.38 days; conversion to open surgery occurred in 2.93% of cases, with in-hospital mortality of 3.52%. CUSUM analysis identified case 125 as the proficiency inflection point, after which console time significantly decreased (94.95 ± 24.32 vs. 113.38 ± 35.04 minutes; p<0.001), while ventilator duration, ICU and hospital stay, complications, and mortality remained comparable between phases. Readmission and re-exploration rates were low (2.05% each), with no deaths at 6-month follow-up. CUSUM failure analysis confirmed complication rates remained within acceptable thresholds throughout the study.ConclusionsRobotic-assisted BIMA CABG demonstrated acceptable outcomes, with operative efficiency improving after approximately 125 cases. These findings support its feasibility in experienced, high-volume centers and warrant further multicentre evaluation.

42914789.title: Long-term communication and swallowing disability in adults with persistent critical illness following COVID-19: A mixed-methods observational study.
42914789.abstract: To describe the lived experience of communication and swallowing disability in adults with persistent critical illness following COVID-19. A mixed-methods study. Semi-structured interviews were conducted alongside patient-reported communication and swallowing outcome measures. Participants were recruited from a registry-embedded COVID-Recovery study. All patients were eligible if they were ≥ 18 years, positive PCR for SARS-CoV-2 and had persistent critical illness. This was defined as admission to ICU for >10 consecutive days with invasive mechanical ventilation for at least 24 h. Semi-structured interviews were used to explore communication and swallowing disability. Additional patient-reported outcomes were assessed with the Dysphagia Severity Rating Scale and the La Trobe Communication Questionnaire. General function outcomes were evaluated with the WHODAS 2.0, EQ-5D-5L, HADS, MoCA-Blind, IADL and IES-6. Of the 113 participants followed up, 29/113 (26%) reported communication or swallowing disability, and of these 17/29 (59%) consented to semi-structured interviews. From the 16 participants who answered questions about communication function 100% self-reported difficulty in ≥1 communication domain, including expressive language 13/16 (81%), voice 13/16 (81%), receptive language 9/16 (56%) and speech 5/16 (31%). Although all participants were consuming an oral diet and most with nil texture restrictions (13/17,76%), many reported ongoing swallowing concerns regarding safety and efficiency. Impacts of these new disabilities were beyond physical function and impacted on their activities and participation. Recovery was unclear, prolonged and compounded by judgement from others. Participants navigated their own recovery journey and whilst some were well supported, others described critical healthcare gaps. We identified approximately one quarter of people admitted to ICU for COVID-19 related critical illness with a length of stay of 10 days or more report ongoing communication and swallowing disability at 6 months. The impacts continued well beyond hospital discharge and highlight a need to specifically address swallowing and communication in recovery pathways. Specific assessment of communication and swallowing function is essential for individuals who experience persistent critical illness.

42912419.title: Macrophage activation syndrome is associated with high in-hospital mortality in patients with lupus.
42912419.abstract: ObjectiveTo study the clinical features and outcomes of macrophage activation syndrome in lupus.MethodsThis was a retrospective study conducted in a tertiary care referral centre from 2017 to 2022. Consecutive hospitalised adult-onset SLE patients diagnosed with MAS, fulfilling the Parodi criteria with ferritin >500 ng/ml were included. All the other hospitalised SLE patients without MAS served as controls. Clinical and immunological features and in-hospital mortality was compared between the 2 groups. Risk factors for mortality in MAS patients were determined performing univariate and multivariate analyses with a stepwise logistic regression.ResultsOf 623 hospitalisations in 451 SLE patients, 86 met the case definition for MAS and 526 served as controls. MAS occurred at the time of SLE diagnosis in 54 (62.9%). MAS was associated with fever, hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, cytopenia, and elevated transaminases. Disease activity (clinical SLEDAI 2K) was significantly higher in MAS (mean 13.7 ± 6.5 vs. 8 ± 5.9 (p < 0.001). In-hospital mortality was higher in the MAS compared to the control group [13 (15%) vs 6 (1%), p < 0.001]. Mortality in MAS was associated with higher ferritin (12092.9 ± 2826.5 vs 3993.6 ± 735, <0.001) and aspartate aminotransferase (544 ± 239 vs 167.66 ± 27.28U/L, p < 0.001), seizures (p = 0.035), altered mental status (p = 0.004), shock (p < 0.001), intensive care unit admission (p < 0.001), and mechanical ventilation (p < 0.001). On multivariate regression analysis -ferritin >2400{OR-8.1 95% CI: (1.46-44.85) p - 0.017} and seizures {OR-7.3 95% CI: (1.2-44.29) p - 0.030} were associated with mortality in MAS.ConclusionsMAS is a rare complication of active lupus identified by fever, elevated ferritin, liver transaminases and cytopenia and is associated with high in hospital mortality.

42910620.title: Venous Thromboembolism in Acute Necrotizing Pancreatitis Is Associated With Worse Outcomes, With Subtype-Specific Patterns: A Nationwide Analysis, 2016-2022.
42910620.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) complicates acute necrotizing pancreatitis (ANP), but outcomes across extra-splanchnic deep vein thrombosis (DVT), portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and splenic vein thrombosis (SVT) remain poorly defined. We evaluated national trends and in-hospital outcomes in ANP with versus without VTE and across VTE subtypes. Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), adults hospitalized with principal ANP were identified. Secondary diagnosis codes captured VTE subtypes. Primary analyses compared mortality and major complications in ANP with versus without VTE; secondary analyses compared outcomes by subtype. Among 110,225 ANP hospitalizations, 12.25% had VTE. ANP with VTE had higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.89, P<0.001), longer length of stay (adjusted mean difference 10.7 d, P<0.001), and higher hospitalization charges (adjusted mean difference $151,685, P<0.001). VTE was associated with higher rates of mesenteric ischemia, gastric varices, upper GI bleeding, AKI, sepsis, shock, respiratory failure, ARDS, vasopressor use, mechanical ventilation, blood transfusion, and ICU admissions. On subtype analysis, DVT (aOR 2.39, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 1.45, P=0.001) were associated with higher mortality; SVT was not significantly associated with mortality, though the analysis was limited by few events. PVT was most strongly associated with mesenteric ischemia (aOR 8.28, P<0.001), whereas gastric varices were most associated with SVT (aOR 11.37, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 3.73, P<0.001). VTE in ANP was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, systemic complications, and resource utilization, with substantial heterogeneity across subtypes. DVT-associated ANP showed higher rates of systemic complications, whereas PVT and SVT showed distinct territory-specific vascular-complication patterns. Prospective studies should evaluate phenotype-specific anticoagulation strategies.

42909257.title: Inhaled nitric oxide: Expanding indications beyond traditional boundaries.
42909257.abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that improves ventilation-perfusion matching with minimal effect on systemic blood pressure. Although the FDA approval is restricted to neonatal hypoxic respiratory failure associated with pulmonary hypertension, many clinicians now use iNO in adults with conditions where elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular dysfunction threaten stability and hypoxic respiratory failure. This review examines both the mechanistic rationale and the available evidence for such off-label use. Examples range from acute RV failure in the ICU to perioperative support in cardiac surgery, heart and lung transplantation, and severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, including COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). In these settings, iNO offers rapid afterload reduction and short-term improvement in oxygenation, but randomized trials are lacking and limited studies to date have failed to consistently show outcome benefits. Adverse effects such as methemoglobinemia, nitrogen dioxide toxicity, rebound pulmonary hypertension, and a potential increase in acute kidney injury risk in certain non-cardiac surgical populations. Additionally, cost considerations and other practical limitations must be weighed carefully. Overall, current evidence supports the use of iNO as an adjunctive therapy in carefully selected critically ill patients.

42908943.title: Development and internal validation of triage-stage prediction models for short-term critical outcomes among adult emergency department patients entering observation or hospital-based care: a retrospective study.
42908943.abstract: Risk stratification at emergency department triage may help identify patients who require closer assessment or monitoring. However, prediction models that rely only on information available at the triage stage remain less well evaluated. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models based on triage-stage information for predicting short-term critical outcomes in adult emergency department patients and to interpret a representative explainable model using SHAP analysis. This retrospective observational study included 1,842 consecutive adult patients who completed standardized electronic triage and subsequently entered an emergency observation or hospital-based care pathway at a tertiary general hospital between January 2022 and December 2025. The prediction time point and landmark were defined as completion of electronic emergency triage. Only patients who were free of all outcome components at the landmark were included, and candidate predictors were restricted to routinely available information recorded no later than triage completion. The primary outcome was the first critical event occurring during the subsequent 72 h: intensive care unit admission, endotracheal intubation or invasive mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, objectively documented escalation involving an implemented resuscitation-level intervention, or in-hospital death. Additional sensitivity analyses restricted the outcome to intensive care unit admission, intubation or invasive ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or death and refitted the model without emergency triage level. The cohort was randomly divided into a development cohort and a 30% hold-out cohort. Because the hold-out cohort had already been examined during the original analysis, it was not considered an independent validation set. The primary internal-validation analysis therefore consisted of 10 repetitions of nested cross-validation within the development cohort, using five stratified outer folds for performance estimation and four stratified inner folds for preprocessing and hyperparameter tuning. Logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, XGBoost, and LightGBM were evaluated using the same resampling framework. The previously examined exploratory hold-out cohort was retained only for secondary exploratory analysis. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, classification metrics, Brier score, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP-based interpretation. Bootstrap optimism correction was additionally used to assess overfitting. All 1,842 included patients were event-free at triage completion, and 214 experienced a short-term critical outcome during the subsequent 72-hour period, corresponding to an event rate of 11.6%. The development cohort included 1,289 patients with 150 events, and the previously examined exploratory hold-out cohort included 553 patients with 64 events. In 10 repetitions of nested cross-validation, the mean AUCs were 0.821 ± 0.012 for logistic regression, 0.817 ± 0.015 for random forest, 0.752 ± 0.018 for support vector machine, 0.831 ± 0.013 for XGBoost, and 0.833 ± 0.014 for LightGBM. XGBoost was highest ranked in 42% of repeated outer-validation results, LightGBM in 48%, and logistic regression in 10%. These primary internal-validation results supported broadly comparable performance among XGBoost, LightGBM, and logistic regression rather than consistent superiority of one algorithm. In the secondary exploratory analysis, the representative XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.828 in the previously examined exploratory hold-out cohort. At the development-derived threshold of 0.106, its accuracy was 0.770, sensitivity 0.656, specificity 0.785, positive predictive value 0.286, negative predictive value 0.946, F1 score 0.398, and Brier score 0.080. Its paired comparisons, sensitivity analyses, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP findings in this cohort were interpreted as exploratory. Repeated nested cross-validation showed broadly comparable discrimination for XGBoost, LightGBM, and logistic regression in predicting post-triage short-term critical outcomes. XGBoost was retained as a representative explainable model, whereas its performance and benchmark comparisons in the previously examined exploratory hold-out cohort should be regarded as secondary exploratory analyses. The study does not establish the superiority or independent validation of XGBoost. Evaluation in a genuinely unused temporal cohort and external prospective validation remain necessary before clinical implementation.

42908933.title: Dynamic changes in regional ventilation distribution and end-expiratory lung impedance using electrical impedance tomography: associations with weaning and extubation outcomes.
42908933.abstract: Accurately assessing the optimal timing for extubation remains a significant challenge in intensive care units (ICUs). The rapid shallow breathing index (RSBI) is widely used but lacks insight into regional lung physiology. This study aimed to characterize dynamic changes in regional ventilation distribution and end-expiratory lung impedance (EELI) using electrical impedance tomography (EIT) during spontaneous breathing trials (SBTs) and to explore their association with weaning and extubation outcomes. In this prospective observational study, 52 mechanically ventilated patients undergoing their first SBT were enrolled. EIT parameters, including the Global Inhomogeneity (GI) index, center of ventilation (COV), ventrodorsal ventilation asymmetry (|ROI V-D|), and changes in EELI (ΔEELI), were recorded at four time points. Weaning failure was defined as SBT failure, or as reintubation or noninvasive ventilation within 48 h after extubation. Extubation failure was defined as reintubation or rescue NIV within 48 h. Logistic models coded 1 = failure and 0 = success. SBT failure (n = 19, 36.5%) was associated with progressive deterioration of ventilation, with a significant increase in the GI index (p < 0.001) and a notable spike in |ROI V-D| at T3 (p = 0.005). Extubation failure (n = 9, 27.3% of SBT successes) was associated with a greater cumulative loss of end-expiratory lung volume (ΔEELI T4-T1) compared with the success group (p < 0.001). In secondary exploratory analyses, a combined MLE model of T4 RSBI and T3 GI showed an apparent AUC of 0.923 (95% CI 0.840-0.986) for SBT failure (optimism-corrected AUC: 0.905). A combined model of T4 RSBI and ΔEELI (T4-T1) showed an apparent AUC of 0.875 (95% CI: 0.688-0.988) for extubation failure; with only 9 events, this estimate is hypothesis-generating and requires external validation. EIT-derived parameters offer insights into regional ventilation changes during the weaning process. Increased ventilation inhomogeneity and ventrodorsal mismatch are associated with SBT failure, while loss of end-expiratory lung impedance is associated with extubation failure. Adding EIT parameters to RSBI provided exploratory incremental information for discriminating SBT failure and extubation failure in this cohort. These secondary analyses require external validation before any clinical application can be considered.Clinical Trial Registration: https://www.chictr.org.cn, identifier ChiCTR2500108219.

42908195.title: Bronchodilator Drug Delivery With Pressurized Meter-Dose-Inhaler Versus Jet Nebulizer With Noninvasive-Ventilation in Acute-Exacerbation of COPD: A Randomized Controlled Pharmacokinetic Endpoint Trial.
42908195.abstract: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) and inhaled bronchodilator therapy are foundational in the management of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD). However, optimal drug-delivery strategies during NIV remain uncertain. This study compared bronchodilator delivery via a pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI) interface versus standard jet nebulization during NIV. This randomized, open-label trial enrolled adults with hypercapnic AECOPD requiring NIV. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive ipratropium bromide via pMDI using a modified NIV mask, or via jet nebulizer integrated into the inspiratory limb. Serum ipratropium concentrations at 30 min constituted the primary bioequivalence endpoint, analysed using geometric mean ratios (GMR) and Bayesian posterior probabilities. Secondary outcomes included changes in physiologic parameters, blood gases, ventilatory asynchrony, duration of stay and cost effectiveness. Forty-four patients were randomized; 41 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (pMDI n = 20, nebulizer n = 21). At 30 min, geometric mean serum ipratropium levels were higher with pMDI (110.9 pg/mL) versus nebulization (51.6 pg/mL), yielding a GMR of 2.15. Bayesian analysis showed a 95.9% probability that GMR exceeded the non-inferiority threshold (0.80). At 6 h, differences again favoured pMDI (GMR 3.18; p = 0.022; posterior probability 99.8%). Physiologic outcomes, gas exchange, and NIV duration were similar between groups, though ICU stay was shorter in the pMDI arm. No safety concerns or device-related complications were observed. Post hoc cost analysis showed markedly lower therapy cost with pMDI. pMDI-based bronchodilator delivery during NIV using a customized interface is feasible, safe, cost-efficient, and achieves higher systemic drug levels than jet nebulization. Larger multicentre trials are warranted to determine clinical impact. Clinical Trials Registry of India CTRI/2023/07/054734.

42908181.title: Clinical Outcomes and Complications of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) in Adult Patients With COVID-19 in Central and Eastern Europe: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42908181.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
42908181.abstract: BACKGROUND Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a rescue therapy for severe COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). International datasets do not consistently report Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) separately. We aimed to assess mortality, clinical characteristics, and complications of ECMO-treated COVID-19 patients across the CEE region. MATERIAL AND METHODS We conducted a systematic review with single-arm meta-analyses of observational studies. PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from January 2020 to August 2025 for studies reporting ECMO outcomes in adult (≥18 years) COVID-19 patients from CEE countries, with at least 10 ECMO-treated patients. Conference abstracts and overlapping cohorts were excluded. The study protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251077593). RESULTS Twelve studies included 802 patients from 6 countries. Pooled in-hospital mortality was 65% (95% CI 0.57-0.72; I²=70.6%; 10 studies; n=691), and ICU mortality was 61% (95% CI 0.47-0.74; I²=85.8%; 7 studies, n=526). Country-level in-hospital mortality estimates were 54% for the Czech Republic and 76% for Poland but were descriptive because of the small number of studies and wide CIs. Mean pre-ECMO mechanical ventilation duration was 4.8 days (95% CI 3.7-5.8; I²=4.4%), ECMO duration was 17.8 days (95% CI 12.8-22.9; I²=79.8%), and ICU length of stay was 23.6 days (95% CI 7.5-39.7; I²=92.6%). Serious bleeding occurred in 40% (95% CI 22-61%; I²=85.7%). Certainty was very low for all pooled outcomes. CONCLUSIONS These CEE-specific estimates provide regional benchmarks, but substantial heterogeneity and very low certainty limit international comparisons and country-level interpretation. Standardized regional registries, prospective multicenter data, harmonized complication reporting, and long-term outcome assessment are needed.

42907377.title: Impact of Intraoperative Fluid Balance on Postoperative Clinical Outcomes after Single-Lung Transplantation.
42907377.journal: Annals of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery : official journal of the Association of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons of Asia
42907377.abstract: Single-lung transplantation (SLTx) recipients remain vulnerable to intraoperative fluid overload due to the presence of the native diseased lung. This study evaluated the impact of weight-adjusted intraoperative fluid balance on postoperative outcomes in brain-dead donor SLTx recipients. We analyzed 88 SLTx recipients categorized into low-fluid (<70 mL/kg; n = 44) and high-fluid (≥70 mL/kg; n = 44) groups based on the median (70.3 mL/kg). Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses, with natural-log transformation of mechanical ventilation duration and ICU stay, were adjusted for operative duration, blood loss, and extracorporeal life support (ECLS) use. Donor characteristics were comparable between groups. High fluid balance (≥70 mL/kg) was associated with significantly higher 48-hour primary graft dysfunction (PGD) Grade 3 rates (34.1% vs. 6.8%; P = 0.003), tracheostomy rates (36.4% vs. 9.1%; P = 0.004), longer mechanical ventilation (4 vs. 2 days; P = 0.016), and ICU stay (10 vs. 6 days; P = 0.011). Postoperative ECLS continuation at 48 hours was identical (2.3% vs. 2.3%). In multivariable analysis, high fluid balance remained significantly associated with 48-hour PGD Grade 3 (odds ratio: 4.91; P = 0.039). A high intraoperative fluid balance was independently associated with severe 48-hour PGD Grade 3 following SLTx, supporting careful attention to intraoperative fluid balance in these patients.

42906198.title: Right ventricular function across different non-invasive respiratory support strategies in severe community-acquired pneumonia.
42906198.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
42906198.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) systolic impairment is clinically relevant in acute respiratory failure, but its relationship with respiratory support modality in severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) outside the intensive care unit (ICU) is poorly defined. To compare RV longitudinal systolic performance and hospital length of stay (LOS) among patients receiving non-invasive ventilation (NIV), high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), or Venturi-mask oxygen therapy. In this single-centre prospective observational study, adults with severe CAP (Pneumonia Severity Index class IV-V) requiring high-concentration oxygen or non-invasive respiratory support were enrolled. The modality was selected in the emergency department according to the treating physician's clinical and gas-exchange assessment. Echocardiography was performed shortly after ward admission while patients remained on the initial support modality. Seventy patients were included (NIV, n = 21; HFNC, n = 22; Venturi mask, n = 27). Baseline demographic and cardiometabolic characteristics were comparable across groups. TAPSE and lateral tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S') showed a graded pattern, with the lowest values during NIV, intermediate values during HFNC, and the highest values with the Venturi mask (p < 0.001 for both). Mean LOS was 27.8 ± 5.0, 27.4 ± 2.9, and 15.2 ± 4.0 days, respectively (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, age and respiratory support modality were associated with LOS. RV systolic performance and LOS differed across clinically selected respiratory support groups. These associations may reflect clinical severity rather than device-related effects. These findings reinforce the often-overlooked clinical importance of RV assessment in acute respiratory failure, extending observations from ARDS cohorts to severe CAP outside the ICU.

42905942.title: Comparing the Post-Omicron Impact of COVID-19 and Non-COVID-19 Respiratory Viral Infections in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients.
42905942.abstract: Effective treatment and prevention for respiratory viral infections (RVI) in solid organ transplant recipients (SOTR) are lacking; clinical differences in COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 (ncRVI) post-omicron are unknown. We compared severity and outcomes across SOT groups. A single-center retrospective study of health system RVI in adult SOTR during 2022-2023 was conducted. Overall, 520 RVI episodes in 504 patients were included: 488 had 1 episode and 16 had 2 episodes. Lung, kidney, and heart transplant recipients comprised of 40.9%, 34.3%, and 20.8% of the cohort. There were 352 episodes of COVID-19 RVI and 148 ncRVI. All-cause and RVI-related hospitalization were comparable between COVID-19 and ncRVI (47.7% vs. 43.9%, p = 0.50; 32.1% vs. 31.1%, p = 0.91 respectively). Oxygen supplementation occurred in 11.9% of COVID-19 RVI and 11.5% of ncRVI with a maximum requirement (median, IQR) of 4.0 (2.0-18.8) and 2.0 (2.0-3.0) liters respectively (p = 0.005). Intensive care unit (ICU) admission occurred in 7.1% and 6.1%; non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in 2.3% and 4.1%; mechanical ventilation (I&V) in 4.0% and 2.0%; and inotropic/vasopressor support in 1.7% and 1.4%, for COVID-19 versus nCRVI, respectively. Patients with COVID-19 had ongoing symptoms in 16.8%, 10.2%, and 2.6% at 30 days, 3 month, and 12 month follow up respectively, compared with 16.9%, 4.7%, and 2.0% in ncRVI. Twelve-month mortality, rejection and graft dysfunction were similar between groups. COVID-19 and ncRVI pose significant and comparable risk to SOTR in this post-omicron era, in hospitalization, oxygen requirement, and persistent symptoms. Treatment and prevention should be prioritized in this population.

42904208.title: Effect of Etomidate Induction on Intraoperative Hemodynamics, Postoperative Inflammation, and Recovery After Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
42904208.abstract: Etomidate is commonly used for anesthetic induction because of its favorable hemodynamic profile but may cause adrenocortical suppression. Whether its use is associated with hemodynamic stability, and postoperative inflammatory and recovery outcomes after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) remains uncertain. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adults undergoing elective LSG from January 2014 through December 2024. The exposure was etomidate use during anesthetic induction. The primary outcome was time-weighted average MAP (TWA-MAP). Secondary outcomes included time-weighted average MAP below 65 mmHg (TWA65), hypotensive event rate, proportion of time with hypotension, generalized average real variability of MAP (ARV-MAP), postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) and interleukin-6 (IL-6), and recovery outcomes. Propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjusted for measured baseline confounding; sensitivity analyses assessed the robustness of the findings. A total of 1215 patients were screened, of whom 935 were included (271 received etomidate and 664 did not). After IPTW, etomidate use was associated with higher TWA-MAP (adjusted mean difference [MD], 3.01 mmHg; 95% CI, 1.78 to 4.24) and lower TWA65 (adjusted MD, -0.05 mmHg; 95% CI, -0.09 to -0.01), hypotensive event rate (adjusted MD, -0.16 n/h; 95% CI, -0.24 to -0.07), and proportion of time with hypotension (adjusted MD, -1.27 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.07 to -0.47). However, ARV-MAP was higher (adjusted MD, 0.28 mmHg/min; 95% CI, 0.10 to 0.47). CRP concentrations were higher on postoperative days 1 and 3 (adjusted MD, 9.15 mg/L; 95% CI, 5.41 to 12.89; and adjusted MD, 16.15 mg/L; 95% CI, 9.86 to 22.45, respectively), as were IL-6 concentrations (adjusted MD, 14.35 pg/mL; 95% CI, 11.52 to 17.18; and adjusted MD, 8.56 pg/mL; 95% CI, 6.66 to 10.46, respectively). Etomidate use was also associated with longer time to extubation and postoperative length of stay, and higher odds of ICU admission (all P <0.05). Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. In patients with obesity undergoing LSG, etomidate use during anesthetic induction was associated with a lower intraoperative hypotension burden but greater MAP variability, higher postoperative inflammatory marker concentrations, and worse recovery outcomes. These associations warrant prospective investigation to clarify their clinical significance. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2600123339).

42903899.title: Limiting collateral damage: Nosocomial infections in patients with temporary mechanical circulatory support.
42903899.abstract: The use of temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for patients with cardiopulmonary compromise is on the rise. While these tMCS systems provide life-saving interventions, they also pose a significant risk of nosocomial infections, which are associated with higher mortality rates. Patients receiving tMCS are critically ill and require intensive care, increasing their vulnerability to infections. Common nosocomial infections include bloodstream infections (BSI) and ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in patients with ECMO and wound-related complications in patients with microaxial temporary ventricular assist devices (tVADs). Key preventative measures include the incorporation of sound ICU practices such as chlorhexidine washes, minimizing disconnections, instituting VAP bundles, and promoting enteral nutrition. The practice of continuing prophylactic antibiotics while patients are on ECMO is not routinely recommended. While treatment strategies hinge primarily on antibiotics, ensuring adequate therapeutic levels of antibiotics is challenging and may contribute to suboptimal response to systemic antibiotics in these patients. A strategy of early liberation of patients from ECMO and conversion to temporary ventricular support (temporary LVAD, RVAD, or both) may promote early extubation and patient mobilization. Whether this strategy independently reduces infectious complications remains unknown. This review examines the epidemiology and etiology of nosocomial infections in patients receiving tMCS, summarizes current prevention and treatment strategies, and discusses the impact of infection on clinical outcomes.

42903563.title: Feeding practices during high-flow nasal cannula: current evidence and clinical implications for respiratory care.
42903563.abstract: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy is increasingly used as a noninvasive respiratory support modality across acute and critical care settings. Although nutritional management is integral to the care of patients with respiratory failure, established guidelines for feeding patients receiving HFNC are lacking, and clinical decisions vary widely, reflecting persistent uncertainty about HFNC's effects on swallowing function, airway protection, and aspiration risk. This narrative review found that HFNC may alter swallowing biomechanics, particularly at flow rates >40 L/min, potentially increasing the risk of choking and aspiration. Evidence on aspiration risk is heterogeneous, deriving largely from healthy volunteers and pediatric bronchiolitis cohorts. Adult evidence is limited to retrospective studies; the largest found no increase in respiratory deterioration with enteral feeding. Most institutions lack formal feeding protocols, and practice is driven by individual clinician judgment. Areas of consensus include the safety of early enteral feeding in hemodynamically stable patients and the avoidance of routine prolonged withholding of nutrition based solely on HFNC use. Disagreement persists regarding routine swallowing assessment, optimal flow thresholds during feeding, and the prioritization of oral versus tube feeding. Safe feeding in patients receiving HFNC requires a multidisciplinary, individualized approach that balances respiratory support against nutritional adequacy. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to define safe flow thresholds, validate bedside assessment tools, and establish standardized feeding guidelines, particularly in adult and critically ill populations.

42903157.title: Case Report: mNGS-negative Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome with small bowel obstruction as the initial manifestation in a glucocorticoid-exposed COPD patient: a fatal case.
42903157.abstract: Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome (SHS) is a life-threatening condition in immunocompromised hosts with an extremely high mortality rate. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) demonstrates limited sensitivity for parasitic detection, and its clinical value remains to be fully elucidated. The conventional microscopy remains an indispensable tool for the diagnosis of parasitic infections. A 73-year-old male patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and cerebral infarction presented with abdominal pain and distension for 7 days and no bowel movement for 3 days. He was diagnosed with incomplete small bowel obstruction at an outside hospital and treated with fasting, enemas, meropenem, and methylprednisolone. He was subsequently transferred to our hospital due to acute lower respiratory tract infection. Chest radiography revealed bilateral diffuse infiltrates, and his condition rapidly deteriorated, requiring admission to the intensive care unit (ICU), endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Stool smear and retrospective sputum examination both identified larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis. However, mNGS of sputum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) obtained upon admission failed to detect any parasitic sequences. The patient was treated sequentially with albendazole and ivermectin, in combination with broad-spectrum antibacterial, antifungal, and antiviral therapy. He ultimately died on February 11, 2025, due to severe pneumonia, sepsis, and bone marrow suppression. For immunocompromised hosts with multiple risk factors, particularly those exposed to glucocorticoids, active parasitic microscopic examination of stool and respiratory secretions should be pursued when unexplained pulmonary infiltrates coexist with gastrointestinal symptoms, even in the setting of negative mNGS results, to avoid missed diagnosis.

42902830.title: Computed tomography angiography with three-dimensional reconstruction for planning aortic valve replacement via right anterior mini-thoracotomy.
42902830.journal: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
42902830.abstract: This study explored the value of computed tomography angiography (CTA) with three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction in aortic valve replacement (AVR) via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. Clinical data were retrospectively collected from 168 patients who underwent AVR at our institution in China between 1 July 2018 and 1 September 2022. After 1:1 propensity score matching, the experimental group (right anterior mini-thoracotomy) and control group (median sternotomy) each comprised 43 patients. Patients in the experimental group underwent preoperative aortic CTA with 3D reconstruction to guide individualised selection of the intercostal incision site. Perioperative and clinical outcomes were compared between groups. The experimental group had significantly lower 24-hour postoperative drainage volume and shorter mechanical ventilation time, intensive care unit stay, and total hospital stay than the control group (all P<0.001). No intraoperative conversion to median sternotomy or postoperative reoperation for bleeding or pericardial tamponade occurred in the experimental group. Postoperatively, five patients (11.6%) developed atelectasis or pulmonary infection, five (11.6%) developed pleural effusion, and five (11.6%) developed subcutaneous emphysema or pneumothorax; none required thoracentesis. Aortic cross-clamping and cardiopulmonary bypass times were approximately 8 minutes longer, respectively, in the experimental group. At 24 months, the incidence of the composite endpoint-including all-cause mortality, cardiocerebrovascular complications, and readmission for massive pleural effusion or coagulation dysfunction-did not differ significantly between groups. Preoperative CTA with 3D reconstruction enables accurate localisation of the right intercostal incision for AVR via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. This technique preserves minimally invasive surgery benefits and does not increase risks of mid/long-term adverse events.

42901278.title: Diaphragm ultrasound-guided PEEP titration in COPD with dynamic hyperinflation.
42901278.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by airflow limitation, dynamic hyperinflation, and intrinsic positive end-expiratory pressure (iPEEP), which increase inspiratory threshold load and complicate ventilatory support. Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is the preferred initial ventilatory support for COPD exacerbations complicated by acute or acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis, while invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) may be required when NIV fails. External PEEP may reduce the inspiratory threshold load in patients with expiratory flow limitation, although excessive levels can increase lung volume and compromise hemodynamics. During IMV, PEEP adjustment requires assessment of respiratory mechanics, expiratory flow, hyperinflation, and cardiovascular tolerance. During NIV, where iPEEP cannot usually be measured directly, expiratory positive airway pressure (EPAP) should be adjusted according to clinical response, patient-ventilator interaction, and signs of excessive lung inflation. Inappropriate ventilatory assistance may also contribute to diaphragm dysfunction. Diaphragm ultrasound allows bedside assessment of muscle thickness and inspiratory thickening fraction (DTF), although these measurements are influenced by ventilatory assistance, respiratory drive, and lung volume. This review examines the physiological basis, available evidence, and limitations of using diaphragm ultrasound to complement PEEP adjustment in patients with COPD and dynamic hyperinflation. No DTF target or clinical benefit of ultrasound-guided PEEP titration has been established in this population.

42901157.title: Refractory Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Supported by Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation due to Leptospirosis at Réunion Island and a Literature Review.
42901157.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
42901157.abstract: Leptospirosis is a zoonosis prevalent on Réunion Island. Severe forms with acute respiratory failure can lead to refractory hypoxemia, requiring the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). The aim for the present study was to describe all cases of leptospirosis complicated by refractory acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring veno-venous ECMO on Réunion Island and to conduct a literature review.
