This retrospective observational study was conducted in a multidisciplinary intensive care unit of the University Hospital of Réunion Island. The aim was to describe the clinical, biological, and prognostic characteristics of patients who developed leptospirosis complicated by refractory ARDS requiring ECMO between January 2011 and December 2024. A total of 14 patients with a median age of 38 years and few comorbidities were included. The organ failure most commonly associated with respiratory involvement was acute kidney injury (93%). The median delay between mechanical ventilation and ECMO support was 0 (0-1) days. The median duration of ECMO support was short (7 [4-12] days). The mortality rate in this population was 29%. A systematic literature review revealed 50 cases of patients with leptospirosis requiring ECMO, with a median age of 34 years and a mortality rate of 20%. The favorable prognosis of patients with refractory ARDS due to leptospirosis justifies the use of ECMO. Early referral to a center equipped with ECMO is essential, given the rapid decline in respiratory function.

42900938.title: Rural-Urban Parity and Socioeconomic Gaps in Traumatic Brain Injury Outcomes.
42900938.journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
42900938.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of death and disability in the United States. Rural residence and low community income are independently associated with poorer health outcomes, mediated by variations in injury mechanism and healthcare access. We evaluated the impact of geographic location on injury patterns and acute-care metrics in adults with TBI treated at Maryland's statewide Level I trauma center. Adults (≥18 years of age) with radiographically confirmed TBI admitted between 2017 and 2021 were identified retrospectively from the institutional trauma registry. Rural residence was defined using Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes. This single-center study included only patients surviving to hospital admission. Primary outcomes included hospital length of stay (LOS) and discharge to hospice or death. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) and ventilator days and discharge disposition. Of 2,812 patients diagnosed with TBI during the study period, 267 (9.5%) resided in rural areas. Compared with nonrural patients, rural patients were older (median age 67 vs 60 years, P < .001) and lived in lower income communities. However, after adjustment for demographic and clinical covariates, rural residence was not associated with higher hospital LOS quartile category (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.18; 95% CI, 0.91-1.53; P = .20), discharge to hospice or death (aOR 1.67; 95% CI, 0.95-2.94), or discharge to a nonhome setting (aOR 0.93; 95% CI, 0.66-1.31). Groups showed no significant differences in critical care use, including ICU and ventilator durations. Worse outcomes were associated primarily with injury severity, including lower Glasgow Coma Scale scores and higher Injury Severity Scores. In a well-established regional trauma network, we found that among patients admitted with traumatic brain injury, residing in a rural area was not independently associated with worse in-hospital outcomes compared to patients who resided in nonrural (urban and suburban) communities. These findings suggest that a coordinated statewide trauma triage and access to tertiary neurotrauma care may help other systems similarly reduce rural disparities after severe head injury.

42900380.title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio as a marker of major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
42900380.abstract: This study examined whether the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and whether this association differs from that of absolute ICU admission glucose. This single-center retrospective study included 731 surgical episodes from 709 adults who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. SHR was calculated as the first ICU glucose divided by HbA1c-derived estimated average glucose. The primary outcome was an unweighted composite of 30-day mortality, stroke, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 3 acute kidney injury, reoperation for bleeding, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and deep sternal wound infection. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinically relevant covariates. The composite outcome occurred in 90 surgical episodes (12.3%). SHR was associated with the composite outcome after adjustment (odds ratio [OR], 1.103 per 0.1 increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.008-1.208; P = 0.033), whereas ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated (OR, 1.019 per 10 mg/dL increase; 95% CI 0.946-1.096; P = 0.626). SHR at ICU admission was associated with major postoperative complications in the primary analysis, whereas absolute ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated after multivariable adjustment. Confidence intervals for SHR included 1.0 in several sensitivity analyses. SHR warrants prospective evaluation as an early postoperative risk marker after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

42899468.title: Prospective, Population-Based Evaluation of Costs and Outcomes of Status Epilepticus According to the New Definition.
42899468.abstract: To address the paucity of data on outcomes and costs of status epilepticus (SE) following the updated 2015 International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) definition and changes in clinical practice guidelines in Germany. This prospective population-based study (October 2018-March 2020) included adult patients from postal code area prefix 35, representative of Germany, diagnosed with SE according to the 2015 ILAE definition. Costs were calculated using German Diagnosis-Related Groups (G-DRG). In total, 181 patients were included. Mean inpatient costs were €10,543 (median €6376; range €845-€133,267), corresponding to €939 per hospital day (median €580.8; range €76.8-€12,115). Mean length of stay (LOS) was 11 days (median 9; range 1-67). In univariable analyses, super-refractory SE was associated with higher costs and longer LOS (both p < 0.001), while acute symptomatic etiology was associated with longer LOS (p = 0.006). On multivariable analysis, mechanical ventilation was the strongest independent predictor of costs (Exp(B) = 2.918, 95% CI 1.753-4.857; p < 0.001), and etiology was overall significantly associated with cost variation (p = 0.022), with acute symptomatic SE showing the highest adjusted costs. Discharge destination correlated with SE severity, with most patients with non-refractory SE discharged home (p = 0.028). This study provides population-based data on costs and outcomes of SE in Germany, serving as a basis for future cost-effectiveness analyses. Compared with earlier studies, lower direct costs and shorter LOS were observed. Identification of high-risk constellations may support clinical decision-making and optimize monitoring, treatment escalation, and allocation of intensive care resources.

42899320.title: Comments on "Predictive accuracy of lung and diaphragmatic ultrasound in weaning from mechanical ventilation: a comparison with the Rapid Shallow Breathing Index".
42899320.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
42899320.abstract: Dear Editor, We read with interest the study by Shalini Bellan et al. on weaning outcomes in critically ill patients who underwent invasive mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours...

42898697.title: "White-Out Lung" Following Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) Initiation for Acute Refractory Respiratory Failure From Obstructive Lung Disease: A Case Series.
42898697.abstract: Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) has been used as a salvage therapy for respiratory failure despite mechanical ventilation. However, evidence for its utility and associated complications remains limited. We hereby present a case report of sudden lung collapse in patients with obstructive physiologies after initiating VV-ECMO. Our case report focuses on acute lung opacification that occurred within hours of initiating VV-ECMO. Given the growing number of ECMO runs for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), intensive care teams should be aware of ventilatory changes and complications associated with the lung rest strategy while on VV-ECMO, facilitating early recognition and prompt intervention.

42898614.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the timing of rehabilitation training intervention for recipients of extracorporeal membrane oxygenators.
42898614.abstract: To systematically evaluate the effects of early versus delayed rehabilitation training interventions (RTI) on clinical outcomes in patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized controlled studies, and observational cohort studies comparing early and delayed RTI in patients receiving ECMO. We searched databases including Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, China Science and Technology Journal Database, and China Biology Medicine disc from inception to 1 April 2025. Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers. Outcomes included complications, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay (LOS), duration of mechanical ventilation, ECMO duration, and in-hospital mortality. Twelve studies (five RCTs, four non-RCTs, and three cohort studies) were included. Compared with delayed RTI, early RTI significantly reduced the risk of complications [risk ratio (RR) = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.26-0.69, P < 0.001], shortened ICU LOS [mean difference (MD) = -1.12 days, 95% CI: -1.30 to -0.94, P < 0.001], and reduced hospital LOS (MD = -4.69 days, 95% CI: -8.11 to -1.27, P = 0.007). No significant differences were found in mechanical ventilation duration (MD = 0.14 days, P = 0.914), ECMO duration (MD = -1.77 days, P = 0.136), or in-hospital mortality (RR = 0.72, P = 0.097). Sensitivity analysis excluding one study demonstrated a greater reduction in hospital LOS significant (MD = -5.82 days, 95% CI: -9.34 to -2.30, P = 0.001), while other outcomes remained unchanged. Early RTI is associated with reduced complications and improved recovery outcomes (ICU/hospital stay) in ECMO patients compared with delayed RTI. However, due to the limited number and moderate quality of included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution. High-quality RCTs are needed to confirm these results. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420251025533, PROSPERO CRD420251025533.

42898067.title: Phenotypic characterization of patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage: a data-driven analysis of a multicentre, retrospective, nationwide cohort.
42898067.abstract: Severe diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) is a potentially fatal complication of ANCA-associated vasculitides (AAV). This study aimed to identify distinct clinical phenotypes among patients to the ICU, and to examine their association with mortality. We conducted an ancillary analysis of the national multicenter retrospective PLEXHIA cohort, including 197 patients with severe AAV-related DAH, defined by respiratory symptoms with new infiltrates consistent with alveolar hemorrhage, along with oxygen saturation ≤85%, high-flow oxygen or mechanical ventilation requirement. Kohonen self-organizing maps were applied to predefined clinical variables at ICU admission, excluding treatment and outcomes. Clusters were interpreted and compared regarding organ involvement, severity, management, and mortality at 30 and 90 days. Between 2012 and 2024, 197 patients (66 years old, 52% female) were included, revealing marked clinical heterogeneity. Three phenotypes emerged: The MPO pulmonary-renal (MPO-PR) cluster included patients with anti-MPO ANCA, renal involvement and high oxygen requirements. The mild-respiratory (Mild-R) cluster included predominantly female patients with less severe respiratory compromise and mild renal involvement. The PR3 multi-organ (PR3-MO) cluster involved younger patients with anti-PR3 ANCA, severe acute respiratory failure and multiorgan failure. Renal replacement therapy was most frequent in the MPO-PR group (73%), while invasive mechanical ventilation was most common in the MPO-PR and PR3-MO groups (71% and 68%). Thirty-day mortality differed significantly: 23% (MPO-PR), 4% (mild-R cluster), and 14% (PR3-MO cluster). This large ICU cohort highlights three clinically relevant phenotypes of AAV-related DAH, which could inform the development of phenotype-driven immunosuppressive strategies.

42897086.title: Gastrointestinal and Urological Tract Injuries During Cesarean Delivery: A Surgical Review With National Epidemiologic Data.
42897086.abstract: BackgroundCesarean delivery is the most common major surgical procedure performed worldwide, accounting for approximately one-third of US deliveries. Gastrointestinal (GI) and urological (URO) tract injuries are uncommon but disproportionately morbid complications. Increasing complexity, particularly repeat cesarean and placenta accreta spectrum (PAS), and uneven on-site subspecialty coverage have expanded the role of general surgeons as intraoperative consultants for these injuries, especially outside large tertiary centers.MethodsWe analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2005-2019) to characterize the contemporary epidemiology, predictors, and outcomes of GI/URO injuries during cesarean delivery, complemented by a literature review focused on intraoperative recognition and management principles most relevant to the consulting general surgeon.ResultsAmong 3 816 895 cesarean deliveries, 8891 involved a documented GI/URO injury requiring surgical intervention (≈233 per 100 000). Bladder injuries predominated (78.2%), followed by bowel repair (13.3%), bowel resection (7.8%), and ureteral injuries (1.3%). Injuries were associated with markedly higher ICU admission (3.4% vs 0.2%), respiratory failure (1.7% vs 0.1%), in-hospital mortality (0.22% vs 0.01%), and resource utilization. Prior cesarean delivery was the strongest predictor of URO injury (OR 2.92; 95% CI 2.71-3.13).ConclusionsGI/URO injuries during cesarean delivery are uncommon but highly morbid, and the operative complexity that produces them is rising. With variable on-site subspecialty coverage, the general surgeon is frequently the first operative consultant. Familiarity with intraoperative principles, prevention strategies in high-risk cases, structured recognition, and initial repair or damage-control temporization should be considered a core competency for surgeons covering trauma, rural, or emergency general surgery call.

42896438.title: Focal upper limb peripheral nerve injury after prone positioning in patients with ARDS: A prospective neurophysiological cohort study.
42896438.abstract: To investigate the incidence, timing, and neurophysiological characteristics of focal upper limb peripheral nerve injury (PNI) related to positional brachial plexus involvement after prone positioning in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Prospective single-centre observational cohort study conducted in the ICU of an academic tertiary-level hospital in Milan (Italy), between April 2022 and September 2025. All adult patients with ARDS requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and treated with prone positioning were screened. Patients underwent predefined longitudinal neurophysiological assessments at baseline, after each prone positioning cycle and before ICU discharge, whenever feasible. Focal upper limb PNI was defined using specific electrodiagnostic criteria. Cumulative incidence analyses accounted for ICU death as a competing event. Overall, 128 prone positioning cycles were performed in 54 patients. Focal upper limb PNI occurred in 11 patients (20.4%; 95% CI 10.6-33.5), after a median of 2 prone positioning cycles (IQR 1-3) and 36 h (IQR 21-50) of cumulative prone exposure. By day 28, the estimated cumulative incidence was 29.1% (95% CI 11.6-46.7), rising to 42.7% (95% CI 17.6-67.9) in patients exposed to at least one uninterrupted prone cycle lasting ≥24 h, compared with 8.6% (95% CI 0-20.4) in patients with shorter exposure (p = 0.047). Among prone positioning-related complications, pressure ulcers were the most frequent, occurring in 40.7% (22/54) of patients and predominantly involving the facial region, whereas no vascular access loss or accidental endotracheal tube displacement were recorded. Focal upper limb PNI was a frequent, clinically relevant, and potentially under-recognised complication of prolonged prone positioning in patients with ARDS. A prone positioning bundle should include systematic upper limb surveillance, repeated reassessment of limb, head and shoulder alignment, and early detection of focal asymmetric upper limb weakness, particularly during uninterrupted prone cycles lasting 24 h or longer.

42895961.title: Weathering the storm: Predictors and resource burden of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity after severe traumatic brain injury.
42895961.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
42895961.abstract: Reported incidence of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) after severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) approaches one-third, largely from cohorts that excluded early deaths. Predictors and resource consequences remain unclear. We identified predictors of PSH development and associations between diagnosis, PSH Assessment Measure (PSH-AM) subscores [clinical features scale (CFS) and diagnosis likelihood tool (DLT)], and resource utilization. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with severe TBI admitted to a tertiary care center intensive care unit (ICU) (October 2020-September 2025), stratified by PSH diagnosis. Two reviewers assigned PSH-AM scores. PSH cannot be diagnosed until the syndrome declares itself over days, so exposure is conditioned on survival; mortality is reported descriptively. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of PSH diagnosis. Log-transformed linear regressions estimated associations of PSH diagnosis and subscores with hospital length of stay (LOS), ICU LOS, and ventilator days. Thirty-day composite outcomes, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and landmark analysis evaluated robustness. Of 509 patients with severe TBI, 86 (17%) developed PSH. Younger age [odds ratio (OR): 0.97 (95% CI: 0.96-0.98); P<0.001) and higher ISS [1.05 (1.02-1.07); P<0.001] independently predicted PSH. PSH was associated with longer hospital LOS (372.9%), ICU LOS (278.3%), and more ventilator days (266.4%; all P<0.001). Mortality was 11.6% (PSH) versus 35.9% (non-PSH). IPTW demonstrated PSH had fewer days alive and out of hospital (-46.8%; P<0.001) and landmark analysis highlighted fewer ventilator-free days (-40.2%; P=0.0097) and ICU-free days (-46.9%; P<0.001). Higher DLT subscores were associated with longer hospital (36.3%; P=0.001) and ICU (23.3%; P=0.005) stays, whereas the CFS subscore showed no associations. The PSH diagnosis is contingent on survival. Younger patients with severe TBI who survive their initial injuries are more likely to develop PSH and occupy hospital beds meaningfully longer. The diagnosis likelihood tool, not the clinical features scale, tracks with that burden. Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

42895548.title: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in a high-altitude trauma cohort: in-hospital clinical outcomes and resource use in a propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study.
42895548.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
42895548.abstract: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models. Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001). Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay. Not applicable.

42894821.title: Beyond the Classic Triad: A Case of GQ1b Antibody-Positive Bickerstaff Brainstem Encephalitis Overlap Syndrome.
42894821.abstract: Anti-GQ1b antibody syndrome encompasses related postinfectious neurologic disorders, including Miller Fisher syndrome, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis. Recognizing overlap among these phenotypes can be difficult in the intensive care unit because profound unresponsiveness and loss of brainstem reflexes may be attributed to sedation or structural brain injury. A middle-aged man developed perioral numbness, blurred vision, ataxia, extremity paresthesias, and facial weakness after an upper respiratory infection. His condition progressed rapidly to respiratory failure, autonomic instability, generalized areflexia, and prolonged coma-like unresponsiveness. Brain imaging remained unrevealing. Cerebrospinal fluid showed albuminocytologic dissociation, and serum testing was positive for anti-GQ1b antibodies. He received intravenous immunoglobulin and intensive supportive care. Ocular and distal motor responses later returned, followed by resolution of the coma-like state, although ventilatory support was still required at transfer. This case demonstrates that severe anti-GQ1b overlap can produce profound but potentially reversible neurologic dysfunction and supports cautious neuroprognostication while the diagnostic evaluation is ongoing.

42894062.title: Immature neutrophil response is associated with cardiac complications after non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage.
42894062.abstract: Acute non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is complicated by systemic inflammation and cardiac dysfunction that contribute to the high rates of morbidity and mortality. To better define the mechanistic relationship between immune response and cardiac complications, we evaluated subpopulations of circulating immune cells and their associations with abnormalities of cardiac rhythm, injury biomarkers, and mechanical function after hemorrhage. In this single-site prospective observational study, we screened all adult patients presenting to our neurocritical care unit with non-traumatic SAH who required external ventricular drain (EVD) placement for treatment of hydrocephalus. Following informed consent, peripheral blood samples were obtained at post-bleed days (PBDs) 1, 3, 5, 7, and 10. Subjects were separated into groups based on evidence of cardiac abnormalities (cAbn(+))" versus "no cardiac abnormalities (cAbn(-))," and flow cytometric analysis was used to identify and quantify immune cell subpopulations. Circulating neutrophil-secreted factors, including myeloperoxidase (MPO), were measured in plasma using ELISA. We measured associations between these immune factors and cardiac abnormalities. Sixty patients were enrolled between January 2018 and August 2023. Our patient cohort was 65% female with a median age of 58 (IQR 51-68). Poor grade SAH (Hunt Hess = 4-5) occurred in 52% (n = 31) of patients. In the overall cohort 47 (78%) required prolonged mechanical ventilation (> 24-hours), and 52 (87%) underwent coil embolization/clipping of their aneurysm. The average ICU and hospital lengths of stay (LOS) were 18.5 (IQR 12.2-22) and 23 (IQR 18.2-33.8) days, respectively. In-hospital mortality for enrolled patients was 11.8% and overall mortality 6 months after discharge was 25% (n = 15). 40% (n = 24) of patients were discharged home, 37% (n = 22) to acute rehabilitation, 8% (n = 5) to SNF, and 3% (n = 2) to hospice. Cardiac abnormalities after SAH were associated with increased circulating neutrophil counts but not monocyte or lymphocyte levels. Circulating neutrophils in patients with cardiac abnormalities also had reduced cell-surface expression of maturation markers CD10, CD14, and CD16 in patients with cardiac abnormalities. Elevated levels of immature neutrophils and circulating levels of lipocalin-2, and myeloperoxidase (MPO) correlated with increased Hunt-Hess score, ICU, and hospital length of stay. Higher grade SAH was associated with increased immature neutrophil response, which was associated with cardiac abnormalities. These cardiac abnormalities tracked with increased levels of pro-inflammatory lipocalin-2 and MPO, and worse outcomes.

42893207.title: Investigation of the correlation between serum levels of interleukin-6 and clinical and paraclinical findings in COVID-19 patients.
42893207.journal: Current therapeutic research, clinical and experimental
42893207.abstract: COVID-19 frequently presents with pneumonia. Impaired immune function, particularly in older adults and immunocompromised individuals, increases susceptibility to infection and contributes to higher morbidity and mortality. Among inflammatory cytokines, Interleukin-6 (IL-6) plays a pivotal role in immune dysregulation and cytokine storm. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the association between serum IL-6 levels and clinical, laboratory, radiological, and outcome-related findings among hospitalized patients with COVID-19. This descriptive-analytical cross-sectional study included 210 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at Shahid Beheshti Hospital, Kashan. Serum IL-6 was measured as part of their diagnostic and therapeutic workup. Demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, laboratory markers, imaging findings, and outcomes were recorded. Patients with incomplete data were excluded. Data were analyzed using SPSS software version 26. The mean age of patients was 50.37 ± 17.48 years, with a slight male predominance (51%). Hypertension was the most common comorbidity (31.9%). Abnormal laboratory markers included elevated LDH (64.3%), ESR (61.0%), lymphopenia (59.5%), and CRP (58.6%). Pulmonary involvement on CT was noted in 91.5% of patients, with moderate involvement most frequent (41.4%). ICU admission occurred in 17.1% and mechanical ventilation was required in 10.5%. The mean CALL score was 8.63 ± 2.33, and average hospital stay was 6.70 ± 5.27 days. Serum IL-6 levels were significantly associated (P < 0.05) with age, oxygen saturation, lymphopenia, LDH, CRP, CT involvement, disease severity, ICU admission, mortality, and length of hospitalization. Elevated serum IL-6 strongly reflects disease severity and adverse outcomes in COVID-19, highlighting its potential as a prognostic biomarker to guide clinical assessment and management.

42891931.title: Diagnostic yield of endotracheal aspirate and bronchoalveolar lavage in ventilator-associated pneumonia: A single-centre study.
42891931.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy of endotracheal aspirate (ETA) with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) culture, considered the reference standard, in identifying the causative pathogens of VAP. This study was conducted as a cross-sectional study at Haji Adam Malik General Hospital, Medan, Indonesia. A total of 95 samples from mechanically ventilated patients were analysed using both ETA and BAL in similar institutions. The results demonstrated that 49 samples were positive by both ETA and BAL, while 11 were BAL-positive but ETA-negative, and 31 were ETApositive but BAL-negative. The sensitivity of ETA culture was 81.67%, whereas specificity was 11.43%. The positive predictive value (PPV) was 61.25%, and the negative predictive value (NPV) was 26.67%, yielding an overall diagnostic accuracy of 55.79%. These findings highlight the moderate reliability of ETA in detecting VAP pathogens, with limitations in ruling out infection due to its low NPV. To conclude, the relatively high sensitivity and ease of use suggest that ETA remains a useful initial diagnostic tool, particularly in resource-limited settings, though confirmation with more definitive methods, such as BAL, is recommended to guide appropriate antimicrobial therapy.

42891390.title: Myxoedema Coma With Type 2 Respiratory Failure and Hypothermia in an Oedematous Patient: A Case Report.
42891390.abstract: Myxoedema coma is a rare, life-threatening endocrine emergency representing the most severe form of hypothyroidism. We present the case of a South Asian woman in her early 70s admitted with generalised oedema, chest pain, general malaise, and reduced appetite. Initially treated as decompensated heart failure, she deteriorated with hypothermia, hypotension, bradypnea, and reduced consciousness, requiring intensive care admission and intubation. Thyroid function testing revealed profound hypothyroidism (TSH 67 mU/L, T4 <2 pmol/L), confirming myxoedema coma. She received intravenous liothyronine and levothyroxine with clinical improvement. This case highlights the noteworthy phenomenon of cold hypercapnia alongside highlighting the diagnostic challenges of myxoedema coma, which may mimic or exacerbate cardiac and respiratory failure. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion in at-risk patients, as delayed recognition and treatment significantly increase mortality.

42891078.title: Efficacy of combination therapy with minocycline for treating Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infections.
42891078.abstract: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is a multidrug-resistant opportunistic pathogen associated with substantial in-hospital mortality. However, data supporting the efficacy of treating S. maltophilia infections using a combination of antimicrobials remain inconclusive. To assess whether adjunctive minocycline improves clinical outcomes of S. maltophilia infections compared with standard monotherapy. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted at Siriraj Hospital, Thailand. Adults with confirmed S. maltophilia infections were randomized to receive minocycline or a matching placebo in addition to monotherapy with either levofloxacin or trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. This trial enrolled 112 patients (71.4% [n = 80/112] of patients requiring an intensive care unit [ICU] and 66.1% [n = 74/112] of patients were diagnosed with ventilator-associated pneumonia [VAP]). Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were balanced between intervention and control groups. Adjunctive minocycline did not significantly reduce 28-day-mortality (n = 24/55[43.6%] vs n = 22/57[38.6%], P = 0.590) but did achieve significantly higher microbiological response rates at early assessment (n = 25/55[45.5%] vs n = 8/57[14.0%], P < 0.001) and the end of treatment (n = 44/55[80.0%] vs n = 32/57[56.1%], P = 0.023). In contrast, clinical response rates did not differ between groups at either 72 h after the start of study treatment or the end of study treatment. In multivariable analysis, two factors were independently associated with 28-day mortality: history of antibiotic use before admission (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 7.65, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.04-28.76; P = 0.030) and septic shock (aOR: 7.24, 95% CI: 2.75-19.23; P < 0.001). Although adding minocycline to either levofloxacin or trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole therapy enhanced microbiological eradication, it did not confer a measurable survival or clinical advantage. Combination therapy was well tolerated. This study is potentially of interest to those treating ICU patients, as the majority of infections were VAP.

42889781.title: Phenotypic Characterization of Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolated From Patients With Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia: Insights Into Resistance Mechanisms and Biofilm Formation.
42889781.abstract: Background In patients receiving mechanical ventilation in intensive care units (ICUs), ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a serious illness connected with healthcare. Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa)is among the most often used pathogens linked to VAP and is increasingly characterized by multidrug resistance, β-lactamase production, and biofilm-forming ability. This study focused on assessing the antimicrobial susceptibility pattern, prevalence of multidrug resistance, extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) production, metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) production, and biofilm-forming ability among isolates of P. aeruginosa collected from endotracheal tube (ETT) aspirates of individuals with VAP. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional research study was carried out in the Microbiology Department at Krishna Charitable Hospital and Medical Research Center, Karad, India. A total of 104 non-repetitive P. aeruginosa isolates acquired from ETT aspirates of patients clinically suspected of VAP were included. Identification was carried out utilising conventional microbiological and biochemical methods. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method. ESBL and the production of MBLs were detected phenotypically by combined disk diffusion methods. The Congo red agar (CRA) method and the Christensen's tube method were used to evaluate biofilm development. Results Among the 104 VAP patients, 72 (69.23%) were male, and 32 (30.77%) were female. The highest proportion of cases was observed in the 21-40-year age group (45.65%). Most (49.04%) of VAP cases occurred in the medical intensive care unit (MICU), and 54.81% of cases appeared five days after starting mechanical ventilation. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing revealed complete resistance to piperacillin and imipenem (100% each), followed by piperacillin-tazobactam and meropenem (98.08% each), ciprofloxacin (97.12%), ceftazidime (95.19%), levofloxacin (94.23%), and cefepime (87.50%). Aztreonam demonstrated the highest susceptibility (83.65%). ESBL production was detected in 7 (6.73%) isolates, whereas MBL production was identified in 80 (76.92%) isolates. Biofilm formation was observed in 54 (51.92%) isolates by the Christensen's tube method and in 23 (22.12%) isolates by the CRA method. Conclusions A significant occurrence of multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa was found among those who had VAP. Extensive antimicrobial resistance, high MBL production, and frequent biofilm formation highlight the therapeutic obstacles linked to these infections. Continuous surveillance of antimicrobial resistance, strict infection-control measures, and judicious antibiotic use are essential to reduce the transmission of resistant strains and improve patient outcomes.

42886572.title: Influence of Perioperative Variables on Surgical Site Infection in Patients With Frailty and Prefrailty Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
42886572.abstract: Surgical site infection (SSI) in patients with frailty undergoing myocardial revascularization is a major clinical challenge, and there is a gap in the literature related to this topic. This study aimed to identify perioperative variables associated with SSI in patients with frailty and prefrailty undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting within 30 days of the procedure. This retrospective observational study included 467 patients with frailty or prefrailty aged 60 years and older who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting in 6 Brazilian centers between January 2018 and December 2024. Frailty was defined using the Fried criteria. SSI was defined as a wound with exposed tissue with positive culture requiring antibiotic treatment. Univariate and multivariate analyses were carried out. The rate of SSI was 5.6% (26/467). The New York Heart Association classification (P=.02), Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI; P=.01), use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB; P=.003), CPB time (P=.02), total surgery time (P<.001), occurrence of bleeding (P=.04), mechanical ventilation time (P=.001), length of hospital stay (P<.001), intensive care unit stay (P<.001), and need for reoperation (P<.001) variables were associated with SSI in unadjusted comparisons. In the multivariate model, the CCI (odds ratio 1.58, 95% CI 1.25-1.99; P<.001) and use of CPB (odds ratio 4.89, 95% CI 1.71-13.94; P=.003) were independently associated with SSI. The CCI and the use of CPB were independently associated with SSI.

42886410.title: Mechanical ventilation-associated AKI: toward a multimodal and kidney-protective ventilatory framework.
42886410.abstract: Mechanical ventilation-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) represents a complex manifestation of lung-kidney cross-talk driven by hemodynamic alterations, neurohumoral activation, systemic inflammation and disturbances in gas exchange and acid-base homeostasis. Beyond static ventilatory settings, increasing evidence suggests that dynamic fluctuations in airway and perfusion parameters, including static driving pressure (ΔP), positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), mean airway pressure (Pmean), and effective renal perfusion pressure (eRPP) may substantially influence renal vulnerability during mechanical ventilation. This comprehensive narrative review synthesizes current mechanistic and clinical evidence on the relationship between mechanical ventilation and AKI and proposes an integrated framework for future research on the interplay between ventilatory stress, venous congestion, renal perfusion, and inflammatory injury. Emerging bedside tools such as renal Doppler indices, venous excess ultrasound score (VExUS), and kidney injury biomarkers are discussed as components of an integrated physiologic approach for early recognition and risk stratification of ventilator-associated AKI. We further propose a multimodal conceptual framework integrating respiratory mechanics, congestion assessment, perfusion monitoring, and biomarkers to support individualized kidney-protective ventilation strategies. Future research should prioritize standardized physiologic monitoring, time-varying exposure analyses, causal mediation approaches, and prospective multicenter studies to better define renal-protective ventilatory targets and advance precision critical care.

42886404.title: Device-Associated Sepsis and Brain Injury: Transitioning From Early Infection Control to Late Neuroprotection.
42886404.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a complex neuroinflammatory condition characterized by diffuse brain dysfunction arising from systemic infection without direct central nervous system invasion. In modern critical care, device-associated infections (DAIs) caused by invasive medical devices, such as central line-associated bloodstream infections, ventilator-associated pneumonia, and catheter-associated urinary tract infections, have become critical drivers of intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired sepsis. Biofilm formation on these devices establishes persistent inflammatory reservoirs that continuously shed microorganisms, pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs), and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) into the circulation, sustaining systemic immune activation. This review outlines an integrated mechanistic framework linking DAIs to acute brain dysfunction. Systemic inflammation and endothelial activation trigger microvascular dysfunction, impaired cerebral autoregulation, and blood-brain barrier disruption. These peripheral vascular alterations allow inflammatory mediators to access the central nervous system, where they induce microglial and astrocytic reactivity. Persistent neuroimmune activation compromises neurotransmitter homeostasis-causing glutamate excitotoxicity and cholinergic deficits-while impairing neuronal mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. The resulting oxidative stress, energy failure, and self-amplifying neuroinflammatory feedback loops culminate in synaptic damage and neuronal injury. Clinically, this manifests as altered consciousness, delirium, seizures, and long-term neurocognitive impairment. By framing SAE as a concurrent, multidimensional continuum rather than a linear sequence, this review highlights the critical role of early infection prevention, timely device removal, and targeted neuroprotective strategies aimed at stabilizing vascular integrity and mitigating neuroinflammation.

42885872.title: Dysregulated complement activation in COVID-19: The Role of Soluble Complement Inhibitors.
42885872.abstract: In viral infections, complement activation can contribute to viral clearance, but excessive activation, as observed in severe COVID-19, may drive immunopathology. While much is known about complement-activating factors in COVID-19, insight into the role of endogenous complement inhibitors remains limited. We performed a longitudinal analysis within the BEAT-COVID cohort, comprising hospitalized patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) or ward, and age-matched healthy controls. Serum levels of the complement activation marker soluble membrane attack complex (sC5b-9) and soluble inhibitors C1-Inhibitor (C1-INH), C4b-Binding Protein (C4BP), Factor H, and Factor I were measured by ELISA. In vitro endothelial complement sensitivity was assessed by flow cytometry. Soluble inhibitors were also measured in a cohort of patients with long COVID. Patients admitted to the ICU showed elevated sC5b-9 levels compared to patients admitted to the ward and controls, correlating with disease severity, length of hospitalization, and need for mechanical ventilation, but not mortality. Unexpectedly, levels of all soluble complement inhibitors were elevated, particularly in patients admitted to the ICU. Factor H levels positively correlated with sC5b-9. Endothelial cells pre-incubated with serum from patients admitted to the ICU became more susceptible to complement attack. In patients with long COVID, Factor H and C4BP levels remained elevated compared to pre-pandemic healthy controls. Severe COVID-19 is characterized by extensive complement activation despite elevated circulating inhibitor levels, suggesting impaired local complement regulation at the cell surface, potentially amplified by overwhelming systemic activation, rather than inhibitor deficiency.

42885332.title: Immediate versus gradual noninvasive ventilatory pressure-or-duration step-down in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: a randomized trial.
42885332.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
42885332.abstract: Despite the proven role of noninvasive ventilation (NIV) as an effective treatment for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure (AHRF) in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), no clear agreement has been reached regarding the ideal weaning strategy. This study aimed to compare three NIV weaning strategies in terms of efficiency and safety among COPD patients with AHRF. A total of 105 COPD patients stabilized on NIV were enrolled in this randomized clinical trial and equally distributed into three groups (n=35 each): duration step-down (group A), pressure step-down (group B), and immediate withdrawal (group C). The primary endpoint was successful weaning within 48 hours. Secondary outcomes included duration of NIV use, lengths of ICU and hospital stay, predictors of weaning failure, and complication rates. The results of this study indicated that successful weaning rates differed significantly among the groups, being highest in group A (82.9%), followed by group B (74.3%), and lowest in group C (54.3%) (p<0.01). Compared with other strategies, immediate withdrawal was associated with higher rates of weaning failure. Although NIV duration was significantly shorter in group C (p<0.001), complication rates and post-discharge outcomes were similar across the three groups. In this trial, gradual duration- and pressure-based step-down strategies were associated with higher rates of successful NIV weaning than immediate withdrawal, with the highest observed success rate in the duration-based step-down group.

42882100.title: Malignant Tracheal Stenosis: A Narrative Review of Current Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approaches.
42882100.abstract: Background: Malignant tracheal stenosis (MTS) is a rare, life-threatening condition caused by primary tracheal tumor, mainly adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), and more rarely other primary neoplasms such as lymphomas, or local extension/metastasis from adjacent malignancies (thyroid, esophageal, lung, or mediastinal cancers). Accounting for <0.1% of respiratory tumors, MTS presents with progressive respiratory failure, requiring urgent multidisciplinary care involving thoracic surgery, interventional pulmonology, oncology, and intensive care. Diagnosis relies on clinical evaluation, advanced imaging and endoscopy. Bronchoscopy (BC) remains the best investigation for direct visualization and biopsy or performing therapeutic maneuvers. Prognosis depends on histology, local extent, and achieving R0 resection. Tracheal resection with primary anastomosis remains the curative standard for resectable cases. Interventional procedures (debulking, laser, cryotherapy, stenting) are essential for palliative management and acute stabilization. Methods: A structured (non-systematic) search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science (1965-2025) was performed using MeSH/Emtree terms and free-text keywords. Studies were included if they evaluated adult patients with malignant central airway stenosis, primary tracheal tumors, or secondary invasion undergoing surgical, bronchoscopic, or multimodal interventions, including ECMO support. Results: Malignant tracheal stenosis (MTS)-predominantly adenoid cystic and squamous cell carcinomas-imposes a critical clinical burden despite its low incidence. Complete surgical resection with negative margins remains the curative treatment for resectable disease. In unresectable cases, multimodal palliative interventions (stenting, laser/electrocautery ablation, and mechanical debulking) provide rapid airway restoration and quality-of-life improvements, whereas ECMO is an established rescue or adjunctive support strategy in selected critical airway procedures performed in experienced centers. Three-dimensional bioprinting and tissue-engineered reconstruction remain experimental or early clinical, and bioresorbable stents and artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools remain investigational; none is currently part of routine MTS management. Conclusions: R0 resection for appropriately selected resectable disease and interventional airway management for unresectable symptomatic disease are the best-supported strategies, although the evidence derives mainly from retrospective series from specialized centers. Emerging technologies require prospective validation before clinical adoption. Management should be individualized, multidisciplinary and centralized in experienced airway centers.

42882032.title: Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia: The Role of Kidney-Lung Crosstalk and Renal Replacement Therapy, a Narrative Review.
42882032.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) results from dynamic inter-organ interactions rather than isolated organ failures. Among these, kidney-lung crosstalk is a key determinant of outcomes in critically ill patients. Acute kidney injury (AKI) promotes pulmonary dysfunction through hemodynamic, inflammatory, endothelial, and metabolic mechanisms, while acute respiratory failure and mechanical ventilation may aggravate renal injury. Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) may represent a clinical consequence of these interactions, although causality remains uncertain. Renal replacement therapy (RRT) may further influence kidney-lung crosstalk through several physiological mechanisms. To summarize current evidence on kidney-lung crosstalk, evaluate its potential contribution to VAP susceptibility, and examine the role of RRT in modulating these interactions. Methods: Narrative review of experimental, translational, and clinical studies investigating bidirectional kidney-lung interactions in critical illness. Results: Kidney-to-lung crosstalk involves fluid overload, venous congestion, immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, and metabolic disturbances. Lung-to-kidney signaling is driven by mechanical ventilation, ventilator-induced lung injury, hypoxemia, and hypercapnia. Clinical evidence is strongest for fluid overload, venous congestion, and mechanical ventilation, whereas endothelial dysfunction and uremic toxins remain supported mainly by experimental data. AKI-associated immune dysfunction and prolonged mechanical ventilation provide biologically plausible mechanisms linking AKI to VAP, but definitive causal evidence is lacking because of methodological limitations. RRT may influence these interactions through optimized fluid balance, correction of acid-base disorders, improved antimicrobial pharmacokinetics, and potentially extracorporeal immunomodulation. However, no randomized trial has demonstrated a direct reduction in VAP incidence attributable to RRT. Conclusions: Kidney-lung crosstalk is a major driver of organ dysfunction in critical illness, yet translation into targeted therapies remains limited. Current evidence supports integrated organ-protective strategies-including lung-protective ventilation, individualized fluid management, VAP prevention, and optimized antimicrobial therapy-while future advances will rely on biological phenotyping, biomarker-guided risk stratification, and robust causal inference approaches.

42881739.title: Effects of a Standardized Music Intervention on Propofol Requirements and Serum Interleukin-6 and Prolactin in Deeply Sedated Mechanically Ventilated Adults: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
42881739.abstract: Background/Objectives: Prolonged exposure to sedative agents in critically ill patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Music interventions have emerged as a promising non-pharmacological strategy to improve patient comfort and potentially reduce sedative requirements. This prespecified secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial originally powered to detect differences in cortisol concentrations evaluated the effects of a standardized music intervention on sedative requirements and selected inflammatory and neuroendocrine biomarkers in deeply sedated mechanically ventilated adults. Methods: An open-label randomized controlled trial involving 110 critically ill adults receiving IMV under deep sedation was conducted. Participants were randomly assigned to a 60-min standardized music intervention delivered through active noise-cancelling headphones or to standard care. Changes in sedative requirements, serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) and prolactin (PRL) concentrations, physiological parameters, and safety outcomes were assessed. Results: Among participants receiving propofol at the time of the intervention (n = 84), the music intervention group showed a significantly greater reduction in propofol requirements than those receiving standard care (between-group difference 0.079 mg/kg/h, 95% CI 0.008-0.149; p = 0.029). Any reduction in propofol requirements was observed in 46.7% of intervention participants compared with 7.7% of controls. BIS values remained within the target range for deep sedation throughout the intervention period, and no clinically relevant changes were observed in physiological or ventilatory parameters. No significant between-group differences were observed in IL-6 or PRL concentrations after adjustment for baseline values (IL-6: p = 0.606; PRL: p = 0.093). No intervention-related adverse events were reported. Conclusions: A standardized music intervention was associated with reduced propofol requirements without evidence of a between-group difference in BIS trajectory during the intervention period and without clinically relevant physiological instability in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients. No significant between-group effects were observed on IL-6 or PRL concentrations during the study period. As a prespecified secondary analysis of a trial originally powered for a different primary outcome, these findings should be interpreted in that context and warrant confirmation in future randomized trials specifically designed to evaluate music-related effects on sedative requirements. Future randomized trials incorporating appropriate attention-control conditions are warranted to further clarify the specific effects attributable to the musical stimulus.

42966646.title: Dysphagia in Patients With High-Flow Nasal Cannulas: Risk and Practice Implications.
42966646.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
42966646.abstract: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy is often used in critical care, but its effects on swallowing function remain unclear. Dysphagia in hospitalized patients is associated with complications and prolonged length of stay, yet screening and referral practices vary widely. Limited evidence exists to guide evaluation of dysphagia risk factors among patients receiving HFNC therapy. To identify patients most at risk for developing dysphagia during HFNC therapy and to examine differences in clinical outcomes based on dysphagia status. This retrospective chart audit reviewed adult inpatients (≥21 years) who received HFNC therapy between 2022 and 2024. Of 1038 eligible patients, 210 were randomly selected for chart audit; 195 were included after exclusions. Data included HFNC settings, dysphagia status, and clinical outcomes. No dose-response relationship was identified between dysphagia and HFNC settings, including flow rate, fraction of inspired oxygen, or duration. Dysphagia during admission was not associated with mortality (all P's > .36) or preexisting dysphagia status (χ2 = 3.7, P = .16). However, patients with dysphagia had longer intensive care unit stays than patients without dysphagia and patients with unknown dysphagia status (P = .04 and P = .09, respectively), and dysphagia status was associated with intubation (χ2 = 13.6, P = .001), with intubation most common among patients with dysphagia. This cohort showed no association of HFNC settings with dysphagia status, and no specific triggers were identified to inform standardized dysphagia screening protocols for patients receiving HFNC therapy. Dysphagia was associated with intubation and prolonged intensive care unit stay.

42966241.title: Province-wide assessment of emergency care capacity and skills in a rural provincial health system: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment in Battambang, Cambodia.
42966241.abstract: Emergency care capacity remains critically limited in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly in rural areas where specialists and infrastructure are scarce. In Cambodia, stroke and ischemic heart disease are leading causes of mortality, and trauma burdens are increasing alongside rapid infrastructure development. Evidence on emergency equipment availability and frontline provider skills at the facility level in rural provinces remains limited. A facility-based cross-sectional assessment was conducted across all seven public referral hospitals in Battambang Province, Cambodia, in January 2023. Emergency equipment availability was evaluated through structured interviews and direct visual confirmation against the World Health Organization (WHO) Guidelines for Essential Trauma Care. Clinical skill examinations were administered to physicians (two scenario-based cases: acute stroke with airway compromise; traumatic injury with tension pneumothorax and intra-abdominal bleeding) and nurses (a Basic Life Support [BLS] scenario assessed in pairs). Hospitals were stratified by Complementary Package of Activities (CPA) level: CPA1 (basic care only), CPA2 (including surgery and intensive care), and CPA3 (highest provincial level). At Complementary Package of Activities (CPA)1 (basic care only) hospitals, intubation equipment and 12-lead electrocardiogram were each available in only 25% of facilities. None had a crash cart, blood transfusion capacity, basic metabolic panel, or coagulation testing. In the stroke scenario, airway patency was confirmed by 28.6% of physicians at CPA1 hospitals, compared with 70.0% at CPA2 hospitals (including surgery and intensive care), 57.1% at the CPA3 hospital (highest provincial level), and 75.0% at the Provincial Health Department. In the trauma scenario, no physician at CPA1 hospitals correctly performed spinal immobilization with the spine kept straight or thoracentesis at the correct anatomical location. Among 38 nurse pairs, 97.4% initiated chest compressions promptly, but only 21.1% demonstrated correct compression technique, and 13.2% provided effective bag-valve-mask ventilation. Deficiencies in equipment and clinical skills were most pronounced at CPA1 hospitals. Emergency care capacity in Battambang Province was substantially limited, with the greatest deficiencies at CPA1 hospitals. Recurrent low-cost training and targeted strengthening of basic emergency care should be prioritized at lower-level facilities.

42966059.title: Vitamin D supplementation is associated with reduced requirement for mechanical ventilation in patients with pneumonia: a large-scale, propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study from MIMIC-IV.
42966059.abstract: Vitamin D plays an important role in host immune defense against infection. However, the potential prognostic benefit of vitamin D supplementation in patients with pneumonia remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between vitamin D supplementation and clinical outcomes among patients with pneumonia. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. Patients with pneumonia were included and categorized into early vitamin D supplementation and non-supplementation groups. Baseline characteristics were balanced using propensity score matching. The primary outcome was the requirement for mechanical ventilation. Secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, new ICU admission, in-hospital and 28-day mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression were performed. A total of 13 092 eligible patients were included: 859 in the vitamin D supplementation group and 12 233 in the non-supplementation group. After PSM (n = 1716), early vitamin D supplementation was significantly associated with a lower requirement for mechanical ventilation (5.83% versus 9.56%, P = 0.004) and lower 28-day mortality (9.32% versus 13.87%, P = 0.003). The association between early vitamin D supplementation and the requirement for mechanical ventilation remained significant among female patients, patients without chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, patients with relatively low serum total calcium levels, and patients with relatively high white blood cell counts. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed delayed onset of mechanical ventilation in the early vitamin D supplementation group. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis showed that early vitamin D supplementation was independently associated with a reduced requirement for mechanical ventilation. No significant association was observed between vitamin D supplementation and length of hospital stay, new ICU admission, or in-hospital mortality. Among patients with pneumonia, early vitamin D supplementation was independently associated with a lower requirement for mechanical ventilation and reduced 28-day mortality. Future studies are warranted to explore these associations.

42965657.title: Airway Pressure Release Ventilation Versus Conventional Ventilation in Adults With or at Risk for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
42965657.abstract: To assess whether airway pressure release ventilation (APRV) reduces mortality compared with conventional invasive ventilation in adults with established acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), acute lung injury, or conditions considered to confer a high risk of ARDS. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception through August 15, 2026. We analyzed parallel-group randomized trials using random-effects models. Mortality at trial-defined follow-up was the primary outcome. We used Cochrane RoB 2 to assess risk of bias and GRADE to assess certainty of evidence. CRD420251170819. Nine trials involving 585 participants were included. No mortality benefit was demonstrated (risk ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.72-1.26). Ventilator-free days showed no clear difference (mean difference [MD] 3.83 days, 95% CI - 1.69 to 9.34; I²=83%). APRV was associated with a higher PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio (MD 56.21 mm Hg, 95% CI 24.63-87.79; I²=84%) and shorter ICU stay (MD - 2.53 days, 95% CI - 4.43 to - 0.64; I²=71%). Ventilation duration showed no clear difference (five trials, 413 participants; MD - 2.44 days, 95% CI - 4.96 to 0.09; I²=78%). Peak airway pressure was lower and mean airway pressure was higher with APRV. This synthesis does not establish that APRV improves survival, ventilator-free days, or ventilation duration. Oxygenation and ICU-stay findings require caution because populations, protocols, outcome timing, and risk of bias varied. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. These data do not establish mortality equivalence or superiority over contemporary lung-protective ventilation. CRD420251170819; registered 17 October 2025.

42965346.title: Application of Electrical Impedance Tomography-Guided Pulmonary Rehabilitation Strategy in Patients with Respiratory Failure.
42965346.abstract: This study investigated pulmonary rehabilitation strategies guided by electrical impedance tomography (EIT) in patients with respiratory failure. A total of 92 patients with respiratory failure admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of a tertiary Grade A hospital in Chongqing from July 2024 to January 2025 were selected and randomly divided into a control group and an experimental group, with 46 cases in each group, using a random number table. The control group received conventional pulmonary physical therapy nursing strategies. The experimental group additionally received EIT-guided positioning, vibratory sputum clearance, and early mobilization. Relative regional tidal-ventilation distribution, PaO₂/FiO₂, respiratory rate, and pulse oxygen saturation were assessed at baseline and on the following three days; ICU stay, and delirium incidence were also compared. Finally, 44 cases in the control group and 44 cases in the experimental group completed the study. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant time effects across the four ventral-to-dorsal layers and significant group and interaction effects for the dorsal layer. Dorsal ventilation share was higher in the experimental group on days 2 and 3, but not significantly different on day 1. No significant group, time, or interaction effects were found for the four lung quadrants. The experimental group had higher PaO₂/FiO₂, shorter ICU stay (6.55 vs. 7.75 days), and lower delirium incidence (25.0% vs. 45.5%). Respiratory rate decreased, and pulse oxygen saturation increased over time in both groups, without significant group or interaction effects. The EIT-guided strategy may improve regional ventilation distribution and oxygenation, shorten ICU stay, and reduce delirium in patients with respiratory failure.

42965215.title: A rare cause of pneumomediastinum and descending necrotizing mediastinitis: Untreated odontogenic abscess.
42965215.abstract: Pneumomediastinum is the presence of free air within the mediastinum and may be primary or secondary. Secondary pneumomediastinum typically follows trauma, invasive procedures, mechanical ventilation, or dental interventions using pressurized air; odontogenic causes without prior intervention are exceptionally rare. We report the case of a 52-year-old male with liver cirrhosis who presented with chest and neck pain 2 days after being diagnosed with a dental abscess and receiving antibiotics, with no dental procedure performed. He had fever, cervical swelling with crepitus, odynophagia, and dysphagia. Computed tomography revealed extensive subcutaneous emphysema tracking from the cervical region into the mediastinum, and inflammatory markers were elevated. He was diagnosed with secondary pneumomediastinum complicated by descending necrotizing mediastinitis and underwent mediastinal exploration and surgical drainage. Cultures grew Parvimonas micra. Postoperatively, he required intensive care and mechanical ventilation for 8 days. With culture-directed antibiotics and multidisciplinary management, he recovered fully and was discharged without sequelae. Anaerobic bacterial gas production may contribute to this rare complication. Clinicians should consider secondary pneumomediastinum in patients with chest and neck pain in the setting of odontogenic infection, even without preceding dental procedures, as early recognition, prompt imaging, surgical drainage, and definitive source control are critical for favorable outcomes.

42965211.title: Emergency department extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: Current concepts, systems-based implementation, and future directions.
42965211.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) has emerged as a time-critical resuscitative strategy for carefully selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest and other reversible causes of circulatory or respiratory failure. As the role of emergency department ECMO (ED ECMO) continues to expand, emergency physicians have become integral members of multidisciplinary extracorporeal resuscitation teams. This review aims to summarize the current evidence on ED ECMO while highlighting practical considerations for program implementation, workflow optimization, and future directions. This invited narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the indications, patient selection, cannulation strategies, pericannulation management, and postcannulation physiological challenges of ED ECMO, with particular emphasis on extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation. In addition to published literature, practical aspects of ED ECMO implementation, including multidisciplinary team organization, operational governance, workflow optimization, quality metrics, and institutional experience, are discussed. Emerging concepts such as artificial intelligence-assisted decision support, digital twin-enabled system modeling, and regional implementation strategies are also reviewed. Current evidence indicates that successful ED ECMO depends not only on technical proficiency but also on timely patient selection, standardized protocols, efficient multidisciplinary coordination, and optimized operational systems. Contemporary implementation frameworks emphasize integrated governance, continuous quality improvement, and structured performance metrics to enhance clinical effectiveness. Emerging digital technologies, including artificial intelligence and systems modeling, may further improve patient selection, operational efficiency, and program scalability. ED ECMO should be regarded as a comprehensive, systems-based resuscitation strategy rather than a standalone rescue procedure. Future progress is likely to depend on the integration of evidence-based patient selection, standardized workflows, multidisciplinary collaboration, intelligent operational systems, and continuous quality improvement. The development of regional ED ECMO networks supported by robust emergency medical service infrastructure may improve timely access to extracorporeal resuscitation and optimize patient outcomes.

42963310.title: Safety and Outcomes of Prone Positioning in the Early Postoperative Period following Cardiac Surgery.
42963310.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42963310.abstract: To evaluate prone positioning (PP) safety and its respiratory and hemodynamic effects in patients with moderate-to-severe respiratory failure after cardiac surgery via median sternotomy. Retrospective, single-center, observational cohort study. Cardiovascular intensive care unit at a tertiary academic hospital. Thirty-eight consecutive adult patients undergoing PP for acute respiratory failure within 30 days of median sternotomy cardiac surgery between 2004 and 2024. Protocolized PP sessions under deep sedation, neuromuscular blockade, and advanced hemodynamic monitoring. Median PP duration was 24 hours (IQR 16-26); 47.4% underwent their first session within 5 postoperative days. The primary endpoint was PP-related complications (mediastinitis/sternal dehiscence). Secondary endpoints included gas exchange, vasoactive requirements, and in-hospital mortality. Mediastinitis occurred in one patient (2.6%), comparable to non-proned populations. PP significantly improved oxygenation, with the PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio increasing from 82.8 ± 26.1 mmHg at baseline to 177.5 ± 68.9 mmHg at 4 hours into the maneuver and to 175.0 ± 70.8 mmHg at PP completion (both p < 0.001). No significant hemodynamic deterioration or increased vasoactive support occurred. Overall mortality was 44.7%. Advanced age (≥75 years) and baseline hypercapnia (PaCO₂ ≥50 mmHg) were independent predictors of mortality. PP was safe after recent median sternotomy and elicited a marked improvement in oxygenation without increasing sternal complications. These findings support considering PP for selected patients with moderate-to-severe postoperative adult respiratory distress syndrome following cardiac surgery.

42962711.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions.
authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)(⁎)
American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)(⁎)
Asia-Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL)
Latin American Association for the Study of the Liver (ALEH)
Society on Liver Disease in Africa (SOLDA)
42962711.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.

42961991.title: Associated factors for stress ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding in patients with sepsis or septic shock: A systematic review.
42961991.abstract: Sepsis continues to be a major contributor to death among critically ill individuals and places a heavy strain on healthcare resources. In addition to causing systemic inflammation and affecting hemodynamics, sepsis has a significant effect on the gastrointestinal system, leading to complications like stress ulcers and notable gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB), which worsen patient outcomes. While stress ulcer prophylaxis (SUP) has traditionally been included in sepsis treatment protocols, the concept of applying it universally is being increasingly scrutinized due to the absence of definitive mortality advantages and the risk of adverse effects, such as hospital-acquired pneumonia. Nevertheless, there is a notable gap in synthesized research that specifically addresses the independent risk factors for stress ulcers in sepsis patients. We carried out a systematic review in accordance with PRISMA standards, exploring eight databases (CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, Sinomed, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library) from their inception until September 1, 2026. We included observational analytical studies (either cohort or case-control) that examined factors linked to stress ulcers or significant gastrointestinal bleeding in adult patients with sepsis. Two researchers independently handled the selection of studies, extraction of data, and evaluation of quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Due to the limited number of studies for each association between associated factors and outcomes, a narrative synthesis was utilized. A total of six studies encompassing 131,568 individuals suffering from sepsis or septic shock were analyzed. The incidence rates of stress ulcers or gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) varied between 2.0% and 32.3%. The identified associated factors were divided into three categories: patient-related (older age, history of GIB, cirrhosis, HIV, cancer/immunosuppression), disease-related (coagulopathy, kidney impairment, high BUN levels, severity of illness scores, source of infection), and treatment-related (mechanical ventilation, use of anticoagulants, corticosteroid therapy, duration of ICU stay). Specifically for stress ulcer, factors such as respiratory failure, high BUN levels, shock, and increased HMGB1/TLR2/TLR4 levels were found to be independently linked to a higher odds. In summary, the likelihood of developing stress ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding in patients with sepsis is shaped by a variety of factors related to the patient, their illness, and the treatments they receive. Key indicators that consistently emerge include issues with blood coagulation, the presence of shock, the need for mechanical ventilation, liver and kidney dysfunction, the severity of the disease, and any previous occurrences of gastrointestinal bleeding. These results advocate for tailored strategies for stress ulcer prophylaxis based on individual risk rather than a one-size-fits-all approach, offering crucial insights for precise clinical decision-making. Additional high-quality research is essential to confirm and enhance the understanding of these associated factors. PROSPERO (CRD420251242849).

42960283.title: Pre-emptive Circulatory Support Before Emergency Tracheal Intubation: A Systematic Review.
42960283.abstract: Emergency tracheal intubation is associated with peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse, and pre-emptive circulatory support is frequently used to mitigate this risk despite uncertain evidence. We conducted a systematic review of randomised and comparative non-randomised studies evaluating pre-emptive circulatory support initiated before or at induction in adults undergoing emergency or urgent tracheal intubation. Eligible interventions included prophylactic vasopressors, intravenous fluid boluses, hypertonic saline, blood products, deliberate circulation-first strategies, and multi-component care bundles. The primary outcome was peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse within 30 minutes of induction, defined according to individual study criteria. MEDLINE via PubMed, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 30 August 2026, with additional searches of ClinicalTrials.gov and citation lists. Risk of bias (RoB) was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool for randomised trials and the Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool for non-randomised studies. Fourteen independent cohorts comprising two randomised trials and 12 comparative non-randomised studies, with more than 7,400 participants overall, were included. Two randomised trials evaluated a pre-emptive 500 mL crystalloid bolus and found no reduction in peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse. Observational evidence for prophylactic vasopressors was inconsistent, with substantial changes between crude and adjusted estimates and substantial concerns regarding confounding. Studies evaluating circulation-first strategies or pre-intubation blood products generally reported associations favouring earlier circulatory resuscitation, but these findings were strongly influenced by confounding and treatment selection. Multi-component care bundles were also associated with fewer peri-intubation complications, but the independent contribution of their circulatory components could not be determined. Overall, the available evidence indicates that pre-emptive crystalloid administration does not reduce peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse, while evidence for prophylactic vasopressors, circulation-first strategies, and multi-component interventions remains insufficient to support routine use. Further randomised trials are needed, particularly among physiologically high-risk adults.

42960060.title: Continuous versus intermittent endotracheal tube cuff pressure control for the prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia: A focused systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
42960060.abstract: Continuous endotracheal tube cuff pressure control is intended to maintain cuff pressure within the recommended range, reduce microaspiration, and prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). However, randomized trials have produced apparently inconsistent findings. The clinical question is therefore not only whether continuous control lowers VAP overall, but also why physiologic benefits have not translated consistently into patient-important infection outcomes. We performed a focused systematic review and evidence synthesis of randomized studies comparing continuous versus intermittent endotracheal tube cuff pressure control in critically ill adults. Trial characteristics, comparator intensity, endpoint definitions, risk-of-bias considerations, and directly extractable outcome data were reviewed from the original reports. Because the included studies used non-identical primary outcomes, the primary synthesis was qualitative. Exploratory random-effects meta-analyses were restricted to outcomes with directly extractable binary event counts. Five randomized studies involving 1,355 analyzed patients were included.
