Early single-center studies suggested that continuous cuff pressure control improved cuff pressure stability, reduced microaspiration-related markers, and in some settings lowered infection-related endpoints. In contrast, the two largest later multicenter trials did not demonstrate a consistent reduction in VAP or ventilator-associated respiratory infection (VARI). An exploratory pooled analysis of four studies with directly extractable VAP-like binary outcomes showed no statistically significant reduction with continuous control (risk ratio 0.89, 95% confidence interval 0.63-1.24; I2 = 55.8%). A sensitivity analysis using the Vietnam trial's primary VARI endpoint rather than VAP yielded a similar result (risk ratio 0.92, 95% confidence interval 0.67-1.28; I2 = 57.7%). Exploratory pooled intensive care unit (ICU) mortality across all five studies was also not significantly different (risk ratio 0.91, 95% confidence interval 0.77-1.07; I2 = 0%). Continuous cuff pressure control improves cuff pressure stability and may reduce microaspiration-related markers, but current randomized evidence does not demonstrate a consistent overall reduction in clinically important infection outcomes across diverse ICU settings. The apparent inconsistency in the literature is best explained by differences in endpoint choice, comparator intensity, timing of intervention, baseline preventive practices, and patient population. Continuous control should therefore be regarded as a context-dependent adjunct rather than a universally proven stand-alone VAP-prevention strategy.

42959802.title: Impact of Proportional Assist Ventilation Versus Pressure Support Ventilation on Adult Liberation From Mechanical Ventilation: A Revised Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of RCTs.
42959802.abstract: Pressure assist ventilation (PAV) is considered superior to pressure support ventilation (PSV). We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate comparative effectiveness in terms of weaning outcomes. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane for eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published before October 2025 that directly compared clinical outcomes of PAV and PSV in mechanically ventilated adults. R program was used to calculate risk ratio (RR) and mean difference (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). After screening the titles, abstracts, and full texts, we included eight RCTs consisting of 1057 patients in our systematic review and meta-analysis. PAV was associated with a higher rate of weaning success as compared to PSV (RR: 1.09; 95% CI, 1.01-1.18; p = 0.03; I 2 = 23%). PAV was associated with a lesser duration of ventilation (MD: -1.06; 95% CI, -1.82 to -0.29, p = 0.006; I 2 = 0%) and intensive care unit (ICU) stay (MD: -1.49; 95% CI: -2.43 to -0.54, p = 0.002; I 2 = 25%) as compared to PSV. However, no statistically significant benefit was observed for PAV over PSV with regard to rate of reintubation (RR: 0.82; 95%, CI: 0.58-1.16, p = 0.21, I 2 = 0%) and mortality (RR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.63-1.25 p = 0.4I 2 = 30%). PAV is superior to PSV for weaning, showing increased success and shorter duration of ventilation and ICU stays, though reintubation and mortality rates were similar.

42959567.title: Pulmonary Endarterectomy After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty: A Single-Center USA Experience.
42959567.abstract: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) is the treatment of choice for operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), while balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is reserved for inoperable disease. However, operability is subjective and there are patients who may undergo BPA prior to PEA. It is not clear if prior BPA affects PEA outcomes. We present a series of patients from a single, high-volume, referral center who underwent PEA after prior BPA. CTEPH patients who underwent BPA prior to undergoing PEA at the University of California, San Diego between January 2013 and July 2025 were included. Post-PEA outcomes were compared to all PEA patients who did not have prior BPA from the year 2022. Twenty-one patients were identified. Average number of BPA sessions prior to PEA was 3.4 ± 2.1. The most common reason for initial BPA was distal disease deemed inoperable (43%). Average total circulatory arrest time was 61.5 ± 21.8 min, compared to 47.9 ± 19.3 min (p = 0.003) in the control PEA cases (n = 188). Post-operatively, the PEA after BPA cohort had longer ventilator days (p < 0.001), ICU days (p = 0.022) and post-operative length of stay (LOS) (p < 0.001); there were also higher rates of post-operative bleeding (p < 0.001) requiring transfusions (p = 0.033) and return to the operating room (p = 0.008). There was one death related to prior BPA complications despite adequate endarterectomy with improved hemodynamics. There was similar hemodynamic improvement post-operatively in both cohorts. Although prior BPA made PEA more challenging and increased select post-operative complications, it is not a contraindication for successful PEA.

42958471.title: What triggers intraoperative blood pressure/heart rate surges and postoperative hypertonia during unilateral biportal endoscopy?
42958471.abstract: Unilateral biportal endoscopy (UBE) is an increasingly utilized minimally invasive technique for lumbar degenerative disease. Dural tear is a recognized complication (incidence 1.9-5.8%), typically associated with cerebrospinal fluid leakage and intracranial hypotension. However, the unique irrigation dynamics of UBE - an open two-portal system permitting high-flow continuous irrigation - may produce a distinctly different pathophysiology when an occult dural defect is present. The anesthesiology literature contains few descriptions of the acute intraoperative hemodynamic manifestations of this phenomenon. A 49-year-old woman (ASA physical status I) underwent UBE for L4-L5 and L5-S1 disc herniation under total intravenous anesthesia. The procedure was complicated by intraoperative wrong-level surgery (L4-L5 misidentified as L5-S1), necessitating complete portal withdrawal, re-localization, and re-establishment of the surgical field, which prolonged the operation to 4 h 23 min with a cumulative irrigation volume of 51,000 mL. Approximately 2.5 h after incision, progressive, treatment-refractory tachycardia (70 → 117 beats/min) and hypertension (up to 183/102 mmHg) developed; esmolol and urapidil produced minimal antihypertensive effect despite concurrent augmentation of anesthetic depth. On postoperative review, the scrub nurse recalled observing a suspected dural tear approximately 10 min before the hemodynamic escalation, which had not been communicated intraoperatively. Following extubation, the patient exhibited impaired consciousness, persistent tachypnea (40-50 breaths/min), and generalized hypertonia with decerebrate posturing. Multidisciplinary evaluation excluded epileptic seizure, metabolic encephalopathy, malignant hyperthermia, and intraoperative awareness. Suspected acute intracranial hypertension secondary to massive irrigation fluid entry into the subarachnoid space via the unrecognized dural defect was considered the most likely diagnosis. The patient was reintubated and managed in the intensive care unit with osmotic diuresis (furosemide, mannitol), corticosteroids, and sedation. Consciousness recovered the following morning, limb hypertonia resolved by postoperative day 11, and the patient was discharged on day 14 without neurological deficit. This case suggests that an occult dural tear during UBE with large-volume irrigation may produce a paradoxical hemodynamic profile of progressive, therapy-resistant hypertension and tachycardia - contrasting with the bradycardia and hypotension classically associated with intracranial hypotension from cerebrospinal fluid leaks. The triad of (i) progressive, treatment-refractory hypertension and tachycardia, (ii) prolonged UBE duration (> 2 h), and (iii) large-volume irrigation (> 20 L) may represent a high-risk pattern warranting immediate intraoperative communication between anesthesia and surgical teams and consideration of intracranial pressure-directed interventions. This observation is hypothesis-generating and requires validation in larger studies.

42958092.title: Serum calpain-5 as a biomarker for disease severity and clinical outcomes in COVID-19 patients.
42958092.abstract: Calpain is one of the intracellular calcium-activated cysteine proteases and exerts pivotal functions in many diseases. The aim was to explore the relationship of serum calpain-5 concentration and Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) via a cohort study. The whole 338 COVID-19 patients were selected. Clinical features and demographic information were collected. The concentration of serum calpain-5 was measured via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Serum calpain-5 concentration was upregulated with increased severity scores, including SMART-COP, 4 C-Mortality, CURXO, A-DROP, DTPNCP, COVID-GRAM, PSI, and CURB-65 in COVID-19 patients. Spearman correlation analyses suggested there were tight correlations between serum calpain-5 level and numbers of clinical features. Additionally, multivariate linear and logistic regression models showed that serum calpain-5 level was positively associated with severity scores. Moreover, the frequencies of mechanical ventilation, vasoactive agent usage, ICU admission, and death during hospitalization within 30 days were grown with elevated serum calpain-5 concentration on admission. Logistic regression analyses demonstrated that serum higher calpain-5 on admission elevated the risk of adverse prognosis during hospitalization within 30 days. The concentration of serum calpain-5 is positively correlated with disease severity and adverse prognosis, implying calpain-5 may be involved in the progression of COVID-19. Serum calpain-5 level may served as a useful biomarker for guiding clinicians in managing and monitoring disease outcome in COVID-19 patients. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

42957982.title: Bacterial epidemiology and attributable mortality of Ventilator-associated pneumonia before and after COVID-19 pandemic (2018-2021).
42957982.abstract: BackgroundVentilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in mechanically ventilated patients. The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly modified VAP epidemiology and microbial ecology.MethodsWe conducted a prospective multicenter cohort study within the REA-REZO network (≈20% of French ICU beds), 1 January 2018-31 December 2021. All adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation were included. VAP was defined according to ECDC criteria. Primary endpoints were VAP incidence density (per 1000 ventilation-days) and 30-day attributable mortality. Secondary endpoints included resistance patterns and pre-pandemic versus pandemic trends.ResultsAmong 98,047 patients, 12,251 patients developed VAP, with an incidence of 18.9/1000 ventilation-days. Peak incidence occurred at day 10 (29/1000 ventilation-days). Thirty-day attributable mortality was 4.9% [95% CI 3.7;6.2], rising to 7.2% [6.0;8.5] at 60 days. Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 78.0% of isolates, predominantly Enterobacterales (46%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (20%). Third-generation cephalosporin resistance reached 27% in Enterobacterales and 25% in P. aeruginosa. The COVID-19 patients had a higher VAP rate (19.5% vs 9.7%, p<0.001) and mortality (36.9% vs 31.0%, p<0.001).ConclusionsVAP remains highly prevalent in French ICUs with substantial attributable mortality. The COVID-19 pandemic nearly doubled VAP incidence and worsened resistance profiles. Intensified prevention bundles during the first 10 days of ventilation and reinforced antimicrobial stewardship are critical.

42869822.title: [Research progress on mechanism of traditional Chinese medicine in treating acute lung injury based on endoplasmic reticulum stress].
42869822.journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
42869822.abstract: Acute lung injury(ALI) is a severe pulmonary condition with a high mortality rate, and is also a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among intensive care unit patients. Endoplasmic reticulum stress(ERS) is a key central mechanism in ALI. It primarily regulates endoplasmic reticulum function by activating the unfolded protein response and modulating three core pathways-inositol-requiring enzyme 1(IRE1), activating transcription factor 6(ATF6), and protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase(PERK)-which in turn regulate processes such as oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and autophagy. It is involved in processes including apoptosis, inflammatory storm, and calcium homeostasis, thereby influencing the progression of ALI. TCM offers therapeutic advantages through its multi-targeted and multi-pathway approach, improving the course of ALI by modulating ERS. This paper reviewed the experimental evidence and mechanisms for single herbs and their chemical constituents or extracts(casticin, ursolic acid, toosendanin, resveratrol, ginsenosides, and total flavonoids from Patrinia villosa), TCM compound formulas(Zhenwu Decoction, Buzhong Yiqi Decoction, and Dushen Decoction), and Chinese patent medicines(Lianhua Qingwen Capsules and Jingfang Granules) to modulate ERS for the treatment of ALI. It elucidated the scientific rationale behind the use of TCM to modulate ERS for ALI treatment, providing a mechanistic basis and research directions for the prevention and treatment of ALI by integrated traditional Chinese and western medicine.

42857167.title: Relative suppression of pyroptosis- and necroptosis-related transcriptional programs and enrichment of ferroptosis-related signatures are associated with fatal sepsis: multi-cohort bulk and single-cell transcriptomic evidence.
42857167.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
42857167.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome caused by a dysregulated host response to infection and remains a major cause of mortality in critically ill patients. Multiple forms of programmed cell death (PCD) may contribute to immune dysregulation and organ injury, but their transcriptional patterns across disease severity and outcome remain incompletely defined. We performed an integrative transcriptomic analysis of five public sepsis cohorts, including single-cell RNA sequencing datasets GSE167363 and GSE151263 and three bulk transcriptomic cohorts. Primary outcome analyses focused on cohort-defined fatal sepsis (28-day non-survivors in GSE65682 and the deposited sepsis-death group in GSE63042), whereas pneumonia/ARDS comparisons were treated as secondary exploratory analyses. PCD-related transcriptional programs were evaluated across clinical groups and immune-cell populations. Six candidate genes were further assessed by RT-qPCR in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 and THP-1 cells as targeted in vitro transcriptional validation. In GSE65682, 28-day non-survivors showed lower pyroptosis, necroptosis and apoptosis program scores but higher ferroptosis scores than survivors, and higher pyroptosis scores were associated with better 28-day survival. GSE154918 instead showed broader increases in PCD-related program scores from healthy controls to infection/sepsis groups, reflecting a disease-versus-control contrast rather than an outcome contrast. In the LPS model, CASP1, RIPK3 and NLRP3 were upregulated, whereas SIRT1, BCL2 and HIF1A were downregulated. These cell experiments assessed acute inflammatory transcriptional responsiveness and were not intended to reproduce the mortality-associated direction observed in patient cohorts. Multi-cohort analyses identified outcome-associated PCD transcriptional patterns in sepsis, including relative suppression of pyroptosis- and necroptosis-related programs and enrichment of ferroptosis-related signatures in non-survivors. The LPS experiments provide complementary mRNA-level evidence that selected PCD genes are transcriptionally responsive to inflammatory stimulation, but they do not constitute directional or functional validation of the fatal-sepsis signature. Functional and prospective clinical validation remains required.

42850295.title: Expanded proinflammatory CD4 T cells expressing toll like receptor 4 in trauma associated acute lung injury.
42850295.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is characterised by hypoxia and inflammation that derives from diverse aetiologies. Delineating the molecular pathogeneses may identify treatable subgroups and inform clinical trials. Using a multi-omics approach, we analysed trauma-associated ALI (n = 9), COVID-19 ALI (n = 11), ICU controls (n = 13) using scRNA-seq, serum cytokine profiling, and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) microbiome analysis. We identified a population of activated CD4+ T cells expressing Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and downstream NOD-, LRR- and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome complex, predominantly in trauma-associated ALI (23% of CD45+ Cells) compared to COVID-19 ALI (14%) and ICU controls (15%). Serum IL-1RA and IL-6 were upregulated in trauma ALI, along with TLR4-binding ligand hyaluronan. TLR4 expression on CD4+ T cells was confirmed by spectral cytometry. Lung microbiome analysis revealed distinct diversity in trauma-associated ALI compared to COVID-19 ALI. These findings highlight TLR4-mediated inflammation in trauma-associated ALI and suggest potential precision medicine approaches for ALI management.

42844585.title: Pre-ECMO characteristics, organ dysfunction and exploratory mortality prediction in COVID-19 versus non-COVID-19 ARDS treated with veno-venous ECMO: a retrospective cohort study.
42844585.abstract: The transferability of pre-ECMO characteristics and established mortality prediction tools across COVID-19 (C-19) and non-COVID-19 (nC-19) acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains uncertain. We compared clinical characteristics, organ dysfunction, respiratory support and outcome in a large cohort of patients treated with veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (vvECMO), and explored mortality prediction in C-19 ARDS. This retrospective single-center cohort study included n = 600 vvECMO patients (C-19: n = 245, nC-19: n = 355) hospitalized at the Charité ARDS ECMO Center from 01/2007 to 12/2018 (nC-19) and 03/2020-01/2022 (C-19). Pre-ECMO clinical and laboratory variables were compared between cohorts and by ICU survival. RESP score performance was assessed, and an exploratory C-19 ECMO mortality prediction (CEMP) score was derived from pre-ECMO variables using an explainable machine-learning workflow with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). C-19 patients were older (median 57.0 vs. 51.0 years, p < 0.0001), more often male (74.7% vs. 66.8%, p = 0.0337), and had a higher BMI (29.3 vs. 26.0 kg/m², p < 0.0001). nC-19 patients had a higher CCI (3 vs. 2, p = 0.0137) and SOFA score (12 vs. 11, p = 0.0004). Septic shock before vvECMO initiation was more prevalent in nC-19 patients (65.4% vs. 13.9%, p < 0.0001), and nC-19 patients had higher median baseline bilirubin, creatinine, and lactate levels (all p < 0.0001). nC-19 patients had higher median PEEP, pPeak, and plateau pressure than C-19 patients, whereas their PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio was lower (p < 0.0001). Duration of vvECMO support was longer in C-19 patients (26.0 vs. 12.6 days, p < 0.0001); ICU mortality did not differ significantly (55.1% vs. 47.9%, p = 0.0966). RESP showed limited discrimination in C-19 patients, and the CEMP derivation analysis yielded an apparent AUC of 0.757 (95% CI 0.69-0.82). This large single-center comparative vvECMO cohort highlights differences between C-19 and nC-19 ARDS in organ dysfunction burden, respiratory characteristics, and treatment duration. ICU mortality did not differ significantly between groups. RESP showed limited discrimination in C-19; CEMP remains exploratory and requires calibration and independent external validation before clinical application.

42830899.title: An augmented rehabilitation package incorporating immersive virtual reality during early recovery after ARDS: A randomized controlled trial.
42830899.abstract: Survivors of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) frequently experience cognitive impairment, psychological symptoms, and reduced health-related quality of life after intensive care. Immersive virtual reality (VR) may provide an engaging, multimodal adjunct to conventional rehabilitation, but evidence in the ARDS recovery population remains limited. In this single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 88 ARDS patients in the rehabilitation phase were randomized 1:1 to a 4-week augmented rehabilitation package incorporating immersive VR in addition to usual care (n = 44) or usual care alone (n = 44). One control participant was lost to follow-up, and 87 participants were included in the available-case analysis. The primary outcome was change in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score from baseline to 4 weeks. Secondary outcomes included the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) scores. The main between-group analysis used analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), with follow-up score as the dependent variable and baseline score as the covariate. Baseline imbalances were observed for age, MoCA, SF-36, and HADS-A scores. After adjustment for corresponding baseline scores, the VR group showed greater improvement in MoCA score than the control group (adjusted between-group effect: 1.42, 95% CI 0.86-1.98; p < 0.001). The VR group also showed higher SF-36 scores (adjusted effect: 13.20, 95% CI 11.85-14.54; p < 0.001) and lower HADS-A scores (adjusted effect: -2.55, 95% CI -3.23 to -1.88; p < 0.001). In the VR group, 29 of 44 participants (65.9%) reported being very satisfied or satisfied with the intervention. An augmented rehabilitation package incorporating immersive VR was associated with short-term improvements in cognition, health-related quality of life, and anxiety symptoms during early ARDS recovery. Because the package also entailed additional structured rehabilitation exposure, staff attention, interaction, repeated activity, feedback, and treatment time, and because the control condition was not time- or attention-matched, the observed differences cannot be attributed specifically to VR. These single-center, short-term, hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger studies with time- and attention-matched controls. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600122078; retrospectively registered on 8 April 2026, after completion of participant recruitment.

42948347.title: Intelligent nano delivery systems: Classification, stimuli-responsive mechanisms, and therapeutic applications in critical illnesses.
42948347.abstract: Critical illnesses such as sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) evolve rapidly and are dominated by systemic inflammatory dysregulation, oxidative stress, and abrupt microenvironmental remodeling, which collectively narrow the therapeutic window and amplify treatment-related toxicity. Conventional pharmacotherapy is often limited by non-selective biodistribution, insufficient lesion exposure, and dose-limiting adverse effects. Intelligent nano-delivery systems (INDS) address these barriers by coupling pathological cues (e.g., pH gradients, redox/ROS imbalance, and disease-associated enzymes) to defined carrier-state transitions, thereby enabling lesion-confined activation, controlled bioavailability, and, in selected designs, real-time readouts. In this review, we summarize the design logic of stimulus-responsive and targeting modules, and critically discuss how they translate endogenous signals into payload release or functional actuation in representative critical-illness settings. We further highlight emerging directions, including self-adaptive multi-input gating and biomimetic interfaces, and discuss key translational constraints (manufacturability, safety, and reproducibility) that must be addressed to advance INDS toward critical-care practice.

42947113.title: Association of esketamine with acute lung injury and macrophage polarization-related markers after ATAAD surgery.
42947113.abstract: To investigate the association between perioperative esketamine use, postoperative acute lung injury (ALI), and macrophage polarization-related markers in patients undergoing acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) surgery. A total of 124 patients with ATAAD treated at our hospital between January 2022 and December 2024 were retrospectively included. Postoperative ALI was assessed within the first 24 h after ICU admission following ATAAD surgery, and patients were classified into the ALI group (n = 52) and non-ALI group (n = 72) accordingly. Univariate analysis and binary logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with postoperative ALI after ATAAD surgery. Patients were further analyzed according to perioperative esketamine use to evaluate differences in macrophage polarization-related markers and clinical outcomes. Binary logistic regression analysis showed that hypertension was independently associated with an increased risk of postoperative ALI (OR = 5.586, 95% CI: 1.832-17.034, P = 0.002), whereas perioperative esketamine use was independently associated with a reduced risk of postoperative ALI (OR = 0.155, 95% CI: 0.061-0.394, P < 0.001). After propensity score matching, 45 matched pairs were retained. In the matched cohort, postoperative ALI occurred in 11 patients in the esketamine group and 23 patients in the non-esketamine group (24.4% vs. 51.1%, P = 0.011). Perioperative esketamine use remained associated with a lower risk of postoperative ALI after matching (OR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.13-0.74, P = 0.008). Patients in the esketamine group also showed a lower postoperative M1-related index and M1/M2 ratio, a higher M2-related index, and a shorter hospital stay. Perioperative esketamine use was associated with a lower risk of postoperative ALI after ATAAD surgery and was accompanied by favorable changes in macrophage polarization-related markers. Given the retrospective single-center design and limited sample size, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger prospective studies. Not applicable. This was a retrospective observational study and did not involve prospective assignment of participants to an intervention.

42945998.title: Molecular Subtypes in Acute Respiratory Illness and Sepsis.
42945998.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
42945998.abstract: Sepsis and acute respiratory illness are clinical syndromes that encompass profound biological heterogeneity. The resulting heterogeneity of treatment effect is now widely understood as the explanation to why immunomodulatory trials in critical care have not me their study endpoints, thereby misclassifying effective therapies as futile while concealing harm in biologically ineligible subgroups. High-dimensional molecular profiling offers a route to resolve this heterogeneity into tractable subgroups or subtypes. Here we review molecular subtypes across adult and paediatric sepsis, pneumonia, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), spanning transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic platforms. Blood transcriptomic frameworks derived independently in multiple countries, and subsequently harmonized by international consensus efforts, converge on recurring immune archetypes: a myeloid inflammatory state dominated by neutrophil activation; a mixed myeloid and lymphoid dysregulated state carrying the highest mortality; and a relatively immunocompetent state with preserved lymphocyte function and the most favourable clinical trajectory. Plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling recapitulate this architecture at orthogonal molecular layers, arguing that these archetypes are platform-independent rather than artefacts of any single technology. Cross-syndrome convergence is asymmetric, which plausibly reflects the methodological differences between top-down latent class analysis in ARDS and bottom-up unsupervised clustering in sepsis. Secondary analyses of randomized controlled trials consistently show subtype-dependent responses to treatment strategies, with a coherent directionality with potential benefit in hyperinflammatory states, and harm in immunosuppressed or adaptive immune-prevalent states. Subtype membership is not static; trajectory, not baseline assignment, most strongly encodes prognosis. Realising precision critical care now requires prospective, subtype-stratified trials of which none has yet been completed.

42929978.title: Role of Interleukin 17 in Severe Acute Pancreatitis: Human Retrospective Pilot Study.
42929978.abstract: Background/Objectives: Severe acute pancreatitis accounts for 20% of acute pancreatitis episodes and carries a substantial mortality risk. The systematic severity of the disease is driven by a massive cytokine release, with Interleukin-17 (IL-17) acting as a crucial modulator of the pro-inflammatory cascade. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of serum IL-17 at admission and correlate it with multi-organ dysfunctions and clinical-biological outcomes in patients with severe acute pancreatitis. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a cohort of 35 patients with severe acute pancreatitis. Demographic, etiological, and clinical-biological baseline characteristics were extracted. Serum IL-17 levels were determined at admission using the ELISA method, and data were statistically analyzed. Results: Significantly higher levels of IL-17 were observed in patients who developed multi-organ failure. Prognostic thresholds were identified via ROC analysis to predict organ dysfunctions: ≥19.77 pg/mL for neurological dysfunction (AUC = 0.814, p = 0.003) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (AUC = 0.756, p = 0.024); ≥18.45 pg/mL for respiratory (p = 0.004) and cardiovascular dysfunctions (AUC = 0.820, p = 0.002); and ≥19.81 pg/mL for renal dysfunction (AUC = 0.735, p = 0.020). Furthermore, univariate binary logistic regression identified elevated serum IL-17 as a significant prognostic factor for mortality among patients admitted to the intensive care unit (OR = 1.062, p = 0.048). Conclusions: Serum IL-17 at admission functions as a significant prognostic biomarker that reflects the severe systemic pro-inflammatory status in severe acute pancreatitis and mirrors the risk of subsequent organ dysfunctions and mortality. Incorporating IL-17 into initial risk stratification protocols may assist clinicians in timely therapeutic escalation.

42927821.title: Sepsis-associated efferocytosis deficiency: Molecular mechanisms and novel therapeutic targets.
42927821.abstract: Despite advances in critical care, sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality driven by a profoundly dysregulated host immune response. Increasingly, defective efferocytosis-the fundamental physiological process for clearing dead cells-has been identified as a critical catalyst in sepsis pathophysiology. Under normal conditions, efferocytosis resolves inflammation and maintains tissue homeostasis. However, during sepsis, the efferocytotic capacity of phagocytes is severely paralyzed. This clearance failure results in a massive accumulation of apoptotic and necrotic cellular debris within the tissue microenvironment, triggering an unabated release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). Consequently, this substrate overload sustains a self-amplifying inflammatory storm that accelerates tissue injury and precipitates multiple organ failure. In this review, we dissect the diverse modalities of programmed cell death in sepsis and map the subsequent breakdown of the core, multi-step efferocytotic machinery. We systematically explore the molecular basis of efferocytosis failure across distinct organ-specific complications, including acute lung injury, sepsis-associated encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, and septic cardiomyopathy. Finally, we evaluate emerging targeted therapies aimed at restoring efferocytotic efficiency, highlighting a crucial conceptual shift from primarily suppressing inflammation to actively promoting its resolution and repairing host immunity.

42924420.title: Cyclosporine treatment of ARDS due to severe COVID-19: The I-SPY COVID Adaptive Platform Trial.
42924420.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42924420.abstract: Aberrant host response to SARS-CoV-2 infection causes severe lung injury and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) with resultant multiorgan failure and death. Cyclosporine, a calcineurin inhibitor with potent immunosuppressant and direct antiviral properties, was hypothesized to reduce cytokine-driven injury in hospitalized patients with severe COVID-19 ARDS. To evaluate whether cyclosporine improves time to recovery and reduces mortality in critically ill patients with COVID-19, using the I-SPY COVID adaptive platform trial design. In this phase 2, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial, non-intubated and intubated adults with confirmed COVID-19 requiring ≥6L/min oxygen received oral cyclosporine 5mg/kg/day in two divided doses for 5 days, added to standard backbone therapy (dexamethasone and remdesivir), or standard therapy alone. Co-primary endpoints were time to recovery and time to death, assessed using Bayesian proportional-hazard models with pre-specified graduation thresholds. Of 238 randomized patients (110 cyclosporine, 128 control), 28-day recovery rates were 65.9% vs. 71.1% and 28-day mortality rates were 10.7% vs. 11.3%, respectively. The posterior probability that cyclosporine improved recovery was 6% (graduation threshold >97.5%) and that it reduced mortality was 59.6% (graduation threshold >90%), meeting neither pre-specified efficacy criterion. Serious adverse events were more frequent with cyclosporine (17.3% vs. 7.0%, p = 0.016). No significant differences in inflammatory plasma biomarkers were observed between groups. Cyclosporine did not meet pre-specified efficacy thresholds for recovery or mortality in severe COVID-19 ARDS and was associated with a higher rate of serious adverse events. These results do not support its addition to standard care in this population.

42921520.title: Acute lung injury: an integrated view of molecular drivers, immune dysregulation, and emerging therapeutic strategies.
42921520.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI, a term widely used in preclinical animal studies, while the clinical definition of ALI was eliminated in the Berlin criteria) and its severe human clinical counterpart, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), constitute life-threatening clinical syndromes characterized by diffuse alveolar damage, pulmonary edema, and severe hypoxemia. These conditions are associated with dismal mortality rates and significantly impair patient survival and recovery. Over the past decades, advancements in critical care medicine and molecular biology have deepened our understanding of the pathological mechanisms underlying ALI and ARDS. Aberrantly activated signaling pathways and molecular and cellular events have emerged as key elements to decipher core pathogenic processes, identify early biomarkers, and develop novel therapeutic strategies. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ALI and ARDS, encompassing their definition, historical context, epidemiology, and common etiological factors, with a focus on recent advances in pathological mechanisms, signaling pathways, epigenetic regulation, and therapeutic interventions. Treatment approaches include lung-protective ventilation, fluid management, targeted pharmacotherapy, mesenchymal stromal cell therapy, and nanomaterial-based delivery systems. These developments offer valuable insights into the complex mechanisms of preclinical ALI and human ARDS and contribute to the advancement of clinical diagnosis and treatment.

42911388.title: Patterns, and outcomes of airbag -related penetrating injuries: a retrospective analysis from a level 1 trauma center.
42911388.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
42911388.abstract: The deployment of defective airbag inflators can generate high-velocity metallic fragments that cause face, neck or chest penetrating injuries with potentially lethal consequences. This study aimed to describe the injury patterns, management, and outcomes of suspected airbag-related penetrating injuries (ARPI) among patients in a Middle Eastern country. A retrospective observational study of patients presenting with penetrating injuries suspected of being related to defective airbag deployment. Data were obtained from the Qatar National Trauma Registry (QNTR), electronic medical records, emergency medical services (EMS), emergency department (ED), and Mortuary. Data were collected and analyzed descriptively. A total of 16 patients had suspected ARPIs between April 2019 and February 2026. The mean age was 33.1 ± 8.3 years, and 93.8% were male. Metallic foreign bodies (FBs) from airbag inflator fragmentation were documented in 11/16 (68.8%) patients by imaging, and surgical removal while in 4/16 patients there were only entry-exit wounds after deployment of airbags following car crash. In one case, airbag deployed while mechanic was repairing a car steering wheel. Penetrating neck (43.8%), thoracic (31.3%), and maxillofacial injuries (31.3%), predominantly mandibular fractures, were most common. Surgical intervention was required in 11 (68.8%) patients and 7/16 required intensive care unit admissions. Five patients died (31.3%), including one at the scene (transported directly by the EMS, no CPR, and moved to the hospital mortuary), two died at the ED after unsuccessful CPR and two died during the hospital course (one presented with cardiac arrest and died on the sixth day and the other one required prolonged ECMO for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and died after 4 months). Airbag inflator rupture can produce serious injury patterns resembling patterns of ballistic trauma, characterized by penetrating neck wounds, maxillofacial fractures and thoracic injuries. These injuries are potentially associated with high mortality, surgical intervention, and critical care utilization. The full extent of these injuries is undetermined as some victims may have simply died at the scene without the benefit of trauma center evaluation or post-mortem examination.

42910759.title: Development and Internal Validation of a 24-Hour Landmark Model for 28-Day Mortality in Sepsis-Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
42910759.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) carries substantial short-term mortality. Differences in predictor timing, validation design, and comparators complicate evaluation of published prediction models. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 955 adults with sepsis-associated ARDS who reached a 24-h landmark after intensive care unit (ICU) admission. All-cause mortality was assessed by day 28 from ICU admission. Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-only logistic regression, conventional multivariable logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were compared. The multivariable models used 26 candidate predictors (30 encoded parameters). Five repetitions of five-fold outer cross-validation with three-fold inner tuning provided held-out predictions. Evaluation included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, classification metrics, and decision-curve net benefit. Held-out tree-based Shapley additive explanations described XGBoost predictions. Among 955 patients, 474 (49.6%) died. AUCs based on averaged held-out probabilities were 0.732 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.698-0.761) for LASSO, 0.729 (0.696-0.761) for conventional regression, 0.709 (0.674-0.740) for XGBoost, 0.707 (0.673-0.739) for random forest, and 0.581 (0.545-0.617) for SOFA alone. The LASSO-minus-conventional-regression AUC difference was 0.003 (95% CI, -0.003 to 0.010). Intervals resampled fixed predictions without refitting. LASSO had a Brier score of 0.209, calibration intercept of -0.001, and slope of 1.065. The final equation retained age, Charlson Comorbidity Index, arterial oxygen partial pressure/fraction of inspired oxygen ratio, SOFA, lactate, bilirubin, other infection site, and vasopressor use. LASSO provided moderate discrimination without a clear advantage over conventional regression. The separately tuned final equation requires source-data verification, external validation, and prospective clinical-utility assessment before clinical use.

42909258.title: Characterization of an Unusual Severe Yellow Fever Outbreak in the Colombian Andean Region.
42909258.abstract: Yellow fever (YF) reemerged in Colombia's Andean region during 2024-2025, outside the country's historically recognized endemic areas. We characterized critically ill adults admitted during this outbreak and described clinical features, organ dysfunction, supportive care, and in-hospital outcomes. We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of consecutive adults with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR)-confirmed YF admitted to the national referral intensive care unit in Ibagué, Tolima, Colombia, from March through September 2025. Clinical, laboratory, complication, intervention, and outcome data were prospectively captured using a standardized case report form. Sixty-one patients were analyzed; 22 died (36.1%). Non-survivors had lower platelet counts and fibrinogen and higher INR, aminotransferases, lactate dehydrogenase, and creatinine at ICU admission. Shock, acute kidney injury, acute respiratory distress syndrome, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and severe bleeding were more frequent among non-survivors. Prior YF vaccination was self-reported by 10 patients (16.4%). Severe YF in this Andean outbreak was characterized by hepatic-coagulation abnormalities and multisystem organ dysfunction. The occurrence of critical illness outside historically recognized endemic areas supports surveillance and vaccination strategies that can adapt to changing epidemiological risk.

42898721.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome in a 28-Year-Old Male Subsequent to Inappropriate Naloxone Administration.
42898721.abstract: Tramadol, a centrally-acting analgesic, is widely used for the management of moderate to severe pain. It is preferred in clinical settings due to its superior effectiveness and safety profile compared to other opioids. However, recent research has indicated a potential risk of tramadol-induced seizures, especially when consumed in high dosages or in combination with other substances. We present a case of a 28-year-old male who was brought to the Emergency Department approximately 30 minutes after administering 0.4 mg of naloxone intravenously by Emergency Medical Services (EMS) personnel. The administration was necessitated by a decline in the patient's level of consciousness, the onset of lip cyanosis, and suspected tramadol poisoning. The patient was intubated on-site before being transported to the Emergency Department. Upon arrival, despite receiving 40% FiO2, his O2 saturation was at 88%. Bibasilar crackles were detected during chest auscultation. A CT scan of his chest revealed the presence of bilateral alveolar infiltrates, primarily in the lower lobes. As a result, the patient was diagnosed with acute respiratory distress syndrome and was transferred to the intensive care unit for further care.

42892954.title: Feasibility and Safety of Intraoperative Abdominal Warming During Spinal Surgery in the Prone Position: A Pilot Study.
42892954.abstract: Inadvertent perioperative hypothermia caused by general anesthesia leads to several complications, including shivering, coagulopathy, surgical site infections, and delayed wound healing. Prone positioning for spine surgery severely restricts the available body surface area for warming, complicating intraoperative temperature management. This study investigated a novel approach utilizing the anatomical space beneath the chest and abdomen created by a standard four-point bolster support to maintain intraoperative core body temperature using standard pediatric underbody forced-air warming blankets. This prospective, single-arm pilot study enrolled six adult patients undergoing elective spinal surgery in the prone position under general anesthesia at Akita Red Cross Hospital, Akita, Japan. No active preoperative warming was performed. A pediatric underbody forced-air warming blanket (SWU-2009; ICU Medical Inc., San Clemente, CA, USA) was pre-positioned in the suspended thoracoabdominal space of the four-point support and operated at 40 °C. Core body temperature (monitored via a temperature-sensing urinary catheter) and skin condition were recorded from induction to the end of surgery. Six patients (mean age: 66.8 ± 16.7 years, mean surgical duration: 230.2 ± 55.5 minutes) were analyzed. The median core temperature was 36.5 °C (interquartile range (IQR): 36.4 °C-36.5 °C) at induction, 36.6 °C (IQR: 36.4 °C-36.9 °C) at incision, and 37.0 °C (IQR: 36.7 °C-37.1 °C) at the end of surgery. Although transient mild hypothermia (< 36.0 °C) occurred in two patients, both recovered to normothermia within 90 minutes. No patient developed redness, blisters, or thermal burns. Abdominal warming utilizing the suspended space of a four-point bolster support was feasible to implement without occurrences of skin-related complications, demonstrating potential to contribute to intraoperative temperature stabilization. While adequately powered comparative trials are required to definitively evaluate its clinical efficacy, this approach provides preliminary insights into practical thermal management in standard operating rooms.

42875238.title: [Role of secrum albumin-to-creatinine ratio in assessing the prognosis of sepsis].
42875238.journal: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
42875238.abstract: To investigate the role of serum albumin-to-creatinine ratio (sACR) in prognostic assessment of patients with sepsis. A retrospective cohort study was conducted. Patients with newly diagnosed sepsis admitted to the emergency intensive care unit (ICU) and comprehensive ICU of the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University from October 2023 to October 2024 were enrolled. Baseline data and laboratory parameters within 24 hours of admission, including white blood cell count (WBC), C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), serum albumin, and creatinine, were collected, and sACR was calculated. The Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II(APACHE II) and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) were recorded at admission. The 28-day survival status and survival time were documented. Patients were divided into sepsis group and septic shock group according to sepsis severity, and further divided into survivor group and non-survivor group based on 28-day outcomes. The above parameters were compared between groups. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was used to identify independent prognostic factors for 28-day mortality. Receiver operator characteristic curves (ROC curves) were plotted to evaluate the predictive value of each indicator, and the areas under the curves (AUCs) were compared using DeLong's test. A total of 177 patients with newly diagnosed sepsis were included, comprising 66 in the sepsis group and 111 in the septic shock group; 94 survived and 83 died within 28 days. Significant differences were observed between the sepsis and septic shock groups in age, WBC, CRP, PCT, APACHE II score, SOFA score, and sACR (all P<0.05), with sACR being higher in the sepsis group [2.98 (1.82, 4.10) vs. 2.26 (1.19, 3.08)]. Significant differences were also found between survivors and non-survivors in WBC, CRP, PCT, APACHE II score, SOFA score, and sACR (all P<0.05), with sACR being higher in survivors [3.17 (1.87, 4.20) vs. 1.80 (0.95, 2.25)]. Cox regression analysis showed that CRP (HR=1.004, 95%CI was 1.001-1.007, P=0.043), APACHE II score (HR=1.078, 95%CI was 1.049-1.108, P<0.001), and SOFA score (HR=1.105, 95%CI was 1.027-1.189, P=0.008) were independent risk factors for 28-day all-cause mortality, while sACR was an independent protective factor (HR=0.795, 95%CI was 0.646-0.978, P=0.030). ROC curve analysis revealed that CRP, APACHE II score, SOFA score, and sACR had certain predictive value for 28-day prognosis; the AUC of sACR was 0.765, with an optimal cut-off value of 2.446, yielding a sensitivity of 66.0% and specificity of 77.1%. DeLong's test indicated that the predictive performance of sACR was similar to that of SOFA score, superior to CRP, but inferior to APACHE II score. As a novel composite biomarker, sACR has potential adjunctive value in assessing disease severity and predicting prognosis in patients with sepsis.

42851303.title: Case Report: rectal perforation and Fournier's gangrene after irinotecan in a bevacizumab-exposed, previously irradiated patient.
42851303.abstract: Bevacizumab-associated intestinal perforation and Fournier's gangrene have been reported separately; however, the potential contribution of residual anti-VEGF exposure prior to subsequent chemotherapy in previously irradiated pelvic tissue remains underrecognized. Radiotherapy causes fibrosis and microvascular injury, bevacizumab impairs healing, and irinotecan-induced diarrhea may exacerbate perforation risk. Deferring DRE, imaging, and surgical consultation in patients with unexplained perineal or buttock pain increases the risk. A 61-year-old man with rectal adenocarcinoma received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by total mesorectal excision and ileostomy in March 2024. After adjuvant chemotherapy, surveillance in March 2025 revealed recurrence with pelvic invasion and liver/lung metastases. He received eight cycles of XELOX plus bevacizumab, then bevacizumab maintenance, stopped on 4 March 2026 for rectal hemorrhage. This 22-day interval is shorter than the label-mandated 28-day hold and NCCN-recommended ≥6-week washout for surgery-standards primarily addressing wound healing rather than chemotherapy sequencing. Five days after irinotecan initiation, grade 3 diarrhea developed. He was admitted on 13 April 2026 with diarrhea, left buttock pain; he received empirical ceftazidime plus moxifloxacin. On 14 April, DRE, imaging, and surgical consultation were deferred due to pain. By 18 April, septic shock developed with perineal necrosis and crepitus. CT confirmed Fournier's gangrene. Emergency debridement with abscess curettage and seton drainage was performed. Fecal diversion was declined. Antibiotics were escalated to meropenem then vancomycin after cultures grew VSEfm. He left the ICU but needed twice-daily dressing changes. Two weeks postoperatively, care shifted to palliation, and he died of multiorgan failure. This case raises the hypothesis that, in previously irradiated tissue, residual bevacizumab exposure at the time of subsequent irinotecan initiation-exacerbated by irinotecan-induced diarrhea and pre-existing rectal mucosal damage-may have contributed to rectal perforation and subsequent Fournier's gangrene. Notably, while bevacizumab and irinotecan are routinely combined, whether extrapolating surgical washout standards (≥6 weeks) to anti-VEGF sequencing before high-mucosal-toxicity chemotherapy warrants prospective investigation. Unexplained perineal or buttock pain in such patients should trigger urgent clinical evaluation, including DRE when feasible, imaging, and early surgical consultation, to prevent diagnostic delay.

42957093.title: Predictors of severe measles outcomes in hospitalized patients in Jerusalem, 2025.
42957093.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
42957093.abstract: Measles is a vaccine-preventable disease. Defining risk factors for poor outcomes in hospitalized patients can improve future measles outbreak preparedness. Data were collected on all confirmed measles cases that were evaluated at one of the emergency departments (ED) in the three main hospitals in Jerusalem from the first reported case of the current outbreak on April 10th to December 31st, 2025. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed using robust Poisson multivariable models to calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR) for hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and death. Among 786 individuals who visited the ED with confirmed measles, the rates of hospital admission (≥1 day), ICU, ECMO and death were 83.4%, 6.4%, 0.8%, and 1.4%, respectively. Complete data were available for 567 patients, of whom 303 (53.4%) were males. Median age was 2.1 years (IQR 1.2-3.8), and 474 (83.6%) were younger than 5 years. Most patients were unvaccinated (91.0%). Secondary infections were frequent, including lobar pneumonia (28.7%) and community-acquired bacteremia (3.5%). Respiratory support and severe dehydration were associated with hospital admission (IRR 1.4, 95% CI 1.3-1.5; p<0.001 and 9.5, 4.8-18.4; p<0.001, respectively) and ICU admission (IRR 1.3, 1.2-1.4; p<0.001 and 5.2, 2.1-12.4; p<0.001, respectively). Community-acquired bacteremia was associated with death or ECMO (IRR 44.5, 12.5-158.6; p<0.001). Despite high access to medical care in this urban setting, measles caused substantial morbidity and mortality. Respiratory compromise, severe dehydration, and bacteremia identified patients at increased risk of severe outcomes.

42921198.title: Association of SOFA-2 with in-Hospital Mortality in Refractory Septic Shock: A Multicohort Retrospective Study with a 12-Hour Landmark.
42921198.abstract: SOFA-2 is an updated organ dysfunction score designed to reflect contemporary intensive care practice. Its clinical relevance in refractory septic shock (RSS) remains unclear. We primarily evaluated the association between SOFA-2 and subsequent in-hospital mortality among patients who were alive and hospitalized at a 12-hour landmark after RSS identification. Comparison with conventional SOFA was secondary and exploratory. This retrospective cohort study used MIMIC-IV as the primary cohort, with external consistency analyses in eICU-CRD and a local institutional cohort. RSS was operationalized using available electronic health record variables based on the SCCM/ESICM consensus framework, although some consensus elements were incompletely captured. Patients who died or were discharged before the 12-hour landmark were excluded from the primary analysis. SOFA-2 and conventional SOFA were assessed during the first 12 hours after RSS identification, with follow-up beginning at the landmark. Cause-specific Cox models were used for the primary analysis. Proportional-hazards diagnostics, time-varying coefficient models, time-dependent AUC, restricted cubic spline, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were also performed. The primary cohort included 1276 patients, of whom 719 died during hospitalization. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-point increase in SOFA-2 was associated with higher subsequent in-hospital mortality (HR 1.12, 95% CI 1.10-1.14), and the HR per 1-SD increase was 1.54 (95% CI 1.43-1.67). The association attenuated over follow-up but remained positive at 7, 14, and 28 days. Conventional SOFA showed similar per-point associations. Exploratory time-dependent AUC analyses showed only small numerical differences between the two scores. The association was generally consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses and directionally consistent in the external cohorts. Among patients meeting database-operationalized RSS criteria who were alive and hospitalized at the 12-hour landmark, higher SOFA-2 scores were associated with higher subsequent in-hospital mortality.

42911180.title: Clinical impact of a rapid urine diagnostic algorithm combined with antimicrobial stewardship in patients with suspected urinary sepsis.
42911180.journal: Revista espanola de quimioterapia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Quimioterapia
42911180.abstract: Early appropriate antimicrobial therapy is a key determinant of outcome in sepsis, yet conventional urine culture takes 24-48 hours. We evaluated the clinical impact of a rapid microbiological algorithm applied directly to urine, combined with antimicrobial stewardship, in patients with suspected urinary sepsis. Prospective quasi-experimental two-phase cohort study at a tertiary hospital. In adults with simultaneous urine and blood cultures, an initial observational phase formed the comparison cohort (conventional culture), and a second phase the intervention cohort, in which urine underwent Gram stain, laser-nephelometry growth detection (Alfred 60/AST), MALDI-TOF-MS identification, rapid susceptibility testing, and immunochromatographic ESBL and carbapenemase detection, with immediate reporting and recommendations by an infectious diseases specialist. Multivariable models (logistic and negative binomial) were adjusted for age, sex, Charlson index, department and qSOFA. We included 594 patients (297 per cohort). The algorithm achieved organism identification in 92.6% of cases, with a median turnaround time of 7.25 versus 75.0 hours (p<0.001), and 98.6% agreement with culture. Overall mortality was 6.1% versus 11.1% (p=0.039). After adjustment, the intervention was associated with significant reductions in hospital stay (IRR 0.82; p=0.012), days of therapy (IRR 0.79; p<0.001), intravenous antibiotics (IRR 0.83; p=0.001), need for ICU admission (OR 0.42; p=0.003) and overall mortality (OR 0.44; p=0.011). A rapid urine diagnostic algorithm, integrated with an expert stewardship intervention, was associated with lower antibiotic consumption and improved outcomes in suspected urinary sepsis. Combining rapid diagnostics with expert advice appears key to translating microbiological information into effective therapeutic decisions.

42895663.title: Association Between Albumin-Bilirubin Index and Clinical Outcomes in Septic Acute Kidney Injury Patients.
42895663.abstract: BackgroundThe albumin-bilirubin index (ALBI) has been reported as a prognostic marker in various clinical conditions; however, its value in patients with septic acute kidney injury (AKI) has not been clearly evaluated. This study aimed to investigate the association between ALBI and clinical outcomes in this population.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. ALBI was analyzed as both a continuous variable in the primary analysis and a categorical variable according to tertiles in sensitivity analysis. The primary outcomes were 28-day, 60-day, 90-day, and 1-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) transfer, septic shock, and disease severity. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between ALBI and mortality, and restricted cubic spline analyses were performed to assess potential nonlinearity. Subgroup analyses were further conducted to examine the consistency across different sub-group populations.ResultsOverall, 6700 patients with septic AKI were included. In adjusted Cox models, each 1-standard deviation increase in ALBI was associated with higher risks of 28-day mortality (HR 1.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.10-1.22), 60-day mortality (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.10-1.19), 90-day mortality (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.08-1.18), and 1-year mortality (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.14). The association between ALBI and mortality was generally consistent across most prespecified subgroups. Higher ALBI was also linked with septic shock (odds ratio [OR] 1.15, 95%CI 1.08-1.21, P < .001), ICU transfer (OR 1.09, 95%CI 1.02-1.16), and greater disease severity. RCS curves showed a nonlinear increase in mortality risk with ascending ALBI. Sensitivity analyses based on ALBI tertiles yielded broadly consistent findings.ConclusionHigher ALBI was independently associated with increased short- and long-term mortality and adverse clinical outcomes in septic AKI patients.

42888582.title: Association of baseline non-severe anemia with clinical outcomes following the first recorded diagnosis of systemic sclerosis: A matched cohort study.
42888582.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the highest mortality among systemic autoimmune diseases, yet the prognostic significance of anemia around the time of the first recorded SSc diagnosis is unclear. We examined whether baseline anemia is associated with early mortality and complications. This retrospective matched cohort study identified female adults with a first recorded SSc diagnosis between January 2010 and December 2024 from the TriNetX Research Network. Patients were required to have at least 5 years of pre-index observation without a documented SSc diagnosis. The network comprised 140 healthcare organizations, with approximately 70% of patients in the United States across all 9 census regions and 30% at international sites. Anemia was defined as hemoglobin (Hb) ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL and non-anemia as ≥12.0 g/dL, measured within ±30 days of diagnosis. For the Hb-stratified analysis, the anemia cohort was categorized as Hb ≥10.0 to <12.0 g/dL or ≥8.0 to <10.0 g/dL. One-to-one propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, and Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality during days 31 to 365 among patients surviving the 30-day landmark period; secondary outcomes were sepsis, acute kidney injury, intensive care unit admission, pulmonary fibrosis, and elevated C-reactive protein (≥10 mg/L). After matching, 5410 patients remained in each cohort. Baseline anemia was significantly associated with higher 1-year mortality (HR, 2.54; 95% CI, 1.99-3.22; P < .001) and with increased risks of sepsis (HR, 3.20; 95% CI, 2.38-4.30), acute kidney injury (HR, 2.24; 95% CI, 1.80-2.78), intensive care unit admission (HR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.47-2.51), and elevated C-reactive protein (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.37-1.74; all P < .001); no significant association was observed for pulmonary fibrosis (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.96-1.17; P = .229). Associations persisted in sensitivity analyses and over 3-year follow-up. Mortality risk showed a graded pattern across Hb strata (Hb ≥10.0-<12.0 g/dL: HR, 1.66; Hb ≥8.0-<10.0 g/dL: HR, 3.33). Baseline anemia was associated with increased mortality and acute systemic complications following the first recorded SSc diagnosis; these observational findings warrant prospective validation.

42881879.title: Legionella Septic Cardiomyopathy Requiring Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Followed by Presumed Complement-Mediated Thrombotic Microangiopathy: A Case Report.
42881879.abstract: Background:Legionella pneumophila rarely causes profound myocardial dysfunction and malignant ventricular arrhythmias. Persistent thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury during recovery may additionally raise concern for thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), although distinguishing complement-mediated disease from secondary causes in critically ill patients is challenging. Case Presentation: A 64-year-old man presented after five days of fever with recurrent ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation, cardiac arrest, and refractory shock. Echocardiography demonstrated diffuse biventricular hypokinesia with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 18%, while urgent coronary angiography showed no acute coronary occlusion. Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation, and organ support were initiated. Levofloxacin was administered from admission, before sputum sequencing identified L. pneumophila. VA-ECMO was removed after four days. Persistent anaemia and thrombocytopenia with progressive acute kidney injury despite clinical improvement prompted evaluation for thrombotic microangiopathy. ADAMTS13 activity was 92%, soluble C5b-9 was elevated to 648 ng/mL, and schistocytes were not identified. Presumed complement-mediated TMA was treated with four weekly doses of eculizumab, followed by haematological and renal improvement. Sepsis, extracorporeal support, transfusions, and gastrointestinal bleeding confounded diagnosis and treatment attribution. At three months, LVEF was 59%, platelet count 237 × 109/L, and creatinine 97 µmol/L. Conclusions: VA-ECMO may bridge selected patients with severe septic myocardial dysfunction to recovery. Persistent cytopenias and kidney injury warrant structured TMA evaluation. In critically ill patients, complement-mediated TMA requires integrated assessment rather than reliance on a single complement biomarker or clinical response to complement inhibition.

42964594.title: Procalcitonin and Presepsin in Gram-Negative Sepsis: Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Antimicrobial Stewardship Perspectives.
42964594.abstract: Because delayed pathogen identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing might delay effective treatment, sepsis caused by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria continues to be a significant problem in intensive care units. The clinical usefulness of procalcitonin (PCT) and presepsin as early indicators for Gram-negative sepsis diagnosis, disease severity prediction, treatment response monitoring, and antimicrobial stewardship is assessed in this review. While presepsin provides quick early identification and significant prognostic value, particularly in culture-negative sepsis, PCT is notably useful in distinguishing Gram-negative infections from Gram-positive or fungal etiologies. Before traditional culture findings are available, serial monitoring of both biomarkers may assist in detecting treatment failure, delayed biomarker clearance, and potential multidrug-resistant infections. Confounding variables like burns, trauma, renal failure, surgery, and sterile inflammation must be taken into account during interpretation, though. Rapid molecular diagnostics combined with PCT and presepsin may enhance early treatment choices, lower needless antibiotic exposure, and promote precision-based care for critically ill septic patients.

42964465.title: Systematic review of the current landscape and imaging-based definition of septic cardiomyopathy.
42964465.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
42964465.abstract: Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) has no current unified definition, although it can be associated with significant mortality. It encompasses a wide spectrum of cardiac dysfunction ranging from mild to severe systolic and/or diastolic dysfunction of the left and/or right ventricle. The objective of this review is to evaluate the imaging modalities and parameters used to define SCM and the clinical outcomes. We conducted a systematic review of the literature, including studies up to August 2025, examining the impact of cardiac dysfunction, specifically related to the systolic and/or diastolic dysfunction of the left or right ventricle. We focussed on mortality and comparable phrases as the primary outcome. We considered all cardiac imaging methods. All relevant studies were identified in a search strategy including MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus. About 2669 articles were identified, of which 142 full-text publications were evaluated. Final analysis included 87 publications. Forty five articles provided a definition of SCM. Seventy studies used TTE. Eighteen studies associated LV dysfunction to mortality. Thirteen studies found an association between diastolic dysfunction or RV dysfunction and mortality. About 64% of the studies assessed cardiac function within 24-h of admission. Twenty eight studies re-assessed reversibility of cardiac dysfunction. Cardiac dysfunction is commonly reported in the critically ill septic population. There was considerable heterogeneity with regards to the diagnostic criteria of SCM, parameters used to determine cardiac dysfunction, outcomes evaluated, timing of study or assessing reversibility. Given the high prevalence of cardiac dysfunction in sepsis, a unified assessment and definition of SCM is needed.

42857397.title: Early-Phase Computed Tomography Bowel Diameter and Neurological Outcomes Post-Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.
42857397.abstract: We aimed to conduct an exploratory investigation on the association between bowel diameter on early-phase abdominal computed tomography (CT) and neurological outcomes in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). This observational study included patients who underwent ECPR for OHCA and abdominal CT before intensive care unit admission between January 2015 and December 2021 at a tertiary emergency medical center. Maximum bowel diameter was measured with a picture archiving and communication system by an investigator blinded to outcomes. The primary endpoint was unfavorable neurological outcomes at 1 month, defined as Cerebral Performance Category 3-5. The discriminatory ability of bowel diameter was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Data from 181 patients were analyzed (median age, 57 years; 84.5% male). Bowel diameter demonstrated a weak ability to predict unfavorable neurological outcomes, with an AUC of 0.58 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47-0.70). However, higher discriminatory performance was observed in subgroups of patients aged ≥ 65 years (AUC, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.69-0.96) and those with initial nonshockable rhythms (AUC, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.47-0.91). The results of this exploratory investigation suggest that bowel diameter may represent a potential adjunctive marker associated with functional outcomes post-ECPR for OHCA.

42831735.title: Derivation and Validation of Operational Definitions From Claims Data for Identifying Cardiogenic Shock.
42831735.abstract: To derive and validate a claims-based operational definition for cardiogenic shock (CS) using administrative data against clinically adjudicated reference standards. Diagnostic accuracy study. Two independent clinical cohorts, a single-center cardiac ICU (CICU) registry and a multicenter CS registry (REtrospective and prospective observational Study to investigate Clinical oUtcomes and Efficacy of left ventricular assist device for Korean patients with cardiogenic shock [RESCUE]), and a nationwide administrative database from the Korean National Health Insurance Service. A total of 10,156 patients from the CICU registry and 1,247 patients from the RESCUE registry. For population-level application, 207,419 patients were identified from the national claims database. None. A claims-based algorithm defined CS using the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision code R57.0 or cardiac disease codes combined with treatment-based criteria reflecting hemodynamic support, including mechanical circulatory support or vasoactive therapy. In the CICU cohort, the algorithm demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.89 and specificity of 0.90, with an overall accuracy of 0.90. In the RESCUE cohort, sensitivity was 0.95. When applied to the nationwide database, 207,419 patients with CS were identified. The cumulative mortality rates were 37.9% at 12 months, 49.9% at 5 years, and 61.7% at 10 years. A claims-based definition combining diagnostic codes with treatment-based criteria demonstrated high diagnostic performance for identifying CS. This approach enables reliable large-scale epidemiologic studies and long-term outcome assessments using administrative data and may facilitate system-level evaluation of critical care delivery in patients with CS.

42829321.title: Resuscitative Transesophageal Echocardiography Simulation-Based Education for Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Cannulation Guidance.
42829321.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42829321.abstract: A simulation-based learning (SBL) resuscitative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) course was developed to teach a focused extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) cannulation guidance protocol for critical care practitioners. The four-hour SBL course was conducted for critical care practitioners with no prior formal TEE training. University hospital, simulation center. Critical care practitioners, voluntary. The course implemented ordered sessions: didactics, TEE simulation, and hands-on ECPR cannulation simulation scenarios. Pre and post course knowledge assessment and surveys were completed. Median knowledge assessment score improved from 53% to 93% (P < .001). Survey responses yielded significant median score improvement in comfort levels of SBL TEE for ECPR guidance using a 5-point Likert scale (p-value <0.001). An SBL resuscitative TEE course focused on ECPR cannulation guidance can provide a framework for teaching these skills to critical care practitioners.

42828628.title: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome: an emerging fatal zoonotic infection.
42828628.abstract: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome is a potentially fatal respiratory zoonotic infection caused by New World hantaviruses, and it is acquired mostly via inhaling aerosolized excreta from infected rodents. Over the past 30 years, HCPS has expanded beyond its initial foci, and recent events suggest a potential for spread beyond traditionally endemic regions. The disease rapidly progresses from a vague prodrome to acute cardiopulmonary failure with a high fatality rate despite optimum supportive treatment. Pathophysiology involves endothelial failure, increased vascular permeability, acute thrombocytopenia and excessive immunological responses resulting in capillary leak syndrome and cardiogenic shock. It is still hard to clinically suspect early since the prodromal symptoms are vague and mirror common viral infections and respiratory disorders. Diagnostic confirmation needs serological testing or genetic approaches, which are typically unavailable in resource-limited endemic situations, leading to considerable diagnostic delays. Management is generally supportive, with early ICU admission, judicious hydration management, mechanical breathing and cardiopulmonary support including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in refractory patients. The recent multi-country Andes virus epidemic on a cruise ship in May 2026 highlights the potential for fast worldwide transmission of HCPS outside of usual endemic settings. This review summarizes the current information on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic techniques, and treatment options for HCPS. We also highlight the pressing need for improved global surveillance, rapid point-of-care diagnostics, global awareness among health care workers, and ongoing development of preventive vaccines and effective antiviral therapies to address this significant public health threat.

42948399.title: Postoperative cardiac arrest after cardiac surgery: Can we improve our rescue rate?
42948399.abstract: Despite improvements in rescue strategies, postoperative cardiac arrest in adults undergoing cardiac surgery has not been examined in the contemporary era. This study assesses the incidence, outcomes, and predictors of survival in patients who had an in-hospital cardiac arrest after cardiac surgery. Adult patients with cardiac arrest after open surgery from January 2012 to May 2019 at a single institution were studied. Patients were excluded if they underwent heart transplantation or left ventricular assist device implantation, experienced preoperative or intraoperative cardiac arrest, received preoperative or intraoperative temporary mechanical circulatory support, or were deemed as do not resuscitate or care was withdrawn before the arrest. Of 9946 patients, 162 (1.6%) experienced a postoperative arrest with failure to rescue in 59 patients (36.4%). The etiology of cardiac arrest was cardiovascular in 101 patients (62.3%), respiratory in 27 patients (16.7%), metabolic in 15 patients (9.3%), other in 12 patients (7.4%), and unknown in 7 patients (4.3%). Thirteen patients (8.0%) were placed on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation postarrest with only 4 (30.8%) surviving to discharge. Patients were more likely to die in-hospital if they had postoperative, prearrest organ dysfunction (adjusted odds ratio, 7.08, 95% CI, 2.92-17.16). Although the incidence of cardiac arrest was low, more than one-third of patients failed to be rescued. Prearrest major organ dysfunction portended a significantly worse prognosis. Early recognition of a nonthriving patient and rapid escalation of specialized care may be critical in successful rescue from cardiac arrest and aborting catastrophic outcomes.

42934677.title: Mortality risk model for acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: development, external validation, and exploratory application in a VA-ECMO cohort.
42934677.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
42934677.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) carries a high risk of in-hospital death. Randomized evidence does not support routine VA-ECMO use in unselected AMI-CS populations. Objective and interpretable risk stratification is clinically important when advanced mechanical circulatory support is considered. This was a retrospective, multi-database model development and validation study with exploratory application in a local VA-ECMO-treated AMI-CS cohort. An in-hospital mortality prediction model was developed in AMI-CS patients who did not receive ECMO treatment using the MIMIC-IV database. Candidate measurements were summarized using the worst values accumulated during the first 24 h after ICU admission. Variable shrinkage was performed using LASSO logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation, and the model was established using multivariable logistic regression. Internal validation included the original fixed-structure bootstrap and an additional full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity analysis. The latter repeated preprocessing, LASSO selection, post-LASSO handling, and model refitting within each resample. External validation was performed in the eICU cohort. The model was then applied exploratorily to the local VA-ECMO-treated AMI-CS cohort to describe model transportability and the relationship between observed and predicted outcomes. The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 355 patients, of whom 127 died in hospital (35.77%). LASSO selected 8 clinical predictors. The apparent AUC was 0.829 (95% CI 0.785-0.874). After the final model was refitted in 200 fixed-structure bootstrap resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.814. In 500 full-pipeline bootstrap resamples, all repetitions were valid, the mean optimism was 0.0436, and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.786 (empirical 2.5th to 97.5th percentile range: 0.745-0.832). The AUCs from the MIMIC-IV complete-case and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses were 0.820 and 0.840, respectively. In the eICU complete-case cohort, the AUC was 0.806 (95% CI 0.691-0.921), O/E was 0.733, the calibration intercept was - 0.986, and the calibration slope was 0.671. After multiple imputation in all 224 eligible eICU patients, the AUC was 0.771, O/E was 0.754, the calibration intercept was - 0.756, and the calibration slope was 0.528. The local cohort included 40 VA-ECMO-treated patients.
