Reading isolate-level surveillance data through the BPPL 2024 and AWaRe frameworks adds a priority- and stewardship-oriented layer to the conventional antibiogram. These proportions describe cultured isolates, not the frequency of resistant infection in patients. The low Enterobacterales carbapenem resistance relative to national benchmarks warrants multi-center, consumption-linked confirmation.

42911179.title: [Integration of beta-lactam therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) into routine clinical practice within an Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP)].
42911179.journal: Revista espanola de quimioterapia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Quimioterapia
42911179.abstract: La monitorización terapéutica de los niveles plasmáticos de antibióticos beta-lactámicos para el ajuste de dosis y la consecución de objetivos farmacocinéticos/farmacodinámicos es una estrategia destinada a optimizar la dosificación en pacientes críticos y en pacientes con características especiales. El objetivo de este estudio es describir la actividad llevada a cabo durante el año 2023 en nuestro hospital, en colaboración con todos los departamentos clínicos implicados: el Servicio de Análisis Clínicos (Farmacocinética y Microbiología), el Servicio de Farmacia y la Unidad Territorial de Infección Nosocomial, en el marco de un Programa de Optimización de Antimicrobianos. Estudio retrospectivo observacional descriptivo sobre la aplicación de la monitorización terapéutica de betalactámicos. Los clínicos solicitan una interconsulta al Servicio de Farmacia para iniciar la monitorización terapéutica de los niveles plasmáticos de betalactámicos. Una vez que el paciente alcanza el estado estacionario, se obtiene una muestra de sangre. Si se realizan ajustes de dosis, se vuelve a medir el nivel plasmático tras 24-48 horas. Todas las determinaciones de niveles plasmáticos realizadas durante 2023 se registraron en una hoja de cálculo Excel, junto con las modificaciones del tratamiento derivadas de los niveles plasmáticos medidos. Se definió un nivel óptimo como una concentración cuatro veces superior a la concentración mínima inhibitoria (CMI) del microorganismo causante sin alcanzar niveles tóxicos. Se realizaron un total de 717 determinaciones en 487 pacientes; el 43,3% ingresaron en la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos, mientras que el resto estaban hospitalizados en otros servicios. Se realizaron ajustes de dosis en el 34,6% de los pacientes críticos, en comparación con el 32,6% en los pacientes no críticos. En el 79.3% de los pacientes con aislamientos microbiológicos, se alcanzó el objetivo terapéutico de mantener concentraciones libres del fármaco por encima de la CMI del patógeno. La monitorización terapéutica de los niveles plasmáticos de betalactámicos podría ser una herramienta útil para la optimización de la dosis y la consecución de los niveles plasmáticos óptimos. Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) of plasma levels of beta-lactam antibiotics for dose adjustment and achievement of pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic targets is a strategy aimed at optimizing dosing in critically ill patients and in patients with special characteristics. The aim of this study is to describe the activity carried out during the year 2023 at our hospital, in collaboration with all the clinical departments involved: the Clinical Analysis Department (Pharmacokinetics and Microbiology), the Pharmacy Department, and the Territorial Nosocomial Infection Unit, within the framework of an Antimicrobial Stewardship Program. This is a retrospective observational descriptive study about the TDM of beta-lactam antibiotics. Clinicians request a consultation with the Pharmacy Department to initiate therapeutic drug monitoring of beta-lactam plasma levels. Once the patient reaches steady-state conditions, a blood sample is collected. If dose adjustments are made, a new plasma level is measured after 24-48 hours. All plasma level determinations performed during 2023 were recorded in an Excel spreadsheet, along with treatment modifications derived from the measured plasma levels. An optimal level was defined as a concentration four times higher than the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of the causative microorganism without reaching toxic levels. A total of 717 determinations were performed in 487 patients; 43.3% were admitted to the Intensive Care Unit, while the remainder were hospitalized in other departments. Dose adjustments were made in 34.6% of critically ill patients, compared to 32.6% among non-critical patients. In 79.3% of patients with microbiological isolates, the therapeutic target of maintaining free drug concentrations above the MIC of the pathogen was achieved. TDM of beta-lactam plasma levels is a useful tool for dose optimization and achievement of therapeutic target.

42909907.title: Molecular epidemiology and resistance mechanisms of carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli in a referral hospital in Lima, Peru.
42909907.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (CR-GNB) represent a significant public health threat, as they are associated with high mortality in healthcare settings. Carbapenemase production is the predominant resistance mechanism, and horizontal gene transfer drives the rapid dissemination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). This study aimed to characterize the phenotypic and genotypic AMR profiles of CR-GNB isolated from patients at Arzobispo Loayza National Hospital (Lima, Peru) between October 2021 and January 2022. We conducted a cross-sectional study and collected clinical and epidemiological data from patients with bacterial infections. MALDI-TOF identified pathogens, and antimicrobial susceptibility was interpreted according to CLSI guidelines. A subset of isolates underwent whole-genome sequencing (Illumina) to determine genomic resistance markers. A total of 159 patients were included (median age = 54 years; 66.7% male); 72.3% had confirmed clinical infections, and 66% were admitted to the ICU. The most frequent infection types were pneumonia, urinary tract infection and bacteraemia. Overall, 97.5% of isolates were classified as XDR. Carbapenem resistance approached 100% (imipenem 99.4%, meropenem 98.7%). Whole-genome data revealed clonal diversity among Klebsiella pneumoniae (ST13/ST15) carrying bla NDM-1; Acinetobacter baumannii uniformly harboured bla OXA-23; and Pseudomonas aeruginosa included high-risk clones ST357 (bla IMP-93) and ST111 (bla IMP-18, bla VIM-2). These findings demonstrate a critical burden of XDR-GNB and the presence of multiple carbapenemases (NDM, IMP, KPC and VIM) associated with clinically relevant high-risk lineages. Strengthening molecular surveillance, optimizing antimicrobial stewardship and reinforcing infection-control measures are urgently needed to contain CR-GNB in critical-care settings in Peru.

42892792.title: Risk Factors and Outcomes of Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus faecium Bloodstream Infection in Hematologic Malignancies and Stem Cell Transplant Recipients: A Case-Control Study.
42892792.abstract: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) bloodstream infection (BSI) represents a growing challenge in hematology-oncology settings. This study aimed to characterize the epidemiology, risk factors, and prognostic impact of VREfm BSI within a mixed adult hematology-oncology and transplant unit. We conducted a retrospective matched case-control study (2014-2024). Multivariable conditional logistic regression identified factors associated with VREfm BSI, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models assessed nonlinear exposure-response relationships between antimicrobial classes and VREfm BSI. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards regression. VREfm BSI incidence rose from 0.02 to 0.07 per 1000 person-days (2014-2018 vs 2019-2024). A high-risk composite comprising recipients of allogeneic stem cell transplant and/or AML (adjusted OR [aOR], 3.90; 95% CI, 1.87-8.15; P < .001) and ICU admission (aOR, 5.63; 95% CI, 2.15-14.78; P < .001), were independently associated with VREfm BSI. Cumulative days of carbapenems (aOR, 1.09/day; 95% CI, 1.02-1.17; P = .013), beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitors (aOR, 1.09/day; 95% CI, 1.02-1.16; P = .006), and systemic antifungals (aOR, 1.12/day; 95% CI, 1.03-1.22; P = .009) exhibited duration-dependent associations. RCS models demonstrated a nonlinear, duration-dependent association with cumulative antibiotic exposure, including antianaerobic agents (P < .001). VREfm BSI was associated with increased mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.63-2.66; P < .001). VREfm BSI reflects the interplay between host susceptibility and nonlinear, duration- and spectrum-dependent antibiotic exposure pressure. This underscores the importance of antimicrobial stewardship strategies as a potential intervention to mitigate risk.

42891256.title: Multipathogen antimicrobial resistance in a Romanian tertiary-care hospital: a retrospective antibiogram analysis, January-July 2025.
42891256.abstract: Routine microbiology data can show not only isolated resistance events but also the wider hospital ecology in which antimicrobial resistance (AMR) emerges. We analyzed the complete January-July 2025 antibiogram export from a Romanian tertiary-care hospital, along with a targeted extended-testing file. The scope was deliberately broader than a single-organism carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae analysis. We performed a retrospective descriptive analysis using 3,270 antibiogram records from 3,012 patient identifiers. Organisms, sample types, resistance labels, and extended-test results were extracted from laboratory text fields. Organism occurrences within polymicrobial reports were counted separately to describe the full pathogen spectrum. The dataset contained 4,039 organism occurrences. Enterobacterales were the largest group, followed by Gram-positive cocci, non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli, and yeasts. Escherichia coli and K. pneumoniae were the most frequent Enterobacterales, and clinically relevant resistant organisms were also identified among Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacter cloacae complex, Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Enterococcus faecium and Candida species. The extended-testing file contained 100 organism occurrences from 85 patient identifiers, mainly extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative isolates. Cefiderocol testing corresponded predominantly to K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii complex, whereas aztreonam/avibactam was concentrated mainly in extensively drug-resistant Enterobacterales, especially K. pneumoniae. The data support a multipathogen AMR interpretation: carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, non-fermenters, resistant Gram-positive cocci and yeasts coexist in the same hospital ecology. Empirical therapy, infection-control actions and stewardship decisions should be guided by syndrome, sample source, prior colonization and local species-level resistance patterns.

42966286.title: Fungal biofilm-associated infections in immunocompromised African populations: A narrative review of Candidozyma auris emergence, antifungal resistance mechanisms, and laboratory detection algorithms.
42966286.abstract: Candidozyma auris the abbreviation C. auris is retained throughout has become one of the most concerning hospital-acquired fungal infections over the past decade, colonizing the environment and skin for extended periods, exhibiting multidrug resistance, and forming biofilms that are resistant to both the host immune response and antifungal treatments. Sub-Saharan and North African medical institutions have a unique set of risks: a significant HIV-positive population, widespread malnutrition, high rates of tuberculosis co-infection, the appearance of critical care units, and diagnostic laboratories that often lack the tools to accurately identify emerging yeast species. This paper aims to analyze the current understanding of the emergence and prevalence of C. auris infections in African healthcare facilities, discuss the properties of biofilm formed by this yeast that facilitate its persistence and resistance to treatment, examine the features of immunosuppressed African patients who are at the highest risk of C. auris colonization and infection, and identify the available laboratory tests that can be used to diagnose this fungus in African hospitals. A narrative review has been performed to gather the evidence on the emergence of C. auris in African healthcare facilities and describe the general trends in its clinical presentation. The data were retrieved from reports and research articles published in peer-reviewed journals, utilizing resources such as national and multinational surveillance records, World Health Organization documents, and scientific publications from regional reference labs that investigate the clinical characteristics and treatment of C. auris infections and report on the local epidemiology of this yeast. Four principal findings emerge. First, documented African activity is concentrated in South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria and Egypt and is dominated by clade III and clade I, but the apparent continental increase conflates genuine transmission with rapidly improving detection capacity and should not be read as an incidence estimate. Second, fluconazole resistance is consistently high across African series (of the order of 85-90%), amphotericin B resistance is elevated relative to global pooled estimates (approximately 15-35%, highest in the clade III-dominated South African series), whereas echinocandin resistance remains below 5% but is no longer negligible. Third, biofilm growth confers a reversible, largely non-genetic tolerance matrix-mediated drug sequestration, biofilm-induced efflux upregulation and persister-cell dormancy that raises effective inhibitory concentrations by one to more than two orders of magnitude above planktonic values, so routine susceptibility reports systematically understate the drug exposure required in device-associated infection. Fourth, the dominant diagnostic constraint across the continent is not the absence of technology as such but systematic misidentification by the conventional biochemical panels that remain the mainstay of African yeast identification; this is addressable through a tiered algorithm anchored on a low threshold of suspicion rather than on universal access to mass spectrometry or sequencing. We conclude that C. auris preparedness in Africa is best pursued not as a vertical, pathogen-specific programme but as an explicit extension of the antimicrobial resistance surveillance, laboratory strengthening and infection prevention frameworks already under construction across the region, with tiered diagnostics, antifungal stewardship, biofilm-aware clinical management and the systematic evaluation of natural product-derived adjunctive agents as the immediate priorities.

42959813.title: Spatiotemporal trajectories of antimicrobial resistance in bloodstream infections in China: a nationwide longitudinal surveillance study from 2014 to 2023.
42959813.journal: The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific
authors: Blood Bacterial Resistant Investigation Collaborative System (BRICS) Study Group
42959813.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) impose a substantial global burden, increasingly complicated by antimicrobial resistance (AMR). We aimed to characterise decade-long trends in BSI pathogens and major resistance phenotypes across mainland China. We analysed BSI surveillance data from 72 hospitals across 22 provinces in the Bacterial Resistant Investigation Collaborative System (BRICS) between 2014 and 2023. Isolates were transferred to a central reference laboratory for species identification and standardised antimicrobial susceptibility testing, with raw minimum inhibitory concentration values retrospectively reinterpreted using 2025 CLSI guidelines. Fourteen continuously participating hospitals formed a sentinel cohort. Among 76,211 non-duplicate BSI isolates, Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae predominated, with K. pneumoniae increasing by 0.91 percentage points annually (95% CI 0.59-1.23; p < 0.001). Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing E. coli decreased from 61.5% to 47.4%, MRSA from 39.0% to 26.2%, and ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae from 30.5% to 21.5% (all p < 0.001). Conversely, carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae increased from 7.0% to 14.9%, peaking at 22.5% in 2018, with marked spatial heterogeneity. CRAB remained persistently high (55.2-64.3%). Resistance proportions were higher in intensive care units, older patients and male patients for several phenotypes. Major resistance phenotypes declined during a decade of nationwide antimicrobial stewardship, while the contribution of K. pneumoniae to BSIs increased and carbapenem resistance remained a major challenge. Future AMR strategies should integrate antimicrobial stewardship with targeted infection prevention, outbreak control, and genomic surveillance. This study was supported by Prevention and Control of Emerging and Major Infectious Diseases-National Science and technology Major Project (2025ZD01903301), National Key R&D Program of China (2024YFC2311304) and Research Project of Jinan Microecological Biomedicine Shandong Laboratory (JNL-2025004B).

42873064.title: Prioritization and Severe Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation.
42873064.abstract: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) is the leading cause of early morbidity and mortality after lung transplantation (LTx). Critically ill candidates may receive priority on the transplant waiting list; however, the relationship between prioritization and the development of severe PGD remains unclear. We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained cohort including all consecutive LTx performed at a tertiary center between January 2016 and June 2025. Recipients were categorized according to prioritization status. Severe PGD was defined as grade 3 PGD according to the International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation criteria. Clinical characteristics and outcomes were compared between prioritized and non-prioritized recipients. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of severe PGD, and survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Among 310 LTx recipients, 74 (23.8%) were prioritized. They were younger, had a higher prevalence of pulmonary hypertension, and were more frequently hospitalized before transplantation, particularly in the intensive care unit. Severe PGD occurred more often among prioritized recipients (24% vs 7%). However, prioritization was not independently associated with PGD after adjustment. Pre-transplant extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support emerged as the strongest independent predictor of severe PGD. Thirty-day mortality was similar between groups, whereas prioritized recipients had higher 90-day and 1-year mortality. Prioritized LTx recipients have greater pre-transplant clinical severity, higher crude rates of severe PGD, and worse short-term survival. However, prioritization itself was not independently associated with PGD, suggesting that underlying disease severity and need for advanced support are the main drivers of post-transplant outcomes.

42856053.title: Development of the ECMO nursing self-efficacy Perception scale: A validity and reliability study.
42856053.abstract: Caring for patients receiving ECMO in the ICU is a complex process that requires advanced knowledge, technical skills, and confident clinical decision-making from nurses. Despite the increasing use of ECMO in Türkiye, no comprehensive, validated tool exists to measure ICU nurses' self-efficacy in ECMO care. This methodological study aimed to develop the ECMO Nursing Self-Efficacy Perception Scale (ECMO-SEPS) and evaluate its psychometric properties. The scale was developed in two stages. In the first stage, an item pool was generated through an extensive literature review and qualitative interviews with seven ICU nurses experienced in ECMO care. In the second stage, the scale's content and construct validity were assessed using confirmatory factor analysis, including convergent and discriminant validity evaluations. Reliability analyses included internal consistency, evaluated by Cronbach's alpha coefficients, and test-retest reliability, assessed with intraclass correlation coefficients. The final scale consists of 37 items across three subscales: cognitive, affective, and psychomotor, collectively explaining 70.5% of the total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the three-factor structure with acceptable to good model fit indices. The overall Cronbach's alpha was 0.97, with 0.97, 0.81, and 0.96 for the cognitive, affective, and psychomotor subscales, respectively, indicating high internal consistency. Test-retest results demonstrated excellent stability over time. In conclusion, the ECMO-SEPS is a valid and reliable instrument for objectively assessing ICU nurses' self-efficacy in ECMO care. Its use may facilitate standardized evaluations and inform evidence-based education, workforce planning, and clinical practice in ECMO programs.

42855857.title: Deep Neural Network-Driven Early Recognition in Cardiopulmonary Failure: A Paradigm Shift Underway in Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support?
42855857.abstract: The contemporary intensive care unit generates an overwhelming magnitude of high-frequency, granular physiological data. However, conventional decision-making for patients requiring temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) remains tethered to reactive, threshold-driven manual adjustments, underutilizing continuous data streams and failing to optimize the complex patient-machine interaction. This review examines the integration of deep neural networks (DNNs) as a candidate strategy for advanced clinical decision support. By identifying a continuous "digital phenotype," hierarchical deep learning architectures signal a shift toward real-time trajectory recognition in tMCS. We establish a four-tier functional taxonomy-prognosticative, descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive-to categorize translational milestones from automated pump-speed optimization to closed-loop homeostatic regulation. Operational challenges are analyzed through the TEIP (Transparency, Explainability, Interpretability, and Performance) Core-Lens Framework, navigating the dynamic equilibrium between computational density and clinical explainability. We further evaluate the evolving global regulatory landscape, advocating for a foundation on verified empirical safety and rigorous clinical trial validation over absolute mathematical transparency in high-density architectures. Implementing a strategic roadmap including context-specific validation, multimodal integration, and human-centered design is quintessential to safely transform passive hardware into intelligent systems. As the field evolves, DNN technology offers a consequential opportunity to advance early cardiopulmonary failure recognition into a clinical reality.

42848051.title: Veno-Venous ECMO after Penetrating Trauma: A Viable Option With Individualized Anticoagulation.
42848051.abstract: BackgroundThe incidence, clinical characteristics, complications, and outcomes for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in penetrating trauma cases are mostly unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the concept that ECMO could be a safe and effective therapy after severe penetrating injury at a single high-volume center.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective case series of all penetrating trauma patients supported with ECMO at a single Level I trauma center between January 2022 and June 2025. Data collected included demographics, injury patterns, ECMO indications and cannulation details, anticoagulation management, operative interventions performed on ECMO, bleeding and thrombotic complications, and clinical outcomes.ResultsEight patients were supported with veno-venous ECMO, all male, with a median age of 36 years and a median Injury Severity Score of 20. Injury mechanisms included six gunshot wounds and two stab wounds, with a median PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 71 at ECMO consultation. Anticoagulation was individualized, with initiation delayed a median of 4 days after cannulation, and one patient received no anticoagulation throughout their ECMO course. Four patients underwent major operative procedures while on ECMO. Three patients had manageable bleeding complications, and three had thrombotic complications not associated with anticoagulation interruption. Overall survival to hospital discharge was 75% (6/8 patients).DiscussionThis case series demonstrates basic proof of concept that ECMO can be safely implemented in carefully selected penetrating trauma patients. Individualized anticoagulation strategies and concurrent operative management were feasible with manageable complications. Further multicenter studies are needed to define optimal patient selection and anticoagulation practices.

42845574.title: Results Reporting and Registry-Linked Publications Among Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Studies Registered on ClinicalTrials.gov: A Cross-Sectional Meta-Research Study.
42845574.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) research has expanded rapidly, but how often completed ECMO studies make their results publicly available is not known. This cross-sectional meta-research study examined ECMO study records on ClinicalTrials.gov at a census date of 13 September 2026. A field-scoped query of the registry's application programming interface returned 524 records, of which 493 met prespecified eligibility criteria after duplicate model-assisted screening with every decision checked by the first author. The primary outcome was the proportion of completed studies with a primary completion date at least 12 months before the census date that had summary results posted on the registry. Registry-linked PubMed references were classified by article type. Of the 493 studies, 268 (54.4%) were observational and 471 (95.5%) had a non-industry lead sponsor. In the 184-study 12-month-observable completed cohort, 14 had posted summary results (7.6%, 95% CI 4.6 to 12.4), and one had done so within 12 months of primary completion. Posting was more frequent in interventional than observational studies (17.6% versus 1.7%, risk difference 15.9 percentage points, 95% CI 7.5 to 26.7). Sixty-one studies (33.2%) carried at least one registry-linked PubMed reference, and 60 (32.6%) were linked to an article reporting their results. All four records meeting a post hoc registry-based approximation of applicable clinical trial status had posted results, but this subgroup was too small, and its classification too uncertain, to support any inference about regulation. Summary-results posting was uncommon among completed ECMO studies, a majority of which are observational and therefore outside the scope of United States statutory reporting requirements.

42843714.title: Congenital hepatopulmonary fusion in right congenital diaphragmatic hernia: Surgical strategy and outcomes in a multicenter cohort.
42843714.abstract: Congenital hepatopulmonary fusion (CHPF) is a rare anomaly associated with right congenital diaphragmatic hernia (RCDH), for which optimal diagnosis and surgical management remain undefined. This study aimed to explore the impact of surgical separation on outcomes. A retrospective multicenter study reviewed neonates with intraoperatively or radiologically confirmed CHPF associated with RCDH. Demographic data, imaging, surgical strategy, and outcomes were analyzed. Patients were stratified according to whether surgical separation of the fusion was performed (CHPF-S) or not (CHPF-NS). Forty-three patients were included (26 CHPF-S and 17 CHPF-NS). Prenatal diagnosis of RCDH occurred in 20.9% of cases, while most diagnoses were made postnatally. Imaging findings suggestive of CHPF were identified preoperatively in a minority of patients, with computed tomography angiography providing additional information regarding vascular anatomy in selected cases. Baseline demographic characteristics, gestational age, birth weight, and CDH defect distribution were comparable between groups. The age at surgical repair differed, however not significantly, with earlier intervention in the CHPF-S group (9.0 ± 15.8 vs 17.9 ± 24.2 days, p = 0.099). Complete parenchymal fusion was more frequently observed in the CHPF-NS group, whereas partial fusion was more common in the CHPF-S group. Pulmonary hypertension occurred in 55.8% of patients and extracorporeal life support was required in 7.0%. Overall mortality was 27.9%, including 7 deaths in the CHPF-NS group and 5 in the CHPF-S group (41.2% vs 19.2%, p = 0.117), predominantly related to severe pulmonary hypertension. Surgical separation of the fusion may be selectively advisable in hemodynamically stable patients with a thin membrane or partial fusion, although non-separation often remains prudent. In critically ill neonates, patch repair or closure around the fused organs without separation represents a safer alternative. Early suspicion of CHPF in RCDH and thorough preoperative planning are essential to optimize outcomes.

42955314.title: [Nursing competencies in ECMO care: a scoping review].
42955314.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is used in cases of refractory cardiac or pulmonary failure and places high demands on the treatment team, particularly on nursing staff, whose required competencies have scarcely been described in German-speaking countries. The primary aim was to map the international evidence on nursing competencies in the care of adult ECMO patients. Secondary aims included identifying specialised nursing roles and drawing implications for the German-speaking countries. The scoping review was conducted in accordance with the guidelines of the Joanna Briggs Institute and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses- Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The literature search was carried out in MEDLINE, CINAHL and Scopus, as well as in reference lists. German- and English-language primary studies published between 2009 and May 2026 were included. A total of n = 14 studies were included, comprising n = 7 qualitative (n = 6 [semi-structured] interview studies, n = 1 focus group interview) and n = 7 quantitative (n = 3 cross-sectional studies, n = 1 Delphi survey, n = 1 prospective cohort study, n = 1 prospective observational study, and n = 1 quasi-experimental study) studies. Based on the identified evidence, a multidimensional competency profile for ECMO nursing care can be described, including the necessary knowledge, practical skills, and professional attitudes. In addition, specialised nursing roles were identified. No studies meeting the inclusion criteria were identified for German-speaking countries. A multidimensional competency profile emerges that is internationally anchored in specialised nursing roles; however, empirical data, role profiles and structured qualification pathways are lacking in German-speaking countries.

42950893.title: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation as rescue therapy for patients with suspected high-risk pulmonary embolism: A multicenter retrospective cohort study.
42950893.abstract: For patients with suspected high-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) who cannot undergo computed tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) because of unstable hemodynamics, the optimal strategy, namely, prioritizing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or revascularization, remains unclear. This study investigated whether prioritizing ECMO is associated with increased survival rates. A total of 117 patients with suspected high-risk PE admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) at four ECMO centers were retrospectively enrolled (2013-2024). Among these patients, 79 received ECMO (ECMO group), whereas 38 underwent thrombolysis therapy (thrombolysis group). The baseline and preintervention management characteristics were comparable between the groups. In-hospital mortality was lower in the ECMO group than in the thrombolysis group (33/79, 41.8% vs 22/38, 57.9%), although the difference was not significant (P = 0.15). Multivariate Cox analysis revealed that treatment with ECMO was associated with a reduced risk of in-hospital mortality (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.45, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.25-0.79, P = 0.006). An elevated pretreatment Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score was identified as an independent risk factor for mortality (HR = 1.14, 95% CI 1.06-1.22, P < 0.001). Kaplan‒Meier curves and log-rank tests revealed better 28-day survival in the ECMO group than in the thrombolysis group (P = 0.041). Among the 79 patients who received ECMO, 63 had CTPA-verified high-risk PE, with 34 surviving to discharge (34/63, 54.0%). For hemodynamically unstable patients with suspected high-risk PE, prioritizing ECMO is a safe strategy that serves as an independent protective factor against in-hospital mortality, despite nonsignificant findings in unadjusted analyses. Larger studies are warranted to validate these results.

42946513.title: The Operational Impact of a Tertiary Hospital Heliport in Lisbon: A One‑Year Operational Review.
42946513.abstract: Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) are a key component of modern emergency and critical care systems, improving access to time‑sensitive interventions for critically ill patients. In Portugal, the certification and reopening of the Santa Maria Hospital Heliport (SMHH) in March 2025 established a continuously 24/7 hospital heliport in Lisbon. To describe the first year of operation of the SMHH and evaluate its role in national aeromedical connectivity and patient redistribution within a metropolitan hospital network. A retrospective descriptive study was conducted including all helicopter movements recorded at the SMHH between March 2025 and March 2026, using the institutional operational registry. Variables included number of landings, temporal distribution, mission type and final destination. During the first year of operation, a total of 235 landings were recorded. Primary HEMS mission accounted for approximately 60% of all operations, followed by secondary inter-hospital transfers (35%) and specialized ECMO and organ missions (5%). Less than 10% of helicopter missions to the Lisbon metropolitan area required diversion to alternative certified heliports. The implementation of a certified 24/7 hospital heliport established an effective aeromedical hub for the Lisbon metropolitan area, faciliting direct helicopter acces and coordinated distribution of patients to the most appropriate referral hospitals, while potentially reducing the need for secondary ground transfers. Further studies are required to quantify its impact on transfer times and patient outcomes.

42940736.title: Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Requiring ECMO: Current Evidence, Controversies, and Unresolved Questions.
42940736.abstract: Background/Objectives: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) remains one of the most challenging conditions in neonatal critical care. Despite advances in prenatal assessment and neonatal management, substantial uncertainty persists regarding ECMO selection, mode and duration of support, and timing of diaphragmatic repair. This review summarizes the available evidence and critically examines the major unresolved questions in the management of infants with CDH requiring ECMO. Methods: A narrative review was conducted based on a literature search in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for studies published between June 2005 and June 2026. Additional relevant publications were identified through reference screening, and selected foundational studies predating the search period were included when appropriate. Prospective and retrospective studies, registry-based analyses, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant consensus statements were considered. Evidence was narratively synthesized, with particular attention to disease severity, methodological limitations, and survivor bias. Results: Available evidence highlights substantial heterogeneity in disease severity and management. Prenatal and postnatal markers aid risk stratification, but no single parameter reliably predicts ECMO requirement or defines the optimal management strategy. To date, no clear survival advantage has been demonstrated for either veno-arterial or veno-venous ECMO, although veno-arterial ECMO remains the predominant mode of support in most centers; mode selection should therefore be individualized according to cardiopulmonary physiology, patient characteristics, anatomy, and institutional expertise. Surgical timing remains particularly controversial. While repair after ECMO decannulation has been associated with favorable outcomes, recent observational analyses suggest that early repair during ECMO may be beneficial in selected patients, although the optimal timing remains uncertain. Prolonged ECMO may provide additional time for pulmonary and cardiovascular recovery, although this potential benefit must be weighed against the cumulative morbidity of prolonged support. Conclusions: Management should be individualized according to disease severity, clinical trajectory, cardiopulmonary recovery, and institutional expertise. Current evidence does not support a universal strategy for ECMO initiation, mode, surgical timing, or duration. Prospective multicenter studies using standardized definitions and adequately accounting for disease severity are needed to reduce practice variation and better define optimal management.

42908132.title: Lunar phases, meteorological conditions, astrological signs, and postoperative outcomes of acute type A aortic dissection: Results of a retrospective cohort study.
42908132.abstract: BackgroundAcute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) is a surgical emergency associated with high mortality. While patient-related risk factors are well-established, beliefs persist regarding the influence of lunar phases, meteorological conditions, and astrological signs on disease occurrence and outcomes.MethodsWe retrospectively analysed all patients who underwent emergency surgery for ATAAD at Bordeaux University Hospital between 1996 and 2020. The primary objective was to assess the association between environmental factors (lunar phases, atmospheric pressure, temperature, and astrological signs) and ATAAD incidence. Secondary objectives included assessing their association with 30-day mortality and postoperative morbidity (intensive care unit length of stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation use, and mesenteric infarction). Meteorological data were available for 603 patients from 2010 onward.ResultsAmong 920 patients (70% male; mean age 63 ± 13 years), the 30-day mortality rate was 9.7%. Lunar phases were not associated with ATAAD incidence (first quarter 26%, last quarter 25%, new moon 25%, full moon 24%; p = 0.91), mortality, or complications. Atmospheric pressure showed no association with ATAAD occurrence or outcomes. Temperature showed a weak correlation with ATAAD incidence (r = 0.11, p = 0.01), but not with mortality. Astrological signs were not associated with ATAAD incidence, mortality, or morbidity. Longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration (odds ratio [OR] = 0.994 per minute; p = 0.01) and diabetes (OR = 4.63; p = 0.01) were associated with 30-day mortality.ConclusionsEnvironmental factors were not associated with ATAAD incidence or outcomes. Established clinical factors remain the primary determinants of mortality.

42901307.title: Veno-arterial ECMO for the management of propofol infusion syndrome following cardiac surgery.
42901307.journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion
42901307.abstract: Propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS) has been described in patients requiring prolonged sedation with this drug, as may occur in some cases after cardiac surgery. Its treatment is based on discontinuation of the drug and supportive management of organ dysfunction until resolution. In the postoperative period of cardiac surgery, diagnosing PRIS poses a challenge, since it must be differentiated from other, more common complications such as postcardiotomy shock. In these patients, PRIS may fatally worsen the prognosis. Veno-arterial ECMO therapy may help maintain cardiac output. Both the diagnosis of PRIS after cardiac surgery and its treatment with ECMO have been scarcely reported. We present a case of PRIS after cardiac surgery successfully managed with ECMO.

42897514.title: Longitudinal recovery of physical function after lung transplantation: a comparative analysis of ECMO and non-ECMO recipients.
42897514.abstract: Lung transplantation (LT) improves survival in patients with end-stage lung disease; however, recovery of physical function after transplantation remains insufficiently characterized, particularly in critically ill recipients bridged with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Understanding longitudinal functional recovery and potential differences between ECMO and non-ECMO recipients is essential for optimizing post-transplant rehabilitation strategies. We retrospectively analyzed 84 adult patients who underwent lung or heart-lung transplantation between 2018 and 2023. Physical function was assessed at 6 and 12 months using the 6-minute walk test, gait speed, and strength measures. Changes over time and group differences were evaluated using longitudinal statistical models. Fifty patients (59.5%) required ECMO support. Overall physical function significantly improved from 6 to 12 months, with 93.4% achieving independent ambulation by 12 months. ECMO recipients had a lower proportion of independent ambulation at 6 months compared with non-ECMO recipients. At 12 months, no statistically significant between-group difference was observed in the proportion of patients achieving independent ambulation. LT recipients showed significant improvement in physical function between 6 and 12 months after transplantation. ECMO-bridged recipients had lower independent ambulation rates at 6 months, while no statistically significant between-group difference was observed at 12 months. Further studies incorporating pretransplant and early postoperative assessments are needed to better characterize functional recovery after lung transplantation.

42885534.title: Preoperative echocardiographic parameters do not predict early outcomes after arterial switch operation in late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum.
42885534.abstract: To determine whether preoperative echocardiographic parameters can predict early postoperative outcomes after arterial switch operation in late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum. This prospective study examined preoperative demographic characteristics, echocardiographic findings, and left ventricular strain parameters in 35 patients undergoing arterial switch operation for late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum. Further, their correlation with postoperative variables, including length of ICU stay, postoperative hospital stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support, and inotropic score, was assessed. The median age at surgery was 45 days, and the median weight was 3.4 kg. The median interventricular septal thickness was 4.1 mm, and the median left ventricular mass index was 26.4 g/m2. The median average left ventricular strain was -24.19. Thirteen patients required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support. The whole cohort had a median extracorporeal membrane oxygenation duration of 0 days. The median length of ICU stay was 12 days, and the median length of postoperative hospital stay was 17 days. The median inotropic score was 28. There was no case of early mortality. None of the preoperative echocardiographic parameters showed a statistically significant association with postoperative outcomes. Preoperative echocardiographic parameters, including left ventricular strain, did not significantly predict early postoperative outcomes after arterial switch operation in patients with late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum. Postoperative outcomes in this patient group are likely influenced by multiple preoperative factors rather than a single preoperative echocardiographic parameter.

42935932.title: Transforming Inpatient Glycemic Management: A System-Wide Approach to Reducing Hyperglycemia and Hypoglycemia.
42935932.abstract: Diabetes affects >37 million U.S. adults and poses major inpatient challenges. Up to 25% of noncritically ill hospitalized patients have diabetes, and many develop stress hyperglycemia. Hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia lead to complications, extended hospital stays, readmissions, and mortality. Our Northern California academic medical center launched a system-wide quality improvement initiative to optimize inpatient glycemic management. Key interventions included establishing an inpatient glycemic team consisting of endocrinologists and advanced practice nurses, implementing standardized insulin order sets with decision support tools, developing glycemic dashboards, and introducing an intensive care unit pharmacist-comanaged insulin protocol. Education emphasized the importance of evidence-based insulin use and workflow efficiency, including the synchronization of point-of-care (POC) glucose testing, meal delivery, and insulin administration. POC glucose data from acute care inpatients were analyzed over 7 years grouped into early (2017-2019), transition (2020-2021), and mature (2022-2024) phases of the quality improvement program. Glucometrics included percent patient-days with day-weighted mean (DWM) glucose >180 mg/dL, percent days with glucose ≥300 mg/dL, and percent days with hypoglycemia <70 mg/dL and severe hypoglycemia <54 mg/dL, assessed biannually. Logistic regression analysis was used to assess differences between phases. Hyperglycemia declined significantly: percent patient-days with DWM glucose >180 mg/dL fell from 35.2% to 31.0% (P < 0.001). Percent days with glucose ≥300 mg/dL decreased from 11.3% to 8.4%, hypoglycemia <70 mg/dL dropped from 3.5% to 2.9%, and severe hypoglycemia <54 mg/dL dropped from 1.1% to 0.8%. A quality improvement strategy incorporating standardized protocols and education sustainably improved glycemic control and safety across a large academic medical center.

42868093.title: Charting the future: A multi-setting medical chart study of advance care planning in Parkinson's disease and atypical Parkinsonism.
42868093.abstract: BackgroundAdvance Care Planning (ACP) enables people with progressive diseases to document and communicate future treatment preferences. For Parkinson's disease (PD) and atypical parkinsonism (AP), ACP is particularly important because of disease complexity, symptom burden, the progressive nature of the disease, and cognitive decline, yet its implementation across care settings remains unclear.MethodsWe conducted a medical chart review of 189 deceased patients with PD or AP who died in nursing homes (n = 91), hospitals (n = 58), or at home (n = 40) in the Netherlands. For patients who died at home, data were obtained from their general practice records. Data on treatment preferences, care discussions and palliative care goals were extracted at one year and six weeks before death.ResultsDocumentation of treatment preferences increased towards death but differed markedly between settings. Nursing homes recorded resuscitation and ICU limitations early and comprehensively, whereas hospitals made major updates only in the final weeks of life. In general practices, ACP documentation was limited. Nursing homes and hospitals more frequently addressed disease-specific scenarios, palliative sedation and end-of-life issues, while general practices more often reported preferred place of death and euthanasia. Palliative care goals in nursing homes covered all domains, while in hospitals and general practices they mainly related to physical aspects.ConclusionACP remains inconsistently documented and frequently delayed until the final weeks of life, when crises or cognitive decline may hinder meaningful participation. Earlier, iterative ACP-supported by clinician training, PD-specific guidance, and system-level measures such as ACP prompts in electronic medical records-could foster a more proactive and person-centered palliative approach aligned with patient values throughout the disease trajectory.

42836182.title: Optimal Dosing Strategies for Remimazolam Across Diverse Patient Populations: A Clinical Narrative Review.
42836182.abstract: Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine that is hydrolyzed by carboxylesterase 1 (CES1) to the inactive metabolite CNS 7054. Since regulatory approval in 2020 it has been adopted globally for procedural sedation and general anesthesia, supported by an expanding evidence base of randomized trials, population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling studies, dose-finding sequential-allocation analyses, and meta-analyses. Synthesizing 92 studies published between January 2020 and April 2026, this narrative review defines dose optimization across diverse populations. For adult procedural sedation, a fixed 5 mg initial bolus followed by 2.5 mg maintenance titrations achieves moderate sedation with a hemodynamic and respiratory profile that compares favorably with propofol, whereas general anesthesia requires an induction rate of 6 to 12 mg kg-1 h-1 followed by maintenance at 1.0-2.0 mg kg-1 h-1. Dosing demands a 25-30% reduction in the elderly (≥ 65 years), higher weight-adjusted requirements in pediatric patients (1-18 years), and lean or corrected body weight scalars in obesity, while severe hepatic impairment reduces clearance by approximately 38% and opioid co-administration yields a 15-63% synergistic reduction in effective concentrations. Several quantitative estimates, however, derive from single-center trials with fewer than 30 participants per arm that have not been externally validated. To help clinicians weigh these recommendations, each population-level dosing estimate is graded by the strength and external validity of its supporting evidence (A, B, or C); most special-population point estimates rest on single-center studies (grade C) and are best regarded as starting points rather than established standards. Crucially, the halted Japanese Phase II intensive care unit trial (ONO-2745-04) serves as a key safety counter-narrative: continuous infusions exceeding 24 hours in critically ill patients may be associated with drug accumulation and delayed emergence, suggesting that organ-independent clearance may not be guaranteed when CES1 activity is compromised. Major evidence gaps persist for infants under one year of age, long-duration anesthesia, CES1 polymorphisms, and non-East-Asian populations.

42832427.title: Impact of a Geriatric Co-management Service on Surgical Cancer Care for Older Adults.
42832427.abstract: In 2011, Brown University Health's Division of Geriatrics started its inaugural geriatric co-management service to improve older adult (OA) care for patients with hip fractures. Its success in care and cost reduction prompted the health system to expand geriatric co-management. Meanwhile, oncology surgeons treat increasingly older and frailer patients due to improved therapies and survival. The literature established what we saw here: increased mortality and complications in frail OA and failure of strategies like Enhanced Recovery After Surgery and Prehabilitation. In 2021, the division launched an oncologic surgery co-management program. Explicit to its launch, hospital sponsors required a 2-year study for benchmarks and quality metrics with a primary outcome of reducing mortality and delirium. QI metrics were developed through PowerBI dashboards using hospital and EMR data, analyzing 4,359 cases, which measured length of stay (LOS), readmissions, mortality, and disposition, from July 2018 to August 2024. We compared outcomes between the pilot (Geri) and those with no geriatric involvement (UC) using 1:1 propensity score matching. Bivariate analyses used chi-square and Student's t-tests for descriptive comparisons and multivariate linear or logistic regression analyses for outcome rates and adjusted when appropriate. The matched sample consisted of 309 cases in each group. 14% were underrepresented minorities. The Geri group had a lower odds ratio (OR) for hospice or in-hospital mortality (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.12-0.61, p = 0.0016), as well as significantly lower odds of delirium, measured by a positive CAM (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.11-0.73, p = 0.0086). ICU admission was lower in the geri group, although not statistically significant (18 vs 25, p = 0.0690). Overall hospital length of stay was longer in the geri group (8.2 ± 15.4 vs. 6.2 ± 5.6 days, p = 0.0350). Geri patients were less likely to be discharged home (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.33-0.77) but were more likely to be discharged to a skilled nursing facility (OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.43-3.53) or inpatient rehabilitation facility (OR 8.52, 95% CI 1.04-69.6). Conclusion: Geriatric co-management in surgical oncology significantly reduced mortality and delirium as measured by CAM among OA, demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient outcomes. Although LOS increased and home discharges decreased, these results may indicate more appropriate discharge planning for this patient population. Geriatric co-management represents a critical, evidence-based component of surgical oncology care for OA. This study adds to the growing evidence supporting the role of Geriatric Medicine in improving the quality of care for OA.

42889950.title: Relationship Between Blood Urea Nitrogen to Albumin Ratio and Risks of Mortality and Delirium in Pancreatitis Patients: A Retrospective Analysis of the MIMIC-IV Database.
42889950.abstract: This study is aimed at evaluating the predictive value of the blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio (BAR) for both mortality and delirium risk in patients with pancreatitis. Pancreatitis carries a substantial mortality risk and significant long-term sequelae, with delirium being a severe neurological complication, underscoring the clinical need for effective prognostic markers. A retrospective cohort study was performed using the MIMIC-IV v3.0 database. A total of 1748 ICU patients meeting diagnostic criteria for pancreatitis (ICD-9/10 codes: 577.0, 577.1, K85) with documented baseline blood urea nitrogen (BUN) and albumin levels were included. BAR was calculated (BUN[mg/dL]/Albumin[g/dL]) and patients were stratified into quartiles (Q1: BAR < 3.0; Q2: BAR 3.0-5.0; Q3: BAR 5.0-9.2; Q4: BAR ≥ 9.2). The primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and delirium occurrence (identified using ICD-9 codes 293.0, 293.1, and ICD-10 codes F05, F05.9). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression (mortality) and logistic regression (delirium) were employed, adjusting for demographics, illness severity scores (GCS, SAPS II, OASIS, and Charlson Comorbidity Index), and comorbidities. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to explore nonlinear associations. Higher BAR levels significantly correlated with greater disease severity: compared with Q1, Q4 exhibited a higher Charlson Comorbidity Index and mortality rate. BAR was an independent predictor of delirium; each 1-unit increase in BAR was associated with a 2.7% increased risk of delirium (adjusted OR = 1.027, 95% CI: 1.009-1.044), and patients in Q4 had a significantly higher risk compared with those in Q1 (adjusted OR = 1.882, 95% CI: 1.157-3.108). After multivariable adjustment, BAR was not significantly independently associated with mortality (Q4 adjusted HR = 1.022, p = 0.8). RCS analysis revealed BAR > 9.0 as a high-risk threshold, characterized by delirium OR > 1.78 and mortality HR > 1.97. The BAR quartile model yielded AUCs of 0.635 and 0.599 for predicting mortality and delirium, respectively, indicating modest predictive ability. BAR independently predicts delirium risk and reflects disease severity in pancreatitis patients, but does not demonstrate significant independent predictive value for mortality after accounting for confounders. The identified threshold (BAR > 9.0) supports the utility of BAR as a supplementary biomarker for delirium risk stratification in this population.

42956429.title: Incidence, timing, severity, and predictors of venous thromboembolism after open abdominal wall reconstruction.
42956429.abstract: Venous thromboembolic events, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, represent serious and potentially preventable complications following open abdominal wall reconstruction. This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of venous thromboembolic events after open abdominal wall reconstruction. A single-institution prospectively maintained database was queried for open abdominal wall reconstruction (2010-2025). Standard statistical analyses and multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of venous thromboembolic events. Among 2,907 open abdominal wall reconstructions, 49 venous thromboembolic events (1.7%) occurred: 31 pulmonary embolisms ± deep vein thrombosis and 18 deep vein thromboses alone. Average body mass index was 34.6 ± 10.0 kg/m2, and 18.4% had prior venous thromboembolic events. Preoperative chemoprophylaxis was administered in 77.6% of venous thromboembolic event cases, and 93.8% of patients who received postoperative chemoprophylaxis had no interruption. Compared with patients without venous thromboembolic events, those with venous thromboembolic events had larger defect sizes (314.5 ± 222.7 vs 199.8 ± 187.5 cm2; P < .001) and longer operative times (233.4 ± 74.9 vs 187.2 ± 84.4 minutes; P < .001). Among 29 classified pulmonary embolisms, 13 were nonmassive, 12 submassive, and 4 massive/fatal. Advanced interventions were required in 12.2%, 16.3% required transfusion, and 16.3% underwent inferior vena cava filter placement. Among venous thromboembolic event patients, 40.8% required intensive care unit transfer, with 20.4% requiring reintubation. Average length of stay was longer in venous thromboembolic event patients (11.4 ± 9.8 vs 5.7 ± 8.8 days; P < .001). Multivariable regression identified body mass index (odds ratio, 1.09; 95% confidence interval, 1.04, 1.14; P < .001), prior venous thromboembolic events (odds ratio, 4.51; 95% confidence interval, 1.91, 10.62; P < .001), and operative time (odds ratio, 1.005; 95% confidence interval, 1.001, 1.010; P = .008) as independent predictors of venous thromboembolic event. Postoperative venous thromboembolic event following open abdominal wall reconstruction is uncommon but associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Higher body mass index, prior venous thromboembolic event, and longer operative time independently predicted venous thromboembolic event, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and prevention strategies.

42878772.title: Should the esophageal balloon catheter be deployed to personalize ventilation of ARDS? Authors' reply.

42873095.title: Irisin is associated with survival in sepsis and attenuates macrophage pro-inflammatory responses with involvement of AMPK signaling.
42873095.abstract: Sepsis is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, yet effective targeted therapies remain limited. We evaluated the prognostic significance of irisin, a myokine, in sepsis cohort and examined its immunomodulatory effects on macrophages using a translational approach. Patients were enrolled in a prospectively collected sepsis registry and biobank. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was conducted to assess independent association between irisin and 30-day mortality. Mechanistic studies used macrophages ex vivo and a murine cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model. Higher serum irisin was independently associated with lower 30-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.955, 95% confidence interval 0.913-0.999, p=0.044) in patients with sepsis (N=655). Irisin showed modest discrimination for 30-day mortality (AUROC 0.609), with no statistically significant difference from lactate (AUROC 0.652; p=0.145). In vitro , irisin suppressed LPS-induced pro-inflammatory cytokine production, preserved AMPK phosphorylation, attenuated IκBα degradation, and reduced pro-inflammatory markers in macrophages. Several of these cellular effects were attenuated following AMPKα1 depletion. In vivo , irisin improved 7-day survival after CLP (75% vs. 36%, p<0.05) and reduced systemic inflammatory cytokines at 24 hours. Higher serum irisin was independently associated with lower 30-day mortality in patients with sepsis, although its standalone discriminatory performance was modest. Experimental findings further showed that irisin improved survival and attenuated macrophage inflammatory responses, with AMPK signaling contributing to several cellular effects. These findings support further evaluation of irisin as part of integrated prognostic assessment and investigation of irisin-related signaling in sepsis.

42872940.title: Integrated Use of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation and Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System for Refractory Cardiotoxic Ingestion: A Single-Center Case Series.
42872940.abstract: Cardiotoxic ingestions of calcium-channel blockers and beta-adrenergic antagonists are highly lethal, often causing refractory vasoplegic shock and noncardiogenic pulmonary edema. While venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a recognized rescue therapy for cardiogenic shock, the roles of venovenous ECMO and albumin dialysis-specifically the molecular adsorbent recirculating system (MARS)-as well as the effectiveness of linking patients to therapy through a coordinated referral process remain underexplored. We describe five consecutive patients with severe cardiotoxic ingestions managed via a regionally triggered transfer pathway. Patients presented with profound hypotension and respiratory failure despite standard therapies. All five patients received MARS for drug clearance and vasoplegia management; two required venovenous ECMO for refractory hypoxemia. One patient died due to profound myocardial poisoning; four survived to discharge. Complications included continuous renal replacement therapy filter clotting and catheter-associated thrombosis. A coordinated regional protocol enabling early access to ECMO and MARS is feasible in massive cardiotoxic ingestions.

42870337.title: Computed Tomography-Derived Psoas Muscle Quantity, Attenuation, and 1 Year Mortality in Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
42870337.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42870337.abstract: Computed tomography (CT)-derived skeletal muscle characteristics may provide prognostic information in patients receiving venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV ECMO), but the relative contributions of muscle quantity and attenuation remain uncertain. We retrospectively studied adults who received VV ECMO for severe respiratory failure between 2014 and 2023 and underwent abdominal CT within 48 h before ECMO initiation. Psoas muscle index (PMI) and attenuation were measured using an artificial intelligence-based pipeline, and combined PMI-attenuation phenotypes were evaluated for 1 year mortality. Among 92 patients, 53 (57.6%) died within 1 year. In Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, and initial Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score and stratified by bridge-to-transplantation status, higher PMI (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] per standard deviation increase, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.41-0.82) and higher attenuation (aHR per 5 Hounsfield unit increase, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.77-0.97) were associated with lower 1 year mortality. When modeled simultaneously, PMI remained significant, whereas attenuation did not. The low PMI/low attenuation phenotype had the highest mortality risk (aHR, 5.30; 95% CI, 2.10-13.34). PMI showed a more robust association with 1 year mortality, while combined PMI-attenuation phenotyping may identify a particularly high-risk subgroup.

42866594.title: Comparison of the approaches to combine Renal Replacement Therapy with Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation - a Scoping Review.
42866594.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used for cardiac and respiratory failure and is associated with high rates of acute kidney injury (AKI) and fluid overload requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT). ECMO and RRT can be run independently in parallel, or RRT hemofilter or device can be integrated into the ECMO circuit. Several parallel and integrated ECMO-RRT configurations have been described, but the optimal approach remains uncertain.This scoping review mapped the available literature comparing at least two ECMO-RRT configurations, summarized reported outcomes, and identified knowledge gaps. We searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov without restrictions, with the final search conducted on February 9, 2026. Eligible studies compared at least 2 ECMO-RRT configurations linked to reported outcomes. Data on study characteristics, configurations, outcomes, and anticoagulation were extracted and synthesized. Of 6,806 records, 20 studies were included: 12 were clinical including 1 randomized controlled trial, 3 in vitro, 1 in silico, and 4 surveys. More than 8 ECMO-RRT connection schemes have been described by clinical studies since 2013. No consistent differences in efficiency or clinical outcomes were observed between the configurations compared. Integrated methods were associated with longer or comparable hemofilter lifespan. Surveys confirmed heterogeneous medical practices, and 2 safety concerns (unstoppable pressure alarms and air embolism) were reported. Evidence on ECMO-RRT configurations is limited and heterogeneous. Future systematic and rigorous comparison of all the configurations through preclinical and clinical studies is needed to harmonize medical practices and inform the development of guidelines.

42866167.title: Prediction of noninvasive ventilation failure: a narrative review.
42866167.abstract: With the increasing clinical application of noninvasive ventilation (NIV) and the accumulation of evidence-based medical data, NIV has become an important therapeutic intervention for various types of respiratory failure. However, a subset of patients still experience NIV failure. Compared with those with successful NIV, patients who develop NIV failure tend to have a poorer prognosis and an elevated risk of mortality. Therefore, the accurate identification and early prediction of NIV failure risk are crucial for guiding clinical decision-making and optimizing treatment strategies. This article reviews recent advances in research on the risk prediction of NIV failure, covering single-variable prediction approaches, simple variable combination-based prediction, weight-based multivariable prediction models, and emerging artificial intelligence algorithm-driven prediction models. Despite the progress made in NIV failure prediction, existing models still have limitations, such as insufficient generalizability, complex calculation of some multivariable scoring systems, and poor interpretability of artificial intelligence (AI) models. The core contribution of this review is to systematically sort out the advantages and limitations of various prediction methods, integrate prediction indicators and models suitable for different patient populations, and provide practical guidance for clinical practice and direction for future research.

42864741.title: Forty-Eight Hour Lactate Normalization Predicts Favorable Neurologic Recovery and Survival in Venoarterial ECMO for Cardiogenic Shock.
42864741.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42864741.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for cardiogenic shock (CS) is associated with high mortality and poor neurological outcomes. Dynamic assessment of metabolic recovery, reflected by lactate normalization, may offer additional prognostic value compared with static severity indices. We retrospectively analyzed 662 consecutive patients from the multicenter RESCUE II registry who remained on venoarterial ECMO for at least 48 hours. Patients were stratified by 48 hour lactate level: 48 hour lactate normalization group (< 2.0 mmol/L, n = 371) and persistent lactate elevation group (≥ 2.0 mmol/L, n = 291). The primary outcome was favorable neurologic discharge (FND), defined as discharge with a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2. The persistent lactate elevation group had a higher SOFA score (9.8 ± 3.2 vs. 8.5 ± 3.4, p < 0.001) and initial serum lactate (7.9 ± 4.8 mmol/L vs. 6.0 ± 4.3 mmol/L, p < 0.001). Lactate normalization was associated with a higher rate of FND (71.4% vs. 41.9%, p < 0.001), remained an independent predictor of FND (odds ratio [OR]: 3.12, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.21-4.41, p < 0.001), and was associated with lower risks of all-cause death (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.49, 95% CI: 0.38-0.64, p < 0.001) at 12 months. In conclusion, lactate normalization within 48 hours of ECMO initiation is associated with favorable neurologic status and 12 month survival.

42864673.title: Prophylactic high-flow nasal oxygen vs. conventional oxygen for prevention of postoperative respiratory complications: a randomized trial.
42864673.abstract: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are a major cause of morbidity after lung resection, particularly in older adults. Following extubation, noninvasive respiratory support strategies are increasingly used to prevent respiratory deterioration, but the role of prophylactic high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) in this setting remains uncertain. In this single-center, open-label randomized controlled trial, patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy or segmentectomy for stage I-IIIa non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomized to HFNC or conventional oxygen therapy (COT). The primary outcome was PPC severity during hospitalization, analyzed using ordinal logistic regression; the incidence of clinically relevant PPCs (grade ≥ 2) was also compared between groups. Secondary outcomes included longitudinal respiratory symptoms (mMRC, LCQ-MC, sCSS) and symptom-related functional interference (MDASI-LC), analyzed using mixed-effects models. A total of 210 patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis (HFNC, n = 104; COT, n = 106). HFNC reduced PPC severity (ordinal OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.28-0.91; P = 0.022) and moderate-to-severe PPCs (23.1% vs. 39.6%; absolute risk difference, -15.6%; 95% CI, -28.0% to -3.2%; P = 0.010). HFNC was associated with a lower burden of clinically relevant PPCs. Secondary analyses also suggested improvements in early postoperative respiratory symptoms and symptom-related functional interference. Secondary analyses also suggested improvements in early postoperative respiratory symptoms and symptom-related functional interference. No differences were observed in physiological outcomes or length of stay. In older adults undergoing lung resection, prophylactic HFNC reduced in-hospital PPC burden and was associated with more favorable early postoperative respiratory recovery. These findings suggest that prophylactic HFNC may provide benefit as a potential preventive respiratory support option in selected older or higher-risk postoperative patients, although routine prophylactic use in all patients undergoing lung resection is not supported by the present findings. This study was approved by the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2200063161) on 01 Sep 2022 and the first patient was enrolled after pre-registration.

42863592.title: Mechanical versus manual bag-valve ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation in adults with cardiac arrest: a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.
42863592.abstract: Optimal ventilation delivery during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) remains uncertain. Current resuscitation guidelines do not recommend mechanical ventilation (MV) over manual bag-valve ventilation (BV). We evaluated the association between MV use during CPR and clinical outcomes in adults with cardiac arrest compared with manual BV. We searched 6 bibliographic databases from inception through May 31, 2026. Included studies compared MV and BV ventilation CPR in adult cardiac arrest patients. Patients receiving MV at any moment during CPR were classified as the MV group; those receiving only BV comprised the BV group. Primary outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital admission, survival to hospital discharge, and good neurological outcome. Secondary outcomes included physiologic variables and pneumothorax. We calculated pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) using Bayesian random-effects meta-analyses. Eight studies involving 6847 patients were included. For the primary outcome, MV use during CPR was associated with a higher rate of ROSC than BV use (pooled RR, 1.20; 95% CrI, 1.04-1.42), with a 99% posterior probability of benefit. Posterior probabilities favoring MV for survival to admission, survival to discharge, and good neurological outcome were 92.3%, 93.6%, and 92.2%, respectively. Pneumothorax incidence was similar between groups. In adult cardiac arrest, MV use during CPR was associated with higher ROSC compared with manual BV. Evidence for improved survival and neurological outcomes remains imprecise and inconclusive.

42862322.title: The pulmonary circulation in ARDS: from pathophysiology to clinical applications.

42855036.title: Early post-ROSC laboratory phenotypes and clinical outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a 10-year national cohort study.
42855036.abstract: Prior phenotyping in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) relied predominantly on prehospital indicators, which neither describe nor grade the underlying ischemia-reperfusion injury. We aimed to derive laboratory-based phenotypes and describe their clinical characteristics and outcome associations. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult resuscitated OHCA patients of presumed cardiac etiology between 01/02/2011 and 01/01/2022, linking Singapore's national OHCA and cardiovascular databases. Unsupervised latent class analysis (LCA) was applied to 14 laboratory variables within six hours post-return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Stability was confirmed through split-sample validation. Logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards model, adjusted for age, sex and initial cardiac rhythm, assessed poor neurological recovery at hospital discharge, 30-day and 3-year mortality. Among 1514 eligible patients (median age 65.0 years, 73.6% males), LCA identified three distinct phenotypes: multi-organ dysfunction (MOD, N = 286), homeostatic (HOM, N = 967), and immune-dysregulated (IMD, N = 261), independently reproduced in derivation (entropy = 0.817) and replication (entropy = 0.892) subsamples. The most discriminative variables were creatinine, eosinophil and lymphocyte. Compared to MOD, both HOM (aOR: 0.50, 95% CI 0.30-0.78, p = 0.004) and IMD (aOR: 0.46, 95% CI 0.26-0.78, p = 0.005) phenotypes had significantly lower odds of poor neurological recovery. This pattern was consistent for 30-day mortality (HOM aHR: 0.71, 95% CI 0.61-0.83; IMD aHR: 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.94) and 3-year mortality (HOM aHR: 0.70, 95% CI 0.60-0.82; IMD aHR: 0.74, 95% CI 0.62-0.90), all p ≤ 0.01. Early post-ROSC laboratory data identified three prognostically distinct phenotypes among resuscitated OHCA patients. These exploratory findings support external validation and investigation of phenotype-guided therapies.

42853446.title: Impact of side hole design of drainage cannulas on flow velocity and predilection sites for low-flow areas in veno-venous ECMO circuits.
42853446.abstract: Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VV-ECMO) (VV-ECMO) and Veno-Artial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VA-ECMO) have become evidence-based therapy options for patients with most severe heart and/or lung failure. Cannulas continue to play a central role as the direct interface between patients and extracorporeal circulation. However, severe side-effects, such as coagulation and haemolysis, may result not only from a blood pump but also from inappropriate cannula design. Based on the multi-stage lighthouse design of a draining ECMO cannula, the area of the side holes was varied in both shape and size in the distal and proximal directions. Using a Computer-Aided Design (CAD)- Model of cannulas (19,21,23 French (Fr)) appropriate simulation models were created in the non-reactive plenum. The resultant numerical 3D simulations are based on physiological boundary conditions and on the flows covering different ECMO-flow rates. The current cannula design reveals no-flow zones, which induce thrombus formation, especially when using blood-flow rates below 2 L/min. New geometric cannula design variants revealed an improvement in pressure loss, but at the expense of pronounced no-flow zones in the distal region. During drainage, the largest proportion of the total volume flow drains through the proximal row of side holes. Here, the pressure and thus the flow for both, immediately drops to the level of the surrounding plenum. This means that risk areas for haemostasis develop more distally. The direct influence of the design is evident in the proximally exponentially reduced side holes. They significantly reduce the extent of the no-flow zones. Simulations of the reference cannula showed that suction to the vessel wall and thus closure of some side holes contributes to an overall improvement in flow within the cannula. When reducing the blood-flow rate in ECMO therapy, stagnation areas may develop within the drainage cannula. The geometry of the side holes has an important impact. A comparison of the different designs shows that distal growth of the side hole area results in improved flow behaviour.

42848707.title: Automated Versus Manual Occlusion Pressure at 100 ms With Hamilton C6 Using the Software Version 1.2.3: From Bedside to the Bench and Back to Bedside.
42848707.abstract: Occlusion pressure at 100 ms after the start of inspiratory effort (P0.1) is a marker of respiratory drive and a predictor of weaning outcomes in mechanically ventilated patients. Some ventilators, like the Hamilton C6 (Hamilton Medical AG, Bonaduz, Switzerland), estimate P0.1 automatically (P0.1vent) without performing an actual airway occlusion, potentially leading to inaccuracies. This prospective clinical and bench study aimed to assess the accuracy of P0.1vent compared with the manual occlusion method (P0.1occ) during spontaneous breathing trials (SBT) and following a reventilation period with varying ventilator settings. The clinical part of the study included patients undergoing SBT on Hamilton C6 (software version 1.2.3) with zero pressure support (PS) and zero end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) and reventilation (PS +8 cm H2O, PEEP +5 cm H2O). P0.1vent and P0.1occ were collected every 15 minutes.
