Bench part evaluated the P0.1vent and P0.1occ of the Hamilton C6 (software version 1.2.3) connected to a lung simulator (ASL 5000) creating different breathing efforts across different lung mechanics and varying PS and PEEP levels. In patients, P0.1vent values were significantly higher than P0.1occ (median, 11.0 vs. 1.0 cm H2O; p < 0.001), with a mean bias of 8.5 cm H2O. Similar overestimations were observed during the reventilation period (6.0 vs. 1.0 cm H2O; mean difference, 6.5 cm H2O; p < 0.001). Bench results confirmed the variable accuracy of P0.1vent found in the clinical part of the study, with biases ranging from nearly perfect (0.2 cm H2O) under high PS to 2.3 cm H2O under low PS. Automatic P0.1 estimation by the Hamilton C6 (software version 1.2.3) is inaccurate during SBTs. Manual occlusion remains essential for reliable P0.1 assessment at the bedside.

42847657.title: 2026 Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report: Executive Summary and Key Changes.
42847657.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
42847657.abstract: The Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report provides a comprehensive, annually updated evidence-based approach to asthma diagnosis, assessment, treatment, and prevention across the lifespan. Its central approach is personalized, iterative care based on the Assess-Adjust-Review cycle for both symptom control and reduction of future risk (including severe exacerbations, persistent airflow limitation, and treatment-related harm). GINA emphasizes objective confirmation of diagnosis wherever possible, and regular assessment of lung function, inhaler technique, adherence, multimorbidity, risk factors (including Type-2 biomarkers), and patient goals and preferences. GINA strongly recommends that all adults, adolescents, children and most preschoolers with asthma should receive inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing treatment. GINA recommends against short-acting beta2-agonist (SABA)-only treatment. For adults/adolescents, GINA Track 1 using low-dose ICS-formoterol, an anti-inflammatory reliever (AIR), either as-needed-only (AIR-only) or as maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART), is preferred because of its substantial reduction in severe exacerbations compared with SABA-based regimens, and its simplicity. Age-specific treatment pathways in children also emphasize ICS-containing therapy and exacerbation prevention. For difficult-to-treat and severe asthma, GINA provides structured guidance, emphasizing diagnostic verification, optimization of modifiable factors, inflammatory phenotyping, biologic therapy selection, and (as for all patients) systemic corticosteroid stewardship. Acute exacerbation care incorporates long-term preventive treatment, including post-discharge reassessment of management and action plan. Key 2026 updates include expanded AIR options for adults and children, revised guidance on severe asthma and selection of biologic treatment, and substantial updates to acute asthma management. GINA integrates evidence-based management with shared decision-making, self-management education, implementation, and global advocacy to reduce preventable asthma morbidity and mortality.

42838495.title: Prehospital prognostication after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in tertiary care centers: the R-EDByUS score in the JAAM-OHCA registry.
42838495.abstract: The R-EDByUS score predicts unfavorable neurological outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) using prehospital variables alone, with separate models based on return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) status at hospital arrival. However, whether the score remains valid in patients transported to tertiary care centers is uncertain. We therefore aimed to validate it externally in this setting. Using the JAAM-OHCA Registry, we analyzed adult patients with presumed cardiogenic OHCA transported to tertiary care centers. The regression-based R-EDByUS score was applied to predict unfavorable neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category 3-5) at 1 month in the prehospital ROSC and ongoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) cohorts. Discrimination and calibration were assessed, and score performance was examined across in-hospital intervention subgroups (percutaneous coronary intervention, targeted temperature management, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation). We also assessed the proportion of patients with unfavorable outcomes among those with a predicted probability ≥99%. Of 29,345 patients, 3305 were classified into the prehospital ROSC cohort and 26,040 into the ongoing CPR cohort. The score showed good discrimination, with areas under the curve of 0.906 and 0.913, and good calibration in the prehospital ROSC cohort. Discrimination was lower among patients who received PCI, TTM, or ECMO in the ongoing CPR cohort. Among patients with a predicted probability ≥99%, 100% (112/112; prehospital ROSC) and 99.9% (20,560/20,588; ongoing CPR) had unfavorable outcomes. The R-EDByUS score showed good discrimination in the JAAM-OHCA Registry, supporting its use for early risk stratification in cardiogenic OHCA even in tertiary care centers.

42831018.title: Pre-admission prescription of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and mortality in critical illness: a national cohort study from 2020 to 2023.
42831018.abstract: We aimed to determine whether selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) prescription within 30 days before intensive care unit (ICU) admission was associated with 30-day and 90-day mortality in critically ill adults, and to evaluate effect modification by underlying psychiatric disorders. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study of adults with a first ICU admission in South Korea from 2020 through 2023. Pre-admission SSRI prescription was defined using prescription supply records during the 30 days before ICU admission. Propensity score matching and Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate 30-day and 90-day mortality. Pre-admission SSRI prescription was associated with lower 30-day and 90-day mortality after propensity score matching. Similar associations were observed in the full cohort and when prescription coverage included the day immediately before ICU admission. The associations appeared stronger among patients with documented psychiatric disorders. Pre-admission SSRI prescription was associated with lower short- and intermediate-term mortality in critically ill adults. These observational findings do not establish a causal protective effect and should be interpreted in light of potential residual confounding. None.

42823723.title: Subphenotype-specific serum proteomic signatures in patients with ARDS.
42823723.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality. Previous studies have identified reproducible hyperinflammatory and hypoinflammatory ARDS subphenotypes with distinct clinical outcomes and treatment responses. Although recent transcriptomic studies have provided insights into biological differences between these subphenotypes, the role of the circulating proteome remains incompletely understood. In this prospective study, patients with ARDS were classified into hyperinflammatory or hypoinflammatory subphenotypes using a previously validated 3-variable classifier based on bicarbonate, interleukin-6, and soluble tumor necrosis factor receptor 1. Serum proteomic profiling was performed to identify differentially abundant proteins between subphenotypes. Biological pathways were examined using gene set enrichment analysis. To provide cellular expression context for the subphenotype-associated serum proteins, serum proteomic data were mapped onto publicly available single-cell RNA-seq datasets from peripheral blood mononuclear cells, neutrophils, and tracheal aspirates. Among 31 patients with ARDS, 13 (42%) were classified as having the hyperinflammatory subphenotype and 18 (58%) as having the hypoinflammatory subphenotype. Both 28-day and in-hospital mortality were higher in the hyperinflammatory subphenotype than in the hypoinflammatory subphenotype (46% vs. 11%, P=0.04; 62% vs. 11%, P=0.01, respectively). In total, 54 serum proteins were differentially abundant between subphenotypes. These proteins represented biologically relevant categories, including endothelial injury, immunoregulation, coagulation/fibrinolysis, complement regulation, tissue remodeling, and metabolism-related proteins. Gene set enrichment analysis identified pathways differentially enriched between subphenotypes, including cell adhesion, cell-cell signaling, and cytokine responses (all FDR < 0.10). In external single-cell RNA-seq reference datasets, genes encoding the subphenotype-associated proteins were expressed predominantly in CD14 and CD16 monocytes in PBMCs, showed distinct expression patterns across immature and CD163+IL1R2^hi^ circulating neutrophil states, and were expressed mainly in macrophage and monocyte populations, with additional epithelial expression, in tracheal aspirates. Serum proteomic profiling identified distinct protein patterns associated with established ARDS inflammatory subphenotypes, providing insights into the biological heterogeneity of ARDS.

42956360.title: Dynamic Early Postreperfusion Physiology Is Associated With Organ Recovery After Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.
42956360.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42956360.abstract: Prognostication after extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) predominantly relies on characteristics available before or at initiation of extracorporeal support. We investigated whether the early metabolic response to extracorporeal reperfusion provides complementary information on subsequent recovery. We retrospectively analyzed 91 patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated with ECPR. Lactate was assessed before and 12 h after extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) initiation. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, successful ECMO weaning, cerebral edema/hypoxic brain injury, and favorable neurological survival. Associations were adjusted for low-flow duration. Twelve hour lactate was lower in survivors than nonsurvivors (5.45 vs. 9.04 mmol/L; p = 0.002), whereas prereperfusion lactate did not differ. In paired measurements (n = 38), mortality discrimination increased from an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.47 before reperfusion to 0.80 at 12 h. Each 5 mmol/L higher 12 h lactate was associated with mortality (odds ratio [OR] = 2.73), lower odds of ECMO weaning (OR = 0.44), and cerebral edema/hypoxic injury (OR = 2.07) after low-flow adjustment. Early metabolic response after extracorporeal reperfusion was associated with survival and both circulatory and cerebral recovery. Dynamic post-reperfusion physiology may provide complementary information beyond static pre-reperfusion assessment.

42955503.title: Adjunctive therapeutic plasma exchange as rescue therapy in septic shock due to streptococcal infection: a multicentric retrospective cohort study.
42955503.abstract: Septic shock due to streptococcal infection (SRSS) carries a high mortality and is in part driven by toxin-mediated inflammation. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) may modulate the septic host responses by removing injurious mediators while replenishing protective plasma factors, but data specific to SRSS is lacking. We performed a retrospective, multicenter, cohort study of adults with SRSS between 2012-2024. Patients from three tertiary care ECMO centers in Germany and Switzerland were included requiring (i) streptococcal spp. detected in blood or primary focus and (ii) septic shock according to sepsis-3 definition. Adjunctive TPE with fresh frozen plasma at the intensivists` discretion was compared with standard of care (SOC). The primary outcome was 90-day-hospital mortality. Key exploratory outcomes included 24-h kinetics of vasoactive-inotropic score(VIS) and lactate, as well as SRSS-related complications. Results were validated in a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort. Of 149 patients, 31 (20.8%) received TPE and 118 (79.2%) SOC. TPE patients were more severely ill at baseline: SOFA 14 (IQR 13.5-15) vs 11 (IQR 8-14) (p<0.001); lactate 6.4 vs 2.8 mmol/L (p<0.001); Vasoactive-Inotropic-Score (VIS) 70.7 vs 23.3 (p<0.001); more frequent invasive ventilation (87% vs 65%), VV-ECMO (36% vs 19%), and renal replacement therapy (96.8% vs 52.5%). Overall, 90-day hospital mortality was 27.5% (TPE 29.0%, SOC 27.1%). Following SOFA-score adjustment, TPE was associated with lower mortality risk (aHR 0.67 [95% CI 0.5-0.9]; p=0.009). This was validated in the PSM cohort, with an aHR for TPE of 0.44 (95% CI 0.3-0.8); p=0.002. Mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant VIS reduction only with TPE (fixed effect 24-h change, p=0.027) and improved lactate decrease versus SOC. In SRSS, adjunctive TPE was associated with rapid hemodynamic stabilization and improved lactate kinetics. Exploratory adjusted survival analyses support prospective evaluation of TPE in SRSS.

42934457.title: Understanding Neurogenic Patient-Ventilator Discordance and its Management.
42934457.abstract: Patients with an acutely injured brain may resist the mechanical physics of the ventilator. Neurogenic respiratory breathing patterns generated by the patient may result in the ventilator failing to synchronize with this abnormal drive. This asynchrony may be perceived as distress and with a high respiratory drive could also lead to global lung stress and diaphragmatic myoinjury, and affect liberation from the mechanical ventilator at a later point. Patient-ventilator synchrony concerns have rarely been prioritized in neurocritical care guidelines and are often inappropriately treated with escalating sedation. Starting with the essentials of waveform interpretation and moving towards more complex interpretations of these asynchronies, this review provides insight into the common themes of neurogenic synchrony concerns in mechanically ventilated patients. High respiratory drive, double-triggering/ breath-stacking, and reverse triggering are the most prevalent observations. Adjusting the ventilator can improve patient-ventilator interaction and a number of options to remediate these synchrony concerns are provided.

42933455.title: Efzofitimod versus placebo in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
42933455.abstract: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis. In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using stratified block randomisation to receive monthly intravenous infusions of efzofitimod 3 mg/kg, efzofitimod 5 mg/kg, or placebo over a 48-week treatment period, including a 12-week oral corticosteroid taper targeting 0 mg per day (starting on day 15). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete. Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment. Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. The results from steroid tapering indicate that oral corticosteroid doses can be more aggressively reduced in many patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis. aTyr and Kyorin.

42919460.title: Association of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Radiographic Findings Identified by Machine Learning and Outcomes of Patients Receiving Invasive Mechanical Ventilation.
42919460.abstract: To determine whether predictions from a deep learning model that identifies acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) findings on chest radiographs (CXRs) can also predict clinical outcomes beyond traditional indicators of hypoxemia and illness severity. Retrospective cohort study. Single academic medical center. None. Adult patients with CXRs performed at the time of invasive mechanical ventilation initiation. We applied a deep learning model that was previously trained to identify bilateral airspace opacities consistent with ARDS to CXRs of 6591 patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. The resulting ARDS-CXR scores were evaluated for their ability to discriminate risk of 28-day mortality and their association with 28-day mortality and time to extubation after adjusting for a patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV. The median ARDS-CXR score was -2.09, corresponding to an ARDS probability of 15%, and 1089 (17%) patients had a positive score, corresponding to an ARDS probability above 50%. Twenty-eight-day mortality was 35.1% among patients with a positive score and 13.5% among patients with a negative score. ARDS-CXR scores below the ARDS threshold also stratified risk, with mortality increasing from 12.8% at a score of -2 to 19.9% at -1 and 27.5% at 0. The ARDS-CXR score area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve was 0.68 (95% CI, 0.66-0.70) for predicting 28-day mortality, whereas the Pao2/Fio2 AUROC was 0.64 (95% CI, 0.62-0.66). After adjusting for either the patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV, a 1-point increase in the ARDS-CXR score was significantly associated with higher 28-day mortality or prolonged time to extubation. A deep learning-derived ARDS-CXR score quantifying radiographic findings of ARDS independently predicted mortality and ventilator outcomes beyond hypoxemia and illness severity. Algorithmically derived markers of lung injury severity from chest imaging could be used to support clinical care decisions, predictive enrichment in research studies, or incorporated into a future ARDS definition.

42912181.title: Predictors of Survival in Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Supported Immunocompromised Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Patients.
42912181.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42912181.abstract: Immunocompromised patients frequently develop acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO), yet evidence on prognostic factors in this population remains limited. This single-center retrospective study evaluated 90 day outcomes and identified predictors of mortality in immunocompromised ARDS patients supported with VV-ECMO. Between September 2009 and December 2021, 112 ARDS patients (49 immunocompromised and 63 immunocompetent) who received VV-ECMO were included. Baseline characteristics and outcomes were compared between groups; multivariate Cox regression analyzed 90 day mortality predictors, with subgroup analyses by immune status. Ninety day mortality was comparable between nonimmunosuppressed and immunosuppressed patients. Pre-ECMO platelet count <75 × 109/L was the sole independent predictor of 90 day mortality, and this association was observed exclusively in immunocompromised patients. Immunocompromised patients with a platelet count ≥75 × 109/L achieved survival comparable to immunocompetent patients, whereas those with a platelet count <75 × 109/L had fewer ventilator-free and ECMO-free days. Immunocompromised status per se was not independently associated with 90 day mortality in VV-ECMO-supported ARDS patients. Pre-ECMO platelet count emerged as a critical risk stratification tool: immunocompromised patients with a platelet count ≥75 × 109/L demonstrated favorable outcomes, whereas those with lower counts were at substantially increased risk.

42903821.title: Innate immune response in COVID-19 pneumonia during the pandemic: a prospective cohort study.
42903821.abstract: Dysregulated innate immunity contributes to COVID-19 severity, but its evolution over the periods of the pandemic is undefined. The aim of the study was to compare ex vivo innate immune responses in COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and assess associations with pandemic period, severe respiratory failure (SRF), mortality, and circulating microRNA patterns. In this prospective cohort study conducted at 2 tertiary hospitals in Athens, Greece, 102 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 pneumonia and 28 with non-COVID-19 community-acquired pneumonia were enrolled. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were isolated during the first 24 hours before any immune intervention other than dexamethasone and stimulated for cytokine production. SRF was defined as a PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio <150 mmHg necessitating invasive or non-invasive ventilation. Exploratory serum microRNA sequencing was performed in a small subset. On Day 1, release of TNFα and IL-6 was higher by the PBMCs of patients with COVID-19 pneumonia than non-COVID-19 CAP; the opposite was found for IL-1RA. Patients infected by the Omicron variant had higher production of TNFα and lower of IL-6. Using multivariate logistic regression analysis, it was confirmed that over-time decrease of the production of IL-6 by the PBMCs of patients with COVID-19 was a risk factor for progression into SRF and 28-day mortality. COVID-19 pneumonia and non-COVID-19 CAP exhibited distinct patterns of ex vivo PBMC responsiveness, characterized by higher TNF-α and IL-6 production in COVID-19. Functional cytokine responses also varied across pandemic periods.

42900697.title: Assessment of Tidal Volume in Patients Undergoing Noninvasive Ventilation: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42900697.abstract: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is widely used in acute respiratory failure (ARF), yet the association between high tidal volume (Vt) and clinical outcomes remains incompletely defined. We evaluated the association between Vt and NIV failure overall and by ARF type, and its relationship with respiratory and clinical outcomes. MEDLINE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and Latin American and Caribbean Health Science Literature (1976 to September 2025). Observational studies of adults with ARF treated with NIV reporting Vt or Vt normalized to predicted body weight (Vt/PBW) in NIV success and failure groups. Three pairs of reviewers identified studies and extracted data independently. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Risk of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Eleven studies (1136 patients) were included. Vt/PBW was higher in NIV failure vs. success (mean difference [MD], 1.02 mL/kg [95% CI, 0.60-1.45 mL/kg]), whereas absolute Vt did not differ (MD, 1.30 [-33.31 to 35.91]). In hypoxemic ARF, Vt/PBW remained higher in NIV failure (MD, 0.89 mL/kg [95% CI, 0.04-1.73 mL/kg]); no data were available for hypercapnic ARF. Post hoc analyses showed that higher Vt/PBW was associated with increased mortality (odds ratio, 9.11; 95% CI, 3.88-21.37), higher respiratory rate (RR; MD, 3.14 breaths/min [95% CI, 1.36-4.92 breaths/min]), and lower Paco2 (MD, -2.38 mm Hg [95% CI, -4.16 to -0.5938 mm Hg]), but no with pressure support (PS) level (MD, 0.24 [95% CI, -0.81 to 1.29]). Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. In adults with ARF treated with NIV, higher Vt/PBW was associated with NIV failure and worse outcomes. These findings reflect prognostic associations rather than causality, and interventional studies with systematic Vt monitoring are needed. Importantly, elevated Vt/PBW, higher RR, lower Paco2, and increased mortality, without differences in PS, collectively implicate elevated respiratory drive as a driver of increased mortality (PROSPERO [CRD42024584977]).Findings: Higher Vt/PBW was associated with NIV failure, particularly in hypoxemic respiratory failure; post hoc analyses showed associations with increased mortality, higher respiratory rate, and lower Paco2.

42899407.title: Eligibility for Early Mobilization in Mechanically Ventilated Adults: A Multicenter Study.
42899407.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42899407.abstract: Early mobilization of mechanically ventilated patients within 72 hours of intubation is underutilized despite its known clinical benefits. The most cited barrier to implementation is physiologic instability. To quantify eligibility for early mobilization across established physiologic criteria in a multicenter cohort of mechanically ventilated adults and estimate the relative impact of structural and process implementation barriers. Retrospective cohort of adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation for ≥4 hours across nine CLIF Consortium health systems (2018-2024) and MIMIC-IV (2008-2022). Four physiologic eligibility criteria, from clinical trials (Chicago, TEAM) and consensus guidelines (Green, Yellow), were applied between 8am and 5pm within 72 hours of intubation. Random-effects meta-analysis compared eligibility across criteria and quantified the relative effect of two implementation barriers: weekday-only availability (structural) and 4-hour continuous eligibility (process). Among 223,281 hospitalizations, 86.9-95.6% met eligibility for mobilization within 72 hours of intubation across all 4 criteria. Compared with Chicago trials criteria, eligibility was reduced under TEAM (SHR 0.782, 95% CI 0.746-0.820) and Green (SHR 0.631, 0.611-0.651) but not Yellow (SHR 0.990, 0.976-1.005). Restricting eligibility to weekdays (structural) or requiring continuous eligibility (process) each reduced eligibility by 26-39% across all four criteria (SHR range 0.61-0.74); imposing both barriers together reduced eligibility by 45-56% (SHR range 0.44-0.55). Most mechanically ventilated adults met physiologic eligibility criteria for early mobilization within 72 hours of intubation. Structural and process barriers, such as staff availability on weekends and sustained eligibility for care coordination, reduced opportunity more potently than physiologic instability alone.

42898077.title: Permissive versus conventional weaning from venovenous ECMO in patients with ARDS: a retrospective cohort study.
42898077.abstract: Criteria for weaning from venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-V ECMO) in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remain poorly standardized. Some patients are decannulated despite persistent abnormalities in respiratory mechanics once oxygenation and carbon dioxide clearance are considered adequate. We aimed to compare outcomes associated with permissive versus conventional V-V ECMO weaning. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study including adult patients with refractory ARDS treated with V-V ECMO between January 2015 and December 2022 who were successfully decannulated while receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. Permissive weaning was defined as ECMO decannulation despite persistence of at least one of the following criteria during the sweep gas-off trial: plateau pressure ≥30 cmH₂O, driving pressure ≥20 cmH₂O, positive end-expiratory pressure ≥15 cmH₂O, or tidal volume ≤5 mL/kg predicted body weight. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality after ECMO decannulation. Secondary outcomes included liberation from mechanical ventilation within 90 days, analyzed using competing-risk models with death as a competing event. Associations with mortality were assessed using landmark Cox proportional hazards models anchored at decannulation. Among 469 patients treated with V-V ECMO, 280 successfully decannulated patients were included; 117 (42%) underwent permissive weaning and 163 (58%) conventional weaning. Baseline characteristics were broadly similar, although body mass index was higher and SARS-CoV-2 ARDS more frequent in the permissive group. Patients undergoing permissive weaning had longer ECMO support (19 [9-37] vs. 12 [6-27] days; p < 0.01). At the sweep gas-off trial, respiratory mechanics remained more impaired in the permissive group, whereas oxygenation parameters were comparable. In landmark analysis, permissive weaning was associated with higher 90-day mortality in both univariable (hazard ratio [HR] 3.53, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.62-7.66; p < 0.01) and multivariable analyses (adjusted HR 4.45, 95% CI 1.98-9.97; p < 0.01). However, permissive weaning was not associated with delayed liberation from mechanical ventilation by day 90 (adjusted subdistribution HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.70-1.17; p = 0.4). Among patients with severe ARDS successfully decannulated from V-V ECMO, permissive weaning was associated with increased 90-day mortality but not with delayed liberation from mechanical ventilation.

42893020.title: Agreement between chest radiograph and computed tomography for the diagnosis of acute respiratory distress syndrome: A retrospective observational study.
42893020.abstract: The presence of bilateral lung infiltrates on chest imaging is a mandatory clinical criterion for the diagnosis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Although lung infiltrates are usually identified on chest radiograph in clinical practice, chest computed tomography (CT) outperforms chest radiograph for the diagnosis of lung infiltrates. We hypothesized that the performance of chest radiograph for the diagnosis of ARDS, as compared to chest CT as reference, is limited. We conducted a retrospective, single-center, observational study over a 7-year period, including patients who met all but the imaging criterion for ARDS (defined by the Berlin criteria) and who underwent a chest CT and a chest radiograph the same day. Chest CT was interpreted by two radiologists and considered as the gold standard diagnosis of ARDS whereas chest radiographs were interpreted by two intensivists. The primary outcome was the agreement between chest radiograph and chest CT for the diagnosis of ARDS in the overall population. Secondary outcomes included the performance of chest radiograph for the diagnosis of ARDS in the overall population and in predefined subgroups, especially based on patient characteristics, imaging features, timing between chest radiograph and CT, and inter-rater agreement. Agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa, and diagnostic performance using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and accuracy for the primary outcome and subgroup analyses. Out of the 277 patients included during the study period, prevalence of ARDS on chest CT among hypoxemic intubated patients fulfilling all but the imaging criteria for ARDS was 81%. Overall, the agreement was fair to moderate and consistent across subgroups. Sensitivity of chest radiograph for the diagnosis of ARDS ranged from 74% to 80%, higher in patients with four quadrants involved on chest radiograph (100%), and lower in patients with focal ARDS on chest CT (54-67%). Chest radiograph has limited performance for the diagnosis of ARDS, and at least 20% of patients with ARDS on chest CT were not diagnosed using chest radiograph. Systematic chest CT in hypoxemic intubated patients may reduce the under-recognition of ARDS and contribute to effective implementation of protective ventilation strategies.

42963517.title: Quantified Brain Atrophy and Risk of Severe Mass Effect in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
42963517.abstract: Large middle cerebral artery (MCA) infarctions can result in life-threatening cerebral edema. Quantitative brain atrophy may improve risk stratification for severe edema. We examined whether quantitative brain atrophy is associated with severe midline shift after large ischemic stroke and whether incorporating atrophy improves prediction beyond established clinical and radiographic predictors. This was a retrospective observational cohort study of patients with greater than or equal to half MCA ischemic infarction, presentation within 24 h of last known well time, and at least one follow-up head computed tomography (CT), admitted to two academic hospitals with comprehensive stroke centers between 2006 and 2024. The study was approved by the institutional review boards of both centers. Brain atrophy was quantified as the inverse of standardized brain volume on admission head CT. The primary outcome was severe radiographic mass effect, defined as midline shift ≥ 5 mm on follow-up CT. The secondary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable regression models assessed associations between quantified atrophy and outcomes. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing models with and without atrophy using measures of goodness of fit, calibration, and discrimination. Among 565 patients (mean age 67.5 ± 15.7 years; 49.9% female), 223 (39.5%) developed severe mass effect. Greater atrophy was associated with lower odds of midline shift ≥ 5 mm [odds ratio (OR) 0.44, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.34-0.58], but not with in-hospital mortality. Incorporation of atrophy improved prediction of severe mass effect compared with the baseline model [likelihood ratio test χ2 (1) = 41, p < 0.001; Akaike information criterion (AIC) 703 vs. 741; Bayesian information criterion (BIC) 733 vs. 767; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.68 vs. 0.60]. Quantified brain atrophy is independently associated with a reduced risk of severe mass effect after large MCA stroke and improved the performance of established predictive models. Incorporation of this imaging biomarker may enhance early risk stratification, monitoring, and intervention planning for patients at risk of life-threatening cerebral edema.

42960861.title: Beyond safe storage: closing product-safety gaps in childhood ingestion injuries in Japan.
42960861.abstract: Unintentional ingestion of medicines and button batteries by young children is developmentally predictable. Japan has relied mainly on caregiver warnings, and it is unclear how far prevention has been built into products. Japan has no general legal requirement for child-resistant medicine packaging. Such packaging could add protection when safe storage fails. Serious ingestions continue, while mandatory toy standards leave gaps in protection across household products. National hospital-based surveillance of household product ingestions was narrowed in 2019, limiting assessment of national burden and policy effects. Australia and the United States have introduced button battery safety requirements that extend beyond toys. Japan could require child-resistant packaging for medicines that are toxic in small doses, require secure battery compartments across household products, extend packaging and warning standards to online sales, and rebuild surveillance. Poison centres could help guide surveillance and prioritise medicines for packaging requirements.

42951282.title: Impact of a large measles outbreak associated with transmission in the Americas and Canada's loss of measles elimination status: descriptive cohort study.
42951282.abstract: To describe the epidemiological characteristics, public health response, and evidence of international spread of a large measles outbreak that contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status. Descriptive analysis of the cohort of measles outbreak cases reported to Ontario's public health surveillance system during the outbreak period: epidemiological week of 28 October 2024 to 6 October 2025. Ontario, Canada. Individuals meeting the outbreak case definition for confirmed or probable measles infection during the outbreak period. Exposure to measles virus associated with the Ontario outbreak and related transmission chains. Demographic characteristics, vaccination status, admission to hospital, complications, pregnancy associated outcomes, mortality, and evidence of international spread based on measles virus genotyping and sequencing. Cases were identified using an outbreak-specific case definition incorporating epidemiological, clinical, laboratory, and viral sequencing criteria. Phylogenetic analysis of measles virus sequences was used to assess evidence of onwards spread to other countries. The outbreak consisted of 2377 cases (2064 confirmed and 313 probable) over 49 weeks and contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status. Most cases (2146/2377, 90.3%) occurred among members of historically under-vaccinated communities, with limited spillover into the broader population. Among the 2377 cases, approximately three quarters of cases (n=1736, 73.0%) occurred in individuals aged 19 years or younger, 2121 (89.2%) were unvaccinated, and 97 (4.1%) had unknown vaccination status. The outbreak was associated with 166 (7%) admissions to hospital, 13 (<1%) admissions to intensive care unit, 51 (2.1%) infections during pregnancy, 10 (<1%) congenital measles infections, one (<1%) case of encephalitis, and one (<1%) infant death. Sequencing identified a novel N450 distinct sequence identifier that was subsequently detected in countries including the United States of America, Mexico, and the Netherlands. The outbreak strain was designated a World Health Organization named strain (MVs/Ontario.CAN/47.24). These findings highlight the risk of measles re-establishment in countries that have attained elimination and underscore the importance of culturally appropriate community engagement to build trust in immunisation and prevent future outbreaks. This outbreak shows the fragility of measles elimination in the presence of long standing immunity gaps within interconnected communities across the Americas and the population-level protection that limited broader community transmission.

42820877.title: The Lazarus Protocol: Rescue Catheter Ablation of Incessant Ventricular Fibrillation by Purkinje Substrate Denetworking in Critically Ill Patients With Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
42820877.abstract: We report a case series of 3 critically ill patients with refractory incessant ventricular fibrillation (VF) who underwent catheter ablation using high-density mapping of the Purkinje system during ongoing VF, combined with targeted Purkinje denetworking and myocardial substrate modification. All patients were supported with advanced mechanical circulatory support, including venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation or venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation with Impella support, and procedures were guided by electroanatomic mapping with multimodality imaging integration. Purkinje potentials and abnormal electrograms within infarcted and border-zone myocardium were targeted, resulting in restoration and maintenance of sinus rhythm with no inducible ventricular arrhythmias after ablation. These findings suggest that, in carefully selected patients, combined Purkinje-targeted ablation and substrate modification may provide a life-saving rescue strategy for otherwise refractory incessant VF.

42819597.title: Teaching and training of anaesthesia and critical care technicians in India - Towards a competency-based modular framework.
42819597.abstract: There is currently a lack of published guidance on competency-based curriculum design specifically tailored to Anaesthesia and Critical Care Technicians (ACTs) training in India, creating a need for a structured and standardised educational framework. This review was undertaken to address the need for a competency-based educational framework for ACTs in India, aligning existing training programmes with contemporary national educational reforms and international standards while enhancing clinical competence, patient safety, and workforce readiness. In this article, we propose integrating key components, such as competency domains, entrustable professional activities, workplace-based assessments, and simulation-based training, into the existing educational framework without altering the mandated hours or examination weights. We outline ten teaching-learning modules, ensuring a balance across foundational sciences, applied anaesthesia, critical care, ethics, and simulation. This strategic restructuring of Diploma in Anaesthesia and Critical Care Technician training programmes has the potential to significantly improve clinical skills and enhance patient safety protocols. The literature search for this article was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL using terms related to competency-based education, allied health training, anaesthesia, and critical care.

42822778.title: Intensive care unit-acquired infection is the main driver of resource utilization, independent of antimicrobial resistance.
42822778.abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are frequent in intensive care units (ICUs) and are associated with substantial clinical and economic burden. However, the independent contribution of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) beyond the occurrence of infection remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 802 adult ICU admissions in a tertiary university hospital. Patients were classified into three groups: no ICU-acquired HAI (N = 666), HAI without AMR (N = 105), and HAI with AMR (N = 31). Primary outcomes were ICU length of stay (LOS) and hospital costs; hospital mortality was analysed as a secondary outcome. Generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, Simplified Acute Physiology Score II (SAPS II), and comorbidities were used. A restricted analysis among infected patients evaluated the independent association of AMR. ICU-acquired HAI occurred in 17% of patients, with AMR identified in 3.9%. ICU LOS increased across groups (6 vs 19 vs 21 days; P < 0.001). In adjusted analyses, ICU LOS was 7.6 days in patients without HAI, 21.7 days in patients with HAI without AMR, and 30.3 days in those with AMR. Adjusted hospital costs were €29,105, €60,065, and €70,164, respectively. In analyses restricted to infected patients, AMR was not independently associated with ICU LOS or hospital costs. ICU-acquired infection was the primary driver of increased ICU LOS and hospital costs. After adjustment for severity and comorbidity burden, AMR was not independently associated with additional resource utilization among infected patients. These findings highlight infection prevention as a priority for reducing ICU burden, alongside antimicrobial stewardship strategies.

42822676.title: Impact of antimicrobial stewardship implementation in an intensive care unit in Central India - A microbiologist-intensivist driven initiative.
42822676.abstract: This study evaluates a microbiologist-intensivist-driven prospective audit-feedback model in a 13-bedded tertiary-care critical care unit in Central India, using interrupted time-series analysis (ITS) to assess its impact on antimicrobial consumption (AMC), alongside diagnostic stewardship and patient outcomes. This quasi-experimental study included both retrospective and prospective data collected over 20 months, divided into a 3-month pre-intervention phase (PIP), 12-month intervention phase (IP), and 5-month follow-up phase (FUP). Patients receiving targeted antimicrobials for more than 48 h were included. Baseline AMC was recorded during PIP. During the IP, bi-weekly AMSP rounds with real-time recommendations on antimicrobial therapy, sample collection, and infection control practices were conducted. Culture reports, relevant laboratory parameters (leucocyte count, procalcitonin, invasive fungal markers), and clinical status (fever, vasopressor requirement, SOFA score) were reviewed to assess the appropriateness of therapy. AMC was measured as days of therapy/1000 patient-days and ITS analysis was done. A total of 398 patients were enrolled (PIP: 83; IP: 315). Cumulative average AMC significantly decreased from 2019.1 (PIP) to 1659.5 (IP) and was sustained during FUP (1635.2) even though ITS analysis revealed non-significant improvement. Use of reserve antimicrobials, including colistin/polymyxin, linezolid, and ceftazidime-avibactam-aztreonam, declined during IP. The mean number of antibiotics per patient decreased from 4.0 to 3.3, while ICU stay showed a numerical reduction from 13.5 to 10.7 days, although this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.09). Mean SOFA across PIP (5.8) and IP (5.9) was similar. Urine, endotracheal and blood culture sampling declined significantly, reflecting more judicious, clinically guided testing. A microbiologist-intensivist-driven AMSP is feasible and may reduce AMC in Indian ICU where infectious disease specialists are scarce. Integrating microbiology expertise with bedside decision-making offers a practical and scalable stewardship model for high-burden Lower Middle-Income Countries, and a scalable template for programme expansion.

42822832.title: Evaluating the cost-effectiveness of a conservative approach to oxygen therapy for invasively ventilated adults in intensive care: the UK-ROX trial.
42822832.journal: Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research
42822832.abstract: There is a lack of economic evaluation evidence on the optimal oxygen dosing level for mechanically ventilated critically ill patients. This study reports the health economic outcomes of a large-scale randomized controlled trial (RCT), UK-ROX, and conducts a full cost-effectiveness analysis of conservative versus usual oxygen therapy. All-cause mortality, health related quality of life (HrQoL), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), costs, and incremental net monetary benefit (INB) were assessed at 90 days post-randomization. HrQoL was derived from information collected via an EQ-5D-5L questionnaire using an appropriate mapping function. Total healthcare costs include resource use that occurred in adult ICUs, general wards, and follow-up health services. The cost effectiveness analysis (CEA) used regression methods to report the cost-effectiveness and summarised the uncertainties around the incremental cost-effectiveness results. After adjustment for prespecified baseline variables, the estimated incremental costs of conservative oxygen therapy versus usual oxygen therapy were -£968 (95% CI -£2279 to £342). The adjusted mean differences in EQ-5D utility score and life-years were 0.004 (95% CI -0.016 to 0.025) and -0.003 (95% CI -0.006 to 0.001), and incremental QALYs were 0.001 (95% CI -0.002 to 0.003). As a result, the mean INB of conservative oxygen therapy was £979 (95% CI -£334 to £2292). Conservative and usual oxygen therapy resulted in similar QALYs, and while conservative therapy appeared cost-saving with positive INBs, both estimates have uncertainty.

42821858.title: From Knowledge to Outcomes: The Effect of Nursing Care Bundle Training on Knowledge, Compliance, and Ventilator-associated Pneumonia Rates in Intensive Care Units (A Quasi-intervention Study, 2025).
42821858.journal: Dimensions of critical care nursing : DCCN
42821858.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a serious infection in ICUs, contributing to prolonged mechanical ventilation and higher mortality. This study aimed to enhance ICU nurses' knowledge and compliance with ventilator care bundle practices to reduce the incidence and mortality of VAP among mechanically ventilated patients at Benha University Hospitals. This quasi-experimental study included all nurses working in the central and intermediate ICUs (N = 262). The intervention comprised 12 structured educational sessions and bedside demonstrations. Data collection included pre-questionnaires and post-questionnaires to assess nurses' knowledge, observation checklists to measure compliance with the VAP care bundle, and patient surveillance records to track VAP incidence and mortality rates. Postintervention analysis revealed a significant improvement in nurses' knowledge scores on general infection control and VAP prevention guidelines, as well as a significant increase in compliance with the VAP care bundle (P < .001). General infection control knowledge score was a significant predictor of VAP prevention knowledge (B = 0.632, P < .01). Clinically, the program resulted in a nearly one-third reduction in VAP incidence (central ICU: -29.1%; intermediate ICU: -28.5%), preventing ∼1 infection for every 10 ventilated patients. Mortality among ventilated cases was cut by almost half in the intermediate ICU (-53.8%) and by one-third in the central ICU (-30.9%). The care bundle training program significantly improved ICU nurses' knowledge, boosted adherence to evidence-based ventilator care practices, and contributed to lowering the VAP incidence rate and related mortality. These results represent not only statistical significance but also a substantial, life-saving impact.

42820590.title: Advances in mechanical ventilation over the past 25 years: from protective ventilation to post-ICU recovery.

42818587.title: Clinical significance of controlling nutritional status score in predicting ICU admission, prolonged hospitalization, and in-hospital mortality in emergency sepsis: a single-center retrospective study.
42818587.abstract: Sepsis is associated with high mortality in critically ill patients. Existing prognostic tools are often complex or require specialized testing. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score in patients with sepsis in the emergency department. A retrospective analysis of 1,200 sepsis patients admitted to the emergency department of the Affiliated Changsha Central Hospital, Hengyang Medical School, University of South China from January 2020 to June 2025 was conducted. Kaplan-Meier analysis, multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic splines (RCS), receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were employed to evaluate the associations between the CONUT score and ICU admission, prolonged hospitalization, and in-hospital all-cause mortality. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. Time-dependent Cox regression revealed that each one-point increase in the CONUT score was associated with an 11% increase in the risk of in-hospital mortality (HR = 1.11, 95% CI:1.02-1.21). After adjusting for potential confounders, logistic regression analysis further demonstrated that, the CONUT score was significantly associated with ICU admission (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09-1.23) and prolonged hospitalization (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.05-1.17). RCS revealed linear positive correlations. ROC analysis showed that CONUT was superior to SOFA for predicting prolonged hospitalization, and combining CONUT with SOFA enhanced predictive performance. DCA indicated the combined model provided the highest clinical net benefit. Advanced age, diabetes, and mechanical ventilation modified the associations between CONUT and certain outcomes. Elevated CONUT scores are independently associated with adverse outcomes in emergency department sepsis patients, serving as a simple prognostic indicator for early risk stratification.

42819557.title: Prospective Molecular and Phenotypic Characterization of blaCTX-M and blaTEM ESBL Genes in Uropathogenic Escherichia coli from ICU Patients at Three Tertiary-Care Hospitals in Tabriz, Iran.
42819557.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) caused by extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli have become a major therapeutic challenge worldwide, especially in intensive care units. In northwestern Iran, the molecular epidemiology of the key resistance genes blaCTX-M and blaTEM, along with their potential co-carriage on plasmids, remains poorly understood. This gap limits the development of effective local empirical treatment guidelines and infection control strategies. A cross-sectional study was conducted at three tertiary-care hospitals in Tabriz, Iran (2025). We identified 100 non-duplicate Escherichia coli isolates recovered from ICU patients with UTIs using standard microbiological methods. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed by the disk diffusion method according to CLSI 2024 guidelines. ESBL phenotype was confirmed using the combined disk test with Ceftazidime and Clavulanic acid. Genotypic detection of blaTEM and blaCTX-M was performed by conventional PCR. Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests were used to assess statistical associations. Among 135 culture-positive urine specimens, E. coli was the predominant pathogen (74.07%), followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae (11.85%). Universal resistance to Cefotaxime (100%) and high resistance to Ceftazidime (95%) were observed. Imipenem retained the highest in vitro activity (82% susceptibility). Phenotypic ESBL production was detected in 48/100 (48%) isolates. Among ESBL producers, blaTEM was present in 28 (58.3%), blaCTX-M in 20 (41.7%), and both genes co-occurred in 18 isolates (37.5%). The observed co-occurrence significantly exceeded expected values under independence (observed: 18 vs. expected: 11.7; Chi-square p = 0.0005; Fisher's exact p = 0.00025), demonstrating non-random co-occurrence consistent with, but not proof of, plasmid-mediated co-carriage. ESBL-producing E. coli carrying both blaTEM and blaCTX-M are highly prevalent among ICU-associated UTI in Tabriz. The statistically significant non-random co-occurrence of these genes has direct implications for surveillance strategies, necessitating simultaneous genotyping of both genes. Carbapenems remain effective, underscoring the urgency of their stewardship to prevent the emergence of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) in this setting.

42836073.title: Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan for the Pragmatic Trial Examining Oxygenation Prior to Intubation of Preoxygenation With Noninvasive Ventilation vs Oxygen Mask in Critically Ill Adults.
42836073.abstract: Hypoxemia is a common and life-threatening complication during emergency tracheal intubation of critically ill adults. The administration of supplemental oxygen before the procedure (ie, preoxygenation) decreases the risk of hypoxemia during intubation. Does preoxygenation with noninvasive ventilation prevent hypoxemia during tracheal intubation of critically ill adults compared with preoxygenation with an oxygen mask? The Pragmatic Trial Examining Oxygenation Prior to Intubation (PREOXI) is a prospective, multicenter, nonmasked randomized comparative effectiveness trial being conducted in seven EDs and 17 ICUs across the United States. The trial compares preoxygenation with noninvasive ventilation vs oxygen mask among 1,300 critically ill adults undergoing emergency tracheal intubation. Eligible patients are randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either noninvasive ventilation or an oxygen mask before induction. The primary outcome is the incidence of hypoxemia, defined as a peripheral oxygen saturation of < 85% between induction and 2 min after intubation. The secondary outcome is the lowest oxygen saturation between induction and 2 min after intubation. Enrollment began on March 10, 2022, and is expected to conclude in 2023. The PREOXI investigation will provide important data on the comparative effectiveness of preoxygenation with noninvasive ventilation vs oxygen mask for the prevention of hypoxemia during emergency tracheal intubation. Specifying the protocol and statistical analysis plan before the conclusion of enrollment increases the rigor, reproducibility, and interpretability of the trial. ClinicalTrials.gov; No.: NCT05267652; URL: www.clinicaltrials.gov.

42846240.title: Investigating Why Clinicians Deviate from Standards of Care: Liberating Patients from Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU.
42846240.journal: Proceedings of the SIGCHI conference on human factors in computing systems. CHI Conference
42846240.abstract: Clinical practice guidelines, care pathways, and protocols are designed to support evidence-based practices for clinicians; however, their adoption remains a challenge. We set out to investigate why clinicians deviate from the "Wake Up and Breathe" protocol, an evidence-based guideline for liberating patients from mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU). We conducted over 40 hours of direct observations of live clinical workflows, 17 interviews with frontline care providers, and 4 co-design workshops at three different medical intensive care units. Our findings indicate that unlike prior literature suggests, disagreement with the protocol is not a substantial barrier to adoption. Instead, the uncertainty surrounding the application of the protocol for individual patients leads clinicians to deprioritize adoption in favor of tasks where they have high certainty. Reflecting on these insights, we identify opportunities for technical systems to help clinicians in effectively executing the protocol and discuss future directions for HCI research to support the integration of protocols into clinical practice in complex, team-based healthcare settings.

42824567.title: Pancreatic microbiota composition and diversity in pancreatitis-associated infection: a systematic review with focus on infected pancreatic necrosis.
42824567.abstract: Pancreatitis-associated intra-abdominal infection (PA-IAI), particularly infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN), is a serious complication of severe acute pancreatitis and contributes substantially to late morbidity and mortality. Sequencing-based technologies have expanded the detection of microorganisms in pancreatic infection; however, the characteristics of pancreatic microbiota and their clinical relevance have not been systematically summarized. A systematic literature search was conducted in seven electronic databases to identify studies evaluating pancreatic microbiota in patients with pancreatitis-associated infection. Studies reporting microbial composition or diversity using sequencing-based approaches were included. Study characteristics, microbial findings, diversity patterns, clinical outcomes, and methodological details were systematically extracted and synthesized. Six studies involving 235 participants were included; 188 participants contributed pancreatic or peripancreatic microbiota data. Most available evidence was derived from patients with IPN. Sequencing-based approaches generally detected a broader range of microbial taxa than conventional culture, with enteric-associated microorganisms frequently detected, while phylum-level dominance varied among studies. Reported diversity patterns varied between studies and could not be directly compared because of methodological heterogeneity. Although IPN was associated with worse clinical outcomes, current evidence did not demonstrate that specific microbial taxa or microbiota characteristics independently predicted mortality, organ failure, or treatment response. Current evidence indicates that pancreatic microbiota in pancreatitis-associated infection, particularly IPN, are characterized by frequent detection of enteric-associated microorganisms and substantial methodological heterogeneity. Sequencing-based approaches may provide additional microbiological information beyond conventional culture and may influence clinical management; however, whether sequencing-guided management changes improve antimicrobial stewardship or patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain. Future prospective studies using standardized microbiome workflows are required to determine the clinical significance of pancreatic microbial characteristics. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261295285, identifier: CRD420261295285.

42952500.title: Glycemic dysregulation and insulin resistance across acute and post-acute COVID-19: a systematic review and meta-analysis of etiologic and prognostic evidence.
42952500.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can disrupt glucose regulation through inflammation, adipose-tissue dysfunction, impaired insulin signaling, and variable β-cell compensation. These evidence domains remain incompletely integrated. To synthesize evidence on glycemic dysregulation and insulin resistance or insulin sensitivity across acute and post-acute COVID-19, including metabolic trajectories and associations with adverse clinical outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were searched. Eligible studies evaluated glucose regulation and at least one insulin-resistance or insulin-sensitivity measure during or after COVID-19. Etiological and prognostic evidence was analyzed as related but distinct domains. Prognostic meta-analysis evaluated study-defined acute hyperglycemic phenotypes; insulin-resistance or insulin-sensitivity assessment was a study-level eligibility criterion rather than part of a participant-level composite exposure. Unadjusted risk ratios (RRs) from event counts were pooled using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Non-combinable evidence was synthesized according to Synthesis Without Meta-analysis principles. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools, and certainty was evaluated with GRADE. The protocol and analytical plan were retrospectively registered in OSF on August 21, 2026 (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/K5FWU). Twenty independent studies represented by 23 reports. Acute hyperglycemic phenotypes were associated with increased short-term all-cause mortality (four studies; 1,079 participants; RR 2.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.21-3.64; I2=31.3%; 95% prediction interval 0.96-4.56) and invasive mechanical ventilation (three studies; 679 participants; RR 3.64, 95% CI 1.74-7.61; I2=0%). Mortality estimates remained directionally stable in sensitivity analysis. Adding a large study using peak in-hospital glucose preserved the mortality association but produced substantial heterogeneity for ventilation. Etiological evidence showed no uniform post-COVID trajectory: insulin resistance or glycemic abnormalities resolved in some populations, persisted in others, and progressed toward newly diagnosed diabetes in a subset. Mechanistic evidence implicated inflammatory stress, adipose-tissue dysfunction, impaired insulin signaling, and variable β-cell responses. Study-defined acute hyperglycemic phenotypes were associated with adverse COVID-19 outcomes in studies that also assessed insulin resistance or insulin sensitivity. These unadjusted estimates should not be interpreted as effects of a combined phenotype or as causal associations. Persistent metabolic abnormalities occurred heterogeneously, supporting standardized participant-level definitions and controlled longitudinal studies. https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/K5FWU, identifier 10.17605/OSF.IO/K5FWU.

42920117.title: Considerations for emergency airway management and resuscitation in cancer patients: a review.
42920117.abstract: Cancer patients frequently present to the emergency department (ED) with malignancy or treatment-related critical illness, requiring airway intervention or resuscitation. Multiple factors such as anatomical distortion, treatment sequelae, frailty, and complex goals-of-care considerations create unique challenges. This narrative review aims to provide practical, evidence-informed guidance in airway management and resuscitation of oncologic patients. We conducted a review of the literature addressing airway management, physiologic alterations associated with malignancy and cachexia, pharmacologic considerations for rapid sequence intubation, and resuscitation outcomes in cancer populations. We synthesized relevant clinical guidelines and studies to develop an overview of recommendations applicable to ED practice. Cancer patients present numerous airway management challenges due to tumor or surgical airway alternations, post-radiation fibrosis, edema, and bleeding. Physiologic factors-including reduced functional residual capacity, anemia, muscle wasting, and systemic inflammation-shorten safe apnea time, increase risk of peri-intubation hypoxia, and hemodynamic instability. Malnutrition, organ dysfunction, and chemotherapy toxicity alter pharmacokinetics, necessitating individualized selection and dosing of induction and paralytic agents. Early anticipation of difficulties in airway management, optimized preoxygenation, advanced airway techniques, and multidisciplinary involvement are essential. Resuscitation planning must incorporate realistic prognostication and clear discussions regarding code status. Late or absent documentation of goals-of-care remains common. Airway management and resuscitation in cancer patients require a specialized, patient-centered approach. Future research should address comparative outcomes in the cancer population and support development of ED-specific oncologic protocols. Integration of structured goals-of-care frameworks and early palliative care help ensure ethically aligned, high-quality emergency care.

42820550.title: Life-sustaining therapy limitation in critical illness: unequal weights of demographics, disease severity, and comorbidities.
42820550.abstract: To identify independent clinical predictors of life-sustaining treatment limitation in critically ill adults and to quantify their relative contribution across predefined conceptual domains. We conducted a retrospective cohort study including all adults admitted to a tertiary medical-surgical intensive care unit in Brazil between May 2016 and May 2020. Patients with documented life-sustaining treatment limitations (withholding or withdrawal) were compared with those who received full treatment. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of life-sustaining treatment limitation, and predictors were grouped into conceptual domains to assess their relative contributions. Among 6,725 intensive care unit admissions, 336 patients (5.0%) had documented life-sustaining treatment limitation. Compared with patients without limitation, those with life-sustaining treatment decisions were older (median 77 versus 67 years; p < 0.001), more frequently frail (Clinical Frailty Scale ≥ 5: 7.6% versus 3.1%; p = 0.002), and had more metastatic cancer (15.6% versus 5.8%; p < 0.001). Independent predictors of life-sustaining treatment limitation included age ≥ 80 years (OR 2.08; 95%CI 1.32 - 3.28), frailty (OR 2.37; 95%CI 1.53 - 3.71), metastatic cancer (OR 2.38; 95%CI 1.53 - 3.71), medical admission (OR 1.86; 95%CI 1.02 - 3.40), higher SAPS 3 scores (OR 1.02 per point; 95%CI 1.01 - 1.03), and prolonged mechanical ventilation (OR 5.78 for ≥10 days). The presence of any organ support was inversely associated with life-sustaining treatment limitation (OR 0.69; 95%CI 0.49 - 0.97). When predictors were aggregated into conceptual domains and evaluated using Wald χ² proportions, acute illness severity and life-suppor-related variables accounted for approximately 45% of the model signal, followed by demographic factors (≈38%) and chronic comorbidities (≈17%). Life-sustaining treatment limitation decisions in critically ill adults are influenced by frailty, comorbidities, and acute severity. Grouping predictors into conceptual domains enhances interpretability and may support more structured and transparent decision-making frameworks in intensive care unit settings.

42822164.title: A scalable educational intervention to reduce airway-related harm in low-resource PICUs: A design-test-scale experience.
42822164.abstract: Across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), an estimated 1.7 billion children lack access to safe surgical and perioperative care. In Latin America, pediatric postoperative mortality remains several-fold higher than in high-income countries, driven largely by preventable airway and critical-care complications. Following the death of an infant after an unplanned extubation in El Salvador, system-level gaps in airway safety, sedation, and communication were identified, motivating development of a scalable intervention to strengthen postoperative critical care for intubated children. This work was designed at Hospital Nacional de Niños Benjamín Bloom, in San Salvador and subsequently tested at Fundación Hospital Infantil Napoleón Franco Pareja in Cartagena, Colombia. Both institutions faced high unplanned extubation rates, variable airway-safety practices, and limited structured training. Using Ariadne Labs ARC (Design-Test-Scale) implementation pathway, we created a bilingual, online pediatric airway and critical-care curriculum alongside a telesimulation-based emergency team-training program. Forty-five short, multilingual video modules addressed airway management, sedation, respiratory therapy, nursing priorities, and teamwork. Remote, high-fidelity simulation reinforced crisis resource management and role clarity, with local champions trained to run courses independently. In El Salvador, early implementation was associated with reductions in unplanned extubations and PICU mortality. In Colombia, 101 clinicians completed the curriculum and 39 completed telesimulation training, with mortality declining from 22.4% to 9.5% post-intervention. A combined digital curriculum and telesimulation model can strengthen airway safety, communication, and crisis readiness in resource-constrained PICUs. Following successful design and testing, the model is positioned for scale across LMIC pediatric intensive care settings.

42823139.title: Guillain-Barré syndrome temporally associated with respiratory syncytial virus vaccination.
42823139.abstract: An older woman developed acute progressive limb weakness associated with pain, paraesthesia and falls 2 weeks after receiving a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine. Initial examination and imaging suggested alternative diagnoses, including cervical spondylotic disease and cerebrovascular pathology and early neurophysiology was non-diagnostic. During admission, she deteriorated with urinary retention, areflexia and type 2 respiratory failure requiring intubation and ventilation and was commenced on intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Cerebrospinal fluid analysis later demonstrated albumin-cytologic dissociation and repeat nerve conduction studies confirmed an acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy consistent with Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS). She improved following intensive care and IVIG, with partial recovery of limb strength and functional status and was discharged to a rehabilitation facility. This case illustrates a rare but important possible association between RSV vaccination and GBS; highlights the diagnostic challenges of early presentations with non-specific symptoms and inconclusive investigations; and emphasises the need for serial assessment and early escalation of care to optimise patient outcomes.

42818790.title: Case Report: Postoperative pulmonary embolism causing obstructive shock and circulatory collapse after gynecologic surgery: successful rescue with VA-ECMO.
42818790.abstract: Very-high-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) occurring within hours after major surgery presents a therapeutic dilemma because urgent reperfusion may be required at precisely the time when bleeding risk is greatest. We describe a 45-year-old woman who developed catastrophic bilateral PE approximately two hours after elective gynecologic surgery consisting of myomectomy and ovarian endometriotic cyst excision. Shortly after surgery, she experienced abrupt respiratory failure, profound hypotension, and rapidly progressive circulatory collapse. On arrival at a tertiary intensive care unit, arterial blood gas analysis revealed severe respiratory acidosis (pH 7.019; PaCO2 82 mmHg), and the patient remained unstable despite mechanical ventilation, high-dose vasopressors, and conventional resuscitative measures. Because of refractory obstructive shock and the prohibitive hemorrhagic risk associated with recent pelvic surgery, emergent venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) was instituted before definitive radiological confirmation. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography subsequently demonstrated extensive bilateral pulmonary arterial thrombosis involving both proximal and distal branches. Management was further complicated by ongoing postoperative bleeding during mandatory anticoagulation for ECMO support, requiring repeated transfusion of blood products and frequent adjustment of anticoagulant therapy. During recovery, the patient also developed residual left popliteal deep vein thrombosis, postoperative inguinal hematoma, and surgical-site infection caused by extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli. Despite these challenges, she was successfully weaned from ECMO and mechanical ventilation, transitioned to oral rivaroxaban, and discharged without neurological sequelae. This case illustrates the complexity of managing acute PE when life-saving reperfusion strategies must be balanced against a substantial risk of postoperative bleeding. It also adds to the limited literature describing successful use of VA-ECMO as a bridge to recovery in immediate postoperative PE complicated by obstructive shock and circulatory collapse.

42819542.title: Case Report: Coinfection of influenza A and Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia.
42819542.abstract: The coinfection of influenza A and Chlamydia psittaci pneumoniae is rarely described in China. However, the clinical features of these diseases pose a significant diagnostic challenge. Therefore, it is necessary to report and review such a potentially fatal case. We report an 89-year-old male patient requiring admission to the intensive care unit with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, shock and MODS. He presented with fever, fatigue, anorexia and dyspnea. The patient exhibited severe hypoxemia, shock, hepatic dysfunction (elevated liver enzymes and serum bilirubin), acute kidney injury and a SOFA score of 17. Mechanical ventilation (MV) and venous-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) were established for respiratory support. The initial diagnosis focused on influenza A for his positive influenza A nucleic acid. However, the patient's imaging presentation was not coupled with viral pneumonia, which raised suspicion for other pathogens. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected coinfection of C psittaci, influenza A H3N2 virus, and Klebsiella pneumoniae in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Concurrent targeted NGS (tNGS) detected C. psittaci in blood. Omadacycline and baloxavir marboxil were prescribed. The patient's condition improved, and he was successfully weaned from VV-ECMO and MV. He was discharged and recovered on day 60 of the follow-up. This case underscores the diagnostic complexity of coinfection and the use of NGS testing in this severe condition and the role of omadacycline in psittacosis.

42820335.title: Atypical late neurosyphilis presenting as status epilepticus: diagnostic and screening implications.
42820335.abstract: Neurosyphilis is a serious complication of poorly treated syphilis due to Treponema pallidum invasion of the central nervous system. Symptoms vary from silent infection to severe neurological deficits. Despite progress in diagnostics and treatment, the diagnosis is frequently missed because it is not considered, particularly in atypical presentations and in patients with no evident risk factor. . A 45-year-old man presented with confusion, speech difficulties, and left-sided weakness following subtle behavioral changes. In the emergency department, he had a witnessed focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizure starting with head deviation to the left and tonic posturing of the left arm. Brain CT was normal, while MRI revealed right thalamic and bilateral temporal FLAIR hyperintensities with diffusion restriction in the thalamus. CSF showed mild pleocytosis (17 WBC/µL) and raised protein (67.6 mg/dL). Serum treponemal screening was positive with an RPR titre > 1:32. Neurosyphilis was confirmed by a reactive CSF non-treponemal test (RPR 1:2) in a patient with compatible clinical and CSF findings; the CSF TPHA titre was >1:10,240, which is supportive but not in itself a diagnostic criterion.Levetiracetam was started on admission and intravenous penicillin G on day 2, after the diagnosis was confirmed. Because EEG and MRI suggested possible focal status epilepticus, valproate and phenytoin were added. The patient developed respiratory failure needing mechanical ventilation and deep vein thrombosis. After extended ICU stay and rehabilitation, he recovered with mild residual critical illness myopathy and cognitive deficits. Neurosyphilis is not intrinsically difficult to diagnose, provided it is considered, including outside the classically recognised risk groups such as men who have sex with men.

42820767.title: Systemic Injury Burden, Not Pneumothorax Size, Predicts Prolonged Chest Tube Duration in Traumatic Pneumothorax: A Retrospective Analysis at a Level 1 Trauma Center.
42820767.abstract: Prolonged chest tube (CT) duration in traumatic pneumothorax (PTX) is associated with increased complications and greater patient discomfort.
