This retrospective study characterized clinical and procedural factors associated with prolonged CT duration (>48 hours) in adult patients presenting at a level I trauma center undergoing tube thoracostomy for traumatic PTX between January 2020 and June 2023. Among 203 patients (mean age 46 years; 75% male; 86.7% blunt trauma), the mean CT duration was 77.6 hours. There was no significant difference in initial PTX size between patients who had a normal CT duration and patients who had prolonged CT duration. Prolonged CT duration occurred more frequently with open CT, bilateral CT, ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, supplemental oxygen on arrival, and longer hospital stay. Chest tube duration correlated significantly with higher injury severity score (ISS), higher chest AIS, larger tube size, lower presenting blood pressure, and higher heart rate. These findings suggest that systemic injury burden, rather than PTX characteristics like size, identifies patients likely to require prolonged CT duration.

42819475.title: Postoperative pulmonary complications after totally thoracoscopic cardiac surgery: a retrospective cohort study comparing single-lumen and double-lumen endotracheal tubes.
42819475.abstract: Double-lumen tubes (DLTs) are standard for one-lung ventilation in totally thoracoscopic cardiac surgery but are associated with airway injury and postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs). This study compared perioperative outcomes between single-lumen tube (SLT)-based and DLT-based strategies in 176 adults undergoing elective totally thoracoscopic cardiac surgery (SLT, n = 94; DLT, n = 82). This was a single-center retrospective cohort study. The SLT-based strategy employed a single-lumen tube with two-lung ventilation supplemented by brief, controlled intermittent lung collapse when enhanced surgical exposure was required, whereas the DLT-based strategy employed a double-lumen tube with one-lung ventilation throughout the main phase of surgery. The primary outcome was PPC incidence; secondary outcomes included airway complications and recovery metrics. Multivariable and sensitivity analyses were performed. Baseline characteristics were balanced. The anesthesia-to-incision time was shorter in the SLT group (57 vs. 67 min; P < 0.001). The SLT group had lower PPC incidence [29% vs. 56%; adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 0.30; 95% CI, 0.16-0.58], including lower rates of respiratory infection (7% vs. 22%) and atelectasis (18% vs. 39%). Airway complications were also less frequent (23% vs. 48%; aOR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.18-0.68). Mechanical ventilation duration (17.5 vs. 21.0 h; P = 0.009) and ICU stay (28.0 vs. 36.0 h; P < 0.001) were shorter in the SLT group. An SLT-based strategy was associated with improved perioperative efficiency, fewer pulmonary and airway complications, and faster recovery. These findings warrant further investigation in prospective studies.

42820893.title: Perioperative Nursing Management of Patients Undergoing Nonsupercharged Cervical Roux-en-Y Esophagojejunostomy: A Single-Center Retrospective Descriptive Case Series.
42820893.journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
42820893.abstract: Perioperative nursing after esophageal reconstruction is demanding, and nonsupercharged cervical Roux-en-Y esophagojejunostomy shifts nursing surveillance away from microvascular patency toward the more gradual signs of marginal conduit hypoperfusion. Nursing-focused reports describing phase-specific surveillance, documentation, and escalation for this reconstruction are lacking. This study aimed to describe an institutional perioperative nursing pathway together with the clinical outcomes and nursing process indicators observed in patients undergoing this procedure. This study adopted a single-center, retrospective descriptive case-series design. In this study, we reviewed 22 consecutive patients with esophageal cancer who underwent nonsupercharged cervical Roux-en-Y esophagojejunostomy between January 2021 and April 2025. Data were retrospectively abstracted from routinely maintained clinical and nursing records. An institutional perioperative nursing pathway combining routine esophageal perioperative care with procedure-specific surveillance of the cervical jejunal conduit was in use throughout the study period. No formal sample-size calculation was performed and no comparator group was available; therefore, clinical outcomes and nursing process indicators were summarized descriptively. The median operation time was 274.0 minutes (IQR 255.8-288.5), median mechanical ventilation time 18.0 hours (IQR 14.0-19.8), median intensive care unit stay 4.0 days (IQR 3.0-5.2), and median total hospital stay 12.0 days (IQR 8.8-14.0). Enteral nutrition was initiated at a median of postoperative day 5.0. The early mobilization target was documented in 86.4% (19/22) of patients by postoperative day 2, all patients ambulated by postoperative day 4, and respiratory exercises were recorded at a median of 4 sessions per day (IQR 3-5). Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications were recorded in 22.7% (5/22) of patients, anastomotic leakage in 18.2% (4/22, all endoscopically confirmed), and pulmonary complications in 4.5% (1/22). Perfusion warning events were documented in 31.8% (7/22) of patients; all were managed according to the predefined nursing escalation process and resolved or did not progress. No graft necrosis, re-exploration, or 30-day death occurred. This case series describes the implementation of a structured perioperative nursing pathway for nonsupercharged cervical Roux-en-Y esophagojejunostomy and the outcomes observed under it. Perfusion warning events and anastomotic complications were documented without graft necrosis or reoperation. These preliminary observational findings offer practical clinical insight but do not establish pathway effectiveness. Prospective multicenter studies are required to evaluate implementation fidelity, measurement reliability, clinical effectiveness, and generalizability.

42819128.title: In-hospital outcomes and documented 90-day readmission to the index hospital in older patients with Parkinson's disease hospitalised for lower respiratory tract infection: a single-centre retrospective cohort study.
42819128.abstract: Lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) is a major cause of hospitalisation in older adults with Parkinson's disease (PD), but it remains uncertain whether PD-related measures provide clinically relevant information beyond general vulnerability and acute infection severity. We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of patients aged ≥65 years with neurologist-diagnosed PD who were hospitalised for LRTI between 2018 and 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of intensive care unit admission, invasive mechanical ventilation, or in-hospital death. Documented readmission to the index hospital within 90 days among survivors was analysed as a secondary exploratory outcome. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression models evaluated clinical factors associated with these outcomes. A hierarchical extension added Hoehn-Yahr stage and pre-admission wheelchair- or bed-bound status to the base clinical model. Calendar-period analyses and bootstrap internal validation were performed. Among 246 patients, 62 (25.2%) experienced the composite in-hospital outcome. In the PD-specific extended model, higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (adjusted odds ratio [OR] per 1-point increase 1.19, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.00-1.42), hypoxaemia (OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.01-3.96), serum albumin <35 g/L (OR 3.18, 95% CI 1.65-6.14), sepsis or septic shock (OR 2.41, 95% CI 1.17-4.98), and pre-admission wheelchair- or bed-bound status (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.08-4.01) were associated with the outcome. Hoehn-Yahr stage, PD duration, tube feeding, and antiparkinsonian medication burden were not independently associated. Among 228 patients discharged alive, 74 (32.5%) had a documented readmission to the index hospital. Hypoalbuminaemia (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.82, 95% CI 1.12-2.95) and non-home discharge (HR 1.96, 95% CI 1.19-3.24) were among the factors associated with documented same-hospital return. Bootstrap-corrected discrimination was 0.81 for the extended logistic model and 0.70 for the Cox model. Severe in-hospital deterioration was associated mainly with general physiological vulnerability, acute infection severity, and pre-admission mobility dependence, whereas most other available PD-specific measures showed no clear independent association. These findings support integrated clinical assessment but not a validated PD-specific prediction strategy; the post-discharge analysis reflects documented return to the index hospital rather than complete population-level readmission.

42819172.title: An explainable machine learning approach to predicting carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae with imbalanced data and resistance-ratio validation.
42819172.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
42819172.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) is a major global health threat. Predicting resistance from electronic medical records (EMRs) may support infection control and antimicrobial stewardship, but class imbalance can impair detection of resistant isolates. This study developed an interpretable machine-learning framework for predicting carbapenem-resistant versus carbapenem-susceptible K. pneumoniae. We retrospectively analyzed 5,794 records collected from 2014 to 2024, including 999 carbapenem-resistant and 4,795 carbapenem-susceptible isolates. The prediction anchor was culture-specimen collection (T0), and all predictors were restricted to information available at or before T0. Seven algorithms and 18 sampling strategies were evaluated using patient-grouped five-fold cross-validation with fold-specific preprocessing. The selected resampling pipeline was compared with Platt-calibrated XGBoost using sensitivity-targeted, F2-maximizing, and cost-sensitive thresholds. Feature-restriction analyses, multiplicity-adjusted comparisons, ICU subgroup analysis, reconstructed prevalence scenarios, calibration assessment, and same-center temporal validation were also performed. XGBoost and LightGBM showed comparable discrimination after multiplicity adjustment. ENN-BLSMOTE-XGBoost increased sensitivity and reduced the very-major-error rate (VME) at the default threshold, but slightly reduced ranking discrimination and increased false-positive alerts. Sensitivity-targeted threshold optimization of calibrated XGBoost produced an operating point close to that of the resampled model, indicating that much of the sensitivity gain could be achieved without changing the training distribution. After all duration-based predictors were excluded, ENN-BLSMOTE-XGBoost retained an ROC AUC of 0.940 and a PR AUC of 0.833. In the 2025 temporal cohort, the calibrated ENN-BLSMOTE-XGBoost model achieved an ROC AUC of 0.889, a PR AUC of 0.684, a sensitivity of 0.749, and a VME of 0.251; Platt scaling reduced its Brier score from 0.121 to 0.108. SHAP analysis identified ICU admission, vascular system disease, days of indwelling urinary catheterization, days of carbapenem use, and days of endotracheal intubation as the five highest-attribution predictors. A web calculator was developed to provide calibrated probability estimates referenced to the 17.24% resistance prevalence of the development cohort. The proposed model effectively addresses class imbalance in predicting carbapenem resistance in K. pneumoniae and may support early identification of patients at risk of harboring carbapenem-resistant isolates, thereby informing infection control and antimicrobial stewardship.

42924493.title: High-Flow Nasal Cannula and Virological Surveillance in Severe Bronchiolitis: A Retrospective PICU Study in Southern Brazil.
42924493.abstract: Acute Viral Bronchiolitis (AVB) is a leading cause of hospitalization among infants and young children, with Human orthopneumovirus (Respiratory Syncytial Virus [RSV]) representing the most prevalent etiologic agent. Despite its clinical relevance, data describing the epidemiological profile of AVB cases in Pediatric Intensive Care Units (PICUs) remain limited, particularly regarding advanced statistical modeling adjusting for modern respiratory support and testing biases. This observational, retrospective, and analytical study included 210 children aged 0-2 years with laboratory-confirmed AVB admitted to a private PICU in Southern Brazil between 2019 and 2023. To stabilize analyses affected by zero-event cells, Firth's penalized maximum likelihood logistic regression was utilized. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to assess the independent impact of high-flow oxygen therapies.The mean age was 5.76 months (SD = 4.46). The mean Modified Tal Score at admission was 7.4. RSV was the most frequently identified virus (72.4%). The apparent increase in viral diversity in later years, specifically Rhinovirus A/B/C (23.4%) and Enterovirus (7.7%), reflects a profound detection bias introduced by the adoption of an expanded 24-pathogen multiplex panel rather than a true epidemiological shift. Adjusted multivariate analysis demonstrated that HFNC use was independently associated with lower odds of invasive mechanical ventilation after adjustment for measured confounders (aOR = 0.54, 95% CI: 0.31 to 0.92; p = 0.02).These findings highlight the impact of testing methodologies on virological surveillance. Rigorous adjusted analyses confirm that the early application of modern non-invasive respiratory support is independently associated with lower odds of invasive mechanical ventilation.

42931939.title: Non-invasive ventilation for general paediatricians.
42931939.abstract: Over the past two decades, non-invasive ventilation (NIV) has transitioned from being primarily used in specialist intensive care units to becoming a standard intervention in high dependency units, general paediatric units, emergency departments, and increasingly, patients' homes. Despite this expansion, many general paediatricians still perceive NIV as outside their primary expertise. With this review, we aim to address that gap and equip general paediatricians with the knowledge and confidence to appropriately initiate NIV, monitor its effectiveness, and recognise when escalation of care is required. We narratively reviewed the physiological rationale for non-invasive respiratory support (NRS), including high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) and the two principal modalities of NIV-continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP)-and summarised disease-specific evidence from recent literature, including randomised trials, systematic reviews, and international consensus statements. This is a narrative rather than a systematic review: we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Paediatric Respiratory Reviews for English-language publications from January 2018 to June 2026 using the terms "non-invasive ventilation", "high-flow nasal cannula", "CPAP", "BiPAP", and "children", supplemented by references already known to the authors, and selected articles for relevance and recency, prioritising randomised trials, systematic reviews, and consensus statements. HFNC is an oxygenation device rather than a ventilatory device, and its mechanism, clinical applications, and therapeutic goals differ from CPAP and BiPAP. We introduce the Indications, Contraindications, Equipment, Mode and settings, Assessment and monitoring, Next steps (ICEMAN) framework as a practical tool for structured and safe initiation of NIV in routine clinical practice, and apply it across bronchiolitis, acute severe asthma, pneumonia and hypoxaemic respiratory failure, neuromuscular disease, and obstructive sleep apnoea. The essential requirements to initiate NIV outside the PICU are well-trained staff, appropriate monitoring, a reliable oxygen supply, and a clear plan for escalation to a higher level of care. Selection of patients for NIV outside the PICU requires careful attention to indication, contraindications, equipment, monitoring, and escalation pathway by using frameworks like ICEMAN. • HFNC, CPAP, and BiPAP are established, physiologically distinct respiratory therapies now used well beyond the PICU. • The ICEMAN framework, updated with PALICC-2 ARDS criteria, gives non-specialists a structured, teachable approach to safe NIV initiation.

42890624.title: Characteristics of Bacterial Isolates from Patients with Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia and the Hospital Environment in Urmia, Iran.
42890624.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia is a nosocomial infection involving hospitalized patients using mechanical ventilation. The endotracheal tube is a place for colonizing microbial populations and subsequent biofilm formation, leading to relative drug resistance. Also, the hospital environment may worsen the infection. This study aims to identify the microbial cause of the infection and evaluate its characteristics. Sampling was done using endotracheal tube suction among hospitalized patients and from different places in intensive care units in selected hospitals in Urmia, Iran. All specimens were identified by microbial and biochemical tests. Then, the antibiotic susceptibility tests were performed using disk diffusion and minimum inhibitory and bacteriocidal concentrations for selected antibiotics. Finally, the biofilm formation rates of all isolates were evaluated. The majority of clinical bacterial isolates were Gram-negative bacilli, including A. baumannii. Bacillus spp. and Staphylococcus aureus were the most isolated bacteria from environmental samples. The antibiotic susceptibility testing results showed that most Gram-negative bacilli were resistant to common antibiotics and were extensively-drug resistant. The intermediate rate was higher than resistance to colistin, but evidence showed the efficiency of colistin against Gram-negative bacilli. Most of the isolates were strong biofilm producers, and this was correlated with the extensively drug-resistant pattern of bacteria. The evidence shows that Ventilator-associated pneumonia is a critical infection. According to the findings, there is a high rate of biofilm formation and consequent drug resistance among bacterial causes of Ventilator-associated pneumonia, which needs new insights for preventing and controlling this healthcare problem.

42890012.title: A Rare Mechanism of Hypoxemia: A Case Report.
42890012.abstract: The leading causes of hypoxemia and acute respiratory failure commonly observed in the intensive care unit setting are ventilator/perfusion mismatch and intrapulmonary shunt. The main objective of the current report was to describe the treatment and the diagnostic procedures in a patient with methemoglobinemia. A 66-year-old woman arrived at the emergency department after suddenly losing coordination while walking and reported having experienced increased cough and sputum in the previous days. The patient, a current smoker with 35 pack-years, had comorbidities and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, requiring long-term oxygen therapy. Extensive laboratory analyses revealed elevated methemoglobin (MetHb) levels, increasing from 10% upon admission to 25% of total hemoglobin (Hb), and the onset of post-surgical anemia (Hb 9.6 g/dL). In the present case, the hypoxemia was caused by an increase in MetHb levels, in addition to anemia due to surgical intervention and overhydration. Antibiotic and diuretic therapy for treating infection and right heart failure was effective, leading to a favorable postoperative course.

42932768.title: FDA-Authorized AI/ML Tool for Sepsis Prediction: Development and Validation.
42932768.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition that demands prompt treatment for improved patient outcomes. Its heterogenous presentation makes early detection challenging, highlighting the need for effective risk assessment tools. Artificial intelligence (AI) models could potentially identify patients with sepsis, but none have previously been authorized by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for commercial use. This study outlines the development and validation of the Sepsis ImmunoScore, the first FDA-authorized AI-based software designed to identify patients at risk of sepsis. In this prospective study, we enrolled adult patients (18+ years of age) suspected of infection, as indicated by a blood culture order, from five U.S. institutions between April 2017 and July 2022. The participants were divided into an algorithm development cohort (n=2366), an internal validation cohort (n=393), and an external validation cohort (n=698). The primary end point was sepsis presence (as defined by Sepsis-3) within 24 hours of test initiation. Secondary end points included length of hospital stay, intensive care unit (ICU) admission within 24 hours, mechanical ventilation use within 24 hours, vasopressor use within 24 hours, and in-hospital mortality. The Sepsis ImmunoScore demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy, with an area under the curve of 0.85 (0.83 to 0.87) in the derivation cohort, 0.80 (0.74 to 0.86) in internal validation, and 0.81 (0.77 to 0.86) in external validation. The scores were categorized into four sepsis risk levels with corresponding likelihood ratios: low (0.1), medium (0.5), high (2.1), and very high (8.3). These risk categories also predicted in-hospital mortality: low (0.0%), medium (1.9%), high (8.7%), and very high (18.2%) in the external validation cohort. Similar trends were observed for other metrics, such as length of hospital stay, ICU utilization, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressor use. The Sepsis ImmunoScore demonstrated high accuracy for the identification and prediction of sepsis and critical illness metrics that could enable prompt identification of patients at high risk of sepsis and adverse outcomes, potentially improving clinical decision-making and patient outcomes. (Funded by the Defense Threat Reduction Agency and others.).

42822213.title: Lung ultrasound findings in ARDS based on the 2023 global definition: Characteristics and prognostic value of different LUS scores.
42822213.abstract: The primary objective was to describe the distribution characteristics of lung ultrasound (LUS) findings in patients meeting the 2023 global definition of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The secondary, exploratory aim was to evaluate the prognostic association of LUS scores with 28-day mortality. This prospective study included 224 patients admitted to the ICU/EICU of Ningxia Medical University General Hospital from January to September 2025. LUS signs (regional/total scores, pleural line abnormalities) were collected within 24 h of admission. Prognostic value was assessed using ROC curve analysis. The 28-day mortality rate was 29.46% (66/224). Total LUS aeration score correlated positively with pleural line abnormalities (r = 0.505, P < 0.001). Survivors showed higher proportions of A-lines and normal pleural lines, while non-survivors had more fused B-lines. Pleural line abnormalities showed the strongest exploratory association with 28-day mortality (AUC = 0.617, 95% CI: 0.550-0.681, P = 0.008). Early LUS signs differ significantly between survivors and non-survivors among patients meeting the 2023 ARDS definition. Pleural line abnormalities showed an exploratory association with 28-day mortality, suggesting potential value for bedside risk stratification.This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Registration Number:ChiCTR2600117533).

42823008.title: Emergency Burn Resuscitation: Where Evidence Meets Practice.
42823008.journal: Emergency medicine clinics of North America
42823008.abstract: The initial management of a critically ill burn patient sets the trajectory for their entire hospital course. Understanding standards of care is essential, but moving beyond rote formulas for airway management, fluids, and analgesia is critical to ensuring appropriate care and preventing iatrogenic harm. This article provides an evidence-based guide for emergency physicians on when and how to pivot from standard care to nuanced, life-saving interventions that address the dynamic pathophysiology of severe burns.

42821856.title: Perceived Competence and Educational Gaps in ECMO Nursing: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Survey in Italy.
42821856.journal: Dimensions of critical care nursing : DCCN
42821856.abstract: To evaluate the perceived competence, clinical experience and training needs of Italian nurses involved in ECMO patient care. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in 12 accredited ECMO centers across Italy, targeting ICU nurses with at least 6 months of ECMO experience. The questionnaire assessed perceived competence, procedural exposure, emergency preparedness, nontechnical skills, and training background. Among 162 respondents, most reported adequate perceived competence regarding ECMO indications and monitoring. However, practical experience with procedures such as cannulation, circuit change, and interhospital transfer was limited. Confidence in managing emergencies without immediate perfusionist support was low. Preferred training modalities included simulation and on-the-job coaching. Nontechnical skills such as teamwork and critical thinking were widely recognized as essential. The study reveals a substantial gap between perceived theoretical competence and practical readiness among ECMO nurses in Italy. Training variability and lack of formal curricular structures contribute to limited preparedness, especially for emergency management. Standardized, simulation-based training programs should be implemented nationally to improve ECMO nursing competence, focusing on emergency scenarios and nontechnical skills. Establishing certification pathways may enhance professional recognition and safety in ECMO care.

42911227.title: Transfer timing is not independently associated with ECMO utilization in outborn congenital diaphragmatic hernia: a severity-adjusted analysis.
42911227.abstract: To evaluate whether time from birth to arrival at a tertiary extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)-capable center is independently associated with ECMO utilization among outborn neonates with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). We hypothesized that longer transfer intervals would be associated with greater ECMO utilization after adjustment for disease severity and anatomic characteristics. We performed a retrospective cohort study of outborn neonates with CDH transferred to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit with ECMO capability. Transfer interval was analyzed using multivariable logistic regression adjusting for CDHSG postnatal score and anatomic characteristics. Among 46 neonates, 21 (45.7%) required ECMO and 25 (54.3%) did not. Infants requiring ECMO had greater CDHSG postnatal scores and more frequent intrathoracic liver herniation. After adjustment, transfer time was not independently associated with ECMO utilization (aOR 0.79, 95% CI 0.50-1.23). Intrathoracic liver herniation remained independently associated (aOR 8.65, 95% CI 1.52-49.38), whereas CDHSG score did not reach statistical significance. Within the transfer intervals observed, transfer time was not independently associated with ECMO utilization. These findings suggest that transport duration alone may be less informative than underlying disease characteristics in this cohort.

42955372.title: Early echocardiographic hemodynamic phenotypes and clinical outcomes in congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
42955372.abstract: Early postnatal hemodynamic adaptation may contribute to outcome heterogeneity in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). We evaluated whether echocardiography-defined hemodynamic phenotypes within 24 h of birth were associated with cardiorespiratory severity and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or death. This retrospective cohort included infants with CDH admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit from 2021 to 2025 who underwent echocardiography within 24 h. Phenotypes were classified as no/mild pulmonary hypertension (PH), right ventricular (RV)-predominant PH, or left ventricular (LV)-involved PH based on ventricular function and ductal/atrial shunt direction. Associations with prenatal severity, respiratory indices, and ECMO or death were assessed. Among 66 infants, 21 had no/mild PH, 22 RV-predominant PH, and 23 LV-involved PH. ECMO or death occurred in 0%, 27.3%, and 65.2%, respectively (P < 0.001). Compared with RV-predominant PH, LV-involved PH was associated with greater respiratory severity and more frequent LV dysfunction; observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio (O/E LHR) did not differ significantly between these two groups. Ordinal phenotype severity remained associated with ECMO or death after adjustment for O/E LHR (odds ratio (OR), 5.98; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.76-20.31; P = 0.004). However, the comparison between LV-involved and RV-predominant PH was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for O/E LHR (OR, 3.42; 95% CI, 0.87-15.10). Early hemodynamic phenotype was associated with cardiorespiratory severity and ECMO or death in CDH. LV-involved PH identified a high-risk phenotype and may complement prenatal anatomic risk stratification, although its independent prognostic value beyond prenatal lung size requires validation. • Prenatal lung size and liver herniation are established markers of disease severity and outcome in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). • Pulmonary hypertension and ventricular dysfunction contribute substantially to early cardiorespiratory instability and adverse outcomes in infants with CDH. • Early echocardiographic phenotypes were associated with cardiorespiratory severity and ECMO or death. • LV-involved PH identified a high-risk phenotype, although its prognostic value beyond prenatal severity remains uncertain.

42966843.title: Seasonal dynamics and prognostic determinants of respiratory failure in critically ill adults: a multicenter retrospective observational study in Northern China.
42966843.abstract: Respiratory failure is a common and severe syndrome in critical care, associated with poor prognosis, and its incidence and healthcare burden among critically ill patients are increasing. This study aimed to investigate seasonal patterns of respiratory failure admissions and their associations with meteorological factors and to evaluate the contributions of clinical and meteorological features to model-predicted in-hospital mortality. This multicenter retrospective observational study included adults with respiratory failure admitted to emergency intensive care units (EICUs) between 2022 and 2024. Clinical and meteorological datasets were linked based on admission time and regional location. Seasonal trends were analyzed using seasonal-trend decomposition with Loess (STL), while quasi-poisson generalized additive models (QP-GAMs) and distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs) were used to examine meteorological effects. A random forest model combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to quantify global and individual feature contributions to model-predicted in-hospital mortality. Among 1,837 critically ill patients with respiratory failure, 57.8% were male, with a median age of 66 years; 34.2% had hypoxemic type and 64.1% hypercapnic type, with overall in-hospital mortality of 54.3%. STL analysis revealed marked seasonal variation, peaking in winter and reaching a minimum in summer. QP-GAMs and DLNMs suggested nonlinear and lagged associations of temperature and relative humidity with monthly respiratory failure admission counts. In the random forest model, age and mechanical ventilation had the largest mean absolute SHAP values, followed by other clinical features. This study revealed nonlinear and lagged associations between meteorological factors and monthly respiratory failure admissions, with the highest admission counts observed in winter, followed by spring. In the fitted random forest model, clinical and physiological features contributed more to mortality predictions than meteorological variables.

42967154.title: Responsible use of new antibiotics for critically ill patients suffering from infections due to carbapenem-resistant organisms-a narrative review for an enablement strategy.
42967154.abstract: Infections caused by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative (MDR-GN) bacteria, particularly carbapenem-resistant organisms (CROs), constitute a significant burden in critically ill patients (CIPs). A multidisciplinary, collaborative approach is essential for responsible antibiotic use in CIPs, balancing the necessity for effective treatment with mitigation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). While the efficacy of existing antibiotics against CROs is increasingly limited due to resistance development and suboptimal pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic properties, several barriers impede the widespread adoption of new agents, including selective susceptibility testing, limited availability, high costs, and concerns regarding the fostering of resistance. Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) strategies aim to optimize antibiotic use; however, there is an ongoing debate between restrictive and enabling approaches for new antibiotics in CIPs with CRO infections. While restrictive strategies focus on limiting antibiotic use to mitigate resistance, they may delay necessary treatment and negatively impact professional culture. Enablement strategies promote informed decision-making and accessibility when needed but require substantial workforce and expertise. In this narrative review and expert opinion, we propose an algorithm supporting a coordinated AMS approach in CIPs, emphasizing the importance of early diagnosis and appropriate therapy. We advocate for an enablement strategy for new antibiotics in CIPs with MDR-GN infections, aiming to reduce mortality and toxicity associated with older agents. This strategy should be integrated into local AMS programmes under the guidance of experienced clinicians.

42966832.title: Aggression in Psychiatric High and Intensive Care Wards: A Mixed Methods Study of Incidence and Professionals' Reflections.
42966832.journal: Administration and policy in mental health
42966832.abstract: This mixed methods study investigates aggression in acute psychiatric care, focusing on both incidence and professional reflections across 23 High and Intensive Care wards in the Netherlands. Using a sequential explanatory design, quantitative data on aggressive incidents were collected over 12 months and followed by qualitative focus groups with nurses and team leaders. Aggression, predominantly physical and often targeting staff, was frequently reported, while the cause of incidents was unknown in 31.6% of cases, highlighting the need for improved risk management and early recognition. Despite an emphasis on de-escalation, restrictive measures remained predominant, and emotional consequences for staff, such as humiliation and trauma, were significant. Team culture and management's response to incidents, especially through structured reporting and reflection, were identified as key factors in improving care quality and safety. The findings underscore the importance of fostering a supportive team culture, implementing proactive risk management strategies, and encouraging multidisciplinary collaboration. This study provides practical guidance for clinicians, nurses, and managers in acute psychiatric care, aiming to reduce aggression and enhance both staff and patient well-being. Finally, the results highlight areas where further research is needed, particularly regarding the causes of aggression and the effectiveness of preventive interventions.

42967146.title: Listeria monocytogenes Sepsis With Meningitis Complicating Biologic Immunosuppression in a Patient With Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Secondary to Adult-Onset Still's Disease: A Case Report.
42967146.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) are treated with potent immunosuppression, including high-dose corticosteroids and biologic agents such as anakinra, which can result in an increased risk of opportunistic infections such as listeriosis (infection with Listeria monocytogenes (L. monocytogenes)). This case report describes a 34-year-old man on a background of AOSD receiving escalated doses of steroids and anakinra for a probable flare-up of HLH. Whilst inpatient, he developed high-grade pyrexia (39.3°C), acute confusion, and neurological deterioration, requiring admission to the ICU for intubation and ventilatory support. Investigations revealed blood cultures positive for L. monocytogenes, and lumbar puncture findings were consistent with acute bacterial meningitis. The patient clinically improved with targeted antimicrobial therapy and was successfully extubated, with subsequent normalisation of his inflammatory markers. He was discharged with a planned taper of his immunosuppressive therapy. This case emphasises the synergistic risk of infection associated with biologic therapy and high-dose corticosteroid use and the importance of maintaining a low threshold for considering listeriosis in immunocompromised patients, particularly in the presence of neurological deterioration.

42967138.title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
42967138.abstract: To evaluate the effects of preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine on postoperative myocardial injury biomarkers in patients undergoing on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG were assigned to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg) or saline 30 min before bedtime on the night before surgery and again 30 min before anesthesia induction. The primary outcome was serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) at 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included perioperative cardiac biomarkers, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative delirium, and adverse events. For the prespecified primary outcome, hs-cTnT concentrations at 24 h after surgery were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (estimated marginal means, 170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L; P < 0.001). Postoperative creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) concentrations were also lower in the dexmedetomidine group (all P < 0.05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P = 0.030), although between-group differences at individual postoperative time points were not significant. The dexmedetomidine group had higher Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire scores (62 [60-64] vs 44 [41-50]; P < 0.001) and a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (14.3% vs 37.1%; P = 0.029). Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups. In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500111431.

42967404.title: Impact of early microbiology laboratory activation on rapid diagnosis and antimicrobial optimization in a sepsis alert pathway.
42967404.abstract: Rapid microbiological diagnosis is important in sepsis, but the contribution of early microbiology laboratory activation (EMLA) within sepsis alert pathways is unclear. We prospectively included consecutive adults with sepsis alert activation at a tertiary-care hospital between November 2022 and June 2023. EMLA was defined as direct telephone notification of the on-call microbiologist after sepsis alert activation. The primary outcome was etiological microbiological diagnosis within 24 hours. Secondary outcomes included rapid diagnostic techniques, antimicrobial de-escalation and time to de-escalation. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between EMLA and early diagnosis, adjusting for Charlson Comorbidity Index, septic shock, clinical service, and infection focus. Among 327 patients, an etiological diagnosis was established in 209 (63.9%); EMLA was documented in 213 (65.1%). Diagnosis within 24 hours was achieved in 127/213 (59.6%) patients with EMLA versus 40/114 (35.1%) without EMLA (p < 0.001). EMLA remained independently associated with early diagnosis (adjusted OR 2.99, 95% CI 1.80-4.98; p < 0.001). Rapid diagnostic techniques were used more frequently with EMLA (54.5% vs 43.0%, p = 0.045). De-escalation occurred in 171 patients (52.3%) and was performed earlier with EMLA (median 3 [IQR 2-4]. vs 4 [IQR 3-5]. days, p = 0.030). DOT, mortality, ICU admission, and hospital length of stay did not differ significantly. EMLA was independently associated with earlier microbiological diagnosis and antimicrobial de-escalation. These findings suggest that direct clinician-microbiologist communication may therefore be an important organizational component of diagnostic stewardship in sepsis.

42967102.title: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation With Ventricular Unloading in Fulminant Influenza A (H1N1) Perimyocarditis: A Case Report.
42967102.abstract: Fulminant perimyocarditis is an uncommon cause of cardiogenic shock and refractory cardiac arrest. We describe Influenza A (H1N1)-associated perimyocarditis managed with a stepwise extracorporeal resuscitation strategy. A 54-year-old woman presented with chest pain, hypoxemia, and cardiogenic shock. Electrocardiography (ECG) showed diffuse ST-segment elevation. Echocardiography revealed severe biventricular dysfunction and a fibrinous pericardial effusion and coronary angiography excluded obstructive disease. Despite vasoactive support and mechanical circulatory support with microaxial flow pump Impella CP (flow 2.7 L/min.), she deteriorated to Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) Stage E with pulseless electrical activity (PEA). During automated chest compressions, mechanical circulatory support with femoral Impella CP was rapidly escalated to venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). Respiratory polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was positive for Influenza A (H1N1) virus. Antiviral therapy, heparin anticoagulation, ventilation, and organ support were instituted. Hemodynamics stabilized, lactate cleared, and neurological examination after decannulation was intact. Progressive myocardial recovery permitted VA-ECMO explant on Day 3 and Impella CP removal 24 h thereafter. She was extubated on Day 6 and discharged from intensive care unit (ICU) on Day 10. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging confirmed myocarditis; echocardiography at follow-up showed preserved biventricular function. In fulminant perimyocarditis with refractory arrest, rapid activation of an extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) pathway with early VA-ECMO-combined with ventricular unloading-can bridge to myocardial recovery and favorable neurological outcome. Regional systems enabling safe transfer under continuous cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) are critical.

42968127.title: Age-weighted red cell distribution width index for predicting mortality in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure: a retrospective cohort study.
42968127.abstract: Acute respiratory failure (ARF) represents one of the most common critical illnesses in intensive care units (ICUs), with persistently high mortality rates. Red cell distribution width (RDW) has demonstrated value in predicting prognosis of respiratory diseases; however, conventional RDW fails to account for age-related effects on red blood cell morphology. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the Age-Weighted RDW Index (AWRI) in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure. This retrospective cohort study utilized data from the eICU Collaborative Research Database, enrolling 24,709 ICU patients with acute respiratory failure after sequential exclusion. AWRI was defined as RDW × (1 + age/100). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and five machine learning algorithms with SHAP-based interpretability were applied to evaluate the independent prognostic value and nonlinear risk patterns of AWRI. Among 24,709 patients (median age 66.0 years; 54.0% male), in-hospital mortality was 18.8%. AWRI was independently associated with mortality in the fully adjusted model (Q4 vs. Q1: HR 1.42, 95% CI 1.28-1.59, P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis identified a significant nonlinear relationship with two key thresholds: AWRI ≤ 16.3% was associated with markedly reduced mortality risk (HR 0.453, 95% CI 0.281-0.730) and AWRI ≥ 27% with persistently elevated risk (HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.22-1.40). In machine learning analysis, AWRI ranked as the highest-importance predictor among 17 routine admission variables (mean |SHAP| = 0.30), and the XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.748, outperforming APACHE IV (AUC = 0.670, P < 0.001). AWRI demonstrated superior discrimination compared with conventional RDW (AUC 0.608 vs. 0.572, P < 0.001). AWRI independently predicts in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure, outperforming both conventional RDW and APACHE IV in discriminative ability and achieving comparable performance to SOFA-2 from a single routine blood count. Its clinically interpretable nonlinear risk thresholds and highest-ranked machine learning importance support integration into routine risk stratification at ICU admission.

42969318.title: Clinico-epidemiological Spectrum of Candidemia in the Intensive Care Unit: A Prospective Observational Study from a Tertiary Care Center of Central India.
42969318.abstract: Candidemia represents the most common healthcare-associated bloodstream infection globally, with significant morbidity and mortality in intensive care units (ICUs). This study aimed to evaluate the clinico-epidemiological characteristics, species distribution, antifungal susceptibility patterns, and mortality predictors of ICU-acquired candidemia from a tertiary care hospital in Central India. The prospective observational study enrolled adult patients (≥18 years) admitted to the ICU with clinical sepsis. ICU-acquired candidemia was defined as a positive blood culture for Candida species developing ≥48 h after ICU admission. Demographic data, risk factors, antibiotic susceptibility, and clinical outcomes were systematically recorded. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 25.0. Among 1128 ICU patients with clinical sepsis admitted during the study period, 55 developed candidemia (55/1128, 4.88%). Nonalbicans Candida (NAC) species predominated (81.8%), with Candida parapsilosis being the most common (30.9%), followed by Candida tropicalis (27.3%), and Candida albicans (18.2%). The major risk factors included Foley catheterization (100%), recent antibiotic exposure (67.3%), diabetes (56.4%), chronic kidney disease (CKD)/dialysis, and central venous catheterization (38.2% each). Significant antifungal resistance was observed in NAC species, particularly Candida auris and Candida guilliermondii, showing complete resistance to fluconazole and voriconazole. Overall mortality was 23.6%, with Candida glabrata showing 100% mortality. Factors significantly associated with mortality on univariate analysis included diabetes (P = 0.003), CKD requiring dialysis (P = 0.001), mechanical ventilation (P < 0.001), and central venous catheterization (P < 0.001). This study demonstrates a significant epidemiological shift toward NAC species in ICU-acquired candidemia, with emerging multidrug-resistant pathogens posing therapeutic challenges. Enhanced infection control measures, routine susceptibility testing, and species-specific treatment strategies are essential for improving patient outcomes.

42968548.title: Use of a molecular syndromic panel for the etiological diagnosis of bloodstream infections in critically ill patients: impact on clinical outcomes and antimicrobial use from a multicenter, prospective study.
42968548.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSI) frequently occur in critically ill patients and remain associated with high mortality rates. A prospective, observational, multicenter investigation was carried out through the MULTI-SITA platform to evaluate how the addition of a molecular syndromic panel, the BIOFIRE® Blood Culture Identification 2 (BCID2) Panel (BCID2 panel), to conventional blood culture diagnostics influenced key clinical endpoints and antimicrobial use. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality within 30 days following the onset of BSI. Among the 126 included critically ill patients with BSI, multivariable analysis identified SOFA score (hazard ratio [HR] 1.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-1.34, p < 0.001), other concomitant infections requiring antibiotic therapy (HR 2.61, 95% CI 1.18-5.79, p = 0.018), and BSI caused by Acinetobacter spp. (HR 4.35, 95% CI 1.10-17.18, p = 0.036), Staphylococcus aureus (HR 3.38, 95% CI 1.26-9.08, p = 0.016), or Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (HR 15.97, 95% CI 2.43-104.54, p = 0.004) as associated with increased mortality, while no association was observed between use of the BCID2 panel and mortality (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.42-2.25, p = 0.941). In secondary analyses, the use of the BCID2 panel resulted in more events of either early antimicrobial de-escalation or initiation of appropriate therapy at day one from BSI onset compared with a standard blood culture workflow (55.6% vs. 31.7%, p = 0.015). In critically ill patients with BSI, implementation of a molecular syndromic panel influenced antimicrobial management decisions without affecting mortality. Additional investigations are warranted to clarify the long-term antimicrobial stewardship implications of treatment strategies guided by molecular syndromic panels-based diagnostic workflows.

42971690.title: Machine learning prediction of 30-day mortality in adults with a positive blood culture.
42971690.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
42971690.abstract: A positive blood culture is a clinically heterogeneous finding that may represent true bloodstream infection, transient bacteremia or contamination-diagnostic uncertainty that complicates early clinical decision-making. We aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning models to predict 30-day all-cause mortality in adults with a positive blood culture. Retrospective cohort study using MIMIC-IV. Adult hospitalizations with at least one positive blood culture were included (first positive culture per admission); potential contaminants were retained to reflect real-world uncertainty. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, organ support and microbiological variables were used as predictors. Nine supervised machine learning algorithms were trained with repeated 10-fold cross-validation, evaluated in an independent test cohort and calibrated; thresholds were optimized with the Youden index. Of 5731 episodes, 742 patients (12.9%) died within 30 days. Test-set ROC AUC ranged from 0.759 to 0.801. After threshold optimization, the random forest model showed the best overall performance (sensitivity 0.788, specificity 0.707, balanced accuracy 0.748; Brier score 0.0999, calibration slope 1.03). ICU admission at onset, mechanical ventilation, bilirubin, urea and the Charlson comorbidity index were the main predictors. Machine learning models can provide clinically meaningful early prediction of 30-day mortality in patients with a positive blood culture using routinely available data. Focusing on the moment of blood culture positivity rather than established sepsis syndromes, this approach supports early risk stratification in a diagnostically heterogeneous population.

42971097.title: V-V ECMO for refractory near-fatal asthma: A 12-year single-centre observational study of clinical outcomes and psychological impact.
42971097.abstract: To review the clinical data of adult patients receiving veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) for near-fatal asthma at a single UK respiratory ECMO centre, including morbidity and mortality follow up. Retrospective single-centre case series (2013-2025). A specialized UK respiratory ECMO centre. 79 adult patients with near-fatal asthma refractory to maximal conventional critical care management including mechanical ventilation. Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. 79 patients (median age 35 years, 53% female and 47% male) were included. Pre-ECMO physiological derangement was profound (median pH 7.05, PaCO2 14.7 kPa). Median ECMO duration was 3 days (IQR 2-4). Survival to ICU discharge and 6-month survival was 98.7%. Complications occurred in 27.8% of patients, most frequently acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy (10.1%). At 6-month follow-up, clinically significant anxiety and depression were present in 27.9% and 20.9% of survivors, respectively, while 37.2% screened positive for post-traumatic stress symptoms. Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) represents an effective rescue therapy for patients with refractory near-fatal asthma, demonstrating excellent short- and long-term survival outcomes when applied in carefully selected cases. The incidence of complications remains acceptable and manageable within this context. The prevalence of anxiety and depression in this cohort appears to be lower than that reported in a published systematic review of the broader ECMO population; however, rates of post-traumatic stress symptoms are comparatively higher.

42970133.title: Individualized treatment effects of high flow nasal oxygen in immunocompromised patients.
42970133.abstract: High flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) has become a common first-line practice for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (ARF). In immunocompromised patients, ARF is the leading cause of ICU admission, yet a randomized trial found no overall benefit of HFNO in this population. To assess whether baseline characteristics influence HFNO's effectiveness in preventing invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in immunocompromised patients with ARF. A causal forest machine-learning algorithm was derived in the HIGH trial (776 patients randomized to HFNO or conventional oxygen) to predict the HFNO effects on day-28 IMV incidence. Patients with a "do-not-intubate" order (n = 72) were excluded. Model performance was validated through 500 bootstrap iterations and patients were categorized into terciles based on predicted HFNO benefit. Transportability of the model was assessed in an independent observational cohort (818 patients). Among the 704 participants, HFNO's average effect on day-28 IMV was not significant. However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment responses was identified (predicted benefit: from 20.2% [IQR 15.5%-23.9%] absolute IMV risk reduction with HFNO to 7.4% risk reduction [2.9%-11.2%] with conventional oxygen). Patients with the highest predicted benefit were older, more frequently solid organ transplant recipients, less neutropenic, more severely hypoxemic/tachycardic, but with lower non-respiratory sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores. In this subgroup, HFNO was associated with a significant lower incidence of IMV. In the observational cohort, the benefit-ranking performance was preserved, although absolute effect estimates were less calibrated. These results suggest HFNO might benefit specific immunocompromised patients with ARF. Further prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

42970120.title: Severe ARDS and secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis complicating a flare of adult-onset Still's disease: a case-based review.
42970120.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic inflammatory disorder in which parenchymal lung disease is an increasingly recognised complication, and macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) - that is, haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) secondary to an autoinflammatory or autoimmune condition (MAS-HLH) is a well-established one. Both carry disproportionately high morbidity and mortality. Although AOSD-associated lung disease and MAS-HLH are increasingly recognised as co-occurring manifestations of the same hyperinflammatory process, their combination, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) as the most severe form of lung involvement, remain under-reported. We report a 42-year-old woman with a background of AOSD who developed severe ARDS in the context of a five-week interruption of conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) around incision and drainage of a perianal abscess with complicating fistulous disease and a flare during that period. She developed severe hypoxaemic respiratory failure requiring intubation on the day of admission and later prone positioning, subsequently complicated by development of MAS-HLH, evidenced by hyperferritinaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia, fever and bone marrow-confirmed haemophagocytosis. Her disease trajectory was further complicated by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) reactivation. Management required sequential multi-target immunomodulation with corticosteroids, anakinra, ruxolitinib, tocilizumab and rituximab. She was mechanically ventilated for 19 days in intensive care and discharged from ICU on day 34 and from hospital following clinical stabilisation on day 73. This case illustrates that AOSD-related pulmonary disease can present as fulminant ARDS rather than the more indolent infiltrative patterns typically described and may be associated with other manifestations of AOSD including MAS-HLH. Because of concomitant infection and viral reactivation, the illness could not be attributed to AOSD alone. The case also describes survival following early multidisciplinary, multi-target immunomodulation delivered alongside antimicrobial cover, although the overlapping use of several agents precludes any conclusion about their individual or combined efficacy.

42969834.title: Evaluation of early hydrocortisone use for hemodynamic shock in adult burn patients with suspected critical illness related corticosteroid insufficiency.
42969834.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
42969834.abstract: Critical illness-related corticosteroid insufficiency (CIRCI) presents as refractory hemodynamic shock in critically ill patients. Research on CIRCI and its treatment in burn patients is limited. We sought to review the use of corticosteroids in a burn population during their first week of hospitalization. The burn registry and the electronic medical records were queried for burn patients admitted between January 2015 and December 2025. The following variables were abstracted: demographics, burn history, hospital course, and treatments. Outcome variables included length of stay (LOS), infections, graft loss, pharmacological treatment, and mortality. The two groups were compared with Student's T-test and Chi Square where appropriate. A multivariant analysis was performed to determine independent predictors of CIRCI, infection and mortality. Significance was determined at p<0.05 level. The study group consisted of 87 patients in hemodynamic shock receiving vasopressors, with 47 also receiving corticosteroids. The corticosteroid group had larger burns (37.6 v 25.1%), more resuscitation (15.9 v 8.1 L), more vasopressor days (6.23 v 3.7 d), more ventilator days (19.72 v 7.83 d), more infections (66% v 34%) and longer LOS (51.53 v 26.05 d), all p<0.05. On multivariant analysis, variables independently related to the diagnosis of CIRCI were age and resuscitation fluids; to infection were corticosteroid use; and to mortality were age. Overall, over 50% of patients in hypotensive shock during their first week of treatment were diagnosed and treated with corticosteroids for suspected CIRCI. More study is needed to determine the appropriate role of corticosteroid use in early burn treatment.

42969594.title: Seven versus 14 days of polymyxin-based therapy for ventilator-associated pneumonia due to carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii : A randomised feasibility trial.
42969594.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
42969594.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) due to carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii ( CRAB ) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality in intensive care units (ICUs), yet the optimal antibiotic duration of therapy remains uncertain. We compared outcomes of 7-day versus 14-day polymyxin-based therapy for CRAB-VAP. We conducted a single-centre, open-label, randomised feasibility trial in a tertiary-care respiratory ICU from March 2017 to October 2024. Patients with microbiologically confirmed CRAB-VAP who met predefined clinical stability criteria on day 7 were randomised 1:1 to either discontinue antibiotics on day 7 or continue treatment for 14 days. Treatment comprised intravenous colistin or polymyxin B with adjunctive nebulised colistin. The primary outcome was relapse of CRAB-VAP. Secondary outcomes included antibiotic-free days through day 28, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU and hospital length of stay, and 28-day all-cause mortality. We randomised 41 patients (7-day n = 22; 14-day n = 19). Relapse occurred in 1 (4.5%) versus 2 (10.5%) patients (risk ratio [RR] 0.43; 95% CI: 0.04, 4.31) in the 7-day versus 14-day groups, respectively. The 7-day group had more antibiotic-free days (mean difference: 6.9 days; 95% CI: 5.1, 8.7 days). Acute kidney injury occurred in 0% versus 31.6% (RR 0.07; 95% CI: 0.004, 1.15). Other outcomes, including 28-day mortality (45.5 vs 63.2%; RR 0.72; 95% CI: 0.40, 1.30), were similar. In clinically improving CRAB-VAP, a 7-day discontinuation strategy was feasible. Clinical outcome estimates, including relapse and mortality, were imprecise and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. These findings support evaluation in larger, adequately powered multicentre trials.

42968383.title: Prognostic Performance of PaO2/FIO2 versus SpO2/FIO2 Ratios in Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure.
42968383.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42968383.abstract: Concurrently measured PaO2/FIO2 (PF) and SpO2/FIO2 (SF) exhibit moderate-to-high correlation. However, their performance for risk stratification when using PF if available, or SF if not, as operationalized in recent acute respiratory distress (ARDS) and sequential organ failure assessment score (SOFA-2) guidance, is unknown. Measure the prognostic performance of PF- and SF-defined hypoxemic respiratory failure severity. We conducted a retrospective observational study of patients receiving invasive or non-invasive mechanical ventilation, or high-flow nasal oxygen across 58 Common Longitudinal ICU data Format (CLIF) consortium hospitals. We used the lowest PF, if available, or SF if not, from the first 24 hours of respiratory support to define ARDS and SOFA-2 severity categories. We characterized risk of in-hospital death or hospice discharge by day 28 by severity category, and evaluated prognostic performance using logistic regression models with area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROC). We then evaluated whether PF- or SF-defined patients' risk of death or hospice differed after adjustment for other patient risk factors. Oxygenation severity was defined with PF in n = 40,820 patients, and SF in n = 16,906. In-hospital death or hospice discharge was higher for PF (33.4%) versus SF (23.4%) patients, overall, and within each severity category. The SF-AUROC was numerically higher (0.60 [95%-CI:0.58-0.61]) than PF-AUROC (0.57 [95%-CI:0.57-0.58]). After adjustment, there was no statistical difference in outcome between PF and SF-defined patients. PF and SF thresholds for severity categories recommended as equivalent in ARDS and SOFA-2 guidance define populations with different mortality, but have similar risk discrimination.

42962929.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions.
authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)
American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)
Asia-Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL)
Latin American Association for the Study of the Liver (ALEH)
Society on Liver Disease in Africa (SOLDA). Electronic address: jasmohan.bajaj@vcuhealth.org
Society on Liver Disease in Africa (SOLDA)
42962929.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.

42970082.title: Refining ECPR candidate selection: from fixed criteria to a dynamic probability-of-benefit framework.
42970082.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a rescue strategy for selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest. However, identifying patients most likely to achieve neurologically meaningful survival remains challenging. Conventional selection criteria, including age, initial rhythm, witnessed arrest, bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), and no-flow and low-flow duration, are clinically useful but may be insufficient when interpreted as isolated thresholds. We conducted a narrative review of contemporary evidence on ECPR patient selection, incorporating randomized trials, observational studies, registries, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and current guideline and consensus recommendations. Evidence was critically evaluated with particular attention to patient-level prognostic factors, arrest setting, dynamic physiological and metabolic variables, ECPR logistics, and system-level determinants of outcome. Current evidence supports a multidimensional rather than single-variable approach to ECPR candidacy. Favorable arrest characteristics, potentially reversible etiology, shorter low-flow duration, and preserved physiological reserve remain important; however, chronological low-flow time should be interpreted alongside the quality and effectiveness of ongoing CPR. Dynamic information-including transient return of spontaneous circulation, lactate kinetics, arterial pH, end-tidal carbon dioxide, and hemodynamic parameters-may further refine assessment of biological viability. Frailty, comorbidity burden, cerebral perfusion, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-related contraindications should also be incorporated into decision-making. Importantly, selection cannot be separated from system performance: Cannulation strategy, transport logistics, institutional experience, and the ability to establish extracorporeal circulation rapidly may substantially modify the likelihood of benefit. Differences between out-of-hospital and in-hospital cardiac arrest further limit the universal application of rigid eligibility criteria. Candidacy for ECPR should be viewed as a dynamic, probability-based assessment rather than a checklist of fixed thresholds. Integrating arrest characteristics, reversibility, evolving physiology, patient reserve, and system capability may provide a more clinically meaningful framework for identifying patients most likely to achieve neurologically favorable survival after ECPR.

42968937.title: Actionable Biomarkers in Acute Exacerbations of COPD: Corticosteroid and Antibiotic Stewardship.
42968937.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
42968937.abstract: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) arise from heterogeneous inflammatory and infectious processes, yet systemic corticosteroids and antibiotics are often prescribed empirically. This narrative review evaluates biomarkers according to the acute treatment decisions they can support, drawing on randomized trials and supporting clinical studies evaluated through August 9, 2026. Blood eosinophils have the most developed evidence for corticosteroid guidance: trials support treatment selection or withholding in primary care and serial treatment shortening after an initial dose in hospitalized patients. C-reactive protein supports antibiotic stewardship most clearly in primary care, with more limited inpatient evidence. Procalcitonin can reduce antibiotic use in selected non-intensive-care inpatients, whereas the intensive-care trial failed to establish non-inferiority for mortality and did not reduce antibiotic exposure. These findings depend on the tested population, sampling time, threshold, and treatment rule. Rapid molecular pathogen tests improve diagnostic yield and turnaround time; their integration into COPD-specific treatment algorithms remains a research priority. Multimarker strategies and acute biologic treatment offer further avenues for investigation, with acute biologic evidence currently derived from a mixed asthma/COPD population. Organizing evidence around a biomarker-decision-population framework separates established stewardship applications from emerging treatment strategies. Clinical utility ultimately depends on whether the complete strategy preserves or improves patient outcomes and can be delivered reliably in routine care.

42968049.title: Efficacy and safety of combined intraventricular/intrathecal and intravenous polymyxin B for postsurgical neurosurgical infections due to MDR/XDR-GNB: a retrospective cohort study.
42968049.abstract: Intracranial infections caused by multidrug-resistant or extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (MDR/XDR-GNB) represent a significant challenge in neurosurgical critical care, with limited effective treatment options. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intraventricular/intrathecal (IVT/ITH) and intravenous polymyxin B in patients with post-neurosurgical MDR/XDR-GNB intracranial infections, focusing on long-term outcomes and neurotoxicity. This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted across seven hospitals in the West China region between December 2019 and June 2021. Patients with culture-confirmed MDR/XDR-GNB intracranial infection were enrolled and divided into two groups based on whether they received IVT/ITH polymyxin B. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality, with secondary outcomes including pathogen clearance rate, neurological status at discharge, and adverse events. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate treatment effects. A total of 70 patients were included, with 24 in the IVT/ITH group and 46 in the control group. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The most common pathogens isolated were Acinetobacter baumannii (67.1%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (24.3%), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (4.3%), with 98.6% of isolates susceptible to polymyxin B. IVT/ITH polymyxin B was associated with significantly improved 90-day survival (adjusted HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.26-0.98) and higher pathogen clearance rates (58.3% vs. 26.7%, p < 0.001). No significant differences in adverse effects, including neurotoxicity, were observed between groups, although a trend toward higher seizure incidence was noted in the IVT/ITH group. IVT/ITH and intravenous administration of polymyxin B significantly improved long-term survival and microbial clearance in patients with MDR/XDR-GNB intracranial infections, with a favorable safety profile. These findings support its use as a promising therapeutic strategy in resource-limited settings where this combined local-systemic regimen is not feasible. This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of West China Hospital, approval number 278.
