42972522.title: Association between the HACOR score and mortality in patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure: a retrospective cohort study.
42972522.abstract: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) is a common critical condition in the intensive care unit (ICU). Accurate early prediction of the risk of death is of great significance for clinical decision-making. Although HACOR score was initially used to predict the failure of non-invasive ventilation in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) patients, the relationship between the HACOR score and the mortality remains unclear. Therefore, a retrospective cohort study was conducted to evaluate the ability of the HACOR score to predict mortality risk in patients with AHRF. Patients diagnosed with AHRF were extracted from the MIMIC-IV database and divided into two groups (low‑risk < 6 vs. high‑risk ≥ 6) based on the median HACOR score. The relationship between the HACOR score and all‑cause mortality at 28, 90, and 365 days was evaluated. To investigate the association between HACOR score and mortality in AHRF patients, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed. This study included 2774 patients (median age 68 years, IQR 57-79; 57.9% male). The mortality rates in the high-risk group (HACOR ≥ 6) were significantly higher than those in the low-risk group (< 6) at 28 days, 90 days, and 365 days (28 days: 38.3% vs. 28.2%, P < 0.001; 90 days: 46.1% vs. 35.7%, P < 0.001; 365 days: 52.5% vs. 44.3%, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that the survival probability of the high-risk group was lower (log-rank P < 0.001). Cox regression analysis indicated that for every 1-point increase in the HACOR score, the risk of death significantly increased (P < 0.001), and restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a linear association between the score and mortality, with a significant threshold effect at HACOR = 6. Subgroup analysis further showed that a HACOR score ≥ 6 was consistently associated with a 28-day mortality rate across various demographic and clinical characteristics (all P < 0.05), reinforcing the robustness of the score. This study confirmed that an increase in the HACOR score was significantly associated with an increased mortality rate at 28 days, 90 days, and 365 days in patients with AHRF. For every 1-point increase in the score, the risk of death increased, and the threshold effect was significant when HACOR = 6. These findings highlight the utility of the HACOR score for risk stratification in clinical practice.

42972291.title: Platelet trajectory patterns and 28-day mortality in ICU stroke patients: a retrospective cohort study based on the MIMIC-IV database.
42972291.abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Platelet abnormalities are common in critically ill patients, but dynamic trajectory patterns and their prognostic value in intensive care unit (ICU) stroke patients remain unclear. This retrospective cohort study included 1,562 ICU stroke patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database (version 3.1). Latent class trajectory models (LCTM) were used to identify platelet trajectory patterns during the first 5 days of ICU admission. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to assess the association between trajectory groups and 28-day mortality. Exploratory effect decomposition analysis was conducted to explore the relative contribution of baseline platelet levels and subsequent platelet decline to prognosis. Four distinct platelet trajectory groups were identified: High-Declining (14.7%), Moderate-Low Stable (52.4%), Low-Rising (4.5%), and Moderate-High Stable (28.4%). The High-Declining group had the highest 28-day mortality (34.1% vs. 20.4% in the Moderate-Low Stable group, P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, the High-Declining group was associated with a 56% increase in mortality risk compared with the Moderate-Low Stable group (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.56, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.17-2.07, P = 0.002). Exploratory effect decomposition analysis revealed a suppression pattern: the direct protective effect of higher Day 2 platelet was offset by an indirect harmful effect mediated through greater subsequent platelet decline (Average Component Mediation Effect [ACME] = 0.017 on the probability-difference scale, 95% CI: 0.010-0.026, P < 0.001), suggesting that rapid platelet decline may reflect a high-risk phenotypic pattern associated with this trajectory group. Platelet trajectory patterns are associated with 28-day mortality and may serve as prognostic indicators in ICU stroke patients. A high baseline platelet level with rapid decline represents the highest-risk phenotype and, if confirmed in future prospective studies, may help identify patients requiring closer clinical evaluation to screen for underlying deteriorating conditions.

42972235.title: Association between thymosin α1 therapy and 28-day mortality risk in critically ill patients with tuberculosis-related sepsis: a retrospective cohort study.
42972235.abstract: Patients with tuberculosis (TB)-related sepsis often experience profound immune dysregulation and poor clinical outcomes. Evidence of immunomodulatory therapeutic efficacy in this population remains limited. We evaluated the association between thymosin α1 (Tα1) use and 28-day all-cause mortality in critically ill TB-related sepsis patients and explored whether the strength of this association varied with the baseline lymphocyte count. This single-centre retrospective cohort study included critically ill, adult TB-related sepsis patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) in 2017-2025. Exposure was any Tα1 use during ICU stay. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Association analyses included multivariable Cox regression, restricted mean survival time (RMST) analyses, and exploratory restricted cubic spline (RCS) modelling. Sensitivity analyses were performed. Among 327 patients, 160 received Tα1 and 167 served as controls. Tα1 use was associated with a lower hazard of 28-day mortality after adjustment for baseline covariates (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.54; 95% confidence interval, 0.36-0.79; P = 0.002); sensitivity analyses showed estimates of similar direction. The proportional hazards assumption was violated; consequent RMST analysis revealed longer adjusted restricted mean survival in the Tα1 group. Exploratory RCS modelling suggested nonlinear variability in the association between Tα1 use and 28-day mortality across baseline lymphocyte counts, which appeared more pronounced at intermediate lymphocyte counts (approximately 0.8-1.2 × 10⁹/L); however, this data-driven pattern is hypothesis-generating. Among ICU patients with TB-related sepsis, Tα1 use was associated with lower observed 28-day mortality, but causality cannot be inferred. The identified variability in this association across baseline lymphocyte counts requires external validation. Not applicable.

42977593.title: Critical Care Management of Patients With Acute Fulminant Myocarditis.
42977593.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42977593.abstract: Fulminant myocarditis is a life-threatening inflammatory cardiac syndrome characterized by severe myocardial injury and abrupt deterioration of cardiac function, leading to rapidly progressive cardiogenic shock. Patients often require intravenous vasoactive therapy and/or temporary mechanical circulatory support to maintain systemic perfusion and prevent multiorgan failure. Although frequently preceded by a viral prodrome and affecting young and healthy individuals, fulminant myocarditis encompasses diverse etiologies, including immune-mediated and toxin-related subtypes, with major implications for diagnosis and treatment. Optimal management relies on early recognition, prompt admission to specialized cardiac intensive care units, and rapid access to advanced diagnostics, including endomyocardial biopsy and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, to confirm myocardial inflammation, exclude ischemic disease, and guide etiology-directed therapy. Hemodynamic stabilization requires tailored use of vasopressors and inotropes while minimizing catecholamine-related arrhythmias and myocardial oxygen demand. For refractory shock, early escalation to temporary mechanical circulatory support, most commonly venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, is central to restore perfusion and provide a bridge to recovery or advanced therapy. Because fulminant myocarditis frequently involves malignant arrhythmias and multiorgan dysfunction, integrated critical care management is essential. This review summarizes a practical intensive care approach to fulminant myocarditis, emphasizing early diagnosis, individualized hemodynamic and device-based support, multiorgan management, and phenotype-driven immunomodulatory treatment strategies.

42976438.title: Real-world outcomes of continuous infusion of sedative agents in critically ill patients with invasive mechanical ventilation.
42976438.abstract: Current guidelines recommend non-benzodiazepine (non-BZD) sedatives -dexmedetomidine (DEX) and propofol (PPF) - over benzodiazepines (BZD) in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, but real-world evidence from Asian patients remains limited. We evaluated the clinical outcomes of different continuous-infusion sedatives in this population in Taiwan. This retrospective cohort study used electronic health records from a tertiary medical center in Taiwan. Adults receiving continuous intravenous sedation within 48 h of intubation were included. Patients with preexisting ventilator dependence, status epilepticus, or prior tracheostomy were excluded. Groups were 1:1 propensity score matched. Outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (LOS), time to extubation, mortality, and total hospitalization cost. Prespecified pairwise comparisons evaluated DEX vs. BZD, PPF vs. BZD, and DEX vs. PPF. Of 2065 eligible patients, 605 matched pairs were analyzed. Compared with BZD, non-BZD sedation was associated with shorter ICU LOS (9.4 vs. 11.9 days, P = 0.032), earlier extubation (4.1 vs. 6.5 days, P = 0.015), and lower hospitalization cost (US$21,559 vs. US$26,258, P < 0.001), without a significant difference in 90-day mortality (36.7% vs. 38.7%, P = 0.489). In pairwise comparisons with BZD, DEX was associated with significantly shorter ICU LOS and time to extubation, whereas the benefit of PPF was primarily a reduction in hospitalization cost. Non-BZD sedatives were associated with shorter ICU LOS, earlier extubation, and lower hospitalization costs without a detectable mortality difference. These findings are consistent with guideline recommendations favoring non-BZD sedation, although residual confounding remains possible.

42973384.title: Effect of Diaphragmatic Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation on Diaphragm Function and Clinical Outcomes in ICU Mechanically Ventilated Patients: A Meta-analysis and Systematic Review.
42973384.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
42973384.abstract: To evaluate the effects of diaphragmatic neuromuscular electrical stimulation (DNMES) on diaphragmatic function and clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated patients in the intensive care unit (ICU). We searched major databases to May 2026 for RCTs. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, assessed bias, and performed meta-analysis; GRADE assessed evidence certainty. Nineteen RCTs (1,437 patients) were included. Meta-analysis showed that DNMES significantly improved diaphragmatic thickening fraction (DTF) (SMD=1.32, 95%CI[0.73, 1.91], P<0.0001), diaphragmatic excursion (DE) (SMD=1.25, 95%CI[0.77, 1.72], P<0.00001), maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) (MD=2.46, 95%CI[1.22, 3.69], P<0.0001), and rapid shallow breathing index (RSBI) (MD=-14.08, 95%CI[-21.38, -6.77], P=0.0002). DNMES also reduced the duration of mechanical ventilation (MD=-2.14, 95%CI[-2.84, -1.43], P<0.00001) and ICU length of stay (MD=-2.30, 95%CI[-2.85, -1.75], P<0.00001), increased weaning success rate (RR=1.29, 95%CI[1.17, 1.42], P<0.00001), and decreased weaning failure rate (RR=0.62, 95%CI[0.49, 0.77], P<0.0001). GRADE evidence quality assessment revealed moderate quality for 2 outcomes, low quality for 3 outcomes, and very low quality for 3 outcomes. DNMES may improve diaphragmatic function and weaning outcomes, shorten ventilation and ICU stay, but the certainty of evidence remains predominantly low to very low due to substantial heterogeneity, high risk of bias, and limited trial reporting; large RCTs are needed.

42975860.title: Contemporary management of severe generalized tetanus: an evidence-based review.
42975860.abstract: Severe generalized tetanus remains associated with substantial mortality despite being vaccine preventable. Management is complicated by limited high-quality evidence, conflicting trial results, and the need to balance effective control of spasms and autonomic dysfunction against the risks of prolonged mechanical ventilation. We describe the management of a 57-year-old man with Ablett grade III generalized tetanus and use this case as a clinical framework for an expert narrative review. The review synthesizes randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, prospective studies, and relevant observational literature addressing neuromodulatory therapy, airway management, autonomic dysfunction, intrathecal antitoxin, and supportive critical care. The patient was managed using a multimodal strategy comprising continuous midazolam infusion, magnesium sulphate, oral baclofen, dexmedetomidine, intramuscular and intrathecal human tetanus immunoglobulin, and meticulous low-stimulation supportive care. Therapy was titrated using serial bedside assessment of neuromuscular burden. He recovered without endotracheal intubation, neuromuscular blockade, or tracheostomy and was discharged on day 21. We argue that discordant findings in tetanus trials are substantially attributable to heterogeneity in disease severity, clinical practice, airway management thresholds, and resource availability, rather than to true therapeutic inconsistency. Available evidence supports a physiology-directed multimodal approach using agents with complementary mechanisms to suppress spasms and autonomic dysfunction while preserving spontaneous ventilation whenever safely feasible. Management of severe tetanus should focus on achieving physiological targets rather than escalating individual drugs. A structured, individualized, multimodal neuromodulatory strategy delivered within an experienced, low-stimulation critical care environment may allow selected patients to be managed without mechanical ventilation; safety cannot be established from a single case and requires prospective evaluation. Greater emphasis should also be placed on preventive adult immunization, as vaccination remains the intervention most likely to reduce the burden of severe tetanus.

42975800.title: Practice variation in mechanical circulatory support: a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of Japanese interventional cardiologists in the CVIT Kyushu-Okinawa chapter.
42975800.abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) practice for cardiogenic shock may vary with institutional resources and operator experience, but data from Japanese interventional cardiologists are limited. We conducted an anonymous cross-sectional survey of 720 members of 83 Japanese Association of Cardiovascular Intervention and Therapeutics (CVIT)-certified or affiliated training hospitals in the CVIT Kyushu-Okinawa Chapter (September-October 2025); 536 returned questionnaires (74.4%), and consent was confirmed for 385 (53.5%). The primary analysis included 276 respondents who had performed intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), or Impella CP insertion within 12 months: 163 at Impella-capable and 113 at non-Impella-capable hospitals. Documented MCS and extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation protocols were more frequently reported by respondents from Impella-capable hospitals (46% vs. 6% and 39% vs. 13%, respectively), as was collaboration with emergency and critical care physicians; no statistically significant difference was detected in perceived need for collaboration. MCS selection varied between groups. At Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock stage C, IABP (44%) and Impella CP (48%) were selected with similar frequency among respondents in Impella-capable hospitals, whereas IABP was selected by 79% in non-Impella-capable hospitals. At stage E, ECPELLA (79%) and VA-ECMO plus IABP (84%) predominated, respectively. Among respondents with device-specific operator experience within 12 months, vascular access and anticoagulation practices varied between groups. Procedural anxiety was lower with higher CVIT qualification; however, 19% of board-certified members reported anxiety about Impella CP insertion and 45% about emergency intubation. These findings identify MCS practice variation across several domains warranting further evaluation.

42973563.title: Dynamic Lactate Trajectories are Associated with Mortality in Severe Pneumonia: A Retrospective Cohort Study with External Validation.
42973563.abstract: Severe pneumonia represents a major threat to survival. Lactate, routinely measured in the intensive care unit (ICU), provides valuable clinical insights. Exploring its dynamic trajectories and their association with outcomes may help guide risk-stratified interventions and optimize management. This retrospective cohort study included patients with severe pneumonia from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database (2008-2022, derivation cohort) and Shanghai General Hospital (2016-2024, external validation cohort). Latent growth mixture modeling (LGMM) was applied to five serial lactate measurements (0, 12, 24, 36, and 48 hours) to identify trajectory subgroups. The outcome was all-cause mortality at 28-, 60-, and 90-days. Associations between trajectories and mortality were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression, with sensitivity analyses including landmark analysis and restricted mean survival time estimation. Discriminative performance was assessed using Harrell's C-index. In the derivation cohort (n = 870), four trajectories were identified: stable-normal (T1, 40.1%), fluctuating-worsening (T2, 7.8%), rapid-resolving (T3, 32.3%), and persistent-abnormal (T4, 19.8%). T2 was associated with the highest adjusted mortality risk at 28 days (HR 2.82, 95% CI 1.93-4.11), 60 days (HR 2.75, 95% CI 1.92-3.93), and 90 days (HR 2.63, 95% CI 1.85-3.73). T4 had the longest mechanical ventilation and ICU stay (p < 0.05). The same four trajectories were reproduced in the external validation cohort (n = 289), and T2 was again independently associated with 90-day mortality (HR 3.02, 95% CI 1.19-7.67, p = 0.02), although the four-group Log rank tests did not reach statistical significance in this smaller cohort. Dynamic lactate trajectories are associated with prognosis in severe pneumonia. The fluctuating-worsening trajectory (T2), in which lactate rose again after an initial decline to values around 7.5 mmol/L, was associated with the highest mortality in this cohort, whereas the persistent-abnormal trajectory (T4) was associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation and ICU stay without a significant increase in adjusted mortality.

42973554.title: Assessing Oxygen Weaning Readiness in NICU Patients Using Oxygen Saturation Histograms: A Systematic Review.
42973554.abstract: Weaning late preterm and term infants from respiratory support remains challenging because clinicians must balance the risks of hyperoxia and hypoxia while determining when room air trials and discharge are appropriate. Oxygen saturation histograms provide an objective method for evaluating oxygenation trends over time, but standardized approaches for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) patients, particularly infants ≥34 weeks' gestation, remain limited. This systematic review evaluated whether oxygen saturation histogram patterns can predict readiness for room air trials or inform discharge decisions in NICU patients receiving nasal continuous positive airway pressure, high-flow nasal cannula, or low-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy. Studies involving infants with major congenital anomalies, postmenstrual age greater than 42 weeks, or invasive mechanical ventilation, intubation, or tracheostomy extending beyond 36 weeks' postmenstrual age in the very low birth weight subgroup were excluded. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across multiple databases from July to December 2024, and two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed risk of bias using a modified Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. Nine studies met the inclusion criteria. Across the available evidence, greater time within target oxygen saturation ranges was associated with readiness for oxygen weaning, whereas excessive time below or outside defined thresholds suggested the need for continued monitoring or respiratory support. However, study populations, saturation thresholds, monitoring durations, and outcome definitions varied substantially, preventing meta-analysis and limiting direct standardization. Oxygen saturation histograms appear promising as an adjunctive tool for guiding oxygen weaning and discharge decisions in NICU patients, but validated thresholds for late preterm and term infants are not yet established. Multicenter prospective studies using consistent histogram definitions, standardized room air trial criteria, and long-term outcome assessment are needed to support individualized and evidence-based respiratory care.

42973509.title: Association of liberal versus restrictive oxygen saturation targets with mortality in mechanically ventilated stroke patients: a multicenter retrospective propensity-matched analysis.
42973509.abstract: Optimal oxygen saturation targets in mechanically ventilated stroke patients remain uncertain. While restrictive oxygen strategies are increasingly adopted in general critical care, their impact in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) are unclear. We evaluated the association between restrictive versus liberal oxygen saturation targets during the first 48 h of mechanical ventilation and short-term mortality in stroke patients. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX database (2006-2026). Adult patients (≥18 years) with a stroke diagnosis who required invasive mechanical ventilation and had documented peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) values within the first 48 h of ventilation were included. Patients were stratified according to early oxygen saturation targets: restrictive (SpO₂ 92-96%) versus liberal (SpO₂ ≥ 97%). Propensity score matching (PSM) by demographics, comorbidities, and stroke severity was performed separately within the combined stroke cohort and prespecified AIS and ICH subgroups to balance demographic and clinical covariates. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 30 and 90 days. Secondary outcomes included 30-day tracheostomy and ventilator-associated pneumonia. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. p-value was set at 0.05. Among 17,207 mechanically ventilated stroke patients, 2,366 received restrictive and 14,841 liberal oxygen saturation targets prior to matching. After PSM, 2,350 patients remained in each group. Restrictive oxygenation during the first 48 h was associated with higher mortality at 1 month (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.03-1.23; p = 0.008) and 3 months (HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02-1.20; p = 0.014). In AIS, restrictive oxygenation was similarly associated with increased mortality at 1 month (HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.11-1.43) and 3 months (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.08-1.37). No statistically significant mortality difference was observed in ICH. Restrictive oxygenation was associated with lower 30-day tracheostomy rates (8.5% vs. 13.1%; RR 0.653, p < 0.001), with no difference in VAP. Restrictive oxygen saturation targets during the first 48 h of mechanical ventilation may be associated with higher short-term mortality in stroke, driven primarily by the AIS group. These findings suggest that early oxygenation strategy may have subtype-specific implications and warrant prospective evaluation in stroke focused randomized trials.

42973200.title: State of the art: thoracic ultrasound.
42973200.abstract: Thoracic ultrasound has continued to expand beyond simple bedside triage into a quantitative, procedure-guiding and increasingly artificial intelligence-augmented tool across pleural and respiratory medicine. This review summarizes the literature published over the past year, highlighting developments in effusion characterization, pneumothorax diagnosis, image-guided pleural procedures, artificial intelligence, training standards, critical care applications, malignant pleural effusion management, and diaphragm/interstitial lung disease assessment. Elastography and contrast-enhanced ultrasound have moved from exploratory to comparative and multicentre randomized evaluation for effusion characterization and biopsy guidance. Meta-analyses have reaffirmed the superiority of point-of-care ultrasound over chest radiography for both pneumothorax and thoracentesis guidance. Artificial intelligence tools have shown that they can close the acquisition-skill gap for novice operators, although automated interpretation (particularly B-line quantification) remains inconsistent against expert consensus. A new UK national training standard for pleural procedures has been published, alongside the first validated thoracic-specific competency assessment tool. A large multicentre randomized trial found that a point-of-care ultrasound-driven diagnostic pathway did not improve early discharge rates in emergency department patients with dyspnoea, an important negative finding. Diaphragm and quantitative lung ultrasound continue to accumulate evidence as noninvasive markers of interstitial lung disease severity and ventilator weaning readiness. The past year's literature confirms thoracic ultrasound's trajectory from a purely diagnostic adjunct towards a quantitative, procedure-integrated and artificial intelligence-supported modality, while also delivering important cautionary and negative findings that temper enthusiasm and clarify where evidence remains immature.

42972966.title: Rapid sequence induction: a narrative review.
42972966.abstract: Pulmonary aspiration of gastric contents remains an important cause of anaesthetic morbidity and mortality, and is important medicolegally. Rapid sequence induction is a multi-element technique designed to mitigate risk in those patients at increased risk of pulmonary aspiration during induction of general anaesthesia. We undertook a narrative review to summarise evidence and evidence gaps focusing on controversial aspects of rapid sequence induction. Despite widespread use of rapid sequence induction, many elements of the technique lack robust evidence and consensus. Nasogastric tubes can be used to reduce gastric content, but do not empty the stomach reliably. Correctly applied cricoid force obstructs the hypopharynx and has a limited impact on airway management, but incorrect application can cause clinically significant difficulties. Correct location of cricoid force may require ultrasound localisation of the cricoid cartilage. Applying the correct force, which varies with age and sex, is improved by education, practice and feedback. The use of videolaryngoscopy during rapid sequence induction is supported by evidence. The role of gastric ultrasound in determining anaesthetic technique is uncertain. Cardiovascular complications of rapid sequence induction are common, particularly in the patients who are critically ill, and modifications to the technique may reduce their frequency and severity. Effective use of airway rescue techniques may require removal of cricoid force. There is insufficient evidence for many of the elements of rapid sequence induction to determine whether they reduce patient harm or to state confidently that they do not. Controversies and evidence gaps should be acknowledged. Despite this, optimal use of rapid sequence induction requires a thorough knowledge of the subject, including areas of uncertainty to guide individualised risk assessment; clinical decision-making; and practical conduct of the technique.

42972526.title: A multicenter comparative study of saline contrast electrical impedance tomography method versus CTPA for the diagnosis of acute pulmonary embolism: a trial protocol.
42972526.abstract: Life-threatening acute pulmonary embolism (PE) requires rapid diagnosis, but the current gold standard, CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA), involves radiation, contrast, and patient transport risks. Bedside saline contrast electrical impedance tomography (EIT) offers non-invasive, radiation-free, rapid assessment of ventilation-perfusion matching and previous case reports and single-center pilot study showed its promising value for diagnosing PE; however, robust multicenter validation is lacking. This multicenter nationwide study aims to further validate the diagnostic performance of saline contrast EIT compared with CTPA for detecting acute PE. This diagnostic test is conducted across multiple hospitals of varying tiers in China. Patients with acute respiratory failure suspected of acute PE will be screened. Within 24 hours, each participant receives both CTPA and saline contrast EIT, the latter involving a bolus injection of either 10 mL 10% NaCl via a central venous catheter or 15 mL 5% NaHCO₃ via a peripheral vein. Using CTPA as the gold standard, saline contrast EIT data are analyzed offline to derive key diagnostic parameters-including dead space percentage, intrapulmonary shunt percentage, and ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) match percentage-whose diagnostic performance for acute PE will be subsequently evaluated. The continuous variables dead space%, intrapulmonary shunt%, and V/Q match% will be assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves with area under the curve calculations to differentiate PE from non-PE patients. Optimal diagnostic thresholds will be determined using the point closest to the top-left corner or maximum Youden's index, followed by calculation of sensitivity, specificity, Youden's index, accuracy, Kappa statistic, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, positive likelihood ratio, and negative likelihood ratio at these thresholds. We hypothesize that in our national multicenter diagnostic trial, parameters derived from saline contrast EIT may exhibit favorable diagnostic performance for CTPA-confirmed PE, particularly massive PE. If this hypothesis is validated, saline contrast EIT could provide prompt, noninvasive, convenient, and rapid bedside evaluation for critically ill patients with clinically suspected PE who are hemodynamically unstable and difficult to transport. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07190079) on 22 September 2025.

42972547.title: Effect of pirfenidone on the short- and long-term outcomes in pulmonary infection-related acute respiratory distress syndrome: a prospective cohort study.
42972547.abstract: Pirfenidone, approved for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), slows lung function decline and reduces fibrosis, including in post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis. Its early use in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains uncertain. This study evaluated the effects of early pirfenidone administration on short- and long-term outcomes in pulmonary infection-related ARDS. In this prospective cohort study, 97 ARDS patients were consecutively recruited and assigned to Pirfenidone (n = 29), Glucocorticoid (n = 38), or Control (n = 30) groups according to the severity and clinical course of the disease by the attending clinical team, all receiving standard care. Short-term outcomes included 28-day mortality, ICU length of stay, and hospital length of stay. Long-term outcomes at 3 and 6 months included chest CT fibrosis score, pulmonary function [forced vital capacity (FVC) and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)], SpO2/FiO2 ratio, modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea score, and Activities of Daily Living (ADL) score. Safety was assessed via adverse events and laboratory parameters. At 6 months, the Pirfenidone Group had significantly lower chest CT fibrosis scores than the Glucocorticoid Group [3.0 (0.0-6.5) vs. 6.0 (4.0-8.0), p < 0.05], which was comparable to that of the Control Group. FVC, SpO2/FiO2, and ADL scores at 3 and 6 months were significantly higher in the Pirfenidone Group compared with both Glucocorticoid and Control groups (all p < 0.01). Long-term outcomes improved relative to baseline (p < 0.05). Short-term outcomes, mMRC scores, and safety indicators showed no significant differences among groups (p > 0.05). No severe drug-related adverse events were observed. Early pirfenidone administration in pulmonary infection-related ARDS enhances long-term functional recovery and reduces fibrosis without increasing safety risks, although it does not significantly impact short-term outcomes. These findings support the consideration of early antifibrotic therapy in ARDS management.

42975427.title: Network Trauma Research Series: Modeling Trauma Complexity - In Vitro Models to Study Traumatic Lung Damage.
42975427.abstract: Polytrauma, defined as severe injury to multiple body regions, frequently affects the head and thorax and induces a systemic immune response that can favor secondary infections such as pneumonia. In particular, thoracic trauma substantially increases the risk of post-traumatic pneumonia, as direct lung injury, impaired respiratory function, and the frequent need for mechanical ventilation predispose patients to pulmonary infections, thereby contributing to adverse clinical outcomes. To improve translational understanding of these interactions, complex in vitro models have been developed to experimentally dissect the biological mechanisms underlying injuries of the lung. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current in vitro lung models and their suitability to analyze trauma induced lung damage and following infection. Key methodological variables are the selection of appropriate cell lines, the modeling of air - liquid interface or barrier function and the simulation of the trauma. Importantly, experimental approaches should clearly distinguish between inflammatory stimulation and mechanical injury, as these represent distinct pathophysiological processes. Collectively, the models discussed herein highlight the importance of standardized and physiologically relevant in vitro trauma models for advancing mechanistic insights and facilitating the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.

42972582.title: Coagulopathy and anticoagulation management in adult ECPR patients.
42972582.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a lifesaving strategy for refractory cardiac arrest, restoring systemic perfusion when conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation fails. However, ECPR profoundly disrupts haemostasis, driven by the combined effects of whole-body ischaemia-reperfusion injury, systemic inflammation, endothelial activation, platelet dysfunction, and blood contact with extracorporeal surfaces. Together, these processes create a highly dynamic and unstable thromboinflammatory milieu, marked by the simultaneous risk of thrombosis and life-threatening bleeding. Systemic anticoagulation is required to maintain circuit patency and prevent thromboembolic complications, yet optimal strategies remain uncertain. Haemostasis during ECPR is highly dynamic, shaped by the underlying aetiology of cardiac arrest, patient-specific characteristics, and circuit-related factors. This complexity underscores the limitations of fixed anticoagulation targets and the need for individualized, context-sensitive management guided by continuous clinical and laboratory assessment. Despite the increasing global adoption of ECPR, high-quality evidence to guide anticoagulation practices remains scarce. Current strategies are largely extrapolated from other extracorporeal life support populations, contributing to substantial inter-centre variability. This review synthesizes the available evidence on coagulopathy and anticoagulation in adult patients receiving ECPR and discusses emerging approaches to monitoring and anticoagulation management.

42978061.title: The Integration of Music Therapy in the Intensive Care Unit: Health Care Professionals' Experience of an Emerging Paradigm.
42978061.abstract: To explore how intensive care unit healthcare professionals experienced and interpreted music therapy delivered to critically ill patients, including its perceived relevance to patient experience, care interactions, the ICU environment and their own professional experience during care. A qualitative study with a hermeneutic phenomenological approach. A qualified music therapist delivered live, individualised music therapy sessions to critically ill patients alongside ongoing ICU care, including selected procedures when clinically appropriate. Fourteen healthcare professionals who had each been present during one patient-directed session participated in an individual semi-structured interview 24-48 h later. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Four themes were developed: (1) Comfort and patient engagement; (2) Support during invasive procedures; (3) Humanisation, relationships and the ICU environment; and (4) Perceived contextual influences on healthcare professionals' experience. Participants perceived music therapy primarily in relation to patient comfort, engagement and support during selected procedures and potentially distressing care activities. They also associated its presence with more humanised relationships and a calmer ICU environment. Although the sessions were directed towards patients, some participants described positive contextual influences on their immediate experience while observing or providing care. Healthcare professionals perceived patient-directed music therapy as a potentially valuable complementary intervention alongside ongoing ICU care. Within their accounts, its presence was associated with patient comfort and engagement, support during selected procedures and potentially distressing care activities, more humanised and relational care and a calmer care environment. Some participants also described perceived positive contextual influences on their immediate experience while observing or providing care. These findings provide considerations for nursing practice when patient-directed music therapy is being considered in ICU care. Nurses may contribute to assessing the patient's clinical condition, willingness and capacity to participate, identifying or communicating musical preferences, coordinating the timing of sessions with the multidisciplinary team and facilitating referral to a qualified music therapist. Careful planning is required to ensure that sessions do not interfere with clinical monitoring, necessary procedures or patient safety. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) to enhance transparency and methodological rigour in qualitative studies involving interviews. No patient or public contribution.

42977955.title: Facilitators and barriers to the early implementation of speaking valves in intensive care: a qualitative study using normalisation process theory.
42977955.abstract: The utilization of tracheostomy in conjunction with mechanical ventilation significantly impacts various physiological functions, particularly the ability to communicate verbally. Speaking valves, integrated into the ventilator circuit, restore phonation and are recognised internationally as best practice, yet remain underused in Swedish intensive care units (ICUs). Beyond enabling verbal communication, the early use of speaking valves has been associated with improved swallowing, secretion management, and reduced duration of mechanical ventilation. The TRACH INSPIRE project aims to promote their implementation in Swedish ICUs. This study explored facilitators and barriers to the early interprofessional implementation of speaking valves in tracheostomised, mechanically ventilated ICU patients. This qualitative study design analysed 19 semi-structured interview data, pre-implementation, with ICU professionals (intensivists, nurses, physiotherapists, and speech-language pathologists) from two participating ICUs in the TRACH INSPIRE project conducted in January-February 2025. Inclusion criteria were that the participants must have participated in the interprofessional competency training for the TRACH INSPIRE project. No formal exclusion criteria were defined. The Data were analysed using deductive content analysis guided by the Normalisation Process Theory (NPT), which examines how new practices are embedded into routine care. Twelve subcategories were identified that were organized according to the NPT. Facilitators included a shared understanding of the intervention's value, strong professional commitment, structured implementation processes, managerial support, clearly defined roles, effective interprofessional collaboration, targeted training, and open communication. Barriers centred on organisational constraints such as limited resources, low patient volumes, lack of a comprehensive implementation strategy, and documentation-related challenges. Early implementation of speaking valves in mechanically ventilated, tracheostomised ICU patients is supported by high interprofessional engagement, shared recognition of benefits, and structured training. However, operational limitations, small eligible patient populations, and documentation burdens present notable challenges. Inclusive team strategies, maintaining competencies, and streamlined processes may promote sustainable integration into routine ICU practice.

42979684.title: Lactate-To-Albumin Ratio and Mortality in Critically Ill Patients with Pneumonia: Insights From the MIMIC-IV Database.
42979684.journal: Journal of primary care & community health
42979684.abstract: ObjectivesTo evaluate the association of the lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) with short- and long-term mortality in critically ill patients with pneumonia.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV, version 3.1) database, including adult patients with pneumonia admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). LAR was calculated using lactate and albumin measurements obtained around ICU admission and categorized into tertiles. The primary outcome was 60-day mortality, and the secondary outcome was 180-day mortality. Restricted cubic spline analysis, multivariable Cox regression, and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed to evaluate the association between LAR and mortality. The incremental prognostic value of LAR added to the SOFA score was assessed using discrimination and reclassification measures.ResultsA total of 5,610 patients were included and stratified into tertiles of LAR after restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a nonlinear association between LAR and mortality (P for nonlinearity <0.001 for both outcomes). Mortality increased progressively across LAR tertiles. For 60-day mortality, rates were 26.3% in T1, 34.9% in T2, and 48.1% in T3. For 180-day mortality, corresponding rates were 33.6%, 42.9%, and 54.4%, respectively (all p<0.001). In multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, higher LAR tertiles were associated with increased mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) for 60-day mortality of 1.20 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-1.35) for T2 and 1.54 (95% CI, 1.37-1.73) for T3, compared with T1. Similar associations were observed for 180-day mortality, with HRs of 1.20 (95% CI, 1.08-1.33) and 1.50 (95% CI, 1.34-1.67), respectively. LAR demonstrated better discriminative performance than lactate and comparable performance to albumin. Adding LAR to SOFA increased the area under the curve from 0.660 to 0.687 (absolute change, 0.027; 95% CI, 0.019-0.036), with a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.245 (95% CI, 0.194-0.296).ConclusionsHigher LAR was associated with increased short-term and long-term mortality in critically ill patients with pneumonia. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate the prognostic value and clinical utility of LAR.

42978870.title: Respiratory medicine in the ICU 2026: From physiology to precision care.
42978870.abstract: This annual review summarizes major advances in respiratory medicine in the intensive care unit (ICU) published in 2025, focusing on high-impact clinical and translational studies most likely to influence current practice and future research. Across the field, 2025 strengthened the evidence base for key physiological concepts while more clearly defining where physiological strategies translate into clinical benefit and where broadly applied interventions remain insufficient, reflecting an increasing shift toward precision-based respiratory care. Precision medicine advanced through open-source inflammatory acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) subphenotype classifiers and trajectory-based physiological phenotypes that outperform static definitions and support time-dependent treatment strategies. Evidence for non-invasive respiratory support expanded in obesity, immunocompromised patients, and procedure-related hypoxemia, emphasizing that implementation factors such as duration, staffing, and positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) strategy strongly influence success. Prospective multicenter cohorts reinforced the prognostic relevance of driving pressure (DP) and mechanical power, whereas randomized trials indicated that DP-guided PEEP titration and advanced ventilator modes do not reliably improve patient-centered outcomes when broadly applied under lung-protective targets. A major 2025 development was the operationalization of spontaneous breathing risk, and bedside indices of inspiratory efforts (Pocc and P0.1) were linked to pendelluft and outcomes, with oxygenation severity modifying harm versus benefit, supporting an effort-guided framework for preventing patient self-inflicted lung injury. In ARDS, prolonged inhaled volatile sedation failed to improve outcomes and was associated with possible harm compared with intravenous sedation. The largest 2025 oxygen trial showed no mortality benefit for broadly conservative targets, while subgroup analyses suggested heterogeneity of treatment effect. Electrical impedance tomography advanced toward bedside stratification and individualized titration, including emerging three-dimensional approaches. Finally, 2025 strengthened long-term outcome data for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and ICU survivorship, reinforcing recovery as a core component of respiratory critical care.

42979190.title: Early Prediction of Multidrug-Resistant Organism Infection in ICU Patients Using Routinely Available Clinical Data: Development and Temporal Validation of Prediction Models.
42979190.abstract: Multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) infections pose a critical threat in intensive care units (ICUs), yet diagnostic delays hinder timely intervention. This study aimed to develop and temporally validate prediction models for early identification of MDRO infection in ICU patients using routinely available clinical data. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from ICU patients admitted in a tertiary hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Predictors were selected using Lasso-Cox regression based on data within 48 hours of ICU admission. Three models-Cox proportional hazards regression, Random Survival Forest (RSF), and Survival XGBoost-were developed on a training set (2021-2023) and temporally validated on a validation set (2024). Model performance was assessed using competing-risk time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, and inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted (IPCW) Brier score. Multiply imputed datasets were used in a sensitivity analysis. A total of 11,510 records (239 MDRO infections) in the training set and 4,381 records (178 MDRO infections) in the validation set were analyzed. Twenty-three predictors were selected, including previous MDROs detection, invasive device use, usage of antibiotics and elevated neutrophil percentage. In temporal validation, the time-dependent AUCs at 72 hours were 0.830 for Cox regression, 0.880 for RSF, and 0.793 for Survival XGBoost; the corresponding values at 600 hours were 0.733, 0.748, and 0.731. Discrimination declined with longer prediction horizons. All three models systematically underestimated absolute MDRO infection risk in the temporal validation cohort, particularly at later time points. The sensitivity analyses produced results broadly consistent with those of the main analysis. Prediction models using routine clinical data within 48 hours of ICU admission provided useful discrimination for subsequent MDRO infection, particularly at earlier prediction horizons. These findings support the feasibility of individualized MDRO infection risk estimation using electronic medical record data, while prospective evaluation is required before the models are used to guide clinical decisions.

42978137.title: Impact of Neuromuscular Blocking Agents on Hospital Outcomes in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Sepsis: Propensity Score Analyses of A Nationwide Sepsis Cohort.
42978137.abstract: The impact of neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) on hospital outcomes in patients with sepsis requiring mechanical ventilation (MV) remains uncertain and warrants further evaluation. We analyzed data from a nationwide sepsis cohort comprising 20 university-affiliated or tertiary hospitals, including adult patients with sepsis who required MV. Patients who received continuous intravenous NMBAs within 3 days of intensive care unit (ICU) admission were compared with those who did not. To adjust for baseline imbalances, both inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM) were used. Of 13,827 patients with sepsis, 1,255 receiving MV were analyzed (mean age, 68.3 ± 13.9 years; 65.7% male; NMBA use, 25.7%). In the IPTW-adjusted Cox model, NMBA use was not associated with in-hospital mortality. Similarly, in the PSM cohort (292 NMBA-treated vs. 292 matched controls), in-hospital mortality did not differ between groups (17.1% vs. 18.8%; P = 0.590). However, NMBA use was associated with a longer ICU stay (absolute difference: 3.0 days [95% confidence interval, 0.3-5.7]; P = 0.003) and showed a trend toward a longer MV duration and hospital stay (Wilcoxon signed-rank test). Kaplan-Meier analysis also demonstrated significantly longer ICU stays in the NMBA group (log-rank P = 0.006). The incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia was significantly higher in the NMBA group (8.6% vs. 4.5%; P = 0.044). In patients with sepsis requiring MV, the use of NMBAs was not associated with in-hospital mortality but was linked to longer ICU stays and a higher incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia. These findings underscore the need for cautious use of continuous NMBA infusion in this population.

42978866.title: Occurrence of hypoxic liver injury in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: A retrospective cohort study.
42978866.abstract: Hypoxic liver injury (HLI) is a frequent and life-threatening complication occurring in up to 10% of critically ill patients. HLI can be typically found in a setting of cardiac, circulatory, or respiratory failure. Data regarding the occurrence, course, and outcome of HLI in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is scarce. This study aimed to investigate the incidence, clinical characteristics, and outcome of HLI in critically ill, mechanically ventilated patients with ARDS. This is a single-center, retrospective observational study conducted at the intensive care units (ICUs) of a tertiary-care university hospital in Hamburg, Germany from December 1, 2017 to April 30, 2021. It includes all consecutive critically ill adult patients who met the Berlin Definition criteria for moderate or severe ARDS and required invasive mechanical ventilation within 48 h of ICU admission and for more than 48 h. Clinical course characteristics and key laboratory markers were systematically compared and analyzed according to HLI diagnostic status across all enrolled patients. HLI was defined according to established criteria as elevation of aminotransferase levels (>20-fold upper-limit-of-normal). Predictors of HLI occurrence, clinical course, and outcome were assessed. In total, 434 critically ill patients with ARDS were included. During the ICU stay, 22.4% (n=97) developed HLI. Baseline characteristics including age, sex, and body mass index were comparable between patients with and without HLI. The median Charlson Comorbidity Index was comparable in both groups (3 vs. 3 points; P=0.36). A higher disease severity on admission represented by the sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) score was observed in patients with HLI (11 vs. 10 points; P <0.001). The median arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2)/ fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) ratio was 81 mmHg (interquartile range [IQR]: 60-109 mmHg) in patients with HLI compared to 79 mmHg (IQR: 60-106 mmHg) in patients without HLI, respectively (P=0.900). Overall, 35.0% (n=152) of patients required veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation therapy, including 39.2% (n=38) within the HLI group and 33.8% (n=114) without HLI. The incidence of renal replacement therapy (RRT) was 87.6% (n=85) among patients with HLI and 53.1% (n=179) among those without HLI (P <0.001). ICU mortality was 74.2% (n=72) and 58.2% (n=196) in the patients with or without HLI, respectively (P <0.001). Regression analysis identified cholestasis (odds ratio [OR]=2.061, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.220 to 3.481, P <0.010) and RRT (OR=4.732, 95% CI: 2.416 to 9.267, P <0.001) as factors significantly associated with new-onset HLI. Occurrence of HLI was independently associated with mortality (hazard ratio [HR]=1.710, 95% CI: 1.273 to 2.297, P <0.001). HLI is a common condition in critically ill patients with ARDS, and its occurrence is highly associated with mortality. HLI may serve as prognostic marker in critically ill patients with ARDS.

42980514.title: Platelet Transfusion Practices in the PICUs: Multicenter, Observational Study, in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus, 2024.
42980514.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
42980514.abstract: We aimed to describe the use of platelet transfusions among critically ill children managed in Türkiye in late 2024. Secondarily, we sought to determine these practices in relation to the 2022 Transfusion and Anemia Expertise Initiative-Control/Avoidance of Bleeding (TAXI-CAB) recommendations for critically ill pediatric patients. Prospective study (October-December 2024). 22 PICUs in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus. Patients of 1 month to 18 years who received at least one platelet transfusion in the PICU. None. Out of 2693 PICU admissions, 200 patients (7.4%) received 577 platelet transfusions. Of the transfusions, 383 of 577 transfusions (66.4%) were for prophylaxis, most frequently for isolated thrombocytopenia (194/383, 50.7%). Regarding the transfusion threshold for prophylaxis, in the 194 cases of isolated thrombocytopenia, the median (interquartile range [IQR]) pretransfusion platelet count was 24 (IQR, 16-38) × 109/L, which differed from the TAXI-CAB consensus statement guidance of less than 10 × 109/L. Platelet transfusion, as opposed to not, was associated with 20-fold greater odds of 28-day mortality (p < 0.001), and among the 200 patients receiving platelets, multivariable analysis showed that lower pretransfusion platelet count, support with invasive mechanical ventilation, and hospital-acquired infections collectively accounted for 34% of the variance in model performance for classifying 28-day mortality. Our 2024 national, multicenter PICU study across Türkiye and Northern Cyprus shows that around two-thirds of transfusion episodes were for prophylaxis, and multivariable logistic regression modeling identified patient factors associated with greater odds of 28-day mortality. The median pretransfusion threshold for isolated thrombocytopenia was around 20 × 109/L, which is double the less than 10 × 109/L in the 2022 TAXI-CAB consensus statement. Given the heterogeneity of critically ill patients and practice environments, understanding the reasons behind these practices may help inform future research and consensus recommendations.

42979103.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia in males and females: A post hoc analysis of the prospective multicenter multinational EUVAP cohort.
42979103.abstract: Sex is a major cause of heterogeneity in the epidemiology, management, response to treatment, and outcome of infectious and respiratory diseases. We aimed to describe differences between males and females in characteristics, management, and mortality among patients affected by ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). We performed a post hoc exploratory analysis of the EUVAP/CAP cohort, a prospective multinational cohort study of patients requiring mechanical ventilation in 27 intensive care units from nine countries. Sexes were compared with respect to baseline characteristics, interventions, and outcomes in univariate and adjusted analyses. Among the 2436 intubated adult patients in the cohort, 450 (18.5%) developed VAP; of these VAP cases, 293 (65.1%) were male, and the median age was 64 years. Compared with females, males had more comorbidities, and underwent bronchoscopy more frequently (20.5% vs. 11.5%, P=0.016) and triple antibiotic therapy (33.1% vs. 22.3%, P=0.016)., Intensive care unit mortality was 41.3% vs. 45.2% (P=0.422). In multivariate analysis, age in years (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=1.02, 95%confidence interval [CI]: 1.00 to 1.04), septic shock (aOR=1.72, 95%CI: 1.02 to 2.91), McCabe score (life expectancy 1-5 years vs. >5 years: aOR=1.53, 95%CI: 0.81 to 2.54; <1 year vs. >5 years: aOR=7.67, 95%CI: 2.41 to 24.39; P=0.002), and infection with high risk bacteria for multidrug resistance (aOR=1.86, 95%CI: 1.12 to 3.09; P=0.016) were independently associated with mortality, but not sex (aOR for males vs. females=0.92, 95%CI 0.56 to 1.49; P=0.722). The relation between sex and mortality was not affected by age <50 years. The risk of mortality did not differ between sexes in patients affected by VAP. Affected males had more comorbidities, heavy alcohol use, and underwent bronchoscopy and triple antibiotic therapy more frequently.

42979476.title: Remimazolam for Precision Sedation and Anaesthesia in Vulnerable Populations: A Narrative Review of Pharmacological Mechanisms, Stratified Clinical Evidence, and Individualised Perioperative Strategies.
42979476.abstract: Sedation and anaesthesia in vulnerable populations are complicated by altered pharmacokinetics, variable pharmacodynamic sensitivity, and limited physiological reserve. The extent of these differences depends on the underlying condition, disease severity, comorbidity, and treatment setting. These issues are common in older adults, patients with obesity or obstructive sleep apnoea, organ dysfunction, cardiovascular vulnerability, critical illness, and neurological or psychiatric comorbidity. Conventional sedatives may be poorly tolerated in these settings. Propofol can cause hypotension and respiratory depression. Midazolam may lead to delayed recovery and accumulation. Dexmedetomidine may be limited by bradycardia and slow onset. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine that undergoes rapid carboxylesterase-mediated hydrolysis and can be antagonised with flumazenil. This narrative review examines its pharmacology, clinical evidence, and practical use across nine vulnerable populations. The synthesis prioritised population-specific clinical studies, pharmacokinetic studies, comparative trials, systematic reviews, and major guidelines. For short procedures, the most consistent evidence concerns older adults and haemodynamically vulnerable patients, in whom remimazolam has often been associated with less hypotension than propofol and faster recovery than midazolam. These findings are based mainly on short-term physiological and recovery outcomes. Evidence in mild to moderate hepatic or renal dysfunction is supportive but remains sparse in severe disease. Data for obesity or obstructive sleep apnoea, prolonged ICU sedation, paediatric care, obstetrics, and neurological or psychiatric vulnerability are limited or indirect. Remimazolam should therefore be considered according to the clinical objective, the expected duration and depth of sedation, opioid exposure, airway risk, and organ reserve. Its pharmacological advantages have not yet been shown to improve delirium, cognition, mechanical ventilation, functional recovery, or long-term safety. Further studies should focus on population-specific dosing models and patient-centred outcomes.

42978660.title: Stroke-associated pneumonia after acute ischemic stroke: early temporal dynamics, nonlinear risk factors, and time-dependent prognostic impact.
42978660.abstract: Stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) is a common complication following acute ischemic stroke, yet its early occurrence patterns, nonlinear risk factors, and time-dependent prognostic impact remain incompletely characterized. We investigated SAP incidence, temporal distribution, risk factors, and independent impact on in-hospital outcomes. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 3,347 consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke (2019-2025). SAP was diagnosed within 7 days after admission using consensus criteria. Cox models with restricted cubic splines identified risk factors and nonlinear relationships. Time-dependent Cox models, Gamma generalized linear models, and logistic regression were used to assess associations between SAP and in-hospital outcomes. Multiple imputation, complete-case, and landmark analyses verified robustness. SAP developed in 428 patients (12.8%), with 55.1% occurring within 72 h (peak day 3). Independent risk factors included older age (HR 1.02), pre-stroke mRS 3-5 (HR 1.39), COPD (HR 1.69), cardioembolism (HR 1.71), dysphagia (HR 2.02), and nasogastric tube insertion within 48 h (HR 2.31) (all p < 0.05). Admission NIHSS, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, and albumin showed nonlinear associations with SAP risk (all P-nonlinear <0.05). Time-dependent analyses revealed SAP independently associated with in-hospital death (HR 2.34), ICU transfer (HR 2.81), invasive mechanical ventilation (HR 3.47), prolonged length of stay (RoM 1.35), and poor functional outcome (OR 1.90) (all p < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness. SAP occurs early after acute ischemic stroke, with identifiable risk factors exhibiting nonlinear relationships, and independently predicts adverse in-hospital outcomes. Findings support forward-shifted preventive strategies, including early swallowing assessment, feeding pathway optimization, airway protection, and nutritional support, in high-risk patients during the first days of hospitalization.

42978763.title: Procalcitonin as a prognostic factor in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD without pneumonia: a prospective multicenter cohort study.
42978763.abstract: Pneumonia frequently precipitates AECOPD, and procalcitonin (PCT) has been utilized to guide antibiotic administration in these patients. However, the specific role and clinical significance of PCT in AECOPD patients who do not have pneumonia remains unexplored and is yet to be thoroughly evaluated. We conducted univariate and multivariate cox regression analyses to identify independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality among AECOPD patients. The Youden index was applied to determine the optimal cutoff value for PCT, which was then used to categorize participants into two groups based on this threshold. Subsequently, we compared the clinical manifestations and outcomes of patients between these groups, and Kaplan-Meier curves were con-structed and analyzed using the log-rank test. A subgroup analysis was also conducted in patients with/without antibiotic using during hospitalization. A total of 6,791 hospitalized AECOPD patients of 10 tertiary care hospitals within China was enrolled in our study from September 2017 to July 2021. Univariable and multivariable cox regression analyses revealed that PCT (HR 1.016, 95% CI 1.003-1.029, p = 0.014) as independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality in AECOPD patients. The ROC analysis established an optimal cut-off value of 0.11 for predicting in-hospital mortality. The PCT high group (≥0.11 ng/mL) demonstrated higher proportion of chronic underlying diseases, and higher age-adjusted Charlson comorbidity index score, increased in-hospital mortality, greater ICU admission rates, higher rates of invasive mechanical ventilation, and a longer length of stay (all P < 0.001). PCT and the cut-off value of 0.11 could also have effective prognostic value in both subgroups of patients with/without antibiotic usage. PCT emerged as an independent risk factor for in-hospital mortality in AECOPD patients without pneumonia. Those with elevated PCT levels (≥0.11 ng/mL) exhibited a higher burden of comorbidities, a potential of pro-infection or pro-inflammation and poorer clinical outcomes. http://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.aspx?proj=12162, identifier ChiCTR2100044625.

42981093.title: Overall Survival in Adults With Acute Myeloid Leukemia Initiating Quizartinib vs Midostaurin With Chemotherapy.
42981093.abstract: Midostaurin and quizartinib are approved with intensive chemotherapy (IC) in patients with newly diagnosed FLT3 internal tandem duplication (ITD)-positive acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but no randomized clinical trials have directly compared them. To compare 1-year overall survival (OS) among patients with FLT3-ITD variant AML initiating IC with midostaurin or quizartinib. This multicenter, retrospective cohort study included patients with newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD variant AML treated at 12 US referral centers between January 1, 2018, and May 31, 2025. Data analysis was performed from January 2026 to August 2026. Induction therapy with IC plus midostaurin or quizartinib. The primary outcome was 1-year overall survival (OS). Secondary outcomes included 1-year event-free survival (EFS), induction response, and hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) rates at first remission; FLT3 clearance after induction was exploratory. Safety outcomes included rates of febrile neutropenia, infections, intensive care unit use, total parenteral nutrition and granulocyte colony-stimulating factor use, discharge to a rehabilitation facility after index hospitalization, and early mortality. Cox proportional hazards regression models were adjusted for baseline covariates and HCT as time dependent. Among 215 patients (median [IQR] age, 56.0 [45.0-65.0] years; 119 [55.3%] female), 127 (59.1%) received midostaurin and 88 (40.9%) received quizartinib. Median (IQR) follow-up was 667.0 (289.0-1368.0) days for midostaurin and 324.0 (168.0-546.5) days for quizartinib, reflecting the latter's more recent approval. One-year OS was 78.0% for midostaurin and 93.0% for quizartinib (hazard ratio [HR], 0.22; 95% CI, 0.08-0.58; P = .002). The 1-year EFS was 56.0% for midostaurin and 77.0% for quizartinib (HR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.25-0.74; P = .003). Patients receiving quizartinib had higher rates of composite complete remission (75 [85.2%] vs 93 [73.2%]; P = .03), whereas rates of FLT3 clearance after induction (20 [38.5%] for quizartinib vs 27 [40.3%] for midostaurin; P = .84) and HCT in first remission (47 [53.4%] for quizartinib vs 83 [65.4%] for midostaurin; P = .08) were comparable. Midostaurin was associated with higher intensive care unit use (19 [15.0%] vs 4 [4.5%]; P = .02), discharge to a rehabilitation facility (9 [7.1%] vs 1 [1.1%]; P = .04), and treatment interruptions (32 [25.2%] vs 10 [11.4%]; P = .01). A sensitivity analysis limited to patients treated in 2023 or later (more balanced follow-up) showed directionally consistent but nonsignificant OS and EFS differences. In this cohort study of adults with FLT3-ITD variant AML, IC plus quizartinib was associated with improved 1-year survival, induction response, and safety compared with IC plus midostaurin.

42985816.title: Association of Lactate-to-Albumin Ratio With 28-Day Mortality in Critically Ill Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Cohort Study Based on the MIMIC-IV Database.
42985816.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is not uncommon among critically ill patients, especially in those with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure. Its high mortality rate remains a major challenge in the intensive care setting. The frequent apnea and respiratory failure during sleep in OSA patients, along with the intermittent hypoxemia caused by it, are accompanied by a series of systemic pathological and physiological changes. Metabolic imbalance is a key characteristic of the underlying pathological mechanism of this disease. However, the association between lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) and the prognosis of OSA patients remains to be fully elucidated. To date, a paucity of studies has evaluated the prognostic capabilities of these indicators. The majority of these studies have focused on the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and the results are contradictory, insufficient to fully clarify their clinical significance. Relying solely on lactate may not fully reflect patients' physiological conditions, whereas integrating LAR can provide a more comprehensive and accurate description of the metabolic state. This study aims to explore the relationship between LAR and 28-day mortality rates in ICU patients with OSA, using data from the MIMIC-IV database. Patients diagnosed with OSA were selected from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (v.2.2) database, identified by specific ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes (detailed in the Methods section). To assess the predictive power of LAR, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, Kaplan-Meier (K-M) survival curve analysis, logistic regression analysis, and subgroup analysis were employed. LAR was analyzed both as a categorical variable (based on the optimal cutoff) and as a continuous variable. The sample population comprised 807 patients diagnosed with OSA who were admitted to the intensive care unit for the first time. The 28-day mortality rate was 20.44%. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) for LAR was 0.730 (95% CI: 0.686-0.772), which was comparable with OASIS (0.736; 95% CI: 0.695-0.776) and superior to SOFA (0.637; 95% CI: 0.591-0.683; DeLong test p = 0.500). The optimal cutoff value for LAR was 0.791. The high-LAR group demonstrated a poor prognosis in the K-M analysis (p < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression demonstrated a significant association between LAR and unfavorable outcomes, with an odds ratio (OR) of 3.00 (95% CI: 1.83-4.90, p < 0.001) when analyzed as a dichotomous variable, and an OR of 1.52 per unit increase (95% CI: 1.27-1.82, p < 0.001) when analyzed as a continuous variable. Subgroup analysis revealed no statistically significant interaction between LAR and any subgroup (p for interaction: 0.052-0.906). LAR is a rational and easily accessible biomarker that is significantly associated with 28-day mortality in ICU patients with OSA. These findings are only applicable to OSA patients who received lactate and albumin testing during ICU admission, and the results cannot be generalized to the entire population of ICU patients with OSA.

42983840.title: Treatment and outcomes of difficult-to-treat Stenotrophomonas maltophilia pneumonia in the intensive care unit: a multinational retrospective cohort study.
42983840.abstract: Difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR) in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is an emerging concern in ICU-acquired pneumonia, associated with high mortality and limited evidence to guide therapy. This study aimed to evaluate the association between antibiotic regimens and 30-day mortality in DTR S. maltophilia ICU-acquired pneumonia. We conducted a multicenter, international, retrospective study across 31 centers in eight countries, including all adult patients with DTR S. maltophilia ICU-acquired pneumonia treated with ≥24 hours of an in vitro-active antibiotic. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included clinical cure and a composite of 30-day survival with clinical cure. Each agent was analyzed as a separate exposure using modified Poisson regression with robust variance in a day-3 landmark cohort. Combination therapy and treatment duration were evaluated using overlap weighting. A total of 119 patients were included. Thirty-day mortality was 37.8%. Tigecycline was associated with higher 30-day mortality (aRR 1.95, 95% CI 1.21-3.13). Aztreonam/ceftazidime-avibactam showed a favorable but non-significant trend toward lower mortality (aRR 0.38, 95% CI 0.12-1.15), as did colistin (aRR 0.51, 95% CI 0.22-1.20). No agent other than tigecycline was significantly associated with any outcome, and the active agents had wide, overlapping confidence intervals. Neither combination therapy nor a treatment duration longer than 8 days was associated with any outcome. Tigecycline was associated with excess mortality and should be used with caution. Aztreonam/ceftazidime-avibactam and colistin trended toward lower mortality, whereas the other agents, including cefiderocol, appeared neutral. The study is underpowered to separate the active agents, and these hypothesis-generating findings require prospective confirmation.

42983565.title: Eleven questions on Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome management in the ICU.
42983565.abstract: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) due to Andes virus (ANDV) is a fulminant yet potentially reversible cause of respiratory and circulatory failure requiring timely critical care. This article addresses eleven practical questions on ICU management, drawing on clinical experience and research from the Chilean healthcare system. The recommendations cover early recognition, diagnostic workup, haemodynamic monitoring, cautious fluid and vasoactive support, respiratory management, VA-ECMO referral, daily ICU care, recovery, common pitfalls, and therapies with limited evidence. Because no antiviral or immunomodulatory therapy has consistently improved outcomes, survival relies on early suspicion, physiology-guided supportive care, and rapid escalation to ECMO-capable centres when severe cardiopulmonary failure develops.

42986439.title: Consensus on a core outcome set for ventilation trials in critically ill patients with acute brain injury: results of an international Delphi consensus study.
42986439.abstract: Clinical research evaluating mechanical ventilation liberation in patients with acute brain injury (ABI) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity, limiting evidence synthesis. We aimed to develop an internationally endorsed core outcome set (COS) and a hierarchical composite endpoint for ventilation trials in neurocritical care. Following COS-STAD/COS-STAP standards, we conducted a 4-round international Delphi study. Candidate outcomes were identified via a scoping review. A multidisciplinary panel from 31 countries scored outcomes using a 9-point GRADE scale. Inclusion required >70% rating as "critical" (score 7-9) and ≤15% as "not important" (1-3). Two consensus meetings were held to categorize outcomes, select representative measures, and ratify a hierarchical composite endpoint. 78 stakeholders participated in Round 1; 60 completed all rounds (23.1% attrition). Fifty-four outcomes achieved Delphi consensus. At Consensus Meeting 1, these were organized into 16 categories; the highest-scoring outcome per category was selected. Three outcomes were not ratified due to disease-specificity (NIH Stroke Scale) or lack of universal applicability (brain death, coma-free days). The final COS comprised 13 outcomes across 5 domains: respiratory function, survival, complications, functional status, and quality of life. A 3-level hierarchical composite endpoint was ratified at Consensus Meeting 2: (1) intensive care unit survival, (2) no reintubation within 72 hours, and (3) days alive without mechanical ventilation. This study establishes the first COS for ventilation weaning trials in ABI patients. Widespread adoption of these 13 outcomes and the hierarchical composite endpoint will standardize reporting, enable meaningful evidence synthesis, and facilitate clinical translation in neurocritical care. Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) Initiative, registration number 2320.

42985282.title: Mechanical insufflation-exsufflation for clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
42985282.journal: Canadian journal of respiratory therapy : CJRT = Revue canadienne de la therapie respiratoire : RCTR
42985282.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of mechanical insufflation-exsufflation (MI-E) compared with usual care in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults. # Methods We searched Embase, MEDLINE via PubMed, CINAHL, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to April 2026 that compared MI-E with usual care in mechanically ventilated adults. The primary outcome was duration of mechanical ventilation. Secondary outcomes included the amount of aspirated airway secretions, respiratory system compliance, airway resistance, length of ICU stay, and mortality. Meta-analysis was performed when at least two studies provided clinically and methodologically comparable data. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. # Results Six RCTs involving 492 participants were included. For the primary outcome of mechanical ventilation duration, only one RCT contributed to the effect estimate (MD, -2.67 days; 95% CI, -6.91 to 1.57; very-low-certainty evidence). MI-E increased the amount of aspirated airway secretions compared with usual care (MD, 1.47 g; 95% CI, 0.74 to 2.19; very-low-certainty evidence). No statistically significant differences were observed in respiratory system compliance or airway resistance. ICU length of stay also showed no difference (2 RCTs; MD, -1.75 days; 95% CI, -4.61 to 1.10; very-low-certainty evidence). Mortality was evaluated by one RCT (risk ratio, 1.56; 95% CI, 0.44 to 5.50; very-low-certainty evidence). # Conclusions The effects of MI-E on clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients remain uncertain because the available evidence is of low to very low certainty. MI-E may improve airway secretion clearance; however, evidence regarding mechanical ventilation duration, ICU length of stay, and mortality remains very uncertain.
