At a PM2.5 concentration of 30 μg/m3 compared with the reference concentration of 10 μg/m3, 14.2% higher odds of HAP were observed (95% CI: 2.6-27%). The stratified analyses indicated stronger associations among elders aged ≥ 60 years, patients with body mass index (BMI) > 23.9 kg/m2 and patients with diabetes. Additional adjustment for clinical covariates, including duration of mechanical ventilation, confirmed the robustness of the observed exposure-response association. These findings revealed a substantial and robust link between short-term PM2.5 exposure and elevated HAP incidence in the vulnerable population undergoing cardiovascular surgeries.

42989315.title: Early adequate empiric antifungal therapy and 28-day mortality in ICU patients with candidemia: a pooled patient-level analysis of EUROBACT-1 and EUROBACT-2 cohorts.
42989315.abstract: The optimal timing of empiric antifungal therapy in patients with suspected candidemia remains uncertain. In practice, many antifungal treatments initiated empirically are eventually found to be unnecessary, exposing patients to potential toxicity, selection of non-albicans Candida species, emergence of resistance, and additional costs. The objective of the study was to evaluate whether adequate empiric antifungal therapy initiated within 2 days after blood culture draw was associated with 28-day mortality. We performed a pooled secondary analysis of two prospective worldwide observational cohorts (EUROBACT-1 and EUROBACT-2) including adult patients with Candida bloodstream infection. The exposure was defined as receipt of adequate antifungal therapy within 2 days after blood culture draw. Propensity scores for receiving early adequate antifungal therapy were estimated using prespecified covariates, and inverse probability of treatment weights were applied in a weighted Cox proportional hazards model to assess the association with 28-day mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted according to study cohort, Candida species, and presence of hypotension at the time of bloodstream infection. As a sensitivity analysis, a frailty Cox proportional hazards model including a random center effect was performed. The final study population included 272 patients with candidemia from 158 centers, including 81 from EUROBACT-1 and 191 from EUROBACT-2. One hundred and ten patients received early adequate antifungal therapy and 162 did not. Overall, 38.6% of patients (105/272) died within 28 days, including 40.9% (45/110) in the early adequate therapy group and 37.0% (60/162) in the non-early adequate therapy group. In the weighted Cox model, early adequate antifungal therapy was not significantly associated with 28-day mortality (HR 1.23, 95% CI 0.82-1.83, p = 0.314). Results were consistent across subgroup analyses according to study cohort, Candida species, the presence of hypotension at the time of bloodstream infection, as well as in the frailty Cox sensitivity analysis. Early adequate antifungal therapy was not independently associated with improved 28-day survival in ICU patients with candidemia. These findings support a more targeted approach to early empirical antifungal treatment and underscore the need to identify patient subgroups most likely to benefit from immediate therapy.

42993724.title: Association of unmet discharge needs on readmission or mortality among acute respiratory failure survivors during the COVID-19 pandemic: The Addressing Post-Intensive Care Syndrome (APICS-COVID) multicenter prospective cohort study.
42993724.abstract: Survivors of acute respiratory failure (ARF) often face long-term impairments known as Post-Intensive Care Syndrome. These impairments, coupled with fragmented healthcare, contribute to high rates of readmission and mortality. The COVID-19 pandemic challenged healthcare systems, providing an important opportunity to evaluate healthcare fragmentation before and during the pandemic. From December 2020 to July 2022, this prospective multicenter study (APICS-COVID) enrolled ARF survivors discharged home from acute care hospitalization. The primary exposure was unmet healthcare needs within 1-4 weeks post-discharge and the primary composite outcome was 3-month readmission and mortality. We additionally compared unmet healthcare needs in this study versus a predominately pre-pandemic cohort from an identical study protocol (APICS-01). Of 201 patients enrolled, 94% had at least one unmet healthcare need. The median (IQR) number of healthcare needs upon discharge was 18 (11-25) and the median proportion of unmet healthcare needs was 26% (17-36%). Follow-up appointments were the most frequent unmet need. Higher vs. lower unmet healthcare needs were not significantly associated with 3-month readmission or mortality (aRR 0.61, p = 0.22). Compared to the APICS-01 cohort, the frequency of 3-month readmission/mortality was lower (14% vs. 29%, p = 0.26), despite higher unmet needs in the APICS-COVID cohort (26% vs. 16%, p < 0.001). Across six US academic hospitals during the COVID-19 pandemic, we did not detect a significant association between higher and lower unmet healthcare needs and 3-month readmission or mortality. Compared to APICS-01, unmet follow-up appointments increased but readmission and mortality decreased. Home health services, durable medical equipment, and medications remained robust during pandemic conditions.

42993667.title: Effect of Infection-Site-Targeted Postural Drainage on Mechanical Ventilation Duration in Intensive Care Unit Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
42993667.journal: The journal of nursing research : JNR
42993667.abstract: Mechanical ventilation (MV) is essential for intensive care unit (ICU) patients with respiratory failure, but prolonged MV increases the risk of complications. This study was conducted to evaluate the effect of infection-site-targeted postural drainage, guided by imaging, on patient outcomes compared with conventional care. In this randomized controlled trial, 384 ICU patients requiring MV were assigned to either the personalized-care group (PCG), which received imaging-guided drainage, or the routine-care group (RCG), which received standard positional changes. The primary outcome was MV duration, and secondary outcomes included PaO2/FiO2 (PF) ratios, ICU/hospital length of stay, and 28-day mortality. The PCG was found to have significantly shorter MV duration (median 7 vs. 9 days, p<.05) and higher PF ratios at critical time points (X2, X4, X5; p<.001). A shorter average ICU stay length was reported for the PCG (12.3 vs. 13.4 days), although the difference was not significant after multivariable adjustment. No between-group difference was observed in terms of 28-day mortality. The results indicate that imaging-guided, nursing-led postural drainage effectively improves pulmonary function and shortens MV and ICU lengths of stay without increasing mortality risk, supporting the integration of individualized pulmonary care, potentially enhanced through intelligent technologies, into routine ICU practice.

42993191.title: Independent predictors of 28-day mortality in ICU patients with Acinetobacter baumannii versus Non-Acinetobacter baumannii gram-negative tracheal aspirate isolates.
42993191.abstract: This study evaluated independent risk factors affecting 28-day mortality in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with Acinetobacter baumannii versus non-A. baumannii Gram-negative bacilli isolated from tracheal aspirate cultures. Overall, 120 ICU patients (66 males, 54 females; age: 36-94) enrolled between January 2024 and December 2025 were divided into two equal groups: the A. baumannii (n = 60) and the non-A. baumannii (n = 60). Age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) score, APACHE II score, septic shock rates, and CRP levels were similar between groups (P > 0.05). However, carbapenem resistance (98.3% vs. 56.7%; P < 0.001), mechanical ventilation (MV) requirement (75.0% vs. 53.3%; P = 0.022), and 28-day mortality (63.3% vs. 40.0%; P = 0.018) were significantly higher in the A. baumannii group. ICU length of stay was significantly shorter in the A. baumannii group (16.5 vs. 26.5 days; P = 0.008), due to early-period mortality. Predominant non-A. baumannii pathogens were Klebsiella pneumoniae (51.7%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (35%). Multivariate logistic regression identified MV requirement (aOR: 4.706, 95% CI: 1.792-12.359, P = 0.002), A. baumannii infection (aOR: 2.512, 95% CI: 1.055-5.983, P = 0.037), and higher CCI score (aOR: 1.523, 95% CI: 1.155-2.007, P = 0.003) as independent predictors of 28-day mortality. A. baumannii isolation from tracheal aspirates and MV requirement are strong independent risk factors for 28-day mortality in ICU patients. High carbapenem resistance restricts therapeutic options and drives early mortality. Early diagnosis, rapid microbiological identification, targeted antimicrobial therapy, and strict infection control practices are paramount to improving survival outcomes in critically ill patients.

42991817.title: Characteristics and Hospital Outcomes of Patients Admitted to the Intensive Care Unit Because of Haematological Malignancy-A Service Evaluation.
42991817.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) admission due to haematological malignancy (HM) has previously been questioned due to high mortality. While mortality-associated factors have been studied in HM patients to guide decision making and clinical practice, UK-based research remains limited. This single-centre retrospective service evaluation (SE) aimed to review characteristics and hospital outcomes of patients admitted to our ICU because of HM. Consecutive adults with HM-related admissions to a multi-specialty ICU between January 2022 and October 2024 were retrospectively identified. Data were extracted for patient characteristics, ICU interventions and hospital outcomes. Associations with ICU mortality rates were also assessed. During the SE, there were 227 ICU admissions of HM patients, of which 168 were HM-related and, hence, included in subsequent analysis. The most common reasons for admission were respiratory failure (36.3%) and sepsis (26.2%). ICU and in-hospital mortality rates were 44.0% and 53.0%, respectively. ICU mortality rates increased significantly with APACHE II and SOFA scores (both p < 0.001), and in patients with leukaemia (p = 0.021), graft versus host disease (p = 0.001), treatment limitations (p < 0.001) or that were chemotherapy naïve (p = 0.044). In patients surviving to ICU discharge, 31.9% were unable to mobilise out of bed at this point. By hospital discharge, 94.9% of surviving patients were mobile; however, 25.3% required ongoing rehabilitation. This SE describes the characteristics, outcomes and mortality-associated factors in patients with HM-related admissions to our ICU, which may be useful in aiding clinician understanding and guiding future practice. Prospective, robust studies are needed to validate findings and explore future opportunities to enhance patient outcomes in this cohort. The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

42990992.title: Comments on Kroken et al.'s "Long-term frailty trajectory in older ICU survivors requiring mechanical ventilation: a prospective cohort study in Norway".

42990983.title: Physiological implications of tracheostomy in critical care-a narrative review.
42990983.abstract: Tracheostomy is a core component of critical care medicine. Although its use is traditionally justified by anticipated improvements in respiratory mechanics and patient comfort, the exact pathophysiological mechanisms are complex. The objective of this narrative review is to examine the physiological changes associated with tracheostomy, focusing on alterations on respiratory mechanics, patient-ventilator interactions, and the implications for speech and swallowing. A comprehensive literature search of the PubMed (MEDLINE) database was conducted for articles published up to May 2026. The review synthesized data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective and retrospective observational studies, and relevant systematic reviews involving critically ill adult populations. Contrary to common clinical belief, transitioning from an endotracheal tube (ETT) to a tracheostomy leads to a marginal reduction in dead space (Vd). The primary respiratory benefit is a reduction in the resistive work of breathing (WOB). Post-tracheostomy dysphagia and dysphonia are highly prevalent and multifactorial, driven by pre-existing laryngeal trauma from intubation and the loss of trans-laryngeal airflow. Evidence demonstrates that early cuff deflation significantly reduces silent aspiration and enhances laryngeal rehabilitation. The clinical benefits of tracheostomy can be appreciated through an understanding of the physiological effects of tracheostomy. Management of patients with tracheostomy in critical care requires early, multidisciplinary intervention.

42990941.title: Evaluation of Phenobarbital and Benzodiazepine Use for Alcohol Withdrawal Treatment in the Medical Intensive Care Unit.
42990941.abstract: There is a high prevalence of alcohol use disorder (AUD) leading to a significant risk of alcohol withdrawal syndrome (AWS) in critically ill patients. However, despite existing guidelines, there is limited evidence on the use of phenobarbital for AWS as part of a standardized protocol for medical intensive care unit (ICU) patients. This study aims to compare ICU length of stay for patients receiving phenobarbital and benzodiazepines versus benzodiazepines alone when treating AWS. This study was a single-center, retrospective, pre-post analysis that compared pre-pathway patients admitted between January 2017 and January 2020 who received benzodiazepines alone to post-pathway patients admitted between August 2022 and September 2024 who received phenobarbital in addition to benzodiazepines for AWS. Patients were included if they were hospitalized with an ICD-10 code for alcohol withdrawal, admitted to the ICU with medical critical care as the primary team, and, for the post-pathway group, must have received phenobarbital from the pathway. The primary outcome was ICU length of stay, while secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay, incidence and length of mechanical ventilation, cumulative benzodiazepines dose, incidence of delirium, and use of adjunctive medications for AWS. A total of 132 patients were included in the analysis (n = 92 pre-pathway and n = 40 post-pathway). The median ICU length of stay for the pre-pathway group was 2.95 (interquartile range [IQR] 1.80-5.05) days compared to 2.60 (IQR 1.95-6.75) days for post-pathway group (P = .86). The median hospital length of stay was statistically significant at 8.9 (IQR 5.0-15.5) days for the pre-pathway group compared to 6 (IQR 3.3-12.05) days for the post-pathway group (P = .02). There was no significant difference in mechanical ventilation, use of anti-psychotics, or use of adjunctive agents for AWS (P > .05). There was no significant difference found in the ICU length of stay between the pre-pathway group and the post-pathway group. However, the hospital length of stay for the post-pathway group was statistically shorter than that of the pre-pathway group. These findings suggest that phenobarbital seems to be safe and effective alternative for AWS, and benzodiazepine-sparing regimens should be considered.

42989800.title: Percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy in adult intensive care: An ANZICS consensus statement.
42989800.abstract: Percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy (PDT) is a commonly performed procedure in intensive care units; However, the high-quality evidence base guiding many aspects of its practice remains limited, resulting in variation across clinicians and institutions. This statement was drafted by a panel of experts, later reviewed by an expert working group comprising representatives from the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society and the College of Intensive Care Medicine, and endorsed by the boards of both organisations. The recommendations presented are based on the best available evidence and, where evidence is scarce, on structured expert consensus. The scope of this statement is confined to PDT in adult intensive care patients. This document reflects current practice at the time of publication and is intended to be a living document, subject to regular review to include emerging evidence and evolving standards of care. In summary, this consensus statement provides evidence-informed, expert-guided recommendations to standardise PDT practice in adult ICUs across Australia and New Zealand, while acknowledging current variability and gaps in the evidence base.

42992375.title: Gender differences in acute poisoning: a 35-year cohort study.
42992375.abstract: Drug overdose is an increasingly common cause of death, more commonly in males. In contrast, women present more commonly to emergency departments with overdose. We therefore aim to investigate gender differences in the characteristics and severity of acute poisoning. Adult (18-64 y) poisoning admissions to a tertiary toxicology service were reviewed (1990-2024), and females were compared to males. Data were extracted from a prospective database, including drug/toxin ingested, clinical effects, treatment, length of stay, intensive care admission and death. Primary outcomes were death, intensive care admission and intubation. There were 22,316 (75%) deliberate self-poisonings - 14,101 females (63%), 8,178 males and 37 transgender; 2,101 (7%) recreational overdoses - 695 (33%) females and 1,406 (67%) males. Females ingested more paracetamol/analgesics, antidepressants and quetiapine, while males ingested more alcohol, amphetamines and opioids. Median age for deliberate self-poisoning in females (33 years [IQR:24-44 years]) was similar to males (34 years [IQR:25-44 years]). There were 1,268 females (9.0%) admitted to intensive care, compared to 912 males (11.2%), which was significantly different (absolute difference 2.2%;95% CI:1.3-3.0%; P < 0.001). Less females were intubated than males (790 [5.6%] vs 549 [6.7%]; P = 0.001). Inpatient mortality was similar for females (32; 0.2%) and males (24; 0.3%), and no difference in length of stay. More females had hypotension, while more males developed coma and hepatotoxicity. Males were more likely to receive sedation and naloxone. Gender differences were similar for recreational poisoning, except greater mortality in males. Gender remained an independent predictor of intensive care and intubation in a multivariate logistic regression model, with males more likely to be intubated and admitted to intensive care. More males took recreational overdoses, including opioids, and females had more deliberate self-poisoning, with less toxic medications. Female deliberate self-poisoning patients were less commonly intubated and admitted to intensive care. Drug type did not account for the gender difference in outcomes. We found only minor differences between inpatient morbidity and mortality for females compared to males. Males were more likely to be admitted to intensive care and be intubated, mainly due to higher rates of coma.

42992140.title: Association Between Eosinophils and Readmission in Patients with Eosinophil-Fluctuating AECOPD: A Multi-Threshold PWP-GT Analysis.
42992140.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
42992140.abstract: Although peripheral blood eosinophils (EOS) have been extensively studied as a biomarker for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), the association between EOS and COPD prognosis remains controversial. Our objective was to analyze the relationship between EOS and readmission in patients with EOS-fluctuating COPD. This is a retrospective, single-center study of inpatients admitted to the Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine at Anhui Second People's Hospital between January 2021 and June 2026 due to at least two acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD). Prentice-Williams-Peterson Gap Time (PWP-GT) models were established using EOS thresholds of 100cells/ μL, 200cells/ μL, 30cells/ μL, 1%, 2%, and 3%. The relationship between EOS levels at the time of the previous hospitalization and the time interval until the next hospitalization was analyzed. The study included 224 patients and 1095 hospitalizations. EOS ≥ 300 cells/ μL (HR = 0.767, 95% CI: 0.602-0.977, P = 0.032) and EOS% ≥ 3% (HR = 0.804, 95% CI: 0.671-0.965, P = 0.019) were independent protective factors against readmission. EOS ≥ 100 cells/μL (P = 0.070), EOS ≥ 1% (P = 0.100), EOS ≥ 2% (P = 0.094), and EOS ≥ 200 cells/μL (P = 0.189) were not significantly associated with readmission. The protective effects of EOS ≥ 300 cells/μL and EOS% ≥ 3% were consistent across subgroup analyses stratified by sex, history of acute exacerbations, mechanical ventilation, and comorbidities. The protective effect of EOS was more pronounced in patients aged <65 years and in those using inhaled pharmacotherapy. Patients with EOS-fluctuating AECOPD have a unique prognostic profile. Higher eosinophil levels were associated with a lower risk of rehospitalization.

42991563.title: Risk Factors for Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia in Patients Ventilated for Non-Pulmonary Conditions: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study (PULMIVAP).
42991563.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a frequent complication of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), yet its determinants in patients ventilated for non-pulmonary indications remain poorly characterized. Data were derived from the PULMIVAP multicenter prospective cohort (ClinicalTrial: NCT04849039), conducted in 8 Northern Italian intensive care units (January 2021-April 2024). All adults receiving IMV for non-pulmonary indications were enrolled if expected to require IMV >48 hours and antibiotic-free for ≥3 days preceding intubation. Clinical and therapeutic data were collected for up to 15 days of IMV; microbiological sampling was performed according to clinical indication. The primary outcome was time to first VAP within 15 days of IMV (VAP15). Associations between baseline characteristics, time-varying exposures, and VAP15 were evaluated. Thirty-day mortality from IMV initiation was a secondary outcome. Among 406 patients, 148 (36%) developed VAP15, at a median of 6 days (IQR 4.0-7.5) with an incidence rate of 43.2 per 1000 ventilator-days at risk (95% confidence intervals [95% CI], 36.4-49.9). Non-neurologic diagnosis (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.51; 95% CI, 0.31-0.86), female sex (aHR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.36-0.75), and early antibiotic initiation (days 1-2 of IMV, aHR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.45-0.93) were independently associated with lower risk of VAP15. Predominant pathogens were Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella spp., and Haemophilus influenzae; multidrug-resistant organisms were uncommon. VAP15 showed no competing relationship or significant association with mortality (overall, 20.4%). In patients receiving IMV for non-pulmonary indications, non-neurologic diagnosis, female sex, and early antibiotic exposure were associated with lower observed VAP incidence, though causality cannot be inferred. Risk-stratified prevention strategies warrant further investigation into this population.

42991039.title: Update in short-term mechanical circulatory support: indications, devices and complications.
42991039.abstract: Despite advances in early recognition, aetiology-directed therapy, intensive cardiovascular care and short-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS), cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with high mortality and morbidity. MCS can restore systemic perfusion and stabilise patients as a bridge to recovery or advanced heart failure therapies, or as a bridge-to-decision when the final therapeutic destination remains uncertain. However, appropriate patient and device selection remains challenging. The optimal timing of support is uncertain, as both premature implantation and delayed use in advanced shock may limit benefit while increasing complications. Device selection should therefore be individualised according to the predominant patient phenotype, including left ventricular, right ventricular or biventricular failure, concomitant respiratory failure, vascular access and anatomical considerations. Randomised trials have focused predominantly on acute myocardial infarction-related CS, whereas data in heart failure-related and acute-on-chronic CS remain limited. Recent trials have also shown that greater haemodynamic support does not uniformly translate into improved survival, highlighting the importance of matching device physiology to shock phenotype and clinical trajectory. MCS is associated with clinically relevant complications, including major bleeding, haemolysis, limb ischaemia, stroke, thrombosis and vascular injury. Accordingly, its use should be considered within a strategy integrating reversibility, neurological prognosis, recovery potential, a realistic definitive therapeutic strategy, technical feasibility and anticipated complication risk. This Mini Review summarises contemporary indications, devices and complications of MCS in CS, with emphasis on phenotype-guided selection, timing, intensive care management and current evidence gaps.

42989095.title: Risk factors and molecular epidemiology of ST2-type carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii carrying bla(OXA-23-like) and bla(OXA-51-like) genes.
42989095.abstract: The emergence and spread of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB, A. baumannii) has raised significant concerns and challenges globally. This study analyzes the risk factors, distribution of antibiotic resistance genes, and virulence genes associated with CRAB infections, and explores the molecular epidemiological characteristics of CRAB. The findings provide scientific evidence for the development of prevention and treatment strategies for CRAB. A total of 100 patients diagnosed with A. baumannii(AB) infection through culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were included in the study. These patients were classified into the CRAB group and the carbapenem-sensitive A. baumannii (CSAB) group based on their susceptibility to carbapenem antibiotics. Univariate analysis was used to screen for factors associated with CRAB infection, and significant variables were included in a multivariate logistic regression analysis. Additionally, five CRAB strains carrying both blaOXA-51-like and blaOXA-23-like genes were randomly selected for multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and whole-genome sequencing. The analysis included the identification of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs), virulence factor genes, pathogen-host interaction annotations from the Pathogen Host Interactions Database, and functional annotations through Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG). Significant differences were observed between the CRAB group and the CSAB group in terms of length of hospital stay (P = 0.022, OR = 1.068), ICU admission rate (P = 0.019, OR = 8.032), prior carbapenem use (P = 0.028, OR = 4.445), and mechanical ventilation use (P = 0.044, OR = 7.226). In vitro antimicrobial susceptibility testing showed that all CRAB strains were resistant to ceftriaxone, ceftazidime, and ciprofloxacin, with some strains showing resistance to levofloxacin (87.5%) and doxycycline (93.8%), but remaining sensitive to tigecycline and polymyxin B. Through multiplex PCR analysis, we tested 48CRAB strains (carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii). The results revealed that 41 of these strains carried both the blaOXA-51-like and blaOXA-23-like genes. The presence rate of OXA-type β-lactamase genes and efflux pump genes in randomly selected positive strains is 100%. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) annotation results indicated that the genes of these randomly selected positive strains were primarily involved in cellular processes, metabolic pathways, and environmental information processing, and exhibited strong enzymatic activity and binding functions. Length of hospital stay, ICU admission, prior carbapenem use, and mechanical ventilation are susceptibility factors for carbapenem resistance in A. baumannii infections at this hospital. MLST typing and multiplex PCR analysis indicate the spread of ST2-type blaOXA-51-like and blaOXA-23-like positive CRAB infections in the hospital, with ST2-type CRAB potentially being the dominant clone in circulation. Whole-genome sequencing revealed the resistance and virulence characteristics of CRAB strains isolated from clinical samples at this hospital, and showed that these CRAB strains from the hospital are distinct from those found in different provinces and cities in China.

42988923.title: [Prolonged mechanical ventilation after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting].
42988923.abstract: Following coronary bypass surgery, postoperative intensive care plays a central role in the subsequent course of the illness. It is well known that patients with prolonged mechanical ventilation have an increased risk of developing numerous secondary organ complications and consequently have higher morbidity and mortality. The objective of this study was to validate established risk factors for prolonged postoperative mechanical ventilation after isolated coronary bypass surgery in a recent, representative patient collective. In this retrospective, single-center study, all patients who underwent isolated coronary bypass surgery in 2024 and subsequently received interdisciplinary intensive care at the Ulm University Clinic were included. The 312 patients included in the study were between 45 and 85 years old; 84% (n = 262) were male. The median ventilation time for all patients was 15 h (Q1 = 11 h; Q3 = 21 h), whereby 19.5% (n = 61) required prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV). In the multiple logistic regression analysis, intraoperative perfusion time (OR = 1.01; 95% CI 1.0-1.02; p = 0.04) and postoperative peak lactate (OR = 1.26; 95% CI 1.12-1.41; p < 0.001) were significant independent risk factors for PMV. The PMV group also had significantly lower oxygenation indices (Horovitz index = paO2/FiO2), more positive fluid balances on the first and cumulatively on the second postoperative day, longer ischemia and surgical times, and higher European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) scores. Hospital mortality was significantly higher at 8.2% (n = 5) in the PMV group than in the non-PMV group at 0.8% (n = 2). A comprehensive risk profile for prolonged mechanical ventilation is an essential component of intensive care risk stratification and treatment planning. It enables a differentiated assessment of severity and complexity of underlying diseases and thereby associated organ dysfunction. Against this backdrop, necessary intensive care interventions can be initiated early and potentially contribute to improve treatment outcomes.

42989388.title: Bougie guided versus Endotracheal tube with Stylet guided intubation in critically injured patients with Difficult airway characteristics (BEST trial): randomised clinical trial.
42989388.journal: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine
42989388.abstract: Emergency airway management in critically injured trauma patients is frequently complicated by distorted anatomy, airway contamination, cervical spine immobilisation, and prior airway manipulation. Although bougie and stylet are commonly used adjuncts for tracheal intubation, evidence comparing their effectiveness in difficult trauma airways remains limited. We aimed to compare first-pass intubation success between bougie-guided and stylet-guided tracheal intubation in critically injured trauma patients with predefined difficult airway characteristics. In this prospective randomised clinical trial, 188 adult critically injured trauma patients requiring emergency tracheal intubation and having at least one predefined difficult airway characteristic were randomised to bougie-guided intubation (Group B, n = 94) or stylet-guided intubation (Group S, n = 94). All first-attempt intubations were performed by trauma anaesthesia senior residents using video laryngoscopy and a standardised drug-assisted delayed sequence intubation protocol. The primary outcome was first-pass intubation success. Secondary outcomes included time to intubation, rescue airway interventions, need for alternate adjunct or front-of-neck access, and peri-intubation complications. First-pass intubation success was achieved in 67 of 94 patients (71.3%) in Group B and 63 of 94 patients (67.0%) in Group S, corresponding to an absolute difference of 4.3% points (95% CI, - 8.9 to 17.2; p = 0.53). Time to successful first-attempt intubation was similar between groups (39.55 ± 11.72 s in Group B versus 37.97 ± 13.54 s in Group S; mean difference 1.58 s, 95% CI - 2.80 to 5.97; p = 0.48). Emergency front-of-neck access was required in one patient in Group B. Oesophageal intubation occurred in five patients (5.3%) in Group S and in none in Group B; this difference did not reach statistical significance using Fisher's exact test (p = 0.059). On multivariable logistic regression, polytrauma with facial fractures was associated with increased odds of first-pass intubation failure (adjusted OR 2.54, 95% CI 1.10-5.83; p = 0.028). In selected trauma patients with predefined difficult-airway characteristics undergoing protocolised delayed sequence intubation with video laryngoscopy, no statistically significant difference in first-pass success was observed between bougie-guided and stylet-guided intubation. Oesophageal intubation occurred only in the stylet group, an exploratory finding that requires confirmation in larger studies. The trial was approved by the Institute Ethics Committee (IEC-INT-2022/MD-543) and registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2022/11/047043).

42995086.title: [Surgery in transition: Impact of the early COVID-19 pandemic on visceral surgery in Germany].
42995086.journal: Zeitschrift fur Evidenz, Fortbildung und Qualitat im Gesundheitswesen
42995086.abstract: Changes in visceral surgical care in Germany during the early COVID-19 pandemic have not yet been sufficiently described. To date, data on in-hospital mortality and postoperative complications remain limited. In this retrospective analysis, anonymized administrative data from the Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Destatis) for the period from 2018 to 2021 were evaluated comparatively, focusing on the most frequently performed visceral surgical procedures nationwide. Demographic characteristics, procedure volumes, length of hospital stay on regular wards and intensive care units, postoperative complications, and in-hospital mortality were analyzed. A total of approximately 2.1 million procedures were recorded over the 4-year study period. Compared with the pre-pandemic years 2018 and 2019, procedure volumes decreased by approximately 9% in 2020 and 2021, respectively. The average length of stay in the intensive care unit and in hospital decreased during the pandemic. Postoperative complications, including pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, sepsis, and peritonitis, increased during the pandemic years compared with the preceding years. Overall in-hospital mortality in visceral surgery increased from 2.43% in 2018 to 2.55% in 2020 and 2.53% in 2021. In particular, in-hospital mortality in colorectal surgery increased from 7.37% in 2019 to 7.95% in 2021, while the mortality among COVID-19-positive patients following colorectal procedures reached 48%. In contrast, mortality rates in esophageal, hepatic, and pancreatic surgery remained largely unchanged. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Germany experienced a substantial reduction in the volume of visceral surgical procedures and hospital length of stay, while postoperative complications and in-hospital mortality increased. A potential causal relationship with SARS-CoV-2 cannot be established based on the available data. These findings emphasize the importance of systematically evaluating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on surgical care in Germany and of developing evidence-based strategies to maintain surgical capacity and patient safety during future pandemics.

42993902.title: Beyond Prophylaxis: Antimicrobial Stewardship for Bacterial Infections in Cirrhosis.

42992670.title: Genomic Features and Risk Factors of Carbapenem-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Bloodstream Infections.
42992670.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) bloodstream infection is associated with high mortality and limited treatment options. This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single Chinese hospital from January 2020 to January 2026 and included adult patients with P. aeruginosa bloodstream infection. Clinical data were extracted from the hospital information system, and whole-genome sequencing was performed on 48 CRPA isolates to determine multilocus sequence types, carbapenemase genes, and capsular serotypes. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with CRPA acquisition. Among 110 patients, 48 (43.6%) had CRPA bloodstream infection. Prior ICU stay within 1 month (adjusted OR = 5.67, 95% CI: 2.81-11.45, p < 0.001) and prior carbapenem exposure within 30 days (adjusted OR = 3.89, 95% CI: 1.92-7.88, p < 0.001) were independent risk factors for CRPA acquisition. ST-3757 was the predominant sequence type (39/48, 81.3%), KPC-2 was the predominant carbapenemase gene (32/48, 66.7%), and O11 was the most frequent serotype (12/48, 25.0%). All ST-3757 isolates shared pairwise average nucleotide identity above 98.5%, and phylogenetic analysis placed them in a single well-supported clade. These findings indicate that prior healthcare exposure and carbapenem use drive CRPA bloodstream infection in this setting and that an ST-3757-O11-KPC-2 lineage is locally epidemic, supporting targeted antimicrobial stewardship and genomic surveillance.

42995736.title: Clinical impact of early enteral nutrition support combined with comfort nursing on prognosis of critically ill ICU patients undergoing ventilator assisted ventilation.
42995736.journal: Malawi medical journal : the journal of Medical Association of Malawi
42995736.abstract: We aimed to clarify the impact of early enteral nutrition support combined with comfort nursing on the prognosis of critically ill patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) who received ventilator-assisted ventilation. 100 critically ill patients admitted to our ICU were selected and randomly divided into the control group (CG) and the observation group (OG). The OG initiated early enteral nutrition support within 24 h after admission to ICU and received comfort nursing. The CG initiated enteral nutrition support after admission to the ICU based on monitoring biochemical indicators and received routine ICU nursing. The nutritional status, immune function, total malnutrition rate, incidence of pulmonary infection, ventilator weaning time and ICU hospitalization time of the two groups were measured and compared. The levels of albumin (ALB), total protein (TP), and globulin (GLB) in both groups were higher than those at admission to the ICU, while OG group were higher than CG group (P < 0.05). The PCT levels of both groups decreased compared to the levels during the period from admission to the ICU, while OG group was greater decrease than CG group (P < 0.05). The overall malnutrition rate in OG group was lower than that in CG group (P < 0.05). The incidence of pulmonary infection in OG group was lower than that in CG group (P < 0.05). The time to weaning from the ventilator and the ICU stay time in OG group were shorter than those in CG group (P < 0.05). For critically ill ICU patients undergoing ventilator assisted ventilation, early enteral nutrition support combined with comfort nursing can effectively reduce risk of malnutrition and pulmonary infection, enhance immune function, create convenient conditions for early weaning and early conversion to general wards, with broad clinical application prospects.

42998595.title: Living with mechanical ventilation: A grounded theory study of patients' experiences in the intensive care unit.
42998595.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
42998595.abstract: Mechanical ventilation (MV) is an essential life-sustaining intervention in intensive care units (ICU). However, beyond its physiological benefits, patients frequently experience profound physical dependence, communication barriers, and emotional distress. Understanding these experiences is essential to inform person-centred nursing care and humanisation strategies in critical care settings. The aim of this study was to explore the experiences of patients receiving invasive MV, identify the meanings attributed to these experiences, and generate a substantive theory to inform humanised critical care nursing. A qualitative study based on Classical Grounded Theory (Glaser and Strauss) was conducted. Adult patients who received invasive MV for at least 48 h in the ICU at Vall d'Hebron University Hospital (Barcelona, Spain) participated in semistructured interviews. Data were analysed using constant comparative analysis involving open, axial, and selective coding, supported by NVivo 12 software. Guba and Lincoln's criteria were applied to ensure trustworthiness. Extreme Vulnerability was identified as the core category explaining patients' experiences. Participants described profound bodily dependence associated with invasive medical devices and immobility, an inability to communicate that generated frustration and helplessness, and emotional isolation during critical illness. Nurses mitigated distress by recognising nonverbal communication, maintaining a therapeutic presence, and providing continuity of care, while family members provided emotional support through their reassuring presence and by helping healthcare professionals interpret participants' nonverbal cues. Following ICU discharge, participants described the transition to the general ward not only as a positive step towards recovery but also as a period of adjustment characterised by uncertainty and reduced perceived continuity and intensity of care. Invasive MV was experienced not only as a life-sustaining intervention but also as a period of profound bodily dependence, disrupted communication, and reliance on others during critical illness. These findings highlight the need to integrate technical excellence with person-centred, relational care. By providing a substantive grounded theory of Extreme Vulnerability, this study highlights the central role of critical care nurses in leading person-centred interventions, promoting active family involvement, and humanising intensive care practice throughout the care trajectory.

42998594.title: Height estimation in intensive care: A comparative study.
42998594.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
42998594.abstract: Accurate height and weight measurements are essential in critical care to guide various aspects of patient management, including medication dosing, ventilator settings and the calculation of physiological parameters. However, there is no consensus on the optimal method for estimating height in the intensive care unit (ICU). The aim of this study was to determine the accuracy of various methods of height estimation in the critical care setting, including a smartphone measurement application. This cross-sectional study was performed in the intensive care unit at Sunshine Coast University Hospital. Participants were adult volunteers recruited from intensive care staff or outpatient waiting areas. Height was measured using four different methods. Direct measurements using paper tape or the Measure™ (Apple Inc, USA) iPhone app, and an indirect measurement derived from ulna length, were compared with the gold-standard stadiometric height measurement. Seventy-seven participants were included in the analysis. The paper tape and iPhone methods demonstrated excellent agreement with stadiometric height, with strong correlations on Bland-Altman analysis and Deming regression (R2 = 0.89 and 0.91, respectively). By contrast, predictions made using ulna length were less accurate (R2 = 0.59). The Barbosa ulna model demonstrated moderate accuracy in estimating height (R2 = 0.73) but showed reduced accuracy across different sexes and age groups in our population. Population-specific equations were derived, increasing the accuracy of tape, iPhone, and ulna-based methods (R2 = 0.91, 0.93, and 0.72 respectively), demonstrating their potential applicability for predicting height from ulna length. Paper tape and iPhone methods provided the most accurate height estimations. However, population-specific ulna equations offer a practical alternative when direct measurement is not feasible in real-world critical care settings.

42997294.title: Clinical Profile, Indications, and Maternal Outcomes of Obstetric Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Admissions: A Retrospective Study With Emphasis on Critical Care Interventions.
42997294.abstract: Background Maternal morbidity and mortality continue to pose considerable problems to global health systems, especially in developing countries like India. The monitoring of the number of patients admitted to obstetric intensive care units (ICU) is an important measure of the incidence of severe maternal morbidity and the quality of emergency obstetric care available to patients. Objective To improve maternal health care services, there must be an understanding of the clinical characteristics, reasons for admission, and outcomes of these patients. Methods  A retrospective observational study was conducted in the obstetric ICU of a tertiary care teaching hospital from January 2025 through December 2025. A total of 120 obstetric patients (pregnant women and women within 42 days postpartum) admitted to the ICU were included. Information regarding patients' demographic characteristics, obstetric profile, reasons for ICU admission, critical care interventions performed, and maternal outcomes was obtained from medical records. The collected data were analyzed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corporation, Armonk, USA). Results A total of 120 obstetric patients were admitted to the intensive care unit. Hypertensive disorders were the most common indication for ICU admission (42; 35%), followed by obstetric hemorrhage (36; 30%) and sepsis (18; 15%). Blood transfusion was the most frequently provided critical care intervention (84; 70%), followed by mechanical ventilation (48; 40%), vasopressor support (30; 25%), and dialysis/renal replacement therapy (6; 5%). Overall, 102 (85%) patients recovered and were discharged, while 18 (15%) patients died. Delayed referral, multi-organ dysfunction, and requirement for mechanical ventilation were significantly associated with maternal mortality (all p < 0.001). Conclusion Hypertensive disorders and obstetric hemorrhage were the leading indications for obstetric ICU admission. Delayed referral, multi-organ dysfunction, and requirement for mechanical ventilation were significantly associated with maternal mortality. Timely referral and access to multidisciplinary critical care remain important in the management of critically ill obstetric patients.

42995430.title: Unraveling Improvisational Behavior Among Critical Care Nurses in Relation to Integral Leadership, Job Crafting, and Digital Competence: A Moderated Mediation Analysis.
42995430.abstract: To examine the direct and indirect associations of integral leadership on critical care nurses' improvisational behavior through job crafting and to test the moderating role of digital competence. Critical care nurses work in high-acuity, technology-intensive environments that require rapid judgment, flexible coordination, and adaptive responses when routine procedures are insufficient. However, limited evidence explains how improvisational behavior can be shaped among critical care nurses within digitally transforming healthcare systems. A cross-sectional analytical correlational design was used. Data were collected over three months in 2025 from 425 critical care nurses working in 31 intensive care units across 10 hospitals in Egypt. Anonymous, self-administered questionnaires were used to assess integral leadership, job crafting, digital competence, and improvisational behavior. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and regression-based moderated mediation analysis. Integral leadership was positively associated with critical care nurses' improvisational behavior and job crafting, while job crafting was positively associated with improvisational behavior. Integral leadership demonstrated a significant direct association with improvisational behavior, and its indirect association through job crafting was also significant. Digital competence was positively associated with job crafting and significantly moderated the relationship between integral leadership and job crafting, with a stronger association observed among nurses with higher digital competence. The conditional indirect association of integral leadership with improvisational behavior through job crafting was also stronger at higher levels of digital competence. The findings highlight the importance of considering integral leadership, proactive work redesign, and digital competence together when understanding improvisational behavior in critical care nursing. This integrated perspective may help nursing organizations create work environments that enable nurses to respond adaptively to unexpected clinical demands while maintaining safe and professionally appropriate practice. Nurse managers should create conditions that support safe improvisational behavior by providing nurses with leadership support and appropriate autonomy, encouraging responsible job crafting within professional boundaries, and providing targeted digital competence training. Simulation-based training and structured debriefing of unexpected clinical situations may also help nurses develop and reflect on adaptive responses while maintaining patient-safety standards.

42998371.title: Analysis of tranexamic acid in hemoptysis: effectiveness in a noninterventional evaluation (ATHENE).
42998371.abstract: Hemoptysis is a common reason for respiratory ICU admission and may rapidly become life‑threatening. For patients not requiring immediate bronchial artery embolization (BAE), no pharmacologic standard exists. Despite growing use after encouraging early reports, the real‑world effectiveness of nebulized tranexamic acid (TXA) in ICU practice remains uncertain. To assess whether nebulized TXA reduces early hemoptysis recurrence in ICU patients not requiring emergent BAE. Single‑center retrospective cohort (2017-2021) including adults admitted for hemoptysis; exclusions were bleeding >200 mL at admission or BAE within 6 h. Propensity score matching (1:2, with replacement) used admission bleeding volume, etiology, prior hemoptysis, and anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy, with adequate post‑matching balance. The primary endpoint was 72‑hour recurrence (≥50 mL cumulative bleeding). Secondary endpoints included 30‑day recurrence, acute respiratory failure, BAE, length of stay, and 30‑day mortality. Conditional logistic regression was applied. Among 228 patients, 75 (33%) received nebulized TXA, with use rising from 0% to 78% over the study period. After matching (75 TXA and 147 control observations), hemoptysis recurrence at 72 h was similar between groups: recurrence occurred in 12.3% of patients in the control group versus 10.7% in the TXA group, with no significant difference between groups (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.37-2.32). No differences were found in 30‑day recurrence, acute respiratory failure, BAE, or length of stay. Thirty‑day mortality was higher in the TXA group (9.3%vs 1.9%; OR5.9, 95%CI1.2-28.8), driven by few events mostly related to underlying malignancy. In this real‑world ICU cohort, nebulized TXA did not reduce hemoptysis recurrence at 72 h. Nonetheless, TXA use increased markedly during the study period, reflecting a significant shift in clinical practice. This rapid uptake underscores clinical interest and strengthens the need for adequately powered randomized trials to define the role of inhaled TXA in hemoptysis management.

42997605.title: Comparison of costs and health outcomes of mPOCT NEAR technology to PCR and LFD for influenza detection in the United Arab Emirates.
42997605.abstract: Influenza shares many symptoms with other respiratory diseases, making clinical diagnosis challenging. This study evaluated the clinical and economic outcomes of influenza testing using a rapid molecular point-of-care platform based on isothermal nicking enzyme amplification reaction (mPOCT NEAR), compared with laboratory-based polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and lateral flow diagnostic (LFD) antigen testing, from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) private healthcare payer perspective. A 1-year health economic model was developed. Two high-risk populations were assessed: older adults and children under 5 years. Outcomes included antimicrobial use, otitis media cases, intensive care unit admissions, mechanical ventilation, and prevention of secondary transmissions. Direct medical and complication costs were included. Two antimicrobial scenarios were modeled: antimicrobial use-derived from literature (scenario 1), and antiviral-only treatment for test-positive patients (scenario 2). Across both scenarios, mPOCT NEAR reduced total healthcare costs and improved clinical outcomes compared with PCR-lower antibiotic use, fewer otitis media cases and intensive care unit admissions, and reduced mechanical ventilation and secondary transmissions.Compared with LFD testing, mPOCT NEAR reduced secondary transmissions by 57% in scenario 1 and demonstrated broader clinical benefits in scenario 2. Overall cost savings were observed versus comparators. mPOCT NEAR is cost-saving and clinically advantageous, supporting efficient resource allocation in UAE private healthcare settings.

42997403.title: Evolving Epidemiology of Invasive Candidiasis in Southwest China: A Four-year Analysis of Species Distribution, Antifungal Resistance Profiles, and Mortality Risk Factors.
42997403.abstract: The purpose of this study was to explore the strain distribution, clinical characteristics, antifungal sensitivity and risk factors of 30-day mortality of invasive Candida infection of hospitalized patients. We conducted a four-year retrospective study at a tertiary teaching hospital in Southwest China, enrolling non-duplicate strains isolated from invasive candidiasis samples obtained from hospitalized patients. Of the 345 non-duplicate invasive candidiasis cases, 145 (42%) were candidemia cases. Candida albicans (44.3%) was the most identified species, followed by C. glabrata (18.2%), C. tropicalis (14.5%), and C. parapsilosis (12.5%). Amphotericin B and echinocandins demonstrated potent in vitro activity, whereas Candida species exhibited high resistance rates to azole antifungals, particularly C. tropicalis, whose resistance rate approaches 30%. Compared to patients in general wards, ICU patients exhibited more severe clinical symptoms, higher rates of invasive medical procedures and antibiotic exposure. Multivariate analysis identified hepatobiliary disease, surgical interventions within 6 months, tracheal intubation, ICU admission, and use of aminoglycosides and tetracyclines as independent risk factors for 30-day mortality. Additionally, the study revealed that elevated levels of BDG, and IL-6, as well as reduced PLT, were associated with increased 30-day mortality. A better understanding of the specific risk factors associated with ICU stays could facilitate earlier identification of high-risk candidates for antifungal therapy initiation, thereby improving clinical outcomes for critically ill patients with invasive candidiasis.

42997367.title: Clinical Profile of Patients With Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Patterns of Pseudomonas aeruginosa: A Cross-sectional Prospective Study From a Tertiary Care Hospital in Central India.
42997367.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an important healthcare-associated opportunistic pathogen in healthcare settings, particularly among critically ill and hospitalized patients. Multidrug resistance, particularly carbapenem resistance, is a major problem that restricts treatment options and increases morbidity rates for patients admitted to intensive care. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profile of patients with P. aeruginosa infection and determine the antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of the isolates in a tertiary care hospital in Central India. A hospital-based, cross-sectional prospective study was conducted in the Department of Microbiology, Index Medical College, Hospital and Research Centre, Indore, from January 2023 to December 2025. The study was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee (ref. no.: MU/Research/EC/Ph.D/2023/028). A total of 171 non-duplicate clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa obtained from patients of all age groups were included. Isolates were identified using standard phenotypic methods, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed by the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method according to CLSI 2023 guidelines. Clinical and laboratory data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics, version 27.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, USA), with the chi-square test used to assess associations. From a total of 171 P. aeruginosa isolates, 72 (42.1%) were recovered from respiratory specimens, followed by pus/wound swabs (24.0%), urine (16.4%), and blood (10.5 %). Most isolates were obtained from ICU patients (69.6%), and male patients constituted 65.5% of cases. Hospital-acquired/ventilator-associated pneumonia was the commonest clinical presentation (35.7%). The highest antimicrobial resistance was observed with ceftriaxone (69.0%), ceftazidime (60.2%), and cefepime (57.9%), followed by aztreonam (55.6%), piperacillin-tazobactam (53.8%), and levofloxacin (49.7%). Resistance to imipenem and meropenem was 44.4% and 40.4%, respectively, whereas polymyxin B showed the lowest resistance (2.3%). Significant associations were observed between antimicrobial resistance and ICU stay, prior antibiotic exposure, mechanical ventilation, urinary catheterization, central line/IV catheter use, diabetes mellitus, COPD, chronic kidney disease, and immunocompromised status (p<0.05). P. aeruginosa showed a substantial antimicrobial resistance burden, particularly among ICU patients. Regular local antibiogram surveillance, antimicrobial stewardship, and stringent infection prevention and control measures are essential for optimizing therapy and limiting the emergence of resistant strains.

42997175.title: Profound Hyperbilirubinemia During Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning and Subsequent Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report.
42997175.abstract: Carbon monoxide poisoning is classically associated with neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, while severe exposure may also cause systemic toxic-hypoxic injury. Profound direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia without mechanical biliary obstruction is rarely described. We report a 55-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, chronic tobacco use, COPD, and hepatic steatosis who presented with altered mental status and jaundice after suspected household carbon monoxide exposure. Her carboxyhemoglobin level was > 30%, and she required intubation, intensive care, vasopressor support, and three hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Initial testing showed total bilirubin of 23.1 mg/dL and direct bilirubin of 13.1 mg/dL, despite only mild AST elevation and near-normal ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Imaging showed hepatic steatosis and cholelithiasis without convincing biliary obstruction, and the documented workup for viral, autoimmune, metabolic, hemolytic, and vascular causes was unrevealing. Her liver dysfunction was considered multifactorial, with possible carbon monoxide-related toxic-hypoxic injury superimposed on underlying steatotic or alcohol-related liver vulnerability. After transient improvement, she developed coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, recurrent shock with clinical and imaging concern for acute cholecystitis, worsening hyperbilirubinemia peaking near 49-50 mg/dL, encephalopathy, respiratory failure, and multiorgan failure. Cholecystostomy yielded dark green bile without documented purulence, and aspirate cultures showed no growth; biliary sepsis was therefore not microbiologically confirmed. She died in the hospital after goals-of-care discussions. The initial bilirubin-predominant pattern was atypical for classic hypoxic hepatitis and may have reflected overlapping hepatic insults. This case emphasizes broad evaluation and cautious causal interpretation; it does not establish that carbon monoxide exposure alone caused the initial hyperbilirubinemia.

42996715.title: Deep learning-based CT lesion analysis and radiological burden stratification in clinically diagnosed ventilator-associated pneumonia.
42996715.abstract: Ventilator associated pneumonia (VAP) is a major complication in the intensive care unit (ICU) and requires objective computed tomography (CT) evaluation. Therefore, this article conducted a retrospective research analysis and developed a multimodal deep learning framework. Firstly, this retrospective study included 512 patients clinically diagnosed with VAP, and then utilized a developed multimodal deep learning framework for voxel-level lesion segmentation, multi-label radiological discovery classification, and radiological burden grading. This framework integrates the anatomical priors of TotalSegmenter, a three-dimensional (3D) Swin UNETR multitasking network, and cross attention fusion of CT features and ventilation parameters. Ultimately, the study showed that the Dice score for internal validation was 0.847, the macroscopic mean area (AUC) under the subject's working characteristic curve was 0.919, and the weighted kappa was 0.826. External validation showed a Dice score of 0.821, with no significant difference between scanner manufacturers. After adjusting for clinical covariates, including acute physiology and chronic health assessment II (APACHE II) scores, there was still a significant correlation between radiation load level and 28 day mortality (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.34, P < 0.001), supporting its potential prognostic relevance.

42996897.title: Beyond flow: a ventricular-load framework for VA-ECMO in cardiogenic shock.
42996897.abstract: Cardiogenic shock still carries a 30-day mortality of approximately 40%-50% despite reperfusion, vasoactive support and modern intensive care. Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) can rapidly restore systemic perfusion, but recent randomised evidence has reframed its role. In infarct-related shock, randomised trials have not shown a clear survival benefit from routine early VA-ECMO; ECLS-SHOCK and pooled analyses also found more bleeding and vascular complications. In the same period, DanGer Shock showed that a primary microaxial-pump (Impella CP) strategy improved survival in a carefully selected population with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock, although it was tested against standard care rather than head-to-head against VA-ECMO and does not isolate unloading as the causal mechanism. Read together, these data motivate the central argument of this review: peripheral VA-ECMO is usefully managed not only as a problem of circulatory flow, but also as a dynamic problem of ventricular loading. We advance this as an organising framework rather than as a demonstrated mechanism, since differences in patient selection between these trials offer a competing and equally tenable explanation. Retrograde aortic return increases effective LV afterload, while venous drainage reduces preload; the clinical result depends on the interaction between circuit flow, native contractility and biventricular loading conditions. This narrative, non-systematic review synthesises contemporary trial evidence, the physiology and treatment of LV loading, and approaches to serial assessment of the supported heart, from haemodynamics and bedside echocardiography to emerging deformation and advanced imaging tools. VA-ECMO should therefore be viewed as a time-limited bridge whose net benefit depends on reversible disease, early recognition of clinically relevant ventricular overload and repeated assessment of recovery, escalation options and futility.

42996917.title: Tracheostomy-related bleeding and stomal complications: a literature review.
42996917.abstract: Tracheostomy is one of the most commonly performed procedures in critically ill patients, with bleeding representing the most frequent early complication. Stomal bleeding and granulation tissue formation create ongoing management challenges that can complicate patient care. Other complications include stomal infection, subcutaneous emphysema, focal airway stenosis, and tracheoinnominate fistula (TIF), which differ in clinical severity and management. Current management relies on reactive measures, yet no standardized approach exists for preventing or managing persistent minor bleeding around the tracheostomy site. This study aims to review the incidence, pathophysiology, risk factors, and current management of tracheostomy-related bleeding and stomal complications, with emphasis on identifying gaps in prevention and treatment strategies. We conducted targeted literature searches using PubMed/MEDLINE for English-language human studies published between January 1, 2000 and September 17, 2026 involving adults aged 19 years or older. Search terms included "tracheostomy", "tracheotomy", "bleeding", "hemorrhage", "granulation tissue", "tracheoinnominate fistula", "stomal infection", "cellulitis", "abscess", "decannulation", "dislodgement", "subcutaneous emphysema", "tracheal stenosis", "ECMO", "transplantation", "immunosuppression", "tranexamic acid", "epinephrine", and "cautery". We extracted data on incidence rates, management approaches, and clinical outcomes. Bleeding is the most common early complication of tracheostomy procedures, occurring in 0.6-5.0% of cases overall, with rates reaching 5.7% for major or minor bleeding and up to 40% in high-risk populations such as patients on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Stomal infections, airway complications, and early accidental decannulation is also important to consider in tracheostomy patients. Subcutaneous emphysema was primarily associated with early mechanical complications, whereas focal airway stenosis represented a later consequence of granulation. Management of minor superficial bleeding generally consisted of direct pressure, packing, correction of reversible coagulopathy, and selected topical or cautery-based interventions. TIF remained distinct from these complications because even limited or transient bleeding may precede catastrophic hemorrhage, necessitating urgent recognition and escalation when a vascular source is suspected. Tracheostomy-related bleeding and stomal oozing represent common complications with limited preventive options. Current management is reactive, relying on manual pressure application, packing materials, and procedural interventions. Particular attention should be made to distinguish minor superficial bleeding from sentinel or life-threatening hemorrhage. Novel approaches could potentially reduce bleeding complications, minimize granulation tissue formation, and improve patient comfort during the critical early post-tracheostomy period.

42996070.title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients.
42996070.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
42996070.abstract: Alterations in intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) alpha power and anesthetic dose-adjusted EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) have been associated with both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium (POD) among older surgical patients, yet the neurologic underpinnings of alterations in these anesthetic brain response patterns are unknown. We conducted a single center prospective observational cohort study (ALADDIN), of older adults undergoing non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery, which included preoperative structural and resting state functional MRI, lumbar punctures to obtain CSF, 32 channel intraoperative EEG recordings, and repeated POD assessments. To account for anesthetic dose, frontoparietal EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) was adjusted using our established formula: [intraoperative alpha power]/(2.5 - end-tidal MAC fraction). Multivoxel pattern analysis (MVPA) with follow-up seed-to-voxel analyses identified functional connectivity patterns associated with intraoperative ADA-FP alpha power. Voxel-wise regression analysis with threshold free cluster estimation (TFCE) correction was used to evaluate associations between cortical thickness and ADA-FP alpha power. CSF biomarker values were obtained from NULISA proximity extension assays. Delirium incidence and severity was assessed with the 3-Minute Diagnostic Confusion Assessment Method (3D-CAM). Delirium severity area under the curve (AUC) during hospitalization was defined as the sum of all 3D-CAM delirium severity scores within the postoperative hospitalization period (for up to 7 days after surgery). The Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) was used in cases of non-verbal/intubated patients. ALADDIN enrolled 215 patients, of whom 168 underwent surgery and had high-quality intraoperative EEG data (44.6% female; mean age 70.9 years). MVPA showed that ADA-FP alpha power was associated with altered functional connectivity within the bilateral frontal poles, left superior frontal gyrus and the right superior parietal lobule (p-FWE < 0.05). Seed-to-voxel analyses revealed that higher ADA-FP alpha power was associated with increased connectivity between DMN MVPA regions and DMN, DAN and salience/ventral attention and decreased connectivity with visual regions. Conversely, right superior parietal lobule connectivity shifted towards greater DMN segregation and increased somatosensory/motor coupling (p-FWE < 0.05). Lower ADA-FP alpha power was also associated with lower cortical thickness in left occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortices (TFCE-corrected p < 0.05). ADA-FP alpha power was also lower among participants with (vs those without) postoperative ward/floor delirium (mean difference, 1.33; 95% CI, 0.22 to 2.44; p=0.019), and ADA-FP alpha power was inversely associated with peak delirium severity (spearman's rho = -0.26; 95% CI, -0.40 to -0.11; p <0.001) and delirium severity AUC (spearman's rho = -0.28; 95% CI, -0.42 to -0.13; p < 0.001). These findings suggest a functional and structural neuroanatomic basis for the decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power values seen among some older surgical patients, which may explain the association between decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and increased rates of both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium. More specifically, these findings suggest that altered default mode and dorsal attention network connectivity is linked to decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and raise the possibility that preoperative/baseline functional connectivity alterations within these networks may play a role in delirium risk.

43000177.title: Association Between Medication-Related Skin Punctures and Delirium in the ICU: An Exploratory Cohort Study.
43000177.journal: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
43000177.abstract: Delirium is among the most common neurological complications in intensive care unit (ICU) patients, yet many medication-related contributors remain poorly understood. As medication experts, pharmacists are uniquely positioned to lead efforts in identifying, mitigating, and preventing drug-related risk factors for delirium. One underexplored risk factor is the frequency of medication-related skin punctures. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the association between ICU delirium and the number of medication-related skin punctures, with the goal of identifying potential pharmacist-driven interventions to reduce delirium as well as improve patient experience and outcomes. This was a retrospective, observational, exploratory cohort study conducted in the ICU of a 384-bed community hospital. Patients were divided into two groups, low-punctures and high-punctures, using the median number of skin punctures per day as the threshold for defining groups. The primary outcome was the incidence of delirium. Secondary outcomes were delirium-free days, all-cause mortality, hospital length of stay (LOS), and ICU LOS. A total of 404 patients were included in this study. The median number of medication-related skin punctures was 3.79 per day. There were 205 patients in the low-punctures group (0 to less than 4 punctures per day) and 199 patients in the high-punctures group (at least 4 punctures per day). The high-punctures group was associated with increased odds of delirium (odds ratio [OR] 2.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-3.58, p = 0.007). There was no significant difference in delirium-free days, hospital LOS, and all-cause mortality between groups; however, ICU LOS was significantly longer in the high-punctures group (7 vs. 5 days, p < 0.001). The frequency of medication-related skin punctures ICU patients received may be associated with an increased risk of delirium. These exploratory findings support future research evaluating the impact of pharmacist-driven "skin puncture stewardship" on ICU delirium prevention, patient experience, and overall clinical outcomes.

42999543.title: Prevalence of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder in Iranian Intensive Care Unit Survivors and Related Factors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42999543.abstract: Intensive care unit survivors are discharged with various psychological complications, among which post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is one of the most significant. The main aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of PTSD and its associated factors among Iranian intensive care unit (ICU) survivors. This systematic review and meta-analysis included studies published in English and Persian from 2000 to 2025. Electronic gateways and databases, including MEDLINE via PubMed, MEDLINE via OVID, ISI Web of Knowledge, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library, Magiran, Wiley, Scientific Information Database (SID), and Google Scholar, were searched. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal checklist. Data were analyzed using STATA software (version 17.0, StataCorp/LC, USA). Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, and a random-effects model was applied to estimate pooled prevalence. A significant level of P<0.001was considered. The pooled prevalence of PTSD in Iranian ICU survivors was 36.4% (95% CI: 23.5-48.3; I2=98.75%; P<0.001). The prevalence in Iranian women, 51.47% (95% CI: 45.01-57.92; I2=97.52%), was higher than in Iranian men, 48.53% (95% CI: 42.08-54.99; I2=97.52%). Common related factors included older age, prolonged ICU hospitalization, history of psychiatric disorders, mechanical ventilation, and drug abuse. The prevalence of PTSD among Iranian ICU survivors is relatively high. Identification of associated factors underscores the need for early screening, comprehensive follow-up programs, and targeted psychological interventions, particularly for high-risk populations.

43000034.title: Efficacy Heterogeneity of Hemoperfusion Plus Continuous Venovenous Hemofiltration for Hypertriglyceridemia-Induced Acute Pancreatitis Stratified by Severity of Inflammatory Response.
43000034.journal: Therapeutic apheresis and dialysis : official peer-reviewed journal of the International Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Dialysis Therapy
43000034.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the heterogeneity in the efficacy of hemoperfusion (HP) plus continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH) versus CVVH alone in reducing the incidence of severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) among patients with hypertriglyceridemia-induced acute pancreatitis (HTG-AP), stratified by the inflammatory marker C-reactive protein (CRP). In addition, we assessed secondary outcomes encompassing laboratory response, disease severity and organ function, healthcare resource utilization, and treatment-related indicators, so as to delineate the broader efficacy profile of the combination therapy and its relationship with the primary endpoint. Furthermore, we sought to identify a CRP-based therapeutic window for the combination therapy. This single-center retrospective study included 204 patients who were assigned to the HP + CVVH group (n = 103) or the CVVH group (n = 101). Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the overall difference in efficacy between the two groups. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) were employed to analyze the nonlinear relationship between treatment efficacy and CRP levels and to identify a CRP-based therapeutic window. Secondary outcomes were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression for categorical variables and generalized linear models for quantitative variables. After multivariable adjustment, the incidence of SAP did not differ significantly between the HP + CVVH and CVVH groups (p > 0.05). RCS analysis revealed a significant interaction between treatment group and CRP levels. The conditional odds ratio for SAP (HP + CVVH vs. CVVH) was significantly below 1 only within a specific CRP range: 194.96-296.91 mg/L in the primary analysis and 200.77-285.81 mg/L after propensity score adjustment (p < 0.05). Regarding secondary outcomes, HP + CVVH was associated with significantly lower CRP, procalcitonin, and triglyceride levels on day 3, more SIRS-free days within 14 days, lower peak intra-abdominal pressure, shorter ICU length of stay, fewer CVVH sessions, earlier initiation of enteral nutrition, and higher blood purification-related costs (all p < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in organ failure-free days, incidence of pancreatic necrosis, hospital length of stay, total hospitalization cost, total morphine equivalent dose, carbapenem use, or duration of mechanical ventilation (all p > 0.05). HP + CVVH showed no overall superiority to CVVH alone in preventing SAP. Nevertheless, secondary outcome analyses demonstrated improved inflammatory control, faster resolution of systemic inflammatory response, reduced intra-abdominal pressure, and better recovery in several resource-related and treatment-related indicators, indicating measurable biological and clinical process benefits. These benefits, however, did not translate into a uniform reduction in SAP. The effect of HP + CVVH on the hard endpoint was conditional, nonlinear, and dependent on baseline inflammatory burden, with significant benefit confined to a specific CRP therapeutic window. Therefore, improvements in secondary endpoints should not be equated with hard-endpoint benefit, and the decision to initiate HP + CVVH should be individualized according to the intensity of the inflammatory response.
