42999829.title: Boerhaave Syndrome: Case Report on a Rare Complication of Semaglutide Use.
42999829.abstract: Esophageal perforation is a rare but life-threatening condition with high morbidity and mortality, particularly when diagnosis is delayed. Boerhaave syndrome, a spontaneous esophageal rupture often triggered by forceful emesis, can present variably and is frequently difficult to recognize early. We report the case of a 62-year-old female patient who developed Boerhaave syndrome two days after initiating semaglutide therapy for weight loss. She presented with intractable nausea, vomiting, and acute chest pain. The chest CT was concerning for esophageal perforation. She rapidly deteriorated into hypoxemic respiratory failure and septic shock. She underwent emergent thoracotomy with primary repair of the perforation. She continued to be treated for septic shock in the ICU, but ultimately she recovered and was discharged on hospital day 17. As GLP-1 use continues to expand, clinicians should maintain awareness of rare but life-threatening complications such as Boerhaave syndrome, as early recognition, prompt imaging, and timely surgical intervention are critical to improving outcomes.

42999828.title: Clinical Characteristics, Etiologies, and Outcomes of Adults Presenting With Altered Mental Status to the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
42999828.abstract: Background Altered mental status (AMS) is a common emergency presentation with diverse neurological, infectious, metabolic, toxicological, and systemic causes. Objective The objective of this study was to describe the clinical characteristics, underlying etiologies, management patterns, and clinical outcomes of adults presenting to the emergency department with AMS, and to identify independent clinical factors associated with in-hospital mortality. Methods This retrospective cohort study was conducted at Allama Iqbal Teaching Hospital, Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan, from April 2024 to April 2026 and included 210 adult patients presenting with AMS. Demographic and baseline clinical characteristics, including age, gender, body mass index, smoking status, presenting symptoms, duration of AMS, known comorbidities, medication history, substance use, and relevant previous neurological or systemic illnesses, were recorded. Results Of 210 patients, 174 (82.9%) survived, and 36 (17.1%) died. The mean age was 61.74±16.64 years, and 118 (56.2%) were male. Neurological causes were most common (29.0%), followed by infectious (21.4%), metabolic/endocrine (16.2%), and toxicological causes (11.9%). Non-survivors were older than survivors (72.10±13.80 vs. 59.60±16.40 years, p<0.001) and had lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores (6.90±3.20 vs. 11.60±3.10, p<0.001), lower oxygen saturation (89.10±8.00% vs. 94.60±4.40%, p<0.001), and higher serum lactate levels (4.80±2.70 vs. 2.30±1.60 mmol/L, p<0.001). Intensive care unit (ICU) admission was required in 61 (29.0%) patients, while 42 (20.0%) required mechanical ventilation. Conclusion Altered mental status was associated with considerable ICU utilization and in-hospital mortality. Neurological and infectious causes predominated, while severe impairment of consciousness, elevated lactate, hypoxemia, hypotension, infectious etiology, and advanced age were independently associated with increased odds of mortality.

42999672.title: Cerebral Air Embolism Following Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography Stent Removal: A Rare and Fatal Complication.
42999672.abstract: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is a generally performed procedure for biliary pathology. Although usually safe, air embolism is an exceptionally rare but potentially fatal complication. We report the case of a 79-year-old female (ASA II) with a history of dyslipidemia and obesity, who presented for elective ERCP and biliary stent removal. She had previously undergone ERCP and open cholecystectomy for choledocholithiasis. During this time, sedation was administered by using fentanyl, midazolam, and propofol via target-controlled infusion. The procedure was initially uneventful; however, at its conclusion, the patient developed sudden desaturation, bradycardia, and a reduced level of consciousness. Computed tomography (CT) imaging revealed multiple cerebral air emboli. Despite intensive care management and ventilatory support, the patient deteriorated and died 2 days later. This case highlights the importance of maintaining vigilance for air embolism, even in seemingly straightforward ERCP procedures, especially in elderly patients. Early recognition and immediate management are vital to improving outcomes.

42999355.title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning from Ventilator Waveforms: A Pilot Feasibility Study.
42999355.abstract: Rationale: Modern ventilators generate high-frequency pressure and flow waveforms that contain respiratory mechanics, patient respiratory effort, and patient-ventilator interactions. However, these waveform data remain underutilized for representation learning. Objective: We conducted a pilot feasibility study to evaluate whether self-supervised representation learning can extract clinically relevant respiratory information from ventilator waveforms. Methods: We developed a self-supervised representation learning framework for mechanical ventilation waveforms using airway pressure and flow signals. The model was pretrained on unlabeled waveform segments over 255,355 breaths spanning 197.1 hours of mechanical ventilation across 115 patients and learned latent respiratory representations. Frozen embeddings were subsequently evaluated on held-out patients using downstream tasks, including ventilator mode classification, prediction of respiratory physiological variables, and reconstruction of waveforms. Measurements and Main results: Pretrained embeddings enabled recovery of ventilator modes, achieving a bootstrap-derived median balanced accuracy of 0.791 (95% CI: 0.715, 0.858) and macro-F1 score of 0.765 (95% CI: 0.682, 0.839). The learned representations also supported the prediction of respiratory physiological variables, including respiratory rate and positive end-expiratory pressure. Reconstruction of unseen waveforms achieved a median Pearson correlation of 0.801 (95% CI: 0.727, 0.870) for pressure waveforms and 0.783 (95% CI: 0.709, 0.838) for flow waveforms between the reconstructed and original waveforms. Conclusions: This pilot study demonstrates the feasibility of self-supervised representation learning from ventilator waveforms. Our framework introduces ventilator waveforms as a potentially useful data modality in critical care and establishes a foundation for future investigations of patient-ventilator asynchrony, respiratory state monitoring, and optimization of liberation from mechanical ventilation.

42999910.title: Delayed High-Output Chylothorax Following Thymectomy for Thymoma.
42999910.abstract: Chylothorax is an uncommon complication following thymectomy and results from disruption of the thoracic duct or its tributaries during surgery. We report the case of a 50-year-old man with autoimmune myasthenia gravis who developed a delayed postoperative chylothorax following video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) thymectomy for a type B2 thymoma, Masaoka stage I. On postoperative day 21, the patient presented with acute respiratory distress and severe hypoxemia. Chest computed tomography revealed a large left-sided pleural effusion with extensive passive lung collapse. Thoracentesis in the emergency department evacuated 1.5 L of milky pleural fluid, followed by an additional 4 L after chest tube drainage in the intensive care unit. Pleural fluid analysis revealed a triglyceride concentration of 188 mg/dL, with chylomicrons detected, confirming the diagnosis of chylothorax. The fluid also showed marked lymphocytic predominance (96%). Management included pleural drainage, a strict fat-free diet, and octreotide, administered as a 100 µg slow intravenous loading dose followed by continuous infusion at 50 µg/h. Pleural drainage showed an overall decreasing trend and eventually ceased. Octreotide was discontinued after 13 calendar days, and the chest tube was removed without requiring additional invasive or surgical intervention. The patient was subsequently discharged home. This case illustrates that post-thymectomy chylothorax may present several weeks after surgery and that conservative management may achieve a favorable outcome even in the setting of substantial initial pleural drainage.

43001426.title: Complications of Midazolam-Containing Versus Midazolam-Free Analgosedation in Mechanically Ventilated Adult ICU Patients: A Systematic Review.
43001426.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) patients requiring mechanical ventilation (MV) frequently need analgosedation strategies that combine analgesia and sedation. Analgosedation, often administered with midazolam, is widely employed in middle and low-income countries, but it carries a substantial risk of complications, particularly in older or comorbid patients. Acknowledging these complications is critical for patient safety and quality of care. To examine complications associated with midazolam-containing versus midazolam-free analgosedation in mechanically ventilated adult intensive care unit patients. This systematic review was conducted according to the PRISMA guidelines. A comprehensive search of Scopus, MEDLINE (PubMed), and Web of Science identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2015 and 2025. Studies meeting predefined eligibility criteria underwent risk-of-bias assessment using the Cochrane RoB2 tool. Nine RCTs were included. Midazolam-containing analgosedation regimens were generally associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, increased respiratory depression and higher incidence of neurological complications, particularly delirium. In contrast, midazolam-free analgosedation regimens, especially those using short-acting opioids, were associated with shorter mechanical ventilation duration and fewer haemodynamic incidents. ICU length of stay and healthcare costs favoured opioid-only analgosedation protocols, although mortality findings were inconsistent across studies. Compared with midazolam-free analgosedation, midazolam-containing analgosedation regimens in mechanically ventilated adult ICU patients are associated with a higher incidence of respiratory and neurological complications. Opioid-only protocols appear to offer a more favourable complication profile and may facilitate earlier weaning and shorter ICU stays. These findings support cautious use of midazolam and emphasize the importance of individualized, goal-directed analgosedation strategies. Enhancing critical care nursing staff's awareness of complications associated with different analgosedation regimens is essential to promote vigilant clinical monitoring, thereby reducing adverse events and supporting safer patient management.

43001416.title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Self-Reported Practices of Emergency and Intensive Care Nurses in Managing Traumatic Brain Injury.
43001416.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide, with a growing burden in low- and middle-income countries. Nurses in emergency and intensive care units (ICUs) play a critical role in TBI management, yet little is known about their competencies in Palestine. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes and self-reported practices of emergency and intensive care unit nurses regarding traumatic brain injury management and to identify factors associated with these outcomes. A descriptive cross-sectional survey using stratified random sampling was conducted in governmental and private hospitals in the northern West Bank, Palestine. Data were collected in January 2025 using a validated Arabic questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation coefficients and multiple linear regression analyses were performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 151 nurses participated, yielding a response rate of 61.4% (151/246). Nurses demonstrated generally good foundational knowledge, particularly in Glasgow Coma Scale interpretation and recognition of neurological responses, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring. Attitudes were predominantly positive, with strong support for specialised training. Self-reported practices included maintaining adequate blood pressure and initiating deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis. Knowledge correlated significantly with attitude and self-reported practice, and attitude correlated strongly with self-reported practice. Previous TBI training, higher educational level and longer clinical experience were associated with better outcomes. Emergency and intensive care unit nurses demonstrated adequate foundational knowledge and positive attitudes towards traumatic brain injury management, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring and selected self-reported practices. Structured continuing professional development, standardised protocols and organisational support are needed to strengthen neurotrauma nursing care. The findings support context-sensitive continuing education, simulation, standardised protocols and organisational measures that enable nurses to translate knowledge into consistent neurotrauma care in resource-constrained settings.

43001415.title: Building Consensus Among Intensive Care Nurses on the Scope of Practice for Registered Nurses Deployed to Intensive Care During Surge Events: A Real-Time Delphi Study.
43001415.abstract: Disaster events that overwhelm health system capacity often require the deployment of nurses from non-critical care clinical areas to supplement the specialist intensive care workforce. However, the role of deployed registered nurses in intensive care is poorly defined and without clear role boundaries, experienced intensive care nurses often bear disproportionate supervisory burdens, and deployed staff may assume clinical responsibilities for which they are inadequately prepared. Developing a scope of practice for deployed nurses is essential for safe, effective surge responses. To achieve expert consensus on the scope of practice of deployed registered nurses in a surged intensive care unit. A Real-Time Delphi study was conducted using a web-based platform. A 65-item survey was administered to a panel of experienced Australian intensive care nurses and educators with expertise in training and/or supervising nurses deployed to intensive care during surge events. Participants rated activities that could potentially be undertaken by deployed registered nurses in a surged intensive care setting using a 5-point Likert scale across two dimensions: appropriateness for delegation and importance within a tiered nursing model. Consensus was defined a priori as ≥ 70% agreement. Free-text comments were analysed thematically. Fifteen expert panellists completed the survey. Of the 69 items assessed, 33 reached consensus and were retained as constituting the scope of practice for registered nurses deployed to intensive care. Consensus items spanned neurological observation, basic cardiovascular monitoring, gastrointestinal care, fluid balance documentation, and essential nursing cares. No consensus was reached for mechanical ventilation, non-invasive ventilation or renal replacement therapy. This study resulted in a consensus-derived scope of practice for deployed registered nurses in a surged intensive care. The findings establish clear role boundaries to support safe, tiered nursing care during future surge events and provide a foundation for developing targeted upskilling programs. The findings offer intensive care clinicians, educators, and health services a practical foundation for planning surge nursing models before surge events occur. Clearer role delineation may also reduce uncertainty for deployed nurses and lessen the supervisory burden on experienced intensive care staff.

43000297.title: Impact of rapid pathogen detection in ICU patients with suspected pneumonia on antimicrobial therapy: randomized, controlled open-label feasibility trial (IRISPAT-1).
43000297.abstract: Evidence that multiplex polymerase chain reaction (mPCR) improves antimicrobial therapy and clinical outcomes in the critical care setting is limited. We assessed the impact of rapid mPCR on antibiotic therapy in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients with suspected pneumonia. IRISPAT-1 was a single center, randomized, controlled open-label trial designed to determine the feasibility, safety, and potential impact of rapid respiratory pathogen detection on antibiotic therapy in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients with suspected pneumonia. Mechanically ventilated adults with suspected pneumonia and treated with new antibiotics within 24 h were randomized to standard care or mPCR using BioFire® FilmArray® Pneumonia Panel in addition to standard care (FA Pneumonia Panel group). Primary outcome was time interval (hours) to appropriate antimicrobial therapy. Forty mechanically ventilated patients with suspected pneumonia were randomized (20 = standard care, 20 = FA Pneumonia Panel) between July 7, 2024 and October 4, 2025. Median (IQR) time to appropriate antibiotic therapy was shorter in the FA Pneumonia Panel group compared to the standard care group (7 [5-16] vs. 72 [41-140] hours, HR 3.3; 95%CI [1.6, 6.6], p = 0.001). Adherence to treatment algorithm was observed in 90% (18/20) of patients in the FA Pneumonia Panel group. There were no differences in use of broad-spectrum antibiotics, duration of antibiotics, ventilator free days or vasopressor free days and 28-day mortality between treatment groups. Rapid mPCR with high adherence to antibiotic algorithms shortened time to appropriate antibiotics compared to standard care in mechanically ventilated patients with suspected pneumonia. Registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06478953) on June 23, 2024.

43003715.title: Impact of primary series vaccination on clinical presentations and outcomes among critically ill patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in Taiwan during the Omicron era.
43003715.journal: Journal of microbiology, immunology, and infection = Wei mian yu gan ran za zhi
43003715.abstract: Among critically ill patients infected by the Omicron variant of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on outcomes varied. A retrospective cohort study including adults with active COVID-19 admitted to dedicated intensive care units was conducted at a medical center in southern Taiwan between April 27, 2022 and Apr 26, 2023. Baseline characteristics, clinical presentations, management, and outcomes were compared between patients with and without primary series vaccination (PSV). Logistic regression and propensity score matching were used to identify factors associated with clinical outcomes. Among 397 critically ill patients with COVID-19, 194 (48.9%) had not completed PSV. Patients without PSV more often presented with pneumonia (67.5% vs. 46.3%, p < 0.001), acute respiratory distress syndrome (53.1% vs. 30.1%, p < 0.001), had a higher in-hospital mortality rate (34.5% vs. 24.6%, p = 0.0305), longer hospital stays (median 21.5 days vs. 18.0 days, p = 0.018), and fewer ventilator-free days at 28 days (median 18 days vs. 24 days, p = 0.004). In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, factors associated with in-hospital mortality included solid organ malignancies, higher SOFA score, and lack of PSV. The association of PSV and lower in-hospital mortality remained significant in a propensity score-matched cohort (odds ratio 0.46, 95% confidence interval 0.26-0.81, p = 0.008). Among critically ill patients infected by SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant, prior receipt of PSV was associated with a favorable outcome, as evidenced by a lower in-hospital mortality rate and more ventilator-free days at 28 days.

43002827.title: Direct ICU admission versus floor-to-ICU upgrade in geriatric patients with multiple rib fractures and flail chest: A national analysis.
43002827.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
43002827.abstract: It remains unclear whether direct ICU admission benefits geriatric patients compared with delayed floor-to-ICU upgrade. The study evaluated the association of direct ICU admission versus floor-to-ICU upgrade with clinical outcomes in geriatric trauma patients with flail chest and thoracic injury, stratified by oxygenation compromise, frailty, and rib fracture burden. This retrospective cohort study used the 2017-2024 ACS-TQIP-PUF to identify patients aged 65 years or older with blunt trauma, flail chest, at least three rib fractures, an Injury Severity Score of 9 or greater, and thoracic injury. Patients were classified as floor admission without ICU upgrade, direct ICU admission, or floor-to-ICU upgrade. The primary adjusted analysis compared direct ICU admission with floor-to-ICU upgrade, using floor-to-ICU upgrade as the reference group. A total of 6743 patients were included. Mortality did not differ significantly between direct ICU admission and floor-to-ICU upgrade in the primary adjusted analysis (aOR 0.732, 95% CI 0.467-1.148, p = 0.174). Direct ICU admission was associated with lower odds of unplanned intubation (aOR 0.355, 95% CI 0.251-0.502, p < 0.001), ARDS (aOR 0.412, 95% CI 0.172-0.987, p = 0.047), sepsis (aOR 0.352, 95% CI 0.171-0.725, p = 0.005), and DVT (aOR 0.444, 95% CI 0.209-0.942, p = 0.034). Mortality was lower with direct ICU admission among patients with 3-5 documented rib fractures (aOR 0.535, 95% CI 0.296-0.969, p = 0.039), and the association with fewer unplanned intubations persisted across all subgroups. In the secondary analysis, both direct ICU admission and floor-to-ICU upgrade were associated with higher mortality, lower odds of discharge home, and fewer ventilator-free days than floor admission without ICU upgrade. Direct ICU admission was associated with lower odds of unplanned intubation, ARDS, sepsis, and DVT compared with floor-to-ICU upgrade. These findings support identifying at-risk geriatric rib fracture patients for direct ICU admission before deterioration occurs.

43001781.title: Draft genome sequences of two Stenotrophomonas muris isolates, CBAS 1154 and CBAS 1234, recovered from patients with ICU-acquired ventilator-associated sepsis.
authors: Ribeiro Gomes de Queiroz Crespo I
43001781.abstract: We report the high-quality draft genome sequences of two clinical Stenotrophomonas muris isolates recovered from the lower respiratory tract of intensive care unit patients with ventilator-associated sepsis in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Based on our review of the available literature, we found no previous records of this species from Brazil.

43001150.title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning‑based Prediction Model for ICU‑Acquired Weakness in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
43001150.abstract: ICU-acquired weakness (ICU-AW) is a common and devastating complication of critical illness associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation and increased mortality, whereas externally validated tools for early risk stratification remain insufficient. This study aimed to construct and validate machine learning models to predict ICU-AW risk in critically ill patients. A total of 535 patients from three medical centers were divided into a training set (n = 276), an internal validation set (n = 119) and an external validation cohort (n = 140). Candidate predictors were restricted to variables available within the first 48 hours of ICU admission. Five algorithms including logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), classification and regression tree (CART) and XGBoost were trained with 10-fold cross-validated grid search and compared using DeLong tests. Six predictors were retained: age, Glasgow Coma Scale score, SOFA score, sepsis, renal failure and hypoalbuminemia. All five models displayed favorable predictive capacity in the internal validation set (AUROC 0.906-0.939). In external validation, SVM (0.853, 95% CI 0.779-0.915) and LR (0.841, 0.765-0.906) outperformed RF (0.802), XGBoost (0.790) and CART (0.685), and the difference between SVM and LR was not statistically significant (DeLong P = 0.085). Tree-based algorithms presented near-perfect apparent performance that attenuated markedly in the external cohort, indicating overfitting. The LR model, which offered statistically comparable discrimination with full transparency, was converted into a nomogram (external AUROC 0.841) with positive net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities of 1-81%. A six-predictor logistic model based on variables available within 48 hours of ICU admission predicted ICU-AW comparably to tuned machine learning classifiers and showed stable cross-center performance. The nomogram may assist early risk stratification, and prospective studies are warranted to confirm whether model-guided care improves patient outcomes.

43002637.title: Effects of advanced practice nurse-driven sedation weaning and early extubation after cardiac surgery amid health care disruption in South Korea.
43002637.journal: Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners
43002637.abstract: Cardiovascular disease has reached unprecedented levels, leading to a substantial increases in the number of cardiac surgeries. Despite the life-saving efforts of surgery, complications remain, including pulmonary complications, which can lead to death. To mitigate these complications, early extubation has emerged as an evidence-based practice for patients undergoing cardiac surgery. The physician shortages that occurred after the mass resignation of physician trainees in South Korea disrupted postoperative care provided in intensive care units (ICU) and impeded early extubation. Our institution accordingly expanded the advanced practice nurses' (APNs) scope of practice to include performing extubation when deemed clinically appropriate after cardiac surgery. This practice change led APNs to develop and implement a sedation weaning and early extubation protocol. To evaluate the effects of an APN-driven protocol implemented in the cardiac ICU. This retrospective study compared two group outcomes: preimplementation and postimplementation groups. This study revealed differences in health outcomes between the two groups of patients. Beneficial health outcomes were achieved due to this protocol in the opioid use and ventilator time of patients with low grade of heart failure in the postprotocol group, which were 16.7% lesser and 17.0% shorter than those in the preprotocol group. This APN-driven protocol proves its effectiveness without causing compromised health outcomes during a health care crisis in South Korea. This protocol incorporating nursing staff autonomy for both sedation and extubation can be implemented and tested for its usefulness for instances where gaps of care occur such as during physician shortages.

43001418.title: Tracheostomy and Home Invasive Ventilation in Severe Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia: A Scoping Review of Indications, Timing, Outcomes and Transitional Care.
43001418.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
43001418.abstract: To map the literature on tracheostomy and home invasive ventilation in infants and children with severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), including indications, timing, respiratory outcomes, comorbidities, complications, growth, neurodevelopment, social determinants and transitional care. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL/EBSCO from inception to 30 June 2026. Search terms combined BPD or chronic lung disease of prematurity with tracheostomy or tracheotomy. Eligible studies included infants or children with BPD who underwent tracheostomy, received chronic invasive ventilation or were discharged on home mechanical ventilation. Conference abstracts without full-text articles, duplicate precursor abstracts, reviews and editorials were excluded from primary synthesis. Forty-one studies were included. Evidence was mainly retrospective, including cohorts, administrative database studies, multicentre registries and single-centre observational studies. Tracheostomy was generally considered for persistent invasive ventilation, failed extubation, high respiratory support needs, pulmonary hypertension, airway malacia, growth failure, sedation burden or limited developmental progress. Timing varied widely across centres. Pulmonary hypertension was associated with illness severity and mortality risk, although many children receiving home ventilation improved over time. Among survivors, ventilator liberation and decannulation were common but often occurred over several years. Airway complications, readmissions and operative airway interventions were frequent. Evidence also highlighted centre-level variation, racial and social disparities and limited caregiver-centred data. Tracheostomy and home invasive ventilation in severe BPD represent a prolonged care trajectory. Future work should define consensus indications, optimise timing, standardise transitional care and prioritise family-centred and equity-focused outcomes.

43001151.title: Successful Trastuzumab Desensitization After a Severe Infusion-Related Reaction with Acute Hypoxemia and Suspected Pulmonary Toxicity in HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Case Report.
43001151.abstract: Trastuzumab is a cornerstone of treatment for HER2-positive breast cancer. Infusion-related reactions are common during the first administration, but severe reactions with hemodynamic instability and acute respiratory compromise are uncommon. We report a 36-year-old woman with de novo HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer involving the lungs who developed hypotension, presyncope, oxygen desaturation, and acute hypoxemic respiratory failure 35 minutes after the initiation of her first trastuzumab infusion. Chest computed tomography showed known bilateral pulmonary metastases and new bibasal opacities, raising concern for an overlapping severe infusion-related reaction and inflammatory pulmonary toxicity. Trastuzumab was discontinued, and the patient recovered after respiratory support and systemic corticosteroids. Following complete clinical recovery and resolution of the inflammatory radiological findings, a multidisciplinary team performed a rapid drug desensitization protocol under intensive care monitoring. The full trastuzumab target dose was successfully administered without immediate or delayed breakthrough reaction, and the protocol was repeated in subsequent 12 total cycles, allowing continued HER2-targeted therapy without disease progression. This case illustrates that rapid drug desensitization may permit trastuzumab reintroduction after a severe immediate infusion-related reaction in carefully selected patients once suspected pulmonary toxicity has fully resolved. Desensitization should not be interpreted as protection against recurrent drug-induced pneumonitis and requires individualized risk-benefit assessment, allergy evaluation, pulmonary reassessment, and administration in a specialized setting.

43000275.title: Acute motor-sensory axonal neuropathy with brain death-like manifestations: two case reports and literature review.
43000275.abstract: Acute motor-sensory axonal neuropathy (AMSAN) presenting with brain death-like features is rare, rapidly progressive, and easily mistaken early in the course for brain death of unclear cause or for locked-in syndrome. Misdiagnosis may delay timely immunotherapy and supportive care. We describe two such patients from a single center and summarize the published adult literature to improve recognition of this fulminant presentation. We retrospectively reviewed two patients treated at Yichang Central People's Hospital between 2016 and 2024 who developed brain death-like manifestations in the setting of AMSAN. We also searched CNKI, Wanfang Data, and PubMed for relevant reports published up to June 2025. Both patients developed rapidly progressive generalized paralysis, external and internal ophthalmoplegia, respiratory failure, and disappearance of brainstem reflexes, thereby simulating brain death. Electrophysiological studies showed severe motor-sensory axonal neuropathy and cerebrospinal fluid findings supported the diagnosis. One patient improved after intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), whereas the second showed no early response to IVIG but improved after subsequent plasma exchange. Our literature review identified 28 adult patients with fulminant Guillain-Barré syndrome presenting with brain death-like manifestations, most of whom required prolonged mechanical ventilation and experienced slow, incomplete motor recovery. AMSAN presenting with brain death-like features is characterized by acute onset and complete systemic paralysis, typically initially manifesting as limb weakness and paralysis of both extraocular and intraocular muscles, followed by respiratory muscle paralysis. All patients require prolonged mechanical ventilation and intensive care treatment, rapidly presenting with clinical manifestations resembling "brain death." At this stage, electrophysiological studies and lumbar puncture are particularly crucial for definitive diagnosis. Early initiation of immunotherapy, such as IVIG infusion or plasma exchange, is critical. Patients often show gradual recovery of extraocular and intraocular muscles first; however, most experience poor recovery of respiratory muscle paralysis and limb weakness, significantly prolonging hospitalization and severely impacting patients' work and daily life, highlighting the need for prospective studies to evaluate therapeutic strategies beyond standard IVIG and plasma exchange. While emerging agents such as efgartigimod show preliminary promise in refractory GBS, current evidence is limited to small case reports, and prospective studies are critically needed.

43003727.title: Use of von Willebrand Factor in VA-ECMO‒Associated Acquired von Willebrand Syndrome: A Nationwide Retrospective Study.
43003727.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
43003727.abstract: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) is a life-saving therapy for refractory cardiocirculatory failure but carries a high bleeding risk, partly due to acquired von Willebrand syndrome (aVWS). With limited evidence-based treatments, von Willebrand factor (VWF) is often used off-label. This study examines nationwide use of VWF in VA-ECMO patients with aVWS in Germany and compares bleeding, thromboembolic events, and survival between treated and untreated patients. Retrospective cohort study based on reimbursement data (2019-2023). Multi-institutional analysis of adult VA-ECMO cases treated in German hospitals. 530 adult patients supported with VA-ECMO and diagnosed with aVWS. Administration of any dose of VWF during VA-ECMO support versus no VWF treatment. Of 530 patients, 389 (73%) received VWF across 35 of 71 centers contributing patients. Intracranial hemorrhage occurred less frequently in the VWF group (8% v 15%, p = 0.0238). However, haemothorax (37% v 20%, p = 0.0028) was more common with VWF. Thromboembolic events did not differ between groups. ICU LOS was shorter in VWF-treated patients (14 v 18 days, p = 0.0168). The 90-day survival was numerically higher in the VWF group but did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.188). In this cohort of VA-ECMO patients with aVWS, VWF was frequently used and associated with lower ICH rates and shorter intensive care unit length of stay, there was no evidence of increased thromboembolic events, but higher rates of other bleeding complications. Prospective randomized trials are warranted to clarify the impact of VWF on clinical outcomes.

43000635.title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Patients With Pulmonary Hemorrhage.
43000635.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
43000635.abstract: Severe pulmonary hemorrhage may lead to refractory hypoxemia and/or hemodynamic collapse and cause high mortality. However, the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in this patient population is rare. The aim of this study is to better define and understand this patient population by exploring the baseline characteristics, complications, and outcomes of patients who receive ECMO support due to pulmonary hemorrhage, based on data extracted from the extracorporeal life support organization (ELSO) registry. Between 2003 and 2023, 96 patients received ECMO due to pulmonary hemorrhage. Complications occurred in 54% of the patients, mainly acute kidney injury (AKI) with need for renal replacement therapy (RRT; 28%) and bleeding (pulmonary, gastrointestinal) (15%). Respiratory infections occurred in 37.1% of the patients. The most common diagnostic/therapeutic procedures were computed tomography scans in 9%, bronchoscopy in 41%, surgery in 8%, and apheresis in 6% of the patients. Interventional radiology procedures were performed in only 2% of the patients. Interpretation of these data should be performed cautiously, as underreporting is a known limitation of the ELSO Registry. Forty-seven patients (49%) were weaned from ECMO, and 46 (48%) survived until discharge. Survival and complication rates are comparable to the overall ECMO cohort in the ELSO Registry, which makes ECMO a feasible strategy in this patient population.

42999907.title: A targeted mass spectrometric assay for quantitative detection of fibrinogen in plasma.
42999907.journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
42999907.abstract: Fibrinogen is a key glycoprotein that plays a central role in clot formation, structure, and stability. Both quantitative fibrinogen deficiency and qualitative abnormalities can lead to bleeding or thrombotic disorders. Accurate quantification of fibrinogen antigen is essential for clinical evaluation; however, current immunoassays and clot-based surrogate methods are prone to interference and may lack traceability to international standards. To develop a targeted mass spectrometry-based assay for accurate quantification of fibrinogen antigen in plasma and to compare its performance with established functional and immunoturbidimetric assays. We developed a targeted liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry-based assay using isotope-labeled peptides that accurately measures fibrinogen antigen concentration with high precision (coefficient of variation < 20%) across a broad linear dynamic range of 10.2 to 1307.5 mg/dL, enabling accurate detection of hypofibrinogenemia and hyperfibrinogenemia. Assay performance was evaluated in healthy donors (n = 47) and clinical specimens (n = 31). Fibrinogen antigen levels in normal donors followed a normal distribution (mean ± SD, 315 ± 42 mg/dL). The targeted assay, employing selected reaction monitoring, correlated strongly with immunoturbidimetry (Pearson's correlation coefficient [r] = .943) and the Clauss and prothrombin time-derived fibrinogen assays (r = .91 and r = .93, respectively). Stratification by clinical category confirmed elevated fibrinogen levels in thrombosis-related disorders, intermediate levels in controls, and low levels in liver disease and critical illness. The liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry-based assay provides precise, accurate quantification of fibrinogen across a wide clinical range and aligns closely with existing methods while offering analytical specificity. With further clinical validation, it could be used as a diagnostic clinical test.

43004255.title: The association of ICU admission time with mortality in patients with severe pneumonia requiring invasive mechanical ventilation: a retrospective, single-center, multicampus cohort study.
43004255.abstract: Nighttime admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) has been associated with worse outcomes in some critically ill populations. However, evidence specific to patients with severe pneumonia is limited. We evaluated the association between ICU admission time and 30-day mortality among patients with severe pneumonia requiring invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ICD-coded severe pneumonia who received IMV in four campuses at a tertiary medical center between 2020 and 2024. Patients were categorized according to their ICU admission time and our institutional staffing schedule: daytime admission (08:00-15:59) and nighttime admission (16:00-07:59 the following day). The primary outcome was 30-day mortality after ICU admission. Survival analysis and multivariable Cox regression were used to test the association between admission time and 30-day mortality. A total of 9,611 patients were included in the analysis. Among them, 6,058 patients were admitted at night, and 3,553 during the daytime. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 3,476 patients remained in each group. There was no statistically significant difference in 30-day mortality following ICU admission between the two groups (hazard ratio [HR], 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.92-1.09; P = 0.914). After adjustment for age, sex, relative weight, lactate, patient source, type of admission, and septic shock, multivariable Cox regression showed that daytime ICU admission was not an independent protective factor for 30-day mortality (adjusted HR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.93-1.10; P = 0.794). In this cohort of patients with severe pneumonia requiring IMV, ICU admission timing was not significantly associated with 30-day mortality. The findings should be interpreted in light of residual confounding and the institution-specific staffing model.

43007421.title: Efficacy and safety of oliceridine versus remifentanil for analgesia in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults (CO-ROAM): a multicenter, assessor-blinded, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial.
43007421.abstract: Remifentanil provides effective analgesia during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), but its utility is limited by opioid-related adverse events. Oliceridine, a G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist, may decouple analgesia from these effects, but lacks evidence in critically ill patients. This multicentre, assessor- and patient-blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial was conducted across 19 intensive care units (ICUs) in China. Adults receiving IMV were randomised 1:1 to oliceridine or remifentanil, titrated to a Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool score below 3. The primary endpoint was time in target analgesic range (TTR; non-inferiority margin -10%). Of 307 randomised patients, 304 comprised the modified intention-to-treat population (151 oliceridine, 153 remifentanil). Median TTR was 96.0% versus 92.3% (absolute difference 3.7%, 95% CI -0.3-5.7%). Oliceridine was associated with fewer mild-to-moderate adverse drug reactions (ADRs), occurring at 15.9 versus 22.2 events per 100 patient-days (IRR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00, P = 0.049), and a lower rate of respiratory depression during the study period (0% vs. 4.6%, P = 0.015). Post-extubation respiratory depression (0% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.005) and analgesic-sedation costs were both lower with oliceridine. IMV duration, ICU stay, and 28-day mortality did not differ. Subgroup analyses identified a nominal ADR benefit in patients with Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II > 17 and a larger nominal TTR difference in those without acute respiratory distress syndrome. Oliceridine provides non-inferior analgesia to remifentanil with a more favourable respiratory safety profile and lower costs in critically ill adults. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06454292 (registered June 11, 2024).

43005516.title: A multicenter-validated machine learning model for predicting in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with cirrhosis.
43005516.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) patients with cirrhosis face a high in-hospital mortality risk. We aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable machine learning model for early mortality prediction using routinely collected variables from the first 24 hours of ICU admission. In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, the model was developed and internally validated on the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU) and externally validated on Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV (MIMIC-IV), Northwestern ICU (NWICU), and Shenzhen People's Hospital (SZPH). The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Features selected by LASSO were used to build an XGBoost model. Performance was evaluated by AUROC and Brier score, with calibration curves and decision curve analysis, and compared with five established scores (MELD, MELD-Na, Child-Pugh, SOFA, CLIF-SOFA) and logistic regression using DeLong's tests. SHAP provides interpretable feature attribution. We included 3,891 patients with cirrhosis (eICU, n=1,870; MIMIC-IV, n=1,697; NWICU, n=134; SZPH, n=190); in-hospital mortality rates were 19.79%, 28.76%, 38.81%, and 47.37%, respectively. The final model used 10 predictors (prothrombin time, mechanical ventilation, creatinine, mean arterial pressure, lactate, respiratory rate, total bilirubin, oxygen saturation, heart rate, and white blood cell count). It showed good discrimination and calibration internally (AUROC 0.814; Brier 0.125) and generalized to external cohorts (AUROCs 0.781, 0.733, and 0.719 in MIMIC-IV, NWICU, and SZPH, respectively). In MIMIC-IV cohort, XGBoost significantly outperformed MELD-Na, Child-Pugh, and SOFA, while differences versus MELD, CLIF-SOFA, and logistic regression were not significant. In eICU internal validation cohort, XGBoost significantly outperformed Child-Pugh and SOFA but not other comparators; in SZPH cohort, it showed comparable discrimination to all comparators. We developed and multicenter-validated an interpretable XGBoost model predicting in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with cirrhosis, with competitive or superior discrimination versus established scores. Prospective validation, local recalibration, and implementation studies are warranted.

43004217.title: Moderate aortic stenosis identified during intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis and 90-day mortality: a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV echocardiography database.
43004217.abstract: Moderate aortic stenosis is associated with reduced survival in ambulatory cardiology populations, but its prognostic significance when identified during an intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis is unknown. We examined its association with 90-day mortality in this setting. Retrospective cohort using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) version 3.1 and its echocardiogram-matched subset (MIMIC-IV-ECHO). We included each adult's first intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis with an interpretable baseline transthoracic echocardiogram recording peak aortic jet velocity. Stenosis was graded from the peak velocity (no stenosis < 2.0, sclerosis or mild 2.0-2.9, moderate 3.0-3.9, severe ≥ 4.0 m/s). The echocardiogram defined time zero; the primary outcome was all-cause mortality within a fixed 90-day window. Associations were estimated with multivariable Cox models adjusted for acute-illness severity and comorbidity, with propensity-score matching, velocity-gradient concordance grading, pre-specified ejection-fraction subgroups, and an E-value. Of 12,878 patients (10,511 no stenosis, 1,797 sclerosis, 411 moderate, 159 severe), 3,605 died within 90 days. Crude 90-day mortality rose across grades (26.1%, 34.4%, 40.4%, 46.5%). After adjustment, the hazard increased monotonically: sclerosis 1.17 (95% CI 1.07-1.28), moderate 1.33 (1.13-1.56), severe 1.61 (1.27-2.03). The moderate-stenosis association was modest but consistent, attenuating slightly in the most conservative specifications (propensity-score matched 1.20 [1.02-1.40]; parsimonious 1.22 [1.05-1.43]); the E-value was 1.73 (lower limit 1.41). It was numerically concentrated in the first two weeks (1.58 [1.30-1.93], days 0-14) and numerically larger with reduced (1.47 [1.10-1.97]) than preserved ejection fraction (1.10 [0.87-1.39]); neither the proportional-hazards nor the grade-by-ejection-fraction interaction test was significant (interaction P = 0.21), and both are exploratory numerical patterns, not demonstrated effect modification. In non-cardiac critical illness, velocity-defined moderate aortic stenosis identified during the intensive care admission was independently associated with higher 90-day mortality, with exploratory numerical patterns of greater early risk and of greater risk with reduced ejection fraction. These data identify a higher-risk phenotype; they do not establish a causal adverse effect of moderate valvular obstruction itself. It is best regarded as a prognostic marker warranting closer surveillance rather than, on current evidence, a target for valve intervention.

43004116.title: Metabolic response during neuromuscular electrical stimulation in critically ill patients with deep sedation: a prospective observational study.
43004116.abstract: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) is a potential strategy to counteract skeletal muscle atrophy in critically ill patients unable to engage in early mobilization. However, it is difficult to confirm whether the exercise load applied by NMES is sufficient to elicit a physiological effect in patients under sedation or with impaired consciousness, as the appropriate stimulus intensity and exercise load of NMES are generally assessed using subjective responses. This study aimed to evaluate changes in energy expenditure during NMES in sedated, mechanically ventilated patients using indirect calorimetry. This single-center observational study included 22 mechanically ventilated patients under deep sedation in the intensive care unit (ICU). Energy expenditure was measured using indirect calorimetry during NMES sessions. The primary outcome was the difference in energy expenditure before and during NMES. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to calculate the adjusted mean difference in energy expenditure. A clinically meaningful increase in energy expenditure attributable to NMES was predefined as 150 kcal/day, which was assumed based on an increase in energy expenditure when sitting on the edge of the bed. In total, 26 NMES sessions involving 22 participants were included in the analysis. The mean energy expenditure was 1,137 ± 170 kcal/day pre-NMES and 1,350 ± 228 kcal/day during NMES. The adjusted increase in energy expenditure during NMES was 213.8 kcal/day (95% confidence interval, 137.1-290.3). This increase reached statistical significance when tested against the predefined threshold of 150 kcal/day (P = 0.02). The exercise load provided by NMES could be objectively assessed by measuring increases in energy expenditure. Although a statistically significant increase in energy expenditure was observed during NMES compared to pre-NMES levels, the magnitude of this increase was minimal. Further research is needed to determine whether NMES protocols that enhance energy expenditure are associated with muscle mass preservation, strength maintenance, and the prevention of ICU-acquired weakness.

43009391.title: Early Deep Sedation and Short-term Outcomes After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Retrospective Multicenter Cohort Study Using the MIMIC-IV and eICU Databases.
43009391.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
43009391.abstract: To investigate the association between early sedation depth and short-term outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and to characterize the dose-response relationship between sedation depth and mortality. Retrospective multicenter observational cohort study using the MIMIC-IV (v3.1) and eICU (v2.0) databases. Multi-institutional; intensive care units contributing to the MIMIC-IV (v3.1) and eICU (v2.0) databases. A total of 2,556 adults (≥18 years) undergoing isolated CABG with invasive mechanical ventilation ≥24 hours. This cohort represents a higher-acuity subset of CABG patients requiring prolonged postoperative mechanical ventilation (≥24 hours). None. Participants were stratified by mean Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) score during the first 24 hours after intensive care unit admission: deep sedation (RASS ≤-3), light sedation (-3 < RASS < 1, reference), and agitation (RASS ≥1). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes were ventilation duration and intensive care unit length of stay. Deep sedation was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (41.0% v14.1%, p < 0.001), which persisted after adjustment (pooled generalized linear mixed-model odds ratio 3.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.52-4.00; propensity-matched odds ratio 3.08, 95% CI 2.33-4.10). Deep sedation was associated with increased mortality hazard (hazard ratio 2.05, 95% CI 1.71-2.44) and reduced successful extubation in Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis (subdistribution hazard ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.57-0.74). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a J-shaped relationship between RASS and mortality, with the lowest risk between RASS -1 and 0. Exploratory XGBoost/Shapley Additive Explanations analysis showed consistent patterns. Early deep sedation was independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality and reduced extubation success in mechanically ventilated CABG patients requiring prolonged postoperative mechanical ventilation. The RASS range of -1 to 0 was associated with the lowest mortality and may inform prospective studies of sedation optimization in this high-acuity population. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation before clinical implementation and should not be extrapolated to routine low-risk CABG patients with an uncomplicated postoperative course and early extubation.

43009312.title: Association of Early Palliative Care with End-of-Life Care Quality and Nonbeneficial Treatments in Taiwan: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.
43009312.abstract: Early palliative care has been associated with reduced aggressive care near the end of life (EOL), particularly among patients with cancer. However, evidence regarding the association between early palliative care and potentially nonbeneficial treatments near the EOL remains limited, particularly among patients with noncancer terminal illnesses and in real-world clinical practice. To examine the association between early palliative care, EOL care quality indicators, and nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill cancer and noncancer patients under a universal health insurance system. This retrospective population-based study used Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database to identify adults who received palliative care within one year before death in 2019. Early palliative care was defined as initiation of any palliative care service more than 90 days before death. Outcomes included indicators of EOL care quality and nonbeneficial treatments within the last 30 days of life. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models were used to adjust for demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and terminal diagnoses. Among 46,343 decedents, 17.2% received early palliative care. Early palliative care was associated with lower odds of aggressive EOL care, including more than one emergency department visit, more than one hospitalization, a hospital stay exceeding 14 days, intensive care unit admission, in-hospital death, use of an endotracheal tube, ventilator support, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Early palliative care was also associated with reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments, including blood transfusion and tube feeding or intravenous nutrition. In a nationwide cohort, early palliative care was associated with improved EOL care quality and reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill patients. These findings underscore the clinical importance of earlier palliative care involvement in supporting patient-centered decision making near the EOL and reducing potentially nonbeneficial interventions.

43008383.title: Two pathways to pressure injury in the mechanically ventilated patient.

43007959.title: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci: Local epidemiology and clinical outcomes.
43007959.abstract: Aim: To study local epidemiology, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and clinical outcomes of VRE infections among inpatients. Materials and Methods: A retrospective observational study was carried out on all patients admitted with culture-confirmed Vancomycin-resistant enterococci infections between July 2025 and January 2026 in Najaf, Iraq. Data on demographic characteristics, clinical information, antimicrobial exposure, microbiological findings, and outcomes were obtained from medical records. Results: A total of 84 patients with Vancomycin-resistant enterococci infection were included. The mean age was 56 ± 18 years, and 57.1% were male. Prior antibiotic exposure was seen in 75.0% of the patients, while 33.3% had previously received Vancomycin therapy. Enterococcus faecium was the predominant species 73.8%, followed by Enterococcus faecalis 21.4%. All isolates were resistant to Vancomycin, while resistance rates against ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, and high-level gentamicin were 70.2%, 63.1%, and 52.4% respectively. Susceptibility to linezolid and daptomycin was still high (97.6% and 98.8% respectively). Urine was the most common specimen source 40.5%, followed by blood cultures 26.2%. In terms of clinical outcomes, 36.9% were admitted to the ICU, 26.2% had a bloodstream infection, 21.4% needed mechanical ventilation, 14.3% had septic shock, and there was an overall mortality rate of 23.8%. Conclusions: infections due to Vancomycin-resistant enterococci impose a huge healthcare burden in our setting; E. faecium is the leading species and is multidrug resistant. It was, however, associated with significant mortality despite preserved susceptibility to linezolid and daptomycin. Therefore, continuous surveillance coupled with antimicrobial stewardship and strict infection control practices is needed to contain the spread and impact of VRE infections.

43007299.title: Ketamine Vs. Etomidates and Cardiovascular Collapse During Emergency Tracheal Intubation: A Secondary Analysis of the DEVICE and PREOXI Trials.
43007299.abstract: Emergency tracheal intubation in critically ill adults is a high-risk procedure. To evaluate associations of ketamine vs. etomidate with cardiovascular collapse and other peri-intubation outcomes. Secondary analysis of individual-participant data from the DEVICE and PREOXI trials, treating induction medication as an observational exposure. The cohort included 2357 adults intubated in emergency departments or ICUs; 1822 received etomidate, 312 ketamine, and 223 other induction regimens. The primary outcome was cardiovascular collapse, defined as new or increased vasopressor use, nadir systolic blood pressure below 65 mm Hg, or cardiac arrest between induction and 2 minutes after intubation. Secondary outcomes included severe hypoxemia (oxygen saturation < 80%) and procedural outcomes. In weighted analyses, cardiovascular collapse occurred in 14.0% of etomidate recipients and 20.4% of ketamine recipients. In weighted, covariate-adjusted models, ketamine was associated with higher odds of cardiovascular collapse (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.80; 95% CI, 1.24-2.62) and new or increased vasopressor use (aOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.02-2.23), nominally lower odds of severe hypoxemia (aOR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.28-0.88), and shorter modeled time to successful intubation (hazard ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.02-1.33). The latter two associations were not significant after multiplicity adjustment. Estimates for systolic blood pressure below 65 mm Hg and cardiac arrest were too imprecise for reliable inference. Successful intubation on the first attempt and 28-day in-hospital mortality did not clearly differ between ketamine and etomidate. Compared with etomidate, ketamine was associated with higher odds of cardiovascular collapse, primarily reflecting new or increased vasopressor use. Associations with severe hypoxemia and intubation time did not remain significant after multiplicity adjustment. Because induction medication was not randomized and residual confounding remains possible, these associations should not be interpreted as causal.

43005936.title: Iatrogenic Botulism Following Cosmetic Botulinum Toxin Injection During a 2025 United Kingdom Outbreak: A Case Report.
43005936.abstract: Iatrogenic botulism is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of cosmetic botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) administration. This report describes a 30-year-old woman who developed progressive neurological symptoms following cosmetic BoNT injections during the 2025 outbreak of iatrogenic botulism in England. She initially presented with headache, facial numbness, throat discomfort, and paraesthesia, with reassuring clinical observations and neurological examination. Over the following days, she developed bilateral ptosis, diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia, dry mouth, and generalized weakness, prompting re-presentation approximately nine days after injection. The evolving ocular and bulbar syndrome following recent BoNT exposure raised clinical suspicion of iatrogenic botulism. Critical care and difficult airway teams were involved, and serial respiratory monitoring, including forced vital capacity assessment, was undertaken. Botulism antitoxin was administered following specialist advice, with subsequent neurological improvement and no progression to respiratory failure. Serum for botulinum toxin testing was obtained only after antitoxin administration, limiting optimal laboratory confirmation. Neurological examination subsequently returned to normal, although residual nausea and reduced oral intake persisted. This case highlights the potential for iatrogenic botulism to evolve after an initially reassuring presentation, the importance of respiratory surveillance in patients with bulbar symptoms, and the need to obtain diagnostic serum before antitoxin administration without delaying clinically indicated treatment.

43005415.title: Enhanced recovery after cardiac surgery: evidence-based pathways for contemporary perioperative care.
43005415.journal: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery
43005415.abstract: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) programmes have transformed perioperative care across multiple surgical specialties. In cardiac surgery, ERAS Cardiac pathways integrate multimodal, evidence-based interventions to attenuate surgical stress, expedite recovery, and optimise resource use. This systematic review summarises contemporary evidence for ERAS protocols in adult cardiac surgery and evaluates their impact on clinical and health-system outcomes. This review was conducted in line with PRISMA 2020 recommendations. Electronic databases (Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library) were searched for studies from 2010 to October 2025 evaluating ERAS or fast-track pathways in adult cardiac surgery. Eligible studies compared a multicomponent ERAS/fast-track protocol with usual care and reported at least one of the following: length of stay (LOS), complications, mortality, costs, or patient-reported outcomes. Narrative synthesis was undertaken due to heterogeneity in interventions and outcome reporting. A PRISMA 2020 flow diagram is shown in Figure 1. Recent systematic reviews and meta-analyses, together with large observational cohorts, demonstrate that ERAS Cardiac programmes are generally safe and are associated with reduced ICU and hospital LOS, lower rates of selected complications (especially pulmonary complications and delirium), decreased opioid exposure, and improved mobilisation without evidence of an increase in reintubation, readmission, or mortality. Key protocol elements include preoperative optimisation (education, prehabilitation, and anaemia management), minimally invasive surgical approaches when appropriate, goal-directed anaesthesia with structured early extubation pathways, multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia, and standardised early mobilisation and nutrition. Emerging economic evaluations suggest that ERAS Cardiac is cost-saving or at least cost-neutral despite upfront implementation costs, while limited data on patient-reported outcomes indicate high satisfaction and perceived control over recovery. The available evidence supports ERAS Cardiac as a comprehensive framework that may improve recovery after cardiac surgery, primarily by shortening LOS and reducing complications and opioid use, without clear evidence of compromised safety. Wider implementation requires multidisciplinary engagement, local adaptation of turnkey order sets, robust audit, and inclusion of patient-centred outcomes in future trials. High-quality randomised and pragmatic studies focusing on long-term functional recovery, health-related quality of life, and cost-effectiveness remain priorities.

43004993.title: Optimal Timing of Tracheostomy After Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: Identification of a Clinically Relevant Threshold.
43004993.abstract: In patients with severe traumatic brain injury (TBI), tracheostomy is frequently required during prolonged intensive care. Although tracheostomy timing influences clinical outcomes, most prior studies have relied on arbitrary cut-off values. This study investigated the association between the intubation-to-tracheostomy interval and post-tracheostomy pneumonia and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (LOS), and sought to identify empirically derived timing thresholds. A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single medical center (January 2016-December 2025). Patients with severe TBI (Glasgow Coma Scale≤8) who underwent endotracheal intubation and subsequent tracheostomy were included. Univariable and multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were performed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to identify optimal timing thresholds. Seventy patients were included. Early tracheostomy (≤11 days from intubation) was independently associated with a lower risk of post-tracheostomy pneumonia (adjusted odds ratio, 0.16; 95% confidence interval, 0.03-0.82; p=0.028). The intubation-to-tracheostomy interval was also an independent predictor of ICU LOS (β=0.56, p<0.001). ROC analysis identified 11 days as the optimal threshold for pneumonia risk (area under the curve [AUC]=0.67) and 13 days for prolonged ICU stay (AUC=0.68). The intubation-to-tracheostomy interval independently predicts both pneumonia and ICU LOS in severe TBI. An empirically derived optimal tracheostomy window of 11-13 days from intubation is proposed, supporting empirically derived, threshold-based timing strategies over conventional arbitrary cut-offs.

43006184.title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
43006184.abstract: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain. This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated. A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099). In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

43005159.title: Global trends and emerging frontiers in neutrophil extracellular trap-related sepsis research: a bibliometric analysis.
43005159.abstract: Sepsis remains a major challenge in critical care medicine, and NETs have emerged as important regulators linking inflammation, immunity, coagulation, and tissue injury. However, the global development trajectory and research frontiers of NET-related sepsis studies remain unclear. Publications related to NET-related sepsis research from 2004 to September 19, 2026, were independently retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus databases. After database-specific screening, 263 WoSCC records and 499 Scopus records were retained for separate analyses using VOSviewer and CiteSpace to evaluate publication trends, collaboration networks, knowledge structures, thematic evolution, and emerging research attention. The WoSCC and Scopus analytical datasets contained 263 and 499 records, respectively. WoSCC analysis showed that China had the highest publication output, whereas the United States had the highest citation impact and collaboration strength among the listed countries. Cleaned author-keyword analysis highlighted sepsis, neutrophil extracellular traps, NETosis, inflammation, neutrophil, platelet, acute lung injury, and septic shock. Cross-database comparison showed a high correlation in complete-year publication trends (Spearman's ρ = 0.986) and partial overlap in high-frequency author keywords. Independent database analyses indicate sustained growth and a progressively interconnected knowledge structure in NET-related sepsis research. The results describe publication, collaboration, citation, and thematic attention patterns; they do not establish biomarker performance or therapeutic efficacy. Future studies may benefit from standardized NET measurement and reporting, multicenter validation of NET-related biomarkers and predictive models, and appropriately designed clinical investigations.

43005274.title: Comparative effectiveness of enoxaparin versus unfractionated heparin for 30- and 90-day mortality in sepsis patients without severe renal dysfunction: a retrospective cohort study.
43005274.abstract: Although enoxaparin is known to be superior to UFH for thromboprophylaxis, the comparative effect of enoxaparin versus UFH on mortality in sepsis remains unknown. To address this gap, we compared the two agents in sepsis patients without severe renal impairment, thereby minimizing confounding due to differential drug clearance. In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed data from the eICU Collaborative Research Database. We included adult patients with sepsis and no severe renal impairment (eGFR ≥ 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) who received prophylactic anticoagulation with either enoxaparin or UFH. The primary outcomes were 30-day ICU mortality and 90-day in-hospital mortality. Survival analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox proportional hazards models. Sensitivity analyses were conducted using inverse probability of treatment weighting. A total of 2,341 patients were enrolled (1,260 in the enoxaparin group and 1,081 in the UFH group). After adjusting for confounders, multivariate Cox regression showed that the hazard ratio (HR) for enoxaparin versus UFH was 0.94 (95% CI: 0.67-1.32, P = 0.726) for 30-day ICU mortality and 0.86 (95% CI: 0.66-1.12, P = 0.271) for 90-day in-hospital mortality. Subgroup analyses showed no significant heterogeneity across predefined strata of age, sex, or BMI (all P for interaction >0.05). These findings were supported by inverse probability of treatment weighting analysis. In this cohort of sepsis patients without severe renal impairment, enoxaparin was associated with numerically lower but not statistically significant hazard ratios for both 30-day ICU and 90-day in-hospital mortality compared with UFH. These findings do not establish the superiority of either agent. Larger, prospective studies are warranted to confirm the observed associations.

43005430.title: Case Report: Rescue with Impella 5.5 after HeartMate 3 failure- a bridge to heart transplantation.
43005430.abstract: We present the first reported case of simultaneous HeartMate 3 (HM3) and Impella 5.5 support as a bridge to heart transplantation. A 35-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy presented to our facility for the evaluation of low-flow alarms 2 years post-HM3 implantation. The HM3 device was set to 5,200 RPM (2.9 L/min); the patient was asymptomatic and had no edema or orthopnea. He was actively listed for heart transplantation at the time of presentation. A chest CT scan revealed evidence of hypoattenuation next to the bend relief portion of the outflow cannula, and therefore, the patient was admitted for monitoring and transplant evaluation. Bivalirudin (0.12 mg/kg/h) was initiated. Over the next 18 days, the patient remained clinically stable with a pulsatility index ranging between 3 and 4. An echocardiogram performed on day 18 to assess clot burden revealed eccentric left ventricular hypertrophy with septum deviation to the right and a left ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDd) of 70 mm, and hence, milrinone (0.25 µg/kg/min) was initiated. Right heart catheterization revealed a right atrial (RA) pressure of 18 mmHg, a right ventricle (RV) pressure of 54/2 mmHg, a pulmonary artery (PA) pressure of 55/28 (37) mmHg, a pulmonary capillary wedge pressure of 32, a pulmonary artery pulsatility index of 1.5, a Fick cardiac output of 7.7 L/min, and a Fick cardiac input of 3.4 L/min/m2. On day 40, the patient complained of cough, fever (38.1°C), and shortness of breath, following which he was intubated and started on meropenem (2 mg) intravenously (IV) three times a day (TID). His left ventricular assist device (LVAD) flow rate decreased to 1.2 L/min, with increasing alarm frequency and worsening hemodynamics. CT angiography revealed extensive near-occlusive hypodense filling defects in the proximal outflow cannula consistent with thrombosis, leaving only a 1-2 mm residual lumen.The team chose to support the patient's worsening hemodynamics and cardiogenic shock with an Impella 5.5 device rather than take him for emergent surgical exploration for his outflow graft obstruction. The Impella 5.5 device was placed in a standard fashion via the left axillary artery, and it delivered flow rates of 2.6-3.1 L/min. Concurrently, HM3 was maintained at flow rates of 1.5-2.0 L/min. Despite persistent low-flow alarms on HM3, the patient's hemodynamics improved after the Impella 5.5 device was implanted [heart rate, 101 beats per minute; BP, 104/77 (88) mmHg; RA, 2 mmHg; PA, 35/19 (24) mmHg; venous oxygen saturation (SvO2)], 69%), and he became ambulatory. His United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) status was upgraded to status 1e because of the risk of stroke. Over the next 6 days, the patient was maintained under close observation, and he remained clinically stable in the ICU. The estimated glomerular filtration rate remained between 41 and 50 mL/min/1.73 m2.Six days after Impella 5.5 placement, the patient underwent a prolonged and complex heart transplant. One week post-transplant, the patient had normal biventricular graft function and stable renal function, was extubated, and was ambulatory on dobutamine medication (4 µg/kg/min). Two weeks later, the patient was discharged, with stable cardiac function and standard immunosuppression. Two months post-transplant, he showed grade 2R rejection, which was adequately treated. Currently, 6 months post-transplant, he remains stable while being maintained on the standard post-transplant immunosuppression and cardiac rehabilitation. This is the first reported case highlighting the feasibility of Impella 5.5 support after HM3 failure as a bridge to transplantation for short-term hemodynamic stabilization in the setting of LVAD outflow obstruction and cardiogenic shock without the need for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation or emergent chest exploration, which may complicate or delay transplantation.

43008343.title: Ultrasound assessment of the optic nerve sheath diameter in adult patients with suspected intracranial hypertension: A scoping review.
43008343.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
43008343.abstract: The aim of this study was to map how the ultrasound measurement of the optic nerve sheath diameter is performed in adults with suspected intracranial hypertension. This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the JBI Collaboration and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping review guidelines. Two independent reviewers searched PubMed, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS), Nursing Database (BDENF), Cochrane Library, Scopus, Embase, Livivo, Web of Science Core Collection, and the CAPES thesis and dissertation repository. Grey literature included Google Scholar. Of the 2019 records identified, 239 were included. Optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) ultrasonography is primarily performed in adults with suspected or at risk of intracranial hypertension, particularly critically ill, neurocritical care, emergency, and trauma patients. Across the included studies, patients were assessed in the supine position, with their eyes closed, using a high-frequency linear transducer in B-mode. The optic nerve is most consistently measured 3 mm posterior to the globe. The included studies showed variability in ONSD cut-off values suggestive of increased intracranial pressure. Lower thresholds, particularly >5.0 mm, showed high sensitivity (99%) but lower specificity (73%), whereas values between 5.6 and 6.3 mm tended to provide greater specificity. Studies assessing diagnostic performance reported favourable results for ONSD ultrasonography; however, heterogeneity in cut-off values, populations, reference standards, and measurement techniques precludes the definition of a universally accepted threshold. ONSD is a viable, noninvasive approach for assessing suspected intracranial hypertension; it most commonly employs a high-frequency linear transducer in B-mode. The optic nerve is most consistently measured 3 mm posterior to the globe. However, variability in measurement techniques and cut-off values highlights the need for greater standardisation. Furthermore, the limited number of studies addressing the role of nursing indicates a knowledge gap that must be bridged to integrate ONSD ultrasound into nursing practice.
