Of 2,002 responses, 1,896 unique adult ICU units were included. AKI diagnosis was reported by 97.9% of ICUs, whereas 63.2% explicitly implemented staging and 75.9% used both UO and SCr for diagnosis. Hourly UO monitoring increased from 49.6% in routine practice to 74.1% in sepsis, 75.0% in AKI, and 77.7% in sepsis-associated AKI. Dynamic UO monitoring was implemented in 14.8% of ICUs; 83.5% reported increased nursing workload, and 69.9% identified workload or insufficient staffing as the main barrier. After FDR correction, geographic region, nurse-to-bed ratio, and baseline monitoring intensity were associated with UO-monitoring practices. The median AKI-MIS was 68.1 (IQR, 60.3-74.9), with higher adjusted scores in teaching hospitals. Among participating adult ICU units across all 31 provincial-level administrative regions of mainland China, AKI diagnosis and monitoring were widely reported, but substantial heterogeneity remained across monitoring systems. These findings provide a broad descriptive benchmark and identify priorities for strengthening standardisation, risk-responsive escalation, and closed-loop response pathways.

42881432.title: Delayed methotrexate toxicity after initial clearance in a critically ill patient with severe fluid overload.
42881432.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) toxicity is a life-threatening complication in oncology patients. We report a 19-year-old male with newly diagnosed Burkitt lymphoma who received high-dose methotrexate as part of induction chemotherapy and initially met protocol-defined serum clearance criteria with suspected delayed MTX toxicity. This prolonged toxicity was due to possible redistribution from extravascular fluid compartments in the setting of severe fluid overload and renal dysfunction. Five weeks after methotrexate administration, a detectable serum methotrexate concentration (0.4 µmol/L) was identified despite no additional exposure. His course was complicated by tumor lysis syndrome, pleural effusions and anasarca, bowel perforations requiring multiple surgeries, acute respiratory distress syndrome, persistent pancytopenia, progressive renal and hepatic dysfunction, recurrent infections, and multiorgan failure. Despite treatment with leucovorin, urine alkalinization, continuous kidney replacement therapy, and high-flux hemodialysis, serum MTX concentrations demonstrated recurrent detectable elevations. This case highlights how altered pharmacokinetics in critical illness may render serum clearance thresholds unreliable and underscores the need for heightened clinical suspicion for delayed drug toxicity in critically ill patients with dynamic volume shifts or unexplained multiorgan dysfunction.

42966546.title: HEMATOLOGICAL AND RENAL BIOMARKERS IN CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS WITH COVID-19 IN A BRAZILIAN ICU: A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY.
42966546.abstract: and Objectives: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is associated with high morbidity and mortality, especially in critically ill patients. This study aimed to evaluate the behavior of hematological and renal biomarkers and their association with mortality in brazilian ICU patients with COVID-19. This retrospective cohort study included 52 adult patients admitted to a Brazilian ICU between June 2020 and September 2021. Hematological parameters, urea, creatinine, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were assessed at admission and at the final outcome. Statistical analyses were performed in two stages: first, comparisons were made between sexes (male vs. female); subsequently, patients were stratified into survivors and non-survivors for group comparisons. Between-group analyses were conducted using the Mann-Whitney U test, with paired comparisons performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of mortality. Patients who died during hospitalization (non-survivors, n=29) showed higher levels of urea, creatinine, leukocytes, and neutrophils, and lower hemoglobin and platelet counts compared to survivors (n=23) (p<0.001). Renal and hematological alterations were independently associated with mortality. Dynamic changes in hematological and renal biomarkers are strongly associated with mortality. Serial monitoring may improve risk stratification in critically ill COVID-19 patients.

42965007.title: Association between fibrosis-4 index and 30-day all-cause mortality in critically ill patients hospitalised with acute heart failure: a retrospective cohort study from the MIMIC-IV database.
42965007.journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
42965007.abstract: The Fibrosis-4 index (Fib-4), a non-invasive liver fibrosis biomarker, is increasingly linked to cardiovascular risk, but its role in acute heart failure (AHF) remains unclear. We evaluated its association with 30-day all-cause mortality in critically ill patients with AHF. This retrospective observational study enrolled 1535 ICU patients with AHF from the MIMIC-IV database. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality within 30 days from the date of hospital admission. Baseline characteristics, comorbidities, laboratory data, and clinical information were extracted. Patients were divided into survival and mortality groups, and baseline differences were compared. Lasso regression identified variables influencing prognosis, which were then included in a restricted cubic splines (RCS) model. Three multivariable logistic regression models (Model 1 unadjusted; Model 2 adjusted for INR, age, BUN, and potassium; Model 3 fully adjusted for pO2 max, WBC, lymphocytes, BUN, calcium, glucose, anion gap, potassium, INR, ALP, CRRT, CK-MB, age, peripheral vascular disease, and CHA2DS2-VASc score) were constructed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis assessed the predictive performance of Fib-4. Subgroup analysis evaluated potential differences across population subgroups. Sensitivity analyses using complete-case analysis and multiple imputation were performed to address missing data. The mortality group (n = 219, 14.3%) exhibited significantly higher Fib-4 values than the survival group (n = 1316). Lasso regression identified 16 variables influencing prognosis, including Fib-4. RCS analysis showed a positive correlation between Fib-4 and 30-day mortality risk (p-overall = 0.006, p-nonlinear = 0.330). After adjustment for confounders, logistic regression demonstrated that Fib-4 was an independent risk factor (Model 1: OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.07-1.13, p < 0.001; Model 2: OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 1.05-1.11, p < 0.001; Model 3: OR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.09, p = 0.002). The area under the ROC curve (AUC) for Fib-4 predicting 30-day mortality was 0.665, indicating modest predictive value. The optimal cutoff was 2.25 (sensitivity 74.0%, specificity 51.4%). Quartile analysis showed a dose-response relationship (Q4 vs. Q1: OR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.28-4.92, p = 0.007 in Model 3). Subgroup analyses revealed no significant interaction. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings. In critically ill patients with AHF, the Fib-4 index is independently associated with 30-day mortality but provides only modest predictive discrimination. This readily available, cost-effective marker may offer adjunctive information for early risk stratification, but its clinical utility should be interpreted with caution given the limited AUC.

42964124.title: OmniTFT: an EHR-driven multi-target forecasting model for ICU clinical decision support systems.
42964124.abstract: Accurate multivariate time-series forecasting of vital signs and laboratory results is crucial for electronic health record (EHR)-driven clinical decision support systems in intensive care units (ICUs). However, vital signs are susceptible to noise and exhibit rapid fluctuations, while laboratory results are characterized by missing values and measurement lags, making it challenging to forecast heterogeneous ICU variables within a common framework. We introduce OmniTFT, a Temporal Fusion Transformer-based multi-target forecasting model for ICU EHR time series. OmniTFT combines state-balanced sliding-window sampling with three training regularizers: frequency-aware embedding shrinkage, historical group-entropy regularization, and shock-alignment regularization. A shared backbone with target-specific heads enables multiple forecasting tasks within a common training and inference framework while preserving target-specific temporal resolutions and forecast horizons. OmniTFT was trained on MIMIC-IV (n = 13,277) and independently validated on two cohorts: the MIMIC-III CareVue cohort (n = 4,188) and the eICU cohort (n = 23,238). Component ablation and sampling sensitivity analyses were conducted using a fixed patient partition and ten different training seeds. On the MIMIC-IV test set, OmniTFT achieved the lowest MAE for five of eight targets, ranked second for creatinine and respiratory rate, and ranked third for temperature. In a retrospective analysis in eICU, adding the OmniTFT forecast of the subsequent unobserved 24 h to the complete observed record improved discrimination for incident moderate-to-severe acute kidney injury compared with the observed record alone (AUROC 0.763, 95% CI: 0.674-0.852 vs. 0.693, 0.598-0.787, ΔAUROC + 0.070, DeLong p = 0.009), and identified 73.3% vs. 57.8% of subsequent events when 30% of patients were flagged for review. OmniTFT provides a shared-backbone framework for forecasting heterogeneous ICU variables while preserving target-specific temporal configurations. Retrospective results in disease-enriched cohorts support broader external validation and suggest its potential as an EHR-integrated forecasting component for clinical decision support.

42963532.title: Types of adult intensive care units and admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023: a nationwide cohort study.
42963532.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
42963532.abstract: Türkiye has one of the highest intensive care unit (ICU) bed capacities among middle-income countries but also globally. Nevertheless, little is known about the characteristics of ICUs in Türkiye, their temporal trends, and ICU admissions and readmissions. We sought to analyze the structural characteristics of all adult ICUs and the clinical profiles of ICU admissions across Türkiye. We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using data from the Turkish Ministry of Health National Electronic Database. We analyzed adult ICU admissions across all levels and types over 6 years (2018-2023) and documented patient demographics, comorbidities, admission diagnoses, and ICU outcomes. We retrieved data on 3,362,539 ICU admissions. Among 22 ICU types, mixed ICUs accounted for the highest proportion of admissions (31.4%), followed by coronary (23.7%), anesthesiology (14.3%), medical (6.1%), and surgical (6.0%) ICUs. The proportion of mixed ICU beds decreased from 44.0% in 2018 to 25.1% in 2023. Most ICU beds were in state (public) hospitals (50.8%), followed by private hospitals (34.8%). The number of ICU beds increased from 2019, with a notable rise in state hospitals after 2020. The average number of ICU admissions was 659 per 100,000 population annually. The median patient age was 65 [interquartile range, 39-91] yr, and the ICU mortality was 15.5%. The leading admission diagnoses were respiratory failure (10.1%), cerebrovascular disease (7.1%), and acute kidney injury (5.2%). Hypertension (67.5%) and coronary artery disease (44.8%) were common comorbidities, particularly in nonsurvivors. The 7-day ICU readmission rate was 3.0%. The present comprehensive analysis of ICU admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023 highlights a shift toward specialization with a decrease in mixed ICUs. The impact of ICU diversity on resource use and patient outcomes requires further evaluation.

42961460.title: Tunneled Dialysis Catheter for KRT for Acute Kidney Injury in the Intensive Care Unit: CON.

42959017.title: Incidence and Outcomes of Acute Kidney Injury in Critically Ill Patients: A Retrospective Study at a Tertiary Care Hospital.
42959017.abstract: Acute kidney injury is common among critically ill patients and is associated with longer ICU stay, higher resource use and increased mortality. Evidence from low- and middle-income countries, including Nepal, remains limited. This study describes the incidence, severity distribution and clinical outcomes of AKI in a tertiary care ICU. We conducted a hospital based retrospective observational study at Dhulikhel Hospital, Nepal. All adults admitted to the ICU from 1 st may 2023 to 30 th April 2024 were screened using ICU registry. AKI was defined and staged using KDIGO serum criteria. Demographic data, comorbidities, ICU interventions and outcomes were extracted. Associations were examined using appropriate statistical tests. Among 1113 patients, 1064 were enrolled for analysis. The incidence of AKI was 29.6%. Patients with AKI were older (median age 60 vs 55 years, p < 0.001), had longer ICU stays (median 3 vs 2 days, p < 0.001), were more frequently on invasive mechanical ventilation (39.6%vs 26%, p < 0.001). Type 2 diabetes mellitus was significantly associated with AKI (39.0% vs 28.0%, p = 0.001). AKI severity correlated with worse outcomes including higher mortality and adverse outcomes increasing from 12.7% in patients without AKI to 38% in stage 3 AKI. Renal replacement therapy was required in 2.3% of patients, mainly in stage 2 and 3 AKI. Acute kidney injury is a common and a serious complication among critically ill patients, associated with increased mortality and prolonged ICU stay. Early recognition and targeted management strategies, particularly for high-risk groups, are needed in resource limited settings.

42879942.title: Emergency medicine pharmacotherapy literature of 2025.
42879942.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
42879942.abstract: The purpose of this article is to summarize pharmacotherapy-related emergency medicine (EM) literature indexed in 2025. Articles were selected using a modified Delphi approach. The table of contents from predetermined journals were reviewed and independently evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system by paired authors. Pharmacotherapy-related publications deemed to be GRADE 1A and 1B were reviewed by the collective group for inclusion in the review. This article synthesizes and evaluates findings from 7 randomized controlled trials, 10 guidelines, clinical policies, position statements, or consensus recommendations, and 11 meta-analyses, providing critical insight into their potential clinical impact. Covered topics include guideline or policy updates on advanced cardiac life support, rapid sequence intubation, tranexamic acid in trauma, acute coronary syndromes, and hypertension. Randomized controlled trials covering sedative use in rapid sequence intubation, treatment of sexually transmitted infections and bacterial vaginosis, sodium bicarbonate for severe acidemia and acute kidney injury in the critically ill, and thrombolytic therapy beyond traditional time windows for ischemic stroke are also reviewed. Additional topics include nebulized and low-dose ketamine for analgesia, erector spinae plane block for renal colic, two-bag versus three-bag acetylcysteine regimens for acetaminophen overdose, QT prolongation in antipsychotic overdose, and naltrexone for opioid dependence.

42879641.title: Hematological indices as predictors of in-hospital adverse outcomes in patients with COVID-19.
42879641.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
42879641.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic required medical teams to make rational decisions with limited resources, especially in Brazil. Various diagnostic tools, clinical guidelines, and existing indices were adopted to predict the risk of death and other adverse outcomes. The objective of this study was to validate three hematological indices [neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and lymphocyte-monocyte ratio (LMR)] for predicting adverse hospital outcomes in patients with COVID-19 in an observational cohort at a hospital in northeastern Brazil between April 2020 and October 2021. Hematological indices were calculated based on admission blood counts and correlated with hospital outcomes: in-hospital death, invasive mechanical ventilation, and renal replacement therapy. The analysis determined the frequencies of outcomes, established index thresholds, and assessed their association and accuracy and factors associated with hospital survival. Intra-hospital outcomes reflected disease severity; 34.62% of patients required admission to the ICU, 26.21% invasive mechanical ventilation, 4.2% renal replacement therapy, and 21.04% died. Advanced age, ICU requirement, and higher NLR were associated with higher risk of death. Multivariate analysis identified NLR as the only index associated with worse prognosis, with a cutoff point of 5.24 at hospital admission, showing a sensitivity of 84.0% and accuracy of 86.9%. The negative predictive value of 95.52% was highly significant, assisting hospital management by focusing efforts on higher-risk patients. These findings highlight the predictive value of the NLR, PLR, and LMR indices as valuable markers for risk stratification in patients hospitalized with COVID-19, offering a broader view of prognosis and guiding more personalized management and care strategies.

42866125.title: The effects of hemoadsorption in patients with sepsis-associated persistent severe AKI who require CRRT: A prospective, randomized controlled pilot study.
authors: Acute Kidney Injury Precision Prevention and Treatment Research Team(AKI-PPT)
42866125.abstract: Sepsis-associated persistent severe acute kidney injury (S-PAKI) is marked by a sustained hyperinflammatory response and is associated with a poor prognosis. Hemoadsorption functions by removing circulating cytokines and other inflammatory mediators. This study aims to evaluate the impact of CVVH combined with hemoadsorption on the prognosis of patients with S-PAKI who need CRRT. This prospective, randomized, single-center pilot study involved 76 S-PAKI patients who required CRRT. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either CVVH combined with hemoadsorption (CVVH + HA group, n = 38) or conventional CVVH therapy (CVVH group, n = 38). The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included changes in Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores, renal functional prognosis, alterations in biomarker and cytokine levels, changes in hemodynamic parameters, as well as the duration of renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation, ICU stay, and overall hospital stay among survivors. The CVVH + HA group showed a statistically non-significant trend to lower 30-day all-cause mortality compared to the CVVH group (36.8% vs. 52.6%, P = 0.159). A post hoc exploratory subgroup analysis revealed that among patients with Chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 14 (CCL14) levels greater than 1.3 ng/ml, the mortality risk in the CVVH + HA group was lower than that in the CVVH group. In terms of secondary outcomes, hemoadsorption therapy significantly decreased APACHE II and SOFA scores, enhanced cytokine clearance, and improved hemodynamic status; however, it did not lead to significant improvements in renal functional prognosis, nor did it shorten the duration of mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, ICU stay, or overall hospital stay among survivors. In this pilot trial, hemoadsorption therapy did not significantly reduce 30-day mortality across the entire cohort. However, a post hoc exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a potential association with improved survival in patients with elevated urinary CCL14 levels. These exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in adequately powered, biomarker-guided randomized trials. ChiCTR2400093572, registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) on December 09, 2024.

42824912.title: National Overview of Designated Infectious Disease Control Institutions and Medical Response Resources in the Republic of Korea, 2025.
42824912.abstract: This study assessed the regional distribution of infectious disease control institutions and medical response resources to support preparedness and resource management. We examined 223 institutions designated for infectious disease control or operating national infectious disease beds as of June 30, 2025. Institutional characteristics were obtained from Regional Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and local governments, while medical resource data were obtained from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service. We assessed regional distribution, bed capacity, ownership, institution type, national infectious disease bed status, negative-pressure isolation beds, critical care equipment, and personnel. The largest numbers of institutions were in Jeonnam (44), Gyeongnam (40), and Busan (30). Of the 223 institutions, 123 (55.2%) had fewer than 300 beds and accounted for 239 negative-pressure isolation beds, compared with 1,571 negative-pressure isolation beds in institutions with ≥300 beds. Overall, the institutions had 5,823 ventilators, 314 extracorporeal membrane oxygenation devices, and 812 continuous renal replacement therapy devices. There were 174 infectious disease specialists, 318 pulmonologists, and 40 pediatric infectious disease specialists. Major equipment and specialist personnel were concentrated in regions with large hospitals, particularly Seoul, Gyeonggi, and Busan. Medical response resources varied by region and hospital size, with negative-pressure isolation beds, critical care equipment, and specialized personnel concentrated in larger hospitals and select regions. These findings reveal that infectious disease response capacity should be assessed not only by the number of designated institutions but also by the distribution and availability of medical resources.

42824807.title: Association Between Cardiopulmonary Bypass Time and Early Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Adults.
42824807.abstract: Introduction Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) has improved the safety and precision of complex cardiac surgery, but its inflammatory, embolic, and hemodynamic effects may contribute to postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI). This study explored whether longer CPB duration was associated with early postoperative AKI and related renal and clinical recovery outcomes in adult cardiac surgical patients. Methodology This prospective observational comparative study was conducted at the Department of Cardiac Surgery of the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NICVD) in Dhaka, Bangladesh, from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2024. It included 100 adult cardiac patients aged 18-65 years who underwent cardiac surgery under CPB, selected by convenience sampling after ethical approval. Patients were divided into two equal groups after surgery according to recorded CPB duration: Group A included 50 patients with CPB time ≤120 minutes, while Group B included 50 patients with CPB time >120 minutes. Patients with pre-existing chronic kidney disease, kidney transplant history, emergency surgery, ejection fraction below 30%, previous cardiac surgery, or surgery without CPB were excluded. Results The two study groups were broadly comparable at baseline, with similar mean age (37.8±13.73 vs. 38.46±13.30 years; p=0.8), age distribution (p=0.93), gender distribution (male 58% vs. 52%; p=0.69), comorbidities, body mass index (BMI) profile, and underlying cardiac disease pattern. Smoking, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia were distributed without significant difference, while most patients in both groups had normal BMI, and isolated valvular heart disease was the commonest diagnosis. The intended difference between the groups was clearly established by CPB duration, with a mean CPB time of 93.00±11.42 minutes in Group A and 137.10±12.08 minutes in Group B (p<0.001). After surgery, patients with longer CPB time showed lower urine output at 24, 48, and 72 hours, with all differences reaching statistical significance (p<0.001). Although baseline serum creatinine was statistically insignificant (0.83±0.11 vs. 0.86±0.13 mg/dL; p=0.108), postoperative serum creatinine became significantly higher in Group B at 24, 48, and 72 hours (p<0.001). Postoperative AKI occurred in seven patients (14%) in Group A but in 23 patients (46%) in Group B, showing more than a threefold higher occurrence among patients with CPB time >120 minutes (p<0.001). Renal replacement therapy was required only in Group B in four patients (8%), and in-hospital mortality also occurred only in Group B in three patients (6%), though these differences were not statistically significant. Patients in the longer CPB group required longer mechanical ventilation (8.90±3.84 vs. 6.98±2.69 hours; p<0.001), longer ICU stay (10.15±4.68 vs. 4.87±1.58 days; p<0.001), and longer postoperative hospital stay (14.36±5.55 vs. 10.11±3.05 days; p<0.001). Conclusion Prolonged CPB time was significantly associated with greater early postoperative renal stress, higher AKI occurrence, and slower recovery, though the findings require cautious interpretation due to the single-center design, convenience sampling, short follow-up, and unadjusted perioperative factors.

42953943.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Major Postoperative Complications After Noncardiac Surgery Under General Anesthesia Using Routinely Available Electronic Health Record Data: Retrospective Multicenter Development and Validation Study.
42953943.abstract: Postoperative complications after noncardiac surgery under general anesthesia remain a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and resource-intensive care. Conventional risk assessment tools rely mainly on preoperative information and may not capture perioperative physiological and procedural factors associated with postoperative risk. This retrospective multicenter observational study aimed to develop and validate electronic health record (EHR)-based machine learning (ML) models for predicting major postoperative complications and to evaluate their discrimination, overall probabilistic performance, calibration, and potential clinical utility. We analyzed 35,702 adults who underwent noncardiac surgery under general anesthesia at 3 tertiary hospitals between January 2021 and March 2025. Preoperative, intraoperative, and early postoperative variables were extracted from diagnosis procedure combination (DPC) claims, EHRs, and anesthesia information systems. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of in-hospital death, unplanned reoperation, prolonged mechanical ventilation, new initiation of renal replacement therapy, and postoperative infection. Logistic regression (LR), extreme gradient boosting (XGB), and light gradient boosting machine (LGBM) models were developed using preoperative variables alone or with 7 additional intraoperative and early postoperative variables. Leave-one-facility-out internal-external cross-validation (IECV) was the primary validation framework, with a stratified random 80:20 hold-out analysis as secondary validation. Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC), Brier score, scaled Brier score, calibration measures, and decision curve analysis. The primary composite outcome occurred in 3884 of 35,702 patients (10.9%). In pooled IECV, perioperative models consistently outperformed the corresponding preoperative models. AUROC increased from 0.784-0.791 to 0.810-0.817, PR-AUC increased from 0.356-0.361 to 0.405-0.413, Brier scores decreased from 0.082-0.083 to 0.078-0.080, and scaled Brier scores increased from 0.144-0.151 to 0.175-0.191. Calibration varied across facilities; pooled calibration slopes for the perioperative models ranged from 0.875 to 0.902, and calibration intercepts ranged from -0.367 to -0.222, indicating overly extreme predictions and overall risk overestimation. Exploratory decision curve analysis generally showed greater net benefit for perioperative models across threshold probabilities of 0.01-0.30, although the curves overlapped substantially. Secondary and sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary findings. Adding routinely available intraoperative and early postoperative variables produced modest but consistent improvements in postoperative risk prediction compared with preoperative variables alone. However, facility-specific variation in calibration limits direct transportability of absolute risk estimates. The models may support prioritization for postoperative clinical reassessment, but exploratory decision curve analysis did not establish a specific intervention or triage threshold. Local recalibration and prospective workflow evaluation are required before clinical implementation.

42953825.title: Effectiveness of combined management of automated red cell exchange and therapeutic plasma exchange in a patient of sickle cell disease presenting with acute chest syndrome and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
42953825.abstract: Acute chest syndrome (ACS) is a severe complication of sickle cell disease (SCD) that demands prompt medical attention. Approximately one-fifth of patients with a history of ACS progress rapidly to respiratory failure within 24 h, often leading to multiorgan failure. A 23-year-old male with a history of SCD and multiple vaso-occlusive crises presented to the emergency department with fever, chest pain, and breathlessness. Diagnosed with SCD 8 years prior, he had been on hydroxyurea 500 mg daily but had discontinued the medication 3 months back. He was admitted to the intensive care unit for urgent management and placed on noninvasive ventilation. The chest X-ray revealed new right lung consolidation. As the clinical condition deteriorated, he was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation in the prone position. Routine management included intravenous (IV) morphine, antibiotics, and IV fluids. The patient urgently required a transfusion of two packed red blood cell units due to a critically low hemoglobin level of 4.1 g/dl, followed by automated red cell exchange (RCE). Automated RCE improved the PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and prone ventilation was no longer necessitated. He was suspected of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis due to fever, splenomegaly, hypertriglyceridemia, and hyperferritinemia. He was treated with therapeutic plasma exchange of 1.2 plasma volumes, followed by IV immunoglobulin. Hemodialysis was performed to treat acute kidney injury. His condition gradually improved, and he was extubated.

42946589.title: Machine Learning-Based Mortality Prediction for Mechanically Ventilated Liver Failure Patients: A Retrospective Study.
42946589.abstract: To develop a mortality prediction model for patients with liver failure who require mechanical ventilation (MV) in ICU. This retrospective study utilized data from the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV (v3.0) databases. Variables included demographics, liver function markers, ventilator parameters, severity scores, comorbidities, use of vasoactive drugs and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) as well as length of ICU and hospital stay. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Five machine learning algorithms were applied: logistic regression, decision tree, Bagging, neural network, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). The dataset was randomly split into a training set (70%) and a test set (30%). Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and calibration plots. Predictive factors were ranked for the best-performing model by importance. A total of 2336 patients were identified from the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV databases. On the test set, the AUC values for each model were as follows: logistic regression (0.836), decision tree (0.768), neural network (0.774), Bagging (0.854), and XGBoost (0.875). Calibration curves showed good agreement for all models except the neural network. Among the 5 algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the highest predictive performance. The top 5 predictors identified were length of hospital stay, SAPS II score, use of vasoactive drugs, total bilirubin and length of ICU stay. Machine learning-based models can effectively predict in-hospital mortality in liver failure patients receiving mechanical ventilation. Among the 5 algorithms tested, the XGBoost model achieved the best overall performance.

42940536.title: Complications and Hospital Resource Utilization Associated with ECMO in COVID-19 ARDS with Acute Kidney Injury: Insights from United States National Inpatient Sample, 2020-2022.
42940536.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication of COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), yet the impact of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) on outcomes in this high-risk population remains unclear. We performed a retrospective, survey-weighted study using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database from 2020-2022 to compare outcomes among adults hospitalized with COVID-19-associated ARDS and AKI managed with invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) alone versus IMV and ECMO. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, while secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT), complications, hospital length of stay (LOS), and healthcare utilization. Among 198,395 hospitalizations with COVID-19 ARDS complicated by AKI, 4730 received IMV and ECMO. ECMO use was not associated with statistically significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.81-1.12). However, ECMO was associated with greater odds of RRT, intracranial hemorrhage, disseminated intravascular coagulation, cardiogenic shock, vasopressor use, tracheostomy, acute liver failure, deep vein thrombosis, ischemic stroke and ICU-acquired weakness. ECMO was also associated with longer LOS and higher hospitalization charges. Among hospitalizations with COVID-19-associated ARDS and AKI, ECMO was not associated with statistically significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality but was associated with markedly higher complication burden, longer hospitalization, and substantially greater healthcare resource utilization.

42935540.title: Independent correlates of vancomycin steady-state trough concentration among patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery: observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump support.
42935540.abstract: Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) combined with valve surgery represent a high-risk surgical population with substantial perioperative hemodynamic disturbances and highly variable organ function, leading to high variability in vancomycin pharmacokinetics. Conventional vancomycin dosing solely on renal function frequently fails to achieve target trough concentrations in this complex subgroup. This study aimed to identify independent correlates c of vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations (Css-min), and to report observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, to inform individualized therapeutic drug monitoring. A single-center retrospective observational study enrolled adult patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery from January 2018 to October 2024. Clinical data and vancomycin TDM records were extracted from electronic medical records. Vancomycin Css-min was detected by enzyme-multiplied immunoassay technique. Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) accounting for within-patient repeated TDM measurements were used to identify clinical correlates of Css-min. IABP support was pre-specified and force-entered into the multivariable model based on clinical observations and pathophysiological reasoning, independent of univariate screening results. We performed a sensitivity analysis for patients with at least one TDM within postoperative day 7, prespecified interaction tests for effect modification, and binary logistic-GEE for the supratherapeutic endpoint (Css-min > 20 mg/L). A two-tailed P < 0.05 was set as statistical significance. A total of 283 eligible patients with 473 valid Css-min measurements were included. Multivariate GEE demonstrated that categorical vancomycin dosing regimen, age, ventilator dependence ≥96 h, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), IABP support, serum creatinine (Scr), and serum urea nitrogen (SUN) were positively associated with higher geometric-mean Css-min. Associations remained largely consistent in the sensitivity-analysis subgroup of patients with at least one early-phase TDM within postoperative day 7. A significant CRRT-by-postoperative-time interaction was detected, indicating that the influence of CRRT on vancomycin exposure varied across different postoperative phases. Of note, the association signal linking IABP to supratherapeutic trough concentrations (Css-min>20 mg/L) was modest and requires cautious interpretation. Multiple clinical factors jointly affect vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations in patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery, including dosing regimen, age, renal biomarkers, and critical-care supportive interventions such as IABP, CRRT and prolonged mechanical ventilation. IABP support represents an intriguing observational signal; this finding remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective external validation before it can guide formal dose-adjustment strategies. Individualized vancomycin management for this population should comprehensively integrate hemodynamic support measures and laboratory indices rather than depend merely on renal-function markers. This study focuses on clinically accessible trough concentration monitoring rather than constructing complex pharmacokinetic models, which is more in line with real-world clinical practice.

42909257.title: Inhaled nitric oxide: Expanding indications beyond traditional boundaries.
42909257.abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that improves ventilation-perfusion matching with minimal effect on systemic blood pressure. Although the FDA approval is restricted to neonatal hypoxic respiratory failure associated with pulmonary hypertension, many clinicians now use iNO in adults with conditions where elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular dysfunction threaten stability and hypoxic respiratory failure. This review examines both the mechanistic rationale and the available evidence for such off-label use. Examples range from acute RV failure in the ICU to perioperative support in cardiac surgery, heart and lung transplantation, and severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, including COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). In these settings, iNO offers rapid afterload reduction and short-term improvement in oxygenation, but randomized trials are lacking and limited studies to date have failed to consistently show outcome benefits. Adverse effects such as methemoglobinemia, nitrogen dioxide toxicity, rebound pulmonary hypertension, and a potential increase in acute kidney injury risk in certain non-cardiac surgical populations. Additionally, cost considerations and other practical limitations must be weighed carefully. Overall, current evidence supports the use of iNO as an adjunctive therapy in carefully selected critically ill patients.

42903157.title: Case Report: mNGS-negative Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome with small bowel obstruction as the initial manifestation in a glucocorticoid-exposed COPD patient: a fatal case.
42903157.abstract: Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome (SHS) is a life-threatening condition in immunocompromised hosts with an extremely high mortality rate. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) demonstrates limited sensitivity for parasitic detection, and its clinical value remains to be fully elucidated. The conventional microscopy remains an indispensable tool for the diagnosis of parasitic infections. A 73-year-old male patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and cerebral infarction presented with abdominal pain and distension for 7 days and no bowel movement for 3 days. He was diagnosed with incomplete small bowel obstruction at an outside hospital and treated with fasting, enemas, meropenem, and methylprednisolone. He was subsequently transferred to our hospital due to acute lower respiratory tract infection. Chest radiography revealed bilateral diffuse infiltrates, and his condition rapidly deteriorated, requiring admission to the intensive care unit (ICU), endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Stool smear and retrospective sputum examination both identified larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis. However, mNGS of sputum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) obtained upon admission failed to detect any parasitic sequences. The patient was treated sequentially with albendazole and ivermectin, in combination with broad-spectrum antibacterial, antifungal, and antiviral therapy. He ultimately died on February 11, 2025, due to severe pneumonia, sepsis, and bone marrow suppression. For immunocompromised hosts with multiple risk factors, particularly those exposed to glucocorticoids, active parasitic microscopic examination of stool and respiratory secretions should be pursued when unexplained pulmonary infiltrates coexist with gastrointestinal symptoms, even in the setting of negative mNGS results, to avoid missed diagnosis.

42901157.title: Refractory Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Supported by Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation due to Leptospirosis at Réunion Island and a Literature Review.
42901157.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
42901157.abstract: Leptospirosis is a zoonosis prevalent on Réunion Island. Severe forms with acute respiratory failure can lead to refractory hypoxemia, requiring the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). The aim for the present study was to describe all cases of leptospirosis complicated by refractory acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring veno-venous ECMO on Réunion Island and to conduct a literature review. This retrospective observational study was conducted in a multidisciplinary intensive care unit of the University Hospital of Réunion Island. The aim was to describe the clinical, biological, and prognostic characteristics of patients who developed leptospirosis complicated by refractory ARDS requiring ECMO between January 2011 and December 2024. A total of 14 patients with a median age of 38 years and few comorbidities were included. The organ failure most commonly associated with respiratory involvement was acute kidney injury (93%). The median delay between mechanical ventilation and ECMO support was 0 (0-1) days. The median duration of ECMO support was short (7 [4-12] days). The mortality rate in this population was 29%. A systematic literature review revealed 50 cases of patients with leptospirosis requiring ECMO, with a median age of 34 years and a mortality rate of 20%. The favorable prognosis of patients with refractory ARDS due to leptospirosis justifies the use of ECMO. Early referral to a center equipped with ECMO is essential, given the rapid decline in respiratory function.

42900380.title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio as a marker of major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
42900380.abstract: This study examined whether the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and whether this association differs from that of absolute ICU admission glucose. This single-center retrospective study included 731 surgical episodes from 709 adults who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. SHR was calculated as the first ICU glucose divided by HbA1c-derived estimated average glucose. The primary outcome was an unweighted composite of 30-day mortality, stroke, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 3 acute kidney injury, reoperation for bleeding, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and deep sternal wound infection. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinically relevant covariates. The composite outcome occurred in 90 surgical episodes (12.3%). SHR was associated with the composite outcome after adjustment (odds ratio [OR], 1.103 per 0.1 increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.008-1.208; P = 0.033), whereas ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated (OR, 1.019 per 10 mg/dL increase; 95% CI 0.946-1.096; P = 0.626). SHR at ICU admission was associated with major postoperative complications in the primary analysis, whereas absolute ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated after multivariable adjustment. Confidence intervals for SHR included 1.0 in several sensitivity analyses. SHR warrants prospective evaluation as an early postoperative risk marker after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

42898067.title: Phenotypic characterization of patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage: a data-driven analysis of a multicentre, retrospective, nationwide cohort.
42898067.abstract: Severe diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) is a potentially fatal complication of ANCA-associated vasculitides (AAV). This study aimed to identify distinct clinical phenotypes among patients to the ICU, and to examine their association with mortality. We conducted an ancillary analysis of the national multicenter retrospective PLEXHIA cohort, including 197 patients with severe AAV-related DAH, defined by respiratory symptoms with new infiltrates consistent with alveolar hemorrhage, along with oxygen saturation ≤85%, high-flow oxygen or mechanical ventilation requirement. Kohonen self-organizing maps were applied to predefined clinical variables at ICU admission, excluding treatment and outcomes. Clusters were interpreted and compared regarding organ involvement, severity, management, and mortality at 30 and 90 days. Between 2012 and 2024, 197 patients (66 years old, 52% female) were included, revealing marked clinical heterogeneity. Three phenotypes emerged: The MPO pulmonary-renal (MPO-PR) cluster included patients with anti-MPO ANCA, renal involvement and high oxygen requirements. The mild-respiratory (Mild-R) cluster included predominantly female patients with less severe respiratory compromise and mild renal involvement. The PR3 multi-organ (PR3-MO) cluster involved younger patients with anti-PR3 ANCA, severe acute respiratory failure and multiorgan failure. Renal replacement therapy was most frequent in the MPO-PR group (73%), while invasive mechanical ventilation was most common in the MPO-PR and PR3-MO groups (71% and 68%). Thirty-day mortality differed significantly: 23% (MPO-PR), 4% (mild-R cluster), and 14% (PR3-MO cluster). This large ICU cohort highlights three clinically relevant phenotypes of AAV-related DAH, which could inform the development of phenotype-driven immunosuppressive strategies.

42886410.title: Mechanical ventilation-associated AKI: toward a multimodal and kidney-protective ventilatory framework.
42886410.abstract: Mechanical ventilation-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) represents a complex manifestation of lung-kidney cross-talk driven by hemodynamic alterations, neurohumoral activation, systemic inflammation and disturbances in gas exchange and acid-base homeostasis. Beyond static ventilatory settings, increasing evidence suggests that dynamic fluctuations in airway and perfusion parameters, including static driving pressure (ΔP), positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), mean airway pressure (Pmean), and effective renal perfusion pressure (eRPP) may substantially influence renal vulnerability during mechanical ventilation. This comprehensive narrative review synthesizes current mechanistic and clinical evidence on the relationship between mechanical ventilation and AKI and proposes an integrated framework for future research on the interplay between ventilatory stress, venous congestion, renal perfusion, and inflammatory injury. Emerging bedside tools such as renal Doppler indices, venous excess ultrasound score (VExUS), and kidney injury biomarkers are discussed as components of an integrated physiologic approach for early recognition and risk stratification of ventilator-associated AKI. We further propose a multimodal conceptual framework integrating respiratory mechanics, congestion assessment, perfusion monitoring, and biomarkers to support individualized kidney-protective ventilation strategies. Future research should prioritize standardized physiologic monitoring, time-varying exposure analyses, causal mediation approaches, and prospective multicenter studies to better define renal-protective ventilatory targets and advance precision critical care.

42882032.title: Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia: The Role of Kidney-Lung Crosstalk and Renal Replacement Therapy, a Narrative Review.
42882032.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) results from dynamic inter-organ interactions rather than isolated organ failures. Among these, kidney-lung crosstalk is a key determinant of outcomes in critically ill patients. Acute kidney injury (AKI) promotes pulmonary dysfunction through hemodynamic, inflammatory, endothelial, and metabolic mechanisms, while acute respiratory failure and mechanical ventilation may aggravate renal injury. Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) may represent a clinical consequence of these interactions, although causality remains uncertain. Renal replacement therapy (RRT) may further influence kidney-lung crosstalk through several physiological mechanisms. To summarize current evidence on kidney-lung crosstalk, evaluate its potential contribution to VAP susceptibility, and examine the role of RRT in modulating these interactions. Methods: Narrative review of experimental, translational, and clinical studies investigating bidirectional kidney-lung interactions in critical illness. Results: Kidney-to-lung crosstalk involves fluid overload, venous congestion, immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, and metabolic disturbances. Lung-to-kidney signaling is driven by mechanical ventilation, ventilator-induced lung injury, hypoxemia, and hypercapnia. Clinical evidence is strongest for fluid overload, venous congestion, and mechanical ventilation, whereas endothelial dysfunction and uremic toxins remain supported mainly by experimental data. AKI-associated immune dysfunction and prolonged mechanical ventilation provide biologically plausible mechanisms linking AKI to VAP, but definitive causal evidence is lacking because of methodological limitations. RRT may influence these interactions through optimized fluid balance, correction of acid-base disorders, improved antimicrobial pharmacokinetics, and potentially extracorporeal immunomodulation. However, no randomized trial has demonstrated a direct reduction in VAP incidence attributable to RRT. Conclusions: Kidney-lung crosstalk is a major driver of organ dysfunction in critical illness, yet translation into targeted therapies remains limited. Current evidence supports integrated organ-protective strategies-including lung-protective ventilation, individualized fluid management, VAP prevention, and optimized antimicrobial therapy-while future advances will rely on biological phenotyping, biomarker-guided risk stratification, and robust causal inference approaches.

42909258.title: Characterization of an Unusual Severe Yellow Fever Outbreak in the Colombian Andean Region.
42909258.abstract: Yellow fever (YF) reemerged in Colombia's Andean region during 2024-2025, outside the country's historically recognized endemic areas. We characterized critically ill adults admitted during this outbreak and described clinical features, organ dysfunction, supportive care, and in-hospital outcomes. We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of consecutive adults with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR)-confirmed YF admitted to the national referral intensive care unit in Ibagué, Tolima, Colombia, from March through September 2025. Clinical, laboratory, complication, intervention, and outcome data were prospectively captured using a standardized case report form. Sixty-one patients were analyzed; 22 died (36.1%). Non-survivors had lower platelet counts and fibrinogen and higher INR, aminotransferases, lactate dehydrogenase, and creatinine at ICU admission. Shock, acute kidney injury, acute respiratory distress syndrome, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and severe bleeding were more frequent among non-survivors. Prior YF vaccination was self-reported by 10 patients (16.4%). Severe YF in this Andean outbreak was characterized by hepatic-coagulation abnormalities and multisystem organ dysfunction. The occurrence of critical illness outside historically recognized endemic areas supports surveillance and vaccination strategies that can adapt to changing epidemiological risk.

42844256.title: Plasma proteomics defines two reproducible subphenotypes of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury with distinct outcomes.
42844256.abstract: Sepsis is the leading cause of acute kidney injury in critically ill patients, and this complication carries a high risk of death. The biology underlying it varies between patients, which may explain why treatments have not succeeded. Here we show, using an ensemble method that groups patients by patterns across hundreds of blood proteins in three independent groups of patients, that sepsis-associated acute kidney injury comprises two reproducible subphenotypes. One subphenotype shows widespread activation of inflammation, metabolism, and oxidative stress; the other shows a quieter profile. Patients in the inflammatory subtype have higher mortality, more complications, and fewer days alive and out of the intensive care unit. A simple seven-protein test reproduces these groupings and identifies them accurately in separate cohorts. In a randomized trial, the drug ilofotase alfa appears to benefit the inflammatory subtype but not the other, suggesting that this classification could guide future treatment.

42942373.title: Lower Plasma Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Levels During Critical Illness Are Associated with Subsequent Dialysis Requirement.
42942373.abstract: Background and Objectives: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), best known for its role in cognitive function, is an anti-inflammatory protein proposed as a potential therapeutic target and diagnostic biomarker in sepsis. However, studies investigating circulating BDNF levels in patients with sepsis have yielded conflicting results, reporting both increased and decreased concentrations. Comorbid conditions, particularly liver cirrhosis, pancreatitis, and kidney failure, may contribute to these discrepancies. Therefore, the primary aim of this study was to investigate the association between plasma BDNF levels and these comorbidities in patients with sepsis. Materials and Methods: Plasma BDNF concentrations were measured in 250 critically ill patients with systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), sepsis, or septic shock and 40 healthy controls. Among these patients, 56 had liver cirrhosis, 44 had pancreatitis, and 94 required dialysis. Results: Patients with SIRS/sepsis/septic shock exhibited significantly lower plasma BDNF levels than healthy controls. Plasma BDNF concentrations were unchanged in patients with concomitant liver cirrhosis, increased in the 44 patients with pancreatitis, and significantly decreased in those with acute kidney injury requiring dialysis (AKI-D), compared with patients without pancreatitis and those without AKI-D, respectively. When patients were stratified by dialysis status, plasma BDNF levels were similar among patients with SIRS, sepsis, and septic shock. Plasma BDNF levels did not change in ventilated patients or in those who did not survive. Furthermore, patients with COVID-19-related sepsis and those with non-COVID-19 etiologies showed comparable plasma BDNF concentrations. However, plasma BDNF levels in non-dialysis and dialysis patients were not, or were only weakly, associated with routine measures of renal function. Plasma BDNF levels positively correlated with platelet count, which predicted BDNF levels in patients with SIRS/sepsis/septic shock. Conclusions: Plasma BDNF levels are similarly reduced in patients with SIRS/sepsis/septic shock and are further decreased in AKI-D, whereas patients with pancreatitis exhibit higher BDNF levels. Platelet count, which decreased in AKI-D and was higher in pancreatitis, predicted plasma BDNF levels, suggesting platelet count as an important factor affecting plasma BDNF levels.

42864500.title: Mapping the knowledge landscape and identifying frontiers of mitochondrial dysfunction in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: a four-decade bibliometric and visualized analysis.
42864500.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction has been recognized as a central pathogenic event and is under active investigation as a candidate therapeutic target in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). This study aims to employ multi-tool bibliometric analysis to systematically map the four-decade intellectual landscape of this field, thereby identifying emerging research hotspots and outlining priority-setting directions for future pharmacological investigation. Because publication and citation metrics quantify scholarly attention rather than therapeutic efficacy, the pathways highlighted here reflect research trends and priority-setting signals, not established therapeutic targets. A comprehensive literature retrieval was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus up to March 18, 2026. Following rigorous data cleaning, 837 publications were analyzed using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix R package to visually evaluate publication trends, knowledge networks, and evolving research hotspots. Cumulative publication output exhibits sustained exponential growth (R2 = 0.997), accelerating significantly post-2010. China and the USA dominate global productivity, though institutional collaboration networks reveal pronounced regional clustering. Notably, publication hubs have transitioned significantly from traditional critical care journals to molecular and pharmacological journals, consistent with a shifting emphasis of scholarly attention toward molecular and pharmacological research themes. Keyword and citation burst analyses suggest that the research frontier has evolved from broad physiological observations to specific subcellular executioners. Mitochondria-mediated programmed cell death (apoptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis) and oxidative stress have become the most prominent bibliometric hotspots and candidate pharmacological targets. The field of SA-AKI research has shown a pronounced, publication-driven shift from clinical phenotyping to the target-driven molecular deconstruction of mitochondrial damage; we emphasize that this result reflects research priorities, not proven therapeutic efficacy of these targets. To overcome current translational bottlenecks and off-target effects of existing agents, future drug development should transition from isolated in vitro models toward clinical multi-omics validation. Developing innovative targeted delivery systems (such as engineered nanomaterials and exosomes) and multi-target synergistic therapies will need rigorous empirical testing to determine whether they can precisely mitigate the complex SA-AKI "mitochondrial storm".

42857434.title: Retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis masquerading as perforated viscus: a rare case report.
42857434.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
42857434.abstract: Necrotizing fasciitis is a rapidly progressive, life-threatening soft-tissue infection associated with high mortality, particularly when diagnosis is delayed. While most cases involve the extremities or perineum, retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis is exceedingly rare. Its deep anatomical location often results in vague clinical presentations, allowing extensive infection before overt signs develop, which poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Early recognition and timely intervention are critical to improving outcomes. We report the case of a 40-year-old male who presented with nonspecific abdominal and flank pain, and low-grade fever of 2 days duration. Imaging revealed extensive retroperitoneal gas and fascial involvement. Urgent exploratory laparotomy confirmed necrosis of the bilateral abdominal wall fascia and retroperitoneal involvement. Initial surgical debridement was performed along with broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy. Postoperatively, the patient underwent repeat surgical drainage. Despite initial stabilization, he progressed to acute kidney injury, hyperbilirubinemia, and biochemical evidence of pancreatitis, necessitating intensive care. The patient ultimately succumbed to uncontrolled sepsis with multiorgan failure on the sixth postoperative day. Retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis is difficult to diagnose due to nonspecific symptoms and deep anatomical location. Imaging, particularly contrast-enhanced computed tomography, is essential for detecting fascial necrosis and retroperitoneal gas. Even with prompt surgical debridement and broad-spectrum antibiotics, the infection can progress rapidly along fascial planes, causing secondary abscesses and multiorgan dysfunction. Retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis can progress silently and rapidly, leading to multiorgan failure. Heightened clinical suspicion, early imaging, and prompt surgical management are crucial for improving patient outcomes.

42853715.title: Clinical Significance of Klotho, Fibroblast Growth Factor 23, and Their Ratio for Acute Kidney Injury in Sepsis Patients.
42853715.journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
42853715.abstract: The sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is common in patients with sepsis and associated with poor outcomes, yet serum creatinine and urine output have limited value for early assessment. We examined whether admission Klotho, fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), and the Klotho/FGF23 ratio were associated with SA-AKI and short-term outcomes and compared their discriminative performance. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 320 patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with Sepsis-3-defined sepsis. SA-AKI (n = 112) was retrospectively identified according to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Klotho and FGF23 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in stored serum samples collected within 24 h of ICU admission. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis, and adjusted associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Patients with SA-AKI had lower Klotho, higher FGF23, and a reduced Klotho/FGF23 ratio at admission (all p < 0.001). The ratio showed the highest area under the curve biomarkers for SA-AKI (0.84; 95% confidence interval 0.79-0.88) and remained associated with SA-AKI after multivariable adjustment (odds ratio 2.25; 95% confidence interval 1.46-3.53). The ratio decreased with increasing KDIGO stage. Among patients with SA-AKI, a low ratio remained associated with lower 3-month renal recovery, longer ICU and hospital stays, higher in-hospital mortality, and greater 3-month chronic kidney disease progression after adjustment. The admission Klotho/FGF23 ratio was associated with SA-AKI, higher KDIGO stage, and short-term outcomes and showed the highest observed discrimination among the three biomarkers.

42852417.title: Spontaneous Tumor Lysis Syndrome in Refractory Metastatic Esophageal Adenocarcinoma Presenting With Septic Shock.
42852417.abstract: Spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome (STLS) presents a diagnostic challenge when it occurs in patients with advanced solid malignancies and concurrent critical illness. We present a case of STLS in a 30-year-old man with refractory metastatic esophageal adenocarcinoma who presented with hypotension, anuria, and severe metabolic derangements. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated hyperuricemia (18.1 mg/dL), hyperkalemia (7.6 mmol/L), hyperphosphatemia (7.8 mg/dL), and acute kidney injury. Ionized calcium was also low at 1.03 mmol/L despite hypoalbuminemia, with laboratory and clinical findings consistent with TLS by Cairo-Bishop thresholds. His final treatment was initiated 19 days before presentation, with the continuous fluorouracil infusion completed approximately 17 days before presentation, placing the presentation well outside the conventional treatment-related timeframe. His course was complicated by septic shock secondary to methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia. Despite supportive care and rasburicase administration, he developed multiorgan failure and was transitioned to hospice. This case highlights the rare occurrence of spontaneous TLS in metastatic esophageal adenocarcinoma and emphasizes the importance of early recognition and consideration in any patient with high tumor burden.

42844600.title: Acute kidney injury at a tertiary nephrology referral center: predictors of renal recovery and in-hospital mortality.
42844600.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a global health problem associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite advances in prevention and management, in-hospital mortality remains high, particularly among critically ill patients. To determine incidence, risk factors of AKI among patients admitted to Mansoura Nephrology and Dialysis Unit (MNDU), a tertiary nephrology referral center in Dakahlia governorate, Egypt, over one year, and to identify predictors of renal recovery at discharge and in-hospital mortality. This prospective observational study was conducted from June 2022 to May 2023 and included adult patients admitted with various kidney disorders. Patients were classified into AKI and non-AKI groups according to KDIGO 2012 criteria. Clinical, laboratory, and outcome data were analyzed, and multivariable regression analyses were used to identify independent predictors of in-hospital mortality and renal recovery after AKI. A total of 839 patients were enrolled, including 330 (39.3%) with AKI and 509 (60.7%) without AKI. The most common pathophysiological causes of AKI were pre-renal (54.2%) followed by intrinsic renal (38.5%) one. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in AKI than non-AKI group (17.3% vs. 3.8%), with septic shock being the leading cause of death (84.2%). Among patients with AKI, 45.2% achieved complete renal recovery, 21.8% had partial recovery, and 33.0% had no recovery at discharge. On multivariable logistic regression analyses, KDIGO Stage 3 AKI (adjusted OR 0.277, P = 0.046), kidney replacement therapy (adjusted OR 0.409, P = 0.004), and requirement of vasopressor therapy (adjusted OR 0.041, P < 0.001) were independently associated with lower odds of renal recovery, whereas necessity of vasopressor therapy emerged as the only independent predictor of in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 420.511, 95% CI 97.451-1814.543; P < 0.001). AKI was common among hospitalized patients and was associated with substantially increased in-hospital mortality. Vasopressor requirement was the strongest independent predictor of mortality, emphasizing the prognostic impact of hemodynamic instability and critical illness severity. Severe AKI (KDIGO Stage 3), kidney replacement therapy, and vasopressor necessity were independently associated with reduced renal recovery at discharge. These readily available clinical indicators may support early risk stratification and guide closer monitoring of high-risk patients.

42829648.title: VISTA Confers Renal Protection in Murine Hemorrhage/Infection-Induced Acute Kidney Injury: Associations with Altered NGAL and HMGB1 Expression.
42829648.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) represents a serious complication associated with both short- and long-term morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients. Severe trauma complicated by infection represents a high‑risk clinical trigger for AKI. V‑domain immunoglobulin suppressor of T‑cell activation (VISTA) is an immune‑checkpoint molecule with immunomodulatory functions, yet its role in trauma‑sepsis‑induced AKI remains incompletely defined. In this experimental study, male wild‑type (WT) and VISTA‑deficient (VISTA-/-) C57BL/6 mice were utilized to establish a two‑hit murine AKI model combining hemorrhagic shock and cecal ligation and puncture (Hem/CLP). Blood and kidney tissues were collected 24 hours after hemorrhage/CLP. VISTA expression on neutrophils and monocytes in peripheral blood was assessed by flow cytometry. Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen were measured according to manufacturer protocols. Cytokine levels were determined by ELISA, and corresponding mRNA expression was analyzed via RT-PCR. Kidney injury severity was evaluated histologically by pathologists. Protein levels of neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and high mobility group box 1 were examined by Western blot. VISTA expression was significantly elevated on circulating neutrophils and monocytes following injury (all p < 0.05). Histopathological assessment revealed aggravated kidney injury in the AKI model (p = 0.0056), which was further exacerbated in VISTA-deficient mice (p = 0.0357). Consistent with this, serum creatinine (p = 0.014) and blood urea nitrogen (p = 0.005) levels were markedly higher in VISTA-deficient mice compared to controls. Pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 (p = 0.0335) and TNF-α (p = 0.0283) were increased in AKI mice and further elevated in VISTA-deficient mice (p = 0.0014 and 0.0001, respectively), whereas anti-inflammatory IL-10 showed a converse trend (p = 0.0056 and 0.0019, respectively). RT-PCR confirmed corresponding changes in cytokine mRNA expression. Western blot analysis indicated decreased neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (p < 0.0001) and increased high mobility group box 1 protein (p = 0.0009) levels in VISTA-deficient mice. Collectively, our results demonstrate that VISTA‑deficient mice develop more severe early‑phase hemorrhage/sepsis‑induced AKI. Altered NGAL and HMGB1 protein expression occur in parallel with VISTA‑associated renal protection; further functional validation is required to establish causal mechanistic relationships and to evaluate the translational potential of VISTA‑targeted approaches.

42952822.title: Landmark-specific phenotypic heterogeneity in CRRT discontinuation timing: a multi-landmark target trial emulation using MIMIC-IV.
42952822.abstract: The optimal timing for discontinuing continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) in critically ill patients remains uncertain. Observational studies commonly simplify discontinuation timing into "early" vs. "delayed" categories, yet the same label may correspond to different clinical states at different stages of illness. We evaluated whether the clinical meaning of the early-discontinuation label and its association with 30-day mortality varied across landmarks and analytic frameworks. Using MIMIC-IV (2008-2019), we emulated a target trial among adults who were alive and still receiving CRRT 48 h after initiation. Early discontinuation was defined as stopping CRRT within 24 h after the 48-hour landmark, whereas delayed discontinuation was defined as continuing CRRT beyond 24 h. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Analyses included crude Cox regression, baseline IPTW-Cox, multi-landmark analyses at 48, 72, 96, and 120 h, a marginal structural model (MSM) using time-varying IPTW, and clone-censor-weighting (CCW) with stabilized censoring weights under a 24-hour grace period. Phenotype decomposition was also performed to assess the clinical composition of patients classified as having early discontinuation at different landmarks. A total of 1,432 patients were included, of whom 369 (25.8%) met the definition of early discontinuation. Baseline IPTW-Cox suggested that early discontinuation was associated with higher 30-day mortality (HR 1.36, 95% CI 1.13-1.64; P = 0.001). Multi-landmark HRs ranged from 1.13 to 1.35 without a monotonic pattern; precision decreased at later landmarks, and the landmark-by-exposure interaction was not statistically significant. The MSM estimate was OR 1.16 (95% CI 0.82-1.63; P = 0.40), and the revised CCW estimate was HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.91-1.28; P = 0.38). Phenotype decomposition showed that sepsis prevalence increased from 55.6% at 48 h to 69.1% at 120 h, baseline vasopressor exposure increased from 55.8% to 71.9%, and urine output decreased from 818 mL to 524 mL. Baseline IPTW generated a significant signal suggesting harm from early CRRT discontinuation, but this was not reproduced in multi-landmark, MSM, or CCW analyses. Phenotype decomposition indicated that "early weaning" captures different clinical profiles at different time points rather than a stable, homogeneous exposure. Observational CRRT weaning studies should consider dynamic treatment strategies, time-varying causal methods, and clinically grounded outcome definitions.

42945221.title: SIRT5 deficiency exacerbates sepsis acute renal injury by activating ACSL4/FTH1 axis dependent ferroptosis.
42945221.abstract: Sepsis‑associated acute kidney injury (S‑AKI) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients, yet effective targeted therapies remain lacking due to an incomplete understanding of its pathogenesis. Ferroptosis, an iron‑dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has recently been implicated in AKI, but the upstream regulators of this process in sepsis remain undefined. Here, we identify SIRT5, a mitochondrial NAD ⁺ ‑dependent desuccinylase, as a critical endogenous suppressor of ferroptosis in S‑AKI. Using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) murine model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)‑stimulated HK‑2 proximal tubular cells, we show that SIRT5 expression is significantly downregulated in septic kidney injury. Renal tubular‑specific ablation of Sirt5 exacerbated CLP‑induced renal dysfunction, structural damage, and tubular cell death, whereas AAV9‑mediated SIRT5 overexpression attenuated these pathological changes. Mechanistically, SIRT5 deficiency tipped the balance of the ACSL4/FTH1 axis toward ferroptosis: it increased ACSL4‑dependent membrane lipid remodeling and reduced FTH1‑mediated iron sequestration, accompanied by suppression of the antioxidant enzyme GPX4. Consequently, lipid peroxidation, iron overload, and mitochondrial damage were markedly amplified. Notably, knockdown of ACSL4 in SIRT5‑deficient HK‑2 cells effectively reversed lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, and cell death, establishing ACSL4 as a key downstream effector of SIRT5‑mediated ferroptosis suppression. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized SIRT5-ACSL4/FTH1 regulatory axis that governs ferroptotic susceptibility in renal tubular cells during sepsis, and suggest that pharmacological restoration of SIRT5 activity or blockade of ACSL4‑driven ferroptosis may offer novel therapeutic avenues for S‑AKI.

42941541.title: oXiris-Based Blood Purification Efficacy in Adults with Septic Shock and Acute Kidney Injury: The PURE Multicenter Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
42941541.abstract: Background/Objectives: Randomized evidence for the oXiris adsorptive membrane in septic shock remains limited. We estimated its effect on 28-day mortality and explored short-term physiologic outcomes in adults with septic shock and acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy. Methods: PURE was a multicenter, single-blind, parallel-group pilot randomized trial in Saudi Arabia. Participants were randomized 1:1 to oXiris-based or conventional continuous venovenous hemodialysis. The primary comparison used unadjusted mortality risk estimates. Secondary observations were summarized descriptively; adjusted and post-hoc Bayesian sensitivity analyses are reported in the main text and supplement. Results: Of 204 randomized participants, 202 were analyzed (oXiris, 100; control, 102). Twenty-eight-day mortality was 39.0% (39/100) versus 47.1% (48/102), respectively (risk ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.60-1.14; risk difference, -8.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -21.7 to 5.6; p = 0.247). Reported 72 h norepinephrine dose, lactate, C-reactive protein, and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score were lower with oXiris; reported intensive care unit (ICU) stay was also shorter. Secondary descriptive observations are limited by unverifiable time-specific denominators and handling of intercurrent events. Premature filter clotting was reported in 8/100 versus 7/102 participants; no device-related adverse events were reported, but safety ascertainment was limited. Conclusions: This pilot trial did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in 28-day mortality, although mortality was numerically lower in the oXiris group. Consistent protocol implementation and encouraging, hypothesis-generating physiologic observations provide a foundation for a definitive trial with complete longitudinal ascertainment.

42934835.title: Circulating NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation Is Associated With Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury and Disease Severity: A Prospective Pilot Study.
42934835.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is a severe and prevalent complication in critically ill patients, characterized by high mortality and a lack of reliable biomarkers that reflect inflammatory pathway activation and disease severity. Although the NLRP3 inflammasome is known to mediate inflammatory responses, pyroptosis, and renal injury, its clinical relevance in human SA-AKI remains poorly defined. This study aimed to characterize the expression profiles, dynamic trajectories, and clinical associations of circulating NLRP3 inflammasome components in patients with SA-AKI. Thirty adult patients with sepsis (13 with SA-AKI and 17 without AKI) were prospectively and consecutively enrolled. Sepsis was defined according to the Sepsis-3 consensus criteria, whereas AKI was diagnosed and staged exclusively using the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Serum protein levels of NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, cleaved caspase-1, IL-1β, and IL-18, and transcript levels of NLRP3, ASC, and caspase-1, were determined on days 1, 3, 5, and 7 after enrollment using ELISA and quantitative real-time PCR. Statistical analyses included group comparisons, Spearman rank correlations, linear mixed-effects models, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses to assess concurrent group discrimination. Because samples were collected post-classification, these analyses describe post-diagnostic expression kinetics rather than prediction of future AKI onset. The expression of NLRP3 inflammasome-related molecules was significantly upregulated in the SA-AKI group and correlated with renal dysfunction and elevated illness-severity scores (SOFA and APACHE II).
