Exploratory ROC analyses suggested strong discrimination of concurrent AKI status for ASC, caspase-1, and NLRP3 transcript levels, with the strongest overall performance observed on day 3. These estimates are hypothesis-generating because of the small sample size and post-classification sampling. The NLRP3 inflammasome pathway is prominently activated in patients with SA-AKI and is closely associated with renal dysfunction and systemic illness severity. Circulating components of this pathway are candidate biomarkers of concurrent SA-AKI, but their ability to predict AKI onset or prognosis requires validation in larger prospective cohorts sampled before AKI develops.

42928790.title: Factors Associated with Early Sepsis-Associated Liver Injury and Predictors of 30-Day Mortality: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
42928790.abstract: Sepsis-associated liver injury (SALI) is associated with higher mortality, but the factors associated with early SALI and the determinants of mortality in patients with SALI remain incompletely understood. This retrospective cohort study included 524 consecutive patients with sepsis (Sepsis-3) in a tertiary intensive care unit (ICU). SALI was defined as total bilirubin ≥2 mg/dL with international normalized ratio ≥1.5, or alanine aminotransferase ≥68 U/L (twice the local upper limit of normal), within 24 hours of ICU admission. Factors independently associated with SALI and with 30-day mortality in SALI were identified by logistic regression after multiple imputation and elastic-net selection, with bootstrap internal validation. Of 523 evaluable patients, 135 (25.8%) met the SALI definition, and their 30-day mortality was higher (63.4% vs 50.0%, p=0.010). Factors independently associated with SALI were macrophage activation-like syndrome (MALS) (aOR: 5.33), an abdominal focus (aOR: 4.03), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) score ≥5 (aOR: 3.07), acute kidney injury on admission (aOR: 2.29) and log-ferritin (aOR: 1.31; 1.48 without MALS and DIC) (all p<0.05; optimism-corrected area under the curve [AUC]: 0.770). Among patients with SALI, immunosuppressive therapy (OR: 8.13), a thoracic focus (OR: 8.62), log-ferritin (OR: 2.04) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) (OR: 1.08 per second) were independently associated with 30-day mortality (all p<0.05); appropriate antibiotic therapy showed a non-significant protective trend (p=0.076). The mortality model showed good discrimination (optimism-corrected AUC: 0.857) but limited calibration (slope: 0.562). SALI was associated with higher 30-day mortality in sepsis. Because the factors associated with SALI were assessed concurrently with liver injury, they describe its clinical profile rather than predict its development. Immunosuppressive therapy, a thoracic focus, higher ferritin levels and prolonged aPTT were associated with 30-day mortality in SALI. These findings should be interpreted with caution and require external validation.

42909947.title: Baseline and 7-Day Dynamic Changes of T Helper 17/Regulatory T Cells Ratio and Their Association with Renal Recovery and Prognosis in Sepsis-Induced Acute Kidney Injury: An Exploratory Analysis.
42909947.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SAKI) is a serious complication with high mortality. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between T helper 17 (Th17)/regulatory T cells (Treg) immune imbalance and renal function recovery in patients with SAKI, with a novel focus on evaluating both baseline and early dynamic changes as exploratory biomarkers for renal recovery and overall prognosis. Sixty adult patients with SAKI admitted to the intensive care unit were enrolled and followed for 28 days. Based on renal recovery, patients were stratified into recovery and non-recovery groups, with further subgroup analysis. Clinical data and blood samples were collected serially. Renal recovery occurred in 42 patients (70%). Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) stage 3, a higher baseline Th17/Treg ratio (time zero [D0]) and a greater decrease in this ratio over 7 days (Δ7) demonstrated potential statistical correlations with non-recovery. The D0 ratio differentiated non-recovery with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.804 (cut-off >0.31128), and the Δ7 ratio (reflecting early immune trajectories during the first week) with an AUC of 0.762 (cut-off <-0.2055). A low baseline ratio with a high Δ7 was associated with early, complete recovery. A D0 ratio >0.31128 or a Δ7 ratio <-0.2055 was retrospectively observed to correlate with significantly higher 28-day mortality (60.0% vs 40.0%, p<0.05). The discriminative efficacy of D0 and Δ7 Th17/Treg ratios was comparable to KDIGO staging for renal non-recovery in patients with SAKI. Baseline and early dynamic Th17/Treg measures showed an observational trend with renal non-recovery in this single-centre prospective cohort of patients with SAKI. However, this study is limited by its small sample size and observational design. These exploratory findings, including the data-derived thresholds, require validation in larger cohorts with prespecified temporal analysis before clinical application.

42900653.title: When Insulin Must Wait: The Role of Renal Replacement Therapy in Refractory Hypokalemia During Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis.
42900653.journal: The American journal of case reports
42900653.abstract: BACKGROUND Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a common life-threatening metabolic emergency characterized by hyperglycemia, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and ketosis. Severe hypokalemia before insulin therapy is uncommon but may complicate management and delay treatment. CASE REPORT A 37-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of generalized abdominal pain and progressive shortness of breath. He was drowsy and tachypneic, with Kussmaul respirations. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe DKA, acute kidney injury, and severe hypokalemia. Insulin therapy was initially withheld according to the DKA protocol. Intravenous potassium supplementation failed to achieve sustained correction, resulting in repeated interruptions of insulin therapy. Due to refractory hypokalemia, an emergency 2-hour session of intermittent hemodialysis was performed, followed by continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). During CRRT, serum potassium increased, serum creatinine decreased, metabolic acidosis improved, and the anion gap closed. Insulin therapy was resumed without further interruption. However, the clinical course was complicated by severe septic shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and catastrophic intracerebral hemorrhage, ultimately resulting in death. CONCLUSIONS Severe hypokalemia at presentation in DKA poses a critical therapeutic challenge because insulin therapy must be withheld until the electrolyte abnormality is corrected. In rare cases of refractory hypokalemia, CRRT may serve as an adjunctive strategy to facilitate metabolic stabilization and safe DKA management. This case adds to the limited literature and highlights the need for further studies to clarify the role and effectiveness of this approach. Biochemical resolution of DKA may not correspond to clinical recovery, and critically ill patients warrant continuous monitoring.

42898682.title: Precision fluid therapy in sepsis: fluid responsiveness vs. fluid tolerance.
42898682.abstract: Intravenous fluid is the most frequently administered drug in septic shock and one of the least precisely dosed. Two decades of trials have progressively dismantled the assumption that more fluid is better: protocolized early goal-directed therapy failed to improve on contemporary usual care, high-volume bolus protocols caused frank harm where organ support was limited, and restrictive strategies applied after an initial resuscitation have proven neutral rather than superior. What has replaced a universal volume prescription is a pair of questions that must be asked separately for each patient and repeated over time: will this patient's cardiac output actually rise with more fluid (fluid responsiveness), and can the lungs, kidneys, and venous system absorb that volume without harm (fluid tolerance)? This narrative review examines how to answer both questions in the modern intensive care unit. We ground the discussion in Guytonian venous return physiology and in the revised Starling model, in which sepsis-induced glycocalyx degradation makes infused crystalloid a short-acting drug with a cumulative side-effect profile. Using an index case of a mechanically ventilated patient with pneumococcal septic shock, atrial fibrillation, lung-protective tidal volumes, obesity, and acute kidney injury, we show why the two most widely used bedside indices, respiratory variation in inferior vena cava diameter and pulse pressure variation, are physiologically invalid in precisely the patients in whom the fluid decision is hardest, and why maintenance infusions and fluid creep deserve the same scrutiny as boluses. We make the case for direct stroke volume measurement paired with a reversible dynamic challenge, most commonly a passive leg raise, as the one approach that remains interpretable across arrhythmia, low tidal volume, spontaneous respiratory effort, and elevated intra-abdominal pressure, and we discuss dynamic arterial elastance as a complementary tool for predicting whether arterial pressure will follow flow. We review the outcome evidence, including the FRESH trial and supporting meta-analyses, the emerging literature on sepsis endotypes and subphenotypes, and the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign recommendations. Finally, we address fluid tolerance and de-resuscitation, where venous congestion assessment and lung ultrasound are increasingly used, and outline where the evidence remains thin.

42895663.title: Association Between Albumin-Bilirubin Index and Clinical Outcomes in Septic Acute Kidney Injury Patients.
42895663.abstract: BackgroundThe albumin-bilirubin index (ALBI) has been reported as a prognostic marker in various clinical conditions; however, its value in patients with septic acute kidney injury (AKI) has not been clearly evaluated. This study aimed to investigate the association between ALBI and clinical outcomes in this population.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. ALBI was analyzed as both a continuous variable in the primary analysis and a categorical variable according to tertiles in sensitivity analysis. The primary outcomes were 28-day, 60-day, 90-day, and 1-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) transfer, septic shock, and disease severity. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between ALBI and mortality, and restricted cubic spline analyses were performed to assess potential nonlinearity. Subgroup analyses were further conducted to examine the consistency across different sub-group populations.ResultsOverall, 6700 patients with septic AKI were included. In adjusted Cox models, each 1-standard deviation increase in ALBI was associated with higher risks of 28-day mortality (HR 1.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.10-1.22), 60-day mortality (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.10-1.19), 90-day mortality (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.08-1.18), and 1-year mortality (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.14). The association between ALBI and mortality was generally consistent across most prespecified subgroups. Higher ALBI was also linked with septic shock (odds ratio [OR] 1.15, 95%CI 1.08-1.21, P < .001), ICU transfer (OR 1.09, 95%CI 1.02-1.16), and greater disease severity. RCS curves showed a nonlinear increase in mortality risk with ascending ALBI. Sensitivity analyses based on ALBI tertiles yielded broadly consistent findings.ConclusionHigher ALBI was independently associated with increased short- and long-term mortality and adverse clinical outcomes in septic AKI patients.

42888582.title: Association of baseline non-severe anemia with clinical outcomes following the first recorded diagnosis of systemic sclerosis: A matched cohort study.
42888582.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the highest mortality among systemic autoimmune diseases, yet the prognostic significance of anemia around the time of the first recorded SSc diagnosis is unclear. We examined whether baseline anemia is associated with early mortality and complications. This retrospective matched cohort study identified female adults with a first recorded SSc diagnosis between January 2010 and December 2024 from the TriNetX Research Network. Patients were required to have at least 5 years of pre-index observation without a documented SSc diagnosis. The network comprised 140 healthcare organizations, with approximately 70% of patients in the United States across all 9 census regions and 30% at international sites. Anemia was defined as hemoglobin (Hb) ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL and non-anemia as ≥12.0 g/dL, measured within ±30 days of diagnosis. For the Hb-stratified analysis, the anemia cohort was categorized as Hb ≥10.0 to <12.0 g/dL or ≥8.0 to <10.0 g/dL. One-to-one propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, and Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality during days 31 to 365 among patients surviving the 30-day landmark period; secondary outcomes were sepsis, acute kidney injury, intensive care unit admission, pulmonary fibrosis, and elevated C-reactive protein (≥10 mg/L). After matching, 5410 patients remained in each cohort. Baseline anemia was significantly associated with higher 1-year mortality (HR, 2.54; 95% CI, 1.99-3.22; P < .001) and with increased risks of sepsis (HR, 3.20; 95% CI, 2.38-4.30), acute kidney injury (HR, 2.24; 95% CI, 1.80-2.78), intensive care unit admission (HR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.47-2.51), and elevated C-reactive protein (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.37-1.74; all P < .001); no significant association was observed for pulmonary fibrosis (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.96-1.17; P = .229). Associations persisted in sensitivity analyses and over 3-year follow-up. Mortality risk showed a graded pattern across Hb strata (Hb ≥10.0-<12.0 g/dL: HR, 1.66; Hb ≥8.0-<10.0 g/dL: HR, 3.33). Baseline anemia was associated with increased mortality and acute systemic complications following the first recorded SSc diagnosis; these observational findings warrant prospective validation.

42883699.title: Flow Cytometry and AI-Driven Biomarker Discovery in Acute Kidney Injury: From Mechanistic Insights to Translation Applications in Clinical and Austere Environments.
42883699.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a complex and multifactorial syndrome characterized by the rapid decline of renal function following ischemic, septic, traumatic, hypoxic, or nephrotoxic insults. Despite advances in critical care, exacerbation of AKI is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, progression to chronic kidney disease (CKD) and multiorgan dysfunction. Current therapies remain largely supportive and do not directly target the molecular pathways driving AKI, underscoring the need for mechanism-based diagnostics and precision-guided therapeutic strategies. Accumulating evidence supports that AKI is driven by mechanistic crosstalk among cellular injury pathways involving mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, endothelial damage, immune dysregulation, and regulated cell death. Flow cytometry has emerged as a powerful platform for high-dimensional single-cell and extracellular vesicle analysis, enabling comprehensive assessment of immune cell phenotypes, platelet activation, endothelial alterations, mitochondrial dysfunction, and circulating extracellular vesicles associated with AKI. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and emerging explainable AI (XAI) enhance the ability to identify clinically relevant patterns from complex datasets. This review aims to integrate AKI pathophysiology with flow cytometry-based biomarker discovery and AI-enabled analytical approaches. We discuss translational applications in AKI-relevant clinical settings, including trauma, hemorrhagic shock, sepsis, and radiation-combined injury, with particular emphasis on Prolonged Casualty Care and other austere environments, where rapid, mechanism-based diagnostics are critically needed.

42882158.title: Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Optimization and Therapeutic Drug Monitoring of Beta-Lactam Antibiotics in Abdominal Sepsis: Current Evidence, Challenges, and Clinical Perspectives-A Narrative Review.
42882158.abstract: Background: Abdominal sepsis is associated with profound pharmacokinetic (PK) alterations that make standard beta-lactam dosing regimens potentially inadequate in critically ill patients. Increased volume of distribution, hypoalbuminemia, augmented renal clearance (ARC), acute kidney injury (AKI) and the PK complexity of the peritoneal compartment collectively impair the ability of conventional dosing to achieve pharmacodynamic (PD) targets. These PK derangements are clinically relevant but incompletely characterized in intra-abdominal infections (IAI)- specific cohorts, as most available data derive from broader critically ill populations. Beta-lactam antibiotics, the cornerstone therapy in IAIs, are particularly susceptible to these alterations, especially in the context of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens. Methods: We conducted a structured narrative review of the literature published between 2010 and 2026, searching PubMed and Embase using terms related to pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, therapeutic drug monitoring, beta-lactam antibiotics, abdominal sepsis, and intra-abdominal infection in critically ill patients. Additional references were identified through manual bibliography screening, including seminal studies predating the search window. No formal systematic review methodology was applied. Results: PK/PD optimization in abdominal sepsis can be organized around four proposed domains: extended or continuous infusion of beta-lactams to maximize the time above the minimum inhibitory concentration; therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) to guide individualized dose adjustment in the presence of ARC, AKI, or continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT); tailored dose optimization during CRRT; and target attainment analysis against MDR organisms. Extended and continuous infusions improve PD target attainment and are associated with improved outcomes in some observational studies, although prospective IAI-specific evidence is lacking and the evidence supporting these strategies derives largely from broader intensive care unit populations. Conclusions: In abdominal sepsis, integrating PK/PD principles and TDM-guided dosing represents a pharmacologically rational strategy to optimize beta-lactam exposure and improve target attainment against MDR pathogens. Rigorous IAI-specific prospective studies are needed to establish definitive TDM-guided dosing protocols and translate these pharmacological strategies in this high-acuity setting.

42964914.title: When Hydronephrosis Was Not Physiological: A Case of Septic Shock Secondary to Obstructive Uropathy in Pregnancy.
42964914.abstract: Urosepsis in pregnancy is a life-threatening condition requiring early recognition, rapid multidisciplinary escalation and timely source control. Physiological hydronephrosis is common during pregnancy and may obscure clinically significant urinary tract obstruction. We report a 26-year-old gravida 5 para 3 woman at 30 weeks' gestation who presented with severe right-sided loin pain. Initial ultrasound demonstrated moderate right hydronephrosis without a visible calculus. Within hours, she deteriorated with pyrexia, acute kidney injury, lactic acidosis and septic shock. Computed tomography demonstrated high-grade obstruction of the right renal collecting system secondary to a ureteropelvic junction calculus with associated inflammatory change. Following maternal deterioration and evidence of foetal compromise, an urgent multidisciplinary decision was made to proceed with category 1 caesarean delivery followed by cystoscopy and right ureteric stent insertion. Cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae. The patient subsequently required intensive care support including invasive ventilation, vasopressors, renal replacement therapy and treatment for disseminated intravascular coagulation. Both maternal and neonatal outcomes were favourable. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing physiological hydronephrosis from pathological obstruction in pregnancy and emphasises the importance of source control in infected obstructive uropathy.

42964288.title: Development and validation of a prognostic prediction model for elderly patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury based on interpretable machine learning.
42964288.abstract: Elderly patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) have high short-term mortality; early identification of high-risk individuals is critical for personalized intervention. Traditional clinical scoring systems relying on linear assumptions and conventional machine learning models often lack interpretability, hindering translation to clinical practice. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable prognostic model for 28-day in-hospital mortality in elderly SA-AKI using routinely available clinical variables. Clinical data of 11,468 elderly SA-AKI patients were retrospectively extracted from the MIMIC-IV database and divided into training and internal test sets at a 7:3 ratio using stratified random sampling. A dual feature selection strategy combining LASSO regression and random forest was applied. Five machine learning models-decision tree, logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost-were constructed in parallel. Model discrimination and calibration were evaluated by AUC, Brier score, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. External independent validation was performed using a clinical cohort of 257 patients from the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University. The SHAP method was used for global and individual-level interpretability of the optimal model. Dual feature selection identified 10 independent predictors: age, weight, red blood cell distribution width, arterial partial pressure of oxygen, blood lactate, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, blood urea nitrogen, serum creatinine, and respiratory rate. Among the five models, XGBoost demonstrated the best performance, with training AUC 0.9898 (accuracy 0.9472) and external validation AUC 0.9156 (accuracy 0.8560), indicating strong generalizability. SHAP global importance ranking showed age as the primary driver, followed by serum creatinine and arterial partial pressure of oxygen. Each core feature exhibited a nonlinear association with 28-day mortality risk, with clear model-derived risk inflection points rather than clinical intervention thresholds. The XGBoost-based interpretable model exhibits excellent discriminative performance and robust external generalizability for predicting 28-day mortality in elderly SA-AKI. The SHAP attribution framework renders model decisions transparent, providing quantitative evidence-based support for early risk stratification and hypothesis generation for individualized organ-protective strategies in the ICU.

42847974.title: Age-Based Preoperative Transthoracic Echocardiography, Intraoperative Hypotension, and Postoperative Outcomes in Older Adults Undergoing Noncardiac Surgery: A Regression Discontinuity Analysis.
42847974.abstract: The clinical value of routine preoperative transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) in older adults remains controversial. Existing evidence is largely observational and vulnerable to confounding by indication, limiting causal interpretation of whether preoperative TTE improves intraoperative management and perioperative outcomes. We aimed to evaluate the local effect of routine age-based preoperative TTE using a quasi-experimental design. This single-center retrospective cohort study used a fuzzy regression discontinuity design based on an institutional policy of routine preoperative TTE in patients aged ≥75 years. Eligible patients were aged 60 to 89 years and underwent elective noncardiac surgery under general anesthesia from July 2017 to August 2024. To minimize confounding by indication, patients with guideline-based indications or other clinical conditions likely to prompt preoperative TTE independent of age were excluded. The primary outcome was intraoperative hypotension (IOH), defined as the duration of mean arterial pressure <65 mm Hg. Exploratory secondary outcomes included 30- and 90-day mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), planned and unplanned intensive care unit (ICU) or cardiac care unit (CCU) admission, and postoperative length of hospital stay. Continuity of baseline characteristics and density of the running variable were assessed. Among 7270 patients, the probability of undergoing preoperative TTE increased by 43.1 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], 33.3-52.9) at the 75-year-old cutoff, confirming a strong first-stage discontinuity. The estimated local effect of preoperative TTE on IOH was a 24.8-minute reduction (95% CI, -71.1 to 21.5). Sensitivity analyses using alternative bandwidths and covariate adjustment yielded similar findings. Point estimates for 30-day mortality (-2.1%; 95% CI, -6.0 to 1.8), 90-day mortality (-3.2%; 95% CI, -10.4 to 3.9), and AKI (-3.6%; 95% CI, -15.9 to 8.6) were below zero but imprecise. Point estimates were also below zero for unplanned ICU or CCU admission (-6.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -12.2 to 0.2) and postoperative length of hospital stay (-7.0 days; 95% CI, -14.6 to 0.5). Baseline characteristics and the density of the running variable (age) showed no clear discontinuity at the cutoff. Using a quasi-experimental design that reduces susceptibility to confounding by indication, we found no clear evidence that routine age-based preoperative TTE reduced IOH or improved postoperative outcomes near the threshold. The estimates were imprecise, and clinically meaningful benefit or harm could not be excluded. These findings suggest that age alone may be insufficient to justify routine preoperative TTE and support further evaluation of selective risk-based strategies.

42846417.title: Early adjunctive vasopressin was not associated with a lower 7-day risk of renal replacement therapy in norepinephrine-treated patients with cirrhosis: a target-trial-informed study with external replication.
42846417.abstract: Early adjunctive vasopressin can reduce catecholamine exposure in vasodilatory shock, but whether it prevents severe kidney failure in norepinephrine-treated patients with cirrhosis is uncertain. We conducted a target-trial-informed landmark study using MIMIC-IV as the primary cohort and eICU-CRD as an external replication cohort. Adults with a first intensive care unit admission, cirrhosis or advanced chronic liver disease, and norepinephrine initiation within 24 h of admission were eligible. Treatment was classified at a 6-h landmark as vasopressin initiated within 6 h of norepinephrine or no vasopressin during that window; patients in the latter group could receive vasopressin later. The primary outcome was new renal replacement therapy (RRT) between the landmark and day 7. Propensity-score overlap weighting was prespecified as the primary analysis. The MIMIC-IV cohort included 1,086 patients (early vasopressin, n = 295; no early vasopressin, n = 791), and the eICU-CRD cohort included 356 patients (n = 91 and n = 265, respectively). Before weighting, vasopressin recipients had greater shock and liver-disease severity. Early vasopressin was not associated with lower odds of new RRT in MIMIC-IV (overlap-weighted odds ratio [OR] 1.37, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.83-2.26; P = 0.214), eICU-CRD (OR 1.10, 95% CI 0.45-2.69; P = 0.833), or the pooled analysis (OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.84-2.01; P = 0.235). Mortality was higher among early-vasopressin recipients, but this secondary association remained highly vulnerable to confounding by indication. Weighted absolute-risk estimates, cumulative RRT incidence, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses provided no supporting renal-benefit signal; creatinine trajectories were evaluated descriptively because follow-up measurements were susceptible to survivor selection. Among norepinephrine-treated patients with cirrhosis or advanced chronic liver disease who were alive and RRT-free 6 h after norepinephrine initiation, early adjunctive vasopressin was not associated with less RRT by day 7. The findings do not challenge vasopressin use for hemodynamic support when clinically indicated, but do not support early initiation solely as a renal-protective strategy.

42912570.title: Serum ammonia improves early risk stratification beyond West Haven criteria in acute liver failure.
42912570.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
authors: US Acute Liver Failure Study Group
42912570.abstract: The prognosis of patients with acute liver failure (ALF) presenting with low grade hepatic encephalopathy (HE) defined by the West Haven criteria (WHC) is difficult to establish. We studied the association between HE severity, assessed by WHC and serum ammonia, with outcomes across different age groups. Retrospective analysis of the prospective multicentre United States ALF Study Group registry (2000-2016). Exposures were WHC and serum ammonia on day 1 post inclusion. Endpoints were transplant-free survival (TFS) and mortality due to cerebral events on day 21. Findings were validated in a different and more recent (2010-2023) European cohort. Among 1092 patients, median age was 39 years and 526 (48.2%) had acetaminophen toxicity. On day 1, 968 (88.6%) patients were in the intensive care unit and 669 (61.3%) were receiving any specific organ support (ventilation vasopressors, or renal replacement therapy). TFS and cerebral mortality on day 21 were 45.2% and 6.3%, respectively. Patients with hyperammonemia (≥50 µmol/L) on day 1 had lower TFS on day 21 than others, both for WHC grades 1-2 (53.0% vs. 65.2%) and 3-4 (31.8% vs. 60.9%). Higher ammonia on day 1 was independently associated with lower TFS on day 21, irrespective of WHC grade (odds ratio of 0.958 per each 10 µmol/L increment). Ammonia on day 1 of ≥100 µmol/L showed a significant threshold effect for TFS or cerebral mortality on day 21. Patients with <40 years had the highest probability of cerebral mortality on day 21. In ALF, serum ammonia may help to define HE and assess prognosis earlier, irrespective of WHC grade. Patients with early serum ammonia of ≥100 µmol/L require optimized monitoring and treatment.

42907145.title: Association of Iron Deficiency Anemia with Outcomes in Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Analysis.
42907145.abstract: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently have iron deficiency anemia (IDA), but the mechanism by which this condition affects clinical outcomes is not well understood. The purpose of this study was to assess whether IDA is associated with mortality in patients with AF. Data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) for 2021-2022 examined IDA and inpatient outcomes in a nationally representative cohort of hospitalized adults diagnosed with AF. Patients were categorized by IDA status. The factors assessed were mortality, hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, thromboembolic and cardiovascular complications, and overall hospital expenses. Hospital, clinical, and demographic factors were included in multivariable logistic and linear regression models. Of the 8.35 million AF hospitalizations, 7.1% had associated IDA. IDA was linked to multiple comorbidities along with increased risk of hypotension (OR: 1.15, 95% CI 1.12-1.17, P<0.001), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.25, 95% CI 1.23-1.27, P<0.001), and heart failure (Adjusted Odds Ratio [AOR]: 1.29, 95% CI 1.27-1.31, P<0.001). Ironically, IDA was linked independently to decreased risks of cardiac arrest (AOR: 0.70, 95% CI 0.66-0.73, P<0.001), transient ischemic attack (AOR: 0.58, 95% CI 0.53-0.63, P<0.001), stroke (OR: 0.49,95% CI 0.47-0.51, P<0.001), and in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.66, 95% CI 0.64-0.68, P<0.001). IDA was also associated with increased hospital expenses and increased LOS (P<0.001). IDA was linked to higher morbidity and healthcare use in those with AF admitted to the hospital, but there was a decrease in mortality and thromboembolic events. These results suggest the possibility of tailored iron therapy and imply a complex interaction between IDA and AF-related outcomes.

42902397.title: Crystalloid vs colloid for Hemodynamics during Anesthesia INduction in TAVR patients (CHAIN-T): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
42902397.abstract: To assess whether preload with colloids could reduce hypotension during induction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared to crystalloids. This study is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled trial conducted at Xijing Hospital. A total of 116 patients scheduled for elective TAVR under general anesthesia will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the colloid group or the crystalloid group, receiving either 5 ml/kg of colloid or crystalloid solution before anesthesia induction infused over 15 min. The primary outcome is the area under curve (AUC) of the change in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from baseline during the induction period (until 15 min after induction). Secondary outcomes include the incidence of intraoperative hemodynamic instability, the use of intraoperative vasoactive drugs, the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on the first postoperative day, postoperative hospital length of stay, the rate of intensive care unit (ICU) admission postoperatively, all-cause mortality during hospitalization and by 30 days after surgery, and the incidence of renal replacement therapy by 30 days after surgery. The results of this study will provide evidence on optimizing fluid preload to prevent hypotension during induction, reduce postoperative complications, and enhance recovery for patients undergoing TAVR. The findings are expected to promote anesthesia protocols in this patient population. The study protocol and statistical analysis plan were approved by the institutional Ethics Committee of Xijing Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University (XJLL-KY-20252560). The study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07329660) on December 29, 2025.

42960546.title: Artificial intelligence and continuous renal replacement therapy.
42960546.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is an important intervention in the treatment of acute kidney injury (AKI) in intensive care, and its application scope continues to expand alongside technological advancements and an increasing patient population. However, in current clinical practice, several factors, including individual patient differences, dynamic treatment needs, and the rational allocation of medical resources, pose challenges to CRRT implementation. The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) offers new approaches to address some of these challenges, and its applications in developing decision-support models, refining workflows, and supporting patient communication and education may contribute to more precise and efficient CRRT management. In this article, we discuss the current evidence and potential applications of AI in CRRT, as well as the challenges and strategies for clinical implementation, aiming to provide a reference for future research and clinical translation of AI-assisted CRRT.

42873453.title: Clinical validation of an intra-abdominal pressure monitoring system by comparison with pneumoperitoneum pressure.
42873453.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
42873453.abstract: In critically ill patients, intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) is associated with organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Acute kidney injury may occur early, since the kidney is particularly vulnerable to elevated intra-abdominal pressure (IAP). Accurate and timely measurement of IAP is essential for early detection of IAH and the initiation of appropriate therapeutic interventions. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess the accuracy of an IAP monitoring system compared to a reference standard, the CO2 insufflator, during laparoscopy. The second aim was to assess the changes in renal biomarker levels during and after increases in IAP through pneumoperitoneum. A prospective cohort study in patients undergoing laparoscopy at the University Medical Center Groningen. IAP measurements were performed with a urinary catheter using an IAP monitoring system (Accuryn® Monitoring System, Accuryn Medical) and compared to the pressure set at the CO2-insufflator system. Bland-Altman analysis was performed with accounting for repeated measures. Urine samples were collected at several time-points and Kidney Injury Molecule 1 (KIM-1), Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase 2 (TIMP-2), urinary Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin (NGAL), Liver-type Fatty Acid-Binding Protein (L-FABP), and albumin-creatinine ratio were measured. Between March 2025 and January 2026, 99 measurements were performed in 29 patients. One patient (3%) underwent hemicolectomy, and 28 patients underwent endometriosis surgery (97%). Analysis showed a bias of -1.4 mmHg (95% CI (-1.96 - (-0.82)) and limits of agreement of - 5.96 mmHg and 3.2 mmHg (95% CI -6.8-3.99) between the IAP monitoring system and the CO2-insufflators. The precision was 2.3 mmHg. The levels of renal biomarkers KIM-1, TIMP-2 and albumin/Cr ratio increased during laparoscopy compared to baseline, suggesting that relatively small IAP increases during laparoscopy have a subclinical effect on the kidney. The IAP monitoring system underestimated the IAP set by the CO2-insufflator by approximately 1 mmHg. The wide limits of agreement warrant cautious interpretation. Overall, the IAP monitoring system showed reasonable accuracy and precision. The increase of several renal biomarkers during laparoscopy compared to baseline may reflect a direct effect of elevated IAP on the kidney.

42871982.title: Early postoperative galectin-3 for risk stratification of delayed graft function after kidney transplantation.
42871982.abstract: Delayed graft function (DGF) is a major early complication after kidney transplantation. Galectin-3 (Gal3), a mediator of inflammation and fibrosis, is associated with renal injury, but its role in predicting DGF remains unclear. This study evaluated whether early postoperative Gal3 levels predict DGF and clinical outcomes. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult kidney transplant recipients from deceased donors (January 2021-December 2022). Gal3 was measured preoperatively, at intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and at ICU discharge. The primary outcome was DGF, defined as renal replacement therapy within 7 days. A base clinical model (age, cold ischemia time, creatinine at ICU admission) was compared with a Gal3-extended model, assessed by area under the curve (AUC), Brier score, calibration, bootstrap optimism correction, and categorical net reclassification improvement. Among 182 patients, 35 (19.2%) developed DGF. Gal3 at ICU admission was significantly higher in DGF patients (52.3 vs. 40.0 ng/ml, P < .001) and was independently associated with DGF (odds ratio per 5-ng/ml increase: 1.19; 95% confidence interval: 1.05-1.35; P = .008). Adding Gal3 modestly improved the AUC from 0.705 to 0.744 and the Brier score from 0.144 to 0.139. The Gal3-extended model retained superior discrimination after bootstrap correction. An exploratory prediction score demonstrated increasing DGF risk across score categories. Gal3 measured at ICU admission was independently associated with DGF and provided modest incremental risk-stratification value. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

42870968.title: Transaxillary access for ascending aortic and root surgery: a single-center comparison with full and partial sternotomy.
42870968.abstract: Minimally invasive approaches for ascending aortic and root surgery remain controversial regarding operative complexity and safety. The transaxillary (TAX) approach avoids sternotomy entirely but has not been compared with both full sternotomy (FS) and partial upper sternotomy [minimally invasive cardiac surgery (MIC)]. This study evaluates perioperative outcomes across these three access strategies. Between January 2022 and December 2025, 194 consecutive patients undergoing elective isolated ascending aortic or root surgery were retrospectively analyzed. Surgical access was FS (n=52), MIC (n=106), or TAX (n=36). TAX suitability was assessed by team consensus on electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated computed tomography (CT). Primary endpoints were in-hospital mortality, major complications [Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) composite], and hospital length of stay. TAX was compared with MIC after 1:2 propensity score matching. FS served as descriptive reference. FS patients had higher EuroSCORE II (median 2.7 vs. MIC 2.2 vs. TAX 2.3%, P=0.006). Cardiopulmonary bypass time was longer in TAX {196 [interquartile range (IQR): 175-239] vs. MIC 160 [138-192] vs. FS 172 [140-198] min, P<0.001}, while cross-clamp time did not differ (P=0.34). In-hospital mortality was 3.8% (FS), 0% (MIC), and 0% (TAX). Major complications occurred in 26.9%, 12.3%, and 8.3% (P=0.02), and acute kidney injury (AKI) in 28.8%, 8.5%, and 2.8% (P<0.001). One stroke occurred in the FS group. In the matched cohort (34 TAX vs. 68 MIC), bypass time remained longer in TAX {196 [175-240] vs. 160 [139-190] min, P<0.001}, whereas cross-clamp time, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital stay, major complications (5.9% vs. 11.8%), AKI (2.9% vs. 10.3%), atrial fibrillation, and wound complications did not differ significantly. TAX ascending aortic and root surgery was feasible in carefully selected patients, with no in-hospital mortality, no stroke, and no wound complications. In a propensity-matched comparison with partial upper sternotomy, early outcomes did not differ significantly despite longer bypass time. TAX extends the sternal-sparing concept to the aortic root and ascending aorta and warrants prospective evaluation.

42868953.title: Predicting acute kidney injury in type B aortic dissection: development and validation of a clinical nomogram.
42868953.abstract: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication in patients with Type B Aortic Dissection (TBAD). Existing prediction models are mainly derived from type A or mixed cohorts and do not account for the distinct pathophysiology of TBAD. This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram for individualized AKI risk prediction in TBAD patients. Data were obtained from the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) and the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV). The eICU-CRD cohort was used for model development and internal validation, while MIMIC-IV served for external validation. A three-step variable selection strategy combining Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), univariate, and multivariate logistic regression analyses was applied. Model performance was evaluated using the Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve (AUC), calibration curves, and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). Six independent predictors were identified: ICU length of stay, minimum glucose, minimum sodium, maximum bicarbonate, minimum creatinine, and minimum diastolic blood pressure. The nomogram showed excellent discrimination, with AUCs of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.893-0.956), 0.922 (95% CI: 0.869-0.967), and 0.921 (95% CI: 0.895-0.944) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement, and DCA indicated clinical utility within a threshold probability range of 0-70%. This study developed a practical nomogram based on six readily available variables for dynamic in-hospital prediction of AKI in TBAD patients. The model may assist early risk stratification, although further prospective validation is warranted.

42867193.title: Associations of base excess and alactic base excess with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 acute kidney injury in patients with acute ischemic stroke.
42867193.abstract: To identify the associations of base excess (BE) and alactic base excess (aBE) with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 acute kidney injury (AKI) in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). In this cohort study, 1,377 adult patients with AIS were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. A univariable logistic regression model was used to explore the associations of all variables with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI during the ICU stay of patients. Confounding factors were screened using bidirectional stepwise regression. Subgroup analysis was stratified based on age, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA), and comorbidities. Forest plot was plotted to identify the associations of BE and aBE with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI in AIS patients in different subgroups. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) was plotted. A total of 1,377 participants were included, of whom 680 developed KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI during their ICU stay. After adjusting for covariates including SOFA, sodium, anticoagulants, furosemide, and aspirin, we found that the association between BE < -5.124 mmol/L and KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI was significant (OR = 1.51, 95% CI: 1.05 - 2.16). As for aBE, we observed that aBE < -3.444 mmol/L might be related to KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI (OR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.12 - 2.20). In the adjusted model, aBE < -3.444 mmol/L was associated with elevated OR of KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI in AIS patients (OR = 1.43, 95% CI: 1.00 - 2.04). RCS revealed the non-liner associations of BE and aBE with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI in AIS patients. Low BE or aBE were associated with an increased risk of KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI in patients with AIS.

42866800.title: Gastroparesis in heart failure: temporal trends, clinical correlates, and outcomes in a large national cohort.
42866800.abstract: Gastrointestinal complications of heart failure are increasingly recognized, but the epidemiology and clinical significance of gastroparesis in this population remain poorly defined. We evaluated a national multicenter cohort of adults with heart failure to characterize temporal trends in gastroparesis incidence, identify factors associated with its development, and assess its association with clinical outcomes. We used a national multicenter database to identify adults diagnosed with heart failure from 2005 to 2025. Temporal trends in gastroparesis incidence were evaluated at 5-year intervals, multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify factors associated with its development, and 5-year cardiorenal and healthcare utilization outcomes were compared between patients with and without gastroparesis. Among 3,913,826 patients with heart failure, gastroparesis incidence increased more than tenfold during the study period, from 35.6 to 402.3 cases per 100,000 person-years. Diabetes mellitus [hazard ratio (HR) =4.54], chronic mesenteric ischemia (HR =2.16), ascites (HR =1.55), and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HR =1.60) were independently associated with gastroparesis. Patients with concomitant gastroparesis experienced significantly higher risks of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) [31.8% vs. 19.7%; odds ratio (OR) =1.90; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.80-1.99; P<0.001], acute kidney injury, end-stage renal disease, emergency department visits, and intensive care unit admission (38.9% vs. 22.6%; OR =2.19; 95% CI: 2.11-2.27; P<0.001). These findings identify gastroparesis as an increasingly recognized comorbidity in patients with heart failure that may represent a high-risk phenotype. The observed associations further suggest that venous congestion and impaired splanchnic perfusion may contribute to the development of gastric dysmotility in this population.

42862670.title: Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury with Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) Scoring Versus Renal Resistive Index (RRI) in Patients Undergoing On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Prospective Observational Study.
42862670.abstract: The diagnosis of acute kidney injury (AKI) using conventional markers such as serum creatinine and urine output is often delayed, prompting interest in bedside ultrasound-based predictors. This study compared renal resistive index (RRI) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) scoring for early prediction of AKI after on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). In this prospective observational study, 180 adult patients were enrolled. RRI and VExUS assessments were performed preoperatively and within 3 hours of cardiothoracic ICU admission. AKI was diagnosed within 48 hours postoperatively using kidney disease: improving global outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed for RRI and VExUS parameters, and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using area under ROC curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity. AKI occurred in 48 patients (26.7%). Postoperative RRI showed excellent discrimination for AKI (AUROC 0.854; cut-off ≥0.68: sensitivity 75%, specificity 86%, negative predictive value [NPV] 90.5%), outperforming preoperative RRI (AUROC 0.681). VExUS showed limited predictive performance (preoperative AUROC 0.588; postoperative AUROC 0.623). The baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in the AKI group was significantly lower than in the patients who did not develop AKI [70.3 ml/min/1.73 m2 vs 79.4 ml/min/1.73 m2]. Diabetes mellitus was more common in the AKI group (62.5% vs 35.6%, P = 0.002). Postoperative urine output remained significantly lower in AKI patients on day 1 and day 2 (P < 0.001). Postoperative RRI ≥ 0.68 demonstrated the best predictive performance for early AKI in our cohort, outperforming preoperative RRI, ΔRRI or change in RRI, and VExUS scores, supporting the predominant role of intrarenal arterial hemodynamic alterations in early postoperative renal injury.

42862669.title: Incidence and Predictors of Acute Kidney Injury Among Postoperative Cardiac Surgery Patients in Tanzania.
42862669.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) is a severe postoperative complication linked to increased morbidity and mortality. Data on the incidence and predictors of CSA-AKI in sub-Saharan Africa, including Tanzania, are limited. This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of AKI in patients who underwent cardiac surgery at Tanzania's National Cardiac Institute. This prospective study included 177 patients. AKI was defined using the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria based on serum creatinine (SCr) changes at 24, 48, and 72 h postoperatively. The patients' clinical profiles were collected and analyzed using SPSS version 27.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Chi-square tests and modified Poisson regression were used to identify associated factors at 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with P < 0.05. The prevalence of postoperative AKI was 53%, with the majority of patients presenting with AKI stage I (72.9%). In the multivariable analysis, diabetes mellitus (Adjusted Prevalence Ratio (aPR )1.32, 95% CI 1.02-1.70; P = 0.038), American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) IV status (aPR 1.39, 95% CI 1.10-1.76; P = 0.007), blood transfusion (transfusion: aPR 3.63, 95% CI 1.15-11.41; P = 0.027), triple components (aPR 3.41, 95% CI 1.08-10.78; P = 0.037), and prolonged cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time of 181-240 min (aPR 3.53, 95% CI 1.51-8.25; P = 0.004) and > 240 min (aPR 3.80, 95% CI 1.57-9.18; P = 0.003) were independent predictors of AKI. Female sex was independently associated with a lower prevalence of AKI (aPR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.88; P = 0.004). Patients who developed AKI had significantly longer stays in the intensive care unit (ICU) (aPR 2.39, 95% CI 1.39-4.12; P = 0.002). The prevalence of CSA-AKI is remarkably high in this setting, posing a significant clinical burden. Key preoperative and intraoperative predictors were also identified. These results reinforce the importance of perioperative patient optimization, strategies to minimize CPB exposure, transfusion practice optimization, and surveillance of high-risk patients.

42862668.title: Three-Point Bedside Congestion Score (IJV Collapsibility + IVC Collapsibility + Central Venous Pressure) in Elective Mitral Valve Surgery: A Prospective Observational Study.
42862668.abstract: Systemic venous congestion and right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction are key drivers of postoperative hemodynamic instability, prolonged ventilation, and acute kidney injury (AKI) after mitral valve surgery. Comprehensive echocardiography is informative but may be impractical in high-throughput pre-anesthesia workflows. We evaluated a pragmatic three-point bedside congestion score combining internal jugular vein (IJV) collapsibility, inferior vena cava (IVC) collapsibility, and invasively measured central venous pressure (CVP) for preoperative risk stratification. In this prospective, observational, single-center study, 100 consecutive adults (>18 years) undergoing elective mitral valve surgery for mitral stenosis were enrolled. A bedside ultrasound was performed in the preoperative area with patients in a 45° head-elevated position during quiet, spontaneous respiration. One point was assigned for each abnormal component (IJV collapsibility <18%, IVC collapsibility <25%, and CVP >12 mmHg), yielding a total score of 0 to 3. Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) was dichotomized at 17 mm. Outcomes included vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay, AKI, and in-hospital mortality. Discrimination for AKI and mortality was evaluated using a 5-fold cross-validated receiver operating characteristic (ROC) area under the curve (AUC) with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Calibration was assessed using recalibration intercept and slope, and decision curve analysis was used to explore clinical net benefit across threshold probabilities. The observed score distribution concentrated at 0 to 2 and 3; therefore, patients were analyzed as low score (0 to 2; n = 50) versus high score (3; n = 50). Compared with low-score patients, high-score patients had higher postoperative VIS (median 18.0 vs 10.0), longer ventilation (31.5 vs 22.0 hours), longer ICU stay (10.0 vs 5.5 days), and longer hospital stay (23.0 vs 12.5 days). AKI occurred in 40% versus 20%, and mortality in 10% versus 2% in high- versus low-score groups. In the combined 2 × 2 stratification, low score with normal TAPSE had no AKI or mortality, whereas high score with abnormal TAPSE had AKI in 55.6% and mortality in 14.8%. The combined score + TAPSE model showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.77 for AKI; AUC 0.782 for mortality) with near-ideal calibration in this dataset. Decision curve analysis suggested a higher net benefit for the combined model than single-predictor models across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.05 to 0.30. A simple three-point bedside congestion score stratifies postoperative risk after elective mitral valve surgery. Incorporating TAPSE into preoperative assessment provided a rapid and reliable means of excluding significant RV dysfunction, thereby reinforcing the validity of the threepoint scoring system. Multicenter external validation and evaluation of score-guided perioperative protocols are warranted.

42859375.title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio as a predictor of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute kidney injury: a retrospective cohort study.
42859375.abstract: To investigate the relationship between the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) and the risk of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute kidney injury (AKI), and to evaluate its predictive performance. A retrospective cohort study used the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) and MIMIC-III databases. SHR was defined as the ratio of admission blood glucose to estimated average glucose. Restricted cubic spline regression analyzed the nonlinear relationship between SHR and in-hospital mortality. Multivariate logistic regression and subgroup analyses were applied to validate the robustness of the association. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was employed to evaluate the predictive performance of SHR. Among 2180 patients, in-hospital mortality was 18.8% (263/1,398) in MIMIC-IV and 19.8% (155/782) in MIMIC-III. SHR showed a U-shaped relationship with in-hospital mortality, where SHR > 1.19 or < 0.50 significantly increased death risk (P < 0.05). The overall pattern was consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. ROC curve analysis demonstrated that SHR had better predictive performance than conventional severity and comorbidity scores for hospital mortality in AKI patients. The highly consistent results from both databases indicate reliability. SHR is an independent predictor of in-hospital mortality in AKI patients. By distinguishing the extreme low-SHR range from the intermediate lowest-risk range, this study further characterized the bidirectional nonlinear risk pattern, facilitating early identification of high-risk patients for risk stratification.

42859065.title: Acute Kidney Injury After Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review of Pharmacological and Non-Pharmacological Interventions.
42859065.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42859065.abstract: To identify and synthesize all randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions for the prevention of cardiac surgery‒associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI). We performed a systematic review of RCTs evaluating pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies. Interventions were qualitatively synthesized, and meta-analysis was performed when at least 4 RCTs were available. Hospitals. Adults undergoing cardiac surgery. Pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies to prevent CSA-AKI. A total of 207 RCTs, including 63,785 patients and evaluating 55 interventions, were identified. Most studies were small (median sample size 120) and single-center (76.7%) and reported neutral results (149/206), whereas 49 reported benefit and 8 reported harm. N-Acetylcysteine was the most frequently studied pharmacological intervention (19 RCTs), and remote ischemic preconditioning was the most frequently studied non-pharmacological intervention (34 RCTs). Among interventions evaluated in at least 4 RCTs were the use of dexmedetomidine (odds ratio [OR] 0.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.29-0.80), fenoldopam (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.33-0.98), nitric oxide (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.43-0.88), and remote ischemic preconditioning (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.90) were associated with lower odds of CSA-AKI. Among interventions evaluated in fewer than 4 RCTs were signals of benefit reported for amino acids, atrial natriuretic peptide, goal-directed perfusion, and KDIGO-based care bundles. Only a limited number of interventions were associated with lower odds of CSA-AKI; these findings require cautious interpretation and confirmation in adequately powered RCTs.

42858063.title: Rhabdomyolysis Following Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy.
42858063.abstract: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy remains a favorable treatment option for locally advanced prostate cancer in patients with obstructive lower urinary tract symptoms. However, the steep Trendelenburg lithotomy position required for this procedure can result in serious complications, particularly in patients with obesity. Here, the case of a 66-year-old man with obesity (BMI, 35 kg/m2), insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, and multiple comorbidities is reported, who underwent robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (console time, approximately 4 h) for clinically staged cT3a cN1 prostate cancer. Immediately after surgery, the patient developed severe gluteal pain, sensorimotor deficits, and massive rhabdomyolysis, resulting in anuric acute kidney injury and respiratory insufficiency. The clinical course was further complicated by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia type II and a grade IV gluteal pressure ulcer. A 22-day intensive care stay was required, including continuous hemodiafiltration and transfusion of 12 units of erythrocytes. With multidisciplinary management, renal function partially recovered, and the patient was discharged with minimal residual neuropathic deficits. This case highlights the importance of comprehensive preoperative risk assessment and provides clinically relevant insights into the recognition and multidisciplinary management of severe complications associated with prolonged positioning during robot-assisted radical prostatectomy.

42847998.title: Development and validation of a cefepime population pharmacokinetic model to guide treatment for patients with hospital-acquired pneumonia requiring renal replacement.
42847998.abstract: Cefepime is used in critically ill pneumonia patients, but dosing in renal replacement therapy (RRT) is complicated by altered renal function, extracorporeal removal, and variability in pulmonary epithelial lining fluid (ELF) exposure. We sought to develop an integrated model linking systemic, extracorporeal, and pulmonary cefepime pharmacokinetics in RRT. Pharmacokinetic (PK) data from critically ill adults receiving cefepime and requiring RRT were included. In a dedicated continuous RRT (CRRT) cohort (n = 8), pre- and post-filter plasma and effluent PK data were collected. Additional patients (n = 43) requiring RRT also contributed plasma and ELF samples. A non-parametric population PK model was developed using an 80/20 subject-level development-validation split. Covariate models assessed the impact of residual renal function, effluent flow rate, body size, and fixed intradialytic hemodialysis (HD) clearance. Monte Carlo simulations evaluated plasma and ELF target attainment across dosing strategies, weight strata, and minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). The final model jointly described systemic, extracorporeal, and pulmonary cefepime disposition using piecewise central volume, native clearance, linear effluent-flow-dependent CRRT clearance, fixed HD clearance, and ELF distribution. Simulations showed adequate plasma target attainment, whereas ELF attainment was sensitive to MIC, target, regimen, and body weight. Continuous infusions of 4 g/day provided adequate ELF attainment at MICs ≤4 mg/L. Plasma-based cefepime target attainment may overestimate pulmonary exposure during RRT, particularly at higher MICs, body weights, and fT>MIC targets. External validation and prospective studies are needed to refine pulmonary target estimates and determine whether plasma-guided Bayesian dosing can reliably ensure site-of-infection exposure.

42846849.title: Insulin resistance, metabolic phenotypes, and the obesity paradox: a triglyceride glucose-body mass index framework in partial kidney diseases.
42846849.abstract: Insulin resistance(IR) is a key driver of cardiorenal-metabolic diseases. The Triglyceride Glucose-Body Mass Index (TyG-BMI), a composite marker of lipid-glucose metabolism and overall adiposity, has gained traction as a predictive tool. Its clinical application, however, is complicated by non-linear and sometimes paradoxical associations with clinical outcomes, a phenomenon reminiscent of the"obesity paradox". This review critically evaluates the performance of TyG-BMI across the spectrum of kidney disease, aiming to reconcile these divergent findings through a metabolic-endocrine framework. We performed a narrative synthesis of observational studies and secondary analyses of large-scale public databases such as National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey(NHANES), China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study(CHARLS), UK Biobank, Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV(MIMIC-IV), identified through PubMed and Google Scholar, to evaluate the association of TyG-BMI with the incidence, progression, and prognosis of acute kidney injury (AKI), diabetic kidney disease (DKD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic syndrome(CKM). TyG-BMI shows significant, context-dependent predictive value. In early-stage or metabolically heterogeneous populations, elevated TyG-BMI consistently predicts higher disease risk. Conversely, in advanced stages (e.g., end-stage renal disease, stage 4 CKM), the association frequently becomes U-shaped, with low TyG-BMI paradoxically linked to excess mortality. This reflects its dual nature: the TyG component captures 'metabolic toxicity', while BMI proxies 'nutritional reserve'. Thus, the 'obesity paradox' may represent a metabolic phenotype spectrum-from metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) to metabolically unhealthy lean (MUL)-that the combination of its TyG and BMI components helps differentiate. For disease incidence prediction, TyG-BMI is often outperformed by indices of central obesity (e.g., Triglyceride-Glucose-Waist Circumference Index(TyG-WC), Triglyceride-Glucose-Waist-to-Height Ratio(TyG-WHtR); for mortality in advanced illness, the standalone TyG index may be superior. TyG-BMI is a valuable tool for metabolic phenotyping and risk stratification in kidney disease, with its paradoxical associations highlighting the complex interplay between metabolic health and nutritional reserve. Future research must establish context-specific clinical thresholds. TyG-BMI is preferentially useful in settings where waist circumference is unavailable, in early CKD screening, and in select type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) subgroups. In advanced CKD, dialysis, critical illness, and CKM stage 4, alternative indices such as TyG index, TyG-WC, or TyG-WHtR should be prioritized due to the confounding effects of fluid overload and catabolic state.

42846740.title: Beyond renal support: biological modulation across pathophysiological domains during continuous renal replacement therapy - a randomized pilot study.
42846740.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is the preferred extracorporeal renal support modality for haemodynamically unstable critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI). Although regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) is primarily used to maintain circuit patency, its biological effects may extend beyond anticoagulation itself. We hypothesized that different anticoagulation strategies are associated with distinct biological modulation across complementary pathophysiological domains during CRRT. We conducted a prospective randomized pilot trial comparing RCA with systemic unfractionated heparin in critically ill adults with AKI requiring CRRT (1:1 allocation). Serial blood samples were obtained before CRRT initiation, at 1 hour and at 24 hours, with paired pre- and post-filter sampling at 1 and 24 hours. Biomarkers represented redox homeostasis (glutathione -GSH, GSSG- and their ratio), neutrophil activation (myeloperoxidase -MPO-), cellular injury (cell-free DNA -cfDNA-) and systemic inflammation (C-reactive protein -CRP-). Healthy reference participants established physiological reference values. Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models with fixed effects for time, anticoagulation strategy and their interaction. This trial was registered in the European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT No. 2016-004361-12) and at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06646328). Twenty patients were randomized equally to RCA or systemic heparin; baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Among six biomarkers spanning four pathophysiological domains, only MPO showed a significant systemic time × anticoagulation interaction (P = .008); although baseline-adjusted sensitivity analyses did not confirm a significant between-group difference. GSH and cfDNA changed significantly over time irrespective of anticoagulation strategy (both P = .016), while the GSSG/GSH ratio approached a treatment-level difference (P = .067). Across the extracorporeal circuit, CRP increased significantly post-filter at both timepoints, MPO increased at 1h, and GSH showed an anticoagulation-dependent pre-to-post change at 1h. No significant differences were observed in secondary clinical outcomes. These pilot findings suggest that different anticoagulation strategies during CRRT may show domain-specific, rather than uniform, biological modulation, most evident within the neutrophil activation domain, with additional evidence of biomarker-specific kinetics across the extracorporeal circuit. These exploratory results are compatible with the concept that extracorporeal therapies may influence distinct domains differently, a hypothesis warranting confirmation in adequately powered, prospectively designed studies before implications for precision extracorporeal therapy can be drawn.

42844960.title: Clinical Profile, Prognostic Indicators, and Outcomes in Patients with Acute Pyelonephritis: Comparing Emphysematous with Nonemphysematous Pyelonephritis.
42844960.abstract: Emphysematous pyelonephritis (EPN) is a life-threatening necrotizing infection of the upper urinary tract, resulting in high morbidity and mortality. Comparative data between EPN and non-EPN are scarce, especially from developing countries. To compare the clinical profile, prognostic indicators, management strategies, and outcomes in patients with emphysematous and nonemphysematous acute pyelonephritis (APN). This was a prospective observational study conducted in a tertiary care teaching institute in North India from March 2022 to December 2025 and included 120 consecutive adult patients with APN. Radiological imaging was used to classify patients as EPN or non-EPN. Of the 120 patients, 99 (82.5%) had non-EPN and 21 (17.5%) had EPN. The most common comorbidity was diabetes mellitus (75.0%) and was associated more frequently with EPN (95.2% vs. 70.7%, P = 0.024). Uncontrolled glycemia (glycosylated hemoglobin: >7.5%) was present in 67.5% of patients and significantly associated with EPN (P = 0.047). Escherichia coli was the most common pathogen found in urine (43.7%) and blood (62.5%) cultures. Radiological or surgical interventions were needed in 56.7% of patients, and renal replacement therapy and intensive care admission were needed in 34.2% and 22.5%, respectively. Mortality was higher in the EPN group than in the non-EPN group (14.3% vs. 3.0%; P = 0.066). EPN is the severest form of APN and is associated with worse glycemic control, increased requirement for invasive procedures, and higher in-hospital mortality. Early diagnosis, prompt imaging, appropriate antimicrobial therapy, and timely multidisciplinary management are essential to improve clinical outcome.

42843126.title: The association between cardiac surgery - associated acute kidney injury and elevated liver function tests. A single-center cohort study.
42843126.abstract: Acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery (CSA-AKI) is common and associated with worse outcome. Venous congestion contributes to CSA-AKI and liver dysfunction. We hypothesized that elevated liver enzymes may serve as early markers for CSA-AKI. In a single-center cohort study we included adult cardiac surgery patients during a 6-year period. Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) were measured at ICU admission, 12 h and 24 h. The primary objective was to assess whether liver enzymes at ICU admission, normalized to their upper limits of normal (ULN), predicted CSA-AKI. Secondary outcomes included prediction of CSA-AKI severity, use of renal replacement therapy (RRT), and the association between central venous pressure (CVP) and liver enzymes. Among 3415 patients, 65.4% developed CSA-AKI, 37.4% had AKI stage ≥2 and 3.8% received RRT. AST/ULN and ALT/ULN at ICU admission predicted CSA-AKI [AUC-ROC (95% CI; resp. 0.587 (0.570-0.604); 0.534 (0.517-0.551); both p < 0.001)], with AST performing better (p < 0.001). The discriminating power of AST/ULN and ALT/ULN at ICU admission for AKI ≥2 were respectively AUC-ROC (95% CI); 0.594 (0.577-0.610) and 0.541 (0.524-0.585) (both p < 0.001). AST/ULN 12 h after ICU admission was the strongest predictor for RRT [AUC-ROC (95% CI; 0.751 (0.733-0.768); p < 0.001)], with a 4-fold increased RRT risk when AST exceeded 1.6 times the ULN. AST and ALT 24 h post ICU admission were weakly associated with CVP (respectively: R2 = 0.007; p = 0.003 and ALT: R2 = 0.006; p = 0.004). AST activity may have potential as a predictor of CSA-AKI and use of RRT, although liver enzymes demonstrated a weak association with CSA-AKI.

42838725.title: Streptococcus pneumoniae haemolytic uraemic syndrome in Aotearoa New Zealand across changing pneumococcal conjugate vaccine eras.
42838725.abstract: To describe the epidemiology, clinical features, microbiology and outcomes of paediatric Streptococcus pneumoniae haemolytic uraemic syndrome (SpHUS) in Aotearoa New Zealand across changing pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) eras. Retrospective case series. National paediatric tertiary referral centre, New Zealand. Children aged 0-15 years with SpHUS between 2008 and 2024. Clinical presentation, microbiology and serotype distribution, acute severity and long-term renal outcomes. 39 cases were identified; 26/39 (67%) occurred between 2020 and 2024. Median age was 18 months, with 26/39 (67%) aged <2 years. Māori and Pacific children comprised 24/39 (62%) of cases. Complicated pneumonia was the predominant presentation (36/39, 92%). Among 32 cases with serotype data, 27/32 (84%) were serotype 19A, including 21/21 cases from 2020 to 2024. Most children were PCV-immunised (31/39, 79%), with 6/32 (19%) infected with vaccine-covered serotypes. Disease severity was high: 35/39 (90%) required intensive care and 31/39 (79%) required kidney replacement therapy (median 13 days). Mortality was 2/39 (5%) and 2/39 (5%) required kidney transplantation. Among survivors with follow-up, 13/30 (43%) had chronic kidney disease. SpHUS in New Zealand has increased since 2020, during a period of rising invasive pneumococcal disease, predominantly involving serotype 19A, with high acute severity and substantial long-term kidney morbidity. The burden is disproportionately borne by Māori and Pacific children, highlighting the need for ongoing surveillance and vaccine strategies responsive to local epidemiology.

42837066.title: Diagnostic accuracy of doppler-derived renal ultrasound parameters for predicting acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
42837066.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent and clinically significant complication following cardiac surgery. Doppler-derived renal ultrasound parameters-including the renal resistive index (RRI), semiquantitative power Doppler ultrasound (PDU) scales, and intrarenal venous flow (IRVF)-have been proposed as early, noninvasive predictors of postoperative AKI, but their diagnostic accuracy in this setting remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review of diagnostic test accuracy studies evaluating RRI, PDU, or IRVF for predicting AKI within 7 days after cardiac surgery in adult intensive care unit patients. MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, and clinical trial registries were searched through June 2025. Sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio (DOR), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were extracted or calculated. Meta-analysis was performed for RRI using hierarchical bivariate models; IRVF and PDU were summarized descriptively due to limited studies and heterogeneity. Fourteen studies comprising 1,204 patients were included (12 RRI, 3 IRVF, 1 PDU). RRI thresholds between 0.71 and 0.74 demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance (AUC range 0.72-0.93). IRVF showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.62-0.66). Evidence for PDU was limited to one study. Substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity was observed and overall certainty of evidence ranged from low to moderate. Among Doppler-derived renal ultrasound parameters, RRI appears to have the most consistent diagnostic accuracy for predicting AKI after cardiac surgery. However, methodological heterogeneity, the limited number of studies, and the low-to-moderate certainty of the evidence preclude definitive clinical recommendations. Prospective multicenter validation studies with standardized protocols and prespecified thresholds are warranted.

42836521.title: From prematurity and low birth weight to CKD: opportunities for intervention.
42836521.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
42836521.abstract: Preterm birth (<37 completed gestational weeks), low birth weight (<2500g) and small for gestational age (SGA, birth weight <10th percentile for gestational age) are interrelated neonatal phenotypes that adversely affect lifelong kidney health. They have been grouped under the term small vulnerable newborn (SVN). Being born as SVN ranks fifth among risk factors for early mortality and imposes a lifelong susceptibility for chronic kidney disease (CKD). The combination of extreme prematurity and SGA triples CKD-risk in early adulthood. Globally, around 35 million SVN are born annually and will contribute to rising CKD morbidity and mortality. In SVN, nephron mass is reduced because prematurity interrupts and an adverse intrauterine environment impairs nephron endowment. Maladaptive responses to low nephron mass include glomerular hyperfiltration, glomerular hypertension and glomerular sclerosis. In addition, complications of prematurity cause renal hypoperfusion and pharmacological treatment on the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) can be nephrotoxic, both contributing to neonatal acute kidney injury (AKI). Neonatal AKI is common, has a high acute mortality and is a potentially modifiable second hit towards CKD. Preventive strategies include optimizing maternal health to prevent SVN, improved detection and avoidance of neonatal AKI by reduction of nephrotoxicity and kidney hypoperfusion during NICU-treatment and systematic documentation of AKI at discharge. Physicians and families should be educated about the child's lifelong CKD risk. Follow-up should be stratified by completed gestational weeks, birth weight, occurrence of AKI and comorbidities. Follow-up aims are early identification and treatment of CKD progression factors and complications.

42835122.title: Plasma exchange and double plasma molecular adsorption system combined with continuous renal replacement therapy for hepatitis B-related liver failure complicated by stage 3 acute kidney injury: a case report.
42835122.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver failure can progress rapidly to neurological and renal dysfunction. In this setting, declining aminotransferase levels may be misleading if hepatic synthetic function and extrahepatic organ function continue to deteriorate. A 27-year-old woman presented with severe fatigue, dark urine, and jaundice. Laboratory testing showed marked hepatocellular injury, coagulopathy, HBV infection markers, and an HBV DNA level of 3.57 × 10⁶ copies/mL.
