During hospitalization, serum aminotransferase levels declined substantially; however, bilirubin and coagulation abnormalities worsened, serum creatinine increased from 96 μmol/L on day 1 to 825 μmol/L on day 4, and the patient developed hypersomnia and impaired consciousness. The renal deterioration met criteria for stage 3 acute kidney injury. Following multidisciplinary assessment, plasma exchange combined with a double plasma molecular adsorption system was used for liver-directed extracorporeal support, while continuous renal replacement therapy was initiated primarily for severe acute kidney injury and metabolic support. Consciousness, coagulation, liver function, and renal function subsequently improved. The patient left the intensive care unit on day 7, was discharged on day 24, and maintained normal liver and kidney function during follow-up. This case highlights that declining aminotransferase levels do not necessarily indicate clinical recovery in rapidly progressive HBV-related liver failure. Serial assessment of hepatic synthetic function, neurological status, and renal function identified continued multiorgan deterioration and guided timely, indication-based extracorporeal support. The clinical value of this case lies in the decision-making process for coordinated liver and renal support rather than in the novelty of the individual treatment modalities.

42833842.title: Fulminant multi-organ failure associated with cereulide-producing Bacillus cereus after consumption of improperly stored rice.
42833842.abstract: A male in his 20s with no medical history was found with generalised seizures and profound hypoglycaemia after consuming improperly stored, reheated rice.Initial laboratory tests showed acute liver failure with hyperammonaemia, acute kidney injury and lactic acidosis, which rapidly progressed to multi-organ failure requiring urgent liver transplantation evaluation.With maximal supportive therapy, including glucose, ammonia and glutamine scavengers, renal replacement therapy, haemodynamic and respiratory support, he gradually improved, avoiding transplantation and achieving full neurological recovery. Toxicological analysis of the rice and serum revealed high concentrations of cereulide, a toxin produced by Bacillus cereus This case illustrates that cereulide intoxication can be associated with potentially fatal multi-organ failure, particularly after ingestion of improperly stored starchy foods.Early recognition through targeted dietary history, focused laboratory evaluation and prompt supportive therapy are essential. Increasing awareness among healthcare professionals and safe food storage practices are key preventive measures.

42832436.title: A comparison of phosphate-containing versus conventional hemodialysis solutions for citrate-anticoagulated continuous veno-venous hemodialysis in patients with acute kidney injury.
42832436.abstract: Introduction Acute kidney injury (AKI) frequently necessitates continuous renal replacement therapy, often causing phosphate and magnesium losses. We evaluated whether a phosphate containing, magnesium-enriched dialysate reduces hypophosphatemia and hypomagnesemia compared to phosphate-free dialysate with standard magnesium concentration during citrate-anticoagulated continuous veno-venous hemodialysis (RCA-CVVHD) in ICU patients. Methods Single-center observational study comparing two adult ICU cohorts undergoing RCA-CVVHD from 2011-2014. The 2011-2012 cohort received phosphate-free dialysate with standard magnesium concentration (0.75 mmol/L) and intravenous phosphate and magnesium supplementation. The 2013-2014 cohort received a phosphate-containing (1.25 mmol/L), magnesium-enriched (1.0 mmol/L) dialysate. The primary endpoint was the incidence of hypophosphatemia and severe hypophosphatemia within 72 hours. Secondary outcomes included magnesium and calcium disturbances, delivered dialysis dose, solute control, filter lifespan, and clinical outcomes. Results We analyzed 85 patients in the 2011-2012 and 97 in the 2013-2014 cohort. Hypophosphatemia (92% vs. 68%, p < 0.001) and severe hypophosphatemia (65% vs. 28%, p < 0.001) were less frequent with phosphate-containing dialysate. Phosphate and magnesium levels were higher (p<0.008) with the phosphate-containing, magnesium-enriched solution. Fewer patients required phosphate (23% vs. 81%, p < 0.001) or magnesium (35% vs. 76%, p < 0.001) infusions. Ionized calcium and total calcium remained within target range in both cohorts. The delivered dialysis dose was 31.0±8.1 mL/kg/h in the 2011-2012 and 28.6±6.6 mL/kg/h in the 2013-2014 cohort (p = 0.025). More filters reached the maximum lifespan of 72 hours in the 2013-2014 cohort (64% vs. 75%; p = 0.03). Solute clearance and acid-base control were similar. Conclusion In ICU patients undergoing RCA-CVVHD, a phosphate-containing, magnesium-enriched dialysate was associated with significantly lower incidence and severity of hypophosphatemia, higher phosphate and magnesium levels, and lower need for separate electrolyte infusions. This phosphate-containing solution may offer relevant benefits, including reduced workload and potentially increased patient safety. These findings require confirmation in a RCT that includes relevant clinical endpoints.

42831055.title: Early Diffuse Alveolar Hemorrhage Revealing Leptospirosis Without Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report and Literature Review.
42831055.abstract: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage is a severe manifestation of leptospirosis, typically occurring in advanced stages of the disease and often associated with multiorgan failure. We report the case of a 44-year-old man without significant medical history admitted for acute febrile illness, hypotension, and respiratory symptoms occurring six days after initial symptom onset. Laboratory findings showed thrombocytopenia, elevated inflammatory markers, hepatic cytolysis, and mild acute kidney injury. Chest imaging demonstrated bilateral ground-glass opacities. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) confirmed alveolar hemorrhage, revealing 1,300,000 red blood cells/mm³ with a neutrophil-predominant profile and negative microbiological investigations. Polymerase chain reaction testing confirmed leptospirosis. The patient was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone followed by oral amoxicillin, resulting in rapid clinical and biological improvement. This case highlights an atypical pulmonary presentation of leptospirosis without extra-respiratory involvement. Leptospirosis lung involvement should probably be considered in patients presenting with febrile illness, pulmonary infiltrates, and thrombocytopenia, in endemic settings, even without jaundice or severe renal impairment.

42824508.title: JICS Education: Continuous renal replacement therapy.
42824508.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
42824508.abstract: Delivering continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is an integral mode of organ support provided on intensive care units (ICU). This article provides readers with a comprehensive understanding of CRRT, covering indications for therapy and when and how to start it. Supporting this information are practical tips to help improve therapy efficacy and a summary of the current evidence which should underpin clinical decision making.

42957308.title: Association between intracatheter Ca²(+) trajectory and extracorporeal circuit coagulation in unplanned early withdrawal among patients receiving CRRT: a retrospective cohort study.

42953952.title: Clinical Impact of Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Among Patients With HIV/AIDS and Disseminated Histoplasmosis in a Hyperendemic Region of Northeastern Brazil.
42953952.abstract: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome that may occur in people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA), often triggered by opportunistic infections such as disseminated histoplasmosis (DH). The substantial overlap in clinical and laboratory features between HLH and DH complicates timely diagnosis. To describe HLH among PLWHA with DH and compare clinical, laboratory and outcome characteristics between patients with and without HLH. A retrospective observational study was conducted at São José Hospital of Infectious Diseases, Fortaleza, Brazil, between March 2023 and June 2024. Hospitalised PLWHA with DH were evaluated for HLH based on the presence of ≥ 3 HLH-2004 criteria and an H-Score ≥ 169. Baseline clinical, laboratory and outcome parameters were compared between patients with and without HLH. Among 61 patients diagnosed with DH, 11 (18.0%) met the study criteria for HLH. Patients with HLH were more likely to present with hepatomegaly (p = 0.036), haemoptysis (p = 0.030) and lower platelet counts (p = 0.029). In-hospital mortality was significantly higher among patients with HLH (54.5% versus 18.0%; p = 0.019). These patients more frequently required renal replacement therapy (p = 0.028) and intensive care unit admission (p = 0.048). Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing demonstrated significantly reduced in-hospital survival among patients with HLH (p = 0.015). HLH represents a severe complication in PLWHA with DH and is associated with increased mortality and greater need for intensive care. Early recognition and use of adjunctive diagnostic tools may facilitate timely management and improve clinical outcomes.

42953208.title: Dynamic lactate clearance within the first 48 hours predicts pressure injury during ECMO support: a longitudinal cohort study.
42953208.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association between dynamic lactate clearance and the development of pressure injuries in adult patients undergoing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support and to evaluate its incremental value for early risk prediction. This was a retrospective longitudinal cohort study. A total of 317 adult patients receiving ECMO support were enrolled. Lactate concentrations were measured at ECMO initiation and at 6, 24, and 48 h thereafter. Lactate clearance rates were calculated for each corresponding time point. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent risk factors for pressure injury development. The predictive performance of lactate clearance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, five-fold cross-validation, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Pressure injuries occurred in 95 patients (30.0%). Compared with those without pressure injuries, affected patients exhibited significantly lower lactate clearance rates throughout the first 48 h post-ECMO initiation (all P < 0.001). Independent predictors of pressure injury included higher body mass index, elevated vasoactive-inotropic score, VA-ECMO mode, and concomitant renal replacement therapy. The baseline clinical model yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.710. Incorporating lactate clearance significantly improved model discrimination, with AUCs increasing to 0.796, 0.825, and 0.899 for the 6-hour, 24-hour, and 48-hour models, respectively. Consistent enhancements in predictive accuracy were confirmed by cross-validation, NRI, and IDI analyses. Impaired lactate clearance is independently associated with pressure injury development in critically ill adults supported by ECMO. Dynamic monitoring of lactate clearance substantially enhances risk stratification beyond traditional clinical parameters.

42950910.title: Resting Energy Expenditure in Mechanically Ventilated Surgical-Trauma Patients With and Without Acute Kidney Injury: a single-center retrospective study.
42950910.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
42950910.abstract: To compare resting energy expenditure (REE) measured by indirect calorimetry (IC) in mechanically ventilated surgical-trauma critically ill patients with and without acute kidney injury (AKI); to evaluate differences in REE by sex, age, and body mass index (BMI); and to assess associations between REE, psoas muscle index (PMI) measured using computed tomography scans, and lean body mass (LBM) estimated by predictive equations. This single-center retrospective cohort study conducted at a tertiary academic medical center included mechanically ventilated critically ill adults admitted between 01/01/2012 and 12/31/2023. Exclusion criteria were pediatric, pregnant, or incarcerated patients; quadriplegia, paraplegia, cystic fibrosis; abnormal respiratory quotients; Medical ICU admission; major burns (≥20% TBSA); parenteral nutrition initiated on or after IC; tracheostomy on admission; discharge or death while ventilated; or absence of a nutrition prescription. Of 794 patients screened, 180 met inclusion criteria (AKI n=84; no AKI n=96). At baseline, patients with and without AKI differed significantly in age (59.9 vs 55 years; P = 0.046), BMI (32.2 vs 28.8 kg/m2; P = 0.046), CKD (23.8% vs 3.13%; P < 0.001), and serum creatinine (1.49 vs 0.84 mg/dL; P < 0.001). Of patients with AKI, 71.4% had stage I AKI and 20.2% required renal replacement therapy (RRT). No significant difference in mean REE was observed between patients with and without AKI (1,642 vs 1,665 kcal/day; P = 0.380) . REE was significantly higher in males compared with females (1,806 vs 1,425 kcal/day; P < 0.001), in patients aged 18-65 versus >65 years (1,768 vs 1,428 kcal/day; P = 0.002), and in obese versus non-obese patients (1,841 vs 1,500 kcal/day; P < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, higher BMI (P = 0.003) and male sex (P = 0.028) were independently associated with higher REE, while AKI was not. LBM estimated by predictive equations was more strongly correlated with REE than PMI (P < 0.001), and correlation strength did not differ by AKI status. Measured REE did not differ between ventilated surgical-trauma patients with and without AKI. REE differed by sex, age, and obesity status, and AKI was not associated with within-group differences. BMI and sex were identified as independent predictors of REE. Estimated LBM was strongly correlated with REE independent of AKI status. Given possible residual confounding, further investigation is needed.

42948441.title: Weekend versus weekday cardiac surgery: A comprehensive meta-analysis of more than 500,000 cases with meta-regression.
42948441.abstract: The "weekend effect" describes worse outcomes with weekend hospital care, but its impact on cardiac surgery remains unclear. We performed a comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression to assess whether weekend cardiac surgery is associated with poorer perioperative outcomes than weekday procedures. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies comparing weekend versus weekday cardiac surgery outcomes. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed by procedure type (emergent, coronary artery bypass grafting, acute type A aortic dissection) and geographic region. Meta-regressions explored effects of mean age, percentage of female patients, proportion of emergent cases, and publication year. A day-by-day mortality heat map was constructed to assess daily trends. Seventeen studies comprising 527,195 patients were included; 7.4% underwent surgery on weekends. Weekend surgery was associated with significantly greater mortality (OR, 1.5; 95% CI, 1.2-1.8; P = .001) and longer stay in the intensive care unit (mean difference, 0.4 days; 95% CI, 0.1-0.7; P = .01). No significant differences were found for acute kidney injury, stroke, aortic crossclamp time, reoperation for bleeding, or total hospital stay. The incidence of transient ischemic attack was slightly lower on weekends (OR, 0.8; 95% CI, 0.6-1.0; P = .02). Subgroup analyses showed consistently elevated mortality in weekend cases across emergent, coronary artery bypass grafting, and acute type A aortic dissection subgroups, and in studies from Asia and the United States but not Europe. Meta-regression showed no significant effect of age, sex, emergent case proportion, or publication year on mortality differences. Weekend cardiac surgery is associated with greater mortality and longer stay in the intensive care unit, independent of case mix. The absence of patient-level effect modification suggests that systemic or institutional factors, rather than patient acuity, underlie the weekend effect, supporting the need for policies ensuring consistent care across all days.

42947393.title: Characteristics and Outcomes After General Anaesthesia in Elderly Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
42947393.abstract: Elderly patients are more frail and have a higher burden of comorbidity, which could influence the risk of complications after anaesthesia. The aim of this study was to describe the elderly patient population undergoing general anaesthesia in Denmark. This was a national registry-based observational cohort study of adult patients (≥ 18 years) undergoing general anaesthesia in Denmark in 2020 and 2021, with a primary focus on patients 80 years and above. Patient and procedure characteristics of interest were age, sex, BMI, ASA classification, Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, comorbidities, type of procedure, and class of priority. The primary outcome of interest was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included acute kidney injury within 7 days, length of hospital stay, and number of days in the ICU. A total of 453,133 cases of general anaesthesia in 328,951 unique patients in Denmark during 2020 and 2021 were included in this study. Of these, 25,955 (8%) patients were 80 years of age and above. Elderly patients undergoing general anaesthesia were of higher ASA classification, suffered from a higher degree of comorbidity measured by Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, had a lower proportion of elective procedures and a higher proportion of expedited and urgent procedures. Mortality for all patients at 30 days was 1.5% (n = 4814). While mortality was low for cases aged between 18 and 65 years, 30-day mortality increased for each year after 65 years of age even after adjusting for covariates. Mortality was especially high for patients with high Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, high ASA classification, and for non-elective procedures. In this nationwide registry-based cohort study, we described the elderly patient population undergoing general anaesthesia in Denmark. We found that 30-day mortality increased for each year after 65 years of age even after adjusting for covariates. This large cohort study from Denmark assesses perioperative case factors including age, comorbidity and more, then describing different risk levels for 30 day mortality, particularly with advanced age.

42946360.title: Protocol for an individual patient data meta-analysis for the assessment of risk factors affecting the development and outcome of functional and structural acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery: the METARIS CS-AKI study.

42936270.title: Ischemic Colitis in the Setting of Tirzepatide Use: A Potentially Underrecognized Adverse Effect.
42936270.abstract: Ischemic colitis is an uncommon but serious cause of acute abdominal pain that may result in bowel necrosis and may require surgical intervention. We report the case of a 63-year-old female patient with multiple comorbidities and a history of ischemic colitis, who developed sudden-onset severe cramping and abdominal pain, together with hypotension and diaphoresis, shortly after receiving her weekly tirzepatide injection. The patient reported suffering from chronic constipation with increased frequency of laxative use after beginning tirzepatide (Mounjaro). Laboratory evaluation demonstrated leukocytosis and lactic acidosis, while computed tomography (CT) findings were consistent with ischemic colitis. Her condition rapidly progressed to hypovolemic shock and acute kidney injury (AKI), requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission and segmental bowel resection with colostomy creation. Surgical pathology report confirmed patchy mucosal necrosis consistent with ischemic colitis. This case raises concern for a potential association between tirzepatide use and ischemic colitis in a patient with preexisting risk factors. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for ischemic colitis in patients receiving tirzepatide who present with severe abdominal pain, particularly in the setting of worsening constipation or a prior history of ischemic colitis. This case raises the question of whether a history of ischemic colitis and/or chronic constipation may warrant clinical caution and pharmacovigilance before starting these medications.

42929728.title: Micronutrient deficiencies in continuous renal replacement therapy: A literature review and the emerging role of the pharmacist.
42929728.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
42929728.abstract: Evaluating micronutrient deficiencies in the critically ill population is challenging given the complex clinical picture for many patients. Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is a risk factor for micronutrient deficiencies in this cohort, with deficiencies resulting from increased losses in dialysis effluent or adsorption to tubing or to the dialysis filter. The aim of this article is to summarize pertinent research literature regarding micronutrient supplementation and monitoring in CRRT and identify areas for pharmacists to improve patient outcomes from a nutrition standpoint. A computerized literature search was conducted of the PubMed electronic database, and articles were included if they discussed one of the prespecified micronutrients and renal replacement therapy. The micronutrients specifically addressed in this article are copper, selenium, zinc, L-carnitine, vitamin C, vitamin B1, vitamin B6, and vitamin B9. For each of these micronutrients, we summarize the evidence for deficiencies in CRRT and supplementation strategies. However, in many cases, literature is lacking to support supplementation and monitoring strategies specifically in CRRT. Current literature recognizes that standard supplementation may not be enough in the critically ill population on CRRT, but evidence is lacking for optimal micronutrient supplementation doses and monitoring parameters. Until future literature is available, pharmacists should be aware of these deficiencies and help guide recommendations for supplementation.

42919180.title: Analysis of factors influencing the complications of severe acute pancreatitis combined with hemorrhage.
42919180.abstract: Complications of hemorrhage in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) significantly impact prognosis. However, current research on this topic remains limited. This study aims to analyze the factors influencing hemorrhage in SAP patients. This study retrospectively analyzed clinical data from SAP patients admitted to our hospital between January 2019 and December 2022. Using propensity score matching and multivariate logistic regression analysis, we identified independent factors influencing hemorrhage. Additionally, we developed a nomogram prediction model for bleeding in SAP patients and generated an ROC curve to assess its accuracy. Prognosis was also evaluated. Based on the exclusion criteria, 804 patients were included in the study, with 97 (12.1%) experiencing hemorrhagic complications. After applying propensity score matching, 440 patients were selected, including 88 with bleeding. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified several independent factors influencing hemorrhage in SAP: computed tomography severity index (CTSI) score (OR: 1.771, 95% CI: 1.434-2.187, P < 0.001), infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN) (OR: 4.407, 95% CI: 1.854-10.476, P < 0.001), acute physiology and chronic health evaluation II (APACHE II) score ≥ 15 (OR: 12.323, 95% CI: 5.015-30.282, P < 0.001), abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) (OR: 3.685, 95% CI: 1.462-9.287, P = 0.006), and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) (OR: 0.251, 95% CI: 0.094-0.670, P = 0.006). A nomogram prediction model was constructed, achieving an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.924. The median ICU stay and total hospital stay were significantly longer in the bleeding group compared to the non-bleeding group (30 vs. 7 and 48 vs. 18, P < 0.001). Additionally, the mortality rate was significantly higher in the bleeding group compared to the non-bleeding group (46.6% vs. 6.5%, P < 0.001). The occurrence of bleeding complications in SAP signifies a poor prognosis. Therefore, for patients with elevated CTSI and APACHE II scores, especially those with IPN and ACS, it is crucial to enhance monitoring for bleeding. If necessary, CRRT may be implemented to improve the condition and reduce the risk of hemorrhage.

42919132.title: Association between rhythm control strategy and clinical outcomes in postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a retrospective cohort study.
42919132.abstract: The optimal management strategy for postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains debated. While rhythm control aims to restore sinus rhythm, its impact on clinical resource utilization and long-term outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between an initial rhythm control strategy (as an escalation to rate control) and clinical outcomes compared to rate control alone. This retrospective cohort study identified 663 adult patients who developed POAF after isolated CABG from the MIMIC-IV database. We used two statistical approaches to control for confounding: a primary analysis on a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort and a sensitivity analysis using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) on the entire cohort. The primary outcome was sinus rhythm (SR) conversion within 24 h. Secondary outcomes included length of ICU stay, acute kidney injury (AKI), and long-term mortality. The rhythm control strategy was associated with a higher 24-hour SR conversion rate compared to rate control (PSM cohort: 71.7% vs. 32.3%; OR, 2.65; P = 0.010). However, patients in the rhythm control group had a significantly longer ICU length of stay (median 3.42 vs. 3.08 days; P = 0.026). No significant differences were found in AKI incidence or long-term mortality. Subgroup analysis indicated that the benefit of SR conversion was attenuated in patients with diabetes (P for interaction < 0.05). Findings were consistent in the IPTW sensitivity analysis. Although effective for early rhythm restoration, an initial rhythm control strategy is associated with longer ICU stays and no survival benefit compared to rate control.

42911832.title: Impact of hypothermia level on neurological and renal outcomes in emergency aortic surgery: a single-centre experience.
42911832.abstract: BackgroundTemperature management during emergency surgery for acute aortic syndrome is critical for neurological, renal, and systemic protection. Recent European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) guidelines recommend moderate hypothermia with antegrade cerebral perfusion for hemiarch procedures. Nevertheless, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA) remains common. This study evaluates neurological and other postoperative outcomes across different intraoperative temperature ranges.MethodsA single-centre retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing surgery for acute aortic syndrome between 2018-2023. Demographic, intraoperative, and postoperative data on mortality, hospitalization, neurological, renal outcomes, and blood product usage were collected. Patients were stratified by intraoperative temperature: deep (≤20°C), low-moderate (20.1-24°C), high-moderate (24.1-28°C), and mild (>28°C) hypothermia. Logistic regression identified predictors of binary adverse outcomes. A sensitivity analysis was conducted using 24.0°C as the threshold in hemiarch surgery patients.ResultsA total of 175 patients (median age 64 years; 37% female) were included; of whom 89% underwent hemiarch replacement. Cardiopulmonary bypass duration decreased progressively with warmer intraoperative temperatures, ranging from 270.5 minutes in deep hypothermia to 164 minutes in mild hypothermia. The 30-day mortality was 18.9% (n = 33/175), and the overall stroke rate was 19.4% (n = 34/175). Among patients undergoing hemiarch repair, warmer temperatures were associated with lower stroke incidence (mild hypothermia 11%) compared with high-moderate (8.8%), low-moderate (26%), and deep hypothermia (27%) (p = 0.049), and with shorter intensive care admission (p = 0.036). However, multivariate regression showed that the four-category comparison did not reach significance for the assessed outcomes once adjusted for confounding variables. A sensitivity analysis at 24.0°C showed an independent association with reduced stroke risk (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.08-0.64, p = 0.005).DiscussionOur findings support current EACTS recommendations favouring moderate-to-mild hypothermia for hemiarch replacement, with potential protective effects. Further studies should determine the optimal temperature strategy for patients undergoing total arch replacement.

42910263.title: A gastric dieulafoy lesion presenting with life-threatening upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage during recovery from hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis: a case report.
42910263.abstract: Dieulafoy lesions are an uncommon but potentially life-threatening cause of non-variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding, caused by rupture of a large-caliber submucosal artery through a minute mucosal defect; diagnosis is difficult because bleeding is intermittent and the surrounding mucosa appears nearly normal. Hemorrhage from a gastric Dieulafoy lesion during recovery from hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis (HTG-AP) has rarely been reported. A man in his twenties with severe obesity presented with acute epigastric pain after alcohol and a high-fat meal. Serum triglycerides were 53.67 mmol/L (reference 0.56-1.70), and CT confirmed acute pancreatitis. Because of extreme hypertriglyceridemia and evolving organ dysfunction, he received intensive lipid-lowering therapy, plasma exchange, continuous renal replacement therapy, and supportive care in the ICU, and improved. During recovery he developed sudden massive hematemesis with tachycardia, hypotension, and a fall in hemoglobin to 65.9 g/L. Emergency endoscopy showed extensive intragastric clots and could not locate the source. After stabilization, repeat endoscopy revealed an isolated thrombus-like protrusion with active oozing on the lesser curvature near the cardia, with otherwise normal mucosa, consistent with a Dieulafoy lesion; three metallic clips achieved immediate hemostasis. Contrast-enhanced CT excluded pseudoaneurysm, splenic-vein thrombosis, gastric varices, and other pancreatitis-related vascular complications. No recurrence occurred during hospitalization or approximately seven months of follow-up, with healed mucosa on later endoscopy. A gastric Dieulafoy lesion is a rare but life-threatening cause of bleeding during recovery from HTG-AP. A nondiagnostic first endoscopy because of clot retention does not exclude it, and persistent bleeding warrants repeat endoscopy after stabilization and gastric clearance. Bleeding should not be attributed solely to stress injury or anticoagulation; an underlying structural lesion should be sought. Clipping achieved durable hemostasis in this patient, but a single case cannot establish comparative efficacy.

42910240.title: Creatinine Clearance, Ceftazidime-Avibactam Exposure, and Clinical Outcomes in a Real-World TDM Cohort: A Retrospective Observational Study.
42910240.abstract: Ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) is a key option for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) infections, but whether creatinine clearance (CrCL) independently predicts outcomes or reflects disease severity is unclear. We investigated CrCL, drug exposure, and outcomes in patients with severe Gram-negative infections receiving CAZ-AVI with therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM). This retrospective study included 224 patients receiving CAZ-AVI TDM at a tertiary hospital in China (May 2024-May 2025). Three cohorts were defined: trough-concentration (n=224) for factors influencing trough concentrations; concentration-outcome (n=194) for concentration-outcome associations using LASSO; and stable-dose (n=165) for baseline CrCL and outcomes. CrCL was analysed using restricted cubic splines and five prespecified analysis CrCL strata. Multivariable adjustment, E-values, LASSO, and bootstrap-validated ROC were used to separate CrCL from disease severity. CrCL was the dominant determinant of ceftazidime and avibactam trough concentrations (β = -0.224 and -0.047; q = 0.040 and 0.033, respectively). The unadjusted CrCL-28-day mortality association (OR 0.993, P = 0.030) was attenuated after adjusting for SOFA and APACHE II (OR 0.996, P = 0.285; E-value = 1.07) and after full adjustment (OR 0.996, P = 0.468; E-value = 1.06). LASSO retained SOFA (OR 2.18), CRRT (OR 1.88), age (OR 1.13), and ICU admission (OR 1.03), excluding CrCL. SOFA stratification showed minimal incremental prognostic value for CrCL. The exploratory multivariable model yielded an AUC of 0.760 vs 0.571 for CrCL alone (optimism-corrected AUC: 0.793 vs 0.577). CrCL drives CAZ-AVI trough-concentration variability but appears to be a marker of disease severity rather than an independent predictor of outcomes. Given the observational design and absence of individual MIC data, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. TDM may be best targeted at patients with extreme pharmacokinetic phenotypes, pending prospective validation. Prospective studies with MIC data are needed to define pathogen-specific targets.

42909099.title: Use of intraoperative right ventricular strain as a predictor of outcomes in adult heart transplant patients.
42909099.abstract: Right ventricle (RV) evaluation in the perioperative period is challenging for anesthesiologists, given the limited objective assessment methods available for transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Speckle-tracking strain imaging may offer a more objective evaluation of RV function. This study evaluated the predictive value of intraoperative RV free wall strain (RVFWS) for early outcomes following orthotopic heart transplantation (OHT). This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of 147 adults who underwent isolated OHT between January 2025 and December 2025. Patients with multiorgan transplant, congenital cases, and those without measurable intraoperative RVFWS were excluded. Post-bypass RVFWS was measured using TEE at a single time point with speckle-tracking analysis. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included severe primary graft dysfunction, 30-day mortality, need for postoperative venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), vasoactive-inotropic score, and cardiac index at 24 and 72 h, and intensive care unit length of stay. Multivariable Firth-penalized logistic and median quantile regressions were used, adjusted for a priori pre-transplant weighted risk score. The median post-bypass RVFWS was -13.9% IQR (interquartile range) -19.3 to -9.6. Fourteen recipients (9.5%) died within 90 days of transplantation. After adjusting for the pre-transplant risk score, RVFWS was independently associated with higher 90-day mortality [odds ratio (OR) 2.84 per 5% decrease in magnitude, 95% confidence interval 1.65-5.58; p < 0.001]. Among the secondary outcomes, the associations with severe primary graft dysfunction (OR 2.70; raw p = 0.001), CRRT (OR 1.58; raw p = 0.001), and 30-day mortality (OR 2.94; raw p = 0.002) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni adjustment for eleven secondary comparisons (adjusted p = 0.011, 0.011, and 0.022, respectively). RVFWS demonstrated higher discrimination for 90-day mortality [area under the curve (AUC) 0.83] than qualitative intraoperative RV grading (AUC 0.68), although this difference in AUC did not reach statistical significance. RVFWS retained independent prognostic value in a combined model. Intraoperative post-bypass RVFWS is a feasible and objective intraoperative measure that is independently associated with early adverse outcomes after adult OHT. RVFWS shows promise as a signal of early allograft dysfunction that is not fully explained by pre-transplant risk factors.

42906746.title: Hemoadsorption to prevent acute kidney injury in elective cardiac surgery: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials with meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis.
42906746.abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) improves postoperative outcomes compared with the standard of care. We systematically searched EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing hemoadsorption versus standard care in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Data were analyzed using a frequentist approach and trial sequential analysis (TSA). The primary outcome was the incidence of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) within 7 days after surgery. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025634991). A total of six RCTs comprising 798 patients were included. Four RCTs (n = 723; 355 hemoadsorption, 368 control) reported CSA-AKI incidence, which did not significantly differ between groups (RR = 0.93 [95% CI: 0.71-1.21], p =  0.57; I² = 42.0%). Hemoadsorption was not associated with significant differences in secondary outcomes: interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor, 28-day mortality, SOFA score, and ICU length of stay. Hemoadsorption during CPB was not associated with a reduction in CSA-AKI or with improvement in secondary clinical outcomes in elective patients undergoing cardiac surgery. However, the accrued sample represented only 48% of the heterogeneity-adjusted required information size (1,491 patients), and the cumulative Z-curve crossed neither the monitoring nor the futility boundary. PROSPERO International Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025634991; January 31, 2025).

42905412.title: Ex Vivo Assessment of Lamotrigine Clearance During Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy.
42905412.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) provides renal support for unstable ICU patients but significantly alters drug concentrations. For patients on long-term antiepileptics such as lamotrigine, CRRT may increase risk for breakthrough seizures due to subtherapeutic levels. Conversely, CRRT may aid in lamotrigine overdose. While partial clearance of lamotrigine by intermittent hemodialysis has been reported, CRRT clearance is not well studied. This study determined lamotrigine extraction by CRRT in an ex vivo system. Medication was administered at two concentrations: one therapeutic and one supratherapeutic to closed-loop, blood-primed, ex vivo CRRT circuits. Drug concentrations were measured in plasma, hemofiltrate (effluent), and matching control samples at specific time points. For each time point, percent recovery of lamotrigine was calculated, and differences between CRRT circuits and controls were analyzed using two-sample t-tests. Plasma lamotrigine concentrations decreased rapidly, with 10% (n = 3, SD = 4%) and 17% (n = 2, SD = 3%) recovery at four hours for therapeutic and supratherapeutic doses, respectively. Although lower starting concentrations trended toward greater clearance, differences were not statistically significant (P = .13). Control concentrations remained stable, with approximately 100% recovery. Lamotrigine concentrations were significantly affected by CRRT circuits. Patients receiving lamotrigine who require CRRT may need dosing adjustments to maintain clinical efficacy. Additionally, CRRT effectively clears lamotrigine, suggesting potential utility in overdose management.

42903855.title: Outcome-Gap Analysis of High-MELD Deceased-donor Liver Transplantation Using Institutional Reference Values from Living-donor Liver Transplantation.
42903855.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology
42903855.abstract: Benchmarking in liver transplantation has largely relied on low-risk deceased-donor or multicenter cohorts. We derived living-donor liver transplantation (LDLT)-based institutional reference values and evaluated domain-specific outcome gaps in high-Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) deceased-donor liver transplantation (DDLT) in an LDLT-dominant setting. Adult liver-transplant recipients treated at a high-volume tertiary center between June 2016 and December 2024 were analyzed. A predefined low-risk LDLT cohort was used to derive institutional reference values. Continuous cutoffs were defined as the 75th percentile of the LDLT distribution, and binary endpoints as observed LDLT event rates. High-MELD DDLT outcomes were assessed across clinical resource use, global morbidity, organ/graft dysfunction, survival/graft outcomes, and biliary-vascular complications. The cohort included 423 LDLT reference recipients and 203 high-MELD DDLT recipients. LDLT-derived cutoffs were 7.39 h for operation duration, 2 red blood cell (RBC) units, 4 intensive care unit (ICU) days, and 24 hospital days. High-MELD DDLT exceeded reference values for transfusion, ICU stay, 30-day Clavien-Dindo (C-D) grade ≥ III morbidity (49.8% vs 29.3%; gap +20.4 percentage points [pp]), acute kidney injury (AKI) stage ≥3 (6.9% vs 1.7%; gap +5.2), and early allograft dysfunction (EAD) (40.4% vs 8.7%; gap +31.6). One-year graft and patient survival were lower in high-MELD DDLT (73.6% vs 92.1% and 76.9% vs 94.5%). Biliary complications showed negative gaps, indicating graft-type-dependent morbidity that required separate interpretation. LDLT-derived institutional reference values identified high-MELD DDLT outcome gaps, mainly in clinical resource use, major morbidity, organ/graft dysfunction, graft loss, and mortality. These values may help describe excess burden without serving as exclusion thresholds.

42903445.title: Beginning Kidney Replacement Therapy Before or After Liver Transplantation: Does the Timing of Dialysis Matter? A Cohort Study.
42903445.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) in liver transplant patients is associated with increased morbidity, mortality, and reduced graft survival. However, the impact of the timing of dialysis initiation-before versus after transplantation-remains unclear. To characterize liver transplant recipients with Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Stage 3 AKI-requiring dialysis (AKI-D) according to the timing of kidney replacement therapy (KRT) initiation (pre- versus posttransplant) and to evaluate 90-day mortality. Secondary objectives included identifying independent predictors of dialysis dependence and assessing liver graft function at 90 days. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included all consecutive adult liver transplant recipients who received dialysis in a Brazilian intensive care unit (ICU) between 1999 and 2015. The study was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of the Federal University of Sao Paulo (UNIFESP), with a waiver of informed consent. Patients were grouped according to the timing of dialysis initiation: pre- or postliver transplantation. Multiple logistic regression was used to identify predictors of 90-day mortality and dialysis dependence. Ninety-day liver graft survival was analyzed using a multivariate Cox model. A total of 356 liver transplant patients with AKI-D were included. Of these, 109 (30.6%) initiated dialysis within 4 weeks before transplantation and 247 (69.4%) within 4 weeks after transplantation. The timing of dialysis initiation was not associated with 90-day mortality or dialysis dependence. Independent predictors of 90-day mortality included graft dysfunction and use of continuous KRT as the initial modality. Impaired pretransplant renal function and a history of diabetes mellitus were predictors of 90-day dialysis dependence. Posttransplant dialysis was associated with a twofold increased risk of liver graft failure. The timing of dialysis initiation (pre- versus posttransplantation) was not associated with 90-day mortality or dialysis dependence. However, initiation of dialysis after transplantation was associated with an increased risk of liver graft dysfunction.

42894613.title: Lactate as a predictive biomarker and therapeutic target in cardiopulmonary bypass-associated acute kidney injury.
42894613.abstract: Elevated lactate is a common metabolic perturbation following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). This study evaluates the clinical predictive value of lactate and explores its mechanism involving protein lactylation. Machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to multicenter intensive care databases identified preoperative lactate as a dominant predictor of CPB-acute kidney injury (AKI) risk. To validate these predictions biologically, rat CPB and cellular models were utilized. Experimental results demonstrated that CPB induces glycolytic reprogramming, lactate accumulation, and elevated pan-lysine lactylation. Inhibiting the production of lactate was associated with decreased protein lactylation, lower oxidative stress, and reduced local tissue inflammation, thereby mitigating renal injury. Collectively, our interpretable ML predictive models identify lactate as a top clinical predictor of CPB-AKI, while our experimental data establish the lactate-lactylation axis as a potential mechanistic pathway linking metabolic dysfunction to renal damage. This axis represents a candidate therapeutic target requiring further validation.

42894582.title: Incidence and Progression of Acute Kidney Injury Following Head and Neck Surgeries for COVID-19-Associated Mucormycosis: A Prospective Observational Study.
42894582.abstract: COVID-19-associated mucormycosis (CAM) surged because of the combination of systemic corticosteroids, poorly controlled diabetes mellitus, and altered host immunity. Rhino-orbito-cerebral mucormycosis (ROCM) requires extensive surgical debridement and systemic nephrotoxic liposomal amphotericin B (L-AMB) therapy. This study evaluated the incidence, temporal course, and association of postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) with various clinical factors in this high-risk surgical cohort. This prospective observational cohort study enrolled 49 adult patients who underwent major head and neck surgical debridement for ROCM and required postoperative critical care management. We excluded patients with established renal failure. We performed and recorded serial clinical and biochemical monitoring daily over the next five days. AKI incidence and severity were staged according to Acute Kidney Injury Network (AKIN) criteria. A total of 49 patients were evaluated for AKI, of which 9 developed AKI (18.4%). Patients who developed AKI had a higher mean age (56.6 ± 10.0 years versus 49.4 ± 10.3 years) and preoperative serum creatinine (1.1 ± 0.5 vs 0.9 ± 0.2 mg/dL), but these differences were not statistically significant. However, patients who developed post-operative AKI had a significantly lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (87.4 ± 27.1 vs 102.9 ± 17.4 mL/min/1.73 m²; p = 0.03), and a significantly higher prevalence of AKI was found in patients having pre-existing hypertension (77.8% vs. 32.5%; p = 0.02). Conversely, mean duration (p = 0.35), cumulative preoperative L-AMB dose (p = 0.319), and background diabetes mellitus (p = 0.136) did not differ significantly between groups. AKI was noted in nearly one-fifth of patients after ROCM surgery and was more common in older patients with hypertension and poorer baseline renal function. Baseline renal function appeared more important than cumulative L-AMB exposure or diabetes, highlighting the need for early renal risk assessment and close postoperative monitoring.

42889400.title: Timing dictates efficacy: evaluating the prophylactic and therapeutic potential of dimethyl fumarate against LPS-induced shock.
42889400.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a serious and often fatal condition that is caused by endotoxemia as a result of systemic inflammation and uncontrolled oxidative stress. Although dimethyl fumarate (DMF) has shown to have immunomodulatory and antioxidant activity, its specific prophylactic and therapeutic activity in endotoxemia-induced AKI remains unclear. to study DMF's effect on endotoxemia-induced AKI in a mouse in vivo model. We divided the mice (Swiss albino) into eight equal groups. The endotoxemia-induced AKI was treated by intraperitoneal injection with LPS (5 mg/kg). Prophylactic cohorts received oral DMF (50 or 100 mg/kg/day) for three consecutive days prior to the challenge. Therapeutic cohorts were given a single DMF dose one hour after the treatment. At six hours, gross renal function (BUN, creatinine), cytokine levels, Nrf2/HO-1 activation, oxidative damage biomarkers, inflammasome/apoptotic pathways and acute tubular necrosis (ATN) histopathology were assessed. LPS challenge resulted in severe renal dysfunction, the onset of a massive cytokine storm and acute tubular destruction. The pre-treatment of DMF prevented the TLR4/NF-κB inflammatory pathway and the overall renal cytoarchitecture was preserved. On the other hand, therapeutic DMF demonstrated a unique anti-inflammatory "ceiling effect" where both low and high doses inhibited NF-κB activation. Therapeutic DMF was more robust in structural and functional rescue, upregulating the Nrf2/HO-1 defense axis, neutralizing reactive oxygen species, and blocking the final inflammasome priming and pyroptotic actions. The timing of intervention fundamentally dictates pharmacological efficacy. Prophylaxis offers strong preventative shielding, whereas high-dose therapeutic DMF successfully mitigates ongoing oxidative storms, providing a compelling and highly translatable rationale for clinical repurposing in critical care nephrology.

42889164.title: Efficacy and safety of nafamostat mesilate for anticoagulation during ECMO/CRRT: insight from the integrated meta-analysis and FAERS pharmacovigilance study.
42889164.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) require a balance between maintaining circuit patency and minimizing bleeding risk. Nafamostat mesilate (NM) is a short-acting anticoagulant with distinctive pharmacokinetic properties, including rapid metabolism and a short half-life, which may reduce prolonged systemic anticoagulant exposure. These characteristics make NM a potential alternative to conventional anticoagulation strategies, particularly for patients at high risk of bleeding. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of NM as an anticoagulant for ECMO/CRRT. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials and cohort studies comparing NM with sodium citrate, unfractionated heparin (UFH), or no anticoagulation. A meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate filter lifespan, bleeding events, thromboembolic events, and 28-day/intensive care unit (ICU) mortality. Reporting characteristics and potential safety signals for the three anticoagulants were also compared using data from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). The meta-analysis included 17 studies involving 1,893 patients. Filter lifespan did not differ significantly between the NM and control groups (mean difference [MD] = 1.29 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.09-3.66), whereas the risk of bleeding events was significantly lower in the NM group (odds ratio [OR] = 0.61; 95% CI, 0.43-0.86). Subgroup analyses showed that NM was associated with a significantly lower risk of bleeding than sodium citrate (OR = 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.90) and no anticoagulation (OR = 0.41; 95% CI, 0.19-0.90); sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of this finding. The FAERS analysis included 24,238 reports, comprising 233 for NM, 1,612 for sodium citrate, and 22,393 for UFH, with distinct reporting profiles observed among the three anticoagulants. Representative signals for NM included disseminated intravascular coagulation (n = 17; ROR = 112.68, 95% CI: 69.69-182.19), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (n = 12; ROR = 15.44, 95% CI: 8.74-27.29), and decreased platelet count (n = 13; ROR = 7.52, 95% CI: 4.35-13.00). NM may reduce bleeding risk while maintaining a filter lifespan comparable to that achieved with other anticoagulation strategies, potentially providing an individualized anticoagulation option for patients at high risk of bleeding. In clinical practice, coagulation abnormalities, changes in platelet counts, and bleeding-related events should be closely monitored.

42882077.title: Acute Kidney Injury in Hospitalized Patients with Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Frequency, Factors Associated with AKI, and Clinical Outcomes.
42882077.abstract: Background: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is a common infectious disease associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent complication of CAP and may adversely affect clinical outcomes. This study aimed to determine the frequency of AKI and identify factors associated with AKI in hospitalized patients with CAP. Methods: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary care university hospital in Türkiye and included patients aged >18 years hospitalized with CAP between July 2024 and July 2025. Only patients initially admitted to the general ward were included. Patients receiving dialysis for end-stage renal disease, those with active malignancy, those receiving immunosuppressive therapy, and those with incomplete data were excluded. Demographic characteristics, vital signs, laboratory findings, comorbidities, smoking status, and medication histories were recorded. AKI was defined according to KDIGO criteria using the closest clinically stable pre-admission serum creatinine value obtained within 7-365 days before hospitalization as baseline. Results: Among 161 patients, AKI was identified in 60 (37.3%), including 43 patients who fulfilled the KDIGO criteria at hospital admission and 17 who developed AKI during hospitalization. Eight patients with AKI (13.3%) required hemodialysis, although none became permanently dialysis-dependent. Patients with AKI had longer hospital stays (p = 0.038) and a greater need for intensive care (p = 0.028). They were older and had higher respiratory rates, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and red cell distribution width (RDW) values and lower diastolic blood pressure. DM and CKD were more common in the AKI group. In multivariable analysis, confusion (adjusted OR 5.03, 95% CI 1.01-25.02; p = 0.048), CKD (adjusted OR 6.00, 95% CI 1.28-28.13; p = 0.023), and higher BUN levels (adjusted OR 1.095 per 1 mg/dL increase, 95% CI 1.046-1.146; p < 0.001) were independently associated with AKI. These associations were retained in a Firth penalized logistic regression sensitivity analysis. Conclusions: AKI was common among hospitalized patients with CAP and was associated with longer hospital stay and greater intensive care utilization. Confusion, pre-existing CKD, and elevated BUN levels were independently associated with AKI, whereas DM was not independently associated after multivariable adjustment. Given that most AKI cases were already present at hospital admission, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than predictors of incident AKI.

42965379.title: Robotic-Assisted Partial Nephrectomy in a Solitary Kidney in a von Hippel-Lindau Renal Cell Carcinoma.
42965379.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease is a rare autosomal dominant tumor syndrome caused by germline mutations in the VHL gene. Patients may develop multiple, bilateral, and recurrent renal cell carcinomas (RCCs), posing a major therapeutic challenge, particularly in those with a solitary kidney, where preservation of renal function is critical to prevent end-stage renal disease and dialysis dependence. This case demonstrates the surgical management of multiple renal tumors in a solitary kidney. A 37-year-old man with VHL disease (c.257C > G, p.P86R mutation) and a solitary right kidney following previous left radical nephrectomy presented with three progressive clear cell RCC (ccRCC) lesions, the largest measuring 4.8 cm, despite ongoing treatment with belzutifan, a HIF-2α inhibitor. A transperitoneal robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) was performed. A fourth tumor was identified intraoperatively. Complete excision of all tumors with negative surgical margins was achieved. Postoperatively, severe acute kidney injury (AKI) developed, requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), which was complicated by forearm necrosis resulting from calcium substitution paravasation. An additional complication included a right pneumothorax. Following intensive care management, including pleural drainage, renal function gradually recovered, and CRRT was discontinued on postoperative day 8. This case demonstrates that RAPN can provide tumor control while preserving renal tissue in patients with VHL-associated multifocal RCC and a solitary kidney. However, the procedure carries a substantial risk of severe postoperative AKI requiring temporary renal replacement therapy.

42965335.title: Efficacy and Safety of Nafamostat Mesilate Injection in Patients Receiving Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Meta-Analysis.
42965335.abstract: The objective of the study was to assess the efficacy and safety of nafamostat mesilate injection in patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Dichotomous and continuous outcomes were analyzed using fixed-effect or random-effects models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) or mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Eight studies involving 1,189 patients were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with no anticoagulation, nafamostat mesilate injection was associated with lower mortality (OR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.44-0.76; p < 0.001) and longer filter lifespan (MD, 7.00; 95% CI, 1.50-12.50; p = 0.01). These estimates were derived predominantly from nonrandomized studies and should be interpreted with caution. However, no significant difference was found between nafamostat mesilate injection and no anticoagulation in bleeding complications (OR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.51-2.34; p = 0.82), total duration of CRRT (MD, 4.46; 95% CI, -0.13-9.04; p = 0.06), the proportion of patients requiring transfusion (OR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.54-1.03; p = 0.07), and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (MD, -0.24; 95% CI, -3.85-3.37; p = 0.90) in patients receiving CRRT. The available evidence suggests that nafamostat mesilate injection may be associated with lower mortality and longer filter lifespan compared with no anticoagulation in patients receiving CRRT. However, no clear difference was observed in bleeding complications, total duration of CRRT, the proportion of patients requiring transfusion, or ICU length of stay. These findings are limited by the predominance of nonrandomized designs, small numbers of studies, and substantial heterogeneity. Additional adequately powered randomized studies are needed before clinical benefit can be considered established.

42960880.title: Plasma magnesium levels and postoperative atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery: a cohort study.
42960880.abstract: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is common after cardiac surgery, and hypomagnesemia has been proposed as a modifiable risk factor. In centers with active magnesium repletion protocols, however, overt hypomagnesemia has become uncommon. We aimed to determine whether postoperative plasma magnesium concentration is independently associated with POAF. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 435 adults undergoing cardiac surgery at a hospital specializing in cardiovascular disease. Postoperative plasma magnesium concentration, assessed at intensive care unit admission, as the mean value, and as the lowest value, was evaluated as the primary exposure in multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for relevant preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative covariates. Isolated coronary artery bypass grafting was the most frequent procedure (46.6%). Overall mortality was 3.2%, and POAF incidence was 16.8%. Under active repletion, hypomagnesemia occurred in only 3.4% of patients. None of the three magnesium measures was independently associated with POAF. In contrast, age, type of surgical procedure, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and postoperative acute kidney injury were independently associated with POAF. Under a protocol of active postoperative magnesium repletion, we did not detect an independent association between plasma magnesium concentration-within the observed normal-to-high range-and POAF. This complication was primarily related to age, type of surgery, and severe ventricular dysfunction, factors that should guide postoperative risk stratification; acute kidney injury showed a concurrent association with POAF and may act as a marker of shared postoperative risk factors rather than a causal factor.

42959808.title: Severe Rhabdomyolysis and Acute Kidney Injury Following Rosuvastatin Reinitiation During Ticagrelor Therapy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
42959808.abstract: Rhabdomyolysis is a potentially life-threatening condition characterized by skeletal muscle injury, marked elevation of creatine kinase (CK), and potential development of acute kidney injury (AKI). Statins are a well-recognized cause of rhabdomyolysis, although the risk may be influenced by concomitant medications and patient-related factors. We present a case of severe rhabdomyolysis and AKI following initiation of high-intensity rosuvastatin therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention. A 66-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted with acute coronary syndrome. Coronary angiography revealed a critical lesion in the left anterior descending artery, and a drug-eluting stent was implanted. Her low-density lipoprotein cholesterol was 184 mg/dL, and her triglycerides were 356 mg/dL. She was discharged on rosuvastatin 40 mg once daily, ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily, aspirin 75 mg once daily, perindopril, and amlodipine. One month later, she developed generalized weakness, fatigue, and severe myalgia. Initial laboratory investigations demonstrated elevated serum creatinine, alanine aminotransferase, and aspartate aminotransferase. Two days later, she developed anuria, severe muscle pain, and dark-red urine. On admission, CK and serum creatinine were markedly elevated. She denied other medication use, toxic exposure, or recent muscle trauma. Rhabdomyolysis with severe AKI was suspected, and she was admitted to the intensive care unit. Rosuvastatin was immediately discontinued, and ticagrelor was replaced with clopidogrel. Despite intravenous hydration and supportive treatment, metabolic acidosis and renal dysfunction worsened, with a serum creatinine level of 6.3 mg/dL, BUN of 82 mg/dL, and bicarbonate of 15 mmol/L. Hemodialysis was initiated. On the fourth day, she developed severe dyspnea and hypoxemia associated with pulmonary congestion, requiring additional consecutive hemodialysis sessions. Cardiac causes of pulmonary edema were excluded by electrocardiography and echocardiography. Her clinical condition subsequently stabilized, and CK and creatinine levels progressively decreased. She was discharged with continued renal monitoring, and serum creatinine decreased to 1.3 mg/dL by the third week after discharge. This case highlights the potential for severe rhabdomyolysis and AKI following high-intensity rosuvastatin therapy, particularly in patients with multiple comorbidities. Early recognition of myalgia, dark urine, oliguria, and markedly elevated CK levels is essential. Prompt discontinuation of the suspected medication, aggressive supportive management, and timely initiation of renal replacement therapy can be crucial in preventing further complications and facilitating recovery.

42959331.title: A Mixed-Methods Assessment of Health Care Professionals' Perspectives on CRRT Delivery and Opportunities for Improvement.
42959331.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is the preferred dialysis modality for critically ill patients with acute kidney injury, yet its delivery and quality vary across institutions. This study aimed to identify gaps in CRRT practice and explore strategies to improve CRRT delivery from the perspective of multidisciplinary health care professionals. Convergent parallel mixed methods. This study was conducted during the 2024 CRRT Academy and included multidisciplinary participants comprising trainees (residents and fellows), clinicians (nephrologists and intensivists), clinical staff (nurses, nurse practitioners, and pharmacists), and industry/research affiliates. Quantitative data were collected using a survey assessing CRRT practices, standardization, and collection of quality metrics. Qualitative data were obtained through 5 semistructured focus group discussions (4 with participants and 1 with CRRT Academy faculty) and were analyzed using a combined inductive-deductive thematic approach in NVivo 15. There were 83 participants: 54 trainees, 19 clinicians, 8 clinical staff, and 2 industry/research affiliates, with 10-24 participants in each focus group. The following 4 key themes were identified as relevant to improve CRRT delivery from participant focus groups: (1) teamwork and multidisciplinary communication, (2) collection and tracking of CRRT-relevant metrics, (3) protocol standardization while allowing flexibility to individualize care, and (4) education for clinicians and clinical staff. The faculty focus group emphasized the need for institutional financial support and leadership-driven quality improvement (QI) initiatives, highlighting the importance of nephrologist advocacy. Participants reported significant variability in CRRT processes, QI data collection, and education across institutions, with limited adoption of CRRT key performance indicators owing to lack of consensus and workflow integration challenges. Participants primarily represented academic centers and the majority were trainees, which may limit generalizability of the findings. However, given the paucity of mixed-methods evidence about current CRRT practice, this study provides novel insights that can help advance standardization. This study underscores key areas for improving CRRT delivery, including interprofessional collaboration, data-driven QI, protocol standardization, and targeted education. Addressing these themes may help improve CRRT processes of care and patient-centered outcomes.

42868069.title: Opsonic Peptide MOP3 Attenuates Ischemic Acute Kidney Injury.
42868069.abstract: Renal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) induced acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common and serious condition characterized by renal dysfunction, inflammation, tubular injury, and cell death. Extracellular cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (eCIRP) is a damage-associated molecular pattern that contributes to inflammation and tissue injury. MFG-E8-derived oligopeptide 3 (MOP3) is an opsonic peptide that binds eCIRP and promotes its phagocytic clearance. Here, we investigated the therapeutic effects of MOP3 in a murine model of renal I/R-induced AKI. Mice were subjected to 30 minutes of bilateral renal ischemia and treated with MOP3 or vehicle at the onset of reperfusion. Blood and kidney tissues were collected 20 h later. Renal inflammation, kidney function, tubular injury markers, histological damage, and cell death were assessed by RT-qPCR, biochemical assays, Western blotting, hematoxylin and eosin staining, and TUNEL staining. MOP3 treatment reduced circulating eCIRP by 40% and renal IL-6, IL-1β, MIP-2, and KC mRNA expression by 43%, 84%, 73%, and 69%, respectively, compared with vehicle treatment. Serum urea nitrogen, creatinine, and NGAL levels were reduced by 56%, 63%, and 44%, respectively, after MOP3 treatment. MOP3 also decreased renal KIM-1 and NGAL mRNA expression by 88% and 44% and reduced their protein levels by 29% and 45%, respectively. Furthermore, MOP3 attenuated renal tubular injury and decreased TUNEL-positive cells. These findings demonstrate that MOP3 attenuates inflammation, renal dysfunction, tubular injury, and cell death following renal I/R, suggesting that MOP3 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemic AKI.

42868027.title: The Easiest Decision in the Room: Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in Cirrhosis.

42866594.title: Comparison of the approaches to combine Renal Replacement Therapy with Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation - a Scoping Review.
42866594.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used for cardiac and respiratory failure and is associated with high rates of acute kidney injury (AKI) and fluid overload requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT). ECMO and RRT can be run independently in parallel, or RRT hemofilter or device can be integrated into the ECMO circuit. Several parallel and integrated ECMO-RRT configurations have been described, but the optimal approach remains uncertain.This scoping review mapped the available literature comparing at least two ECMO-RRT configurations, summarized reported outcomes, and identified knowledge gaps. We searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov without restrictions, with the final search conducted on February 9, 2026. Eligible studies compared at least 2 ECMO-RRT configurations linked to reported outcomes. Data on study characteristics, configurations, outcomes, and anticoagulation were extracted and synthesized. Of 6,806 records, 20 studies were included: 12 were clinical including 1 randomized controlled trial, 3 in vitro, 1 in silico, and 4 surveys. More than 8 ECMO-RRT connection schemes have been described by clinical studies since 2013. No consistent differences in efficiency or clinical outcomes were observed between the configurations compared. Integrated methods were associated with longer or comparable hemofilter lifespan. Surveys confirmed heterogeneous medical practices, and 2 safety concerns (unstoppable pressure alarms and air embolism) were reported. Evidence on ECMO-RRT configurations is limited and heterogeneous. Future systematic and rigorous comparison of all the configurations through preclinical and clinical studies is needed to harmonize medical practices and inform the development of guidelines.

42842391.title: Individualized Treatment Effects of Cefepime vs Piperacillin-Tazobactam in Adults Hospitalized with Acute Infection.
42842391.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
authors: Evidence-based Individualized Treatment Effects (EvITE) Group and the Pragmatic Critical Care Research Group
42842391.abstract: Among adults hospitalized with acute infection, a recent randomized trial observed no significant average treatment effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam on acute kidney injury or death, but fewer days-alive-and-free-of delirium and coma with cefepime. To determine whether patients' individual characteristics modify the effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam on outcomes. In this secondary analysis of the Antibiotic Choice On Renal Outcomes (ACORN) trial, an effect model was derived and validated to predict the effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam for adults hospitalized with acute infection. The primary outcome was survival without acute kidney injury; the secondary outcome was survival without delirium or coma. The individualized treatment effect predicted in the validation cohort significantly modified the effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam on survival without acute kidney injury (Qini 1.68; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.25-3.18; p-value = 0.01). Among 626 patients predicted to experience ≥5% benefit from cefepime, 81.2% of patients randomized to cefepime survived without acute kidney injury, versus 74.2% randomized to piperacillin-tazobactam (difference, 7.1%; 95%CI, 0.25 to 13.9%). Among 203 patients predicted to experience ≥5% benefit from piperacillin-tazobactam, 56.6% of patients randomized to cefepime survived without acute kidney injury, versus 63.0% randomized to piperacillin-tazobactam (difference, -6.3%; 95%CI, -20.7 to 8.2%). The effect of trial group on survival without delirium or coma was not modified by individual characteristics. Patients' individual characteristics modified the effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam on survival without acute kidney injury but not on survival without delirium or coma.

42919415.title: Clinical prediction models in cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
42919415.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) is a frequent postoperative complication associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Clinical prediction models (CPM) may identify high-risk patients enabling targeted preventive interventions and improved outcomes. The objective of the study was to identify available CPMs for the risk of developing CSA-AKI and summarize their performance. A systematic search of studies published in Pubmed, Scopus, the Chocrane Library and Web of Science was conducted, including studies that developed or validated CPMs for CSA-AKI in adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. Data were extracted by two independent reviewers. Summary measures of diagnostic performance were calculated when feasible using random-effects models. Calibration and sensitivity analyses were also performed. The pooled incidence of CSA-AKI was 26.3% (95% CI, 26.0-26.4), whereas CSA-AKI requiring renal replacement therapy (CSA-AKI RRT) occurred in 2.2% of patients (95% CI, 2.1-2.2). Among validated CPMs, Thakar 2005 demonstrated the best predictive performance for CSA-AKI RRT: pooled AUC 0.80 (95% CI, 0.77-0.82), sensitivity of 0.87, and a specificity of 0.49 at a threshold of ≥ 3 points. Calibration analyses indicated underestimation of risk. The Mehta 2006 and Wijeysundera 2007 models also demonstrated good discrimination. Discrimination for the prediction of milder stages of CSA-AKI was poorer, but newer models such as the Demirjian 2022 model showed promising performance. Accurate and well-validated CPMs can facilitate risk stratification for CSA-AKI which can influence clinical practice and research. Thakar 2005 demonstrated very good discrimination for predicting CSA-AKI RRT, whereas more validation studies for the prediction of milder stages of CSA-AKI are warranted.

42895972.title: Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation in Dextrocardia: Lessons From a Complex Redo Case.
42895972.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42895972.abstract: Dextrocardia with situs solitus poses significant surgical challenges for left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, particularly in patients with prior sternotomy and complex valvular disease. We report on a 60 year old man with dextrocardia, advanced heart failure, prior mechanical mitral valve replacement, and bicuspid aortic valve disease who underwent successful Corheart 6 LVAD implantation during redo sternotomy with concomitant bioprosthetic aortic and mitral valve replacement. Intraoperative findings included extensive pannus/thrombus on the mechanical mitral prosthesis (causing relative stenosis) and an unsuspected 10 g left atrial thrombus, both of which were removed. Total cardiopulmonary bypass time was 330 minutes, and aortic cross‑clamp time was 233 minutes. Postoperative acute kidney injury requiring dialysis resolved, and the patient was discharged after 137 days. At 1 year follow-up, the left ventricular end-diastolic diameter decreased from 69 to 66 mm, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) remained stable (28-25%), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class improved from IIIb‑IV to II, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) recovered from 32 ml/min at 9 months to 51 ml/min at 1 year.

42890494.title: Renal microcirculation in acute kidney injury: bridging haemodynamics, inflammation and repair.
42890494.abstract: The kidneys receive a disproportionately high share of cardiac output relative to their mass, reflecting their central role in solute clearance and fluid regulation. The renal microcirculation is anatomically complex and regionally heterogeneous, with steep gradients in perfusion and oxygen tension from cortex to medulla. This architecture supports efficient filtration and reabsorption but renders specific nephron segments supply-dependent and susceptible to injury during haemodynamic instability, hypoxia, inflammation, or exposure to toxins. These vulnerabilities can lead to acute kidney injury (AKI), where microvascular dysfunction often precedes changes in global renal perfusion. The renal microvasculature comprises glomerular capillaries followed by efferent arterioles supplying either cortical peritubular capillaries or the medullary vasa recta. Regional endothelial heterogeneity, limited medullary oxygen availability, countercurrent oxygen shunting, and the high metabolic demand of tubular sodium transport create intrinsic susceptibility to injury. In AKI, sepsis, ischaemia-reperfusion, surgery, nephrotoxins, and venous congestion may trigger early endothelial activation and glycocalyx injury, promoting increases permeability, leukocyte and platelet adhesion, altered vascular tone, capillary obstruction, and interstitial oedema. These changes impair perfused capillary density and oxygen diffusion. Microvascular dysfunction may persist despite normalisation of systemic haemodynamics, reflecting a loss of haemodynamic coherence and contributing to regional hypoxia and reduced glomerular filtration.Tubular injury further amplifies these abnormalities. Reduced NaCl reabsorption increases delivery to the macula densa, activates tubuloglomerular feedback, and promotes afferent vasoconstriction, while tubular obstruction, filtrate backleak, and interstitial pressure oppose filtration and compromise peritubular perfusion. The relative contribution of these mechanisms differs across sepsis-associated, ischaemia-reperfusion, perioperative, nephrotoxic, congestive, and predominantly haemodynamic AKI phenotypes.When repair is incomplete, persistent endothelial dysfunction, pericyte detachment, capillary rarefaction, chronic hypoxia, and fibrosis promote nephron dropout, loss of renal functional reserve, and progression from AKI to chronic kidney disease. Clinical assessment currently relies on complementary surrogates, including perfusion imaging, venous congestion assessment, oxygenation monitoring, and endothelial or tubular biomarkers. Renal microvascular dysfunction contributes to the initiation, functional expression, persistence, and long-term consequences of AKI. A phenotype-oriented approach integrating perfusion, congestion, oxygenation, endothelial injury, and tubulo-vascular interactions may improve mechanistic understanding and support the development of targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies.
