42958591.title: Recalibrating the urine output criteria for acute kidney injury: stage-specific thresholds matched to creatinine-stage-derived mortality.

42818624.title: Comparative evaluation of five nutrition-inflammation indices for predicting 28-day ICU mortality in critically ill patients with bone infections: a dual-cohort study with external validation and interpretable machine learning.
42818624.abstract: Malnutrition and systemic inflammation are highly prevalent among critically ill patients with bone infections and may independently predict adverse outcomes. Five composite nutrition-inflammation indices-the modified Nutrition Risk in the Critically Ill (mNUTRIC) score, Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI), Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI), Index of Nutritional Assessment (INA), and Hemoglobin-Albumin-Lymphocyte-Platelet (HALP) score-have been proposed as prognostic tools; however, their comparative performance in the bone infection intensive care unit (ICU) population has not been systematically defined. A dual-cohort retrospective study design was employed. The internal derivation cohort comprised ICU patients with bone infections from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database (n = 917; 28-day ICU mortality 12.1%), and the external validation cohort was drawn from the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University (n = 256; 28-day mortality 16.0%). All five indices were calculated from laboratory and clinical data collected within 24 h of ICU admission. Multivariable logistic regression (three hierarchical adjustment models), restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and subgroup analyses were performed to examine the independent associations of each index with 28-day ICU mortality. For predictive model development, a dual LASSO-Boruta feature selection strategy was applied to the derivation cohort, yielding 14 core features (events-per-variable ratio [EPV] = 7.9). Five machine learning (ML) models - logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), XGBoost, LightGBM, and support vector machine (SVM) - were trained with synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) and five-fold stratified cross-validation. Discriminative performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). The optimal model was further evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values computed directly for the final LightGBM model with external stability validation, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). A fully nested cross-validation with feature selection repeated within each training fold confirmed the robustness of the external performance. A total of 917 ICU patients with bone infections were included in the derivation cohort. In the fully adjusted model, HALP lowest tertile (T1, ≤ 171.11; odds ratio [OR] = 3.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.13-5.46, p < 0.001) and low PNI (< 45; OR = 2.48, 95% CI 1.09-5.66, p = 0.031) remained independently associated with 28-day ICU mortality, whereas the associations of mNUTRIC, GNRI, and INA were attenuated to non-significance after full adjustment. RCS analysis confirmed a significant nonlinear dose-response relationship for HALP (p-nonlinearity < 0.001). In both cohorts, PNI (derivation AUROC 0.761; external 0.742) and HALP (0.745; 0.713) demonstrated the highest discriminative performance among the five indices, while GNRI lost discrimination owing to a near-universal at-risk classification (94.9% of the derivation cohort). Subgroup analysis showed the HALP-mortality association was consistent across all clinical strata (all interaction p > 0.27). Among ML models, LightGBM achieved the highest external AUROC (0.956, 95% CI 0.921-0.985). SHAP analysis of the final LightGBM model identified APS III, acute kidney injury (AKI), and arterial oxygen tension (PO2) as the most important predictors, with the ranking highly stable in the external validation cohort. DCA demonstrated superior net clinical benefit for the ML model over any single index across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. Among five nutrition-inflammation indices evaluated in critically ill patients with bone infections, HALP and PNI were the leading independent predictors of 28-day ICU mortality, with HALP showing a robust, strongly nonlinear threshold effect that was consistent across all subgroups and adjustment models. In contrast to its dominant role in cardiothoracic populations, GNRI lost discriminative value here because nearly all patients were classified as at-risk. An interpretable ML model integrating 14 routinely available clinical features achieved excellent external discrimination (AUROC = 0.956) and clinical utility, supporting its potential as a decision-support tool for early risk stratification in this high-risk population.

42819542.title: Case Report: Coinfection of influenza A and Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia.
42819542.abstract: The coinfection of influenza A and Chlamydia psittaci pneumoniae is rarely described in China. However, the clinical features of these diseases pose a significant diagnostic challenge. Therefore, it is necessary to report and review such a potentially fatal case. We report an 89-year-old male patient requiring admission to the intensive care unit with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, shock and MODS. He presented with fever, fatigue, anorexia and dyspnea. The patient exhibited severe hypoxemia, shock, hepatic dysfunction (elevated liver enzymes and serum bilirubin), acute kidney injury and a SOFA score of 17. Mechanical ventilation (MV) and venous-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) were established for respiratory support. The initial diagnosis focused on influenza A for his positive influenza A nucleic acid. However, the patient's imaging presentation was not coupled with viral pneumonia, which raised suspicion for other pathogens. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected coinfection of C psittaci, influenza A H3N2 virus, and Klebsiella pneumoniae in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Concurrent targeted NGS (tNGS) detected C. psittaci in blood. Omadacycline and baloxavir marboxil were prescribed. The patient's condition improved, and he was successfully weaned from VV-ECMO and MV. He was discharged and recovered on day 60 of the follow-up. This case underscores the diagnostic complexity of coinfection and the use of NGS testing in this severe condition and the role of omadacycline in psittacosis.

42820515.title: A secondary analysis of the SODa-BIC randomized clinical trial using multiple hierarchical composite outcomes.
42820515.abstract: The Sodium Bicarbonate for Metabolic Acidosis in the ICU (SODa-BIC) trial assessed the effect of sodium bicarbonate on Major Adverse Kidney Events at 30 days (MAKE30) in critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis. Although the trial demonstrated no significant difference in the primary outcome, the individual components showed differing magnitudes and directions of effect; we undertook an exploratory analysis of the SODa-BIC trial using different hierarchical outcomes to better understand potential treatment effects of sodium bicarbonate. Post-hoc analysis of the SODa-BIC trial. All patients included in the SODa-BIC trial were eligible. The primary outcome was a win ratio analysis with a hierarchy consisting of death, requirement for renal replacement therapy, persistent renal dysfunction, and hospital length of stay. Several sensitivity and subgroup analyses were conducted. The primary analysis resulted in 59,250 pairs from 488 patients. Consistent with the SODa-BIC analysis, there was no overall evidence of a treatment effect of sodium bicarbonate, with a win ratio of 0.97 (95%CI 0.79 - 1.19) and a Desirability of Outcome Ranking probability of 0.49 (95%CI 0.45 - 0.54). A majority of pairwise comparisons were resolved by mortality and hospital length of stay. Evidence of significant treatment effect modification was observed across subgroups defined by acute kidney injury and severity of acidemia. In this post-hoc analysis of the SODa-BIC trial, the use of hierarchical composite outcomes did not alter the neutral overall interpretation of the original trial. However, this analysis provides additional insight into the relative contribution of individual components of the primary outcome.

42822699.title: Survival outcomes after liver transplantation in acute-on-chronic liver failure: A prospective study.
authors: Investigators of the CHANCE study group
42822699.abstract: The impact of liver transplantation (LT) on mortality among patients with advanced cirrhosis who have two organ failures (acute-on-chronic liver failure-2 [ACLF-2]) or ≥ three organ failures (ACLF-3) is unclear. Adults with decompensated cirrhosis with or without ACLF (grades 1-3), undergoing LT at 63 liver transplant centers worldwide were prospectively enrolled between 2021 and 2023 and followed for one year. Patients with ACLF-2 or ACLF-3 who were declined for LT were also prospectively followed for one year. Among the 144 patients declined for LT, 73% of those included with ACLF-2 and 88% of those with ACLF-3 died within 1 year. Of the 612 transplanted patients, 2% were re-transplanted and 12% died during the year. According to ACLF status at LT, the case-fatality rate without re-transplantation was 21% with ACLF-3 (42% when patients had five or six organ failures), 10.5% with ACLF-2, 10% with ACLF-1 (one organ failure), and 9% without ACLF. During the post-LT period, ACLF-3 patients experienced longer intensive care stay but similar ward stay, readmission rate and requirement for long-term renal replacement therapy. In time-to-event multivariable analyses, variables that were associated with higher post-LT mortality were being transplanted in Asia (vs. Europe or North America) or having ACLF-3 at LT (vs. no ACLF). The risk of dying after LT was similar in Asia vs. Latin America or with ACLF-2 vs. no ACLF. Patients with severe ACLF who underwent LT showed markedly better survival outcomes than those who were declined. Patients with five or six organ failures had high risk of post-LT death cautioning against routine LT in this population. ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04613921.

42967895.title: Acute liver failure triggered by hemolytic crisis in a glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficient patient with hepatitis A: A case report.
42967895.abstract: Hepatitis A virus infection is one of the most common causes of acute viral hepatitis and usually results in a mild, self-limiting illness. (Biju Illolil Kuniyil) However, in rare cases, it can progress to acute liver failure, particularly in vulnerable individuals. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency is one of the most common enzymatic disorders globally. This X-linked condition predisposes red blood cells to oxidative damage and acute hemolytic episodes triggered by infections, drugs, or foods. (Aradhana Aneja) We report a 53-year-old man who presented with acute hepatitis and subsequently developed severe intravascular hemolysis, acute kidney injury, and acute liver failure. Fractionated bilirubin demonstrated significant indirect hyperbilirubinemia, and lactate dehydrogenase levels were markedly elevated, supporting intravascular hemolysis. A quantitative enzyme assay confirmed glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency. The patient developed coagulopathy and Grade II hepatic encephalopathy, fulfilling diagnostic criteria for acute liver failure. He required intravenous N-acetylcysteine, therapeutic plasma exchange, and hemodialysis. The patient recovered following multidisciplinary intensive care. This case highlights the importance of recognising glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency in patients with viral hepatitis who develop disproportionate anaemia and hyperbilirubinemia.

42967049.title: Extensive Stray-Dog Mauling as Major Contaminated Crush Trauma Causing Severe Rhabdomyolysis, Acute Kidney Injury, and Overt Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation: Recovery Without Renal Replacement Therapy.
42967049.abstract: An adolescent male developed severe rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, overt disseminated intravascular coagulation, and respiratory fluid overload after extensive stray-dog mauling. The course reflected overlapping traumatic, inflammatory, and infectious mechanisms. He recovered without renal replacement therapy through source control, individualized antimicrobials, conservative renal support, and timely transition to de-resuscitation.

42970124.title: Sodium bicarbonate therapy for metabolic acidosis in critically ill patients: a Bayesian systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
42970124.abstract: To evaluate the effects of sodium bicarbonate therapy on mortality and renal outcomes in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis. We performed a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intravenous sodium bicarbonate with placebo or usual care in adult intensive care unit patients with metabolic acidosis. MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL were searched from inception to December 2025, with an updated search on 2 April 2026. The primary outcome was short-term all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT) initiation, 90-day mortality, RRT-free days, vasopressor-free days, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay and adverse events. Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed. Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%. For RRT initiation, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk (RR 0.74, 95% CrI 0.59-0.98), with a posterior probability of benefit of 97.2%. Effects on other outcomes were small or imprecise, and no consistent safety signal was identified. Current randomised evidence does not demonstrate a clear survival benefit from sodium bicarbonate therapy in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis, but suggests a high probability of reducing RRT initiation. Further trials should define the patients most likely to benefit. PROSPERO registration: CRD420251246519.

42968967.title: Severe Propofol Infusion Syndrome Managed With Multimodal Critical Care: A Case Report.
42968967.abstract: Rapid cardiovascular collapse with severe metabolic derangement during propofol sedation should raise concern for propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS). A 21-year-old man with previous traumatic brain injury presented with refractory status epilepticus requiring mechanical ventilation and prolonged propofol sedation. Following four days of infusion, he developed abrupt bradycardia, cardiogenic shock, severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, hypertriglyceridemia, and significant left ventricular dysfunction. The combination of prolonged propofol exposure and rapidly evolving multiorgan failure was considered consistent with PRIS. Propofol was discontinued immediately. Management included administration of multiple vasoactive infusions, sodium bicarbonate, calcium chloride, dual high-effluent continuous renal replacement therapy via two dialysis circuits, high-dose euglycemic insulin, and enteral L-carnitine. Hemodynamic improvement occurred within approximately six hours, followed by recovery of cardiac and renal function. He was discharged from the intensive care unit on day 30 and later returned home after rehabilitation without dialysis dependence. This case highlights the importance of early recognition of PRIS and rapid escalation of individualized organ support in severe presentations, while acknowledging that the contribution of individual adjunctive therapies cannot be determined from a single case.

42971097.title: V-V ECMO for refractory near-fatal asthma: A 12-year single-centre observational study of clinical outcomes and psychological impact.
42971097.abstract: To review the clinical data of adult patients receiving veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) for near-fatal asthma at a single UK respiratory ECMO centre, including morbidity and mortality follow up. Retrospective single-centre case series (2013-2025). A specialized UK respiratory ECMO centre. 79 adult patients with near-fatal asthma refractory to maximal conventional critical care management including mechanical ventilation. Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. 79 patients (median age 35 years, 53% female and 47% male) were included. Pre-ECMO physiological derangement was profound (median pH 7.05, PaCO2 14.7 kPa). Median ECMO duration was 3 days (IQR 2-4). Survival to ICU discharge and 6-month survival was 98.7%. Complications occurred in 27.8% of patients, most frequently acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy (10.1%). At 6-month follow-up, clinically significant anxiety and depression were present in 27.9% and 20.9% of survivors, respectively, while 37.2% screened positive for post-traumatic stress symptoms. Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) represents an effective rescue therapy for patients with refractory near-fatal asthma, demonstrating excellent short- and long-term survival outcomes when applied in carefully selected cases. The incidence of complications remains acceptable and manageable within this context. The prevalence of anxiety and depression in this cohort appears to be lower than that reported in a published systematic review of the broader ECMO population; however, rates of post-traumatic stress symptoms are comparatively higher.

42970339.title: Cefepime Dose Individualization in Early Sepsis: A Pragmatic Feasibility Trial Protocol.
authors: Beta-Lactam Optimization and Outcomes Management (BLOOM) Study Group
42970339.abstract: Cefepime is a core antibiotic in sepsis treatment, yet standard dosing yields 10- to 30-fold exposure variability in critical illness. In the early "golden hours" of sepsis, low cefepime levels (affecting up to 70% of cases) may lead to organ dysfunction progression, treatment failure, and antimicrobial resistance. Empiric dose escalation to overcome low levels can increase the risk of dose-dependent neurotoxicity. We developed and qualified a population pharmacokinetic model using patient weight and estimated glomerular filtration rate from creatinine and cystatin C that, in simulation, improved attainment of effective and safe drug levels. To describe the Beta-Lactam Optimization and Outcomes Management (BLOOM) 1 pragmatic feasibility trial. This single-center, cluster-randomized, pragmatic feasibility trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07287332) was approved with a waiver of informed consent. Participants are critically ill adults (age ≥ 18 yr), hospitalized at Mayo Clinic (Rochester, MN), who are receiving cefepime for suspected or documented sepsis. A screening tool embedded in the electronic health record (EHR) identifies eligible patients newly initiated on cefepime (≤ 1 previous dose in 48 hr) who are then randomized to care groups (clusters) that use an individualized dosing algorithm (intervention) or usual-care dosing (control). Exclusions are cephalosporin allergy, acute kidney injury, kidney replacement therapy, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and missing inputs required for the algorithm (weight, creatinine, cystatin C). Recruitment began on January 15, 2026, and is expected to conclude by January 2027 (target enrollment, ≥ 300 patients). For eligible patients, EHR-embedded clinical decision support prompts the cluster-assigned dosing approach, with final dose decisions made by the clinical team. Feasibility, fidelity, and exploratory pharmacokinetic and clinical outcomes will be assessed using mixed methods. This workflow-integrated pragmatic feasibility trial will determine whether personalized cefepime dosing can be implemented in routine practice to optimize timely sepsis therapy while maintaining safety.

42970569.title: Machine learning for predicting mortality in patients with sepsis and its associated complications: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
42970569.abstract: Sepsis remains a leading cause of death in intensive care units worldwide and may be accompanied by complex complications, including encephalopathy, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, myocardial dysfunction, and delirium, each of which substantially increases the risk of poor outcomes. Machine learning, a promising approach for prognostic prediction, can capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical risk factors. However, its predictive performance in sepsis and its specific complications remains unclear. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for relevant literature through April 2026. Studies that aimed to develop or validate machine learning models to predict mortality in adult patients with sepsis and its associated complications were included. The random-effects or bivariate model was used to calculate the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. Overall, machine learning models show moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis, with a combined AUC of 0.82 for the training set (46 studies, 15 models) and 0.79 for the validation set (50 studies, 25 models). Logistic regression is the most widely evaluated model, demonstrating stable performance (validation AUC = 0.81). Integrated methods, including random forest and XGBoost, performed equally well, with AUCs between 0.81 and 0.83 in both groups. Although LightGBM and DL-CMT achieved the highest AUCs in the training and validation sets, respectively, both estimates were based on a single study. Among the complications, the evidence for sepsis-associated encephalopathy (AUC = 0.81, 3 studies) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (AUC = 0.80, 4 studies) is the most conclusive and best demonstrated. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury showed moderate and stable performance (validation AUC = 0.79, 4 studies). Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy showed significant attenuation from training to validation (AUC 0.84 vs 0.78, all from a single study), and random forest performed well in training (AUC = 0.98) but was not widely reported. Septic shock reached the highest AUC (0.95), but this was based on a single study. The predictive utility of sepsis-associated delirium is limited (AUC = 0.67, 1 study), and sepsis-induced myocardial injury is moderate (AUC = 0.77, 1 study).For long-term mortality, evidence is extremely lacking. Only SAE (AUC 0.88 during training and 0.86 during validation) and SCRS (combined AUC 0.76) provided single study estimates, ruling out reliable conclusions. In this meta-analysis, machine learning models showed moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis. Among complications, SAE and SIC had the strongest evidence and best performance, whereas SAD showed limited utility. Evidence for long-term mortality was extremely scarce. These findings support the potential role of machine learning in early prognostic risk stratification, yet they also highlight the urgent need for rigorous external validation and higher-quality studies, particularly for under-investigated complications.

42971011.title: Electrical burn injury and rhabdomyolysis.
42971011.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42971011.abstract: Electrical burns account for 3-5% of burn admissions, with high morbidity and mortality due to deep muscle injury and systemic complications. Rhabdomyolysis is common and a major contributor to acute kidney injury and death. To review the current evidence on the pathophysiology, systemic complications, diagnosis, and management of electrical burn injuries, with particular emphasis on rhabdomyolysis and its implications for intensive care management. A structured narrative review of the literature on electrical burn injuries was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Scopus, with a focus on rhabdomyolysis and its implications for acute kidney injury. Rhabdomyolysis is a frequent event in patients with electrical burns and represents a major factor in the development of acute kidney injury. Creatine phosphokinase > 5000 IU/L and myoglobinuria are associated with an increased risk of renal complications. Early fluid resuscitation and prompt recognition of compartment syndrome improve outcomes. Evidence does not support routine use of alkalinization or mannitol. Renal replacement therapy should be guided by conventional indications for acute kidney injury, as current evidence does not support its prophylactic initiation. Early identification of rhabdomyolysis and optimization of renal perfusion are critical. An evidence-based practical framework is presented.

42968961.title: Optimizing Polymyxin B Exposure in Carbapenem-Resistant Organism-Associated Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia: A Retrospective Observational Study.
42968961.abstract: The area under the 24-hour concentration-time curve (AUC0-24h) is a key pharmacokinetic parameter for polymyxin B (PMB), but the optimal exposure target in critically ill patients remains uncertain. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PMB AUC0-24h and clinical efficacy in patients with carbapenem-resistant hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP), and to identify the optimal therapeutic AUC0-24h range for PMB. This retrospective observational study included patients with carbapenem-resistant HAP who received intravenous PMB and therapeutic drug monitoring. Plasma PMB concentrations were measured by validated ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS). The primary outcome was 14-day clinical treatment success, and the secondary outcome included acute kidney injury (AKI). Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess exposure-outcome relationships. A total of 138 patients were included, the median age was 68 years, and 110 (79.7%) were male. Clinical success was achieved in 63 (45.7%) patients. Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii accounted for 77.5% of infections. The median AUC0-24h of PMB was 77.5 (55.6, 105.6) mg·h/L. An AUC0-24h > 77 mg·h/L enabled to predict the clinical treatment success, while AUC0-24h > 110 mg·h/L enabled to predict the AKI incidence. In multivariable analysis, AUC0-24h < 77 mg·h/L was an independent risk factor for reduced clinical treatment success (OR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13-0.78; p = 0.013), while AUC0-24h > 110 mg·h/L significantly increased AKI risk (OR: 3.24, 95% CI: 1.06-10.47; p = 0.043). The AUC0-24h of PMB is closely associated with both 14-day clinical treatment success rates and the incidence of AKI in patients with carbapenem-resistant HAP, with an optimal range from 77 to 110 mg·h/L.

42970131.title: The right drug in the wrong biological state? Alkaline phosphatase and cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury.

42978718.title: Carbapenem Renal Dose Discordance and Acute Kidney Injury in the Intensive Care Unit: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
42978718.journal: The Journal of pharmacy technology : jPT : official publication of the Association of Pharmacy Technicians
42978718.abstract: Renal function changes rapidly in the intensive care unit (ICU), and carbapenem dosing above renal-adjusted recommendations is a potentially preventable medication safety issue. To evaluate the association between carbapenem renal dose discordance and acute kidney injury (AKI); treatment failure was exploratory. This ethics-approved retrospective cohort included adults receiving carbapenems for at least 48 hours in a Vietnamese hospital ICU (January 2024-April 2026). Discordance was at least 1 day above renal-adjusted recommendations based on estimated Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance and clinical indication. Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria defined AKI. Robust Poisson regression estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs). Matched outcome models additionally adjusted for Glasgow Coma Scale category and septic shock. A post hoc Bonferroni threshold of α = .003125 was applied. Of 490 patients, 78 (15.9%) had discordant dosing. Acute kidney injury occurred in 28/78 (35.9%) with discordant dosing versus 18/412 (4.4%) with concordant dosing. Discordance was associated with AKI in the primary analysis (aRR, 8.061; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.135-15.714; P < .001) and among 68 matched pairs (aRR, 5.937; 95% CI, 2.112-16.694; P = .001). Associations with treatment failure did not meet the corrected threshold in the primary analysis (aRR, 1.586; 95% CI, 1.023-2.458; P = .039) or among matched pairs (aRR, 1.164; 95% CI, 0.723-1.875; P = .532). Carbapenem renal dose discordance was associated with AKI, although causation cannot be established. Daily renal dose review by pharmacists is a practical medication safety target that warrants prospective evaluation.

42978852.title: Hypotension prediction index to predict hemodynamic instability related to renal replacement therapy in critically ill patients: A prospective observational study.
42978852.abstract: Fluid removal during continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is a frequent cause of hemodynamic instability (HI) in critically ill patients, yet clinicians lack reliable tools to anticipate intolerance to ultrafiltration. We aimed to determine the performance and clinical utility of the hypotension prediction index (HPI) to predict HI in critically ill patients undergoing fluid removal with CRRT. We conducted a prospective observational study including consecutive patients receiving CRRT with fluid removal in a tertiary intensive care unit (ICU) of Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Vaudois, Lausanne, Switzerland, between March 2022 and August 2023. Arterial pressure waveforms were recorded using FloTrac and HemoSphere Advanced Monitor and HPI was computed every 20 s (offline, for blinding). An HPI alarm was defined as three consecutive HPI values ≥85; an HI event was defined as three consecutive mean arterial pressure readings <65 mmHg, initiation or escalation of vasopressor therapy, or clinical signs of hemodynamic intolerance. We evaluated the performance of HPI for predicting HI within the following 15-min window. To assess HPI clinical utility at bedside, we computed alarm-to-event delays, the proportion of HPI alarms followed by HI and the proportion of HI preceded by at least one HPI alarm. We repeated analyses considering only "new" alarms and "new" HI, defined respectively as alarms and HI events preceded by a 60-min event-free interval. We recorded 223,660 observations corresponding to 1243 h of monitoring. HPI was ≥85 in 33.4% of observations and MAP <65 mmHg in 11.0%. Overall, HPI demonstrated good discriminative performance for predicting HI (area under the curve of the receiver operating characteristic curve=0.89), with high sensitivity (99.7%) and specificity (81.6%). However, positive predictive value (PPV) was low, as only 54.7% of alarms were followed by HI, with a mean alarm-to-event delay of 103 s. Bootstrapped analyses performed to adjust for varying importance of individual patients confirmed these findings. When considering new alarms (n=147) and events (n=174), only 33 (22.4%) alarms were followed by an HI, and 34 (19.4%) HI were preceded by an alarm. Sensitivity analyses considering a lower cutoff for HPI and a shorter event-free period to define a new event confirmed these findings. Although HPI shows excellent statistical performance for predicting HI during CRRT with fluid removal, its clinical utility is limited by short time-to-event delay, frequent false-positive alarms, and prolonged time with high HPI values. These findings underscore the gap between predictive accuracy and bedside utility of monitoring tools in critical care.

42978892.title: What's new in the management of acute kidney injury in the ICU?

42978866.title: Occurrence of hypoxic liver injury in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: A retrospective cohort study.
42978866.abstract: Hypoxic liver injury (HLI) is a frequent and life-threatening complication occurring in up to 10% of critically ill patients. HLI can be typically found in a setting of cardiac, circulatory, or respiratory failure. Data regarding the occurrence, course, and outcome of HLI in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is scarce. This study aimed to investigate the incidence, clinical characteristics, and outcome of HLI in critically ill, mechanically ventilated patients with ARDS. This is a single-center, retrospective observational study conducted at the intensive care units (ICUs) of a tertiary-care university hospital in Hamburg, Germany from December 1, 2017 to April 30, 2021. It includes all consecutive critically ill adult patients who met the Berlin Definition criteria for moderate or severe ARDS and required invasive mechanical ventilation within 48 h of ICU admission and for more than 48 h. Clinical course characteristics and key laboratory markers were systematically compared and analyzed according to HLI diagnostic status across all enrolled patients. HLI was defined according to established criteria as elevation of aminotransferase levels (>20-fold upper-limit-of-normal). Predictors of HLI occurrence, clinical course, and outcome were assessed. In total, 434 critically ill patients with ARDS were included. During the ICU stay, 22.4% (n=97) developed HLI. Baseline characteristics including age, sex, and body mass index were comparable between patients with and without HLI. The median Charlson Comorbidity Index was comparable in both groups (3 vs. 3 points; P=0.36). A higher disease severity on admission represented by the sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) score was observed in patients with HLI (11 vs. 10 points; P <0.001). The median arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2)/ fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) ratio was 81 mmHg (interquartile range [IQR]: 60-109 mmHg) in patients with HLI compared to 79 mmHg (IQR: 60-106 mmHg) in patients without HLI, respectively (P=0.900). Overall, 35.0% (n=152) of patients required veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation therapy, including 39.2% (n=38) within the HLI group and 33.8% (n=114) without HLI. The incidence of renal replacement therapy (RRT) was 87.6% (n=85) among patients with HLI and 53.1% (n=179) among those without HLI (P <0.001). ICU mortality was 74.2% (n=72) and 58.2% (n=196) in the patients with or without HLI, respectively (P <0.001). Regression analysis identified cholestasis (odds ratio [OR]=2.061, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.220 to 3.481, P <0.010) and RRT (OR=4.732, 95% CI: 2.416 to 9.267, P <0.001) as factors significantly associated with new-onset HLI. Occurrence of HLI was independently associated with mortality (hazard ratio [HR]=1.710, 95% CI: 1.273 to 2.297, P <0.001). HLI is a common condition in critically ill patients with ARDS, and its occurrence is highly associated with mortality. HLI may serve as prognostic marker in critically ill patients with ARDS.

42978886.title: Global heterogeneity and implementation gap in acute kidney injury prevention: Results from the AKI-PURIFY survey.
42978886.abstract: Despite substantial advances in critical care nephrology, the real-world implementation of diagnostic tools and evidence-based preventive strategies for acute kidney injury (AKI) in critically ill patients remains poorly defined. Understanding the gap between guideline recommendations and bedside practice is essential to inform targeted quality-improvement initiatives. The AKI-PURIFY survey was designed to provide a contemporary international overview of AKI diagnosis and management in the ICU, with emphasis on implementation of the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) preventive strategies and determinants with its adoption. We hypothesized that implementation of evidence-based preventive care varies across healthcare settings and is influenced by clinician training and organizational capacity. AKI-PURIFY was a multicenter, international online survey endorsed by the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM), conducted between February and April 2024. Healthcare professionals involved in intensive care unit (ICU) management of AKI were invited to participate. The survey explored diagnostic strategies, implementation of the KDIGO kidney prevention strategy, renal replacement therapy practices, and perceived organizational and educational barriers. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted to identify factors independently associated with the use of diagnostic tools and the implementation of preventive strategies. A total of 703 respondents completed the survey. Routine implementation of the KDIGO kidney prevention strategy was reported by 36.3% of participants (47.0% among valid responses). Diagnostic practices varied across ICU and resource settings, and the use of AKI damage biomarkers remained low. In adjusted analyses, inadequate training (odds ratio [OR]=0.56, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.37 to 0.84, P=0.007) and higher organizational barrier scores (OR=0.78, 95% CI: 0.63 to 0.97, P=0.030) were independently associated with lower implementation. Clear income-level gradients were observed across diagnostic strategies, training adequacy, and organizational capacity. Adoption of guideline-recommended AKI prevention strategies remains inconsistent worldwide and is influenced by modifiable educational and system-level factors. Addressing this gap will require coordinated, context-sensitive strategies integrating structured training and scalable quality-improvement frameworks.

42985594.title: Incidence, Predictors, and Clinical Outcomes of Acute Kidney Injury in Critically Ill Patients: A Retrospective Study.
42985594.abstract: Background Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication among critically ill patients and is associated with prolonged hospitalization, increased need for organ support, and higher mortality. Objective The objective of the study is to determine the incidence of AKI among critically ill patients, identify its independent predictors, and evaluate its association with major clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective observational study was conducted at Services Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, from June 2023 to June 2026 and included 261 adult critically ill patients. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, clinical severity scores, laboratory parameters, treatment-related factors, and clinical outcomes were extracted from medical records. Results AKI developed in 102 of 261 patients, corresponding to an incidence of 39.1%. Among patients with AKI, 42 (41.2%) had Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) stage 1, 34 (33.3%) had stage 2, and 26 (25.5%) had stage 3 disease. Compared with patients without AKI, those with AKI had higher intensive care unit (ICU) mortality (35 (34.3%) vs. 19 (11.9%)), in-hospital mortality (41 (40.2%) vs. 24 (15.1%)), and renal replacement therapy requirement (21 (20.6%) vs. 0 (0.0%)), as well as longer ICU and hospital stays and longer duration of mechanical ventilation (all p < 0.001). Factors independently associated with AKI included chronic kidney disease (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 3.12, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.34-7.28), vasopressor support at ICU admission (aOR 2.86, 95% CI 1.49-5.50), sepsis or septic shock (aOR 2.74, 95% CI 1.48-5.08), mechanical ventilation at ICU admission (aOR 2.09, 95% CI 1.08-4.04), increasing serum lactate (aOR 1.31, 95% CI 1.10-1.57), higher Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score (aOR 1.09, 95% CI 1.04-1.14), and increasing age (aOR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.05). Conclusion AKI affected more than one-third of critically ill patients and was associated with a greater observed clinical burden, including higher mortality, greater need for renal replacement therapy, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and longer ICU and hospital stays. Chronic kidney disease, sepsis or septic shock, vasopressor support at ICU admission, mechanical ventilation at ICU admission, higher serum lactate, higher APACHE II score, and increasing age were independently associated with AKI. Because clinical outcome comparisons were unadjusted, the observed differences in mortality, mechanical ventilation duration, and length of stay do not establish AKI as an independent determinant of these outcomes.

42982537.title: Rethinking Fluid Balance: The Shift Toward Deresuscitation in Critical Care.
42982537.journal: Advances in kidney disease and health
42982537.abstract: Intravenous fluid therapy is central to resuscitating critically ill patients, yet accumulating evidence shows that excessive fluid administration and positive fluid balance contribute directly to respiratory failure, acute kidney injury, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and mortality. Modern fluid stewardship reframes intravenous fluids as pharmacologic agents with dose-dependent toxicity and emphasizes the ROSE (Resuscitation, Optimization, Stabilization, and Evacuation) model. Observational studies consistently link fluid overload (often defined as fluid balance >5% baseline weight) to worse outcomes, and early or protocolized deresuscitation (removal of accumulated fluid once perfusion goals have been achieved) through diuretics or ultrafiltration can reliably achieve negative fluid balance and improve pulmonary parameters without increasing acute kidney injury. Randomized trials of restrictive strategies demonstrate improved ventilator-free days and shortened length of stay but no mortality benefit, underscoring the need for individualized, physiology-guided approaches. Evidence for active deresuscitation remains mixed. Diuretic-based protocols can lower mortality and reduce renal replacement therapy use in select populations, while ultrafiltration studies highlight the importance of avoiding both insufficient (<1 mL/kg/h) and excessive (>1.75 mL/hg/h) fluid removal rates. Knowledge gaps persist around optimal timing, patient selection, hemodynamic monitoring, and fluid removal targets. Ongoing trials aim to refine protocolized resuscitation and better define strategies to safely restore euvolemia, mitigate organ dysfunction, and improve outcomes in critical illness.

42988639.title: Female Sex and Ventilatory Recovery After Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
42988639.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42988639.abstract: This study evaluated whether female sex is associated with postoperative mechanical ventilation duration and prolonged ventilation >24 hours after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Retrospective multicenter cohort study. Four German academic centers, 2017-2023. Five hundred seventy-four adults with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%; 70 (12.2%) were women. None. Primary outcomes were postoperative mechanical ventilation duration and intensive care unit length of stay. The primary models were adjusted for baseline/preoperative covariates without CPB. Female sex corresponded to +30.2% longer ventilation (95% CI -3.6% to +75.8%; p = 0.086), which did not reach conventional statistical significance, and higher odds of ventilation >24 hours (aOR 1.82, 95% CI 1.01-3.26; p = 0.045). Adding CPB strengthened the estimates, whereas extracorporeal life support exclusion and center fixed-effects adjustment attenuated them. In 69 matched pairs, women had longer ventilation (16.0 [8.0-33.2] v 11.0 [5.8-18.0] hours; p = 0.021) and more ventilation >24 hours (30.9% v 13.2%; p = 0.029). No clear association was observed with acute kidney injury or 30-day mortality. Female sex showed a model-dependent association with prolonged postoperative ventilation in this HFrEF CABG cohort. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation with standardized perioperative and extubation protocols.

42984532.title: Successful application of low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation in CRRT for patients with liver failure: a retrospective case series study of 11 patients.
42984532.abstract: To investigate the clinical efficacy, safety and operational feasibility of a low-dose regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) combined with low-dose nafamostat mesylate (NM) mixed anticoagulation regimen in continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for patients with liver failure, so as to provide clinical reference for the selection of CRRT anticoagulation strategies for such special high-risk critically ill patients. A retrospective case series study was conducted. Eleven patients with liver failure who received CRRT in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University were enrolled. All patients were treated with CVVHDF mode and uniformly implemented the low-dose citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. CRRT treatment parameters, anticoagulant drugs, and infusion doses of calcium and sodium bicarbonate were standardized. The monitoring frequency of peripheral blood gas and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and the criteria for dose stratification adjustment were standardized. Data including patients' demographic baseline data, CRRT treatment duration, filter service life, blood gas electrolytes, dynamic changes of APTT, pipeline and filter coagulation, bleeding and metabolic adverse events, organ function and clinical outcomes were collected for summary and analysis. A total of 11 patients with liver failure undergoing CRRT in CVVHDF mode were enrolled in this study, using the low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. After treatment, the median filter life of patients reached 48 (38, 68.75) hours, with no severe pipeline or filter coagulation; there were no significant abnormalities in systemic coagulation indicators. One case (9.1%) had mild oral mucosal bleeding; no severe massive bleeding occurred. Hypocalcemia and metabolic alkalosis were observed in several patients but were not severe, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred. PCT was lower than baseline (P = 0.005) and APACHE II score was improved (P = 0.011) over the course of ICU treatment; however, all patients simultaneously received antibiotics, vasopressors, source control, and other ICU supportive care, and these changes therefore cannot be attributed to the mixed anticoagulation regimen. Liver and kidney function showed no obvious deterioration. In this small, single-center retrospective case series, a low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen was feasible to implement in patients with liver failure receiving CRRT. In this cohort, the median filter life was 48 h, no severe filter or pipeline coagulation was observed, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred; one case (9.1%) had mild bleeding. Because no comparator group was included, whether these observations reflect a benefit of the mixed regimen over conventional RCA, nafamostat alone, systemic heparin, or no anticoagulation cannot be determined. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered, multicenter, prospective controlled trials.

42983655.title: Urinary kidney injury molecule-1 as a diagnostic biomarker for persistent severe acute kidney injury: a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.
42983655.abstract: Despite the vast amount of literature dedicated to biomarkers and acute kidney injury (AKI), the persistent state of AKI has been relatively neglected. The objective of this study was to systematically review relevant studies and evaluate the diagnostic value of urinary kidney injury molecule 1 (uKIM-1) for persistent severe AKI in adults. We searched the PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials databases up to December 2025. Eligible studies included adult patients and assessed the diagnostic value of uKIM-1 for persistent severe AKI. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) was used for quality assessment. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, area under the curve (AUC) and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) values were calculated via a Bayesian bivariate diagnostic meta-analysis model. Eight studies with 2349 patients were selected for meta-analysis. 378 patients were diagnosed with persistent severe AKI. The included studies were published between 2011 and 2025 and involved heterogeneous clinical settings, including intensive care, emergency department, postoperative, sepsis, COVID-19, and liver transplantation populations. The estimated sensitivity of uKIM-1 was 0.67 (95% CrI, 0.59-0.75), and the specificity was 0.73 (95% CrI, 0.61-0.84). The pooled DOR was 5.91 (95% CrI, 2.91-11.20), and the AUC was 0.75 (95% CrI, 0.62-0.84). Sensitivity analyses using alternative cutoff selections and prior specifications showed generally stable estimates. This Bayesian meta-analysis indicates that uKIM-1 has moderate diagnostic value for persistent severe AKI in adults. Current evidence does not support its use as a standalone biomarker, and future studies should evaluate its incremental value in combination with other biomarkers and clinical variables.

42986372.title: Recovery after more than one month of dialysis in legionella-associated acute kidney injury: a case evaluated with gallium-67 scintigraphy and renal biopsy.
42986372.abstract: Distinguishing tubulointerstitial nephritis (TIN) from acute tubular necrosis (ATN) is clinically important in Legionella-associated acute kidney injury (AKI), because TIN may respond to corticosteroid therapy whereas ATN does not. However, kidney biopsy is often not feasible in critically ill patients, and noninvasive approaches to guide treatment decisions are needed. We report a 73-year-old man with severe Legionella pneumonia complicated by dialysis-dependent AKI persisting for more than one month despite resolution of the infection and discontinuation of all antibiotics by Day 9. Markedly elevated urinary beta2-microglobulin (118,539 μg/L at Day 28) and diffuse intense bilateral renal uptake on gallium-67 scintigraphy (grade 5, clearly exceeding liver and vertebral body uptake) on Day 31 supported ongoing renal inflammation in the setting of prolonged tubular injury. A diagnostic trial of prednisolone (0.5 mg/kg/day) was initiated; from approximately 1 week later, urine output increased, serum creatinine declined, and hemodialysis was successfully discontinued on Day 43. Renal function returned to pre-illness baseline by Day 57 (serum creatinine 0.75 mg/dL). Kidney biopsy performed after clinical stabilization showed acute tubular injury with chronic tubulointerstitial changes and a focal, reactive T-cell infiltrate; prior or partially treated TIN could not be excluded. This case shows that renal recovery remains possible in Legionella-associated AKI even after more than 1 month of dialysis dependence, and suggests that gallium-67 scintigraphy, interpreted alongside serial urinary tubular injury markers, may provide ancillary evidence of ongoing renal inflammation when biopsy is not immediately feasible.

42985103.title: Meta-analysis of the effect of nafamostat mesilate versus no-anticoagulation regimens in adult patients undergoing continuous renal replacement therapy.
42985103.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is a critical treatment for critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. However, effective anticoagulation of the extracorporeal circuit remains a clinical challenge. Nafamostat mesilate (NM), a serine protease inhibitor, possesses localized anticoagulation properties; however, its efficacy and safety in high-bleeding-risk populations have not been systematically evaluated. To compare the efficacy and safety of NM anticoagulation and no-anticoagulation regimens in patients undergoing CRRT. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies were retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, MEDLINE, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, the Cochrane Library, Wanfang Database, Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database. We included studies on adult patients receiving CRRT where the intervention and control groups were treated with NM anticoagulation and no-anticoagulation regimens, respectively. Primary outcomes included filter lifespan, number of filters used, coagulation indicators, bleeding events, and in-hospital mortality. The meta-analysis was conducted using RevMan 5.4 software. Eight studies involving 969 patients were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that, compared with the control group, the NM group had a significantly prolonged filter lifespan (P = 0.01) and a reduced number of filters used (P < 0.0001). The activated partial thromboplastin time (P = 0.89), prothrombin time (P = 0.88), and international normalized ratio (P = 0.60) showed no significant differences. Both groups demonstrated clinically similar risks of bleeding events (P = 0.53). However, the NM group demonstrated a significantly reduced in-hospital mortality, compared with the control group (P = 0.02). The NM anticoagulation regimen effectively extended the CRRT filter lifespan, reduced resource consumption, and improved patient survival outcomes without increasing the bleeding risk, demonstrating particular value for high-bleeding-risk populations. Future multicenter RCTs are warranted to validate applicability of NM in non-East Asian populations. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261399024, identifier: PROSPERO CRD420251077578.

42984163.title: Discontinuation of continuous kidney replacement therapy: current evidence and protocolized approaches for safe and timely liberation.
42984163.abstract: Continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) is a cornerstone of organ support in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. While substantial evidence exists regarding the optimal timing of CKRT initiation, clear criteria to guide its discontinuation remain lacking. In clinical practice, decisions regarding CKRT discontinuation are often based on heterogeneous and institution-specific approaches, reflecting the absence of reliable and standardized indicators of kidney recovery. Various biomarkers, including serum creatinine, cystatin C, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin, and urinary urea excretion, have been investigated for their potential to predict kidney recovery. Among these, urine output has been the most consistently reported and widely utilized parameter, although considerable heterogeneity exists in measurement timing, cutoff values, and the use of diuretics. In addition to individual biomarkers, several protocolized approaches incorporating multiple clinical parameters have been proposed. These include scoring systems, the furosemide stress test, and protocols incorporating the urinary urea excretion index. However, most proposed approaches remain insufficiently validated and should be regarded as supportive frameworks rather than definitive decision tools. Institutional protocols further highlight the variability in clinical practice, although urine output consistently emerges as a central component in decision-making. This review summarizes current evidence on biomarkers associated with kidney recovery and discusses emerging protocolized approaches for CKRT discontinuation. Further studies are needed to establish reliable and reproducible tools to guide optimal discontinuation and improve clinical outcomes in critically ill patients.

42983500.title: Harmonizing the diagnosis of citrate accumulation - a call for standardized criteria.
42983500.abstract: Regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) has emerged as the gold-standard strategy for continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), yet its widespread adoption remains hindered by perceived complexity, heterogeneous protocols, unclear contraindications, and inconsistent terminology. A central challenge lies in the recognition and management of citrate accumulation, for which no single, reliable biomarker exists. The total-to-ionized calcium (tCa/iCa) ratio is widely utilized as a sensitive surrogate, but its specificity is limited by multiple confounding factors, including serum albumin concentration, acid-base status, and exogenous calcium administration. Current evidence supports a paradigm shift from reliance on static thresholds toward a dynamic, physiology-based assessment to define citrate accumulation. The kinetics of the tCa/iCa ratio, when interpreted alongside evolving metabolic parameters, particularly lactate trends, systemic ionized calcium, and acid-base status, provide a more robust framework for identifying citrate accumulation. Crucially, an elevated tCa/iCa ratio should not indiscriminately prompt the discontinuation of RCA. Targeted adjustments to the CRRT prescription can often safely mitigate citrate burden while preserving circuit patency. In the absence of a validated and widely available method for the direct measurement of plasma citrate levels, we propose a stepwise approach incorporating routinely measured screening tools and confirmatory parameters. Studies incorporating direct plasma citrate concentration measurements should be conducted to validate these criteria alongside readily available bedside surrogate markers. Refining this framework is essential to enhance the safe implementation of RCA and ultimately improve outcomes in critically ill patients.

42982539.title: Acute Kidney Injury After Hematopoietic Stem CellTransplantation.
42982539.journal: Advances in kidney disease and health
42982539.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is a curative intervention for various hematologic malignancies. However, it is associated with an exceptionally high rate of acute kidney injury with a cumulative incidence of 55%. The risk is highest for unmatched allogeneic transplantation involving myeloablative conditioning regimens. The need for kidney replacement therapy can approach 21% especially in critically ill recipients with unacceptably high all-cause and nonrelapse mortality. Various factors predispose to kidney injury extending from the toxicity of conditioning regimen to a myriad of complications spanning up to 100 days post-transplantation. An understanding of this timeline as well as the pathophysiology of the various processes facilitates early recognition and prompt management. Advances in therapeutics bring optimism in improving outcomes and minimizing progressive tissue injury.

42983571.title: Time-varying dose decisions in CRRT: why marginal structural and baseline Cox estimates should not be pooled.

42993042.title: Impact of frailty on acute kidney injury in patients followed-up in the intensive care unit.
42993042.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
42993042.abstract: Frailty in elderly patients is an important determinant of clinical outcomes in intensive care units, particularly in relation to acute kidney injury (AKI). This study investigated the association between frailty and AKI in the geriatric population. This prospective observational study included 120 patients. Frailty was assessed via the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) and the Edmonton Frail Scale (EFS). Patients were categorized according to the presence or absence of AKI. Demographic data, frailty scores, laboratory parameters, and clinical outcomes, including mortality, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressor use, were compared. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with the development of AKI. The mean age of the participants was 79.7±7.5 years. Comorbidities such as diabetes and hypertension were common, and AKI was observed in 29.1% of patients. The incidence of AKI was significantly higher among patients classified as frail according to the CFS (p=0.002). Patients with AKI presented increased mortality rates and an increased need for mechanical ventilation and vasopressors. The AKI group presented significantly lower hemoglobin, platelet, and albumin levels and higher baseline creatinine levels. Multivariate analysis revealed that elevated baseline creatinine was an important predictor of AKI. Frailty assessed by the CFS was associated with AKI development in unadjusted analyses; however, this association was not maintained after multivariable adjustment. No significant association was observed between AKI and frailty assessed by the EFS. Baseline serum creatinine was the only independent predictor of AKI. These findings suggest that frailty assessment, particularly using the CFS, may serve as a complementary clinical tool for early risk recognition and patient stratification rather than an independent predictor of AKI. AKI development in critically ill older adults appears to be multifactorial.

42995086.title: [Surgery in transition: Impact of the early COVID-19 pandemic on visceral surgery in Germany].
42995086.journal: Zeitschrift fur Evidenz, Fortbildung und Qualitat im Gesundheitswesen
42995086.abstract: Changes in visceral surgical care in Germany during the early COVID-19 pandemic have not yet been sufficiently described. To date, data on in-hospital mortality and postoperative complications remain limited. In this retrospective analysis, anonymized administrative data from the Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Destatis) for the period from 2018 to 2021 were evaluated comparatively, focusing on the most frequently performed visceral surgical procedures nationwide. Demographic characteristics, procedure volumes, length of hospital stay on regular wards and intensive care units, postoperative complications, and in-hospital mortality were analyzed. A total of approximately 2.1 million procedures were recorded over the 4-year study period. Compared with the pre-pandemic years 2018 and 2019, procedure volumes decreased by approximately 9% in 2020 and 2021, respectively. The average length of stay in the intensive care unit and in hospital decreased during the pandemic. Postoperative complications, including pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, sepsis, and peritonitis, increased during the pandemic years compared with the preceding years. Overall in-hospital mortality in visceral surgery increased from 2.43% in 2018 to 2.55% in 2020 and 2.53% in 2021. In particular, in-hospital mortality in colorectal surgery increased from 7.37% in 2019 to 7.95% in 2021, while the mortality among COVID-19-positive patients following colorectal procedures reached 48%. In contrast, mortality rates in esophageal, hepatic, and pancreatic surgery remained largely unchanged. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Germany experienced a substantial reduction in the volume of visceral surgical procedures and hospital length of stay, while postoperative complications and in-hospital mortality increased. A potential causal relationship with SARS-CoV-2 cannot be established based on the available data. These findings emphasize the importance of systematically evaluating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on surgical care in Germany and of developing evidence-based strategies to maintain surgical capacity and patient safety during future pandemics.

42992094.title: Reversal of severe diuretic resistance by dexmedetomidine-associated polyuria in type 1 cardiorenal syndrome: a case report.
42992094.abstract: Dexmedetomidine is a selective α2-adrenergic agonist widely used for sedation in intensive care settings. Although hypotension and bradycardia are well-recognized adverse effects, dexmedetomidine-associated polyuria is a rare and unpredictable adverse effect. An 84-year-old man with ischaemic dilated cardiomyopathy, permanent atrial fibrillation, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and chronic kidney disease was admitted to the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit with type 1 cardiorenal syndrome, severe systemic and pulmonary congestion, oliguria, and acute kidney injury. Despite continuous intravenous furosemide infusion, sequential nephron blockade, and dual vasoactive support with norepinephrine and dobutamine, the patient developed persistent oligo-anuria and worsening congestion. Dexmedetomidine infusion was initiated for psychomotor agitation and disorientation. Shortly thereafter, urine output abruptly increased to approximately 250 mL/h, accompanied by rapid decongestion and improvement in renal function. Following dexmedetomidine withdrawal, oliguria, congestion and renal dysfunction recurred. Rechallenge with dexmedetomidine again induced profound polyuria, with urine output peaking at 650 mL/h and a 10-kg weight loss over 48 h, allowing de-escalation of diuretic therapy and withdrawal of vasoactive support. The Naranjo score was 6, supporting a probable causal relationship. This case demonstrates a reproducible temporal association between dexmedetomidine administration and profound polyuria, confirmed by positive rechallenge. To our knowledge, this is the first report in which dexmedetomidine-associated polyuria was temporally associated with reversal of severe diuretic resistance and clinically meaningful decongestion in type 1 cardiorenal syndrome. Recognition of this rare adverse effect may be relevant in critically ill cardiac patients.

42995049.title: Association of duration of amino acid infusion and renal protection: the less, the better. Response to Br J Anaesth. 2026; 137: 652-3.

42994823.title: Association between pre-stroke anemia and risk of acute kidney injury following ischemic stroke: A multi-institutional retrospective cohort study.
42994823.abstract: Although anemia is an established risk factor for acute kidney injury (AKI), its specific impact on post-stroke AKI remains inadequately explored. This study aimed to investigate the association between pre-stroke anemia and the risk of developing AKI after acute ischemic stroke. This retrospective study, using the TriNetX research network database, identified adult patients who experienced their 1st recorded ischemic stroke between January 2010 and December 2023. Patients were categorized based on hemoglobin levels within 3 months pre-stroke: anemia (hemoglobin ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL) versus control (hemoglobin ≥12.0 g/dL). After 1:1 propensity score matching, we analyzed the outcomes at 1-year follow-up. The primary endpoint was the development of AKI during the follow-up period. Secondary endpoints comprised all-cause mortality, pneumonia, and intensive care unit admission. After propensity score matching, 61,896 patients were included in each cohort. Patients with pre-stroke anemia had a significantly higher 1-year risk of AKI (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.83-1.96), mortality (HR: 1.86, 95% CI: 1.80-1.93), pneumonia (HR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.69-1.84), and intensive care unit admission (HR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.55-1.65) compared to controls (all P < .001). A graded association was observed between increasing anemia severity and adverse outcomes. The findings remained robust across sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Pre-stroke anemia is associated with an increased risk of post-stroke AKI and other adverse outcomes. However, given the observational nature of this study, future prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings and elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

42992167.title: Bloodstream Infections After Cardiac Surgery: Pathogen Distribution, Antimicrobial Resistance, and a Nomogram Prediction Model.
42992167.abstract: Postoperative bloodstream infection (BSI) is a severe complication following cardiac surgery, associated with significant mortality. This study aims to characterize pathogen profiles, antimicrobial resistance and independent risk factors for BSI in a Chinese cardiac surgery cohort. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of postoperative BSI in patients who underwent cardiac surgery at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from January 2019 to December 2024. Patients who developed postoperative BSI were identified and a 1:1 propensity score matched analysis were performed to adjust for baseline characteristics of patients. Univariate and multivariate analysis were applied to identify independent risk factors for postoperative BSI. R software was used to construct a prediction nomogram, followed by internal validation. During the study, a total of 10,007 patients underwent heart surgery, and 164 pairs of patients were successfully matched using propensity score matching. Gram-negative bacteria were the most common pathogens (64.1%), followed by Fungi (18.2%) and Gram-positive bacteria (17.6%). Among Enterobacterales, 33.8% were carbapenem-resistant, with carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) accounting for 63.6% of K. pneumoniae isolates. Meanwhile, 85.0% (17/20) of A. baumannii isolates were multidrug-resistant A. baumannii (MDRAB). The 90-day mortality rate in the BSI group was 39.0%, significantly higher than that in the non-BSI group (4.9%, P < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression identified impaired cardiac function (New York Heart Association II-IV, NYHA II-IV) (OR=5.583, 95% CI:2.681-11.627), pulmonary infection (OR =4.053, 95% CI:1.692-9.710), emergency surgery (OR=9.629, 95% CI:2.962-31.301), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) (OR=2.796, 95% CI:1.096-7.134), continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT Postoperative ICU stay ≥ 14 d) (OR=4.758, 95% CI:1.854-12.211) and postoperative ICU stay ≥14 d (OR=14.616, 95% CI:6.765-31.577) as independent risk factors for postoperative BSI. The nomogram showed good discrimination and calibration after internal validation, with an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.913 and a mean absolute calibration error of 0.026. Postoperative BSI in cardiac surgery patients is associated with high mortality. A nomogram based on impaired cardiac function (NYHA II-IV), pulmonary infection, emergency surgery, CABG, CRRT and postoperative ICU stay ≥14 d displayed high accuracy and consistency in predicting the risk of postoperative BSI. These results facilitate early risk stratification and guide preventive strategies in high-risk cardiac surgical patients.

42992385.title: Rotational thromboelastometry and endothelial-derived extracellular vesicle changes in thrombotic microangiopathy versus other envenoming syndromes following hump-nosed pit viper envenoming.
42992385.abstract: Thrombotic microangiopathy is an uncommon complication of snakebite with unclear pathophysiology. We explore the mechanisms of venom-induced consumption coagulopathy, thrombotic microangiopathy and acute kidney injury in hump-nosed pit viper bites. A prospective observational study was conducted at District General Hospital Horana, Sri Lanka (June 2023 to December 2024). Thirty-five patients were recruited, including: local envenoming alone (20), venom induced consumption coagulopathy (2), thrombotic microangiopathy (5) and acute kidney injury without thrombotic microangiopathy (8). Laboratory tests were performed every 12 hours, and rotational thromboelastometry (delta and platelet) and flow cytometry for extracellular vesicles at the earliest diagnosis of envenoming. All thrombotic microangiopathy cases developed severe acute kidney injury, with 4/5 requiring dialysis. All eight cases of isolated acute kidney injury had mild kidney dysfunction that resolved. The international normalized ratio was normal in patients with thrombotic microangiopathy and acute kidney injury, however rotational thromboelastometry revealed coagulation abnormalities, including fibrinogen dysfunction despite normal fibrinogen levels, in patients with thrombotic microangiopathy. Isolated acute kidney injury had mild to moderate rotational thromboelastometry abnormalities. Endothelial-derived extracellular vesicles were proportionally highest in the thrombotic microangiopathy (median 12.6%) group. Red cell-derived extracellular vesicles were raised in thrombotic microangiopathy and isolated acute kidney injury groups. Thrombotic microangiopathy and severe acute kidney injury are associated in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming. Rotational thromboelastometry revealed coagulation abnormalities, missed by conventional coagulation testing. Thrombotic microangiopathy in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming was associated with raised endothelial- and red cell-derived extracellular vesicles. Rotational thromboelastometry is more sensitive than conventional coagulation testing for detecting coagulopathy and the associated risk of developing thrombotic microangiopathy and AKI in hump-nosed viper bites. Endothelial injury may be a factor in the pathogenesis of thrombotic microangiopathy in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming.

42997845.title: Chloride load and serum chloride in critically ill adults: a randomization-anchored analysis of the BaSICS trial.
42997845.abstract: 0.9% saline solution has a supraphysiological chloride concentration and has been associated observationally with acute kidney injury and mortality. How randomized fluid type changes serum chloride early in critical illness, and what determines this change, remain uncertain. Focusing on the first three days after randomization, we estimated the randomized saline-versus-Plasma-Lyte difference in serum chloride and its variation by renal function, the observational association with study-saline volume, and the sources of variation in serum chloride. This secondary analysis of BaSICS (75 Brazilian ICUs; Plasma-Lyte 148 vs 0.9% saline) included participants with baseline serum chloride and at least one measurement on days 1-3. A Bayesian hierarchical longitudinal model estimated the treatment effect over time and its variation by baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Group-level analyses used day 2, which balanced accumulated exposure against attrition of measurements. We normalized randomized between-group differences, estimated an inverse-probability-weighted within-saline volume association, and partitioned modeled variation in serum chloride. Among 3,482 patients (33% of the trial population), serum chloride rose 2.15 mmol/L (95% confidence interval, 1.76-2.53) more with saline than with Plasma-Lyte by day 2, when saline recipients had received on average 145.7 mmol more study-fluid chloride, corresponding to 1.47 mmol/L per 100 mmol of additional chloride (1.17-1.81). Within saline recipients, the weighted association was +0.31 mmol/L per 100 mmol (0.22 to 0.44). The day-2 between-group difference decreased by 0.29 mmol/L (95% credible interval, 0.12 to 0.46) per 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 higher baseline eGFR (+3.0 mmol/L at 30 vs +1.8 mmol/L at 90 mL/min/1.73 m2). Of modeled variation in serum chloride, the fluid component accounted for 0.7% (0.4-1.0; 1.8% with randomized arm included); measured baseline characteristics, almost entirely baseline serum chloride, for 48.1%; persistent patient-specific differences not explained by measured characteristics for 24.5%; and day-to-day within-patient fluctuation for 26.9%. Over the first three ICU days, randomization to saline increased serum chloride relative to Plasma-Lyte, and the between-group difference was larger at lower baseline eGFR. Most modeled variation in serum chloride reflected each patient's baseline chloride and persistent patient-specific differences that measured characteristics did not explain; the fluid component was small. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02875873.

42997294.title: Clinical Profile, Indications, and Maternal Outcomes of Obstetric Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Admissions: A Retrospective Study With Emphasis on Critical Care Interventions.
42997294.abstract: Background Maternal morbidity and mortality continue to pose considerable problems to global health systems, especially in developing countries like India. The monitoring of the number of patients admitted to obstetric intensive care units (ICU) is an important measure of the incidence of severe maternal morbidity and the quality of emergency obstetric care available to patients. Objective To improve maternal health care services, there must be an understanding of the clinical characteristics, reasons for admission, and outcomes of these patients. Methods  A retrospective observational study was conducted in the obstetric ICU of a tertiary care teaching hospital from January 2025 through December 2025. A total of 120 obstetric patients (pregnant women and women within 42 days postpartum) admitted to the ICU were included. Information regarding patients' demographic characteristics, obstetric profile, reasons for ICU admission, critical care interventions performed, and maternal outcomes was obtained from medical records. The collected data were analyzed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corporation, Armonk, USA). Results A total of 120 obstetric patients were admitted to the intensive care unit. Hypertensive disorders were the most common indication for ICU admission (42; 35%), followed by obstetric hemorrhage (36; 30%) and sepsis (18; 15%). Blood transfusion was the most frequently provided critical care intervention (84; 70%), followed by mechanical ventilation (48; 40%), vasopressor support (30; 25%), and dialysis/renal replacement therapy (6; 5%). Overall, 102 (85%) patients recovered and were discharged, while 18 (15%) patients died. Delayed referral, multi-organ dysfunction, and requirement for mechanical ventilation were significantly associated with maternal mortality (all p < 0.001). Conclusion Hypertensive disorders and obstetric hemorrhage were the leading indications for obstetric ICU admission. Delayed referral, multi-organ dysfunction, and requirement for mechanical ventilation were significantly associated with maternal mortality. Timely referral and access to multidisciplinary critical care remain important in the management of critically ill obstetric patients.

42996144.title: Artificial intelligence simulation study of Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (TPE) using an 8- State Markov State-Transition Model integrated within a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo Framework.
42996144.abstract: Introduction Sepsis-induced organ dysfunction remains a leading cause of mortality in critical care. While recent evidence suggests that Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (TPE) may improve outcomes, significant heterogeneity among septic patient populations in prior trials might have contributed to mixed responses and thus fueled clinical skepticism. To address this challenge and to model TPE effectiveness across varying levels of sepsis severity, we utilized a time-dependent, 8-state transition Markov model integrated with a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) framework. Methods An AI-generated "digital twin" cohort (N = 10,000) was randomized 1:1 to standard care (SC) or adjuvant TPE groups. Transition probabilities were parameterized using a pooled relative risk (RR) of 0.58, derived from five recent meta-analyses. The model incorporated specific hazard multipliers for acute kidney injury (AKI; 1.5x), thrombocytopenia (1.3x), and high-dose vasopressor requirements (1.25x). Patient flow was simulated through eight clinically defined health states over a 28-day horizon. Outcomes included 28-day survival, absolute risk reduction (ARR), and number needed to treat (NNT) stratified by Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score quartiles (8, 12, 16, and 20). Bayesian methods were employed to determine survival probabilities and hazard ratios (HR) with 95% credible intervals (CrI).
