42842203.abstract: Identification of infection in critically ill patients remains challenging, as conventional biomarkers such as C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT) and white blood cell count (WBC) frequently lack diagnostic accuracy. The Intensive Care Infection Score (ICIS), a host-response biomarker derived from hematological parameters, reflects both innate and adaptive immune response. To compare diagnostic performance of ICIS, CRP, PCT, and WBC, expert adjudication was used to determine presence or absence of infection. Diagnostic accuracy parameters including receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were calculated. 770 samples from 382 critically ill patients were included. ICIS demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.914 (95% CI 0.892-0.933), compared with CRP (AUC 0.889; 95% CI 0.865-0.910), PCT (AUC 0.847; 95% CI 0.819-0.871), and WBC (AUC 0.697; 95% CI 0.663-0.729). At the optimal cut-off value of > 3, ICIS achieved a sensitivity of 80.7% and specificity of 89.3%. ICIS showed the lowest false-positive rate (10.7%) and a negative predictive value of 88.7%. ICIS demonstrated good diagnostic performance in critically ill patients and can contribute to antimicrobial stewardship as a novel host-response diagnostic.

42838356.title: Burden of sepsis in obstetric critically ill patients: A qualitative systematic review.
42838356.abstract: Sepsis is a major contributor to maternal morbidity and mortality worldwide and represents one of the leading causes of intensive care unit (ICU) admission among obstetric patients. However, the burden and clinical profile of the most severely affected women remain incompletely defined. This systematic review aimed to estimate the epidemiology, characteristics, and outcomes of sepsis in critically ill obstetric patients. A comprehensive search was conducted for studies published between 2013 and 2025, including studies of women requiring ICU admission for sepsis during pregnancy or the post-partum. Following the screening process, 25 of the 5847 screened studies met the inclusion criteria. All were observational. The overall population included 7,434,710 hospitalised obstetric patients, including 3,593 obstetric ICU admissions for sepsis. The incidence of intensive care unit admissions ranged from 21 to 857 every 10,000 hospitalized obstetric patients and reached incidences of 11.3% among hospitalized obstetric patients with sepsis. Sepsis accounted for 5.7% of obstetric ICU admissions. Half of the patients had one organ dysfunction, while a quarter had three or more, with respiratory and cardiovascular insufficiencies being the most common. The main infection sources were the genital, respiratory, and urinary tracts. Septic shock occurred in 16.6% of the cases. The mean Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score was 6.2 and the Acute Physiologic Assessment and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score was 12.3. ICU and hospital stay were 3 and 8 days. Mortality varied significantly (median 4.6%), with marked disparities between high- and low-income countries. Robust epidemiological monitoring is therefore urgently required. PROSPERO under ID 2023 CRD42023446466.

42838259.title: Ex vivo functional immune alterations in ICU patients with Legionnaires' disease, a proof-of-concept study.
42838259.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
42838259.abstract: Legionnaires' disease (LD), caused by Legionella pneumophila intracellular bacterium, leads to intensive care unit (ICU) admission in 20-40% of cases. While ICU-LD patients display lung injury or septic shock (SS), their functional immune response remains poorly understood. This proof-of-concept study assessed ex vivo immune gene expression in ICU-LD and non-ICU-LD patients. Whole blood from ICU-LD (n = 6), non-ICU-LD (n = 8), LD-unrelated SS (n = 14) and healthy volunteers (HVs) (n = 9) was stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Expression of 93 immune-related genes was quantified using nCounter (NanoString Technologies) and expressed relative to HVs. Functional enrichment analyses were performed using the STRING database. ICU-LD patients displayed a 1.6-fold higher number of less induced genes (35/93 vs 22/93) and lower gene expression (median log2(FC): -1.9 vs -1.2, P = 0.0011) than non-ICU-LD. Top five pathways identified as enriched in ICU-LD but not in non-ICU-LD patients were cellular response to LPS, regulation of IFN-β production, I-κB/NF-κB complex, IFN regulatory factor complex and TRAF6-mediated NF-κB activation. Ex vivo immune gene expression alterations were found in LD patients, particularly in ICU-LD patients. ICU-LD patients displayed lower expression of genes involved in crucial pathways for Legionella replication control. These preliminary findings support further studies to evaluate the impact of LD patients' immune response on disease severity.

42835169.title: Association of carvedilol with mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis: a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study.
42835169.abstract: To evaluate the association between carvedilol use and mortality in patients with sepsis. All adult critically ill patients with sepsis were retrospectively identified from the MIMIC-IV database. Patients who received carvedilol between sepsis diagnosis and Intensive Care Unit(ICU) discharge were designated as the intervention group and were matched 1:1 with non-users using propensity score matching. The primary outcomes were 28-day and 365-day all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to examine the association between carvedilol and outcomes. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses including time-dependent Cox regression were conducted to test robustness. A total of 33,453 patients were included, of whom 1,084 received carvedilol. After propensity score matching, 1,082 pairs were successfully matched. Kaplan-Meier survival curves showed significant differences in survival probabilities between the two groups. After adjusting for confounders using multivariate Cox regression, the hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) for carvedilol use on 28-day and 365-day all-cause mortality were 0.53 (0.43-0.66) and 0.66 (0.57-0.76), respectively. Furthermore, carvedilol use was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (OR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.37-0.64; P < 0.001). Subgroup and sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. Carvedilol use during the period from sepsis diagnosis to ICU discharge was associated with reduced mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis. However, prospective studies are warranted to further guide the use of carvedilol in this population.

42834317.title: Oscillation and Lung Expansion Therapy as Rescue Airway Clearance in Critically Ill Adults: A Case Series.
42834317.abstract: Retained airway secretions and lobar collapse are common in hospitalized adults with advanced lung disease. Conventional airway clearance depends on respiratory effort, requiring both an adequate inspiratory volume and sufficient expiratory airflow, and on cough strength, and therefore fails most often in the patients who need it most. Oscillation and lung expansion (OLE) therapy delivers continuous positive expiratory pressure (CPEP), continuous high-frequency oscillation (CHFO), and aerosolized medication in a single 10-min treatment, but reported experience is largely confined to postoperative prophylaxis and the home setting. We describe six consecutive adults (aged 18-77 years) treated with OLE (Volara system) at a Canadian tertiary center between March 2023 and April 2026, after conventional airway clearance had failed or after escalation to near-maximal noninvasive respiratory support. Feasibility (delivery of OLE as prescribed at the prevailing level of respiratory support) and tolerability (absence of adverse events or discontinuation for intolerance) were assessed retrospectively. Diagnoses were cystic fibrosis exacerbation (n = 2), thoracic malignancy with lobar collapse from mucus plugging (n = 2), metapneumovirus pneumonia in VEXAS (vacuoles, E1 enzyme, X-linked, autoinflammatory, somatic) syndrome (n = 1), and autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis with sepsis (n = 1). In each, the realistic alternatives were bronchoscopy, intubation, or palliation. All six demonstrated secretion clearance, radiographic re-expansion, or both. Supplemental oxygen requirements fell in five, two did not require the intensive care transfer or intubation that had been anticipated, and no adverse event was observed following OLE, including in one patient with a recently drained pneumothorax. One patient with metastatic malignancy died of her cancer during the same admission despite radiographic re-expansion. OLE was feasible and well tolerated when used as rescue airway clearance in high-acuity adults. These observations, while hypothesis-generating, require prospective, protocolized evaluation before OLE can be recommended for this indication.

42830745.title: Persistent lymphopaenia in critically ill patients with and without sepsis: An Australian and New Zealand point prevalence study.
42830745.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
authors: Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Point Prevalence Program and The George Institute for Global Health
42830745.abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of persistent lymphopaenia, defined as an absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) < 1.0 × 109/L on both the first and second intensive care unit (ICU) days in patients with sepsis and the association of persistent lymphopaenia with advanced organ support. A prospective, multicentre, binational point prevalence study of adult patients treated in participating ICUs in June 2023 was conducted. Main outcome measures included prevalence of persistent lymphopaenia in patients with sepsis versus those without sepsis, hospital and ICU mortality, length of stay, and organ support patterns. Among 829 adult patients in 59 ICUs, 307 (37%) had persistent lymphopaenia, and 338 (40.8%) met sepsis criteria. Persistent lymphopaenia was associated with greater illness severity (mean Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score: 19.4 vs. 16.8, p < 0.001). Persistent lymphopaenia was more common in patients with sepsis than in those without sepsis (44.7% vs. 31.8%, p < 0.001); this difference remained after adjusting for predefined covariates (odds ratio: 1.51, 95% confidence interval: 1.12-2.03, p = 0.008). For patients with sepsis and persistent lymphopaenia, there was a 6% increase in mortality compared to those without lymphopaenia, although this did not reach statistical significance. For patients without sepsis, hospital length of stay was 16.5 days in those who had persistent lymphopaenia versus 14.4 days in those without persistent lymphopaenia (95% confidence interval: 0.5-3.7, p = 0.01). Persistent lymphopaenia is common in critically ill patients, particularly those with sepsis. Future prospective and interventional investigations are required to clarify the clinical significance of persistent lymphopaenia in critically ill adults and its potential as a therapeutic target.

42825283.title: Dynamic prediction of the development of extrahepatic organ failures in ICU patients with decompensated cirrhosis.
42825283.abstract: Extrahepatic organ failure (EOF) is a critical determinant of short-term mortality in patients with decompensated cirrhosis within the intensive care unit (ICU). However, traditional prognostic tools are largely static and fail to capture the rapidly fluctuating physiological characteristic of critical illness. This study aimed to develop and validate a dynamic artificial intelligence (AI) framework to provide real-time predictions of the presence of ≥2 EOF 12 hours later. We analysed adult patients with decompensated cirrhosis from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV; derivation) and eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; external validation). Using a late-fusion architecture, we combined risk estimates from a machine-learning model and a deep-learning model. Both models incorporated longitudinal vital signs and non-time-series clinical variables, using summary features and sequential vital signs, respectively. The model processed 45 variables subsequently refined to 14 key predictors. The sliding-window framework combined hourly vital signs (6-hour dynamic window), recent laboratory parameters (24-hour window) and current organ failure status. The model continuously incorporated newly available data to predict the presence of ≥2 EOF 12 hours later. Performance was evaluated via area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration and decision curve analysis (DCA). The derivation cohort included 1486 patients, with 1666 patients in the external validation cohort. The optimal late-fusion configuration paired a CatBoost model trained after synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) resampling with a deep-learning model combining fully convolutional networks and gated recurrent units (FCN-GRU). The combined model achieved an AUROC of 0.830 (95% CI 0.783 to 0.876) at the 12-hour prediction horizon. The model demonstrated strong calibration (intercept -0.027) and consistent net clinical benefit across relevant probability thresholds in DCA. Sensitivity analyses showed stable performance across 6-hour (AUROC 0.821) and 24-hour (AUROC 0.834) prediction horizons as well as within the sepsis subgroup (AUROC 0.820). Robust discriminative capability was maintained in external validation (AUROC 0.774, 95% CI 0.743 to 0.805). By tracking continuously evolving physiological trajectories, this AI-driven approach accurately predicts EOF in patients with decompensated cirrhosis. It provides reliable risk estimates 12 hours ahead, serving as a dynamic alternative to conventional static risk scores.

42957303.title: Effects of perfusion-guided permissive hypotension and early vasopressin initiation in adults with septic shock: protocol for a multicentre 2×2 factorial randomised controlled trial in Japanese intensive care units.

42953638.title: Multidisciplinary Antimicrobial Stewardship Program in an Indian ICU: A Time-Series Analysis of Diagnostic Practices and Antibiotic Use.
42953638.abstract: Background ICUs are high-risk environments for antimicrobial resistance (AMR). We evaluated the impact of a multidisciplinary Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (AMSP) on diagnostic stewardship, prescribing patterns, and antimicrobial consumption in an Indian tertiary critical care setting. Methods  A 17-month retrospective observational study was conducted, comparing an eight-month pre-implementation phase (January-August 2024) with a nine-month post-implementation phase (September 2024-May 2025). The AMSP included staff training, structured prescription orders, prospective audits, and monthly feedback. Key metrics included pre-antibiotic culture collection, institutional guideline adherence, surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis (SAP) compliance, and standardized consumption densities (defined daily dose (DDD)/100 bed-days and days of therapy (DOT)/1,000 bed-days), evaluated using interrupted time-series (ITS) regression. Results  Across 7,682 ICU admissions (3,514 pre- vs. 4,168 post-implementation), pre-antibiotic culture collection increased significantly: blood cultures increased from 331 (20.2%) to 560 (45.8%; p < 0.001), and urine cultures increased from 1,365 (53.0%) to 1,583 (64.6%; p < 0.001). Empirical guideline adherence improved from 1,618 (46.0%) to 3,005 (72.1%; p < 0.001), and SAP compliance increased from 1,352 (35.5%) to 2,083 (63.2%; p < 0.001). Total antimicrobial consumption density decreased by 44.0% (120.04 to 67.17 DDD/100 bed-days; p < 0.001), and duration density declined by 39.6% (981.23 to 592.91 DOT/1,000 bed-days; p < 0.001; ITS regression step-reduction p < 0.001). Meropenem exposure remained strictly controlled and stable (165 (4.7%) vs. 208 (5.0%); p = 0.549). Conclusion  The multidisciplinary AMSP successfully contained overall antibiotic selection pressure while preserving carbapenems through optimized beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor utilization. Microbial ecology remained stable, with Klebsiella spp. and Escherichia coli predominating. Unadjusted case-mix differences represent a recognized study limitation. Implementing a multidisciplinary AMSP achieved sustained reductions in antimicrobial consumption and improved diagnostic practices, providing a feasible framework to combat resistance in resource-limited ICUs.

42952723.title: Association of red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.
42952723.abstract: Critically ill patients with aortic dissection remain at high risk of adverse ICU outcomes, including ICU mortality. The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection. Data were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. ICU mortality was defined as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay, acute kidney injury (AKI), and renal replacement therapy (RRT) use. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the discriminative performance of RAR for ICU mortality. The optimal RAR cutoff was determined using Youden's index and was considered exploratory. Calibration plots and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. RAR showed modest discrimination for ICU mortality (AUC: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.552-0.765). The exploratory cutoff value of RAR was 5.182. Compared with the low-RAR group, the high-RAR group had higher ICU mortality (21.8% vs. 6.7%; P < 0.001), a higher prevalence of sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay (82.8% vs. 61.1%; P < 0.001), and more frequent RRT use (33.3% vs. 9.4%; P < 0.001). The AUC increased from 0.706 for SOFA alone to 0.731 for SOFA plus RAR, indicating only limited incremental discrimination. Higher early-ICU RAR was associated with ICU mortality and other adverse ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection, but its discrimination was modest, its incremental value beyond SOFA was limited, and external validation is required.

42949725.title: Prognostic Value of the Delta Neutrophil Index for Predicting 28-Day Mortality in Intensive Care Unit Patients with Candidemia.
42949725.abstract: Candidemia is associated with substantial mortality in critically ill patients, and early identification of patients at increased risk of death remains challenging. The delta neutrophil index (DNI), an automated hematological parameter reflecting circulating immature granulocytes, has been proposed as a prognostic marker in sepsis, but its role in candidemia remains unclear. This retrospective study included adults who developed candidemia during intensive care unit hospitalization between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2023; patients with neutropenia, haematological malignancy receiving ongoing chemotherapy, or granulocyte colony-stimulating factor therapy were excluded. Patients were classified as survivors or non-survivors according to 28-day all-cause mortality after blood culture collection. DNI, leukocyte count, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin were evaluated 24 hours before, at the time of, and 24 hours after blood culture collection. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with mortality, and receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed the prognostic performance of DNI. Among 246 patients, 132 survived and 114 died. Non-survivors had higher APACHE II scores and more frequent acute kidney injury. DNI and procalcitonin levels were significantly higher in non-survivors at all three time points. In the primary multivariable model, acute kidney injury, DNI at blood culture collection, and procalcitonin at blood culture collection were independently associated with mortality; the association of DNI was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after further adjustment for Candida species and antifungal therapy. DNI showed limited discrimination, with area under the curve values ranging from 0.608 to 0.625; the highest value was observed at blood culture collection (0.625), with a cutoff of 2.4, 43.0% sensitivity, and 82.6% specificity. DNI may aid mortality risk stratification in candidemia but should not be used as a standalone prognostic marker.

42948314.title: Sulbactam/Durlobactam for CRAB Bacteremia and Pneumonia in a Critically Ill Patient in China: A Case Report.
42948314.abstract: Evidence supporting sulbactam/durlobactam (SUL-DUR) for carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) bloodstream infection remains limited, particularly in critically ill patients with multiorgan failure. A 25-year-old man underwent emergency splenectomy for a ruptured splenic artery aneurysm with 7500 mL estimated blood loss. On transfer to our ICU, PaO2/FiO2 was 68 mm Hg, consistent with severe ARDS. He subsequently developed a grade B postoperative pancreatic fistula. A quality-graded sputum specimen grew carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and CRAB, and a peripheral blood culture drawn during cefoperazone-sulbactam therapy grew CRAB, indicating breakthrough bacteremia; the blood isolate was susceptible to SUL-DUR but resistant to both carbapenems. Ceftazidime-avibactam was replaced with imipenem-cilastatin plus SUL-DUR for eight days, with nebulized colistimethate sodium. Concurrent care included source control, prone ventilation, and pancreatic collection drainage. Procalcitonin had normalized before SUL-DUR began, whereas IL-6 and hs-CRP rose around the positive blood culture and fell during SUL-DUR; he was extubated on ICU day 27. A post-extubation withdrawal episode with convulsions, bronchospasm, and lactic acidosis resolved with rescue sedation. He was discharged from the ICU on June 17, 2026, with negative follow-up blood cultures, and remained well at outpatient review on July 30. This case adds real-world experience regarding the potential role of SUL-DUR in CRAB bacteremia with pneumonia. Because recovery occurred alongside source control, ventilatory support, and sequential antimicrobial therapy, the outcome cannot be attributed to SUL-DUR alone. Larger prospective studies are required to define its role in CRAB bloodstream infection.

42947576.title: From Framework to Toolkit: Practical Guidance for Using the PrOcess Evaluation of Trials In Critical care (POETIC) Framework.
42947576.abstract: The PrOcess Evaluation of Trials In Critical care (POETIC) framework was developed to support systematic evaluation of Context, Fidelity, Dose, Reach, and an integrative assessment of Quality of Delivery (QoD). Its practical use, however, requires explicit guidance on selecting measures, constructing QoD, assessing changing context, and governing prospective use. We undertook a retrospective comparative synthesis of process evaluations embedded in four randomized U.K. critical care trials: Biomarker-guided antibiotic stewardship in suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAPrapid-2), Provision of Psychological Support to People in Intensive Care (POPPI), Sedation AND Weaning In CHildren (SANDWICH), and Alpha-2 agonists for sedation to produce Better outcomes from critical illness (A2B). We selected them because they informed POETIC's development or application and provided sufficiently detailed quantitative and qualitative evidence. We mapped the reports, protocols, and process evaluation findings to the five dimensions; compared recurring and contradictory patterns, quantitative-qualitative agreement, measurement and interpretation problems, and mechanism-specific limitations; and translated our learning into guidance for applying the framework. The relevance and measurement of POETIC dimensions varied according to how each intervention was expected to work. Contextual influences changed over time and differed between sites. Combined assessments of QoD required explicit decisions about component selection, weighting, thresholds, aggregation, and missing data. VAPrapid-2 showed why a separate Dose measure and a QoD composite were not meaningful for a one-off diagnostic recommendation; POPPI used a weighted site composite; SANDWICH summarized delivery of four intervention components, staff training, and patient Reach; and A2B combined four equally weighted indicators in a 0-12 site score. This cross-trial learning informed practical guidance on selecting measures, assessing context over time, integrating quantitative and qualitative findings, constructing QoD, and governing prospective use. POETIC is best used as a mechanism-aligned, mixed-method scaffold rather than a requirement to measure every dimension or calculate a universal composite. Prospective use is feasible when outputs, recipients, review times, permitted actions, and safeguards are prespecified. The framework and accompanying toolkit support reproducible assessment while protecting trial integrity.

42943519.title: Distribution and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns of Critical and High-Priority Gram-Negative Pathogens Isolated from Endotracheal Aspirates in an Intensive Care Unit.
42943519.abstract: Lower respiratory tract infections represent the world's deadliest infectious disease, responsible for approximately 2.5 million deaths worldwide. The aim of the study was to determine the distribution and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of the main critical and high priority Gram-negative bacteria isolated from endotracheal aspirates obtained from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) patients. We conducted a four-year microbiological surveillance study (2022-2025) in a tertiary Romanian ICU. A total of 1529 Gram-negative bacterial isolates were detected in 1391 endotracheal aspirates. Most frequently reported were Pseudomonas aeruginosa (422-27.60%), Acinetobacter baumannii (296-19.36%), Escherichia coli (274-17.92%) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (271-17.73%). The prevalence of MDR Acinetobacter baumannii declined to approximately 40% in 2025, whereas XDR isolates increased to 13.51%, twice the 2022 value. Carbapenem resistance among Acinetobacter baumannii remained high (around 70%) in 2025, despite a significant decline from 2022 (p < 0.001). Approximately 65% of K. pneumoniae isolates were MDR/XDR, with an increase in carbapenem resistance. MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa increased significantly from 14.14% in 2022 to 39.84% in 2025 (p < 0.001) and a significant upward trend in carbapenem resistance was registered, exceeding 70% for imipenem in 2025. These findings underscore the need for continuous microbiological and epidemiological surveillance and targeted interventions to prevent the spread of highly resistant pathogens.

42941684.title: Clinical Factors and Composite Biomarkers Associated with Intensive Care Unit-Acquired Weakness: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
42941684.abstract: Background/Objectives: Intensive care unit-acquired weakness is a common neuromuscular complication among critically ill patients, but associations of readily available composite biomarkers with this condition remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics, risk factors, and composite biomarkers associated with intensive care unit-acquired weakness. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 135 critically ill patients admitted to intensive care units between December 2020 and December 2023. Patients were classified into an intensive care unit-acquired weakness group (n = 57) and a group without intensive care unit-acquired weakness (n = 78) according to Medical Research Council sum score criteria. Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, composite biomarkers, and hospitalization outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analyses were performed. Results: Older age, sepsis, hemodialysis, mechanical ventilation, and glucocorticoid use remained associated with intensive care unit-acquired weakness after adjustment for the other covariates in the model. Affected patients had lower albumin and hemoglobin levels and longer intensive care unit and hospital stays. The neutrophil-to-albumin ratio, inflammatory burden index, creatinine-to-albumin ratio, and serum urea-to-creatinine ratio were higher in affected patients. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed modest discrimination, with areas under the curve ranging from 0.602 to 0.665. Conclusions: Intensive care unit-acquired weakness was associated with clinical and treatment-related factors, hypoalbuminemia, prolonged hospitalization, and elevated composite biomarkers. The composite biomarkers showed only modest discrimination, and their incremental values beyond clinical assessment and clinical utility remain unestablished. Residual confounding by illness severity and nutritional exposure cannot be excluded.

42940427.title: Artificial Intelligence in Intensive Care: From Clinical Applications to Ethical and Medico-Legal Challenges.
42940427.abstract: From a medico-legal perspective, AI functions as a clinical decision support tool without legal autonomy. Responsibility for AI-assisted clinical decisions remains subject to the applicable legal and regulatory framework and depends on the degree of human oversight. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming intensive care medicine, offering advanced tools for data processing, prediction, and clinical decision support. This narrative review explores current applications of AI in the intensive care unit (ICU), along with associated ethical, medico-legal, and regulatory challenges. AI systems, particularly those based on machine learning and deep learning, have demonstrated promising predictive performance across several intensive care applications. Systematic reviews of machine learning models for ICU prediction tasks have reported AUROC values generally ranging from approximately 0.80 to over 0.90 for early sepsis prediction and ARDS risk stratification, although performance decreases in external validation cohorts. AI has also shown encouraging performance in predicting weaning success and supporting mechanical ventilation management, while evidence of improved patient-centered clinical outcomes remains limited A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed and Scopus for studies published between January 2015 and December 2025. Additionally, AI contributes to continuous patient monitoring, reduction in false alarms, and improved workflow efficiency. Despite these advances, most models are derived from retrospective and single-center datasets, limiting generalizability and real-world applicability. Moreover, only a limited number of AI systems have undergone prospective clinical evaluation or demonstrated improvements in patient-centered outcomes following real-world implementation. A key limitation of current AI systems is the "black box" nature of many algorithms, which reduces interpretability and may undermine clinician trust. Furthermore, algorithmic bias, data quality issues, and limited external validation raise concerns regarding safety, equity, and reliability. Importantly, improved predictive accuracy does not necessarily translate into better clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for prospective validation studies. From a medico-legal perspective, AI functions as a clinical decision support tool without legal autonomy. Responsibility for AI-assisted clinical decisions remains subject to the applicable legal and regulatory framework and depends on the degree of human oversight, the intended use of the AI system, and the relevant jurisdiction. The emergence of regulatory frameworks, such as the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), reflects the increasing regulation of healthcare AI according to the intended purpose, level of autonomy, and potential impact of each system, emphasizing requirements for transparency, human oversight, and data protection.

42939963.title: Albumin Supplementation Preserves Systemic Antioxidant Defenses in Critically Ill, Septic Patients: A Prospective Comparative Study.
42939963.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by a dysregulated host response to infection, commonly accompanied by hypoalbuminemia (<30 g/L serum albumin level), associated with excessive production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, leading to oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and organ injury. Low serum albumin reflects increased vascular permeability, reduced hepatic synthesis, and enhanced proteolysis. It also indicates the loss of albumin's antioxidant and anti-inflammatory functions beyond oncotic regulation. Hypoalbuminemia may exacerbate this by reducing plasma antioxidant capacity and free radical scavenging, supporting interest in albumin supplementation as a potential therapeutic strategy. Methods: This prospective, randomized study investigated the effects of 3-day albumin administration in ICU patients (n = 38) with sepsis and hypoalbuminemia by assessing changes in oxidative stress and inflammatory markers. Results: Albumin supplementation increased serum albumin (p < 0.001) and was associated with higher total antioxidant capacity (Day 3 p = 0.045; Day 5 p = 0.004), glutathione levels (Day 3 p = 0.003; Day 5 p = 0.008), and protein sulfhydryl groups (Day 3-5 p = 0.004). Albumin-treated patients showed increased urinary concentration of the oxidative stress-related tyrosine isomers ortho- and meta-tyrosine (p = 0.004 and p = 0.001, respectively). Catalase activity and myeloperoxidase, procalcitonin, and IL-1β levels did not differ between groups, while IL-6 declined over time (p = 0.029). Conclusions: Based on our results, in septic patients with hypoalbuminemia, short-term albumin supplementation seems to restore serum albumin and improve systemic redox status, as evidenced by increased total antioxidant capacity, glutathione, and protein sulfhydryl levels. However, albumin supplementation did not significantly affect systemic inflammatory markers or cytokine dynamics. Albumin appears to act primarily by modulating oxidative stress, supporting its role as an adjunctive therapy to restore redox homeostasis in sepsis.

42938754.title: The Impact of an Intensive Care Unit Antimicrobial Stewardship Program on the Appropriateness of Meropenem Prescribing at a Tertiary Hospital: A Retrospective Quasi-Experimental Study.
42938754.abstract: Background: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) prevalence has been increasing in Saudi Arabia, posing a significant public health concern. Antimicrobial stewardship programs (ASPs) play an important role in reducing resistance by ensuring appropriate antibiotic use. Our study aimed to assess the appropriateness of meropenem prescriptions pre-ASP and post-ASP implementation in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) ward. Method: This is a retrospective quasi-experimental pre-post study conducted over 3 years, from 2020 to 2023 at King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz University Hospital (KAAUH). The study included adult ICU patients who received meropenem therapy. The primary objective was to evaluate the appropriateness of meropenem prescriptions in the ICU before and after ASP implementation. The secondary objectives were to identify reasons for inappropriate prescribing and evaluate the interventions implemented to address inappropriate meropenem use. Result: A total of 113 patients were included: 34 in 2020, 41 in 2022, and 38 in 2023. Appropriate meropenem prescribing increased significantly from 23.5% in 2020 to 26.8% in 2022 and 57.9% in 2023 (p = 0.003), while inappropriate prescribing decreased from 76.5% to 73.2% and 42.1%, respectively. Treatment duration also differed significantly across study periods (p = 0.002), with courses of 7-10 days increasing from 24.2% in 2020 to 53.7% in 2022 and 52.6% in 2023, while courses exceeding 10 days decreased from 51.5% to 12.2% and 18.4%, respectively. Among inappropriate prescriptions, an inappropriate antimicrobial spectrum was the predominant reason (81.9%), with no inappropriate dosing identified. Documented stewardship interventions differed significantly across periods (p < 0.001): de-escalation increased from 0% in 2020 to 43.3% in 2022 and 50.0% in 2023, while prescriptions completed without documented intervention decreased from 69.2% to 23.3% and 18.8%, respectively. Conclusion: ASP implementation was associated with a significant improvement in the appropriateness of meropenem prescribing and a shift toward shorter treatment durations among adult ICU patients. Nevertheless, inappropriate prescribing remained substantial in the second post-implementation year, emphasizing the need for continued antimicrobial stewardship interventions and ongoing monitoring of carbapenem use.

42938719.title: Integrating Plasma mNGS into ICU Antimicrobial Stewardship: A Four-Phase Framework.
42938719.abstract: Background: Plasma metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) may complement conventional microbiology in critically ill patients, yet its contribution to antimicrobial stewardship in the intensive care unit (ICU) remains unclear. Methods: In this retrospective, single-center observational study, we analyzed 243 paired mNGS-blood culture episodes from 180 ICU patients. We applied a four-phase stewardship framework that integrated clinical severity, biomarker kinetics, blood culture results, mNGS findings, and clinical assessment. Treatment adaptations were classified as escalation, de-escalation, discontinuation, or no change. Multivariable regression identified factors associated with stewardship modification and mortality. Results: Active treatment adaptation occurred in 121 of 243 episodes (49.8%), comprising 61 escalations, 39 de-escalations, and 21 discontinuations. mNGS positivity was independently associated with treatment modification (OR 2.66, 95% CI 1.23-5.75; p = 0.014), whereas blood culture positivity showed an inverse association (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.20-1.04; p = 0.062). Mortality was primarily linked to physiologic severity and host-response markers, particularly SAPS II and procalcitonin. In-hospital survival did not differ between patients who received stewardship-guided adaptation and those in whom empirical antibiotic therapy was maintained (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.57-1.81; log-rank p = 0.951). Conclusions: Microbiological findings, particularly mNGS, were associated with antimicrobial treatment adaptation but not independently with mortality. Because mNGS was embedded within a multimodal diagnostic and clinical pathway, its independent contribution cannot be fully separated from concurrent microbiological, biomarker, and clinical information. These findings should be regarded as exploratory and require prospective multicenter validation.

42938231.title: Association Between the Modified Renal Angina Index and Major Adverse Kidney Events at 90 Days in Critically Ill Adults: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
42938231.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adult modified Renal Angina Index (mRAI) formulations predict acute kidney injury, but their association with major adverse kidney events at 90 days (MAKE90) remains unclear. We examined the association in critically ill adults without established chronic kidney disease (CKD). Methods: This retrospective cohort included 250 adults admitted to a tertiary intensive care unit (ICU) between December 2023 and April 2025. mRAI was calculated from data available at ICU admission. MAKE90 was defined as death, renal replacement therapy, or persistent renal dysfunction within 90 days. We used logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, and nested-model comparisons. Results: Admission mRAI was higher in patients with MAKE90 than in those without MAKE90 (median 10 [IQR 5-20] vs. 3 [IQR 1-6]; p < 0.001). After adjustment for SOFA score and sepsis, mRAI remained associated with MAKE90 (adjusted OR per point from the linear model, 1.073; 95% CI, 1.032-1.116). Spline analysis demonstrated a significant nonlinear association (p = 0.004), indicating that the per-point OR should be interpreted as a summary estimate rather than a constant effect across the score range. The AUC of mRAI was 0.752 (95% CI, 0.691-0.814), higher than that of admission AKI stage (0.653) and not significantly different from APACHE II (0.702) or SOFA (0.718). Adding mRAI to SOFA and sepsis raised the AUC from 0.735 to 0.782. Conclusions: In critically ill adults without established CKD, higher admission mRAI remained associated with MAKE90 after adjustment for SOFA score and sepsis and showed moderate discrimination. External validation in larger, independent cohorts is needed to confirm these findings.

42938190.title: From Host Response to Microbiological Risk: Association of the RIN-IM Score with Culture-Positive Sepsis and Antimicrobial Resistance in Critically Ill Adults.
42938190.abstract: Background/Objectives: Early identification of microbiologically confirmed sepsis and antimicrobial-resistant infection remains challenging in critically ill patients. The renal-inflammatory-nutritional-metabolic (RIN-IM) score integrates serum creatinine, the systemic immune-inflammation index, pan-immune inflammation value, serum albumin, and triglyceride-glucose index. This study investigated the association of the RIN-IM score with culture-positive sepsis and antimicrobial resistance phenotypes in critically ill adults. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 318 adults with sepsis admitted to the intensive care unit between 1 January 2023 and 31 March 2026. The RIN-IM score was calculated from laboratory measurements obtained within 24 h and categorized as low (0-3), intermediate (4-6), or high risk (7-10). The primary outcome was culture-positive sepsis. Secondary analyses, restricted to patients with culture-positive sepsis, examined associations between RIN-IM and multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), and pandrug-resistant phenotypes. Results: Culture-positive sepsis was identified in 154 patients (48.4%). The median RIN-IM score was higher in culture-positive than in culture-negative patients (6 [interquartile range, 4-8] vs. 4 [2-5]; p < 0.001). Culture positivity increased from 29.1% in the low-risk group to 50.4% in the intermediate-risk group and 74.6% in the high-risk group. Each one-point increase in RIN-IM was independently associated with culture-positive sepsis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21-1.51), while high- versus low-risk classification was associated with an aOR of 4.65 (95% CI, 2.25-9.62). Among culture-positive patients, 67 (43.5%) had MDR, and 20 (13.0%) had XDR infections. Each one-point score increase was independently associated with MDR infection (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.12-1.48). The exploratory XDR analysis was based on 20 events and used Firth's bias-reduced logistic regression; a one-point score increase was associated with XDR infection (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.09-1.52), but the categorical estimates were imprecise. The score demonstrated moderate discrimination for culture-positive sepsis (AUC, 0.752; 95% CI, 0.699-0.805) and MDR infection (AUC, 0.724; 95% CI, 0.643-0.805); discrimination for XDR infection was exploratory (AUC, 0.742; 95% CI, 0.635-0.849). Twenty-eight-day mortality increased from 13.6% to 27.7% and 47.9% across the three risk categories (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Higher admission RIN-IM scores were associated with culture-positive sepsis. Among patients with culture-positive sepsis, higher scores were also associated with MDR infection; this subgroup analysis was conditioned on microbiological confirmation and should not be interpreted as prediction of resistant infection in the overall sepsis population. The association with XDR infection was exploratory, based on only 20 events, and requires confirmation in larger independent cohorts. Because RIN-IM assessment and microbiological sampling were not fully time-synchronized, these findings should not be interpreted as real-time microbiological prediction or evidence of clinical utility. RIN-IM should not replace culture-based diagnosis, susceptibility testing, individual risk-factor assessment, local antibiograms, or clinical judgment. The observed associations do not establish a direct biological relationship between RIN-IM and microbial burden or antimicrobial resistance.

42935506.title: Curtobacterium albidum/citreum bacteremia in an intensive care unit patient: The first case report.
42935506.abstract: A 70-year-old man was admitted to a local hospital complaining of fever for 3 days. After 8 days of hospitalization, his platelet count began to decrease, his respiratory rate increased, and he was transferred to the intensive care unit of our hospital. His vital signs upon admission were as follows: Glasgow Coma Scale score, 10 (E3V1M6); pulse, 118 bpm; blood pressure, 119/68 mmHg; respiratory rate, 26/min; peripheral capillary oxygen saturation, 99% on 5 L/min of oxygen; as well as generalized jaundice. Blood cultures obtained on day one were negative, and the patient's general condition gradually improved. However, on day 20, gram-positive rods were isolated from two of the four blood cultures obtained (aerobic bottles only). Vancomycin was initiated, and the following day the infecting organism was identified as Curtobacterium albidum/citreum. However, a second blood culture obtained on day 22 was still positive. Bone marrow examination confirmed a diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and chemotherapy was initiated on day 25; however, the patient's general condition deteriorated, and he died on day 26. 16S rRNA analysis revealed a 99% match with C. citreum, a Corynebacterium-like gram-positive rod that colonizes rice and other crops. However, only a few human infections have been reported, including one previous report of possible catheter-related bacteremia based on recovery from a single aerobic bottle. To our knowledge, no prior case of probable clinically significant Curtobacterium bacteremia supported by repeated recovery from separate blood-culture collections has been documented. The number of reports is likely to increase as the use of matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry becomes more widespread. C. albidum/citreum can cause nosocomial infections in immunocompromised patients, and further studies are required to determine the optimal therapeutic agents.

42933837.title: Effect of interferon gamma as a treatment for post-aggressive immunosuppression in critically ill (INFINITY trial): study protocol for a randomised Bayesian double-blind controlled trial.
42933837.abstract: Critically ill patients frequently develop a delayed immune dysfunction after the initial insult, commonly referred to as post-aggressive immunosuppression (PAIS). Persistently reduced monocytic human leucocyte antigen-DR (mHLA-DR) expression is a widely used biomarker of PAIS and has been associated with intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired infections, prolonged organ support and excess late morbidity and mortality. To date, no immunostimulatory strategy has proven efficacy in improving patient-centred outcomes in this population. Interferon gamma-1b (IFN-γ1b) can restore monocyte function and antigen presentation in experimental and clinical settings and has shown biological plausibility and acceptable tolerability in critically ill patients. The INFINITY trial aims to determine whether short-course IFN-γ1b, initiated in patients with biomarker-defined PAIS, increases ventilator-free days compared with placebo. INFINITY is a national, multicentre, phase II, Bayesian, superiority, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel-group trial with a 1:1 allocation ratio conducted in 6 ICUs in France. Adult ICU patients (≥18 years) with high initial severity (Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) at ICU admission ≥6), receiving invasive mechanical ventilation at inclusion, and presenting with mHLA-DR <8000 AB/C measured between days 5 and 10 are eligible. Key non-inclusion criteria include pre-existing immunodeficiency, expected prolonged ventilation due to chronic conditions and contraindication to IFN-γ1b. Randomisation is centralised via a secure electronic system and stratified by centre. Participants receive either IFN-γ1b (Imukin) 2×106 IU (0.1 mg) subcutaneously every 24 hours for 3 consecutive days or matched placebo (0.9% sodium chloride), in addition to standard care. The primary endpoint is ventilator-free days alive at day 28. Secondary endpoints include mHLA-DR kinetics (day 0–7), lymphocyte count, ICU-acquired infections, antibiotic-free days, ICU-free days, SOFA kinetics and all-cause mortality at day 28 and day 90, alongside safety outcomes. A total of 170 participants (85 per group) are planned. Analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle using Bayesian models with pre-specified interim analyses and stopping guidelines. The study will be conducted in accordance with European regulations and was independently reviewed and approved by the French Ethics Committee Comité de Protection des Personnes Ile de France (EUCT number: 2023–5 06 725-11-00). The results will be reported in international peer-reviewed journals and presented at international and national conferences. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06694740; registered on 19 November 2024 (submitted 12 November 2024). Available at: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06694740.

42931899.title: Beyond avoiding failure: the proactive and beneficial role of appropriate antimicrobial therapy in the ICU.

42930768.title: Critical Care Ultrasound-Guided Targeted Volume Management as Precision Medicine: Predicting Clinical and Financial Impacts.
42930768.abstract: Precision medicine in the intensive care unit (ICU) is increasingly defined by individualized, bedside physiologic assessment rather than protocolized treatment algorithms. Critical care ultrasound for targeted volume management (CCUS-TVM) operationalizes this shift by helping clinicians answer two questions before administering intravenous (IV) fluids: is it safe, and will it be effective? Static measures, such as inferior vena cava (IVC) assessment and the Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (VExUS), identify venous congestion and predict fluid intolerance, while dynamic measures, such as change in left ventricular outflow tract velocity time integral or carotid flow time after passive leg raise, predict volume responsiveness. Together, these tools allow clinicians to tailor resuscitation to an individual patient's underlying hemodynamics, complementing the four-interface model of shock physiology. Recent meta-analyses and the 2024 Society and Critical Care Medicine and 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines show that CCUS-TVM-particularly dynamic assessment-contributes to fewer episodes of renal replacement therapy and mechanical ventilation, shorter ICU stays, and decreased mortality. Beyond clinical benefit, this communication presents an original, exploratory estimate of the potential per-patient cost savings associated with dynamic CCUS-TVM in sepsis- approximately $2600-4400-driven by reductions in renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation, and ICU length of stay. Taken together, CCUS-TVM offers a clinically validated and economically favorable framework for advancing precision medicine in resuscitation.

42928831.title: High-Dose Tigecycline for Multidrug-Resistant Serratia Infections in Critically Ill Adults: A Systematic Review of Direct and Indirect Clinical Evidence.
42928831.abstract: Evidence for high-dose tigecycline in severe multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections comes mainly from non-Serratia cohorts. Its value in critically ill adults with resistant Serratia infection is uncertain. PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, and Consensus were searched up to July 17, 2026. Two evidence sets addressed high-dose tigecycline effectiveness, pharmacokinetics, and safety, and clinical and microbiological evidence for resistant Serratia. Study-level risk ratios were presented without pooling. Searches identified 2,294 records, and 36 studies reported in 37 publications were included. No study reported a verified high-dose regimen in confirmed resistant Serratia infection with a separately extractable organism-specific outcome. Six observational studies used the same high-dose and standard-dose definitions. Fixed 28-day or 30-day mortality risk ratios ranged from 0.34 to 1.30, and all 95% confidence intervals crossed 1.0. Clinical response favored high dose in two studies, with risk ratios of 1.73 (95% confidence interval: 1.22-2.46) and 1.48 (95% confidence interval: 1.08-2.02). Microbiological response favored high dose in two studies, with risk ratios of 1.75 (95% confidence interval: 1.09-2.81) and 1.92 (95% confidence interval: 1.12-3.28). No pooled estimate was calculated. High dose produced a greater fibrinogen decline in one cohort (-3.05 ± 1.67 versus -1.75 ± 1.90 g/L; p=0.038) and more hepatic or platelet abnormalities in another. Direct evidence for high-dose tigecycline in resistant Serratia infection is absent. Indirect studies show possible response benefits without a consistent survival advantage. Treatment decisions should consider infection site, susceptibility, active alternatives, and coagulation risk. By synthesizing both pathogen-specific studies and relevant indirect clinical evidence, this review aimed to provide a more comprehensive assessment of the potential role of high-dose tigecycline in critically ill adults with resistant S. marcescens infections.

42928527.title: Illness Severity Modifies the Mortality Burden of Sepsis in Critically Ill Adults: Evidence of Severity-Dependent Shock Heterogeneity in 64,703 ICU Admissions.
42928527.abstract: Illness severity scores such as SAPS II implicitly assume that condition-specific mortality contributions - including that of sepsis - remain constant across the severity spectrum. From a shock pathophysiology perspective, distributive shock from sepsis may carry different reversibility profiles than cardiogenic or neurogenic shock at equivalent severity. Whether illness severity modifies the mortality burden of sepsis remains unevaluated. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 64,703 ICU admissions from MIMIC-IV (2008-2019). Sepsis was defined by Sepsis-3 criteria; baseline severity by SAPS II with fractional polynomial modeling. Multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms assessed effect modification; average marginal effects (AMEs) were estimated across the SAPS II spectrum. ICU-type interaction heterogeneity was tested. Sepsis occurred in 42.7% of admissions; 30-day mortality was 12.9%. The sepsis-mortality association varied significantly by severity (interaction p<0.001). At SAPS II 30, sepsis was associated with higher mortality (AME +3.8%, 95%CI 3.2-4.3%); this attenuated and became non-significant at SAPS II 50-55. At SAPS II 80, septic patients had lower adjusted mortality (AME -7.3%, 95%CI -9.6 to -5.0%). This crossover was present in unadjusted data (SAPS II ≥70: 61.5% vs 69.2%) and consistent across eight sensitivity analyses. The mortality burden of sepsis is not constant across the severity spectrum: it confers additional risk at low-to-moderate severity, but a crossover pattern emerges with lower mortality at high severity - robust in crude and adjusted analyses and consistent across ICU types. These findings implicate severity-dependent shock reversibility and have implications for prognostication, clinical trial design, and quality benchmarking.

42927992.title: Can Platelet Indices Predict Gram-Positive Bacterial Infections in ICU Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
42927992.abstract: BackgroundUntil now, blood culture remains the gold standard for diagnosis of bloodstream infections (BSI). We investigated the diagnostic accuracy of complete blood count (CBC), particularly platelet indices, as a less expensive and more rapid alternative for the diagnosis of BSI, which allows for early proper antibiotic administration.MethodsA total of 169 patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) from July 2023 to July 2025 who had suspected BSI and were tested via blood culture (BC). Patients were classified into a BSI group (n = 143) and a non-BSI group (n = 26). The BSI group was further classified into three subgroups as Gram negative bacteremia (n = 87), Gram positive bacteremia (n = 46) and candidemia (n = 10). Demographic parameters and hematological parameters were recorded and compared between the groups. To evaluate sensitivity and specificity, we constructed receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.ResultsPatients with positive blood culture had significantly higher PCT, CRP, Neutrophil, PDW, MPV, MPV/PLT, PDW/PLT, and lower PWR, MPV/PCT, PDW/PCT & PLT/PCT compared to patients with negative blood culture. PLT/PCT, PCT, MPV/PCT, CRP, PDW & PDW/PCT have the highest AUCs (AUCs were 0.73, 0.71, 0.70, 0.69, 0.69 & 0.68, respectively). RDW, MPV/PLT, and PDW/PLT significantly increase, and platelet count significantly decreases among patients with Gram-positive compared to patients with Gram-negative bacterial infection. RDW, platelet, MPV/PLT & PDW/PLT have the highest AUC and accuracy in diagnosis of Gram-positive bacteria (AUC were 0.64, 0.62, 0.62 & 0.62, respectively).ConclusionThe RDW, platelet count, MPV/PLT, and PDW/PLT demonstrated the greatest accuracy in predicting Gram-positive bacterial infections.

42926925.title: Meningitis, encephalitis, and beyond: A practical intensive care unit guide to severe central nervous system infections.
42926925.abstract: Infections of the central nervous system can require immediate admission to an intensive care unit (ICU) because of initial severe neurologic presentation or systemic complications or may be encountered during the course of a hospital stay because of secondary complications. Brain infections include community-acquired or healthcare-associated meningitis, ventriculitis, encephalitis, and brain abscesses, which share specific clinical features but have different pathophysiology, risk factors, and outcomes. In this review, we will provide a practice-based overview of severe presentations of brain infections as encountered by the intensivist, focusing on early decision-making, the sequence of diagnostic and management decisions, and encountered complications. We illustrate the review with case examples to offer real-life illustrations of challenging decision-points. Key take-home points include understanding the first-hour priorities for de novo presentation of meningitis and encephalitis with a focus on early initiation of antimicrobial treatment; awareness of limitations in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-based diagnostics for early encephalitis and in healthcare-associated meningitis and ventriculitis, and the importance of an expedited, non-CSF-based diagnostic approach to brain abscesses.

42923688.title: Prior use of dihydropyridines is associated with reduced mortality among patients with sepsis in the intensive care unit: a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV database.
42923688.abstract: Evidence regarding the survival benefits of dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers in patients with sepsis is limited. This study aimed to investigate whether prior use of dihydropyridines is associated with improved survival in patients with sepsis in the intensive care unit (ICU). We extracted relevant information on patients diagnosed with sepsis from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database (version 2.0). Patients were divided into a dihydropyridine group and a no-dihydropyridine group based on drug prescription records. The primary outcomes were 30-day, 60-day, and 90-day mortality. After propensity score matching, univariate and multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the association between dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker use and survival in patients with sepsis. A total of 20,796 patients were included in the analysis. After propensity score matching, 1,232 patients who had used dihydropyridines and 1,232 who had not were included. Multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models showed that prior use of dihydropyridines was significantly associated with reduced 30-day (hazard ratio [HR], 0.800; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.662-0.968; P = 0.021), 60-day (HR, 0.776; 95% CI, 0.653-0.922; P = 0.004), and 90-day (HR, 0.760; 95% CI, 0.645-0.895; P = 0.001) mortality. In this retrospective cohort study, prior use of dihydropyridines was associated with improved survival among patients with sepsis in the ICU.

42921842.title: Molecular Characterization and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns of Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative Bacilli Isolated from Intensive Care Unit Patients in a Tertiary Care Hospital.
42921842.abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacilli (GNB) present a critical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), severely limiting therapeutic options. This study evaluated the prevalence and molecular resistance mechanisms of GNB in ICU patients. Hospital-acquired urinary tract infections are among the most common healthcare-associated infections in ICUs. The emergence of MDR Gram-negative bacilli has reduced available treatment options and increased morbidity. This study aimed to evaluate antimicrobial resistance patterns and characterize major resistance genes among Gram-negative bacilli isolated from ICU patients. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from 2019 to 2022 across two tertiary centers in North India. We analyzed 427 non-duplicate MDR GNB isolates from ICU urinary samples. Identification followed standard biochemical protocols. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed through Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion as per Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. Phenotypic detection of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL), AmpC, and carbapenemase production was performed, alongside molecular characterization of resistance genes (blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M, blaNDM, blaIMP, blaVIM, blaOXA). In the present study, most isolates originated from the medical ICU (66.0%). Most MDR GNB isolates were from males (52%), and the majority of patients belonged to the age group > 60 years. The predominant isolates were Escherichia coli (60%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (19%), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (12%). Alarmingly high resistance rates to Cephalosporins (>90%), Fluoroquinolones (>80%), and Carbapenems (70% overall) were observed. Overall, 40.9% of isolates were ESBL producers, 24.82% AmpC producers, and 13.81% Carbapenemase producers. Molecular analysis revealed a high prevalence of blaCTX M (100%), blaVIM (66%), and blaNDM (48%). The high prevalence of diverse resistance mechanisms underscores the impact of indiscriminate antimicrobial use. Implementation of stringent antimicrobial stewardship and robust infection control practices is essential to mitigate the spread of MDR pathogens in critical care settings.

42910296.title: Sepsis without borders: Why Europe-China collaboration is essential for precision critical care.

42906252.title: Does transfusion of blood products increase the risk of multidrug-resistant infections in critically ill patients?
42906252.abstract: To investigate the association between transfusion of blood products during intensive care unit (ICU) stay and the incidence of ICU-acquired colonisation and infection with multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria (ICU-MDR-col, ICU-MDR-inf, respectively). Secondary analysis of two prospective multicentre cohort studies conducted in eight ICUs in France. Adult patients admitted to participating ICUs were enrolled consecutively from May 2019 to June 2021. All patients underwent systematic screening for colonisation with MDR bacteria at admission and weekly thereafter. Exposure to transfusion of blood products during ICU stay, including packed red blood cells (PRBCs), fresh frozen plasma (FFP) and platelet concentrates (PCs), was recorded. The primary outcome was the incidence of ICU-MDR-col and/or ICU-MDR-inf (ICU-MDR-col/inf) until ICU discharge, censored at day 28. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of ICU-MDR-col and ICU-MDR-inf, considered separately. Associations were assessed using mixed-effects Poisson regression models adjusted for prespecified confounders. Subgroup analyses were performed according to immunosuppression status at ICU admission. Among 1103 patients, 358 (32.5%) received transfusion of any blood product. Overall, 292 (26.5%) patients experienced at least one ICU-MDR-col/inf event. Transfusion was associated with an increased incidence of ICU-MDR-col/inf (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR] 1.31, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06-1.62; p = 0.013), mainly driven by ICU-MDR-inf (aIRR 1.62, 95% CI 1.16-2.24; p = 0.004), but not ICU-MDR-col considered individually. This association was restricted to PRBC transfusion. No significant heterogeneity was observed according to immunosuppression status. Transfusion of PBRCs was associated with an increased incidence of ICU-acquired MDR infections, with no significant heterogeneity observed according to immunosuppression status. These findings support a restrictive approach to transfusion and warrant further investigation into its immunological and ecological consequences in critically ill patients.

42904452.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Trends in COVID-19 Patients with Hospital Infection in Intensive Care: A Retrospective Study in Central Italy, 2020-2022.
42904452.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was exacerbated by COVID-19 pandemic. This study describes prevalence and trends of AMR in patients with diagnosed severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection admitted during 2020-2022 to the intensive care unit (ICU) in Molise region, central Italy. A retrospective study was conducted, including patients aged ≥ 18 years with at least one positive bacterial or fungal culture during ICU stay. Data were related to patient demographics, ICU outcomes, healthcare-associated infections, and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles. During the 2020-2022 period, 103 ICU admissions met the inclusion criteria, yielding 268 isolations, of which 157 underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Apart from high proportion of Candida albicans, Gram-negative bacteria predominated, with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Acinetobacter baumannii among the most frequent. Resistance to beta-lactams and carbapenems was consistently high, while it ranged from 53.8% to 66.7% to fluoroquinolones and remained above 50% to aminoglycosides. Tetracycline resistance showed significant year-to-year variation, increasing in 2022 compared with both 2020 and 2021. AMR rates in COVID-19 patients in ICU were persistently high throughout the pandemic, with critical resistance levels in Gram-negatives, underlining the need to reinforce infection prevention and control measures and antimicrobial stewardship programs and align prescribing practices with World Health Organization AWaRe recommendations, even during public health emergencies.

42904370.title: Prevalence, Clinical Correlation, and Antifungal Susceptibility of Candidemia Patients in Various Intensive Care Unit's of a Tertiary Care Hospital in Jharkhand.
42904370.abstract: Candidemia represents grave healthcare-associated fungal infections. Being an opportunistic pathogen, Candida is becoming a cause of significant morbidity and mortality in patients at greater risk. The aim of the present study was to examine Candida isolates collected from blood cultures in intensive care unit patients at a tertiary care hospital in Jharkhand and to illustrate their various properties and its clinical correlations along with various antifungal susceptibility profiles. In this prospective study of 12 months, Candida isolates from blood were differentiated by conventional methods and compared by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight and VITEK 2 compact automated system. Findings were clinically correlated with various parameters like death, patients requiring assisted ventilation, and number of hospital stay days. Out of 985 positive blood cultures, 95 were Candida species (9.64%). Seventy-nine isolates were Non-Albicans Candida (83.15%) and 16 isolates were Candida albicans (16.8%). Candida tropicalis 30 isolates (31.5%) was isolated, followed by Candida glabrata, Candida parapsilosis, and others. Mean age of the patients was 18.67 years. With a mortality rate of 45.2%, children were mostly deceased, accounting for 58% of all the deaths. Male predominance is seen, constituting 72% of all the deaths. C. tropicalis and C. glabrata were the most common organisms leading to death, both contributing 31% each, while C. tropicalis is the most common organism due to which patients required assisted ventilation. These isolates were susceptible to common antifungals. Judicious start of antifungal drugs in patients of high risk is very important. This study will help clinicians to opt for best antifungal agents in the management of candidemia shortening hospital stay days.

42903729.title: Renal Dose-Adjustment Concordance in Critically Ill Patients with AKI and CKD: A Cross-sectional Study.
42903729.journal: Iranian journal of pharmaceutical research : IJPR
42903729.abstract: Kidney dysfunction complicates drug dosing in the intensive care unit (ICU). Guidance is well established for stable chronic kidney disease (CKD) but is less certain in acute kidney injury (AKI), in which renal function can change rapidly. To assess concordance between prescribed maintenance regimens and reference-based renal dose-adjustment recommendations for adults with AKI, CKD, or AKI superimposed on CKD. This cross-sectional study included 80 adults admitted to four ICUs in 2024. Acute kidney injury was classified according to the Risk, Injury, Failure, Loss, and end-stage renal disease (RIFLE) criteria using serial creatinine measurements and/or urine output, whereas CKD required documented chronicity. Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance (CrCl) was used to match patients to dosing-reference categories. Each patient-medication pair was classified once according to maintenance-dose amount and dosing interval, using UpToDate as the primary reference and the Sanford Guide as a supplementary source. Among 414 patient-medication pairs, 211 (51.0%; patient-level cluster-bootstrap 95% CI, 46.2%-55.8%) were discordant: 125 were lower and 86 were higher than recommended. Vancomycin (41.4%), ciprofloxacin (40.0%), and levofloxacin (40.0%) had the highest drug-specific discordance proportions. Nephrology and pulmonology had the highest patient-level service proportions (62.5% and 61.5%, respectively). Reference discordance was frequent, particularly for antimicrobials. Because measured exposure and clinical outcomes were unavailable, these findings identify regimens requiring review rather than confirming prescribing errors.

42898838.title: Burden and risk factors of acquisition of multi-drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria among intensive care patients at a tertiary care setting.
42898838.abstract: Multi-drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (MDR-GNB) are a major healthcare challenge, particularly among patients admitted to intensive care units (ICUs). The objective of the current study was to assess the risk of acquisition of MDR-GNB in ICU patients and the associated risk factors and outcomes. A prospective cohort study among adult ICU patients was conducted in two tertiary care hospitals in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between 2021 and 2022. Specimens were examined at admission, during stay, and before discharge for all patients. Acquisition of MDR-GNB was confirmed by a positive culture/polymerase chain reaction before discharge among patients who were negative at admission. A total of 307 patients were included. The mean age was 56.7 ± 18.2 years and 62.2% were males. Out of 307, 82 (26.7%) patients acquired MDR-GNB during their ICU stay. The most common MDR-GNB pathogens were Klebsiella spp. (47.1%), Acinetobacter spp. (14.7%), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (12.7%), Enterobacter spp. (10.8%), and Escherichia coli (5.9%). Approximately 40.2% of MDR-GNB presented as infection and 59.8% as colonization. In multi-variate analysis, the following variables were independent predictors of MDR-GNB acquisition; pneumonia at admission, central line use, urinary catheter use, renal comorbidity, and prolonged hospitalization. Patients who acquired MDR-GNB had significantly higher mortality (34.1% vs 5.3%, P<0.001) and ICU length of stay (median of 26 vs 10 days, P<0.001). The findings underscore the high risk and burden of MDR-GNB acquisition in the ICU setting. There is an urgent need for enhanced infection control strategies and antimicrobial stewardship activities to reduce MDR-GNB acquisition and its negative impact.

42898658.title: Association of early neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio trajectories with cardiac recovery and live ICU discharge in patients with sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
42898658.abstract: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SIC) is characterized by potentially reversible myocardial dysfunction accompanied by a profound systemic inflammatory response. However, the prognostic significance of early dynamic changes in the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in patients with SIC remains unclear. This study aimed to identify distinct early NLR trajectories and examine their associations with cardiac recovery and live discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU). This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with SIC admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Hebei Cangzhou Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine. NLR values were collected at ICU admission and at 24, 48, and 72 h thereafter. Latent class mixed modeling was used to identify distinct 72-h NLR trajectories. A 72-h landmark design was applied. The primary outcome was live ICU discharge within 28 days, with ICU death treated as a competing event and analyzed using Fine-Gray regression. The secondary outcome was cardiac recovery by days 5-7, defined as a follow-up left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of ≥50% or an absolute increase of ≥10 percentage points from baseline. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between NLR trajectories and cardiac recovery. A total of 510 patients contributed 2,040 longitudinal NLR measurements. Three distinct trajectories were identified: low-stable (n = 230, 45.1%), high-decreasing (n = 170, 33.3%), and persistent-high (n = 110, 21.6%). The geometric mean NLR changed from 7.85 to 6.16, from 18.47 to 8.01, and from 14.95 to 22.87, respectively, during the first 72 h. Live ICU discharge occurred in 85.7%, 67.1%, and 36.4% of patients in the three groups, respectively. Compared with the low-stable group, the adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios for live ICU discharge were 0.49 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.38-0.63; P < 0.001] for the high-decreasing group and 0.25 (95% CI, 0.17-0.37; P < 0.001) for the persistent-high group. Cardiac recovery occurred in 80.4%, 61.8%, and 42.7% of patients, respectively. The corresponding adjusted odds ratios were 0.48 (95% CI, 0.29-0.79; P = 0.004) and 0.27 (95% CI, 0.14-0.51; P < 0.001). Associations with live ICU discharge were consistent across predefined subgroups. Septic shock showed an exploratory interaction with the association between NLR trajectories and cardiac recovery (P for interaction=0.034). Sensitivity analyses yielded similar results. Early 72-h NLR trajectories were independently associated with cardiac recovery and live ICU discharge in patients with SIC. A persistent-high trajectory identified patients with the poorest prognosis, whereas a high-decreasing trajectory was associated with intermediate outcomes. Serial assessment of NLR may provide a simple and clinically accessible tool for early risk stratification in SIC, although prospective external validation is warranted.

42894723.title: Application of Machine Learning Models to Predict Tigecycline Exposure in Critically Ill Patients Using Different Limited Sampling Strategies.
42894723.abstract: The high variability in the pharmacokinetics of tigecycline may impact therapeutic efficacy, particularly in critically ill patients. This study introduces machine learning (ML) methods, aiming to clarify their effectiveness in individualized drug exposure prediction and determine the optimal modeling strategy. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) method was used to screen the covariates. Four ML models, random forest, extreme gradient boosting, multilayer perceptron, and long short-term memory network (LSTM), were trained and tested using 751 concentrations from 98 patients in the pharmacokinetic dataset to predict the area under the steady-state plasma concentration-time curve within 24 hours (AUC0-24h) of tigecycline. Furthermore, on the internal test set, we evaluated the accuracy of the published tigecycline Population Pharmacokinetics (PopPK) models. Seven covariates were screened out by LASSO method, including total bilirubin, creatinine clearance, Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, body mass index, serum creatinine, age, and prothrombin time. Internal validation showed that, among the four ML models, the LSTM model performed the best, with the combination of covariates and the plasma concentration feature "C0 + C0.5 + C6" exhibited the optimal predictive performance (R2: 0.887, RMSE: 2.496 mg·h/L, F20: 75%). In comparison, the model combining covariates with C0 was the most concise and better suited to practical computational conditions; its LSTM model was comparable to some PopPK models in terms of overall trend fitting and systematic bias control (R2: 0.818, RMSE: 3.164 mg·h/L, F20 = 60%). The LSTM model established in this study enables an accurate estimate of tigecycline AUC0-24h. Three-point sampling provided the lowest prediction error, whereas C0 alone reduced the sampling burden. These findings provide an effective modeling reference for tigecycline therapeutic drug monitoring.

42894669.title: Assessing the Influence of Propofol Sedation Versus Propofol-Free Sedation on Recovery From Sepsis and Septic Shock in Mechanically Ventilated ICU Patients: A Retrospective, Propensity-Score Matched, Cohort Study.
42894669.abstract: Propofol-mediated immunosuppression has been postulated in preclinical research, yet translational clinical evidence is lacking. We, therefore, retrospectively evaluated the influence, if any, of propofol versus non-propofol sedation on critical care requirements, prognosis, and risk of re-infection among mechanically ventilated patients with sepsis or septic shock.
