This model can assist clinicians in identifying sepsis patients at high risk for early hypothermia and implementing early intervention to reduce mortality.

42876688.title: Prognostic discrimination of SOFA-2 vs. SOFA-1 and incremental information from cardiovascular scoring and vasoactive support intensity in patients with sepsis receiving early vasoactive therapy.
42876688.abstract: Patients with sepsis who require vasoactive support during the first 24 h of intensive care represent a heterogeneous population. It is uncertain whether the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-2 score improves mortality discrimination compared with the SOFA-1 score and whether observed circulatory support intensity provides complementary prognostic information. This multicohort observational study used Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) for a 24-h conditional landmark analysis. Patients alive and still in the ICU beyond 24 h were followed from ICU admission +24 h through ICU day 28 for reconstructed all-cause mortality. We compared SOFA-1 and SOFA-2, evaluated SOFA-2 total and cardiovascular scores, analyzed first-24-h five-agent norepinephrine-equivalent peak burden (norepinephrine, epinephrine, dopamine, phenylephrine, and vasopressin), and internally evaluated an exploratory drug-composition model. Fixed strata were assessed directionally in eICU Collaborative Research Database and an independent-center high-risk stress test cohort with cohort-specific endpoints. The MIMIC-IV 24-h landmark cohort included 11,892 patients and 2,687 post-landmark deaths. SOFA-2 showed no observed discrimination advantage over SOFA-1 (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, 0.731 vs. 0.732; difference, -0.0005; 95% confidence interval, -0.0086 to 0.0076; P = 0.908). The SOFA-2 cardiovascular score had lower discrimination than the SOFA-1 cardiovascular score (0.663 vs. 0.676; P = 0.006). Mortality was 51.94% for the exploratory SOFA-2 ≥12 group and 17.09% below 12, and increased from 11.30% to 47.45% across four study-defined peak burden categories. The SOFA-2-plus-drug-composition model had an apparent AUROC of 0.768 and a bootstrap-corrected AUROC of 0.767, but it was not externally validated. Fixed strata preserved the direction of risk ranking in both external cohorts, whereas absolute risk and calibration differed. SOFA-2 did not show an observed overall mortality discrimination advantage over SOFA-1 in this population. SOFA-2 total and cardiovascular scores, together with observed vasoactive support intensity, provided complementary prognostic description at 24 h. The ≥12 rule is exploratory, and drug-related associations do not establish causal treatment effects or clinical decision utility.

42875238.title: [Role of secrum albumin-to-creatinine ratio in assessing the prognosis of sepsis].
42875238.journal: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
42875238.abstract: To investigate the role of serum albumin-to-creatinine ratio (sACR) in prognostic assessment of patients with sepsis. A retrospective cohort study was conducted. Patients with newly diagnosed sepsis admitted to the emergency intensive care unit (ICU) and comprehensive ICU of the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University from October 2023 to October 2024 were enrolled. Baseline data and laboratory parameters within 24 hours of admission, including white blood cell count (WBC), C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), serum albumin, and creatinine, were collected, and sACR was calculated. The Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II(APACHE II) and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) were recorded at admission. The 28-day survival status and survival time were documented. Patients were divided into sepsis group and septic shock group according to sepsis severity, and further divided into survivor group and non-survivor group based on 28-day outcomes. The above parameters were compared between groups. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was used to identify independent prognostic factors for 28-day mortality. Receiver operator characteristic curves (ROC curves) were plotted to evaluate the predictive value of each indicator, and the areas under the curves (AUCs) were compared using DeLong's test. A total of 177 patients with newly diagnosed sepsis were included, comprising 66 in the sepsis group and 111 in the septic shock group; 94 survived and 83 died within 28 days. Significant differences were observed between the sepsis and septic shock groups in age, WBC, CRP, PCT, APACHE II score, SOFA score, and sACR (all P<0.05), with sACR being higher in the sepsis group [2.98 (1.82, 4.10) vs. 2.26 (1.19, 3.08)]. Significant differences were also found between survivors and non-survivors in WBC, CRP, PCT, APACHE II score, SOFA score, and sACR (all P<0.05), with sACR being higher in survivors [3.17 (1.87, 4.20) vs. 1.80 (0.95, 2.25)]. Cox regression analysis showed that CRP (HR=1.004, 95%CI was 1.001-1.007, P=0.043), APACHE II score (HR=1.078, 95%CI was 1.049-1.108, P<0.001), and SOFA score (HR=1.105, 95%CI was 1.027-1.189, P=0.008) were independent risk factors for 28-day all-cause mortality, while sACR was an independent protective factor (HR=0.795, 95%CI was 0.646-0.978, P=0.030). ROC curve analysis revealed that CRP, APACHE II score, SOFA score, and sACR had certain predictive value for 28-day prognosis; the AUC of sACR was 0.765, with an optimal cut-off value of 2.446, yielding a sensitivity of 66.0% and specificity of 77.1%. DeLong's test indicated that the predictive performance of sACR was similar to that of SOFA score, superior to CRP, but inferior to APACHE II score. As a novel composite biomarker, sACR has potential adjunctive value in assessing disease severity and predicting prognosis in patients with sepsis.

42875237.title: [Correlation between glycemic variability coefficient and sepsis-induced coagulopathy and analysis of risk factors].
42875237.journal: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
42875237.abstract: To investigate the association between glycemic variability coefficient (CV) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC), analyze the related risk factors for SIC in septic patients, and further explore the clinical value of glycemic CV as a potential predictor for SIC. A retrospective case-control study was conducted. General data, laboratory findings, therapeutic interventions, and disease severity scores of septic patients admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine of the First Hospital of Qinhuangdao from July 2021 to June 2024 were collected. Blood glucose CV within 24 hours of admission was used as the exposure variable, and SIC served as the primary outcome. Patients were divided into Q1, Q2, Q3, and Q4 groups according to quartiles of glycemic CV within 24 hours of intensive care unit (ICU) admission, with Q1 as the reference. Baseline clinical characteristics were compared among the four groups. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to analyze the effect of glycemic CV on SIC occurrence after adjusting for various confounders. Subgroup analyses were used to explore potential interaction effects and further verify the robustness of the results. A restricted cubic spline model was applied to examine the dose-response relationship between glycemic CV and SIC. Patients were divided into SIC and non-SIC groups based on the presence of SIC. Univariate analysis was used to identify risk factors for SIC, and significant variables were entered into binary logistic regression to determine independent risk factors. Receiver operator characteristic curve (ROC curve) was plotted to assess the predictive value of glycemic CV for SIC. A total of 440 patients with sepsis were enrolled, including 110 in Q1 (glycemic CV<19.5%), 109 in Q2 (19.5%≤glycemic CV<26.0%), 111 in Q3 (26.0%≤glycemic CV<31.5%), and 110 in Q4 (glycemic CV≥31.5%). Multivariate logistic regression showed that after adjustment for confounders, each 10% increase in glycemic CV was associated with an increased risk of SIC [odds ratio (OR)=1.049, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.024-1.074, P<0.001]. Compared with Q1, the risk of SIC remained significantly higher in Q4 (OR=2.739, 95%CI was 1.427-5.255, P=0.002). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis revealed a linear dose-response relationship between glycemic CV and SIC risk (overall P<0.001, nonlinear P=0.828), with the risk increasing linearly as glycemic CV rose. Subgroup analyses showed no significant interaction between glycemic CV and sex, age, diabetes, Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II(APACHE II), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA), use of vasoactive agents, use of corticosteroids, or anticoagulant therapy, consistently supporting elevated glycemic CV as a risk factor for SIC. Among the 440 patients, 280 were in the non-SIC group and 160 in the SIC group. Multivariate logistic regression including significant variables from univariate analysis identified high glycemic CV (OR=1.049, 95%CI was 1.024-1.074, P<0.001), high body mass index (BMI; OR=1.175, 95%CI was 1.106-1.248, P<0.001), and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT; OR=3.286, 95%CI was 1.561-6.919, P=0.002) as independent risk factors for SIC. ROC curve analysis showed that the area under the curve (AUC) of glycemic CV for predicting SIC was 0.624, with a cutoff value of 24.5%, yielding a specificity of 52.1% and sensitivity of 70.6%. There is a positive linear relationship between glycemic CV and the risk of SIC in septic patients. High glycemic CV, high BMI, and CRRT are independent risk factors for SIC. Glycemic CV has certain predictive value for SIC, and monitoring glycemic CV may facilitate early identification and prevention of SIC, thereby improving patient outcomes.

42874286.title: What every intensivist should know about dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.
42874286.abstract: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) is an underrecognized, load dependent cause of hemodynamic instability in critically ill patients. Although classically associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, it frequently occurs in the ICU in settings such as septic shock, hypovolemia, postoperative states, and right ventricular failure. Standard shock therapies, including inotropes and afterload reduction, may paradoxically worsen obstruction and lead to escalating hemodynamic instability. Bedside echocardiography is central to diagnosis, typically revealing a small hyperdynamic left ventricle and a late-peaking Doppler profile. Management focuses on restoring preload, increasing afterload, and reducing excessive contractility. In some patients, LVOTO is secondary to right ventricular failure, requiring targeted right ventricular support. Dynamic LVOTO is a reversible and often iatrogenic cause of shock. Early recognition and physiology-guided management can rapidly improve hemodynamics and prevent harmful therapeutic escalation.

42873554.title: Escalating Vasopressor Intensity and the Goals-of-Care Documentation Gap in Septic Shock: Relevance to the Proposed Refractory Shock Threshold.
42873554.abstract: BackgroundThe 2026 joint SCCM/ESICM Delphi consensus identified vasopressor intensity as a defining feature of refractory septic shock, yet its relationship to real-world goals-of-care documentation remains unclear.ObjectivesWe assessed the association between escalating vasopressor intensity and documented surrogate goals-of-care markers among septic shock decedents.MethodsRetrospective cohort study of adult septic shock decedents in MIMIC-IV (2008-2022) requiring vasopressors ≥6 h and surviving ≥24 h after initiation. Vasopressor intensity was quantified by peak norepinephrine equivalent (NEE) dose during ICU stay and stratified as: 0.01-0.50 (stratum 1), >0.50-0.99 (stratum 2), and ≥1.00 µg/kg/min (stratum 3). The primary outcome was death without documented surrogate goals-of-care markers, defined as having neither a documented do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order nor documented palliative care involvement.ResultsThe final cohort included 2458 patients: stratum 1 (n = 1033), stratum 2 (n = 909), and stratum 3 (n = 516). Death without documented goals-of-care markers increased across strata (23.8%, 28.3%, 31.2%; p-for-trend=0.001). After multivariable adjustment, stratum 3 patients remained more likely than stratum 1 to die without documented goals-of-care markers (aOR 1.32; 95% CI 1.02-1.69; p = 0.03). Palliative care documentation declined progressively with increasing vasopressor intensity (59.2%, 52.0%, 46.9%; p-for-trend<0.001), accompanied by lower rates of integrated DNR/palliative care documentation (47.0%, 40.0%, 36.4%; p-for-trend<0.001). Patients exceeding the Delphi-proposed refractory shock threshold (NEE >0.50 µg/kg/min) were more likely to die without documented goals-of-care markers than those below the threshold (29.3% vs 23.8%; p = 0.002).ConclusionHigher vasopressor intensity was paradoxically associated with a greater likelihood of death without documented goals-of-care markers and with lower palliative care documentation. These findings suggest a disconnect between escalating physiologic severity and documentation of surrogate goals-of-care markers in refractory septic shock and warrant further evaluation.

42873407.title: The impact of intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiac surgery for infective endocarditis.
42873407.abstract: Postoperative sepsis and/or systemic inflammatory response syndrome caused by infective endocarditis (IE) can lead to significant postoperative mortality. Intraoperative hemoadsorption therapy has shown promising results in the treatment of sepsis and dysregulated inflammatory response during cardiac surgery. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of intraoperative hemoadsorption in high-risk patients with IE undergoing cardiac surgery. A total of 176 high-risk patients with IE were enrolled from 10/2020 to 10/2024. Patients with intraoperative hemoadsorption (HA group, n = 93) were compared to patients without hemoadsorption (control, n = 83). The primary endpoint was a composite of 30-day mortality, incidence of vasoplegic syndrome within the first 24 h and 7 days postoperatively, and intensive care (ICU) stay, analyzed using an unmatched hierarchical win-ratio method. There were no differences in baseline characteristics between the groups. The mean hemoadsorption time was 106 ± 61 min in the HA group. Vasoplegic syndrome was more frequent in the control group (49.4% vs. 24.7%, p < 0.001). Importantly, 30-day mortality was also significantly lower with intraoperative hemoadsorption (7.5% vs. 20.5%, p = 0.003). The mean ICU stay was shorter in the HA group (7.8 ± 4.6 vs. 11.5 ± 4.2 days, p < 0.001). The analysis met the primary endpoint in favor of patients receiving intraoperative hemoadsorption (win ratio 3.83; 95% CI 2.55, 5.74; p < 0.001). In high-risk cardiac surgery patients with IE, the intraoperative use of hemoadsorption was associated with a significantly lower incidence of postoperative vasoplegic syndrome and lower overall 30-day mortality. These findings should be interpreted in the context of the study's methodological limitations and confirmed in future randomized controlled trials. This study was approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB00012919) of the French Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery (CERCSFCTCV20251021).

42872518.title: Dynamic Co-Evolution of C-Reactive Protein and Albumin in Early Sepsis: A Group-Based Dual-Trajectory Analysis for Risk Stratification.
42872518.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
42872518.abstract: The coupled evolution of inflammation and metabolic dysfunction during early sepsis is incompletely characterized. Although C-reactive protein (CRP) and albumin (ALB) are established markers of these processes, their joint longitudinal patterns have rarely been examined. We used group-based dual-trajectory modelling (GBDTM) to identify distinct coevolutionary patterns of CRP and ALB and to evaluate their associations with mortality in patients with sepsis. This retrospective observational study included patients admitted to the ICU of Beijing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Capital Medical University, between June 2014 and March 2025. All included adults met the Sepsis-3 criteria. Among 462 patients with sepsis, serial CRP and ALB measurements obtained on days 1, 3, 5, 7 and 14 after ICU admission were analysed using GBDTM. The selected three-class model showed acceptable classification quality (entropy = 0.80; class-specific average posterior probabilities [AvePPs] = 0.84-0.92) and identified slow-decreasing (79.65%), rapid-decreasing (10.39%) and increasing (9.96%) inflammatory phenotypes. The 28-day mortality rate was highest in the increasing group (52.2% vs. 32.6% and 33.3%; log-rank p = 0.034). In the fully adjusted Cox model, the increasing trajectory was associated with 28-day mortality (HR 1.943, 95% CI: 1.202-3.140; p = 0.007) and 60-day mortality (HR 1.946, 95% CI: 1.218-3.108; p = 0.005). Parsimonious models adjusted for age, sex, and SOFA or the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score yielded broadly similar estimates. Joint CRP-ALB trajectories identify clinically interpretable dynamic phenotypes during early sepsis. These findings support the joint trajectory as a hypothesis-generating, complementary phenotyping marker that requires external prospective validation.

42872280.title: Sepsis and Chronic Liver Disease: Mortality and Prognostic Factors. A 12-Year Retrospective Analytical-Descriptive Observational Study.
42872280.abstract: Patients with chronic liver disease are at increased risk of developing infections and sepsis. Although high mortality in this context is well documented, the prognostic factors associated with poorer survival in patients admitted to the ICU have not been fully defined. To describe the characteristics of critically ill patients with chronic liver disease and sepsis, to determine mortality, and to analyze the factors associated with a poorer prognosis. An observational, retrospective, descriptive and analytical study of a cohort of patients with chronic liver disease and a diagnosis of sepsis admitted to the ICU at the Hospital Clínico Universitario Lozano Blesa, in Zaragoza, Spain, between 2012 and 2023. A total of 71 patients were included, 69% were male, and 51% had alcohol-related liver disease. In the bivariate analysis, higher Child-Pugh and MELD scores at admission, elevated bilirubin and INR levels, as well as the type of infection, were associated with a poorer prognosis. The ICU mortality rate was 54.9%. Independent predictors of mortality were a higher MELD score at admission (OR: 1.21; 95% CI: 1.02-1.45), Gram-positive bacterial infection (OR: 7.58; 95% CI: 1.95-29.50), and fungal infection (OR: 7.36; 95% CI: 2.10-25.75). Sepsis in patients with chronic liver disease is associated with high mortality. A higher MELD score at admission and the presence of Gram-positive bacterial or fungal infections were identified as independent prognostic factors for death.

42871828.title: Global Direct In-scope Suction Study: An EAU-endourology Multicenter Prospective Collaboration (DISS-study).
42871828.abstract: Direct in-scope suction (DISS) facilitates continuous stone dust evacuation during flexible ureteroscopy (FURS), but prospective evidence validating its clinical efficacy and safety remains limited. To evaluate the stone-free rates (SFRs), perioperative outcomes, and limitations of DISS during successfully completed FURS for renal and ureteric stones in real-world practice, with the primary outcome being 30-d computed tomography (CT)-determined SFR. A prospective, multicenter, investigator-led registry was conducted across 16 centers in 14 countries (NCT05297331). Adults undergoing FURS with the Pusen 7.5-Fr DISS scope for any-sized renal/ureteric stones were included. The primary outcome was 30-d postoperative noncontrast CT SFR, classified as grade A (zero residual fragments [ZRF]) and grade B (single ≤2-mm fragment). Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of ZRF status. A total of 540 patients (median age 55 yr; 57% male) were enrolled. Anomalous kidneys were present in 12% (horseshoe 5.0% and malrotation 3.9%). Median stone volume was 590 mm3. Overall SFR (grades A and B) was 93% (501/540; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 90%-95%), with grade A achieved in 71% (386/540). Major complications were rare: no sepsis requiring intensive care unit admission, no transfusions, and only 2.6% ureteral access sheath (UAS)-related injuries (all Traxer grade 1). Postoperative fever >38°C occurred in 6.7% of the patients (36/540). On multivariable analysis for renal stones, stone volume (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.56, 95% CI = 0.39-0.79; p = 0.001) predicted lower odds of grade A status, whereas prestenting (adjusted OR 1.32, 95% CI = 0.76-2.33; p = 0.3) and UAS use (adjusted OR 0.76, 95% CI = 0.46-1.26; p = 0.3) were not statistically significantly associated with grade A status. Flexible ureteroscopy for kidney and ureteral stones using the 7.5-Fr DISS achieves high SFR with low morbidity in real-world practice. Stone burden remains a key determinant of complete renal stone clearance using DISS.

42869739.title: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT in Sepsis.
42869739.abstract: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tompgraphy/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) has emerged as a valuable whole-body metabolic imaging modality in sepsis and related systemic infectious disorders. Exploiting increased glucose metabolism in activated inflammatory cells, it facilitates localization of occult infective foci, detection of septic embolization, and guidance of source control when conventional investigations are inconclusive. Evidence demonstrates high diagnostic yield and meaningful impact on clinical management, particularly in sepsis of unknown origin and high-risk bacteraemia. However, diagnostic accuracy depends on appropriate patient preparation and timing. This review summarizes current evidence, practical challenges, emerging applications, and future research priorities for integrating 18F-FDG PET/CT into sepsis care.

42868705.title: Association between the duration of the first hemofilter after septic shock and septic shock resolution in severely burned patients receiving continuous blood purification.
42868705.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42868705.abstract: Septic shock is a major cause of mortality in severe burn patients. Our objective was to evaluate the association between the duration of the first hemofilter following septic shock and recovery from septic shock in severely burned patients treated with continuous blood purification combined with adsorption. A prospective, quasi- experimental study at department of Intensive Care, Vietnam National Burn Hospital. The study consisted of 55 episodes of septic shock in 38 severe burn patients with total burn size ≥ 20% of total body surface area. Continuous blood purification using the oXiris hemofilter conducted within 6 h of septic shock (SS) diagnosis, and after raising systolic blood pressure to above 90 mmHg. TNF-α and IL-6 concentrations decreased significantly over time after filtration, with mean hourly reductions of 0.33 pg/mL (SE = 0.16; p = 0.037) and 5.37 pg/mL (SE = 2.29; p = 0.019), respectively. After 24 h of continuous blood purification, plasma endotoxin levels decreased significantly compared with those at 6 h after continuous blood purification (47 (27.5-89.55) pg/mL vs. 68.3 (53.45-120.25) pg/mL, p = 0.003). The longer the duration of the first filtration session after septic shock, the higher the IL-6 concentration measured at 24 h after septic shock (r = 0.36, p = 0.008). Replacement of the first hemofilter at 12 h after initiation of blood purification increased the likelihood of septic shock resolution by 3.89-fold (p = 0.001). The predictive performance for shock resolution was moderate (AUC = 0.74, sensitivity: 75%, specificity: 73.68%). The longer the duration of the first filtration session after septic shock, the higher the IL-6 concentration at 24 h. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that the pre-CVVHDF SOFA score, pre-CVVHDF plasma IL-6 concentration, and first hemofilter replacement within 12 h were independent factors associated with septic shock reversal.

42865940.title: Epidemiology, risk factors and clinical outcome of community-acquired pneumonia in severely immunosuppressed patients: a comprehensive analysis from the multinational, prospective CAPNETZ Cohort.
42865940.abstract: Despite growing evidence that immunosuppression (IS) influences aetiology and prognosis of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), there remains a lack of data from representative multicentre studies. The multinational prospective CAPNETZ study includes patients with CAP and HIV since 2017, and with other causes of IS since 2020. We present the first comprehensive analysis of patients with CAP and IS (HIV with low CD4 cells, systemic steroids, immunosuppressive drugs, antineoplastic treatment, neutropenia, primary immunodeficiency, transplantation, haematological neoplasia) included within CAPNETZ until December 2023. IS cases were matched 1:1 with non-IS patients. The primary end-point was 30-day mortality and/or organ replacement therapy. Additionally, cases of CAP caused by non-core respiratory pathogens (NCRPs) according to an international consensus were evaluated. Univariate and multivariate risk factor analyses and evaluation of predictive scores by receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed. We included 232 patients with IS, most commonly after antineoplastic therapy (37.5%), systemic steroids (36.2%) and immunosuppressive drugs (35.8%). 10.3% reached the primary end-point. Overall, IS was not associated with prognosis compared to matched non-IS patients, but patients with immunosuppressive drugs had a significantly lower risk. The qSOFA, CRB-65 and CURB-65 scores showed limited prediction (area under the curve 0.57-0.64) and insufficient sensitivity for the primary end-point. CAP caused by NCRPs occurred in 16.4% in IS and was associated with transplantation, previous anti-infective treatment and intensive care unit admission, but SARS-CoV-2, Haemophilus influenzae and Streptococcus pneumoniae were the most common pathogens in both groups. This study demonstrates the relevance and heterogeneity of CAP in IS and highlights the need for individualised risk stratification and treatment.

42865138.title: Calprotectin as a Prognostic Marker for Sepsis Independent of Renal Dysfunction.
42865138.abstract: The role of calprotectin in sepsis pathophysiology is becoming increasingly recognized; however, optimal biomarkers for sepsis prognosis are lacking. We compared the prognostic accuracy of calprotectin with that of established biomarkers. In this single-center prospective cohort study, patients who met the Sepsis-3 criteria were recruited between December 2022 and January 2024. Blood samples were collected at sepsis recognition (day 0) in the emergency department and on days 3 and 7 during the intensive care unit admission. Ninety patients with community-onset sepsis were included (median age, 79 yrs [69-85]; 51 women [56.7%]), and 17 patients (18.9%) died during hospitalization. Pneumonia was the most common etiology in both survivors and non-survivors. Calprotectin showed good prognostic performance across all time points, without significant temporal differences (area under the curve [AUC], day 0, 0.785 [95% confidence interval, 0.681-0.890]; day 3, 0.800 [0.680-0.921]; day 7, 0.813 [0.696-0.930]; all P <0.001). After estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) adjustment, the predictive performance of calprotectin was preserved, whereas presepsin and procalcitonin showed significant renal function dependency. Calprotectin did not significantly correlate with eGFR and showed good prognostic performance regardless of renal dysfunction status. Incremental value analyses revealed that serial calprotectin measurements provided no significant improvement over baseline assessment. In pneumonia-induced sepsis, calprotectin consistently showed the highest AUC, regardless of renal adjustment. Calprotectin demonstrated reliable prognostic performance for hospital mortality in community-onset sepsis independently of renal dysfunction, warranting validation in larger cohorts. A single measurement at initial presentation could provide clinically useful early prognostic information.

42864750.title: Glucose control and clinical outcomes in surgical patients: A narrative review.
42864750.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
42864750.abstract: Perioperative hyperglycemia occurs in up to 40% of noncardiac and 80% of cardiac surgery patients, frequently independent of a diabetes diagnosis; it is driven by the neuroendocrine stress response, inflammatory cytokine release, and postoperative insulin resistance. Elevated glucose promotes protein glycosylation, which impairs wound healing and immune function, and it has been consistently associated with surgical site infection, anastomotic leak, prolonged length of stay, and increased mortality across surgical subspecialties. This narrative review examines biochemical aspects of glycogen metabolism and stress-induced insulin resistance, synthesizes evidence linking hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) thresholds to surgical outcomes, and summarizes contemporary guidelines from the American Diabetes Association, Endocrine Society, European Society of Cardiology, Society of Critical Care Medicine, and Surviving Sepsis Campaign. Current consensus favors moderate, protocolized glucose targets (generally 100-180 mg/dL) while avoiding iatrogenic hypoglycemia. Preoperative optimization toward an HbA1c near 7%, judicious carbohydrate loading, and avoidance of glycemic extremes offer meaningful, modifiable strategies to improve outcomes in surgical and critically ill surgical patients.

42864644.title: Periprosthetic joint infection as the leading indication associated with in-hospital death after revision hip and knee arthroplasty: a ten-year single-centre retrospective cohort study of 103 in-hospital deaths among 2495 patients.
42864644.journal: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
42864644.abstract: Revision arthroplasty procedures are associated with increased in-hospital morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to characterise in-hospital death after revision hip and knee arthroplasty, with particular focus on periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) as the leading indication among decedents. In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, all patients who died in hospital after revision hip or knee arthroplasty between 2014 and 2024 were identified among 2495 patients with revision surgery coded as OPS 5-821* and 5-823*. Primary procedures and patients younger than 18 years were excluded. Clinical and microbiological data of these 103 decedents were reviewed to characterise the circumstances, timing and causes of in-hospital death, including ICU admission, septic shock, and reoperation. Clinical characteristics, causes of death, and treatment strategies were described according to revision indication for periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), periprosthetic fracture (PF), and other indications. Of 2495 patients undergoing revision surgery over the study period, 103 patients (4.1%) died in hospital. Decedents were predominantly elderly, with a median age of 80 years (IQR 70-85) and a higher proportion of women (58.3%) than men (41.7%). PJI was the indication for revision in the majority of decedents (n = 78/103, 75.7%), and sepsis was the leading cause of death overall (n = 69/103, 67.0%) and among patients with PJI (n = 64/78, 82.1%). Patients with PJI had elevated CRP-level, with median value of 260.0 mg/l (IQR 148.5-339.3) and nearly half showed polymicrobial joint infection (n = 36/78, 46.2%). PJI was the leading indication among patients who died in hospital after revision arthroplasty. Positive blood cultures, elevated preoperative CRP, and polymicrobial infection characterised this cohort of fatal cases and may reflect greater disease severity, although this descriptive analysis cannot establish them as independent risk factors. Comparative studies including surviving patients are needed to confirm which characteristics independently predict adverse outcomes and to inform perioperative risk stratification and surgical decision-making.

42864500.title: Mapping the knowledge landscape and identifying frontiers of mitochondrial dysfunction in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: a four-decade bibliometric and visualized analysis.
42864500.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction has been recognized as a central pathogenic event and is under active investigation as a candidate therapeutic target in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). This study aims to employ multi-tool bibliometric analysis to systematically map the four-decade intellectual landscape of this field, thereby identifying emerging research hotspots and outlining priority-setting directions for future pharmacological investigation. Because publication and citation metrics quantify scholarly attention rather than therapeutic efficacy, the pathways highlighted here reflect research trends and priority-setting signals, not established therapeutic targets. A comprehensive literature retrieval was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus up to March 18, 2026. Following rigorous data cleaning, 837 publications were analyzed using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix R package to visually evaluate publication trends, knowledge networks, and evolving research hotspots. Cumulative publication output exhibits sustained exponential growth (R2 = 0.997), accelerating significantly post-2010. China and the USA dominate global productivity, though institutional collaboration networks reveal pronounced regional clustering. Notably, publication hubs have transitioned significantly from traditional critical care journals to molecular and pharmacological journals, consistent with a shifting emphasis of scholarly attention toward molecular and pharmacological research themes. Keyword and citation burst analyses suggest that the research frontier has evolved from broad physiological observations to specific subcellular executioners. Mitochondria-mediated programmed cell death (apoptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis) and oxidative stress have become the most prominent bibliometric hotspots and candidate pharmacological targets. The field of SA-AKI research has shown a pronounced, publication-driven shift from clinical phenotyping to the target-driven molecular deconstruction of mitochondrial damage; we emphasize that this result reflects research priorities, not proven therapeutic efficacy of these targets. To overcome current translational bottlenecks and off-target effects of existing agents, future drug development should transition from isolated in vitro models toward clinical multi-omics validation. Developing innovative targeted delivery systems (such as engineered nanomaterials and exosomes) and multi-target synergistic therapies will need rigorous empirical testing to determine whether they can precisely mitigate the complex SA-AKI "mitochondrial storm".

42863577.title: Integrated mechanisms of the Gut-X axis and multi-organ injury in Sepsis.
42863577.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome defined by infection-triggered dysregulation of the host response, and its persistently high mortality and marked clinical heterogeneity remain major barriers to early risk stratification and individualized management. While the gut is increasingly recognized as a key modulator of the systemic sepsis response, current evidence does not support a universal, upstream causal role for intestinal alterations in the initiation of multi-organ injury. In this review, we synthesize current evidence linking gut microbial dysbiosis and intestinal barrier dysfunction to the systemic dissemination and perturbation of microbial and host-derived signals in sepsis. We organize the downstream effects of individual gut-organ axes into three interconnected host-response domains. These domains are immune-inflammatory dysregulation, metabolic reprogramming, and neuroendocrine dysregulation. These domains overlap and have no established hierarchical order. The same signal may engage several domains simultaneously. We further classify intestinal alterations according to three analytical roles. These are prediction, mediation, and amplification. We also propose that heterogeneous organ phenotypes emerge from interactions between shared systemic signals and organ-specific susceptibility. Importantly, definitive evidence for a causal role remains scarce in human sepsis because the temporal sequence of these processes is incompletely defined and because infection source, antibiotics, nutrition, vasoactive support, secondary infection, and other intensive-care exposures substantially modify both the gut and distant organs. Ageing-related barrier vulnerability, immunosenescence, inflammaging, frailty, sarcopenia, and reduced physiological reserve may further modify these interactions. The Gut-X framework currently provides a model for organizing and generating mechanistic and longitudinal hypotheses. Its application to clinical stratification or patient selection for treatment remains unvalidated.

42862469.title: Healthcare pathways and outpatient management prior to community-acquired sepsis hospitalization in Germany, 2016-2019.
42862469.abstract: Sepsis often presents with non-specific symptoms that delay diagnosis and treatment. This study characterized pre-hospital outpatient and emergency care among patients with community-acquired sepsis (CAS) in Germany prior to hospitalization. This population-based observational cohort study used de-identified health claims data from over 340,000 AOK-insured adults admitted to hospital between 2016 and 2019 with an ICD-10-GM code for sepsis plus organ dysfunction, with each patient contributing only their first qualifying hospitalization (index case). Patients without ICD-10-GM codes for and suggestive of nosocomial infection were included and their healthcare utilization in the week before admission was categorized into: hospital emergency care (HEC), outpatient care only (OC), or no healthcare utilization (no HCU) (excluding patients exclusively hospitalized in the week prior sepsis hospitalization). Treatment and patient characteristics, sepsis features, and outcomes as documented in health claims data were compared across groups using descriptive and non-parametric statistics. Among 238,247 patients identified with CAS, 12.7% received HEC, 61.8% OC, and 25.5% had no HCU. HEC patients were younger, more severely ill, with higher ICU admission and mortality rates compared to the other groups. In the OC group, most patients (82.3%) had encounters with general practitioners, and 45.1% received OC on the day of admission. The last infection-related encounter occurred on average 2.0 days (SD 2.3) prior to sepsis hospitalization. Among OC patients, 48.7% underwent infection-related laboratory diagnostics, and 11.4% received anti-infective prescriptions. Most patients with CAS had healthcare contact in the week prior to hospitalization, predominantly in outpatient care. The frequent encounters shortly before admission and low rates of anti-infective prescription may suggest opportunities for earlier recognition and better risk stratification, e.g. by strengthening sepsis awareness and diagnostic strategies in outpatient settings. The study was pre-registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00031302) on 05/05/2023.

42862455.title: The effect of preload on Doppler systolic time in a large emergency department cohort with suspected sepsis.
42862455.abstract: Change in the corrected flow time of the common carotid artery (ccFTΔ) during a preload challenge (PC) is a surrogate for stroke volume change (SVΔ) to infer preload responsiveness (PR). This is a retrospective cohort study comprising patients with suspected sepsis in a large, publicly funded, academic emergency department; no patient health information is linked to the Doppler assessments. Carotid Doppler spectrograms from a wireless, wearable critical care Doppler ultrasound system are analyzed for ccFTΔ during a PC (either infusion of 300 mL of crystalloid over 3 min or a Trendelenburg maneuver). The primary objectives of this study are to describe the proportion of PR patients by previously described ccFTΔ thresholds (i.e., both 4 and 7 ms ccFTΔ ), describe time-to-peak (TTP) ccFTΔ, and evaluate the ability of baseline ccFT to detect ccFTΔ during PC, using both the equations of Wodey and Bazett. Comparisons of related outcomes were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm procedure, baseline ccFT discrimination was quantified using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and TTP was estimated using patient-level bootstrap resampling. Threshold-agnostic ccFTΔ trajectories were additionally explored using unsupervised k-means clustering of patient-level temporal responses for both correction equations. A PC was attempted in 4367 patients and an adequate ccFTΔ was collected from 4,128 patients (95%). In total, 982,937 Doppler cardiac cycles are included. The median ccFTΔ was 7.3 milliseconds (ms). 51.9% of patients had a ccFTΔ ≥ 7 ms, while 68.6% had a ccFTΔ ≥ 4 ms by the equation of Wodey. For Bazett, these fractions were 61.2% and 73.5%, respectively. For patients identified as PR based upon either a 4 ms or 7 ms ccFTΔ threshold, the time-to-peak ccFTΔ was 27.5 s for both equations. Baseline absolute ccFT did not discriminate PR from PUR patients under both correction formulae (AUROC 0.56-0.57). To our knowledge this is the largest reported dataset of ED patients with suspected sepsis receiving PR assessments by Doppler ultrasound, comprising nearly 1 million Doppler cardiac cycles obtained from over 4100 ED patients. Both 7 ms and 4 ms ccFTΔ thresholds described clinically-accepted rates of PR. The TTP was roughly 30 s into PC and baseline ccFT did not accurately detect ccFTΔ during PC. Finally, a hypothesis-generating analysis identified four distinct ccFTΔ trajectories during PC which may represent unique preload response patterns during PR testing.

42860932.title: From Rare to Rising: A Story of Enterobacter-associated Pneumonia Evolving in the Community.
42860932.abstract: Pneumonia is a common cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide and is the fifth leading cause of death. It is generally caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and some atypical microorganisms. Interestingly, a member of ESKAPE pathogens, mainly Enterobacter cloacae complex, is increasingly showing its presence in the samples of lower respiratory tract specimens. Emergence of multidrug resistance (MDR) in these bacteria, including resistance to last-resort carbapenems, has led to an increased interest in this organism causing pneumonia. (1) Prevalence of E. cloacae complex among community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) patients and (2) antibiotic resistance pattern of these pathogens. Respiratory samples from adult patients were processed according to standard microbiological techniques, including direct smear examination, incubation in blood, MacConkey and chocolate agar plates, and Gram staining. Identification of E. cloacae complex and antibiotic susceptibility testing, along with resistance patterns, was performed by automated ID/AST instrument. About 15.7% of E. cloacae complex-associated CAP patients were found over a 1-year study period. Antimicrobial susceptibility tests indicated a MDR profile in 58.3% of isolates. Resistance was mostly to carbapenems (72.73%), followed by aztreonam (69.7%), piperacillin-tazobactam (68%), and fluoroquinolones (63.6%). E. cloacae complex is an emerging and clinically significant pathogen causing CAP. Its MDR profile contributes to an increased tendency to intensive care unit admission and the development of sepsis. Hence, detecting this pathogen in lower respiratory tract specimens should be treated as a high alert and should prompt treatment at the earliest.

42859819.title: Necrotizing fasciitis secondary to Wohlfahrtiimonas chitiniclastica in the absence of myiasis.
42859819.abstract: Wohlfahrtiimonas chitiniclastica is a rare Gram-negative bacillus associated with fly larvae, myiasis, chronic wounds, and severe polymicrobial infection. We report a 71-year-old woman with diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, severe peripheral vascular disease, and previous contralateral above-knee amputation who presented with septic shock secondary to an infected right hallux ulcer. Radiographs demonstrated soft-tissue gas extending into the distal calf. Emergency exploration revealed extensive necrosis and dishwater pus tracking proximally along the flexor hallucis longus tendon, consistent with necrotizing fasciitis. Radical debridement was performed, although major amputation was initially declined. Tissue and pus cultures grew W. chitiniclastica and Enterococcus faecalis; no larvae were identified. Despite temporary clinical stabilization with intensive care support and broad-spectrum antibiotics, the foot remained non-viable and definitive above-knee amputation was required. The patient improved rapidly following source control and was discharged to rehabilitation. This case highlights the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and definitive source control for survival.

42859359.title: Multimorbidity patterns and outcomes among adults (non-maternity) with community-onset sepsis in Ireland: a retrospective national analysis of acute hospital data, 2020-2025.
42859359.abstract: Community-onset sepsis accounts for most sepsis cases and frequently occurs in individuals with underlying comorbidity. While national analyses in Ireland have described its epidemiology, impact of multimorbidity and how comorbidities co-exist to form patterns remain poorly characterised. To identify multimorbidity patterns among adult (non-maternity) episodes with community-onset sepsis and examine their association with critical care admission and in-hospital mortality. We conducted a secondary analysis of Hospital In-Patient Enquiry data from all acute public hospitals in Ireland from January 2020 to December 2025. Community-onset sepsis was defined using the present-on-admission flag. The sample comprised adult episodes aged ≥ 16 years excluding maternal admissions from conception to 6 weeks postpartum. K-means clustering identified patterns of co-occurring diseases. Multivariable logistic and negative binomial regression examined associations between patterns and outcomes. Of 80,628 sepsis admissions, 58,101 (72.0%) were community-onset. Of these, 53,812 (93.0%) were adult (non-maternity); of these, 35,316 (65.6%) had at least one Charlson comorbidity. Five data-derived multimorbidity patterns were identified: metabolic-multimorbid (31%), oncological-dominant (29%), renal-metabolic (15%), progressive metabolic (13%) and cardiopulmonary (12%). Outcomes varied across patterns, with differences in critical care admission and in-hospital mortality. Cardiopulmonary pattern had the highest odds of in-hospital mortality (adjusted-OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.86-2.17). Charlson comorbidity was recorded in approximately two-thirds of adult community-onset sepsis episodes and formed data-derived patterns associated with differences in critical care admission and in-hospital mortality. Multimorbidity clustering may support future risk stratification research and targeted clinical vigilance for episodes at highest risk of adverse outcomes.

42857531.title: An Unusual Presentation of Invasive Group A Streptococcus-A Review of Epidemiology and Challenges in Management.
42857531.abstract: Invasive Group A Streptococcus (iGAS) infection is a disease state with increasing incidence internationally. This case report outlines a patient with severe septic shock from Group A beta-haemolyticStreptococcus within a provincial intensive care unit (ICU) in New Zealand. Consequently, this case has prompted discussion on the local change in epidemiology for Group A beta-haemolytic Streptococcus (GAS) and a review of the evidence of recognised interventions for iGAS and Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome (STSS).

42857434.title: Retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis masquerading as perforated viscus: a rare case report.
42857434.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
42857434.abstract: Necrotizing fasciitis is a rapidly progressive, life-threatening soft-tissue infection associated with high mortality, particularly when diagnosis is delayed. While most cases involve the extremities or perineum, retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis is exceedingly rare. Its deep anatomical location often results in vague clinical presentations, allowing extensive infection before overt signs develop, which poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Early recognition and timely intervention are critical to improving outcomes. We report the case of a 40-year-old male who presented with nonspecific abdominal and flank pain, and low-grade fever of 2 days duration. Imaging revealed extensive retroperitoneal gas and fascial involvement. Urgent exploratory laparotomy confirmed necrosis of the bilateral abdominal wall fascia and retroperitoneal involvement. Initial surgical debridement was performed along with broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy. Postoperatively, the patient underwent repeat surgical drainage. Despite initial stabilization, he progressed to acute kidney injury, hyperbilirubinemia, and biochemical evidence of pancreatitis, necessitating intensive care. The patient ultimately succumbed to uncontrolled sepsis with multiorgan failure on the sixth postoperative day. Retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis is difficult to diagnose due to nonspecific symptoms and deep anatomical location. Imaging, particularly contrast-enhanced computed tomography, is essential for detecting fascial necrosis and retroperitoneal gas. Even with prompt surgical debridement and broad-spectrum antibiotics, the infection can progress rapidly along fascial planes, causing secondary abscesses and multiorgan dysfunction. Retroperitoneal necrotizing fasciitis can progress silently and rapidly, leading to multiorgan failure. Heightened clinical suspicion, early imaging, and prompt surgical management are crucial for improving patient outcomes.

42857028.title: Comparison of Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA), Quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA), Obstetrically Modified SOFA, and Obstetrically Modified qSOFA Scores for Predicting Maternal Outcomes in High-Risk Obstetric Patients.
42857028.abstract: Introduction Maternal morbidity and mortality remain significant challenges in obstetric critical care. Early identification of organ dysfunction is essential for timely intervention and improved outcomes. This study compared the prognostic performance of the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA), quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA), obstetrically modified SOFA (omSOFA), and obstetrically modified qSOFA (omqSOFA) scores in predicting maternal outcomes among high-risk obstetric patients. Methods A prospective observational study was conducted among 200 high-risk obstetric patients admitted to a tertiary care center. Twelve patients who left against medical advice were excluded from outcome-based analyses, leaving 188 patients for final evaluation. SOFA, qSOFA, omSOFA, and omqSOFA scores were calculated at admission. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to determine the predictive performance of each scoring system for maternal mortality. Area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and optimal cutoff values were calculated. Results Among the 188 patients included in the final analysis, 15 maternal deaths occurred. SOFA demonstrated the highest discriminatory ability for predicting maternal mortality, with an AUC of 0.97 (95% CI: 0.94-0.99) at a cutoff value of ≥10, followed by omSOFA with an AUC of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.89-0.97) at a cutoff value of ≥9. qSOFA and omqSOFA showed AUCs of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.68-0.84) and 0.79 (95% CI: 0.71-0.87), respectively. qSOFA and omqSOFA demonstrated 100% sensitivity and negative predictive value at a cutoff score of ≥2, while SOFA and omSOFA provided superior specificity and overall discriminatory performance. Conclusions Among high-risk obstetric patients, SOFA demonstrated the highest discriminatory ability for predicting maternal mortality, followed by omSOFA. While qSOFA and omqSOFA showed lower specificity, they demonstrated excellent sensitivity and negative predictive value, making them useful bedside screening tools for early risk identification. Incorporation of these scoring systems into obstetric critical care practice may facilitate timely risk stratification and early intervention. Further multicentre studies are required to validate these findings in larger and more diverse obstetric populations.

42856548.title: Elevated blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio is associated with incident sepsis-associated delirium: evidence from a weighted competing-risk analysis in a multicenter cohort study.
42856548.abstract: Sepsis-associated delirium (SAD) is a frequent manifestation of acute brain dysfunction in sepsis. Although the blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio (BAR) has been associated with prognosis in critically ill patients, its relationship with incident SAD remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between early BAR and incident SAD. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients with sepsis from MIMIC-IV as the primary cohort and eICU-CRD as an independent replication cohort. BAR was calculated from eligible blood urea nitrogen and serum albumin measurements obtained within 24 h after the index time. The primary outcome was 7-day incident delirium; 3-day delirium was additionally evaluated in MIMIC-IV. Death before delirium was treated as a competing event. Covariates were selected using Boruta and LASSO regression. CBPS-based inverse probability weighting and Fine-Gray competing-risk regression were applied, with restricted cubic spline, subgroup, and exploratory XGBoost/SHAP analyses. A total of 10,565 patients were included (9,612 MIMIC-IV; 953 eICU-CRD). In MIMIC-IV, the highest BAR quartile was associated with a greater subdistribution hazard of 7-day delirium vs. the lowest quartile (fully adjusted sHR 1.36, 95% CI 1.13-1.64; P = 0.001; P for trend = 0.002). Continuous BAR was also associated with 7-day delirium (sHR per 1-unit increase 1.00, 95% CI 1.00-1.01; P = 0.013), with similar findings for 3-day delirium. In eICU-CRD, the highest BAR quartile was likewise associated with 7-day delirium (sHR 2.20, 95% CI 1.13-4.29; P = 0.020; P for trend = 0.012), whereas the continuous association was not statistically significant (sHR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02; P = 0.075). Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested potential nonlinearity, particularly in MIMIC-IV. Exploratory SHAP analyses ranked BAR among the most influential model-based predictors in both cohorts. Higher early BAR, particularly values in the highest quartile, was associated with a greater subdistribution hazard of incident SAD, and the highest-quartile association was independently reproduced in eICU-CRD. BAR may serve as a simple risk-associated marker for identifying patients with sepsis at higher risk of incident delirium.

42855975.title: Nailfold Capillaroscopy Reveals Peripheral Microcirculatory Trajectories in Septic Shock.
42855975.abstract: BackgroundSepsis-induced microcirculatory dysfunction may persist despite systemic hemodynamic stabilization, yet longitudinal changes in peripheral microvascular structure and flow during recovery remain insufficiently characterized. We used nailfold capillaroscopy (NFC) to characterize these changes during recovery from septic shock.MethodsIn this prospective two-center study, patients with Sepsis-3 septic shock underwent NFC during shock and after clinician-confirmed hemodynamic stabilization. Baseline NFC analyses required analyzable initial recordings; longitudinal analyses required paired assessments and survival to reassessment. Mortality was prespecified as the primary outcome. Longitudinal NFC changes and the association between change in red blood cell (RBC) velocity and lactate clearance were prespecified; outcome-stratified analyses were post hoc and exploratory.ResultsOf 25 patients meeting clinical eligibility criteria, 21 were enrolled, 19 had analyzable baseline NFC recordings, and 15 had paired assessments; four died before reassessment. Baseline RBC velocity was 0.268 mm/s in survivors and 0.290 mm/s in non-survivors (P = 0.653). In the paired cohort, RBC velocity increased from 0.295 to 0.550 mm/s; median within-patient change was 0.167 mm/s (95% CI, 0.067 to 0.609; P = 0.1531). The median within-patient change in capillary length was 42.1 μm (95% CI, -7.3 to 65.3; P = 0.0125). Median ΔRBC velocity was 0.393 mm/s in survivors and -0.127 mm/s in non-survivors; the between-group median difference was 0.520 mm/s (95% CI, -0.042 to 1.368; P = 0.0256). The prespecified association between ΔRBC velocity and lactate clearance was positive but imprecise (Spearman's rho = 0.41; 95% CI, -0.15 to 0.77; P = 0.133).ConclusionsNFC captured dynamic and heterogeneous peripheral microcirculatory changes despite systemic hemodynamic stabilization. Increased RBC velocity among survivors suggests that serial NFC may complement conventional macrocirculatory assessment by providing information on microcirculatory recovery. These findings support further prospective evaluation of NFC as a feasible bedside tool for longitudinal microcirculatory monitoring.

42855756.title: [A preliminary study on the protective effect of dapagliflozin on multi-organ function in the early stage of sepsis].
42855756.abstract: Objective: This preliminarily study aims to evaluate the short-term efficacy and safety of dapagliflozin on multi-organ functions in patients with sepsis. Methods: This single-center, prospective, randomized controlled clinical trial enrolled 136 patients with sepsis to the Intensive Care Unit of Northern Jiangsu People's Hospital between April and December 2025. The patients were randomly assigned to the intervention group and the control group. Both groups received standardized treatment for sepsis, and the intervention group was also administered with dapagliflozin at a dose of 10 mg for 5 days. Changes in the sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores after the intervention served as the primary outcome. The secondary outcomes included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), renal function indicators, and clinical prognosis. Results: There were no statistically significant differences in the baseline data and changes in SOFA scores before and after treatment between the two groups (50 patients per group, P>0.05). On the 5th day of treatment, the median LVEF was significantly higher in the intervention group [60.0% (55.0%, 62.5%)] than in the control group [55.0% (49.0%, 58.0%), P<0.001]. The 28-day all-cause mortality rate in the intervention group [26% (13/50)] was lower than in the control group [36% (18/50)], but the variance did not reach statistical significance (P=0.387). The incidences of adverse events were comparable between both groups. The intervention group showed higher distribution of urine ketone body grades (Z=-2.1, P=0.040), but ketoacidosis was not observed. Conclusions: The short-term treatment of sepsis patients with dapagliflozin did not significantly reduce the SOFA scores, but improved LVEF and showed a trend of reducing all-cause mortality at 28 days. The short-term treatment was safe.

42853715.title: Clinical Significance of Klotho, Fibroblast Growth Factor 23, and Their Ratio for Acute Kidney Injury in Sepsis Patients.
42853715.journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
42853715.abstract: The sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is common in patients with sepsis and associated with poor outcomes, yet serum creatinine and urine output have limited value for early assessment. We examined whether admission Klotho, fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), and the Klotho/FGF23 ratio were associated with SA-AKI and short-term outcomes and compared their discriminative performance. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 320 patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with Sepsis-3-defined sepsis. SA-AKI (n = 112) was retrospectively identified according to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Klotho and FGF23 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in stored serum samples collected within 24 h of ICU admission. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis, and adjusted associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Patients with SA-AKI had lower Klotho, higher FGF23, and a reduced Klotho/FGF23 ratio at admission (all p < 0.001). The ratio showed the highest area under the curve biomarkers for SA-AKI (0.84; 95% confidence interval 0.79-0.88) and remained associated with SA-AKI after multivariable adjustment (odds ratio 2.25; 95% confidence interval 1.46-3.53). The ratio decreased with increasing KDIGO stage. Among patients with SA-AKI, a low ratio remained associated with lower 3-month renal recovery, longer ICU and hospital stays, higher in-hospital mortality, and greater 3-month chronic kidney disease progression after adjustment. The admission Klotho/FGF23 ratio was associated with SA-AKI, higher KDIGO stage, and short-term outcomes and showed the highest observed discrimination among the three biomarkers.

42853452.title: Hemodynamic trajectory phenotypes may modify associations between corticosteroid timing and outcomes in septic shock.
42853452.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
42853452.abstract: Corticosteroid trials in septic shock show conflicting results, with patient heterogeneity and treatment timing as likely contributors. We evaluated whether associations between corticosteroid timing and clinical outcomes differed by hemodynamic trajectory phenotype defined by dynamic time warping clustering of Blood Pressure-Vasopressor Index (BPRI) trajectories across three ICU cohorts. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using MIMIC-IV as the derivation cohort and eICU-CRD and PINES as validation cohorts. Adult patients with septic shock receiving vasopressors were included. Hemodynamic phenotypes were identified from 168-h BPRI trajectories. Corticosteroid timing was classified as early (≤ 6 h) or late (> 6 h) after sepsis onset. In MIMIC-IV, inverse probability of treatment weighting with cause-specific Cox regression was used to estimate associations between timing and 28-day mortality, hospital length of stay, and ventilation duration within each phenotype. Validation cohorts were analyzed using multivariable Cox regression, and cohort-specific estimates were summarized using random-effects meta-analysis with I2. Two phenotypes were identified in MIMIC-IV: Deteriorated (N=2,082, 38%), with declining hemodynamics and higher mortality, and Improved (N=3,361, 62%), with stable or rising trajectories. Similar trajectory patterns were observed in eICU-CRD and PINES. In the Deteriorated phenotype, late corticosteroids were associated with lower 28-day mortality in MIMIC-IV (HR 0.88 [0.78-0.98]) and shorter ventilation duration (HR 0.65 [0.58-0.73]) compared with early administration. The mortality association was not consistently replicated in validation cohorts, whereas the ventilation association was observed in PINES Deteriorated patients. In the Improved phenotype, late steroids showed no consistent mortality or hospital length-of-stay association. Exploratory hemodynamic response analysis showed a more favorable BPRI slope for late versus early steroids in the Deteriorated phenotype. Hemodynamic trajectory phenotypes identified clinically meaningful variation in the relationship between corticosteroid timing and outcomes in septic shock. In the Deteriorated phenotype, delayed corticosteroid initiation was associated with lower 28-day mortality and shorter recovery, whereas the Improved phenotype showed no mortality advantage from delayed treatment. These findings support incorporating dynamic hemodynamic trajectories into future studies of corticosteroid timing in septic shock.

42853142.title: A Simple Platelet-Centered Coagulation-Inflammation Combined Score for Predicting In-Hospital Mortality in Sepsis.
42853142.abstract: Accurate mortality prediction in sepsis requires assessing coagulation and inflammatory disturbances, yet existing scores are complex or incompletely capture these interconnected processes. We developed and internally validated a simple score combining inflammatory and platelet-related indicators with clinical parameters to predict in-hospital mortality in sepsis. This retrospective study included 6175 adults with sepsis from the MIMIC-IV database. Patients were randomly divided into training (n=4322) and validation (n=1853) cohorts. Candidate predictors were screened by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and final variables entered multivariable logistic regression to construct the Coagulation-Inflammation Combined Score (CICS). Performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, internal bootstrap validation, and decision curve analysis. Of 6175 patients, 807 (13.1%) died during hospitalization. The final CICS incorporated five routinely available variables: lactate, Glasgow Coma Scale score, age, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and platelet count. Discrimination was good, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.768 (95% CI, 0.747-0.788) in training and 0.806 (95% CI, 0.776-0.835) in validation cohorts, comparable to SOFA (DeLong P=0.526 and P=0.180). Calibration was acceptable (Brier scores 0.102 and 0.091). Bootstrap validation indicated minimal optimism, and decision curve analysis showed exploratory findings across clinically relevant thresholds. The CICS is a parsimonious prognostic score using five routinely available variables from the first 24 hours after ICU admission. It showed discrimination comparable to SOFA, acceptable calibration, and favorable decision-curve performance. CICS should be interpreted as a separate prognostic score for early ICU stratification once first-24-hour data are available, rather than for emergency department triage or ICU admission decisions.

42852848.title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Predicting 28-Day Mortality in Patients with Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy and Heart Failure.
42852848.abstract: IntroductionPatients with sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) and heart failure (HF) represent a clinically relevant but understudied subgroup in the intensive care unit, and early risk stratification may be important for guiding management. This study aimed to develop and temporally validate machine-learning models for predicting 28-day mortality in patients with SAE and HF.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, patients with SAE and HF were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and III (MIMIC-III) databases. The MIMIC-IV cohort was randomly divided into a training set and an internal testing set, whereas the MIMIC-III cohort served as a temporally distinct testing set. Variables with more than 30% missing data were excluded, and the remaining missing values were handled using multiple imputation. Candidate predictors were first screened by univariable analysis and then entered into multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors of 28-day mortality. Six variables (age, weight, respiratory rate, Logistic Organ Dysfunction System score, first 24-h urine output, and Charlson Comorbidity Index) were used to construct five models: logistic regression, XGBoost, LightGBM, support vector machine, and AdaBoost. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), classification metrics, calibration, and decision-curve analysis.ResultsA total of 1249 patients with SAE and HF were included, comprising 833 in the training set, 205 in the internal testing set, and 211 in the temporal testing set. Machine-learning models and logistic regression outperformed conventional severity scores (SOFA, SAPS II, and LODS). In the temporal testing set, XGBoost achieved the highest AUROC (0.824), whereas logistic regression showed similar discrimination (AUROC 0.816) but more stable calibration and better overall balance across performance domains.ConclusionWe developed and temporally validated models for predicting 28-day mortality in patients with SAE and HF. Among the evaluated models, logistic regression showed the most balanced overall performance and may be the most clinically applicable model for individualized risk stratification.

42852417.title: Spontaneous Tumor Lysis Syndrome in Refractory Metastatic Esophageal Adenocarcinoma Presenting With Septic Shock.
42852417.abstract: Spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome (STLS) presents a diagnostic challenge when it occurs in patients with advanced solid malignancies and concurrent critical illness. We present a case of STLS in a 30-year-old man with refractory metastatic esophageal adenocarcinoma who presented with hypotension, anuria, and severe metabolic derangements. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated hyperuricemia (18.1 mg/dL), hyperkalemia (7.6 mmol/L), hyperphosphatemia (7.8 mg/dL), and acute kidney injury. Ionized calcium was also low at 1.03 mmol/L despite hypoalbuminemia, with laboratory and clinical findings consistent with TLS by Cairo-Bishop thresholds. His final treatment was initiated 19 days before presentation, with the continuous fluorouracil infusion completed approximately 17 days before presentation, placing the presentation well outside the conventional treatment-related timeframe. His course was complicated by septic shock secondary to methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia. Despite supportive care and rasburicase administration, he developed multiorgan failure and was transitioned to hospice. This case highlights the rare occurrence of spontaneous TLS in metastatic esophageal adenocarcinoma and emphasizes the importance of early recognition and consideration in any patient with high tumor burden.

42851709.title: Early Surgical Escalation and Structured Multidisciplinary Pathways Improve Limb-Salvage Outcomes in Necrotizing Fasciitis: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project.
42851709.abstract: Necrotizing fasciitis (NF) is a rapidly progressive, life-threatening soft-tissue infection characterized by extensive fascial necrosis and systemic toxicity. Reported mortality ranges from 20% to 40%, driven largely by diagnostic delay. Orthopedic units carry a disproportionate burden, particularly for lower-limb disease. This two-cycle quality improvement project (QIP) examined whether structured diagnostic pathways and early multidisciplinary escalation could reduce time to surgery and improve limb-salvage outcomes. Twenty-seven patients with confirmed or suspected NF were managed across two sequential audit cycles at a tertiary orthopedic center (Cycle 1, n = 14; Cycle 2, n = 13). Mean age was 52.1 ± 11.3 years; 80% had lower-limb involvement, and 70% had diabetes mellitus. Following QIP implementation, median time to surgical decision fell from 11.5 ± 3.2 to 6.8 ± 2.1 hours (P = 0.002). Recovery rates rose from 14.3% to 84.6% (P < 0.001) and major amputation rates declined from 35.7% to 15.4% (P = 0.04). Documentation of Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis scores and finger-sweep testing improved significantly. In-hospital mortality remained comparable (21.4% vs. 23.1%). A structured, protocol-driven approach to NF management - encompassing mandatory diagnostic documentation, early senior involvement, and multidisciplinary team activation - substantially improves surgical timeliness and limb-salvage rates. Mortality reduction may require parallel optimization of perioperative sepsis management and critical care pathways.

42851353.title: Longitudinal sepsis-induced coagulopathy score trajectories and mortality in relation to early prophylactic heparin: a multicentre cohort study.
42851353.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
42851353.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) evolves dynamically, and a single-timepoint score may not capture its longitudinal course. This study characterised SIC score trajectories, evaluated their associations with mortality, and conducted exploratory analyses of early prophylactic unfractionated heparin exposure. SIC score trajectories were characterised using a latent class mixed model. Trajectory-class prediction models were developed from baseline features within the first 24 hours of ICU admission using five algorithms. Heparin analysis used a 48-hour landmark design; weighted Fine-Gray models and cumulative incidence functions estimated 28-day post-landmark in-hospital mortality. The study enrolled 20,168 patients from MIMIC-IV and 5,829 from eICU-CRD. Three SIC trajectories were identified-Persistently High, Rising-then-Falling, and Resolving-comprising 31.9%, 10.6%, and 57.5% of patients in MIMIC-IV and 49.1%, 7.2%, and 43.7% in eICU-CRD. Relative to the Resolving trajectory, adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios (sHR) for mortality were 1.65 (95% CI 1.52-1.78) and 1.33 (1.18-1.49) for Persistently High and Rising-then-Falling in MIMIC-IV, and 1.73 (1.51-1.99) and 1.67 (1.33-2.11) in eICU-CRD. Prophylactic heparin was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard of 28-day post-landmark mortality in MIMIC-IV (sHR=0.908, 95% CI 0.839-0.983, P = 0.018); in an exploratory interaction analysis, the point estimate was more pronounced at higher predicted probabilities of the Persistently High trajectory, but this pattern was not replicated in eICU-CRD (sHR 0.877, 95% CI 0.744-1.034, P = 0.118). SIC score trajectories stratify septic patients into three trajectory classes-Persistently High, Rising-then-Falling, and Resolving-each showing a graded association with 28-day mortality. Early prophylactic unfractionated heparin showed an exploratory association with lower post-landmark mortality in MIMIC-IV that was not independently replicated in eICU-CRD. Although these findings do not support treatment recommendations or trajectory-based anticoagulation decisions, they provide a basis for formulating hypotheses for future prospective studies.

42851303.title: Case Report: rectal perforation and Fournier's gangrene after irinotecan in a bevacizumab-exposed, previously irradiated patient.
42851303.abstract: Bevacizumab-associated intestinal perforation and Fournier's gangrene have been reported separately; however, the potential contribution of residual anti-VEGF exposure prior to subsequent chemotherapy in previously irradiated pelvic tissue remains underrecognized. Radiotherapy causes fibrosis and microvascular injury, bevacizumab impairs healing, and irinotecan-induced diarrhea may exacerbate perforation risk. Deferring DRE, imaging, and surgical consultation in patients with unexplained perineal or buttock pain increases the risk. A 61-year-old man with rectal adenocarcinoma received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by total mesorectal excision and ileostomy in March 2024. After adjuvant chemotherapy, surveillance in March 2025 revealed recurrence with pelvic invasion and liver/lung metastases. He received eight cycles of XELOX plus bevacizumab, then bevacizumab maintenance, stopped on 4 March 2026 for rectal hemorrhage. This 22-day interval is shorter than the label-mandated 28-day hold and NCCN-recommended ≥6-week washout for surgery-standards primarily addressing wound healing rather than chemotherapy sequencing. Five days after irinotecan initiation, grade 3 diarrhea developed. He was admitted on 13 April 2026 with diarrhea, left buttock pain; he received empirical ceftazidime plus moxifloxacin. On 14 April, DRE, imaging, and surgical consultation were deferred due to pain. By 18 April, septic shock developed with perineal necrosis and crepitus. CT confirmed Fournier's gangrene. Emergency debridement with abscess curettage and seton drainage was performed. Fecal diversion was declined. Antibiotics were escalated to meropenem then vancomycin after cultures grew VSEfm. He left the ICU but needed twice-daily dressing changes. Two weeks postoperatively, care shifted to palliation, and he died of multiorgan failure. This case raises the hypothesis that, in previously irradiated tissue, residual bevacizumab exposure at the time of subsequent irinotecan initiation-exacerbated by irinotecan-induced diarrhea and pre-existing rectal mucosal damage-may have contributed to rectal perforation and subsequent Fournier's gangrene. Notably, while bevacizumab and irinotecan are routinely combined, whether extrapolating surgical washout standards (≥6 weeks) to anti-VEGF sequencing before high-mucosal-toxicity chemotherapy warrants prospective investigation. Unexplained perineal or buttock pain in such patients should trigger urgent clinical evaluation, including DRE when feasible, imaging, and early surgical consultation, to prevent diagnostic delay.

42850671.title: Phenotype-based appropriateness of IGM-enriched polyclonal immunoglobulin use in critical illness: report of an expert consensus.
42850671.journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
42850671.abstract: Sepsis and septic shock result from a dysregulated host response to infection, encompassing both hyperinflammatory and immunosuppressed phenotypes. Although immunomodulatory adjunctive therapies have been extensively investigated over the past decades, none have demonstrated consistent clinical efficacy. In contrast, low circulating immunoglobulin levels are common in septic patients and are associated with greater disease severity and poorer outcomes, providing a biological rationale for the use of polyclonal intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIg) as phenotype-targeted adjunctive therapies. This expert consensus sought to systematically evaluate the appropriateness of IVIg therapy across predefined and clinically relevant scenarios in critically ill patients and deliver pragmatic, phenotype-oriented guidance. A multidisciplinary Italian panel comprising experts in intensive care, infectious diseases, transplant medicine, and oncology applied a modified RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. The process integrated a structured literature review (PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library) with anonymous 9-point Likert scale ratings. Indications were classified according to the median score as appropriate (7-9), uncertain (4-6), or inappropriate (1-3), and interpanel disagreement was assessed using the Interpercentile Range Adjusted for Symmetry.
