We included systematic reviews of adult in-hospital populations evaluating EWS as either prognostic tools for deterioration or mortality, or as interventions implemented within track-and-trigger or rapid response systems. Primary study overlap was quantified using the corrected covered area (CCA). We synthesized evidence narratively and tabularly, emphasizing ED-related data. From 502 records identified, 21 systematic reviews comprising 343 primary studies were included. We identified ED-relevant evidence in 12 reviews. In ED populations, EWS demonstrated moderate-to-good discrimination for mortality and clinical deterioration (National EWS area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values: 0.88 for 24-hour mortality, 0.86 for 48-hour mortality). Across ED and mixed acute-care cohorts, Early Warning Scores also showed fair performance for predicting ICU admission and composite adverse outcomes (AUROC ~0.70-0.75). In sepsis-focused analyses relevant to ED populations, quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) demonstrated low sensitivity but high specificity for 28/30-day mortality (sensitivity 0.41, 95% CI, 0.24-0.62; specificity 0.88, 95% CI, 0.81-0.92). The SOFA score showed high sensitivity and moderate specificity for in-hospital mortality (sensitivity 0.89, 95% CI, 0.88-0.90; specificity 0.69, 95% CI, 0.68-0.69). Evidence on the clinical impact of EWS implementation in ED and other emergency settings was limited and heterogeneous. In EDs, Early Warning Scores support early risk stratification and identification of patients at risk of deterioration, particularly for short-term mortality and escalation of care. Their impact on patient-important outcomes remains uncertain. Early Warning Scores should complement clinical judgment, triage systems, and structured escalation protocols. They should not be a standalone tool. Future research should prioritize standardized thresholds, transparent reporting, and rigorous comparative and implementation studies defining the role of EWS in emergency care.

42900705.title: Variability in automated sepsis case detection: a systematic analysis of implementation methods in clinical data repositories.
42900705.journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
42900705.abstract: To systematically review and characterize methodological heterogeneity in sepsis case detection using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III) and eICU-CRD databases. We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of PubMed and Web of Science (publication years 2016-2024). Studies were eligible if they applied the SOFA-based Sepsis-3 definition to MIMIC-III or eICU-CRD, provided at least one explicit label-calculation detail, reported a traceable detection rate, and met further criteria detailed in the PRISMA flow diagram. We classified each study by study type and unit of analysis (patients, admissions, or ICU stays) and extracted methodological details on sepsis case detection across 6 domains. For studies with available source code, we additionally examined code structure and repository dependencies to identify methodological decisions across these domains. Of 396 publications screened, 64 met inclusion criteria and 12 provided source code. Sepsis detection rates ranged from 3.4% to 65.2% in MIMIC-III and from 9.8% to 47.9% in eICU-CRD. Substantial variability persisted among studies using identical cohort definitions within both databases (MIMIC-III: 16.9%-42.2%; eICU-CRD: 13.9%-31.4%). In a generalized linear mixed model, between-study heterogeneity was extreme (overall τ²≈0.79; 95% prediction interval for a new study's detection rate 5%-63%), and study-level characteristics-including database, study type, infection detection method, code availability, and unit of analysis-explained only a small proportion of this variance (≈9%), with no characteristic reaching statistical significance. The overall proportion of studies reporting methodological details varied by domain: SOFA calculation (53.1%), infection detection methods (42.2%), temporal windows (37.5%), aggregation methods (26.6%), and missing-data handling (17.2%). Source code analysis identified 321 implementation decisions, revealing heterogeneity in baseline SOFA definitions (SOFA = 0 vs dynamic baseline), temporal windows (infection-centered vs ICU-admission-centered) and infection detection methods (antibiotic-culture matching vs APACHE-based diagnosis). Dependencies among several MIMIC-III repositories suggested propagation of implementation decisions across studies. Clinically validated sepsis definitions yield substantially different detection rates across studies using identical datasets. Statistical modeling showed that this variability is driven almost entirely by between-study implementation differences rather than sampling error or study characteristics. To improve reproducibility in sepsis research and the robustness of sepsis prediction models, we recommend standardized reporting of sepsis case detection methodology and the publication of version-controlled source code.

42900653.title: When Insulin Must Wait: The Role of Renal Replacement Therapy in Refractory Hypokalemia During Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis.
42900653.journal: The American journal of case reports
42900653.abstract: BACKGROUND Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a common life-threatening metabolic emergency characterized by hyperglycemia, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and ketosis. Severe hypokalemia before insulin therapy is uncommon but may complicate management and delay treatment. CASE REPORT A 37-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of generalized abdominal pain and progressive shortness of breath. He was drowsy and tachypneic, with Kussmaul respirations. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe DKA, acute kidney injury, and severe hypokalemia. Insulin therapy was initially withheld according to the DKA protocol. Intravenous potassium supplementation failed to achieve sustained correction, resulting in repeated interruptions of insulin therapy. Due to refractory hypokalemia, an emergency 2-hour session of intermittent hemodialysis was performed, followed by continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). During CRRT, serum potassium increased, serum creatinine decreased, metabolic acidosis improved, and the anion gap closed. Insulin therapy was resumed without further interruption. However, the clinical course was complicated by severe septic shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and catastrophic intracerebral hemorrhage, ultimately resulting in death. CONCLUSIONS Severe hypokalemia at presentation in DKA poses a critical therapeutic challenge because insulin therapy must be withheld until the electrolyte abnormality is corrected. In rare cases of refractory hypokalemia, CRRT may serve as an adjunctive strategy to facilitate metabolic stabilization and safe DKA management. This case adds to the limited literature and highlights the need for further studies to clarify the role and effectiveness of this approach. Biochemical resolution of DKA may not correspond to clinical recovery, and critically ill patients warrant continuous monitoring.

42900319.title: Pancreatic stone protein versus conventional biomarkers for prognostic discrimination in sepsis: a meta-analysis of paired AUC comparisons.
42900319.abstract: Pancreatic stone protein (PSP) has been proposed as a prognostic biomarker in sepsis, but its comparative performance versus C-reactive protein (CRP) and procalcitonin (PCT) remains uncertain. We performed a meta-analysis of direct within-study paired AUC comparisons between PSP and CRP and/or PCT in critically ill adults with sepsis, septic shock, or acute infection-related conditions in whom sepsis development or clinically relevant adverse outcomes were prospectively evaluated. Differences in AUC (ΔAUC) were pooled using random-effects models. The principal conservative analysis included one comparison per independent cohort and comparator. Seven studies comprising 803 unique participants contributed 21 paired comparisons. In the principal conservative analysis, PSP showed a higher prognostic AUC than CRP, with a pooled ΔAUC of 0.179 (95% CI 0.095-0.262; p < 0.001), although between-cohort heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 81.65%). Compared with PCT, the pooled ΔAUC was 0.153 (95% CI 0.114-0.193; p < 0.001), with no observed heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%). The mortality-only sensitivity analysis showed a similar pooled effect for PSP versus CRP (ΔAUC 0.17, 95% CI 0.08-0.26), with substantial heterogeneity persisting, and for PSP versus PCT (ΔAUC 0.153, 95% CI 0.114-0.193), with no observed heterogeneity. Exclusion of the clinically distinct intra-abdominal infection cohort (Michailides et al.) likewise did not materially change the PSP-versus CRP estimate (ΔAUC 0.166, 95% CI 0.077-0.256). The direction and approximate magnitude of the pooled effects were also preserved across alternative assumptions for the within-study correlation. Available comparative evidence suggests that PSP may have greater prognostic discrimination than CRP and PCT. The findings were broadly maintained across sensitivity analyses, but the limited number of independent cohorts and substantial heterogeneity in the CRP comparison warrant caution. Further prospective studies are required to confirm these findings and establish their clinical relevance. This systematic review was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261340301).

42898695.title: Hepatic biomarker trajectories and mortality in septic adults with type 2 diabetes and recorded dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor exposure versus metformin-based therapy: A propensity-score-matched cohort study.
42898695.abstract: To determine whether recorded dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor exposure, compared with metformin, is associated with worse hepatic biomarker trajectories or mortality in adults with type 2 diabetes and sepsis. In three critical care databases (MIMIC-IV, eICU-CRD, NWICU), adults with type 2 diabetes and sepsis with a DPP-4 inhibitor record were matched 1:3 within each database to metformin comparators on age, sex, body mass index, 24-h SOFA and day-1 estimated glomerular filtration rate. The day 1-7 total bilirubin trajectory was analysed by linear mixed-effects regression under nine specifications including log transformation, flexible day terms, doubly robust adjustment and inverse-probability-of-observation weighting. Matching yielded 105 DPP-4 inhibitor and 297 metformin patients; a pre-admission exposure record was present in 60.0%. The between-group difference in bilirubin slope was +0.048 mg/dL/day (95% CI -0.029 to 0.126; p = 0.221), with p between 0.109 and 0.436 across specifications. No other hepatic outcome survived multiplicity correction. Alkaline phosphatase rose more steeply on the primary specification (+6.97 U/L/day; q = 0.005) but was fragile: 12 of 28 sensitivity analyses retained p < 0.05. In-hospital mortality was 21.0% versus 13.5% (risk ratio 1.56, 95% CI 0.97-2.49), attenuating to 1.23 (0.67-2.29) with documented pre-admission exposure. There was no statistically detectable difference in bilirubin trajectory between recorded DPP-4 inhibitor and metformin exposure, although differences below the cohort's detectable-effect threshold cannot be excluded. An ALP signal was fragile and hypothesis-generating. Mortality findings are exploratory and non-causal. These associations with recorded exposure cannot inform inpatient management.

42898682.title: Precision fluid therapy in sepsis: fluid responsiveness vs. fluid tolerance.
42898682.abstract: Intravenous fluid is the most frequently administered drug in septic shock and one of the least precisely dosed. Two decades of trials have progressively dismantled the assumption that more fluid is better: protocolized early goal-directed therapy failed to improve on contemporary usual care, high-volume bolus protocols caused frank harm where organ support was limited, and restrictive strategies applied after an initial resuscitation have proven neutral rather than superior. What has replaced a universal volume prescription is a pair of questions that must be asked separately for each patient and repeated over time: will this patient's cardiac output actually rise with more fluid (fluid responsiveness), and can the lungs, kidneys, and venous system absorb that volume without harm (fluid tolerance)? This narrative review examines how to answer both questions in the modern intensive care unit. We ground the discussion in Guytonian venous return physiology and in the revised Starling model, in which sepsis-induced glycocalyx degradation makes infused crystalloid a short-acting drug with a cumulative side-effect profile. Using an index case of a mechanically ventilated patient with pneumococcal septic shock, atrial fibrillation, lung-protective tidal volumes, obesity, and acute kidney injury, we show why the two most widely used bedside indices, respiratory variation in inferior vena cava diameter and pulse pressure variation, are physiologically invalid in precisely the patients in whom the fluid decision is hardest, and why maintenance infusions and fluid creep deserve the same scrutiny as boluses. We make the case for direct stroke volume measurement paired with a reversible dynamic challenge, most commonly a passive leg raise, as the one approach that remains interpretable across arrhythmia, low tidal volume, spontaneous respiratory effort, and elevated intra-abdominal pressure, and we discuss dynamic arterial elastance as a complementary tool for predicting whether arterial pressure will follow flow. We review the outcome evidence, including the FRESH trial and supporting meta-analyses, the emerging literature on sepsis endotypes and subphenotypes, and the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign recommendations. Finally, we address fluid tolerance and de-resuscitation, where venous congestion assessment and lung ultrasound are increasingly used, and outline where the evidence remains thin.

42896710.title: Clinical characteristics of necrotizing soft tissue infection among patients with high LRINEC scores.
42896710.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
42896710.abstract: The Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC) score is a widely used adjunctive diagnostic tool for necrotizing soft tissue infection (NSTI). However, patients with high LRINEC scores do not uniformly have NSTI and often represent a diagnostic gray zone requiring urgent differentiation from other severe soft tissue infections. This study aimed to clarify the clinical characteristics of NSTI among patients with high LRINEC scores. We retrospectively reviewed patients hospitalized for severe soft tissue infections with sepsis between January 2014 and December 2023 with LRINEC scores ≥6, classified as NSTI (n = 11) or non-NSTI (n = 9). Non-NSTI cases were limited to severe cellulitis with bacteremia requiring intensive care. Clinical findings, laboratory parameters, imaging findings, and vasopressor use within 24 h after hospital arrival were compared. Patients with NSTI had significantly higher white blood cell counts and serum creatinine levels. Fluid collection along the fascia and gas formation on CT were more frequent in the NSTI group. Mean blood pressure at presentation did not differ between groups; however, vasopressor use within 24 h after hospital arrival was significantly more common in the NSTI group, suggesting early hemodynamic deterioration or greater disease severity. In patients with high LRINEC scores, NSTI was associated with marked inflammatory response, renal dysfunction, specific CT findings and early hemodynamic instability. Early vasopressor requirement should be interpreted primarily as a marker of early hemodynamic deterioration or disease severity, rather than a diagnostic characteristic specific to NSTI.

42895627.title: Vasopressors Combination Therapy (Norepinephrine Plus Vasopressin Receptor Agonists) Improve Septic Shock Outcome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42895627.abstract: BackgroundStudies showed different results of vasopressors combination therapy in septic shock patients. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the outcomes of combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists in adult septic shock.MethodsCochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and PubMed databases were searched up to September 27, 2026, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists versus norepinephrine alone in septic shock patients. Two reviewers independently extracted data on mortality, ICU length of stay, renal replacement therapy (RRT) and adverse events. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) was applied to assess random error.ResultsTwenty-one RCTs involving 3873 septic shock patients were included. The results showed that the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists was associated with lower mortality at the longest complete follow-up compared with norepinephrine alone (RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.83 to 0.99, P = .02), but with an increased risk of digital ischemia (RR = 2.21, 95% CI 1.15 to 4.27, P = .02). Subgroup analysis indicated that the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists may provide survival benefits for more severe septic shock patients (RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.00, P = .04). Moreover, compared with norepinephrine alone, the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin showed a trend towards reducing the longest follow-up mortality (RR = 0.89, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.00, P = .05). TSA indicated lack of firm evidence for a beneficial effect.ConclusionsIn adults with septic shock, the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists may reduce mortality at the longest complete follow-up compared with norepinephrine alone (low quality of evidence), but may increase risk of digital ischemia (low quality of evidence). This benefit mainly appeared in more severe septic shock patients. Moreover, norepinephrine plus vasopressin may confer a survival advantage.

42893147.title: Extensive Gastric Necrosis and Perforation Secondary to Intragastric Balloon-Related Gastric Outlet Obstruction: A Case Report.
42893147.abstract: Intragastric balloons (IGBs) are widely used as temporary endoscopic therapy for obesity, but rare complications can be catastrophic. A 55-year-old woman presented with severe epigastric pain, persistent vomiting, and progressive abdominal distension four months after the placement of a 650-mL Orbera intragastric balloon (Apollo Endosurgery, Austin, TX). She was hypotensive and tachycardic and presented with generalized peritonitis. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed marked gastric distension, antropyloric balloon impaction, absent mural enhancement along the lesser curvature, pneumoperitoneum, and free intraperitoneal fluid. Emergency laparotomy uncovered extensive gastric necrosis with a 4-cm perforation. The intact balloon was removed, and total gastrectomy without immediate esophagojejunal reconstruction was performed along with feeding jejunostomy. Histopathological examination confirmed complete transmural infarction and necrosis of the lesser curvature, severe diffuse acute ischemic injury of the adjacent gastric wall with vascular microthrombi, and localized fibrinous peritonitis, with no malignant neoplasm. Despite intensive care, refractory septic shock and multiorgan failure continued to progress, and the patient died 72 hours postoperatively. This case highlights the need for urgent imaging and source control when persistent pain, vomiting, or distension develops in a patient with an IGB.

42892717.title: [A delayed threat: S. aureus sepsis 4 years post-IUD insertion in a healthy young woman].
42892717.abstract: Intrauterine devices (IUDs) are highly effective long-acting reversible contraceptives with an established safety profile. Infectious complications are rare and usually occur shortly after insertion, typically involving polymicrobial pathogens. Staphylococcus aureus is an uncommon pathogen in this context, but its biofilm-forming ability may contribute to delayed and severe presentations. A healthy 25-year-old primiparous woman developed septic shock four years after the insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (Mirena®). She was admitted to the intensive care unit with fever, abdominal pain, and hemodynamic instability requiring vasopressor support. The IUD was removed, and cultures grew methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), while blood cultures were negative. She subsequently improved following device removal, targeted intravenous antibiotics, and supportive intensive care. Notably, nasal carriage was negative in the patient but positive in her partner, suggesting a possible source of colonization. This case illustrates a rare but life-threatening complication of IUD use: septic shock secondary to S. aureus biofilm infection, manifesting years after device insertion. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for device-related infection in women with unexplained sepsis. Prompt device removal, targeted antimicrobial therapy, and multidisciplinary ICU care are critical for optimal outcomes. The possible contribution of partner colonization to the pathogenesis of such infections warrants further investigation.

42892565.title: The Association of the Systemic Oxygen Delivery to Oxygen Consumption Ratio With Mortality, Heart Transplantation, and Mechanical Circulatory Support.
42892565.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42892565.abstract: To identify if the delivery of oxygen over consumption of oxygen (DO2/VO2) ratio is significantly associated with clinical outcomes such as mortality, need for heart transplantation, or need for a mechanical circulatory support device. Retrospective cohort study. Medical and surgical cardiac intensive care units of the Mayo Clinic. Adult patients (≥18 years old) admitted to the cardiothoracic surgical or cardiac intensive care units between January 2012 and December 2025 were included if they underwent invasive hemodynamic assessment with simultaneous arterial blood gas, mixed venous blood gas, hemoglobin, and mean arterial pressure. Patients were excluded if they had their venous oxygen saturations drawn from a central line or a peripherally inserted central catheter, as well as those admitted for sepsis/septic shock. No interventions were performed on patients. DO2/VO2 demonstrated a nonlinear association with mortality. Using the median value of 4.73 as a reference point, patients with a DO2/VO2 value of ∼2 had the highest likelihood of mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis using a prespecified cut-point of 5 did not demonstrate any significant relationship with mortality, likely because of the underlying nonlinear relationship. There was no significant association between DO2/VO2 ratio and the need for mechanical circulatory support or heart transplantation. DO₂/VO₂ is a marker of systemic oxygen balance that complements conventional hemodynamic indices. A categorical threshold of 5 did not show an association with clinical outcomes, but continuous analyses did suggest that a low DO₂/VO₂ may identify a high-risk phenotype.

42891567.title: Torque Teno Virus Viremia in Complicated Staphylococcus aureus Infection: Prevalence, Viral Load, and Associations With Inflammatory Markers and Clinical Outcomes.
42891567.abstract: Torque teno virus (TTV) is a recognized marker of immune competence, but its relevance in severe bacterial infections is unclear. We evaluated prevalence, viral load, and clinical relevance of TTV viremia in complicated Staphylococcus aureus infection (CSAI). In this ancillary analysis of two prospective pharmacokinetic cohort studies at a Swiss university hospital, stored plasma samples were tested for TTV DNA using TTV R-GENE PCR, and cytokines were measured by multiplex immunoassay. Associations between TTV load, inflammatory biomarkers, and clinical outcomes (including 30-day mortality) were assessed. Among 103 patients (median age 67.9 years; 85% with bloodstream infection), TTV viremia was detected in 76% at baseline with a median viral load of 2.85 log10 copies/mL (IQR 1.87-3.56). Levels remained stable over 1 week despite declining inflammatory markers. Baseline TTV load was numerically higher in 30-day non-survivors (3.53 vs. 2.83 log10 copies/mL; p = 0.054) and not associated with mortality after adjusting for age, sex, and SOFA score (OR 1.29 per log10 increase; 95% CI 0.82-2.02; p = 0.268). TTV load was not associated with ICU admission, bacteremia duration, or length of stay. TTV viremia is common in CSAI but shows no significant association with inflammation or short-term outcomes, suggesting limited value for risk stratification.

42890793.title: Bulk peripheral-blood transcriptomic analysis identifies a STAT3/ARG1-associated myeloid immunosuppressive signature in sepsis.
42890793.abstract: Sepsis involves immune dysregulation with myeloid activation and impaired antigen presentation. This study identified a compact immunosuppressive transcriptional signature associated with signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) and arginase 1 (ARG1) using public peripheral-blood transcriptomic datasets. GSE28750, including 10 sepsis samples and 20 healthy controls, was used for discovery; GSE65682, including 120 sepsis-related baseline/ICU-admission samples and 40 healthy controls, was used for external validation. Differential expression, enrichment, ssGSEA, and correlation analyses were performed in GSE28750, whereas candidate-gene directionality and composite-signature performance were reproduced in GSE65682. Differential expression analysis identified 482 genes, with 301 upregulated and 181 downregulated. Representative STAT3/ARG1-associated myeloid and immunoregulatory genes were upregulated, whereas HLA-DRA and HLA-DRB1 were downregulated. Enrichment analysis highlighted myeloid activation, IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling, arginine metabolism, and impaired antigen processing and presentation. Sepsis samples had higher myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC)-like scores than controls (0.72 ± 0.21 vs. -0.36 ± 0.18, P = 1.1 × 10 - 7). The composite signature showed exploratory diagnostic performance, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.94 and 0.88 in the discovery and validation cohorts, respectively. This study provides a reproducible bioinformatic framework and candidate transcriptional signature for assessing sepsis-related myeloid immunosuppressive remodeling. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05087-1.

42890776.title: Protective Effect of Xuebijing Injection on Gastrointestinal Function in Septic Patients of Non-Gastrointestinal Origin.
42890776.abstract: The purpose of this study was to assess the 28-day prognosis and gastrointestinal protection of early Xuebijing in non-gastrointestinal sepsis. Septic patients with infection origins outside the gastrointestinal system and no history of acute gastrointestinal injury (AGI) were included in this single-center retrospective analysis. The two groups' baseline characteristics were balanced by propensity score matching (PSM). Secondary objectives were organ function, enteral nutrition tolerance, inflammatory markers, AGI onset time, and clinical outcomes. The primary endpoint was the incidence of 28-day AGI. After matching, each group had 87 patients, and the baseline variables were evenly distributed among them (P > 0.05). The 28-day cumulative AGI rate for the Xuebijing group was 44.8%, which was considerably lower than the control group's rate of 69.0% (P = 0.002). Additionally, there was a significant delay in the beginning of AGI in the treated group (log-rank P < 0.001). Furthermore, Xuebijing treatment resulted in shorter hospital and ICU stays as well as larger drops in CRP, PCT, and SOFA ratings (all between-group P < 0.05). Patients receiving Xuebijing achieved earlier enteral nutrition initiation (P = 0.0016) and a higher rate of day‑7 caloric targets (66.7% vs 49.4%, P = 0.031). Feeding intolerance showed a trend toward being lower in the Xuebijing group (24.14% vs 39.08%), but this difference did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.050); 28‑day mortality and adverse events also did not differ significantly between groups. Xuebijing use initiated within 24 hours of sepsis diagnosis in septic patients without pre-existing AGI was associated with protection of gastrointestinal function and improvement in several secondary outcomes, including lower AGI incidence, shorter hospital stays, reduced inflammation and organ dysfunction, and better enteral nutrition outcomes, without additional safety concerns. However, no significant difference in 28-day mortality was observed.

42889592.title: Successful endoscopic vacuum therapy in diffuse gastric hemorrhage secondary to acute ischemia: a case report.
42889592.abstract: Acute gastric ischemia is rare and may lead to diffuse mucosal bleeding, often refractory to conventional endoscopic therapy. We describe the case of a 42-year-old critically ill burn patient who developed persistent upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage unresponsive to medical treatment, in whom the novel use of endoscopic vacuum therapy (EVT) was undertaken. Serial endoscopies demonstrated progressive mucosal healing, reduced necrosis, and effective bleeding control. EVT promoted granulation tissue and ulcer healing, avoiding surgical intervention. No EVT-related adverse events occurred. Despite successful hemostasis, the patient later died from a sepsis-related adverse event. In conclusion, this case illustrates EVT as a viable and effective approach for managing refractory diffuse gastric bleeding secondary to ischemia. EVT may offer a minimally invasive alternative to surgery in critically ill patients where standard therapies fail.

42889198.title: Prognostic value of T lymphocyte CD40L expression levels in patients with sepsis.
42889198.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the expression characteristics of CD40L on peripheral blood T lymphocytes in patients with sepsis and explore its value in assessing disease severity and prognosis. This prospective study collected blood samples and clinical data from adult sepsis patients admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine at the First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University between March 2023 and March 2024, with the primary endpoint being 28-day mortality. Multivariate Cox regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association between T lymphocyte CD40L expression and 28-day mortality. Additionally, machine learning algorithms were applied to determine the importance of CD40L-related features, and latent class mixed model analysis was conducted to identify different expression trajectories. A total of 112 sepsis patients were included, with a 28-day mortality rate of 20.5%. CD40L expression levels on peripheral blood CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes were significantly higher in sepsis patients compared to healthy controls. Three distinct expression patterns were identified for both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Patients with persistently low CD40L expression levels had significantly lower survival rates (P < 0.001). Moreover, multivariate Cox analysis identified day 1 CD40L levels on CD4+ (HR 0.712, 95% CI 0.606-0.837, P < 0.001) and CD8+ T cells (HR 0.593, 95% CI 0.481-0.731, P < 0.001) as an independent predictor of 28-day mortality. ROC analysis revealed strong associations between day 1 CD40L expression and mortality, with AUCs of 0.847 and 0.875, respectively. Finally, the combination of CD40L expression with SOFA scores improved clinical decision-making compared to SOFA scoring alone. Peripheral blood T lymphocyte CD40L was identified as an independent predictor of 28-day mortality in sepsis patients. Identifying distinct expression trajectories of CD40L in peripheral blood T lymphocytes can effectively assist in predicting short-term prognosis in patients with sepsis.

42888340.title: Best Practices for Optimizing Recovery from Sepsis; Results of an Expert Panel.
42888340.abstract: Over one million patients survive sepsis annually in the USA. After sepsis, patients often experience new morbidity, with high rates of readmission and post-acute mortality. However, there are limited data to inform best practices to support recovery from sepsis. We convened an expert panel to rate the validity, importance, and resource intensity of 18 care practices aimed to support recovery from sepsis using the RAND/UCLA appropriateness method (a modified Delphi approach). The multidisciplinary panel consisted of 15 experts in sepsis, critical care, hospital medicine, primary care, geriatrics, nursing, and quality improvement, as well as Veteran patient representatives. In addition to the panel members' scores of care practices, panel deliberations were used to understand members' selections. Among the 18 care practices considered, all received agreement in final grading, 10 (56%) were rated as valid, and eight (44%) were rated as uncertain validity. Among 10 valid practices, five were rated as high importance and only moderately resource-intensive-suggesting they should be prioritized for implementation. The high-importance, moderate resource-intensity practices were as follows: scheduling recommended follow-up prior to discharge; screening for limitations in basic and instrumental activities of daily living (I/ADLs) and need for durable medical equipment (DME); educating patients on signs and symptoms of sepsis; educating patients on common symptoms after sepsis (e.g., fatigue, shortness of breath, brain fog); and counseling patients and/or caregivers on discharge medications and their indications. Study limitations include the panel composition (majority VHA clinicians, no social work representation), which may have impacted ratings. The expert panel used a validated method to prioritize care practices for supporting recovery from sepsis. These ratings can be used to improve management, inform quality improvement efforts, and guide resource allocation.

42885115.title: Investigating Fibrinolysis Resistance in Sepsis Using High-Multiplex Plasma Proteomics: A Statistical Analysis Plan.
42885115.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy is characterised by consumptive coagulation abnormalities and resistance to fibrinolysis, which is increasingly recognised as a driver of microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and mortality. The molecular determinants of the fibrinolysis-resistant phenotype remain incompletely defined. To present a pre-specified statistical analysis plan for a plasma proteomic investigation of fibrinolysis resistance in 89 samples collected serially from 32 critically ill patients with sepsis, using the Olink Explore HT platform (approximately 5400 proteins). The plan is designed to characterise protein associations with a validated bedside measure of fibrinolysis resistance, the ratio of tissue plasminogen activator-induced lysis time to fibrin clot amplitude (TPA-LT/FIBA10). The associations will be examined across the fibrinolysis resistance severity continuum and between three ordinal severity grades, and over time within individual patients. The analytic framework combines five complementary approaches: (i) limit-of-detection-based data filtering, (ii) continuous-variable modelling of protein abundance against TPA-LT/FIBA10 using limma-trend regression, (iii) categorical comparison across severity grades using empirical Bayes moderated statistics, (iv) linear mixed-effects modelling of longitudinal intra-patient trajectories and (v) pathway-level enrichment analysis to translate statistical associations into mechanistic hypotheses. A semi-supervised pathway clustering analysis will describe how proteins change by fibrinolysis resistance in eight a priori defined domains. This multi-model design is intended to define genuine biological signals in a high-dimensional dataset while remaining transparent about the exploratory nature of several components. The statistical reasoning behind each method is discussed alongside anticipated limitations. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06680180.

42882191.title: IgM- and IgA-Enriched Polyclonal Intravenous Immunoglobulin Therapy in Sepsis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
42882191.abstract: Background/Objectives: Evidence for adjunctive intravenous immunoglobulin therapy in sepsis remains conflicting. This study evaluated the association of IgM- and IgA-enriched polyclonal intravenous immunoglobulin (IgGAM) therapy with clinical outcomes, including post hoc analyses according to initial empiric antibiotic therapy (IEAT) appropriateness. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 50 adults with sepsis or septic shock according to Sepsis-3 criteria, treated between November 2006 and March 2010. Twenty-five patients received adjunctive IgGAM plus standard sepsis management, and 25 received standard management alone. Primary outcomes were 28-day intensive care unit (ICU) mortality, overall ICU mortality, and in-hospital mortality. Results: Overall, 28-day ICU mortality was 28.0% with IgGAM and 32.0% with control (relative risk, 0.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.37-2.05; p = 0.758); other mortality outcomes did not differ significantly. Kaplan-Meier survival distributions also did not differ significantly (log-rank p = 0.208). During the ICU stay, vasopressor therapy was required in 68% of the IgGAM group and 92% of the control group (p = 0.034); corresponding study day 1 requirements were 60% and 76% (p = 0.225). In the complete-case longitudinal analysis (IgGAM group, n = 20; control group, n = 25), SOFA scores decreased significantly over time within the IgGAM group (p = 0.017), whereas no significant within-group change was observed in the control group (p = 0.616). In the post hoc appropriate-IEAT subgroup, 28-day ICU mortality was 0.0% versus 36.8% (p = 0.026), in-hospital mortality was 25.0% versus 63.2% (p = 0.038), and Kaplan-Meier survival distributions differed significantly (log-rank p = 0.004). The 60-day restricted mean survival time was 58.1 versus 38.4 days, with a difference of 19.8 days (95% CI, 11.1-28.4). Conclusions: Adjunctive IgGAM therapy was not associated with significant differences in mortality overall. Findings in the post hoc appropriate-IEAT subgroup were hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted cautiously given potential selection bias, residual confounding, and multiple comparisons. Prospective evaluation within optimized sepsis care is warranted.

42882158.title: Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Optimization and Therapeutic Drug Monitoring of Beta-Lactam Antibiotics in Abdominal Sepsis: Current Evidence, Challenges, and Clinical Perspectives-A Narrative Review.
42882158.abstract: Background: Abdominal sepsis is associated with profound pharmacokinetic (PK) alterations that make standard beta-lactam dosing regimens potentially inadequate in critically ill patients. Increased volume of distribution, hypoalbuminemia, augmented renal clearance (ARC), acute kidney injury (AKI) and the PK complexity of the peritoneal compartment collectively impair the ability of conventional dosing to achieve pharmacodynamic (PD) targets. These PK derangements are clinically relevant but incompletely characterized in intra-abdominal infections (IAI)- specific cohorts, as most available data derive from broader critically ill populations. Beta-lactam antibiotics, the cornerstone therapy in IAIs, are particularly susceptible to these alterations, especially in the context of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens. Methods: We conducted a structured narrative review of the literature published between 2010 and 2026, searching PubMed and Embase using terms related to pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, therapeutic drug monitoring, beta-lactam antibiotics, abdominal sepsis, and intra-abdominal infection in critically ill patients. Additional references were identified through manual bibliography screening, including seminal studies predating the search window. No formal systematic review methodology was applied. Results: PK/PD optimization in abdominal sepsis can be organized around four proposed domains: extended or continuous infusion of beta-lactams to maximize the time above the minimum inhibitory concentration; therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) to guide individualized dose adjustment in the presence of ARC, AKI, or continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT); tailored dose optimization during CRRT; and target attainment analysis against MDR organisms. Extended and continuous infusions improve PD target attainment and are associated with improved outcomes in some observational studies, although prospective IAI-specific evidence is lacking and the evidence supporting these strategies derives largely from broader intensive care unit populations. Conclusions: In abdominal sepsis, integrating PK/PD principles and TDM-guided dosing represents a pharmacologically rational strategy to optimize beta-lactam exposure and improve target attainment against MDR pathogens. Rigorous IAI-specific prospective studies are needed to establish definitive TDM-guided dosing protocols and translate these pharmacological strategies in this high-acuity setting.

42881967.title: Association of Postoperative Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio with Suspected Infection, Culture Positivity, Sepsis, and Septic Shock in 1408 Patients After Cranial Neurosurgery.
42881967.abstract: Background/Objectives: The early postoperative stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) may capture acute glycemic stress relative to chronic glycemia, but its association with infection-related events after cranial neurosurgery remains uncertain. We evaluated these associations in critically ill patients after cranial neurosurgical procedures. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 1408 adults in MIMIC-IV after eligible cranial neurosurgical procedures. SHR was calculated from the first serum glucose measurement 6-24 h after surgery and estimated average glucose was derived from HbA1c. Primary outcomes were electronic health record (EHR)-defined suspected infection, culture-positive infection from any qualifying specimen, Sepsis-3-defined sepsis, and an EHR-based septic shock proxy. The secondary outcome was 90-day mortality. Results: In fully adjusted models, each 0.1-unit increase in SHR was associated with suspected infection (OR 1.08, 95% CI 1.04-1.12), culture-positive infection (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.09), Sepsis-3-defined sepsis (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.03-1.11), and septic shock (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.05-1.15). In nested analyses, each 1-SD increase in SHR was associated with 90-day mortality (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.29-1.96). Associations persisted in 24-h lag analyses. Adding SHR yielded small, non-significant AUC increases but improved reclassification for Sepsis-3-defined sepsis and septic shock. Conclusions: Higher early postoperative SHR was associated with EHR-derived, all-source infection-related and sepsis-related events and 90-day mortality in a heterogeneous postoperative neurocritical care cohort. These findings do not establish that SHR predicts postoperative neurosurgical infection; prospective external validation is required before clinical use.

42965242.title: Manganese Deposition Encephalopathy Associated With Prolonged Total Parenteral Nutrition: A Case Report.
authors: Beluzzo da Mota de Lima Sinke G
42965242.abstract: Manganese encephalopathy is a rare neurological disorder most commonly associated with chronic occupational exposure or impaired hepatobiliary elimination. We report a case of suspected manganese deposition encephalopathy associated with prolonged total parenteral nutrition in a critically ill patient with severe abdominal disease and cholestatic dysfunction. A 50-year-old man was admitted with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, tachycardia, and jaundice. Computed tomography demonstrated acute pancreatitis with pancreatic necrosis, choledocholithiasis, cholelithiasis, and superior mesenteric artery thrombosis. His clinical course was complicated by abdominal sepsis, anasarca, anemia, spontaneous hematomas, and the need for prolonged intensive care and total parenteral nutrition. On hospital day 41, he developed rigidity and involuntary movements involving the tongue and upper limbs, prompting neurological assessment. Serum manganese was 3.1 µg/L (reference value: 2 µg/L), and brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated T1 hyperintensity in the globus pallidus, findings compatible with manganese encephalopathy. Treatment with levodopa/benserazide produced a limited response, with persistent severe parkinsonism and inability to ambulate despite gradual improvement in tetraparesis associated with concurrent critical illness neuropathy. The patient was discharged on hospital day 129. This case highlights the importance of considering manganese toxicity in critically ill patients receiving prolonged parenteral nutrition, particularly in the setting of impaired biliary elimination, and supports early neurological surveillance and monitoring of trace elements.

42965188.title: Hyponatremia in septic shock: Pathophysiology, fluid resuscitation challenges, and neurological complications.
42965188.journal: Journal of family medicine and primary care
42965188.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by organ dysfunction due to a dysregulated host response to infection, with septic shock representing its most severe form and carrying high mortality in intensive care units (ICUs). Among critically ill patients, hyponatremia (serum sodium) <135 mmol/L is a common electrolyte disturbance associated with worse outcomes. While prior studies have explored hypernatremia in septic shock, the pathophysiology, clinical implications, and management of hyponatremia in this context remain underexplored, creating uncertainty for clinicians regarding fluid resuscitation strategies and neurological safety. This narrative review aimed to synthesize current evidence on hyponatremia in septic shock, focusing on underlying mechanisms, resuscitation challenges, and neurological complications. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EMBASE, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2017 and 2025, including clinical cohorts, case reports, and systematic reviews. The findings indicate that hyponatremia in septic shock arises from non-osmotic vasopressin release, systemic inflammation, acute kidney injury, and fluid shifts during aggressive resuscitation. Large-volume crystalloid administration may exacerbate sodium derangements, while rapid correction poses a risk of osmotic demyelination syndrome (ODS), even under guideline-adherent practices. Case reports suggest plasma exchange may provide the most consistent benefit in severe neurological complications. In conclusion, hyponatremia in septic shock reflects complex neuroendocrine, inflammatory, and renal interactions. Optimized management requires individualized fluid strategies, cautious sodium correction, and prolonged neurological monitoring to mitigate complications and improve outcomes in critically ill patients.

42965100.title: Inflammatory and nutritional indices as predictors of poor prognosis in pyogenic liver abscesses: a retrospective cohort study.
42965100.abstract: This retrospective study of 458 pyogenic liver abscesses (PLA) patients explored the link between inflammation/nutrition-based indices and poor prognosis in PLA, aiming to enhance the prediction of poor prognosis such as mortality, septic shock, or intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Patient data, including demographics, comorbidities, clinical presentations, laboratory results, and treatment outcomes, were extracted from medical records. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to identify independent predictors and evaluate their discriminative power. A simplified joint prediction model was developed based on rigorous variable selection criteria, and its performance was assessed using internal validation. Patients with poor prognosis (n = 33) exhibited lower lymphocyte counts, hemoglobin, platelets, and albumin, alongside elevated inflammation markers. Multivariable analysis identified the neutrophil-to-albumin ratio (NAR) (odds ratio (OR) 6.87 per standard deviation (SD), 95% confidence interval (CI) [2.13-22.17], p = 0.001), prognostic nutritional index (PNI) (OR 0.99 per SD, 95% CI [0.894-0.997], p = 0.038), and controlling nutritional status (CONUT) score (OR 1.37 per SD, 95% CI [1.164-1.602], p < 0.001) as independent predictors. ROC analysis showed these indices had good discriminative ability (PNI: area under the curve (AUC) = 0.757, p < 0.001; PLR: AUC = 0.704, p < 0.001; CONUT: AUC = 0.803, p < 0.001; PLT: AUC = 0.740, p < 0.001). Notably, a joint prediction model combining platelet count (PLT) and CONUT achieved superior prediction with an AUC of 0.822. This investigation reveals that easily obtainable inflammatory and nutritional indices (NAR, PNI, CONUT and PLT) serve as reliable predictors of poor prognosis in PLA. A combined model integrating PLT and CONUT demonstrates promising discriminative performance, enabling early risk stratification.

42964914.title: When Hydronephrosis Was Not Physiological: A Case of Septic Shock Secondary to Obstructive Uropathy in Pregnancy.
42964914.abstract: Urosepsis in pregnancy is a life-threatening condition requiring early recognition, rapid multidisciplinary escalation and timely source control. Physiological hydronephrosis is common during pregnancy and may obscure clinically significant urinary tract obstruction. We report a 26-year-old gravida 5 para 3 woman at 30 weeks' gestation who presented with severe right-sided loin pain. Initial ultrasound demonstrated moderate right hydronephrosis without a visible calculus. Within hours, she deteriorated with pyrexia, acute kidney injury, lactic acidosis and septic shock. Computed tomography demonstrated high-grade obstruction of the right renal collecting system secondary to a ureteropelvic junction calculus with associated inflammatory change. Following maternal deterioration and evidence of foetal compromise, an urgent multidisciplinary decision was made to proceed with category 1 caesarean delivery followed by cystoscopy and right ureteric stent insertion. Cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae. The patient subsequently required intensive care support including invasive ventilation, vasopressors, renal replacement therapy and treatment for disseminated intravascular coagulation. Both maternal and neonatal outcomes were favourable. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing physiological hydronephrosis from pathological obstruction in pregnancy and emphasises the importance of source control in infected obstructive uropathy.

42964594.title: Procalcitonin and Presepsin in Gram-Negative Sepsis: Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Antimicrobial Stewardship Perspectives.
42964594.abstract: Because delayed pathogen identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing might delay effective treatment, sepsis caused by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria continues to be a significant problem in intensive care units. The clinical usefulness of procalcitonin (PCT) and presepsin as early indicators for Gram-negative sepsis diagnosis, disease severity prediction, treatment response monitoring, and antimicrobial stewardship is assessed in this review. While presepsin provides quick early identification and significant prognostic value, particularly in culture-negative sepsis, PCT is notably useful in distinguishing Gram-negative infections from Gram-positive or fungal etiologies. Before traditional culture findings are available, serial monitoring of both biomarkers may assist in detecting treatment failure, delayed biomarker clearance, and potential multidrug-resistant infections. Confounding variables like burns, trauma, renal failure, surgery, and sterile inflammation must be taken into account during interpretation, though. Rapid molecular diagnostics combined with PCT and presepsin may enhance early treatment choices, lower needless antibiotic exposure, and promote precision-based care for critically ill septic patients.

42964465.title: Systematic review of the current landscape and imaging-based definition of septic cardiomyopathy.
42964465.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
42964465.abstract: Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) has no current unified definition, although it can be associated with significant mortality. It encompasses a wide spectrum of cardiac dysfunction ranging from mild to severe systolic and/or diastolic dysfunction of the left and/or right ventricle. The objective of this review is to evaluate the imaging modalities and parameters used to define SCM and the clinical outcomes. We conducted a systematic review of the literature, including studies up to August 2025, examining the impact of cardiac dysfunction, specifically related to the systolic and/or diastolic dysfunction of the left or right ventricle. We focussed on mortality and comparable phrases as the primary outcome. We considered all cardiac imaging methods. All relevant studies were identified in a search strategy including MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus. About 2669 articles were identified, of which 142 full-text publications were evaluated. Final analysis included 87 publications. Forty five articles provided a definition of SCM. Seventy studies used TTE. Eighteen studies associated LV dysfunction to mortality. Thirteen studies found an association between diastolic dysfunction or RV dysfunction and mortality. About 64% of the studies assessed cardiac function within 24-h of admission. Twenty eight studies re-assessed reversibility of cardiac dysfunction. Cardiac dysfunction is commonly reported in the critically ill septic population. There was considerable heterogeneity with regards to the diagnostic criteria of SCM, parameters used to determine cardiac dysfunction, outcomes evaluated, timing of study or assessing reversibility. Given the high prevalence of cardiac dysfunction in sepsis, a unified assessment and definition of SCM is needed.

42964288.title: Development and validation of a prognostic prediction model for elderly patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury based on interpretable machine learning.
42964288.abstract: Elderly patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) have high short-term mortality; early identification of high-risk individuals is critical for personalized intervention. Traditional clinical scoring systems relying on linear assumptions and conventional machine learning models often lack interpretability, hindering translation to clinical practice. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable prognostic model for 28-day in-hospital mortality in elderly SA-AKI using routinely available clinical variables. Clinical data of 11,468 elderly SA-AKI patients were retrospectively extracted from the MIMIC-IV database and divided into training and internal test sets at a 7:3 ratio using stratified random sampling. A dual feature selection strategy combining LASSO regression and random forest was applied. Five machine learning models-decision tree, logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost-were constructed in parallel. Model discrimination and calibration were evaluated by AUC, Brier score, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. External independent validation was performed using a clinical cohort of 257 patients from the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University. The SHAP method was used for global and individual-level interpretability of the optimal model. Dual feature selection identified 10 independent predictors: age, weight, red blood cell distribution width, arterial partial pressure of oxygen, blood lactate, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, blood urea nitrogen, serum creatinine, and respiratory rate. Among the five models, XGBoost demonstrated the best performance, with training AUC 0.9898 (accuracy 0.9472) and external validation AUC 0.9156 (accuracy 0.8560), indicating strong generalizability. SHAP global importance ranking showed age as the primary driver, followed by serum creatinine and arterial partial pressure of oxygen. Each core feature exhibited a nonlinear association with 28-day mortality risk, with clear model-derived risk inflection points rather than clinical intervention thresholds. The XGBoost-based interpretable model exhibits excellent discriminative performance and robust external generalizability for predicting 28-day mortality in elderly SA-AKI. The SHAP attribution framework renders model decisions transparent, providing quantitative evidence-based support for early risk stratification and hypothesis generation for individualized organ-protective strategies in the ICU.

42962939.title: Cefiderocol for the treatment of bloodstream infection due to MBL-producing Enterobacterales: a single-center retrospective cohort.
42962939.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) caused by metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producing Enterobacterales are associated with high mortality and limited therapeutic options. Real-world data on cefiderocol remain scarce. We conducted a retrospective, single-centre study (January 2023-April 2025) including adult patients with MBL-producing Enterobacterales BSI who received cefiderocol for ≥72 hours. The main study outcome was 14-day clinical cure rate. Nineteen patients were included (mean age: 62.1 ± 12.1 years; median Charlson comorbidity index: 2.0 [IQR: 1.0 - 4.0]). Most (84.2%) had some form of immunosuppression. BSI sources were intra-abdominal (31.6%), respiratory (21.1%), and urinary tract (21.1%). Septic shock occurred in 10.5% of patients, and 26.3% required ICU admission. Median SOFA score at the initiation of cefiderocol was 5.0 days (4.5 - 8.5). Klebsiella spp. (89.5%) was the most common MBL-producing Enterobacterales (VIM [63.2%], NDM/OXA-48-like [26.3%], NDM [10.5%]). Prior colonization was observed in 36.8% of patients. Empirical therapy mainly included ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam for a median duration of 2 days (IQR 0.5-3.5). Cefiderocol was administered for a median of 8.0 days [4.0-14.0], as monotherapy in 79% and as combination therapy in 10.5%. Clinical cure rate was achieved by day +14 in 78.9% (15/19) of patients. All-cause mortality by day +14 was 10.5% (2/19). Cefiderocol resistance emerged during therapy in three out of four patients not achieving clinical and microbiological cure (15.8% [3/19] of the cohort), and mainly involved NDM/OXA-48-like-coproducing K. pneumoniae. Cefiderocol is a potential option for MBL-producing Enterobacterales BSIs, although its efficacy may be limited by the development of treatment-emergent resistance.

42962568.title: Metabolic phenotypes in sepsis: A conceptual framework for phenotype-informed nutrition.
42962568.abstract: Sepsis is a biologically heterogeneous syndrome characterized by profound alterations in immune function and intermediary metabolism that challenge standardized nutritional management. Current clinical nutrition guidelines recommend early enteral nutrition after hemodynamic stabilization, progressive caloric advancement, and avoidance of early full feeding, but they do not incorporate metabolic phenotyping. Emerging evidence from immunometabolism, metabolomics, and systems biology shows recurring, partially overlapping metabolic patterns in sepsis, including hyperglycolytic-hyperlactatemic, mitochondrial-bioenergetic dysfunction, hyperinflammatory Warburg-like, immunoparalytic-tolerant, lipidomic-acylcarnitine, gut-microbiota, and hypercatabolic-muscle wasting domains. These patterns share mechanisms and may coexist or evolve over time; their biological basis should be distinguished from their still unvalidated use as mutually exclusive bedside diagnostic classes. This narrative review examines these biological domains and their nutritional relevance while explicitly separating established, phase-based critical-care nutrition from phenotype-informed treatment hypotheses. In particular, sepsis-associated mitochondrial abnormalities may be tissue- and cell-specific and do not imply generalized suppression of whole-body oxygen consumption. Likewise, hyperglycemia, hyperlactatemia, or increased carbon dioxide production are not validated markers of overfeeding. Residual endogenous substrate production persists during acute critical illness but cannot currently be quantified as total energy flux at the bedside, limiting precise assessment of the combined endogenous and exogenous substrate load. No prospective randomized trial has yet tested nutrition prescribed according to the metabolic domains proposed here. The seven-domain framework therefore organizes recurrent components of sepsis biology; what remains to be validated is its operational use for patient classification and for predicting differential response to nutritional interventions.

42960657.title: First fatal central line-associated bloodstream infection caused by Alistipes onderdonkii.
42960657.abstract: Alistipes onderdonkii (A. onderdonkii) is a rare anaerobic Gram-negative bacillus that forms part of the normal gastrointestinal microbiota but has recently emerged as an opportunistic pathogen in immunocompromised individuals. We report a fatal bacteremia due to A. onderdonkii in a 61-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis via a right internal jugular catheter and multiple comorbidities. He presented with septic shock; catheter cuff infection was evident. Anaerobic catheter blood cultures yielded a slow-growing Gram-negative bacillus identified as A. onderdonkii by MALDI-TOF MS. Susceptibility showed activity to amoxicillin-clavulanate, ampicillin-sulbactam, and metronidazole, with penicillin and ceftriaxone resistance. Therapy was de-escalated to ampicillin-sulbactam. Despite source control and ICU support, the patient developed gastrointestinal bleeding and multiorgan failure, culminating in death. This case highlights the pathogenic potential of A. onderdonkii as a cause of severe bloodstream infection in vulnerable patients with multiple comorbidities and chronic hemodialysis catheters. Increased awareness of this emerging Alistipes species may facilitate timely recognition, appropriate antimicrobial management, and further understanding of its clinical significance.

42842056.title: Impact of initial disease severity and metabolic stress on mortality in patients with suspected external ventricular drain-associated infection.
42842056.abstract: External ventricular drainage (EVD) remains indispensable for managing intracranial pressure and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) disorders. Despite advances in neurosurgical care and infection prevention, EVD-related infections still contribute substantially to morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to identify predictors of mortality and evaluate the clinical relevance of infection-related and metabolic parameters in patients with suspected EVD-associated infection undergoing EVD placement. We retrospectively analyzed all adult patients who underwent EVD insertion and were clinically suspected of having an EVD-associated infection at a tertiary hospital over an 18-month period. Data from electronic medical records included demographics, neurological diagnosis, comorbidities, catheter characteristics, laboratory results, and antimicrobial therapy. EVD-associated infection was defined according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) criteria. Statistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics 26. A total of 102 patients with clinically suspected EVD-associated infection were evaluated. CSF cultures were positive in 33 (32%) cases, most frequently yielding Staphylococcus epidermidis and Acinetobacter baumannii . Intensive care unit (ICU) admission was associated with higher crude mortality rates, likely reflecting greater baseline neurological severity. Initial Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (aOR = 0.85, p = 0.005) was found to be an independent predictor of mortality. Neither sex nor comorbidities predicted death. Hyperglycemia (> 140 mg/dL) and elevated lactate (> 1.2 mmol/L) independently associated with 30-day mortality. Shorter catheterization duration (≤ 5 days) also predicted death, likely reflecting greater neurological compromise. In our selected cohort of patients with clinically suspected EVD-associated infection, CSF culture positivity was not independently associated with mortality, although patients with culture-confirmed infection exhibited higher CSF pleocytosis and Cell Index (CI) values. Among patients with clinically suspected EVD-associated infection, initial neurological severity, together with markers of systemic metabolic stress, were independently associated with 30-day mortality. Hyperglycemia and elevated lactate emerged as key prognostic markers. While elevated CI values may support the diagnosis of culture-confirmed infection, CI did not demonstrate independent prognostic value for mortality. These findings should be interpreted within the context of this selected cohort and should not be generalized to the overall EVD population. Larger prospective studies including a greater number of culture-confirmed infections are needed to confirm these results.

42956907.title: Plasma and Pulmonary Exposure of Eravacycline in a 73-Year-Old Patient with Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Pneumonia.
42956907.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) is a major cause of hospital-acquired pneumonia, associated with high mortality and limited therapeutic options. While eravacycline, a novel fluorocycline antibiotic, demonstrates potent in vitro activity against CRAB, real-world pharmacokinetic data-particularly pulmonary exposure in critically ill patients-remain limited. We report a 73-year-old patient with severe traumatic brain injury who developed CRAB pneumonia during hospitalization. Eravacycline was administered intravenously at a weight-based dose of 69 mg every 12 h. Plasma concentrations were measured at steady state, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples were collected 13 h after the start of infusion for estimation of epithelial lining fluid (ELF) concentrations using the urea dilution method. The peak plasma concentration was 0.564 mg/L at approximately 1 h post-dose, with an AUC0-24,ss of 6.42 mg·h/L. At 13 h post-dose, eravacycline concentrations were 0.192 mg/L in plasma, 0.924 mg/L in left lung ELF, and 0.393 mg/L in right lung ELF. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of the isolate was 0.5 mg/L. No significant adverse events were observed. This case provides real-world evidence of systemic exposure and measurable pulmonary penetration of eravacycline in a critically ill patient with CRAB pneumonia.

42847998.title: Development and validation of a cefepime population pharmacokinetic model to guide treatment for patients with hospital-acquired pneumonia requiring renal replacement.
42847998.abstract: Cefepime is used in critically ill pneumonia patients, but dosing in renal replacement therapy (RRT) is complicated by altered renal function, extracorporeal removal, and variability in pulmonary epithelial lining fluid (ELF) exposure. We sought to develop an integrated model linking systemic, extracorporeal, and pulmonary cefepime pharmacokinetics in RRT. Pharmacokinetic (PK) data from critically ill adults receiving cefepime and requiring RRT were included. In a dedicated continuous RRT (CRRT) cohort (n = 8), pre- and post-filter plasma and effluent PK data were collected. Additional patients (n = 43) requiring RRT also contributed plasma and ELF samples. A non-parametric population PK model was developed using an 80/20 subject-level development-validation split. Covariate models assessed the impact of residual renal function, effluent flow rate, body size, and fixed intradialytic hemodialysis (HD) clearance. Monte Carlo simulations evaluated plasma and ELF target attainment across dosing strategies, weight strata, and minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). The final model jointly described systemic, extracorporeal, and pulmonary cefepime disposition using piecewise central volume, native clearance, linear effluent-flow-dependent CRRT clearance, fixed HD clearance, and ELF distribution. Simulations showed adequate plasma target attainment, whereas ELF attainment was sensitive to MIC, target, regimen, and body weight. Continuous infusions of 4 g/day provided adequate ELF attainment at MICs ≤4 mg/L. Plasma-based cefepime target attainment may overestimate pulmonary exposure during RRT, particularly at higher MICs, body weights, and fT>MIC targets. External validation and prospective studies are needed to refine pulmonary target estimates and determine whether plasma-guided Bayesian dosing can reliably ensure site-of-infection exposure.

42844960.title: Clinical Profile, Prognostic Indicators, and Outcomes in Patients with Acute Pyelonephritis: Comparing Emphysematous with Nonemphysematous Pyelonephritis.
42844960.abstract: Emphysematous pyelonephritis (EPN) is a life-threatening necrotizing infection of the upper urinary tract, resulting in high morbidity and mortality. Comparative data between EPN and non-EPN are scarce, especially from developing countries. To compare the clinical profile, prognostic indicators, management strategies, and outcomes in patients with emphysematous and nonemphysematous acute pyelonephritis (APN). This was a prospective observational study conducted in a tertiary care teaching institute in North India from March 2022 to December 2025 and included 120 consecutive adult patients with APN. Radiological imaging was used to classify patients as EPN or non-EPN. Of the 120 patients, 99 (82.5%) had non-EPN and 21 (17.5%) had EPN. The most common comorbidity was diabetes mellitus (75.0%) and was associated more frequently with EPN (95.2% vs. 70.7%, P = 0.024). Uncontrolled glycemia (glycosylated hemoglobin: >7.5%) was present in 67.5% of patients and significantly associated with EPN (P = 0.047). Escherichia coli was the most common pathogen found in urine (43.7%) and blood (62.5%) cultures. Radiological or surgical interventions were needed in 56.7% of patients, and renal replacement therapy and intensive care admission were needed in 34.2% and 22.5%, respectively. Mortality was higher in the EPN group than in the non-EPN group (14.3% vs. 3.0%; P = 0.066). EPN is the severest form of APN and is associated with worse glycemic control, increased requirement for invasive procedures, and higher in-hospital mortality. Early diagnosis, prompt imaging, appropriate antimicrobial therapy, and timely multidisciplinary management are essential to improve clinical outcome.

42933950.title: Aligning Peripheral Intravenous Catheter Practices with the Vessel Health and Preservation Framework.
42933950.journal: Critical care nursing clinics of North America
42933950.abstract: The Vessel Health and Preservation framework was established with the aim of increasing the implementation of evidence-based vascular access practices and ultimately improving patient outcomes. This model was designed to place attention on reducing infection risks and drive more effective assessments of site selections, appropriate device selection, and increased application of strategies that reduce vascular harm, complications, and patient discomfort. Many conventional nonevidence informed practices with peripheral intravenous catheters continue to persist in critical care. Understanding best evidence to guide vascular access will positively impact patient safety and outcomes.

42876889.title: The Impact of Empiric Linezolid Compared With Vancomycin on Inpatient Outcomes.
42876889.journal: The Journal of pharmacy technology : jPT : official publication of the Association of Pharmacy Technicians
42876889.abstract: Vancomycin and linezolid are commonly used for empiric treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), but differences may influence the preferred agent. Vancomycin requires individualized dosing and drug monitoring, possibly delaying initiation. Linezolid offers fixed dosing, and potentially lower costs, which may improve time to first dose. This study compares clinical, operational, and cost outcomes associated with empiric vancomycin and linezolid use. This single-center, retrospective chart review included a convenience sample of 100 hospitalized adults receiving more than 1 dose of empiric vancomycin or linezolid, stratified by level of care (intensive care unit [ICU] vs non-ICU). The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included time to first dose, adverse events, therapy changes, treatment duration, length of stay (LOS), cost, and vancomycin dosing characteristics. A convenience sample of 100 patients (50 per group) was analyzed. Thirty-day all-cause mortality was 22% with vancomycin versus 12% with linezolid (P = .183). No statistically significant differences were observed in time to first dose (2.03 ± 1.51 hours vs 1.6 ± 1.66 hours, P = .180). No statistically significant difference was detected in therapy changes, treatment duration, hospital/ICU LOS, treatment failure, and adverse events. Vancomycin had a higher medication cost ($46.59 vs $29.52, P = .012). Patients receiving vancomycin had an average of 2.8 levels, requiring a median of 54.6 hours to reach therapeutic range, maintaining it for 29.5% of treatment duration. This study is limited by its retrospective design and small sample size. No statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes were detected between patients receiving empiric linezolid and vancomycin. Linezolid was associated with lower drug acquisition cost.

42874849.title: Genomic epidemiology reveals niche specialization and a virulence-resistance trade-off in ST23 and ST11 hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae.
42874849.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
42874849.abstract: The convergence of hypervirulence and carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae poses a critical public health threat, yet the comparative genomic characteristics and adaptation patterns of dominant clones ST23 and ST11 in clinical settings remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize their divergent adaptive strategies. We performed whole-genome sequencing on 824 hvKP isolates derived from 2,193 clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates collected at a National Regional Medical Center in Central China. Among these, ST23 (n=199) and ST11 (n=140) represented the two predominant sequence types and were compared regarding antimicrobial resistance profiles, resistance determinants, virulence determinants, plasmid replicon types, and phylogenetic relationships using comparative genomic, phylogenetic, and co-acquisition analyses. ST23-hvKP was primarily associated with surgical and medical departments, largely antibiotic-susceptible (MDR 33.7%, CR 1.0%), with near-complete virulence gene profiles (iuc 99.5%, iro 97.5%). Conversely, ST11-hvKP was predominantly ICU-associated and extensively drug-resistant (MDR 97.9%, CR 93.6%), characterized by frequent blaKPC-2 carriage (95.7%) and a highly prevalent IncFII(pHN7A8) replicon (98.6%), with blaKPC-2 strongly associated with IncFII(pHN7A8), but with an incomplete virulence profile (iro 0.7%). Resistance-hypervirulence convergence was markedly higher in ST11 (92.1%) than ST23 (9.5%). Plasmid ecology and co-acquisition analysis revealed a negative correlation between resistance-associated (IncFII/IncR) and virulence-associated (IncFIB(K)) replicons, suggesting that convergence in ST11 involves coexisting distinct plasmid systems rather than detectable plasmid fusion events. Phylogenetic analysis demonstrated distinct clustering patterns between ST23 and ST11. ST23 retains a classic hypervirulent phenotype, whereas ST11 represents a hospital-adapted convergent clone characterized by a complex resistome, an incomplete canonical virulence repertoire, and separate plasmid systems. This niche-specialized resistance-virulence trade-off underscores the need for clone-tailored surveillance and management strategies.

42864947.title: Improving hand hygiene compliance in Greek hospitals: results of a Nationwide Quality Improvement Program (GRIPP-SNF).
42864947.abstract: Hand hygiene (HH) is the most effective way to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and the spread of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. HH compliance is particularly relevant in Greece, which has among the highest rates of HAIs and antimicrobial resistance in the European Union. The aim of our study was to assess current HH practices in Greece and to improve compliance. Prospective observational quasi-experimental (before-after) study. Eight public adult tertiary hospitals. "Physicians, Nurses, and Ancillary Healthcare Workers." Three time periods were defined: the baseline period (December 2021-June 2022), intervention period (July 2022-January 2023), and postintervention period (February 2023-May 2024). An improvement bundle was implemented. A minimum of 30 observations per department per month of HH opportunities were required. Trained observers conducted observations using a standardized data collection tool. Interrupted time-series analysis was performed. 38,069 HH opportunities were observed. Overall compliance was 48.5%. Glove use without proper HH was observed in 72.9% of opportunities. Alcohol-based hand rub was used for HH by 57.8% of HCW who conducted HH. Compliance improved from 37.3% in the baseline period to 53.3% after the intervention (16% increase, P < .001). Improved compliance was observed in 9/13 (69%) intensive care units. Of 10 participating medical and surgical wards, improved compliance was observed in 9 (90%) units, and improvement ranged from 7.2% to 28.3. Overall, we found low compliance rates and gaps in HH practices in Greek hospitals. A quality improvement intervention improved overall HH compliance. This is the largest study of HH compliance in Greek hospitals to date.

42863790.title: High burden of Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales: A prospective cross-sectional study at a tertiary hospital in Morocco.
42863790.abstract: The present study aimed to determine and update the prevalence of Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, to characterize carbapenemase production, and to assess antimicrobial susceptibility in a Moroccan tertiary hospital. A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2021 to December 2022, during which time 6672 Enterobacteriaceae isolates were recovered from clinical specimens from patients with suspected bacterial infections. Species were identified using MALDI-TOF-MS and the BD Phoenix® M50 for antimicrobial susceptibility according to EUCAST screening criteria. NG-Test® CARBA 5 assay was used for carbapenemase detection and characterization. Among the 6672 Enterobacteriaceae isolates, 1289 showed decreased susceptibility to ertapenem (19.3%).
