The effect of this combination therapy on 28-day mortality requires further validation in multicenter prospective studies.

42920550.title: Development and application of a targeted MISCP-S intervention model for psychiatric hospitals.
42920550.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
42920550.abstract: A multi-modal intervention model (MISCP-S) was constructed based on the characteristics of psychiatric medical institutions, to evaluate its impact on the pathogen detection specimen submission rate related to healthcare-associated infection diagnosis and the effect of rational antibacterial use. In a large tertiary psychiatric hospital, we established the MISCP-S Intervention Model (Multidisciplinary Collaboration, Informatization and Intelligence, Stratified Training, Constraints and Incentives, and Process Optimization) tailored to specialty-specific infection control challenges. 1343 HAI cases were collected as the pre-intervention group from January 2022 to November 2023, and 677 cases were collected as the post-intervention group from March 2024 to July 2025. The pathogen detection specimen submission rate increased significantly from 69.47% to 98.38% (P < 0.05), with the appropriateness rate of tests ordered reaching 100%. This improvement was most pronounced in departments with previously low submission rates, such as the acute psychiatric department (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified the intervention, patient location in ICU/internal medicine/chronic care units, and urinary tract infection as significant facilitating factors for specimen submission (all P < 0.05). The therapeutic antimicrobial use rate decreased from 16.03% to 14.61% (P < 0.05). The overall detection rate of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) decreased from 37.44% to 33.74% (P < 0.05). Notably, detection rates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) decreased significantly (both P < 0.05). In contrast, the rate of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) increased from 14.35% to 23.56% (P < 0.05). The proportions of blood cultures and bronchoscopy samples rose from 14.94% to 22.34% and from 3.88% to 8.63%, respectively (both P < 0.05). The MISCP-S intervention model appears to be associated with improvements in specimen submission quality, reductions in overall MDRO detection rates, and enhanced antimicrobial stewardship in psychiatric settings. These findings suggest that the model may offer a replicable framework for similar healthcare institutions.

42918546.title: Recasting antimicrobial resistance surveillance through contemporary analytical frameworks: An integrated analysis using the WHO bacterial priority pathogens list 2024 and AWaRe classification in a tertiary care hospital of Saurashtra, Western India.
42918546.abstract: Indian antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance rarely uses contemporary global frameworks, and Saurashtra is under-represented in the national evidence base. We applied the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List (BPPL) 2024 and the WHO AWaRe (Access-Watch-Reserve) classification to institutional surveillance data, with national and global benchmarking. Cross-sectional analysis of 2195 non-duplicate clinical bacterial isolates (May-October 2024) at a government tertiary care teaching hospital. Susceptibility testing followed CLSI M100-S33 (Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion); multi-drug resistance (MDR) followed Magiorakos criteria. Isolates were assigned to BPPL 2024 tiers by resistant phenotype, and agent-level resistance was grouped by AWaRe 2023 category. MDR correlates were explored by multivariable logistic regression. The isolate was the unit of analysis; proportions describe cultured isolates, not infections or patients. Isolates meeting Critical-priority phenotypes numbered 1192 (54.3% of the isolate pool): third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (n = 1086; 49.5%; ceftriaxone resistance 78% in E. coli and 61% in K. pneumoniae) and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (n = 106; 4.8%). High-priority phenotypes accounted for at most 228 isolates (10.4%). Within the Access group, Enterobacterales resistance was high to ampicillin (89.7% in E. coli) and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid (77-83%) but lower to gentamicin (22-33%); Watch-group fluoroquinolone resistance was 47-73%. Meropenem resistance in E. coli (1%) and K. pneumoniae (7%) was markedly lower than ICMR AMRSN 2023 national estimates (40% and 54%). MDR was present in 58.6% of isolates and was independently associated with ICU admission, age >60 years, tracheal-aspirate specimens, and surgical-department admission. Reading isolate-level surveillance data through the BPPL 2024 and AWaRe frameworks adds a priority- and stewardship-oriented layer to the conventional antibiogram. These proportions describe cultured isolates, not the frequency of resistant infection in patients. The low Enterobacterales carbapenem resistance relative to national benchmarks warrants multi-center, consumption-linked confirmation.

42913057.title: Omadacycline in the treatment of diverse bacterial infections: A retrospective analysis of clinical outcomes and adverse events.
42913057.journal: Journal of infection and public health
42913057.abstract: Omadacycline, a novel aminomethylcycline antibiotic approved for community-acquired bacterial infections, lacks comprehensive real-world evidence regarding its safety and effectiveness. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes and adverse events associated with omadacycline utilization. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of inpatients administered omadacycline at *********************************** between January 2023 and June 2025. Effectiveness was assessed using chi-squared tests and Mann-Whitney U tests, while factors predictive of adverse drug reactions were identified by multivariable logistic regression. Among 717 enrolled patients, treatment success was achieved in 490 (68.3%), including 110 (15.3%) with complete improvement and 380 (53.0%) with partial improvement. Treatment failure, comprising stable disease and deterioration, was observed in 25.1% and 6.6% of patients, respectively. The empirical treatment group had an effectiveness rate of 69.1%. The targeted therapy group had an effectiveness rate of 66.7%. All-cause mortality was 3.3% (n = 24). Of these, 75% (n = 18) died of bacterial infections. The overall microbial clearance rate was 49.7% (338/680). Eradication rates varied across specific bacterial subgroups. The highest clearance rate was observed for Haemophilus influenzae at 63.2%. Ten types of adverse reactions were documented. The most common were transaminase elevation (30.8%; n = 221), hepatic impairment (22.3%; n = 160), nausea/vomiting (5.4%; n = 39), diarrhea (3.9%; n = 28), and rash (2.8%; n = 20). Omadacycline demonstrates clinically acceptable effectiveness against a variety of bacterial infections, including those caused by drug-resistant pathogens. It has therefore become an important clinical option, particularly for critically ill patients, offering new therapeutic approaches. However, given the occurrence of hepatic adverse events, close monitoring of liver function during treatment is recommended. This is especially important for patients with pre-existing liver disease, for whom appropriate drug selection and dose adjustment are critical.

42911179.title: [Integration of beta-lactam therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) into routine clinical practice within an Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP)].
42911179.journal: Revista espanola de quimioterapia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Quimioterapia
42911179.abstract: La monitorización terapéutica de los niveles plasmáticos de antibióticos beta-lactámicos para el ajuste de dosis y la consecución de objetivos farmacocinéticos/farmacodinámicos es una estrategia destinada a optimizar la dosificación en pacientes críticos y en pacientes con características especiales. El objetivo de este estudio es describir la actividad llevada a cabo durante el año 2023 en nuestro hospital, en colaboración con todos los departamentos clínicos implicados: el Servicio de Análisis Clínicos (Farmacocinética y Microbiología), el Servicio de Farmacia y la Unidad Territorial de Infección Nosocomial, en el marco de un Programa de Optimización de Antimicrobianos. Estudio retrospectivo observacional descriptivo sobre la aplicación de la monitorización terapéutica de betalactámicos. Los clínicos solicitan una interconsulta al Servicio de Farmacia para iniciar la monitorización terapéutica de los niveles plasmáticos de betalactámicos. Una vez que el paciente alcanza el estado estacionario, se obtiene una muestra de sangre. Si se realizan ajustes de dosis, se vuelve a medir el nivel plasmático tras 24-48 horas. Todas las determinaciones de niveles plasmáticos realizadas durante 2023 se registraron en una hoja de cálculo Excel, junto con las modificaciones del tratamiento derivadas de los niveles plasmáticos medidos. Se definió un nivel óptimo como una concentración cuatro veces superior a la concentración mínima inhibitoria (CMI) del microorganismo causante sin alcanzar niveles tóxicos. Se realizaron un total de 717 determinaciones en 487 pacientes; el 43,3% ingresaron en la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos, mientras que el resto estaban hospitalizados en otros servicios. Se realizaron ajustes de dosis en el 34,6% de los pacientes críticos, en comparación con el 32,6% en los pacientes no críticos. En el 79.3% de los pacientes con aislamientos microbiológicos, se alcanzó el objetivo terapéutico de mantener concentraciones libres del fármaco por encima de la CMI del patógeno. La monitorización terapéutica de los niveles plasmáticos de betalactámicos podría ser una herramienta útil para la optimización de la dosis y la consecución de los niveles plasmáticos óptimos. Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) of plasma levels of beta-lactam antibiotics for dose adjustment and achievement of pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic targets is a strategy aimed at optimizing dosing in critically ill patients and in patients with special characteristics. The aim of this study is to describe the activity carried out during the year 2023 at our hospital, in collaboration with all the clinical departments involved: the Clinical Analysis Department (Pharmacokinetics and Microbiology), the Pharmacy Department, and the Territorial Nosocomial Infection Unit, within the framework of an Antimicrobial Stewardship Program. This is a retrospective observational descriptive study about the TDM of beta-lactam antibiotics. Clinicians request a consultation with the Pharmacy Department to initiate therapeutic drug monitoring of beta-lactam plasma levels. Once the patient reaches steady-state conditions, a blood sample is collected. If dose adjustments are made, a new plasma level is measured after 24-48 hours. All plasma level determinations performed during 2023 were recorded in an Excel spreadsheet, along with treatment modifications derived from the measured plasma levels. An optimal level was defined as a concentration four times higher than the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of the causative microorganism without reaching toxic levels. A total of 717 determinations were performed in 487 patients; 43.3% were admitted to the Intensive Care Unit, while the remainder were hospitalized in other departments. Dose adjustments were made in 34.6% of critically ill patients, compared to 32.6% among non-critical patients. In 79.3% of patients with microbiological isolates, the therapeutic target of maintaining free drug concentrations above the MIC of the pathogen was achieved. TDM of beta-lactam plasma levels is a useful tool for dose optimization and achievement of therapeutic target.

42909907.title: Molecular epidemiology and resistance mechanisms of carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli in a referral hospital in Lima, Peru.
42909907.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (CR-GNB) represent a significant public health threat, as they are associated with high mortality in healthcare settings. Carbapenemase production is the predominant resistance mechanism, and horizontal gene transfer drives the rapid dissemination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). This study aimed to characterize the phenotypic and genotypic AMR profiles of CR-GNB isolated from patients at Arzobispo Loayza National Hospital (Lima, Peru) between October 2021 and January 2022. We conducted a cross-sectional study and collected clinical and epidemiological data from patients with bacterial infections. MALDI-TOF identified pathogens, and antimicrobial susceptibility was interpreted according to CLSI guidelines. A subset of isolates underwent whole-genome sequencing (Illumina) to determine genomic resistance markers. A total of 159 patients were included (median age = 54 years; 66.7% male); 72.3% had confirmed clinical infections, and 66% were admitted to the ICU. The most frequent infection types were pneumonia, urinary tract infection and bacteraemia. Overall, 97.5% of isolates were classified as XDR. Carbapenem resistance approached 100% (imipenem 99.4%, meropenem 98.7%). Whole-genome data revealed clonal diversity among Klebsiella pneumoniae (ST13/ST15) carrying bla NDM-1; Acinetobacter baumannii uniformly harboured bla OXA-23; and Pseudomonas aeruginosa included high-risk clones ST357 (bla IMP-93) and ST111 (bla IMP-18, bla VIM-2). These findings demonstrate a critical burden of XDR-GNB and the presence of multiple carbapenemases (NDM, IMP, KPC and VIM) associated with clinically relevant high-risk lineages. Strengthening molecular surveillance, optimizing antimicrobial stewardship and reinforcing infection-control measures are urgently needed to contain CR-GNB in critical-care settings in Peru.

42909138.title: Individualized dosing in the precision medicine era: a narrative review.
42909138.abstract: Individualized dosing has become a cornerstone of precision medicine by optimizing therapeutic efficacy while minimizing toxicity through patient-specific dose selection. Traditional approaches, including weight- and body surface area-based dosing, remain fundamental for many medications but are increasingly complemented by pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD)-guided strategies and model-informed precision dosing (MIPD). This narrative review summarizes current evidence on individualized dosing across four major therapeutic classes: antimicrobial agents, chemotherapy, monoclonal antibodies and immunotherapies, and anesthetic and critical care agents. It highlights the rationale, advantages, and limitations of conventional dosing approaches while discussing the growing adoption of fixed dosing for selected biologics with predictable pharmacokinetics. The review also examines practical challenges associated with individualized dosing, including dose calculation complexity, medication errors, and operational constraints. Finally, emerging precision-dosing strategies, particularly Bayesian adaptive dosing and biomarker-guided dosing, are discussed as promising approaches to further personalize pharmacotherapy. Collectively, these advances support a shift toward more precise, evidence-based, and patient-centered medication dosing.

42909073.title: Whole-genome sequence analysis of a clinical hypervirulent Klebsiella variicola strain recovered from a hospital in Ningxia, China.
42909073.abstract: Klebsiella variicola (KV) infections are being increasingly reported across diverse geographic regions and linked to high mortality. KV displays substantial geographical heterogeneity in antimicrobial resistance profiles, virulence phenotypes, and genetic backgrounds; genetic variants further promote its adaptability to varied environments. In this study, we isolated a strain designated KV7 from the sputum sample of an ICU patient at a tertiary hospital in Ningxia, China, with species confirmation achieved via whole-genome sequencing. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the VITEK 2 Compact automated microbial system. String test, immune cell phagocytosis assay, serum resistance assay, and mouse infection model were applied to evaluate virulence phenotypes. Genomic characterization revealed that KV7 belongs to ST8223 with an unassigned KL type and exhibits hypervirulence while remaining susceptible to tested antibiotics. Its hypervirulence is associated with the virulence plasmid pKV7-vir, which carries numerous virulence factor genes. Multiple mobile genetic elements were also detected on pKV7-vir. Moreover, comparative genomic analysis of KV isolates from China and other countries was performed, laying a theoretical foundation for regional surveillance of this pathogen.

42904165.title: Antibiotic resistance and prevalence of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolated from clinical samples.
42904165.abstract: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is an emerging non-fermenting Gram-negative bacillus increasingly implicated in healthcare-associated infections. Its remarkable ability to form biofilms on inert surfaces and invasive medical devices, together with its intrinsic and acquired resistance mechanisms, makes it a major therapeutic challenge in hospital settings. This study aimed to describe the epidemiological characteristics and antimicrobial susceptibility profile of S. maltophilia isolates recovered in our microbiology laboratory. A retrospective study was conducted on clinical isolates of S. maltophilia obtained from various clinical specimens. The bacterial examination was performed according to standard microbiological guidelines Over the study period, the prevalence of S. maltophilia isolates was 0.25% among all bacterial isolates (34 out of 13,959). Respiratory specimens were the most frequent source (23.53%, n=8), followed by blood cultures (17.65%, n=6). Most isolates originated from intensive care units (47.06%, n=16). Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole retained high efficacy with a susceptibility of 81.48%, whereas Minocycline demonstrated the highest activity, with a susceptibility rate of 100%. In contrast, the high resistance rates were observed for ceftazidime (61.90%). S. maltophilia represents an emerging nosocomial pathogen with significant therapeutic implications. Continuous monitoring of local resistance profiles, along with strengthened infection prevention measures and appropriate antibiotic use, is essential to limit the spread of resistant strains.

42892792.title: Risk Factors and Outcomes of Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus faecium Bloodstream Infection in Hematologic Malignancies and Stem Cell Transplant Recipients: A Case-Control Study.
42892792.abstract: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) bloodstream infection (BSI) represents a growing challenge in hematology-oncology settings. This study aimed to characterize the epidemiology, risk factors, and prognostic impact of VREfm BSI within a mixed adult hematology-oncology and transplant unit. We conducted a retrospective matched case-control study (2014-2024). Multivariable conditional logistic regression identified factors associated with VREfm BSI, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models assessed nonlinear exposure-response relationships between antimicrobial classes and VREfm BSI. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards regression. VREfm BSI incidence rose from 0.02 to 0.07 per 1000 person-days (2014-2018 vs 2019-2024). A high-risk composite comprising recipients of allogeneic stem cell transplant and/or AML (adjusted OR [aOR], 3.90; 95% CI, 1.87-8.15; P < .001) and ICU admission (aOR, 5.63; 95% CI, 2.15-14.78; P < .001), were independently associated with VREfm BSI. Cumulative days of carbapenems (aOR, 1.09/day; 95% CI, 1.02-1.17; P = .013), beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitors (aOR, 1.09/day; 95% CI, 1.02-1.16; P = .006), and systemic antifungals (aOR, 1.12/day; 95% CI, 1.03-1.22; P = .009) exhibited duration-dependent associations. RCS models demonstrated a nonlinear, duration-dependent association with cumulative antibiotic exposure, including antianaerobic agents (P < .001). VREfm BSI was associated with increased mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.63-2.66; P < .001). VREfm BSI reflects the interplay between host susceptibility and nonlinear, duration- and spectrum-dependent antibiotic exposure pressure. This underscores the importance of antimicrobial stewardship strategies as a potential intervention to mitigate risk.

42892782.title: Evaluation of the Saudi national prevention model for reduction of central-line-associated bloodstream infections: A single-center qualitative study.
42892782.abstract: Central-line catheterization is a routine but high-risk procedure in intensive care, with central-line-associated bloodstream (CLABSI) infections remaining a major contributor to patient morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and increased healthcare costs. In response to nationally elevated CLABSI rates, the Saudi Ministry of Health introduced the "Go Green" Project and the CLABSI National Prevention Tool in 2022 to standardize and strengthen prevention practices. To evaluate the national prevention model in a tertiary adult intensive care unit. We conducted semi-structured interviews, direct observations, and document reviews with 29 stakeholders, including nurses, physicians, infection-prevention specialists, and administrators. The study identified two major themes. The first one, "A practical strategy requires both professional human resources and sufficient medical supplies," comprised four codes: staffing, workload overload, competency, and medical supplies. The second theme, "An administrative strategy requires both awareness and behavioral attitudes," was represented by four codes: "Go Green," education and training, hands-off practices, and teamwork. While participants generally demonstrated strong foundational knowledge of CLABSI prevention, gaps remained among a minority. Key barriers included nursing workforce shortages, inconsistent supply availability, and variable competency in ultrasound-guided catheter insertion. Stakeholders emphasized the need for continuous training, improved supply-chain reliability, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration, alongside a sustained cultural commitment to infection-prevention practices. Although the institution achieved national recognition for CLABSI reduction in 2022, long-term success will depend on maintaining adherence to best practices, addressing operational constraints, and ensuring ongoing competency development to meet future performance targets.

42891256.title: Multipathogen antimicrobial resistance in a Romanian tertiary-care hospital: a retrospective antibiogram analysis, January-July 2025.
42891256.abstract: Routine microbiology data can show not only isolated resistance events but also the wider hospital ecology in which antimicrobial resistance (AMR) emerges. We analyzed the complete January-July 2025 antibiogram export from a Romanian tertiary-care hospital, along with a targeted extended-testing file. The scope was deliberately broader than a single-organism carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae analysis. We performed a retrospective descriptive analysis using 3,270 antibiogram records from 3,012 patient identifiers. Organisms, sample types, resistance labels, and extended-test results were extracted from laboratory text fields. Organism occurrences within polymicrobial reports were counted separately to describe the full pathogen spectrum. The dataset contained 4,039 organism occurrences. Enterobacterales were the largest group, followed by Gram-positive cocci, non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli, and yeasts. Escherichia coli and K. pneumoniae were the most frequent Enterobacterales, and clinically relevant resistant organisms were also identified among Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacter cloacae complex, Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Enterococcus faecium and Candida species. The extended-testing file contained 100 organism occurrences from 85 patient identifiers, mainly extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative isolates. Cefiderocol testing corresponded predominantly to K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii complex, whereas aztreonam/avibactam was concentrated mainly in extensively drug-resistant Enterobacterales, especially K. pneumoniae. The data support a multipathogen AMR interpretation: carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, non-fermenters, resistant Gram-positive cocci and yeasts coexist in the same hospital ecology. Empirical therapy, infection-control actions and stewardship decisions should be guided by syndrome, sample source, prior colonization and local species-level resistance patterns.

42966286.title: Fungal biofilm-associated infections in immunocompromised African populations: A narrative review of Candidozyma auris emergence, antifungal resistance mechanisms, and laboratory detection algorithms.
42966286.abstract: Candidozyma auris the abbreviation C. auris is retained throughout has become one of the most concerning hospital-acquired fungal infections over the past decade, colonizing the environment and skin for extended periods, exhibiting multidrug resistance, and forming biofilms that are resistant to both the host immune response and antifungal treatments. Sub-Saharan and North African medical institutions have a unique set of risks: a significant HIV-positive population, widespread malnutrition, high rates of tuberculosis co-infection, the appearance of critical care units, and diagnostic laboratories that often lack the tools to accurately identify emerging yeast species. This paper aims to analyze the current understanding of the emergence and prevalence of C. auris infections in African healthcare facilities, discuss the properties of biofilm formed by this yeast that facilitate its persistence and resistance to treatment, examine the features of immunosuppressed African patients who are at the highest risk of C. auris colonization and infection, and identify the available laboratory tests that can be used to diagnose this fungus in African hospitals. A narrative review has been performed to gather the evidence on the emergence of C. auris in African healthcare facilities and describe the general trends in its clinical presentation. The data were retrieved from reports and research articles published in peer-reviewed journals, utilizing resources such as national and multinational surveillance records, World Health Organization documents, and scientific publications from regional reference labs that investigate the clinical characteristics and treatment of C. auris infections and report on the local epidemiology of this yeast. Four principal findings emerge. First, documented African activity is concentrated in South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria and Egypt and is dominated by clade III and clade I, but the apparent continental increase conflates genuine transmission with rapidly improving detection capacity and should not be read as an incidence estimate. Second, fluconazole resistance is consistently high across African series (of the order of 85-90%), amphotericin B resistance is elevated relative to global pooled estimates (approximately 15-35%, highest in the clade III-dominated South African series), whereas echinocandin resistance remains below 5% but is no longer negligible. Third, biofilm growth confers a reversible, largely non-genetic tolerance matrix-mediated drug sequestration, biofilm-induced efflux upregulation and persister-cell dormancy that raises effective inhibitory concentrations by one to more than two orders of magnitude above planktonic values, so routine susceptibility reports systematically understate the drug exposure required in device-associated infection. Fourth, the dominant diagnostic constraint across the continent is not the absence of technology as such but systematic misidentification by the conventional biochemical panels that remain the mainstay of African yeast identification; this is addressable through a tiered algorithm anchored on a low threshold of suspicion rather than on universal access to mass spectrometry or sequencing. We conclude that C. auris preparedness in Africa is best pursued not as a vertical, pathogen-specific programme but as an explicit extension of the antimicrobial resistance surveillance, laboratory strengthening and infection prevention frameworks already under construction across the region, with tiered diagnostics, antifungal stewardship, biofilm-aware clinical management and the systematic evaluation of natural product-derived adjunctive agents as the immediate priorities.

42964229.title: Case report: When encephalitis is not an infection: two cases of autoimmune GFAP astrocytopathy mimicking infectious encephalitis.
42964229.abstract: Autoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) astrocytopathy is a rare autoimmune inflammatory disease of the central nervous system that frequently mimics infectious meningoencephalitis. Because its clinical presentation, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings, and inflammatory markers often resemble central nervous system infection, diagnosis may be delayed, postponing appropriate immunotherapy. We describe two women with markedly different clinical presentations of GFAP astrocytopathy who were initially managed as suspected infectious meningoencephalitis. Both patients presented with inflammatory CSF findings, negative extensive microbiological investigations, and initial empirical antimicrobial treatment. In the first case, persistent aseptic meningitis with recurrent symptoms prompted autoimmune testing after repeated negative infectious work-up. In the second case, rapidly progressive encephalopathy requiring intensive care initially suggested severe infectious meningoencephalitis. In both patients, neuronal surface and paraneoplastic antibody testing was negative, whereas indirect immunofluorescence detected GFAP-IgG, supporting the diagnosis in the context of the clinical, CSF, neuroimaging, and microbiological findings. Both patients subsequently received corticosteroid treatment and experienced clinical improvement, although residual neurological symptoms persisted in the first patient. These cases highlight the broad clinical spectrum of GFAP astrocytopathy and its potential to closely mimic infectious central nervous system disease. Earlier recognition of GFAP astrocytopathy may facilitate timely consideration of immunotherapy and help reduce diagnostic delay and unnecessary antimicrobial exposure in patients with inflammatory meningoencephalitic presentations and negative infectious investigations.

42961035.title: Performance of mCIM/eCIM in Enterobacterales strains co-encoding NDM and OXA-48-like carbapenemases from South India.
42961035.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) are an increasing public health concern, particularly as carbapenemase-producing isolates, such as NDM and OXA-48-like producers, become more prevalent. Rapid and accurate identification of carbapenemases is crucial to guide appropriate antibiotic therapy. Although recent epidemiologic data show that CRE increasingly harbor multiple carbapenemases, the performance of common phenotypic tests-the modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) and EDTA-modified CIM (eCIM)-has not been well defined in these isolates. We examined the performance of mCIM and eCIM among CRE-encoding NDM, OXA-48-like, or both. We included 172 genotypically confirmed carbapenemase-encoding CRE isolates from perirectal swabs collected from patients admitted to two intensive care units at a hospital in South India. Isolates included Escherichia coli (53.5%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (41.3%), and Enterobacter species (5.3%). Overall, 112 isolates (65.1%) encoded NDM alone, 23 (13.4%) encoded OXA-48-like alone, and 37 (21.5%) encoded both NDM and OXA-48-like. mCIM positivity was 98.2% for NDM, 47.8% for OXA-48-like, and 94.6% for NDM+OXA-48-like encoders; among mCIM-positive isolates, eCIM positivity rates were 99.1%, 91%, and 97.1%, respectively. When compared to molecular carbapenemase gene detection, mCIM/eCIM was highly sensitive for classifying isolates encoding NDM as metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) producers, but significantly misclassified isolates encoding OXA-48-like as having an MBL or lacking a carbapenemase. In the largest collection of NDM and OXA-48-like co-encoding CRE isolates to date, mCIM/eCIM typically reported these as MBL producers. Carbapenemase-encoding Enterobacterales infections are associated with substantial adverse health outcomes, making rapid and accurate carbapenemase detection essential for guiding antibiotic therapy. Although Enterobacterales carrying multiple carbapenemases are increasingly reported worldwide, the performance of common phenotypic assays, mCIM and eCIM, remains insufficiently defined for these strains. In this study of 172 genotypically confirmed carbapenemase-encoding Enterobacterales isolates from hospitalized patients in South India, mCIM/eCIM consistently classified NDM-encoding isolates as metallo-β-lactamase encoders. Additionally, mCIM/eCIM frequently misclassified OXA-48-like-encoding isolates as either metallo-β-lactamase encoders or carbapenemase-negative, highlighting the need to better understand the mechanisms underlying this variable activity. In the largest collection of NDM and OXA co-encoding Enterobacterales isolates reported to date, mCIM/eCIM generally reported co-encoding isolates as metallo-β-lactamase producers. Our results suggest that mCIM/eCIM performance may vary geographically due to variable activity, distribution, and combinations of carbapenemases.

42959813.title: Spatiotemporal trajectories of antimicrobial resistance in bloodstream infections in China: a nationwide longitudinal surveillance study from 2014 to 2023.
42959813.journal: The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific
authors: Blood Bacterial Resistant Investigation Collaborative System (BRICS) Study Group
42959813.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) impose a substantial global burden, increasingly complicated by antimicrobial resistance (AMR). We aimed to characterise decade-long trends in BSI pathogens and major resistance phenotypes across mainland China. We analysed BSI surveillance data from 72 hospitals across 22 provinces in the Bacterial Resistant Investigation Collaborative System (BRICS) between 2014 and 2023. Isolates were transferred to a central reference laboratory for species identification and standardised antimicrobial susceptibility testing, with raw minimum inhibitory concentration values retrospectively reinterpreted using 2025 CLSI guidelines. Fourteen continuously participating hospitals formed a sentinel cohort. Among 76,211 non-duplicate BSI isolates, Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae predominated, with K. pneumoniae increasing by 0.91 percentage points annually (95% CI 0.59-1.23; p < 0.001). Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing E. coli decreased from 61.5% to 47.4%, MRSA from 39.0% to 26.2%, and ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae from 30.5% to 21.5% (all p < 0.001). Conversely, carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae increased from 7.0% to 14.9%, peaking at 22.5% in 2018, with marked spatial heterogeneity. CRAB remained persistently high (55.2-64.3%). Resistance proportions were higher in intensive care units, older patients and male patients for several phenotypes. Major resistance phenotypes declined during a decade of nationwide antimicrobial stewardship, while the contribution of K. pneumoniae to BSIs increased and carbapenem resistance remained a major challenge. Future AMR strategies should integrate antimicrobial stewardship with targeted infection prevention, outbreak control, and genomic surveillance. This study was supported by Prevention and Control of Emerging and Major Infectious Diseases-National Science and technology Major Project (2025ZD01903301), National Key R&D Program of China (2024YFC2311304) and Research Project of Jinan Microecological Biomedicine Shandong Laboratory (JNL-2025004B).

42878771.title: Toward very early vasopressin use in septic shock: observational data accumulate but trial evidence still lacking.

42873095.title: Irisin is associated with survival in sepsis and attenuates macrophage pro-inflammatory responses with involvement of AMPK signaling.
42873095.abstract: Sepsis is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, yet effective targeted therapies remain limited. We evaluated the prognostic significance of irisin, a myokine, in sepsis cohort and examined its immunomodulatory effects on macrophages using a translational approach. Patients were enrolled in a prospectively collected sepsis registry and biobank. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was conducted to assess independent association between irisin and 30-day mortality. Mechanistic studies used macrophages ex vivo and a murine cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model. Higher serum irisin was independently associated with lower 30-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.955, 95% confidence interval 0.913-0.999, p=0.044) in patients with sepsis (N=655). Irisin showed modest discrimination for 30-day mortality (AUROC 0.609), with no statistically significant difference from lactate (AUROC 0.652; p=0.145). In vitro , irisin suppressed LPS-induced pro-inflammatory cytokine production, preserved AMPK phosphorylation, attenuated IκBα degradation, and reduced pro-inflammatory markers in macrophages. Several of these cellular effects were attenuated following AMPKα1 depletion. In vivo , irisin improved 7-day survival after CLP (75% vs. 36%, p<0.05) and reduced systemic inflammatory cytokines at 24 hours. Higher serum irisin was independently associated with lower 30-day mortality in patients with sepsis, although its standalone discriminatory performance was modest. Experimental findings further showed that irisin improved survival and attenuated macrophage inflammatory responses, with AMPK signaling contributing to several cellular effects. These findings support further evaluation of irisin as part of integrated prognostic assessment and investigation of irisin-related signaling in sepsis.

42870302.title: Proteomic identification of resistin as a NET-associated neutrophil activity marker in sepsis.
42870302.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contribute to organ dysfunction in sepsis, yet clinically accessible biomarkers reflecting NET-associated pathology remain limited. We sought to identify circulating proteins associated with NET formation and evaluate their clinical relevance in sepsis. Unbiased proteomic profiling of stimulated human neutrophil supernatants and serum from murine sepsis was performed to identify proteins released during NET formation and elevated in vivo. Candidate biomarkers were selected through integration of these datasets and filtering based on cell type-specific expression profiles, followed by validation in patients with sepsis and healthy controls. Integrative analysis identified five candidate circulating markers associated with NET formation in sepsis: cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide, lactotransferrin, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), resistin, and histone H4. Among these, resistin, a recently recognized neutrophil-associated protein, and NGAL demonstrated the strongest associations with sepsis-associated complications. Both markers were elevated in patients with sepsis and correlated with circulating cell-free DNA levels. In receiver operating characteristic curve analyses, resistin discriminated multiple organ failure (AUC, 0.83) and disseminated intravascular coagulation (AUC, 0.81), whereas NGAL demonstrated similarly robust performance (AUC, 0.84 and 0.79, respectively). Both markers outperformed conventional clinical parameters for discriminating sepsis-associated complications. These findings identify resistin as a circulating marker associated with NET formation that captures key features of sepsis-associated immunothrombosis and organ failure and may improve assessment of disease severity and risk stratification.

42870277.title: Early versus deferred intravenous calcium in patients with sepsis and ionized hypocalcemia: a target-trial emulation.
42870277.abstract: Intravenous calcium is frequently administered during sepsis, yet whether early treatment improves 24-h hemodynamic recovery remains uncertain. We compared 24-h hemodynamic recovery between calcium initiation within 2 h of a non-emergency low-ionized calcium (iCa) result and no calcium initiation during the first 6 h after the result. We conducted a retrospective target-trial emulation of 2016-2025 high-resolution electronic health records from Zigong Fourth People's Hospital. Adults with sepsis, final or corrected iCa of 0.90-1.10 mmol/L, and no emergency indication were eligible at result availability. Strategies were executed calcium within 2 h versus no calcium through 6 h; care after 6 h was unrestricted. Clone-censor weighting and overlap tilting addressed grace periods, measured time-varying confounding, and clinical equipoise. The primary outcome was being alive and vasopressor-free at 24 h. Estimates and two-sided 95% percentile intervals came from 2,000 patient-level bootstrap samples with model refitting. Of 5,993 patients, 1,538 initiated calcium within 2 h, 147 initiated at 2-6 h, and 4,308 received none through 6 h; none of the latter initiated calcium during 6-24 h. The standardized probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery was 69.9% with early calcium and 61.1% with deferral, corresponding to a risk difference of + 8.69 percentage points (95% percentile interval, + 4.66 to + 12.84) and a risk ratio of 1.142 (1.074-1.214). The estimated association varied with baseline norepinephrine-equivalent dose (Holm-adjusted P = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶), whereas the iCa interaction did not remain statistically supported after adjustment (P = 0.097). Early calcium was associated with a 1.29-percentage-point higher observed risk of hypercalcemia (95% percentile interval, + 0.64 to + 2.05). Intervals for severe arrhythmia, new renal replacement therapy, and hospital mortality included the null. Early intravenous calcium was associated with a higher probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery than the deferred strategy, whose observed pathway involved no calcium through 24 h. Estimated effects were larger at higher vasopressor doses. Early calcium was associated with a modestly higher observed risk of hypercalcemia. These findings support randomized evaluation in vasopressor-treated patients. Baseline iCa modification remains exploratory.

42867561.title: Bioactive adrenomedullin dynamics and microcirculatory changes in a porcine model of hemorrhagic shock.
42867561.abstract: Hemorrhagic shock is a leading cause of preventable trauma death, marked by impaired oxygen delivery and endothelial dysfunction. Bioactive adrenomedullin (bio-ADM) regulates endothelial barrier integrity, but its dynamics during hemorrhagic shock and resuscitation remain unclear. This secondary analysis of a porcine hemorrhagic shock model investigated bio-ADM and its association with macro- and microcirculatory parameters during resuscitation. All animals received crystalloid infusion (10 mL/kg/h) from anesthesia induction onward. Shock was induced by blood withdrawal to maintain MAP at 40 ± 5 mmHg for 60 min (T5), before randomization to control (n = 7), fluid (n = 6), or noradrenaline (n = 7) groups, with intervention groups titrated to MAP targets of 65 then 90 mmHg (60 min each). Macrocirculation was assessed via vital signs and pulse contour analysis; microcirculation via hyperspectral imaging (tissue oxygenation, hemoglobin, water index). Fluid resuscitation improved macrohemodynamics and microcirculatory oxygenation versus control and noradrenaline, which failed to sustain perfusion and impaired microcirculatory oxygenation. Bio-ADM increased after shock induction (p < 0.001), peaking at T9 (120 min of therapy). At T5, levels were comparable among control (16.8 [13.6-18.9] pg/ml), fluid (15.65 [15.43-16.55] pg/ml), and noradrenaline (14.3 [7.85-18.95] pg/ml). Thereafter, bio-ADM continued to rise in control (19.7 [17.4-32.6] pg/ml) and noradrenaline (21.2 [14.4-33.45] pg/ml), while stabilizing in the fluid group (12.05 [10.65-15.18] pg/ml); accordingly, the T5-T9 increase was smaller in the fluid group than in control (p = 0.022) or noradrenaline (p = 0.003). The fluid group received ~3-fold more fluid by T9. Higher bio-ADM correlated with lower MAP, higher lactate, and lower ScvO₂, but not oxygen delivery (DO₂); a higher tissue water index correlated with a smaller rise. Bio-ADM increased during hemorrhagic shock, extending previous observations from cardiogenic and septic shock, and represents a comparatively non-specific marker of endothelial and microcirculatory stress rather than specific to any single shock etiology. Effective resuscitation was associated with stabilization, rather than a clear decrease, of bio-ADM levels, though this coincided with higher fluid administration, and dilution cannot be excluded. Whether bio-ADM offers therapeutic utility to guide resuscitation remains unclear, warranting further prospective evaluation in animal and human studies.

42859281.title: Effect of vasopressin and its analogues on microcirculatory perfusion: a systematic review.
42859281.abstract: Arginine vasopressin (AVP) is a non-adrenergic vasopressor increasingly used in the management of shock. While it restores arterial pressure, its effects on the microcirculation remain uncertain, with potential for reduced regional perfusion and tissue oxygenation. The aim of this systematic review is to evaluate the effects of intravenous AVP and its analogues on microcirculatory perfusion across different haemodynamic conditions and vascular beds. A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Web of Science was conducted. Animal and human publications evaluating the effects of intravenous AVP or analogues on microcirculatory perfusion assessed with in vivo microcirculatory imaging or flowmetry techniques were included. Publications were grouped by haemodynamic condition and vascular bed. Of 1693 records, 39 publications (31 animal, 7 human, 1 combined) were included, comprising 43 study-units and 152 individual measurements. Overall perfusion was decreased in 33%, unchanged in 48%, and increased in 19% of measurements, compared with baseline, saline, or other vasopressors. By haemodynamic condition, perfusion was decreased/unchanged/increased (n=study-units; % of measurements) in physiological conditions (n = 14: 57/38/4), vasodilatory or septic shock (n = 23: 24/55/21; versus baseline, fluid resuscitation or noradrenaline), haemorrhagic shock (n = 3: 17/17/67; versus baseline, saline or noradrenaline), cardiac dysfunction or arrest (n = 2: 0/67/33; versus adrenaline or noradrenaline) and cirrhosis-related portal hypertension (n = 1: 0/0/100). Across vascular beds: gastrointestinal tract (n = 18: 30/42/27), kidney (n = 9: medulla 77/23/0, cortex 27/64/9), sublingual bed (n = 7: 19/68/13), cerebral cortex (n = 2: 0/67/33), cutaneous bed (n = 6: 42/42/17), and conjunctiva (n = 1, 100/0/0). AVP and its analogues reduced microcirculatory perfusion most consistently under physiological conditions, whereas effects in vasodilatory or septic shock were more heterogeneous. Across vascular beds, the highest proportion of measurements showing reduced perfusion was in the renal medulla. These results highlight the divergent effects of vasopressin across vascular beds and clinical conditions.

42849299.title: Long-term injectable non-insulin antidiabetic drug use and in-hospital mortality in sepsis: A nationwide analysis of the 2023 National Inpatient Sample.
42849299.abstract: Injectable non-insulin antidiabetic agents have hypothesized antiinflammatory effects in sepsis, but no nationally representative US inpatient analysis has examined their association with in-hospital outcomes. Cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 National Inpatient Sample. Adults with any-listed sepsis and diabetes were included; exposure was documented long-term injectable non-insulin antidiabetic use (ICD-10-CM Z79.85). Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality across three pre-specified comparators. Among 241,808 hospitalizations, 5238 (2.2%) carried Z79.85. Adjusted odds of death were 0.53 (95% CI, 0.45-0.63) versus the full cohort, 0.73 (0.61-0.87) therapy-matched, and 0.77 (0.64-0.93) versus oral therapy alone. The E-value was 1.61. Exposure was associated with lower in-hospital mortality, attenuating under stricter comparators. Findings are hypothesis-generating and subject to residual confounding.

42839288.title: Polymyxin B hemoadsorption in endotoxic septic shock: ten questions on the Tigris trial.
42839288.abstract: The Tigris trial recently reported that polymyxin B hemoadsorption (PMX) achieved a high posterior probability of benefit for mortality in adults with endotoxic septic shock (endotoxemia with multiple organ failure). The trial used a Bayesian framework with a prior derived from a subgroup of an earlier trial (EUPHRATES) and this subgroup was used to design eligibility criteria for Tigris. Ten questions that expose the trial's strengths and limitations are answered in this review. Writing as the trial investigators, our intention is to make the reasoning behind these decisions explicit, so that clinicians and trialists can judge what Tigris does, and does not, demonstrate.

42839239.title: Beyond macrocirculatory targets: a multimodal framework for microcirculatory and organ perfusion monitoring in sepsis.
42839239.abstract: Microcirculatory dysfunction may persist despite restoration of conventional macrocirculatory targets in sepsis, reflecting loss of hemodynamic coherence. This review synthesizes current microcirculatory monitoring approaches according to the physiological information they provide and examines how complementary modalities may be integrated to characterize persistent or regional tissue hypoperfusion. A narrative review of PubMed-indexed literature was conducted, with emphasis on bedside peripheral perfusion assessment, tissue oxygenation and superficial perfusion imaging, direct microvascular visualization, and organ- or tissue-specific monitoring. Recent studies were prioritized together with landmark methodological and validation studies. Available techniques interrogate distinct but overlapping components of the circulation. Bedside peripheral measures provide rapid information on skin reperfusion and vascular tone; spectroscopic and optical techniques characterize tissue oxygenation, reactivity, and spatial perfusion heterogeneity; direct microvascular imaging enables assessment of microvascular density and flow; and organ-specific approaches provide information on renal, cerebral, or retinal perfusion and oxygenation. Discordance between these domains may persist despite improvement in blood pressure or cardiac output, supporting serial multimodal rather than single-variable interpretation. However, substantial heterogeneity in acquisition protocols, measurement sites, devices, analytical methods, and proposed thresholds limits comparability and clinical implementation. Microcirculatory monitoring should currently be viewed as a complementary framework for identifying persistent or heterogeneous tissue hypoperfusion beyond conventional macrocirculatory targets. Its integration into individualized resuscitation remains promising but requires standardized methodology, external validation, and prospective interventional evidence before any single modality or multimodal strategy can be adopted as a validated resuscitation endpoint.

42839201.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Hemopexin as a Sepsis-Specific Signal After Intracerebral Hemorrhage.

42839198.title: Response to the Letter to the Editor Entitled "Cerebrospinal Fluid Hemopexin as a Sepsis-Specific Signal After Intracerebral Hemorrhage" Regarding the Study "Cerebrospinal Fluid Hemopexin as a Candidate Biomarker for Secondary Sepsis and In-hospital Outcome After Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage: An Exploratory Translational Proteomics Study".

42837137.title: Integrating Hemodynamic Indices Into the Definition of Refractory Septic Shock: Is There a Role for Catecholamine Refractoriness and Assistance Guide Based on Cardiogenic Shock Hemodynamics (CRASH) Index?

42837136.title: New Criteria for Refractory Septic Shock: Relying on Treatment to Define a Disease.

42831066.title: High blood pressure-targeted management associated with reduced benefits of higher body mass index in elderly patients with septic shock: a post hoc analysis of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
42831066.abstract: Body mass index (BMI) is an important prognostic factor in sepsis, and an obesity paradox has been reported. A higher mean arterial pressure (MAP) target has been associated with worse outcomes in elderly patients with septic shock. However, whether MAP target strategy alters the association between BMI and outcomes in this population is unknown. We conducted a post hoc analysis of the OPTPRESS trial, a multicenter randomized controlled trial at 29 Japanese centers reporting worse outcomes with a high MAP target in elderly patients with septic shock. A total of 489 patients aged ≥65 years with septic shock were assigned to a control MAP target of 65-70 mmHg (n = 245) or high target of 80-85 mmHg (n = 244). Patients were categorized using Asian BMI cutoffs into underweight (<18.5 kg/m2), normal-weight (18.5-22.9 kg/m2), and higher-BMI (≥23 kg/m2) categories. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. The primary analysis assessed the interaction between BMI category and MAP target strategy. In the control group, mortality decreased across increasing BMI categories (P = 0.03 for the trend), while no trend was observed in the high-target group (P = 0.26 for the trend). After adjustment for age, sex, APACHE II score, Clinical Frailty Scale, and site of infection, MAP target strategy significantly interacted with the higher-BMI category (P = 0.02), but not with underweight (P = 0.41). In the high-target group, both underweight and higher-BMI patients had higher mortality than those with normal BMI (underweight, adjusted HR 1.74 [95% CI 1.02-2.98], P = 0.04; higher BMI, adjusted HR 1.72 [95% CI 1.02-2.87], P = 0.04). Fluid volume per body weight decreased across increasing BMI categories in both groups. The proportion of patients receiving vasopressin increased across BMI categories only in the control group, whereas the body weight-adjusted vasopressin dose among recipients showed no significant trend in either group. In elderly patients with septic shock, mortality decreased across increasing BMI categories under a standard MAP target, whereas patients in the higher-BMI category had higher mortality under a high MAP target. High MAP targets may attenuate the survival benefit of higher BMI, possibly in association with BMI-related patterns in fluid and vasopressor management. Not registered. The original OPTPRESS trial was registered at UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000041775) on 13 September 2020.

42827248.title: Targeting capillary leak in experimental sepsis and endotoxemia: a systematic review of therapeutic agents, methods and models in animal studies.
42827248.abstract: Sepsis-induced capillary leak is a major contributor to circulatory dysfunction and tissue edema, yet remains therapeutically unaddressed: numerous interventions showing promise in preclinical models have failed to demonstrate clinical efficacy. This systematic review aimed to characterise preclinical studies evaluating therapeutic interventions specifically targeting capillary leak and to identify candidates with the highest potential for clinical translation. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science identified in vivo studies in experimental sepsis and endotoxemia evaluating interventions targeting capillary leak. Data on animal models, sepsis induction methods, capillary leak assessment, therapeutic targets, and intervention timing were extracted. Risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE tool. As a complementary step, all retained interventions were cross-referenced against randomized or prospective clinical studies in sepsis published since January 2015 and appraised using a four-criterion translational quality score (reproducibility, quality of the model, clinically relevant timing, and multimodal read-out). Three hundred and three preclinical studies were included, exhibiting substantial heterogeneity in both models and outcomes. Rodent models predominated (81.2%), and lipopolysaccharide-induced endotoxemia was the most common induction method (59.7%). Dye-based assays constituted the most frequent capillary leak read-out in rodents (81.7%), whereas fluid balance and lymph-to-plasma ratios predominated in large-animal studies. The lung was the most frequently evaluated organ. Endothelial activation (12.2%), intercellular junctions (11.2%), and the nitric oxide pathway (8.9%) were the most targeted pathways. A beneficial effect of the intervention on at least one capillary leak outcome results was reported in 93.1% of studies, raising substantial concerns regarding publication bias. Of 232 distinct interventions, only a minority had been evaluated in randomized clinical trials since 2015, and no capillary leak-specific therapy has yet reached high translational priority. Preclinical research on sepsis-induced capillary leak is characterized by methodological heterogeneity, a disproportionately high rate of studies reporting capillary leak reduction, and an overreliance on endotoxemia models. Bridging the translational gap will require standardized assessment of capillary leak, broader use of live-pathogen large-animal models, post-treatment dosing paradigms, and clinical trials enriched for endothelial dysfunction. International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) number CRD42024522372.

42955503.title: Adjunctive therapeutic plasma exchange as rescue therapy in septic shock due to streptococcal infection: a multicentric retrospective cohort study.
42955503.abstract: Septic shock due to streptococcal infection (SRSS) carries a high mortality and is in part driven by toxin-mediated inflammation. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) may modulate the septic host responses by removing injurious mediators while replenishing protective plasma factors, but data specific to SRSS is lacking. We performed a retrospective, multicenter, cohort study of adults with SRSS between 2012-2024. Patients from three tertiary care ECMO centers in Germany and Switzerland were included requiring (i) streptococcal spp. detected in blood or primary focus and (ii) septic shock according to sepsis-3 definition. Adjunctive TPE with fresh frozen plasma at the intensivists` discretion was compared with standard of care (SOC). The primary outcome was 90-day-hospital mortality. Key exploratory outcomes included 24-h kinetics of vasoactive-inotropic score(VIS) and lactate, as well as SRSS-related complications. Results were validated in a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort. Of 149 patients, 31 (20.8%) received TPE and 118 (79.2%) SOC. TPE patients were more severely ill at baseline: SOFA 14 (IQR 13.5-15) vs 11 (IQR 8-14) (p<0.001); lactate 6.4 vs 2.8 mmol/L (p<0.001); Vasoactive-Inotropic-Score (VIS) 70.7 vs 23.3 (p<0.001); more frequent invasive ventilation (87% vs 65%), VV-ECMO (36% vs 19%), and renal replacement therapy (96.8% vs 52.5%). Overall, 90-day hospital mortality was 27.5% (TPE 29.0%, SOC 27.1%). Following SOFA-score adjustment, TPE was associated with lower mortality risk (aHR 0.67 [95% CI 0.5-0.9]; p=0.009). This was validated in the PSM cohort, with an aHR for TPE of 0.44 (95% CI 0.3-0.8); p=0.002. Mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant VIS reduction only with TPE (fixed effect 24-h change, p=0.027) and improved lactate decrease versus SOC. In SRSS, adjunctive TPE was associated with rapid hemodynamic stabilization and improved lactate kinetics. Exploratory adjusted survival analyses support prospective evaluation of TPE in SRSS.

42955163.title: Quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly reveals a non-linear association with 30-day mortality in sepsis: a proof-of-concept pilot study.
42955163.abstract: Direct, cell-resolved quantification of NLRP3 inflammasome activation in clinical patients has not been feasible. Previous studies have relied on indirect surrogates such as downstream cytokines, which are influenced by inflammasome-independent pathways and systemic clearance kinetics, potentially explaining the inconsistent prognostic findings reported in the literature. We applied a proximity ligation assay (PLA) to directly visualise NLRP3-caspase-1 complex formation in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of septic patients, providing a cell-specific, in situ readout of inflammasome assembly at the single-cell level. In this prospective, multicentre proof-of-concept pilot study, 78 patients fulfilling Sepsis-3 criteria were enrolled across three university hospitals. The PLA was validated in THP-1-derived macrophages against established readouts of canonical inflammasome activation prior to clinical application. Patients were stratified into low (n = 28), intermediate (n = 23), and high (n = 27) NLRP3 inflammasome activity groups. Median age was 64 years (IQR: 56-78), 63% were male, and median Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score was 8 (IQR: 4-12). Baseline characteristics, disease severity scores, and routine inflammatory biomarkers did not differ across activity groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed a non-linear pattern of 30-day survival, with the most favourable outcomes in the intermediate activity group. Both low and high activity were associated with increased mortality (log-rank p = 0.003). In adjusted Cox regression, low inflammasome activity (HR 7.88, 95% CI 1.79-34.65; p = 0.006) and high inflammasome activity (HR 4.35, 95% CI 1.01-19.88; p = 0.048) remained associated with 30-day mortality. Modelling PLA activity as a continuous variable using restricted cubic splines confirmed a significant non-linear association with 30-day mortality, independent of the tertile-based categorisation (p for non-linearity = 0.015). This proof-of-concept pilot study demonstrates that direct in situ quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly is feasible in septic patients and reveals a non-linear association with 30-day survival. These findings indicate that PLA-based profiling captures immune heterogeneity beyond routine inflammatory biomarkers. Larger independent cohorts are needed to validate these findings before clinical application or patient stratification can be considered.

42951887.title: Candida Septic Shock: If Every Hour Matters, Who Requires Empiric Therapy?

42945000.title: Serial bedside retinal optical coherence tomography angiography in sepsis associated circulatory dysfunction.

42934779.title: Heterogeneous cardiovascular responses to acute mean arterial pressure augmentation in septic shock: the role of ventriculo-arterial coupling and venous return.
42934779.abstract: In patients with septic shock, vasopressor-induced mean arterial pressure (MAP) augmentation is commonly used to restore tissue perfusion; however, patients may exhibit divergent cardiovascular responses despite achieving similar arterial pressure targets. We hypothesized that this heterogeneity reflects the differences in ventricular adaptation to increases in arterial load and venous return determinants. We conducted a prospective physiological observational study in mechanically ventilated adults with septic shock who underwent transient MAP augmentation from approximately 65 to 85 mmHg after the initial hemodynamic resuscitation. MAP was increased by norepinephrine dose escalation or by adding vasopressin according to clinical judgment. Comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography was performed immediately before and after MAP augmentation. Patients were classified a priori according to the relative changes in cardiac output (CO): flow recruitment (> 15% increase), stable flow (- 15% to + 15%), or flow deterioration (> 15% decrease). Changes in effective arterial elastance (Ea), end-systolic elastance (Ees), VA coupling (Ea/Ees), stroke volume, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), analogue mean systemic filling pressure (Pmsa), and derived venous return variables were analyzed. Thirty-two patients were included. Despite comparable increases in MAP, the cardiovascular responses were heterogeneous: 10 patients (31%) exhibited flow recruitment, 17 (53%) maintained a stable flow, and 5 (16%) developed flow deterioration. Patients with flow deterioration showed a greater increase in Ea without a proportional increase in Ees, resulting in worsening VA coupling (ΔEa/Ees + 0.22 IQR [0.01-0.81]), whereas VA coupling remained stable or improved in patients with preserved or increased flow (p = 0.035). Flow deterioration was also associated with reduced LVEF and changes in the derived venous return indices, which may have contributed to the observed reduction in forward flow. Changes in VA coupling correlated with changes in IVCT (ρ = 0.788, p < 0.0001), MPI (ρ = 0.599, p < 0.0003), stroke volume (ρ =-0.418, p = 0.017), and LVEF (ρ=-0.431, p = 0.0139). Acute MAP augmentation elicits heterogeneous cardiovascular responses in patients with septic shock despite similar increases in arterial pressure. Flow deterioration is characterized by worsening VA coupling, reduced stroke volume, and impaired systolic adaptation, potentially modulated by changes in the derived venous return indices.

42927702.title: Embracing uncertainty in refractory septic shock.

42925135.title: Role of Mitochondrial Impairment in Sepsis-Induced Platelet Activation.
42925135.abstract: Sepsis-induced mitochondrial impairment has been described in different organs, in both animal models and humans. Excessive radical oxygen species (ROS) could be involved in this phenomenon. As a result, antioxidants have been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy, although results remain controversial. Platelet hyperactivation is considered a central pathogenic mechanism in the development of sepsis-induced organ damage. In this study, we aimed to determine whether mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to platelet hyperactivation during sepsis. We also evaluated the effect of ROS scavenging using the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO. Laboratory investigation. University Hospital. Patients with sepsis/septic shock (n = 3/7), nonseptic burn patients (n = 10), and healthy control subjects (n = 10). Platelet mitochondria and isolated platelets from healthy donors were treated in vitro with plasma from patients with sepsis/septic shock and healthy subjects, before and after preincubation with MitoTEMPO. We measured platelet oxygen consumption rates in isolated human platelets using the Seahorse Extracellular Flux Analyzer. Platelet mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activity was measured in mitochondria-enriched fractions by spectrophotometry. Platelet aggregation in platelet-rich plasma was analyzed using light-transmission aggregometry, and leukocyte-platelet adhesion in whole blood by flow cytometry.We found that incubating platelets with septic plasma significantly reduced basal, maximal, and adenosine triphosphate-linked oxygen consumption rate. Incubation of platelet mitochondria with septic plasma also reduced platelet Complex I activity, compared with healthy plasma or plasma from nonseptic burn patients. This decrease was associated with an increase in Epinephrine-induced platelet activation. Preincubating platelets with the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO significantly reversed these effects. Our results show that the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO prevents mitochondrial dysfunction and enhances platelet activation induced by septic plasma in human platelets in vitro. This may help in designing new therapeutic approaches to prevent sepsis-induced organ damage mediated by mitochondrial dysfunction and platelet hyperactivation.

42911410.title: Re: Prognostic significance of the prothrombin time-international normalized ratio to albumin ratio in cancer patients with complication of sepsis: a retrospectively cohort study.

42904906.title: Delay From Hypotension Onset to Appropriate Antifungal Therapy Initiation Is the Critical Determinant of Outcome in Candida Septic Shock.
authors: and the Cooperative Antimicrobial Therapy of Septic Shock (CATSS) Database Research Group
42904906.abstract: To determine the effect of delays in initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy from the initial onset of persistent hypotension to the outcome of Candida septic shock. Retrospective cohort study. A total of 32 academic and community hospitals in Canada, the United States, and Saudi Arabia (July 1989 to June 2018). A total of 850 adult patients with culture-positive Candida septic shock. None. Out of 850 patients with Candida septic shock, 69.2% patients (589) received appropriate antifungal therapy after the onset of persistent hypotension. A strong relationship was observed between the delay in initiation of pathogen-appropriate antifungal (PAA) therapy and hospital survival. The adjusted odds ratio of death was 1.045 per hour of delay (95% CI, 1.035-1.056; p < 0.0001). The survival rate was 86% when an appropriate antifungal for the isolated pathogen was administered within 2 hours of the initial documentation of persistent hypotension. Thereafter, hospital survival decreased an average of 5.0% per hour for each hour of delay to 10-12 hours of delay. In a multivariate analysis, which included the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score and epidemiologic/therapeutic variables, the time to initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy emerged as the single strongest predictor of outcome. Sensitivity analysis further demonstrated that the adverse effects of delayed antifungal treatment were consistent across various subgroups, including different types of infections, pathogens, and antifungal drug classes. Median time to appropriate antifungal therapy was 32.3 hours (interquartile range, 11.2-66.0 hr), with only 16.9% receiving therapy within 6 hours of hypotension onset. Administration of PAAs within the first hours of documented hypotension significantly improved hospital survival. Less than 20% of patients received appropriate antifungals within 6 hours of documented hypotension.

42898064.title: Dynamics of ventriculo-arterial coupling and peripheral tissue perfusion during early resuscitation of septic shock.
42898064.abstract: Left ventriculo-arterial coupling (LVAC), the ratio of arterial elastance to left ventricular end-systolic elastance, is a dimensionless index that depicts the interaction between arterial load and cardiac contractility, reflecting energy transmission from the heart to the proximal arterial tree. Nevertheless, how dynamic variations of LVAC may impact tissue perfusion remains unclear. We evaluated the dynamic relationship between LVAC and capillary refill time (CRT), a peripheral perfusion surrogate, during early resuscitation of septic shock. Adult patients were prospectively included within 4-h of meeting Sepsis-3.0 septic shock criteria. LVAC was estimated at inclusion and 6-hours later by combining transthoracic echocardiography with arterial pressure monitoring, while CRT was simultaneously assessed. Patients were classified as uncoupled when LVAC > 1.36. Variations in CRT between baseline and 6-h were compared across four groups defined by LVAC evolution: (1) coupled-to-coupled; (2) coupled-to-uncoupled; (3) uncoupled-to-coupled; (4) uncoupled-to-uncoupled. Additionally, paired measurements before/after fluid loading and/or dobutamine initiation were analyzed. CRT differences among groups were compared using Kruskal-Wallis testing, followed by Dunn's post-hoc test for pairwise comparisons. Paired-Wilcoxon tests assessed CRT variations before/after interventions according to pre-intervention LVAC status. Eighty-four patients were included. CRT variation between baseline and 6-h differed significantly among groups (Kruskal-Wallis, p = 0.013), with CRT improvement in uncoupled-to-coupled (-33.8 [-53.1 to -1.2]%, p = 0.013) and worsening in coupled-to-uncoupled patients (17.5 [7.1-31.3]%, p = 0.013). Persistently coupled and uncoupled groups exhibited heterogeneous CRT responses at 6-h. Thirty-one fluid loads and thirty-two inotrope interventions were also analyzed. CRT decreased after dobutamine in initially uncoupled patients (-26.2%, p = 0.007) but not after fluid loading (-9.5%, p = 0.656) despite both interventions significantly increasing stroke volume in uncoupled LVAC condition (+14.0%, p = 0.021 and +14.2%, p < 0.001, for fluids and dobutamine, respectively). CRT did not change after either intervention in patients already coupled. Although LVAC improvement was associated with recovery of peripheral perfusion in some patients, and its deterioration with CRT prolongation in others, this relationship proved to be weak. Indeed, inconsistent CRT behavior among persistently coupled or uncoupled patients, and the heterogeneous response to resuscitative interventions suggest peripheral perfusion often evolves independently of energy transmitted from the heart to proximal arterial tree.

42892907.title: Longitudinal measurements of inflammatory mediators in patients at risk of sepsis in the Emergency Department.
42892907.abstract: Sepsis is a complex condition with time‑dependent evolution, and longitudinal biomarker dynamics may improve its characterisation. We hypothesised that biomarker kinetics are associated with sepsis, the intensity of organ dysfunction, and patient survival. This single‑centre, prospective, observational study included adult patients presenting to the Emergency Department with suspected infection and a National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2) ≥3. Blood samples were collected at baseline, 4 and 24 h and pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, as well as other inflammatory mediators or acute-phase reactants, were analysed. Linear and nonlinear mixed-effects models assessed associations between biomarker trajectories over time, sepsis diagnosis, and organ dysfunction severity. Joint models evaluated the predictive value of biomarker kinetics during the first 24 h for in‑hospital mortality. Of 214 screened patients, 173 were analysed and 137(79%) developed sepsis. Linear and nonlinear mixed models showed significant time‑dependent decreases in IL10 (β -0.016, 95%CI -0.028 to -0.004), IL1RN (β -0.014, 95%CI -0.024 to -0.004), and IL6 (β -1.021, 95%CI -1.609 to -0.433 for the first spline 0-4 h). Sepsis diagnosis was associated with higher IL1RN (β 0.378, 95%CI 0.153-0.603) and TNFRSF1A (β 0.40, 95%CI 0.21-0.58); a significant interaction between sepsis and time was observed only for IL6 (β -0.33, CI95% -0.653 to-0.007) for the second spline 4-24 h. Increasing SOFA scores correlated with elevated IL10 (β 0.048), IL1RN (β 0.044), CCL2 (β 0.046), TNFRSF1A (β 0.050), and procalcitonin (PCT; β 2.15), all p < 0.01. The SOFA score-time interaction was significant only for IL6 (β 0.122, 95%CI 0.006 to 0.238 during the first spline 0-4 h followed by β -0.080, 95%CI -0.133 to -0.027 for the second spline 4-24 h). Joint survival models adjusted identified associations between longitudinal IL8 (HR 0.655, 95%CrI 0.582-0.728), TNFRSF1A (HR 0.505, 95%CrI 0.419-0.682), and PCT (HR 1.004, 95%CrI 1.001-1.008) concentrations and survival outcome. However, IL8 and TNFRSF1A showed an unexpected inverse association with survival, and the overall discriminatory performance was modest. In conclusion, Sepsis status and organ dysfunction severity were associated with distinct inflammatory biomarker levels and kinetics. IL6 showed a unique time‑dependent relationship, whereas the dynamics of TNFRSF1A, IL8 and PCT showed exploratory associations with survival. Further studies are warranted to confirm our results.

42890494.title: Renal microcirculation in acute kidney injury: bridging haemodynamics, inflammation and repair.
42890494.abstract: The kidneys receive a disproportionately high share of cardiac output relative to their mass, reflecting their central role in solute clearance and fluid regulation. The renal microcirculation is anatomically complex and regionally heterogeneous, with steep gradients in perfusion and oxygen tension from cortex to medulla. This architecture supports efficient filtration and reabsorption but renders specific nephron segments supply-dependent and susceptible to injury during haemodynamic instability, hypoxia, inflammation, or exposure to toxins. These vulnerabilities can lead to acute kidney injury (AKI), where microvascular dysfunction often precedes changes in global renal perfusion. The renal microvasculature comprises glomerular capillaries followed by efferent arterioles supplying either cortical peritubular capillaries or the medullary vasa recta. Regional endothelial heterogeneity, limited medullary oxygen availability, countercurrent oxygen shunting, and the high metabolic demand of tubular sodium transport create intrinsic susceptibility to injury. In AKI, sepsis, ischaemia-reperfusion, surgery, nephrotoxins, and venous congestion may trigger early endothelial activation and glycocalyx injury, promoting increases permeability, leukocyte and platelet adhesion, altered vascular tone, capillary obstruction, and interstitial oedema. These changes impair perfused capillary density and oxygen diffusion. Microvascular dysfunction may persist despite normalisation of systemic haemodynamics, reflecting a loss of haemodynamic coherence and contributing to regional hypoxia and reduced glomerular filtration.Tubular injury further amplifies these abnormalities. Reduced NaCl reabsorption increases delivery to the macula densa, activates tubuloglomerular feedback, and promotes afferent vasoconstriction, while tubular obstruction, filtrate backleak, and interstitial pressure oppose filtration and compromise peritubular perfusion. The relative contribution of these mechanisms differs across sepsis-associated, ischaemia-reperfusion, perioperative, nephrotoxic, congestive, and predominantly haemodynamic AKI phenotypes.When repair is incomplete, persistent endothelial dysfunction, pericyte detachment, capillary rarefaction, chronic hypoxia, and fibrosis promote nephron dropout, loss of renal functional reserve, and progression from AKI to chronic kidney disease. Clinical assessment currently relies on complementary surrogates, including perfusion imaging, venous congestion assessment, oxygenation monitoring, and endothelial or tubular biomarkers. Renal microvascular dysfunction contributes to the initiation, functional expression, persistence, and long-term consequences of AKI. A phenotype-oriented approach integrating perfusion, congestion, oxygenation, endothelial injury, and tubulo-vascular interactions may improve mechanistic understanding and support the development of targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies.

42819483.title: Derivation of a novel clinical phenotype of sepsis in critically ill patients: a secondary analysis of a multicentre, prospective, observational study.
