42970569.abstract: Sepsis remains a leading cause of death in intensive care units worldwide and may be accompanied by complex complications, including encephalopathy, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, myocardial dysfunction, and delirium, each of which substantially increases the risk of poor outcomes. Machine learning, a promising approach for prognostic prediction, can capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical risk factors. However, its predictive performance in sepsis and its specific complications remains unclear. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for relevant literature through April 2026. Studies that aimed to develop or validate machine learning models to predict mortality in adult patients with sepsis and its associated complications were included. The random-effects or bivariate model was used to calculate the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. Overall, machine learning models show moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis, with a combined AUC of 0.82 for the training set (46 studies, 15 models) and 0.79 for the validation set (50 studies, 25 models). Logistic regression is the most widely evaluated model, demonstrating stable performance (validation AUC = 0.81). Integrated methods, including random forest and XGBoost, performed equally well, with AUCs between 0.81 and 0.83 in both groups. Although LightGBM and DL-CMT achieved the highest AUCs in the training and validation sets, respectively, both estimates were based on a single study. Among the complications, the evidence for sepsis-associated encephalopathy (AUC = 0.81, 3 studies) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (AUC = 0.80, 4 studies) is the most conclusive and best demonstrated. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury showed moderate and stable performance (validation AUC = 0.79, 4 studies). Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy showed significant attenuation from training to validation (AUC 0.84 vs 0.78, all from a single study), and random forest performed well in training (AUC = 0.98) but was not widely reported. Septic shock reached the highest AUC (0.95), but this was based on a single study. The predictive utility of sepsis-associated delirium is limited (AUC = 0.67, 1 study), and sepsis-induced myocardial injury is moderate (AUC = 0.77, 1 study).For long-term mortality, evidence is extremely lacking. Only SAE (AUC 0.88 during training and 0.86 during validation) and SCRS (combined AUC 0.76) provided single study estimates, ruling out reliable conclusions. In this meta-analysis, machine learning models showed moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis. Among complications, SAE and SIC had the strongest evidence and best performance, whereas SAD showed limited utility. Evidence for long-term mortality was extremely scarce. These findings support the potential role of machine learning in early prognostic risk stratification, yet they also highlight the urgent need for rigorous external validation and higher-quality studies, particularly for under-investigated complications.

42969437.title: Vasoactive-Adjusted Shock Index for Risk Stratification in Adult Sepsis.
42969437.abstract: The vasoactive-adjusted shock index (VASI) has been shown to identify a refractory shock phenotype in pediatric sepsis that is associated with high mortality. However, its prognostic value remains unclear in adults. In this retrospective cohort study, group-based trajectory modeling was applied to identify VASI trajectories. Cox regression estimated mortality risk across trajectory groups. Heterogeneity of treatment effect was assessed via covariate balancing propensity scores targeting the average treatment effect on the treated, with interaction terms tested in weighted logistic models. A total of 63853 patients was included. The VASI predicted ICU mortality significantly better than the shock index and provided incremental value beyond SOFA. Two distinct VASI trajectories were identified, with low VASI trajectory that remained consistently low and high VASI trajectory characterized by an early transient rise followed by a sustained decline. The high VASI group had markedly higher 28-day mortality (HR 2.89, 95% CI 2.72-3.08) and 90-day mortality (HR 2.85, 95% CI 2.68-3.03). Hydrocortisone treatment was associated with mortality in both groups, with no significant interaction. Albumin showed a protective effect only in the low VASI group (OR 0.667, 95% CI 0.545-0.816), but the interaction was not significant. The early trajectory of VASI identifies a high-risk clinical phenotype in adult sepsis that is strongly associated with poor outcomes. However, no significant heterogeneity of treatment effect was observed for hydrocortisone or albumin in different VASI trajectories.

42968961.title: Optimizing Polymyxin B Exposure in Carbapenem-Resistant Organism-Associated Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia: A Retrospective Observational Study.
42968961.abstract: The area under the 24-hour concentration-time curve (AUC0-24h) is a key pharmacokinetic parameter for polymyxin B (PMB), but the optimal exposure target in critically ill patients remains uncertain. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PMB AUC0-24h and clinical efficacy in patients with carbapenem-resistant hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP), and to identify the optimal therapeutic AUC0-24h range for PMB. This retrospective observational study included patients with carbapenem-resistant HAP who received intravenous PMB and therapeutic drug monitoring. Plasma PMB concentrations were measured by validated ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS). The primary outcome was 14-day clinical treatment success, and the secondary outcome included acute kidney injury (AKI). Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess exposure-outcome relationships. A total of 138 patients were included, the median age was 68 years, and 110 (79.7%) were male. Clinical success was achieved in 63 (45.7%) patients. Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii accounted for 77.5% of infections. The median AUC0-24h of PMB was 77.5 (55.6, 105.6) mg·h/L. An AUC0-24h > 77 mg·h/L enabled to predict the clinical treatment success, while AUC0-24h > 110 mg·h/L enabled to predict the AKI incidence. In multivariable analysis, AUC0-24h < 77 mg·h/L was an independent risk factor for reduced clinical treatment success (OR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13-0.78; p = 0.013), while AUC0-24h > 110 mg·h/L significantly increased AKI risk (OR: 3.24, 95% CI: 1.06-10.47; p = 0.043). The AUC0-24h of PMB is closely associated with both 14-day clinical treatment success rates and the incidence of AKI in patients with carbapenem-resistant HAP, with an optimal range from 77 to 110 mg·h/L.

42968937.title: Actionable Biomarkers in Acute Exacerbations of COPD: Corticosteroid and Antibiotic Stewardship.
42968937.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
42968937.abstract: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) arise from heterogeneous inflammatory and infectious processes, yet systemic corticosteroids and antibiotics are often prescribed empirically. This narrative review evaluates biomarkers according to the acute treatment decisions they can support, drawing on randomized trials and supporting clinical studies evaluated through August 9, 2026. Blood eosinophils have the most developed evidence for corticosteroid guidance: trials support treatment selection or withholding in primary care and serial treatment shortening after an initial dose in hospitalized patients. C-reactive protein supports antibiotic stewardship most clearly in primary care, with more limited inpatient evidence. Procalcitonin can reduce antibiotic use in selected non-intensive-care inpatients, whereas the intensive-care trial failed to establish non-inferiority for mortality and did not reduce antibiotic exposure. These findings depend on the tested population, sampling time, threshold, and treatment rule. Rapid molecular pathogen tests improve diagnostic yield and turnaround time; their integration into COPD-specific treatment algorithms remains a research priority. Multimarker strategies and acute biologic treatment offer further avenues for investigation, with acute biologic evidence currently derived from a mixed asthma/COPD population. Organizing evidence around a biomarker-decision-population framework separates established stewardship applications from emerging treatment strategies. Clinical utility ultimately depends on whether the complete strategy preserves or improves patient outcomes and can be delivered reliably in routine care.

42968049.title: Efficacy and safety of combined intraventricular/intrathecal and intravenous polymyxin B for postsurgical neurosurgical infections due to MDR/XDR-GNB: a retrospective cohort study.
42968049.abstract: Intracranial infections caused by multidrug-resistant or extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (MDR/XDR-GNB) represent a significant challenge in neurosurgical critical care, with limited effective treatment options. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intraventricular/intrathecal (IVT/ITH) and intravenous polymyxin B in patients with post-neurosurgical MDR/XDR-GNB intracranial infections, focusing on long-term outcomes and neurotoxicity. This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted across seven hospitals in the West China region between December 2019 and June 2021. Patients with culture-confirmed MDR/XDR-GNB intracranial infection were enrolled and divided into two groups based on whether they received IVT/ITH polymyxin B. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality, with secondary outcomes including pathogen clearance rate, neurological status at discharge, and adverse events. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate treatment effects. A total of 70 patients were included, with 24 in the IVT/ITH group and 46 in the control group. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The most common pathogens isolated were Acinetobacter baumannii (67.1%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (24.3%), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (4.3%), with 98.6% of isolates susceptible to polymyxin B. IVT/ITH polymyxin B was associated with significantly improved 90-day survival (adjusted HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.26-0.98) and higher pathogen clearance rates (58.3% vs. 26.7%, p < 0.001). No significant differences in adverse effects, including neurotoxicity, were observed between groups, although a trend toward higher seizure incidence was noted in the IVT/ITH group. IVT/ITH and intravenous administration of polymyxin B significantly improved long-term survival and microbial clearance in patients with MDR/XDR-GNB intracranial infections, with a favorable safety profile. These findings support its use as a promising therapeutic strategy in resource-limited settings where this combined local-systemic regimen is not feasible. This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of West China Hospital, approval number 278.

42975222.title: Clinical Predictors of Neurological Status and Hospital Length of Stay in Patients with Sepsis from Intensive Care Unit.
42975222.abstract: Sepsis frequently leads to muti-organ dysfunction and neurological impairment, contributing to increased morbidity and prolonged hospitalisation. The present study aimed to determine the clinical predictors of multi-organ failure, neurological status and hospital stay duration in patients with sepsis. Patient characteristics, clinical profiles and biochemical markers were recorded for 100 patients with sepsis from intensive care units (ICUs), including serum lactate, albumin, leucocyte count, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) score. Regression analyses were used to perform the associations. The SOFA score was 12 (interquartile range 8-15) and 75% required ICU admission. Mean lactate-albumin ratio (LAR) was 1.73 ± 1.31 and 47% of the study population fell into the high-LAR category. LAR was not independently associated with SOFA score (β =0.45, P = 0.132) or GCS (β =0.18, P = 0.284). GCS scores were significantly higher in males than in females (13.6 ± 1.86 vs. 12.75 ± 1.88). Gender (β =0.86, P = 0.026) and leucocyte count (β = -0.01, P = 0.048) emerged as independent predictors of GCS, with gender exhibiting the strongest effect (0.223). Leucocyte count was inversely correlated with GCS (effect size = -0.198) and served as an independent predictor of hospital stay duration (β =0.205, P = 0.040). LAR was not an independent predictor of level of consciousness/neurological status or organ dysfunction in sepsis. However, gender and leucocyte count independently influenced neurological status, with leucocyte count also predicted length of hospital stay. These findings suggested that inflammatory profiles play a critical role in the development of neurological dysfunction during sepsis.

42972235.title: Association between thymosin α1 therapy and 28-day mortality risk in critically ill patients with tuberculosis-related sepsis: a retrospective cohort study.
42972235.abstract: Patients with tuberculosis (TB)-related sepsis often experience profound immune dysregulation and poor clinical outcomes. Evidence of immunomodulatory therapeutic efficacy in this population remains limited. We evaluated the association between thymosin α1 (Tα1) use and 28-day all-cause mortality in critically ill TB-related sepsis patients and explored whether the strength of this association varied with the baseline lymphocyte count. This single-centre retrospective cohort study included critically ill, adult TB-related sepsis patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) in 2017-2025. Exposure was any Tα1 use during ICU stay. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Association analyses included multivariable Cox regression, restricted mean survival time (RMST) analyses, and exploratory restricted cubic spline (RCS) modelling. Sensitivity analyses were performed. Among 327 patients, 160 received Tα1 and 167 served as controls. Tα1 use was associated with a lower hazard of 28-day mortality after adjustment for baseline covariates (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.54; 95% confidence interval, 0.36-0.79; P = 0.002); sensitivity analyses showed estimates of similar direction. The proportional hazards assumption was violated; consequent RMST analysis revealed longer adjusted restricted mean survival in the Tα1 group. Exploratory RCS modelling suggested nonlinear variability in the association between Tα1 use and 28-day mortality across baseline lymphocyte counts, which appeared more pronounced at intermediate lymphocyte counts (approximately 0.8-1.2 × 10⁹/L); however, this data-driven pattern is hypothesis-generating. Among ICU patients with TB-related sepsis, Tα1 use was associated with lower observed 28-day mortality, but causality cannot be inferred. The identified variability in this association across baseline lymphocyte counts requires external validation. Not applicable.

42974462.title: Early D-Dimer-Lactate Risk Categories and ICU Mortality in Patients with Sepsis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
42974462.abstract: D-dimer and lactate are commonly measured early in sepsis and reflect complementary coagulation and metabolic stress pathways. Whether a simple combined D-dimer-lactate risk stratification is associated with ICU mortality remains clinically relevant. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients with sepsis admitted to the ICU. High D-dimer was defined as the cohort upper quartile (Q75 = 2958), and elevated lactate was defined as lactate ≥2 mmol/L. Patients were classified into four categories: neither elevated, D-dimer only, lactate only, and both elevated. Non-core covariates with missing values were handled using multiple imputation. Logistic regression models estimated the association with ICU mortality after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, infection source, five binary comorbidities, and SOFA score. This study included 779 patients with complete D-dimer, lactate, and ICU mortality data. ICU mortality increased across the combined categories: 26/311 (8.4%, 95% CI 5.5-12.0) in neither elevated, 7/74 (9.5%, 95% CI 3.9-18.5) in D-dimer only, 49/273 (17.9%, 95% CI 13.6-23.0) in lactate only, and 49/121 (40.5%, 95% CI 31.7-49.8) in both elevated. In the fully adjusted model, the both-elevated category was associated with higher ICU mortality compared with neither elevated (OR 3.94, 95% CI 2.03-7.67; P<0.001). Lactate-only elevation was also associated with mortality (OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.15-3.48; P=0.015), whereas isolated high D-dimer was not (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.34-2.24; P=0.771). The four-category scheme alone showed numerically lower discrimination than lactate alone (AUC 0.691 vs 0.740). Adding the categories to the base clinical model increased the AUC from 0.791 to 0.813 (delta AUC 0.022; P=0.029), an exploratory finding that should not be interpreted as proof that the categories improve prediction beyond lactate. Early D-dimer-lactate risk categories were associated with ICU mortality and identified a clinically interpretable high-risk subgroup among ICU patients with sepsis. Their predictive utility beyond lactate and established clinical predictors remains uncertain. These categories should be interpreted as pragmatic risk stratification rather than evidence of a validated biological phenotype or statistical synergy, and external validation is warranted.

42973926.title: Outcome and Risk Factors for Death of Burn Patients with Septic Shock.
42973926.journal: Annals of burns and fire disasters
42973926.abstract: This study determined mortality rate and risk factors for death of burn patients suffering septic shock. An observational study was conducted on 38 severe adult burn patients who developed septic shock at the burn intensive care unit, National Burn Hospital, from January 2023 to June 2024. Patients were divided into survivor and non-survivor groups. Results showed that 23 patients died, accounting for 60.53%. Age, gender, admission time post burn, incidence of inhalation injury, required mechanical ventilation on admission as well as onset time of septic shock were not significantly different between groups (p >.05). Compared to the survivor group, burn extent and deep burn area were significantly larger in the non-survivor group (p <.05). Baseline parameters including white blood count, total plasma protein and albumin concentration were significantly lower (p <.01); rate of positive blood cultures (56.52% vs. 20%; p=.03) and plasma IL-6 level (689.46 pg/mL vs. 243.16 pg/mL, p=.02) were significantly higher in the non-survivor group. Meanwhile, plasma level of endotoxin and TNF-α were not remarkably different between the two groups. Multivariate analysis showed that only plasma IL-6 level at the septic shock onset was an independent risk factor for death (p <.05) with AUC at .73, cut-off point at 249.46 pg/mL, sensitivity at 82.61% and specificity at 60%. Further studies should be conducted to confirm the role of IL-6 in the prognosis of burn patients with septic shock complication.

42973509.title: Association of liberal versus restrictive oxygen saturation targets with mortality in mechanically ventilated stroke patients: a multicenter retrospective propensity-matched analysis.
42973509.abstract: Optimal oxygen saturation targets in mechanically ventilated stroke patients remain uncertain. While restrictive oxygen strategies are increasingly adopted in general critical care, their impact in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) are unclear. We evaluated the association between restrictive versus liberal oxygen saturation targets during the first 48 h of mechanical ventilation and short-term mortality in stroke patients. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX database (2006-2026). Adult patients (≥18 years) with a stroke diagnosis who required invasive mechanical ventilation and had documented peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) values within the first 48 h of ventilation were included. Patients were stratified according to early oxygen saturation targets: restrictive (SpO₂ 92-96%) versus liberal (SpO₂ ≥ 97%). Propensity score matching (PSM) by demographics, comorbidities, and stroke severity was performed separately within the combined stroke cohort and prespecified AIS and ICH subgroups to balance demographic and clinical covariates. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 30 and 90 days. Secondary outcomes included 30-day tracheostomy and ventilator-associated pneumonia. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. p-value was set at 0.05. Among 17,207 mechanically ventilated stroke patients, 2,366 received restrictive and 14,841 liberal oxygen saturation targets prior to matching. After PSM, 2,350 patients remained in each group. Restrictive oxygenation during the first 48 h was associated with higher mortality at 1 month (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.03-1.23; p = 0.008) and 3 months (HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02-1.20; p = 0.014). In AIS, restrictive oxygenation was similarly associated with increased mortality at 1 month (HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.11-1.43) and 3 months (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.08-1.37). No statistically significant mortality difference was observed in ICH. Restrictive oxygenation was associated with lower 30-day tracheostomy rates (8.5% vs. 13.1%; RR 0.653, p < 0.001), with no difference in VAP. Restrictive oxygen saturation targets during the first 48 h of mechanical ventilation may be associated with higher short-term mortality in stroke, driven primarily by the AIS group. These findings suggest that early oxygenation strategy may have subtype-specific implications and warrant prospective evaluation in stroke focused randomized trials.

42975560.title: Correlation between phenotypic disc diffusion test and PCR molecular test for detection of methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus epidermidis and Staphylococcus hominis.
42975560.abstract: Introduction. Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS), particularly Staphylococcus epidermidis, are leading opportunistic pathogens in neonatal intensive care units, frequently associated with late-onset sepsis and medical device colonization.Gap statement. Cefoxitin disk diffusion has been adopted internationally as a surrogate marker for mecA, but its accuracy in CoNS is heterogeneous; high resistance rates and erratic phenotypic expression in species like Staphylococcus hominis indicate that the existing phenotypic-only approach does not transfer reliably between species and cohorts.Aim. Evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of oxacillin agar dilution (AD) and cefoxitin disc diffusion against mecA PCR in 664 coagulase-negative staphylococcal isolates collected over an 8-year period (2006-2014) at a tertiary-level hospital.Methodology. Phenotypic detection of methicillin resistance was performed by oxacillin AD with 4% NaCl/24 h and by cefoxitin disk diffusion (≤24 mm), using mecA PCR as the reference standard; inducible clindamycin resistance (iMLS_B) was screened by D-test. All isolates were stratified by species (S. epidermidis, S. hominis) and cohort (neonatal versus adult), with concordance quantified using Cohen's κ coefficient under the Landis and Koch framework.Results. S. epidermidis accounted for 87.2% and S. hominis for 8.6% of isolates, with 83.1% originating from neonates. In neonatal S. epidermidis, mecA prevalence reached 80%. Oxacillin AD demonstrated superior performance with 87.1% sensitivity (neonates) and 78.3% (adults), with moderate agreement in both subgroups (κ=0.44-0.54, respectively). The D-test further revealed a 20.8% prevalence of the inducible clindamycin resistance phenotype (iMLS_B) in neonatal S. hominis, indicating a high risk of therapeutic failure despite an apparently susceptible routine antibiogram, a prevalence nearly 20-fold higher than that observed in neonatal S. epidermidis (1.0%, n=5), identifying S. hominis as a particularly problematic inducible-clindamycin-resistance reservoir in the NICU setting.Conclusion. High resistance rates and erratic phenotypic expression in species like S. hominis, together with the unequal accuracy of phenotypic methods between neonates and adults, require a species-specific diagnostic approach. While oxacillin AD remains a robust predictor for both species and cohorts in this setting, systematic D-test implementation and mecA molecular confirmation are essential to ensure effective antimicrobial therapy.

42974192.title: From cytokine storm to adaptive dysregulation: temporal evolution of the inflammatory network and phase-specific intervention strategies in fulminant viral myocarditis.
42974192.abstract: Fulminant viral myocarditis (FVM) is characterized by acute onset and rapid progression, often deteriorating into cardiogenic shock, malignant arrhythmias, and multi-organ failure within days. Its pathological essence does not lie in the "quantitative accumulation" of focal lymphocytic infiltration seen in ordinary myocarditis, but rather in a "qualitative shift" driven by diffuse myocardial edema compounded by a multi-cytokine cascade. Accumulating evidence indicates that the "inflection point" of myocardial injury is determined not by viral load per se, but by the dysregulated pattern recognition of viral antigens by the innate immune system and the resultant imbalance of the inflammatory network. The organising framework of this review is temporal (hyperacute to acute to reparative immune states). A spatial dimension, contrasting the circulating and the cardiac-resident immune compartments, is developed wherever direct or closely analogous data exist, but it carries far less evidence than the temporal dimension and is treated as secondary to it. Myocarditis that is immune-mediated without a replicating cardiotropic virus, including vaccine-associated and checkpoint-inhibitor disease, is used here as a labelled comparator and not as part of the entity under review. The virus invades cardiomyocytes and vascular endothelium via receptors with non-canonical distribution, subsequently triggering type I interferon responses and necroptosis through endosomal and cytosolic pattern-recognition receptors, and initiating a cascade effect via damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). The driver of cardiomyocyte death does not stay constant across this course: virus-intrinsic cytopathic and ferroptotic death predominates in the first days, myeloid-mediated killing takes over through the remainder of the first week, and cytotoxic lymphocytes become the principal effectors thereafter. The hyperacute phase is characterized by macrophage phenotypic drift, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and a "cytokine storm" whose earliest cellular sources in viral myocarditis are myeloid rather than T-cell derived. The acute phase features the "clearance-injury" paradox of cytotoxic T cells and the failure of immune checkpoint regulation, and a subset of patients may subsequently follow what the authors describe as a candidate immunoparalysis trajectory rather than an established third stage of disease - a state provisionally characterized by regulatory T cell (Treg) expansion, paradoxical elevation of interleukin-10 (IL-10), and downregulation of monocyte human leukocyte antigen-DR (HLA-DR). Its reported association with secondary infection and adverse outcome derives largely from sepsis and critical-care cohorts and has not been demonstrated in FVM. Building on this "inflammatory time window," the authors propose a phase-specific framework intended to generate hypotheses rather than to recommend treatment: in the hyperacute phase, "fire-extinguishing" approaches (complement blockade and cytokine adsorption) may represent a potential alternative to broad-spectrum immunosuppression; in the acute phase, selective blockade of individual pathways according to inflammatory subtype may be worth exploring; and in the reparative phase, measures aimed at restoring regulatory immune capacity may be considered for study. None of these pathways, and none of the biomarker values discussed in the main text, has been prospectively validated in FVM. Finally, this review envisions individualized decision-making guided by multi-omics and dynamic immune monitoring, emphasizing that the prognosis of FVM depends on the capacity for "dynamic phenotyping and real-time switching" of immune status, rather than reliance on any single therapeutic modality.

42973892.title: Antibiotic use, Resistance Patterns and Clinical Outcomes in Critically Burned Patients: A Retrospective Study From a Tertiary Burn Center in Albania.
42973892.journal: Annals of burns and fire disasters
42973892.abstract: Severe burn injuries induce profound physiological and immunological alterations that significantly affect the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of antimicrobial agents. These changes complicate standard dosing strategies and demand individualized, PK/PD-driven approaches to antimicrobial therapy to prevent treatment failure, resistance and toxicity. This retrospective clinical-analytical study included 154 pediatric and adult patients admitted to the ICU of a tertiary burn center in 2023. Antimicrobial use was quantified using the defined daily dose (DDD) and normalized per 100 patient-days. Logistic regression was applied to identify predictors of antibiotic use. Sepsis occurred in 16.2% of patients, with significantly higher mortality (36%) compared to non-septic patients (3.8%, p<0.0001). Septic patients were older, had larger burn areas, deeper burns, and longer ICU stays. Infections were predominantly caused by Gram-positive bacteria, with MRSA comprising 53% of Staphylococcus aureus isolates. Antibiotic use was significantly greater among septic patients, with 80% receiving ≥3 regimens. Overall, antibiotic consumption was 56.76 DDD/100 patient-days, with metronidazole, ceftriaxone and amikacin being the most used agents. Logistic regression revealed that each 1% increase in burn surface area increased the odds of antibiotic use by 1.6 times, and each additional hospital day by 2.9 times. Septic burn patients experience significantly higher mortality and antibiotic exposure. The high prevalence of resistant organisms such as MRSA underscores the need for local antibiogram-guided therapy. Burn size and length of stay are strong predictors of antibiotic use. Therapeutic drug monitoring and PK/PD-based dosing are essential for optimizing antimicrobial therapy and minimizing resistance in this vulnerable population.

42972975.title: Pancreas-Intestine Composite Transplantation for Simultaneous Loss of Pancreatic and Intestinal Function (With Video).
42972975.abstract: Pancreas-intestine composite transplantation (PITx) is a therapeutic option for patients with irreversible loss of both pancreatic and intestinal function. We report a case of PITx in a 16-year-old male who developed fulminant Type 1 diabetes mellitus complicated by non-occlusive mesenteric ischemia, resulting in extensive intestinal necrosis. Despite intensive surgical and critical care management, the patient ultimately required total small intestinal resection and total pancreatectomy. After recovery from sepsis and multiorgan dysfunction, the patient's general condition stabilized, and PITx was considered an appropriate therapeutic option. The composite graft consisted of the pancreas, duodenum, small intestine, and right colon. Arterial inflow was reconstructed using a single Carrel patch incorporating the celiac axis and superior mesenteric artery, and venous outflow was established by portal vein anastomosis. Postoperatively, pancreatic endocrine function was restored, allowing stable glycemic control without exogenous insulin, and intestinal graft function enabled the gradual advancement of enteral and oral nutrition. This report highlights the key technical considerations and anatomical principles of PITx and demonstrates that tailored composite graft transplantation can restore both pancreatic and intestinal function while preserving unaffected abdominal organs in highly selected patients with combined pancreatic and intestinal failure.

42972097.title: [New sepsis guidelines: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 and German Sepsis Society 2025 -Competing or complementary?].
42972097.abstract: Sepsis is one of the leading causes of death in intensive care units worldwide. In German-speaking countries, patient management is primarily guided by two sets of guidelines: the international Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) guidelines and the S3 guidelines of the German Sepsis Society (DSG). While the DSG guidelines were published in 2025 as an evidence-based adaptation of the SSC 2021 guidelines, the SSC has since released an updated international version in 2026. To provide a structured analysis of the key content areas, similarities and differences between the two guidelines, with a particular focus on the timing of treatment initiation, anti-infective treatment and hemodynamic management. Both guidelines reflect not so much a fundamental shift in strategy but more a consolidation of evidence and a refinement of concepts. Three overarching themes can be identified: a broadened perspective encompassing the entire continuum of care, from the prehospital setting to post-sepsis follow-up, the increasing integration of antibiotic stewardship principles and in SSC 2026, the introduction of a graded sepsis terminology (definite/probable/possible/unlikely). Areas of agreement include the importance of early anti-infective treatment, the preferential use of balanced crystalloids, norepinephrine as the first-line vasopressor, the inclusion of capillary refill time as a perfusion parameter and a strong recommendation for prolonged or continuous beta-lactam infusion. Differences are evident in the specificity of antimicrobial recommendations, the definition of risk factors warranting empirical antifungal treatment and several new recommendations introduced in SSC 2026, such as a lower mean arterial pressure (MAP) target of 60-65 mm Hg for patients aged ≥ 65 years, initiation of treatment in the prehospital setting and source control within 6 h. The DSG 2025 and SSC 2026 guidelines should be regarded as complementary rather than competing frameworks. The DSG 2025 remains the practical, high-resolution handbook for care in the Central European context, while the SSC 2026 outlines the international direction: away from a purely acute care set of rules towards an individualized, continuum-based model of care.

42975533.title: Dual Protective Mechanisms of Neostigmine in Septic Shock: Cholinergic Anti-Inflammatory Pathway and Intestinal Barrier Preservation.

42975523.title: Certainty of Evidence and Interpretation of Effects in Inhaled Antibiotics for Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.

42975517.title: Hypercapnia in Ventilated Sepsis: Signal, Target, or Lung-Protective Tradeoff?

42972580.title: Distinct transcriptomic signatures discriminate hyperinflammation from immune paralysis in sepsis: a single-cell RNA sequencing study.
42972580.abstract: Sepsis is a highly heterogeneous syndrome characterized by variable immune dysregulation states, including hyperinflammation and immunosuppression. Previous immunotherapy attempts in sepsis have largely failed, likely due to a "one-size-fits-all" approach that ignores each patient's immune status. The recent ImmunoSep randomized clinical trial demonstrated that precision immunotherapy guided by the presence of either macrophage activation-like syndrome (MALS) or immune paralysis can improve early organ dysfunction in sepsis patients. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these immune endotypes remain unclear. To identify the immunological signatures that distinguish MALS and immune paralysis. We used single-cell RNA sequencing to profile circulating leukocytes of 6 healthy controls and 16 sepsis patients classified as MALS, immune paralysis or unclassified (when criteria for neither of these two immune endotypes were applicable). Classification was based on surrogate biomarkers ferritin and HLA-DR expression on monocytes. Thereafter, the transcriptional programs of these groups were compared. Pronounced differences were detected mainly in the transcriptional signature of monocytes from these patients, with a clear distinction between MALS and immune paralysis. Unsupervised clustering analysis revealed the existence of MALS-specific monocyte clusters, as well as one sepsis-specific monocyte cluster that was linked to greater comorbidity burden and may reflect increased clinical vulnerability in sepsis. These findings were validated in two independent cohorts, in which urosepsis was characterized by heterogeneous MALS and immune paralysis monocyte signatures. Moreover, MALS-specific monocyte clusters showed overlapping transcriptional signatures with severe COVID-19. Our findings shed light on the heterogeneous immune landscape underlying sepsis and provide opportunities for patient stratification for future therapeutic development.

42972412.title: Deconstructing cardiovascular heterogeneity in septic shock: V0-LV invariance, vasopressin mismatch, and RVR circularity.

42972380.title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction and obstructive coronary artery disease in sepsis-associated myocardial injury: authors' reply.

42978718.title: Carbapenem Renal Dose Discordance and Acute Kidney Injury in the Intensive Care Unit: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
42978718.journal: The Journal of pharmacy technology : jPT : official publication of the Association of Pharmacy Technicians
42978718.abstract: Renal function changes rapidly in the intensive care unit (ICU), and carbapenem dosing above renal-adjusted recommendations is a potentially preventable medication safety issue. To evaluate the association between carbapenem renal dose discordance and acute kidney injury (AKI); treatment failure was exploratory. This ethics-approved retrospective cohort included adults receiving carbapenems for at least 48 hours in a Vietnamese hospital ICU (January 2024-April 2026). Discordance was at least 1 day above renal-adjusted recommendations based on estimated Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance and clinical indication. Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria defined AKI. Robust Poisson regression estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs). Matched outcome models additionally adjusted for Glasgow Coma Scale category and septic shock. A post hoc Bonferroni threshold of α = .003125 was applied. Of 490 patients, 78 (15.9%) had discordant dosing. Acute kidney injury occurred in 28/78 (35.9%) with discordant dosing versus 18/412 (4.4%) with concordant dosing. Discordance was associated with AKI in the primary analysis (aRR, 8.061; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.135-15.714; P < .001) and among 68 matched pairs (aRR, 5.937; 95% CI, 2.112-16.694; P = .001). Associations with treatment failure did not meet the corrected threshold in the primary analysis (aRR, 1.586; 95% CI, 1.023-2.458; P = .039) or among matched pairs (aRR, 1.164; 95% CI, 0.723-1.875; P = .532). Carbapenem renal dose discordance was associated with AKI, although causation cannot be established. Daily renal dose review by pharmacists is a practical medication safety target that warrants prospective evaluation.

42980468.title: Dynamic phenotyping and organ cross-talk in sepsis-associated organ injury: from physiological trajectories to precision critical care.
42980468.abstract: Sepsis-associated organ injury remains a major cause of mortality in critically ill patients. Conventional assessment relies largely on physiological indicators, including lactate, mean arterial pressure (MAP), PaO2/FiO2 ratio, creatinine, urine output, and organ dysfunction scores. However, these isolated values or single-variable trends may incompletely capture the temporal instability and biological heterogeneity that characterize sepsis. Increasing evidence indicates that dynamic trajectories, variability patterns, and evolving subphenotypes may better characterize disease progression, organ recovery, and treatment responsiveness. In parallel, critical care medicine is moving from syndrome-level classification toward treatable traits, individualized treatment effects, and precision critical care. Dynamic phenotyping focuses on physiological trajectories, including lactate clearance, oxygenation evolution, hemodynamic variability, glycemic variability, and renal recovery, but its major value may lie in interpreting relationships among trajectories across organ systems. Interpretation of dynamic phenotypes therefore requires attention to cross-system temporal relationships, including coordinated recovery, coupled deterioration, and discordant recovery. From this trajectory-based perspective, sepsis-associated organ injury can be viewed as an interconnected multiorgan network involving lung-kidney, gut-lung, gut-liver, gut-kidney, and endothelial-organ cross-talk. Organ cross-talk may help explain dynamic coupling among organ systems, whereas microcirculatory-mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to trajectory mismatch through impaired tissue perfusion, oxygen delivery-utilization uncoupling, bioenergetic failure, maladaptive metabolic reprogramming, and defective mitochondrial quality control. This trajectory-based perspective may inform future precision critical care, while most trajectory-guided strategies remain investigational and require prospective validation before routine clinical adoption.

42978137.title: Impact of Neuromuscular Blocking Agents on Hospital Outcomes in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Sepsis: Propensity Score Analyses of A Nationwide Sepsis Cohort.
42978137.abstract: The impact of neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) on hospital outcomes in patients with sepsis requiring mechanical ventilation (MV) remains uncertain and warrants further evaluation. We analyzed data from a nationwide sepsis cohort comprising 20 university-affiliated or tertiary hospitals, including adult patients with sepsis who required MV. Patients who received continuous intravenous NMBAs within 3 days of intensive care unit (ICU) admission were compared with those who did not. To adjust for baseline imbalances, both inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM) were used. Of 13,827 patients with sepsis, 1,255 receiving MV were analyzed (mean age, 68.3 ± 13.9 years; 65.7% male; NMBA use, 25.7%). In the IPTW-adjusted Cox model, NMBA use was not associated with in-hospital mortality. Similarly, in the PSM cohort (292 NMBA-treated vs. 292 matched controls), in-hospital mortality did not differ between groups (17.1% vs. 18.8%; P = 0.590). However, NMBA use was associated with a longer ICU stay (absolute difference: 3.0 days [95% confidence interval, 0.3-5.7]; P = 0.003) and showed a trend toward a longer MV duration and hospital stay (Wilcoxon signed-rank test). Kaplan-Meier analysis also demonstrated significantly longer ICU stays in the NMBA group (log-rank P = 0.006). The incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia was significantly higher in the NMBA group (8.6% vs. 4.5%; P = 0.044). In patients with sepsis requiring MV, the use of NMBAs was not associated with in-hospital mortality but was linked to longer ICU stays and a higher incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia. These findings underscore the need for cautious use of continuous NMBA infusion in this population.

42979103.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia in males and females: A post hoc analysis of the prospective multicenter multinational EUVAP cohort.
42979103.abstract: Sex is a major cause of heterogeneity in the epidemiology, management, response to treatment, and outcome of infectious and respiratory diseases. We aimed to describe differences between males and females in characteristics, management, and mortality among patients affected by ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). We performed a post hoc exploratory analysis of the EUVAP/CAP cohort, a prospective multinational cohort study of patients requiring mechanical ventilation in 27 intensive care units from nine countries. Sexes were compared with respect to baseline characteristics, interventions, and outcomes in univariate and adjusted analyses. Among the 2436 intubated adult patients in the cohort, 450 (18.5%) developed VAP; of these VAP cases, 293 (65.1%) were male, and the median age was 64 years. Compared with females, males had more comorbidities, and underwent bronchoscopy more frequently (20.5% vs. 11.5%, P=0.016) and triple antibiotic therapy (33.1% vs. 22.3%, P=0.016)., Intensive care unit mortality was 41.3% vs. 45.2% (P=0.422). In multivariate analysis, age in years (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=1.02, 95%confidence interval [CI]: 1.00 to 1.04), septic shock (aOR=1.72, 95%CI: 1.02 to 2.91), McCabe score (life expectancy 1-5 years vs. >5 years: aOR=1.53, 95%CI: 0.81 to 2.54; <1 year vs. >5 years: aOR=7.67, 95%CI: 2.41 to 24.39; P=0.002), and infection with high risk bacteria for multidrug resistance (aOR=1.86, 95%CI: 1.12 to 3.09; P=0.016) were independently associated with mortality, but not sex (aOR for males vs. females=0.92, 95%CI 0.56 to 1.49; P=0.722). The relation between sex and mortality was not affected by age <50 years. The risk of mortality did not differ between sexes in patients affected by VAP. Affected males had more comorbidities, heavy alcohol use, and underwent bronchoscopy and triple antibiotic therapy more frequently.

42979336.title: Intradermal thumbtack needling as an adjunctive therapy for sepsis-induced gastrointestinal dysfunction: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
42979336.journal: Journal of traditional and complementary medicine
42979336.abstract: Sepsis-induced gastrointestinal dysfunction (GID) is common in critically ill patients, leading to impaired motility, feeding intolerance, and poor outcomes. Evidence for acupuncture-related neuromodulation remains limited. Intradermal thumbtack needling (ITN), a minimally invasive technique that provides continuous low-intensity stimulation, may serve as an adjunct in Intensive Care Unit (ICU), but its clinical effects remain unexamined. This study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of ITN in patients with sepsis-induced GID. Sixty patients with sepsis-induced GID were randomly assigned to the conventional treatment (CT) group or ITN group. Both groups received standard therapies (ventilation, vasopressors, anti-infectives, fluid resuscitation, gastrointestinal mucosal protection, and prokinetics). The ITN group also received ITN at auricular and body acupoints for 7 days. Gastrointestinal function indicators (acute gastrointestinal injury [AGI] grade, gastric antrum motility index [MI], abdominal circumference, intra-abdominal pressure [IAP]), inflammatory markers, and severity scores were assessed before and after treatment. 28-day mortality, ICU length of stay and adverse events were assessed after treatment. The ITN group showed greater improvement in AGI grade, abdominal circumference, and IAP (all P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed for MI, inflammatory markers, or severity scores (all P > 0.05). 28-day mortality and ICU length of stay did not differ significantly between groups. No ITN-related adverse events occurred. ITN may improve gastrointestinal parameters in sepsis-induced GID patients, but it did not significantly affect gastric motility, systemic inflammation, or global severity scores. Larger, controlled trials are needed to confirm its potential role as adjunctive therapy.

42978218.title: The impact of CHG bathing on healthcare-associated bloodstream infections across a health system serving a predominantly rural population.
42978218.abstract: To evaluate the impact of daily chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) bathing on healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) in patients in a large health system serving a predominantly rural population. Multi-center, quasi-experimental, before-after study. 21 hospitals (including academic, community, and critical access) in a decentralized Appalachian healthcare system. During August and September of 2023, we implemented daily CHG bathing for all patients (of at least two months of age) who had central lines and/or were admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU). We compared the hospital-level monthly incidences of two HAIs, central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) and laboratory-identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection (MRSA-BSI), in the 18 months before and after the intervention, excluding a 2-month rollout period. We modeled the standardized infection ratio (SIR) using negative binomial generalized linear mixed effects models, incorporating each hospital's risk-adjusted predicted number of infections (from NHSN). After implementation of daily CHG bathing, we observed significant reductions in bloodstream infections, with a 35% reduction in CLABSIs (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.650; 95% CI: 0.502-0.841) and a 40% reduction in MRSA bacteremia (IRR 0.599; 95% CI 0.408-0.880). Implementation of daily CHG bathing for high-risk patients across a decentralized, Appalachian healthcare system was associated with reductions in CLABSI as well as MRSA bacteremia.

42979105.title: Sepsis-associated sarcopenia: Emerging insights into mechanisms and therapeutic approaches.
42979105.abstract: As medical treatment advances, a growing proportion of sepsis patients survive from their initial critical illness. However, excessive treatment and diminished quality of life after discharge raise substantial concerns. Sarcopenia affects 40%-70% of sepsis survivors, manifesting as flaccid weakness in the extremities and diaphragm. This condition typically resolves within weeks or months, but in some cases, recovery does not occur and may last for 2 years after intensive care unit discharge. Consequently, sepsis patients with sarcopenia face an unfavorable long-term influence, and they also consume considerable medical resources. The mechanisms and treatments of sepsis-associated sarcopenia (SASP) are increasingly recognized as research priorities. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of molecular mechanisms, measuring parameters, and therapeutic approaches for SASP.

42983840.title: Treatment and outcomes of difficult-to-treat Stenotrophomonas maltophilia pneumonia in the intensive care unit: a multinational retrospective cohort study.
42983840.abstract: Difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR) in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is an emerging concern in ICU-acquired pneumonia, associated with high mortality and limited evidence to guide therapy. This study aimed to evaluate the association between antibiotic regimens and 30-day mortality in DTR S. maltophilia ICU-acquired pneumonia. We conducted a multicenter, international, retrospective study across 31 centers in eight countries, including all adult patients with DTR S. maltophilia ICU-acquired pneumonia treated with ≥24 hours of an in vitro-active antibiotic. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included clinical cure and a composite of 30-day survival with clinical cure. Each agent was analyzed as a separate exposure using modified Poisson regression with robust variance in a day-3 landmark cohort. Combination therapy and treatment duration were evaluated using overlap weighting. A total of 119 patients were included. Thirty-day mortality was 37.8%. Tigecycline was associated with higher 30-day mortality (aRR 1.95, 95% CI 1.21-3.13). Aztreonam/ceftazidime-avibactam showed a favorable but non-significant trend toward lower mortality (aRR 0.38, 95% CI 0.12-1.15), as did colistin (aRR 0.51, 95% CI 0.22-1.20). No agent other than tigecycline was significantly associated with any outcome, and the active agents had wide, overlapping confidence intervals. Neither combination therapy nor a treatment duration longer than 8 days was associated with any outcome. Tigecycline was associated with excess mortality and should be used with caution. Aztreonam/ceftazidime-avibactam and colistin trended toward lower mortality, whereas the other agents, including cefiderocol, appeared neutral. The study is underpowered to separate the active agents, and these hypothesis-generating findings require prospective confirmation.

42988224.title: The evolution of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in Greek intensive care units is driven by local carbapenemase acquisition, nationwide nosocomial spread and emerging resistance to novel antimicrobials.
42988224.abstract: We investigated transmission patterns and therapeutic options for Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CR-Kp) in Greek ICUs. CR-Kp isolates (N=271) were prospectively collected from patients in 17 Greek ICUs between 2021-2023 (INCREASE study, funded by Pfizer). Susceptibility profiles were determined by broth microdilution and genomes sequenced with Oxford Nanopore. All isolates produced carbapenemases: 48% KPC, 20% NDM, 4.4% VIM, 27.6% multi-carbapenemase producers. Resistance to carbapenems, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, and co-trimoxazole exceeded 90%, except for amikacin (73.4%) and colistin (46.5%). Aztreonam-avibactam and cefepime-zidebactam showed the highest susceptibility, 94.5% and 91.6% respectively, yet resistance was >10% among multi-carbapenemase producers. High levels of resistance to cefiderocol (41.7%) and cefepime-taniborbactam (21.4%) were detected. Aztreonam-avibactam resistance co-occurred with VEB-25 and a novel VEB variant. Predominant sequence types included ST39 (28.1%), ST11 (22.7%), and ST258 (18.4%). Time-scaled phylogenies demonstrated that following CG importation CR-Kp often acquired multiple carbapenemases. Over 88% of isolates were implicated in transmission clusters involving 1-8 ICUs across the country. In Greek ICUs, CR-Kp appears to emerge via local plasmid acquisition and then spread within and between hospitals. While aztreonam-avibactam and cefepime-zidebactam remain promising treatment options, resistance among multi-carbapenemase producers and diagnostic gaps (notably for VEB variants) are concerning.

42985594.title: Incidence, Predictors, and Clinical Outcomes of Acute Kidney Injury in Critically Ill Patients: A Retrospective Study.
42985594.abstract: Background Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication among critically ill patients and is associated with prolonged hospitalization, increased need for organ support, and higher mortality. Objective The objective of the study is to determine the incidence of AKI among critically ill patients, identify its independent predictors, and evaluate its association with major clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective observational study was conducted at Services Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, from June 2023 to June 2026 and included 261 adult critically ill patients. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, clinical severity scores, laboratory parameters, treatment-related factors, and clinical outcomes were extracted from medical records. Results AKI developed in 102 of 261 patients, corresponding to an incidence of 39.1%. Among patients with AKI, 42 (41.2%) had Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) stage 1, 34 (33.3%) had stage 2, and 26 (25.5%) had stage 3 disease. Compared with patients without AKI, those with AKI had higher intensive care unit (ICU) mortality (35 (34.3%) vs. 19 (11.9%)), in-hospital mortality (41 (40.2%) vs. 24 (15.1%)), and renal replacement therapy requirement (21 (20.6%) vs. 0 (0.0%)), as well as longer ICU and hospital stays and longer duration of mechanical ventilation (all p < 0.001). Factors independently associated with AKI included chronic kidney disease (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 3.12, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.34-7.28), vasopressor support at ICU admission (aOR 2.86, 95% CI 1.49-5.50), sepsis or septic shock (aOR 2.74, 95% CI 1.48-5.08), mechanical ventilation at ICU admission (aOR 2.09, 95% CI 1.08-4.04), increasing serum lactate (aOR 1.31, 95% CI 1.10-1.57), higher Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score (aOR 1.09, 95% CI 1.04-1.14), and increasing age (aOR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.05). Conclusion AKI affected more than one-third of critically ill patients and was associated with a greater observed clinical burden, including higher mortality, greater need for renal replacement therapy, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and longer ICU and hospital stays. Chronic kidney disease, sepsis or septic shock, vasopressor support at ICU admission, mechanical ventilation at ICU admission, higher serum lactate, higher APACHE II score, and increasing age were independently associated with AKI. Because clinical outcome comparisons were unadjusted, the observed differences in mortality, mechanical ventilation duration, and length of stay do not establish AKI as an independent determinant of these outcomes.

42985256.title: The frequency of coinfections in patients with coronavirus disease 2019 in intensive care units: Meta-analysis.
42985256.journal: Journal of research in medical sciences : the official journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
42985256.abstract: Patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID19) who require intensive care are vulnerable to additional infectious complications during hospitalization. This review evaluated the frequency and microbiological profile of coinfections reported in intensive care unit (ICU)admitted patients with COVID19. A systematic search was performed in electronic databases for studies published between December 1, 2019, and January 31, 2021. Eligible studies were assessed using the National Institutes of Health quality assessment tools. Quantitative analyses were conducted with Stata version 17. Among 160 retrieved records, 74 studies were eligible for qualitative synthesis, while 42 items provided sufficient data for metaanalysis. The pooled prevalence of coinfection was 35%. Bacterial infections were estimated at 12%, fungal infections at 11%, and viral infections at 5%, while mixedpathogen infections accounted for 16%. Coinfection was more frequent in men than women, with pooled estimates of 69% and 31%, respectively (P < 0.001). No significant association was detected between age and coinfection prevalence (P = 0.65). In ICUtreated patients with COVID19, bacterial pathogens were the leading cause of coinfection, followed by fungal and viral agents. These findings support careful microbiological evaluation in critically ill patients, particularly when clinical deterioration occurs. Early pathogen identification may help guide antimicrobial therapy, reduce unnecessary broadspectrum treatment, and improve clinical outcomes.

42984549.title: Eight-Year Surveillance of Candida albicans Bloodstream Infections in an ICU in Turkey.
42984549.abstract: Although the distribution of Candida species has shifted over the past three decades, Candida albicans remains the leading cause of nosocomial bloodstream infections. This study examined the genetic diversity and antifungal susceptibility of 174 independent C. albicans bloodstream isolates obtained from intensive care unit patients in Turkey. Microsatellite analysis across five loci identified 21 allelic genotypes for elongation factor 3 (CEF3), 12 for carbonic anhydrase III (CAIII), 11 for LOC4, 11 for zinc finger transcription factor-1 (ZNF1), and 9 for killer toxin-resistance protein-6 (KRE6). The multiplex analysis yielded 104 different multi-loci allelic combinations for the 174 strains analyzed, resulting in a discriminatory power of 0.98. Locus-by-locus microsatellite analysis revealed that certain C. albicans strains from the intensive care unit shared identical genotypes. The geometric mean minimum inhibitory concentrations of antifungal agents, in ascending order, were 0.02 mg/L for itraconazole, voriconazole, and posaconazole, 0.03 mg/L for anidulafungin, 0.13 mg/L for caspofungin, 0.20 mg/L for flucytosine, 0.62 mg/L for fluconazole, and 0.67 mg/L for amphotericin B. Findings showed considerable genetic diversity among bloodstream C. albicans isolates, while antifungal resistance remained uncommon. No significant association was observed between antifungal susceptibility and the genotypes analyzed. The presence of identical genotypes among certain strains points to an endogenous origin and a potential common source of infection within the hospital, warranting further investigation.

42983576.title: Assessing vascular barrier permeability in critically ill patients: what are we really measuring?
42983576.abstract: Perturbation of vascular barrier permeability is a central mechanism in the pathophysiology of critical illness, contributing to tissue edema, impaired oxygen diffusion, and organ dysfunction. Despite advances in the field, direct bedside assessment of vascular permeability remains unavailable. Current approaches rely on indirect and compartment-specific surrogates, raising important questions about what is actually being measured. This narrative review summarizes the physiological principles underlying vascular barrier function and its disruption in conditions such as sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and major surgery. Currently available bedside tools used to assess vascular permeability or its consequences are critically appraised, including clinical examination, ultrasonography, transpulmonary thermodilution, bioelectrical impedance analysis, circulating biomarkers of endothelial injury (e.g., glycocalyx degradation products, angiopoietin-2), and albumin kinetics-based methods. While these techniques provide valuable insights, they predominantly reflect downstream consequences such as tissue edema, intravascular volume shifts, or endothelial activation rather than permeability itself. In addition, vascular permeability is a dynamic, context-dependent, and organ-specific process influenced by inflammatory, hemodynamic, and therapeutic factors, further complicating its interpretation. Each method therefore captures only a partial dimension of vascular barrier dysfunction, with important limitations related to specificity, feasibility, validation and standardization. No single bedside tool currently provides a comprehensive assessment of vascular permeability in critically ill patients. A multimodal approach integrating clinical evaluation, imaging, hemodynamic monitoring, and biomarkers is required to better characterize vascular barrier dysfunction. Future research should focus on validating composite indices and developing reliable, real-time bedside tools capable of directly assessing vascular permeability, with the ultimate goal of improving risk stratification and guiding personalized therapeutic strategies.

42987229.title: Postoperative Neuromuscular Paresis and Overlap Syndrome Related to Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Case Report.
42987229.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can cause rare, severe immune-related adverse events. ICI-related overlap syndrome of myositis, myocarditis, and myasthenia gravis (3M) is uncommon yet carries high morbidity and mortality. We report a case with postoperative ICI-induced 3M syndrome that developed extremity paresis following proximal humerus resection and reconstruction. His clinical course was complicated by respiratory failure and septic shock, requiring intensive care. He was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin, corticosteroids, and plasmapheresis, leading to gradual recovery. This case highlights a rare postoperative presentation of 3M syndrome and underscores the importance of early recognition and prompt management.

42983154.title: Bedside endoscopy for significant acute upper gastrointestinal bleed.
42983154.journal: Indian journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Indian Society of Gastroenterology
42983154.abstract: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (AUGIB) is a frequent life-threatening scenario in everyday clinical practice. We undertook a study to assess the etiology and important clinical outcomes in patients with significant AUGIB unstable for transfer to an endoscopy suite. This is a prospective observational study conducted between December 2019 and December 2022, including patients above the age of 16 years with a history of clinically significant AUGIB undergoing bedside endoscopy in an intensive care (ICU)/high dependency unit (HDU) setting. Seventy patients with a mean age (SD) of 51.27 (13.45) years were included. The initial mean (SD) hemoglobin, APACHE score, SOFA score and GCS of these patients were 6.71 (2.14) g%, 20.3 (8.3), 8.28 (4.64) and 10.9 (4.68), respectively. The major causes for AUGIB were portal hypertension in 28 (40%) and peptic ulcer disease in 24 (34.2%) patients. Eight patients (19.5%) experienced rebleed. Radiological intervention was needed for three patients (4.3%) and surgery for two (2.9%) patients. Overall, 30-day mortality was 54.2%. AUGIB, per se, was the cause for mortality in only 21% of those who died. Sepsis, respiratory failure and liver failure were the factors that independently predicted 30-day mortality. This is the first study specifically looking at the role of bedside endoscopy in AUGIB among South Asian patients. The most common etiologies of AUGIB in our cohort were portal hypertension and peptic ulcer disease. Rebleed, surgery and 30-day mortality rates were 19.5%, 2.9% and 54.2%, respectively. A majority of the deaths were due to underlying co-morbidities.

42981604.title: A Volatilomics Approach for the Identification of Volatile Organic Compounds as Biomarkers of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia Using GC-MS.
42981604.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a common and serious complication of patients at intensive care units (ICUs), contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Current diagnostic approaches for VAP rely on clinical, radiological, and invasive methods, which are time-consuming, carry risks, and may result in delayed or inconclusive findings. The need for rapid, reliable, and non-invasive diagnostic tools is critical. Biomarkers and specifically volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath have emerged as promising candidates for this purpose. In this study, we applied gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) with solid-phase microextraction (SPME) to analyze breath VOC profiles in critically ill children and explore their potential as early indicators of VAP. Results reveal significant challenges in breath volatilomics, including batch effects and variability in VOC detection. However, normalization strategies allowed for meaningful comparisons across multiple time points, revealing subtle trends in VOC profiles that could differentiate patients with high and low suspicion of VAP. Notably, VOCs such as octanol and benzyl alcohol showed reduced levels in patients with higher suspicion of VAP at Day 6, suggesting potential associations with respiratory infection severity. While preliminary, these findings support further investigation into breath-based VOC signatures as a non-invasive, early diagnostic tool for VAP in pediatric ICUs. This approach could enhance diagnostic accuracy and inform timely clinical decisions, improving patient outcomes.

42980831.title: Systemic corticosteroids in critical illness: an evidence-based framework for clinical decision-making.
42980831.abstract: Systemic corticosteroids are pivotal in managing inflammation-driven critical illnesses, yet bedside translation remains inconsistent. This systematic review establishes an evidence-based framework for clinical decision-making by horizontally synthesizing contemporary evidence across severe community-acquired pneumonia (sCAP), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and septic shock. A systematic electronic search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library up to early 2026. Peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials (RCTs), systematic reviews, and meta-analyses published in English were eligible. Data regarding population characteristics, dosing regimens, initiation timing, duration, and safety profiles were independently extracted and qualitatively synthesized. Landmark trials define context-dependent efficacy: early hydrocortisone continuous infusion significantly reduces 28-day mortality in sCAP (CAPE COD), while a 10-day dexamethasone regimen improves ventilator-free days and survival in moderate-to-severe ARDS (DEXA-ARDS). In septic shock, early hydrocortisone-fludrocortisone combination accelerates shock resolution and lowers 90-day mortality (APROCCHS). These outcomes align with distinct pharmacological profiles: hydrocortisone provides dual glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid activity to restore vascular tone, whereas dexamethasone exerts potent transrepression of proinflammatory transcription factors. To mitigate steroid-induced harm, protocolized safety targets are essential, including maintaining blood glucose at 140-180 mg/dL and actively monitoring for secondary infections. Corticosteroids do not exert a uniform class effect. Bedside success requires personalized, protocolized regimens optimized by scenario-specific timing, dosing, and proactive adverse-event monitoring.

42988561.title: Descending Necrotizing Mediastinitis After Thyroidectomy.
42988561.abstract: Thyroidectomy is a commonly performed endocrine procedure with generally low complication rates. Descending necrotizing mediastinitis (DNM) is an exceptionally rare but life-threatening complication resulting from cervical infections that spread into the mediastinum. DNM following thyroid surgery has been reported only rarely. We analyzed retrospectively five patients who developed DNM following thyroid surgery between 2023 and 2025 at two tertiary centers. The patients' demographics, comorbidities, surgical procedures, clinical presentation, imaging, microbiology, treatment, complications, and outcomes were reviewed. The diagnosis was based on clinical and radiological evidence of cervicomediastinal infection, with operative confirmation in the four patients who underwent surgical drainage. A literature review was conducted using PubMed, MEDLINE, and Embase. The case series included four women and one man (age 35-68, mean 53.8 years). All patients had at least one comorbidity, including obesity, cardiovascular or respiratory disease, immune compromise, and chronic nicotine use. Surgical procedures included total thyroidectomy (n = 3) and hemithyroidectomy (n = 2). Symptoms developed 2-10 days postoperatively, including cervical pain, swelling, fever, dysphagia, dyspnea, tachycardia, and subcutaneous emphysema. Contrast-enhanced (CT) of the neck and chest demonstrated findings consistent with DNM in all patients, with operative confirmation in the four patients requiring surgical drainage. Microbiological analyses identified Streptococcus pyogenes in three patients and Streptococcus pneumoniae in one patient. Concomitant methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) was isolated in one of the patients with S. pyogenes, while an additional patient had a positive rapid Group A Streptococcus test without confirmatory culture. Treatment included cervical drainage (n = 4), thoracic intervention (n = 2), tracheal repair (n = 1), and ICU admission (n = 4). Complications included acute kidney failure, septic shock, pleural/pericardial effusions, pulmonary embolism, and cardiac arrest. All patients survived with hospital stays ranging 7 to 42 days (median 21). Although the acute infectious process resolved in all patients, some required rehabilitation and one experienced long-term disability affecting daily activities and work capacity. DNM after thyroidectomy is rare but potentially life-threatening. Early recognition, contrast-enhanced CT, prompt surgical drainage, and broad-spectrum antibiotics are essential. Awareness of predisposing factors and vigilant postoperative monitoring improves outcomes.

42988424.title: Which barriers and solutions do (psycho-)medical providers perceive at the interface of acute care, rehabilitation and aftercare of patients with sepsis? An interdisciplinary online focus group study in Germany.

42986805.title: Compliance with the 2021 surviving sepsis campaign Hour-1 Bundle and impact on patient outcomes in a resource-limited setting: A quality improvement initiative in a referral hospital in Rwanda.
42986805.abstract: Sepsis and septic shock are common life-threatening conditions associated with high mortality globally. Compliance with the Society of Critical Care Medicine's Hour-1 Bundle for sepsis management has the potential to improve outcome, but the bundle is infrequently applied in resource-constrained settings. We assessed level of compliance with the Hour-1 bundle among patients diagnosed with sepsis and septic shock at the Accident and Emergency Department (AED) or Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of University Teaching Hospital of Butare, Rwanda. We conducted training for nurses and doctors in the AED and ICU, with the goal of improving compliance. We re-assessed bundle compliance one month after the training. We used univariate and multivariate analyses to evaluate the association of compliance and fluid resuscitation with hospital mortality while adjusting for severity of illness and other covariates. Our finding showed that seventy-eight patients were enrolled during the pre-intervention period, and 82 in post-intervention. The overall compliance with at least 4 elements of the Hour-1 bundle before the intervention was 14%, and 76% after the intervention (p < 0.001). Mortality was lower in the post-intervention period than in the pre-intervention period (51.2% vs 74.4%; p = 0.003). Non-survivors had a significantly lower bundle compliance than survivors (35% vs 80%; adjusted OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.05-0.57; p = 0.004). Administered 2 liters of IV fluids and beyond during the first hour was independently associated with higher mortality (adjusted OR 19.38, 95% CI 5.63-66.75; p < 0.001). Findings from this Quality Improvement project suggest that compliance with the Hour-1 sepsis bundle in a resource-constrained setting can be improved with training, can improve outcome.. Administration of ≥2 liters during the first hour in those was independently associated with a higher in-hospital mortality, although bundle-compliant resuscitation was not. More research is needed, both on the implementation of sepsis bundles in resource-constrained settings, to assess if all bundle elements are as effective in these settings as recommended in the international guidelines.

42986663.title: Beyond blood: a narrative review of advancements in saliva-based diagnostics.
42986663.abstract: Human whole saliva is an accessible, noninvasive biofluid reflecting systemic and oral physiology, offering a viable alternative to invasive venipuncture and its associated pre-analytical vulnerabilities (e.g. ex vivo glycolysis). This narrative review synthesizes salivary biomarkers across major clinical domains, focusing on glycemic control (glucose, 1,5-anhydroglucitol, α2-macroglobulin), cardiovascular risk indices (cTnI, hs-CRP, sAA), critical care and sepsis surveillance (IL-10, acute-phase proteins), endocrinology (free steroid hormones), infectious diseases (HIV, HCV, SARS-CoV-2), oncological liquid biopsy (exosomal miRNAs, ctDNA), and neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease (Aβ42, p-tau181, lactoferrin). Analytical modalities - ranging from high-sensitivity immunoassays to wearable electrochemical biosensors and mass spectrometry - are critically evaluated. Furthermore, this review delineates regulatory-cleared diagnostic platforms (FDA PMA/510(k), EUA, CE-IVD, and SAMHSA-certified panels for viral antibodies, late-night salivary cortisol, and toxicology) from emerging discovery-phase panels. Widespread clinical translation remains constrained by unstandardized collection protocols, oral matrix interference, and a lack of normative reference intervals. Transitioning salivary testing into mainstream diagnostics requires three priorities: (1) universal sampling standardization incorporating flow-rate normalization, (2) engineering matrix-matched biosensors tailored for sub-picomolar detection, and (3) rigorous multicenter prospective trials to validate definitive clinical cutoffs, dynamic blood-saliva correlation kinetics, and digital point-of-care integration.

42985457.title: Association Between Platelet Count/Lactate Dehydrogenase Ratio and In-Hospital Mortality in the Patients With Sepsis-Induced Myocardial Injury.
42985457.abstract: Sepsis-induced myocardial injury (SIMI) is a severe complication with high mortality, yet effective prognostic prediction tools remain limited. Although platelet-derived indices have been explored in SIMI, these metrics primarily reflect systemic inflammation rather than the extent of myocardial injury or metabolic status. We retrospectively analyzed 3071 critically ill individuals with SIMI admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) General Hospital between January 2020 and October 2025. The association between the platelet count (PLT)/lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) ratio and in-hospital mortality was assessed using multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Subgroup analyses evaluated consistency across clinically relevant strata. The PLT/LDH ratio was independently associated with lower in-hospital mortality (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.44, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.34-0.57, p < 0.001). Compared with the lowest tertile, the highest tertile of PLT/LDH ratio was associated with a 67% reduction in risk (HR = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.25-0.43, p < 0.001). The PLT/LDH ratio demonstrated modest, statistically significant incremental discriminative performance over PLT or LDH alone (both p < 0.05). A nonlinear relationship was observed, with an inflection point at approximately 0.306 (p for nonlinearity < 0.0001). Subgroup analyses revealed a consistent association across all subgroups, with significant interactions for sex, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and liver disease (all p for interaction < 0.05). The PLT/LDH ratio is independently associated with in-hospital mortality in patients with SIMI. It may serve as a simple and practical tool for prognostic prediction in patients with SIMI upon ICU admission.

42983655.title: Urinary kidney injury molecule-1 as a diagnostic biomarker for persistent severe acute kidney injury: a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.
42983655.abstract: Despite the vast amount of literature dedicated to biomarkers and acute kidney injury (AKI), the persistent state of AKI has been relatively neglected. The objective of this study was to systematically review relevant studies and evaluate the diagnostic value of urinary kidney injury molecule 1 (uKIM-1) for persistent severe AKI in adults. We searched the PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials databases up to December 2025. Eligible studies included adult patients and assessed the diagnostic value of uKIM-1 for persistent severe AKI. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) was used for quality assessment. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, area under the curve (AUC) and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) values were calculated via a Bayesian bivariate diagnostic meta-analysis model. Eight studies with 2349 patients were selected for meta-analysis. 378 patients were diagnosed with persistent severe AKI.
