Across 190 unique device placements, zero device-related adverse events were observed (adverse event rate 0%; 95% CI upper bound 1.6%, rule of three). In the thrombocytopenic subgroup (n=47), zero device-related adverse events were observed (95% CI upper bound 6.4%). No device-related mucosal bleeding, perforation, ulceration, necrosis, or device malfunction requiring intervention was documented. The device achieved 100% successful fecal diversion, with no major leakage event (defined as stool output requiring linen replacement) recorded. The per-assessment leakage rate was 1.7% (11 positive assessments out of 646 total), all representing minor peripheral moisture requiring only topical hygiene management with no linen change. Daily nursing time with ASM was 6.8 minutes per patient per day; contextual comparison with published estimates of 120 minutes per patient per day (IBC protocol) and 174 minutes per patient per day (absorbent pad management) from Vargo et al. yields estimated differences of 94% and 96%, respectively, subject to methodological differences between datasets. Retrospective chart review identified no chemotherapy delays or ICU length of stay prolongation attributable to device-related complications. This early institutional experience with a novel pressure-free ASM across 190 unique oncology ICU placements, including 47 in patients with severe thrombocytopenia, was not associated with any observed device-related adverse event. These findings represent hypothesis-generating preliminary data and do not establish superiority over conventional devices. The clinical need for safe fecal management alternatives in thrombocytopenic oncology patients is substantive; these data provide rationale for appropriately powered prospective comparative trials.

42906252.title: Does transfusion of blood products increase the risk of multidrug-resistant infections in critically ill patients?
42906252.abstract: To investigate the association between transfusion of blood products during intensive care unit (ICU) stay and the incidence of ICU-acquired colonisation and infection with multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria (ICU-MDR-col, ICU-MDR-inf, respectively). Secondary analysis of two prospective multicentre cohort studies conducted in eight ICUs in France. Adult patients admitted to participating ICUs were enrolled consecutively from May 2019 to June 2021. All patients underwent systematic screening for colonisation with MDR bacteria at admission and weekly thereafter. Exposure to transfusion of blood products during ICU stay, including packed red blood cells (PRBCs), fresh frozen plasma (FFP) and platelet concentrates (PCs), was recorded. The primary outcome was the incidence of ICU-MDR-col and/or ICU-MDR-inf (ICU-MDR-col/inf) until ICU discharge, censored at day 28. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of ICU-MDR-col and ICU-MDR-inf, considered separately. Associations were assessed using mixed-effects Poisson regression models adjusted for prespecified confounders. Subgroup analyses were performed according to immunosuppression status at ICU admission. Among 1103 patients, 358 (32.5%) received transfusion of any blood product. Overall, 292 (26.5%) patients experienced at least one ICU-MDR-col/inf event. Transfusion was associated with an increased incidence of ICU-MDR-col/inf (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR] 1.31, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06-1.62; p = 0.013), mainly driven by ICU-MDR-inf (aIRR 1.62, 95% CI 1.16-2.24; p = 0.004), but not ICU-MDR-col considered individually. This association was restricted to PRBC transfusion. No significant heterogeneity was observed according to immunosuppression status. Transfusion of PBRCs was associated with an increased incidence of ICU-acquired MDR infections, with no significant heterogeneity observed according to immunosuppression status. These findings support a restrictive approach to transfusion and warrant further investigation into its immunological and ecological consequences in critically ill patients.

42894798.title: Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation in adult patients admitted to an intensive care unit.
42894798.abstract: Most existing recommendations for atrial fibrillation are derived from cardiology settings. However, atrial fibrillation is also highly prevalent among patients admitted to intensive care units and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Therefore, its management in this specific context warrants dedicated guidance. To address this need, The French Intensive Care Society has developed formalized expert recommendations using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology. Twenty-four questions addressing the management of atrial fibrillation were evaluated in adult patients admitted to intensive care units. Of these, twenty-one focused specifically on new-onset atrial fibrillation, one addressed pre-existing atrial fibrillation, and two were applicable to both conditions. The assessment encompassed the role of transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography, the management of potentially reversible triggers (optimization of fluid status, magnesium supplementation, serum potassium targets, and screening for thyroid dysfunction…), strategies for mitigating hemodynamic risk (indications and modalities for rhythm and rate control), and the management of thrombotic risk (indications, regimens, and duration of therapeutic anticoagulation). Eighteen recommendations were formulated, all of which achieved strong agreement among the expert panel. Only two recommendations were supported by a low level of evidence (GRADE 2+), whereas the remaining sixteen relied on evidence that could not be classified within the GRADE framework and were therefore issued as expert opinions. For six additional aspects of atrial fibrillation management, the experts concluded that the available evidence was insufficient to support the formulation of a reliable recommendation.

42892527.title: Octreotide Plus Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) versus PPI alone in Non-Variceal Upper gastrointestinal (GI) Bleeding in intensive care unit (ICU): A Multi-Center Randomized Trial.
42892527.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
42892527.abstract: To compare clinical outcomes between PPI therapy alone and PPI combined with octreotide in patients with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. This prospective, randomized, double-blind, multi-center study included 56 patients allocated to either PPI alone or PPI plus octreotide. Baseline demographics and comorbidities were comparable between groups. Laboratory parameters were assessed over three days. Clinical outcomes included rebleeding, transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation, surgical intervention, ICU stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Prothrombin time was significantly higher in the PPI plus octreotide group (median 19 s vs 11.1 s; p=0.001), and urine output was significantly lower (p=0.011). Despite these differences, there were no significant differences in rebleeding rates, blood product transfusion, ICU stay, mechanical ventilation, or need for surgery. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in the PPI plus octreotide group (39.3% vs 7%; p=0.011). Hospital length of stay was significantly shorter in the PPI plus octreotide group, likely reflecting higher early mortality rather than improved clinical recovery. The addition of octreotide to PPI therapy did not improve bleeding-related outcomes. Prolonged prothrombin time did not correlate with increased bleeding or transfusion needs. These findings suggest no clinical benefit of adjunctive octreotide in this study and underscore the importance of appropriate patient selection.

42889246.title: Tranexamic acid use and progression to clinically important bleeding in critically ill patients with non-clinically important non-variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding: a retrospective cohort study.
42889246.abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used to reduce bleeding in perioperative and hemorrhagic conditions, but its role in upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) remains controversial. This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated whether TXA use was associated with reduced progression to clinically important gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) in critically ill patients with non-clinically important non-variceal UGIB. Adult ICU patients who developed non-clinically important non-variceal UGIB between 2018 and 2022 were included. Among them, 154 patients receiving TXA within 24 h after bleeding onset (mean duration 1.71 ± 1.42 days; mean total dose 2.12 ± 2.36 g) were compared with 1,660 patients who received neither TXA nor other hemostatic agents. After propensity score matching, 154 matched pairs were analyzed. Progression to clinically important GIB did not differ significantly between the TXA and non- TXA groups before matching (5.8% vs. 5.7%; P=0.951, 95% CI: 0.450-1.707) or after matching (5.8% vs. 7.8%; P=0.664, 95% CI: 0.562-3.164); Exploratory univariate conditional logistic regression analysis showed that TXA use was not associated with this outcome (OR 1.333, 95% CI 0.562-3.164; P=0.514). In the matched cohort, TXA was not associated with significant differences in endoscopy requirement, transfusion requirement, hospital length of stay, in-hospital mortality, or thrombotic complications. Inverse probability of treatment weighting analysis yielded consistent results for the primary outcome (5.1% vs. 5.8%; P=0.418, 95% CI: 0.840-1.522). In critically ill patients with non-clinically important non-variceal UGIB, TXA use was not associated with a statistically detectable reduction in progression to clinically important GIB or improvements in major clinical outcomes. Routine empirical use of TXA in this population should be approached with caution.

42964650.title: Severe Thrombocytopenia Induced by Re-Exposure to Piperacillin/Tazobactam: A Case Report in Critically Ill Patient With COVID-19.
42964650.abstract: Drug-induced thrombocytopenia is a condition where certain medications can significantly reduce the platelets in the blood. This can increase the risk of bleeding and bruising. We reported a case of a 73-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities who was admitted to the hospital with COVID-19. Upon admission, the patient received multiple antibiotics, including Piperacillin/Tazobactam. In the following days, she developed severe thrombocytopenia upon re-exposure to Piperacillin/Tazobactam. Other causes of thrombocytopenia were systematically excluded. After discontinuing the Piperacillin/Tazobactam and administering intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), the thrombocytopenia resolved. A Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score was calculated and indicated a probable (i.e., 6 points) adverse drug reaction. This case underscores the importance of considering Piperacillin/Tazobactam as a potential cause of severe thrombocytopenia in critically ill patients, even in the presence of confounding factors such as COVID-19. To our knowledge, this is a rarely reported presentation in a patient with a recent COVID-19 infection. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between COVID-19 and drug-induced thrombocytopenia.

42963576.title: Platelet-containing systemic inflammatory indices show reduced prognostic discrimination in critically ill cirrhosis: a MIMIC-IV cohort study with external validation in eICU-CRD.
42963576.abstract: Complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices are increasingly used as prognostic markers in critical illness. Three of the commonest, the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), contain the platelet count, which in cirrhosis is determined largely by processes other than inflammation. They have not been compared head-to-head in critically ill cirrhosis. In a retrospective MIMIC-IV cohort of adults with cirrhosis in intensive care, six indices were derived from the first white cell differential within 24 h, and discrimination for in-hospital mortality was measured by the area under the ROC curve (AUC), with external validation in eICU. Because each platelet-containing index equals a platelet-free counterpart multiplied by the platelet count (e.g. SII = platelet × neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR]), testing that multiplication was the primary analysis, with the neutrophil count as a positive control. Of 2,227 patients, 627 (28.2%) died in hospital. NLR discriminated best (AUC 0.651) and the platelet-containing indices lowest (PLR 0.546). Multiplying by the platelet count degraded discrimination (NLR to SII, ΔAUC - 0.048; SIRI to PIV, - 0.038; both p < 0.001), whereas multiplying by the neutrophil count improved it (+ 0.093, p < 0.001), the change depending on which cell count was introduced. The platelet count alone discriminated no better than chance (AUC 0.522), added nothing to a model containing MELD-Na, OASIS, age, and sex (ΔAUC + 0.0003), and showed no independent association with mortality when entered separately. The ranking was reproduced externally (eICU, n = 800). The conventional platelet-containing indices did not outperform their platelet-free counterparts. Thrombocytopenia in critically ill cirrhosis is multifactorial and no direct measure of portal hypertension was available, so the reason cannot be established here. Incremental value over established severity scores was marginal for every index, and indices from other diseases require re-evaluation in cirrhosis before use.

42864674.title: Robotic-assisted versus conventional coronary artery bypass grafting: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and trial sequential analysis of 39,918 patients.
42864674.abstract: Robotic-assisted coronary artery bypass grafting (RA-CABG) is an evolving minimally invasive alternative to conventional CABG (C-CABG), but comparative evidence remains fragmented. We conducted a comprehensive systematic review, meta-analysis, and trial sequential analysis to compare outcomes between RA-CABG and C-CABG. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science through January 2026. Studies comparing RA-CABG to C-CABG reporting at least one outcome of interest were eligible. Random-effects meta-analyses using DerSimonian-Laird estimators were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I. Trial sequential analysis evaluated the conclusiveness of cumulative evidence. Nine studies comprising 39,918 patients (13,638 RA-CABG; 26,280 C-CABG) were included. All included studies were observational in design, and long-term outcome data were sparse. RA-CABG was associated with significantly lower mortality (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.43-0.69; P < 0.001; I²=0%), atrial fibrillation (OR 0.53; P < 0.001), respiratory failure (OR 0.31; P < 0.001), blood transfusion (OR 0.28; P < 0.001), hospital length of stay (MD - 1.95 days; P < 0.001), and ICU stay (MD - 22.7 h; P < 0.001). Stroke showed a non-significant trend favoring RA-CABG (OR 0.76; P = 0.071). Trial sequential analysis confirmed conclusive evidence for mortality, atrial fibrillation, respiratory failure, and blood transfusion. Results were robust across sensitivity analyses. In this meta-analysis of observational studies, RA-CABG was associated with significantly improved short-term outcomes compared to C-CABG across multiple endpoints, with conclusive statistical evidence for four of seven binary outcomes. However, all included studies were observational, and these associations should be interpreted with caution given potential residual confounding and case-selection bias. Multicenter randomized trials with long-term follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

42859575.title: Severe Colchicine Toxicity After Ingestion of a Dose Below Traditionally Reported Lethal Levels: A Case Report.
42859575.abstract: Colchicine is a widely utilised drug for the management of conditions such as gout, pericarditis and familial Mediterranean fever. It has a narrow therapeutic index, with a significant risk of toxicity in overdose leading to life-threatening consequences. We present a case of severe colchicine toxicity following ingestion of 20 mg (0.26 mg/kg), resulting in multi-organ failure requiring intensive care management. Rapid deterioration with hyperthermia, electrolyte derangement, rhabdomyolysis, coagulopathy and significant bone marrow suppression necessitated IV antibiotics, platelet transfusion and granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (GCSF) and subsequent admission to critical care for vasopressors and ventilatory support. The patient eventually improved with resolution of haematological and renal parameters, was reviewed by the mental health team and discharged with full functional recovery. This case underscores the importance of early recognition, aggressive supportive care, and multidisciplinary management of patients presenting with colchicine overdose, in order to achieve a favourable outcome. The unpredictable relationship between colchicine dose and clinical outcome highlights the need for close monitoring even following relatively low-dose ingestion. Increased clinician awareness of colchicine toxicity and its delayed manifestations is essential for timely intervention in such critical cases.

42846634.title: Rotational Thromboelastometry (ROTEM)-Guided Assessment of Hemorrhagic Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation in Septic Shock: A Case Report of Purpura Fulminans and Multiorgan Failure.
42846634.abstract: Sepsis-associated coagulopathy may progress rapidly from early thromboinflammation to overt disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) with mixed thrombotic and hemorrhagic manifestations. We report the case of a 30-year-old man with a history of methamphetamine use who presented after generalized tonic-clonic seizure activity, severe neurological impairment, hypoxemia, shock, and suspected sepsis. Initial evaluation showed severe metabolic derangement, acute kidney injury, aspiration risk during airway management, and suspected central nervous system infection. During intensive care unit evolution, the patient developed refractory septic shock, severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, rhabdomyolysis, recurrent hypoglycemia, profound mixed acidosis, anuric acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy, progressive thrombocytopenia, gastrointestinal bleeding, airway bleeding, catheter-site bleeding, and rapidly progressive violaceous bullous and necrotic skin lesions compatible with purpura fulminans. Clinical and laboratory findings were consistent with overt DIC with a prominent hemorrhagic phenotype. Serial rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM) assessment demonstrated progressive coagulation failure, with late fibrin-based thromboelastometry (FIBTEM) findings showing severely reduced fibrin-based clot firmness consistent with fibrinogen-dependent clot failure. Hemostatic management included fibrinogen replacement, blood component therapy, tranexamic acid, and local hemostatic measures. Despite invasive mechanical ventilation, dual vasopressor therapy, corticosteroids, antimicrobial therapy, bicarbonate therapy, continuous renal replacement therapy, and targeted hemostatic resuscitation, the patient progressed to irreversible shock and cardiac arrest without return of spontaneous circulation. This case highlights the value of integrating clinical bleeding phenotype, conventional coagulation testing, DIC scoring, and viscoelastic assessment in critically ill septic patients with rapidly evolving coagulopathy.

42951749.title: Perioperative Lactate, Survival, and Complications Following Lung Transplantation.
42951749.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42951749.abstract: To examine perioperative lactate and its association with survival and postoperative complications following lung transplantation (LTx). Single-center retrospective cohort study. Academic tertiary-care transplant center. Adult patients undergoing LTx between February 2018 and January 2023. None. Serum lactate was measured at 6-hour intervals from the start of surgery, and the maximum value within the first 0 to 6 hours was recorded. Patients were categorized into the high-lactate group (upper quartile, ≥4.2 mmol/L) and low-lactate group (lower 3 quartiles). Primary outcomes were 1-year and overall survival. Secondary outcomes included renal failure, venous thromboembolism (VTE), primary graft dysfunction grade 3 (PGD3), mechanical ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and post-transplant length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Among 225 recipients (median age, 62.3 years; 34.2% female), high lactate was not associated with 1-year or overall survival. However, recipients with high lactate had higher rates of PGD3 at 72 hours (42.1% v 13.1%, p < 0.001), longer mechanical ventilation duration (3 days v 2 days, p = 0.003), longer ICU stay (11.6 days v 7 days, p = 0.013), and higher in-hospital mortality rate (7% v 0.6%, p = 0.019). No significant differences were observed in renal failure, VTE, or post-transplant length of stay. Elevated perioperative serum lactate was associated with PGD3 at 72 hours, prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer ICU stay, and in-hospital mortality but not 1-year or overall survival following LTx. These findings suggest that perioperative lactate may aid in identifying high-risk patients early in their postoperative course despite its lack of association with long-term survival.

42948114.title: Left atrial pressure continuous monitoring improves early postoperative outcomes after double-lung transplantation for pulmonary hypertension.
42948114.abstract: Double-lung transplantation (DLTx) has become the treatment of choice for patients with end-stage pulmonary hypertension (PH). However, DLTx remains a demanding procedure, associated with a greater incidence of severe primary graft dysfunction (PGD) compared with other indications. PH-induced cardiac remodeling includes diastolic left heart dysfunction, which may increase the risk of PGD. We hypothesized that continuous monitoring of left atrial pressure (LAP) could improve early outcomes. We retrospectively reviewed the chart of patients who underwent DLTx for PH between 2015 and 2022. The use of postoperative LAP monitoring was left to the discretion of the attending transplant surgeon. A total of 135 patients underwent DLTx for PH. Among them, 72 were managed either with prophylactic postoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or with ECMO weaning guided by transesophageal echocardiography and Swan-Ganz catheter, whereas 63 underwent systematic ECMO weaning after the placement of a LAP catheter maintained for 3 to 5 days. Both groups were comparable regarding age, PH diagnoses, and disease severity. The LAP group showed significantly less postoperative ECMO use (25% vs 83%, P < .001), shorter duration of mechanical ventilation (5 days [2-13] vs 17.5 days [7-35], P < .001), shorter stay in the intensive care unit (10 days [6-25] vs 28 days [14-49], P < .001), and lower rates of bleeding, groin infection, and overall complications (P ≤ .05). Intraoperative red blood cell transfusion was identified as an independent predictor of LAP monitoring strategy failure. Ninety-day postoperative mortality was not significantly different between groups (1.5% vs 8.3%, P = .12). Continuous postoperative monitoring of LAP after DLTx for PH was associated with improved early outcomes. This strategy may help reduce the incidence of severe postoperative complications in this high-risk population.

42947228.title: The impact of prior asymptomatic COVID-19 infection on outcomes following coronary bypass surgery.
42947228.abstract: The optimal timing and expected postoperative course of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) after asymptomatic coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remain uncertain. Evidence guiding cardiac surgical practice has largely been extrapolated from mixed surgical cohorts or broader cardiac surgery series rather than from isolated CABG populations. This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults who underwent isolated CABG during 2021-2022. Patients with documented asymptomatic preoperative SARS-CoV-2 infection were compared with patients without documented prior COVID-19. Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative variables were extracted from institutional records. Outcomes included early clinical recovery, respiratory support, transfusion exposure, laboratory trajectories, and mortality. A timing subgroup analysis (< 4 weeks vs >= 4 weeks from infection to surgery) was prespecified as exploratory. Seventy-six patients met eligibility criteria: 37 with prior asymptomatic COVID-19 and 39 without documented prior COVID-19. The cohort was predominantly male (81.6%), low risk by EuroSCORE II, and largely elective. Baseline demographics, major comorbidities, ventricular function, operative priority, number of grafted vessels, cardiopulmonary bypass time, cross-clamp time, extubation time, intensive care unit stay, hospital stay, oxygen requirement, and transfusion exposure were similar between groups. Postoperative complications were more frequent in the prior-COVID group (16.2% vs 0.0%; risk difference 16.2%, 95% CI 3.8-31.1%; P = 0.011), whereas mortality remained rare and not significantly different (2.7% vs 0.0%; P = 0.487). Longitudinal laboratory analyses showed expected perioperative inflammatory and hematologic changes within both groups, without consistent between-group separation. In the exploratory timing subgroup, no statistically significant differences were detected between earlier and later surgery, but this analysis was markedly underpowered. In this single-center exploratory cohort of predominantly elective, low-risk CABG patients, prior asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection was not associated with a generalized worsening of early postoperative recovery, although postoperative complications were more frequent in the exposed group. These data are insufficient to inform CABG timing recommendations after asymptomatic infection and should not be extrapolated to unstable or higher-risk patients. Larger multicenter studies with better exposure characterization, vaccination data, and longer follow-up are required.

42945812.title: Injury patterns and early operative demand in a combined military and civilian casualty cohort: A single-centre study from the first 11 weeks of the 2023 Israel-Hamas war.
42945812.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
42945812.abstract: Modern asymmetric warfare and large-scale terror attacks produce distinctive wounding patterns that differ from conventional state-on-state conflict and impose specific early demands on receiving trauma systems. The 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel and the ensuing war generated a compressed surge of combined civilian and military casualties. We characterized injury patterns and linked them to early in-hospital resource use at a single tertiary trauma centre across the opening weeks of the conflict. We performed a retrospective descriptive cohort study of 192 consecutive trauma casualties admitted between 7 October and 24 December 2023. Demographics, mechanism of injury, injured anatomical regions, Injury Severity Score (ISS) and acute interventions were abstracted from the institutional trauma dataset. Mechanism and anatomical categories were not mutually exclusive. Variables were summarised as medians (IQR) or counts (percentages); missing data were not imputed and percentages were computed over non-missing observations. Casualties were young (median age 24 years, IQR 21-35) and predominantly male (84.4%). Penetrating (43.2%) and shrapnel (31.2%) mechanisms predominated, followed by acoustic trauma (12.0%). Extremities were most often injured (lower limb 41.7%, upper limb 35.4%); 68.8% had at least one extremity injury and 37.0% had two or more injured regions. Median ISS was 9 (IQR 4-16); 26.5% of those with a recorded ISS had ISS ≥16. Blast and crush carried the highest median ISS (25 and 16). Early resource use was substantial: 23.4% required emergency surgery via direct emergency-room-to-operating-room transfer, 10.9% mechanical ventilation and 5.2% packed red-cell transfusion. This extremity-predominant, penetrating-and-shrapnel profile, with a small but disproportionately severe blast and crush subgroup and frequent acoustic trauma, translated into early demand for emergency surgery, ventilation and transfusion. These patterns support resourcing limb-salvage and damage-control surgery, blood-bank and intensive-care readiness, and audiologic follow-up in military and mass-casualty trauma planning.

42945027.title: Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: feasibility, practical benefits, and surgical pitfalls from a single-center experience.
42945027.abstract: To describe surgical outcomes, technical considerations, and feasibility of redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery using initial cases as a reference cohort. A single-center, retrospective review of minimally invasive mitral valve surgery performed between January 2014 and January 2024 was conducted. Perioperative data, mid-term survival, and cardiac-related events were assessed in both initial and redo groups. A total of 647 patients were included: 30 in the redo group and 617 in the initial group. The redo group had higher European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II scores (p < 0.001). In the redo group, 26 (86.7%) had undergone previous cardiac surgery via sternotomy, and 18 (60.0%) had previous mitral valve surgery. The operative time was longer in the redo group (p = 0.041), while the cross-clamping time was longer in the initial group (p = 0.019), and cardiopulmonary bypass time was comparable between groups (p = 0.95). Intubation time (p = 0.049), intensive care unit stay (p = 0.020), and in-hospital stay (p = 0.003) were longer in the redo group. However, there were no significant differences in postoperative chest tube output for 24 h (p = 0.32) or blood transfusion requirements (p = 0.087). The overall survival rates at 5 years were 70.7% (95% CI: 41.0%-87.0%) vs. 92.0% (95% CI: 88.0%-94.0%) for the redo and initial groups, respectively. Freedom from cardiac-related events did not significantly differ between groups. Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery was feasible despite higher surgical risk and longer operative times. Early and mid-term cardiac-related outcomes appeared acceptable, although overall survival was lower in redo cases.

42910620.title: Venous Thromboembolism in Acute Necrotizing Pancreatitis Is Associated With Worse Outcomes, With Subtype-Specific Patterns: A Nationwide Analysis, 2016-2022.
42910620.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) complicates acute necrotizing pancreatitis (ANP), but outcomes across extra-splanchnic deep vein thrombosis (DVT), portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and splenic vein thrombosis (SVT) remain poorly defined. We evaluated national trends and in-hospital outcomes in ANP with versus without VTE and across VTE subtypes. Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), adults hospitalized with principal ANP were identified. Secondary diagnosis codes captured VTE subtypes. Primary analyses compared mortality and major complications in ANP with versus without VTE; secondary analyses compared outcomes by subtype. Among 110,225 ANP hospitalizations, 12.25% had VTE. ANP with VTE had higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.89, P<0.001), longer length of stay (adjusted mean difference 10.7 d, P<0.001), and higher hospitalization charges (adjusted mean difference $151,685, P<0.001). VTE was associated with higher rates of mesenteric ischemia, gastric varices, upper GI bleeding, AKI, sepsis, shock, respiratory failure, ARDS, vasopressor use, mechanical ventilation, blood transfusion, and ICU admissions. On subtype analysis, DVT (aOR 2.39, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 1.45, P=0.001) were associated with higher mortality; SVT was not significantly associated with mortality, though the analysis was limited by few events. PVT was most strongly associated with mesenteric ischemia (aOR 8.28, P<0.001), whereas gastric varices were most associated with SVT (aOR 11.37, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 3.73, P<0.001). VTE in ANP was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, systemic complications, and resource utilization, with substantial heterogeneity across subtypes. DVT-associated ANP showed higher rates of systemic complications, whereas PVT and SVT showed distinct territory-specific vascular-complication patterns. Prospective studies should evaluate phenotype-specific anticoagulation strategies.

42966241.title: Province-wide assessment of emergency care capacity and skills in a rural provincial health system: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment in Battambang, Cambodia.
42966241.abstract: Emergency care capacity remains critically limited in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly in rural areas where specialists and infrastructure are scarce. In Cambodia, stroke and ischemic heart disease are leading causes of mortality, and trauma burdens are increasing alongside rapid infrastructure development. Evidence on emergency equipment availability and frontline provider skills at the facility level in rural provinces remains limited. A facility-based cross-sectional assessment was conducted across all seven public referral hospitals in Battambang Province, Cambodia, in January 2023. Emergency equipment availability was evaluated through structured interviews and direct visual confirmation against the World Health Organization (WHO) Guidelines for Essential Trauma Care. Clinical skill examinations were administered to physicians (two scenario-based cases: acute stroke with airway compromise; traumatic injury with tension pneumothorax and intra-abdominal bleeding) and nurses (a Basic Life Support [BLS] scenario assessed in pairs). Hospitals were stratified by Complementary Package of Activities (CPA) level: CPA1 (basic care only), CPA2 (including surgery and intensive care), and CPA3 (highest provincial level). At Complementary Package of Activities (CPA)1 (basic care only) hospitals, intubation equipment and 12-lead electrocardiogram were each available in only 25% of facilities. None had a crash cart, blood transfusion capacity, basic metabolic panel, or coagulation testing. In the stroke scenario, airway patency was confirmed by 28.6% of physicians at CPA1 hospitals, compared with 70.0% at CPA2 hospitals (including surgery and intensive care), 57.1% at the CPA3 hospital (highest provincial level), and 75.0% at the Provincial Health Department. In the trauma scenario, no physician at CPA1 hospitals correctly performed spinal immobilization with the spine kept straight or thoracentesis at the correct anatomical location. Among 38 nurse pairs, 97.4% initiated chest compressions promptly, but only 21.1% demonstrated correct compression technique, and 13.2% provided effective bag-valve-mask ventilation. Deficiencies in equipment and clinical skills were most pronounced at CPA1 hospitals. Emergency care capacity in Battambang Province was substantially limited, with the greatest deficiencies at CPA1 hospitals. Recurrent low-cost training and targeted strengthening of basic emergency care should be prioritized at lower-level facilities.

42959567.title: Pulmonary Endarterectomy After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty: A Single-Center USA Experience.
42959567.abstract: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) is the treatment of choice for operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), while balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is reserved for inoperable disease. However, operability is subjective and there are patients who may undergo BPA prior to PEA. It is not clear if prior BPA affects PEA outcomes. We present a series of patients from a single, high-volume, referral center who underwent PEA after prior BPA. CTEPH patients who underwent BPA prior to undergoing PEA at the University of California, San Diego between January 2013 and July 2025 were included. Post-PEA outcomes were compared to all PEA patients who did not have prior BPA from the year 2022. Twenty-one patients were identified. Average number of BPA sessions prior to PEA was 3.4 ± 2.1. The most common reason for initial BPA was distal disease deemed inoperable (43%). Average total circulatory arrest time was 61.5 ± 21.8 min, compared to 47.9 ± 19.3 min (p = 0.003) in the control PEA cases (n = 188). Post-operatively, the PEA after BPA cohort had longer ventilator days (p < 0.001), ICU days (p = 0.022) and post-operative length of stay (LOS) (p < 0.001); there were also higher rates of post-operative bleeding (p < 0.001) requiring transfusions (p = 0.033) and return to the operating room (p = 0.008). There was one death related to prior BPA complications despite adequate endarterectomy with improved hemodynamics. There was similar hemodynamic improvement post-operatively in both cohorts. Although prior BPA made PEA more challenging and increased select post-operative complications, it is not a contraindication for successful PEA.

42879511.title: Clinical features and outcomes of neuroleptospirosis in French Guiana: Insights from a retrospective study (2015-2021).
42879511.abstract: Leptospirosis is a re-emerging public health threat in French Guiana with a broad clinical spectrum. Neurological involvement (neuroleptospirosis) lacks a consensus definition and may be underrecognized. This study aimed to characterize its epidemiology, clinical features, outcomes, and associated factors. A multicenter retrospective study was conducted across healthcare facilities in French Guiana from 2015 to 2021. Consecutive hospital-managed patients with laboratory-confirmed or probable leptospirosis were included. Neuroleptospirosis was defined by neurological symptoms combined with objective cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and/or neuro-imaging abnormalities. Patients with and without neurological involvement were compared. Among 146 patients, 18 (12%) met the criteria for neuroleptospirosis, corresponding to a mean annual incidence of 0.88 cases/100,000 inhabitants (95% conference interval [CI], 0.52-1.39). Presentations were meningeal (78% [14/18]), encephalitic (17% [3/18]) or meningoencephalitic (6% [1/18]). Lumbar puncture was performed in 28/146 (19%) patients; pleocytosis was observed in 18/28 (64%). The median CSF leukocyte count was 42 cells/mm3 (interquartile range [IQR], 13-240 cells/mm3), with lymphocytic predominance in 8/13 differential counts (62%). CSF protein was mildly elevated (median, 0.51 g/L; IQR, 0.32-0.88), without hypoglycorrhachia. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed abnormalities in 2/8 patients with neuroleptospirosis: one cerebral infarction and one case of pachymeningitis. Age under 30 years (odds ratio [OR], 5.56; 95% CI, 1.72-18), absence of leukocytosis during hospitalization (OR, 3.29; 95% CI, 1.04-10.39), and absence of thrombocytopenia (OR, 4.46; 95% CI, 1.39-14.32) were associated with neuroleptospirosis. Under our diagnostic criteria, neuroleptospirosis cases were associated with favorable outcomes, with lower odds of sepsis (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.10-0.79), no intensive care unit admissions or deaths. This study clarifies the clinical spectrum and outcomes of neuroleptospirosis in French Guiana, highlighting the importance of clinical awareness in tropical endemic settings. Prospective studies incorporating systematic CSF analysis and microbiological testing are needed to improve understanding of its pathophysiology and standardize diagnostic pathways.

42875237.title: [Correlation between glycemic variability coefficient and sepsis-induced coagulopathy and analysis of risk factors].
42875237.journal: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
42875237.abstract: To investigate the association between glycemic variability coefficient (CV) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC), analyze the related risk factors for SIC in septic patients, and further explore the clinical value of glycemic CV as a potential predictor for SIC. A retrospective case-control study was conducted. General data, laboratory findings, therapeutic interventions, and disease severity scores of septic patients admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine of the First Hospital of Qinhuangdao from July 2021 to June 2024 were collected. Blood glucose CV within 24 hours of admission was used as the exposure variable, and SIC served as the primary outcome. Patients were divided into Q1, Q2, Q3, and Q4 groups according to quartiles of glycemic CV within 24 hours of intensive care unit (ICU) admission, with Q1 as the reference. Baseline clinical characteristics were compared among the four groups. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to analyze the effect of glycemic CV on SIC occurrence after adjusting for various confounders. Subgroup analyses were used to explore potential interaction effects and further verify the robustness of the results. A restricted cubic spline model was applied to examine the dose-response relationship between glycemic CV and SIC. Patients were divided into SIC and non-SIC groups based on the presence of SIC. Univariate analysis was used to identify risk factors for SIC, and significant variables were entered into binary logistic regression to determine independent risk factors. Receiver operator characteristic curve (ROC curve) was plotted to assess the predictive value of glycemic CV for SIC. A total of 440 patients with sepsis were enrolled, including 110 in Q1 (glycemic CV<19.5%), 109 in Q2 (19.5%≤glycemic CV<26.0%), 111 in Q3 (26.0%≤glycemic CV<31.5%), and 110 in Q4 (glycemic CV≥31.5%). Multivariate logistic regression showed that after adjustment for confounders, each 10% increase in glycemic CV was associated with an increased risk of SIC [odds ratio (OR)=1.049, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.024-1.074, P<0.001]. Compared with Q1, the risk of SIC remained significantly higher in Q4 (OR=2.739, 95%CI was 1.427-5.255, P=0.002). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis revealed a linear dose-response relationship between glycemic CV and SIC risk (overall P<0.001, nonlinear P=0.828), with the risk increasing linearly as glycemic CV rose. Subgroup analyses showed no significant interaction between glycemic CV and sex, age, diabetes, Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II(APACHE II), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA), use of vasoactive agents, use of corticosteroids, or anticoagulant therapy, consistently supporting elevated glycemic CV as a risk factor for SIC. Among the 440 patients, 280 were in the non-SIC group and 160 in the SIC group. Multivariate logistic regression including significant variables from univariate analysis identified high glycemic CV (OR=1.049, 95%CI was 1.024-1.074, P<0.001), high body mass index (BMI; OR=1.175, 95%CI was 1.106-1.248, P<0.001), and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT; OR=3.286, 95%CI was 1.561-6.919, P=0.002) as independent risk factors for SIC. ROC curve analysis showed that the area under the curve (AUC) of glycemic CV for predicting SIC was 0.624, with a cutoff value of 24.5%, yielding a specificity of 52.1% and sensitivity of 70.6%. There is a positive linear relationship between glycemic CV and the risk of SIC in septic patients. High glycemic CV, high BMI, and CRRT are independent risk factors for SIC. Glycemic CV has certain predictive value for SIC, and monitoring glycemic CV may facilitate early identification and prevention of SIC, thereby improving patient outcomes.

42871828.title: Global Direct In-scope Suction Study: An EAU-endourology Multicenter Prospective Collaboration (DISS-study).
42871828.abstract: Direct in-scope suction (DISS) facilitates continuous stone dust evacuation during flexible ureteroscopy (FURS), but prospective evidence validating its clinical efficacy and safety remains limited. To evaluate the stone-free rates (SFRs), perioperative outcomes, and limitations of DISS during successfully completed FURS for renal and ureteric stones in real-world practice, with the primary outcome being 30-d computed tomography (CT)-determined SFR. A prospective, multicenter, investigator-led registry was conducted across 16 centers in 14 countries (NCT05297331). Adults undergoing FURS with the Pusen 7.5-Fr DISS scope for any-sized renal/ureteric stones were included. The primary outcome was 30-d postoperative noncontrast CT SFR, classified as grade A (zero residual fragments [ZRF]) and grade B (single ≤2-mm fragment). Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of ZRF status. A total of 540 patients (median age 55 yr; 57% male) were enrolled. Anomalous kidneys were present in 12% (horseshoe 5.0% and malrotation 3.9%). Median stone volume was 590 mm3. Overall SFR (grades A and B) was 93% (501/540; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 90%-95%), with grade A achieved in 71% (386/540). Major complications were rare: no sepsis requiring intensive care unit admission, no transfusions, and only 2.6% ureteral access sheath (UAS)-related injuries (all Traxer grade 1). Postoperative fever >38°C occurred in 6.7% of the patients (36/540). On multivariable analysis for renal stones, stone volume (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.56, 95% CI = 0.39-0.79; p = 0.001) predicted lower odds of grade A status, whereas prestenting (adjusted OR 1.32, 95% CI = 0.76-2.33; p = 0.3) and UAS use (adjusted OR 0.76, 95% CI = 0.46-1.26; p = 0.3) were not statistically significantly associated with grade A status. Flexible ureteroscopy for kidney and ureteral stones using the 7.5-Fr DISS achieves high SFR with low morbidity in real-world practice. Stone burden remains a key determinant of complete renal stone clearance using DISS.

42851353.title: Longitudinal sepsis-induced coagulopathy score trajectories and mortality in relation to early prophylactic heparin: a multicentre cohort study.
42851353.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
42851353.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) evolves dynamically, and a single-timepoint score may not capture its longitudinal course. This study characterised SIC score trajectories, evaluated their associations with mortality, and conducted exploratory analyses of early prophylactic unfractionated heparin exposure. SIC score trajectories were characterised using a latent class mixed model. Trajectory-class prediction models were developed from baseline features within the first 24 hours of ICU admission using five algorithms. Heparin analysis used a 48-hour landmark design; weighted Fine-Gray models and cumulative incidence functions estimated 28-day post-landmark in-hospital mortality. The study enrolled 20,168 patients from MIMIC-IV and 5,829 from eICU-CRD. Three SIC trajectories were identified-Persistently High, Rising-then-Falling, and Resolving-comprising 31.9%, 10.6%, and 57.5% of patients in MIMIC-IV and 49.1%, 7.2%, and 43.7% in eICU-CRD. Relative to the Resolving trajectory, adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios (sHR) for mortality were 1.65 (95% CI 1.52-1.78) and 1.33 (1.18-1.49) for Persistently High and Rising-then-Falling in MIMIC-IV, and 1.73 (1.51-1.99) and 1.67 (1.33-2.11) in eICU-CRD. Prophylactic heparin was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard of 28-day post-landmark mortality in MIMIC-IV (sHR=0.908, 95% CI 0.839-0.983, P = 0.018); in an exploratory interaction analysis, the point estimate was more pronounced at higher predicted probabilities of the Persistently High trajectory, but this pattern was not replicated in eICU-CRD (sHR 0.877, 95% CI 0.744-1.034, P = 0.118). SIC score trajectories stratify septic patients into three trajectory classes-Persistently High, Rising-then-Falling, and Resolving-each showing a graded association with 28-day mortality. Early prophylactic unfractionated heparin showed an exploratory association with lower post-landmark mortality in MIMIC-IV that was not independently replicated in eICU-CRD. Although these findings do not support treatment recommendations or trajectory-based anticoagulation decisions, they provide a basis for formulating hypotheses for future prospective studies.

42835425.title: Early systemic heparin exposure is associated with lower mortality, reduced disseminated intravascular coagulation, and fewer thrombotic complications in septic shock.
42835425.abstract: Septic shock is characterized by thrombo-inflammatory dysregulation and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), contributing to organ failure and mortality. The clinical impact of heparin in septic shock remains uncertain. This study evaluated the association between early systemic heparin exposure and clinical outcomes. A retrospective multicenter cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX federated electronic health record network. Adult patients with septic shock receiving early systemic heparin exposure were compared with patients without heparin exposure. Propensity score matching balanced demographics, comorbidities, infection characteristics, organ dysfunction markers, and severity-related variables. Outcomes included mortality, DIC, thrombotic complications, renal outcomes, hematologic complications, and bleeding-related events. Clinical outcomes were assessed over a predefined 30-day follow-up period using risk-based and time-to-event analyses. A total of 105,472 patients per cohort were included. Early systemic heparin exposure was associated with lower mortality (15.3% vs. 20.8%; p < 0.001) and lower rates of DIC (p < 0.001). Thrombotic complications, including ischemic stroke, acute myocardial infarction, overall thrombotic events, and arterial or venous thrombosis, occurred less frequently among heparin-exposed patients (all p < 0.001). In contrast, heparin exposure was associated with higher rates of acute kidney injury, renal replacement therapy, thrombocytopenia, major bleeding, and transfusion requirement (all p < 0.01). Kaplan-Meier analyses were consistent with risk-based analyses. Early systemic heparin exposure was associated with lower mortality, reduced DIC, and fewer thrombotic complications, but increased rates of renal dysfunction and bleeding-related adverse events. These findings highlight a clinically relevant trade-off between potential benefit and harm. Prospective randomized studies are needed to define optimal patient selection and treatment timing.

42954754.title: SEPSIS-INDUCED COAGULOPATHY ATTENUATES THE PROGNOSTIC VALUE OF THE HEMOGLOBIN-ALBUMIN-LYMPHOCYTE-PLATELET (HALP) SCORE IN SEPSIS.
42954754.abstract: The hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score predicts outcomes in sepsis, but its platelet denominator is also a core component of sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC), and may distort its prognostic meaning. We examined whether SIC modifies HALP's association with 28-day mortality. We analyzed 6,218 adults meeting Sepsis-3 criteria in MIMIC-IV. HALP was calculated from first ICU measurements; SIC was defined by the 2017 ISTH criteria (score ≥4). Analyses included multivariable regression, interaction testing, propensity-score methods, and platelet-independent coagulopathy definitions, and evaluation of modified HALP (m-HALP; platelets in the numerator). Twenty-eight-day mortality was 25.6%; SIC incidence was 26.1%. HALP showed a J-shaped association with mortality (P for nonlinearity <0.001). The lowest quartile independently predicted death (adjusted OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.20-1.70; HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.10-1.39). This association persisted in non-SIC patients (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.28-1.79) but was attenuated and non-significant in SIC patients (OR 1.14, 95% CI 0.82-1.60; interaction P=0.006). Albumin carried HALP's discrimination in non-SIC patients, whereas platelets dominated in SIC (OR 0.51 per SD, P=0.001). When coagulopathy was redefined without platelets, the modification was no longer significant (P=0.295), indicating it partly reflects the shared platelet component. m-HALP was inversely associated with mortality in both strata (interaction P=0.691). Results were robust to weighting, 90-day mortality, and alternative Cox models. HALP is an independent prognostic marker mainly in septic patients without coagulopathy; once SIC develops, thrombocytopenia both raises mortality risk and arithmetically inflates HALP. Coagulation status should be assessed before HALP-based risk stratification; m-HALP may offer a platelet-consistent alternative.

42952460.title: Platelet transfusion biology: from hemostatic support to inflammatory and immune signaling.
42952460.abstract: Platelet transfusion remains indispensable for the prevention and treatment of bleeding in hematology, oncology, transplantation, critical care, surgery and trauma. Yet the biological impact of a platelet concentrate extends well beyond numerical correction of thrombocytopenia. Platelets are anucleate but metabolically active immune cells that express pattern-recognition receptors, release cytokines, chemokines, lipid mediators, extracellular vesicles, mitochondria-derived material and damage-associated molecular patterns; and interact with leukocytes, endothelial cells and complement. During collection, processing and storage, platelet concentrates acquire a distinct productspecific phenotype shaped by donor biology, residual plasma, additive solutions, leukoreduction, pathogen reduction, temperature and storage time. These variables affect not only post-transfusion recovery and hemostatic function, but also inflammatory signaling and immune related complications. The recipient is equally important: sepsis, chemotherapy, malignancy, neonatal immune development, endothelial activation and prior alloimmunization can determine whether transfused platelets restore hemostasis, amplify inflammation, or trigger refractoriness. This review explores platelet transfusion through the lens of a biological triad formed by the donor, the platelet product, and the recipient. We focus on how platelet immune receptors, storage-induced inflammatory remodeling, soluble biological response modifiers, extracellular vesicles and complement shape the interactions of transfused platelets with recipient leukocytes and endothelium. Alloimmunization and refractoriness are considered more briefly as recipient-dependent modifiers of platelet recovery and transfusion efficacy. The central challenge is no longer to define a single optimal platelet product, but to engineer and select the right platelet product for the right patient, at the right moment.

42947029.title: Esophagopericardial fistula secondary to battery acid ingestion in a 3-year-old boy: a case report.
42947029.abstract: Esophagopericardial fistula (EPF) is an extremely rare and life-threatening condition associated with a high mortality rate, particularly when diagnosis and intervention are delayed. Here we present the case of a 3-year-old boy who developed EPF secondary to accidental battery acid ingestion. A 3-year-old Yemeni boy presented with persistent epigastric pain, fever, and progressive dyspnea three weeks after accidental ingestion of battery acid, having initially received conservative supportive management at a regional hospital before delayed referral. Clinical examination revealed tachycardia, tachypnea, and a pericardial friction rub. Laboratory investigations demonstrated leukocytosis, severe thrombocytopenia, anemia, hypoalbuminemia, and markedly elevated inflammatory markers, consistent with sepsis. Imaging studies, including an iso-osmolar contrast swallow and CT, identified a 12-mm esophagopericardial fistula located in the distal esophagus, 2.5 cm above the gastroesophageal junction, accompanied by pyopneumopericardium. Following initial stabilization, the patient underwent a right posterolateral thoracotomy. Intraoperatively, gross inspection revealed extensive full-thickness ischemic necrosis and friability of the distal esophagus with inflammation extending to the pericardium, necessitating radical esophagectomy. The pericardium was opened, thoroughly irrigated with warm sterile saline, and a wide pericardial window was created for continuous drainage. An esophagectomy with gastric pull-up reconstruction was performed to achieve source control. Despite aggressive postoperative critical care, the patient developed refractory sepsis with multiorgan failure and died on the sixth postoperative day. This case highlights the poor prognosis of esophagopericardial fistula following corrosive ingestion in children, especially with delayed presentation and subacute progression. Early recognition and immediate referral to specialized tertiary pediatric surgery centers are paramount.

42923891.title: Amniotic fluid embolism Number 11 - 2026.
42923891.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
42923891.abstract: •Amniotic fluid embolism is a rare condition with high maternal mortality. It typically occurs during labor or delivery, and the pathogenesis has not yet been fully elucidated. •Survival of parturients with amniotic fluid embolism requires early recognition, rapid initiation of treatment, and access to skilled care based on the management of critically ill obstetric patients. •The classic clinical presentation of amniotic fluid embolism involves sudden hypoxia and hypotension or cardiopulmonary arrest, accompanied or immediately followed by non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and hemorrhage secondary to disseminated intravascular coagulation. •In cases of amniotic fluid embolism occurring during labor, bleeding typically originates at invasive interventions sites (intravascular lines and urinary catheterization). Following vaginal or cesarean delivery, bleeding arises primarily from the uterus, birth canal lacerations, and incision sites (abdominal wall and episiotomies). •Key laboratory abnormalities observed in amniotic fluid embolism include decreased fibrinogen levels, thrombocytopenia, and elevated D-dimer levels. The latter has limited diagnostic value, as levels are typically elevated during pregnancy and the postpartum period. •Arterial blood gas analysis in amniotic fluid embolism indicates the presence of hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis. Although chest radiography is initially unremarkable, if pulmonary edema and respiratory distress syndrome are present, dense bilateral pulmonary infiltrates may be observed. •The identification of amniotic fluid debris in pulmonary artery catheters or histopathological samples of lung tissue should not be considered diagnostic of amniotic fluid embolism. •The primary goals in managing amniotic fluid embolism are cardiopulmonary resuscitation, hemorrhage control, reversal of coagulopathy, and when indicated, fetal delivery. •In cases of amniotic fluid embolism accompanied by coagulopathy, massive transfusion is a necessary measure for effective, definitive treatment. The infusion of uterotonics, non-surgical invasive interventions (intrauterine balloons and intrauterine suction systems), and surgical procedures (vascular ligation, uterine compression sutures, and hysterectomy) may be used as adjuncts to control hemorrhage but are not considered definitive treatments. •The main differential diagnoses for amniotic fluid embolism include complications of neuraxial anesthesia; hemorrhage due to uterine atony, retained products of conception, and/or birth canal trauma; placental abruption; pulmonary thromboembolism; air embolism; acute myocardial infarction; and anaphylactic, cardiogenic, or septic shock.

42922205.title: Retroperitoneal Hematoma in Essential Thrombocythaemia: A Diagnostic Challenge.
42922205.abstract: Essential thrombocythaemia (ET) is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by sustained thrombocytosis and an increased risk of both thrombotic and haemorrhagic events. While thrombotic complications are more frequent, major bleeding remains a rare but potentially fatal occurrence, particularly when anticoagulant therapy is required. Retroperitoneal haematoma represents one of the most severe bleeding manifestations, often linked to anticoagulation or vascular fragility. We report the case of an 85-year-old woman with ET, obesity, and hypertension who underwent elective total right hip replacement. Postoperatively, she developed pulmonary micro-embolism and was treated with high-dose enoxaparin. Four days later, she suffered sudden haemodynamic collapse due to a massive retroperitoneal haematoma. Enoxaparin was discontinued and replaced with tranexamic acid infusion. Despite urgent surgical evacuation, multiple transfusions, and intensive care, her condition worsened with the development of femoral vein thrombosis, multidrug-resistant sepsis, worsening pulmonary embolism, and severe thrombocytopenia. She died 34 days after surgery. Autopsy confirmed a large organized haematoma compressing the right renal lodge and inferior vena cava, associated with femoral vein thrombosis. This case highlights the therapeutic and diagnostic challenges of ET, in which thrombotic and haemorrhagic risks may coexist and be further complicated by antithrombotic therapy. Despite individualized enoxaparin dosing based on body weight, the patient developed a major retroperitoneal haemorrhage followed by femoral vein thrombosis. Although disseminated intravascular coagulation and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia were both considered in the differential diagnosis, insufficient clinical and laboratory evidence prevented definitive diagnostic confirmation of either condition. Early and accurate diagnostic assessment is crucial in ET patients, where thrombotic and haemorrhagic risks coexist. In the absence of clear guidelines, clinical judgment prevails, underscoring the need to reassess physicians' criminal liability.

42905264.title: [Sepsis-induced coagulopathy].
42905264.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) represents a frequent and prognostically highly relevant complication of sepsis, characterized by a dysregulated interaction between inflammation, endothelial activation and coagulation. Pathophysiologically, the excessive host immune response to pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMP) and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMP), activation of the complement cascade, formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NET) and disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx collectively promote a prothrombotic and antifibrinolytic microenvironment, resulting in microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Approximately 20-25% of critically ill patients with sepsis fulfil the diagnostic criteria for SIC. Current diagnostic approaches rely on scoring systems such as the International Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (ISTH)-SIC, ISTH overt-disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and Japanese Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (JSTH)-DIC scores; however, their clinical utility remains limited as they predominantly collate hemorrhagic parameters even though sepsis is typically characterized by a thrombotically dominated phenotype. Viscoelastic point-of-care assays enable dynamic bedside assessment of coagulation and fibrinolysis, including the frequently occurring hypofibrinolysis or fibrinolytic shutdown, which is associated with an unfavorable outcome; however, for this specific purpose, these methods have not yet been sufficiently validated or established as a diagnostic standard. Data and recommendations on specific therapeutic options are limited. A consistent pharmacological thromboprophylaxis remains the cornerstone in patients with sepsis, with low-molecular weight heparins demonstrating advantages over unfractionated heparin regarding venous thromboembolic complications. Coagulation modulating treatment, such as antithrombin, recombinant thrombomodulin or activated protein C, have thus far failed to demonstrate consistent survival benefits in large randomized clinical trials. Experimental approaches targeting NET formation, complement activation or fibrinolytic modulation appear mechanistically promising but require further clinical validation. Overall, SIC necessitates an individualized, pathophysiology-driven diagnostic and therapeutic approach integrating inflammatory, endothelial, thrombotic and fibrinolytic alterations.

42903397.title: Anticoagulants beyond coagulation: repurposing heparin to mitigate immunothrombosis and inflammatory cascades in sepsis.
42903397.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome caused by a dysregulated host response to infection, in which inflammation, coagulation, endothelial injury, and immune dysfunction interact to drive organ failure and death. Accumulating evidence identifies immunothrombosis as a central mechanism in this process, linking neutrophil extracellular traps, platelet activation, tissue factor expression, circulating histones, and glycocalyx degradation to microvascular collapse and multiple organ dysfunction. Although heparin has traditionally been used as an anticoagulant, its highly sulfated structure also permits interactions that are independent of antithrombin. In addition to inhibiting thrombin generation, heparin can neutralize extracellular histones, interfere with HMGB1- and lipopolysaccharide-related inflammatory signaling, inhibit heparanase, preserve endothelial glycocalyx integrity, and modulate leukocyte trafficking through selectin-related pathways. Most of these non-anticoagulant actions have been demonstrated in cell systems, animal models, human endotoxemia, or diseases other than sepsis, and should therefore be read as biological plausibility rather than as an established clinical effect. The clinical literature addresses three questions that should not be conflated: routine venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in critically ill patients, anticoagulation directed at sepsis-induced coagulopathy or disseminated intravascular coagulation, and experimental immunomodulatory repurposing. The most recent meta-analysis restricted to randomized trials found no significant mortality reduction with heparin across three trials and 426 patients (risk ratio 0.86, 95% confidence interval 0.60-1.24), and the disseminated intravascular coagulation subgroup was also inconclusive. Favorable associations reported in retrospective sepsis-induced coagulopathy cohorts justify prospective phenotype-enriched trials but do not identify established responders. This review summarizes the pathophysiological rationale, mechanistic basis, current clinical evidence, and major safety considerations of heparin use in sepsis, and highlights future directions including precision phenotyping, biomarker-guided therapy, and non-anticoagulant heparin derivatives. At present no heparin preparation, salt, dose, or biomarker threshold is validated for sepsis-specific immunomodulation.

42885115.title: Investigating Fibrinolysis Resistance in Sepsis Using High-Multiplex Plasma Proteomics: A Statistical Analysis Plan.
42885115.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy is characterised by consumptive coagulation abnormalities and resistance to fibrinolysis, which is increasingly recognised as a driver of microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and mortality. The molecular determinants of the fibrinolysis-resistant phenotype remain incompletely defined. To present a pre-specified statistical analysis plan for a plasma proteomic investigation of fibrinolysis resistance in 89 samples collected serially from 32 critically ill patients with sepsis, using the Olink Explore HT platform (approximately 5400 proteins). The plan is designed to characterise protein associations with a validated bedside measure of fibrinolysis resistance, the ratio of tissue plasminogen activator-induced lysis time to fibrin clot amplitude (TPA-LT/FIBA10). The associations will be examined across the fibrinolysis resistance severity continuum and between three ordinal severity grades, and over time within individual patients. The analytic framework combines five complementary approaches: (i) limit-of-detection-based data filtering, (ii) continuous-variable modelling of protein abundance against TPA-LT/FIBA10 using limma-trend regression, (iii) categorical comparison across severity grades using empirical Bayes moderated statistics, (iv) linear mixed-effects modelling of longitudinal intra-patient trajectories and (v) pathway-level enrichment analysis to translate statistical associations into mechanistic hypotheses. A semi-supervised pathway clustering analysis will describe how proteins change by fibrinolysis resistance in eight a priori defined domains. This multi-model design is intended to define genuine biological signals in a high-dimensional dataset while remaining transparent about the exploratory nature of several components. The statistical reasoning behind each method is discussed alongside anticipated limitations. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06680180.

42881879.title: Legionella Septic Cardiomyopathy Requiring Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Followed by Presumed Complement-Mediated Thrombotic Microangiopathy: A Case Report.
42881879.abstract: Background:Legionella pneumophila rarely causes profound myocardial dysfunction and malignant ventricular arrhythmias. Persistent thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury during recovery may additionally raise concern for thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), although distinguishing complement-mediated disease from secondary causes in critically ill patients is challenging. Case Presentation: A 64-year-old man presented after five days of fever with recurrent ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation, cardiac arrest, and refractory shock. Echocardiography demonstrated diffuse biventricular hypokinesia with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 18%, while urgent coronary angiography showed no acute coronary occlusion. Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation, and organ support were initiated. Levofloxacin was administered from admission, before sputum sequencing identified L. pneumophila. VA-ECMO was removed after four days. Persistent anaemia and thrombocytopenia with progressive acute kidney injury despite clinical improvement prompted evaluation for thrombotic microangiopathy. ADAMTS13 activity was 92%, soluble C5b-9 was elevated to 648 ng/mL, and schistocytes were not identified. Presumed complement-mediated TMA was treated with four weekly doses of eculizumab, followed by haematological and renal improvement. Sepsis, extracorporeal support, transfusions, and gastrointestinal bleeding confounded diagnosis and treatment attribution. At three months, LVEF was 59%, platelet count 237 × 109/L, and creatinine 97 µmol/L. Conclusions: VA-ECMO may bridge selected patients with severe septic myocardial dysfunction to recovery. Persistent cytopenias and kidney injury warrant structured TMA evaluation. In critically ill patients, complement-mediated TMA requires integrated assessment rather than reliance on a single complement biomarker or clinical response to complement inhibition.

42871608.title: Fatal multiple organ dysfunction syndrome induced by colchicine poisoning in a patient with underlying alcoholic liver disease: a case report.
42871608.abstract: Colchicine is a drug used primarily to treat and prevent gout. Yet its narrow therapeutic index makes the lethal dose highly variable, influenced by patient-specific factors such as hepatic function and concomitant medications. In vulnerable patients, even doses substantially below the traditionally cited lethal threshold can result in fatal outcomes. We report a case of a 58-year-old male with a history of gout, alcoholic liver disease, and hyperlipidemia who presented with vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain that lasted three days after ingesting 15 mg of colchicine (0.22 mg/kg) for gout pain relief. Upon admission, laboratory findings revealed acute kidney injury, severe metabolic acidosis, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia. Despite aggressive supportive care in the intensive care unit (ICU), including broad-spectrum antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, steroids and recombinant human thrombopoietin (rhTPO), the patient developed progressive multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage. On the eighth day of admission, the family opted to discontinue further organ support, and the patient died shortly thereafter. This case shows that in patients with hepatic impairment, severe colchicine toxicity and fatal outcomes may occur even at doses below the traditionally cited threshold. The case also demonstrates that it is critical for physicians to be alert to the serious adverse effects of inadvertent colchicine overdose when prescribing the drug.

42828628.title: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome: an emerging fatal zoonotic infection.
42828628.abstract: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome is a potentially fatal respiratory zoonotic infection caused by New World hantaviruses, and it is acquired mostly via inhaling aerosolized excreta from infected rodents. Over the past 30 years, HCPS has expanded beyond its initial foci, and recent events suggest a potential for spread beyond traditionally endemic regions. The disease rapidly progresses from a vague prodrome to acute cardiopulmonary failure with a high fatality rate despite optimum supportive treatment. Pathophysiology involves endothelial failure, increased vascular permeability, acute thrombocytopenia and excessive immunological responses resulting in capillary leak syndrome and cardiogenic shock. It is still hard to clinically suspect early since the prodromal symptoms are vague and mirror common viral infections and respiratory disorders. Diagnostic confirmation needs serological testing or genetic approaches, which are typically unavailable in resource-limited endemic situations, leading to considerable diagnostic delays. Management is generally supportive, with early ICU admission, judicious hydration management, mechanical breathing and cardiopulmonary support including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in refractory patients. The recent multi-country Andes virus epidemic on a cruise ship in May 2026 highlights the potential for fast worldwide transmission of HCPS outside of usual endemic settings. This review summarizes the current information on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic techniques, and treatment options for HCPS. We also highlight the pressing need for improved global surveillance, rapid point-of-care diagnostics, global awareness among health care workers, and ongoing development of preventive vaccines and effective antiviral therapies to address this significant public health threat.

42862669.title: Incidence and Predictors of Acute Kidney Injury Among Postoperative Cardiac Surgery Patients in Tanzania.
42862669.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) is a severe postoperative complication linked to increased morbidity and mortality. Data on the incidence and predictors of CSA-AKI in sub-Saharan Africa, including Tanzania, are limited. This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of AKI in patients who underwent cardiac surgery at Tanzania's National Cardiac Institute. This prospective study included 177 patients. AKI was defined using the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria based on serum creatinine (SCr) changes at 24, 48, and 72 h postoperatively. The patients' clinical profiles were collected and analyzed using SPSS version 27.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Chi-square tests and modified Poisson regression were used to identify associated factors at 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with P < 0.05. The prevalence of postoperative AKI was 53%, with the majority of patients presenting with AKI stage I (72.9%). In the multivariable analysis, diabetes mellitus (Adjusted Prevalence Ratio (aPR )1.32, 95% CI 1.02-1.70; P = 0.038), American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) IV status (aPR 1.39, 95% CI 1.10-1.76; P = 0.007), blood transfusion (transfusion: aPR 3.63, 95% CI 1.15-11.41; P = 0.027), triple components (aPR 3.41, 95% CI 1.08-10.78; P = 0.037), and prolonged cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time of 181-240 min (aPR 3.53, 95% CI 1.51-8.25; P = 0.004) and > 240 min (aPR 3.80, 95% CI 1.57-9.18; P = 0.003) were independent predictors of AKI. Female sex was independently associated with a lower prevalence of AKI (aPR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.88; P = 0.004). Patients who developed AKI had significantly longer stays in the intensive care unit (ICU) (aPR 2.39, 95% CI 1.39-4.12; P = 0.002). The prevalence of CSA-AKI is remarkably high in this setting, posing a significant clinical burden. Key preoperative and intraoperative predictors were also identified. These results reinforce the importance of perioperative patient optimization, strategies to minimize CPB exposure, transfusion practice optimization, and surveillance of high-risk patients.

42858063.title: Rhabdomyolysis Following Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy.
42858063.abstract: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy remains a favorable treatment option for locally advanced prostate cancer in patients with obstructive lower urinary tract symptoms. However, the steep Trendelenburg lithotomy position required for this procedure can result in serious complications, particularly in patients with obesity. Here, the case of a 66-year-old man with obesity (BMI, 35 kg/m2), insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, and multiple comorbidities is reported, who underwent robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (console time, approximately 4 h) for clinically staged cT3a cN1 prostate cancer. Immediately after surgery, the patient developed severe gluteal pain, sensorimotor deficits, and massive rhabdomyolysis, resulting in anuric acute kidney injury and respiratory insufficiency. The clinical course was further complicated by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia type II and a grade IV gluteal pressure ulcer. A 22-day intensive care stay was required, including continuous hemodiafiltration and transfusion of 12 units of erythrocytes. With multidisciplinary management, renal function partially recovered, and the patient was discharged with minimal residual neuropathic deficits. This case highlights the importance of comprehensive preoperative risk assessment and provides clinically relevant insights into the recognition and multidisciplinary management of severe complications associated with prolonged positioning during robot-assisted radical prostatectomy.

42846740.title: Beyond renal support: biological modulation across pathophysiological domains during continuous renal replacement therapy - a randomized pilot study.
42846740.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is the preferred extracorporeal renal support modality for haemodynamically unstable critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI). Although regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) is primarily used to maintain circuit patency, its biological effects may extend beyond anticoagulation itself. We hypothesized that different anticoagulation strategies are associated with distinct biological modulation across complementary pathophysiological domains during CRRT. We conducted a prospective randomized pilot trial comparing RCA with systemic unfractionated heparin in critically ill adults with AKI requiring CRRT (1:1 allocation). Serial blood samples were obtained before CRRT initiation, at 1 hour and at 24 hours, with paired pre- and post-filter sampling at 1 and 24 hours.
