Biomarkers represented redox homeostasis (glutathione -GSH, GSSG- and their ratio), neutrophil activation (myeloperoxidase -MPO-), cellular injury (cell-free DNA -cfDNA-) and systemic inflammation (C-reactive protein -CRP-). Healthy reference participants established physiological reference values. Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models with fixed effects for time, anticoagulation strategy and their interaction. This trial was registered in the European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT No. 2016-004361-12) and at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06646328). Twenty patients were randomized equally to RCA or systemic heparin; baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Among six biomarkers spanning four pathophysiological domains, only MPO showed a significant systemic time × anticoagulation interaction (P = .008); although baseline-adjusted sensitivity analyses did not confirm a significant between-group difference. GSH and cfDNA changed significantly over time irrespective of anticoagulation strategy (both P = .016), while the GSSG/GSH ratio approached a treatment-level difference (P = .067). Across the extracorporeal circuit, CRP increased significantly post-filter at both timepoints, MPO increased at 1h, and GSH showed an anticoagulation-dependent pre-to-post change at 1h. No significant differences were observed in secondary clinical outcomes. These pilot findings suggest that different anticoagulation strategies during CRRT may show domain-specific, rather than uniform, biological modulation, most evident within the neutrophil activation domain, with additional evidence of biomarker-specific kinetics across the extracorporeal circuit. These exploratory results are compatible with the concept that extracorporeal therapies may influence distinct domains differently, a hypothesis warranting confirmation in adequately powered, prospectively designed studies before implications for precision extracorporeal therapy can be drawn.

42835122.title: Plasma exchange and double plasma molecular adsorption system combined with continuous renal replacement therapy for hepatitis B-related liver failure complicated by stage 3 acute kidney injury: a case report.
42835122.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver failure can progress rapidly to neurological and renal dysfunction. In this setting, declining aminotransferase levels may be misleading if hepatic synthetic function and extrahepatic organ function continue to deteriorate. A 27-year-old woman presented with severe fatigue, dark urine, and jaundice. Laboratory testing showed marked hepatocellular injury, coagulopathy, HBV infection markers, and an HBV DNA level of 3.57 × 10⁶ copies/mL. During hospitalization, serum aminotransferase levels declined substantially; however, bilirubin and coagulation abnormalities worsened, serum creatinine increased from 96 μmol/L on day 1 to 825 μmol/L on day 4, and the patient developed hypersomnia and impaired consciousness. The renal deterioration met criteria for stage 3 acute kidney injury. Following multidisciplinary assessment, plasma exchange combined with a double plasma molecular adsorption system was used for liver-directed extracorporeal support, while continuous renal replacement therapy was initiated primarily for severe acute kidney injury and metabolic support. Consciousness, coagulation, liver function, and renal function subsequently improved. The patient left the intensive care unit on day 7, was discharged on day 24, and maintained normal liver and kidney function during follow-up. This case highlights that declining aminotransferase levels do not necessarily indicate clinical recovery in rapidly progressive HBV-related liver failure. Serial assessment of hepatic synthetic function, neurological status, and renal function identified continued multiorgan deterioration and guided timely, indication-based extracorporeal support. The clinical value of this case lies in the decision-making process for coordinated liver and renal support rather than in the novelty of the individual treatment modalities.

42831055.title: Early Diffuse Alveolar Hemorrhage Revealing Leptospirosis Without Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report and Literature Review.
42831055.abstract: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage is a severe manifestation of leptospirosis, typically occurring in advanced stages of the disease and often associated with multiorgan failure. We report the case of a 44-year-old man without significant medical history admitted for acute febrile illness, hypotension, and respiratory symptoms occurring six days after initial symptom onset. Laboratory findings showed thrombocytopenia, elevated inflammatory markers, hepatic cytolysis, and mild acute kidney injury. Chest imaging demonstrated bilateral ground-glass opacities. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) confirmed alveolar hemorrhage, revealing 1,300,000 red blood cells/mm³ with a neutrophil-predominant profile and negative microbiological investigations. Polymerase chain reaction testing confirmed leptospirosis. The patient was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone followed by oral amoxicillin, resulting in rapid clinical and biological improvement. This case highlights an atypical pulmonary presentation of leptospirosis without extra-respiratory involvement. Leptospirosis lung involvement should probably be considered in patients presenting with febrile illness, pulmonary infiltrates, and thrombocytopenia, in endemic settings, even without jaundice or severe renal impairment.

42910263.title: A gastric dieulafoy lesion presenting with life-threatening upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage during recovery from hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis: a case report.
42910263.abstract: Dieulafoy lesions are an uncommon but potentially life-threatening cause of non-variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding, caused by rupture of a large-caliber submucosal artery through a minute mucosal defect; diagnosis is difficult because bleeding is intermittent and the surrounding mucosa appears nearly normal. Hemorrhage from a gastric Dieulafoy lesion during recovery from hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis (HTG-AP) has rarely been reported. A man in his twenties with severe obesity presented with acute epigastric pain after alcohol and a high-fat meal. Serum triglycerides were 53.67 mmol/L (reference 0.56-1.70), and CT confirmed acute pancreatitis. Because of extreme hypertriglyceridemia and evolving organ dysfunction, he received intensive lipid-lowering therapy, plasma exchange, continuous renal replacement therapy, and supportive care in the ICU, and improved. During recovery he developed sudden massive hematemesis with tachycardia, hypotension, and a fall in hemoglobin to 65.9 g/L. Emergency endoscopy showed extensive intragastric clots and could not locate the source. After stabilization, repeat endoscopy revealed an isolated thrombus-like protrusion with active oozing on the lesser curvature near the cardia, with otherwise normal mucosa, consistent with a Dieulafoy lesion; three metallic clips achieved immediate hemostasis. Contrast-enhanced CT excluded pseudoaneurysm, splenic-vein thrombosis, gastric varices, and other pancreatitis-related vascular complications. No recurrence occurred during hospitalization or approximately seven months of follow-up, with healed mucosa on later endoscopy. A gastric Dieulafoy lesion is a rare but life-threatening cause of bleeding during recovery from HTG-AP. A nondiagnostic first endoscopy because of clot retention does not exclude it, and persistent bleeding warrants repeat endoscopy after stabilization and gastric clearance. Bleeding should not be attributed solely to stress injury or anticoagulation; an underlying structural lesion should be sought. Clipping achieved durable hemostasis in this patient, but a single case cannot establish comparative efficacy.

42903855.title: Outcome-Gap Analysis of High-MELD Deceased-donor Liver Transplantation Using Institutional Reference Values from Living-donor Liver Transplantation.
42903855.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology
42903855.abstract: Benchmarking in liver transplantation has largely relied on low-risk deceased-donor or multicenter cohorts. We derived living-donor liver transplantation (LDLT)-based institutional reference values and evaluated domain-specific outcome gaps in high-Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) deceased-donor liver transplantation (DDLT) in an LDLT-dominant setting. Adult liver-transplant recipients treated at a high-volume tertiary center between June 2016 and December 2024 were analyzed. A predefined low-risk LDLT cohort was used to derive institutional reference values. Continuous cutoffs were defined as the 75th percentile of the LDLT distribution, and binary endpoints as observed LDLT event rates. High-MELD DDLT outcomes were assessed across clinical resource use, global morbidity, organ/graft dysfunction, survival/graft outcomes, and biliary-vascular complications. The cohort included 423 LDLT reference recipients and 203 high-MELD DDLT recipients. LDLT-derived cutoffs were 7.39 h for operation duration, 2 red blood cell (RBC) units, 4 intensive care unit (ICU) days, and 24 hospital days. High-MELD DDLT exceeded reference values for transfusion, ICU stay, 30-day Clavien-Dindo (C-D) grade ≥ III morbidity (49.8% vs 29.3%; gap +20.4 percentage points [pp]), acute kidney injury (AKI) stage ≥3 (6.9% vs 1.7%; gap +5.2), and early allograft dysfunction (EAD) (40.4% vs 8.7%; gap +31.6). One-year graft and patient survival were lower in high-MELD DDLT (73.6% vs 92.1% and 76.9% vs 94.5%). Biliary complications showed negative gaps, indicating graft-type-dependent morbidity that required separate interpretation. LDLT-derived institutional reference values identified high-MELD DDLT outcome gaps, mainly in clinical resource use, major morbidity, organ/graft dysfunction, graft loss, and mortality. These values may help describe excess burden without serving as exclusion thresholds.

42965335.title: Efficacy and Safety of Nafamostat Mesilate Injection in Patients Receiving Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Meta-Analysis.
42965335.abstract: The objective of the study was to assess the efficacy and safety of nafamostat mesilate injection in patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Dichotomous and continuous outcomes were analyzed using fixed-effect or random-effects models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) or mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Eight studies involving 1,189 patients were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with no anticoagulation, nafamostat mesilate injection was associated with lower mortality (OR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.44-0.76; p < 0.001) and longer filter lifespan (MD, 7.00; 95% CI, 1.50-12.50; p = 0.01). These estimates were derived predominantly from nonrandomized studies and should be interpreted with caution. However, no significant difference was found between nafamostat mesilate injection and no anticoagulation in bleeding complications (OR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.51-2.34; p = 0.82), total duration of CRRT (MD, 4.46; 95% CI, -0.13-9.04; p = 0.06), the proportion of patients requiring transfusion (OR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.54-1.03; p = 0.07), and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (MD, -0.24; 95% CI, -3.85-3.37; p = 0.90) in patients receiving CRRT. The available evidence suggests that nafamostat mesilate injection may be associated with lower mortality and longer filter lifespan compared with no anticoagulation in patients receiving CRRT. However, no clear difference was observed in bleeding complications, total duration of CRRT, the proportion of patients requiring transfusion, or ICU length of stay. These findings are limited by the predominance of nonrandomized designs, small numbers of studies, and substantial heterogeneity. Additional adequately powered randomized studies are needed before clinical benefit can be considered established.

42868679.title: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in burn patients: A 12-year retrospective cohort study in the era of "trauma dosing" low molecular weight heparin.
42868679.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42868679.abstract: Venous thromboembolism is a recognized complication of burn injury, yet the contemporary incidence in the setting of routine pharmacologic prophylaxis remains uncertain. We conducted a twelve-year retrospective cohort study of adult patients admitted to a single academic burn center between 2012 and 2023. The primary outcome was clinically significant venous thromboembolism, defined as pulmonary embolism or deep vein thrombosis above the popliteal vein confirmed by imaging. Univariable and multivariable logistic regressions were performed to identify factors associated with venous thromboembolism. A total of 1056 patients met inclusion criteria. The mean age was 54.7 years, and the mean total body surface area (TBSA) burned was 8.1%. Nineteen patients developed clinically significant venous thromboembolism, corresponding to an overall incidence of 1.8%. Incidence increased stepwise with burn severity, reaching 7.4% among patients with greater than 20% TBSA. Increasing age (1.01, 1.00-1.06) and intensive care unit length of stay (1.02, 1.00-1.03) were independently associated with venous thromboembolism on multivariable analysis. Over the study period, venous thromboembolism incidence decreased, alongside an increase in institutional use of low molecular weight heparin; however, this decline was not statistically significant. In a modern burn population receiving near-universal pharmacologic prophylaxis, the incidence of clinically significant venous thromboembolism was low. These findings support consistent prophylaxis in hospitalized burn patients while highlighting the need for prospective studies to refine risk stratification and dosing strategies.

42847938.title: A Case of Hemorrhagic Shock Due to Abdominal Hemorrhage in Hemophilia A: The Role of Laboratory Medicine in Multidisciplinary Team.
42847938.abstract: Spontaneous abdominal hemorrhage due to hemophilia A is one of the most lethal complications, progressing rapidly and potentially leading to hemorrhagic shock or death. We report a case of a 38-year-old male patient with hemophilia A who presented with massive spontaneous abdominal hemorrhage, leading to a large hematoma and severe hemorrhagic shock. Upon admission, the patient showed unstable vital signs and a significant decline in hemoglobin levels, indicating an extremely perilous condition that required immediate multidisciplinary collaborative intervention. A multidisciplinary team was assembled, including specialists from emergency medicine, intensive care, hematology, cardiothoracic surgery, laboratory medicine, and radiology. The team quickly diagnosed active abdominal hemorrhage and performed successful catheter-directed arterial embolization. Despite ongoing hemoglobin decline after the procedure, the multidisciplinary team employed targeted laboratory monitoring and assessments to identify underlying causes and adjust coagulation factor replacement and transfusion strategies, effectively stabilizing hemoglobin levels. During recovery, the patient developed progressive jaundice, which was determined to be due to the absorption of the large hematoma, thus preventing unnecessary invasive procedures. This case underscores the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in managing complex critical conditions and highlights the vital role of laboratory medicine in accurate diagnosis, decision-making, and management of complications.

42948796.title: Prehospital damage-control amputation and packed red blood cell transfusion for severe bilateral lower-limb crush injury in a remote setting: a case report.
42948796.abstract: Prehospital damage-control amputation in civilian emergency systems is rare, especially combined with prehospital packed red blood cell transfusion. We report a 30-year-old man with bilateral lower-limb crush injury after entrapment in an industrial roller machine in a remote area. Despite initially preserved blood pressure, he developed marked hemodynamic deterioration and arrived at the hospital with a blood pressure of 74/49 mmHg. Both limbs were non-salvageable. Prehospital bilateral amputation with vascular ligation was performed on scene, followed by transfusion of one local unit of packed red blood cells (~200 ml). He survived after stump revision, intensive care, and rehabilitation. This case describes the sequential use of prehospital hemorrhage control and packed red blood cell transfusion during the same prehospital episode in a patient with a life-threatening entrapment injury and delayed transport.

42934571.title: Risk factors associated with maternal near miss in tertiary hospitals in Eskişehir, Türkiye: a case-control study.
42934571.abstract: Maternal near miss (MNM) cases provide valuable insight into the quality and performance of maternal health services. Understanding the factors associated with MNM is crucial for developing effective public health interventions. This study aimed primarily to identify factors associated with MNM and secondarily to report the MNM ratio in tertiary hospitals in Eskişehir, Türkiye. This retrospective, multicenter, case-control study was conducted at two tertiary hospitals in Eskişehir, Türkiye. The medical records of 10,360 women who gave birth between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2023, were reviewed. A total of 53 MNM cases were identified based on the World Health Organization criteria defined by organ dysfunction and life-threatening conditions. For each case, three controls without serious complications were selected, resulting in 159 controls (1:3 ratio). Descriptive statistics, univariate analysis, and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with MNM. The incidence of MNM was calculated as 5.18 per 1,000 live births. The most common maternal complications were severe postpartum hemorrhage (45.2%), uterine rupture (34.0%), and severe preeclampsia (17.0%). The most commonly performed critical interventions were blood transfusion (73.6%), laparotomy (45.3%), and intensive care unit admission (30.2%). Coagulation/hematological dysfunction (58.5%) and uterine dysfunction (47.2%) were the most frequently observed MNM criteria. Multivariate analysis identified anemia (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 16.57; 95% CI: 7.19-38.19), previous cesarean delivery (aOR = 6.22; 95% CI: 2.18-17.77), short interpregnancy interval of two years or less (aOR = 3.68; 95% CI: 1.63-8.32), absence of antenatal care (aOR = 4.69; 95% CI: 1.44-15.21), and presence of chronic disease (aOR = 4.83; 95% CI: 2.11-11.04) as independent risk factors, while preterm birth (aOR = 12.86; 95% CI: 5.95-27.78) emerged as a strong clinical indicator associated with MNM. The results of this study underscore the importance of early identification and management of modifiable risk factors for MNM. Strengthening antenatal care services, improving anemia screening and treatment, promoting evidence-based cesarean delivery practices, and ensuring postpartum family planning support may help improve maternal outcomes and reduce preventable maternal morbidity.

42848051.title: Veno-Venous ECMO after Penetrating Trauma: A Viable Option With Individualized Anticoagulation.
42848051.abstract: BackgroundThe incidence, clinical characteristics, complications, and outcomes for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in penetrating trauma cases are mostly unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the concept that ECMO could be a safe and effective therapy after severe penetrating injury at a single high-volume center.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective case series of all penetrating trauma patients supported with ECMO at a single Level I trauma center between January 2022 and June 2025. Data collected included demographics, injury patterns, ECMO indications and cannulation details, anticoagulation management, operative interventions performed on ECMO, bleeding and thrombotic complications, and clinical outcomes.ResultsEight patients were supported with veno-venous ECMO, all male, with a median age of 36 years and a median Injury Severity Score of 20. Injury mechanisms included six gunshot wounds and two stab wounds, with a median PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 71 at ECMO consultation. Anticoagulation was individualized, with initiation delayed a median of 4 days after cannulation, and one patient received no anticoagulation throughout their ECMO course. Four patients underwent major operative procedures while on ECMO. Three patients had manageable bleeding complications, and three had thrombotic complications not associated with anticoagulation interruption. Overall survival to hospital discharge was 75% (6/8 patients).DiscussionThis case series demonstrates basic proof of concept that ECMO can be safely implemented in carefully selected penetrating trauma patients. Individualized anticoagulation strategies and concurrent operative management were feasible with manageable complications. Further multicenter studies are needed to define optimal patient selection and anticoagulation practices.

42954268.title: The latest guidelines for the perioperative management of the thoracic noncardiac patient: a critical appraisal of the literature.
42954268.abstract: The management of patients before, during, and after surgical procedures on the thorax is influenced by a rapidly expanding set of guidelines that are only partially overlapping. The review is intended for clinicians who are interested in understanding how publication date influences their recommendations, and the points of agreement and divergence between sources. Across the preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases, the reviewed documents converge strongly on core process measures. These measures encompass multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia, a single chest drain, early ambulation, and the avoidance of reflex ICU admission. However, there is less consistency in the numerical thresholds, including exercise-testing cut-offs, transfusion triggers, and drain-removal volumes. The most recent documents demonstrate a shift toward more permissive values and an increasing emphasis on frailty, sarcopenia, and patient-reported outcomes. The core enhanced recovery after surgery process measures have been demonstrated to be reliable. However, it is imperative for clinicians to ascertain the underlying guideline generation for any numerical threshold before its implementation. A significant number of intraoperative decisions are still made based on expert opinion rather than guideline-grade evidence, underscoring the necessity for future trials and consensus on patient-centered outcome measurement.

42873487.title: Safety and Efficacy of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Female Patients: A Secondary Analysis of the ANH Trial.
42873487.abstract: Female patients undergoing cardiac surgery have a higher transfusion burden, yet they remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. Although the ANH trial showed no significant reduction in the proportion of patients receiving allogeneic blood transfusions with acute normovolemic hemodilution, evidence regarding its efficacy and safety specifically in female patients remains limited. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH) compared with usual care in female patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. This was a post hoc secondary analysis of the multicenter, randomized ANH trial, which was conducted at 32 centers in 11 countries from April 2019 to December 2024. Of 2010 patients in the original ANH trial, 405 were women and were included in this analysis; 219 had been randomized to receive ANH and 186 to usual care. This secondary analysis was conducted from August 2025 to January 2026. Withdrawal of at least 650 mL whole blood with crystalloids replacement and reinfusion after cardiopulmonary bypass. The primary outcome was the occurrence of at least 1 allogeneic packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion during the index hospitalization. Safety outcomes included intraoperative hypotension, intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, mortality, and other perioperative complications. The median (IQR) age of the participants was 62 (54-69) years. The occurrence of allogeneic pRBC transfusion was similar in the ANH and usual care groups (38.8% vs 44.6%, respectively; relative risk [RR], 0.87; 95% CI, 0.69-1.10; P = .24). Intraoperative hypotension occurred more frequently with ANH (16.0% vs 4.8% in usual care; RR, 3.30; 95% CI, 1.62-6.74; P = .02). Patients receiving ANH also had longer ICU stays (mean difference, 21.13 hours; 95% CI, 1.89-40.38; P = .03) and hospital stays (mean difference, 1.92 days; 95% CI, 0.14-3.70; P = .04). No significant differences were observed in mortality or other postoperative complications. In this post hoc secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, ANH was not associated with a reduction in allogeneic pRBC transfusion among women undergoing cardiac surgery and was associated with more frequent intraoperative hypotension and longer ICU and hospital stay. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered studies specifically designed to evaluate female patients undergoing cardiac surgery. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03913481.

42872265.title: A single center cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of inpatient postpartum anxiety and post-traumatic stress symptoms using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist for DSM-5.
42872265.abstract: Mental health conditions are now the leading cause of maternal mortality in the United States, prompting calls for universal postpartum anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder screening. However, standardized guidelines for screening implementation remain deficient. This cross-sectional study evaluated the prevalence of inpatient postpartum anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder while exploring associated risk factors. Over a three-week period, we prospectively assessed adult postpartum patients following all delivery modes (vaginal and cesarean, live and stillbirth) at a single academic institution in the US. Screening was performed within 36 hours of delivery using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (score cut off ≥80) and post-traumatic stress disorder checklist for DSM-5 (score cut off ≥28). Data collection included demographic, medical, anesthesia, obstetric and neonatal variables, with assessments conducted in-person or via telephone for any spoken language. Cross-sectional study. Among 275 eligible patients, 263 (95.6%) completed the screening measures. The prevalence of positive postpartum anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder screening was 12.5% and 4.9% respectively, with 3.8% of patients screening positive for both conditions. Worse State-Trait Anxiety Inventory scores were associated with ASA ≥3, pre-term birth and neonatal Apgar scores at 5 minutes <7. Worse post-traumatic stress disorder scores were associated with ASA ≥3, primiparity, spontaneous vaginal delivery, pre-eclampsia, pre-term birth, blood transfusion, Apgar score <7 and neonatal intensive care unit admission. Factors after adjustment associated with positive anxiety screening were a psychiatric history or medication use. No factors after adjustment were associated with positive PTSD screening. Positive screening for inpatient postpartum anxiety was two and a half times more prevalent than for post-traumatic stress disorder. Positive anxiety screening was independently associated with psychiatric history or medication use. Targeted screening for post-traumatic stress disorder may be more appropriate, particularly among patients with pre-existing psychiatric conditions, complicated pregnancies or neonatal morbidity. Future research should focus on determining optimal screening parameters and timing, and intervention guidelines to better support high-risk obstetric populations.

42872004.title: Coagulation Disorders and Thrombotic Events in Patients with COVID-19: A Narrative Review.
42872004.journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
42872004.abstract: This review explores the coagulation disorders and thrombotic events observed in COVID-19 patients, highlighting the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and current management strategies. Important mechanisms contributing to thrombosis include cytokine storm-induced thrombosis, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, macrophage activation syndrome, complement cascade activation, and renin-angiotensin system dysregulation. Thrombotic complications significantly impact mortality and morbidity, with pulmonary emboli frequently observed in autopsy studies. Notably, this prothrombotic state may persist for weeks post-hospitalization. Effective management of COVID-19-associated coagulopathy requires prompt treatment of underlying infections and comprehensive assessment of co-infections in critically ill patients. While heparin and its derivatives remain the cornerstone for managing venous thromboembolism, their efficacy for COVID-19-associated coagulopathy remains to be a subject of investigation. Understanding the complex interplay between inflammation and thrombosis in COVID-19 is crucial for developing targeted therapeutic strategies that address coagulation disorders and the underlying infection.

42866840.title: Short-term perioperative safety and long-term follow-up after robotic-assisted resection of non-renal, non-adrenal retroperitoneal tumors: a 10-year retrospective cohort study.
42866840.abstract: Open surgery remains the conventional approach for large retroperitoneal tumors because of limited operative space, complex vascular anatomy, potential bleeding risk, and oncological concerns. However, evidence regarding robotic-assisted laparoscopic resection for retroperitoneal tumors larger than 10 cm remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, perioperative outcomes, and follow-up results of robotic-assisted laparoscopic resection for non-renal and non-adrenal retroperitoneal tumors, with particular focus on tumors larger than 10 cm. We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent robotic-assisted laparoscopic resection of retroperitoneal tumors at our institution between November 2015 and November 2024. Tumors of renal or adrenal origin were excluded based on postoperative pathological diagnosis. Patients were stratified according to maximum tumor diameter into three groups: >10, >6 to <10, and <6 cm. Baseline characteristics, operative variables, perioperative outcomes, pathological findings, and follow-up results were compared among the three groups. The primary descriptive endpoints were conversion, estimated blood loss, transfusion, postoperative intensive care unit admission, operative time, and postoperative hospital stay. Comparisons were exploratory and unadjusted. A total of 207 patients were included, comprising 27 patients in the >10 cm group, 52 in the >6 to <10 cm group, and 128 in the <6 cm group. There were no significant differences among the groups in age, body mass index, sex distribution, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, transfusion rate, conversion rate, postoperative intensive care unit admission, or follow-up duration.  Two procedures (1.0%) were converted to open surgery. After inclusion of the 3,000 mL bleeding conversion, mean blood loss in the >10 cm group was 300.42±658.94 mL (F=6.4952, P=0.002). Operative time and postoperative hospital stay were longer in the >10 cm group. Malignancy was more frequent in tumors larger than 6 cm than in tumors smaller than 6 cm. In the >10 cm group, liposarcoma, ganglioneuroma, and paraganglioma were the most common pathological diagnoses. In the liposarcoma-specific review, 14 patients underwent 18 robotic procedures; six developed local recurrence, and one died of metastatic disease during follow-up. Robotic-assisted laparoscopic resection was technically feasible in this selected cohort for selected non-renal and non-adrenal retroperitoneal tumors larger than 10 cm when performed in experienced centers. Although larger tumors were associated with longer operative time and postoperative hospital stay, conversion and transfusion rates were low, one major bleeding conversion illustrates an important limitation. For large benign tumors, perioperative outcomes were broadly comparable with those of smaller tumors. For large malignant tumors, robotic surgery may represent a minimally invasive option with acceptable perioperative outcomes; however, careful patient selection and long-term oncological surveillance remain essential. These findings do not establish oncological equivalence to open surgery, particularly for retroperitoneal sarcoma.

42866566.title: Advanced Rheumatic Heart Disease Complicated by Pregnancy, Mitral Valve Disease, Pulmonary Hypertension, and Left Atrial Thrombus: A Multidisciplinary Case Report from Resource-Limited Settings.
42866566.abstract: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality among pregnant women in resource-limited settings. Pregnancy induces significant hemodynamic changes that can decompensate pre-existing valvular heart disease, leading to life-threatening complications for both mother and fetus. A 27-year-old pregnant woman (gravida 6, para 5) at approximately 34-38 weeks presented with progressive shortness of breath, palpitations. Based on the modified World Health Organization (mWHO) classification, she was categorized as Class IV (extremely high risk) bilateral lower limb swelling, cough, fatigue, and reduced appetite. Cardiovascular examination revealed a systolic murmur, loud S1 and S2, with bilateral basal crepitations on respiratory examination. Echocardiography demonstrated an enlarged left atrium (5 cm), moderate mitral stenosis, mild mitral regurgitation, with fixed mitral valve leaflets, pulmonary hypertension, poor right ventricular function, a large left atrial thrombus, Labor occurred spontaneously while on low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH). Mild pericardial effusion, and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (58%). Laboratory investigations showed elevated CRP (48.8 mg/L), thrombocytopenia (platelets 99 ×109/L), mild coagulation abnormalities (INR 1.5), and urinalysis findings consistent with hematuria and proteinuria. Electrocardiography revealed sinus tachycardia, left atrial enlargement, right ventricular hypertrophy pattern, incomplete right bundle branch block, and prolonged QTc interval. The patient received multidisciplinary care including furosemide, metoprolol, and enoxaparin. She delivered a 2.1 kg neonate with good Apgar scores. This case illustrates the severe maternal and fetal risks associated with advanced RHD during pregnancy. The presence of a large left atrial thrombus in a pregnant woman poses significant thromboembolic and hemodynamic risks. Multidisciplinary management involving cardiology, obstetrics, anesthesia, and intensive care is essential for optimizing outcomes. This case highlights the critical importance of early recognition, strict adherence to CARE guidelines and multidisciplinary management, and the need for preventive strategies including primary prevention of rheumatic fever and secondary prophylaxis for RHD in resource-limited settings.

42865678.title: Acute-Onset Iron Overload Cardiomyopathy in Diamond-Blackfan Anaemia: A Case Report of Rapid Ejection Fraction Decline.
42865678.abstract: Diamond-Blackfan anaemia (DBA) is a rare inherited bone marrow failure syndrome causing pure red cell aplasia. Patients frequently require long-term red cell transfusions, predisposing them to iron overload. This case describes a patient with DBA with rapid ejection fraction decline secondary to acute-onset iron overload cardiomyopathy. A 28-year-old male patient with known transfusion-dependent DBA and established iron overload and on deferasirox, presented with a one-week history of orthopnoea, dyspnoea and peripheral oedema. Echocardiography demonstrated severe biventricular impairment with an ejection fraction of 15-25%. This represented a marked decline from an estimated ejection fraction of 45% two years prior. His course was then complicated by fast atrial fibrillation and severe refractory hypokalaemia, leading to escalation to the critical care unit. Cardiac MRI confirmed significant myocardial and hepatic iron loading. He was then managed with intravenous deferrioxamine, heart failure pharmacotherapy and rate control, with subsequent escalation of oral chelation. He was then discharged with combined cardiology and haematology follow-up. This case illustrates a severe complication of DBA: acute-onset iron overload cardiomyopathy causing rapid ejection fraction decline despite ongoing oral chelation. Markedly elevated ferritin, transferrin saturation and serum iron, alongside a normal CRP, supported a diagnosis of severe systemic iron overload. Management required a rapid switch from oral deferasirox to intravenous desferrioxamine. This case demonstrates that severe, acute iron overload cardiomyopathy can occur in patients with transfusion-dependent DBA despite ongoing chelation. It supports the value of further study of cardiac outcomes in this patient group.

42863831.title: Feasibility and Outcomes of External Cephalic Version among Small-for-Gestational-Age Births.
42863831.abstract: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) recommends that external cephalic version (ECV) be offered to patients with malpresentation. The objective of our study was to evaluate the efficacy and perinatal outcomes among births with small-for-gestational-age (SGA) infants after an ECV. This was a population-based, cross-sectional study using National Vital Statistics Systems data of singleton, non-anomalous neonates born after 36 weeks of gestation, with a birth weight of < 2,500 g between 2021 and 2023. Births with a maternal history of previous cesarean delivery were excluded. Births were divided into those who had an ECV attempt and those with a breech fetus at cesarean delivery without a trial of labor. Adverse maternal outcomes (blood transfusion, intensive care unit [ICU] admission, unplanned hysterectomy) and neonatal outcomes (assisted ventilation use, neonatal ICU [NICU] admission, seizures, surfactant use, death) were compared between groups using logistic regression. A total of 8,021 births were included. Of the 8,021 births, 812 (10.1%) had an ECV attempt and 7,209 (89.9%) had a primary breech cesarean delivery. There were significant differences in baseline characteristics between groups. Among the 812 births who had an ECV attempt, 338 (41.6%) had a successful ECV, of which 233 (68.9%) subsequently delivered vaginally. After adjusting for differences, births that had an ECV attempt had lower odds of neonatal-assisted ventilation use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.65, 95% confidence interval [0.46-0.92]) and NICU admission (aOR 0.48, 95% confidence interval [0.40-0.58]) than those who had a primary breech cesarean delivery. There were higher odds of maternal transfusion in the breech cesarean delivery cohort as compared with those who had an ECV attempt (odds ratio 2.81, 95% confidence interval [1.42-5.56]). Although ECV was successful in 41.6% of births with SGA infants, there were lower rates of assisted ventilation use and NICU admission among those who underwent an ECV attempt. · ECV was successful in 41.6% of SGA births.. · After successful ECV, 68.9% delivered vaginally.. · ECV attempts had lower odds of NICU admission..

42855594.title: Beyond Hysterectomy: A Five-Year Single-Center Experience With Uterine-Sparing Surgery for Clinically Diagnosed Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
42855594.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
42855594.abstract: To describe surgical management and maternal outcomes in placenta accreta spectrum, emphasizing initial uterine-sparing management, secondary intervention, and final uterine preservation. This retrospective cohort included 21 patients managed at a tertiary center between June 2018 and August 2023. Clinical severity was classified exclusively from documented intraoperative findings using the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics clinical classification; histopathological findings were evaluated separately. Management strategies, transfusion requirements, maternal morbidity, secondary interventions, and final uterine status were summarized descriptively. Patients with placental retention in situ were reviewed individually. Initial management comprised segmental resection in seven patients, placental-bed hemostatic suturing in six, placental retention in situ in five, and cesarean hysterectomy in three. Uterine-sparing management was undertaken in 18 patients (85.7%). Red blood cell transfusion was administered to 18 patients (85.7%); seven (33.3%) received at least four units, and five (23.8%) required intensive care. Seven patients underwent a secondary intervention. All five patients with placental retention in situ underwent a secondary procedure on postoperative Days 5-68, including three planned relaparotomies; none subsequently underwent hysterectomy. Final uterine preservation was documented in 18 patients (85.7%), and no maternal deaths occurred. Uterine-sparing management was followed by final uterine preservation in most patients but was accompanied by substantial transfusion requirements and frequent secondary interventions. Placental retention in situ was followed by further procedures in all five patients. Initial avoidance of hysterectomy and final uterine preservation should be reported separately.

42853129.title: BUN/Albumin Ratio in Preeclampsia: A Comparative Study of Seven Biomarker Ratios.
42853129.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
42853129.abstract: To evaluate whether the admission blood urea nitrogen to albumin ratio (BAR) predicts adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes in preeclampsia, and to compare its performance against six other laboratory-derived ratios. Records of 252 preeclamptic pregnancies were reviewed and dichotomised at a BAR cut-off of 3.0: low (< 3.0, n = 135) and high (≥ 3.0, n = 117). Composite adverse maternal outcomes included severe complication, intensive-care admission, or transfusion; composite adverse perinatal outcomes included growth restriction, stillbirth, neonatal death, neonatal-unit admission, or 5-min Apgar below 7. BAR was benchmarked against six other ratios: uric acid/albumin ratio (UAR), lactate dehydrogenase/albumin ratio (LAR), C-reactive protein/albumin ratio (CAR), fibrinogen/CRP ratio, fibrinogen/albumin ratio (FAR), and aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase (AST/ALT) ratio (De Ritis) by ROC analysis. Independent predictors were sought through multivariable logistic regression. Patients in the high-BAR stratum showed substantially higher rates of composite adverse obstetric outcome (78.6% vs. 54.1%; p < 0.001), composite adverse maternal outcome (28.2% vs. 6.7%; p < 0.001), maternal intensive-care admission (16.2% vs. 3.7%; p = 0.001), and transfusion (12.0% vs. 2.2%; p = 0.002). BAR yielded the most balanced discrimination across endpoints, with AUCs of 0.68 (95% CI: 0.61-0.75) for the obstetric composite, 0.74 (95% CI: 0.65-0.83) for the maternal composite, and 0.66 (95% CI: 0.59-0.73) for the perinatal composite (all p < 0.01); fibrinogen/albumin and AST/ALT ratios were not predictive. BAR did not differ significantly from UAR or LAR by DeLong test (all p > 0.05) and retained independent association with adverse perinatal outcome after adjustment (adjusted OR 1.32; 95% CI: 1.03-1.70; p = 0.03). Sensitivity analyses showed that UAR retained independent significance for all three composite endpoints, positioning BAR and UAR as complementary bedside markers. An elevated admission BAR identifies preeclamptic women at higher risk of severe maternal and perinatal events, with performance comparable to that of UAR. Both BAR and UAR may serve as simple complementary bedside adjuncts to existing risk stratification tools in preeclampsia.

42850445.title: Impact of antithrombotic therapy on management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for upper gastrointestinal bleeding: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
42850445.abstract: Antithrombotic agents are frequently implicated in upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB), yet their impact on prognosis and management remains unclear. The aim of this study was to assess the impact of pre-existing antithrombotic therapy on the management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB. This study used data from a retrospective, multicenter cohort of adult patients hospitalized for UGIB between January 2019 and December 2020 in Greater Paris University Hospitals. Patients were categorized into four groups according to their pre-existing antithrombotic treatment: antiplatelet therapy, anticoagulant therapy, both, or none. The primary outcome was thirty-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included endoscopy, endoscopic hemostasis, and blood transfusion within 7 days, and intensive care unit admission. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs). Among 928 patients, 226 (24%) were on antiplatelet therapy alone, 154 (17%) on anticoagulant therapy alone, 61 (7%) on combined therapy, and 487 (52%) received no antithrombotic treatment. Thirty-day mortality was 6.9%: 8.4% in the no-antithrombotic group, 6.2% in the antiplatelet group, 4.5% in the anticoagulant group, and 3.3% in the combined therapy group. Compared with the no-antithrombotic group, anticoagulant therapy alone was associated with lower mortality (aOR=0.28, 95% CI 0.10-0.83), while antiplatelet therapy alone or combined therapy were not significantly associated (aOR=0.47, 95% CI 0.19-1.14 and aOR=0.12, 95% CI 0.01-1.11, respectively). Neither anticoagulant nor antiplatelet therapy was associated with secondary outcomes. Antithrombotic therapy had no negative impact on the management or prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB.

42839954.title: Case Report: RAS-associated autoimmune leukoproliferative disorder presenting with early-onset liver failure in a 9-month-old Chinese girl.
42839954.abstract: RAS-associated autoimmune leukoproliferative disorder (RALD) is a rare, nonmalignant lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by splenomegaly, autoimmune cytopenia, monocytosis, and somatic RAS pathway mutations. Severe hepatic failure is an uncommon manifestation. Here, we report a critically ill infant with a diagnosis of RALD who presented with fulminant liver failure. A 9-month-old girl presented with recurrent infections, lymphadenopathy, massive hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenia, coagulopathy, and early-onset liver failure. Disseminated Talaromyces marneffei infection was confirmed by two sets of peripheral blood cultures. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) identified a heterozygous KRAS c.351A>C (p.Lys117Asn, K117N) variant located in the GTP-binding domain. The heterozygous state and clinical context are consistent with a somatic mutation in a subset of hematopoietic cells, rather than a germline variant. The patient died two days after admission despite antibiotics and maximal supportive care, including plasma exchange and intravenous immunoglobulin. This case illustrates that RALD-associated immune dysregulation served as the underlying root cause, on the basis of which a disseminated opportunistic infection developed as the direct cause of the fatal deterioration, revealing a potential link between oncogenic RAS signaling and innate immune dysregulation. It underscores the urgency of early genetic screening in infants with unexplained hepatitis and systemic inflammation, while advocating for novel therapeutic strategies targeting RAS/MAPK pathways.

42838488.title: One-year outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy and catheter-directed thrombolysis in acute pulmonary embolism.
42838488.journal: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
42838488.abstract: Although anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism (PE), mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all patients who underwent MT or CDT for acute PE across a single hospital system between January 2021 and April 2025. Patients were stratified into MT and CDT groups based on the treatment received. Baseline characteristics, procedural data, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. The secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, major adverse events, reintervention, and PE recurrence. Patients were followed up for up to 1 year or until death. A total of 724 patients were included in this study: 569 (79%) underwent MT and 155 (21%) received CDT. The mean age was 63 ± 16 years, and 49% were female. Most patients (76%) were classified as intermediate-high risk, with a mean right ventricle to left ventricle ratio of 1.5 ± 0.5. Bilateral or saddle embolism was present in 93% of patients. Patients in the MT group were more likely to have a simplified PE severity index of >0 (73% vs 60%; P < .001). Age and the rates of cancer, chronic cardiopulmonary disease, and concurrent deep vein thrombosis were similar between the groups. The median procedure duration was longer for MT (66 minutes, interquartile range, 46-89) than for CDT (58 minutes, interquartile range, 40-77; P = .003). The median postoperative length of stay was 3 days in both groups. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative adverse cardiac events (2.5% vs 0%; P = .048), and CDT was associated with higher intensive care unit admission rates (83% vs 36%; P < .001). However, the 30-day mortality rate was similar between the groups (CDT: 2.6% vs MT: 4.6%; P = .27). Additionally, the 1-year incidence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (MT: 4.5% vs CDT: 3.4%; P = .69), PE recurrence (MT: 4.4% vs CDT: 2.5%; P = .31), and all-cause mortality (MT: 7.8% vs CDT: 5.8%; P = .41) were not statistically significantly different between the MT and CDT groups. In this retrospective cohort, MT and CDT for acute PE showed statistically comparable 30-day mortality rates and 1-year recurrence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and PE. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative cardiac complications, and CDT was associated with more frequent intensive care unit admission.

42837815.title: A CXCL10-enriched hepatic-risk phenotype reveals a cell-count paradox in severe COVID-19.
42837815.abstract: Cell-count-derived inflammatory indices, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), are widely used to assess COVID-19 severity, but hepatic dysfunction and thrombocytopenia may alter their prognostic meaning. We tested whether FIB-4-defined hepatic risk modifies the interpretation of cell-count inflammation and whether this discordance has a cytokine or chemokine correlate. We applied an a priori 2 × 2 framework to 575 hospitalized adults with COVID-19 undergoing CT pulmonary angiography, classified by cardiometabolic burden and FIB-4-defined hepatic risk. Associations with oxygen requirement, ICU admission, in-hospital death, composite ICU/death and prolonged hospitalization were analyzed. A separate non-overlapping cytokine cohort of 90 patients was used for cytokine/chemokine profiling. Hepatic-risk phenotypes had higher adjusted odds of adverse outcomes but paradoxically lower NLR, PLR, SII and derived NLR. Significant index × hepatic-risk interactions showed that NLR, SII and dNLR retained their expected risk gradients in non-hepatic-risk patients but were attenuated or absent in hepatic-risk patients. In the cytokine cohort, the cellular pattern was reproduced, CXCL10/IP-10 and IL-8/CXCL8 were selectively elevated, and hepatic-risk patients were enriched in the NLR-low/CXCL10-high quadrant. Cell-normalized CXCL10 metrics and a CXCL10-NLR discordance score supported disproportionate chemokine enrichment relative to suppressed peripheral cell-count readouts. FIB-4-defined hepatic-risk COVID-19 identifies a CXCL10/IP-10-enriched, peripherally cell-count-suppressed inflammatory phenotype. Conventional NLR-, PLR-, SII- and dNLR-based risk interpretation may underestimate clinical risk when hepatic risk is present.

42833886.title: Warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia in Taiwan: A population-based study of epidemiology, treatment patterns, survival and healthcare utilisation (2017-2022).
42833886.abstract: To describe the epidemiology, treatment patterns, overall survival (OS) and healthcare resource use among patients with warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia (wAIHA) in Taiwan, adult patients with ≥1 diagnosis code for autoimmune haemolytic anaemia (AIHA) with record of wAIHA-related treatments between 2017 and 2022 were retrospectively identified from Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database linked with the National Death Registry and Taiwan Cancer Registry. The wAIHA incidence was 1.27 per 100 000 person-years, and the 2022 prevalence was 4.58 per 100 000 persons. Corticosteroid monotherapy was the most common treatment across all lines, with 30.2% of patients remaining on corticosteroids 2 years after diagnosis. Blood transfusions were common in the first year following diagnosis, with 52.5% of patients receiving at least one emergency transfusion. The 5-year OS probability, estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, was 67.1%. The median annualised medical cost was NT$ (New Taiwan dollar) 106 464 (interquartile range [IQR]: 49 088-285 856) or US$ (US dollar) 3327 (IQR: 1534-8933). Intensive care unit admissions were the primary cost driver (adjusted exponentiated coefficient: 2.76 [95% confidence interval: 2.26-3.36]), determined using a generalised linear model with a gamma distribution and log link function. Overall, significant unmet medical needs remain for wAIHA management in Taiwan, including addressing prolonged reliance on corticosteroids, sub-optimal OS outcomes and high medical service use.

42831343.title: [The impact of the World War I (1914-1918) on evolution of transfusion medicine].
42831343.abstract: The knowledge of transfusion therapy that existed in medicine by the beginning of the First World War formed the foundation of transfusion medicine in the 19th century. These knowledges were further expanded in the early years of the 20th century with immunological characteristics of blood groups. The war brought about a harsh necessity and also provided an immense opportunity for widespread implementation and further refinement of previous discoveries. The key achievements of military surgeons between 1914 and 1918 included establishment of the first blood banks and specialized intensive care units adapted for blood transfusion.

42827598.title: Machine learning-based prediction of postoperative venous thromboembolism in orthopedic surgery using the MIMIC-IV database and external validation.
42827598.abstract: A risk prediction model for venous thromboembolism (VTE) after orthopedic surgery was constructed and validated using machine learning algorithms, providing a reference for the early identification of high-risk individuals in clinical settings. Patients who underwent orthopedic surgery were retrospectively collected from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database as the modeling group. The patients were randomly divided into training and internal test sets in a 7:3 ratio. A total of 156 patients who underwent orthopedic surgery in our hospital from January 2022 to July 2025 were selected for the external validation set. Predictive variables were selected using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Six machine learning models were constructed: logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGB), light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), and naive Bayes (NBM). The model performance was evaluated by using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and G-mean. The interpretability of the optimal model was analyzed using the calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and SHAP methods. The MIMIC-IV database included 461 patients (VTE incidence rate, 15.8%). LASSO regression identified two predictive variables: fibrinogen and D-dimer levels. The AUC of the LGBM model in the internal test set was 0.893 (95% CI: 0.820-0.966), and in the external validation, the AUC of the LGBM model was 0.788. The predictive performance of this model was superior to that of the other five models tested. The calibration curve indicated that the model was well calibrated, and the decision curve suggested a clinical net benefit within the 0.1-0.6 threshold range. SHAP analysis showed that elevated fibrinogen and D-dimer levels were positively correlated with the risk of VTE. The LGBM model constructed based on the MIMIC-IV database has excellent predictive efficacy for VTE after orthopedic surgery and certain external generalization abilities. Fibrinogen and D-dimer levels are key predictive factors. This model can serve as a preliminary reference tool for risk stratification of VTE after orthopedic surgery.

42825229.title: Risk Factors, Ultrasonographic-Histopathological Comparison, and Maternal Outcomes of the Placenta Accreta Spectrum: An Ambispective Cohort Study From a Tertiary Care Hospital in Northern India.
42825229.abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is one of the leading causes of severe obstetric haemorrhage and peripartum hysterectomy, with a rising incidence due to increasing caesarean delivery rates worldwide. This study aimed to evaluate the risk factors for PAS, assess the concordance between ultrasonographic and histopathological findings, and determine maternal outcomes at a tertiary referral centre in northern India. An ambispective observational study was conducted in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Upper India Sugar Exchange Maternity Hospital, Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi Memorial Medical College, Kanpur, India, between January 2020 and July 2024. Retrospective data (January 2020-December 2021) and prospective enrolment (January 2022-July 2024) were included in the study. Women with an antenatal or intraoperative diagnosis of PAS were included. Maternal demographics, obstetric history, intraoperative findings, transfusion requirements, intensive care admission, and maternal morbidity and mortality were recorded. Seventy women with PAS were identified during the 4.5-year study period. The institutional burden of PAS among women screened based on predefined risk factors increased from 20/720 (2.8%) in the retrospective period to 50/720 (6.9%) during the prospective period, with an overall burden of 70/1,440 (4.9%). Prior caesarean delivery was the dominant associated risk factor (62/70, 88.6%), with two prior caesarean deliveries in 28/70 cases (40.0%). Low-lying placenta was present in 20/70 women (28.6%), while placenta previa coexisted in 26/70 women (37.1%), giving a combined prevalence of 46/70 (65.7%). Caesarean hysterectomy was required in 58/70 women (82.85%), with a mean estimated blood loss of 1854.3 ± 417.3 mL and substantial perioperative transfusion requirements. One maternal death (1/70,1.43%) occurred; 9/70 (12.9%) women required intensive care. Histopathology confirmed all PAS cases (70/70,100%) and served as the reference standard. Ultrasonography correctly identified all cases of placenta increta (17/17, 100%) and placenta percreta (9/9, 100%) but detected only 26/44(59.1%) cases of placenta accreta. Prior caesarean delivery and coexisting placenta previa were the principal risk factors in this cohort. The rising institutional burden of PAS highlighted the need for early antenatal diagnosis, structured referral pathways, and multidisciplinary perioperative care in tertiary centres.

42956429.title: Incidence, timing, severity, and predictors of venous thromboembolism after open abdominal wall reconstruction.
42956429.abstract: Venous thromboembolic events, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, represent serious and potentially preventable complications following open abdominal wall reconstruction. This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of venous thromboembolic events after open abdominal wall reconstruction. A single-institution prospectively maintained database was queried for open abdominal wall reconstruction (2010-2025). Standard statistical analyses and multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of venous thromboembolic events. Among 2,907 open abdominal wall reconstructions, 49 venous thromboembolic events (1.7%) occurred: 31 pulmonary embolisms ± deep vein thrombosis and 18 deep vein thromboses alone. Average body mass index was 34.6 ± 10.0 kg/m2, and 18.4% had prior venous thromboembolic events. Preoperative chemoprophylaxis was administered in 77.6% of venous thromboembolic event cases, and 93.8% of patients who received postoperative chemoprophylaxis had no interruption. Compared with patients without venous thromboembolic events, those with venous thromboembolic events had larger defect sizes (314.5 ± 222.7 vs 199.8 ± 187.5 cm2; P < .001) and longer operative times (233.4 ± 74.9 vs 187.2 ± 84.4 minutes; P < .001). Among 29 classified pulmonary embolisms, 13 were nonmassive, 12 submassive, and 4 massive/fatal. Advanced interventions were required in 12.2%, 16.3% required transfusion, and 16.3% underwent inferior vena cava filter placement. Among venous thromboembolic event patients, 40.8% required intensive care unit transfer, with 20.4% requiring reintubation. Average length of stay was longer in venous thromboembolic event patients (11.4 ± 9.8 vs 5.7 ± 8.8 days; P < .001). Multivariable regression identified body mass index (odds ratio, 1.09; 95% confidence interval, 1.04, 1.14; P < .001), prior venous thromboembolic events (odds ratio, 4.51; 95% confidence interval, 1.91, 10.62; P < .001), and operative time (odds ratio, 1.005; 95% confidence interval, 1.001, 1.010; P = .008) as independent predictors of venous thromboembolic event. Postoperative venous thromboembolic event following open abdominal wall reconstruction is uncommon but associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Higher body mass index, prior venous thromboembolic event, and longer operative time independently predicted venous thromboembolic event, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and prevention strategies.

42952484.title: Large-bore Mechanical Thrombectomy for Treatment of Intermediate-high Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Single-center Australian Experience.
42952484.abstract: Large-bore mechanical thrombectomy is an emerging treatment for intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism. We report outcomes from an Australian cohort. A retrospective analysis compared patients with intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, defined according to the 2019 European Society of Cardiology guidelines, who were managed before large-bore mechanical thrombectomy implementation (May 2023-April 2024) with those treated with large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (May 2024-October 2025) at a teaching hospital within a multidisciplinary pulmonary embolism response team framework. The primary endpoint was procedural feasibility and safety. Secondary endpoints included hemodynamic changes, intensive care unit utilization and 30-day mortality. Sixty-seven patients were included: 24 treated with large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (median age 66.5, interquartile range 51.8-73.0 years; 58.3% male) and 43 treated with anticoagulation and/or thrombolysis (median age 76.0, interquartile range 65.5-82.5 years; 34.9% male). Technical success was 100%. Mean pulmonary arterial pressure decreased from 28.5 ± 8.7 to 21.2 ± 5.6 mmHg (p < 0.001). Heart rate and respiratory rate improved at 24 hours (both p < 0.001), although adjusted analyses showed no significant between-group differences in hemodynamic changes. Intensive care unit length of stay was shorter in the large-bore mechanical thrombectomy group (20.1 ± 7.9 vs 32.2 ± 17.3 hours, p = 0.003), with multivariable analysis confirming an independent 43% reduction (exp(β) = 0.57, 95% confidence interval 0.42-0.79, p = 0.001). No major bleeding events or deaths within 30-days occurred in the large-bore mechanical thrombectomy group, compared with two major bleeding events (4.7%) and three mortalities (7.0%) in the non-large-bore mechanical thrombectomy group. Large-bore mechanical thrombectomy appears to be a safe and feasible treatment modality for intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism and was associated with reduced intensive care unit utilization compared with conventional therapies. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, prospective studies.

42950354.title: Body mass index and major surgical complications in outpatient surgical abortion: an Australia-wide case-control study.
42950354.abstract: Existing evidence on the association between body mass index (BMI) and surgical abortion complications is inconclusive and derives exclusively from retrospective cohort studies conducted in the United States of America, often underpowered for uncommon surgical outcomes. In Australia, BMI is commonly considered when determining eligibility for outpatient surgical abortion, yet no Australian data have examined its association with major surgical complications. We conducted a retrospective case-control study across 10 oupatient surgical abortion clinics operated by MSI Australia between 2016 and 2024. Cases were procedures complicated by major surgical complications (haemorrhage ≥500 mL, uterine perforation, hospital transfer, laparoscopy, laparotomy, disseminated intravascular coagulation, intensive care admission, blood transfusion, or hysterectomy), identified through mandatory incident reporting. Four gestation-matched controls were selected per case. BMI was analysed as a continuous variable, as obesity (≥30 kg/m2), and by ordered categories. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for parity, gestational age and previous caesarean section. BMI data were available for 775 of 795 individuals (159 cases, 636 controls). Mean BMI was slightly higher among cases than controls (25.9 vs 24.8 kg/m2; P = 0.017), but distributions were similar. Crude associations between BMI, obesity and complications did not persist after adjustment (per-unit increase: adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.01, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.97-1.04; obesity: aOR 1.24, 95% CI 0.78-1.96). BMI was not an independent predictor of major surgical complications in outpatient surgical abortion within the BMI range represented. Risk stratification should prioritise gestational age, parity and previous caesarean section rather than BMI alone, noting limited data for very high BMI categories.

42948609.title: The role of VWF/ADAMTS13 axis in COVID-19-associated coagulopathy.
42948609.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019, which broke out in 2019, is a disease caused by SARS-CoV-2 infection. Although this infection mainly affects the respiratory system, a high incidence of thrombotic events has been observed in severe or critically ill cases and in a considerable number of non-survivors of COVID-19. Although the coagulation dysfunction and hypercoagulability of COVID-19 have been reported in the literature, the specific situation of its coagulation function has not been fully studied. The observation of microvascular thrombosis in COVID-19 patients has attracted our attention to investigate the potential inflammatory endothelial injury or damage. Von Willebrand factor (VWF) and its proteolytic protease, A Disintegrin And Metalloproteinase with ThromboSpondin type 1 motifs, 13 (ADAMTS13), play an important role in maintaining the vascular health and organ perfusion. Therapeutic and prophylactic anticoagulation are important measures to prevent these kinds of thrombotic events, but new treatments such as recombinant ADAMTS13 and anti-VWF nanobody Caplacizumab are being studied in vitro for thrombosis with high efficacy. This review focuses on the discussion of the current research progress of the treatment of COVID-19-associated coagulopathy by correcting the imbalance of VWF-ADAMTS13 axis, the existing problems, and the prospects.

42948504.title: Refractory Obstetric Hemorrhage As the Initial Presentation of Acquired Hemophilia: A Case Report on the Diagnostic Limitations of Viscoelastic Testing.
42948504.abstract: Acquired hemophilia A is a rare autoimmune bleeding disorder caused by the development of autoantibodies against coagulation factor VIII. It is frequently associated with the postpartum period and may present as severe and persistent bleeding in patients without a prior history of coagulopathy, often leading to diagnostic delay. We report the case of a 26-year-old woman in the postpartum period following cesarean section for severe preeclampsia, who developed refractory hemorrhage despite multiple surgical interventions, including exploratory laparotomies, hematoma drainage, and abdominal packing. Laboratory evaluation revealed an isolated prolongation of activated partial thromboplastin time. Mixing studies showed incomplete correction, raising suspicion of a circulating inhibitor. Further testing confirmed severely reduced factor VIII activity and the presence of a factor VIII inhibitor. Serial thromboelastography demonstrated profound hypocoagulability with impaired thrombin generation and episodes of hyperfibrinolysis. The patient was treated with bypassing agents and combined immunosuppressive therapy, resulting in progressive reduction of inhibitor levels and recovery of factor VIII activity, ultimately achieving complete hematologic remission. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of acquired hemophilia A in the postpartum setting and emphasizes the importance of early recognition of isolated coagulation abnormalities. Prompt diagnosis and a coordinated multidisciplinary approach are essential for effective bleeding control and inhibitor eradication in critically ill patients.

42942192.title: Sutureless Aortic Valve Replacement with the Perceval Plus(®) Versus TAVI: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of Postoperative Outcomes, Hematological Dynamics, and Inflammatory Response.
42942192.abstract: Perceval Plus and TAVI are increasingly used for severe aortic stenosis, both relying on a self-expanding nitinol stent design, yet evidence specific to Perceval Plus remains limited regarding postoperative clinical outcomes and hematological and inflammatory dynamics. We compared postoperative clinical outcomes and longitudinal platelet/CRP dynamics between Perceval Plus and TAVI in a retrospective single-center cohort, in which 26 propensity score-matched pairs were obtained (1:1 matching) from patients undergoing Su-AVR (Perceval Plus, n = 53) or TAVI (self-expanding Medtronic devices, n = 101). Mortality, echocardiographic outcomes, and rates of postoperative atrial fibrillation and conduction disturbances showed no statistically significant differences between groups, while TAVI was associated with shorter ICU and hospital stay and Su-AVR required higher FFP transfusion (p = 0.016). Platelet count declined in both groups, with a deeper nadir in Su-AVR (postoperative day 3: 66% decline) versus TAVI (day 4: 27% decline), with a significant group × time interaction (p = 0.013); CRP rose in both groups but more rapidly and to a greater magnitude in Su-AVR (time and group × time interaction, both p < 0.001). Su-AVR and TAVI showed no statistically significant differences in the clinical safety outcomes assessed but differed in postoperative hematological and inflammatory magnitude, likely reflecting multifactorial procedure- and device-related mechanisms, warranting confirmation in larger, prospective, multicenter studies.

42941708.title: Outcome-Specific Performance of HALP, AIMS65, Glasgow-Blatchford, and Rockall Scores in Emergency Department Patients with Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
42941708.abstract: Background/Objectives: The Hemoglobin-Albumin-Lymphocyte-Platelet (HALP) score integrates hematologic, nutritional, immune, and platelet parameters, but its prognostic value in acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) remains uncertain. We compared the performance of HALP with AIMS65, Glasgow-Blatchford Score (GBS), and Rockall scores. Methods: We retrospectively studied consecutive adults with endoscopy-confirmed UGIB presenting to the emergency department from January 2021 through December 2024. Outcomes were in-hospital mortality, packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion within 24 h, and composite severe UGIB, defined as ≥2 PRBC units transfused within 24 h or UGIB-related intensive care unit admission. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and areas under the curve (AUCs); pairwise comparisons used the correlated-sample DeLong test. Firth-penalized logistic regression assessed the adjusted association between HALP and in-hospital mortality. Results: Of 209 patients, 24 (11.5%) died and 36 (17.2%) had variceal bleeding. For mortality, AUCs were 0.580 for inverse HALP, 0.802 for AIMS65, 0.733 for GBS, and 0.731 for Rockall. For 24-h PRBC transfusion, AUCs were 0.629, 0.642, 0.814, and 0.511, respectively; for severe UGIB, they were 0.622, 0.594, 0.781, and 0.501. No statistically significant adjusted association between HALP and mortality was observed (aOR, 0.91 per 10-point increase; p = 0.571). Conclusions: HALP showed limited discrimination across the evaluated UGIB outcomes, and no statistically significant adjusted association with mortality was observed. AIMS65 had the highest observed AUC point estimate for mortality, although its AUC did not differ significantly from those of GBS or Rockall. GBS had the highest AUCs for PRBC transfusion and severe UGIB. These findings support outcome-specific selection of UGIB risk scores and do not support the use of HALP as a stand-alone risk-stratification tool without external validation.

42939218.title: Association Between Pre-Transfusion Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome and Transfusion-Associated Adverse Events in Dogs: A Retrospective Study.
42939218.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
42939218.abstract: Blood transfusion is an important supportive therapy in critically ill dogs, but transfusion reactions (TRs) remain a clinically relevant complication. This retrospective study evaluated whether pre-transfusion systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) was associated with transfusion-associated adverse events in dogs. Medical records of dogs receiving red-cell-containing blood products at a veterinary referral hospital in the Republic of Korea between December 2023 and May 2026 were reviewed. Among 146 transfusion episodes from 100 dogs, 142 episodes with evaluable primary outcomes were included in the primary outcome analysis. Transfusion-associated adverse events were identified more frequently in the SIRS group than in the No SIRS group (32.7% vs. 11.4%; p = 0.007). In univariable logistic regression, SIRS was associated with increased odds of the primary outcome (OR, 3.78; 95% CI, 1.36-10.51; p = 0.011). In a patient-clustered multivariable generalized estimating equation (GEE) analysis, the adjusted OR remained elevated at 3.57, although the association did not reach statistical significance (95% CI, 0.98-12.98; p = 0.053). Each additional fulfilled SIRS criterion was associated with increased odds of the primary outcome (OR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.10-2.41; p = 0.014). However, the association was attenuated and was not statistically significant in sensitivity analyses using stricter outcome definitions based on imputability and independent re-adjudication. These findings suggest an association between pre-transfusion SIRS and clinically suspected transfusion-associated adverse events under the broad retrospective primary outcome definition, but the results were sensitive to the level of diagnostic certainty required for outcome classification. The findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies using standardized reaction definitions and blinded outcome assessment.

42937735.title: A case report of pulmonary embolism following endoscopic cervical discectomy in an elderly patient with cervical disc herniation.
42937735.abstract: Posterior percutaneous endoscopic cervical discectomy (P-PECD) is a minimally invasive procedure for cervical spine disorders. Although it is associated with less surgical trauma and faster postoperative recovery, serious perioperative thromboembolic complications may still occur. A 65-year-old woman with cervical disc herniation, right upper limb pain, and multiple comorbidities underwent posterior percutaneous endoscopic cervical discectomy after unsuccessful conservative treatment. On the 2nd postoperative day, she developed dizziness and decreased oxygen saturation. On the 3rd postoperative day, she complained of chest tightness. Laboratory testing revealed a markedly elevated plasma D-dimer level. Venous color Doppler ultrasound of both lower limbs demonstrated thrombosis in the bilateral calf muscular veins, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography confirmed multiple pulmonary emboli. The patient received oxygen therapy, continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring, anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin, and other supportive treatments. She was transferred to the intensive care unit for further monitoring and management. The patient's respiratory and circulatory status gradually stabilized, and her chest tightness and dizziness resolved. She was subsequently transferred back to the pain ward and discharged in stable condition. This case highlights that minimally invasive spinal surgery does not eliminate the risk of perioperative venous thromboembolism. Comprehensive preoperative thrombotic risk assessment, individualized perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy, appropriate thromboprophylaxis, early mobilization, and timely recognition and treatment of suspected APE are important for improving perioperative safety.

42936677.title: Real-world implementation of AI-assisted PERT-workflow and its association with care processes and budget impact: a retrospective cohort study.
42936677.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. In intermediate-high and high-risk PE, timely escalation beyond anticoagulation is critical, yet real-world pathways are often delayed. Pulmonary embolism response teams (PERTs) improve decision-making, but activation remains inconsistent. Whether artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled triage strengthens PERT and improves acute PE care has not been elucidated so far.
