We retrospectively screened 2500 patients presenting to our university hospital with a symptomatic central or segmental PE between 08/2022 and 07/2024. Clinical and economic outcomes were compared during a 1-year timeframe before and after implementation of an AI algorithm that analyses CT scans, flags suspected PE, and supports PERT triage. 424 patients met inclusion criteria. AI-supported triage increased PERT activation from 9.2% to 84.5% (P < 0.001). Time from CT completion to PE diagnosis decreased from 2.1 to 1.3 h (P < 0.01). Time from PE diagnosis to interventional therapy was reduced by 50% (P < 0.05). Hospital/ICU length-of-stay and 30-day mortality showed non-significant reductions. Model-based economic analysis showed lower 1-year per-patient costs and annual savings associated with AI-supported PERT. Implementation of an AI-supported PERT workflow was associated with significant improvements in PE care processes, including higher PERT activation rates and shorter diagnostic and treatment intervals. Numerical reductions in mortality, hospital/ICU length-of-stay did not reach statistical significance. The exploratory budget impact model suggested potential cost savings, mainly driven by trends in reduced resource utilization; however, these findings require prospective validation using adequately powered clinical endpoints.

42936544.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Large-Bore Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis for Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A PEERLESS Randomized Controlled Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
42936544.journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
42936544.abstract: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (LBMT) compared with catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) for the treatment of intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE). A combined decision tree and Markov model was developed to estimate lifetime health care costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALY), and net monetary benefit from the perspective of the United States health care system. Event probabilities during PE management were derived from the PEERLESS randomized controlled trial. Resource utilization, costs, and long-term event probabilities were established from published literature. Scenario analyses and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed to characterize uncertainty. In the base case analysis, LBMT was cost-saving to CDT (ie, lower costs and higher QALY), with a net monetary benefit of $5850 for the willingness-to-pay threshold of $120,000/QALY for LBMT when compared to CDT. In the PE management phase, LBMT yielded a net $4755 cost-saving and 0.009 QALY gained per patient vs CDT, driven in large part by reduced intensive care unit utilization (-$6454), shorter hospital stay (-$2217), avoided thrombolytic costs (-$4068), and fewer 30-day readmissions (-$1134). The long-term care phase yielded a total of $32,012 additional costs per patient over the lifetime with no incremental difference in costs or QALY between groups. These additional costs were driven by venous thromboembolism-related death ($12,377), chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension diagnosis and treatment ($8080), postacute anticoagulation management ($4512), and recurrent venous thromboembolism ($3289). LBMT remained cost-saving across scenarios evaluating CDT cost assumptions and device-specific chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension rates. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings across multiple parameter ranges. Intervention with LBMT in intermediate-risk PE patients in the United States is economically attractive when compared with CDT, resulting in reduced costs and marginally improved patient benefit.

42932940.title: Characterization of von Willebrand factor-enriched extracellular vesicles and their association with platelet adhesion in COVID-19.
42932940.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
42932940.abstract: Microvascular thrombosis is a hallmark of severe COVID-19 and a major contributor to adverse clinical outcomes. Extracellular vesicles have emerged as key mediators of thromboinflammation, yet their functional and molecular characteristics remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the prothrombotic activity, cellular origin, and von Willebrand factor (VWF) composition of plasma-derived small extracellular vesicles (SEVs) from hospitalized patients with COVID-19. We demonstrate that SEVs from critically ill patients with COVID-19 markedly enhance platelet adhesion and thrombus formation under arterial shear conditions and promote endothelial activation, as evidenced by increased release of ICAM-1 and VCAM-1. These SEVs were highly enriched in ultra-large VWF multimers, with significantly elevated high-to-low molecular weight ratios compared with controls. Flow cytometric analysis showed increased circulating SEVs derived from leukocytes, platelets, and endothelial cells in severe disease, with VWF-positive SEVs predominantly originating from endothelial cells. The enrichment of VWF-SEVs was independent of gender and diabetes status, suggesting a primary association with disease severity. Collectively, these findings indicate that SEVs, particularly those rich in endothelial-derived VWF, are associated with platelet activation and may contribute to the prothrombotic milieu in COVID-19. These findings underscore the importance of VWF-positive SEVs as biomarkers of disease severity and warrant further investigation into their role in COVID-19-related vascular pathology.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Circulating small extracellular vesicles in patients with COVID-19 carrying ultra-large VWF multimers boost platelet adhesion and activate endothelial cells, highlighting a potential driver and biomarker of COVID-19-associated coagulopathy.

42927239.title: Antenatal diagnosis and classification for placenta accreta (adherence) spectrum: Clinical practice guideline and recommendations by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine and the Perinatal Medicine Foundation.
42927239.abstract: This practical guidance was developed by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine in collaboration with the Perinatal Medicine Foundation to support antenatal diagnosis and clinical management in pregnancies at risk for placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). It provides an evidence-informed approach to screening, diagnosis, referral, and peripartum planning across healthcare settings with different resources. PAS is increasingly encountered alongside rising cesarean delivery rates, use of in vitro fertilization, and a history of uterine surgery. It remains associated with severe maternal morbidity, including massive hemorrhage, large-volume transfusion, uterine rupture, peripartum hysterectomy, pelvic organ injury, intensive care admission, and maternal death. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care are therefore central to management. Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is considered a potential precursor of PAS. Women with a low implantation site and a previous cesarean delivery are at increased risk. Early transvaginal ultrasound is advised in women with a previous cesarean delivery to establish the implantation site, identify CSP, and support counseling and timely consideration of uterine-preserving treatment. In the second and third trimesters, combined transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound assesses placental location, myometrial thickness and contour, and the uterovesical interface. Sonographic markers include placental lacunae, placental bulge, uterovesical hypervascularity, and bridging vessels, which may occur individually or in combination. Two-dimensional grayscale ultrasound is the mainstay of antenatal assessment, supported by color Doppler; three-dimensional imaging may provide additional information in selected specialist settings. Magnetic resonance imaging has a complementary role when ultrasound is inconclusive, placental location is non-anterior or non-previa, or technical factors limit visualization. Suspected CSP or PAS should prompt referral to a perinatal center with multidisciplinary expertise, blood product support, adult and neonatal intensive care, and access to complex pelvic surgery. Delivery timing and surgical preparation should be individualized.

42925840.title: Intraoperative and postoperative fluid administration is associated with transfusion in open arteriovenous malformation and aneurysm surgery.
42925840.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
42925840.abstract: Red blood cell transfusion to manage hemodynamic instability or blood loss during and after open cerebrovascular surgery has been associated with postoperative complications, making transfusion avoidance an important quality-improvement target. Iatrogenic hemodilution from liberal crystalloid administration may contribute to perioperative anemia, but its relevance in open aneurysm and arteriovenous malformation (AVM) surgery is poorly defined. We investigated factors associated with receiving intraoperative and postoperative transfusion in these open cerebrovascular procedures and the association between transfusion and early postoperative outcomes. In this single-center retrospective propensity-matched cohort study, patients who underwent open aneurysm or AVM surgery and received an intraoperative or postoperative red blood cell transfusion were matched 1:1 with non-transfused controls. Perioperative variables-including intraoperative and 72-h postoperative fluid administration, estimated blood loss, physiological parameters, comorbidities, and laboratory values-were compared using univariate analysis, and multivariable Firth logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with transfusion. To address the temporal relationship between fluid and transfusion, a time-anchored analysis compared pre-transfusion fluids received with fluids received by controls to the same time point. Intensive care unit and hospital length of stay were evaluated. Fifty-six patients (28 transfused, 28 controls) were analyzed. Transfused patients received more intravenous fluid in the first 72 postoperative hours (13.1 ± 4.4 vs 9.8 ± 4.6 L, p = 0.009), and transfusion percentage increased across fluid quartiles (21 %, 50 %, 64 %, and 64 %; p for trend = 0.020). Transfused patients also had a higher American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class and longer operative duration. Similarly, in the time-anchored analysis, receiving more fluids was associated with transfusion (adjusted OR 1.28 per L, 95 % CI 1.14-1.45), including after additional adjustment for ASA class (OR 1.23, 95 % CI 1.08-1.40). Intensive care unit and hospital stays were longer among transfused patients, but the differences were not statistically significant. Greater fluid administration perioperatively was associated with receiving intraoperative or postoperative transfusion after open aneurysm and AVM surgery. These findings are consistent with, but do not establish, a contribution of iatrogenic hemodilution, and they support prospective evaluation of fluid management.

42925040.title: Advantages and Limitations of the Use of Robots in Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair: Results From a Matched Direct Comparison.
42925040.abstract: To compare the surgical outcomes of nonrobotic and robotic minimally invasive mitral valve repair. We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair from January 2014 to March 2024. After excluding the learning curve cases, early and midterm outcomes were compared. A total of 422 patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair (nonrobotic, n = 103; robotic, n = 319) were enrolled. The robotic group had a higher EuroSCORE II (P < 0.001). After propensity matching, the final cohort included 84 and 168 patients in each group. In the robotic group after matching, concomitant procedures remained significantly more frequent (P = 0.030). However, operative time (P = 0.782) and cross-clamping time (P = 0.452) were comparable, whereas cardiopulmonary bypass time was significantly longer in the robotic group (P = 0.031). Postoperative blood transfusion (P < 0.001), chest tube output within 24 h (P < 0.001), and intensive care unit stay (P = 0.042) remained higher in the robotic group after matching. Postoperative mitral regurgitation was no greater than mild in both groups (P = 0.146). At 4 years, overall survival was 94.4% versus 98.4% (P = 0.215), and freedom from recurrence of moderate or greater mitral regurgitation was 98.5% versus 97.9% (P = 0.230) after matching. These results are consistent with those observed before matching. Robotic mitral valve repair demonstrated comparable perioperative and midterm outcomes despite greater transfusion requirements and a higher frequency of concomitant procedures. The higher rate of concomitant procedures should be interpreted with caution because it may partly reflect differences in surgical era and patient selection.

42924162.title: Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension With Cold Agglutinins Needing Pulmonary Thromboendarterectomy: The Use of Therapeutic Plasma Exchange.
42924162.abstract: Cold agglutinins can be detected in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) during pulmonary thromboendarterectomy (PTE) pre-operative testing. Peri-operative management of these patients in anticipation of deep hypothermic circulatory arrest can be challenging and has not been standardized. We describe our relevant experience and suggest a potential protocolized pre-operative approach with this observational, retrospective cohort study. A chart review of all patients undergoing PTE surgery for CTEPH (1107 patients) at UC San Diego between 2019 and 2025 was performed. An Institutional Review Board approved quality improvement database on all patients undergoing PTE surgery was used. Twenty-one patients (1.9%) screened positive for cold agglutinins pre-PTE. A high co-prevalence of antiphospholipid syndrome and cold agglutinins was noted (17/21; 81%). Thermal amplitude testing (when possible) was positive for nine patients between 15°C and 18°C. Fifteen patients underwent therapeutic plasma exchange (median of two sessions) with albumin and plasma replacement fluid followed by PTE surgery with standard cooling protocol. There were no incidents of agglutination or hemolysis peri- or post-operatively. Three patients had post-operative airway hemorrhage, two of which developed heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). There was one mortality in the setting of HIT with recurrent thrombosis and bleeding. Median intensive care unit and hospital length of stays were 3 and 12.5 days, respectively. We suggest a protocolized approach for the identification and management of high-risk patients with cold agglutinins, which may include therapeutic plasma exchange pre-operatively. This can successfully mitigate the potential risk of hypothermic circulatory arrest causing agglutination during surgery.

42923921.title: Successful vaginal birth after two or more cesareans versus failed trial of labor: A systematic review and meta-analysis of maternal and fetal outcomes.
42923921.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
42923921.abstract: To assess maternal and neonatal outcomes associated with a failed versus successful (VBAC-2). A systematic search across Pubmed, Embase and Cochrane was conducted up to October 2025, supplemented by backward snowballing. Studies with pregnant women with a two or more previous cesarean deliveries undergoing a trial of labor were included. No restrictions were applied. Data on maternal and neonatal outcomes and risk and protective factors were extracted. The DerSimonian and Laird random effects model was applied, reporting Odds Ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was evaluated using I2 statistics and the Cochran Q test. Methodological quality was appraised using the Cochrane Risk-of-bias tool for non-randomized trials (ROBINS-I). Out of 4065 studies screened, 12 studies (n= 3429) were included. We observed higher odds of postpartum hemorrhage (OR 1.98), maternal transfusion (OR 3.29), uterine rupture (OR 6.47), and neonatal intensive care unit admission (OR 6.44) in the VBAC-2 failure group. Epidural anesthesia (OR 0.56) and a history of previous vaginal birth (OR 0.27) were identified as protective factors, while a higher Body Mass Index was a risk factor for VBAC- 2 failure. These findings highlight the critical need for comprehensive patient counseling, risk assessment, and heightened clinical vigilance to optimize care strategies in this high-risk population.

42919781.title: Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Decreases Intraoperative Allogeneic Transfusion in Cyanotic Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery.
42919781.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
42919781.abstract: To evaluate the effect of autologous platelet-rich plasma (aPRP) on perioperative allogeneic blood product transfusion requirement in patients undergoing cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD) surgery and patients' prognosis. A retrospective cohort study. A tertiary university hospital. A total of 95 patients with CCHD who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) between January 2020 and August 2025 were included, of whom 81 (85.3%) underwent redo operation. Patients were divided into the aPRP group and the control group according to whether aPRP apheresis was employed. In the aPRP group, aPRP was harvested after anesthesia and transfused back to the patient after protamine neutralization, whereas the concurrently collected concentrated red blood cells (cRBCs) were reinfused during CPB or chest closure (from weaning from CPB to skin closure). In the original cohort, the aPRP group had significantly lower packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion rates, as well as PRBC and fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion volume, than the control group. After propensity score matching, the intraoperative PRBC transfusion rate no longer differed significantly between groups (aPRP v control: 17.4% v 43.5%, p = 0.180). However, the PRBC transfusion volume remained significantly lower in the aPRP group, both as total volume (0 [0, 0] v 0 [0, 400] mL; p = 0.037) and as weight-adjusted volume (0 [0, 0] v 0 [0, 15.7] mL/kg; p = 0.045). The matched intraoperative FFP transfusion requirements were also significantly reduced in the aPRP group (200 [0, 600] v 600 [400, 1,000] mL, p < 0.05). Viscoelastic testing indicated significantly improved coagulation and platelet function following aPRP administration in the treatment group. No difference in intraoperative blood loss, postoperative allogeneic blood products, 24-hour chest tube drainage, use of coagulation agents, postoperative ventilation time, or intensive care unit stay was observed. In a predominantly redo cohort of patients with CCHD undergoing cardiac surgery, the use of aPRP was associated with reduced intraoperative allogeneic blood and plasma transfusion requirements, and it also effectively preserved hemostatic function in these patients. However, the reduction in allogeneic product use may not be primarily due to the preserved hemostatic function conferred by aPRP but rather to autologous substitution of allogeneic products.

42918714.title: Pre-hospital pulse pressure as an early predictor of active hemorrhage in trauma patients.
42918714.abstract: Early identification of active hemorrhage (AH) is a critical challenge in trauma care. Narrowed pulse pressure (PP) has been associated with AH at the time of emergency department arrival; however, its role in the prehospital setting remains unclear. The aim of this study was to evaluate the utility of prehospital PP as an early predictor of AH in trauma. We conducted a retrospective multi-centre study (January 2017 - January 2020) including adult trauma patients at all three level 1 trauma centers in Alberta, Canada. AH was defined as either operative or interventional radiology hemorrhage control within 24 h of arrival, or transfusion of ≥ 4 units of packed red blood cells within 4 h. ROC and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to characterize associations between prehospital PP and AH. 2177 patients met inclusion criteria, of whom 68 (3%) had active hemorrhage. Compared to non-bleeding patients, AH patients had significantly narrower median prehospital PP (40 mmHg, IQR 29-52 vs 53, IQR 42-67; p < 0.001) and lower median systolic blood pressure (SBP; 111 mmHg, IQR 101-136 vs 138, IQR 122-156; p < 0.001). Prehospital PP demonstrated moderate ability to predict hemorrhage (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.67-0.79), comparable to SBP (AUC 0.74, 95% CI 0.67-0.81). Narrowed prehospital PP was independently associated with AH (odds ratio 1.51, 95% CI 1.28-1.79), reflecting a 51% increase in the risk of hemorrhage for each 10 mmHg the PP narrowed. Compared to non-bleeding patients, AH patients had worse outcomes including increased risk of ICU admission (63% vs 18%; p < 0.001), prolonged hospital length of stay (22 days, IQR 8-53 vs 7 days, IQR 4-15; p < 0.001), and increased mortality, although this did not reach statistical significance (18% vs 10%; p = 0.068). Prehospital PP ≤ 45 mmHg identifies patients at risk for active hemorrhage and given its high negative predictive value, is most useful to rule-out patients without active hemorrhage in the prehospital setting. PP is a useful adjunct to support early recognition of hemorrhage in trauma. This is particularly relevant for trauma centres serving large geographic regions, where prolonged transport times delay definitive hemorrhage control. Its incorporation into the prehospital assessment has potential to help facilitate timely mobilization of hemorrhage control resources that actively bleeding patients require.

42911035.title: Respiratory Syncytial Viral Infections Among Hospitalized Youth With Sickle Cell Disease.
42911035.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) imposes substantial risk to all infants, but its impact on youth with SCD (Y-SCD) is underexplored. With newer, highly effective RSV monoclonal antibodies (RSV-mAb), research is needed to inform their use in Y-SCD. This single-center study of Y-SCD aged 0-21 years identified 667 hospitalizations that included RSV testing. Of these, 5% were positive for RSV, and 68% occurred in Y-SCD beyond their first RSV season. Intensive care, positive pressure ventilation, and transfusion were required in 21%, 32%, and 21% of hospitalizations, respectively. Findings indicate that multicenter studies are warranted to determine if RSV-mAbs improve outcomes in Y-SCD.

42890580.title: Pretreatment body mass index as a prognostic factor for clinical course and survival in primary surgically treated oral squamous cell carcinoma - a retrospective study.
42890580.abstract: In oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), body mass index (BMI) is an available but imperfect marker of nutritional reserve. Evidence on pretreatment BMI in surgery-based European OSCC cohorts remains limited, especially regarding perioperative outcomes. This study evaluated associations of pretreatment BMI with overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and perioperative outcomes after curative-intent R0 resection. This retrospective single-center cohort included adult patients with previously untreated primary OSCC, available pretreatment BMI, and curative-intent R0 surgery between 2014 and 2023. BMI was assessed continuously and by World Health Organization (WHO) categories. OS and RFS were analyzed using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, pathological T category, nodal status, microvascular free-flap reconstruction, and diabetes mellitus. Perioperative outcomes included red blood cell (RBC) transfusion, RBC units transfused, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) placement, and intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay. A total of 274 patients with available pretreatment BMI were included; 116 deaths occurred. Five-year OS ranged from 31.4% in patients classified as underweight to 82.0% in patients with obesity. Higher BMI was associated with lower mortality (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99; p = 0.013), and obesity was associated with improved OS compared with normal weight (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.26-0.96; p = 0.037). BMI was not significantly associated with RFS after adjustment (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.97, 95% CI 0.93-1.00; p = 0.080). Higher BMI was associated with fewer perioperative RBC transfusions (any transfusion: OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98; p = 0.012; number of units: OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.95; p = 0.001). BMI was not independently associated with PEG placement or hospital length of stay; ICU findings depended on BMI modeling. Higher pretreatment BMI was associated with better OS and lower perioperative RBC transfusion requirements, whereas associations with RFS and most other perioperative outcomes were not significant after adjustment. Given the retrospective design and limitations of BMI as a body-composition marker, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Pretreatment BMI may help identify low-BMI patients warranting early supportive-care assessment.

42887298.title: Prevalence and predictors of early blood transfusion in renal transplant recipients: a retrospective study.
42887298.abstract: Anemia associated with chronic kidney disease is driven by reduced erythropoietin synthesis, chronic inflammation, and decreased red blood cell lifespan. During and after renal transplant surgery, recipients may need blood transfusions. Transfusion rates exhibit significant inter-center variability, largely driven by differing clinical criteria among transplant surgery, nephrology, and intensive care units. A retrospective study was conducted of 407 renal transplant recipients who underwent transplantation from May 15, 2023 to August 16, 2025 at the Shahid Dharmabhakta National Transplant Center, Nepal. Early transfusion was defined as any blood product administration occurring within 14 days post-surgery. Clinical and Laboratory variables were compared between transfused and non-transfused patients using either the Mann-Whitney U test or chi-square test as appropriate. Variables significant in univariate analysis were included in multivariate logistic regression to identify predictors of transfusion. Ninety-five patients (23.34%) required transfusions with leukoreduced red blood cells being the most common blood product. Univariate analysis revealed that preoperative hemoglobin levels, diabetic nephropathy, and the length of hospital stay were significantly associated with transfusion requirements. Multivariate analysis showed that preoperative hemoglobin and length of stay were predictors of transfusion. The hemoglobin nadir for the transfused group reached a mean of 6.3 ± 1.05 g/dL and a median of 6.1 g/dL, with an interquartile range from 4.2 to 10.0 g/dL. The results of this study show that a conservative transfusion approach can be effective in achieving good clinical outcomes, especially in resource limited centers.

42886584.title: Patient Blood Management Adoption and Transfusion-Threshold Concordance Among Romanian Anesthesiologists: National Survey Analysis.
42886584.abstract: Romania issued national patient blood management (PBM) guidelines in 2018. A 2023 national survey described the overall uptake of PBM among anesthesiologists but did not examine which clinicians and institutions adopted PBM, nor whether stated transfusion thresholds aligned with a study-defined restrictive reference. This study aimed to identify determinants of PBM adoption and to quantify transfusion-trigger concordance, using a planned, exploratory, cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2023 survey. We analyzed 511 responses to the 38-item Romanian Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care (SRATI) PBM survey. Three adoption outcomes (applying PBM, a formal hospital PBM group, and routine preoperative anemia treatment) were modeled by multivariable logistic regression against physician grade, hospital category, and local PBM educational events. Eight standardized clinical vignettes (age×cardiac disease×bleeding state) were scored against a restrictive hemoglobin reference (7 g/dL general; 8 g/dL with cardiac disease). The reported timing of the preanesthetic consultation (4 frequency items) was additionally examined as a determinant of preoperative anemia treatment. This was a planned, exploratory secondary analysis; the robustness of the main findings was examined in sensitivity analyses that accounted for survey attrition and for alternative transfusion-threshold scoring rules. Overall, 73.7% (373/506) reported applying PBM, 33.1% (158/477) reported a formal PBM group, and 33.5% (117/349) reported routine preoperative anemia treatment. Local PBM educational events were the strongest adjusted correlate of reported adoption (applying PBM: adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 9.78, 95% CI 4.33-22.07; P<.001; formal group: aOR 7.72, 95% CI 4.30-13.88; P<.001). Earlier preanesthetic consultation was associated with routine preoperative anemia treatment (aOR 1.79 per frequency level for consultation more than 7 days before surgery, 95% CI 1.36-2.35; P<.001). Transfusion-trigger concordance was lower for older than younger patients in otherwise identical scenarios (eg, active bleeding without cardiac disease: 195/345, 56.5% at ≥65 years vs 288/347, 83% at <65 years), and 56.5% (196/347) endorsed a liberal trigger (hemoglobin ≥8 g/dL) in at least one noncardiac scenario. Self-reported PBM application was not associated with a restrictive transfusion pattern (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 0.69-1.98; P=.56). Findings were unchanged across scoring rules, and reported PBM application was similar among respondents who did and did not complete the demographic block (246/329, 74.8% vs 127/177, 71.8%; P=.53). In this exploratory cross-sectional analysis, reported PBM adoption was associated more strongly with local educational activity than with hospital category or physician seniority. Self-reported PBM application was not associated with restrictive stated thresholds in hypothetical scenarios, and respondents selected more liberal thresholds for older patients. Standardized multidisciplinary pathways, earlier anemia screening shared with the surgical team, and education focused on transfusion decisions may help address these gaps. Prospective studies using observed process measures, transfusion practice, and clinical outcomes are needed.

42885756.title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
42885756.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
42885756.abstract: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m2), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m2), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (Pfor interaction <0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80], Pfor interaction <0.05). An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

42883774.title: D-Dimer in Viral Respiratory Infections: Established Evidence in COVID-19 and Emerging Evidence in Other Respiratory Viruses.
42883774.abstract: Viral respiratory infections remain a major cause of global morbidity and mortality, with severe disease increasingly recognized to involve profound interactions between inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, coagulation activation, and immunothrombosis. D-dimer, a fibrin degradation product and established biomarker of fibrin turnover, has gained considerable attention because of its strong association with adverse outcomes in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). This narrative review compares the evidence for D-dimer in COVID-19 with that available for other respiratory viruses and deliberately separates three questions that are frequently conflated: whether D-dimer predicts severity or death (prognostic), whether it identifies or excludes venous thromboembolism (diagnostic), and whether it identifies patients who benefit from anticoagulation (treatment-predictive). In COVID-19, elevated D-dimer is reproducibly associated with disease severity, thromboembolic complications, intensive care unit admission, and mortality, and the association persists after adjustment; however, discrimination is only moderate, incremental value over routine clinical variables has rarely been tested, and randomized trials have not established D-dimer as a treatment-selection biomarker. Outside of COVID-19, the evidence is substantially weaker and uneven: influenza is supported mainly by comparative cohorts, adenovirus by a single unvalidated paediatric prediction model, and the only direct study of D-dimer and clinical severity in bronchiolitis was negative, while for MERS-CoV, parainfluenza, and human metapneumovirus, we identified no study relating D-dimer to a clinical outcome. Moreover, substantial heterogeneity in assay methodology, sampling strategies, and proposed cut-off values restricts standardization and cross-study comparisons. We therefore present COVID-19 as a mechanistic and methodological reference rather than a validated universal rule, and summarize the evidence in a structured table and a visual evidence map. Overall, D-dimer appears to represent an integrated biomarker of coagulation activation, endothelial injury, and systemic inflammation rather than thrombosis alone, supporting its role in risk stratification while underscoring the need for context-specific interpretation. The cross-viral propositions advanced here should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Future prospective multicentre studies using standardized assays, serial biomarker assessment, and multimarker prediction models are required to establish pathogen-specific prognostic frameworks and define the role of D-dimer in precision medicine for viral respiratory infections.

42882215.title: Isolated Robotic Mitral Valve Replacement Across Body Mass Index Categories: Early Perioperative Outcomes.
42882215.abstract: Background: Obesity may pose additional technical and perioperative challenges in robotic mitral valve surgery. This study evaluated early perioperative outcomes of isolated robotic mitral valve replacement (MVR) across BMI categories. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 146 patients who underwent isolated robotic MVR at a single center, categorized into BMI categories of <25 kg/m2 (n = 60), 25.0-29.9 kg/m2 (n = 38), or ≥30 kg/m2 (n = 48). Preoperative characteristics, operative variables, and early postoperative outcomes were compared among groups. The study was exploratory. Four clinically selected outcomes, cardiopulmonary bypass time, ventilation duration, hospital length of stay, and postoperative left ventricular ejection fraction, were evaluated using adjusted median quantile regression with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and multiplicity across postoperative outcomes was addressed using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate. Results: Patients with BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 were older and had a higher prevalence of diabetes and higher EuroSCORE II values. Unadjusted comparisons of cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times, conversion to sternotomy, ventilation duration, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay, drainage volume, and transfusion requirements yielded p values > 0.05. In adjusted analyses of the four selected outcomes, all 95% confidence intervals for the BMI-group estimates included zero. Pneumonia was numerically more frequent in patients with BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 (10.4% vs. 2.6% and 1.7%), but the estimates were imprecise. In-hospital mortality was low, with one death overall. Only eight patients had BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2. Conclusions: Among patients considered suitable for robotic MVR, the adjusted estimates showed no statistically detectable association between BMI category and the selected early outcomes. However, the confidence intervals did not establish equivalence, and the findings apply only to selected robotic surgical candidates.

42881844.title: The DRESS/HLH Overlap Syndrome: A Systematic Review of Clinical Features, Triggers, and Outcomes.
42881844.abstract: Background/Objectives: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) are life-threatening conditions characterized by immune dysregulation. Several reports have identified an overlap between these entities; however, clinical characteristics, triggers, and outcomes remain poorly defined. The objective of this study was to characterize the clinical features and outcomes of DRESS/HLH overlap syndrome. Methods: We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of PubMed, Embase, and MEDLINE. Studies were included if they reported cases meeting criteria for DRESS syndrome and HLH. Results: Thirty-six patients were included, 75% female and 27.8% pediatric. Initial misdiagnosis occurred in 30.6% and was associated with higher mortality (45.5% vs. 20.0%). Antibiotics were the most frequent triggers (36.1%) and 11.1% of patients had no trigger identified. Mean latency was 27.9 days for DRESS syndrome and 35 days for HLH, with shorter latency in antibiotic-associated cases. DRESS syndrome and HLH most commonly occurred sequentially (n = 22, 61.1%) and in 52.8% of cases DRESS preceded HLH. Fever and rash were present in 88.9%. Laboratory abnormalities included hyperferritinemia (91.7%), eosinophilia (77.8%), anemia (75.0%), and thrombocytopenia (75.0%). Hepatic involvement was nearly universal (94.4%), followed by renal involvement (36.1%). Viral reactivation was observed in 38.9%, multiorgan failure in 36.1%, and ICU admission in 19.4% of cases. Mortality was 27.8% and higher in steroid-refractory cases and those with multiorgan failure. Treatment included corticosteroids (97.2%), with IVIG (33.3%), etoposide (13.9%), and cyclosporine (5.6%) used in severe cases. Conclusions: DRESS-HLH overlap represents a severe hyperinflammatory syndrome with high mortality. Early recognition and escalation of therapy are essential to improve outcomes. This is the largest and most uniformly characterized cohort of DRESS/HLH overlap reported to date, and the first to stratify mortality by diagnostic accuracy, temporal pattern, corticosteroid responsiveness, and multiorgan failure. Because the syndrome is rare and the evidence base consists almost entirely of single-case reports, multicenter collaboration and a prospective registry are needed to define incidence and optimal therapy.

42964158.title: Palliative care in hematologic malignancies: a bibliometric review and visualization analysis from 2000 to 2025.
42964158.abstract: Patients with hematologic malignancies experience a substantial symptom burden and uncertain disease trajectories, yet palliative care is often integrated later than in solid-tumor oncology. This study characterized publication patterns, collaboration networks, research topics, and citation structures in this literature from 2000 to 2025. The Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus were searched on June 10, 2026, for English-language articles and reviews published during 2000-2025. After database integration, deduplication, screening, and full-text treatment-content verification, 307 publications were included. VOSviewer and the bibliometrix package in R were used to summarize annual output, leading contributors, keyword co-occurrence, trend topics, thematic communities, keyword bursts, local citations, and reference co-citation. A structured narrative synthesis contextualized highly cited and recent publications. The corpus comprised 258 articles and 49 reviews published between 2001 and 2025. Annual output increased at a descriptive rate of 17.6% and was higher after 2017, reaching 49 publications in 2025. The United States contributed 146 publications, while international co-authorship accounted for 14.98% of the corpus. Duke University and Harvard University were the leading institutional groups, Thomas W. LeBlanc was the most productive author, and the Journal of Palliative Medicine published the most articles. Seven palliative, supportive care, or hospice journals accounted for 38.8% of publications, whereas three leading hematology journals contributed 19 articles. Keyword co-occurrence, median publication years, thematic communities, and burst analyses indicated that recent publications more frequently addressed early palliative care, integration, communication, quality of life, health care access, equity and disparities, and care alongside hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation. The substantive literature described late referral, intensive care near death, transfusion access, prognostic uncertainty, caregiver needs, and limited primary palliative care capacity. This literature has expanded and increasingly examines concurrent palliative care during intensive hematologic treatment. Research remains concentrated in a limited number of countries, institutions, author groups, and palliative care journals. Further empirical studies could examine underrepresented settings and topics, including community, rural, and international care, caregiver support, primary palliative care, equity, and palliative transfusion. These bibliometric findings describe the structure and topics of the literature; they do not address clinical effectiveness or changes in practice.

42959758.title: The effect of vitamin C supplementation additive to the priming solution on postoperative bleeding in coronary artery bypass grafting: A randomized controlled trial.
42959758.abstract: Patients undergoing cardiac surgery often experience bleeding during and after the procedure. Antioxidants such as Vitamin C (VC) are used to manage postoperative bleeding and inflammation after cardiac surgery. A total of 110 patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) were enrolled. Patients were randomly assigned into two groups of 55 participants each. In the intervention group, 25 mg/kg of VC was added to the CPB priming solution. In the control group, 25 mg/kg of normal saline was added instead. Nurse recorded the amount of chest tube drainage on intensive care unit (ICU) entry, and 2, 4, 6, 12, and 24 hours. They also documented the amount of blood product transfusion required during surgery and in the ICU. The amount of chest tube drainage in the control group was higher than the intervention group, but this difference was not statistically significant between the two groups (P > 0.05). The amount transfused blood in the operating room and in the ICU in the intervention group was 1.64±0.79 and 2.14±1.17 ml, respectively, and in the control group it was 1.69±0.84 and 2.52±1.68 ml, which was not statistically significant between the two groups (P > 0.05). There was no significant difference in duration of ICU and hospital stay between the two groups (P > 0.05). Adding VC to the CPB prime showed a non-significant trend toward reduced postoperative bleeding after CABG. Current evidence from this study is insufficient to recommend routine use; further larger trials are needed.

42958300.title: Effects of mechanical thrombectomy combined with anticoagulation vs anticoagulation monotherapy for acute intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial (CAPE study, ChiCTR2500095253, https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn/clinicalResearch/researchInfo?id=c57630b7-51ec-4b24-83e1-85b9c0a835d6).
42958300.abstract: Treatment of intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism is still debated. Interventional therapy is being increasingly widely applied in clinical practice. Numerous studies have confirmed that interventional therapy is effective. Both catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) and mechanical thrombectomy (MT) showed improvement in some efficacy outcomes compared with anticoagulation monotherapy. A recent study showed that MT has lower rates of clinical deterioration and/or bailout and postprocedural intensive care unit use compared with CDT, with no difference in mortality or bleeding, which makes the application of MT in clinical practice increasingly widespread. Recently, STORM-PE, the first randomized controlled trial to test the efficacy and evaluate the safety of MT combined with anticoagulation compared with anticoagulation monotherapy for the treatment of intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, showed that treatment with MT combined with anticoagulation resulted in a significantly greater reduction in right ventricular/left ventricular (RV/LV) diameter ratio at 48 h versus anticoagulation monotherapy, with comparably low rates of major adverse events in both treatment arms. However, whether MT combined with anticoagulation is more effective than anticoagulation monotherapy needs more evidence, especially in Asian populations. The CAPE study is a currently enrolling national multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing MT with MPA 8F guiding catheter [Cordis (Shanghai) Medical Device Co., Ltd] combined with anticoagulation vs anticoagulation monotherapy. A total of 156 patients with acute intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism stratified by the classification of the latest guideline of European Society of Cardiology (ESC) will be enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio. The primary efficacy endpoint was reduction of RV/LV diameter ratio assessed by computed tomographic angiography (CTPA) at 48 h. The secondary efficacy endpoint was the incidence of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary disease including chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. The primary safety endpoint was serious adverse events including major bleeding through 3 months visit. CAPE is a RCT to compare the short and long efficacy of MT combined with anticoagulation and anticoagulation monotherapy for acute intermediate-high pulmonary embolism. The result will give more evidence for selection of different strategies for physicians. CAPE study is registered in Chinese Clinical Trial Registry identifier (ChiCTR2500095253,  https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn/clinicalResearch/researchInfo?id=c57630b7-51ec-4b24-83e1-85b9c0a835d6 ). Registered on November 26 2024.

42957613.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Mechanical Thrombectomy and Anticoagulation in Intermediate- to High-Risk Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42957613.abstract: The comparative effectiveness of catheter-based mechanical thrombectomy in intermediate to high-risk acute PE remains uncertain. We reviewed comparative evidence to determine how thrombectomy performs against anticoagulation alone. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through September 13, 2026. We selected adult studies that compared mechanical thrombectomy plus anticoagulation with anticoagulation alone in intermediate to high-risk PE. Random-effects pooling was supplemented by sequential study removal, influence assessment, and Baujat plots. Seven studies including 9371 participants were eligible: 2 randomized trials and 5 cohort studies. Thrombectomy was associated with fewer 30-day deaths (odds ratio [OR], 0.28; 95% CI, 0.17-0.47) and a greater improvement in RV/LV ratio (mean difference, -0.25; 95% CI, -0.36 to -0.13). The groups did not differ significantly in bleeding (OR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.57-1.18) or PE-related mortality (OR, 1.25; 95% CI, 0.22-7.28). ICU and hospital stays were not significantly reduced, and these endpoints varied substantially between studies. Mortality and bleeding were less sensitive to individual reports than length-of-stay outcomes. Thrombectomy was linked to lower early all-cause mortality and more favorable right ventricular recovery without a significant bleeding excess. Its effects on PE-specific death and resource use remain uncertain. More adequately powered randomized trials are needed to define which intermediate to high-risk patients should receive the procedure.

42870302.title: Proteomic identification of resistin as a NET-associated neutrophil activity marker in sepsis.
42870302.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contribute to organ dysfunction in sepsis, yet clinically accessible biomarkers reflecting NET-associated pathology remain limited. We sought to identify circulating proteins associated with NET formation and evaluate their clinical relevance in sepsis. Unbiased proteomic profiling of stimulated human neutrophil supernatants and serum from murine sepsis was performed to identify proteins released during NET formation and elevated in vivo. Candidate biomarkers were selected through integration of these datasets and filtering based on cell type-specific expression profiles, followed by validation in patients with sepsis and healthy controls. Integrative analysis identified five candidate circulating markers associated with NET formation in sepsis: cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide, lactotransferrin, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), resistin, and histone H4. Among these, resistin, a recently recognized neutrophil-associated protein, and NGAL demonstrated the strongest associations with sepsis-associated complications. Both markers were elevated in patients with sepsis and correlated with circulating cell-free DNA levels. In receiver operating characteristic curve analyses, resistin discriminated multiple organ failure (AUC, 0.83) and disseminated intravascular coagulation (AUC, 0.81), whereas NGAL demonstrated similarly robust performance (AUC, 0.84 and 0.79, respectively). Both markers outperformed conventional clinical parameters for discriminating sepsis-associated complications. These findings identify resistin as a circulating marker associated with NET formation that captures key features of sepsis-associated immunothrombosis and organ failure and may improve assessment of disease severity and risk stratification.

42864514.title: Optimal Transfusion Thresholds in Patients with Acute Brain Injury: A Bayesian Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
42864514.abstract: The optimal transfusion threshold for acute brain injury (ABI) remains uncertain. Previous studies comparing liberal and restrictive transfusion strategies have yielded inconsistent findings. Therefore, we performed a Bayesian network meta-analysis to compare the effectiveness and safety of different transfusion thresholds in patients with ABI. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), and the Cochrane Library was performed to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing red blood cell transfusion thresholds in patients with ABI. The primary outcomes were mortality and unfavorable functional outcome. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated from the Bayesian network meta-analysis, and treatment rankings were assessed using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Six RCTs involving 2599 patients were included. Four transfusion thresholds were evaluated (hemoglobin levels of 7, 8, 9, and 10 g/dL). Compared with a transfusion threshold of 7 g/dL, a threshold of 9 g/dL was associated with a lower risk of unfavorable functional outcome (RR 0.86, 95% CrI 0.78-0.94; direct evidence from two trials). Compared with 8 g/dL, the estimated effect favored a 9 g/dL threshold, but the evidence was indirect and did not reach statistical significance (RR 0.79, 95% CrI 0.63-1.00). No clear differences in adverse events were observed across the evaluated thresholds. The 9 g/dL threshold ranked highest according to SUCRA values for both mortality and neurological outcomes. Meta-regression analysis suggested that baseline hemoglobin level may represent a potential source of heterogeneity in the effect of liberal transfusion strategies on functional outcomes. Among the evaluated transfusion thresholds, a threshold of 9 g/dL ranked most favorably for functional outcome and was associated with a lower risk of unfavorable functional outcome than 7 g/dL, without clear differences in mortality, infectious complications, or thromboembolic events.

42839199.title: Rethinking Platelet Dysfunction in Traumatic Brain Injury: From Platelet Count to Hemostatic Phenotype.
42839199.abstract: Coagulopathy after traumatic brain injury (TBI) is multifactorial and dynamic, with major implications for hemorrhagic progression and outcome. Platelet dysfunction is an underrecognized component that may occur despite preserved platelet count. For the purpose of this point of view, platelet dysfunction refers to any measurable impairment in agonist-induced aggregation, receptor-pathway responsiveness [adenosine diphosphate (ADP)/P2Y12 and arachidonic acid (AA)/ cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) axes], or platelet contribution to whole-blood-clot strength, occurring disproportionate to or in the absence of thrombocytopenia. Functional impairment can appear early and has been associated with TBI severity, intracranial hemorrhage progression, transfusion requirements, and mortality. Conventional coagulation tests and platelet count are insufficient to identify this phenotype. Platelet function assays, including thromboelastography (TEG) with platelet mapping, may help characterize selected high-risk patients. However, the evidence remains largely observational, thresholds are heterogeneous, interassay concordance is poor, and platelet transfusion or desmopressin should not be regarded as routine interventions. This point of view reframes platelet dysfunction after TBI as a dynamic hemostatic phenotype and argues for prospective phenotype-guided trials.

42837141.title: Competing Paradigms in Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Hemostatic Transfusion.

42833236.title: Combined amivantamab, lazertinib, and bevacizumab in patients with EGFR-mutant advanced non-small-cell lung cancer with acquired resistance to a third-generation EGFR tyrosine-kinase inhibitor (ETOP 18-21 AMAZE-lung): a prospective, international, multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial.
42833236.abstract: MET and angiogenic pathways are activated in EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) upon resistance to tyrosine-kinase inhibitors (TKIs). Amivantamab, an EGFR and MET bispecific antibody, is approved in combination with chemotherapy for EGFR-mutant NSCLC post-osimertinib progression based on results of the MARIPOSA-2 trial. We assessed the activity and safety of combined amivantanab, lazertinib, and bevacizumab-a chemotherapy-sparing strategy-for patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC and acquired resistance to a third-generation EGFR TKI. ETOP 18-21 AMAZE-lung was a prospective, international, multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial. Adults (aged ≥18 years) with advanced stage, pathologically confirmed non-squamous NSCLC harbouring a sensitising EGFR mutation (exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R, or both) with disease progression following treatment with a third-generation EGFR TKI (osimertinib or lazertinib) given in the first-line or second-line setting were included. Patients received intravenous amivantamab at a fixed dose of 1400 mg or 1750 mg (if bodyweight ≥80 kg) every 3 weeks for two cycles, then 1750 mg or 2100 mg (if bodyweight ≥80 kg) every 3 weeks from cycle three; oral lazertinib at a daily dose of 240 mg; and bevacizumab at a dose of 15 mg per kg every 3 weeks. Treatment was given until progression or intolerable toxicity. The primary outcome was 12-week objective response rate (defined by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours version 1.1), evaluated in the first 60 patients enrolled (intention-to-treat population). To reject an objective response rate of 20% or less versus 40%, at least 19 responses needed to be observed (2·2% significance level with 93% power). Safety was evaluated in terms of any-cause adverse events and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) graded according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0, assessed in all enrolled patients who received at least one dose of trial treatment. The trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05601973) and in the European Medicines Agency's Clinical Trials Information System (EU CT number 2021-002337-42); the primary analysis is complete but follow-up for patients on treatment is ongoing. Between March 27, 2023, and May 21, 2024, 61 patients were enrolled from 17 sites in Europe. Median age was 65 years (IQR 61-70), and most patients were female (43 [70%]) and White (50 [82%]). 37 (61%) patients had never smoked, 38 (62%) had Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 1, and 37 (61%) had stage IVB cancer. All tumours were of adenocarcinoma histology and 18 (30%) patients had asymptomatic brain metastases at screening. At the time of the primary analysis (database cutoff Aug 26, 2024), median follow-up was 9·0 months (IQR 5·8-12·6) and 28 patients were still receiving the treatment combination. Objective response by 12 weeks was shown for 20 patients among the first 60 enrolled (objective response rate 33% [95·6% CI 21-47]), successfully rejecting an objective response rate of 20% or less. Overall, 24 of 61 (39% [95% CI 27-53]) patients showed partial response (22 confirmed at subsequent tumour evaluation). The most commonly reported TRAEs of any grade were infusion-related reaction (35 [58%] of 60 patients) and acneiform rash (30 [50%] of 60 patients). Treatment-related venous thromboembolism of any grade and grade 3-4 was reported in ten (17%) and two (3%) patients, respectively. No treatment-related deaths were observed. Grade 3-4 TRAEs occurred in 26 (43%) of 60 patients, with serious TRAEs observed in 12 (20%) of 60 patients. Combined amivantamab, lazertinib, and bevacizumab showed durable anti-tumour activity, representing a promising chemotherapy-sparing alternative after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs. Safety was consistent with known toxicity profiles. The ETOP IBCSG Partners Foundation and Janssen Pharmaceutica.

42946957.title: Management and Outcomes in Traumatic Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis.
42946957.abstract: Traumatic cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (tCVST) is a rare complication of head trauma associated with increased mortality. Unlike in non-traumatic CVST, there are no consensus guidelines to direct the management of tCVST. Anticoagulation is often used to prevent intracranial complications; however, concurrent traumatic brain injury (TBI) and other injuries complicate treatment decisions, and its clinical benefit remains uncertain. This study describes the epidemiology, management, and clinical and radiographic outcomes of tCVST. This is a retrospective single-center cohort study from a level 1 trauma center in Melbourne, Australia. Patients were identified from the Alfred Health Trauma Registry and hospital coding data between 1 January 2010 and 30 June 2024. Venous imaging was reviewed by two neuroradiologists to confirm tCVST diagnosis and thrombus characteristics. Primary outcomes were defined as discharge destination, with sinus recanalization on follow-up imaging as a secondary outcome. tCVST was confirmed in 138 patients with an incidence of 0.9% in the TBI population and an all-cause inpatient mortality of 10.9% (15 patients). Anticoagulation was used in 78 patients (56.5%) and commenced a median of 5 days after diagnosis [interquartile range (IQR) 2-9]. Patients with anticoagulation generally had less severe traumatic injury, as measured by Injury Severity Score (ISS) and admission Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), but were more likely to have occlusive thrombosis. Among 123 patients who survived to hospital discharge, 93 underwent follow-up venous imaging from day 14, with complete recanalization in 57% by final available imaging. Occlusive thrombosis and multiple sinus involvement were associated with poorer recanalization, while no association between anticoagulation and recanalization was identified. Traumatic CVST is a rare complication of head injury with multiple confounders influencing outcomes and uncertain optimal management. Clinical benefit of anticoagulation in this cohort requires further investigation.

42912170.title: Heparin Retention and Dispersion Following Injection of Locking Fluid in an Acute Hemodialysis Catheter: A Simulation Study.
42912170.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42912170.abstract: Heparin locking is used to maintain patency of acute hemodialysis catheters; however, unintended leakage of locking solution into the systemic circulation may increase bleeding risk. Ideally, locking solution would remain confined to the catheter lumen, maintaining patency while minimizing systemic anticoagulation, yet the mechanisms governing heparin retention and dispersion remain inadequately understood. Patient-specific computational fluid dynamics simulations incorporating non-Newtonian blood flow and species transport were performed using a microcomputed tomography-derived model of an acute dual-lumen hemodialysis catheter to evaluate the effects of injection rate, venous blood flow, and lock volume. Injection of the manufacturer-recommended 1.4 ml lock volume over durations of 0.5-5 seconds resulted in 13-16% (900-1100 U) of injected heparin entering the systemic circulation, yielding transient therapeutic systemic heparin concentrations. Rapid injections increased distal penetration of the locking solution and improved heparin retention (from 84% to 87%). Heparin clearance following injection occurred in two phases consisting of rapid early convective washout followed by prolonged slow diffusive clearance. Reducing lock volume substantially decreased systemic heparin exposure while preserving therapeutic intraluminal heparin concentrations. These findings provide mechanistic insight into catheter locking behavior and suggest that optimization of lock volume may reduce unintended systemic anticoagulation while maintaining catheter patency.

42881421.title: Hemoglobin trends and transfusion practices after cardiac arrest: a cohort study.
42881421.abstract: Hemoglobin targets are absent from post-cardiac arrest guidelines. New trials suggest that patients with brain and myocardial injury, injuries common post-arrest, may benefit from higher hemoglobin targets. Trends in post-arrest hemoglobin and real-world practices remain poorly characterized. We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive adult cardiac arrests at three academic hospitals. We screened in-hospital and out-of-hospital arrests with resuscitation efforts ongoing at hospital arrival for inclusion. Patients who survived the initial resuscitation and had a hemoglobin value measured were included. All post-arrest hemoglobin values and red blood cell transfusions were collected through 30 days; descriptive statistics and graphical visualization were used to present hemoglobin trends and transfusion practices. Exploratory analyses evaluated the association between hemoglobin and in-hospital mortality. Of 2,634 cardiac arrests, 958 met inclusion criteria, with 152 (15.9%) out-of-hospital arrests and 806 (84.1%) in-hospital. The mean initial post-arrest hemoglobin was 9.75 g/dL (SD 2.60), with hemoglobin levels declining progressively over the first 20 days post-arrest. Red cell transfusions were delivered for 369 (38.5%) patients in the 30 days post-arrest, with 1,238 total transfusions. The mean pre-transfusion hemoglobin value was 6.96 g/dL (SD 1.06). Pre-transfusion hemoglobin levels were < 7 g/dL for 762 (61.6%) of transfusions, and ≥ 7 g/dL for 476 (38.4%) of transfusions. Over 30 days, the highest proportion of patients transfused was in the first 48 h. Patients with initial post-arrest hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL had lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.46-0.84, p<0.01). In time-varying analysis, post-arrest hemoglobin through 30 days demonstrated an L-shaped association with mortality, with 95% of the total reduction in mortality hazard captured below 9.20 g/dL. Anemia is common after cardiac arrest, worsening in initial survivors. There is substantial variation in pre-transfusion hemoglobin levels, reflecting clinical equipoise. Clinical trials are needed to disentangle anemia as a driver versus a marker of outcomes, and test whether the risk is modifiable.

42818790.title: Case Report: Postoperative pulmonary embolism causing obstructive shock and circulatory collapse after gynecologic surgery: successful rescue with VA-ECMO.
42818790.abstract: Very-high-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) occurring within hours after major surgery presents a therapeutic dilemma because urgent reperfusion may be required at precisely the time when bleeding risk is greatest. We describe a 45-year-old woman who developed catastrophic bilateral PE approximately two hours after elective gynecologic surgery consisting of myomectomy and ovarian endometriotic cyst excision. Shortly after surgery, she experienced abrupt respiratory failure, profound hypotension, and rapidly progressive circulatory collapse. On arrival at a tertiary intensive care unit, arterial blood gas analysis revealed severe respiratory acidosis (pH 7.019; PaCO2 82 mmHg), and the patient remained unstable despite mechanical ventilation, high-dose vasopressors, and conventional resuscitative measures. Because of refractory obstructive shock and the prohibitive hemorrhagic risk associated with recent pelvic surgery, emergent venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) was instituted before definitive radiological confirmation. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography subsequently demonstrated extensive bilateral pulmonary arterial thrombosis involving both proximal and distal branches. Management was further complicated by ongoing postoperative bleeding during mandatory anticoagulation for ECMO support, requiring repeated transfusion of blood products and frequent adjustment of anticoagulant therapy. During recovery, the patient also developed residual left popliteal deep vein thrombosis, postoperative inguinal hematoma, and surgical-site infection caused by extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli. Despite these challenges, she was successfully weaned from ECMO and mechanical ventilation, transitioned to oral rivaroxaban, and discharged without neurological sequelae. This case illustrates the complexity of managing acute PE when life-saving reperfusion strategies must be balanced against a substantial risk of postoperative bleeding. It also adds to the limited literature describing successful use of VA-ECMO as a bridge to recovery in immediate postoperative PE complicated by obstructive shock and circulatory collapse.

42823132.title: Toxin-induced coagulopathy following a MacMahon viper bite.
42823132.abstract: The management of a snakebite is often challenging due to limited experience, limited access to intensive care, delays in presentation and high variability in venom composition and specific antivenom availability. Classified within the genus Eristicophis, the MacMahon viper is a venomous snake species for which only two detailed case reports exist. Its venom has predominantly haemotoxic properties while neurotoxic and cytotoxic effects are less pronounced. This case illustrates the effects of Eristicophis macmahonii venom on both haemostasis and cardiovascular stability, in addition to a significant local envenomation reaction that required intervention. Laboratory analysis revealed a rapid onset of thrombocytopenia and impaired haemostatic function expressed in rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM) analysis. The first 6 hours represented an acute phase with significant hypotension and associated syncope. In the absence of clinical signs of bleeding, transfusion of blood products or administration of coagulation factors was not initiated. Thrombocytopenia resolved spontaneously within 8 days.

42819064.title: Cesarean Myomectomy: A Retrospective Observational Study at a Tertiary Care Center in Bihar, India.
42819064.abstract: Introduction Fibroids during pregnancy are frequently encountered in our routine obstetric practice. Whether cesarean myomectomy is a safe and practical treatment for women with uterine myomas or if it is completely contraindicated is a topic of much discussion. Due to the apprehension of increased blood loss, there remains a dilemma in obstetricians' decisions on whether to do a cesarean myomectomy or not. Our article may help obstetricians to make an informed decision. Method We did a single-center, uncontrolled, retrospective observational study on 25 cases who were enrolled over two years. Data were analyzed in terms of intraoperative blood loss, need for blood transfusion, operative time, hospital stay, and postoperative morbidity. Results The mean age of patients in our study was 29.1 years, and the mean gestational age at delivery in our study was 37.5 weeks. In our study, the size of uterine fibroids ranged between 4 and 16 cm. The mean operative time was 68.12 minutes. The mean drop in hemoglobin between pre- and post-op was 1.1 g/dL. There was a history of blood transfusion in seven out of 25 cases. There was no significant postoperative morbidity in all the cases, except for one, and the mean hospital stay was five days. Neonatal outcome was good in 22 cases with three neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions. Conclusion  This study concluded that myomectomy is feasible with acceptable short-term outcomes with good technique in expert hands in a tertiary care center. This has the advantages of avoiding a second surgery and cost when cases are selected appropriately.

42867694.title: Ultrasound-guided central venous access in the NICU: indications, insertion and management.
42867694.abstract: Ultrasound-guided cannulation of deep veins has advanced in little more than a decade from the operating room to the neonatal bedside and from a rescue maneuver to a planned procedure. Centrally inserted central catheters (CICCs) and femorally inserted central catheters (FICCs) are quite different from epicutaneo-cava catheters: they are 3-4 Fr power-injectable polyurethane catheters that are easy to tunnel, secured by subcutaneous anchorage, and suitable for blood transfusion, high-flow infusions, repeated blood sampling, and hemodynamic monitoring. This narrative review examines the indications, materials, insertion bundles for CICCs and FICCs in newborns, as well as their management, complications, and the training gap that now limits their diffusion more than any technical obstacle. In published studies, procedural success is 97-100%, immediate complications are absent or rare (when an insertion bundle is used), and the bloodstream infection rate is severalfold lower in infants below 1,500 g and below 1,000 g compared with the epicutaneo-cava catheter. Since the evidence comes mainly from a few high-volume centers with high procedural expertise, the priority for future research is to define strategies - structured programs, simulation, proctoring - to build and maintain the same level of competence in lower-volume units. Though the supporting evidence is observational, Ultrasound-guided CICCs (or FICCs, if in selected cases) appear to be the most appropriate central venous access for the critically ill newborn. • Ultrasound-guided CICCs and FICCs can be placed at the bedside in neonates, including extremely low birth weight infants, and outperform epicutaneo-cava catheters in safety, flow, dwell time, and range of use. • The adoption of insertion bundles reduces immediate and late complications of central venous catheterization in neonates and children. • Multicenter and comparative neonatal data show reproducible procedural success across centers and several-fold lower bloodstream infection rates in the smallest infants, compared with epicutaneo-cava catheters. • The limiting factor is no longer technical feasibility but structured training; tunneling remains the most frequently omitted step in the insertion bundle and the least easily replaced.

42949037.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons

42967895.title: Acute liver failure triggered by hemolytic crisis in a glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficient patient with hepatitis A: A case report.
42967895.abstract: Hepatitis A virus infection is one of the most common causes of acute viral hepatitis and usually results in a mild, self-limiting illness. (Biju Illolil Kuniyil) However, in rare cases, it can progress to acute liver failure, particularly in vulnerable individuals. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency is one of the most common enzymatic disorders globally. This X-linked condition predisposes red blood cells to oxidative damage and acute hemolytic episodes triggered by infections, drugs, or foods. (Aradhana Aneja) We report a 53-year-old man who presented with acute hepatitis and subsequently developed severe intravascular hemolysis, acute kidney injury, and acute liver failure. Fractionated bilirubin demonstrated significant indirect hyperbilirubinemia, and lactate dehydrogenase levels were markedly elevated, supporting intravascular hemolysis. A quantitative enzyme assay confirmed glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency. The patient developed coagulopathy and Grade II hepatic encephalopathy, fulfilling diagnostic criteria for acute liver failure. He required intravenous N-acetylcysteine, therapeutic plasma exchange, and hemodialysis. The patient recovered following multidisciplinary intensive care. This case highlights the importance of recognising glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency in patients with viral hepatitis who develop disproportionate anaemia and hyperbilirubinemia.

42967049.title: Extensive Stray-Dog Mauling as Major Contaminated Crush Trauma Causing Severe Rhabdomyolysis, Acute Kidney Injury, and Overt Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation: Recovery Without Renal Replacement Therapy.
42967049.abstract: An adolescent male developed severe rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, overt disseminated intravascular coagulation, and respiratory fluid overload after extensive stray-dog mauling. The course reflected overlapping traumatic, inflammatory, and infectious mechanisms. He recovered without renal replacement therapy through source control, individualized antimicrobials, conservative renal support, and timely transition to de-resuscitation.

42967019.title: Delayed-Onset Malignant Hyperthermia With Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation Following Successful Prior Anesthetic Use: A Case Report.
42967019.abstract: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a serious perioperative reaction associated with exposure to volatile inhalational anesthetics and/or succinylcholine. Severe episodes may lead to widespread physiologic instability, including coagulopathic complications. This case describes an otherwise healthy middle-aged man who developed MH complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) during a subsequent surgery for a left ankle fracture. MH reactions can be unpredictable due to the involved genes' incomplete penetrance, which is why MH does not always occur each time an MH-susceptible patient is exposed to a triggering agent. This case highlights the importance of maintaining vigilance for MH even in patients with prior uneventful anesthetic exposures. Patients with suspected MH reactions should be referred for genetic testing, with important implications for future anesthetic management of both the patient and their family members.

42971250.title: Trajectories of Coagulation-Fibrinolysis Balance Reveal Hemostatic Heterogeneity in Sepsis: Derivation and Multicenter Validation.
42971250.abstract: The imbalance between coagulation activation and fibrinolysis drives sepsis-induced coagulopathy and organ dysfunction. However, this dynamic process is highly heterogeneous. We aimed to identify longitudinal coagulation-fibrinolysis trajectory phenotypes and to develop a novel prothrombin time (PT)-D-dimer Z-balance score to quantify this evolving hemostatic imbalance. This study included a single-center training cohort (n=1672) and a prospective multicenter external validation cohort (n=1393) of adult septic ICU patients. Joint group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) was applied to daily PT and D-dimer measurements over the first 7 days. Hemostatic, inflammatory and prognostic profiles were compared across phenotypes. Additionally, a daily Z-balance score [Z(PT) - Z(D-dimer)] was constructed to quantify the evolving hemostatic imbalance. Joint modeling reveals three phenotypes: Compensate (Class 1, 51.9%; preserved balance), Coupled (Class 2, 35.5%; intensive but balanced coagulation-fibrinolysis activation), and Consumptive (Class 3, 12.6%; profound coagulation factor consumption with blunted fibrinolysis). The Consumptive phenotype exhibited the most severe systemic inflammation, organ failure, and the highest 28-day mortality (52.1%). Multivariable analysis confirmed Class 3 as an independent predictor of 28-day mortality in both the training (adjusted HR 2.69) and validation cohorts (adjusted HR 3.78). The novel Z-balance score revealed distinct dynamic patterns: Class 3 was characterized by persistently positive yet declining Z-balance (a delayed, partial fibrinolytic response relative to coagulation). Joint longitudinal modeling of PT and D-dimer reveals three distinct coagulation‑fibrinolysis phenotypes in sepsis. The Consumptive phenotype, characterized by profound coagulation and inflammation activation alongside a positive PT-D-dimer Z-balance, identifies a high-risk subpopulation with markedly increased mortality.

42970330.title: From liberal to restrictive and beyond: a narrative review of red blood cell transfusion strategies in the modern era.
42970330.abstract: Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion remains a cornerstone of modern medicine, yet optimal transfusion thresholds continue to be debated.
