Historically, liberal strategies -maintaining hemoglobin (Hb) concentration above 10 g/dL- predominated, but evidence from the 1990s onward has favored restrictive approaches (Hb threshold 7-8 g/dL). This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence on restrictive versus liberal transfusion strategies published between 2021 and 2026, evaluates population-specific considerations, and explores emerging ultra-restrictive thresholds. A structured narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed and Google Scholar with particular emphasis on evidence published between 2021 and 2026. Evidence from randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical practice guidelines is critically discussed. The 2025 Cochrane update (48 trials, >20,000 participants) provided high-certainty evidence that restrictive strategies induce a reduction in the risk or proportion of patients receiving at least one RBC transfusion by 41% without increasing 30-day mortality or major morbidity. Restrictive thresholds are safe in stable critically ill patients, in those undergoing non-cardiac surgery, and in patients with acute gastrointestinal bleeding. However, important exceptions include: acute myocardial infarction (in which liberal strategies may reduce cardiac events), neurocritical care (conflicting evidence on neurological outcomes), chronic transfusion-dependent conditions such as thalassemia (liberal strategies are disease-modifying), and hematologic malignancies (individualized approach required). Ultra-restrictive thresholds (Hb <6-7 g/dL) have emerged as a potential blood conservation tool during shortages but require further safety validation. Restrictive transfusion strategies are safe and effective for many stable adult hospitalized patients, reducing blood product utilization without compromising outcomes. However, individualized approaches remain essential for specific high-risk populations. Ultra-restrictive strategies are promising, but these approaches should currently be considered only in selected contexts pending further safety validation.

42971246.title: Diagnostic value of maternal serum prokineticin-1 for predicting placenta accreta spectrum and adverse maternal outcomes.
42971246.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate maternal serum prokineticin-1 (PROK1) levels in women with placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) of varying degrees, to compare them with cases of placenta previa (PP) and uncomplicated healthy pregnancies, and to determine whether this biomarker can predict disease severity and clinical outcomes. In this observational case-control study involving 153 pregnant women, 54 had singleton pregnancies with PP complicated by PAS, 51 had PP without PAS, and 48 were healthy gestational age-matched singleton controls. Demographic and clinical data, maternal and neonatal outcomes, and maternal serum PROK1 levels were collected for all participants. A receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was generated to assess the sensitivity and specificity of PROK1, and the optimal cut-off value was determined using the Youden index. Associations between PROK1 levels and continuous clinical variables were analyzed using Spearman's rank correlation. The mean maternal serum PROK1 level was markedly elevated in both the PAS group (9.29±10.53 pg/mL) and the PP group (6.65±2.88 pg/mL) compared with the control group (3.19±0.81 pg/mL, p<0.001). A cut-off value of 6.81 pg/mL for maternal serum PROK1 distinguished pregnancies complicated by PAS with a sensitivity of 96.3% and a specificity of 97.9%. A statistically significant negative linear correlation was found between maternal serum PROK1 levels and gestational week at delivery (r=-0.598, p<0.001). Additionally, a statistically significant positive correlation was observed between maternal serum PROK1 concentrations and the duration of maternal hospital stay after delivery (r=0.511, p<0.001). Women who required interventions such as transfusion, ICU admission, arterial ligation, uterine resection, or hysterectomy had significantly higher mean PROK1 levels than those who did not. PROK1 is a crucial factor associated with PAS pregnancies, and an increased PROK1 expression in these cases may alter trophoblast function and placentation. The increased PROK1 expression may be considered a potential indicator of disease severity and adverse maternal outcomes.

42968126.title: Prognostic value of modified thrombelastometry for thromboembolic risk stratification in neurosurgical patients: protocol for a prospective, multicenter, observational study (TENS).
42968126.abstract: Neurosurgical patients, particularly those with intracranial tumours such as glioma or meningioma, face a markedly elevated risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), with reported rates of deep vein thrombosis between 15% and 70% depending on tumour entity and surgical extent. Current prophylactic strategies rely predominantly on pharmacological and mechanical measures and do not account for the individual complexity of coagulation dynamics. Modified thromboelastometry, employing a low-dose tissue plasminogen activator (TPA) test, enables functional assessment of both fibrinolytic capacity and prothrombotic states at the point of care. We hypothesize that preoperative and perioperative thromboelastometric parameters - in particular lysis time (LT) in the low-dose TPA test - are associated with the occurrence of thromboembolic events in neurosurgical patients. TENS is a prospective, multicenter, observational prognostic factor study targeting 350 evaluable participants (up to 369 enrolled to account for attrition) across four university hospitals in Cologne, Munich (two centres), and Oldenburg. Eligible patients are adults (≥ 18 years) scheduled for neurosurgical procedures involving intracranial tumour resection or with an anticipated operative duration of ≥ 4 h. Thromboelastometric measurements (EXTEM, INTEM, FIBTEM, low-dose TPA test) are performed at three defined time points: before surgery, at the end of surgery, and on postoperative day 1. The primary objective is to assess the prognostic association between lysis time (LT) in the low-dose TPA test and objectively imaging-confirmed venous thromboembolic events occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints comprise further thromboelastometric parameters, standard coagulation laboratory values, and clinical outcomes including length of hospital stay, duration of surgery, ICU stay, and days at home at day 30. Modified thromboelastometry has the potential to improve individualised risk stratification for thromboembolism in neurosurgical patients. If lysis time in the low-dose TPA test demonstrates prognostic value for thromboembolic events, this could inform the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic algorithms for high-risk surgical populations. Deutsches Register Klinischer Studien (DRKS), No. DRKS00034388, registered October 8, 2024. Anonymised participant-level data and the statistical analysis code will be made available upon reasonable request to the corresponding author following publication of the primary results, subject to applicable data protection regulations and the terms of the institutional data sharing agreement (see chapter The full study protocol will be publicly accessible via the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS, No. DRKS00034388). The study is currently in active recruitment. Recruitment was initiated at the coordinating centre in Cologne on 19 December 2024, with additional centres opening after completion of their local approval and site-initiation processes. As of March 2026, fewer than 50% of the target sample of 350 evaluable participants had been enrolled. Recruitment is expected to be completed by March 2027.

42977378.title: Intensive Care Unit Management of the Hemodynamically Significant Pulmonary Embolism.
42977378.abstract: Acute pulmonary embolism remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with prognosis determined by right ventricular (RV) adaptation to the abrupt rise in pulmonary vascular resistance. Although most cases can be managed outside the intensive care unit, patients with RV failure, hemodynamic instability, or cardiac arrest require advanced monitoring and intervention. Management in this setting emphasizes rapid diagnosis and risk stratification, timely initiation of reperfusion therapies, and carefully tailored hemodynamic and respiratory support. Optimal outcomes rely on multidisciplinary collaboration, early escalation of care, and individualized, evidence-based decision-making.

42975800.title: Practice variation in mechanical circulatory support: a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of Japanese interventional cardiologists in the CVIT Kyushu-Okinawa chapter.
42975800.abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) practice for cardiogenic shock may vary with institutional resources and operator experience, but data from Japanese interventional cardiologists are limited. We conducted an anonymous cross-sectional survey of 720 members of 83 Japanese Association of Cardiovascular Intervention and Therapeutics (CVIT)-certified or affiliated training hospitals in the CVIT Kyushu-Okinawa Chapter (September-October 2025); 536 returned questionnaires (74.4%), and consent was confirmed for 385 (53.5%). The primary analysis included 276 respondents who had performed intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), or Impella CP insertion within 12 months: 163 at Impella-capable and 113 at non-Impella-capable hospitals. Documented MCS and extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation protocols were more frequently reported by respondents from Impella-capable hospitals (46% vs. 6% and 39% vs. 13%, respectively), as was collaboration with emergency and critical care physicians; no statistically significant difference was detected in perceived need for collaboration. MCS selection varied between groups. At Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock stage C, IABP (44%) and Impella CP (48%) were selected with similar frequency among respondents in Impella-capable hospitals, whereas IABP was selected by 79% in non-Impella-capable hospitals. At stage E, ECPELLA (79%) and VA-ECMO plus IABP (84%) predominated, respectively. Among respondents with device-specific operator experience within 12 months, vascular access and anticoagulation practices varied between groups. Procedural anxiety was lower with higher CVIT qualification; however, 19% of board-certified members reported anxiety about Impella CP insertion and 45% about emergency intubation. These findings identify MCS practice variation across several domains warranting further evaluation.

42972582.title: Coagulopathy and anticoagulation management in adult ECPR patients.
42972582.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a lifesaving strategy for refractory cardiac arrest, restoring systemic perfusion when conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation fails. However, ECPR profoundly disrupts haemostasis, driven by the combined effects of whole-body ischaemia-reperfusion injury, systemic inflammation, endothelial activation, platelet dysfunction, and blood contact with extracorporeal surfaces. Together, these processes create a highly dynamic and unstable thromboinflammatory milieu, marked by the simultaneous risk of thrombosis and life-threatening bleeding. Systemic anticoagulation is required to maintain circuit patency and prevent thromboembolic complications, yet optimal strategies remain uncertain. Haemostasis during ECPR is highly dynamic, shaped by the underlying aetiology of cardiac arrest, patient-specific characteristics, and circuit-related factors. This complexity underscores the limitations of fixed anticoagulation targets and the need for individualized, context-sensitive management guided by continuous clinical and laboratory assessment. Despite the increasing global adoption of ECPR, high-quality evidence to guide anticoagulation practices remains scarce. Current strategies are largely extrapolated from other extracorporeal life support populations, contributing to substantial inter-centre variability. This review synthesizes the available evidence on coagulopathy and anticoagulation in adult patients receiving ECPR and discusses emerging approaches to monitoring and anticoagulation management.

42980514.title: Platelet Transfusion Practices in the PICUs: Multicenter, Observational Study, in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus, 2024.
42980514.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
42980514.abstract: We aimed to describe the use of platelet transfusions among critically ill children managed in Türkiye in late 2024. Secondarily, we sought to determine these practices in relation to the 2022 Transfusion and Anemia Expertise Initiative-Control/Avoidance of Bleeding (TAXI-CAB) recommendations for critically ill pediatric patients. Prospective study (October-December 2024). 22 PICUs in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus. Patients of 1 month to 18 years who received at least one platelet transfusion in the PICU. None. Out of 2693 PICU admissions, 200 patients (7.4%) received 577 platelet transfusions. Of the transfusions, 383 of 577 transfusions (66.4%) were for prophylaxis, most frequently for isolated thrombocytopenia (194/383, 50.7%). Regarding the transfusion threshold for prophylaxis, in the 194 cases of isolated thrombocytopenia, the median (interquartile range [IQR]) pretransfusion platelet count was 24 (IQR, 16-38) × 109/L, which differed from the TAXI-CAB consensus statement guidance of less than 10 × 109/L. Platelet transfusion, as opposed to not, was associated with 20-fold greater odds of 28-day mortality (p < 0.001), and among the 200 patients receiving platelets, multivariable analysis showed that lower pretransfusion platelet count, support with invasive mechanical ventilation, and hospital-acquired infections collectively accounted for 34% of the variance in model performance for classifying 28-day mortality. Our 2024 national, multicenter PICU study across Türkiye and Northern Cyprus shows that around two-thirds of transfusion episodes were for prophylaxis, and multivariable logistic regression modeling identified patient factors associated with greater odds of 28-day mortality. The median pretransfusion threshold for isolated thrombocytopenia was around 20 × 109/L, which is double the less than 10 × 109/L in the 2022 TAXI-CAB consensus statement. Given the heterogeneity of critically ill patients and practice environments, understanding the reasons behind these practices may help inform future research and consensus recommendations.

42981431.title: A synthetic heparin oligosaccharide decouples anticoagulation from heparin-induced thrombocytopenia risk.
42981431.abstract: Low-molecular weight heparin (LMWH) remains clinically indispensable for the prevention and treatment of thrombosis in cardiovascular surgery, hemodialysis, and other critical care settings. However, LMWH is constrained by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) and supply chain vulnerabilities of animal-derived sources. This study used chemoenzymatic synthesis to engineer homogeneous dodecasaccharide 12G-2, decoupling anticoagulant efficacy from HIT risk via dual structural modulation. Substitution with 2-O-sulfated glucuronic acid conferred conformational rigidity, and engineered sulfation attenuated platelet factor 4 (PF4) binding, whereas the antithrombin-binding domain remained intact. 12G-2 exhibited nanomolar anti-Factor Xa (FXa) activity in vitro, enoxaparin-equivalent venous antithrombotic efficacy, and superior arterial antithrombotic activity in murine thrombosis models, and it showed diminished PF4 binding, attenuated pathological β sheet formation, and minimal recognition by HIT-related antibodies in vitro. Both in vitro and in a murine tail-bleeding model, 12G-2 demonstrated high protamine reversibility, exceeding standard LMWH enoxaparin neutralization efficiency. In washed human platelets, 12G-2-PF4 complexes with the HIT-mimicking antibody KKO failed to induce integrin αIIbβ3 activation or P-selectin release and elicited minimal platelet spreading comparable to resting controls. Safety assessments in mice showed no hepatotoxicity at tested doses and low immunogenicity in a murine PF4-heparin immunization model. In PF4-heparin antibody-positive mice, 12G-2 attenuated platelet activation while exerting stronger FXa inhibition than enoxaparin. These findings established 12G-2 as an alternative to LMWH.

42977882.title: Staple Line Reinforcing During Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy: Comparison of Through and Through vs. Lembert's Oversewing Methods: Single Center Experience.
42977882.abstract: The most serious stapler line complications (SLC) following laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) are bleeding and stapler line leakage (SLL). Various oversewing methods are used that reduce SLC by reinforcing the staple line (SLR): Through and Through (TaT) or Lembert suturing. In this retrospective study, we compared the effects of the Lemberts and TaT suturing on SLC incidence. A total of 586 patients were included in the study. These patients were divided into two groups: TaT (n = 386) and Lemberts (n = 200). The primary endpoints were SLL and bleeding. Secondary endpoints included postoperative complications, Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ 3 complications, operative time, oversewing time, length of hospital stay, and mortality. Operative time was longer in the TaT suturing method (p < 0.001), while oversewing time was longer in the Lemberts suturing method (p < 0.001). The incidence of bleeding and SLL was significantly lower with Lembert's suturing method (p = 0.01, p = 0.04; respectively). All postoperative complications, Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ 3 complications and length of hospital stay were more seen in the TaT suturing method (p = 0.002, p = 0.02, p < 0.001; respectively ). The incidence of blood transfusions, intensive care unit stay, and readmission rates were similar between the two methods. Compared to the TaT suturing method, the Lemberts suturing method was associated with a reduction in postoperative bleeding, SLL, all postoperative complications, Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ 3 complications, and length of hospital stay, without causing a major difference in oversewing and total operative time. No differences were found between the two methods in terms of blood transfusion, intensive care unit stay, or mortality.

42977756.title: Regulatable membrane-bound IL-15 engineered TIL cell therapy for immune checkpoint inhibitor-resistant advanced melanoma: pooled analysis of phase 1 and 1/2 trials.
42977756.abstract: Amsokigene autoleucel (amsoki-cel, OBX-115) is a tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapy engineered to express acetazolamide (ACZ)-regulatable membrane-bound interleukin-15, abrogating the need for interleukin-2. In two single-arm trials (completed phase 1 single-center first-in-human (FIH) and ongoing phase 1/2 multicenter Agni-01), patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-resistant advanced melanoma received lymphodepletion and varying doses and schedules of amsoki-cel and ACZ. The primary objective of FIH and Agni-01 phase 1 was safety, tolerability and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D); the primary objective of Agni-01 phase 2 was objective response rate (ORR) at the RP2D. The first patient treated experienced rapid lymphocyte expansion and vasogenic edema of a previously irradiated brain metastasis, prompting protocol modifications and dose deescalation in FIH, including 80% reduction in maximum amsoki-cel dose and 75% reduction in ACZ dose. After preliminary demonstration of safety at the lower dose, doses were increased in FIH, and reescalation was initiated in Agni-01. Across studies, 37 patients were treated (FIH, n = 17; Agni-01, n = 20). Post hoc pooled analysis demonstrated no dose-limiting toxicities, ICU care or treatment-related mortality. Most common grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) included neutropenia (64.9% (24/37)), leukopenia/lymphopenia (56.8% (21/37) each) and anemia/thrombocytopenia (37.8% (14/37) each). Serious TEAEs were reported for 10 patients, including eight patients with grade 3 or higher events (non-hematologic, 13.5% (5/37); hematologic, 13.5% (5/37)). RP2D was selected based on overall safety and tolerability as well as preliminary anti-tumor activity in Agni-01 phase 1. The phase 2 preliminary ORR was 66.7% (6/9). In total, 15 patients were treated at RP2D and comprise the Key Efficacy Set (Agni-01: phase 1, n = 6; phase 2, n = 9), of which 10 patients (66.7%; 95% confidence interval 38-88%) achieved objective responses (including two complete responses). Amsoki-cel demonstrated favorable safety and promising early clinical activity in patients with ICI-resistant melanoma. A separate phase 2 pivotal Agni-01 cohort is ongoing. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT05470283 and NCT06060613 .

42984532.title: Successful application of low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation in CRRT for patients with liver failure: a retrospective case series study of 11 patients.
42984532.abstract: To investigate the clinical efficacy, safety and operational feasibility of a low-dose regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) combined with low-dose nafamostat mesylate (NM) mixed anticoagulation regimen in continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for patients with liver failure, so as to provide clinical reference for the selection of CRRT anticoagulation strategies for such special high-risk critically ill patients. A retrospective case series study was conducted. Eleven patients with liver failure who received CRRT in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University were enrolled. All patients were treated with CVVHDF mode and uniformly implemented the low-dose citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. CRRT treatment parameters, anticoagulant drugs, and infusion doses of calcium and sodium bicarbonate were standardized. The monitoring frequency of peripheral blood gas and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and the criteria for dose stratification adjustment were standardized. Data including patients' demographic baseline data, CRRT treatment duration, filter service life, blood gas electrolytes, dynamic changes of APTT, pipeline and filter coagulation, bleeding and metabolic adverse events, organ function and clinical outcomes were collected for summary and analysis. A total of 11 patients with liver failure undergoing CRRT in CVVHDF mode were enrolled in this study, using the low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. After treatment, the median filter life of patients reached 48 (38, 68.75) hours, with no severe pipeline or filter coagulation; there were no significant abnormalities in systemic coagulation indicators. One case (9.1%) had mild oral mucosal bleeding; no severe massive bleeding occurred. Hypocalcemia and metabolic alkalosis were observed in several patients but were not severe, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred. PCT was lower than baseline (P = 0.005) and APACHE II score was improved (P = 0.011) over the course of ICU treatment; however, all patients simultaneously received antibiotics, vasopressors, source control, and other ICU supportive care, and these changes therefore cannot be attributed to the mixed anticoagulation regimen. Liver and kidney function showed no obvious deterioration. In this small, single-center retrospective case series, a low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen was feasible to implement in patients with liver failure receiving CRRT. In this cohort, the median filter life was 48 h, no severe filter or pipeline coagulation was observed, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred; one case (9.1%) had mild bleeding. Because no comparator group was included, whether these observations reflect a benefit of the mixed regimen over conventional RCA, nafamostat alone, systemic heparin, or no anticoagulation cannot be determined. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered, multicenter, prospective controlled trials.

42983546.title: SERPINC1-mediated hereditary antithrombin deficiency with refractory pulmonary embolism: successful treatment with VA-ECMO and interventional thrombus aspiration.
42983546.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) carries substantial global morbidity and mortality, with 50%-60% of disease variability attributed to genetic factors. Hereditary antithrombin deficiency (HATD), caused by pathogenic variants in the SERPINC1 gene, is an autosomal dominant thrombophilia that confers a 20-40-fold higher risk of VTE, predominantly manifesting as recurrent pulmonary embolism (PE) and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). We report a 22-year-old male with recurrent PE secondary to type II HATD driven by a heterozygous SERPINC1 missense variant (c.1315 C > A, p.Pro439Thr). His second episode of PE progressed to obstructive cardiogenic shock refractory to systemic thrombolysis, accompanied by hemoptysis. Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) was initiated, yet recurrent oxygenator thrombosis occurred despite high-dose unfractionated heparin (UFH) infusion. Laboratory testing revealed an antithrombin III (AT-III) activity level of 39.5%, confirming the diagnosis. Pulmonary angiography followed by mechanical thrombus aspiration was performed, and long-term anticoagulation was switched to rivaroxaban. The patient was successfully weaned from VA-ECMO, with no PE recurrence or adverse cardiovascular events recorded during 5 years of follow-up. This case represents the first published report of a young patient with a SERPINC1 variant complicated by recurrent high-risk PE unresponsive to rt-PA thrombolysis who survived after VA-ECMO-supported pulmonary thrombus aspiration. Early etiological genetic screening for hereditary thrombophilia is essential for managing refractory PE induced by SERPINC1 variants. Individualized regimens combining VA-ECMO, interventional thrombectomy, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) yield favorable clinical outcomes and provide a reference for managing critically ill patients with hereditary thrombophilia.

42985103.title: Meta-analysis of the effect of nafamostat mesilate versus no-anticoagulation regimens in adult patients undergoing continuous renal replacement therapy.
42985103.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is a critical treatment for critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. However, effective anticoagulation of the extracorporeal circuit remains a clinical challenge. Nafamostat mesilate (NM), a serine protease inhibitor, possesses localized anticoagulation properties; however, its efficacy and safety in high-bleeding-risk populations have not been systematically evaluated. To compare the efficacy and safety of NM anticoagulation and no-anticoagulation regimens in patients undergoing CRRT. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies were retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, MEDLINE, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, the Cochrane Library, Wanfang Database, Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database. We included studies on adult patients receiving CRRT where the intervention and control groups were treated with NM anticoagulation and no-anticoagulation regimens, respectively. Primary outcomes included filter lifespan, number of filters used, coagulation indicators, bleeding events, and in-hospital mortality. The meta-analysis was conducted using RevMan 5.4 software. Eight studies involving 969 patients were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that, compared with the control group, the NM group had a significantly prolonged filter lifespan (P = 0.01) and a reduced number of filters used (P < 0.0001). The activated partial thromboplastin time (P = 0.89), prothrombin time (P = 0.88), and international normalized ratio (P = 0.60) showed no significant differences. Both groups demonstrated clinically similar risks of bleeding events (P = 0.53). However, the NM group demonstrated a significantly reduced in-hospital mortality, compared with the control group (P = 0.02). The NM anticoagulation regimen effectively extended the CRRT filter lifespan, reduced resource consumption, and improved patient survival outcomes without increasing the bleeding risk, demonstrating particular value for high-bleeding-risk populations. Future multicenter RCTs are warranted to validate applicability of NM in non-East Asian populations. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261399024, identifier: PROSPERO CRD420251077578.

42983500.title: Harmonizing the diagnosis of citrate accumulation - a call for standardized criteria.
42983500.abstract: Regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) has emerged as the gold-standard strategy for continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), yet its widespread adoption remains hindered by perceived complexity, heterogeneous protocols, unclear contraindications, and inconsistent terminology. A central challenge lies in the recognition and management of citrate accumulation, for which no single, reliable biomarker exists. The total-to-ionized calcium (tCa/iCa) ratio is widely utilized as a sensitive surrogate, but its specificity is limited by multiple confounding factors, including serum albumin concentration, acid-base status, and exogenous calcium administration. Current evidence supports a paradigm shift from reliance on static thresholds toward a dynamic, physiology-based assessment to define citrate accumulation. The kinetics of the tCa/iCa ratio, when interpreted alongside evolving metabolic parameters, particularly lactate trends, systemic ionized calcium, and acid-base status, provide a more robust framework for identifying citrate accumulation. Crucially, an elevated tCa/iCa ratio should not indiscriminately prompt the discontinuation of RCA. Targeted adjustments to the CRRT prescription can often safely mitigate citrate burden while preserving circuit patency. In the absence of a validated and widely available method for the direct measurement of plasma citrate levels, we propose a stepwise approach incorporating routinely measured screening tools and confirmatory parameters. Studies incorporating direct plasma citrate concentration measurements should be conducted to validate these criteria alongside readily available bedside surrogate markers. Refining this framework is essential to enhance the safe implementation of RCA and ultimately improve outcomes in critically ill patients.

42987338.title: Renal Decline Before Heart Transplantation in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Recipients: United Network for Organ Sharing Analysis.
42987338.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42987338.abstract: Although baseline renal impairment and post-heart transplantation (HT) dialysis are established clinical predictors, the prognostic impact of pre-HT renal decline in patients bridged with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed patients from the United Network for Organ Sharing registry who underwent HT following LVAD support between 2009 and 2024. Renal decline was defined as a greater than or equal to 40% reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from listing to HT. Among 10,454 patients, 624 (6.0%) experienced pre-HT renal decline. Patients with renal decline had longer waitlist durations (median 297 vs. 197 days; p < 0.001), lower eGFR at HT (42.0 vs. 70.6 ml/min/1.73 m2; p < 0.001), and higher rates of post-HT dialysis (23.7 vs. 12.8%; p < 0.001). Independent predictors of renal decline included longer waitlist time and perioperative blood transfusions, whereas HeartMate 3 LVAD use was protective. Renal decline was independently associated with an increased risk of post-HT dialysis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.64) and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 1.16), with post-HT dialysis strongly predicting mortality (aHR: 3.48). Renal deterioration is a significant predictor of post-HT dialysis and mortality in LVAD-bridged patients. Incorporating renal trajectory into risk stratification may enhance candidate selection and promote perioperative renal protection strategies.

42994879.title: Association between inpatient aspirin exposure and 28-day mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy: A cohort study.
42994879.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the association between inpatient aspirin exposure and 28-day mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC). We conducted a retrospective cohort study extracting data from the MIMIC-IV v3.1 database (2008-2022). Adult critically ill patients with SIC in the intensive care unit (ICU) were included. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Secondary outcomes encompassed mortality (e.g., in-hospital, ICU, 60-day, 90-day, and 1-year) and duration of ICU-free, ventilation-free, or vasopressor-free days within 28 days of admission to the ICU. Multivariable Cox regression, propensity score matching (PSM), inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), overlap weighting (OW), pairwise algorithmic weighting (PA), and doubly robust estimation were employed to control confounders. Robustness of findings was assessed through subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Among 9095 critically ill patients with SIC, 3207 (35.3%) received aspirin during ICU hospitalization. After 1:1 propensity score matching (2069 pairs), inpatient aspirin exposure was independently associated with significantly lower 28-day mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.85; P < .001). This association remained consistent across multiple analytical methods including IPTW (HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.70-0.84; P < .001), OW (HR 0.72; 95% CI: 0.61-0.84; P < .001), PA (HR 0.73; 95% CI: 0.61-0.84; P < .001), and doubly robust estimation (HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.61-0.94; P < .001). Inpatient aspirin exposure was also associated with more favorable secondary clinical outcomes (all P < .001). In critically ill patients with SIC, inpatient aspirin exposure was independently associated with lower 28-day mortality and more favorable clinical outcomes. These findings should be interpreted as an association rather than evidence of a causal therapeutic effect. Prospective randomized studies are warranted to validate these findings.

42993994.title: Platelet transfusion practices in the intensive care: To know, to do and not to do.

42990884.title: Personalised approach to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients (PROSPER): A randomised, parallel-group, electronic medical record (EMR)-embedded feasibility trial.
42990884.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
42990884.abstract: Data are limited regarding optimal low molecular weight heparin dosing for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients. This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial. Patients, weighing ≥100 kg who required thromboprophylaxis were eligible. Enoxaparin was commenced with weight-based dosing and anti-Xa level-guided adjustment (target peak anti-Xa level 0.2-0.4 IU/mL) or usual care (40 mg twice daily). The primary outcome was peak anti-Xa level at 'steady state' (after ≥3 enoxaparin doses). The feasibility threshold was set at 95% of steady state anti-Xa levels in the intervention group being less than the threshold for therapeutic anticoagulant effect (≤0.6 IU/mL). Fifty participants (intervention n = 17, control n = 33) received 331 doses of enoxaparin (median of 4 [interquartile range {IQR}: 3-7] doses per participant, and a dose of 50 [IQR: 50-60] mg (intervention) and 40 [IQR: 40-40] mg (control)). Thirty-two 'steady state' peak anti-Xa measurements were recorded from 24 patients (12 intervention and 12 control). The proportion of peak anti-Xa levels that were ≤0.6 IU/mL was: 15 of 17 (88%) vs. 15 of 15 (100%). There were fewer peak anti-Xa measurements below the prophylactic range (<0.2 IU/mL) in the intervention group compared with the control group (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 5 of 15 [33%]). Six patients developed venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 4 of 33 [12%]). Major bleeding occurred in one patient in the intervention group. A weight-based dynamic thromboprophylaxis algorithm was implemented via the electronic medical record but did not meet the predefined feasibility threshold.

42994766.title: Early platelet count trajectories and short- and long-term mortality in patients with sepsis: a group-based trajectory modeling study based on the MIMIC-IV database.
42994766.abstract: Platelet abnormalities are common in sepsis; most studies evaluate single measurements. We characterized early platelet count trajectories during the first 48 h after intensive care unit (ICU) admission and evaluated associations with short- and long-term mortality. Adult Sepsis-3 patients were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. Group-based trajectory modeling was applied to platelet counts at 12-48 h after ICU admission. Associations with mortality were examined using Kaplan-Meier, multivariable Cox and logistic models, with propensity-matched, multiple-imputation and reclassification analyses and the 48-h landmark analysis as primary; sepsis-induced coagulopathy was scored using International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) criteria. Among 5,046 ICU stays (4,775 patients), four trajectories were identified: persistently low (n = 1,153; 22.8%), moderate with mild decline (n = 1,847; 36.6%), high with moderate decline (n = 1,516; 30.0%) and very high with marked decline (n = 530; 10.5%). In the primary landmark analysis (n=4,930), adjusted 28-day mortality hazard ratios versus the moderate-with-mild-decline group were 1.66 (95% CI 1.40-1.97), 1.33 (1.12-1.57) and 1.34 (1.07-1.69), consistent at 90 days, 1 year and in whole-cohort and matched analyses. Sepsis-induced coagulopathy affected 82.6% of persistently low patients; trajectory and coagulopathy remained jointly associated with mortality. Trajectory membership improved reclassification over clinical variables (continuous NRI 0.193, 95% CI 0.160-0.281). Early platelet trajectories identify four sepsis patient groups with distinct mortality risk. The persistently low association was most robust; the high-but-declining association was attenuated in five-group analyses. Trajectories add information beyond single measurements.

42994925.title: The Withholding Enteral Feeds Around Transfusion (WHEAT) International Trial: protocol.

42992385.title: Rotational thromboelastometry and endothelial-derived extracellular vesicle changes in thrombotic microangiopathy versus other envenoming syndromes following hump-nosed pit viper envenoming.
42992385.abstract: Thrombotic microangiopathy is an uncommon complication of snakebite with unclear pathophysiology. We explore the mechanisms of venom-induced consumption coagulopathy, thrombotic microangiopathy and acute kidney injury in hump-nosed pit viper bites. A prospective observational study was conducted at District General Hospital Horana, Sri Lanka (June 2023 to December 2024). Thirty-five patients were recruited, including: local envenoming alone (20), venom induced consumption coagulopathy (2), thrombotic microangiopathy (5) and acute kidney injury without thrombotic microangiopathy (8). Laboratory tests were performed every 12 hours, and rotational thromboelastometry (delta and platelet) and flow cytometry for extracellular vesicles at the earliest diagnosis of envenoming. All thrombotic microangiopathy cases developed severe acute kidney injury, with 4/5 requiring dialysis. All eight cases of isolated acute kidney injury had mild kidney dysfunction that resolved. The international normalized ratio was normal in patients with thrombotic microangiopathy and acute kidney injury, however rotational thromboelastometry revealed coagulation abnormalities, including fibrinogen dysfunction despite normal fibrinogen levels, in patients with thrombotic microangiopathy. Isolated acute kidney injury had mild to moderate rotational thromboelastometry abnormalities. Endothelial-derived extracellular vesicles were proportionally highest in the thrombotic microangiopathy (median 12.6%) group. Red cell-derived extracellular vesicles were raised in thrombotic microangiopathy and isolated acute kidney injury groups. Thrombotic microangiopathy and severe acute kidney injury are associated in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming. Rotational thromboelastometry revealed coagulation abnormalities, missed by conventional coagulation testing. Thrombotic microangiopathy in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming was associated with raised endothelial- and red cell-derived extracellular vesicles. Rotational thromboelastometry is more sensitive than conventional coagulation testing for detecting coagulopathy and the associated risk of developing thrombotic microangiopathy and AKI in hump-nosed viper bites. Endothelial injury may be a factor in the pathogenesis of thrombotic microangiopathy in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming.

42997017.title: Sepsis-associated atrial fibrillation: Current insights and research priorities for standardized care.
42997017.abstract: Sepsis-associated atrial fibrillation (SAAF) is a common but serious complication in critically ill patients that is characterized by new-onset atrial fibrillation (AF) during sepsis. This secondary type of arrhythmia typically resolves with sepsis treatment but is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, including prolonged hospital stays, high recurrence rates of AF, and increased risks of heart failure, stroke, and short-term and long-term mortality. In contrast to primary AF, no standardized guidelines have been established for SAAF. To support the development of evidence-based protocols, we conducted a comprehensive review to synthesize the current knowledge of SAAF. Here, we highlight the definition, incidence, and risk factors of SAAF and distinguish it from primary AF and other types of secondary AF, including postoperative and post-myocardial infarction AF. We also describe the multifactorial pathophysiologic mechanisms of SAAF involving systemic inflammation, cytokine release, autonomic dysfunction, myocardial injury, and hemodynamic stress. Key outcomes of patients with SAAF and other types of secondary AF are compared, including in-hospital mortality, long-term AF recurrence, and stroke risk. Furthermore, we discuss various management strategies for SAAF, including methods of rhythm control and rate control in patients with SAAF. Anticoagulation recommendations and challenges for patients with SAAF are highlighted, particularly with respect to thrombotic risk, bleeding risk, and anticoagulation use. We propose a process for anticoagulation decisions in SAAF, which are challenging due to the dynamic interplay between sepsis-induced coagulopathy and thromboembolic risk. Finally, we provide a summary of future research priorities to support large-scale, multicenter trials to define evidence-based protocols that are critical for improving outcomes in this high-risk population.

42996723.title: Time-dependent associations of documented low-dose aspirin administration with 28-day mortality and early safety outcomes in adults with sepsis: a MIMIC-IV cohort study.
42996723.abstract: Associations between aspirin use and sepsis outcomes may reflect treatment timing and clinical selection. This retrospective Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) study included 31,888 adults with Sepsis-3. T0 was defined as the later of intensive care unit (ICU) admission or suspected infection; sepsis ascertainment could occur subsequently. Piecewise time-dependent Cox models evaluated actual enteral aspirin administration of 75-100 mg and 28-day restricted in-hospital and ICU mortality. Baseline sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) measurements were restricted to T0 or earlier. Sensitivity analyses examined exposure history, eligibility timing, and a 24-h matched landmark cohort. A continuous-time marginal structural model (MSM) incorporated lagged clinical information. Modified Poisson models evaluated laboratory and transfusion outcomes. Eligible aspirin administration was recorded at or after T0 for 4,771 patients, including 3,646 within 24 h. Adjusted in-hospital mortality hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.48 (95% CI 0.31-0.75) during 0-24 h and 0.63 (0.51-0.78) during 24-72 h, without clear associations thereafter. ICU estimates were similar. Qualifying SOFA scores occurred after T0 in 24,916 patients; restriction to the 6,972 patients with qualifying SOFA scores by T0 yielded HRs of 0.54 (0.28-1.03) and 0.62 (0.44-0.88) in the first two intervals. The MSM had residual imbalance and truncation-sensitive early estimates. After multiple imputation, the first two in-hospital HRs were 0.50 (0.32-0.79) and 0.66 (0.53-0.82), close to the primary estimates. A hemoglobin decline of ≥2 g/dL during 0-72 h was associated with early aspirin administration [adjusted risk ratio (RR) 1.10, 1.03-1.17], but 606 early recipients had a qualifying decline recorded before their first dose. The temporality-restricted 24-72-h analysis showed no clear association (RR 1.05, 0.91-1.21). Documented aspirin administration was associated with lower early restricted mortality. Retrospective eligibility, residual confounding, and uncertain prior exposure prevent causal interpretation; these findings do not justify initiating aspirin solely for sepsis.

42996610.title: Case Report: Simultaneous continuous renal replacement therapy and endovascular coiling in a poor-grade ruptured distal anterior cerebral artery aneurysm with ESKD and life-threatening hyperkalemia.
42996610.abstract: Poor-grade aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) on maintenance hemodialysis has traditionally been considered futile. Uremic platelet dysfunction and coagulopathy, electrolyte disturbances, and poor multi-organ reserve make these patients poor candidates for aggressive intervention. When a ruptured aneurysm coexists with life-threatening hyperkalemia, the therapeutic window narrows further, because severe hyperkalemia significantly increases the risk of perioperative arrhythmia and cardiac arrest and requires urgent correction. Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) may offer advantages in this setting, but its use during neurointerventional procedures has rarely been reported. A 43-year-old woman with polycystic kidney disease and ESKD on regular hemodialysis presented with sudden coma and was diagnosed with Hunt-Hess grade V aSAH from a ruptured distal anterior cerebral artery (DACA) aneurysm. After 5 days of intensive care, her neurological status improved sufficiently to consider intervention. However, she developed life-threatening hyperkalemia (potassium 7.6 mmol/L). We performed simultaneous continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) and endovascular coiling. No anticoagulation was used in the CRRT circuit; intravenous heparin 0.67 mg/kg was administered separately for the neurointerventional procedure. CRRT was delivered in CVVHDF mode with a net ultrafiltration rate of 1-2 mL/kg/h and a total clearance of approximately 57 mL/kg/h, maintaining hemodynamic and intracranial stability throughout the 2-hour procedure. The aneurysm was completely obliterated (Raymond class I), and potassium decreased to 5.2 mmol/L. The patient recovered neurologically postoperatively but developed refractory bleeding during tracheostomy due to uremic platelet dysfunction and coagulopathy, ultimately leading to airway complications and death at 3 months. Simultaneous CRRT and endovascular coiling was technically feasible in this carefully selected patient with poor-grade aSAH, ESKD, and life-threatening hyperkalemia. However, this is a single-case experience and cannot be generalized, and perioperative bleeding and airway management remained challenging.

42997295.title: Association of composite liver function indices with trauma-induced coagulopathy in adult trauma patients.
42997295.abstract: Trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC) is a life-threatening complication associated with uncontrolled hemorrhage and high mortality in critically ill trauma patients. This study aimed to evaluate the associations and discriminative performance of four composite liver-function indices-ALBI, TBil/ALB, DBil/TBil, and GGT/ALP-with TIC-related outcomes in adult trauma patients. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 634 adult trauma patients. Laboratory data were collected at baseline, 24 h after admission, and 48 h after admission. The primary outcome was the continuous ISTH DIC score assessed 48 h after admission. Overt DIC, non-overt DIC, and ATC were analyzed as secondary or exploratory TIC-related outcomes. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, admission lactate, admission pH, admission temperature, traumatic brain injury, hepatic injury, and surgery. Associations between each index and TIC-related outcomes were examined using multivariable linear and logistic regression analyses. ALBI showed the most consistent associations with TIC-related outcomes and the strongest index-alone discrimination for non-overt DIC among the evaluated indices. The TBil/ALB ratio retained independent predictive value, though with somewhat lower overall consistency. The DBil/TBil and GGT/ALP ratios, by contrast, exhibited weaker associations that varied across time points and outcome definitions. Serial measurements over the first 24 h contributed incremental prognostic information; however, no dynamic index outperformed the baseline ALBI score in predictive strength. ALBI was consistently associated with TIC-related outcomes assessed 48 h after admission, and this association remained stable across the examined clinical subgroups. ALBI may serve as a readily available adjunctive risk marker for early coagulopathy risk stratification. Prospective validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

42996917.title: Tracheostomy-related bleeding and stomal complications: a literature review.
42996917.abstract: Tracheostomy is one of the most commonly performed procedures in critically ill patients, with bleeding representing the most frequent early complication. Stomal bleeding and granulation tissue formation create ongoing management challenges that can complicate patient care. Other complications include stomal infection, subcutaneous emphysema, focal airway stenosis, and tracheoinnominate fistula (TIF), which differ in clinical severity and management. Current management relies on reactive measures, yet no standardized approach exists for preventing or managing persistent minor bleeding around the tracheostomy site. This study aims to review the incidence, pathophysiology, risk factors, and current management of tracheostomy-related bleeding and stomal complications, with emphasis on identifying gaps in prevention and treatment strategies. We conducted targeted literature searches using PubMed/MEDLINE for English-language human studies published between January 1, 2000 and September 17, 2026 involving adults aged 19 years or older. Search terms included "tracheostomy", "tracheotomy", "bleeding", "hemorrhage", "granulation tissue", "tracheoinnominate fistula", "stomal infection", "cellulitis", "abscess", "decannulation", "dislodgement", "subcutaneous emphysema", "tracheal stenosis", "ECMO", "transplantation", "immunosuppression", "tranexamic acid", "epinephrine", and "cautery". We extracted data on incidence rates, management approaches, and clinical outcomes. Bleeding is the most common early complication of tracheostomy procedures, occurring in 0.6-5.0% of cases overall, with rates reaching 5.7% for major or minor bleeding and up to 40% in high-risk populations such as patients on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Stomal infections, airway complications, and early accidental decannulation is also important to consider in tracheostomy patients. Subcutaneous emphysema was primarily associated with early mechanical complications, whereas focal airway stenosis represented a later consequence of granulation. Management of minor superficial bleeding generally consisted of direct pressure, packing, correction of reversible coagulopathy, and selected topical or cautery-based interventions. TIF remained distinct from these complications because even limited or transient bleeding may precede catastrophic hemorrhage, necessitating urgent recognition and escalation when a vascular source is suspected. Tracheostomy-related bleeding and stomal oozing represent common complications with limited preventive options. Current management is reactive, relying on manual pressure application, packing materials, and procedural interventions. Particular attention should be made to distinguish minor superficial bleeding from sentinel or life-threatening hemorrhage. Novel approaches could potentially reduce bleeding complications, minimize granulation tissue formation, and improve patient comfort during the critical early post-tracheostomy period.

42997603.title: Home-based transfusions in hospice patients with hematologic malignancies: a pilot study.
42997603.abstract: Hospice care (HC) for patients with hematologic malignancies (HM) is underutilized due to concerns about cessation of blood transfusions. Home-based transfusion (HBT) programs have proven to be safe, but little research exists for HM patients in HC. We hypothesized that HBT protocol could be safely implemented to reduce symptoms burden, lengthen life expectancy and improve quality of life in HC. In a non-randomized pilot study between 8/2020 and 7/2023, adult transfusion-dependent HM patients were offered weekly transfusion of one unit of packed red blood cells (PRBC) and/or one unit of platelets based on symptoms criteria, not lab values. Exclusion criteria included prior transfusion reactions, extended blood typing, or residence outside 50 miles from the transfusion center. Hospice agencies provided management and support, while Our Blood Institute (OBI) provided palliative HBT. Symptom scores and complete blood counts (CBC) were collected weekly, and EORTC QLQ-C30 quality of life (QOL) questionnaire was completed before and after transfusions. The primary feasibility and safety outcomes were recruitment, ability to administer indicated transfusions, and transfusion reactions. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04454723) on 6/30/2020. We enrolled 21 patients (mean age in years = 67.1 (standard deviation (SD) = 14.4); 100% enrollment, one withdrew consent). Participants received an average of 3.4 units (SD = 3.4) of platelets or PRBCs. No transfusion reactions reported. Mean cost was $571 per week (SD = $939). The EORTC Composite Score least squares-mean difference (post-pre- transfusion) increased 0.18 (SE = 1.88) (p-value = 0.92) but not significantly. Median hospice duration was 11 days, IQR = 8-40 days, 95% CI: 9-33 days. All patients died at home, with no hospitalizations or intensive care unit (ICU) admissions. HBT, in the setting of hospice represents a feasible and safe option for further study to avoid costly hospitalizations and ICU admissions, with limited cost. This trial demonstrates proof of concept for an economical, patient-centered HBT protocol in HM patients receiving HC. P30CA225520, TSET.

42996951.title: Development and external validation of risk prediction models for gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic dissection surgery.
42996951.abstract: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) following surgery for aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening complication associated with elevated mortality and increased healthcare resource utilization. However, reliable predictive tools remain scarce. This study aimed to develop prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery and to externally evaluate an XGBoost (XGB) model using an independent multicenter database. Patients who underwent AD surgery were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database (MIMIC-IV; development cohort) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; external evaluation cohort). The primary outcome was postoperative GIB within 30 days, defined using a composite database-derived algorithm requiring either (I) a hemoglobin (Hb) decrease of ≥2 g/dL accompanied by at least one supporting indicator, including a transfusion record, hemostatic medication use, or endoscopic examination; or (II) the combination of a transfusion record and a GIB diagnosis. An isolated Hb decrease or transfusion record was not sufficient for outcome classification. Routinely available demographic, physiologic, laboratory, and disease-severity variables were extracted. Records with missing values in variables required for the final analysis were excluded before model development. Multivariable logistic regression served as the baseline model, with XGB and random forest employed as comparator models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Brier score, and decision-curve analysis (DCA). The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 935 patients (GIB incidence, 10.7%), whereas the eICU-CRD validation cohort comprised 542 patients (GIB incidence, 12.7%). In the development cohort, the AUCs were 0.887 for logistic regression, 0.962 for XGB, and 0.853 for random forest. In the eICU-CRD cohort, XGB yielded an AUC point estimate of 0.873. This retrospective two-database analysis developed prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery. The models showed discrimination in the analyzed data; however, prospective validation using predictors measured within prespecified pre-event windows is required before clinical implementation.

42999793.title: AB028. Predominance of minimally invasive surgery in the management of thymic neoplasms at a Latin American cancer center: a single-institution cohort.
42999793.abstract: Thymic epithelial neoplasms are rare tumors of the anterior (prevascular) mediastinum, and complete surgical resection is the cornerstone of treatment. Over the past decade, minimally invasive techniques (video-assisted and robot-assisted thoracoscopic surgery, VATS/RATS) have progressively replaced sternotomy for selected thymic tumors while preserving oncological principles. However, most published series originate from high-income centers in North America, Europe, and Asia, and contemporary data from Latin American public referral hospitals remain scarce. We report the surgical management and immediate perioperative safety of thymic neoplasms at a high-volume Brazilian cancer center. Retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained institutional REDCap database at a single tertiary cancer center. Consecutive patients operated on between April 2020 and May 2026 for a clinical and radiological diagnosis of thymic neoplasm were included. Recorded variables comprised demographics, tumor location, preoperative biopsy, surgical approach and conversion, operative time, transfusion, intraoperative complications, postoperative destination, and confirmed pathology. Minimally invasive surgery was defined as a VATS or RATS approach without conversion to open surgery. Data were summarized with descriptive statistics; continuous variables are reported as medians (IQR). Sixty-three patients were included; 40 (65%) were women, with a median age of 66 years (IQR 53 to 73). The lesion was located in the anterior mediastinum in 59 patients (94%), and preoperative biopsy was performed in 26. All procedures were elective. A minimally invasive approach was used in 47 patients (81%; VATS 40, RATS 7), and 11 through an open approach (thoracotomy 7, sternotomy 3, clamshell 1), with one conversion to thoracotomy. Median operative time was 180 minutes. Immediate perioperative safety was favorable, with no transfusions, a single intraoperative complication, and postoperative ward destination in 37 patients versus intensive care in 25. When histologically confirmed, thymoma was the predominant diagnosis, followed by benign lesions and secondary tumors. In this Latin American public cancer center, thymic neoplasms were managed predominantly by minimally invasive surgery (81%), with a low conversion rate and favorable perioperative safety, adding evidence for this approach from an underrepresented region.

43003446.title: Viscoelastic haemostatic assay-guided transfusion versus conventional coagulation testing in critically ill non-cardiac adults with active bleeding or clinically significant coagulopathy: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.

42999907.title: A targeted mass spectrometric assay for quantitative detection of fibrinogen in plasma.
42999907.journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
42999907.abstract: Fibrinogen is a key glycoprotein that plays a central role in clot formation, structure, and stability. Both quantitative fibrinogen deficiency and qualitative abnormalities can lead to bleeding or thrombotic disorders. Accurate quantification of fibrinogen antigen is essential for clinical evaluation; however, current immunoassays and clot-based surrogate methods are prone to interference and may lack traceability to international standards. To develop a targeted mass spectrometry-based assay for accurate quantification of fibrinogen antigen in plasma and to compare its performance with established functional and immunoturbidimetric assays. We developed a targeted liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry-based assay using isotope-labeled peptides that accurately measures fibrinogen antigen concentration with high precision (coefficient of variation < 20%) across a broad linear dynamic range of 10.2 to 1307.5 mg/dL, enabling accurate detection of hypofibrinogenemia and hyperfibrinogenemia. Assay performance was evaluated in healthy donors (n = 47) and clinical specimens (n = 31). Fibrinogen antigen levels in normal donors followed a normal distribution (mean ± SD, 315 ± 42 mg/dL). The targeted assay, employing selected reaction monitoring, correlated strongly with immunoturbidimetry (Pearson's correlation coefficient [r] = .943) and the Clauss and prothrombin time-derived fibrinogen assays (r = .91 and r = .93, respectively). Stratification by clinical category confirmed elevated fibrinogen levels in thrombosis-related disorders, intermediate levels in controls, and low levels in liver disease and critical illness. The liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry-based assay provides precise, accurate quantification of fibrinogen across a wide clinical range and aligns closely with existing methods while offering analytical specificity. With further clinical validation, it could be used as a diagnostic clinical test.

42989669.title: Capillary leak syndrome - A life-threatening complication rarely reported in patients with typhoid fever.
42989669.journal: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association
42989669.abstract: A 9-years-old girl was admitted in to a peripheral hospital with a two-week history of fever and loose stools. Despite initial treatment, her condition worsened. On arrival, she was critically ill, drowsy, lethargic, febrile, Heart Rate 108/min, Respiratory Rate 34/min and Blood Pressure 90/60 mmHg, Capillary Refill time >3 seconds and had cold peripheries. Blood Culture was sent and appropriate antibiotics started. Her condition further deteriorated, with worsening level of consciousness, oedema and abdominal distension. Serum Albumin levels were low (2 g/dL). Blood culture subsequently grew extensively drugresistant Salmonella typhi, and antibiotic therapy was changed accordingly. She developed features consistent with capillary leak syndrome, including oliguria, rising haematocrit, and worsening oedema. Hypotension and impending shock were treated with albumin transfusion and close monitoring of vital signs and urine output. After 48 hours, her BP stabilized, with improvement in consciousness, urine output and resolution of oedema. She was discharged in stable condition after 10 days of treatment.

43007443.title: Outcomes with Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis versus Mechanical Thrombectomy for Patients with Intermediate/High Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Meta-Analysis of 24,090 Patients.
43007443.abstract: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE. Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and the length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Summary estimates were analyzed using a random effects model. A total of 18 studies (24,090 intermediate/high risk patients) were eligible for the analysis. CDT was associated with longer length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (mean difference: 1.01 days, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-1.15) compared with MT. While there was no statistical difference between the two groups regarding the risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01, p = 0.068) and major bleeding (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55, p = 0.705). Similarly, the incidence of other clinical outcomes; all-cause readmission, PE-related readmission, blood transfusion rates, length of hospital stay, cardiac arrest, and stroke, were similar between the two groups. Among patients with intermediate/high risk PE treated with catheter-based therapies, there was no difference regarding the clinical outcomes between CDT and MT, but CDT was associated with a longer ICU stay. Larger, well designed randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

43009312.title: Association of Early Palliative Care with End-of-Life Care Quality and Nonbeneficial Treatments in Taiwan: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.
43009312.abstract: Early palliative care has been associated with reduced aggressive care near the end of life (EOL), particularly among patients with cancer. However, evidence regarding the association between early palliative care and potentially nonbeneficial treatments near the EOL remains limited, particularly among patients with noncancer terminal illnesses and in real-world clinical practice. To examine the association between early palliative care, EOL care quality indicators, and nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill cancer and noncancer patients under a universal health insurance system. This retrospective population-based study used Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database to identify adults who received palliative care within one year before death in 2019. Early palliative care was defined as initiation of any palliative care service more than 90 days before death. Outcomes included indicators of EOL care quality and nonbeneficial treatments within the last 30 days of life. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models were used to adjust for demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and terminal diagnoses. Among 46,343 decedents, 17.2% received early palliative care. Early palliative care was associated with lower odds of aggressive EOL care, including more than one emergency department visit, more than one hospitalization, a hospital stay exceeding 14 days, intensive care unit admission, in-hospital death, use of an endotracheal tube, ventilator support, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Early palliative care was also associated with reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments, including blood transfusion and tube feeding or intravenous nutrition. In a nationwide cohort, early palliative care was associated with improved EOL care quality and reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill patients. These findings underscore the clinical importance of earlier palliative care involvement in supporting patient-centered decision making near the EOL and reducing potentially nonbeneficial interventions.

43009022.title: Sepsis in Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy: A Six-Year Nationwide Analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Healthcare Resource Utilization in Hospitalizations for Hematologic Malignancies.
43009022.abstract: Patients receiving chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy are at increased risk for infection and sepsis due to malignancy-related immune dysfunction, lymphodepleting chemotherapy, and immunosuppression used to treat CAR T-cell toxicities; however, nationally representative estimates of sepsis burden and economic impact remain limited. This study uses nationally representative U.S. data to evaluate patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and healthcare utilization associated with sepsis among hospitalizations involving CAR T-cell therapy. Adult hospitalizations for acute lymphoblastic leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, or multiple myeloma in which CAR T-cell therapy was administered between 2017 and 2022 were identified from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) and stratified by sepsis status. After excluding records with missing covariates, survey-weighted analyses were performed to generate nationally representative estimates. Multivariable regression models were used to evaluate differences in mortality and secondary outcomes, with statistical significance defined as a two-sided p value < 0.05. Among 10,450 weighted CAR T-cell therapy hospitalizations, 645 (6.2%) were complicated by sepsis. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in hospitalizations with sepsis (28.7% vs 1.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 33.96; 95% confidence interval [CI] 18.67-61.75). Sepsis was independently associated with higher odds of acute kidney injury (aOR 4.31), respiratory failure (aOR 11.85), acute hepatic failure (aOR 44.42), and septic shock (aOR 411.05), along with greater use of renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressors. Thrombohemorrhagic events were more frequent among hospitalizations with sepsis, including disseminated intravascular coagulation (aOR 9.30), acute venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.95), acute coronary syndrome (aOR 27.63), acute ischemic stroke (aOR 7.53), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (aOR 6.47), and intracranial hemorrhage (aOR 4.84), as well as increased need for cryoprecipitate and fresh frozen plasma transfusion (aOR 2.70). Sepsis was also associated with longer hospital stay (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR] 1.96) and higher hospitalization charges (adjusted charge ratio [aCR] 1.22). Sepsis was documented in approximately 6% of CAR T-cell hospitalizations and was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, organ dysfunction, critical-care utilization, longer hospitalization, and higher hospitalization charges. These findings highlight the substantial clinical and healthcare burden associated with sepsis in this population.

43004881.title: When the Filter Becomes the Source: POCUS Detection of Inferior Vena Cava Filter Thrombosis Extending Into the Right Atrium.
43004881.abstract: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters are used to prevent pulmonary embolism in patients with venous thromboembolism when anticoagulation is contraindicated. Although uncommon, filter thrombosis can result in thrombus propagation and potentially life-threatening embolic complications. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides a rapid bedside assessment of the heart, lungs, and may facilitate the prompt recognition of unexpected thromboembolic complications. A 43-year-old man with hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage was admitted to the intensive care unit requiring mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. Six days after admission, he developed sudden severe hypoxemia, tachycardia, and hypotension requiring reinitiation of norepinephrine. POCUS demonstrated bilateral anterior A-lines, left femoral and popliteal deep vein thrombosis, and preserved right ventricular (RV) function without echocardiographic evidence of RV strain. Catheter-based pulmonary angiography confirmed subocclusive thrombosis involving segmental branches of the right middle and lower lobes, which was treated with mechanical thromboaspiration, followed by IVC filter placement because anticoagulation was initially contraindicated. Four days later, he developed a new episode of acute hypoxemia despite remaining hemodynamically stable. Repeat POCUS demonstrated a large mobile thrombus in transit within the right atrium. Subcostal longitudinal imaging of the IVC demonstrated a large elongated thrombus attached to the IVC filter, with a freely mobile portion extending into the right atrium. Urgent mechanical thrombectomy and IVC filter replacement were performed. The new filter was positioned approximately 2 cm below the confluence of the hepatic veins with the inferior vena cava. Approximately 24 h later, follow-up POCUS showed no evidence of new thrombus formation. More than 2 weeks after admission, following a follow-up brain CT showing no significant progression of the intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation with enoxaparin was initiated and progressively increased to a full therapeutic dose. This case highlights the value of POCUS for the prompt bedside recognition of an established and potentially life-threatening complication of IVC filter placement. Systematic bedside cardiac and venous ultrasound may identify thrombus propagation into the right atrium even in the absence of RV dilation or echocardiographic evidence of RV strain, facilitating timely endovascular intervention.

43006184.title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
43006184.abstract: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain. This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated. A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099). In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

43008776.title: Fibrinolytic Response to Protein C Zymogen and Plasma in Sepsis-Associated Purpura Fulminans: A Case Series of Nine Consecutive Patients.
43008776.journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
43008776.abstract: Purpura fulminans (PF) is a rare and life-threatening manifestation of disseminated intravascular coagulation, leading to multiorgan failure. Protein C (PC) zymogen supplementation has a strong pathophysiological rationale, but its effects on the viscoelastic fibrinolytic profile have not been described. We retrospectively analyzed nine patients (six adults, three children) admitted to our intensive care units between 2017 and 2025 with PF associated with septic shock, treated with PC zymogen concentrate and fresh frozen plasma (FFP). In the six adults, PC and fibrinolysis were measured before and a median of 13 hours after the PC loading dose, fibrinolysis with modified viscoelastic hemostatic assays (urokinase-modified thromboelastography [UK-TEG] in three, tissue plasminogen activator test [TPA-test, ClotPro] in three). Median (interquartile range) PC rose from 23 (10-31)% to 102 (63-137)% and Lysis, the percentage of clot lysis at the modified assays, from 15 (0-47)% to 78 (60-100)%. All six patients had fibrinolysis resistance before treatment. Lysis increased in five and returned within the reference interval in one; in the three TPA-test patients, lysis time became measurable after treatment but remained above 300 s. Three patients died and four required surgery for necrotic skin or soft tissue lesions. PC and FFP administration was followed by a partial recovery of the fibrinolytic response, which cannot be attributed to PC alone, since plasma was given at the same time. Modified viscoelastic assays may help monitor the response to PC and plasma therapy.

43005745.title: Anesthetic management of right radical nephrectomy and inferior vena cava thrombectomy for giant renal cell carcinoma: a case report.
43005745.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
43005745.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with tumor thrombus extension into the inferior vena cava (IVC) represents a major surgical and anesthetic challenge because of the high risk of massive hemorrhage, hemodynamic instability, and intraoperative tumor embolism. We report the case of a 55-year-old man presenting with a large right renal mass measuring 14 × 14 × 13 cm, with a tumor thrombus extending from the right renal vein into the infrahepatic IVC. The patient underwent right radical nephrectomy with caval thrombectomy under general anesthesia and invasive hemodynamic monitoring. Anesthetic management focused on anticipating major blood loss, preventing thromboembolic complications related to thrombus manipulation, ensuring adequate blood product availability, and maintaining perioperative hemodynamic optimization. Intraoperative blood loss was estimated at 3500 mL, which necessitated transfusion of four units of packed red blood cells and four units of fresh frozen plasma.
