42902175.title: Alcohol-positive polytrauma patients: injury patterns, ICU resource use and mortality at a German Level I trauma center.
42902175.abstract: In most countries, alcohol consumption is so culturally ingrained that even small amounts are permitted while driving. Even at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.5 g/L, ethanol impairs mental and cognitive performance. Studies from the US and Europe estimate that elevated blood alcohol levels may be detected in 10%-40% of all emergency department patients. Against this background, we investigated the impact of alcohol consumption on injury severity, injury patterns, as well as primary and secondary outcomes in polytrauma patients. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included patients admitted to a Level I trauma center via the trauma room and documented in the TraumaRegister DGU® between 2015 and 2023. Serum ethanol was determined routinely in all adolescent and adult trauma room patients. Patients without serum ethanol measurement or younger than 13 years were excluded. Patients with detectable serum ethanol (> 1 mg/dL, detection limit of the laboratory; ALC) were compared with patients without (noALC) using the χ² and Mann-Whitney U tests. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) and pre-injury ASA classification. A dose-response analysis was performed using serum ethanol categories. A total of 1,524 patients were analyzed: 431 (28.3%) were alcohol-positive (ALC) and 1,093 (71.7%) were not (noALC). ALC patients were younger, more often male and had a lower prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (p < 0.001), whereas the ISS did not differ (p = 0.396). They were more frequently victims of violent crime and were overrepresented among pedestrians and falls from < 3 m, whereas motorcyclists were more often sober. Alcohol-positive patients were more often treated in the ICU (90.0% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.048), but this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40; 95% CI 0.96-2.03). Length of ICU stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ, and alcohol was not independently associated with mortality (aOR 0.91; 95% CI 0.56-1.47). Severe TBI was more frequent in alcohol-positive patients (38.5% vs. 29.5%), increased with serum ethanol concentration, and was the strongest predictor of ICU treatment and mortality. Nearly one in three severely injured patients had detectable serum ethanol. After adjustment for confounders, alcohol was not independently associated with mortality or intensive care resource use, and no dose-response relationship was found for these outcomes. The more frequent ICU treatment of alcohol-positive patients appears to be explained by their distinct injury pattern, particularly the concentration-dependent increase in severe TBI.

42896481.title: Slow-tempo piano music listening and short-term anxiety and burnout trajectories in a predominantly nursing sample of ICU healthcare workers: A randomized controlled trial.
42896481.abstract: Healthcare workers in intensive care units (ICUs) are chronically exposed to high-intensity, high-risk clinical environments, where anxiety and burnout are highly prevalent. Music listening is a low-burden, non-pharmacological supportive strategy with potential stress-reducing effects; however, randomized trials evaluating standardized slow-tempo piano music interventions among ICU healthcare workers remain limited. To compare short-term trajectories in self-reported generalized anxiety symptoms and weighted MBI-GS burnout index values between ICU healthcare workers assigned to a slow-tempo piano music intervention and those assigned to a passive control condition. This single-center, open-label, two-group parallel randomized controlled trial was conducted in the ICUs of a tertiary hospital in China. A total of 126 ICU healthcare workers were enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the piano music group or the passive control group, with 63 participants in each group. The piano music group received a 2-week standardized slow-tempo piano music listening intervention consisting of four 30-minute sessions per week, for a total of eight sessions. The listening sessions were conducted outside ICU working hours, after the end of the participant's shift and before bedtime. The passive control group maintained their usual routines and received neither the study-specified music intervention nor a study-arranged 30-minute rest period. Anxiety and burnout were assessed after the 1st, 4th, and 8th sessions using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 scale and the Maslach Burnout Inventory-General Survey. No outcome assessment was conducted before the first intervention session; therefore, the first assessment (T1) was a post-session assessment rather than a pre-intervention baseline. The study was retrospectively registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500097216). All 126 randomized participants completed the three assessments. In the full sample, statistically significant group × time interactions were identified for GAD-7 scores (Wald χ2(2) = 46.29, p < .001) and the weighted MBI-GS burnout index (Wald χ2(2) = 6.78, p = .034). In the T1-adjusted analyses, the passive control group had higher GAD-7 scores than the piano music group at T2 (adjusted mean difference = 1.47, 95% CI [0.69, 2.25], p < .001), whereas the adjusted difference at T3 was not statistically significant (adjusted mean difference = 0.85, 95% CI [-0.03, 1.72], p = .057). The passive control group also had higher adjusted weighted MBI-GS burnout index values at T2 (adjusted mean difference = 0.52, 95% CI [0.24, 0.80], p < .001) and T3 (adjusted mean difference = 0.97, 95% CI [0.71, 1.24], p < .001). In the nurse-only sensitivity analysis, the group × time interaction remained statistically significant for GAD-7 scores but not for the weighted MBI-GS burnout index. The piano music and passive control groups showed different short-term trajectories in self-reported anxiety symptoms and the weighted burnout index. However, because the study lacked a genuine pre-intervention assessment and used a passive control condition, the findings should be regarded as preliminary associations in short-term outcome trajectories, not as evidence of intervention efficacy or a specific effect of piano music. Further trials incorporating a pre-intervention baseline, active comparison conditions, and longer follow-up are warranted.

42895538.title: Perceived inappropriateness of care among ICU clinicians is associated with burnout and intention to leave the job.
authors: on behalf the PICNL-ICU study group

42892077.title: Burn mechanism does not predict ICU mortality beyond the Abbreviated Burn Severity Index: A 24-year registry analysis.
42892077.journal: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
42892077.abstract: Flame burns are consistently associated with higher mortality than scald injuries; however, it is unclear whether burn mechanism independently influences outcome or primarily reflects differences in injury severity. Therefore, we performed a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained registry by including 1069 adult patients with flame or scald burns who were admitted to a tertiary burn intensive care unit between 2000 and 2024. The primary outcome was intensive care unit (ICU) mortality. Logistic regression analyzes evaluated the association between burn mechanism and mortality before and after adjustment for Abbreviated Burn Severity Index (ABSI) and calendar year, with an additional model incorporating the individual ABSI components and calendar year. Patients with flame burns had significantly larger burns, higher ABSI scores, more frequent inhalation injury, and higher prevalence of full-thickness burns (all p < 0.001). Crude ICU mortality was significantly higher following flame burns than scald injuries (27.8% vs. 10.3%; OR 3.36, 95% CI 2.26-5.01; p<0.001). However, burn mechanism was no longer independently associated with mortality after adjusting for ABSI and calendar year (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.63-1.69; p=0.913) or after adjusting for the individual ABSI components and calendar year (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.57-1.71; p=0.967). Age, total body surface area burned, inhalation injury, and full-thickness burns remained independently associated with mortality. These findings indicate that the higher mortality observed after flame burns is attributable to greater injury severity rather than burn mechanism. Therefore, burn mechanism should be regarded primarily as a marker of injury severity rather than an independent predictor of ICU mortality, thereby reinforcing the importance of validated severity scores for prognostic assessment.

42888980.title: Case report: Septic shock associated with Granulicatella adiacens pneumonia in a polytrauma patient following road traffic accident: rare pathogen in critical care.
42888980.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a common and serious consequence of prolonged mechanical ventilation in critically ill polytrauma patients, especially those with underlying comorbidities such as diabetes mellitus. Although VAP is often caused by gram-negative bacilli and Staphylococcus aureus, infection due to fastidious organisms is uncommon and may delay microbiological diagnosis. Granulicatella adiacens, formerly categorized among the nutritionally variant streptococci (NVS), is a fastidious commensal of the oral and genitourinary tract that is most commonly associated with infective endocarditis and bacteremia, whereas pulmonary infections are exceptionally rare. We present a case report of a 50-year-old diabetic male who sustained severe head, thoracic, and skeletal injuries in a high-impact two-wheeler RTA. He acquired ventilator-associated pneumonia with progression to septic shock on the ICU course. The initial cultures (blood, urine, ET aspirate) were sterile, but the following bronchoalveolar lavage G. adiacens as the predominant organism on enriched media, identifying it as the probable etiological agent. A repeat blood culture, obtained on day 4 because of suspected sepsis, subsequently also grew G. adiacens after the patient's death. The patient, in spite of mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, renal replacement therapy, and broad-spectrum antibiotics, developed multi-organ dysfunction and succumbed on ICU day 5. The case brings to the fore the potential possibility of G. adiacens to cause fatal opportunistic infections in polytrauma victims when invasive ICU therapy and metabolic derangements converge. Early suspicion, prompt interventions like BAL sampling, and enriched media or molecular diagnostics can facilitate the detection of fastidious pathogens in culture-negative sepsis, thus facilitating therapeutic targeting and optimizing outcomes.

42964277.title: The lived experience of critical care nurses caring for patients with intensive care unit-acquired weakness: a qualitative study.
42964277.journal: Journal of research in nursing : JRN
42964277.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired weakness (ICU-AW) is a prevalent neuromuscular complication with high morbidity. Understanding the nursing experience is crucial for improving patient outcomes. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences and challenges of critical care nurses caring for patients with ICU-AW. A descriptive qualitative design was employed. Semi-structured, face-to-face interviews were conducted with ten critical care nurses. Data were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using content analysis. Analysis identified three core themes: (1) deficits in disease understanding, (2) challenges in patient nursing and (3) insufficiency of systemic support. The study highlights the complex realities of ICU-AW nursing, contributing a foundational narrative to nursing theory on the burdens of rehabilitation in critical care. It provides direct evidence for policy, recommending mandatory ICU-AW education in nursing curricula, the development of standardised interdisciplinary rehabilitation protocols and institutional support systems to mitigate nurse burnout and enhance collaborative practice.This study illuminates the critical nursing perspective on ICU-AW, advocating for the integration of structured rehabilitative nursing practices, supportive debriefing mechanisms and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration to improve both patient outcomes and nurse job satisfaction.

42958276.title: Associations of alarm fatigue with occupational burnout and sleep quality in ICU nurses: a cross-sectional study.
42958276.abstract: Alarm fatigue is a critical concern in intensive care units (ICUs), where nurses are continuously exposed to high volumes of clinical alarms. This phenomenon has been associated with psychological strain, impaired sleep quality, and occupational burnout. Despite growing evidence, limited studies have simultaneously explored the associations among these variables in ICU nurses. This study aimed to investigate the relationships among alarm fatigue, occupational burnout, and sleep quality in ICU nurses working in hospitals in Kerman and Sirjan, Iran. A descriptive-analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 219 ICU nurses selected through census sampling. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire, the Alarm Fatigue Scale (AFSS), the Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 22, employing independent t-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, Spearman's correlation coefficient, and multivariable linear regression analyses. A significance level of p < 0.05 was considered. More than half of the nurses reported no alarm fatigue (57.5%), while 83.6% experienced poor sleep quality. Emotional exhaustion was low to moderate in most participants, depersonalization was moderate in 56.2%, and reduced personal accomplishment was reported by 96.3%. Alarm fatigue showed weak but statistically significant positive correlations with poor sleep quality (r = 0.230, p = 0.001) and occupational burnout (r = 0.166, p = 0.014). Sleep quality was also weakly but significantly correlated with occupational burnout (r = 0.175, p = 0.010). Alarm fatigue and burnout were significantly associated with gender, employment status, shift type, and general health status. Alarm fatigue, poor sleep quality, and occupational burnout are related occupational health concerns among ICU nurses. Higher alarm fatigue was weakly but significantly associated with poorer sleep quality and greater burnout. These findings suggest that alarm management, shift scheduling, and workforce-related factors may be relevant areas for organizational attention; however, future longitudinal and interventional studies are needed to determine whether such strategies improve sleep quality, reduce burnout, or enhance patient safety. Not applicable.

42839267.title: VIDD or CIADD? The ventilator remains a bona fide culprit.
42839267.abstract: Rosà and colleagues recently proposed that mechanical ventilation (MV) may not be the primary driver of diaphragm dysfunction in critically ill patients, advocating the term "critical illness-associated diaphragm dysfunction" (CIADD) over "ventilator-induced diaphragm dysfunction" (VIDD). While we support distinguishing VIDD from CIADD, we contend that the review's central conclusion underestimates the causal role of MV itself.This commentary addresses three questions in turn. First, does MV injure the diaphragm under controlled conditions? Here the evidence is strong: brain-dead donor studies-dismissed by the authors as a "unique patient category"-are a uniquely informative, though not pure, human model of controlled MV exposure, and their dismissal creates an unfalsifiable position. Second, how much does MV contribute to diaphragm dysfunction in critically ill patients? This is considerably less certain: the molecular abnormalities observed in critically ill patients (ubiquitin-proteasome activation, RyR1 calcium leak, mitochondrial oxidative stress) coincide with pathways that MV reliably induces in controlled animal experiments, providing biological plausibility-though not proof-that MV contributes to the molecular phenotype of critical illness. Third, do MV and critical illness interact? We propose that CIADD should serve as an umbrella term encompassing VIDD as a distinct mechanistic subtype-rather than replacing it-analogous to how "pneumonia" subsumes VAP, HAP, and CAP, and we propose three differentiated model types for future research: pure VIDD models, pure CIADD models, and combined models with factorial design.VIDD and CIADD are mechanistically distinct but interacting entities. Future research should employ models that minimize confounding from critical illness to isolate ventilation-specific injury pathways. Importantly, establishing that VIDD exists is not equivalent to establishing that preventing VIDD is beneficial; clinical trials are needed to demonstrate the feasibility and benefit of diaphragm-protective strategies. Diminishing MV's role risks undermining the mechanistic foundation of diaphragm-protective ventilation strategies.

42876985.title: Development and validation of a prediction model for hypernatremia in patients with severe burns.
42876985.abstract: Hypernatremia is a prevalent and serious electrolyte disturbance in patients with severe burns, associated with significantly increased mortality and prolonged ICU stays. Early identification of high-risk patients could enable timely preventive interventions; however, practical tools for individualized risk stratification are currently lacking. This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram and a web-based calculator for the early prediction of hypernatremia in patients with severe burns. A total of 592 patients with burns covering ≥30% total body surface area were retrospectively included and randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 415) and an internal validation cohort (n = 177). Six independent predictors were identified: TBSA, mechanical ventilation, blood urea nitrogen ≥10 mmol/L, sepsis, glucose ≥9 mmol/L, and inhalation injury. The nomogram achieved an apparent C-index of 0.929 and a bootstrap-corrected C-index of 0.923 in the training cohort, and a C-index of 0.953 in the internal validation cohort. Using dual cutoffs of 90 and 135 points, the low cutoff yielded negative predictive values of 96.4% and 98.1%, and the high cutoff yielded positive predictive values of 75.4% and 65.3% in the training and internal validation cohorts, respectively. The nomogram and web-based calculator provide accurate, individualized risk prediction, facilitating early identification of high-risk individuals and supporting preventive strategies.

42875240.title: [Application of a spontaneous breathing trial based on high-flow oxygen therapy in weaning of mechanically ventilated patients].
42875240.journal: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
42875240.abstract: To evaluate the application efficacy of a spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) based on high-flow oxygen therapy (HFOT) during the weaning process in mechanically ventilated patients. A randomized controlled trial was conducted. A total of 163 patients undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Zhongda Hospital, Southeast University, from September 2024 to July 2025 were enrolled and randomly assigned to the HFOT group (80 cases) or the pressure support ventilation (PSV) group (83 cases). The HFOT group received SBT based on HFOT, while the PSV group received SBT based on PSV. Baseline data were collected and compared between the two groups, and adverse events during SBT were recorded. The primary outcome was the success rate of extubation within 48 hours. Secondary outcomes included vital signs, sputum grade, arterial blood gas parameters measured before SBT and 30 minutes after SBT initiation, SBT success rate, and prognostic outcomes [duration of mechanical ventilation, length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay, hospitalization costs, ICU mortality, in-hospital mortality, and 28-day mortality]. A total of 163 mechanically ventilated patients were included, with 80 in the HFOT group and 83 in the PSV group. There were no statistically significant differences in baseline data or prognostic outcomes between the two groups. The SBT success rates were 100% (80/80) in the HFOT group and 98.8% (82/83) in the PSV group, and the 48-hour extubation success rates were 87.5% (70/80) and 80.5% (66/82), respectively, with no statistically significant differences (both P>0.05). At 30 minutes after SBT initiation, the heart rate (HR0.5) and the decrease in HR (ΔHR0.5) in the HFOT group were significantly lower than those in the PSV group [HR0.5: 87.10±12.73 vs. 94.28±13.60; ΔHR0.5: 0.0 (-3.0, 2.0) vs. -1.0 (-5.0, 1.0); both P<0.05]. No significant differences were observed in other vital signs, sputum grade, or arterial blood gas parameters between the two groups. No safety events occurred in either group during the trial, indicating good safety. Subgroup analysis showed statistically significant interactions between intervention modality and both age and duration of mechanical ventilation (both P<0.05). In patients aged≥65 years, the ICU length of stay in the HFOT group was significantly shorter by a mean of 83.12 hours [95% confidence interval (95%CI) was -151.28 to -14.96] compared with the PSV group. In patients with mechanical ventilation duration≥24 hours, the ICU length of stay in the HFOT group was significantly shorter by a mean of 157.40 hours (95%CI was -254.60 to -60.20) compared with the PSV group. SBT based on HFOT is safe for weaning mechanically ventilated patients and offers certain physiological advantages in improving HR. In elderly patients (≥65 years) and those with prolonged mechanical ventilation (≥24 hours), HFOT-based SBT can significantly shorten ICU length of stay, but it does not show a clear advantage in improving the 48-hour extubation success rate.

42870652.title: Long-Term Impact of Timing on Spinal Implantation for Lumbar Fractures in Polytrauma Patients: A Systematic Review.
42870652.journal: Journal of long-term effects of medical implants
42870652.abstract: The timing of osteosynthesis in polytrauma patients with lumbar spine fractures may influence key clinical outcomes, including hospital length of stay (HLOS), ICU length of stay (ICULOS), and mechanical ventilation duration (VENT DAYS). This systematic review aimed to evaluate how surgical timing affects these outcomes. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and CENTRAL was completed in February 2025. Inclusion criteria involved studies on adult polytrauma patients (> 18 years) with lumbar spine fractures from blunt trauma, requiring surgical fixation, comparing early ( 72 h) surgery. Studies had to report Injury Severity Scores (ISS), outcomes of interest (HLOS, ICULOS, and VENT DAYS), include statistical comparisons between groups, and meet a minimum of "moderate" risk of bias based on the ROBINS-I tool. Out of 588 studies initially identified, three fulfilled the inclusion criteria, involving 1,111 patients-759 underwent early fixation and 352 late. The weighted average age was 39.1 years in the early group and 41.2 years in the late group. The weighted average ISS was 27.3 (early) and 29.2 (late). The weighted average VENT DAYS was 4.9 in the early group and 7.8 in the late group. The weighted average ICULOS was 10.9 d (early) and 13.7 d (late). The weighted average HLOS was 37.9 d (early) and 36.8 d (late). The impact of osteosynthesis on VENT DAYS and ICULOS remains uncertain, while HLOS shows no clinically relevant difference. ISS significantly influences outcomes.

42854438.title: The impact of cannabis on clinical outcomes in burn patients: A systematic review.
42854438.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42854438.abstract: Burn injuries remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with survivors often requiring prolonged hospitalization, complex wound care, and intensive rehabilitation. Concurrently, cannabis use has risen substantially in North America and Europe, with recent data showing cannabis use in approximately 16-18% of burn admissions by 2025. Cannabinoids influence pain, immunity, and cardiopulmonary physiology, making their role in burn recovery clinically relevant but poorly defined. A systematic review was conducted evaluating cannabis exposure and outcomes in burn patients. MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to August 2025. Eligible studies included hospitalized burn patients of any age, with cannabis exposure identified via toxicology, history, or coding, and reported outcomes stratified by cannabis exposure. Outcomes of interest included mortality, infection, graft success, thromboembolism, ventilation, ICU and hospital length of stay, opioid use, discharge disposition, and readmission. Of 1009 studies, eight met inclusion criteria, with sample sizes ranging from 64 to over 300,000 patients. Cannabis exposure was identified via toxicology, history, or coding. Across studies, cannabis was not consistently associated with inpatient mortality. Some single-center analyses reported increased opioid and anxiolytic requirements, higher wound infection rates, longer ICU stays, and more reoperations. National database studies found lower adjusted mortality among cannabis-using patients but higher rates of ventilator-associated pneumonia, venous thromboembolism, and prolonged ICU stays. Heterogeneity was pronounced, with polysubstance use, burn severity, and demographic differences influencing outcomes. Overall, cannabis exposure does not appear to worsen survival in burn patients but may predispose to infectious, respiratory, and thromboembolic complications. The evidence base is limited by retrospective design, inconsistent exposure definitions, and confounding from polysubstance use. Cannabis positivity at admission should prompt heightened monitoring for complications and tailored pain management. Future prospective, multicenter studies with detailed exposure characterization and long-term follow-up are needed to clarify cannabis' role in burn recovery and to inform evidence-based analgesic strategies.

42848737.title: Characterization of Burn Patients at a Level IV Referral Institution in Barranquilla, Colombia: A 5-Year Analysis.
42848737.abstract: Burn injuries represent a major public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. In Colombia, regional epidemiological data remain limited, restricting the development of evidence-based prevention and treatment strategies. This descriptive, observational, retrospective study included 526 patients with burn injuries treated at a level IV referral institution in Barranquilla, Colombia, between November 2018 and November 2023. Sociodemographic, clinical, and outcome variables were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 25.0. Associations with in-hospital mortality were assessed using the Fisher exact test and univariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was defined as P<0.05. The mean patient age was 24.6±21.0 years, and males accounted for 61.8% of the cohort. Scald injuries were the most common mechanism (54.8%), with children younger than 5 years comprising 25.5% of all patients. Major burns were identified in 30.2% of patients. The mean total body surface area burned (TBSA) was 11.7±13.0% (median: 7.0%). Surgical debridement and/or escharotomy were performed in 59.7% of cases, and reconstructive coverage was required in 34.2%. The overall in-hospital mortality rate was 8.4% (n=44). On univariable analysis, the factors most strongly associated with mortality were major burns [odds ratio (OR), 13.13; 95% CI: 5.94-29.03; P<0.001], ICU admission (OR=12.74; 95% CI: 4.49-36.16; P<0.001), and bronchoscopically confirmed airway injury (OR=35.48; 95% CI: 9.02-139.56; P<0.001). Endotracheal intubation was strongly associated with death (35 of 43 intubated patients died), but the association could not be reliably quantified because of near-complete separation. The most frequently documented complications were sepsis (8.2%), pneumonia (3.6%), and documented bacteremia (2.5%); the case-fatality rate among patients with sepsis was 41.9%. Pseudomonas aeruginosa was the microorganism most commonly isolated from tissue cultures. Major burns, airway injury, and ICU admission were the factors most strongly associated with in-hospital mortality in this cohort. The substantial surgical burden underscores the need to strengthen specialized burn-care capacity in the Colombian Caribbean region. Targeted prevention strategies for pediatric and working-age populations, along with national epidemiological surveillance systems, are urgently needed.

42926949.title: Scapulothoracic Disarticulation of the Right Upper Limb After a Car-to-Obstacle Collision: A Case Report.
42926949.abstract: This report details the case of a 26-year-old man, victim of a car-to-barrier collision followed by a rollover. The patient, found conscious, was intubated by the pre-hospital team and admitted in severe hypovolemic shock, with extensive injury to the shoulder and right upper limb. After hemodynamic stabilization, the team performed bilateral chest drainage, a massive transfusion protocol, and a forequarter amputation of the right upper limb with ligation of the subclavian vessels, in a joint procedure by the orthopedic and vascular surgery teams. Postoperatively, he remained in the intensive care unit (ICU), developing ventilator-associated pneumonia, treated with meropenem and vancomycin. After 10 days, the patient was transferred to a ward. He was discharged from the hospital after 15 days of hospitalization and continued with outpatient follow-up, where he presented with phantom limb pain initially treated with gabapentin and controlled with physiotherapy. In the end, he was definitively discharged with good healing, pain improvement, and favorable clinical evolution.

42921809.title: Music-Based Intervention in Postoperative Lung Transplant Care: A Feasibility Study.
42921809.abstract: Music-based interventions may support recovery in medical and surgical settings; however, their implementation during the immediate postoperative period following lung transplantation remains understudied. This single-center randomized feasibility study examined whether a structured music-based intervention delivered by board-certified music therapists could be implemented at clinically meaningful postoperative recovery milestones and explored preliminary trends in pain, anxiety, medication use, sleep, and length of stay. Twenty-nine adult lung transplant recipients (experimental n = 17, control n = 12) were enrolled between September 2021 and September 2023. Participants in the intervention group received music-based intervention sessions during spontaneous awakening trials, 24-48 hr following extubation, and within 72 hr of transfer from the intensive care unit to a step-down unit. Intervention components included patient-preferred live music, music-assisted relaxation, and optional receptive or active music engagement tailored to patient status. Intervention delivery was feasible across all three postoperative milestones, although challenges related to recruitment, retention, sleep measurement, and intervention standardization were identified. Exploratory analyses suggested lower observed pain scores and lower median acetaminophen use in the intervention group compared to standard care; however, no outcomes reached statistical significance. Anxiety outcomes did not differ between groups, and sleep measurement using consumer-grade wearable devices was not feasible. These findings support the feasibility of music-based interventions during postoperative lung transplant recovery and provide guidance for the design of future adequately powered trials using refined outcome measures, milestone-based intervention delivery, and improved implementation strategies.

42897086.title: Gastrointestinal and Urological Tract Injuries During Cesarean Delivery: A Surgical Review With National Epidemiologic Data.
42897086.abstract: BackgroundCesarean delivery is the most common major surgical procedure performed worldwide, accounting for approximately one-third of US deliveries. Gastrointestinal (GI) and urological (URO) tract injuries are uncommon but disproportionately morbid complications. Increasing complexity, particularly repeat cesarean and placenta accreta spectrum (PAS), and uneven on-site subspecialty coverage have expanded the role of general surgeons as intraoperative consultants for these injuries, especially outside large tertiary centers.MethodsWe analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2005-2019) to characterize the contemporary epidemiology, predictors, and outcomes of GI/URO injuries during cesarean delivery, complemented by a literature review focused on intraoperative recognition and management principles most relevant to the consulting general surgeon.ResultsAmong 3 816 895 cesarean deliveries, 8891 involved a documented GI/URO injury requiring surgical intervention (≈233 per 100 000). Bladder injuries predominated (78.2%), followed by bowel repair (13.3%), bowel resection (7.8%), and ureteral injuries (1.3%). Injuries were associated with markedly higher ICU admission (3.4% vs 0.2%), respiratory failure (1.7% vs 0.1%), in-hospital mortality (0.22% vs 0.01%), and resource utilization. Prior cesarean delivery was the strongest predictor of URO injury (OR 2.92; 95% CI 2.71-3.13).ConclusionsGI/URO injuries during cesarean delivery are uncommon but highly morbid, and the operative complexity that produces them is rising. With variable on-site subspecialty coverage, the general surgeon is frequently the first operative consultant. Familiarity with intraoperative principles, prevention strategies in high-risk cases, structured recognition, and initial repair or damage-control temporization should be considered a core competency for surgeons covering trauma, rural, or emergency general surgery call.

42886572.title: Influence of Perioperative Variables on Surgical Site Infection in Patients With Frailty and Prefrailty Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
42886572.abstract: Surgical site infection (SSI) in patients with frailty undergoing myocardial revascularization is a major clinical challenge, and there is a gap in the literature related to this topic. This study aimed to identify perioperative variables associated with SSI in patients with frailty and prefrailty undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting within 30 days of the procedure. This retrospective observational study included 467 patients with frailty or prefrailty aged 60 years and older who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting in 6 Brazilian centers between January 2018 and December 2024. Frailty was defined using the Fried criteria. SSI was defined as a wound with exposed tissue with positive culture requiring antibiotic treatment. Univariate and multivariate analyses were carried out. The rate of SSI was 5.6% (26/467). The New York Heart Association classification (P=.02), Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI; P=.01), use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB; P=.003), CPB time (P=.02), total surgery time (P<.001), occurrence of bleeding (P=.04), mechanical ventilation time (P=.001), length of hospital stay (P<.001), intensive care unit stay (P<.001), and need for reoperation (P<.001) variables were associated with SSI in unadjusted comparisons. In the multivariate model, the CCI (odds ratio 1.58, 95% CI 1.25-1.99; P<.001) and use of CPB (odds ratio 4.89, 95% CI 1.71-13.94; P=.003) were independently associated with SSI. The CCI and the use of CPB were independently associated with SSI.

42965657.title: Airway Pressure Release Ventilation Versus Conventional Ventilation in Adults With or at Risk for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
42965657.abstract: To assess whether airway pressure release ventilation (APRV) reduces mortality compared with conventional invasive ventilation in adults with established acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), acute lung injury, or conditions considered to confer a high risk of ARDS. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception through August 15, 2026. We analyzed parallel-group randomized trials using random-effects models. Mortality at trial-defined follow-up was the primary outcome. We used Cochrane RoB 2 to assess risk of bias and GRADE to assess certainty of evidence. CRD420251170819. Nine trials involving 585 participants were included. No mortality benefit was demonstrated (risk ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.72-1.26). Ventilator-free days showed no clear difference (mean difference [MD] 3.83 days, 95% CI - 1.69 to 9.34; I²=83%). APRV was associated with a higher PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio (MD 56.21 mm Hg, 95% CI 24.63-87.79; I²=84%) and shorter ICU stay (MD - 2.53 days, 95% CI - 4.43 to - 0.64; I²=71%). Ventilation duration showed no clear difference (five trials, 413 participants; MD - 2.44 days, 95% CI - 4.96 to 0.09; I²=78%). Peak airway pressure was lower and mean airway pressure was higher with APRV. This synthesis does not establish that APRV improves survival, ventilator-free days, or ventilation duration. Oxygenation and ICU-stay findings require caution because populations, protocols, outcome timing, and risk of bias varied. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. These data do not establish mortality equivalence or superiority over contemporary lung-protective ventilation. CRD420251170819; registered 17 October 2025.

42892954.title: Feasibility and Safety of Intraoperative Abdominal Warming During Spinal Surgery in the Prone Position: A Pilot Study.
42892954.abstract: Inadvertent perioperative hypothermia caused by general anesthesia leads to several complications, including shivering, coagulopathy, surgical site infections, and delayed wound healing. Prone positioning for spine surgery severely restricts the available body surface area for warming, complicating intraoperative temperature management. This study investigated a novel approach utilizing the anatomical space beneath the chest and abdomen created by a standard four-point bolster support to maintain intraoperative core body temperature using standard pediatric underbody forced-air warming blankets. This prospective, single-arm pilot study enrolled six adult patients undergoing elective spinal surgery in the prone position under general anesthesia at Akita Red Cross Hospital, Akita, Japan. No active preoperative warming was performed. A pediatric underbody forced-air warming blanket (SWU-2009; ICU Medical Inc., San Clemente, CA, USA) was pre-positioned in the suspended thoracoabdominal space of the four-point support and operated at 40 °C. Core body temperature (monitored via a temperature-sensing urinary catheter) and skin condition were recorded from induction to the end of surgery. Six patients (mean age: 66.8 ± 16.7 years, mean surgical duration: 230.2 ± 55.5 minutes) were analyzed. The median core temperature was 36.5 °C (interquartile range (IQR): 36.4 °C-36.5 °C) at induction, 36.6 °C (IQR: 36.4 °C-36.9 °C) at incision, and 37.0 °C (IQR: 36.7 °C-37.1 °C) at the end of surgery. Although transient mild hypothermia (< 36.0 °C) occurred in two patients, both recovered to normothermia within 90 minutes. No patient developed redness, blisters, or thermal burns. Abdominal warming utilizing the suspended space of a four-point bolster support was feasible to implement without occurrences of skin-related complications, demonstrating potential to contribute to intraoperative temperature stabilization. While adequately powered comparative trials are required to definitively evaluate its clinical efficacy, this approach provides preliminary insights into practical thermal management in standard operating rooms.

42868705.title: Association between the duration of the first hemofilter after septic shock and septic shock resolution in severely burned patients receiving continuous blood purification.
42868705.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42868705.abstract: Septic shock is a major cause of mortality in severe burn patients. Our objective was to evaluate the association between the duration of the first hemofilter following septic shock and recovery from septic shock in severely burned patients treated with continuous blood purification combined with adsorption. A prospective, quasi- experimental study at department of Intensive Care, Vietnam National Burn Hospital. The study consisted of 55 episodes of septic shock in 38 severe burn patients with total burn size ≥ 20% of total body surface area. Continuous blood purification using the oXiris hemofilter conducted within 6 h of septic shock (SS) diagnosis, and after raising systolic blood pressure to above 90 mmHg. TNF-α and IL-6 concentrations decreased significantly over time after filtration, with mean hourly reductions of 0.33 pg/mL (SE = 0.16; p = 0.037) and 5.37 pg/mL (SE = 2.29; p = 0.019), respectively. After 24 h of continuous blood purification, plasma endotoxin levels decreased significantly compared with those at 6 h after continuous blood purification (47 (27.5-89.55) pg/mL vs. 68.3 (53.45-120.25) pg/mL, p = 0.003). The longer the duration of the first filtration session after septic shock, the higher the IL-6 concentration measured at 24 h after septic shock (r = 0.36, p = 0.008). Replacement of the first hemofilter at 12 h after initiation of blood purification increased the likelihood of septic shock resolution by 3.89-fold (p = 0.001). The predictive performance for shock resolution was moderate (AUC = 0.74, sensitivity: 75%, specificity: 73.68%). The longer the duration of the first filtration session after septic shock, the higher the IL-6 concentration at 24 h. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that the pre-CVVHDF SOFA score, pre-CVVHDF plasma IL-6 concentration, and first hemofilter replacement within 12 h were independent factors associated with septic shock reversal.

42848609.title: Complex abdomen: proposal of a preliminary conceptual framework, clinical implications, and contemporary perspectives.
42848609.journal: Revista do Colegio Brasileiro de Cirurgioes
42848609.abstract: The open abdomen has become a cornerstone in the care of critically ill patients undergoing damage control surgery, with severe abdominal sepsis, or at risk of abdominal compartment syndrome. These patients frequently develop a multidimensional clinical course - persistent infection, organ failure, loss of abdominal wall integrity, nutritional depletion, and entero-atmospheric fistulas - whose severity appears to emerge from the dynamic interaction among these factors rather than from visceral exposure alone. Current classifications, notably Björck's amended classification, describe the anatomical progression of the open abdomen but do not integrate the physiological, infectious, nutritional, and organizational dimensions of care. The aim is to propose the term "complex abdomen" as a preliminary conceptual framework complementary to - and not a replacement for - existing classifications. Conceptual scientific communication grounded in a narrative review of the literature (MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, SciELO, and LILACS; 2000 to 2025; Portuguese, English, and Spanish), reported according to the SANRA scale. The synthesis followed best-fit framework synthesis, with the Cumulative Complexity Model as the a priori framework. Five constitutive domains are proposed - physiological instability; uncontrolled intra-abdominal infection; loss of abdominal wall domain; entero-atmospheric or complex enteric fistula; nutritional and intestinal failure - together with their associated cut-offs, a contextual organizational modifier recorded separately, and the criterion of simultaneous involvement of two or more domains. The domains, the cut-offs, and the criterion were proposed by the authors on the basis of the literature and clinical experience, without formal consensus and without empirical validation. The construct is presented as a dynamic clinical phenotype assessed at defined time points, not as an obligatory evolutionary stage or a prognostic score. This is a preliminary framework rather than a validated definition. Formalizing this phenotype may improve clinical reasoning, multidisciplinary communication, and the selection of more homogeneous study populations. A three-step validation agenda - modified Delphi consensus, reliability and content validity assessment, and prospective prognostic testing within a multicenter registry - is proposed, together with explicit refutation criteria.

42829648.title: VISTA Confers Renal Protection in Murine Hemorrhage/Infection-Induced Acute Kidney Injury: Associations with Altered NGAL and HMGB1 Expression.
42829648.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) represents a serious complication associated with both short- and long-term morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients. Severe trauma complicated by infection represents a high‑risk clinical trigger for AKI. V‑domain immunoglobulin suppressor of T‑cell activation (VISTA) is an immune‑checkpoint molecule with immunomodulatory functions, yet its role in trauma‑sepsis‑induced AKI remains incompletely defined. In this experimental study, male wild‑type (WT) and VISTA‑deficient (VISTA-/-) C57BL/6 mice were utilized to establish a two‑hit murine AKI model combining hemorrhagic shock and cecal ligation and puncture (Hem/CLP). Blood and kidney tissues were collected 24 hours after hemorrhage/CLP. VISTA expression on neutrophils and monocytes in peripheral blood was assessed by flow cytometry. Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen were measured according to manufacturer protocols. Cytokine levels were determined by ELISA, and corresponding mRNA expression was analyzed via RT-PCR. Kidney injury severity was evaluated histologically by pathologists. Protein levels of neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and high mobility group box 1 were examined by Western blot. VISTA expression was significantly elevated on circulating neutrophils and monocytes following injury (all p < 0.05). Histopathological assessment revealed aggravated kidney injury in the AKI model (p = 0.0056), which was further exacerbated in VISTA-deficient mice (p = 0.0357). Consistent with this, serum creatinine (p = 0.014) and blood urea nitrogen (p = 0.005) levels were markedly higher in VISTA-deficient mice compared to controls. Pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 (p = 0.0335) and TNF-α (p = 0.0283) were increased in AKI mice and further elevated in VISTA-deficient mice (p = 0.0014 and 0.0001, respectively), whereas anti-inflammatory IL-10 showed a converse trend (p = 0.0056 and 0.0019, respectively). RT-PCR confirmed corresponding changes in cytokine mRNA expression. Western blot analysis indicated decreased neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (p < 0.0001) and increased high mobility group box 1 protein (p = 0.0009) levels in VISTA-deficient mice. Collectively, our results demonstrate that VISTA‑deficient mice develop more severe early‑phase hemorrhage/sepsis‑induced AKI. Altered NGAL and HMGB1 protein expression occur in parallel with VISTA‑associated renal protection; further functional validation is required to establish causal mechanistic relationships and to evaluate the translational potential of VISTA‑targeted approaches.

42923891.title: Amniotic fluid embolism Number 11 - 2026.
42923891.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
42923891.abstract: •Amniotic fluid embolism is a rare condition with high maternal mortality. It typically occurs during labor or delivery, and the pathogenesis has not yet been fully elucidated. •Survival of parturients with amniotic fluid embolism requires early recognition, rapid initiation of treatment, and access to skilled care based on the management of critically ill obstetric patients. •The classic clinical presentation of amniotic fluid embolism involves sudden hypoxia and hypotension or cardiopulmonary arrest, accompanied or immediately followed by non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and hemorrhage secondary to disseminated intravascular coagulation. •In cases of amniotic fluid embolism occurring during labor, bleeding typically originates at invasive interventions sites (intravascular lines and urinary catheterization). Following vaginal or cesarean delivery, bleeding arises primarily from the uterus, birth canal lacerations, and incision sites (abdominal wall and episiotomies). •Key laboratory abnormalities observed in amniotic fluid embolism include decreased fibrinogen levels, thrombocytopenia, and elevated D-dimer levels. The latter has limited diagnostic value, as levels are typically elevated during pregnancy and the postpartum period. •Arterial blood gas analysis in amniotic fluid embolism indicates the presence of hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis. Although chest radiography is initially unremarkable, if pulmonary edema and respiratory distress syndrome are present, dense bilateral pulmonary infiltrates may be observed. •The identification of amniotic fluid debris in pulmonary artery catheters or histopathological samples of lung tissue should not be considered diagnostic of amniotic fluid embolism. •The primary goals in managing amniotic fluid embolism are cardiopulmonary resuscitation, hemorrhage control, reversal of coagulopathy, and when indicated, fetal delivery. •In cases of amniotic fluid embolism accompanied by coagulopathy, massive transfusion is a necessary measure for effective, definitive treatment. The infusion of uterotonics, non-surgical invasive interventions (intrauterine balloons and intrauterine suction systems), and surgical procedures (vascular ligation, uterine compression sutures, and hysterectomy) may be used as adjuncts to control hemorrhage but are not considered definitive treatments. •The main differential diagnoses for amniotic fluid embolism include complications of neuraxial anesthesia; hemorrhage due to uterine atony, retained products of conception, and/or birth canal trauma; placental abruption; pulmonary thromboembolism; air embolism; acute myocardial infarction; and anaphylactic, cardiogenic, or septic shock.

42908823.title: Case Report: Delayed complete transection of the sigmoid colon after severe pelvic fracture leading to septic shock.
42908823.abstract: Severe pelvic fractures caused by high-energy trauma may be complicated by bowel injuries. These injuries may be evident at initial presentation or remain occult, resulting in delayed diagnosis. Delayed complete transection of the sigmoid colon associated with pelvic fractures is extremely rare. We describe a 57-year-old woman who was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) following a traffic accident that resulted in a Young-Burgess lateral compression type III pelvic ring injury, hemorrhagic shock, impaired consciousness, and multiple associated injuries. Abdominal CT on post-injury days 1, 2, and 3, emergency focused assessment with sonography for trauma (FAST), and repeated bedside ultrasonography showed no definite bowel injury. Bowel sounds were normal on admission, reduced on day 2, and absent from day 3, but abdominal symptoms could not be assessed reliably. Some inflammatory and organ-function indices partially declined after antimicrobial and supportive treatment. On day 6, abrupt biomarker re-elevation, high fever, progressive abdominal distension, and hemodynamic deterioration prompted repeat CT, which demonstrated extraluminal gas adjacent to the sigmoid colon. Emergency laparotomy confirmed complete sigmoid transection with partial stump necrosis and extensive fecal contamination. The patient survived after colectomy, colostomy, prolonged intensive care, and staged pelvic fixation. This case shows that bowel injury may continue to progress despite repeated negative CT and ultrasonographic examinations and transient improvement in inflammatory markers. When a high-risk mechanism and the clinical trajectory remain discordant, renewed surgical assessment and escalation beyond repeated noninvasive observation should be considered.

42893147.title: Extensive Gastric Necrosis and Perforation Secondary to Intragastric Balloon-Related Gastric Outlet Obstruction: A Case Report.
42893147.abstract: Intragastric balloons (IGBs) are widely used as temporary endoscopic therapy for obesity, but rare complications can be catastrophic. A 55-year-old woman presented with severe epigastric pain, persistent vomiting, and progressive abdominal distension four months after the placement of a 650-mL Orbera intragastric balloon (Apollo Endosurgery, Austin, TX). She was hypotensive and tachycardic and presented with generalized peritonitis. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed marked gastric distension, antropyloric balloon impaction, absent mural enhancement along the lesser curvature, pneumoperitoneum, and free intraperitoneal fluid. Emergency laparotomy uncovered extensive gastric necrosis with a 4-cm perforation. The intact balloon was removed, and total gastrectomy without immediate esophagojejunal reconstruction was performed along with feeding jejunostomy. Histopathological examination confirmed complete transmural infarction and necrosis of the lesser curvature, severe diffuse acute ischemic injury of the adjacent gastric wall with vascular microthrombi, and localized fibrinous peritonitis, with no malignant neoplasm. Despite intensive care, refractory septic shock and multiorgan failure continued to progress, and the patient died 72 hours postoperatively. This case highlights the need for urgent imaging and source control when persistent pain, vomiting, or distension develops in a patient with an IGB.

42889592.title: Successful endoscopic vacuum therapy in diffuse gastric hemorrhage secondary to acute ischemia: a case report.
42889592.abstract: Acute gastric ischemia is rare and may lead to diffuse mucosal bleeding, often refractory to conventional endoscopic therapy. We describe the case of a 42-year-old critically ill burn patient who developed persistent upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage unresponsive to medical treatment, in whom the novel use of endoscopic vacuum therapy (EVT) was undertaken. Serial endoscopies demonstrated progressive mucosal healing, reduced necrosis, and effective bleeding control. EVT promoted granulation tissue and ulcer healing, avoiding surgical intervention. No EVT-related adverse events occurred. Despite successful hemostasis, the patient later died from a sepsis-related adverse event. In conclusion, this case illustrates EVT as a viable and effective approach for managing refractory diffuse gastric bleeding secondary to ischemia. EVT may offer a minimally invasive alternative to surgery in critically ill patients where standard therapies fail.

42883699.title: Flow Cytometry and AI-Driven Biomarker Discovery in Acute Kidney Injury: From Mechanistic Insights to Translation Applications in Clinical and Austere Environments.
42883699.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a complex and multifactorial syndrome characterized by the rapid decline of renal function following ischemic, septic, traumatic, hypoxic, or nephrotoxic insults. Despite advances in critical care, exacerbation of AKI is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, progression to chronic kidney disease (CKD) and multiorgan dysfunction. Current therapies remain largely supportive and do not directly target the molecular pathways driving AKI, underscoring the need for mechanism-based diagnostics and precision-guided therapeutic strategies. Accumulating evidence supports that AKI is driven by mechanistic crosstalk among cellular injury pathways involving mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, endothelial damage, immune dysregulation, and regulated cell death. Flow cytometry has emerged as a powerful platform for high-dimensional single-cell and extracellular vesicle analysis, enabling comprehensive assessment of immune cell phenotypes, platelet activation, endothelial alterations, mitochondrial dysfunction, and circulating extracellular vesicles associated with AKI. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and emerging explainable AI (XAI) enhance the ability to identify clinically relevant patterns from complex datasets. This review aims to integrate AKI pathophysiology with flow cytometry-based biomarker discovery and AI-enabled analytical approaches. We discuss translational applications in AKI-relevant clinical settings, including trauma, hemorrhagic shock, sepsis, and radiation-combined injury, with particular emphasis on Prolonged Casualty Care and other austere environments, where rapid, mechanism-based diagnostics are critically needed.

42868703.title: Early hemodynamic profiles in severely burned patients: A single center cohort study.
42868703.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42868703.abstract: Large burns are associated with a massive inflammatory response and catecholamine release leading to complex cardiovascular disorders. Our aim was to describe the early hemodynamic trajectories following severe burns and to identify distinct hemodynamic trajectory patterns. We retrospectively collected data from patients admitted to our burn center for severe burn injuries between January 2017 and April 2025. Hemodynamic data were obtained by transpulmonary thermodilution coupled with pulse wave analysis. Time series for cardiac index (CI), systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI) and heart rate (HR) were analyzed for the first 96 h. Hemodynamic profiles were compared using dynamic time warping (DTW). Clusters were identified through hierarchical clustering. A total of 107 patients were included (median age 52 years [IQR: 36-65], median total burn surface area burned 40% [IQR: 30-54]); 22 patients died during their ICU stay. In the entire cohort, the hemodynamic profile progressively shifted from a low-cardiac output, vasoconstrictive state to a hyperkinetic, vasoplegic state (CI 2.6 ± 0.8-4.8 ± 1.3 L/min/m2; SVRI 3362[2659-4489] to 1382[1118-1698] dyn.s.cm-5.m2, p < 0.05). Cluster analysis identified two hemodynamic trajectory patterns, one with CI stabilization after an initial rise and another with a continuous increase in CI. SVRI decreased similarly in both clusters. ICU mortality differed between clusters in univariate analysis. This study confirms a two-phase hemodynamic response to severe burns under active fluid resuscitation. It provides evidence for distinct hemodynamic trajectory patterns. These profiles could help optimize individual resuscitation strategies.

42965206.title: Inferior vena cava peak velocity versus collapsibility index to predict volume status in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding: A pilot study.
42965206.abstract: Patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) with hemorrhagic shock secondary to acute gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding represent a substantial proportion of the critically ill population. Accurate evaluation of intravascular volume status in these patients is crucial for guiding fluid resuscitation. However, the limitations of invasive methods and inferior vena cava (IVC) diameter/collapsibility measurements in assessing intravascular volume have been widely discussed in the literature. Despite their validation, noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring techniques remain underutilized in the ED. Therefore, the present study aimed to investigate the predictive value of IVC blood flow velocity measured by Doppler ultrasonography in intravascular volume assessment and to compare it with the IVC collapsibility index. Electrical velocity measurement was used as a surrogate marker of volume deficit. Eighteen patients presenting with a preliminary diagnosis of acute GI bleeding were included in the study. The study population consisted solely of patients with suspected hypovolemia; therefore, no normovolemic control group was included in the study. Demographic, vital, and laboratory data were recorded, along with IVC diameter, collapsibility, IVC peak velocity measured by continuous-wave Doppler, and noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring parameters at admission, at the 30th and 60th min, and immediately after completion of fluid replacement. All data were subjected to statistical analysis. A significant correlation was observed between initial IVC peak velocity and stroke volume variation at admission (P = 0.009). The measurement demonstrated a specificity of 100% and a sensitivity of 84%, although the confidence interval was wide due to the small number of patients without volume deficit. No statistically significant differences were detected at the other time points. This can be explained by the ongoing bleeding and the lack of a valid gold standard. Measurement of IVC peak velocity was found to be a significant predictor of hypovolemia, although it showed limited utility for volume monitoring. Furthermore, it demonstrated superior performance compared to IVC diameter and collapsibility measurements. However, the study does not evaluate its ability to distinguish hypovolemia from true normovolemia.

42880808.title: Characteristics and outcomes of haemorrhage, traumatic brain injury and combined injuries from a South African Trauma Cohort Study.
42880808.abstract: To describe and compare injury severity, clinical management and mortality among haemorrhage, traumatic brain injury (TBI) and combined haemorrhage+TBI cohorts in a South African trauma population. Secondary analysis of data from the Epidemiology and Outcomes of Prolonged Trauma Care (EpiC) multicentre observational cohort study, April 2021 to December 2024. Six government health facilities and affiliated government ambulances across the Western Cape, South Africa. 18 840 adult patients with blunt and/or penetrating traumatic injuries enrolled in the EpiC registry were eligible for this secondary analysis. Patients <18 years of age and prisoners are excluded from EpiC. Burn injuries, non-haemorrhage and non-TBI injuries were excluded from this analysis. Patients were assigned to one of three mutually exclusive cohorts (haemorrhage, TBI or haemorrhage+TBI) using anatomic and physiologic criteria. The primary outcome was crude, all-cause prehospital or in-hospital mortality. Mantel-Haenszel risk ratios (RRs) for mortality were adjusted for injury severity, injury force type and mode of prehospital transportation. Secondary outcomes included critical interventions, hospital admission, length of stay and time from injury to death. A total of 7614 patients met inclusion: 5146 (67.6%) haemorrhage, 1556 (20.4%) TBI and 912 (12.0%) haemorrhage+TBI. The majority were male (85.1%) with a median age of 31 years. Patients with haemorrhage+TBI received more intensive care, including airway interventions (38%), transfusions (41%) and intensive care unit admissions (36%). Crude mortality was highest in haemorrhage+TBI (31.3%), followed by TBI (7.7%) and haemorrhage (5.4%). After injury-pattern specific severity adjustment, mortality risk remained significantly higher in haemorrhage+TBI than in TBI (RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.60 to 2.19) and haemorrhage (RR 3.38, 95% CI 2.96 to 3.85). Estimates were similar after additional adjustment for injury force and prehospital transportation (RR 1.84 and 2.98). In this South African population, haemorrhage+TBI was the least prevalent but most high-risk cohort with greater morbidity and mortality compared with haemorrhage or TBI alone, even after adjusting for injury severity. These findings may inform system level planning and resource allocation particularly in resource-limited settings.

42871870.title: Risk Factors for Poor Outcomes of Mild and Moderate Traumatic Brain Injury Patients in Tanzania: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using Latent Class Analysis.
42871870.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major global health concern, especially in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). LMICs have higher injury rates and limited quality of care. TBI patients can be stratified as mild, moderate, and severe risk based on the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS). Although most poor outcomes are from severe TBIs, mild and moderate TBI patients significantly contribute to the overall morbidity and mortality, and may benefit from early monitoring to identify deterioration of status. Our goal was to identify unique subgroups within the mild and moderate TBI population at a high risk for poor outcomes. We selected mild (GCS 14-15) and moderate (GCS 9-13) TBI patients from a TBI registry collected at a small city, regional referral hospital in Moshi, Tanzania, from May 2014 to April 2017. With these subsets (mild: n = 1738, moderate: n = 346), we performed a latent class analysis (LCA) to define unique patient classes based on clinical course, vital signs, and demographics. We then performed a survival analysis using a Cox proportional hazard model to examine the association of the defined latent classes with clinical outcome. The predictor variables were demographic variables, hospital interventions, and vital signs. The outcome of interest was a dichotomized discharge Glasgow outcome scale extended score (good outcome 7-8 and poor outcome 1-6). The LCA identified five classes among mild TBI patients: Adolescent (18.8%), Assault (31.5%), Young Adult Polytrauma (32.7%), Adult Polytrauma (9.2%), and RTI with ICU (7.8%). Three classes were identified among moderate TBI patients: Assault (20.2%), RTI with ICU (26.3%), and RTI without ICU (53.5%). Road traffic injury was the predominant mechanism in both severity groups (67% and 68%, respectively), and poor outcomes occurred in 4% of mild and 16% of moderate TBI patients. Relative to the lowest-risk reference class, all other mild TBI classes had higher hazards of poor outcomes. Among moderate TBI classes, RTI with ICU had a higher hazard of poor outcome than RTI without ICU (HR 2.58, 95% CI 1.26-5.24). We identified clinically distinct latent classes within GCS-defined mild and moderate TBI groups, with differences in discharge outcomes across classes. These findings suggest that combining GCS category with demographic, physiological, injury, and care-process information may provide additional prognostic stratification. The results do not establish that GCS is inadequate; rather, they support further evaluation of complementary, context-appropriate risk-stratification approaches.

42903085.title: Integrating 72-h BUN/Cr trajectories with interpretable machine learning for 28-day mortality after acute stroke: a dual-center landmark study.
42903085.abstract: The blood urea nitrogen-to-creatinine ratio (BUN/Cr) may reflect renal perfusion and systemic stress, but its early course after acute stroke is unclear. We identified 72-h BUN/Cr trajectories and assessed their role in interpretable machine-learning evaluation of 28-day mortality. This dual-center landmark study included 2,805 ICU patients with acute ischemic stroke, nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage, or nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) version 3.1. Before modeling, patients were split into a training set (n = 1,964) and an internal test set (n = 841). The trajectory and prediction models developed in the training set were applied without modification to the internal test set and the Qinghai external validation cohort (n = 387). Eight algorithms and prespecified nested models were evaluated using Cox regression, discrimination, calibration, paired comparisons, decision curves, and TreeSHAP. A quadratic three-class model identified low/stable, high U-shaped, and rising-to-plateau patterns, with mortality rates of 21.6, 35.9, and 39.7%. Adjusted hazard ratios versus Class 1 were 1.87 (95% CI 1.25-2.79) for Class 2 and 1.73 (1.31-2.29) for Class 3. The training-selected Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) achieved an AUROC of 0.734 (95% CI 0.695-0.773), a calibration slope of 0.894, and an O/E ratio of 1.015 in the internal test set. In the Qinghai external validation cohort, the AUROC was 0.624 (95% CI 0.559-0.689), the calibration slope was 0.459, and the O/E ratio was 1.920. Adding trajectory class to a model already containing routine clinical and static renal variables changed the AUROC by 0.003 in the internal test set (p = 0.515) and -0.014 in the Qinghai external validation cohort (p = 0.130), without a clear gain in discrimination. BUN/Cr trajectories were associated with post-landmark mortality and summarized the three-day renal course. Training-selected LightGBM showed moderate internal discrimination and underwent frozen external evaluation. Trajectory class added modest information beyond routine clinical and static renal variables, while the combined approach provides an interpretable framework for 72-h reassessment.

42885258.title: Key Predictors of Cerebral Vasospasm Following Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42885258.abstract: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a life-threatening condition often leading to complications such as cerebral vasospasm, which causes delayed cerebral ischemia and increases mortality. In intensive care, early identification of vasospasm risk factors by nurses is essential for timely intervention and improved outcomes. We sought to review and synthesize evidence on risk factors associated with cerebral vasospasm after SAH and inform early risk assessment and nursing care strategies in intensive care. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies. A comprehensive search was conducted on August 30 to 31, 2024, across 8 databases. Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist and the Risk of Bias (RoB 2.0) tool. Thirty-eight studies were included in the systematic review, of which 27 were included in the meta-analysis, involving 19 033 patients. Clinical severity measures were most strongly associated with cerebral vasospasm, including Modified Fisher grade (odds ratio (OR) = 2.88; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.04-4.07), Fisher grade (OR = 2.27; 95% CI, 1.91-2.69), and hemodynamic status (OR = 2.56; 95% CI, 1.17-5.59). Aneurysm-related factors and comorbid conditions were associated with increased risk of cerebral vasospasm, whereas clinical biomarkers and inflammatory markers showed relatively smaller effect sizes. Clinical severity scales and hemodynamic status are the strongest predictors of cerebral vasospasm following SAH. These findings support early risk stratification and the implementation of structured monitoring strategies to improve patient outcomes.PROSPERO trial registration number:CRD42024605605 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024605605).

42934942.title: Next-Generation Immunotherapies for Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Monoclonal Antibodies and Immune Checkpoint Modulation.
42934942.journal: APMIS : acta pathologica, microbiologica, et immunologica Scandinavica
42934942.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa represents a critical healthcare challenge, accounting for 7%-10% of hospital-acquired infections globally, with particularly high prevalence in intensive care, burn, and respiratory units, alongside escalating rates of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant strains. The bacterium evades host immunity through multiple mechanisms, including Type III Secretion System effector translocation and biofilm formation via polysaccharide matrices (alginate, Psl, Pel). Antibiotic-based therapies are increasingly ineffective, necessitating host-directed immunotherapeutic strategies. This review synthesizes emerging evidence on monoclonal antibody therapy and immune checkpoint modulation for P. aeruginosa infections. Bispecific antibodies targeting PcrV and Psl enhance opsonophagocytic killing and biofilm disruption through Fc-mediated mechanisms. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1/PD-L1) reverse T-cell exhaustion from chronic antigen exposure and LPS-driven upregulation of inhibitory receptors, restoring antimicrobial function. Combination approaches integrating mAbs with antibiotics and checkpoint blockade show potential for synergistic bacterial clearance in preclinical pneumonia and burn wound models. Clinical translation remains limited by antigen variability (Psl and PcrV epitope polymorphisms), biofilm heterogeneity, and host immunogenetic diversity (Fc receptor polymorphisms, HLA variants, cytokine profiles). Multi-omics profiling may enable personalized treatment selection. Safety concerns regarding immune hyperactivation require carefully dosed, biomarker-guided strategies. Future development demands genomic stratification of responders and optimized therapeutic windows for maximal clinical benefit.

42907148.title: Injury Epidemiology in Emergency Departments in Tbilisi, Republic of Georgia: A Multicenter Study.
42907148.abstract: Injuries are a major cause of mortality, disability, and economic loss worldwide, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries. In the Republic of Georgia, limited emergency department-level data constrain evidence-based injury prevention and trauma care planning. This study aimed to describe the epidemiological profile of injuries presenting to hospital emergency departments. A retrospective observational study was conducted using data extracted from hospital electronic medical records and organized into a predefined injury registry dataset from selected tertiary, multi-profile hospitals in Tbilisi, Republic of Georgia. All patients presenting with acute physical injuries or acute poisoning/toxic exposure were included. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable binary logistic regression were applied. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. A total of 12,563 patients were analyzed; 67.0% were male, the mean age was 24.5 years (SD 15.3), and the median age was 21 years (IQR 16-29). Individuals aged 17-65 years accounted for 51% of cases. Falls were the leading injury mechanism (47%), followed by road traffic injuries (16%). Contusions (18%) and fractures (16.3%) were the most common injury types, with upper extremities (28%) and head injuries (24%) most frequently affected. Most injuries occurred at home (40%). Nearly 80% of patients were discharged within 24 hours, while 20.1% required hospitalization or intensive care. Road traffic injuries were independently associated with higher odds of hospital-level care. Overall, emergency department mortality was 0.6%. Injury-related emergency department presentations in tertiary hospitals in Tbilisi, Republic of Georgia, primarily affected young and working-age populations, placing substantial demands on emergency care. Targeted prevention, improved road and home safety, strengthened emergency medical services, and a national injury surveillance system are urgently needed.

42878969.title: Esophageal resonance Raman spectroscopy tracks mixed venous oxygenation in experimental shock and hypoxemia.
42878969.abstract: Mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) reflects the balance between systemic oxygen delivery and consumption and is widely used as an indicator of tissue oxygenation in critically ill patients. However, its measurement requires invasive venous access. We evaluated whether a customized probe applied to the esophageal mucosa could provide a continuous measurement of regional capillary hemoglobin oxygen saturation (SEsO2) that tracks changes in mixed venous oxygen saturation for early detection of experimental shock with minimal invasiveness. A miniaturized 405 nm resonance Raman spectroscopy (RRS) probe was developed to quantify esophageal regional capillary hemoglobin saturation (SEsO2) based on spectral decomposition of oxy- and deoxy-hemoglobin Raman peaks. Two rat models were investigated: progressive hemorrhage (n = 12) and graded hypoxia (n = 9). At each stage, SvO2, SEsO2, arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2), and serum lactate were measured. Tracking ability and diagnostic accuracy compared to SvO2 and transabdominal near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models (animal random intercepts), (cluster-bootstrapped) receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analyses, and Pearson correlation. In both models, baseline SEsO2 was ~20% higher than SvO2, consistent with a regional capillary measurement distinct from mixed venous blood. In hemorrhage, LME showed SEsO2 was positively associated with SvO2 (β = 0.53, 95% CI 0.43-0.62; p < 0.0001) and inversely associated with lactate (β = -0.15, 95% CI -0.18 to -0.12; p < 0.0001). In ROC analysis, SEsO2 discriminated SvO2 < 40% with AUC 0.98 (95% CI 0.95-1.00). For transabdominal NIRS, the AUC was 0.82 (95% CI 0.70-0.95). During graded hypoxia, SEsO2 was also positively associated with SvO2 (β = 0.51, 95% CI 0.43-0.60; p < 0.0001) and inversely associated with lactate (β = -0.11, 95% CI -0.13 to -0.09; p < 0.0001). Discrimination of SEsO2 for SvO2 < 40% was AUC 0.92 (95% CI 0.82-1.00). Transabdominal NIRS demonstrated discrimination with high uncertainty (AUC 0.56, 95% CI 0.23-1.00). Esophageal RRS enables molecularly specific measurement of regional capillary hemoglobin oxygen saturation and thereby tracks SvO2 across distinct experimental shock paradigms. These preclinical findings support further investigation of esophageal RRS as a potential minimally invasive monitoring approach for detection of systemic oxygen imbalance.

42874521.title: Burn injury management by Dutch physician-staffed HEMS: Findings from the HEMS-BURNS cohort and National Trauma Registry.
42874521.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42874521.abstract: Dutch Physician staffed Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (P-HEMS) are regularly dispatched to provide care to patients with burns on scene. It is unclear if and which patients with burns benefit from P-HEMS care. This study aimed to investigate P-HEMS dispatch and cancellation rates, intervention rates, and patient outcomes in burn care. This was a descriptive retrospective cohort study. Databases of the Rotterdam P-HEMS and the Dutch National Trauma Registry (NTR) were consulted for burn cases between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2023. Data on cancellation, patient characteristics, burn severity and type, prehospital treatment, transportation, treatment times, and mortality were collected and analyzed. Rotterdam P-HEMS was dispatched 976 times for suspected burn injuries, with 455 (46.6%) dispatches being cancelled, mainly due to minor injuries (n = 288; 63.3%). Of 521 non-cancelled dispatches, most involved adults (n = 345; 66.2%) and flame burns (n = 248; 59.6%), while pediatric patients mostly had scald burns (n = 123; 81.5%). P-HEMS specific interventions were performed in 33.6% of non-cancelled dispatches, with a significantly lower rate in children than in adults (14.2% vs 43.5%; p < 0.001) and a significantly lower rate for scald burns than for flame burns (14.6% vs 45.6%; p < 0.001).
