Of 879 patients with burns with HEMS involvement recorded in the NTR, median Injury Severity Score (ISS) was 9 (P25-P75 1-25), median hospital length of stay (HLOS) was 5 days (P25-P75 2-21 days), ICU admission occurred in 465 of 879 cases (52.9%), and in-hospital mortality was 13.7% (n = 120). This retrospective cohort study found that 46.6% of P-HEMS dispatches for patients with burns were cancelled, often due to minor injuries. P-HEMS-specific interventions were performed in 33.6% of non-cancelled dispatches. These findings suggest a need to optimize dispatch criteria to reduce overtriage and improve efficiency of P-HEMS dispatch for burn care.

42868685.title: Clinical value of enteral nutrition combined with supplemental parenteral nutrition in patients with major burns: A retrospective cohort study.
42868685.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42868685.abstract: The hypermetabolic state following major burns frequently leads to severe negative energy balance, posing significant challenges to clinical nutritional management. This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate clinical outcomes associated with enteral nutrition (EN) combined with supplemental parenteral nutrition (SPN) compared with an EN strategy in real-world clinical settings. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from patients with major burns admitted to the burn unit of a tertiary hospital between January 2018 and December 2023. Group allocation was performed retrospectively according to actual parenteral nutrition (PN) contribution to total delivered calories during Days 1-14: patients with < 10% PN contribution were classified into the EN group and those with ≥ 10% were classified into the EN + SPN group. The primary outcome was time to complete wound healing (defined as ≥95% re-epithelialization). Key secondary outcomes included caloric achievement, prealbumin, nitrogen balance, ICU length of stay, catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI), hyperglycemia, and 28-day and 60-day mortality. A total of 186 patients were included (EN+SPN, n = 94; EN, n = 92). The primary outcome, time to complete wound healing, was significantly shorter in the EN + SPN group (32.4 ± 8.7 vs. 41.2 ± 11.3 days, P < 0.001). The EN + SPN group achieved a higher proportion of target calories (87.3% vs. 62.8%, P < 0.001) and showed higher day-14 prealbumin concentrations (196.8 ± 38.4 vs. 158.2 ± 34.1 mg/L, P < 0.001) and improved day-7 nitrogen balance (-1.2 ± 2.8 vs. -6.8 ± 3.4 g/day, P < 0.001). ICU length of stay was shorter (21.4 ± 8.6 vs. 28.2 ± 10.4 days, P < 0.001). Rates of CRBSI (6.4% vs. 4.3%, P = 0.529) and hyperglycemia (33.0% vs. 28.3%, P = 0.485) did not differ significantly. Neither 28-day nor 60-day mortality differed significantly between groups. In patients with major burns, when EN failed to meet target caloric requirements, EN combined with SPN was associated with improved energy delivery, favorable biochemical trajectories, and shorter wound healing time, without an increased association with infection risk. An EN-first burn care pathway with SPN added when EN remains inadequate warrants prospective evaluation.

42868679.title: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in burn patients: A 12-year retrospective cohort study in the era of "trauma dosing" low molecular weight heparin.
42868679.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42868679.abstract: Venous thromboembolism is a recognized complication of burn injury, yet the contemporary incidence in the setting of routine pharmacologic prophylaxis remains uncertain. We conducted a twelve-year retrospective cohort study of adult patients admitted to a single academic burn center between 2012 and 2023. The primary outcome was clinically significant venous thromboembolism, defined as pulmonary embolism or deep vein thrombosis above the popliteal vein confirmed by imaging. Univariable and multivariable logistic regressions were performed to identify factors associated with venous thromboembolism. A total of 1056 patients met inclusion criteria. The mean age was 54.7 years, and the mean total body surface area (TBSA) burned was 8.1%. Nineteen patients developed clinically significant venous thromboembolism, corresponding to an overall incidence of 1.8%. Incidence increased stepwise with burn severity, reaching 7.4% among patients with greater than 20% TBSA. Increasing age (1.01, 1.00-1.06) and intensive care unit length of stay (1.02, 1.00-1.03) were independently associated with venous thromboembolism on multivariable analysis. Over the study period, venous thromboembolism incidence decreased, alongside an increase in institutional use of low molecular weight heparin; however, this decline was not statistically significant. In a modern burn population receiving near-universal pharmacologic prophylaxis, the incidence of clinically significant venous thromboembolism was low. These findings support consistent prophylaxis in hospitalized burn patients while highlighting the need for prospective studies to refine risk stratification and dosing strategies.

42863436.title: Palliative, end-of-life care for the burn-injured patient.
42863436.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42863436.abstract: This review seeks to describe end-of-life trajectories in burns patients, and a holistic approach to care which encompasses the patient, the family and the health care professionals who care for them. It includes relevant considerations in determining the indications for end-of-life care rather than active treatment aimed at cure. Care for the dying burns patient is described in emergency department, intensive care and ward settings. Inclusive communication to ensure appropriate and consensus-based decision-making which is supported by the treating team, patient and family is paramount in developing a shared understanding of the aims of required interventions. Checklists and guidelines support these aims, and examples are provided, along with details of practical challenges in care delivery. The importance of an established pathway to offer organ donation to burns patients with unsurvivable injuries is highlighted, and outcomes from our institution are reported.

42859360.title: Floating knee injuries: a retrospective analysis of treatment outcomes and prognostic factors.
42859360.abstract: Floating knee injury is a rare high-energy trauma pattern frequently associated with concomitant organ injuries. Optimal treatment timing and the role of external fixation remain subjects of ongoing debate. Twenty-one patients who underwent surgery for ipsilateral femoral and tibial fractures were retrospectively reviewed. Fractures were classified using the Fraser and Gustilo-Anderson systems. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Karlström-Olerud criteria. The mean age was 31 ± 12.1 years; 85% of patients were male. The mean follow-up was 66.6 months. The most common injury mechanism was motorcycle accident (71.4%). According to Karlström criteria, 76.1% of patients achieved excellent or good functional outcomes. External fixation was associated with significantly longer total hospital stay (p = 0.003) and higher superficial infection rates (60.0% vs. 6.3%, p = 0.028) however, this likely reflects greater initial injury severity in patients selected for this approach rather than a direct effect of the device. Patients requiring postoperative ICU admission had significantly higher complication rates (75% vs. 23.1%, p = 0.032). The Injury Severity Score (ISS) correlated significantly with operative time (rs = 0.549, p = 0.010). Delayed definitive surgery was associated with longer total hospital stay (rs = 0.492, p = 0.024) but had no effect on functional outcomes or complication rates. Fraser classification and Gustilo-Anderson grade did not significantly influence functional outcomes. Floating knee injuries carry significant morbidity despite favourable functional outcomes in the majority of patients. External fixation prolongs hospitalisation and increases infection risk, highlighting the importance of early conversion to definitive fixation in eligible patients. Postoperative ICU admission may serve as a useful indicator for heightened complication risk.

42857744.title: Successful conservative management of high-grade renal injury in a polytrauma patient: a rare case report.
42857744.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
42857744.abstract: Simultaneous high-grade renal and splenic trauma is rare and challenges the limits of non-operative management (NOM). High-grade renal injuries with collecting-system extravasation, especially when associated with severe splenic laceration, represent scenarios in which clinical decisions must rely primarily on physiologic stability rather than injury grade alone. An 18-year-old hemodynamically stable male presented 4 hours after a bicycle fall onto his left flank, with severe flank pain and gross hematuria. Computed tomography (CT) imaging revealed AAST Grade IV renal trauma with collecting-system involvement, together with concurrent Grade IV splenic laceration and associated nondisplaced rib fractures. The patient was managed with close ICU observation, multimodal analgesia, and serial monitoring. Diagnostic laparoscopy excluded ongoing intraperitoneal bleeding. A left double-J ureteric stent and intraperitoneal drain were placed for urinary diversion and controlled drainage. No nephrectomy, splenectomy, or splenic artery embolization was required. The patient improved steadily and was discharged in stable condition. Serial imaging demonstrated resolution of the perinephric hematoma and identified a nonenhancing, infarcted lower renal pole with preserved global renal function. Mild hydronephrosis, present while the stent was in place, resolved completely following elective removal. This case aligns with current NOM principles, showing that stability-guided conservative strategies with targeted minimally invasive interventions can safely preserve organs even in combined high-grade solid-organ injuries. Structured NOM involving ICU surveillance, temporary urinary diversion, selective minimally invasive procedures, and coordinated multidisciplinary care successfully preserved both renal and splenic function in this combined high-grade trauma case. The outcome supports stability-based decision-making over routine operative intervention and reinforces the safety and effectiveness of individualized conservative pathways in complex blunt abdominal trauma.

42857302.title: Spatial frequency domain assessment of burns in a clinical setting: a comparison of a research-grade and a commercial imager at the UCI Regional Burn Center.
42857302.journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
42857302.abstract: Accurate assessment of burn wounds is critical for determining optimal patient care. The current standard of bedside visual and tactile examination is subjective and has poor accuracy, even when performed by skilled clinicians. Imaging technologies offer more accurate burn classification and have the potential to be used by personnel with less burn-centric training. This study evaluates the performance of two spatial frequency domain imaging (SFDI) systems in a burn intensive care unit (ICU) to classify burn wounds and identify key measurement parameters for future device development. Subjects (N=24) at the University of California, Irvine (UCI) Regional Burn Center were imaged under an IRB protocol using the OxImager RS (research device) and Clarifi RS (clinical device). We present side-by-side comparisons of device performance metrics, including optical property maps across a range of burn severities, to determine optimal SFDI parameters for clinical assessment. Results indicate that while the research-grade system provides a higher resolution of spectral and spatial data, the streamlined clinical system offers significant advantages in acquisition speed and resistance to motion artifacts and ambient light in the ICU environment.

42852424.title: Is Sarcopenia Associated with Worse Postoperative Outcomes following Emergency Laparotomy? A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
42852424.journal: Journal of emergencies, trauma, and shock
42852424.abstract: The association between sarcopenia and many postoperative outcomes is not well-established. This meta-analysis aims to clarify the potential of sarcopenia to predict these postoperative outcomes. A search of PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAK databases was performed until November 2023 in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Studies that met the inclusion criteria were extracted and their quality assessment was done using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The pooled analysis was done using a random-effects model with dichotomous outcomes expressed as odds ratio (OR) and continuous as weighted mean differences with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Seventeen studies met the inclusion criteria with a total of 5879 patients, with 1690 diagnosed with sarcopenia. Sarcopenia was shown to be significantly associated with increased risk of inpatient mortality (OR = 5.18, 95% CI: 1.04-25.68; P = 0.04), 30-day mortality (OR = 3.32, 95% CI: 2.02-5.46; P < 0.00001), 90-day mortality (OR = 4.24, 95% CI: 1.19-15.12; P = 0.03) and 1-year mortality (OR = 2.53, 95% CI: 1.25-5.12; P = 0.01). Sarcopenic was also associated with an increased risk of severe complications, cardiac complications, pulmonary complications, renal complications, postoperative infections, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay and the risk of unfavorable discharge. There was no significant association between sarcopenia and risk of leakage. Our meta-analysis provided insights into sarcopenia and postoperative outcomes of emergency surgeries. We demonstrated the significant association between the presence of sarcopenia and the presentation of postoperative adverse outcomes and markers of worsened quality of recovery.

42847938.title: A Case of Hemorrhagic Shock Due to Abdominal Hemorrhage in Hemophilia A: The Role of Laboratory Medicine in Multidisciplinary Team.
42847938.abstract: Spontaneous abdominal hemorrhage due to hemophilia A is one of the most lethal complications, progressing rapidly and potentially leading to hemorrhagic shock or death. We report a case of a 38-year-old male patient with hemophilia A who presented with massive spontaneous abdominal hemorrhage, leading to a large hematoma and severe hemorrhagic shock. Upon admission, the patient showed unstable vital signs and a significant decline in hemoglobin levels, indicating an extremely perilous condition that required immediate multidisciplinary collaborative intervention. A multidisciplinary team was assembled, including specialists from emergency medicine, intensive care, hematology, cardiothoracic surgery, laboratory medicine, and radiology. The team quickly diagnosed active abdominal hemorrhage and performed successful catheter-directed arterial embolization. Despite ongoing hemoglobin decline after the procedure, the multidisciplinary team employed targeted laboratory monitoring and assessments to identify underlying causes and adjust coagulation factor replacement and transfusion strategies, effectively stabilizing hemoglobin levels. During recovery, the patient developed progressive jaundice, which was determined to be due to the absorption of the large hematoma, thus preventing unnecessary invasive procedures. This case underscores the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in managing complex critical conditions and highlights the vital role of laboratory medicine in accurate diagnosis, decision-making, and management of complications.

42839760.title: Open Fractures in Polytrauma and Non-Polytrauma Patients: Outcomes and Predictive Factors in a Level III Trauma Center.
42839760.journal: Acta chirurgiae orthopaedicae et traumatologiae Cechoslovaca
42839760.abstract: Open fractures represent complex injuries characterized by bone exposure, soft-tissue damage, and a high risk of infection, often requiring multidisciplinary management. In polytraumatized patients, these injuries further increase clinical complexity and hospital resource utilization. The purpose of this study was to evaluate adherence to international guidelines in the management of open fractures at a third-level trauma center and to identify clinical and organizational predictors of outcomes, complications, and hospitalization burden in polytraumatized and non-polytraumatized patients. A retrospective, single-center study was conducted including all patients treated for open fractures between January 2020 and December 2023. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, fracture location, Gustilo-Anderson grade, surgical timing, treatment strategy (Early Total Care or Damage Control Orthopedics), ICU admission, complications, and readmissions were collected. Polytrauma status was recorded. Primary outcomes included infection rate, length of hospital stay, number of admissions, and cumulative hospitalization time. Statistical analysis was performed using Student's t-test, Fisher's exact test, and Pearson correlation, with significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 115 patients were included, of whom 53 (46.1%) were polytraumatized. The mean age was 47.1 years, with a male predominance. Lower-limb fractures were most common, particularly involving the tibia. Grade III injuries accounted for 61.7% of cases. Surgical debridement was performed within 6 hours in 65.2% of patients. External fixation for damage control was used in 73% of cases, with a mean fixation duration of 103 days. Postoperative ICU admission was required in 27.8% of patients. Overall infection rate was 15.7%. Polytraumatized patients experienced significantly longer hospital stays and a higher number of readmissions, but polytrauma status was not associated with increased infection risk. Higher Gustilo-Anderson grade showed a strong correlation with prolonged hospitalization and infection. Damage control strategies were associated with longer cumulative hospitalization and more frequent readmissions but not with higher infection rates. These findings indicate that fracture severity and local tissue damage, rather than polytrauma status itself, are the main determinants of infection risk and hospitalization burden. While polytrauma increases overall resource utilization, standardized multidisciplinary management allows comparable orthopedic outcomes. Damage control orthopedics remains essential in severe cases but implies longer and more fragmented care pathways. In a high-volume trauma center adhering to international guidelines, open fracture outcomes are primarily driven by injury severity. Polytrauma influences hospitalization burden but not infection risk. Awareness of these factors is essential for optimizing trauma pathways, resource allocation, and patient counseling.

42949254.title: What do we know about expressive writing interventions in helping professions? A focused bibliometric review.
42949254.abstract: Expressive writing is widely studied as a psychological intervention supporting emotional processing and well-being, but research involving helping professionals remains limited. This bibliometric study traces the development of scientific production in this area and maps its conceptual structure. A Scopus search identified 167 records, of which 20 documents published between 2009 and 2026 were retained after a PRISMA-based screening. The analysis reveals a small, recently expanding field, with continuous annual publication only since 2021 and output concentrated among a few authors, research groups, journals, and countries, particularly Italy. Its conceptual structure centers on emotional processing and psychological and occupational adjustment, linking burnout, compassion fatigue, coping, job satisfaction, and well-being across palliative care, intensive care, and pandemic-related healthcare contexts. Overall, the field remains context-bound and unevenly developed, highlighting the need for stronger methodological consistency, broader professional and cultural representation, and greater attention to organizational conditions, implementation, and cross-context comparability.

42948796.title: Prehospital damage-control amputation and packed red blood cell transfusion for severe bilateral lower-limb crush injury in a remote setting: a case report.
42948796.abstract: Prehospital damage-control amputation in civilian emergency systems is rare, especially combined with prehospital packed red blood cell transfusion. We report a 30-year-old man with bilateral lower-limb crush injury after entrapment in an industrial roller machine in a remote area. Despite initially preserved blood pressure, he developed marked hemodynamic deterioration and arrived at the hospital with a blood pressure of 74/49 mmHg. Both limbs were non-salvageable. Prehospital bilateral amputation with vascular ligation was performed on scene, followed by transfusion of one local unit of packed red blood cells (~200 ml). He survived after stump revision, intensive care, and rehabilitation. This case describes the sequential use of prehospital hemorrhage control and packed red blood cell transfusion during the same prehospital episode in a patient with a life-threatening entrapment injury and delayed transport.

42935120.title: Work-Family Balance and Presenteeism-Related Productivity Loss in Emergency Nurses: Cross-Sectional Indirect Associations Through Burnout Dimensions and Fatigue.
42935120.abstract: To estimate associations of work-family balance with presenteeism-related productivity loss and to examine cross-sectional statistical indirect associations through the three MBI-HSS burnout dimensions and fatigue among emergency nurses. Emergency nursing combines time-critical care, rotating schedules, and emotional demands. The MBI-HSS defines emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and personal accomplishment as distinct dimensions; a single composite can conceal different associations. We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of deidentified baseline data from 3597 emergency nurses in the Chinese Nurses' Health Cohort (TARGET). The three MBI-HSS dimensions were scored separately and entered simultaneously. Pearson correlations, hierarchical linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors, a joint Wald test, and a generalized indirect-association model with 5000 bootstrap resamples were used. Work-family balance correlated inversely with productivity loss (r = -0.399). The three burnout dimensions were jointly associated with productivity loss (HC3 Wald F = 99.77, p < 0.001). The adjusted total association was B = -0.307 (95% bootstrap CI -0.328 to -0.285), and the association conditional on the three dimensions and fatigue was B = -0.163 (95% bootstrap CI -0.191 to -0.137). The total statistical indirect association was -0.1435 (95% bootstrap CI -0.1621 to -0.1257), representing 46.8% of the total association. The combined dimension-only component was -0.0890 (29.0%), the fatigue-only component was -0.0338 (11.0%), and the combined serial component through a burnout dimension followed by fatigue was -0.0206 (6.7%). Better work-family balance was associated with less presenteeism-related productivity loss. Emotional exhaustion accounted for the largest dimension-specific indirect component; depersonalization was smaller, and the personal-accomplishment component operated in the opposite direction. These cross-sectional decompositions do not establish temporal mediation or causation. The findings support prospective evaluation of scheduling predictability, recovery time, staffing adequacy, and family-supportive supervision as organizational strategies. They do not establish intervention effectiveness.

42919688.title: Growth and burnout in NICU nurses after experiencing adverse event trauma: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
42919688.abstract: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the association between posttraumatic growth (PTG) and occupational burnout among neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) nurses. This multicenter cross-sectional study (February-April 2026) enrolled 660 registered NICU nurses across 18 Chinese provinces. PTG was quantified using the Posttraumatic Growth Inventory (PTGI; 0-100), and burnout was assessed via the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS; 0-132). Multivariable linear regression, smooth curve fitting, and two-piecewise linear regression characterized the exposure-outcome relationship, adjusting for demographic, workload, and event-specific covariates. After multivariable adjustment, PTG exhibited a significant inverse association with burnout (adjusted β = -0.42; 95% CI: -0.48 to -0.35). Threshold analysis identified an inflection point at a PTGI score of 46; below this threshold, PTG was not significantly associated with burnout (β = 0.13; P = 0.16). At or above 46 points, each 1-point increase in PTGI score was associated with a 0.60-point lower burnout score (adjusted β = -0.60; 95% CI: -0.69 to -0.52), with a slope 43% steeper than the conventional linear estimate. PTG was associated with lower burnout scores in a threshold-dependent pattern among NICU nurses. The 46-point PTGI score should be considered provisional and requires longitudinal and interventional validation before clinical use.

42908349.title: Invasive fungal diseases in immunocompetent adults: emerging patterns and clinical challenges.
42908349.abstract: Invasive fungal diseases (IFDs) have traditionally been regarded as complications of classical immunosuppression. However, IFDs are increasingly recognized in adults who are apparently immunocompetent or non-neutropenic, particularly in the setting of severe viral pneumonia, critical illness, diabetes, structural lung disease, surgery, trauma or burns, injection or inhalational drug use, invasive devices, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and previously unrecognized immune dysregulation. This narrative review summarizes emerging patterns and clinical challenges of IFD in apparently immunocompetent adults, integrating invasive molds, endemic dimorphic fungi, and invasive yeasts. The current landscape includes influenza- and COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis, COVID-19-associated mucormycosis, acute invasive mold disease in critically ill patients, tissue-injury- and trauma-associated mold infections, severe endemic mycoses after relevant environmental exposure, and an expanding spectrum of invasive yeasts. The label "immunocompetent" often conceals situational immune dysfunction or an undiagnosed inborn or acquired immune defect. Cohort data are available for several non-classical host groups, whereas evidence for truly healthy adults remains dominated by small series and case reports. In adults without classical immunosuppression, IFD should be suspected when clinical deterioration occurs in the setting of acute illness, disruption of skin or mucosal barriers, indwelling catheters, healthcare exposure, unusual clinical syndromes, relevant geographic exposure, or unrecognized immune defects.

42898422.title: Prevalence and predictors of burnout among Chinese medical postgraduates: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
42898422.abstract: Burnout is a vital concern in healthcare and causes multiple adverse outcomes. This study explored the prevalence of burnout among Chinese medical postgraduates and its associated factors. This cross-sectional study was conducted among medical postgraduates at 15 teaching hospitals across eight cities in Anhui Province, China. Structured questionnaires were administered to collect data on sociodemographic characteristics, occupational exposures, occupational safety factors, anxiety symptoms, and burnout. Multivariate linear regression analysis was applied to identify the predictors of burnout. A total of 1,276 full-time medical postgraduates were included, with a mean age of 26.68 ± 2.65 years and females accounting for 57.29%. Overall, 30.02% of participants reported no burnout, 32.68% mild, 20.22% moderate, and 17.07% severe burnout. In the fully adjusted model, academic postgraduate and strict compliance with standard operating procedures were independently associated with reduced emotional exhaustion; anesthesiology specialty, a history of sharp injury within the past year, concern about occupational exposure, and anxiety symptoms predicted greater emotional exhaustion. Academic postgraduate, pursuing a doctoral degree, intensive care/emergency medicine specialty, strict compliance with standard operating procedures, hospital pre-training safety education, and adequate access to personal protective equipment independently predicted lower depersonalization; surgery and anesthesiology specialties and anxiety symptoms were linked to greater depersonalization. Advanced age and university occupational safety education were independently associated with lower levels of reduced personal accomplishment; anxiety symptoms were significantly correlated with higher levels of reduced personal accomplishment. The cross-sectional design only allows assessment of associations rather than causal relationships; reliance on self-reported questionnaires may introduce response bias and social desirability effects; and the sample recruited solely from Anhui Province limits the generalizability of the findings to other regions. These findings provide targeted insights for developing effective intervention strategies to alleviate burnout and improve the quality of clinical training.

42895566.title: Emergency surgery for blunt abdominal trauma in polytrauma - the impact of time to laparotomy on outcomes.
42895566.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
42895566.abstract: Blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) is common in polytrauma patients. Emergency surgery is required for haemodynamically significant solid organ injury and intra-abdominal hollow organ injury. The effect of time to surgery on outcomes in patients requiring emergency laparotomy remains uncertain. Adult polytrauma patients (ISS > 16) who underwent emergency laparotomy for blunt abdominal trauma between 1996 and 2020 from a trauma registry of a single level one trauma centre were included. Patients were divided into two groups based on the time elapsed from admission to emergency laparotomy: "Super Early" (≤ 60 min) and "Early" (60-180 min). Length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU)-LOS, ventilation time, re-look operations and mortality were assessed. Adjusted logistic regression was used to determine the independent predictive parameters, including timing of surgery, for mortality. The study included 190 polytrauma patients with concomitant blunt abdominal trauma (mean age 42 years (± 17), median ISS of 36 (IQR: 19)). There were 95 patients in each group. Patients in the "Super Early" group had a compromised haemodynamic status and a higher ISS. Liver injury and serous membrane injury were more common in the super early group. The mortality rate was significantly higher in the "Super Early" group (51.6%) compared to the "Early" group (26.3%) (p < 0.001). Death due to haemorrhagic shock was significantly more frequent in the "Super Early" group (36.8%) compared to the "Early" group (13.7%) (p < 0.001). A regression model was adjusted to determine the independent predictors of mortality. Time to emergency laparotomy was not an independent predictor of mortality. However, increased ISS (OR = 1.04, p = 0.049), age (OR = 1.03, p = 0.037) and decreased systolic blood pressure (OR = 0.98, p = 0.025) were found to be significant predictors of mortality. The timing of surgery showed no independent association with mortality as long as an emergency laparotomy was performed within 3 h of admission. The data suggests that patient-specific characteristics, injury severity and clinical status are more important for survival than the timing of an early emergency laparotomy. Future research should focus on determining the role of delayed laparotomy on outcomes in specific subgroups of patients.

42893741.title: Injury patterns, in-hospital outcomes, and resource utilization of acute cuboid and navicular fractures.
42893741.journal: The Journal of foot and ankle surgery : official publication of the American College of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
42893741.abstract: Acute cuboid and navicular fractures can be serious injuries. However, multicenter data on their associated injuries and in-hospital course are limited. To characterize the demographics, injury patterns, in-hospital outcomes, and resource utilization of trauma center patients with acute cuboid and/or navicular fractures. Retrospective cross-sectional database study. The American College of Surgeons National Trauma Data Bank (2017-2019) was queried for acute cuboid and/or navicular fractures. Multivariable regression identified factors associated with discharge to post-acute care, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and hospital length of stay in adults. Overall, 3,424 patients with 4,084 fractures were identified (2,327 with cuboid and 1,637 with navicular fractures, including 540 with both). Road-traffic mechanisms accounted for 64.5%, and 25.1% had polytrauma. Metatarsal, calcaneal, and talar fractures were the most common concomitant injuries. Combined fractures were more often ipsilateral than contralateral (457 vs 18 patients). Despite infrequent complications, 50.2% were discharged home without post-acute services (home health, inpatient rehabilitation, or skilled nursing care). In-hospital mortality was 1.1%. After adjustment, polytrauma (OR 3.75, 95% CI 3.04-4.61), bilateral involvement, and ankle, tibia, fibula, or metatarsal fractures were associated with discharge to post-acute care, whereas fracture pattern was not. Cuboid and navicular fractures are predominantly high-energy injuries that rarely occur in isolation. Post-acute care needs, ICU admission, and length of stay were associated with overall injury burden rather than the specific bone fractured.

42881677.title: Burnout and Quality of Life Among Oncology Palliative Care Professionals: An Exploratory Study.
42881677.abstract: Background/Objectives: Oncology palliative care involves sustained engagement with suffering, loss, complex communication, and end-of-life decisions. This exploratory study compared burnout and quality of life among professionals working in oncology palliative care, intensive care, and emergency care, and secondarily with a heterogeneous reference group. Methods: A cross-sectional convenience sample included 68 healthcare professionals from two hospital units within the same Portuguese public hospital organization: oncology palliative care (N = 22), intensive care (N = 15), emergency care (N = 9), and other healthcare professionals (N = 22). Burnout and quality of life were assessed using the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey and WHOQOL-BREF, respectively. Analyses used complete cases for each multivariate outcome set. Results: No statistically significant multivariate differences were detected across the three clinical groups in burnout (Pillai's Trace = 0.187; F(6, 84) = 1.442; p = 0.208) or quality of life (Pillai's Trace = 0.146; F(10, 78) = 0.613; p = 0.798). In the secondary burnout comparison (n = 38), emotional exhaustion was higher in oncology palliative care (mean difference = 5.78; 95% CI 0.37-11.19; unadjusted p = 0.037; partial η2 = 0.115). No multivariate quality-of-life difference was detected in the secondary comparison (n = 39; p = 0.387). Conclusions: The non-significant findings do not establish equivalence between clinical settings. The nominal emotional-exhaustion difference is hypothesis-generating and requires replication. Small, unequal groups, missing data, multiple testing, and limited occupational characterization constrain precision and interpretation.

42964534.title: Individualized Profiles of Burnout and Sensory Processing Sensitivity in Nurses and Their Associations with Mindfulness and Psychological Well-Being.
42964534.abstract: Nurse burnout is a widespread problem associated with adverse outcomes for both patients and healthcare organizations. Despite evidence that burnout risk is heterogeneous, most profiling research has emphasized burnout symptoms and work characteristics rather than individual susceptibility. Sensory processing sensitivity may help explain why similar work demands are experienced differently across nurses. This cross-sectional study included 405 registered nurses working across all units of a tertiary hospital. Participants completed validated self-report measures of burnout, sensory processing sensitivity, mindfulness, and psychological well-being. Latent class analysis was applied to identify profiles based on burnout and sensory sensitivity indicators. Model selection was guided by information criteria and interpretability. Between-class differences in mindfulness and psychological well-being were examined using analysis of covariance adjusted for age and gender, and associations with work-unit context were evaluated using multinomial logistic regression. Three latent profiles were identified, representing low, moderate, and high burnout. Higher-burnout profiles were characterized by greater sensory processing sensitivity and higher burnout levels, alongside lower mindfulness and psychological well-being. Nurses working in inpatient, procedural, critical care, and emergency units were more likely to belong to higher-burnout profiles. Mindfulness and psychological well-being were inversely associated with membership in higher-burnout profiles, independent of demographic factors. Joint modeling of burnout and sensory processing sensitivity revealed distinct and interpretable nurse profiles that reflect differential vulnerability to occupational burnout. These findings point to the combined role of individual sensitivity and work-unit context in burnout and well-being among nurses.

42958192.title: "Caring in a liminal space": a constructivist grounded theory study examining nurses' approach to end-of-life care provision in acute care settings.
42958192.abstract: Emergency Departments (EDs) and Burn Intensive Care Units (BICUs) frequently care for critically ill patients who may require comfort-focused, end-of-life support. Yet palliative care integration in these traditionally non-palliative environments remains limited. This gap raises important questions about how nurses navigate and deliver end-of-life care in acute settings. This study explored the processes underpinning nurses' provision of end-of-life care in the ED and BICU. A constructivist grounded theory approach, informed by Charmaz, guided the study. Initial purposive sampling followed by theoretical sampling was used to recruit nurses with at least six months of experience in either unit. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and document review. Analysis followed the constant comparative method. Twenty-seven nurses participated. The core category, "caring in a liminal space," captured nurses' experiences of navigating an uncertain and often disorienting care environment in which they felt insufficiently prepared to provide end-of-life care. Three interrelated categories explained this core process- (1) journeying through an undesired, fractured space, (2) engaging in active-passive care processes, and (3) carrying concealed professional grief. Across both settings, nurses tended to adopt a vicarious, survival-oriented approach to care, prioritizing life-sustaining interventions even when comfort care was more appropriate. The end-of-life space was described as emotionally and professionally uncomfortable, contributing to a reliance on active clinical tasks rather than comfort-focused care. These findings demonstrate that nurses' end-of-life practices in acute care are shaped less by individual deficits and more by the structural liminality inherent in ED and BICU environments. Strengthening palliative care integration therefore requires system-level reforms such as embedded palliative care teams, supportive organisational cultures, and clearer care pathways alongside targeted education and interdisciplinary collaboration. Such changes are essential to improve the quality of end-of-life care for patients and families and to better support nurses as they navigate the persistent tensions of this liminal space.

42870767.title: Minimally Invasive Hematoma Evacuation for Acute Spontaneous Supratentorial Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential Analysis.
42870767.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a severe form of stroke associated with high morbidity and mortality. While surgical evacuation aims to reduce hematoma burden and improve outcomes, its clinical benefit over medical management remains uncertain. Previous systematic reviews have evaluated a broad range of surgical interventions for ICH; however, evidence specific to MIS remains less clearly defined. Therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the efficacy and safety of minimally invasive hematoma evacuation in patients with acute spontaneous supratentorial ICH. This meta-analysis was performed in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines and Cochrane recommendations. A comprehensive search of MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted from inception to February 2026. We included randomized controlled trials that compared minimally invasive hematoma evacuation with medical or conventional surgical management. Risk ratios (RR) and mean differences (MD) were pooled using a random-effects model. A total of 12 RCTs involving over 2302 patients were included. Minimally invasive hematoma evacuation significantly reduced all-cause mortality (RR = 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.97; p = 0.02) and 6-month mortality (RR = 0.79, 95% CI 0.64-0.96; p = 0.02). No significant differences were observed in 7-day or 30-day mortality, although a trend favoring the intervention was noted. Functional outcomes, including mRS 0-1 and mRS 0-3, did not improve significantly. Among secondary outcomes, minimally invasive approaches were associated with greater hematoma volume reduction (MD = 62.47; p = 0.04) but also a higher risk of rebleeding (RR = 2.37; p = 0.002) and cardiac events (RR = 5.08; p = 0.009). No significant differences were found in ischemic stroke, renal failure, gastrointestinal bleeding, seizures, urinary tract infections, or length of hospital and ICU stay. Minimally invasive hematoma evacuation significantly decreases mortality in patients with spontaneous ICH, especially with endoscopic techniques; however, it does not markedly enhance functional outcomes and may elevate the risk of complications such as rebleeding and cardiac events. These results underscore the necessity for meticulous patient selection and additional high-caliber trials to enhance treatment strategies.

42843110.title: Effect of preoperative video-based digital educational program on incidence of delirium and length of hospital stay following coronary artery bypass grafting: A randomized controlled trial.
42843110.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
42843110.abstract: Postoperative delirium is common after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and is associated with prolonged hospitalization and delayed recovery. Non-pharmacological educational interventions may improve outcomes, but evidence on structured video-based education for delirium prevention remains limited. To evaluate the effect of a preoperative video-based educational program on postoperative delirium incidence and hospital length of stay among patients undergoing CABG surgery. A parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted at Queen Alia Heart Institute, Jordan, between October 2025 and January 2026. Adult patients scheduled for elective first-time CABG surgery were randomized into intervention and control groups. Both groups received standardized multidisciplinary preoperative education through the institutional Preoperative Clinic, while the intervention group additionally received an 8-minute structured Arabic video-based educational program. Postoperative delirium was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU). Among 226 randomized participants, 213 were analyzed (105 intervention; 108 control). Delirium incidence was lower with intervention (7.6%vs 25.0%, p < .001) and remained significantly associated with study group after adjustment (OR = 3.14, 95% CI: 1.08-9.14, p = .036). Hospital stay was shorter in the intervention group unadjusted (8.38 vs 10.58 days, p < .001), but not after adjustment (B = -0.656, p = .182). Preoperative video-based education was associated with lower postoperative delirium incidence, while its association with shorter hospital stay was not maintained after adjustment. Larger multicenter trials are warranted.

42840768.title: Intraoperative Dexmedetomidine and Postoperative Delirium After Head and Neck Cancer Surgery with Free-Flap Reconstruction: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial.
42840768.abstract: Postoperative delirium is common after major head and neck cancer surgery. We investigated whether intraoperative dexmedetomidine infusion was associated with a lower incidence of postoperative delirium in patients undergoing head and neck cancer surgery requiring free-flap reconstruction. This was a delirium-focused secondary analysis of a single-centre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Adult patients with head and neck cancer scheduled for elective surgery requiring free-flap reconstruction under general anaesthesia were randomly assigned to receive intraoperative dexmedetomidine infusion at 0.3 μg kg-1h-1 until 1 h before the end of surgery; subjects in the placebo group were given comparable volumes of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of delirium during the first 5 postoperative days, assessed once daily using the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the 3-Minute Diagnostic Confusion Assessment Method (3D-CAM). There was less delirium during the initial 5 postoperative days in patients assigned to dexmedetomidine (14.9%, 7 of 47 patients) than in those given placebo (34.7%, 17 of 49 patients). Dexmedetomidine was associated with lower odds of postoperative delirium after adjustment for age, preoperative Mini-Mental State Examination score, and operative time (adjusted odds ratio 0.31, 95% confidence interval 0.10-0.92; p = 0.036). Postoperative pain and early sleep outcomes were improved by dexmedetomidine. Haemodynamic adverse events and postoperative complications did not differ significantly between groups. In patients undergoing head and neck cancer surgery with free-flap reconstruction, intraoperative dexmedetomidine infusion was associated with a lower incidence of postoperative delirium during the first 5 postoperative days, without an apparent increase in perioperative adverse events. ChiCTR2300067376.

42922234.title: Learning Curve in Thoracoscopic Mediastinal Mass Excision: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study Using Cumulative Sum and Multivariable Regression Analysis.
42922234.abstract: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) mediastinal mass excision has become the standard approach for anterior mediastinal lesions. Understanding its learning curve is essential for surgical training and quality assurance. The primary objective was to quantify the association between cumulative case experience (case sequence number) and operative time, the primary outcome, using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis and multivariable regression modelling. We tested the null hypothesis that operative time does not change with increasing case sequence after adjustment for patient-, tumour- and country-related factors. Secondary objectives were to estimate the number of cases required to achieve proficiency and to compare perioperative outcomes across learning phases and between participating countries. This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at five academic and tertiary-care centers in Egypt and Saudi Arabia between January 2023 and December 2025. Seventy-seven consecutive patients undergoing VATS excision of mediastinal masses were categorized into three phases: Early (first 20 cases), Intermediate (next 20 cases), and Late (last 37 cases). Cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis was performed. Operative outcomes, including operative time, blood loss, conversion rate, and postoperative complications, were compared across phases and between countries (Egypt vs. Saudi Arabia). Multivariable linear regression and a linear mixed-effects model with participating centre as a random intercept were used to identify factors independently associated with operative time. Mean operative time significantly decreased across phases (189.5 ± 21.9 vs. 156.5 ± 26.4 vs. 139.7 ± 30.5 minutes; p < 0.001). CUSUM analysis demonstrated a learning curve inflection point between cases 20 and 26. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, myasthenia gravis, presence of a discrete mass, thymic neoplasm and country, case sequence number remained independently associated with shorter operative time (β = -1.14 min per case; 95% CI -1.47 to -0.80; p < 0.001; R² = 0.48, adjusted R² = 0.42), with consistent estimates using robust standard errors and a mixed-effects model with centre as a random intercept (β = -1.37; 95% CI -1.80 to -0.95). Patients treated in Saudi Arabia (n = 7) were older and more often had discrete neoplastic masses, but operative time did not differ significantly between countries before (p = 0.128) or after adjustment (p = 0.548). Conversion to open surgery occurred in 3.9% (n = 3), all in the Intermediate and Late phases. Overall mortality was 2.6% (n = 2), both in the Late phase and associated with complex cases. No significant differences were observed regarding ICU stay, hospital stay, or postoperative complications. VATS mediastinal mass excision is safe and feasible, with surgical proficiency achieved after approximately 20-26 cases. Operative time was the most reliable indicator of learning progression, and the learning effect persisted after multivariable adjustment for patient-, tumour- and country-related factors. Structured mentorship and careful case selection are recommended during the early learning phase.

42868047.title: Fibrinolytic Activation and Its Association with Mortality After Traumatic and Thermal Injury.
42868047.abstract: Characterize plasma markers of fibrinolytic activation and their associations with mortality in burn and trauma patients from hospital admission through 48 hours. Fibrinolytic activation following burn and non-burn trauma is associated with increased mortality. Whether fibrinolytic activation differs between burn and non-burn injury is unknown. Adult patients aged 18 years and older who presented to one of two regional trauma centers or one regional burn center within 4 hours of injury were included. Blood was collected at admission and at hours 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36, and 48. Plasmin-antiplasmin complex (PAP), D-dimer, and plasminogen concentrations in plasma were determined. Of 590 patients, 58.3% presented with blunt, 27.1% with thermal, and 14.6% with penetrating injury. Admission PAP and D-dimer were higher in trauma (blunt and penetrating groups combined) than in burn patients (p<.001). Non-survivors (injury types combined) had higher PAP and D-dimer and lower plasminogen (p<.001) at admission and over time. After adjusting for age, injury severity and % total body surface area burned, admission PAP ≥1645.6 ng/mL was associated with 7.0 times higher odds for mortality (p=.002) and D-dimer ≥6.5 µg/mL was associated with 5.0 times higher odds for mortality (p=.01). Changes in biomarkers over time were similar between trauma and burn patients. Higher fibrinolytic activation was associated with mortality in trauma and burn patients. Trauma patients had higher fibrinolytic activation markers than burn patients, while patterns of change were similar. Data suggest potential for use of similar resuscitative adjuncts to mitigate early fibrinolytic dysfunction in trauma and burns.

42867561.title: Bioactive adrenomedullin dynamics and microcirculatory changes in a porcine model of hemorrhagic shock.
42867561.abstract: Hemorrhagic shock is a leading cause of preventable trauma death, marked by impaired oxygen delivery and endothelial dysfunction. Bioactive adrenomedullin (bio-ADM) regulates endothelial barrier integrity, but its dynamics during hemorrhagic shock and resuscitation remain unclear. This secondary analysis of a porcine hemorrhagic shock model investigated bio-ADM and its association with macro- and microcirculatory parameters during resuscitation. All animals received crystalloid infusion (10 mL/kg/h) from anesthesia induction onward. Shock was induced by blood withdrawal to maintain MAP at 40 ± 5 mmHg for 60 min (T5), before randomization to control (n = 7), fluid (n = 6), or noradrenaline (n = 7) groups, with intervention groups titrated to MAP targets of 65 then 90 mmHg (60 min each). Macrocirculation was assessed via vital signs and pulse contour analysis; microcirculation via hyperspectral imaging (tissue oxygenation, hemoglobin, water index). Fluid resuscitation improved macrohemodynamics and microcirculatory oxygenation versus control and noradrenaline, which failed to sustain perfusion and impaired microcirculatory oxygenation. Bio-ADM increased after shock induction (p < 0.001), peaking at T9 (120 min of therapy). At T5, levels were comparable among control (16.8 [13.6-18.9] pg/ml), fluid (15.65 [15.43-16.55] pg/ml), and noradrenaline (14.3 [7.85-18.95] pg/ml). Thereafter, bio-ADM continued to rise in control (19.7 [17.4-32.6] pg/ml) and noradrenaline (21.2 [14.4-33.45] pg/ml), while stabilizing in the fluid group (12.05 [10.65-15.18] pg/ml); accordingly, the T5-T9 increase was smaller in the fluid group than in control (p = 0.022) or noradrenaline (p = 0.003). The fluid group received ~3-fold more fluid by T9. Higher bio-ADM correlated with lower MAP, higher lactate, and lower ScvO₂, but not oxygen delivery (DO₂); a higher tissue water index correlated with a smaller rise. Bio-ADM increased during hemorrhagic shock, extending previous observations from cardiogenic and septic shock, and represents a comparatively non-specific marker of endothelial and microcirculatory stress rather than specific to any single shock etiology. Effective resuscitation was associated with stabilization, rather than a clear decrease, of bio-ADM levels, though this coincided with higher fluid administration, and dilution cannot be excluded. Whether bio-ADM offers therapeutic utility to guide resuscitation remains unclear, warranting further prospective evaluation in animal and human studies.

42844637.title: Palliative and end-of-life care on the battlefield: a scoping review.
42844637.abstract: Modern conflicts have brought about a paradigm shift in military medicine. In Prolonged Field Care, recommendations have so far focused on damage control and care aimed at ensuring survival. But, particularly in large scale combat operation, not all patients will survive, and despite the development of palliative care in the civilian sector, no extension of this approach has yet been envisaged for military medicine. This review aims to identify knowledge gaps in palliative and supportive care in combat situations. We conducted a literature review in PubMed, CAIRN, Scopus and Embase, with the last search carried out on 31 December 2025, using triangulation at each stage of the screening process. Studies published since 1900 focusing on frontline palliative and end-of-life care for combatants were included. Of 3,629 unique records, 35 articles were included, ranging from World War II-era accounts to current prolonged field care guidelines. Pain management was the most extensively documented topic. Morphine, a historical mainstay, has been increasingly supplemented by oral transmucosal fentanyl citrate and ketamine. Ketamine was favored in austere settings for its hemodynamic stability and multi-route administration. Other analgesics, such as paracetamol and NSAIDs, were also briefly described. Regional anesthesia was recognized as an analgesic force multiplier, though never described in an explicitly palliative context. For expectant and dying casualties, a limited but consistent body of literature addressed opioid titration and palliative sedation, notably via continuous midazolam infusion. Diverse end-of-life-related symptoms were addressed, including nausea, dyspnea, secretions, and delirium. Non-pharmacological measures, such as thermal regulation, mouth care, disarming, and comfort items, were described as accessible across provider levels. Spiritual care and family communication, though addressed in few sources, emerged as important but under-formalized components. Overall, evidence specific to palliative and end-of-life battlefield care remains sparse and largely extrapolated from curative-care literature. Pain management in combat is a well-researched field, but one that is rarely examined in the specific context of end-of-life care. Similarly, there is a notable gap in the literature regarding palliative care in a combat context. Where such topics are addressed, they are often simply a transposition of civilian data. The lack of training and doctrinal guidance prevents the proper integration of this specialized care, which aims to ensure dignity for dying combatants and to reflect the values upon which military medicine is founded. The protocol was pre-registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF) on 8 December 2025 (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/U9RSG).

42929369.title: Preliminary Exploration of the Hepatoprotective Effect of Nanocrystalline Curcumin Against Traumatic Hemorrhagic Shock-Induced Liver Injury in a Desert Dry-Heat Environment: A Network Pharmacology-Based Study.
42929369.abstract: Traumatic hemorrhagic shock (THS) under desert dry-heat conditions can exacerbate secondary liver injury, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic interventions. This study investigated the protective effects of nanocrystalline curcumin (NC-Cur) against THS-induced liver injury in a desert dry-heat environment and explored its potential molecular mechanisms. Network pharmacology, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses, and protein-protein interaction network analysis were used to identify candidate targets. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations examined curcumin-protein interactions. Forty male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to control, model, solvent, or NC-Cur treatment groups (n = 10 each). The model, solvent, and treatment groups underwent traumatic hemorrhagic shock under desert dry-heat conditions. Hepatic injury was assessed by histopathology, serum aminotransferases, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress markers, and Western blotting. Network analysis identified 116 overlapping targets, with heat shock protein 90 alpha A1 (HSP90AA1), AKT serine/threonine kinase 1 (AKT1), and B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) prioritized as the core targets. Docking predicted favorable interactions with all three proteins, while molecular dynamics simulations supported stable binding between curcumin and HSP90AA1. Compared with untreated model rats, NC-Cur-treated rats showed attenuated hepatic histopathological injury, reduced alanine and aspartate aminotransferases, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β, and malondialdehyde, and increased superoxide dismutase. Western blotting indicated reduced HSP90AA1 and increased phosphorylated AKT1 expression after NC-Cur treatment, with changes also observed in BCL-2 expression. These findings suggest that NC-Cur may alleviate liver injury associated with THS under desert dry-heat conditions in male rats, potentially involving HSP90AA1-AKT1-BCL-2-related signaling.

42925135.title: Role of Mitochondrial Impairment in Sepsis-Induced Platelet Activation.
42925135.abstract: Sepsis-induced mitochondrial impairment has been described in different organs, in both animal models and humans. Excessive radical oxygen species (ROS) could be involved in this phenomenon. As a result, antioxidants have been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy, although results remain controversial. Platelet hyperactivation is considered a central pathogenic mechanism in the development of sepsis-induced organ damage. In this study, we aimed to determine whether mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to platelet hyperactivation during sepsis. We also evaluated the effect of ROS scavenging using the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO. Laboratory investigation. University Hospital. Patients with sepsis/septic shock (n = 3/7), nonseptic burn patients (n = 10), and healthy control subjects (n = 10). Platelet mitochondria and isolated platelets from healthy donors were treated in vitro with plasma from patients with sepsis/septic shock and healthy subjects, before and after preincubation with MitoTEMPO. We measured platelet oxygen consumption rates in isolated human platelets using the Seahorse Extracellular Flux Analyzer. Platelet mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activity was measured in mitochondria-enriched fractions by spectrophotometry. Platelet aggregation in platelet-rich plasma was analyzed using light-transmission aggregometry, and leukocyte-platelet adhesion in whole blood by flow cytometry.We found that incubating platelets with septic plasma significantly reduced basal, maximal, and adenosine triphosphate-linked oxygen consumption rate. Incubation of platelet mitochondria with septic plasma also reduced platelet Complex I activity, compared with healthy plasma or plasma from nonseptic burn patients. This decrease was associated with an increase in Epinephrine-induced platelet activation. Preincubating platelets with the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO significantly reversed these effects. Our results show that the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO prevents mitochondrial dysfunction and enhances platelet activation induced by septic plasma in human platelets in vitro. This may help in designing new therapeutic approaches to prevent sepsis-induced organ damage mediated by mitochondrial dysfunction and platelet hyperactivation.

42820514.title: Burnout in the intensive care unit: organizational determinants in focus.

42821860.title: Enhancing ICU Nurse Competence: A Systematic Review of Influencing Factors.
42821860.journal: Dimensions of critical care nursing : DCCN
42821860.abstract: ICU nurses work in high-stakes environments where competence, defined as the integration of knowledge, skills, attitudes, values, and experience, is essential for ensuring patient safety, reducing mortality rates, and providing effective critical care. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched critical care and nursing education journals in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and CINAHL from 2015 to June 2025 for qualitative and quantitative studies on ICU nurse competence. The search strategy incorporated terms such as "educational frameworks for critical care education," "critical care nursing orientation," and "competency-based critical care nurse education." JBI tools were used to assess quality, and narrative synthesis was applied. Of the 1800 studies that were identified, 15 were included in the analysis. This analysis involved 2500 ICU nurses from 9 different countries. Competence is multidimensional. Facilitators such as simulation-based learning improve clinical decision-making, and ethical attitudes promote holistic care. Barriers include workloads that cause burnout and post-COVID infection gaps that lead to errors. Competence levels are high for clinical skills but low for research and family-centered care. Novices struggle in complex ICUs. This review suggests that combining the adoption of standardized, competency-based frameworks, particularly the AACN Synergy Model and the 2021 AACN Essentials, with objective, simulation-enhanced assessment tools can effectively address identified gaps and improve the competence of ICU nurses worldwide.

42823008.title: Emergency Burn Resuscitation: Where Evidence Meets Practice.
42823008.journal: Emergency medicine clinics of North America
42823008.abstract: The initial management of a critically ill burn patient sets the trajectory for their entire hospital course. Understanding standards of care is essential, but moving beyond rote formulas for airway management, fluids, and analgesia is critical to ensuring appropriate care and preventing iatrogenic harm. This article provides an evidence-based guide for emergency physicians on when and how to pivot from standard care to nuanced, life-saving interventions that address the dynamic pathophysiology of severe burns.

42969834.title: Evaluation of early hydrocortisone use for hemodynamic shock in adult burn patients with suspected critical illness related corticosteroid insufficiency.
42969834.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
42969834.abstract: Critical illness-related corticosteroid insufficiency (CIRCI) presents as refractory hemodynamic shock in critically ill patients. Research on CIRCI and its treatment in burn patients is limited. We sought to review the use of corticosteroids in a burn population during their first week of hospitalization. The burn registry and the electronic medical records were queried for burn patients admitted between January 2015 and December 2025. The following variables were abstracted: demographics, burn history, hospital course, and treatments. Outcome variables included length of stay (LOS), infections, graft loss, pharmacological treatment, and mortality. The two groups were compared with Student's T-test and Chi Square where appropriate. A multivariant analysis was performed to determine independent predictors of CIRCI, infection and mortality. Significance was determined at p<0.05 level. The study group consisted of 87 patients in hemodynamic shock receiving vasopressors, with 47 also receiving corticosteroids. The corticosteroid group had larger burns (37.6 v 25.1%), more resuscitation (15.9 v 8.1 L), more vasopressor days (6.23 v 3.7 d), more ventilator days (19.72 v 7.83 d), more infections (66% v 34%) and longer LOS (51.53 v 26.05 d), all p<0.05. On multivariant analysis, variables independently related to the diagnosis of CIRCI were age and resuscitation fluids; to infection were corticosteroid use; and to mortality were age. Overall, over 50% of patients in hypotensive shock during their first week of treatment were diagnosed and treated with corticosteroids for suspected CIRCI. More study is needed to determine the appropriate role of corticosteroid use in early burn treatment.

42971065.title: Surgeons' Immediate Postoperative Prediction After Major Emergency Abdominal Surgery.
42971065.abstract: Major emergency abdominal surgery carries high morbidity and mortality, making accurate risk stratification important. Whether surgeons' immediate postoperative clinical judgment predicts outcomes and how it compares with established surgical risk models remains poorly characterized. Prospective single-center cohort of 411 patients undergoing major emergency abdominal surgery (February 2024-June 2025). Immediately after surgery, the operating surgeon estimated 30-d mortality (ordinal 10% intervals) and the risk of complications (0-10 scale). Discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]) and calibration (observed-to-expected ratio, calibration slope and intercept, Brier score) were assessed. Mortality discrimination was compared with National Emergency Laparotomy Audit and Portsmouth Physiological and Operative Severity Score for the enUmeration of Mortality and Morbidity using the DeLong test. Thirty-day mortality was 11% (47/411). Surgeon-estimated risk showed good discrimination for mortality (AUC: 0.89; 95% confidence interval: 0.85-0.94), comparable to National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (0.90) and Portsmouth Physiological and Operative Severity Score for the enUmeration of Mortality and Morbidity (0.86; P = 0.83 and P = 0.30). Surgeons systematically overestimated absolute mortality (mean predicted: 23% versus observed: 11%; observed-to-expected: 0.48; intercept: -1.17; slope: 1.20). For complications, discrimination was good for sepsis/multi-organ failure (AUC 0.81) and acceptable for intensive care unit admission (0.78) and cardiac complications (0.78), but poor for reoperation (0.62) and mechanical bowel obstruction (0.62), and absent for prolonged paralytic bowel dysfunction (0.51). Higher estimated risk was associated with increased odds of complications. Predicted discharge destination agreed moderately with observed (accuracy 74%; weighted κ 0.61). Surgeons' immediate postoperative assessment showed discriminatory performance of a similar magnitude to established models but systematically overestimated absolute risk and performed better for systemic than procedure-specific complications. This bedside estimate may aid early risk stratification but requires external validation before clinical use.

42971011.title: Electrical burn injury and rhabdomyolysis.
42971011.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
42971011.abstract: Electrical burns account for 3-5% of burn admissions, with high morbidity and mortality due to deep muscle injury and systemic complications. Rhabdomyolysis is common and a major contributor to acute kidney injury and death. To review the current evidence on the pathophysiology, systemic complications, diagnosis, and management of electrical burn injuries, with particular emphasis on rhabdomyolysis and its implications for intensive care management. A structured narrative review of the literature on electrical burn injuries was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Scopus, with a focus on rhabdomyolysis and its implications for acute kidney injury. Rhabdomyolysis is a frequent event in patients with electrical burns and represents a major factor in the development of acute kidney injury. Creatine phosphokinase > 5000 IU/L and myoglobinuria are associated with an increased risk of renal complications. Early fluid resuscitation and prompt recognition of compartment syndrome improve outcomes. Evidence does not support routine use of alkalinization or mannitol. Renal replacement therapy should be guided by conventional indications for acute kidney injury, as current evidence does not support its prophylactic initiation. Early identification of rhabdomyolysis and optimization of renal perfusion are critical. An evidence-based practical framework is presented.

42976777.title: Clinical value of a five-predictor nomogram for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after orthopaedic surgery in ICU patients.
42976777.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the predictive value of a five-predictor nomogram for postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in orthopedic patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU).MethodsClinical data from 224 postoperative orthopedic ICU patients admitted between March 2022 and March 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into a DVT group (n = 73) and a non-DVT group (n = 151). Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors, and a predictive nomogram was constructed based on these variables. The performance of the model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.ResultsThe incidence of postoperative DVT was 32.59%. Patients in the DVT group had significantly higher age, D-dimer, prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), and a higher prevalence of diabetes, preoperative heart failure, and postoperative infection compared with the non-DVT group (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified age, diabetes, preoperative heart failure, PT, and APTT as independent risk factors for DVT. The nomogram demonstrated good predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.877. The sensitivity and specificity were 82.47% and 76.68%, respectively.ConclusionThe five-predictor nomogram provides individualized estimates of postoperative DVT probability in orthopedic ICU patients and may support risk stratification and targeted prevention.

42972259.title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio is associated with delirium in elderly cardiac surgery patients in the postoperative intensive care unit: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
42972259.abstract: Postoperative delirium(POD) is severe in elderly cardiac surgery patients.Elevated glucose levels trigger oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and cerebral metabolic disturbances, which are key mechanisms linking dysglycemia to delirium. Current models lack predictors, and dysglycemia interpretation is confounded by diabetes. The stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) integrates acute glucose and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) to quantify acute metabolic stress, but its predictive value for POD needs validation. This was a multicenter retrospective cohort study involving elderly patients (≥ 65 years) admitted to the ICU following cardiac surgery. The discovery cohort was derived from the MIMIC-IV database (n = 1,087), while the external validation cohort consisted of patients from six Chinese hospitals (n = 982). The primary outcome was POD. The optimal threshold for the SHR was identified using restricted cubic splines (RCS). Subsequently, the independent association between SHR and POD was evaluated via multivariable logistic regression with sequential covariate adjustment. The performance of the prediction model based on this threshold was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. To further ensure the robustness of the findings, we performed propensity score matching (PSM) and comprehensive subgroup analyses. RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear relationship between the SHR and the risk of POD, with an inflection point at 1.09. After extensive covariate adjustment, an SHR ≥ 1.09 was strongly and independently associated with a significantly increased risk of POD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.152; 95% CI, 3.054-5.676, P < 0.001). This robust association was consistently validated in the external cohort (aOR, 3.856; 95% CI, 2.687-5.593, P < 0.001) and persisted in the PSM analysis. Notably, the univariate model based solely on continuous SHR exhibited good discriminative performance (area under the curve [AUC] 0.734), along with favorable calibration and clinical utility, compared with conventional severity scores, indicating SHR's potential value for risk stratification. An elevated SHR (≥ 1.09) was independently associated with a higher odds of POD in elderly cardiac surgery patients. This readily calculable metric may help identify patients at increased risk and guide enhanced monitoring or future intervention trials.

42974218.title: Burnout Among Emergency, ICU and Burn Unit Professionals: A Qualitative Study in Tirana.
42974218.journal: Annals of burns and fire disasters
42974218.abstract: Burnout is an increasingly prevalent issue in healthcare, particularly in high-stress hospital units that demand constant emotional, cognitive, and ethical engagement. This qualitative study explores the lived experiences and clinical consequences of burnout among healthcare professionals working in the Emergency, Intensive Care, and Burn Units at the University Hospital Center "Mother Teresa" in Tirana, Albania. Employing a phenomenological approach, the study involved 18 experienced clinicians (9 physicians and 9 nurses), each with a minimum of five years of service. Semi-structured interviews were conducted, and the data were thematically analyzed to examine how prolonged emotional and occupational stress affects empathy, communication, clinical decisionmaking, and moral sensitivity. The study also investigates how the presence or absence of institutional support shapes these experiences and impacts the quality of patient care. Thematic analysis revealed four central themes: lack of institutional support, moral strain in clinical practice, impaired decision-making, and erosion of empathy, all contributing to compromised care quality. Burnout presents significant risks not only to the mental health of healthcare professionals but also to patient safety, potentially creating a self-reinforcing cycle of emotional disengagement, moral distress, and systemic dysfunction if left unaddressed. As one of the first qualitative investigations of burnout within the Albanian healthcare context, this study offers valuable insights to inform the development of targeted strategies and institutional policies aimed at protecting healthcare workers' well-being and improving the overall quality of patient care.

42973926.title: Outcome and Risk Factors for Death of Burn Patients with Septic Shock.
42973926.journal: Annals of burns and fire disasters
42973926.abstract: This study determined mortality rate and risk factors for death of burn patients suffering septic shock. An observational study was conducted on 38 severe adult burn patients who developed septic shock at the burn intensive care unit, National Burn Hospital, from January 2023 to June 2024. Patients were divided into survivor and non-survivor groups. Results showed that 23 patients died, accounting for 60.53%. Age, gender, admission time post burn, incidence of inhalation injury, required mechanical ventilation on admission as well as onset time of septic shock were not significantly different between groups (p >.05). Compared to the survivor group, burn extent and deep burn area were significantly larger in the non-survivor group (p <.05). Baseline parameters including white blood count, total plasma protein and albumin concentration were significantly lower (p <.01); rate of positive blood cultures (56.52% vs. 20%; p=.03) and plasma IL-6 level (689.46 pg/mL vs. 243.16 pg/mL, p=.02) were significantly higher in the non-survivor group. Meanwhile, plasma level of endotoxin and TNF-α were not remarkably different between the two groups. Multivariate analysis showed that only plasma IL-6 level at the septic shock onset was an independent risk factor for death (p <.05) with AUC at .73, cut-off point at 249.46 pg/mL, sensitivity at 82.61% and specificity at 60%. Further studies should be conducted to confirm the role of IL-6 in the prognosis of burn patients with septic shock complication.

42973892.title: Antibiotic use, Resistance Patterns and Clinical Outcomes in Critically Burned Patients: A Retrospective Study From a Tertiary Burn Center in Albania.
42973892.journal: Annals of burns and fire disasters
42973892.abstract: Severe burn injuries induce profound physiological and immunological alterations that significantly affect the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of antimicrobial agents. These changes complicate standard dosing strategies and demand individualized, PK/PD-driven approaches to antimicrobial therapy to prevent treatment failure, resistance and toxicity.
