While venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a recognized rescue therapy for cardiogenic shock, the roles of venovenous ECMO and albumin dialysis-specifically the molecular adsorbent recirculating system (MARS)-as well as the effectiveness of linking patients to therapy through a coordinated referral process remain underexplored. We describe five consecutive patients with severe cardiotoxic ingestions managed via a regionally triggered transfer pathway. Patients presented with profound hypotension and respiratory failure despite standard therapies. All five patients received MARS for drug clearance and vasoplegia management; two required venovenous ECMO for refractory hypoxemia. One patient died due to profound myocardial poisoning; four survived to discharge. Complications included continuous renal replacement therapy filter clotting and catheter-associated thrombosis. A coordinated regional protocol enabling early access to ECMO and MARS is feasible in massive cardiotoxic ingestions.

42841424.title: Acquired 11β-hydroxylase deficiency adrenal hyperplasia associated with the use of etomidate and/or its analogues through e-cigarettes - a review of 76 cases in Hong Kong.
42841424.abstract: Etomidate and its analogues have been abused via vaping (e-cigarettes) in Hong Kong since 2023. Clinical effects including acute neurological effects, associated injuries, hypokalaemia, menstrual disturbances, and hyperpigmentation had been reported. This study aims to examine the clinical effects and associated adrenal dysfunction resulting from etomidate abuse through the inhalation (vaping) route. This retrospective case series study utilised the Hong Kong Poison Control Centre database. Suspected etomidate abuse cases from 1 January 2023 to May 31, 2025 were identified from the database, by searching for "etomidate" as the poison name or for urine toxicology results positive for etomidate and/or analogues. Cases in which etomidate was prescribed during hospital admission were excluded. Seventy-six cases were included, consisting of 1) Our poison centre's toxicology clinic cases, referred by social worker to us (5 cases) and 2) Our poison centre's "etomidate abuse" consultation/reporting database, consisting of suspected etomidate abusers managed by frontline clinicians of different units and consulted/reported to us (71 cases). Concerning the adrenal dysfunction, clinical features of mineralocorticoid excess (hypokalaemia, low aldosterone/renin levels), apparent glucocorticoid deficiency (low cortisol levels), adrenal androgen excess (virilisation, menstrual disturbances, elevated androstenedione and testosterone levels) and adrenocorticotropic hormone excess (hyperpigmentation, bilateral adrenal hyperplasia, elevated adrenocorticotropic hormone levels) were observed. Three associated deaths were reported. Etomidate abuse results in an acquired form of 11β-hydroxylase deficiency adrenal hyperplasia with clinical features similar to the congenitaladrenal hyperplasia due to 11β-hydroxylase deficiency. For etomidate abusers, reversibility of hypokalaemia, low blood cortisol, and elevated ACTH had been observed in our study in a small subset of our cases. The adrenal dysfunction in etomidate abuse manifest as an acquired 11β-hydroxylase deficiency adrenal hyperplasia, which is a pentad of mineralocorticoid excess, apparent glucocorticoid deficiency, virilisation, adrenocorticotropic hormone excess, and adrenal hyperplasia. Potentially life-threatening acute presentations include trauma sustained during the acute intoxication and severe hypokalemia. Cessation of etomidate abuse remains the cornerstone of managing the adrenal dysfunction, while glucocorticoid replacement should be considered on individual basis. In view of the local prevalence of etomidate abuse, we suggest that etomidate abuse should be considered as an important differential diagnosis in teenage and young adult patients presenting with features suggestive of congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 11β-hydroxylase deficiency, these features include hypokalaemia, virilisation, menstrual disturbances, and hyperpigmentation.

42841420.title: Development and internal validation of an emergency department mortality prediction score for older adults with acute poisoning.
42841420.abstract: Poisoning in older adults is an increasing clinical toxicology problem because age-related physiologic vulnerability, polypharmacy, intentional self-poisoning, and exposure to highly toxic substances can complicate early risk assessment. Existing severity scores lack age-specific validation and often require variables unavailable during initial emergency department assessment. This retrospective observational study used data from six hospitals participating in the fall/slip, self-harm/suicide, and poisoning divisions of the Emergency Department-Based Injury In-depth Surveillance system maintained by the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency. Patients aged 65 years or older who presented with acute poisoning between January 2020 and December 2024 were included. The outcome was all-cause mortality, defined as emergency department death or in-hospital death. Candidate predictors included age; sex; Alert, Voice, Pain, Unresponsive scale; vital signs; poisoning substance category; self-harm/suicidal intent; and alcohol-related presentation. A multivariable logistic regression model was internally validated using five-fold cross-validation and bootstrap optimism correction. Among 1,774 patients, overall mortality was 7.2% (127/1,774). The full model had an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.895, five-fold cross-validated value of 0.860, optimism-corrected value of 0.877, area under the precision-recall curve of 0.472, and Brier score of 0.049. Predictors associated with mortality included older age, impaired mental status, lower systolic blood pressure, higher pulse rate, lower body temperature, high-risk poisoning substances, and self-harm/suicidal intent. The five-item bedside warning score had area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.834; among patients with a score of ≥3, mortality was 27.5%. The full model provides individualized probability estimation, whereas the bedside score provides immediate warning-level risk stratification. An initial-assessment model and a five-item bedside score stratified mortality risk in older adults with acute poisoning. External validation is required before broader implementation.

42900082.title: Key agricultural pesticides responsible for acute pesticide poisoning in rural Sri Lanka - data to guide policy decisions.
42900082.abstract: Acute pesticide poisoning is a major public health problem among agricultural communities in low-and middle-income countries. Using recent surveillance data, this analysis identifies key pesticides responsible for acute poisoning in Sri Lanka to inform timely, evidence-based policy interventions, with relevance to similar agricultural settings. We analyzed interim data from two prospective studies in rural Sri Lanka: 1) a suicide surveillance system (Oct 2023-Apr 2025) and 2) a community-based cohort of 1,200 pesticide sprayers (Jan-Dec 2024). Self-poisoning deaths were identified through police, coroner, and household follow-up data, while occupational poisoning was monitored through bimonthly cohort follow-up. Descriptive analyses were identified the pesticides and active ingredients responsible for poisoning events. Of 1,040 suicides identified, 236 (22.7%) involved pesticide ingestion; a single pesticide was confirmed in 184 (78.0%) of deaths. Insecticides accounted for 165/184 (89.7%) deaths, predominantly the carbamate carbosulfan (120/184, 65.2%; 95% Confidence Intervals (CI) 58.3-72.1) and organophosphorus profenofos (20/184, 10.9%; 95% CI 6.4-15.4), with a small proportion involving illegal pesticides (13/184, 7.1%) or herbicides (19/184, 10.3%). Pesticide sprayers reported 1,311 incidents of acute occupational pesticide poisoning, with 856 events occurring after use of a single identified pesticide. Insecticides were the most frequently implicated, led by profenofos (167/856, 19.5%; 95% CI 16.9-22.1), followed by herbicides, including pretilachlor (125/856, 14.6%; 95% CI 12.2-17.0) and glyphosate (81/856, 9.5%; 95% CI 7.5-11.5). These findings show that most pesticide poisoning is concentrated in two insecticides: carbosulfan and profenofos. Their continued prominence despite earlier regulatory actions suggests ongoing pesticide substitution and highlights the need for strengthened surveillance and targeted regulation. Carbosulfan and profenofos now account for most pesticide suicides in Sri Lanka, while profenofos is also the leading cause of acute occupational pesticide poisoning. These findings highlight the need for ongoing surveillance and timely regulatory review.

42961000.title: Cardiac toxicity and dysrhythmias in acute poisoning: a ten-year cohort study.
42961000.abstract: Cardiac toxicity is frequently cited as an important cause of morbidity and mortality following acute drug overdose. The true incidence of direct drug related clinically significant cardiac complications and malignant dysrhythmias in more recent toxicology practice remains poorly defined. We aim to determine the frequency, nature, and outcomes of cardiac complications in patients presenting with acute poisoning. We conducted a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained clinical toxicology database over a 10-year period. Patients with acute poisoning managed by a specialist toxicology service were included. Cardiac complications were defined as hypotension (systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg) or a primary cardiac dysrhythmia considered temporally related to the poisoning. Sinus tachycardia was excluded. Demographics, exposures, treatments, and outcomes were extracted. A total of 9,743 poisoning presentations were included. Cardiac complications occurred in 473 patients (4.9%). Hypotension occurred in 368 patients (3.8%), primary dysrhythmias in 164 patients (1.7%), and both hypotension and dysrhythmia in 59 patients (0.6%). Most dysrhythmias were isolated bradycardia (139/164, 85%), commonly associated with clonidine (40%) and beta-blocker/calcium channel blocker poisoning (35%). Only 25 patients (0.3% of all poisoning presentations) developed primary dysrhythmias: atrial dysrhythmias (3), conduction abnormalities/delays (10), ectopic rhythms (5), asystole (1) or ventricular dysrhythmias (6; 0.06%). Malignant ventricular dysrhythmias occurred in six patients and were associated with sotalol, methadone, escitalopram, dothiepin, and nortriptyline poisoning. Twenty-one deaths occurred during the study period, but no death was attributable to a primary dysrhythmia temporally related to poisoning.Discussion: In this large cohort of almost 10,000 poisoning presentations, cardiac complications occurred in approximately one in twenty patients. However, almost 95% of these were either hypotension or isolated bradycardia. Only six patients (0.06%) had ventricular dysrhythmias. Our findings support previous studies demonstrating that clinically significant ventricular dysrhythmias are uncommon among unselected populations presenting with acute poisoning. We found that only a few individual drugs, such as sotalol, methadone, tricyclic antidepressants, and escitalopram, were associated with ventricular dysrhythmias, and that such events were rare overall. Cardiac effects occur in approximately 5% of acute poisoning presentations but are predominantly hypotension or sinus bradycardia. Clinically significant ventricular and supraventricular dysrhythmias are uncommon, occurring in less than 0.3% of cases. Death directly attributable to a primary poisoning-related dysrhythmia is rare.

42823017.title: Management of the Critically Ill Patient with Opioid Use Disorder.
42823017.journal: Emergency medicine clinics of North America
42823017.abstract: The management of critically ill patients with opioid use disorder presents a unique challenge, as overdose, withdrawal, or concomitant intoxication, due to an unregulated drug supply, leads to physiologic changes that potentially impact standard treatment. This review article outlines an emergency medicine-focused approach for early recognition and stabilization of opioid overdose or withdrawal. Topics include naloxone, use of medications for opioid use disorder, recognition of concurrent intoxication, treatment of α2-agonist withdrawal, multimodal analgesia, and sedation for opioid-tolerant patients. The acute management of opioid use disorder is an opportunity to prevent withdrawal-related decompensation, improve comfort, and support ongoing engagement in treatment.

42983629.title: Fatal methanol poisoning with paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity, and putaminal hemorrhage: a case report and brief literature review.
42983629.abstract: Methanol poisoning is a widespread issue worldwide. In this case report, we describe a patient with methanol poisoning who experienced tonic spasms, cerebellar and putaminal hemorrhages, and severe neurological complications. Additionally, this report emphasizes the potential link between methanol poisoning and paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH). A 31-year-old male was referred to the emergency department with blurred vision, epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, restlessness, and severe respiratory distress. Two days ago, he drank a locally prepared alcoholic beverage while having dinner. The initial laboratory data showed metabolic acidosis with a high anion gap. The patient was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) with a GCS of 4/15. General supportive treatment (normal saline, DVT prophylaxis, stress ulcer prophylaxis, etc.), sodium bicarbonate, ethanol, dialysis, methylprednisolone, and folic acid were initiated for poisoning management. In the brain CT scan, cerebellar and putamen hemorrhage, and brain edema were reported. We stopped heparin due to the brain hemorrhage, but after a few days, DVT occurred. During hospitalization, the patient experienced several brief and spontaneous tonic spasms with diaphoresis, tachycardia, and tachypnea, so paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) was suspected. He was treated with midazolam and metoprolol for PSH treatment. Unfortunately, the patient developed sepsis and died after 53 days of stay in the ICU. This study highlights that exposure to methanol can result in a range of neurological complications. The administration of heparin in cases of methanol poisoning remains controversial and requires careful evaluation. Furthermore, paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity is an uncommon complication that can result from cerebral injury attributed to methanol poisoning.

42992375.title: Gender differences in acute poisoning: a 35-year cohort study.
42992375.abstract: Drug overdose is an increasingly common cause of death, more commonly in males. In contrast, women present more commonly to emergency departments with overdose. We therefore aim to investigate gender differences in the characteristics and severity of acute poisoning. Adult (18-64 y) poisoning admissions to a tertiary toxicology service were reviewed (1990-2024), and females were compared to males. Data were extracted from a prospective database, including drug/toxin ingested, clinical effects, treatment, length of stay, intensive care admission and death. Primary outcomes were death, intensive care admission and intubation. There were 22,316 (75%) deliberate self-poisonings - 14,101 females (63%), 8,178 males and 37 transgender; 2,101 (7%) recreational overdoses - 695 (33%) females and 1,406 (67%) males. Females ingested more paracetamol/analgesics, antidepressants and quetiapine, while males ingested more alcohol, amphetamines and opioids. Median age for deliberate self-poisoning in females (33 years [IQR:24-44 years]) was similar to males (34 years [IQR:25-44 years]). There were 1,268 females (9.0%) admitted to intensive care, compared to 912 males (11.2%), which was significantly different (absolute difference 2.2%;95% CI:1.3-3.0%; P < 0.001). Less females were intubated than males (790 [5.6%] vs 549 [6.7%]; P = 0.001). Inpatient mortality was similar for females (32; 0.2%) and males (24; 0.3%), and no difference in length of stay. More females had hypotension, while more males developed coma and hepatotoxicity. Males were more likely to receive sedation and naloxone. Gender differences were similar for recreational poisoning, except greater mortality in males. Gender remained an independent predictor of intensive care and intubation in a multivariate logistic regression model, with males more likely to be intubated and admitted to intensive care. More males took recreational overdoses, including opioids, and females had more deliberate self-poisoning, with less toxic medications. Female deliberate self-poisoning patients were less commonly intubated and admitted to intensive care. Drug type did not account for the gender difference in outcomes. We found only minor differences between inpatient morbidity and mortality for females compared to males. Males were more likely to be admitted to intensive care and be intubated, mainly due to higher rates of coma.

42992400.title: Lead poisoning: an important differential diagnosis in acute colonic pseudo-obstruction.
42992400.abstract: Lead poisoning remains an important public health concern. We highlight the findings in a patient with a high blood lead concentration. These images can assist clinicians in making the correct diagnosis. A 44-year-old male presented with a 3-day history of nausea, vomiting, and obstipation. The diagnosis was intestinal obstruction, which failed to respond to conservative management. After exploratory laparotomy and colostomy failed to identify an etiology of acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie syndrome), lead poisoning was diagnosed based on anemia, basophilic stippling of erythrocytes, and a whole-blood lead concentration of 71.87 µg/dL (reference <10.00 µg/dL). The patient recovered with chelation therapy. Abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan revealed copious intraluminal feces and gas within the bowel. Peripheral smear revealed poikilocytosis with basophilic stippling. In patients with acute colonic pseudo-obstruction, abdominal pain and anemia, a detailed history is essential, and lead poisoning should be suspected.

42997175.title: Profound Hyperbilirubinemia During Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning and Subsequent Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report.
42997175.abstract: Carbon monoxide poisoning is classically associated with neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, while severe exposure may also cause systemic toxic-hypoxic injury. Profound direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia without mechanical biliary obstruction is rarely described. We report a 55-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, chronic tobacco use, COPD, and hepatic steatosis who presented with altered mental status and jaundice after suspected household carbon monoxide exposure. Her carboxyhemoglobin level was > 30%, and she required intubation, intensive care, vasopressor support, and three hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Initial testing showed total bilirubin of 23.1 mg/dL and direct bilirubin of 13.1 mg/dL, despite only mild AST elevation and near-normal ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Imaging showed hepatic steatosis and cholelithiasis without convincing biliary obstruction, and the documented workup for viral, autoimmune, metabolic, hemolytic, and vascular causes was unrevealing. Her liver dysfunction was considered multifactorial, with possible carbon monoxide-related toxic-hypoxic injury superimposed on underlying steatotic or alcohol-related liver vulnerability. After transient improvement, she developed coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, recurrent shock with clinical and imaging concern for acute cholecystitis, worsening hyperbilirubinemia peaking near 49-50 mg/dL, encephalopathy, respiratory failure, and multiorgan failure. Cholecystostomy yielded dark green bile without documented purulence, and aspirate cultures showed no growth; biliary sepsis was therefore not microbiologically confirmed. She died in the hospital after goals-of-care discussions. The initial bilirubin-predominant pattern was atypical for classic hypoxic hepatitis and may have reflected overlapping hepatic insults. This case emphasizes broad evaluation and cautious causal interpretation; it does not establish that carbon monoxide exposure alone caused the initial hyperbilirubinemia.

43006831.title: Local complications of peripheral intravenous vasopressor use with phentolamine as an antidote: a retrospective review.
43006831.abstract: Prior studies have indicated that peripheral administration of vasopressors, particularly norepinephrine, can be considered safe, with local complications occurring in 0% to 1.8% of patients. Our study further explored the local skin complications from peripheral vasopressor administration treated with phentolamine in a large health care system. A retrospective chart review was performed on patients who received phentolamine for effects of local infiltration of pressors. Data were collected for demographics, vasopressor dose and duration of use, phentolamine dose and time after extravasation until administration, peripheral intravenous characteristics, as well as outcomes such as length of stay and mortality. Data on patients who did and did not require central venous catheter placement postextravasation were compared. Of 92 patients with infiltrated vasopressor intravenous access who required phentolamine, the mean age was 69, with 65% being female and a mean body mass index of 28 kg/m2. The most common sites of intravenous access were the antecubital fossa (33%) and forearm (27%). Mean number of hours prior to extravasation of peripheral vasopressors requiring phentolamine administration was 21 hours. Mean number of minutes prior to phentolamine administration after extravasation was 131 minutes. Seventy-six percent of patients did not any have significant ischemic tissue injury with extravasation, and 24% of patients had only minor bruising and erythema. Two significant reactions occurred, including deep vein thrombosis and local skin necrosis. Fifty-two percent of patients required a subsequent central venous line placement. The mean length of stay was 5.4 days in the intensive care unit and 11.8 days in the hospital, and in-patient mortality was 17%. In our large cohort of patients with extravasation from peripheral vasopressors managed with local phentolamine administration, severe tissue skin or soft tissue injury was rare.

43003943.title: Fatal polysubstance intoxications involving inhalation of nitazene analogues: identification of fluetonitazepyne and 5-methyl etodesnitazene.
43003943.abstract: The illicit opioid market has undergone notable diversification, with 2-benzylbenzimidazoles (nitazenes) representing an increasingly prevalent class of non-fentanyl synthetic opioids. These compounds challenge forensic toxicology through marked µ-opioid receptor potency and rapid structural evolution, often undetected by routine immunoassay screening. We report two fatal polysubstance intoxications involving inhalation of nitazene analogues via vaping devices, identified in biological matrices. GC-MS-based identification was corroborated by untargeted LC-HRMS screening with in silico data mining and confirmed against certified reference standards.Case 1 involved a 40-year-old male found deceased after an estimated 2-3 days without contact. Fluetonitazepyne was quantified at 0.58 ng/mL in peripheral blood alongside ethanol (0.55 g/kg), supra-therapeutic citalopram (340 ng/mL), sub-therapeutic lithium, and cannabinoid metabolites, concordant with a recovered vaping vial containing the same nitazene. Death could not be established with certainty; based on toxicological findings, it was most likely acute fluetonitazepyne intoxication in the presence of central nervous system (CNS) depressants. Case 2 concerned a 22-year-old male with a witnessed cardiorespiratory arrest following inhalation from a vaping device confirmed to contain 5-methyl etodesnitazene. Despite bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), naloxone administration (1.6 mg), and intensive care, he died from acute anoxic encephalopathy approximately 24 h later. Ante mortem peripheral blood confirmed 5-methyl etodesnitazene at 3.3 ng/mL alongside barbital at toxic concentrations (39 mg/L).Concurrent CNS depressant exposure potentiated fatal respiratory depression, more clearly established in Case 2. These cases document the lethal potential of emerging nitazene analogues and the value of untargeted HRMS-based screening in the absence of certified reference standards.

43006667.title: Impact of a national ban on highly hazardous pesticides on suicide and agricultural productivity in Nepal.
43006667.abstract: Pesticide self-poisoning is a major contributor to suicide in low- and middle-income countries. Between 2019 and 2021, Nepal banned several highly hazardous pesticides and replaced high-concentration aluminium phosphide tablets (3 g 56%) with products of alternative formulations and lower concentration. This study examines the impact of these regulations on pesticide suicides and agricultural productivity. National data on pesticide suicides (April 2017-August 2024) were obtained from two forensic toxicology laboratories. Pesticides were grouped into categories. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for changes in pesticide involvement between the pre-ban (April 2017-February 2020) and post-ban (September 2021-August 2024) periods. Post-ban provincial variation in pesticide suicides was assessed using age-standardised rates and standardised mortality ratios (SMRs). Joinpoint regression was used to assess trends in crop yields (2005-2023). A total of 3,005 and 1,331 pesticide suicides were analysed in pre- and post-ban periods, respectively. The mean monthly number of identified pesticide suicides declined by 56.9% (85.9 to 37.0). The proportions of pesticide suicides involving the categories of organophosphorus pesticides, carbamates, and organochlorines, including banned pesticides such as dichlorvos and triazophos, decreased. In contrast, phosphine gas-generating pesticides increased proportionally (31.1% to 48.2%), largely driven by aluminium phosphide. Post-ban suicides were more common amongst males (56.0%), individuals aged 15-44 years (52.8%), and in Bagmati and Lumbini Provinces (SMRs = 1.26 and 1.35) than their counterparts. No adverse changes in rice, pulse, or vegetable yields were observed. Nepal's 2019-2021 pesticide regulations were associated with reduced involvement of banned organophosphorus pesticides, carbamates, and organochlorines. However, continued aluminium phosphide deaths warrant surveillance and further regulatory action. Our findings were similar compared to previous studies monitoring pesticide exposures after a ban. There are potential policy implications from this study. In Nepal, the 2019-2021 bans were followed by fewer suicides involving banned pesticides without declines in major crop yields, but aluminium phosphide remained prominent after regulation.

43006651.title: Rethinking how poison centres engage with the pesticide industry.
43006651.abstract: Poison centres help to prevent, diagnose and manage poisonings. Part of their prevention activities involves identifying sources of harm, such as toxic pesticides, and working with others to address these, including removing hazardous products from the market. This raises important questions about how poison centres and the health professionals who support their work should interact with commercial actors whose business interests conflict with the public health mission and purpose of poison centres. Partnership working with industries like the pesticide industry may appear intuitively appealing, particularly when access to funds and data are limited. However, such partnerships create considerable risks, including a shift towards industry-favourable interventions that blame pesticide users. This commentary examines these complex issues using examples of partnerships between the pesticide industry, clinical toxicology societies and poison centres. We argue that these interactions have received inadequate attention compared to other areas of medicine and public health. We call for a rethinking of how poison centres engage with the pesticide industry. Among other changes, this requires a strengthening of the international guidance on the provision of poison centres, building on approaches to managing conflicts of interest and engaging with commercial actors in other areas such as food and nutrition. Reflecting critically on industry partnerships and strengthening of governance systems are core to ensuring poison centres prioritise the prevention of harm by removing poisons and not blaming the poisoned.

42879608.title: Post-intensive care unit syndrome: trends and research foci in a bibliometric analysis.
42879608.abstract: to identify the main areas of focus and trends in research on Post-Intensive Care Syndrome, with an emphasis on patient follow-up after discharge from the Intensive Care Unit. search conducted on Web of Science from 2012 to November 2024. The Bibliometrix package and BiblioShiny platform in RStudio were used to explore keywords, trends and co-occurrences, journals, authors, co-citations, and collaboration networks. 120 articles on Post-Intensive Care Syndrome in adults were included. the main keywords include critical illness, quality-of-life, and posttraumatic stress disorder. The most prolific authors are Needham D.M. and Sevin C.M., and the most relevant journals are Critical Care and BMJ Open. The United States leads in publications, followed by the Netherlands and Japan. most studies address a single component of the syndrome, and comparisons between studies are hampered by the diversity of assessment tools. Greater international collaboration, long-term studies, and randomized controlled clinical trials are needed.

42873779.title: Cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of the ISBAR structured handover observation tool for ICU-to-ward patient transfer in China.
42873779.abstract: The Identity, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation (ISBAR) framework is used to standardize clinical handovers. Effective ISBAR implementation requires both training and objective assessment of handover. In Chinese clinical settings, handover quality is commonly evaluated through self-reports or locally developed checklists, which provide limited information about the completeness and accuracy of information transfer. The absence of validated Chinese observational instruments restricts the identification of communication deficiencies, benchmarking of handover performance, and development of targeted workforce training and patient safety interventions. This study aimed to conduct a cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of the ISBAR Structured Handover Observation Tool and evaluate its applicability in Chinese clinical practice. The study was conducted in two phases: cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric evaluation in clinical settings. Content validity was assessed using the content validity index (CVI). Inter-rater reliability was evaluated using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) in a two-way mixed-effects model with absolute agreement. Known-groups validity was examined using the Mann-Whitney U test to compare scores across nurses with varying levels of experience. A total of 233 ICU-to-general ward handovers involving 84 nurses were observed and evaluated. The scale demonstrated good content validity, with item-level CVIs ranging from 0.86 to 1.00 and a scale-level CVI/Ave of 0.98. Based on 50 randomly selected handovers, inter-rater reliability was high, with an ICC of 0.885 for single-rater assessments and 0.939 for average-rater assessments. Known-groups validity analysis showed that nurses with more experience had significantly higher total scores than those with less experience (Z = -4.772, p < 0.001). The Chinese version tool demonstrates satisfactory validity and reliability for evaluating structured handover performance. The tool may be used to identify communication gaps, support competency-based training, monitor handover performance, and provide evidence for patient safety initiatives, facilitating its integration into nursing management and patient safety programs in Chinese clinical settings.

42864196.title: Delivery fidelity was high with variable uptake of optional components in a remote multicomponent rehabilitation intervention in intensive care unit survivors (iRehab): a mixed-methods fidelity assessment.
42864196.abstract: What was the fidelity of a remote multicomponent rehabilitation intervention in intensive care unit survivors (iRehab) across the National Institutes of Health Behavior Change Consortium Treatment Fidelity framework domains (design, training, delivery, receipt and enactment)? iRehab participants (n = 429; 231 intervention, 198 standard care); interviews involved 20 intervention participants, 15 standard care participants and six intervention staff. A mixed-methods fidelity assessment was embedded within the process evaluation of a multicentre randomised controlled trial. Quantitative fidelity was assessed using structured checklists, participant-level tracking data and longitudinal monitoring of potential drift. Qualitative interviews explored fidelity processes across domains. Study design fidelity was maintained, with clear differentiation between the experimental intervention and standard care. Provider training included structured training, competency assessment and ongoing multidisciplinary support. Delivery fidelity was high for one-to-one sessions, with no systematic drift in sampled sessions. Of 231 participants allocated to iRehab, 169 (73%) attended at least five one-to-one appointments. The uptake of optional group-based components was more variable. Qualitative findings indicated participant understanding and engagement, whereas tracking data and participant accounts provided evidence of strategies being applied in daily life. The iRehab intervention was delivered with high delivery fidelity while allowing individualisation to patient needs. For physiotherapists, monitoring of fidelity should extend beyond attendance and exercise prescription to whether patients can independently apply rehabilitation strategies when symptoms, fatigue and everyday demands fluctuate. Defined core components, staff training, staff competency assessment, ongoing support and fidelity monitoring may help support consistent remote delivery.

42864074.title: Working With AI and Robotic Systems While Preserving Clinical Judgement, Professional Accountability and Person-Centred Care: Critical Care Nurses' Perspectives.
42864074.abstract: The integration of AI and robotic systems into critical care necessitates examining how ICU nurses preserve clinical judgement, professional accountability and person-centred care while using these technologies. To explore ICU nurses' perceptions of AI and robotic systems in critical care, focusing on clinical judgement, trust, responsibility, professional roles and person-centred care. A qualitative descriptive study using scenario-based elicitation was conducted. Data were collected through seven semi-structured focus group discussions (FGDs) with 38 ICU nurses working in general, paediatric and cardiovascular surgery ICUs in two hospitals in Istanbul City. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, supported by MAXQDA 2024. Four themes were developed: negotiating trust in AI-supported critical care; preserving human authority, accountability and boundaries; protecting the human core of intensive care nursing; and reimagining AI and robotic systems as supportive partners. ICU nurses evaluated these systems through bedside verification, patient safety, professional responsibility and person-centred care. AI recommendations were useful only when nurses could question, verify, delay or override them according to the patient's current condition. Robotic systems were valuable when they reduced documentation or physical workload, but not when they replaced clinical judgement, emotional presence, reassurance or accountability. ICU nurses conceptualised AI and robotic systems as acceptable only when clinically verifiable, professionally bounded and subordinate to human judgement. The findings support a model of AI- and robot-supported ICU care that is responsible, human-led and person-centred. AI and robotic systems should be implemented in ways that strengthen, rather than replace, nurses' clinical judgement, accountability and bedside presence. Clear protocols are needed to verify AI outputs, define robotic task boundaries, support nurses' authority to question or override recommendations and preserve person-centred care in technologically intensive ICU environments.

42862753.title: Impact of early fluid intake and urine output on mortality in acute pancreatitis: A retrospective cohort study.
42862753.journal: The Journal of international medical research
42862753.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the associations between early fluid-related parameters, including fluid intake, fluid balance, and urine output, within the first 24 h after intensive care unit admission and mortality among critically ill patients with acute pancreatitis.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using the publicly available Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III database. Adult patients with acute pancreatitis admitted to the intensive care unit between 2001 and 2012 were included. Fluid intake, fluid balance, and urine output during the first 24 h after intensive care unit admission were extracted and categorized into four predefined levels. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the associations between early fluid-related parameters and in-hospital mortality, adjusting for baseline demographic characteristics and indicators of disease severity. Generalized propensity score analyses were additionally performed to evaluate the distribution of fluid-related exposures and the potential influence of measured severity-related confounding. Sensitivity analyses using E-values were conducted to assess the potential impact of unmeasured confounding.ResultsAmong critically ill patients with acute pancreatitis, higher early fluid intake levels were associated with increased in-hospital and 28-day mortality after adjustment for baseline characteristics and disease severity. Conversely, higher urine output levels were associated with lower in-hospital and 28-day mortality. Early fluid balance showed weaker and less consistent associations with mortality. Generalized propensity score analyses demonstrated nonrandom distributions of fluid intake, fluid balance, and urine output according to baseline severity-related characteristics, indicating the presence of confounding by indication in early fluid management. After adjustment for measured confounding factors, the observed associations between fluid intake, urine output, and mortality remained consistent. However, residual confounding could not be completely excluded.ConclusionIn critically ill patients with acute pancreatitis, early fluid intake and urine output were associated with mortality outcomes. These parameters may represent potential markers of disease severity, physiological reserve, and response to initial resuscitation rather than direct determinants of outcome. Further prospective studies are required to clarify their clinical significance.

42860025.title: Reallocating Surgical Activity to Expand Critical Care Capacity During the SARS-CoV-2 Pandemic: A Descriptive and Analytical Study in a French University Hospital Network.
42860025.journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
42860025.abstract: The ability to anticipate ICU beds mobilizable through elective surgical postponements during health system shocks remains poorly quantified. Using real-world COVID-19 deprogramming data, we combined a classification of acceptable surgical deferral times with predictive models of expected surgical activity to estimate ICU capacity that can be generated in crisis scenarios. We conducted a retrospective time-series analysis of all surgical procedures performed from 2017 to 2021 in three AP-HP university hospitals. Procedures were classified as non-deferrable (red), deferrable < 1 month (orange), or > 1 month (green). Expected weekly surgical volumes for 2020-2021 without pandemic disruption were predicted using models trained on 2017-2018 and validated on 2019 (XGBoost, Holt-Winters). Multivariable linear regression quantified the association between postponed procedures and ICU beds opened, enabling projection of capacity gains under different postponement scenarios. Among 196,469 procedures, 59% were red, 20% orange, and 21% green. Surgical activity declined by 13% in 2020% and 8% in 2021, while ICU capacity increased by up to 85 and 46 beds, respectively. Reductions were mainly driven by postponement of green procedures (IRR 0.78 [0.75-0.80]). Only postponed green procedures were significantly associated with ICU bed expansion (β = 0.75, 95% CI 0.53-0.97; p < 0.001), accounting for 34.6% of ICU bed demand. Clinically acceptable postponement of low-priority elective surgery contributes substantially to ICU surge capacity. Integrating prioritization and predictive modeling into preparedness strategies may support balanced, data-driven responses to future healthcare system shocks.

42858113.title: Maternal critical care infrastructure and organisational preparedness in Türkiye: a national analysis of the MaCriCare cross-sectional survey.
42858113.abstract: MaCriCare (Maternal Critical Care) study, created as a European initiative, evaluated the availability of maternal critical care services. Since unique strengths and challenges of Turkish data within the MaCriCare study have not yet been evaluated separately, we aimed to assess maternal critical care preparedness and organisation in Turkish obstetric units participating in the MaCriCare cohort. This secondary analysis included validated unit responses collected from September 2021 to January 2022. Survey domians including access to an intensive care unit (ICU), modified early-obstetric warning-score (MEOWS) use, availability of critical-care resources, care locations for pre-eclampsia, postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) and sepsis, and maternal/staff support by focusing service accessibility and annual delivery rate were used. The comparator comprised 993 non-Türkiye units, and 140 Turkish units from 1,133-unit MaCriCare cohort. Responses from 140/403 eligible units (34.7%) represented 305,250 annual deliveries where 501-1,500 and 1,501-3,000 annual deliveries comprised 32.1% and 30.0%, respectively. Rate of same-hospital ICU access was 78.6% and 82.4% and use of any MEOWS system was 27.9% and versus 35.4% in Turkish vs non-Türkiye units, respectively. For pre-eclampsia, 58/140 units (41.4%) reported obstetric-unit care before delivery, followed by separate critical care particularly for PPH varied between 62.1% to 82.9%. Sepsis rate was 86.4%. Unavailable advanced resources included cardiac output monitoring (30.0%), cell salvage (47.1%), and viscoelastic testing (67.1%). Rate of breastfeeding support was 92.7% and maternal psychological screening was 24.5%. Describing maternal critical-care infrastructure and reported organisational arrangements among participating Turkish units may support future service assessment and planning.

42856972.title: Latent profile analysis of mindful self-care and its relationship with professional grief among intensive care unit nurses.
42856972.abstract: Intensive Care Unit (ICU) nurses are particularly at a high risk of professional grief. Mindful self-care practices were confirmed to improve nurses' mental health status. However, the current studies focusing on mindful self-care among ICU nurses are limited, and the relationship between mindful self-care and professional grief has not been confirmed. This study aims to examine the characteristics and influencing factors of different mindful self-care latent profiles among ICU nurses and investigate the relationship between mindful self-care and professional grief. The survey was conducted on 355 ICU nurses from nine hospitals in Shandong Province using the General Demographic Questionnaire, Mindful Self-Care Scale, Grief State Scale Nurses, and Short Form of the Self-Compassion Scale. Latent profile analysis was used to determine the profiles of mindful self-care among ICU nurses. Binary logistic regression was employed to explore the influencing factors of different profiles. A t-test was used to compare professional grief differences among distinct mindful self-care profiles. Mindful self-care among ICU nurses was categorized into the "mindful self-care deficiency profile" (32.5%) and "high mindfulness care profile" (67.5%). Factors influencing mindful self-care profiles included health status, and self-compassion ability (p < 0.05). High mindfulness care profile nurses exhibited lower levels of professional grief (p < 0.001). This study classified ICU nurses' mindful self-care into two latent profiles. ICU nurses with good health status and high self-compassion were more likely to belong to the high-mindfulness-care profile, whose members reported lower professional grief. These findings provide evidence for interventions targeting mindful self-care and professional grief among ICU nurses.

42855915.title: Exploring Nurses' Experiences of Autonomy in Intensive Care Units: A Qualitative Descriptive Study.
42855915.abstract: Nursing autonomy is essential in intensive care units (ICUs). However, there is limited understanding of how nurses perceive autonomy within their practice. To explore nurses' perception and experience of autonomy in ICUs. A qualitative descriptive study. The study was conducted with 14 ICU nurses through interviews from May to August 2025. Nurses' characteristics were described, and interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using a primarily inductive, semantic codebook thematic analysis informed by Braun and Clarke's six-phase framework. Seven main themes and 25 subthemes emerged from the interviews, revealing personal and organizational factors that influence nursing autonomy in ICUs. The themes were as follows: nursing autonomy's definition and perception, clinical practices, facilitators, barriers, perceived influence on patient care, perceived influence on nurse personal and professional development, and future advancements. The findings provide insight into ICU nurses' experiences and perceptions of autonomy. Nurses reported that autonomy was influenced by clinical competence, organizational support, and clear guidelines. Nurses perceived that independent nursing care and timely actions undertaken under approved protocols could support patient care, professional confidence, and job satisfaction. Limited decision-making authority, inadequate staffing, and unclear institutional support were reported as barriers. Nursing autonomy could strengthen nurses' confidence and job satisfaction, which nurses perceived as contributing to better patient care. The findings can guide nurse managers in implementing structured competency-based education, reinforcing clearly defined scopes of practice that are consistent with institutional policies, and adopting supportive leadership practices to promote nursing autonomy. Hospital administrators and national policymakers can further use the findings to advance nursing practice through developing organizational and regulatory frameworks required to authorize and safely support expanded autonomous practice.

42854259.title: Digital Order System Redesign in Emergency-to-Intensive Care Unit Admissions: Prospective Observational Study.
42854259.abstract: Emergency-to-intensive care unit (ICU) admissions are high-stakes transitions in care, where delays or documentation errors can compromise patient safety and disrupt operational efficiency. Although digital order systems can support these workflows, traditional platforms often lack real-time traceability and structured input logic, leaving them vulnerable to duplicate submissions, lost orders, and misaligned ICU bed reservations. The study aimed to examine whether an updated digital order system was associated with differences in emergency-to-ICU admission workflows, including order validity, documentation-error frequencies, and ICU reservation alignment, compared with those of the traditional platform. We conducted a single-center retrospective historical-control formative evaluation of emergency-to-ICU admissions processed through traditional (2023) and updated (2024) digital order systems at a tertiary medical center. Prospectively generated system log and ICU-reservation data were analyzed to quantify order validity, error subtypes (duplicate, lost, and tracking), and admission-to-reservation alignment. Proportions were compared using chi-square tests, with risk ratios (RRs) and absolute differences in proportions reported. Statistical significance was defined as P<.05. The updated system was associated with higher admission-order validity (54.1%-75.4%; RR 1.39, 95% CI 1.25-1.54; P<.001) and lower erroneous-order frequency (45.9%-24.6%; RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.44-0.66; P<.001). Duplicate and lost orders declined, whereas tracking-error frequency showed no meaningful change. ICU reservation alignment also differed, with the admission-to-reservation ratio rising from 0.68 to 0.78 (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.77-0.99; P=.03). The updated digital order system was associated with more consistent emergency-to-ICU workflow patterns, including higher order validity, fewer documentation errors, and closer alignment between admission intent and ICU reservations. These findings are consistent with literature on structured electronic order systems, digital-workflow standardization, and timestamp integrity, and they highlight the potential value of structured, timestamp-driven digital infrastructures in supporting more reliable high-acuity workflows. Further evaluation using time-motion analysis, interaction-log metrics, or mixed methods assessment is warranted to examine the robustness and generalizability of these patterns.

42853967.title: Current Status and Factors Associated With Standard Precautions Compliance Among ICU Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Study.
42853967.abstract: This study aims to assess the compliance of ICU nurses to standard precautions and to identify factors associated with their compliance, thereby providing evidence to inform targeted interventions. This study employed a multicenter cross-sectional design. From June to July 2025, a multicenter survey was conducted among 378 ICU nurses from five tertiary hospitals in China. Data were collected through the Compliance with Standard Precautions Scale and the Perceived Organizational Support Scale. The results were analysed using the Mann-Whitney U test, the Kruskal-Wallis H test, Spearman correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression. This study adhered to the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology checklist. The results showed that the overall compliance rate with standard precautions among ICU nurses in tertiary hospitals was 73.4%. Compliance correlated positively with perceived organizational support (r = 0.328, p < 0.01). Multiple linear regression analysis indicated that gender, occupational exposure within the past 6 months, and perceived organizational support were significantly associated with ICU nurses' compliance with standard precautions. Compliance with standard precautions among ICU nurses in tertiary hospitals remains suboptimal and necessitates targeted improvement. Multifaceted strategies should be implemented to strengthen compliance, with particular emphasis on enhancing perceived organizational support. Nurse managers should routinely assess organizational support perceptions, implement targeted training and psychological support for nurses with occupational exposure. A structured care bundle incorporating these elements may provide a practical framework for improving compliance and reducing healthcare-associated infections. The authors have adhered to the relevant EQUATOR guidelines-STROBE checklist for a cross-sectional study. No patient or public contribution.

42851029.title: PARTNER: Nurse Participation and Professional Experience During Family Conferences in Intensive Care: A Qualitative Study.
42851029.abstract: Effective communication during family conferences (FC) in the intensive care unit (ICU) is essential for supporting families and fostering trust. Although nurses are continuously present at the bedside, their active participation in FC remains limited, structurally constrained and underexplored from the perspective of healthcare professionals. This study aimed to explore the factors shaping ICU nurses' participation in family conferences. This French single-centre qualitative interpretive study used semi-structured interviews with nurses and physicians. Transcripts were analysed using a thematic approach combining inductive and deductive coding, managed with NVivo software and reviewed by a multidisciplinary team. Nineteen HCP participated (14 nurses and 5 physicians). Three axes shaped HCP experience of FC: organizational conditions (setting, time and exclusion from ethical deliberation), interpersonal dynamics with families (comprehension, trust and relational skills) and interprofessional dynamics (nurses' specific role, barriers, facilitators and benefits of their involvement). Nurses did not express dissatisfaction but identified structural constraints limiting their participation, alongside a clear sense of their own legitimacy. Facilitators included clinical experience, physician trust and structured FC. Barriers included limited speaking opportunities, fear of contradicting physicians and exclusion from ethics meetings. When nurses participated actively, HCP perceived consistent benefits: team coherence, richer communication and strengthened family trust. ICU nurses' participation in family conferences is primarily shaped by organisational and interprofessional conditions rather than by their willingness or competence. Structural barriers limit their active involvement despite consistent recognition of their contribution by both professional groups. These findings provide an empirical foundation for developing structured co-facilitation models between physicians and nurses during family conferences, and highlight key organisational conditions to address in daily ICU practice.

42845173.title: Comparison of the Validity and Reliability of Five Pressure Injury Risk Scales in Intensive Care.
42845173.abstract: The lack of consensus on the best pressure injury (PI) risk assessment tools demonstrates the need for further comparative research to identify the most effective options for intensive care unit (ICU) populations. This study compared the predictive validity and reliability of five PI risk assessment tools in adult ICU patients. A prospective cohort study was conducted with patients aged ≥ 18 years, admitted to the ICUs for at least 24 h and without pre-existing PI. Five tools (Braden Scale, CALCULATE, Cubbin & Jackson, EVARUCI and Sunderland) were used daily to assess PI risk until either a PI developed or the participant was discharged, died or completed 21 days in the ICUs. The main outcome measures included area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, sensitivity, specificity, relative risk and reliability. Of the 150 participants, 40 (26.7%) developed PIs. None of the five tools demonstrated good predictive accuracy. AUC values ranged from 0.605 to 0.692 across the five tools, with none exceeding the predefined threshold of 0.70. Participants classified as high risk by Sunderland, Cubbin & Jackson and EVARUCI had a 3.0, 2.5 and 2.1 times higher risk, respectively, of developing a PI. Cubbin & Jackson was the only tool to achieve acceptable reliability values in Cronbach's alpha, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Cohen's weighted kappa. High-risk classification using the Sunderland, Cubbin & Jackson and EVARUCI scales was more strongly associated with subsequent PI development than classification using the other tools. Reliability findings varied across parameters, with Cubbin & Jackson being the only tool to meet acceptable thresholds across all assessed reliability measures. PI assessment in ICU patients should integrate validated tools with clinical judgement to address patient-specific and device-related risk factors.

42845018.title: Early platelet change and 28-day mortality after the day-7 landmark among intensive care unit patients with diagnosis-coded heart failure: A MIMIC-IV cohort study.
42845018.journal: The Journal of international medical research
42845018.abstract: ObjectiveTo assess the association between platelet percent-decrease patterns during the first 168 h after intensive care unit admission and 28-day mortality after a day-7 landmark among intensive care unit patients with a diagnosis of heart failure.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) version 3.1 records from one US center (2008-2022). The day-7 risk set comprised patients who were not recorded as having died before the landmark. Platelet percent decrease from the first to the last available daily mean during the first 168 h was categorized as stable/increase, percent decrease ≤0%; mild decline, percent decrease >0% and ≤30%; or marked decline, percent decrease >30%. Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios for 28-day mortality after the landmark. Supportive analyses examined measurement processes, alternative platelet definitions, narrower heart-failure coding, and an independent 72-h landmark.ResultsAmong 14,762 platelet-classifiable patients in the day-7 risk set, 1736 died within 28 days after the landmark. Observed mortality was 8.66%, 13.14%, and 30.06% in the stable/increase, mild-decline, and marked-decline groups, respectively. Among 14,710 Model 3 complete cases (1729 deaths), adjusted odds ratios were 1.54 (95% confidence interval: 1.37-1.74) for mild decline and 3.51 (95% confidence interval: 2.99-4.12) for marked decline. Adjusted mortality probabilities were 9.08%, 13.07%, and 24.27%, respectively. For marked decline, the odds ratio was 2.69 after adjustment for measurement processes and 2.37 among patients who remained in the intensive care unit on day 7. In the independent 72-h analysis, odds ratios were 1.02 (95% confidence interval: 0.92-1.14) and 1.23 (95% confidence interval: 1.05-1.44).ConclusionsGreater platelet decline was associated with higher mortality after the day-7 landmark. The weaker associations at the 72-h landmark and attenuation after accounting for measurement processes indicate that the magnitude of this association depends on the observation window and may partly reflect prolonged critical illness and monitoring intensity.

42844890.title: Evaluating Meaningful Patient and Public Involvement in Intensive Care Research-A PEIRS-22 Survey.
42844890.abstract: Patient and public involvement (PPI) is increasingly recommended in health research to enhance relevance, quality and implementation of findings. In intensive care research, involving patients, family members and healthcare professionals may help ensure that research addresses outcomes that are meaningful to those affected by critical illness. This study aimed to assess the level of meaningful PPI engagement during the development of a core outcome set (COS) for general intensive care unit (ICU) patients in Denmark. A cross-sectional survey using the Danish version of the Patient Engagement in Research Scale (PEIRS-22) was conducted between December 2024 and January 2025. We invited all members (patients, family, healthcare professionals and researchers) of five research panels, established in 2021 to support COS development across Danish university hospitals (N = 46). PEIRS-22 total scores range from 1 to 100, with higher scores indicating greater meaningful engagement (scores ≥ 70.1 were considered meaningful). Descriptive statistics, item-level analyses and non-parametric comparisons between participant roles were performed. Thirty-seven of 46 participants responded (80.4%): 27.0% (n = 10) were patients/family, 46.0% (n = 17) healthcare professionals and 27.0% (n = 10) researchers. The median PEIRS-22 total score was 78 (IQR 68-93), with 72.0% (n = 27) scoring ≥ 70.1. Engagement differed statistically significant by role (p = 0.004), with researchers reporting the highest scores (median 97), followed by patients/family (89), while healthcare professionals reported lower scores (74). PPI in COS development for general ICU patients was perceived as meaningful overall. However, differences across stakeholder groups and lower achievement of advanced engagement elements suggest opportunities to strengthen shared decision-making, role clarity and perceived relevance, particularly among healthcare professionals. Meaningful involvement of patients, families and clinicians may support the development of more patient-centred intensive care research and outcomes that better reflect the priorities of those affected by critical illness. Meaningful PPI can help ensure that intensive care research reflects the priorities of patients and families. Clear roles, clinical relevance, and opportunities to influence decisions may strengthen engagement, particularly among healthcare professionals. Critical care nurses may play an important role in facilitating collaboration between patients, families, clinicians, and researchers.

42844819.title: Protecting the Privacy of Patients With Impaired Consciousness in Intensive Care: A Qualitative Study.
42844819.abstract: Maintaining privacy in intensive care units (ICUs) is challenging because of high workload, invasive procedures, continuous monitoring and shared care environments. Patients with impaired consciousness may be particularly vulnerable because their ability to express privacy preferences, assert personal boundaries and advocate for themselves is limited. To explore intensive care nurses' experiences of protecting privacy when caring for patients with impaired consciousness. A descriptive qualitative study was conducted with 20 intensive care nurses in Türkiye between March and April 2026. Data were collected through semi-structured online interviews and analysed using inductive thematic analysis. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research guidelines. Four themes were identified: the marginalisation of privacy under clinical priorities; structural and process-related constraints on privacy in intensive care; loss of subjectivity and the mechanisation of care in patients with impaired consciousness; and ethical and psychosocial implications of privacy violations. Privacy in intensive care is shaped not only by individual ethical awareness but also by workload, environmental conditions, care routines and communication practices. Patients with impaired consciousness have the same rights to privacy and dignity as other patients; however, their reduced ability to express preferences, assert personal boundaries and advocate for themselves may make privacy violations less visible and increase their dependence on nurses for protection. Protecting the privacy of patients with impaired consciousness in ICUs requires structured care routines, standardised bedside communication, minimisation of unnecessary exposure during procedures and targeted ethical awareness training to support dignity in everyday practice.

42844742.title: The Experience of Family Visits in the ICU: A Dual-Perspective Qualitative Study of Nurses and Family Members of Comatose Patients.
42844742.abstract: The intensive care unit (ICU) is a crucial place for treating patients in a coma. Visiting activities in this area are often restricted by strict infection control and safety regulations. In the study institution, visiting is limited to a fixed 30-min period each day, which is a relatively strict policy internationally. From the perspectives of both nurses and family members, this study explores the actual experiences of both parties during the limited visiting time, identifies the multiple challenges they face, and provides a basis for optimizing the humanized visiting strategy. A descriptive qualitative research method was adopted. From June to September 2025, 24 nurses and 25 family members of comatose patients from a tertiary hospital's ICU in China were selected as the research subjects. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, and themes were extracted using the inductive content analysis method. The research has distilled four core themes: (1) Waiting: Pre-Visit Burden, Anxiety, and Informational Uncertainty; (2) Encounter: Role Management and Individual Imbalance During the Visit; (3) Aftermath: Post-Visit Self-Adjustment and Continuation of Experience; (4) Undercurrent: Emotional Exhaustion and Role Strain in Long-Term Visiting. The visiting experience of ICU nurses and family members of comatose patients encounters multiple challenges at each stage-before, during, and after the visit. There is also long-term cumulative stress, and both parties lack adequate systematic support. Optimizing the visiting system requires the formulation of corresponding strategies that address the different needs of nurses and families, respectively. ICU nurses can develop standardized information-sharing lists and structured visiting guidance tools, enhance communication training, and establish an emotional support mechanism for both nurses and patients, in order to alleviate emotional exhaustion and optimize the quality of visits within the limited visiting time.

42842040.title: Real-World Deployment and Operational Evaluation of an On-Premise Thermal IoMT System in an Intensive Care Unit.
42842040.abstract: Thermal imaging provides a non-contact approach for continuous environmental monitoring in intensive care units, although most existing studies remain limited to controlled or experimental settings with limited real-world validation. This study aimed to design, deploy, and operationally evaluate a scalable, low-cost, on-premise thermal Internet of Medical Things system in a real intensive care unit. A distributed network of seven thermal acquisition nodes, scalable to thirteen beds, was implemented using embedded devices and radiometric infrared cameras. Thermal images were transmitted through the hospital Wi-Fi network to a local server for storage, indexing, and near real-time visualization. System performance was evaluated using operational metrics including end-to-end latency, throughput, availability, and connectivity incidents. During a 10-day structured evaluation, the system generated 5,763,312 thermal images (approximately 1.47 TB), achieving an aggregate acquisition rate of 6.67 images per second. After architectural optimization, mean latency decreased from 26,344 ms to 126 ms (99.52% reduction), with a median of 117 ms and a 95th percentile of 207 ms. Effective system availability reached 95.29%, with most incidents associated with transient wireless connectivity interruptions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of deploying a distributed thermal IoMT system in a real intensive care unit under hospital information technology governance, offering a preliminary reference model for on-premise, nonintrusive thermal sensing infrastructures in critical care, pending validation across additional institutional and hardware settings.

42839656.title: Research Priorities for Intensive Care Nursing: A Focus Group and Three-Round Delphi Consensus Study.
42839656.abstract: Research priorities for intensive care nursing have been set internationally but not in Japan. We aimed to identify national priorities and compare them with those reported elsewhere. Focus group interviews with 10 expert intensive care unit (ICU) nurses generated 65 categories, which 50 nurses rated over three modified Delphi rounds (consensus, median ≥ 70, then ≥ 80). Categories were restructured into 20 topics; 16 reached consensus. Five independent nursing researchers who had taken no part in the interviews or the Delphi rounds then appraised every topic for validity, applicability, utility and clarity; all 16 were endorsed, and one was reworded. Symptom management, post-intensive care syndrome prevention and ICU nurse education ranked highest, and education- and system-related topics formed about one-third of the agenda, suggesting workforce regulation shapes national research priorities alongside clinical need. The agenda gives Japanese academic societies, funders and post-graduate programmes an explicit basis for targeting research investment.

42837328.title: Patterns and Predictors of Self-Regulatory Fatigue Among Intensive Care Unit Nurses: A Person-Centered Latent Profile Analysis.
42837328.abstract: Intensive care units (ICUs) play a critical role in the public health emergency response system. ICU nurses are the backbone of critical care and must continuously engage in self-regulation while working in highly demanding environments, which may lead to self-regulatory fatigue. Self-regulatory fatigue may affect work engagement and patient safety. However, little is known about the profiles of self-regulatory fatigue among ICU nurses and the factors associated with profile membership. To identify profiles of self-regulatory fatigue among ICU nurses and examine factors associated with profile membership. A cross-sectional survey was conducted between February and August 2025. A total of 687 ICU nurses completed an online questionnaire that collected general demographic information and assessed self-regulatory fatigue, surface acting, and work engagement. Differences among latent profiles were examined using descriptive statistics, univariable analyses, and logistic regression analyses. Three latent profiles were identified: "Low self-regulatory fatigue (Class 1)," "Moderate self-regulatory fatigue (Class 2)," and "High self-regulatory fatigue (Class 3)," accounting for 32.3%, 52.7%, and 15.0%, respectively. In multivariable logistic regression analyses, lower work engagement was independently associated with membership in the moderate self-regulatory fatigue profile compared with the low self-regulatory fatigue profile. However, work engagement was not independently associated with membership in the high self-regulatory fatigue profile compared with the low self-regulatory fatigue profile. Associations of demographic and work-related factors with profile membership differed across the comparisons. The level of self-regulatory fatigue among ICU nurses showed a heterogeneous distribution, with over two-thirds of the participants classified into the moderate or high self-regulatory fatigue profiles. Identifying the sociodemographic and work-related predictors associated with self-regulatory fatigue profiles can facilitate the implementation of tailored interventions for specific subgroups and improve their effectiveness. The findings may help nursing managers understand the heterogeneous profiles of self-regulatory fatigue among ICU nurses. Identifying different profiles of self-regulatory fatigue may inform targeted strategies to alleviate such fatigue and promote continuous quality improvement.

42832483.title: Association between early post-insertion arterial oxygen tension and documented acute upper-body deep or central venous thrombosis in critically ill adults: A retrospective MIMIC-IV cohort study.
42832483.abstract: Abnormal oxygenation may influence thrombosis, but evidence in catheterized critically ill patients remains limited. We examined whether the first arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2) measured within 24 hours after qualifying invasive venous catheter insertion was associated with documented acute upper-body deep or central venous thrombosis during hospitalization. This retrospective observational cohort study used the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database, version 2.2 (MIMIC-IV v2.2) (2008-2019). Adult intensive care unit admissions were included when a qualifying invasive venous catheter was present and an arterial PaO2 measurement was obtained after insertion, within 24 hours, and while the catheter remained in situ. PaO2 was analyzed continuously and categorically (≤80, 81-100, and >100 mmHg). Logistic regression models sequentially adjusted for patient characteristics, laboratory measurements, catheter characteristics, measurement timing, inspired oxygen concentration, respiratory support, and non-respiratory organ dysfunction. Multiple imputation addressed missing covariate data, and patient-clustered robust standard errors accounted for repeated admissions. The cohort included 11,277 hospital admissions from 10,789 patients; 195 admissions (1.73%) had the primary outcome. In the unadjusted model, higher PaO2 was associated with lower odds of the outcome (odds ratio [OR] per 10-mmHg increase, 0.970; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.952-0.987), but this association attenuated after adjustment. In the fully adjusted model, PaO2 was not associated with the outcome (OR, 1.008; 95% CI, 0.989-1.027; P = 0.430). Most secondary analyses supported the primary result, although the 60-minute sensitivity analysis yielded adjustment-dependent estimates. In the complete cohort, a single early post-insertion PaO2 measurement was not independently associated with documented acute upper-body deep or central venous thrombosis. These findings do not support PaO2-based thrombosis risk stratification or modification of oxygen therapy for thrombosis prevention. Future studies should incorporate repeated oxygenation measurements and accurately timed, imaging-confirmed thrombotic outcomes.

42830476.title: Proton pump inhibitors use and clinical outcomes in critically ill patients with pulmonary fibrosis: A retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching.
42830476.abstract: ObjectiveProton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are prescribed in the intensive care unit (ICU), but their association with outcomes in patients with pulmonary fibrosis remains unclear.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database (v3.1). Propensity score matching (PSM) and multivariate regression models adjusted for baseline differences. Landmark, subgroup, dose-response, and exploratory drug-specific analyses were performed.ResultsAmong 551 patients, 286 (51.9%) received PPIs. After PSM, PPI use was associated with higher 30-day mortality (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.08-2.34; p = 0.019), 90-day mortality (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.15-2.30; p = 0.006), ICU mortality (OR 3.22, 95% CI 1.57-6.59; p = 0.001), and longer ICU stay (β 1.90, 95% CI 0.91-2.88; p < 0.001). Associations weakened in the 48-hour landmark analysis, with only 90-day mortality remaining significant (adjusted HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.02-1.90; p = 0.035). Exploratory drug-specific estimates varied across agents but were imprecise. In exploratory cumulative-dose analyses after PSM and adjustment, each 10-mg increase in omeprazole-equivalent exposure was associated with higher ICU mortality (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.01-1.10; p = 0.012) and longer ICU stay (β 0.34 days, 95% CI 0.28-0.40; p < 0.001), but not 30-day or 90-day mortality. Initial timing was not associated with mortality after PSM and adjustment but was associated with longer ICU stays. Subgroup associations were consistent, with an interaction between PPI and H2RA use for ICU length of stay.ConclusionsPPI exposure was associated with higher short-term mortality and longer ICU stay, although the associations weakened in the 48-hour landmark analysis, with only 90-day mortality remaining significant. Higher cumulative PPI doses were associated with higher ICU mortality and longer ICU stay. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation before informing changes in clinical practice.

42829989.title: Experiences of Intensive Care Nurses in Their Practice of Physical Restraint Among Patients: A Qualitative Study.
42829989.abstract: Although physical restraint causes mental and physical harm to patients, such practice occurs worldwide to ensure patient safety. It is non-standard practice for a number of reasons, including the lack of education, training, and protocol. This study aims to determine the experiences of nurses who apply physical restraint to patients. A descriptive phenomenological method was employed in this study, wherein semi-structured interviews were the data collection method. In this qualitative study, the data consisted of semi-structured individual interviews with nurses (n = 20). The data were analysed phenomenologically and were arranged with MAXqda 22 analysis software. The study complies with the COREQ checklist. Six main themes were found from the data. The themes were (i) experiences related to nurses' physical restraint procedures, (ii) ethical balance in nursing, (iii) nurses' emotions, (iv) the meaning of physical restraint, (v) nurses' observations regarding patients' reactions to physical restraints, and (vi) the experience of ethical dilemmas. The nurses perceived physical restraint as being uncomfortable, a necessity or an obligation, as beneficial for patients, and a practice seen as punishment. The findings showed that physical restraint elicited diverse thoughts and emotions among nurses, who reported difficulties in coping with these emotions and insufficient knowledge of restraint procedures. Nurses also described the need to protect patient safety while preserving patient autonomy, highlighting the ethical balance involved in decisions concerning physical restraint. This study has provided insight that can guide clinician nurses, educators, and policy-makers in improving physical restraint administration. The lack of knowledge held among nurses as to physical restraint procedures emphasizes the importance of education and training on this topic and can suggest areas of development for pertinent policies and guidelines. No patient or public contribution.

42829975.title: From Evidence to Bedside: A Qualitative Study of Mindlines in Critical-Care Physiotherapy Practice.
42829975.journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
42829975.abstract: Translating evidence-informed recommendations into routine critical-care physiotherapy remains challenging because clinical decision-making occurs within dynamic and context-dependent environments. The mindlines model provides a conceptual perspective for understanding how clinicians integrate research evidence with experiential, social, and contextual knowledge during everyday practice. However, its application in critical-care physiotherapy remains poorly understood. To explore how physiotherapists working in critical-care units develop and apply mindlines during clinical decision-making and how evidence-informed recommendations are integrated into routine practice. A qualitative exploratory study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 22 experienced physiotherapists from diverse critical-care settings.
