Participants had 5-20 years of ICU experience and were recruited through purposive sampling. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis following an inductive approach, with interpretation informed by the mindlines model. Reporting adhered to the COREQ. 32-item checklist. Five interconnected themes were identified: (1) experience as the primary driver of clinical reasoning, (2) interdisciplinary collaboration shaping decision-making, (3) contextual adaptation of evidence-informed recommendations, (4) time constraints influencing engagement with formal evidence and (5) organisational variation across institutional settings. Participants described integrating research evidence with accumulated clinical experience, multidisciplinary interactions, and contextual factors to support patient-specific decision-making in complex critical-care environments. Clinical decision-making in critical-care physiotherapy reflects the integration of evidence-informed recommendations with experiential, collaborative, and contextual knowledge through clinicians' mindlines. Recognising these knowledge-translation processes may inform educational, implementation, and organisational strategies that strengthen evidence-informed physiotherapy practice in critical-care settings.

42829914.title: Breaking the Silence: A Mixed-Methods Study of Barriers and Solutions to Incident Reporting in Critical Care Units.
42829914.journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
42829914.abstract: Incident reporting is a cornerstone of patient safety, particularly in critical care settings where patients are highly vulnerable to adverse events. Despite international efforts to promote safety reporting, underreporting persists, especially in low- and middle-income countries. Nurses, as frontline providers, are central to detecting and reporting incidents; however, psychological, organizational, and cultural factors often limit their engagement in reporting processes. To explore barriers to incident reporting among nurses working in critical care units and identify nurse-informed solutions to strengthen reporting practices and patient safety culture. A convergent mixed-methods design was employed. A convenience sample of 251 critical care nurses was recruited from eight critical care units of a university hospital. Quantitative data were collected using the researcher-developed Incident Reporting Survey (IRS), which underwent content validation and reliability testing. Descriptive statistics, t-tests, ANOVA, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression were performed using SPSS version 23. Qualitative data were obtained through two open-ended survey questions and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis framework. Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated during interpretation through triangulation to generate a comprehensive understanding of reporting barriers and potential solutions. Nurses reported limited awareness of reporting procedures and reluctance to submit reports. Major barriers included fear of blame and punishment, lack of anonymity, heavy workload, inadequate training, and limited managerial support. Qualitative findings reinforced these issues and further highlighted concerns about professional reputation, ineffective feedback mechanisms, and complex reporting systems. Incident reporting remains insufficient due to interconnected individual and organizational barriers. Cultural, educational, and system-level interventions-particularly non-punitive policies and leadership support-are essential to enhance reporting behaviors and strengthen patient safety outcomes.

42827233.title: Prognostic value of admission D-dimer in acute pancreatitis: association with disease severity and clinical outcomes in a retrospective cohort study.
42827233.abstract: Early risk stratification in acute pancreatitis (AP) is crucial for improving patient outcomes and guiding timely clinical management. D-dimer has emerged as a potential biomarker reflecting activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis and may assist in early risk stratification of patients with acute pancreatitis. However, its prognostic performance remains incompletely validated across different populations. This retrospective cohort study included 200 adult patients diagnosed with acute pancreatitis between March 2023 and March 2024 at a tertiary care hospital. Disease severity was classified using the Revised Atlanta Classification. Admission serum D-dimer was measured within the first six hours after hospital presentation. Admission D-dimer levels were analyzed in relation to clinical severity, BISAP and Ranson scores, ICU admission, length of hospital stay, and in-hospital mortality. Statistical analyses included non-parametric tests, correlation analysis, logistic regression, and ROC curve analysis to evaluate predictive performance. Two hundred consecutive patients, with a mean age of 58.1 ± 17.5 years and 54% male patients, were included in this study. Severity distribution showed 68.5% mild, 17% moderately severe, and 14.5% severe AP. Overall mortality was 7% (n = 14), and 56% (n = 112) required ICU admission. Admission D-dimer levels increased significantly with disease severity, with median values of 1534 ng/mL (mild), 1908.5 ng/mL (moderately severe), and 2960 ng/mL (severe). Non-survivors had markedly higher levels than survivors (3776.5 vs. 1663 ng/mL, p < 0.001). D-dimer showed significant positive correlations with BISAP (ρ = 0.6068), Ranson scores (ρ = 0.3425), and hospital length of stay. ROC analysis demonstrated good discriminatory ability for severe AP (AUC = 0.778; cutoff 2035 ng/mL) and good discriminatory performance for mortality prediction (AUC = 0.912; cutoff 2726 ng/mL, sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 80.1%). However, performance for predicting ICU admission was limited (AUC = 0.579). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that each 1-ng/mL increase in admission D-dimer level was independently associated with higher odds of severe AP (OR = 1.001, p < 0.001). Admission D-dimer is a simple and rapid biomarker associated with disease severity and mortality in acute pancreatitis. While it should not replace established scoring systems, it can serve as a valuable adjunct for early risk stratification, particularly for identifying high-risk patients. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate its clinical utility and define standardized cutoff values.

42826315.title: Sequential changes in serum adipokines and their clinical associations in critically ill COVID-19 patients: A prospective observational study.
42826315.abstract: Adipokines regulate metabolic and inflammatory pathways and may be altered during critical illness. We explored sequential serum adipokine concentrations and their associations with nutritional and clinical variables in critically ill COVID-19 patients. This prospective observational, exploratory study included 30 critically ill COVID-19 patients and 10 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Serum adiponectin, resistin, GLP-1, visfatin, IGF-1, leptin, and acylated ghrelin were measured at intensive care unit admission and on day 7. Biomarker-clinical correlations were analyzed using Spearman correlation, and the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure was applied to account for multiple biomarker comparisons. After false discovery rate correction, longer time to nutrition initiation remained inversely associated with day-7 adiponectin (ρ = -0.464, q = 0.027), GLP-1 (ρ = -0.568, q = 0.015), IGF-1 (ρ = -0.488, q = 0.022), leptin (ρ = -0.539, q = 0.015), and acylated ghrelin (ρ = -0.503, q = 0.021). Several adipokines showed exploratory associations with nutrition-initiation time in this small cohort of critically ill COVID-19 patients. These observational findings do not establish that earlier nutritional support causes changes in adipokine concentrations and require validation in larger, adequately controlled studies.

42823965.title: Association between lactate-to-albumin ratio and in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study.
42823965.abstract: Early risk stratification is critical for critically ill patients with ischemic stroke. The prognostic value of the lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) remains unclear in this population. This single-center retrospective cohort study enrolled adult ICU patients with ischemic stroke from West China Hospital. LAR was calculated using the first lactate and albumin values on ICU admission. Log-transformed LAR was adopted as the main exposure, and the primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression, ROC analysis, quartile stratification, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were performed among 749 patients with complete exposure and outcome data, of whom 576 had complete covariate data and comprised the primary multivariable regression cohort. A total of 749 patients were included, with an in-hospital mortality rate of 30.7%. In complete-case multivariable analysis (N = 576; deaths = 172), log-transformed LAR was independently associated with in-hospital mortality (OR = 1.44, 95%CI: 1.09-1.91, p = 0.010) after full adjustment. Each two-fold increase in LAR was associated with a 29% increase in mortality odds. The highest LAR quartile had a significantly higher mortality risk than the lowest quartile (OR = 2.16, 95%CI: 1.21-3.92). LAR showed modest predictive ability (AUC = 0.628). When modeled as a raw continuous LAR, the direction of association remained consistent but did not reach conventional statistical significance (OR 1.23; 95% CI 0.97-1.56; p = 0.083). Moreover, no significant interaction or non-linearity was found. Elevated LAR is independently linked to higher in-hospital mortality among critically ill ischemic stroke patients. It may serve as a simple adjunctive marker for early risk stratification.

42820788.title: Palliative Care Involvement in Relation to Rapid Response Events: A Focus on Care Intensity at the End of Life.
42820788.abstract: To examine current practice patterns of palliative care involvement in relation to rapid response (RR) events and to evaluate its association with ICU utilization and intensity of care received before death. Retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent a RR event. General medical, cardiology, oncology, and observation patients admitted to a tertiary care academic medical center in the United States. Adults (≥ 18 yr) with an RR event. None. A total of 903 RR events occurred in 616 unique patients. The palliative care team was involved in 110 of 616 (17.9%) patients. Palliative care (PC) involvement was not associated with differences in repeat RR events or ICU transfer rates following an event. In-hospital mortality or hospice discharge occurred in 32.0% (197/616). Palliative care was involved in 36.5% (72/197) of these patients. PC involvement was associated with lower intensity of care within 24 hours before death after adjustment for age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, pre-RR code status, and RR trigger (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.26; 95% CI, 0.14-0.47; p < 0.001; Brant test, p = 0.44). This finding remained across sensitivity analyses for oncology status, primary service line, ICU transfer, and advanced directive documentation. PC consultation occurred only before RR in 16 of 110 (14.5%), only after RR in 63 of 110 (57.3%), and both before and after in 31 of 110 (28.2%). In timing-stratified ordinal regression, PC consultation only after RR (aOR, 0.19; 95% CI, 0.10-0.38; p < 0.001) or both before and after RR (aOR, 0.22; 95% CI, 0.09-0.56; p = 0.002) was associated with less-intense care, while pre-RR PC alone was not (aOR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.33-3.35; p = 0.93). Palliative services may be underutilized in the RR patient population, a group with a high in-hospital mortality rate; when palliative care is consulted, it may be associated with a reduction in the intensity of interventions at the end of life.

42956367.title: Data Stream and Hospital-Level Variation in Intensive Care Unit Vital-Sign Record Density Across Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV and eICU Collaborative Research Database: Retrospective Data Quality Study.
42956367.abstract: Electronic health record-derived process measures such as vital-sign record density are used for quality monitoring, risk prediction, and cross-system benchmarking, but whether they retain consistent meaning across sites and data streams is rarely tested. This study aimed to determine whether vital-sign record density varies primarily by data stream, database, contributing site, or care unit, and what follows for comparative use. We retrospectively analyzed the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) version 3.1 and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) version 2.0. Record density and timing metrics were computed for the first 24 intensive care unit hours from nurse-charted streams and, in eICU-CRD, from the monitor stream. Heart rate was primary; oxygen saturation and respiratory rate were replication variables. Variance was decomposed by database, hospital, and unit using η2 with hospital-clustered bootstrap inference and mixed-effects sensitivity analyses. A hospital-level plausibility floor of 12 nurse-charted heart rate observations per 24 hours was applied for the principal analysis; unrestricted and alternative-floor analyses are reported as sensitivities. A pooled-item MIMIC-IV heart rate count included alarm-limit documentation events, so label-based pooling mixes the two. In 117,572 eICU-CRD stays present in both streams, nurse- and monitor-derived counts were almost unrelated (Spearman ρ=0.024), with bottom-decile overlap at chance. Between-database η2 for record count was 0.960 against the eICU monitor stream and 0.026 against the nurse stream. Eight of 68 eICU-CRD hospitals fell below the plausibility floor and were excluded from principal estimates, a restriction introduced during review. Among the remaining 60 hospitals (88,560 stays), hospital η2 for record count was 0.354 (95% CI 0.259-0.450) against unit-within-hospital η2 of 0.043; for the interval-structure metrics, the hospital and unit components were not separable. For record count, the hospital component fell from 0.441 unrestricted to 0.321 at an hourly floor. A negative-binomial mixed model gave latent-scale hospital and unit variance-partition coefficients of 0.348 (95% CI 0.252-0.457) and 0.112 (0.078-0.163), equivalent to 0.318 and 0.110 observed. A pooled bottom-decile rule agreed with hospital-specific rules on 52.5% (4726/9006) of flagged stays, with 6 hospitals supplying half the pooled decile. The hospital component for record count replicated at 0.322 for oxygen saturation and 0.333 for respiratory rate. Within a multisite nurse-charted stream, vital-sign record volume varied more across contributing sites than across care units within hospitals; for the interval-structure metrics, the site and unit components were not separable at this cohort size. Apparent cross-database differences were reproduced by source-table choice, and site-level variation remained after excluding the most evident contribution-completeness outliers. Comparative use therefore requires specifying the generating stream, enforcing the analytic window, and explicitly modeling site-level variation; the residual site component should not be interpreted as documentation practice alone.

42956012.title: Serial ultrasound assessment of flexor carpi ulnaris and biceps brachii cross-sectional area in critically ill patients: A prospective cohort study.
42956012.abstract: Serial ultrasound measurements may help characterize muscle wasting in critically ill patients. The flexor carpi ulnaris (FCU) is a superficial forearm muscle that may provide an additional assessment site. We described longitudinal FCU and biceps brachii (BB) cross-sectional area (CSA) changes and explored between-muscle differences and clinical associations. This prospective two-center observational study enrolled 23 intensive care unit (ICU) patients; 20 were included in the analysis (median age, 57 years; range, 33-82). CSA was measured on days 0, 5, 7, and 14 after ICU admission. Analyses used Friedman tests, exact conditional Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction, and exploratory Spearman correlations. Post hoc between-muscle comparisons assessed participant-level percentage changes. Mean FCU CSA decreased from 1.36 to 1.08 cm² and mean BB CSA from 6.08 to 5.09 cm² over 14 days, corresponding to reductions of 20.9% and 16.4% in the unrounded group means. The median paired difference in percentage change (FCU minus BB) was -11.9 percentage points on day 7 (unadjusted p = 0.0023), meeting the Bonferroni threshold of 0.05/3. Differences on days 5 and 14 did not meet this threshold (p = 0.1429 and p = 0.2024). Baseline CSA values were correlated (ρ = 0.845, p < 0.001), as were 14-day percentage changes (ρ = 0.549, p = 0.0122); correlation p-values were unadjusted. Serial ultrasound documented decreases in FCU and BB CSA in this small cohort, with an exploratory direct comparison identifying a greater proportional FCU decrease on day 7. These findings support further evaluation of FCU ultrasound as an additional muscle-monitoring measure. Its value for earlier detection of muscle wasting or diagnosis of ICU-acquired weakness requires direct validation.

42955129.title: 24-hour risk updating for major ICU complications after severe trauma: a prospective cohort study.
42955129.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
42955129.abstract: Conventional trauma prognostic models rely primarily on admission data and cannot account for subsequent physiological response to treatment. We evaluated whether routinely collected physiological information available at 24 h provides incremental prognostic information for major intensive care unit (ICU) complications in severely injured patients. We conducted a prospective cohort of adults with severe trauma (Injury Severity Score [ISS] ≥ 15) admitted to the ICU between January 2024 and April 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of major respiratory, hemodynamic, renal, or septic complications during the ICU course. TRISS was compared with an admission ridge model incorporating ISS, Glasgow Coma Scale, hemoglobin, lactate, and international normalized ratio, and a 24-h updated ridge model additionally incorporating 24-h lactate and change in creatinine. Performance was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Among 109 patients, median ISS was 29 (IQR 20-38), and 73 (67.0%) developed major ICU complications. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 for TRISS, 0.873 for the admission model, and 0.887 for the 24-h updated model; Brier scores were 0.178, 0.140, and 0.131. Compared with the admission model, the 24-h updated model improved performance (ΔAUC 0.016, 95% bootstrap interval 0.004-0.030; ΔBrier - 0.010, - 0.017 to - 0.005). Twenty-four-hour lactate and creatinine change were the strongest contributors to the update. In severely injured ICU patients, incorporating physiological evolution during the first 24 h refined admission-based prognostic assessment. Lactate and creatinine trajectories provided incremental information for major ICU complications during the ICU course. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

42954240.title: Reducing Noise and Alarm Burden in Adult Intensive Care Units: An Integrative Review of Interventions and Implications for Nursing Management.
42954240.abstract: To synthesise evidence on noise-reduction and alarm-management strategies in adult intensive care units and examine their implications for nursing management. ICU noise and alarm burden present challenges for patient rest, clinical surveillance, nursing workflow and staff experience. Intervention effectiveness and sustainability remain uncertain. An integrative review guided by Whittemore and Knafl's framework synthesised empirical, implementation and review-level evidence identified through PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL and reference screening. Interventions addressed alarm management, environmental modification, quiet-hour practices, staff engagement and multicomponent implementation. Reported benefits varied across studies, and available evidence did not establish the superiority of bundled approaches. Direct evidence concerning workforce well-being, nursing leadership, clinical surveillance and sustained improvement was limited. Quiet ICU interventions may improve selected acoustic and alarm-related outcomes, but their comparative effectiveness and long-term sustainability remain uncertain. Nurse leaders may consider context-sensitive interventions supported by alarm governance, workflow integration, staff participation and ongoing evaluation. Future studies should assess nursing workload, clinical surveillance, patient safety and sustainability alongside acoustic outcomes.

42953146.title: [Clinical characteristics and in-hospital outcomes of patients receiving antithrombotic therapy in a cardiac intensive care unit in sub-Saharan Africa: a retrospective comparative study at the Cardiology Institute of Abidjan].
42953146.abstract: antithrombotic therapies are essential in the management of cardiovascular diseases but carry a risk of bleeding complications. This study aimed to describe the use of antithrombotic agents and associated complications in a Cardiac Intensive Care Unit, and to analyse trends in their prescription over time. we conducted a retrospective, observational, descriptive, and analytical study including 1,000 patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit of the Institute of Cardiology of Abidjan who received at least one antithrombotic therapy over 12 years. Data were collected in two phases, from 2013 to 2017 and from 2018 to 2024, allowing for the analysis of temporal trends. the mean age was 59.5 ± 14.1 years. Hypertension was the most prevalent cardiovascular risk factor, and acute coronary syndrome was the main indication for antithrombotic therapy. The proportion of patients receiving antithrombotic treatment increased significantly between the two study periods (76.5% vs 78.7%, p = 0.004). The use of fibrinolytic agents also increased significantly (2.6% vs 6.6%). Adverse events related to antithrombotic therapy were predominantly hemorrhagic, with independent risk factors including advanced age (>65 years), use of fibrinolytics, and concomitant use of multiple antithrombotic agents. In-hospital mortality was higher in patients with hemorrhagic events, with no significant difference between the two periods. antithrombotic therapies remain widely used in Cardiac Intensive Care Units in sub-Saharan Africa, with an increasing trend in prescriptions. Rigorous clinical and laboratory monitoring is essential to improve patient outcomes.

42952730.title: Machine learning-based risk prediction for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in non-neutropenic intensive care unit patients, with an exploratory analysis of pathogen-related risk factors.
42952730.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
42952730.abstract: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is increasingly recognized in non-neutropenic patients, but validated bedside risk stratification tools remain scarce. We developed a machine learning model to predict IPA and tested whether corticosteroid effect depends on bacterial co-pathogen. This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 837 non-neutropenic adults hospitalized with pulmonary infections across three tertiary hospitals in China between December 2020 and December 2025. The discovery cohort was split into training and internal validation sets. Four classifiers were compared, with Random Forest selected for optimal performance. The final model was externally validated in an independent cohort. Feature importance was assessed using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis. Corticosteroid-bacteria interactions were examined using subgroup analyses and propensity score matching, with the synergy index S calculated to quantify biological interaction. A simplified bedside score was derived from the top-ranking predictors. The Random Forest model achieved external validation AUC of 0.865. Six predictors consistently dominated across all assessments: Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation, hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 <200 mmHg), diabetes mellitus, organ failure (Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, SOFA >5), lymphopenia (lymphocyte count <0.8×109/L), and ICU (intensive care unit) admission. Corticosteroid exposure did not rank among the top six predictors. However, its association with IPA diverged sharply by bacterial context: OR below 1 with P. aeruginosa (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.214-1.283) but OR above 1 with other Gram-negative bacilli (OR 2.17, 95% CI 0.722-6.535); P for interaction = 0.131; a directional pattern that persisted after propensity matching. The six-variable score derived from these predictors showed AUCs of 0.869 (training), 0.774 (internal validation), and 0.719 (external validation). IPA risk in non-neutropenic ICU patients is shaped more by bacterial co-pathogen context than by corticosteroid exposure alone. The divergent corticosteroid effects across bacterial species challenge the conventional assumption of a uniform steroid-associated risk. The externally validated six-variable score offers a practical, software-free tool to support pathogen-informed, individualized risk stratification and clinical decision-making in the ICU.

42952351.title: How Preceptors Can Cultivate Professional Identity Formation Through Meaningful Participation in Experiential Learning.
42952351.journal: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
42952351.abstract: When engaged in experiential learning, trainees enter a complex ecosystem where expertise relies on collaboration and the intentional use of environmental resources. To better explain this learning environment, this paper will define and describe concepts of educational theory related to situativity theory and the cognitive ecosystems perspective and offer ways to apply them to experiential learning design using an intensive care unit (ICU) as an example practice setting. By viewing the ICU as a cognitive ecosystem, we highlight how recognition and use of available resources and opportunities can support trainee growth and development of a contextualized, or situated, professional identity. Traditionally, experiential learning has emphasized internal mental processes, focusing on how trainees assess patients and recognize medication-related problems. However, expertise extends beyond individual knowledge and includes the ability to recognize and interact with the physical and social elements that exist within the clinical environment. Although the interconnected nature of clinical practice is widely recognized, limited guidance exists for applying situativity theory and cognitive ecosystems to experiential learning design. Viewing a practice setting as a cognitive ecosystem provides a lens for intentionally immersing trainees within the environment to promote meaningful participation in clinical practice. When viewed through this lens, microsystems within the practice setting emerge that support clinical reasoning, communication, and patient care. Across these microsystems, interactions with the resources and people within the environment may promote the development of clinical reasoning and situated professional identity. Intentional interactions within each microsystem can help trainees progress from an observational role to active participation in patient care, progressing beyond basic knowledge acquisition and recall. Using the ICU as an example, we argue that viewing the practice area as a cognitive ecosystem offers opportunities for experiential learning design for preceptors, along with enriching experiences for trainees that are critical for professional identity formation.

42952243.title: Psychological Distress Among Black Surrogates of Intensive Care Unit Patients: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
42952243.abstract: Anticipatory grief and Post-Intensive Care Syndrome-Family (PICS-F) are increasingly recognised as important sources of psychological distress among family members of critically ill patients. However, these experiences remain understudied among Black surrogate decision-makers. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between anticipatory grief and PICS-F and to examine whether emotional closeness and positive religious coping were associated with anticipatory grief among Black family surrogates of intensive care unit (ICU) patients. In this cross-sectional survey study, 70 Black surrogate decision-makers of adult ICU patients were recruited from ICUs at a large metropolitan hospital in the Midwestern United States. Participants completed measures of emotional closeness, positive religious coping, anticipatory grief, anxiety, depression and post-traumatic stress symptoms. Multivariable linear regression analyses examined associations among study variables. Emotional closeness and positive religious coping were not statistically significantly associated with anticipatory grief. Anticipatory grief was statistically significantly associated with higher PICS-F symptoms. Among Black ICU surrogate decision-makers, anticipatory grief was associated with greater psychological distress, suggesting it may represent an important target for future supportive interventions and research.

42952127.title: QUIET Care: A Nursing-Led Conceptual Analysis of Alarm-Related Acoustic Burden in Adult Critical Care.
42952127.abstract: Adult intensive care units (ICUs) generate a persistent acoustic burden from alarms, care activity, equipment and communication. This burden can undermine patient rest and contribute to alarm fatigue, cognitive workload and distress among nurses. To present a nursing-led conceptual framework for addressing alarm-related acoustic burden in adult critical care. Literature-informed conceptual analysis. A structured purposive evidence map was audited using two PubMed searches run on 9 September 2026 (3377 unique records after PMID deduplication) and citation checking. Twenty-nine selected sources were charted against the five domains. This was not a systematic review; no original data, formal consensus or framework validation was undertaken. QUIET Care proposes five connected practice domains: quantify and qualify the sound environment; use patient-specific monitoring and alarms; integrate quiet into workflow; engage people and culture; and track, test and learn. It treats the domains as locally adaptable hypotheses and requires explicit safety balancing measures. QUIET Care is a pragmatic proposal for local co-design and evaluation, not a validated intervention or universal sound target. The framework may help critical care nurses and leaders organise source mapping, alarm customisation, workflow redesign, team ownership and small safety-monitored tests of change while preserving the audibility of urgent alerts.

42951696.title: Network Analysis of Factors Influencing ICU Patient Transfer Readiness: A Social-Ecological Model Approach.
42951696.abstract: ICU transfer readiness is a multidimensional state influenced by informational, functional, emotional and support-related needs. Network analysis can clarify how readiness indicators and emotional distress co-occur as a system, rather than as independent factors. To (1) model conditional associations among ICU transfer-readiness indicators and anxiety/depressive symptoms and (2) identify highly connected and highly predictable targets that may be prioritised in transitional-care interventions. Transfer readiness was measured using the ICU Transfer Readiness Scale (15 items; 0-10) and emotional distress using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS; 14 items; 0-3). A regularised mixed graphical model (MGM) was estimated to accommodate mixed/ordinal data. Edge-weight accuracy, centrality robustness and node predictability (R2) were assessed using bootstrap procedures. Age and gender were included as background variables. A total of 276 ICU patients were included in the analysis. The estimated network showed a clear modular structure: transfer-readiness indicators clustered into personal status, disease knowledge, coping after transition and expected-support domains; HADS symptoms clustered into anxiety and depression domains. Within transfer readiness, the strongest association occurred between two expected-support indicators, suggesting perceived support is tightly interlinked. Within HADS, multiple strong within-subscale connections were observed for both anxiety and depression symptoms. Node predictability ranged from 0.224 to 0.633 (mean 0.434), with the highest predictability for key readiness indicators in the knowledge/coping domains (R2 ≈0.63). Bootstrap analyses supported acceptable stability of the main edge and centrality patterns. Demographic nodes showed comparatively weaker and more cautious-to-interpret associations. ICU transfer readiness and emotional symptoms form structured conditional interdependencies, indicating readiness should be conceptualised and addressed as a connected system rather than isolated determinants. Transitional-care strategies may be strengthened by prioritising highly connected/predictable readiness targets-particularly expected support and key knowledge/coping indicators-while concurrently screening for and addressing anxiety/depressive symptoms to improve transfer preparation and early post-transfer adjustment.

42949044.title: Associations of International Normalized Ratio and Hematocrit With Stroke Status and Machine Learning Mortality Prediction in Critical Care Databases.
42949044.abstract: Stroke is a major cause of mortality and long-term disability. This retrospective cohort study evaluated associations of international normalized ratio (INR) and hematocrit (Hct) with stroke status in 29,831 adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). Stroke status was identified using predefined International Classification of Diseases, Ninth and Tenth Revision codes. INR and Hct were defined using the first measurements within 24 h after ICU admission. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, quartile analyses, restricted cubic splines (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses. Primary analyses used complete-case cohorts, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. A post hoc exploratory secondary analysis among patients with stroke used Cox regression to identify six prognostic variables for machine learning-based prediction of ICU mortality. Stroke proportions decreased across increasing INR quartiles and increased across increasing Hct quartiles. After full adjustment, each 1-unit increase in INR was associated with lower stroke odds, with odds ratios (ORs) of 0.105-0.395 across cohorts, whereas each 1-percentage-point increase in Hct was associated with higher stroke odds (ORs, 1.076-1.103). RCS analyses supported overall associations but not consistent nonlinearity after full adjustment. Multiple-imputation results were directionally consistent. The gradient boosting machine (GBM) model yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.717 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.669-0.766), 0.670 (95% CI, 0.603-0.737), and 0.630 (95% CI, 0.557-0.703) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. INR was inversely associated and Hct positively associated with stroke status. These observational associations require cautious interpretation; the exploratory ICU mortality analysis provides a complementary prognostic perspective among patients with stroke.

42947852.title: Development and validation of a simple clinical prediction model for post-stroke seizures in critically ill patients: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
42947852.abstract: Post-stroke seizures (PSS) are common in critically ill stroke patients, but ICU-specific risk prediction tools are lacking, and the independent impact of PSS on mortality remains controversial. This retrospective multicenter cohort included 6,586 adult stroke patients from 208 US ICUs in the Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). Patients were randomly divided 7:3 into training and internal validation sets. The primary endpoint was coded in-hospital post-stroke seizures identified via diagnosis codes during the index hospitalization. Candidate predictors were screened using logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were, respectively, evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration slopes and calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to evaluate the association between PSS and in-hospital mortality and length of stay. The overall incidence of coded in-hospital PSS was 7.5%. Head-to-head comparison identified SOFA as the best-performing routine ICU severity score for coded PSS prediction, outperforming GCS, OASIS and APACHE II. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified five independent clinical predictors for coded in-hospital PSS: younger age, elevated admission body temperature, pre-existing hypertension, lower mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration, and lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score. The model achieved AUCs of 0.702 in the training set and 0.713 in the validation set, with stable performance across age, gender, and stroke subtype subgroups. A three-tier bedside risk stratification was derived, with observed coded PSS rates of 3.4, 6.8, and 16.2% for low-risk, intermediate-risk, and high-risk groups. After PSM, coded PSS was not associated with increased in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR = 0.84, p = 0.295) or prolonged hospital stay (mean difference = -0.30 days, p = 0.167). We developed and internally validated a simple prediction model for coded in-hospital PSS in critically ill stroke patients. Coded PSS itself was not independently associated with increased mortality. This model remains a research tool that has not undergone external validation and cannot yet guide real-world clinical monitoring or pharmacological intervention. These findings are applicable to clinically evident, coded convulsive seizures and may not generalize to non-convulsive seizure phenotypes.

42947212.title: Association between operative duration and prolonged intensive care unit stay for more than 24 h in lung cancer patients following thoracoscopic lobectomy: a retrospective cohort analysis.
42947212.abstract: Lung cancer remains the primary cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While prolonged operative duration is increasingly recognised as a modifier of surgical risk, its independent association with prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay for more than 24 h following thoracoscopic lobectomy remains inadequately quantified. This study evaluated the association between operative duration and prolonged ICU stay for more than 24 h, including underlying dose-response relationships. We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Informative Surgical Patient dataset for Innovative Research Environment (INSPIRE) database, analysing 2545 surgical cases diagnosed with malignant bronchial or lung neoplasms undergoing curative-intent thoracoscopic lobectomy (2011-2020). Multivariable logistic regression, a generalised additive model, and a two-piecewise linear regression model were employed to assess the effect of operative duration on prolonged ICU stay for more than 24 h, adjusting for potential confounders. The cohort comprised 2545 surgical cases. After adjusting for potential confounders, operative duration demonstrated an independent association with prolonged ICU stay for more than 24 h (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 1.2; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-1.36; P = 0.004). A nonlinear relationship was identified, with an inflection point at 2.39 h. Below this threshold, the OR was 2.967 (95% CI, 1.995-4.414); above it, the OR was 0.802 (95% CI, 0.633-1.015). Operative duration exhibits a nonlinear, time-dependent association with prolonged ICU stay for more than 24 h following thoracoscopic lobectomy in lung cancer patients, persisting after rigorous confounder adjustment. The identified threshold of 2.39 h provides an evidence-based benchmark for surgical quality improvement initiatives. The current secondary analysis was exempt from research registration. The INSPIRE dataset part was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov under the Unique Identifying Number (UIN) NCTO2914444 and is publicly available at https//clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCTO2914444.

42945236.title: Association of a structured prevention algorithm with nurse knowledge and device-related pressure injury severity in critical care: A pre‑post study.
42945236.abstract: Medical Device-Related Pressure Injuries (MDRPI) are a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), yet structured prevention algorithms are lacking. This single-group, pre-test/post-test quasi-experimental study was conducted in the General Intensive Care Unit from February 2025 to April 2025. The sample comprised 38 nurses and 77 patients (39 pre-intervention, 38 post-intervention). Nurses' knowledge was assessed using the MDRPUKQ questionnaire, and patient outcomes were monitored using baseline and post-intervention data on pressure injury prevalence and severity. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26, employing descriptive and inferential statistics including paired t-tests, independent t-tests, chi-square tests, Fisher's exact tests, and multivariable logistic regression. The mean knowledge score increased significantly from 57.74 (SD = 11.15) before training to 89.55 (SD = 5.17) afterward (mean difference: 31.81, 95% CI: 28.35-35.27, P < 0.001, Cohen's d = 3.02). Overall, MDRPI prevalence decreased from 38.5% (95% CI: 24.9-54.1%) pre-intervention to 28.9% (95% CI: 17-44%). However, this difference was not statistically significant using Pearson's chi-square test (χ2 = 0.82, P = 0.365). The distribution of pressure injury stages before implementation was: Stage 1 (28.2%), Stage 2 (7.7%), and Stage 3 (2.6%). Following the intervention, prevalence dropped to Stage 1 (21.1%) and Stage 2 (5.3%), with no new Stage 3 injuries reported. After adjusting for potential confounders (age, Braden score, ICU length of stay, and device exposure duration), implementation of the algorithm was associated with reduced MDRPI occurrence (adjusted OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.19-0.91, P = 0.026). Implementation of the MDRPI prevention algorithm was associated with significant improvement in nurses' knowledge. A numerically lower prevalence was observed. This suggests that injuries caused by medical equipment are largely absent from current mandatory continuing education or postgraduate nursing curricula, reinforcing the need for a thorough review and the integration of this topic into standard educational programs.

42942949.title: Nutritional Status at Admission and Clinical Outcomes in Hospitalized Patients with COVID-19: Results from the MODIeCOSe in Italy Study.
42942949.abstract: Background/Objectives: Poor nutritional status is common among hospitalized patients and may adversely affect the response to severe acute illness. We investigated the association between nutritional status at hospital admission and clinical outcomes in patients hospitalized with COVID-19 during the first two pandemic waves in Italy. Methods: This retrospective multicenter study included 1187 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 across nine Italian centers participating in the MODIeCOSe in Italia registry. Nutritional status was assessed using the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, the Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI), and available anthropometric measures. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital death or transfer to an intensive care unit (ICU). Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the independent association between nutritional status and outcome. Results: Overall, 275 patients (23.2%) experienced the composite adverse outcome. CONUT score was higher in patients with an adverse than in those with a favorable outcome (4.4 ± 2.3 vs. 3.4 ± 1.8; p < 0.001), whereas PNI did not differ significantly. Patients with an adverse outcome also had lower body weight, BMI, waist circumference, and waist-to-height ratio, although anthropometric data were available only in subsets of the cohort. In the main multivariable model adjusted for admission PaO2/FiO2 and relevant clinical covariates, higher CONUT remained independently associated with adverse outcome (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.12-2.45 per 1-SD increase; p = 0.01). The association was similar in a sensitivity analysis excluding PaO2/FiO2 (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.28-2.49; p < 0.001). Conclusions: A higher CONUT score at admission was independently associated with an increased risk of in-hospital death or ICU transfer, supporting its prognostic relevance as an immuno-nutritional index in hospitalized patients with COVID-19.

42934773.title: Preserved anabolic skeletal muscle capacity in response to exercise and protein intake after critical illness.
42934773.abstract: Low muscle mass and persistent weakness are common after critical illness, but the mechanisms behind impaired recovery are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the skeletal muscle anabolic response to combined resistance exercise and protein intake in intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, compared to matched controls without a history of critical illness. We hypothesised that residual anabolic resistance limits muscle regeneration after ICU stay. Former patients were enrolled within 3 to 6 months of intensive care unit discharge. Muscle biopsies were obtained before and after resistance exercise using a flywheel leg extension ergometer, combined with ingestion of 24 g hydrolysed protein. Muscle protein fractional synthetic rate was determined from the incorporation of [ring-²H₅]phenylalanine into mixed-muscle protein during a primed continuous intravenous infusion. Anabolic and proteolytic pathways were measured using standard assays. Group-by-time differences were analysed using linear mixed models. The primary comparison was the between-group difference in pre-to-post change in muscle protein synthesis. Twenty ICU survivors (60 ± 12 years, 30% female, BMI 26.9 (IQR 22.9-28.7), SAPS 3 62.3 ± 15.8) and 20 age- and sex-matched controls were included. ICU survivors had significantly lower quadriceps muscle thickness (p = 0.02) and handgrip strength (p = 0.04) than controls. In ICU survivors, muscle protein synthesis from plasma precursor amino acids was higher at baseline than in controls (0.041%/hour vs. 0.030%/hour, p = 0.009), but increased less (Δ 0.031 vs. Δ 0.040%/hour, p = 0.04). Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis was similar between groups (0.071%/hour vs. 0.070%/hour, p = 0.70). At baseline, ICU survivors showed lower activation of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway. In both groups, the intervention increased anabolic signalling, decreased initiation of autophagy and increased parts of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. In ICU survivors with persistent muscle loss and weakness, the increase in muscle protein synthesis after combined resistance exercise and protein intake was smaller than in controls, in the context of a higher baseline fractional synthetic rate. Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis rates were similar between groups. These findings provide the first mechanistic support for structured exercise-nutrition rehabilitation to promote muscle recovery after critical illness. This study was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05261984), 2022-02-20.

42932524.title: International Retrospective Observational Study of Continual Learning for AI on Endotracheal Tube Placement from Chest Radiographs.
42932524.abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) models often underperform when deployed at new hospitals despite strong performance during development, creating a need for effective adaptation strategies that maintain institutional privacy. Continual learning (i.e., repeatedly retraining a model at each new hospital where it is deployed) can improve performance during and after deployment. To determine whether continual learning could improve model performance across diverse clinical settings without requiring data exchange between hospitals or complex computational setups, we performed a retrospective study of a convolutional neural network model for endotracheal tube (ETT) assessment, comparing three deployment approaches (original model deployment, hospital-specific fine-tuning, and continual learning across hospitals). The study included 2313 intensive care unit chest radiographs across 23 hospitals spanning 12 countries and 5 continents, with 1 hospital held out for external validation. Participants were adults (≥18 years of age) with ETTs placed in 2021 (or earlier if a hospital found too few cases from 2021), identified through standardized key word searches in hospital systems and verified by radiology reports where available. Each hospital contributed approximately 100 anteroposterior radiographs, with 50 used for training, as well as associated deidentified reports and metadata. Each image was preprocessed by the contributing hospital to remove identifiable features and was independently reviewed and annotated by two radiologists. Continual learning models achieved a significantly lower average ETT-carina error of 10.58 mm (standard deviation [±SD], 12.98 mm), compared with 12.49 mm (SD±, 15.37 mm) for models fine-tuned only at their deployment hospital and 16.39 mm (±SD, 21.56 mm) for the original model. In addition, continual learning models outperformed the original model at all hospitals, and they outperformed models fine-tuned only at their deployment hospital at 21 of 22 hospitals. Despite using only 50 training data points from each hospital, continual learning surpassed traditional fine-tuning as a method for improving medical AI model generalization.

42928158.title: Parental perspectives on clinician guidance in value-laden NICU conversations: a qualitative study.
42928158.abstract: Value-laden decisions about life-sustaining treatment for critically ill infants in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) present profound emotional and ethical challenges for parents and clinicians. In such situations, clinicians must balance providing guidance with respecting parental autonomy. We explored parental perspectives on clinician guidance and effective communication during these decisions. We conducted a secondary qualitative analysis within a randomized clinical trial using parental free-text responses to a simulated neonatal decision-making scenario. The study was carried out online between February and April 2024 in Switzerland, Germany, and Austria. Eligible participants were German-speaking parents of preterm infants with prior NICU experience, recruited through patient and parent organizations. Data were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. Among 128 participants (84% female), parents emphasized the importance of clear, detailed, and evidence-based information about their child's condition and treatment options, as well as empathetic, honest, and individualized communication. They valued sufficient time for discussion and reflection, access to second opinions, and attention to the child's quality of life. Parents appeared to retain a sense of decision ownership, while differing in their preferences regarding clinician guidance. Some welcomed explicit recommendations, whereas others preferred neutral, value-sensitive communication that preserved space for independent deliberation. Parents facing complex medical decisions value both high-quality information and empathetic and honest communication. While they generally retain decision ownership, preferences regarding clinician guidance vary, suggesting that clinicians should actively explore how much direction parents want and tailor their communication accordingly. ISRCTN registry under number ISRCTN16123073, registration date: 17/01/2024, ( https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN16123073 ).

42927910.title: Swedish Consensus Recommendation for Follow-Up After ICU Stay.
42927910.abstract: A substantial proportion of intensive care unit (ICU) survivors experience long-term physical, psychological and cognitive impairments after critical illness. However, methods for identifying patients in need of post-ICU support vary widely. As a result, many patients are left without access to established rehabilitation pathways. This consensus recommendation provides a framework for the organisation and content of follow-up for adult ICU survivors in Sweden, informed by available evidence, stakeholder perspectives and expert consensus. The National System for Knowledge-Driven Healthcare Management (NPO) in Sweden commissioned the development of a practice recommendation for the follow-up of critically ill adults. Multidisciplinary experts in ICU survivorship formed a task force group. A systematic literature search in four databases was conducted in 2024 to identify pre-existing systematic reviews on the topic. The literature was reviewed, assessed for quality and recommendations were developed based on the literature evidence. The draft was discussed among multiprofessional groups involved in follow-up, in workshops with critical care nurses (n = 30) and professionals responsible for follow-up clinics (n = 74) and among patient representatives (n = 4). The final draft underwent external peer review by representatives from relevant professional organisations, the national registry for intensive care and governmental agencies in Sweden. The consensus recommendation suggests that all adult patients with an ICU length of stay ≥ 48 h are recommended for follow-up, with an initial contact within 1 week of ICU discharge to assess clinical status, identify early problems and ensure continuity of care. Patients and their families are recommended to be offered an outpatient follow-up visit at 2-3 months after discharge, led by ICU clinicians and, when possible, delivered by a multidisciplinary team. Validated screening tools and objective tests are recommended to assess relevant outcomes, including post-traumatic stress, anxiety, depression, cognitive impairment, physical function and Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) as appropriate. Patients with identified problems should be referred to appropriate healthcare providers or specialist services for further management. This consensus recommendation provides a framework for patient selection, timing and assessment to support a more structured and equitable management of post-intensive care syndrome. Systematic follow up of ICU survivors after hospital discharge is needed in order to assess long-term patient-centred outcomes. This is a consensus set of recommendations and not a GRADE-based clinical practice guideline for doing this, which can be considered by relevant ICUs.

42924620.title: Concept Analysis of Building Rapport in the ICU.
42924620.abstract: Building rapport, understood as establishing a meaningful and trusting relationship through interpersonal interactions between healthcare professionals and patients or their family members, was described in research as early as the 1960s. Although studies highlight its importance in clinical relationships, the concept remains largely undefined, with limited research on experiences of rapport among family members of intensive care unit patients. This concept analysis can help to provide conceptual clarity for future practice and research. This paper aimed to analyse and define the concept of 'building rapport' with ICU family members. The concept analysis framework of Walker and Avant was used, following the systematic steps of identifying uses, attributes, antecedents, consequences and model cases. Data were obtained from Swedish and English dictionaries and peer-reviewed articles identified through a systematic literature search and screening. Titles and abstracts were reviewed, and six studies were selected based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. This analysis clarifies the previously undefined concept of building rapport from the perspective of ICU family members. Building rapport is characterized by empathy and mutual understanding. Key antecedents include communication, time and relationships, while consequences are increased trust and the development of a care partnership. An empirical referent is a shift from family members as passive recipients to active participants in care. Key features of building rapport with ICU family members are empathy and mutual understanding, supported by communication, time and relationships. The findings suggest that rapport may facilitate family participation and care partnerships in intensive care. However, the findings should be interpreted in light of the limited empirical basis and the absence of formal quality appraisal. Clarifying the concept of building rapport may support communication training, reflective practice and active listening strategies that strengthen partnerships with ICU family members.

42922785.title: Epidemiological profile of people with accidental tetanus admitted to the intensive care unit of a public hospital: a retrospective study, Fortaleza, 2017-2024.
42922785.journal: Epidemiologia e servicos de saude : revista do Sistema Unico de Saude do Brasil
42922785.abstract: To analyze the epidemiological profile of people with accidental tetanus admitted to an intensive care unit in Fortaleza from 2017 to 2024. This was a retrospective cohort study conducted in a public hospital in Ceará, Brazil. Individuals aged ≥18 years with a confirmed diagnosis of tetanus, regardless of sex, admitted to the intensive care unit between January 2017 and May 2024, were included. One medical record with insufficient sociodemographic and clinical data was excluded. A total of 44 participants were included in the study, most of whom were male (n=41), predominantly aged 20-40 years (n=20); married (n=19); self-identified as Brown (Brazilian mixed race) (n=40); and had incomplete elementary education (n=20). Most resided in Fortaleza (n=18). Workers in the agricultural and livestock sector (n=14) were the most represented occupational group. The most frequent entry site was the feet (n=15). Most participants were unaware of their vaccination status (n=26). Being 60 years or older (odds ratio OR 11.6; 95% confidence interval 95%CI 1.9; 70.2; p-value 0.003) and smoking (OR 9.8; 95%CI 1.1; 88.2; p-value 0.019) were significantly associated with death as an outcome. The majority of participants were working-age men with incomplete elementary education, primarily employed in the agricultural and livestock sectors. Being 60 years of age or older and smoking were significantly associated with a higher likelihood of death.

42922190.title: A quality improvement initiative in hospital-based speech-language pathology: development and evaluation of a Lean-Agile management model.
42922190.journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
42922190.abstract: Hospital-based speech-language pathology (SLP) plays a strategic role in the care of critically ill patients, particularly in dysphagia management. However, high service demand and limited resources highlight the need for structured management approaches. This quality improvement (QI) study describes the implementation of a Lean-Agile management model and the establishment of a baseline of clinical care indicators to support dysphagia management in a high-complexity hospital setting. This QI initiative used a retrospective descriptive design and was conducted in a high-complexity quaternary public hospital in São Paulo, Brazil. The model comprised four phases: process mapping and value chain construction; clinical demand management using a Kanban-inspired prioritization system; continuous monitoring through predefined process and outcome indicators; and evaluation through retrospective analysis of 1312 adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients receiving dysphagia management between January 2024 and June 2025. Oral intake status was classified using the Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS). Descriptive statistics were used, and proportions are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) (Wilson method). The mean daily service coverage rate was 73%, corresponding to 33 patients seen per day out of a mean daily active demand of 45 patients across 100 ICU beds. The overall prevalence of dysphagia (FOIS 1-5) was 88.95% (95% CI: 87.1%-90.5%), and dependence on an alternative feeding route at initial assessment (FOIS 1-3) was observed in 54.65% (95% CI: 51.9%-57.3%) of patients. The favourable swallowing outcome rate was 80.55% (95% CI: 77.8%-83.0%; N = 869), and the alternative feeding route weaning rate was 77.28% (95% CI: 73.4%-80.8%; N = 493). Unfavourable outcomes were predominantly attributable to poor functional prognosis (52.05%) and clinical severity (30.41%), whereas process-related failures accounted for only 0.5% of the total sample. The Lean-Agile management model provided a structured approach to organizing SLP services in a high-complexity ICU setting and enabled the establishment of a baseline of dysphagia care indicators. Most unfavourable outcomes were attributable to patients' underlying clinical conditions rather than service-related factors. These findings may inform service planning and quality monitoring in similar hospital contexts, pending multicentre evaluation.

42912175.title: Evaluating Humanisation in Intensive Care Nursing Practice: An Exploratory Study Using the HUMAS Scale.
42912175.journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
42912175.abstract: Humanised care is central to nursing practice, yet sustaining relational and emotionally responsive care may be particularly challenging in intensive care environments characterised by technological complexity, clinical instability and repeated exposure to suffering. Humanisation should therefore be understood not as a single professional attribute, but as a multidimensional and context-dependent aspect of nursing practice. To explore humanisation-related dimensions among nurses working in an adult intensive care unit using the Healthcare Professional Humanisation Scale (HUMAS). An exploratory cross-sectional study was conducted among 32 nurses working in an adult intensive care unit. Humanisation-related dimensions were assessed using the Healthcare Professional Humanisation Scale (HUMAS). Descriptive analyses were used to examine scores across the dimensions evaluated by the instrument. Sociability showed the highest mean score (4.4), followed by self-efficacy (3.9), optimistic disposition (3.7), affection (3.6) and emotional understanding (2.9). These aggregated means describe a numerical pattern within this sample. In the absence of reported measures of variability or statistical comparisons, they cannot establish differences between dimensions or explain how nurses expressed these attributes in clinical practice. The findings provide an exploratory description of humanisation-related dimensions among intensive care nurses and suggest that humanisation in this setting should be considered as a multidimensional construct. Further research using larger samples and more comprehensive statistical analyses is needed to examine these dimensions and their expression in intensive care practice.

42912173.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practice Behaviours Regarding Intravenous Drug Incompatibilities Among Intensive Care Unit Healthcare Professionals: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
42912173.journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
42912173.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, clinical attitudes, and behavioural responses of healthcare professionals regarding IV drug incompatibility, identify gaps between knowledge and practice, and determine areas for improvement. A cross- sectional online survey was conducted in Türkiye among physicians and nurses with intensive care unit (ICU) experience. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing knowledge levels, attitudes, and perceived barriers. A total of 380 healthcare professionals participated. Overall knowledge levels were moderate to high (mean score: 10.4 ± 2.2). Most participants recognised the serious clinical consequences of IV drug incompatibility and emphasised its importance for patient safety. However, adherence to standard guidelines was limited, and time constraints and workload were reported as major barriers. Multivariate analysis revealed that nurses had significantly lower knowledge scores than physicians (β = -1.64; 95% CI: -2.15 to -1.13). Despite high awareness, knowledge was not consistently translated into practice. These findings highlight the importance of system-level interventions rather than solely individual-focused training. However, the findings should be interpreted in light of the cross-sectional design, convenience sampling, and reliance on self-reported data.

42908818.title: A machine learning-driven and explainable prediction model for in-hospital mortality in patients with diabetes mellitus and congestive heart failure: integrating XGBoost and SHAP approaches.
42908818.abstract: Patients with congestive heart failure (CHF) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are at elevated risk of in-hospital mortality, particularly in intensive care units (ICUs). Conventional scoring systems may not fully capture the clinical complexity of such comorbidities. This study aimed to construct an interpretable machine learning model to predict in-hospital mortality in this high-risk group. A retrospective study included 573 ICU patients with CHF and T2DM admitted to three hospitals in Henan, China (Jan 2025-Jun 2026). Seven predictors-body mass index (BMI), myocardial infarction, mild liver disease, SOFA score, LODS score, white blood cell (WBC) count, and serum creatinine-were identified via stepwise logistic regression. XGBoost and four other machine learning algorithms (KNN, SVM, CatBoost, AdaBoost) were trained and evaluated. Model performance was assessed using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was used to interpret XGBoost predictions. XGBoost achieved the best performance (AUC 0.917, sensitivity 86.8%, specificity 96.6%, accuracy 74.8%). SHAP analysis indicated that mild liver disease, LODS score, BMI, WBC count, and SOFA score were the top contributors, jointly explaining over 77% of the predictive power. Myocardial infarction, liver disease, elevated WBC, and higher SOFA/LODS scores increased mortality risk, while higher BMI and serum creatinine were protective-supporting the obesity paradox and sarcopenia hypothesis. An XGBoost model with SHAP interpretation provides accurate, explainable prediction of in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with CHF and T2DM, offering a valuable tool for early risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

42908120.title: Intensive Care Nurses' Self-Reported Adherence to Evidence-Informed Microaspiration-Prevention Practices and Potential Implementation Determinants: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
42908120.abstract: To assess intensive care nurses' self-reported adherence to recommended microaspiration-prevention practices and explore potential implementation determinants. Multicentre, cross-sectional. From December 2024 to February 2025, nurses in 31 intensive care units at 17 hospitals in Henan Province, China, completed a questionnaire on 22 preventive practices and 43 implementation-related items informed by the Theoretical Domains Framework. Bivariate analyses, a fully adjusted three-level mixed-effects model accounting for unit and hospital clustering, and generalised estimating equation sensitivity analyses examined associations. Of 510 respondents, 476 were analysed. Mean adherence was 77.17/110 (70.15% of maximum), with basic care scoring highest (73.6%) and risk management lowest (67.2%). After adjustment, adherence was lower in units with 10-14, 15-19 and ≥ 20 beds than in those with < 5 beds; the 5-9-bed group did not differ. Both training exposures were associated with higher adherence in the primary analysis; only evidence-based practice training remained significant in the 14-item analysis. The lowest-scoring items concerned near-term implementation intention (3.10), competing priorities (3.21), and professional responsibility (3.29); the highest concerned time efficiency (4.19), workflow compatibility (4.15) and interest (3.94). Self-reported adherence varied across practices and domains. Intensive care unit bed capacity and training exposure were associated with adherence, and implementation-related findings identified potential areas for further investigation. Findings may guide intensive care unit nurses, nurse managers, and educators in strengthening targeted microaspiration-prevention training, clarifying responsibilities, integrating preventive practices into routine workflows, and reinforcing bedside supervision, particularly in units with 10-14, 15-19, or ≥ 20 beds. The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines were followed. Patient or Public Contribution: None.

42901492.title: Intensivists' Perspectives and Practices on Palliative Care in the ICU: A Nationwide Survey in Korea.
42901492.abstract: While many countries have made progress in integrating palliative care into intensive care units (ICUs), implementation remains highly context-dependent. In Korea, palliative care integration within ICUs remains limited, and intensivists' perspectives on its role and applicability have not been well studied. We conducted a nationwide, cross-sectional online survey of certified intensivists and fellows registered with the Korean Society of Critical Care Medicine between April and May 2024. The questionnaire explored knowledge and confidence in palliative care, current ICU practices, referral patterns, perceived barriers, and preferred strategies for integration. A total of 241 intensivists responded (response rate, 23.9%). Most agreed that palliative care should be incorporated into ICU care (97.1%) and were willing to make referrals (98.3%). Advance care planning, symptom management, and family decision-making were the most expected domains of support. However, fewer reported involvement in psychological support, end-of-life care, or bereavement services. Referral practices were more frequent in institutions with palliative care teams, while lack of resources, unsupportive institutional culture, and unclear processes were commonly cited barriers. Clinical guidelines, professional education, and reimbursement reform were identified as priority strategies for integration. Korean intensivists widely recognize the need for palliative care in the ICU but apply it within a limited scope. To strengthen integration, consensus on definitions, clear referral criteria, and supportive institutional and policy frameworks are required.

42900928.title: Emergency Severity Index Stratified by Post-Triage Lactate: Association with In-Hospital Mortality in Admitted Patients.
42900928.journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
42900928.abstract: The Emergency Severity Index (ESI) is a widely used triage tool in emergency departments (EDs) and is associated with adverse outcomes. Lactate has also been associated with mortality in various ED populations. This study evaluated whether lactate levels measured after triage at the treating physician's discretion are associated with in-hospital mortality across ESI levels in admitted ED patients. This study is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data from adult patients presenting to the ED of a Swiss tertiary care center in 2013, 2015, 2017, and 2019. The study included admitted patients who underwent post-triage lactate measurement at the treating physician's discretion. Only the first lactate value measured in the ED was analyzed and categorized as < 2.0, 2.0-3.9, and ≥ 4.0 mmol/L. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes were 30-day mortality and intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age and sex. Model discrimination was compared using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Among 3,909 patients admitted from the ED who had a lactate drawn (of 17,327 ED presentations during the study period; 22.6%), the median age was 72 years and 2,062 (52.8%) were male. In-hospital mortality occurred in 168 (4.3%), 30-day mortality in 258 (6.6%), and ICU admission in 698 (17.9%). In ESI levels 2 (n = 1,826) and 3 (n = 1,722), crude in-hospital mortality was similar (59 [3.2%] and 44 [2.6%], respectively), but varied after stratification by lactate level. In ESI level 2 patients, in-hospital mortality occurred in 24 (2.0%) among those with lactate < 2.0 mmol/L (n = 1,210) and in 18 (17.8%) among those with lactate ≥ 4.0 mmol/L (n = 101), corresponding to an age- and sex-adjusted absolute risk difference of 16.0% (95% CI, 8.8-23.3). In ESI level 3, in-hospital mortality occurred in 20 (1.6%) at lactate < 2.0 mmol/L (n = 1,254) and in 8 (15.1%) at lactate ≥ 4.0 mmol/L (n = 53), corresponding to a risk difference of 12.5% (95% CI, 3.7-21.3). Discrimination for in-hospital mortality was higher when lactate was considered alongside ESI (area under the curve [AUC] 0.844 versus 0.799; ΔAUC 0.045, 95% CI, 0.021-0.069), with smaller increases for 30-day mortality and ICU admission. In admitted ED patients who had lactate measured after triage at physician discretion, higher lactate levels were associated with increased in-hospital mortality across ESI levels, particularly among patients triaged as ESI levels 2 and 3.

42899333.title: Enhancing Palliative Care Integration in the Cardiac Surgical Intensive Care Unit: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Project.
42899333.journal: The American journal of hospice & palliative care
42899333.abstract: ObjectiveThe rate of unmet palliative care (PC) needs is high in critical care areas, especially in the surgical patient population, where PC involvement is notoriously late in the patient's clinical progression. This quality improvement project aimed to evaluate the ability of education, workflow delineation, and an evidence-based assessment tool to improve the integration of PC in a cardiac surgical intensive care unit (TICU).MethodsThis 12-week project utilized a pre-post intervention design to improve PC integration in a 16-bed TICU that serves cardiac, vascular and thoracic surgical, critical care patients. The intervention included education, workflow delineation, and an evidence-based frailty assessment (FA) implementation. PC consultation rate, advance care planning (ACP) note completion rate, and FA completion rate were measured to assess the feasibility and impact of this intervention on PC integration.ResultsA total of 313 patients were enrolled in this project. There was a 53.5% increase in palliative care consultation (P = 0.16), however the ACP note completion rate remained unchanged. The rate of FA completion rose from 0% to 30.4% (P < 0.0001).ConclusionFA is important in the setting of critical care, surgical patients. The outcomes of this project were similar to those of the existing literature, further revealing that ICUs are challenging care settings in which to connect patients with PC for the first time. Future studies on the effects of FA in the cardiac surgical patient population are warranted to find the most appropriate settings for assessment and associated interventions based on identifying a patient's frailty.

42896625.title: Integrated Single-Myofibre Multi-Omics Correlates Inflammatory State to Myosin Energetics in ICU-Acquired Weakness.
42896625.journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
42896625.abstract: Skeletal muscle atrophy is a pervasive complication of critical illness that worsens survival and recovery, yet remains poorly explained by current clinical or molecular markers. To directly connect disease-associated molecular states to the contractile machinery, this study combined sequential functional, transcriptomic and proteomic profiling of the same single human skeletal myofibres from critically ill patients in the intensive care unit with acquired weakness (ICU-AW) and controls. This integrated approach provides a framework for validating molecular signals directly within the cellular and biomechanical context. Differential expression analyses between control and ICU-AW myofibres show marked donor-level heterogeneity, with no differentially expressed features (FDR < 0.05). Ranked gene set enrichment analyses revealed distinct transcriptional and proteomic signatures between conditions, as well as a subtle yet conserved myofibre state enriched in ICU-AW, characterised by inflammatory and chemotactic gene programmes, intracellular structural remodelling and bioenergetic adaptation. Nineteen features were significantly (FDR < 0.05) altered at both RNA and protein levels from the same myofibre. Overall, these 19 overlapping features link an inflammatory transcriptional landscape to a proteomic shift toward mitochondrial and translational machinery, revealing a coordinated stress-adaptation programme with selective post-translational control in fibres from patients with ICU-AW. Further integration with the functional dataset revealed fibres in this state displayed selectively disrupted myosin dynamics, evidenced by prolonged ATP turnover time of myosin heads in their super-relaxed conformation, suggesting altered myosin energetics as a contributor to muscle dysfunction. These findings define a discrete, disease-associated myofibre state and validate a proof-of-concept integrative single-fibre framework for connecting multi-omic heterogeneity to molecular motor function in complex human disease. The identification of coordinated transcriptomic and proteomic programmes, validated through functional measurement, suggests that targeting this fibre state may offer new therapeutic opportunities in ICU-acquired dysfunction and related muscle disorders.

42891793.title: Clinical course and outcomes of diabetic ketoacidosis in pregnancy: a single-center experience.
42891793.abstract: We evaluated the obstetric and perinatal outcomes of pregnant women hospitalised with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and examined the association between clinical and laboratory parameters and admission to the intensive care unit (ICU). This retrospective observational study included 32 pregnant women managed for DKA between May 2019 and December 2025 at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital, comparing those admitted to the ICU with those who were not. The association of arterial pH and serum bicarbonate with ICU admission was examined using ROC analysis and logistic regression, and biochemical severity markers were compared between pregnancies with and without DKA-related adverse outcomes.
