Implementation approaches included: (A) building statewide governance infrastructure; (B) translating evidence into practice through standardized toolkits; and (C) strengthening communication, teamwork, and process outcomes. Impacts included: (D) demonstrated reductions in maternal and birth morbidity, including 45-95% reductions in early elective deliveries, 76-87% improvements in timely hypertension treatment, and national-level reductions in eclampsia and intensive care unit admissions; and (E) expansion of the collaborative mission toward contraceptive access, opioid use disorder care, and racial health equity. M/PQCs function as a form of primary and secondary prevention, institutionalizing evidence-based protocols before obstetric emergencies occur. M/PQCs' evolution from clinical safety bundles toward equity, access, and social determinants signals an expanding mandate. Future initiatives should prioritize disaggregated outcome reporting, health equity frameworks, and inclusion of community birth and outpatient settings to ensure M/PQC gains are equitably distributed.

42873574.title: Quantitative CT in the real-world evaluation of progressive pulmonary fibrosis; the REVISE PPF multicentre observational study.
42873574.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42873574.abstract: We assessed whether an FDA-cleared quantitative CT (qCT) tool (Brainomix, e-Lung) identifies progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) earlier than routine clinical diagnosis and evaluated the prognostic value of baseline and serial imaging biomarkers. Multicentre retrospective study involving University of Alabama (UAB), Weill Cornell Medicine (WCM) and University of Chicago (UChicago); n = 509. HRCTs were analysed with e-Lung to derive Weighted Reticulovascular Score (WRVS, %), Total Disease Extent (TDE, %), and e-Lung Volume (mL). Prespecified progression thresholds were an absolute WRVS increase of ≥ 3 percentage points, an absolute TDE increase of ≥ 1.5 percentage points, and a relative e-Lung Volume decline of ≥ 10%, over less than 2 years. We compared the earliest qCT progression date with recorded clinical PPF diagnoses, assessed clinically stable controls, and modelled associations with future PPF and mortality using adjusted time-varying Cox models. Among 200 patients with PPF and serial HRCTs meeting the prespecified timing criterion, qCT identified progression earlier in 78% (UAB), 83% (WCM), and 47% (UChicago), with mean lead times of 434, 847, and 220 days, respectively. Among 187 clinically stable patients meeting the same serial-imaging criterion, progression thresholds were met in 67%, 56%, and 42%, respectively. High-risk baseline WRVS (≥15%) predicted future PPF (OR 4.09, 2.48, and 2.30) and mortality (HR 2.03 pooled UAB/WCM; 2.75 UChicago). Per 1-percentage-point increase, adjusted mortality HRs were 1.15 and 1.19 for WRVS and 1.05 and 1.04 for TDE in pooled UAB/WCM and UChicago, respectively. Threshold crossings were also associated with mortality (WRVS: HR 6.50 pooled UAB/WCM, 4.05 UChicago; TDE: 7.60 and 3.26; e-Lung Volume: 8.20 and 2.59). qCT detects radiological progression months to years before clinical PPF diagnoses. Integrating e-Lung into ILD pathways could accelerate treatment decisions and personalize follow-up.

42873570.title: Differential effects of PM2.5 constituents on tuberculosis infection and disease progression in 40,379 student close contacts.
42873570.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42873570.abstract: Outdoor PM2.5 has been increasingly implicated in tuberculosis, yet evidence has largely focused on total PM2.5 mass and has usually considered Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis) infection and active tuberculosis separately. Whether specific PM2.5 chemical constituents differ in their associations with infection and subsequent progression to active disease remains unclear. To assess the associations of PM2.5 and five major constituents with M. tuberculosis infection and subsequent progression to active tuberculosis within the same high-risk population. We conducted two complementary analyses among student close contacts of tuberculosis patients from 458 schools in 12 cities in eastern China during 2020-2024. Daily residential outdoor exposures were assigned from daily modeled estimates of PM2.5 and five major constituents (sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, organic matter, and black carbon) on an approximately 10-km grid, which were interpolated to geocoded addresses. We first assessed associations between exposure averaged over the five years preceding contact screening and M. tuberculosis infection identified by the ESAT6-CFP10 skin test during the contact investigation. We then followed infected students identified at the contact screening to examine associations between time-varying annual exposure and progression to active tuberculosis. Among 40,379 students, 1,269 had M. tuberculosis infection, and 70 infected students progressed to active tuberculosis during follow-up. Each 1-µg/m3 increase in PM2.5 was associated with higher infection risk (OR: 1.043; 95% CI: 1.018, 1.068) and progression risk (HR: 1.094; 95% CI: 1.010, 1.185). All five constituents were positively associated with infection (ORs: 1.156-5.390). Sulfate, nitrate, and ammonium were also positively associated with progression to active tuberculosis (HRs: 1.462-2.680). The findings remained generally consistent in sensitivity analyses. In this large multi-city close-contact study, PM2.5 was associated with both M. tuberculosis infection and subsequent progression to active tuberculosis. Three secondary inorganic aerosol (SIA) constituents, namely sulfate, nitrate, and ammonium, showed the most consistent association patterns across the two outcomes. These findings reinforce the importance of overall PM2.5 control and support further evaluation of coordinated reductions in SIA precursor emissions.

42864513.title: Use of Desmopressin in Spontaneous Nontraumatic Intracerebral Hemorrhage Among Patients Taking Antiplatelet Therapy: Systematic Review and Bayesian Meta-analysis.
42864513.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy-associated intracerebral hemorrhage (APT-ICH) remains a significant neurological concern due to high morbidity and mortality among these patients. Early trials of desmopressin (DDAVP) suggested clinical benefit; however, the number of studies available at the time was limited. This systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis aim to answer whether administration of DDAVP among patients with APT-ICH improves clinical course. Five databases were searched for studies comparing DDAVP and placebo/control/usual care in patients with APT-ICH. Bayesian meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model with three different priors. A total of seven studies were included. There was no difference in overall mortality [odds ratio (OR) 1.23; 95% credible interval (CrI) 0.79-1.91], in-hospital mortality (OR 1.41; 95% CrI 0.88-2.26), or good functional outcome (OR 0.66; 95% CrI 0.34-1.31). Posterior distribution analysis suggested a possible increase in thromboembolic complications and the proportion of patients with poor neurological outcomes among patients on DDAVP. There is currently a lack of convincing evidence of benefit regarding the administration of DDAVP for patients with APT-ICH. Furthermore, there are several signals that raise concerns for harm.This review indicates that there is no clear, well-supported recommendation to administer DDAVP to patients with APT-ICH.The results of Bayesian meta-analysis reveal a concerning signal for harm with DDAVP administration.

42863114.title: Impact of Thoracotomy-Based Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation on Right Ventricular Functional Preservation.
42863114.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42863114.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction remains a critical determinant of outcomes following left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. We used a doubly robust inverse probability weighting based on propensity scores to evaluate the association between surgical approach and clinical outcomes in 187 consecutive patients (thoracotomy: n = 55; sternotomy: n = 132). The primary endpoint was RV systolic function in the early postoperative period, assessed by tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE). Despite comparable baseline RV performance and hemodynamics, the thoracotomy-based approach was associated with superior preservation of postoperative RV systolic function compared to median sternotomy (TAPSE: 12.0 vs. 11.0 mm, p = 0.001). In weighted regression models, median sternotomy was associated with a significant reduction in postoperative TAPSE (β = -0.085, p = 0.036) and a 35% relative increase in hospital length of stay (p = 0.015). Furthermore, accounting for heart transplantation as a competing risk, median sternotomy was associated with a significantly higher hazard of long-term mortality (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR]: 1.78, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.07-3.00, p = 0.027). These findings suggest that the clinical benefits of sternal-sparing techniques extend beyond acute functional protection. This surgical strategy supports the use of less invasive approaches to optimize both early recovery and long-term outcomes in the LVAD population.

42859267.title: Frontal cortical neuroinflammation and circulating biomarkers following cardiopulmonary bypass in sheep.
42859267.abstract: Cerebral hypoxia and neuroinflammation have been implicated in neurocognitive disorders following cardiac surgery, but their postoperative trajectory and relationship with circulating biomarkers are poorly defined. We investigated cerebral tissue oxygenation, neuroinflammation, and plasma biomarkers of neurodegeneration over 4 weeks after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) in sheep. Sixteen adult Merino ewes underwent CPB with a 2-h aortic cross-clamp and recovered for either 48 h (n = 8) or 4 weeks (n = 8). Cerebral tissue oxygenation was monitored. Neuroinflammation was quantified by morphometric analyses of microglia and astrocytes in the frontal cortex in both CPB groups and a naïve control group (n = 8). Plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) were measured serially. Compared with pre-CPB baseline, cerebral tissue oxygenation did not change significantly in the 48-h or 4-week period. In the 48-h post-CPB group, microglial soma sphericity was reduced (0.79 ± 0.04 vs. 0.83 ± 0.02, P = 0.018) compared with naïve controls, indicating microglial activation. Astrocytic GFAP-positive area was also elevated (17 ± 2% vs. 10 ± 2%, P = 0.026). In the 4-week post-CPB group, these measures did not differ significantly from naïve controls. Plasma NfL rose from 138 [96-185] pg/mL at baseline to 198 [149-265] pg/mL at 48 h (P = 0.0007), while GFAP peaked at the end of CPB (14.4 [4.7-32.4] vs. 3.0 [1.3-4.5] pg/mL, P < 0.0001) and normalised by 48 h. CPB induced neuroinflammation characterised by frontal cortical microglial activation and astrogliosis, accompanied by temporal elevations in plasma GFAP and NfL. These findings identify microglial activation as a response to CPB in the setting of preserved tissue oxygenation and provide preliminary evidence of an association between perioperative neuroinflammatory changes and circulating biomarkers GFAP and NfL, supporting further investigation.

42858172.title: Longitudinal Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging to Assess Lung Disease in Cystic Fibrosis.
42858172.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42858172.abstract: Matrix pencil decomposition magnetic resonance imaging (MP-MRI) enables quantitative assessment of lung ventilation and perfusion and was shown to correlate with contrast-enhanced (CE) perfusion MRI. To determine the longitudinal course of MP-MRI parameters in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF). Morpho-functional MRI including CE perfusion MRI and MP-MRI were performed twice in 136 pwCF with a median (range) baseline age of 14.5 (0.1-56.0) years to obtain the morpho-functional MRI score. Perfusion defect percentage (QDP) and ventilation defect percentage (VDP) were calculated by automated software. Additionally, lung clearance index (LCI) and forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) z-score were assessed. The participants were divided in subgroups depending on the clinical course according to cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator therapy, pulmonary exacerbation status and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection status. In the total cohort, VDP improved at follow up. Change in VDP correlated with change in MRI global score, MRI CE perfusion score and FEV1 z-score. Additionally, change in QDP correlated with change in MRI global score, MRI morphology score, MRI CE perfusion score and FEV1 z-score. QDP and VDP remained stable in clinically stable pwCF (n = 55) and improved in clinically improved pwCF (n = 67). In the stable and improved group, change in QDP correlated moderately with change in MRI CE perfusion score. MP-MRI assesses stability and improvement of lung perfusion and ventilation in pwCF. Changes correlate with those of established MRI scores. Therefore, QDP and VDP are sensitive longitudinal outcome parameters for future clinical studies.

42858161.title: Rare Coding Variants in FOXF1 are Associated with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
42858161.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
42858161.abstract: Most patients with nonheritable forms of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) lack identifiable pathogenic variants. Increasing evidence suggests that, in addition to high-impact predicted loss-of-function variants, rare missense coding variants may also contribute to disease pathogenesis. We identified ultra-rare missense variants in FOXF1 in two index cases with PAH. FOXF1 encodes a highly conserved transcription factor essential for lung vascular development. We sought to define the frequency of FOXF1 variants, characterize FOXF1 expression, and assess the functional relevance of FOXF1 alterations in PAH. Three independent international PAH cohorts were analyzed for predicted deleterious FOXF1 variants. FOXF1 expression was evaluated using bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence. Bioinformatic and chromatin-profiling approaches were used to identify potential downstream transcriptional targets, followed by promoter-reporter assays in vitro. Nine novel and one rare missense variants, one start-site variant, and one in-frame deletion in FOXF1 were identified across the three cohorts. FOXF1 expression was reduced in PAH lungs and localized predominantly to the endothelial cell compartment. Histopathological analysis revealed heterogeneous FOXF1 expression, with the lowest levels in phenotypically abnormal endothelial cells within complex vascular lesions. Single-cell analyses confirmed reduced endothelial FOXF1 expression in PAH, whereas broad FOXF1 downregulation across endothelial populations was not observed in other chronic lung diseases. Integration of CUT&Tag and ATAC-seq identified a canonical FOXF1-binding motif within the BMPR2 promoter. Promoter-reporter assays further supported FOXF1-dependent transcriptional regulation of BMPR2 and demonstrated reduced transcriptional activity of PAH-associated FOXF1 variants. Large-scale genomic and transcriptomic analyses support an association between FOXF1 dysregulation and PAH and identify BMPR2 as a potential downstream transcriptional target.

42850620.title: Prehospital transport prioritization and time-varying selection bias in traffic-related multi-patient incidents: a nationwide retrospective cohort study.
42850620.abstract: In prehospital multi-patient traffic incidents, the first ambulance to depart -priority transport - may reflect underlying injury severity rather than a treatment effect, as more severely injured patients are systematically prioritized. Conventional statistical methods often fail to separate this severity-dependent selection from actual outcomes. We applied a "doubly robust" statistical framework (augmented inverse probability weighting, AIPW), which combines a treatment model and an outcome model, to better account for measured differences, reduce selection bias, and examine whether on-scene time modifies this association. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using emergency medical service transport records from the Fire and Disaster Management Agency of Japan (January 2021-December 2023). Of 13,821,224 records, 143,130 patients from traffic-related multi-patient incidents (TMIs; ≥2 patients per incident) with complete data were included. The exposure was priority transport. The primary outcome was physician-assessed death or critical/severe injury at hospital arrival. Marginal adjusted risk differences (RDs) were estimated using AIPW. Effect modification by on-scene time (5-60 min) was assessed by marginal standardization with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals. Sensitivity analyses included overlap restriction and E-value quantification of unmeasured confounding. Among 143,130 patients (median age 41 years; female, 50.57%), 62,769 (43.85%) underwent priority transport. Severe outcomes occurred in 4.35% of priority and 1.87% of non-priority patients. The overall RDs was 2.2% points (95% CI, 2.01-2.36). A significant interaction with on-scene time was observed (p < .001): the marginal RD was peaked at 5 min (6.4% points; 95% CI, 5.6-7.2), declined to a minimum of 1.4% points (95% CI, 1.3-1.6) at approximately 32 min, and increased modestly to 2.4% points (95% CI, 2.0-2.8) at 60 min. Sensitivity analyses confirmed result robustness, yielding an E-value of 3.76 (lower bound, 3.57). The association between priority transport and severe outcome was modified by on-scene time, with the largest risk difference at the shortest on-scene times. This U-shaped pattern is consistent with preferential selection of more severely injured patients for rapid transport, rather than a direct effect of transport order. Accounting for prehospital triage selection when interpreting transport-outcome associations in critical care research.

42838498.title: Most older long-term care residents in Oslo have documented do-not-resuscitate status: a cross-sectional study.
42838498.abstract: With population aging, understanding the frequency and distribution of decisions to attempt or withhold cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in long-term care populations is increasingly important. In Oslo, CPR status, that is, an advance decision about whether CPR should or should not be attempted, is systematically assessed and documented for all long-term care residents. Comprehensive register data therefore provide a unique opportunity to assess advance CPR decisions at the population level. We obtained cross-sectional data on the documented CPR status of nearly all persons aged 50+ years admitted to public or private long-term care facilities in Oslo between 2018 and 2023 (N = 7860). We examined the proportion of long-term care residents with documented positive CPR status (CPR should be attempted) and used multivariable logistic regression to analyze the associations between documented positive CPR status and age, sex, marital status, primary contact (e.g., son, daughter, spouse, professional), functional limitations, institutional relocations, duration of stay, and year of admission. We found that 9.2% of long-term care residents had documented positive CPR status. Documented positive CPR status was related to younger age, fewer limitations, shorter duration of stay, and fewer relocations. Compared with residents first admitted in 2018, documented positive CPR status was less likely among those first admitted between 2019 and 2022, but not among those first admitted in 2023. There was no evidence that documented positive CPR status was related to sex, marital status, primary contact. Our findings provide population-level evidence on documented CPR status in long-term care and highlight the need for future research on how such decisions are made.

42834530.title: Bronchiectasis prevalence, incidence, and exacerbation rates among insured adults in the U.S.: a descriptive analysis.
42834530.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42834530.abstract: Contemporary population-representative data on bronchiectasis epidemiology in the United States remain limited. Existing exacerbation estimates are derived primarily from referral registries that overrepresent severe disease under subspecialty care, while incidence and prevalence calculations are largely based on outdated single-payer data, limiting generalizability. To estimate non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis prevalence and incidence among insured U.S. adults during 2016-2024, characterize exacerbation rates and their composition, and identify baseline factors associated with subsequent exacerbations. We assembled a retrospective cohort of adults with bronchiectasis using MarketScan Commercial, Medicare Supplemental, and Medicaid databases. Cases required two or more bronchiectasis diagnostic claims separated by more than 30 days, excluding individuals with cystic fibrosis, human immunodeficiency virus infection, or organ transplantation. The observation time zero was the second qualifying claim. Quasi-Poisson models were used to estimate annual prevalence, incidence, and exacerbation rates during observable enrollment periods. Annual percent changes quantified temporal trends. A negative binomial model estimated associations between baseline characteristics and post-diagnosis exacerbation rates. We identified 80,749 cases (64.6% female; mean age 65.9 years) and estimated prevalence and incidence of 105.3 and 32.1 per 100,000, respectively, in the combined Commercial-Medicare sample, and 66.1 and 19.0, respectively, in Medicaid. Prevalence increased steadily across payers, whereas incidence remained stable. The overall exacerbation rate was 0.88 events per person-year, declining by approximately 5% annually, with a reduction during the early pandemic period followed by a return to pre-pandemic trajectories by 2024. Outpatient events accounted for nearly 87% of exacerbations in the Commercial-Medicare sample and 65% in Medicaid. Calendar trends were attenuated by 12.3% after adjustment for follow-up. Frequent-exacerbator phenotype at cohort entry was the most strongly associated with higher subsequent exacerbation rates (adjusted rate ratio 1.96), followed by chronic airway infection and underlying respiratory conditions. Greater pulmonologist engagement at baseline was associated with lower exacerbation rates thereafter. Observed prevalence-incidence widening gap suggests case accumulation over time and survival among continuously enrolled beneficiaries. Exacerbation burden was concentrated among individuals with prior exacerbations, chronic airway infection, and respiratory comorbidity, while exacerbation rates decreased over time across payers and subgroups, in part reflecting changes in cohort composition.

42956801.title: Long-term safety and efficacy of twice-yearly depemokimab in type 2 asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype: 2-year integrated analysis of the phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies and AGILE open-label extension.
42956801.abstract: Depemokimab is the first ultra-long-acting biologic, with enhanced interleukin-5 binding affinity, high potency, and extended half-life, enabling twice-yearly dosing. The double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies demonstrated depemokimab efficacy and safety over 52 weeks in patients with asthma with type 2 inflammation and an eosinophilic phenotype. Here, we present long-term safety and efficacy outcomes over the 52-week, phase 3a open-label extension (OLE) of SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 (AGILE) alongside an integrated post-hoc analysis of the 104-week SWIFT and AGILE period. In SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2, patients (aged ≥12 years) with asthma with type 2 inflammation, an eosinophilic phenotype (≥150 cells/μL at screening or ≥300 cells/μL during the previous 12 months), and a history of at least two exacerbations in the previous 12 months despite receiving medium-dose or high-dose inhaled corticosteroids were randomly assigned (2:1) to subcutaneous depemokimab 100 mg or placebo every 26 weeks in addition to standard of care for 52 weeks. Patients who completed SWIFT-1 or SWIFT-2 could join the single-arm, 52-week AGILE OLE study, conducted at 156 centres across 14 countries. Patients continued depemokimab (depemokimab-depemokimab group) or switched to depemokimab from placebo (placebo-depemokimab group). The primary endpoints for the 52-week AGILE OLE period were the incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events, and immunogenicity as measured by the presence of anti-drug antibodies and neutralising antibodies. Secondary efficacy outcomes, including exacerbation rate, St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) score, and pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), were also assessed. Additional post-hoc analyses were carried out to assess safety and efficacy over the 104-week integrated SWIFT and AGILE analysis period. AGILE OLE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05243680. The SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04719832 and NCT04718103. Between March 1, 2022, and May 19, 2025, 629 patients were included in the AGILE OLE study (419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group). During the 52-week AGILE OLE period, adverse events occurred in 297 (71%) of 419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 146 (70%) of 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group; serious adverse events were infrequent (37 [9%] of 419 in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 19 [9%] of 210 in the placebo-depemokimab group), with no treatment-related or fatal serious adverse events reported. In the depemokimab-depemokimab group, the reduced annualised exacerbation rate was sustained over 2 years (0·51 [95% CI 0·43-0·61] in the 52-week SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 period and 0·56 [0·47-0·66] in the AGILE OLE). Improvements in SGRQ total score, ACQ-5 score, and FEV1 were maintained over 2 years. In the placebo-depemokimab group, improvements in clinical outcomes were observed after the switch to depemokimab during the AGILE OLE. Twice-yearly depemokimab was well tolerated and demonstrated sustained efficacy over the 2-year SWIFT and AGILE period, supporting its long-term therapeutic benefit and safety profile. GSK.

42955701.title: Systematic Review and Prognostic-Factor Meta-analysis of Residual or End-of-Treatment Hematoma Burden after Minimally Invasive Evacuation for Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
42955701.abstract: Residual or end-of-treatment (EOT) hematoma burden may explain variation in recovery after minimally invasive evacuation for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). We assessed its association with functional outcome and mortality. Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and PubMed were searched through 10 May 2026 without language or year restrictions. Eligible reports enrolled adults with spontaneous ICH treated by minimally invasive evacuation and related residual/EOT burden to clinical outcomes. Adjusted continuous prognostic estimates were prioritized. Random-effects inverse-variance meta-analysis used log odds ratios (ORs), with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp adjustment as primary inference and DerSimonian-Laird (DL)/Wald analysis as sensitivity analysis. Heterogeneous threshold evidence was summarized without a pooled effect. The review was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261399487). Among 881 records, 62 reports were included qualitatively. Of the reports, 12 underwent quantitative extractability review, 10 contributed quantitative evidence or audit rows, and 3 independent studies entered the exploratory continuous model. Each 1 mL greater residual/EOT volume was directionally associated with lower odds of favorable functional outcome, but the primary estimate crossed the null [OR 0.946, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.879-1.018; k = 3; approximate prediction interval 0.69-1.29]. The DL/Wald sensitivity estimate was OR 0.944 (95% CI 0.914-0.976). The modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-3 analysis included two studies, and heterogeneous threshold evidence was not pooled. Only three independent studies informed the exploratory continuous meta-analysis. Smaller residual/EOT volume was directionally associated with better functional outcome, but the primary estimate was not statistically significant (OR 0.946, 95% CI 0.879-1.018). Future trials should use common imaging and outcome data elements to test EOT volume-outcome associations and whether EOT volume is useful as a technical target; current evidence does not validate a universal cutoff or causal treatment target.

42949105.title: Effect of telemonitoring on adherence to inhalation therapy and pulmonary exacerbations in people with cystic fibrosis (conneCT CF): a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
42949105.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42949105.abstract: Recurrent pulmonary exacerbations contribute substantially to lung function decline in people with cystic fibrosis (CF). Inhalation therapies are a cornerstone of standard of care, yet adherence to inhalation therapies is variable and data on the relationship between adherence and pulmonary exacerbations remain limited. To assess the impact of multimodal telemonitoring and coaching on adherence and pulmonary exacerbations in people with CF. In this prospective, multicenter, unblinded, randomized, controlled trial people with CF aged ≥12 years were randomized (1:1) to either standard of care or an intervention involving continuous objective home monitoring of inhalation adherence, weekly home spirometry, a self-management app, professional telephone coaching, and optional video conferencing over 18 months. The primary endpoint was time to first pulmonary exacerbation. 296 participants were included with a mean age of 31.3 (SD 10.8) years, 54.1% females, mean FEV1% predicted of 70.2% (SD 24.7), 52.7% chronically infected with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and 85.1% on triple CFTR modulator therapy. Baseline adherence was higher in the intervention group (58.1%) than in the control group (44.0%) and remained higher throughout the study (last 6 months: 49.2% vs. 32.6%). Time to first exacerbation did not differ between groups. However, across all participants, a 10% increase in adherence correlated with a 9% reduction in pulmonary exacerbation risk. Participants with FEV1<40% had a 2.4-fold higher risk of exacerbations. Multimodal telemedicine improved inhalation therapy adherence. The association between higher adherence and reduced exacerbations highlights the ongoing importance of inhalation therapy in CF, even with widespread CFTR modulator use. Clinical trial registered with German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00024642).

42946956.title: Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome in Severe Hyponatremia: Independent Association with Sodium Correction Rates When Accounting for Confounding Risk Factors.
authors: for the Kaiser Permanente CREST Network Investigators
42946956.abstract: Clinical guidelines emphasize slow correction of severe hyponatremia to prevent osmotic demyelination syndrome (ODS), though the evidentiary base rarely accounts for confounding factors. A retrospective case-control study of adults with an initial serum sodium concentration ≤ 120 meq/L who were admitted to a 21-hospital-integrated healthcare system between 1 January 2008 and 31 December 2023 was conducted. Maximum 24-h sodium correction rates were defined as slow (< 8 meq/L), moderate (8-12 meq/L), or fast (> 12 meq/L). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) were estimated using Firth's penalized logistic regression. Twenty-three cases of ODS and 9557 non-ODS controls were identified. Compared with controls, ODS cases were more likely to experience fast sodium correction (43% vs. 24%). However, following adjustment for initial serum sodium ≤ 105 meq/L [aOR 10.3, 95% confidence interval (CI) 3.3-32.3], initial serum potassium < 3.0 meq/L (aOR 3.4, 95% CI 1.2-9.3), and history of alcohol abuse (aOR 3.9, 95% CI 1.7-8.8), faster sodium correction rates lacked statistical association with ODS: moderate (aOR 0.6, 95% CI 0.2-2.0) or fast (aOR 1.0, 95% CI 0.3-2.9). Faster sodium correction rates in cases of ODS may be, at least in part, epiphenomena of underlying confounding factors.

42946955.title: High Postoperative Perihematomal Edema Trajectory after Endoscopic Evacuation for Supratentorial Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
42946955.abstract: The clinical relevance of perihematomal edema (PHE) after endoscopic evacuation of supratentorial intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is uncertain. We examined a longitudinal postoperative PHE phenotype and its association with 90-day functional outcome. This two-center retrospective cohort included 136 patients who survived beyond 72 h after endoscopic evacuation of supratentorial ICH and had complete serial computed tomography (CT) and 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) assessment. CT windows were 0-24 h (T1), 48-72 h (T2), and day 5-7 (T3). Before outcome-model fitting, high postoperative PHE trajectory was defined as T3 PHE ≥ 36.6 mL or continuous increase across T1-T2-T3 with a T3-T1 change ≥ 7.7 mL; both thresholds were cohort-derived upper quartiles. Center-adjusted logistic regression examined associated factors and poor 90-day outcome (mRS score 3-6). High postoperative PHE trajectory occurred in 51 patients (37.5%). Intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) severity (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.11 per category, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-4.09), residual hematoma volume (aOR 1.75 per mL, 95% CI 1.35-2.27), and fever duration within 72 h (aOR 1.20 per h, 95% CI 1.08-1.34) were associated with this trajectory. Adding trajectory to the outcome model increased apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.846 to 0.905; trajectory was associated with poor outcome (aOR 25.21, 95% CI 6.13-103.60). Among 131 paired observations, mRS score 0-2 occurred in 71/131 (54.2%) at 90 days and 76/131 (58.0%) at 12 months (two-sided exact McNemar P = 0.125). In this selected cohort of early postoperative survivors, IVH severity, residual hematoma volume, and fever duration were associated with high postoperative PHE trajectory, which was associated with poor 90-day functional outcome. This cohort-derived imaging phenotype warrants external validation as a candidate prognostic marker after endoscopic evacuation.

42934119.title: Therapeutic Targeting of the Macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB Axis Mitigates Pulmonary Hypertension.
42934119.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
42934119.abstract: Immune dysregulation is a pivotal driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, yet therapeutic targeting of inflammation has yielded limited clinical success. Although cytosolic RNA-binding proteins are known to regulate immune responses in PH, the specific role of the nuclear m⁶A reader YTHDC1 remains undefined. To elucidate the function of macrophage YTHDC1 in orchestrating inflammatory vascular remodeling during PH. Expression profiles of YTHDC1 and TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) were evaluated in human and rodent PH specimens. The mechanistic and therapeutic roles of this axis were assessed using myeloid-specific knockout mice and pharmacological inhibitors (YL-5092, 5Z-7-oxozeaenol) across hypoxia-, SU5416/hypoxia-, and monocrotaline-induced PH models. In patients with idiopathic or connective tissue disease-associated PAH, YTHDC1 and TIGAR expression levels were elevated in pulmonary and circulating macrophages, correlating with disease severity. In murine models, myeloid-specific deletion of Ythdc1 or Tigar conferred profound protection against hypoxia- and SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH. Mechanistically, hypoxia upregulated Ythdc1, which directly bound and stabilized Tigar mRNA. The subsequent accumulation of Tigar protein operated non-enzymatically via a specific domain (residues 152-161) to interact with Tak1, thereby activating the NF-κB cascade, augmenting pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and driving pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell proliferation. Pharmacological inhibition of YTHDC1 (YL-5092) or disruption of the TIGAR-TAK1 interaction (5Z-7-oxozeaenol) effectively attenuated vascular inflammation and mitigated PH progression in diverse rodent models. The macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB signaling axis acts as a critical determinant of inflammation and vascular remodeling in PH, representing a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for this disease.

42912180.title: UNOS Registry Analysis: How Does Heart Transplant Recipient Weight Affect Waitlist Days?
42912180.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42912180.abstract: Body weight of heart transplant (HTx) recipients affects waitlist days. However, no prior report exists to articulate this in detail. The aim of this study is to analyze the effect of recipients' weight to HTx. The United Network of Organ Sharing (UNOS) registry was analyzed under the current allocation from 2018 to 2023. The cohort was divided into three even weight groups: low (<77.1 kg), middle (77.1-92.1 kg), and high (>92.1 kg). Candidate/donor demographics, weight distributions, waitlist days in UNOS Status, cumulative incidence of HTx and delisting, post-HTx survival, and cutoff weight for earlier HTx were analyzed. A total of 16,664 HTx recipients were included (5,535: low, 5,537: middle, and 5,592: high). Donors and recipients had a weight distribution mismatch (p = 0.003). For waitlist days, status 1 was comparable; however, the high group with status ≥2 had approximately twice longer waitlist days than the low group. The high group had a lower incidence of HTx (p < 0.001) and higher delisting (p = 0.02) than the low group. One year survival was comparable (p = 0.28). The weight cutoff for earlier HTx was 80 kg with a 21.6% increased rate of HTx (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.216; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.171-1.263, p < 0.001). Recipients weighing <80 kg had earlier HTx and a higher incidence of HTx. The effect of pre-HTx weight management requires further study.

42912174.title: Ex Vivo Heart Perfusion Versus Cold Storage in Prolonged Preservation Period: A Juvenile Porcine Experimental Model.
42912174.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42912174.abstract: Cross-clamp times greater than or equal to 4 hours are critical for donor heart viability. We compared cold storage (CS) and normothermic ex vivo heart perfusion (EVHP) during prolonged preservation using a juvenile porcine model. Twenty-two piglet hearts (~10 kg) were assigned to CS or EVHP for 6 or 8 hours, followed by 2 hours of working-mode (WM) perfusion. Metabolism, cardiac function, and cell damage were compared using two-sample t-tests or Fisher's exact tests, and temporal changes during perfusion were assessed using linear mixed-effects models and generalized estimating equations. During EVHP, the minimal rate of pressure change decreased, and arterial lactate levels increased after 5-6 hours. Compared to CS, EVHP hearts showed higher left atrial pressure (6 vs. 0 mm Hg, p = 0.011), arterial lactate levels during WM (p < 0.001), and NFκB-p65 levels (p = 0.002) at 6 hours, and lower cardiac output (90 vs. 120% of normal, p = 0.026), higher left atrial pressure (7 vs. 3 mm Hg, p = 0.009), higher arterial lactate levels during WM (p < 0.001), and increased neutrophil infiltration (p = 0.033) at 8 hours. Ex vivo heart perfusion hearts deteriorated beyond 5-6 hours and showed greater hemodynamic, metabolic, and inflammatory changes at both 6 and 8 hours. Ex vivo heart perfusion enhancements reducing immune response and inflammation are crucial for expanding the donor pool.

42912017.title: Sensitivity of Damage Markers for Mechanical Trauma to Erythrocytes in Mechanical Circulatory Support Devices: A Multispecies Study.
42912017.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42912017.abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) advancement relies on fully understanding remaining hemocompatibility issues, including identifying and monitoring a variety of damage markers, as hemolysis alone is insufficient to understand the full scope of total blood damage. It is also important to understand how these alternative markers vary between species, as animal surrogates are often used in device development. This work focuses on evaluating erythrocyte-derived extracellular vesicles (ErEVs) released during MCS perfusion as an alternative marker for monitoring erythrocyte damage. Porcine, bovine, and human washed red blood cells (RBCs) were perfused through a blood circulatory loop using the CentriMag pump. Both hemolysis and ErEV production were monitored over time to compare the sensitivity of both to mechanically induced trauma and to observe species-dependent differences. All species produced significant increases in ErEV concentrations, while only human and bovine erythrocytes produced significant increases in free hemoglobin. There were no differences in the normalized index of hemolysis between species, but bovine RBCs produced significantly more ErEVs than human or porcine, which were similar. Regarding damage marker sensitivity, ErEV generation appears to be a promising complementary marker to hemolysis and potentially more sensitive for porcine and bovine models, while more testing is needed for human.

42906567.title: When a vulnerable lung meets a changing climate.

42906566.title: Interstitial lung diseases in a changing climate: emerging risks and opportunities to improve care.
42906566.abstract: Although climate change represents one of the greatest public health challenges of our time, its impacts on patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain unclear. This Personal View synthesises the evidence surrounding established, emerging, and postulated climate change health effects on patients with ILD, who are especially vulnerable to disease due to older age, reduced lung function, and sensitivity to inhaled exposures. Established risk factors for ILD such as air pollution might worsen with climate change, whereas other exposures such as extreme heat, viral illnesses, residential water intrusion, pollen, natural disasters, and desertification could pose novel threats to this population. Knowledge gaps exist across multiple domains, including wildfire smoke effects, the effects of climate on occupational ILD, and disaster preparedness. The incorporation of multiple research modalities, including patient-centred approaches, is crucial to address these gaps. Clinicians, scientists, and professional societies can lead climate-health research, the adoption of mitigation and adaptation strategies, and drive global policy actions to address this growing challenge.

42902802.title: Serial Mass Tuberculosis Screening Among the Elderly in Eastern China from 2021-2023.
42902802.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
42902802.abstract: The impact of repeated community-wide tuberculosis screening is uncertain because evidence from large-scale, multi-round screening campaigns is limited. We evaluated whether annual, community-based, chest-radiography screening was associated with reduced tuberculosis prevalence and detection of asymptomatic disease across multiple screening rounds. We conducted three annual chest X-ray screening rounds (2021-2023) among adults aged ≥60 years in Lanxi City, Zhejiang Province. All participants underwent chest radiography at community health centers, with referral for diagnostic evaluation and bacteriological testing. We estimated detection yields per 100,000 screened persons, assessed trends, and used direct standardization and repeated-participation analyses. Across all rounds, 214,948 screening encounters were completed. From Round 1 to Round 3, screening-detected prevalence declined for overall tuberculosis (233.1 [95% CI, 194.2-279.7] to 146.3 [95% CI, 123.1-173.9] per 100,000 screened persons) and bacteriologically-confirmed tuberculosis (162.1 [95% CI, 130.3-201.7] to 108.6 [95% CI, 88.8-132.7] per 100,000 screened persons). From Round 1 to Round 3, asymptomatic tuberculosis decreased as both a proportion of cases (47.8% to 26.6%) and prevalence among screened participants (111.5 to 38.9 per 100,000). Compared with Round 1, tuberculosis prevalence was lower in Round 2 (-28.1% change; 95% CI, -44.0 to - 7.5) and Round 3 (-37.2% change; 95% CI, -51.2 to - 19.2). The Round 2-to-Round 3 difference was smaller and included the null (-12.8% change; 95% CI, -31.7 to 11.4). Standardization and repeated-participation analyses yielded broadly similar patterns. Serial community-level screening was associated with declining tuberculosis prevalence, including asymptomatic disease, with the largest reduction occurring between the first and second screening rounds.

42895981.title: When Human Tissue Meets the Driveline: Implications of Tissue Integration to Combat Driveline Infections.
42895981.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42895981.abstract: Driveline infection remains a common complication of ventricular assist device (VAD) therapy. These infections often progress from the exit site through the subcutaneous tract to the deeper tunnel and, in severe cases, the pocket, underscoring the vulnerability of the driveline-tissue interface. In this review, we examine the biological and mechanical factors governing tissue-driveline interactions and their implications for tissue integration of the implanted driveline. Dysregulated inflammation, impaired vascular maturation, abnormal extracellular matrix remodeling, repetitive micromotion and traction, and biomaterial-tissue mismatch may all compromise optimal tissue ingrowth of the driveline. Insufficient tissue integration can lead to the formation of microgaps within the driveline tunnel, providing a potential niche for microbial colonization and biofilm formation, thereby contributing to persistent driveline infections. Recognizing the potential association between inadequate tissue integration and the occurrence of driveline infection shifts the focus from microbial eradication alone toward optimizing driveline-tissue interactions across different segments of the driveline. Such an approach may help reduce the incidence of driveline infections in patients requiring long-term VAD support. Finally, strategies to promote tissue integration and long-term driveline stability, including driveline surface engineering, modulation of physicochemical properties, and optimization of surgical techniques, are discussed.

42888320.title: Electroacupuncture Ameliorating Cerebral I/R-Induced Inflammatory Response through the TLR/TRAF6/NF-κB Pathway.
42888320.abstract: The inflammatory response plays a crucial role in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and may offer a new therapeutic approach for stroke. Electroacupuncture has shown potential in treating cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury. Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to four groups: the sham group, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) group, sham electroacupuncture (SEA) group, and electroacupuncture (EA) group. The SEA and EA groups received 30 min of treatment after 60 min of ischemia. Body weight was measured before and 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Neurological function and infarct volume were assessed 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) expression levels of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB were evaluated using western blot and reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The mRNA and protein expression of inflammatory markers was assessed using RT-PCR and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Compared with the MCAO/R group, the EA group exhibited improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume, and down-regulated expression of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB. Additionally, in the EA group, the mRNA and protein expression of proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) were decreased, while the expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine (IL-10) was increased. Electroacupuncture exerts a neuroprotective effect on MCAO/R, potentially through the modulation of the TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB pathways. This treatment may reduce the cerebral I/R-induced inflammatory response by influencing the TLR/TRAF/NF-κB signaling pathway.

42885566.title: A Proposed Consensus Definition of Severe COPD: a modified Delphi Study.
42885566.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42885566.abstract: Advanced interventions are available for patients with more severe COPD despite guideline-recommended therapies, yet this population is heterogeneously defined and inconsistently recognized, and a standardized work-up is lacking, which could lead to mismanagement. To formulate a new, expert-based consensus definition of severe COPD and a minimal set of diagnostics and characteristics to be assessed in the work-up of these patients. A modified Delphi study with two online rounds was conducted between June 2024 and January 2025 with 55 international COPD experts representing all areas of disease management. Sixty-seven (round 1) and 20 (round 2) statements were tested in seven domains: (A) the need for a definition, (B) symptoms, (C) functional impairment, (D) quality of life, (E) physiological impairment, (F) framework definition, and (G) risk factors. Consensus was defined as ≥ 75% agreement. Consensus was reached for 46 (69%) statements in round 1 and 15 (75%) in round 2. Among patients with confirmed COPD, severe COPD was defined as: (1) persistent symptoms, functional impairment, or severely reduced quality of life; (2) despite optimal treatment and not due to comorbidities; and (3) including at least one clinical characteristic: severe airflow obstruction, severely impaired diffusion capacity, severe hyperinflation, frequent exacerbations, chronic respiratory insufficiency, pulmonary hypertension related to COPD, or cachexia or unintentional weight loss related to COPD. The proposed standardized work-up comprised: (1) assessment of patient-reported outcomes for symptoms, quality of life, anxiety and depression; (2) assessment of exacerbation frequency and severity; (3) comprehensive diagnostic testing, including lung function testing, blood gas analysis, imaging, cardiac assessment, and exercise-tolerance testing; and (4) assessment of risk factors for more severe and progressive disease. Using expert consensus, we devised an internationally-supported, proposed definition and work-up for 'severe COPD', accounting for disease heterogeneity. This definition may improve identification of the population and supports a structured evaluation of this often under-recognized and potentially undertreated population. Future studies are warranted to determine its clinical impact, prognostic value, and utility in research.

42962235.title: Impact of Showering Methods on Driveline Exit Site Microbiology and Driveline Infection in Patients With Left Ventricular Assist Devices.
42962235.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42962235.abstract: Driveline infection (DLI) remains a major complication in patients with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD). This study evaluated the impact of different showering methods on bacterial colonization at the driveline exit site (DLES) and the incidence of DLI. Patients who underwent LVAD implantation at our institute from 2008 to 2021 were included and classified into two groups: the open group, in which the DLES was exposed and washed with running water, and the covered group, in which the DLES was sealed with a waterproof dressing during showering. The primary outcome was the incidence of DLI within 3 years following hospital discharge. A total of 103 patients were included (the open group, n = 47; the covered group, n = 56). The DLI-free rate was significantly higher in the covered group than the open group (77% vs. 49%; p = 0.003). Pseudomonas aeruginosa was detected less frequently at the DLES, and DLI caused by P. aeruginosa was significantly reduced in the covered group. Multivariate analysis suggested that the open showering method was an independent risk factor for DLI (hazard ratio, 2.816; 95% confidence interval, 1.325-5.984; p = 0.007). The covered showering method was associated with a significantly lower incidence of DLI, particularly infections caused by P. aeruginosa.

42960873.title: Diagnostic performance of xylazine test strips in urine from fentanyl-positive hospitalized patients.
42960873.abstract: Xylazine is an α-2-adrenergic agonist increasingly detected in the illicit drug supply, particularly in combination with fentanyl, yet no FDA-cleared rapid diagnostic assay exists for detection in biological specimens. Commercially available xylazine test strips, developed to evaluate drug samples, have been proposed for clinical use. We aim to evaluate the clinical screening performance of xylazine test strips when applied to urine specimens from hospitalized patients with fentanyl-positive routine hospital urine drug screening. This single-center diagnostic accuracy study included 250 consecutive residual urine specimens from hospitalized patients with fentanyl-positive routine hospital urine drug screening. Fentanyl positivity was not confirmed by hospital liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. Each specimen underwent testing with a commercially available xylazine test strips and liquid chromatography-mass spectometry for xylazine detection and quantification as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, and exact 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Liquid chromatography-mass spectometry detected xylazine in 71 of 250 specimens (28.4%). Xylazine test strips identified 19 true positives, 139 true negatives, 40 false positives, and 52 false negatives. Sensitivity was 26.8% (95% CI 16.9-38.6%), and specificity was 77.7% (95% CI 70.8-83.5%). Positive and negative predictive values were 32.2% and 72.8%, respectively. The positive likelihood ratio was 1.2 and the negative likelihood ratio was 0.94. Most LC-MS-positive specimens (91.5%) had xylazine concentrations below the manufacturer-reported xylazine test strips detection threshold of 1,000 ng/mL. When applied to urine specimens from hospitalized patients with fentanyl-positive routine hospital urine drug screens, commercially available xylazine test strips demonstrated limited diagnostic utility, largely due to low sensitivity at clinically observed concentration ranges. Xylazine test strips results should not be used in isolation to guide clinical decision-making until validated point-of-care assays designed for biological specimens become available. Commercially available xylazine test strips demonstrate poor clinical screening performance when applied to urine specimens from hospitalized patients with fentanyl-positive routine hospital urine drug screens.

42960868.title: Pragmatic trial of a self-directed intervention for weight loss in obstructive sleep apnea (POWER).
42960868.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
42960868.abstract: Self-directed lifestyle interventions may improve access to weight loss care in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but effectiveness in routine practice is unknown. Test whether a proactively delivered self-directed lifestyle intervention improves weight and sleep-related quality of life versus usual care. POWER enrolled patients with OSA and body mass index of 30-45 kg/m2, recruited from Veteran Affairs (VA) sites nationwide, and randomized participants to a self-directed intervention based on the Diabetes Prevention Program with video-based sessions, readings, and regular coaching reminders or usual care. Co-primary outcomes were change in Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ) and clinical weight in kilograms (kg) from baseline to 12 months post-randomization. Given two primary outcomes, we defined significance at p = 0.025. This trial randomized 696 participants. Mean age was 56.2 years (SD 12.2), with 19.7% identifying as female. Clinical weights at 12 months were available for 81.9% of intervention and 83.6% of control participants. Unadjusted weight declined 2.1 kg (SD 6.8) in intervention and 0.9 kg (SD 5.9) in control (adjusted between-group difference: -1.1 kg, 95%CI -2.0, -0.1; p = 0.037). FOSQ measures were available at 12 months for 78.2% of intervention and 90.5% of control participants. From baseline to 12 months, unadjusted FOSQ improved 1.4 (SD 2.7) points in intervention and 0.9 (SD 2.9) points in control (adjusted between-group difference: 0.6 points, 95%CI 0.2, 1.0; p = 0.001). Among participants with OSA and obesity, a self-directed lifestyle intervention did not improve weight loss and led to improvements in sleep-related quality of life that are of limited clinical importance. Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05104450, registered 10/19/2021.
