42973135.title: Molecular biomarkers for the evaluation of indeterminate pulmonary nodules: a systematic review.
42973135.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
42973135.abstract: Current risk prediction tools for indeterminate pulmonary nodules (IPNs) are imperfect and there is a growing body of research in biomarkers to aid management. We undertook this systematic review to evaluate the current landscape of molecular biomarkers designed for IPN risk stratification. PubMed, CINAHL Complete, and Scopus databases were searched through December 2024. Clinical validation or utility studies of non-invasive molecular biomarkers for IPNs (<30mm) were included. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Database and citation searching identified 1,577 studies from 2007-2024. After abstract and full-text screening, 106 studies were included in the systematic review. Of the 106 studies included, less than half validated the accuracy of the biomarker in an external cohort (n = 48, 45%), while most others (n = 47, 44%) used a split-validation design. The median size of the validation cohort was 112.5 (range: 29 to 1,679). Protein biomarkers were the most commonly evaluated (n = 73), followed by genetic/nucleic acid compounds (n = 40). Risk of bias assessment using the QUADAS-2 tool found 9 studies to be at low risk across all domains, and many studies had an unclear risk due to lack of reporting or clarity. This review highlights the growing and diverse field of molecular biomarker development for the evaluation of pulmonary nodules. The vast majority had no external validation in an intended use cohort. Improvements must be made to the completeness of reporting in the field to address issues with risk of bias and applicability of study results.

42973134.title: Pulmonary hypertension clinic infrastructure is associated with improved care coordination: results from a national survey.
42973134.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

42972684.title: [Diagnoses, outcomes and interventions for nursing care in ICU: a multicentre study for an ICNP Subset proposal].
42972684.abstract: The use of standardized terminology and a classification system is a way to make nursing documentation complete and accurate, with the aim of generating evidence. The International Classification for Nursing Practice (ICNP) is a combinatorial terminology used to describe nursing practice. The intensive care context, in constant evolution, has required the development of advanced skills by nurses in order to improve patients' outcomes. The aim of this study is to propose an ICNP Subset by identifying ICNP diagnoses, outcomes and interventions that describe nursing care practice in an adult ICU setting. The descriptive, retrospective and multicentre study was divided into the following phases: 1. review of nursing documentation; 2. cross mapping and identification of diagnoses, outcomes and interventions; 3. creation and organization of the catalogue; 4. validation with the Delphi method. The Subset is made up of 106 diagnoses, 83 outcomes and 240 interventions. The most representative category for diagnoses was "Circulation" (28.3%, n=30), "Exposure" for interventions (31.6%, n=76) and again "Circulation" for outcomes (28.9%, n=24). The proposal of an ICNP Subset for Intensive Care includes both general and very specific diagnoses, outcomes and interventions, reflecting the transversal nature and the high specialty of nursing care in the intensive care unit.

42980100.title: Why We Need a College of Intensive Care Medicine (UK).
42980100.journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)

42980817.title: ICU resilience, stress and support: perceptions of ICU professionals in an international ESICM survey.

42981017.title: Approaches to assessing functional outcome trajectories in old survivors of intensive care: a narrative review.
42981017.abstract: Patients with critical conditions admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU) undergo one of the most extensive trials of resilience. In addition to considering survival as a crucial outcome, there is a growing awareness of the importance of recovering functional abilities in old ICU patients. In this narrative review, a group of geriatricians and intensivists will discuss previous studies and current approaches to assess functional trajectories in old ICU survivors with a focus on frailty, functional independence and intrinsic capacity. In previous studies, frailty as evaluated with the Clinical Frailty Scale or variants of the Frailty Index has been found to exhibit a dynamic course after a critical illness. Measures of functional independence show a similar pattern after ICU discharge depending on pre-existing impairments and frailty. Although the concept of intrinsic capacity could provide a holistic framework to predict functional impairments, there still is only limited data on its usefulness in the context of a critical illness. Assessing the post-discharge trajectory in old survivors of a critical illness is crucial to detect early signs of complications and adjust individual support. However, current approaches in this field lack validation. Considering the challenges and importance of functional recovery in old ICU patients, more intensive research in the future is imperative in order to determine the best approach to describe, monitor and optimise the health status amongst these individuals.

42981058.title: Operationalizing Reconciliation as an Ethical Decision-Making Framework in Critical Care Nursing: A Conceptual Discussion.
42981058.abstract: Critical care nurses routinely face complex ethical dilemmas arising from rapid, high-stakes decision making in emergencies. The principle of reconciliation offers a structured framework for navigating these tensions by balancing competing stakeholder perspectives. This article critically examines how reconciliation can be operationalized in critical care nursing and proposes structured strategies for its implementation. Reconciliation involves acknowledging conflicting values and seeking mutually acceptable, ethically defensible solutions through open dialogue and mutual understanding. However, applying reconciliation in critical care is challenging due to limited information, severe time pressures, and the need for rapid decisions. Implementing reconciliation strategies can yield numerous benefits, including improved communication, reduced moral distress, increased patient and family satisfaction, and a culture of collaboration. Challenges to implementing reconciliation include time constraints, power imbalances within interprofessional teams, emotional intensity, cultural and religious differences, and legal and institutional constraints. Addressing these challenges necessitates a multifaceted approach that accounts for team dynamics, emotional demands, and legal and institutional structures.

42978570.title: Toxic leadership and nurse outcomes in intensive care units: a cross-sectional analysis of emotional labor and occupational embeddedness.
42978570.abstract: This study aimed to assess occupational embeddedness and examine the relationships among toxic leadership, emotional labor, and occupational embeddedness among intensive care unit (ICU) nurses. A cross-sectional design. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 339 ICU nurses using the Toxic Leadership Behaviors of Nurse Managers Scale, the Emotional Labor Scale, and the Occupational Embeddedness Scale. Descriptive statistics were used to assess variable prevalence. Univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted to identify factors associated with occupational embeddedness. Additionally, Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine the relationships among toxic leadership behaviors, emotional labor, and occupational embeddedness. ICU nurses reported low levels of toxic leadership, while occupational embeddedness was moderate. The monthly income (p = 0.014) and working environment (p < 0.05) were the predictors of occupational embeddedness. Pearson correlation analysis showed a positive correlation between toxic leadership and emotional labor (r = 0.272, p < 0.01), as well as a moderate negative correlation between toxic leadership and occupational embeddedness (r = -0.477, p < 0.01). In addition, deep acting was positively correlated with occupational embeddedness (r = 0.273, p < 0.01). This study clarified the relationship between toxic leadership behavior, emotional labor and occupational embeddedness among ICU nurses. Nursing managers may consider adopting supportive and constructive leadership practices and providing appropriate support for nurses' emotional demands, including strategies that may facilitate adaptive emotional regulation and deep acting. Nursing managers should recognize toxic leadership issues and consider measures to minimize the potential transmission of negative emotions and behaviors to staff. No patient or public contribution.

42981359.title: Psychometric evaluation of the Palliative Nursing Care Quality Scale (PNCQS) among ICU and oncology nurses in Iran.
42981359.abstract: Reliable and culturally adapted instruments are essential for assessing the quality of palliative nursing care. The Palliative Nursing Care Quality Scale (PNCQS) had not been psychometrically evaluated in Iran. This study aimed to translate the PNCQS into Persian and examine its validity and reliability among Iranian nurses. In this methodological study, the PNCQS was translated into Persian according to the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. A total of 620 nurses from oncology and intensive care units in teaching hospitals in Tehran, Tabriz, and Ardabil were recruited using a multi stage cluster sampling strategy with convenience sampling at the final stage. Face, content, and construct validity were evaluated. Construct validity was examined by first testing the original one-factor model using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), followed by exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and cross-validation of the derived factor structure using CFA on an independent sample. CFA was conducted in AMOS using maximum likelihood estimation with bootstrapping (1,000 resamples). Reliability was assessed by internal consistency (Cronbach's α) and two-week test-retest reliability using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). The scale showed excellent content validity (S-CVI = 0.99). The initial CFA demonstrated that the original 20-item unidimensional model did not adequately fit the Iranian data. Subsequent EFA identified a four-factor structure-Family-Centered Care, Empathic and Spiritual Care, Hope and Life Review, and Physical Symptom Management-explaining 51.41% of the total variance. This structure was confirmed by CFA in an independent sample (n = 400), demonstrating good model fit (χ²/df = 2.84, CFI = 0.95, TLI = 0.95, RMSEA = 0.06). Composite reliability exceeded 0.70 for all factors. Although the AVE for Family-Centered Care was slightly below the recommended threshold (0.42), its composite reliability was acceptable (0.81), and discriminant validity was established for all constructs. Cronbach's α was 0.92 for the total scale (subscales: 0.76-0.83), and the two-week test-retest ICC was 0.76. The Persian PNCQS demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties and a culturally appropriate four-factor structure for assessing the quality of palliative nursing care among Iranian nurses. It provides a reliable multidimensional instrument for clinical practice, research, and quality improvement initiatives in palliative care.

42979110.title: The future of wearable sweat sensors in intensive care units: Toward a new era of noninvasive, continuous real-time monitoring.
42979110.abstract: There is an urgent need for noninvasive, continuous patient monitoring technology in the intensive care unit. As an emerging monitoring tool, wearable sweat sensors can obtain multiple biochemical marker information in real-timely and noninvasively, and have significant advantages. This article reviews the basic principles of wearable sweat sensors, biomarkers in sweat, and their application prospects in intensive care units, covering their potential in inflammation monitoring, metabolic management, drug monitoring, and so on, and provides an in depth discussion of technical maturity, clinical verification, system integration, and standardization challenges. It was finally pointed out that wearable sweat sensors are expected to promote the transformation of critical care into personalized, predictive, and preventive medicine through integration with digital health systems.

42978856.title: Diagnostic yield of fiberoptic bronchoscopy-guided bronchial biopsies for suspected lung cancer in intensive care unit: A 10-year retrospective study.
42978856.abstract: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy (FOB)-guided bronchial biopsies are the first-line investigation for suspected lung cancer. Their relevance has not been studied for the exploration of an unknown thoracic abnormality diagnosed on admission to the intensive care unit (ICU). Hence, we aimed at determining the diagnostic yield, safety, and therapeutic impact of FOB-guided bronchial biopsies performed in critically ill patients suspected of lung cancer on ICU admission. We conducted a 10-year monocenter retrospective observational study between January 2013 and December 2022. Using the database of the local Pathology Department, we identified 92 patients who underwent FOB-guided bronchial biopsies in the ICU, and finally included 70 patients who underwent this procedure for a thoracic abnormality suspected of neoplasia at ICU admission. The primary endpoint was the diagnostic yield of FOB-guided bronchial biopsies performed in the ICU. Lung cancer was clinically suspected on mediastinal and/or hilar involvement, mainly masses (n=49; 70.0%). FOB was performed with local anesthesia combined with a remifentanil target-controlled infusion (n=43; 61.4%) associated with standard oxygen therapy (n=34; 48.6%), or general anesthesia (n=26; 37.1%). Pathological findings following FOB-guided bronchial biopsies led to a diagnosis in 41 patients (58.6%). The presence of a mass on the admission chest computed tomography scan (odds ratio [OR]=5.13, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.35-19.40) or an endobronchial growth or mucosal infiltration visualized during FOB (OR=4.22; 95% CI: 1.22-14.50) were associated with high diagnostic yield. Complications occurred in seven patients (10.0%), within 24 h after the FOB procedure. No death was associated with the procedure. ICU and 1-year mortality rates were 27.1% and 60.0%, respectively. FOB-guided bronchial biopsies in the ICU for suspected lung cancer led to the diagnosis in most patients. The safety of the procedure and its potential therapeutical impact should stimulate intensivists to pursue diagnostic investigations for suspected lung cancer in the ICU.

42979101.title: Prognostic factors in ICU patients with community-acquired bacterial meningitis: A post hoc analysis of a multicenter prospective cohort study.
authors: de Villiers de la Noue V
42979101.abstract: Community-acquired adult bacterial meningitis (CABM) is a severe condition associated with significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Previous studies have identified several risk factors for poor outcomes, including advanced age, immunosuppression, and delayed treatment. However, data on ICU-specific prognostic factors remain limited. This study aimed to identify factors associated with ICU admission, predictors of 30-day mortality, and long-term outcomes in ICU-admitted patients with CABM. This post hoc analysis utilized data from 27 ICUs from the COMBAT cohort, a prospective multicenter study in France from February 2013 to July 2015. The study included patients over 18 years old with confirmed CABM. Clinical, microbiological, and ICU-specific data, including Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores, were collected. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality, and secondary outcomes included ICU admission predictors and 12-month functional status. Multivariable logistic regression models with pre-specified clinically relevant variables were used to identify factors associated with 30-day mortality and ICU admission; model performance was assessed using the c-statistic and Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test. Of the 210 patients admitted to the ICU, 36 (17.1%) died within 30 days. Significant predictors of mortality included elevated SOFA scores at ICU admission and on day 3 in univariate and multivariate analyses. Age and non-meningococcal CABM were associated with mortality in the univariate analysis but not in the multivariate analysis. ICU admission was associated with altered consciousness and Neisseria meningitidis CABM according to univariate and multivariate analyses. In multivariable analysis, higher SOFA scores at admission (OR=1.49, 95% CI: 1.28 to 1.74) and on day 3 (OR=1.51, 95% CI: 1.28 to 1.78) were independently associated with 30-day mortality, while altered consciousness (OR=7.51, 95% CI: 4.65 to 15.42) and N. meningitidis identification in cerebrospinal fluid (OR=3.45, 95% CI: 1.15 to 10.00) were independently associated with ICU admission. At 12 months, 51.0% of survivors had poor outcomes on the Glasgow Outcome Scale, with significant neurofunctional impairments observed. This study identified key prognostic factors for ICU admission and 30-day mortality in CABM patients. Altered consciousness and N. meningitidis infection were associated with ICU admission, whereas elevated SOFA scores at admission and on day 3 were associated with mortality. Despite intensive care, mortality rates remain high, and long-term neurofunctional deficits are common among survivors. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01730690.

42987255.title: Digital Health Technologies for Mobility Recovery Among Intensive Care Unit Survivors: Scoping Review.
42987255.abstract: Mobility recovery after critical illness is a complex and multidimensional process. Digital health technologies have emerged as approaches for delivering rehabilitation, monitoring recovery, and facilitating self-management among intensive care unit (ICU) survivors. However, the extent to which current digital health approaches address the multidimensional nature of mobility recovery remains unclear. This scoping review aimed to map the current evidence on digital health approaches supporting mobility recovery among ICU survivors and to examine the mobility domains, outcomes, feasibility, and acceptability associated with these approaches. A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from January 2016 to September 21, 2026. Studies involving adult ICU survivors that used digital health approaches to assess, monitor, support, or promote mobility recovery were included. Mobility outcomes were mapped to the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health domains of body functions and structures, activities, and participation. Clinical outcomes were synthesized separately from implementation and user experience outcomes. Twenty-seven reports representing 24 unique parent studies were included. Digital health approaches comprised telemedicine, telerehabilitation, mobile health, wearable monitoring, virtual reality, robot-assisted rehabilitation, and digital recovery platforms. Telemedicine and telerehabilitation were the most frequently reported approaches, and exercise-based rehabilitation was the predominant intervention component. Mobility outcomes were heterogeneous and concentrated on body functions and structures and activity-level performance, particularly muscle strength, exercise capacity, and functional performance, whereas participation outcomes were less frequently represented. Controlled and comparative studies showed mixed between-group findings, with clinical benefits not consistently demonstrated across primary or mobility-related outcomes. In contrast, feasibility, adherence, usability, and acceptability were generally favorable when assessed, although technical difficulties and incomplete device-generated data were reported in some studies. Digital health technologies offer diverse approaches to supporting mobility recovery after critical illness, but current evidence remains concentrated on physical function and activity-level outcomes, with limited attention to participation and long-term recovery. More rigorous and longitudinal studies using standardized, multidimensional mobility outcomes are needed to clarify clinical effectiveness and support sustainable implementation.

42987069.title: Re-signification of the ICU as a place of technological innovation and intersubjective recognition in the COVID-19 pandemic.
42987069.abstract: This opinion piece proposes a critical reflection on the need to redefine care pathways and establish a new praxis in Intensive Care Units (ICU), based on the concept of affect and from the intersubjective perspective of the hospitalized patient. The COVID-19 pandemic has driven a process of productive restructuring in ICU, with advances in technological resources-such as respirators and care protocols, and transformations in professional practices. At the same time, a revaluation of the subjective dimensions of care has emerged, highlighting the relationship of affecting and being affected among professionals, clients, and family members. The health crisis has highlighted the strategic role of ICU in coordinating severe and critical cases and the need to incorporate affect and intersubjectivity as fundamental dimensions of clinical management, demanding a practice with greater cognitive, technical, and ethical depth.

42983706.title: Coronavirus disease 2019 vaccination and reduced severity-related outcomes in high-risk groups in Thailand during the Omicron period.
42983706.abstract: Despite the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) booster vaccination, individuals with comorbidities continue to experience disproportionately severe COVID-19 disease and adverse outcomes. Evidence on associations between vaccination status and clinical outcomes among high-risk group during period of Omicron predominance in low- and middle-income countries remains scarce. This retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Bangkok, Thailand. It aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of COVID-19 infection in high-risk individuals and assess the association between vaccination status and severity-related outcomes, including hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, need for oxygen therapy, and survival at discharge. Of the 1,379 patients, 1,241 (90.0%) received at least two vaccine doses, mainly AZD1222 for the first 1,105 (87.9%) and second 1,073 (86.5%) doses; BNT162b was the most frequently administered booster with 697 (76.7%) doses. Overall, 725 (52.6%) patients were hospitalized, and 585 (80.7%), 286 (39.4%), and 116 (16%) of whom developed pneumonia, required oxygen therapy, and necessitated ICU admission, respectively. Unvaccinated patients demonstrated higher odds of hospitalization (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 6.9; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.0-11.8; p < 0.001), oxygen therapy (aOR = 6.6; 95% CI: 4.2-10.5; p < 0.001), and ICU admission (aOR = 4.6; 95% CI: 2.5-8.4; p < 0.001). Similarly, patients with 1-2 doses exhibited increased odds of hospitalization (aOR = 3.2; 95% CI: 2.4-4·3; p < 0.001, oxygen therapy (aOR = 2.4; 95% CI: 1.6-3.4; p < 0.001), and ICU admission (aOR = 2.9; 95% CI: 1.7-4.8; p < 0.001) compared with those receiving three doses. Patients with chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease were strongly associated with adverse outcomes and ICU admission. During the Omicron period predominance in Thailand, high-risk patients who received two doses of a viral vector vaccine followed by an mRNA booster remained vulnerable to severe COVID-19 infection; receipt of at least three COVID-19 vaccine doses was associated with significantly lower odds of severe outcomes. These findings highlight the significance of continued vaccination strategies, targeted prevention, and timely clinical management in medically vulnerable populations.

42983226.title: A Survey of Clinician-Reported Management of Hypernatremia in the ICU.
42983226.abstract: Hypernatremia is frequent in the intensive care unit (ICU) and is associated with adverse outcomes. Despite its prevalence, robust evidence to guide treatment is lacking, and global practice patterns are largely unknown. We investigated global treatment preferences and clinicians' willingness to enroll patients in a randomized trial to inform its feasibility. This international cross-sectional online survey comprised 20 primarily closed-ended questions, using five-point Likert-scale responses, across four themes: treatment method, threshold, correction rate, and opinion on a proposed trial. Respondents considered a clinical vignette of hypernatremia developing before or during ICU admission, excluding dehydration and chronic causes. It was distributed to ICU physicians worldwide. The survey was sent to 3053 ICU physicians in 17 countries, with 1051 respondents, yielding a response rate of 34%. Of respondents, 74% were consultants, and 26% were residents. The mean ICU experience was 14 years. Increasing free water intake via enteral route was the most frequently reported treatment strategy (80% reporting "often" or "always"). Moderate hypernatremia (plasma sodium 151-156 mmol/L) was the most frequently reported threshold for initiating correction (533/892, 60%). 45% (396/888) preferred a correction rate of 8-12 mmol/L/day, and 41% (366/888) of < 8 mmol/L/day, with the remainder having no correction rate target or correction rate target of > 12 mmol/L/day. 74% (654/882) reported no barriers to enrolling eligible patients in the proposed trial. Among ICU physicians, correction of hypernatremia is mostly achieved by increasing free water intake using hypotonic fluids, predominantly via the enteral route. Most clinicians initiate treatment once hypernatremia reaches a moderate level, aiming for a correction rate of < 12 mmol/L/day. Most clinicians expressed willingness to enroll eligible patients in the proposed trial. This survey study aimed to sample physician preferences for treatment of hypernatremia when on their way to or in the ICU. This study sampled respondents in many countries, and based on different phases of treatment and assessment, as well as participant willingness for a future treatment trial.

42981517.title: Utilizing Coronary Artery Calcification and the COVID-GRAM Score to Predict Critical Illness in COVID-19 Patients.
42981517.journal: WMJ : official publication of the State Medical Society of Wisconsin
42981517.abstract: Coronary artery calcification (CAC), identified on routine chest computed tomography (CT), has been associated with worse outcomes in hospitalized patients with COVID-19. The COVID-GRAM Score is a risk stratification tool developed to predict critical illness in this population. This study compared the predictive performance of CAC identified on chest CT with that of the COVID-GRAM Score for intensive care unit (ICU) admission among hospitalized patients with COVID-19 and evaluated whether combining these measures improved identification of high-risk patients. We hypothesized that CAC would outperform the COVID-GRAM Score. This retrospective cohort study includes 238 adults hospitalized with COVID-19 at a large academic medical center in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, between July 1, 2020, and July 1, 2021. Data were obtained through electronic medical record database queries and chart review. Eligible patients had confirmed COVID-19 infection and no prior history of coronary artery disease. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, sensitivity and specificity analyses, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The mean age was 64  [SD, 15] years, and 46.2% of patients were women. Patients admitted to the ICU had higher mean COVID-GRAM Scores than those not admitted to the ICU (mean [SD], 168 [45.4] vs 150 [44); P = .01). Any CAC was present in 54.2% of ICU-admitted patients compared with 39.1% of patients not admitted to the ICU, and severe CAC was more common among ICU-admitted patients (18.6% vs 5.6%). The area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.61 for illness risk score derived from the COVID-GRAM model, compared with 0.58 for any CAC and 0.57 for severe CAC. Composite measures combining CAC and illness risk score did not improve discriminatory performance. Neither the COVID-GRAM Score nor CAC effectively predicted ICU admission among hospitalized patients with COVID-19. Combining CAC with the illness risk score did not significantly improve predictive performance, highlighting the need for more robust risk stratification tools.

42980044.title: The Effect of an Introductory Palliative Care Education Program in Increasing Knowledge and Communication Self-Efficacy Among NICU Nurses.
42980044.journal: Journal of hospice and palliative nursing : JHPN : the official journal of the Hospice and Palliative Nurses Association
42980044.abstract: Neonatal palliative care is an essential component of care for the most vulnerable infants and their families, yet its provision in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) remains inconsistent, in part due to gaps in nurse education and training. This project evaluated the effect of a brief, introductory palliative care education program on NICU nurses' knowledge and communication self-efficacy. A one-group pretest-posttest design was used at a private hospital NICU in northern California, where 25 NICU nurses completed a 20-minute self-study video and a small-group role-play session covering the SPIKES and NURSE communication tools. A 10-item investigator-developed survey measured knowledge and self-efficacy at baseline, immediately after training, and 4 weeks later. Mean self-efficacy scores rose from 16.7 at baseline to 19.2 immediately after training and 20.1 at 4-week follow-up, with statistically significant immediate and lasting gains in self-efficacy and overall scores (P < .001), although knowledge gains did not reach statistical significance. Prior infant death experience did not affect gains; however, nurses without prior palliative care education showed significantly greater lasting gains in knowledge and overall scores than those with prior training. Four weeks after training, all participants recalled the communication tool acronyms, and 68% reported using them in practice. This brief, low-cost program improved NICU nurses' communication self-efficacy and can be readily incorporated into NICU orientation and continuing education.

42988434.title: Efficacy of phosphodiesterase-3 (PDE-3) inhibitors for the treatment of cerebral vasospasm in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (aSAH) admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU): a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.

42988047.title: Dietitian involvement and nutritional care organization in intensive care and perioperative settings in France: a cross-sectional survey of healthcare professionals.
42988047.abstract: Nutrition is a key component of care for critically ill and surgical patients, but the organization of nutritional care and the involvement of dietitians in ICU and perioperative pathways remain variable. This survey aimed to describe respondent-reported nutritional care organization and dietitian involvement among healthcare professionals working in ICU and perioperative settings in France, with a focus on dietitian availability, clinical involvement, nutritional governance, and selected aspects of perioperative care. We conducted a voluntary cross-sectional survey among physicians and dietitians working in French ICU and perioperative settings. The survey was disseminated during the French Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care Medicine congress, through national professional nutrition and dietetics networks, and via social media. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Overall, 147 professionals responded, mainly ICU physicians and dietitians, and most worked in university hospitals. Among respondents, dietitian availability was reported in 67% of responses, but dedicated time was frequently limited. Involvement was mainly request-based, and participation in medical meetings or ward rounds was uncommon. A medical nutrition lead was identified in 44% of responses, a written nutrition protocol in 50%, and a task-sharing protocol allowing dietitian prescription in 9%. Reported practices suggest that dietitians are available in many French ICUs and contribute to perioperative care pathways. However, access to dietetic expertise does not necessarily translate into dedicated staffing, routine multidisciplinary participation, or structured nutritional governance. Strengthening local organization through medical leadership, written protocols, and multidisciplinary collaboration may help improve the implementation of nutritional care.

42987777.title: From uncertainty to understanding: Shared decision-making, anxiety, and family satisfaction in the intensive care unit.
42987777.abstract: To examine the relationship between shared decision-making (SDM), online information-seeking, state anxiety, and satisfaction, among family decision-makers of intensive care unit (ICU) patients, and to assess whether anxiety mediates the effect of SDM and information search, on satisfaction. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 105 family members serving as surrogate decision-makers for patients hospitalized in a general intensive care unit in a tertiary center. Data assessing SDM, online information seeking, state anxiety, and satisfaction were collected using validated questionnaires. Analyses used Python 3.12 and AMOS 29. Exploratory factor analyses were conducted using principal axis factoring with varimax rotation. Factor retention was based on eigenvalues greater than 1.0 and inspection of scree plots. Factor loadings ≥ 0.40 were considered meaningful, and potential cross-loadings were evaluated during factor interpretation. The model demonstrated good fit (χ²(12) = 14.21, p = .29, CFI = 0.97, RMSEA = 0.04, SRMR = 0.05). Trust in online information was negatively associated with calmness (β = -0.15, p = .049), indicating that reliance on online sources was linked to reduced emotional stability. The arousal component of anxiety demonstrated a marginal positive association with satisfaction (β = 0.36, p = .052). There were no other significant direct effects. Shared decision-making emerged as a central determinant of family satisfaction in ICU settings, while online information seeking was linked to greater emotional activation. Although the hypothesized mediating role of anxiety was not supported, the findings suggest that emotional responses remain an important aspect of family members' experiences during ICU decision-making. ICU clinicians should strengthen structured family-staff communication and ensure relatives' inclusion in decisions. Guiding families toward trustworthy information sources and addressing both informational and emotional needs may reduce distress and enhance satisfaction with care.

42987170.title: Shortening the Family Satisfaction in the ICU (FS-ICU): Development and Validation of a 12-Item Family Satisfaction Survey for Adult ICUs.
42987170.abstract: To develop and validate a shorter Family Satisfaction in the ICU (FS-ICU) questionnaire that reduces survey length while preserving content and psychometric performance for quality improvement and benchmarking. The FS-ICU survey assesses family perceptions of care, communication, and decision-making and has been translated into multiple languages with implementation across diverse health care systems internationally. In a province-wide electronic implementation in Ontario, more than 40% of initiated surveys were incomplete, suggesting that survey length may limit practicality for large-scale quality improvement and benchmarking. Multistage study using provincial FS-ICU survey data and an independent multicenter validation dataset for item reduction, psychometric evaluation, agreement testing, and external validation of a shortened questionnaire. A 12-member expert working group, convened for a Critical Care Services Ontario initiative, used provincial web-based data from adult ICUs across Ontario to develop a shorter version, FS-ICUshort. External validation was applied to FS-ICUshort using a separate multicenter Canadian revised FS-ICU dataset. A 12-member expert working group led by Dr. Daren K. Heyland, including administrative staff, ICU clinical staff, patient experience specialists, and quality improvement specialists from Ontario, used provincial FS-ICU rollout data. None. Using empirical criteria and expert ratings, the FS-ICU was reduced from 29 to 12 items: seven in the satisfaction-with-care domain (FS-Care) and five in the communication and decision-making domain (FS-DM). FS-ICUshort showed high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.93 for FS-Care, 0.86 for FS-DM, and 0.94 for total). Confirmatory factor analysis supported a two-factor structure with better fit than a single-factor model. Scores from FS-ICUshort closely matched full FS-ICU, with mean differences less than or equal to 1.1 points on a 0-100 scale and intraclass correlations of 0.97-0.99. External validation replicated these results. The 12-item FS-ICUshort maintains the core content and psychometric quality of the original FS-ICU while significantly reducing length, supporting routine use in ICU family experience measurement and benchmarking.

42987111.title: The effect of propolis oral care on oral mucositis in intensive care patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a randomized controlled trial.
42987111.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the preventive effect of adding a propolis gargle to standard oral care on the development of oral mucositis in critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. This randomized controlled trial included 60 critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Both groups received the institutional standard oral care protocol with 0.2% chlorhexidine gluconate three times daily. The intervention group additionally received a propolis gargle three times daily for 15 days. Oral mucosal status was evaluated using the total oral mucosa score. There was no significant difference in oral mucosa scores between the groups at baseline, whereas oral mucosa scores were significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group at the 7- and 15-day follow-ups (p<0.001). Adding propolis gargle to standard oral care significantly reduced the development of oral mucositis in critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. However, because the intervention group received additional oral care exposure, the independent effect of propolis cannot be determined and requires further investigation.Clinical Trial Registration Number: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07426198.

42985223.title: Comparative Performance of the COMHON Index and the Braden Scale for Pressure Injury Risk Assessment in Critically Ill Patients: A Retrospective Observational Study Using Consecutive ICU Sampling.
42985223.abstract: Pressure injuries remain a major patient safety concern in critically ill patients admitted to intensive care units (ICUs). Although the Braden Scale is widely used for pressure injury risk assessment, its performance may be limited in highly complex critical care settings. The COMHON Index was developed as an ICU-specific tool integrating physiological variables related to tissue perfusion and oxygenation. To compare the performance of the COMHON Index and the Braden Scale for pressure injury risk assessment in critically ill patients. A retrospective,longitudinal, comparative observational study was conducted in a single ICU inSpain between January 2023 and December 2024, using consecutive nonprobabilitysampling. A total of 476 critically ill patients were included; ICU-acquired pressure injuries developed in 1.9% of patients during the first 24 h after ICU admission. Greater disease severitywas associated with a higher risk of pressure injury. Higher total Braden scores showed a protective effect, whereas COMHON domains related to consciousness, mobility, hemodynamic stability, and oxygenation were directly associated with pressure injury development. The COMHON Nutrition subscale did not reach statistical significance in univariable analysis (OR: 1.38; p = 0.303). In multivariable analysisusing Firth's penalized logistic regression, impaired nutritional status(COMHON) was associated with pressure injury, whereas the Braden sensoryperception and moisture exposure subscales showed inverse associations. At the Youden-optimized cutoffs (Braden ≤ 10; COMHON ≥ 15), the Braden Scale demonstrated 100.0% sensitivity (95% CI: 66.4-100.0) and 77.1% specificity (95% CI: 73.0-80.8), while the COMHON Index demonstrated 88.9% sensitivity (95% CI: 51.8-99.7) and 73.2% specificity (95% CI: 69.0-77.2). Both instruments showed very high negative predictive values (Braden: 100.0%; COMHON: 99.7%). Both instruments were associated withpressure injury occurrence. The final multivariable model incorporated physiological domains from both instruments, two Braden Scale subscales (sensory perception and moisture exposure) and one COMHON Index domain (nutritional status), suggesting complementary rather than substitutive clinical utility. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the retrospective single-center design and low event rate. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm the clinical utility of ICU-specific risk assessment tools in pressure injury prevention. Integrating ICU-specific physiological parameters into pressure injury risk assessment may support earlier identification of critically ill patients requiring intensified preventive interventions, including repositioning protocols, advanced pressure-redistributing surfaces, nutritional optimization, and closer hemodynamic monitoring. These findings may contribute to more individualized nursing care planning and improved allocation of preventive resources in intensive care settings. This study supports the use of ICU-specific risk assessment tools to strengthen patient safety strategies and optimize individualized nursing interventions in critical care settings.

42985140.title: The Impact of Frequent Alarm Exposure on Intensive Care Nurses-A Mapping of the Current State of Knowledge.
42985140.abstract: The caring environment in an intensive care unit is more intense than anywhere else in the hospital. The responsibilities of the intensive care nurse include operating medical equipment and continuously monitoring and evaluating the patient's health status. Great demands are placed on being able to prioritize and be vigilant as situations can quickly become critical. To facilitate these demands, each medical device has an alarm system that warns if parameters can be life-threatening. Alarms have been shown to have an impact on the nurse, but a mapping of the knowledge area is needed to compile the multifactorial impact that alarms can have. The aim of this study was to map the current state of knowledge regarding how alarms in an intensive care context affect intensive care nurses. A scoping review that contains articles using both quantitative and qualitative methods with the aim of mapping the current area of knowledge. One category, Impact of Alarms Exposer on Nurses and Patient Care Delivery, and four subcategories emerged through the analysis: "Adverse physical effects," "Psychological vulnerability," "Negative effects on the work performance," and "Patient safety at risk." Today's technological advances in medicine, and more specifically in patient monitoring, mean that we can monitor patients to a greater extent. This leads to an increased number of alarms and a work environment characterized by more alarms. The conclusion is therefore that alarms have a multifactorial impact on the physical and mental health and work performance of intensive care nurses.

42984675.title: JICS Education: Organ donation in intensive care. The law, ethics and clinical practice.
42984675.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
42984675.abstract: Deceased organ donation is an integral component of intensive care practice. In the UK, around 8000 people are on the active transplant waiting list at any one time, and approximately 3500 deceased donor transplants are performed annually. This article addresses the legal framework for donation in the UK, including the introduction of deemed consent/authorisation across all four nations, the ethical framework provided by the Donation Actions Framework, the role of the Specialist Nurse for Organ Donation (SNOD), optimisation of the donation after brainstem death (DBD) donor, and management of withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment (WLST) in donation after circulatory death (DCD), including normothermic regional perfusion.

42984333.title: Successful eradication of Candida auris in a tertiary care ICU following a nearly 30 month outbreak: a drastic "Unit reset" protocol.
42984333.abstract: Candida auris is a globally emerging, multidrug-resistant pathogen characterized by extreme environmental persistence and resistance to standard hospital disinfectants. Our ICU faced an endemic outbreak that lasted for 30 months, which was resistant to standard infection prevention and control (IPC) bundles. To evaluate the efficacy of a radical, multi-sectoral "Unit Reset" protocol involving total operational decanting, mechanical disassembly, and inventory disposal after incremental IPC strategies were exhausted. We executed a 120-hour "Unit Reset" in February 2026. The intervention comprised: (1) transferring all patients to a temporary satellite site; (2) total disposal of all pharmaceutical and disposable inventories; (3) structural remediation; and (4) dual-team mechanical disinfection with 5,000 ppm hypochlorite supplemented by 18% automated hydrogen peroxide vapor (HPV). Over the 30-month endemic period, C. auris acquisition rates escalated despite high compliance with standard IPC bundles. Environmental surveillance rounds identified persistent reservoirs on high-touch surfaces that the routine cleaning protocols missed. Following the 120-hour Unit Reset, the ICU was reopened to admissions. During the subsequent 16-week active surveillance window, zero new clinical acquisitions or screening-positive cases were detected, representing the first sustained interruption of transmission since August 2023. When C. auris achieves deep environmental sequestration within deteriorated medical infrastructure or complex equipment housings, incremental "enhanced cleaning" protocols may fail due to biofilm shielding. A radical, coordinated institutional reset can terminate entrenched nosocomial transmission when standard IPC bundles reach their limits.

42982308.title: "Bold and necessary experiments:" The redelegation of authority and responsibility to nurses at the origins of cardiac intensive care.
42982308.abstract: Coronary Care Units (CCUs) were at the forefront of the development of intensive care in the 1960s and 1970s. The development of CCUs, and intensive care more broadly, was enabled by the interplay of expanding medical technology and the evolving role of nurses vis-à-vis physicians. This paper examines the history the CCU at New York Hospital, the teaching hospital of Cornell University School of Medicine and School of Nursing, with a particular focus on role of nurses in the unit's success. Drawing from historical archives of New York Hospital and the Cornell University School of Nursing, this paper argues that that nurses were co-creators, alongside physicians, of the NYH CCU, and demonstrates how nurses drew from the NYH CCU experience to expand critical care services at the local and national level, including by advocating for the creation of the NYH medical intensive care unit (MICU), leading a CCU nurse training program to expand regional CCU capability, and contributing expertise to a federally-sponsored national conference on CCUs. A close reading of this history offers lessons and insights as intensive care medicine moves into an uncertain future, chief among them that work of caring for critically ill patients requires the thoughtful integration of new technologies with hands on care.

42982136.title: Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales in intensive care units: England 2022 point-prevalence survey.
42982136.abstract: Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) are increasingly detected in England; however, national hospital prevalence is unknown. We aimed to generate intensive care unit (ICU) CPE prevalence estimates in England. Randomly selected NHS Trusts were invited to participate in a national point prevalence survey (PPS). Each Trust sampled up to 20 patients per ICU on a single date (between 18/04/2022-2/5/2022). Trust-, ICU-, and patient-level data were collected from medical records, including screening policies, demographics, clinical characteristics, and risk factors. CPE status was determined using routine testing. Sixty-six of 111 invited Trusts (59.5%) participated, contributing data from 68 adult, 10 paediatric, and 43 neonatal ICUs. Testing coverage varied across settings: 40.5% (258/637) of adults, 68.1% (62/91) of paediatric patients, and 27.3% (104/381) of neonates were tested. CPE prevalence in screening or clinical specimens was 1.6% in adults (4/258; 95%CI0.4-3.9%), 1.0% in neonates (1/104; 95%CI0.0-5.2%), and 0% in paediatric patients (0/62; 95%CI0.0-5.8%). Most responding Trusts reported screening policies, particularly for adult (95.4%) and paediatric (100%) ICUs, while neonatal policies were less common (82.1%). Screening accounted for 97.9% of tests. Four of five CPE cases were identified in high-screening ICUs, and two patients initially screened negative before later testing positive. Overall, 112 patients were screened to detect one CPE case. This first national CPE PPS found <2% prevalence in ICUs. Variation in screening practice limits inference about underlying carriage prevalence but highlights heterogeneity in policy implementation. No policy changes are recommended, however, these findings support further evaluation of serial post-admission screening.

42982067.title: Breathlessness mechanisms, measurement, and management in adults: evidence update on behalf of The Dyspnoea Society.
42982067.abstract: Breathlessness affects an estimated 40% of adults living with chronic disease, with substantial consequences for individuals, carers, and health-care systems. This Dyspnoea Society Research Statement, developed for researchers, clinicians, and adults living with or caring for someone with breathlessness, provides a state-of-the-art synthesis of recent advances in chronic breathlessness mechanisms, measurement, and management, and outlines a research agenda for the next decade. Key advancements include establishment of neural respiratory drive as a mechanistic contributor to exertional breathlessness; neuroimaging evidence that breathlessness arises from integration of peripheral and central processes within a dynamic brain network involving sensorimotor and cognitive-affective regions, supporting behavioural and psychosocial interventions; and improved measurement through responsive multidimensional instruments and approaches to quantify symptom abnormality relative to physical activity. Evidence supports early use of low-risk, non-pharmacological interventions for management of breathlessness, whereas evidence for pharmacological therapies is limited in most situations. Health-care redesign, including symptom-focused diagnostic pathways, integrated care models, and disease-agnostic breathlessness services, might help to improve patient outcomes while reducing health-care costs.

42981082.title: Reduced desaturation-based detection of sleep apnea events in self-identified Black individuals across two cohorts.
42981082.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
42981082.abstract: Pulse oximetry may overestimate oxygen saturation in individuals with darker skin pigmentation, potentially reducing detection of desaturation during sleep-disordered breathing. To assess racial/ethnic differences in desaturation-based obstructive event detection and cardiovascular risk, and evaluate heart-rate response as an oximetry-independent marker for risk stratification. We analyzed participants without cardiovascular disease in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis(MESA) and Sleep Heart Health Study(SHHS). We modeled desaturation-based AHI relative to airflow-defined AHI and examined AHI-ΔHR6, defined by respiratory events with a heart-rate increase ≥6 beats/min. Adjusted Cox models evaluated associations with a composite outcome, major adverse cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality(MACE/mortality). Black participants had 21% and 20% lower proportions of airflow-defined events meeting the ≥4% desaturation criterion than White participants in MESA (ratio 0.79[95% CI,0.68-0.93]; p = 0.003) and SHHS (0.80[0.68-0.94]; p = 0.008), respectively. No other racial/ethnic group showed a lower proportion of airflow-defined events meeting desaturation criteria than White participants. AHI-ΔHR6 event detection was similar between Black and White participants in both cohorts. In Whites participants, desaturation-based events were associated with MACE/mortality in MESA but not in SHHS, while desaturation-based AHI measures were not significantly associated with MACE/mortality in Black individuals in either cohort. In contrast, AHI-ΔHR6 was associated with MACE/mortality in MESA (HR 1.33[1.09-1.63];p=0.006) and SHHS (1.26[1.02-1.55]; p = 0.033). Desaturation-based scoring identified a lower proportion of reduced flow events in Black than White participants, whereas heart-rate-response-based event detection was similar across groups, suggesting oximetry-related under-detection in individuals with darker pigment.

42994832.title: Association between the geriatric nutritional risk index and dysphagia in older critically ill patients: A retrospective analysis of the MIMIC-IV database.
42994832.abstract: Evidence regarding the association between nutritional status and dysphagia in older ICU patients remains limited. We assessed the association between the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) and the prevalence of dysphagia in this population. Patients aged ≥ 65 years were identified from the MIMIC-IV (v3.1) database and divided into GNRI quartiles: Q1 (≤89.88), Q2 (89.89-99.19), Q3 (99.20-109.38), and Q4 (≥109.39). Associations were examined using logistic regression models (univariable and multivariable). Potential nonlinearity was modeled by restricted cubic splines (RCS), and the inflection point was identified via threshold-effect analysis. Robustness was then assessed through subgroup and sensitivity analyses. In 1576 patients (mean age 77.3 ± 7.8 years; 44.5% female), a lower GNRI was associated with a higher prevalence of dysphagia. Relative to the lowest quartile (Q1, reference), the adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for dysphagia in Q2, Q3, and Q4 were 0.45 (95% CI 0.30-0.69), 0.42 (95% CI 0.27-0.66), and 0.34 (95% CI 0.21-0.55), respectively (all P < .001; P for trend < 0.001). RCS analysis showed a significant nonlinear association between GNRI and dysphagia (P for nonlinearity = 0.01), and the inflection point was located at a GNRI of 91.21 (95% CI 90.85-91.56). These associations were consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses, although some weighted estimates should be interpreted with caution. In this cohort of older ICU patients who underwent swallowing assessment within 24 hours of admission, a lower GNRI was associated with a higher prevalence of dysphagia defined by bedside nursing swallow-screening. The association appeared more pronounced within the lower GNRI range and attenuated at higher GNRI levels. Overall, these descriptive findings indicate that dysphagia is more prevalent among patients with a lower GNRI, underscoring the importance of closely monitoring swallowing status in this subgroup.

42992494.title: [Investigation of Biofilm Formation and als1, hwp1 and sap1 Genes in Candida Species Isolated from Urine Samples of Intensive Care Patients Using PCR].
42992494.abstract: Candida species are among the important opportunistic agents associated with urinary tract infections and candiduria in intensive care units. Biofilm formation is clinically significant in terms of persistence and antifungal treatment failure in catheter-related infections. This study aimed to investigate the biofilm-forming ability of Candida species isolated from urine cultures of patients followed in intensive care units and the als1, hwp1 and sap1 genes which have been reported to be associated with biofilm, using polymerase chain reaction (PCR). A total of 70 Candida isolates obtained from pediatric and adult urine cultures were included in the study. Biofilm formation was evaluated using the 2,3-bis-(2-methoxy-4-nitro-5-sulfophenyl)-2H-tetrazolium-5-carboxanilide (XTT) reduction method. PCR was performed to detect positivity for the als1, hwp1 and sap1 genes. Biofilm formation was detected in a total of 63 isolates (90.0%). Biofilm formation was more frequent in the adult group (97.1%) than in the pediatric group (82.8%), but the difference was not statistically significant (p= 0.106). Positivity rates for als1, hwp1 and sap1 genes were determined to be 69.6%, 52.2% and 69.6% in Candida albicans isolates and 8.5%, 6.4% and 6.4% in non-albicans Candida species isolates respectively and the difference between the groups was statistically significant (p< 0.001). In C.albicans isolates, the most frequently detected gene profile in biofilm-producing isolates was the als1-hwp1-sap1 triple positivity and this gene combination was more frequently detected in isolates forming moderate to strong biofilms. In our study, als1, hwp1 and sap1 genes were detected significantly more frequently in C.albicans isolates compared to non-albicans Candida isolates. This is consistent with the role of these genes in C.albicans biology. Due to the limitations of boilbased DNA extraction and primers, negative PCR results, particularly for non-albicans Candida species, should not be interpreted as gene absence. While our pediatric unit data contribute to local epidemiology, more advanced extraction methods and larger sample sizes are needed for definitive results.

42989512.title: Perceptions and Needs Regarding Training in Nurse-Performed Lung Ultrasound in ICU: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Survey.
42989512.abstract: This research aims to assess the awareness, willingness to participate in training and specific requirements of Chinese ICU nurses regarding nurse-performed lung ultrasound (LUS). The survey was a cross-sectional study targeting eligible nurses officially working in Chinese ICUs. A structured questionnaire was distributed online to ICU nurses nationwide from May 22, 2023 to August 12, 2023. The questionnaire was designed by a multidisciplinary team, and revised based on expert feedback and pilot testing. It consists of three parts: basic information of participants and their departments, nurses' recognition and application experience with LUS and demand for standardized nurse-performed LUS training. Ethical approval was obtained and informed consent was obtained from all participants before they completed the questionnaire. A total of 1104 questionnaires were analysed. The survey involved 486 hospitals in 31 provinces of Chinese Mainland. Among them, 52.4% were clinical staff nurses without official positions, 86.6% came from tertiary hospitals and 63.0% were working in integrated ICUs. 6.6% of respondents reported that their department did not have an ultrasound machine. 91.8% of the participants were willing to participate in standardized nurse-performed LUS training. 93.6% of the participants believed that nurses should master the technique, and 97.4% recognized the benefits of mastering LUS for patient treatment. Multivariate regression analysis revealed that non-staff-nurse positions, hospital level, previous ultrasound training experience, recognition of the need for mastering LUS, belief in the benefits of mastering LUS for patient treatment, and paying attention to research related to LUS were positively associated with greater willingness to participate in standardized nurse-performed LUS training. Furthermore, the participants expressed the desire to acquire relevant theoretical and operational knowledge in various aspects, including lung diseases (81.4%), basic knowledge of ultrasound (86.3%), theoretical knowledge (81.8%), practical operation of LUS (85.7%), image interpretation (82%) and nursing plans guided by LUS (80.4%). Chinese ICU nurses showed a high level of willingness to participate in standardized nurse-performed LUS training and recognized its clinical value. However, their training needs were diverse, and some reported limited access to ultrasound equipment. These findings support the development of structured, accessible training programmes tailored to ICU nursing practice. The findings suggest a pressing need for more training and education to promote the use of nurse-performed LUS in ICUs. Adequate resources, including equipment and time, should be provided to facilitate LUS practice. These measures may help support safer, more timely bedside assessment and patient care. This study provides preliminary insights into the training preferences of ICU nurses regarding nurse-performed LUS and identifies factors associated with willingness to participate in training. The findings may inform future structured training programmes and support the integration of nurse-performed LUS into ICU practice. This study was reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) checklist for cross-sectional studies. Patients and the public were not involved in the design, conduct, analysis or reporting of this study.

42994283.title: Temporal regularization of a dynamic graph network for ordinal prediction of discharge disposition after ischemic stroke in intensive care.
42994283.abstract: Early identification of poor outcome after acute ischemic stroke is difficult. Electronic health record models often discard the physiological trajectory; whether a biological prior improves prediction is unclear. We studied 5,101 MIMIC-IV admissions with cerebral infarction, ICD-10 I63; 2,874 had a usable intensive care time series, a mapped outcome and static features at a 24 h landmark. The outcome was discharge disposition on a six-level scale, every predictor restricted to the first 24 h. A dynamic graph recurrent network applied a monotone-progress, bounded-drift penalty to its trajectory score, tested against a matched generic smoothness penalty and two negative controls under patient-grouped cross-validation. At the 24 h landmark the gradient-boosted model with time-series summaries reached a macro-AUC of 0.743, 95% CI 0.733 to 0.753. The nested stacking ensemble reached 0.750, 0.739 to 0.760, a difference compatible with zero; it was not transported externally. Reversing or time-permuting the penalty, or substituting a smoothness penalty, left the macro-AUC within 0.002; no pathway information enters the loss. The transported gradient-boosted model reached 0.809 in eICU-CRD and 0.814 in MIMIC-III. A second, harmonized-schema ensemble reached 0.844 in eICU-CRD, 0.029 above its strongest component, but that gain did not carry to MIMIC-III. Discharge disposition after ischemic stroke is partly predictable from the first 24 h of intensive care data, and no ensemble gain was established. The penalty is a generic smoothness constraint motivated by, not derived from, transcriptomic observations. The endpoint is care placement, not functional recovery.

42991713.title: Association and incremental predictive performance of preoperative nutritional and inflammatory indices for postoperative ICU admission after hepatobiliary and pancreatic tumor surgery.
42991713.abstract: Preoperative nutritional and inflammatory status may influence perioperative outcomes in patients undergoing hepatobiliary and pancreatic tumor surgery. This study aimed to compare the associations and incremental predictive value of six nutrition- and inflammation-related indices for postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission. This retrospective cohort study included 1,195 patients undergoing hepatobiliary or pancreatic tumor surgery from the INSPIRE database. We evaluated the geriatric nutritional risk index (GNRI) and five other nutritional and inflammatory indices using logistic regression and restricted cubic splines. Regression estimates were pooled across 20 imputed datasets using Rubin's rules. Predictive metrics were averaged across imputations, with bootstrap assessment of uncertainty and optimism. Among 1,195 patients, 141 (11.8%) experienced postoperative ICU admission. Higher transformed GNRI was associated with lower adjusted odds of ICU admission (OR 0.601, 95% CI 0.497-0.728). Adding GNRI increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.766 to 0.800 (95% CI, 0.764-0.835). The incremental AUC was 0.033 before rounding, and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.780 (95% CI, 0.744-0.816). Albumin alone yielded a similar apparent AUC of 0.799. Other indices added little discrimination beyond GNRI. GNRI showed the highest observed incremental discrimination among the six indices, although albumin alone performed similarly. These findings support further evaluation of preoperative risk assessment in hepatobiliary and pancreatic tumor surgery.

42990066.title: Perceived Organisational Support, Work Engagement and Disaster Literacy Among Critical Care Reserve Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Path Analysis.
42990066.abstract: To examine the associations among perceived organisational support, work engagement and self-reported disaster literacy in critical care reserve nurses, and to assess the indirect association between perceived organisational support and self-reported disaster literacy through work engagement. Hospital resilience during public health emergencies depends on a reserve nursing workforce that can be rapidly mobilised and can translate disaster-related information into safe clinical action. However, the organisational and motivational conditions associated with disaster literacy in this workforce remain insufficiently understood. This cross-sectional survey included all 113 nurses who were enrolled in a critical care training programme and registered in an emergency reserve pool at a tertiary hospital in China. Data from validated self-report instruments were analysed using Pearson correlations and observed-variable path analysis with 5000 bootstrap resamples. The adjusted model included demographic and training covariates. Perceived organisational support correlated with work engagement (r = 0.588) and self-reported disaster literacy (r = 0.540), and work engagement correlated with self-reported disaster literacy (r = 0.565). In the adjusted model, perceived organisational support was associated with work engagement (β = 0.570) and self-reported disaster literacy (β = 0.307), while work engagement was associated with self-reported disaster literacy (β = 0.449). The standardised indirect association through work engagement was β = 0.256 (bias-corrected 95% CI [0.135, 0.440]).The indirect and direct estimates represented approximately 45.5% and 54.5%, respectively, of the total model-estimated association; these percentages reflect mathematical coefficient decomposition in the specified cross-sectional model and should not be interpreted as proportions of a causal mediated effect. Perceived organisational support, work engagement and self-reported disaster literacy were positively associated; however, the cross-sectional design precludes conclusions about temporal order or causality. Nurse managers should consider organisational support and work engagement alongside technical competence when developing reserve-workforce preparedness programmes. Strategies such as protected training time and psychologically safe debriefing warrant prospective evaluation.

42993968.title: Acute Right Heart Failure Following Left Coronary Myocardial Infarction in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Patients: A Case Series and Mechanistic Insight.
42993968.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
42993968.abstract: Right heart failure (RHF) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs). While right coronary artery infarction is a recognized cause of acute RHF, the ventricular consequences of left coronary system infarction in LVAD-supported patients are not well characterized. We describe two patients supported with HeartMate III LVADs who developed acute RHF within 24-48 hours after successful revascularization of acute left coronary system occlusions (mid-left anterior descending artery and left main coronary artery). Both had previously stable LVAD function and no evidence of advanced RHF. After revascularization, each developed hypotension, rising central venous pressure, reduced LVAD flows, and echocardiographic evidence of severe right ventricular (RV) dilation and dysfunction with septal shift toward the left ventricle. Hemodynamic deterioration reversed with inotropic support, diuresis, and LVAD speed adjustment, without mechanical RV support. These cases suggest left coronary acute myocardial infarction (AMI) may precipitate acute RHF in LVAD-supported patients through septal ischemia with impaired ventricular interdependence, acute increases in RV afterload, and relative RV ischemia despite patent right coronary arteries. Heightened surveillance and early echocardiographic assessment after left-sided AMI in LVAD recipients may enable prompt recognition and timely intervention.

42993069.title: Development and Validation of a Pre-COPD Score to Predict Incident COPD.
42993069.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
42993069.abstract: The ability to predict progression from a pre-disease state in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), pre-COPD, to overt COPD remains limited. To test the hypothesis that development of COPD can be predicted by characterizing pre-COPD and creating a simple pre-COPD score. We identified individuals without airflow obstruction, defined as pre-bronchodilator (BD) forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC)≥0.70 and ≥lower limit of normal, from the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS)(N = 14,506), Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS)(N = 8673), and Genetic Epidemiology for COPD (COPDGene) Study(N = 2982). A pre-COPD score was developed in CGPS by assigning 1 point to each of smoking history≥10 pack-years, active smoking, any respiratory symptom, asthma, and pre-BD FEV1/FVC 0.70-0.75, and 4 points for pre-BD FEV1<80% predicted, indicating presence of Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry (PRISm), with external validation in CCHS and COPDGene. Participants were followed for 5-10 years for incident COPD, defined as pre-BD FEV1/FVC<0.70 and FEV1<80% predicted. During follow-up, COPD developed in 669 individuals (4.6%) in CGPS, 685 (7.9%) in CCHS, and 367 (12%) in COPDGene. In CGPS, 10-year incidence was 1.5% in the low-risk, 9.3% in the intermediate-risk, 24% in the high-risk, and 42% in the very high-risk category. Corresponding 5-year incidences were 3.7%, 7.3%, 12%, and 25% in CCHS, and 4.1%, 5.3%, 13%, and 31% in COPDGene, respectively. The pre-COPD score demonstrated good discrimination with areas under curve of 0.88 in CGPS, 0.76 in CCHS, and 0.81 in COPDGene. The pre-COPD score was also associated with exacerbations. The pre-COPD score is useful in predicting the onset of COPD with clinically relevant discrimination in three cohorts with different risk profiles.
